description: The Japanese joke is that Nanjo will not grant a takeback after a mistaken chess move; the English instead makes Kinzo warn Nanjo about a mistake Nanjo is about to make. That changes the participants' actions and the basis of Kinzo's claim that they are even.
sourceReading: 指し間違えた手 is a move already played incorrectly; 待て here requests a takeback, which Nanjo refuses. The comparison concerns each friend refusing the other a concession.

units.text: "Hahahaha...  And you never listen when I warn you about a mistaken chess move you're about to make.  It seems we are even."
units.note: Both advance warning instead of chess takeback; legacy MG-EP01-OP-001 recorded.
units.japanese: 「はっはっはっは…。お前とて、指し間違えた手を待てと言っても聞かぬではないか。ならば相子というものだろう。」
candidates: warn you about a mistaken chess move you're about to make

units.text: "Hahahaha... And you never listen when I warn you about a mistaken chess move you're about to make. It seems only fair, does it not?"

description: Japanese 至りますまい predicts that Kinzo will not get as far as cornering Nanjo's king. WH says he has not cornered it yet, turning a prediction of death before completion into a report about the present board position. The following narration makes the intended lifespan analogy explicit.
sourceReading: Embedded Japanese row 3238 explicitly says Kinzo will die before the game is decided; this corroborates the future prediction, not merely an unfinished board position.

units.text: "......Let us illustrate it with the chess game here.  You have very nearly achieved checkmate...but you have not yet cornered my king."
units.note: MG not yet vs UP prospective failure restored; legacy MG-EP01-OP-002 recorded.
units.japanese: 「……このチェスで例えましょう。金蔵さんの詰めもなかなかですが、私のキングを追い詰めるには至りますまい。」

units.text: "......Let us illustrate it with the chess game here. You have very nearly achieved checkmate, ...but you have not yet cornered my king."

description: Battler denies having the romantic exploits Eva imagines and says he would rather have her introduce him to someone (紹介してほしい). WH replaces that request with “I’d rather it did,” whose antecedent is the supposedly weird experience of leaving girls crying. The reply changes from an inexperienced young man asking for help meeting girls into wishing the alleged exploits had happened.
sourceReading: 紹介してほしい is a desire to be introduced; the surrounding talk supplies girls as its contextual object. It does not mean wanting to have made girls cry.

units.text: "Wh, what?  Y, y, you're joking, right!?  Of course nothing weird like that's ever happened to me!  In fact, I'd rather it did!"
units.note: Both if you know anyone recovers requested romantic introduction rather than wishing experience.
units.japanese:
「わたたたッ、
じょじょ、
冗談じゃないっすよ！
そんな妙な武勇伝、あるわけないじゃない～！　むしろ紹介してほしいくらいっす～！」

description: Japanese calls the speech a suspicious Kansai-like dialect (怪しい関西弁風) and tentatively his own invention (オリジナル？). WH calls it an odd Kansai dialect, dropping both the imitation qualifier and the narrator’s question about its originality. This weakens the explicit joke about a Kanto businessman’s homemade regional persona.
sourceReading: The source distinguishes Kansai-like imitation from unqualified Kansai dialect and marks the originality claim with a question.

units.text: He speaks in an odd and very noticeable Kansai dialect, but he's actually a natural-born Kanto man. Apparently, impressions are everything in the business world, so speaking in a different style than other people is an act that makes him stick out more. ......However, I hear that he gets embarrassed when talking within earshot of a real Kansai person, so he switches back to standard Japanese. ...I don't really get it, but he's definitely an interesting person.
units.note: MG Kansai dialect lacks invented qualification; UP Kansai-style of own creation restores.
units.japanese: 印象的な怪しい関西弁風の方言はオリジナル？のもので、本人は生粋の関東人だ。

units.text: He speaks in an odd and very noticeable Kansai dialect, but he's actually a natural-born Kanto man. Apparently, impressions are everything in the business world, so speaking in a different style than other people is an act that makes him stick out more. ......However, I hear he gets embarrassed when talking within earshot of a real Kansai person, so he switches back to standard Japanese. ...I don't really get it, but he's definitely an interesting person.

units.japanese: 印象的な怪しい関西弁風の方言はオリジナル？　のもので、本人は生粋の関東人だ。何でも、ビジネスの世界では印象付けが大事とかで、他の人とは毛色の違う言葉を狙って話すことで自分をより印象付けようという演出らしいんだが。……もっとも、本場の関西人の前では恥ずかしいので、標準語に戻すんだとか。…よくわからんが面白い人なのは間違いない。

description: After Eva stops a kick at Rudolf’s nose and threatens another blow, Rudolf apologizes for his sister’s 足癖の悪い behavior. WH instead apologizes for “that strange way she walks,” inventing an odd gait and breaking the direct callback to her kicking.
sourceReading: The immediately preceding kick fixes the relevant sense: a bad habit of using her feet against people.

units.text: "...Sheesh, what a pain.  Guess I have to apologize for that strange way she walks too."
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese: 「…はー、いやいや。足癖の悪い姉貴で本当に申し訳ないです。」

units.text: "...Sheesh, what a pain. I'm so sorry she can't help walking like a freak."
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese: 「…はー、いやいや。足癖の悪い姉貴で本当に申し訳ないです」

description: George says Battler seems already to have some of the qualities he himself lacks. WH says Battler has “far surpassed me on all of those counts.” This adds a comparison of degree and replaces some with all, materially amplifying George’s compliment and self-effacement.
sourceReading: それらのいくつか means some of those qualities; すでにある means already possesses. The next clause predicts future overtaking on adulthood.

units.text: "Like me?  Oh, I still have a long way to go.  I still have very little experience out there in the real world, and I need to work on becoming more bold and sociable.  ...I think you've far surpassed me on all of those counts, Battler-kun.  I'm sure you'll outstrip me fast enough when you become an adult." George-aniki scratched his head and laughed, as though trying to hide his embarrassment.
units.note: Both retain far surpassed / all counts against some already present qualities; identical local dramatic function.
units.japanese: 「僕かい？　僕なんかまだまださ。社会経験が全然足りないし社交性も度胸も足りない。…戦人くんには、それらのいくつかがすでにあるように思うよ。だからきっと、成人したら僕なんかすぐに追い抜いちゃうさ。」
candidates: far surpassed me on all of those counts

description: In the metal-detector passage, Japanese contrasts the less imposing atmosphere with an international flight’s procedures, while noting even a small plane is still an aircraft. WH makes the contrast physical: “Our small plane wasn’t as massive as an international flight.” The security rationale becomes an aircraft-size comparison.
sourceReading: 物々しさ describes the imposing or elaborate atmosphere of the checks here, not the aircraft’s mass.

units.text: We had to go through a metal detector before going out on the runway. Our small plane wasn't as massive as an international flight, but it was still a plane. A staff member holding a metal detector checked us all. Once all of us cleared the check, we followed the staff member out onto the runway.
units.note: Both render less imposing security procedures as smaller aircraft size. Same Japanese distinction and local narrative function; WH analysis applies.
units.japanese: 国際線のような物々しさはなかったが、小型機とはいえ一応は飛行機だ。
candidates: wasn't as massive as an international flight

units.text: We had to go through a metal detector before going out on the runway. Our small plane wasn't as massive as an international flight, but it was still a plane. A staff member holding a metal detector checked us all. Once all of us cleared the check, we followed the staff member out onto the runway.
units.note: Both render less imposing security procedures as smaller aircraft size. Same Japanese distinction and local narrative function; WH analysis applies.
units.japanese: 滑走路に出る前に金属検査を受ける。国際線のような物々しさはなかったが、小型機とはいえ一応は飛行機だ。金属探知機を持った職員にボディチェックを受ける。並んだ全員がチェックをクリアすると、職員の先導で滑走路に出た。
candidates: wasn't as massive as an international flight

description: Kumasawa’s お迎え待ち is a death euphemism in her self-deprecating reply: the decrepit woman awaiting her own final summons is welcoming the guests. WH makes her merely the woman waiting to greet them. The repeated お迎え loses the collision of guest pickup and death’s arrival, following Rudolf’s one-foot-in-the-coffin joke.
sourceReading: The greeting sense belongs to お迎えでは; お迎え待ちの老いぼれ qualifies the old woman as awaiting death.

units.text: "Hoh-hoh-ho, Eva-sama, you are harsh as usual.  I found myself with some urgent purchases to make, and while I was at it, I thought I would come welcome you all.  Although, it does give a bad impression if the one waiting to greet you is a decrepit old woman.  Hoh-hoh-ho...!"
units.note: Both use one waiting to greet you, losing awaiting death/final summons pun. Preceding coffin joke establishes source function.
units.japanese: 「ほっほっほ、絵羽さまは相変わらず手厳しゅうございます。急なお買い物がありましたもので、そのついでに皆様のお迎えをしようと思いまして。もっともお迎え待ちの老いぼれのお迎えでは景気もお悪いでしょうが。ほっほっほ…！」

units.text: "Hohohoh, Eva-sama, you're as harsh as ever. I found myself with some urgent purchases to make, and while I was at it, I thought I would come welcome you all. Although, it does give a bad impression if the one waiting to greet you is a decrepit old woman. Hohohoh...!"
units.note: Both use one waiting to greet you, losing awaiting death/final summons pun. Preceding coffin joke establishes source function.

units.text: "Hoh‐hoh‐ho, Eva‐sama, you are harsh as usual. I found myself with some urgent purchases to make, and while I was at it, I thought I would come welcome you all. Although, it does give a bad impression if the one waiting to greet you is a decrepit old woman. Hoh‐hoh‐ho...!"
units.note: Both use one waiting to greet you, losing awaiting death/final summons pun. Preceding coffin joke establishes source function.
units.japanese: 「ほっほっほ、絵羽さまは相変わらず手厳しゅうございます。急なお買い物がありましたもので、そのついでに皆様のお迎えをしようと思いまして。もっともお迎え待ちの老いぼれのお迎えでは景気もお悪いでしょうが。ほっほっほ…！」

description: Rosa has remembered last year’s promise and bought the tea. Kumasawa is touched not only by that remembered promise but by Rosa bringing a gift even for a servant. WH says ‘Whether or not Kumasawa ... remembered’ the promise. It assigns the remembering to the recipient and replaces the additive ばかりか construction with uncertainty.
sourceReading: The preceding narration explicitly identifies Rosa as the person faithfully remembering and fulfilling her promise. Kumasawa is the experiencer of 感激, while the remembered promise and gift are the reasons.

units.text: Whether or not Kumasawa baa-chan remembered this year-old promise, she seemed deeply touched by the fact that someone would bring a gift to a simple servant like her.
units.note: Both correctly assign remembered promise to Rosa and retain not only/but gift to servant. WH recipient/uncertainty error no longer applies; do not copy it into error counts.
units.japanese: 熊沢の婆ちゃんは一年前の約束を覚えていたばかりか、使用人である自分にまで土産を持ってきてくれたことにとても感激しているようだった。

description: Jessica says the boat has four high-performance propellers. WH describes ‘four-base high efficiency propellers,’ treating the machine counter 基 as part of the apparatus description and losing the explicit count of four individual propellers.
sourceReading: ４基 counts four installed units; it does not describe a four-base design. The exceeding-40-knots boast remains separately expressed.

units.text: "Anyway, it's the captain's pride and joy, and it's a kinda modded high-speed boat.  Seems he tinkers with big parts of it.  He was bragging about how he attached four-base high efficiency propellers to it so that he could break 40 knots or something like that.  I just remember how he's always bragging."
units.note: MG retains four-base; UP explicitly four propellers. Count, speed and reported captain boast considered together.
units.japanese: 「何しろ、船長自慢の改造高速艇らしいぜ？　だいぶいじってるらしく、プロペラは高性能のが４基も付いてて最高速度は４０ノットを超えるとか何とか自慢してたなー。いつも自慢されるんで覚えちまったぜ。」

units.text: "Anyway, it's the captain's pride and joy, a kind of modded high-speed boat. Seems he's got it pretty souped up. He was bragging about how he attached four-base high efficiency propellers to make it break 40 knots, or something like that. He talks about it all the time, so I've sorta memorized the spiel."
units.note: MG retains four-base; UP explicitly four propellers. Count, speed and reported captain boast considered together.
units.japanese: 「何しろ、船長自慢の改造高速艇らしいぜ？　だいぶいじってるらしく、プロペラは高性能のが４基も付いてて最高速度は４０ノットを超えるとか何とか自慢してたなー。いつも自慢されるんで覚えちまったぜ」

description: George and Kumasawa bring one well-chilled can of juice per person, with droplets on the cans. WH supplies both glasses with floating ice cubes and canned drinks. It changes surface condensation into ice and adds drinking vessels.
sourceReading: 雫の浮く modifies the chilled 缶ジュース: droplets beading on the cans. 人数分 supplies enough cans for the group.

units.text: George-aniki and Kumasawa baa-chan brought us all glasses with floating ice cubes and canned drinks.
units.note: Both preserve cans with condensation; invented glasses/ice cubes gone.
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴と熊沢の婆ちゃんが、よく冷えた雫の浮く缶ジュースを人数分、持ってきてくれた。

description: George says his parents repeatedly urged him about entrance exams when those exams were approaching. WH says ‘When I was slacking off during exams,’ inventing neglect and moving the pressure into the exam period. This changes his account of his parents’ insistence and his own younger conduct.
sourceReading: 受験を控えてた頃 means when entrance examinations were ahead of him; 控える does not mean slacking off here.

units.text: "Hahaha, oh no.  When I was slacking off during exams, I was always getting told 'exams, exams'.  I thought it was annoying, but now I'm grateful."
units.note: MG before exams removes slacking and preserves upcoming timing. UP retains during/slacking claim. Both express eventual gratitude; defect affects George’s earlier conduct.
units.japanese: 「はっはは、とんでもない。僕も受験を控えてた頃はいっつも受験受験って言われてたよ。うるさくも思ったけど、今は感謝してるよ。」

units.text: "Hahaha, oh no. When I was slacking off during exams, I was always getting told "exams, exams". I thought it was annoying, but now I'm grateful."
units.note: MG before exams removes slacking and preserves upcoming timing. UP retains during/slacking claim. Both express eventual gratitude; defect affects George’s earlier conduct.
units.japanese: 「はっはは、とんでもない。僕も受験を控えてた頃はいっつも受験受験って言われてたよ。うるさくも思ったけど、今は感謝してるよ」

description: After George expresses gratitude for his parents’ pressure, Battler calls him 人間が出来てる, praising his mature character. WH has ‘George-aniki can be human too,’ which reads as discovering human vulnerability or ordinary humanity rather than admiring maturity. It breaks Battler’s impressed response to George’s gratitude.
sourceReading: 人間が出来ている is well-developed character or maturity, not the ability to be human. やっぱり reinforces Battler’s established admiration.

units.text: "Hah, I knew it, George-aniki can be human too...  Anyway, I have to look after myself.  No one tells me what to do!  Well, it's not like I'd listen if they did, hihihi!"
units.note: Awesome/magnanimous express praise for George’s character; can be human too error gone. Magnanimous captures generous gratitude, though mature would be closer.
units.japanese: 「はー、やっぱり譲治兄貴は人間が出来てるなぁ…。ちなみにウチは絶賛放任中だからな。なぁんにも言われないぜぇ？　まー言われたって聞かねぇけどなー、ひっひっひ！」

description: Kumasawa asks whether Battler has not yet returned to the parental home. WH asks whether he still ‘cannot return,’ introducing an obstacle or inability. His reply describes occasional visits and belongings still at the previous house; subsequent narration says he has had to return after his maternal grandparents died.
sourceReading: まだ ... 戻られておられない asks about the state of not yet having returned; the honorific passive-form 戻られる is not an inability construction.

units.text: "Battler-san, you still cannot return to your home?"
units.note: Both ask not yet returned, not cannot return. Subsequent residence account preserves maternal name and forced return after grandparents deaths.
units.japanese: 「戦人さんは、まだご実家には戻られておられないのですか？」

description: Jessica agrees with Battler’s proposed natural cause, but then states that the shrine disappeared this summer. WH carries uncertainty into the separate date statement: ‘It probably disappeared during the summer.’ Readers lose the definite seasonal anchor supplied by the island resident, independently of whether the proposed cause is true.
sourceReading: 私もそうだと思ってる qualifies agreement with the wave explanation. なくなっちゃったのはこの夏のことなんだよ then asserts the season without a probability marker.

units.text: "I think so too.  It probably disappeared during the summer.  Whatever."
units.note: Both give unhedged summer disappearance separately from agreement with wave explanation. WH probable-date error gone. MG last summer refers most recent summer in October setting, not necessarily previous calendar year.
units.japanese: 「私もそうだと思ってるんだけどよ。なくなっちゃったのはこの夏のことなんだよ。何でもよぅ、」

description: Jessica’s 何でもよぅ introduces something heard, continued by Kumasawa’s だとか report of lightning destroying the shrine. WH has Jessica dismiss it with ‘Whatever,’ then makes Kumasawa propose ‘Or perhaps’ lightning. The reported account becomes an alternative she is speculating about rather than an account circulating independently of her suggestion.
sourceReading: 何でも and だとか mark hearsay; they do not certify lightning as fact. The following fishermen’s ominous interpretation is another explicitly attributed report.

units.text: "Or perhaps a huge lightning bolt fell one evening and smashed the shrine...  ......The fisherman whisper that having a thunderbolt fall upon our honored tutelary God would be a certain sign of misfortune.  ...Lightning begone, lightning begone..."
units.note: MG they say / UP apparently and or some such preserve reported lightning account, rather than proposed speculative alternative. Fishermen whispering omen remains distinct from verified cause.
units.japanese: 「ある晩に大きな稲妻が落ちて、御社を砕いてしまったんだとか…。……鎮守様に落雷があるなど、これは不吉の徴に違いないと、漁民たちは囁いておりますねぇ。…くわばらくわばら…。」

description: Gohda says he has been awaiting Battler’s arrival. WH says ‘I do apologize for the wait,’ reversing who waited and adding an apology for a delay in serving him. It changes a prepared welcome into a service apology.
sourceReading: お待ち申し上げておりました is Gohda’s deferential statement that he was waiting.

units.text: "I do apologize for the wait.  I have been working for the Ushiromiya head house since the year before last.  I am Gohda (郷田), your servant.
units.note: Both express anticipating Battler, not apology for service delay.
units.japanese: 「お待ち申し上げておりました。一昨年から右代宮本家にお仕えさせていただいております、使用人の郷田と申します。

description: Battler says apparently some cliff face or quay wall is a huge seagull colony. WH says “The whole wharf looked like it was turning into” a colony. It fixes an unspecified location as the whole wharf, turns qualified report/inference into an apparent past visual observation, and changes an established colony into one in the process of becoming.
sourceReading: どっかの岸壁 leaves the location unspecified; 岸壁 can mean a rock face or quay wall depending on context. なってるらしく presents qualified information about an established colony, not the whole wharf visibly turning into one.

units.text: Except for the small part of the island where those of the Ushiromiya head house live, Rokkenjima had been left uncultivated, apparently transforming into a paradise for wild birds. The whole wharf looked like it was turning into a huge seagull colony, and this island always was full of seagulls. Since those seagulls didn't come to greet us, I felt a bit lonely.
units.note: Both retain unspecified cliff, reported status and established colony, rather than visual whole-wharf formation.
units.japanese: どっかの岸壁がうみねこの巨大コロニーになってるらしく、この島はいつもはうみねこだらけなのだ。
candidates: whole wharf looked like it was turning

description: Maria says she will wait for the seagulls to return when the weather improves, then repeats waiting until tomorrow and until good weather. WH begins ‘They’re waiting for the weather to get better to come back,’ assigning the waiting to the birds. It erases the first explicit statement of her own patient anticipation.
sourceReading: 戻ってくるの待つ is waiting for their return; the following narration confirms Maria is looking forward to tomorrow.

units.text: "Uu-.  They're waiting for the weather to get better to come back.  Waiting for tomorrow.  Waiting for the weather to get better.  Uu-uu-!"
units.note: Both correctly assign waiting to Maria; bird-return anticipation retained.
units.japanese: 「うー。天気良くなって戻ってくるの待つ。明日まで待つ。天気良くなるまで待つ。うーうー！」
candidates: They're waiting for the weather to get better to come back
Waiting for the weather to get better

description: Jessica is anxiously flustering over Kanon’s refusal of Battler’s friendliness. WH says she ‘looked all downcast,’ changing visible agitation into dejection. The next sentence retains her fear that Battler will think badly of Kanon, so this is a local behavioral distortion.
sourceReading: あわあわしてる describes being flustered or panicking, continuing her hurried attempts to smooth the introduction.

units.text: Jessica looked all downcast for some reason. She seemed to think that my impression of Kanon was worsening because of his rejection.
units.note: Panicky/flustered preserve agitation instead of WH downcast; her fear of worsening impression remains.
units.japanese: 朱志香が勝手にあわあわしてる。

description: The narrator says Kanon’s dejected back makes an onlooker feel compelled to leave him quietly alone. WH instead says there is something ‘he just couldn’t let go,’ attributing an unresolved emotional fixation to Kanon. The Japanese explicitly says an observer cannot readily tell what Battler’s kindness made him feel, then describes the observer’s response.
sourceReading: そっとせずにはいられない concerns leaving the distressed boy undisturbed; 何かを感じさせる describes what his posture evokes in someone looking.

units.text: It was extremely difficult for an outside observer to guess what emotions that favor had stirred up in Kanon. But as far as you could tell by watching him hang his head from behind, there was something that he just couldn't let go.
units.note: Both assign inability to let go to Kanon, rather than observer’s impulse to leave him quietly alone. Preceding uncertainty is retained but unsupported emotional fixation added.
units.japanese: でも、そのうな垂れた後姿を見る限り、そっとせずにはいられない何かを感じさせるのだった。

units.text: It would be extremely difficult for an outside observer to guess what emotions that favor had stirred up in Kanon. But as far as you could tell by watching him hang his head, there was something that he just couldn't let go of.
units.note: Both assign inability to let go to Kanon, rather than observer’s impulse to leave him quietly alone. Preceding uncertainty is retained but unsupported emotional fixation added.
units.japanese: その好意が、嘉音に何の感傷を与えているのか、傍目に理解することはとても難しかっただろう。でも、そのうな垂れた後姿を見る限り、そっとせずにはいられない何かを感じさせるのだった。

description: Battler finds no incongruity between Kinzo’s frightening reputation and his own memories. WH says he is ‘not the least unsettled by his terrifying image.’ It replaces consistency of the description with absence of fear, despite the following memories of oppressive tension and his present nervousness about greeting Kinzo.
sourceReading: 違和感 ... ない says nothing feels inconsistent or out of place in that image.

units.text: ......Well, I'm not the least unsettled by his terrifying image. I don't have many memories of meeting him over the years, but I remember Grandpa, his face always full of menacing thunder-clouds, always making his surroundings shrink away with a sharp look. I remember that the room's atmosphere got so tense whenever he was around, you couldn't even breathe.
units.note: Both express believing the frightening reputation, consistent with memories and present apprehension; neither retains WH absence-of-fear claim.
units.japanese: ……まぁそのおっそろしいイメージには違和感は寸分もない。
candidates: least unsettled by his terrifying image

description: Jessica specifies that Kinzo struck her bare buttocks with a wooden sword. WH says ‘maidenly, innocent ass,’ retaining indignation and the blow but omitting that she was bare-skinned. ‘Innocent’ does not convey 生尻, a concrete part of the humiliating punishment.
sourceReading: 乙女 supplies the maiden framing; 生尻 supplies uncovered buttocks.

units.text: Like me, I've gotten slapped with a wooden sword.  On my ass, my ass!  On my maidenly, innocent ass!"
units.note: MG retains maidenly, innocent ass; UP explicitly says maidenly naked ass. JP 生尻 remains present.
units.japanese: 私なんか木刀で引っ叩かれたことあるしよー。尻だぜ尻！　それも乙女の生尻をよー！」

units.text: I've even gotten slapped with a wooden sword. On my ass, my ass! On my maidenly, innocent ass!"
units.note: MG retains maidenly, innocent ass; UP explicitly says maidenly naked ass. JP 生尻 remains present.
units.japanese: 「私なんか木刀で引っ叩かれたことあるしよー。尻だぜ尻！　それも乙女の生尻をよー！」

description: Once Maria must stay behind, Battler realizes they cannot simply leave her alone. George immediately understands and answers for the cousins that they will stay too. WH says telling Maria to house-sit is ‘a pretty lame excuse for leaving her behind,’ criticizing the parental instruction instead of establishing the cousins’ reason for remaining.
sourceReading: 置いてきぼりってわけには行かない is the narrator’s recognition that leaving her alone is not an option, following her assigned stay.

units.text: Telling Maria to house-sit was a pretty lame excuse for leaving her behind. George-aniki soon realized it and gave a clear reply for all of us.
units.note: Both explicitly say the cousins cannot leave Maria alone/behind, preserving their reason for staying rather than WH criticism of a lame parental excuse.
units.japanese: 真里亞が留守番することになった以上、置いてきぼりってわけには行かない。
candidates: pretty lame excuse for leaving her behind

description: Jessica says the busy servants will later come to greet the cousins, teasing George that he would have preferred Shannon to welcome him. WH makes it ‘we’ll go and greet them properly afterwards.’ The direction and initiative of the promised meeting are reversed.
sourceReading: 挨拶に来る describes coming to this group for a greeting; the next reference to Shannon’s welcome specifies the implied visitor.

units.text: "They're probably busy with cleaning or lunch arrangements.  It's alright, we'll go and greet them properly afterwards.  Shannon's reception will sure be better than Gohda's nosy one, right?  Heehehe!"
units.note: MG she’ll drop by preserves coming to cousins. UP we’ll go and greet them retains original WH direction reversal.
units.japanese: 「多分、掃除とか昼飯の準備とかで忙しいんだよ。大丈夫、後でちゃんと挨拶に来るぜ。郷田の出しゃばりの出迎えより、紗音の出迎えの方が良かったーってんだろ？　へっへへ！」
candidates: we'll go and greet them properly afterwards

units.text: "They're probably busy with cleaning or lunch arrangements. It's alright, we'll go and greet them properly afterwards. Basically, you wanted Shannon out there to greet you, not that Gohda getting in the way, right?! Heeheheh!"
units.note: MG she’ll drop by preserves coming to cousins. UP we’ll go and greet them retains original WH direction reversal.
units.japanese: 「多分、掃除とか昼飯の準備とかで忙しいんだよ。大丈夫、後でちゃんと挨拶に来るぜ。郷田の出しゃばりの出迎えより、紗音の出迎えの方が良かったーってんだろ？　へっへへ！」
candidates: we'll go and greet them properly afterwards

description: Hideyoshi says Eva may use her poisonous tongue on him, but should moderate it with those who lack his resistance. WH instead says he does not mind but vulnerable people ‘are in for a stormy ride.’ It preserves the poison joke while removing his direct request to Eva to ease up on the victims.
sourceReading: 絵羽も ... 相手にはちぃと加減せんとな addresses Eva and urges restraint.

units.text: "Wahahahaha!  Since I get to hear that poison-tongue every day, I must be poison-proof by now!  I don't pay it much mind, but poor souls without resistance are in for a stormy ride!  Wahahahaha!"
units.note: Both preserve Hideyoshi explicit request to Eva to moderate her poisonous speech with people without resistance.
units.japanese: 「わっはっはっは！　わしゃあその毒舌を毎日聞かされとるから、もう毒に耐性がついてしもぅたわ！　絵羽も、わし相手には構わんが耐性のない相手にはちぃと加減せんとな！　わっはっはっは！」
candidates: are in for a stormy ride

description: Gohda has already delayed the tea through his own mistake and wasted time remaking it. Knowing the conspicuous service task will now earn him no credit, he passes it to Shannon. WH says he passes it on because he ‘wouldn’t be able to make it on time,’ giving a scheduling reason instead of avoidance of a now unprofitable public appearance.
sourceReading: ポイントが稼げない means unable to gain credit or approval, after the narration establishes his vanity and ownership of the prestigious task.

units.text: There was no way that a showoff like Gohda would ever hand over a flamboyant job like carting the tea to the guests in the first place. He had ended up wasting time preparing the tea a second time. So, knowing that he wouldn't be able to make it on time, he pushed the task of setting the table on Shannon, who happened to be passing by.
units.note: Both retain Gohda’s loss of social credit/brownie points as the motive for pushing service onto Shannon, rather than inability to finish on time.
units.japanese: だからポイントが稼げないことがわかり、たまたまその場を通りかかった紗音に配膳を押し付けたのだ。
candidates: wouldn't be able to make it on time

description: Kumasawa says that in this particular matter she must also sympathize with Madam. WH says ‘they are just not allowed to sympathize with her.’ It changes an obligation to extend sympathy into a prohibition, and shifts the experiencer from Kumasawa to the two bullied servants. The following reflection explains why she pities Natsuhi too.
sourceReading: 同情しなくてはなりません is must sympathize, with omitted narrator subject. The negation forms an obligation, not a prohibition.

units.text: And also, ...although it's terrible, they are hated by Madam Natsuhi too... Of course, in terms of experience, Madam has been in the family much longer. It's only that, .........they are just not allowed to sympathize with her.
units.note: Both make Kumasawa extend sympathy to Madam; neither retains WH prohibition on servants sympathizing.
units.japanese: ただ、………こればかりは奥様にも同情しなくてはなりません。
candidates: are just not allowed to sympathize

units.text: Of course, in terms of experience, Madam has been in the family much longer. It's only that, .........they are just not allowed to sympathize with her. ...The master is also a truly cruel person... He probably did not realize his own trifling whims passed so much of an inferiority complex to his wife...
units.note: Both make Kumasawa extend sympathy to Madam; neither retains WH prohibition on servants sympathizing.
units.japanese: ただ、………こればかりは奥様にも同情しなくてはなりません。
candidates: are just not allowed to sympathize

description: Kumasawa reflects on how the Master’s passing whim gave Madam Natsuhi an inferiority complex. WH substitutes ‘his wife’ for 奥様. It explicitly makes Madam the Master’s spouse, an unsupported relationship: this passage uses household titles for Kinzo and Natsuhi, and the family context establishes Natsuhi as Jessica’s mother in the son’s household.
sourceReading: 奥様 refers to household Madam, not a possessive relationship to the previously named お館様. The source leaves the particular past incident unexplained here.

units.text: Of course, in terms of experience, Madam has been in the family much longer. It's only that, .........they are just not allowed to sympathize with her. ...The master is also a truly cruel person... He probably did not realize his own trifling whims passed so much of an inferiority complex to his wife...
units.note: Both use Madam for Natsuhi and preserve Kinzo’s whim causing her inferiority complex; neither makes her Kinzo’s wife.
units.japanese: ご自身の、ちょっとした気まぐれが、奥様にこれほどまでの劣等感をお与えになるとは、どうして思い至らなかったのでしょう…。

description: Battler explains that the expected gag is: he approaches with a lecherous face, she knocks him down and protests. Without that conventional reaction, the joke has no punchline. WH changes 張ッ倒す to ‘Someone trip me’ and お約束 ... オチがつかねぇ to ‘Without your word, I can’t settle down.’ The explanation of his intended comic routine becomes dependence on a verbal assurance and a request to trip him.
sourceReading: お約束 denotes the conventional comedy pattern already described in the preceding narration; オチ is the gag’s payoff, and 張っ倒す is knocking someone down with a blow.

units.text: "...I-in these days, to think that there's a dedicated and virtuous girl like this...  Getting... giddy again!...  ......But, no!  NooOoo!!  I'm coming at her with a perverted face again!  Someone trip me!!  No~oo, pervert!  Without your word, I can't settle down!  Please, I beg you, smack me!  Like this, smack!  Hit meeee~!!"
units.note: Both preserve knocking/smacking Battler down and completing the gag/punchline rather than original WH tripping and verbal-assurance reading.
units.japanese: 「…い、今時、こんな献身美徳な子がいるとは…。軽い眩暈すら覚えるぜ。……でも駄目だ！　ダメなんだぁああぁ！！　俺がエロい顔で迫る！　張ッ倒す！！　イヤ～ン、エッチ！　そういうお約束じゃないとオチがつかねぇんだよぉ、頼むよお願いだよ、俺を引っ叩いてくれよ！　こう、バチンっと！　バチンっとぉおぉ～！！」
candidates: Without your word, I can't settle

description: Genji dates the exhibition to April of the year before last and says Kinzo had previously ordered the artist to paint it. WH dates the commission itself to that April and then says it was displayed. It collapses the prior commission into the exhibition date.
sourceReading: 一昨年の４月に modifies 展示なされた; 兼ねてより ... 描かせていた describes a painting already commissioned and produced.

units.text: "............You are correct.  In April of the year before last, as it had been arranged, the Master ordered an artist to paint it and it was put on display over there."
units.note: Both date exhibition to April of the year before last and explicitly distinguish the earlier commissioning of the painter.
units.japanese: 「…………左様でございます。一昨年の４月に、お館様が兼ねてより画家に命じて描かせていたものをあそこに展示なされたのでございます。」
candidates: April of the year before last

description: Battler speculates that a parent invented the forest-witch story to keep children safe: perhaps Grandmother, or none other than Grandfather. WH says ‘anybody else other than Grandfather.’ It excludes the very person Japanese explicitly offers as a possible originator.
sourceReading: 他でもない、祖父さま means none other than Grandfather, still under かもしれない.

units.text: ...If children go play in that dangerous forest, something terrible might happen. Someone's parents must have thought so.  ...Maybe my Grandmother, or possibly anybody else other than Grandfather might have said that. Or maybe it's been handed down in this island from long, long ago.
units.note: Both explicitly include Grandfather himself as possible originator rather than excluding him.
units.japanese: そう思った親の誰か。…祖母さまか、あるいは他でもない、祖父さまが言い出したのかもしれない。

description: After describing Kinzo’s belief that the witch exists, Jessica ends with a disgusted dismissal: it is creepy or revolting. WH replaces this with ‘I’m sorry, but she just doesn’t exist.’ It removes her emotional reaction and supplies a direct categorical denial in its place.
sourceReading: 気持ち悪いったらありゃしない is emphatic disgust, not a statement of existence or an apology.

units.text: .........And I'm sorry, but she just doesn't exist."
units.note: Both preserve Jessica disgust/creepiness rather than replacing it with categorical existence denial.
units.japanese: ………はんッ、気持ち悪いったらありゃしないぜ。」
candidates: I'm sorry, but she just doesn't exist

description: Battler remembers Natsuhi seldom joining the children, looking stern and discussing difficult matters with the adults. WH says she gave the impression she was ‘at odds with the other parents,’ changing the content of adult discussion into interpersonal conflict in his childhood memory.
sourceReading: 難しい話をしている is discussing difficult or complicated matters; it does not state she was disagreeing with the people talking.

units.text: ...It feels bad to say it like this, but, not that I hated her, I didn't particularly like her. She never got into our kids' circle, and she always looked difficult to get along with.  And it didn't help that she gave the impression that she was at odds with the other parents.
units.note: Both preserve childhood memory of Natsuhi discussing complicated matters with adults, rather than replacing it with being at odds with parents.
units.japanese: あまり子供の輪に入ってこないし、いつも気難しそうな顔をして、親たちと難しい話をしているという印象しかない。

description: Kinzo challenges the maxim that knocking opens doors and says the fool who taught it was crucified, then threatens Krauss with the same fate. WH says ‘I’ll crucify the imbecile,’ turning the completed crucifixion reference into another prospective threat. It loses the historical barb while preserving the threat to Krauss.
sourceReading: 磔にしたぞ is completed action. The knock-and-open saying also matches the teaching in Matthew 7:7; linking its teacher to crucifixion is an allusion inferred from the juxtaposition, not an independently explicit naming of Jesus in Japanese.

units.text: "Silence!!  Will you not stop that noise, fool!!!  Who told you the door would open if you knocked!?  I'll crucify the imbecile!!  Do you wish to be as well!!??"
units.note: MG I’ll crucify retains future threat in place of completed allusion; UP They crucified preserves past event and subsequent same-fate threat.
units.japanese: 叩けば扉は開かれると誰が教えた！　その馬鹿者は磔にしたぞッ！！　お前もそうされたいのかッ！！」

units.text: "Silence!! Enough with that racket, you fool!!! Who told you the door would be opened if you but knocked?! I'll crucify the imbecile!! Do you wish to suffer the same fate?!!"
units.note: MG I’ll crucify retains future threat in place of completed allusion; UP They crucified preserves past event and subsequent same-fate threat.
units.japanese: 「やかましいッ！！　その音を止めぬか、愚か者ッ！！！　叩けば扉は開かれると誰が教えた！　その馬鹿者は磔にしたぞッ！！　お前もそうされたいのかッ！！」

description: After the water-and-sugar preparation, Genji adds the distinctive flavoring Kinzo likes and adjusts the taste. WH says ‘It improved the original flavor Kinzo liked,’ omitting the separate addition and turning a preparation step into a claim about improvement.
sourceReading: それに ... フレーバーを加え is an addition to the prepared drink; 独自 describes a distinctive or custom flavor, not merely the original flavor being improved.

units.text: It improved the original flavor Kinzo liked and adjusted the taste. ...There was no recipe. Its success was measured only by Kinzo's mood swing when he drank it, and he had learned how to make it only after many decades.
units.note: Both explicitly add Kinzo preferred custom flavoring and then adjust taste, rather than saying it improves the original flavor.
units.japanese: それに、金蔵が好む独自のフレーバーを加え、味を調える。
candidates: improved the original flavor Kinzo liked

description: Genji first inclines the glass as if tasting, then throws back the remaining drink. WH says ‘After that, he agitated it,’ making him shake or stir it rather than drink it down. It interrupts the intimate sharing of the last mouthful between Kinzo and Genji.
sourceReading: くっと煽った in the drinking sequence describes tossing back the drink, not stirring the glass.

units.text: Genji respectfully received the glass and inclined it a little to taste its contents. After that, he agitated it.
units.note: Both have Genji drink/down the remainder after tasting, rather than agitating it.
units.japanese: それから、くっと煽った。

description: Kinzo explains that Moses drew the sole miracle among an astronomical number of roulette outcomes. WH says he acted ‘instead of betting on incalculable odds’ and found a miracle ‘within the eyes of many.’ The enormous product is misread as an avoided wager, and roulette 目 becomes eyes rather than possible results. The explanation no longer clearly links a singular winning outcome, huge risk and miracle-working luck.
sourceReading: 阿僧祇、那由他を掛けたよりも多く counts an immense number of possible 目; 掛けた belongs to multiplying the large quantities. ひとつだけ刻まれた奇跡 is the sole miracle-result among them.

units.text: That is because Moses, instead of betting on incalculable odds in the roulette of those with power, managed to spectacularly draw to himself the single miracle carved within the eyes of many.  That power that can triumph over astronomical odds!!  Yes, magical power is that fortune through which miracles are grasped!!  To obtain this mighty magic power, one must face the risk of despair!!  Those who possess no magical power call that desperation rather than a bet! However, people who truly do possess magic power can grasp hold of that miracle and make the enigma come into being!!  And if that power exists within me...!  I'll seize that miracle!  I'll have a chance at making the wish I devoted my life towards come true!!"
units.note: Both restore roulette outcomes and singular miracle, no eyes phrase or instead-of-betting contradiction. MG numeric specificity separately recorded.
units.japanese: なぜならモーゼは、力ある者たちのルーレットの、阿僧祇、那由他を掛けたよりも多く存在する目の中にひとつだけ刻まれた奇跡を見事引き寄せることができたからだ。その天文学的確率に勝利できる力！！　そう、奇跡を掴み取る運気は即ち魔力なのだ！！　強大な魔力を得るためには絶望的なリスクを背負わねばならぬ！！　魔力持たぬ者はそれを賭けでなく自暴自棄と呼ぼう！　しかし真に魔力ある者はその奇跡を掴み取り、神秘を成就させるのだッ！！　もしも私にその魔力があるならば！　私はその奇跡を掴み取るだろう、生涯を費やした願いを実現できるだろうッ！！」

description: Kinzo is prostrate on the floor and claws at the floor with both hands. WH has him fold onto a bed and tear it. It replaces the location and the surface of his desperate action, introducing a bed into this moment in the study.
sourceReading: 床の上 and 両手で床 refer to the floor; the source repeats the surface in both clauses.

units.text: ......His nonsensical yells segued into a scream...and then into a wail. Kinzo folded over onto the bed, and tore it with both hands. Genji had no choice but to wordlessly watch over his master's lament...
units.note: Both have Kinzo collapse onto floor and claw it, not a bed.
units.japanese: 金蔵はいつしか床の上に伏し、両手で床を掻き毟っていた。

description: Battler contrasts lacking energy with being in a bad mood: the former could suggest serious illness, while the latter at least shows Kinzo’s mind or spirit remains firm. WH instead says ‘if he’s not healthy, and his mood is bad’ it proves he is ‘still hanging on.’ This removes the contrast and shifts the immediate inference from mental firmness to continued endurance despite illness.
sourceReading: 元気がないってんならともかく sets a contrast: if he lacked energy, that would be different. 気はしっかりしてる concerns mental or spirited firmness, and George responds by distinguishing strong will from physical condition.

units.text: "......His disease can't be that bad, can it, with that kinda temper?  I mean, if he's not healthy, and his mood is bad, at least it's proof he's still hanging on."
units.note: Both contrast low energy/illness with bad mood, preserving evidence of mental or spirited firmness and George qualification about bodily health.
units.japanese: 「……機嫌が云々ってことは、病状はそんな悪くないんじゃねぇの？　元気がないってんならともかく、機嫌が悪いってのは、少なくとも気はしっかりしてる証拠だぜ。」
candidates: he's not healthy, and his mood is bad

description: The adult children were routinely slapped despite their age. WH instead says even a good year brought slaps, making business results the concession.
sourceReading: いい年にもなって means despite being mature adults.

units.text: My dad called it a bed of nails. Apparently, it used to be a very serious family meeting, bathed in harsh and angry voices.  Even on a good year, it was common for someone to get slapped.
units.note: Both preserve slapping despite grown age, not concession based on a good business year.
units.japanese: 相当厳しい親族会議だったらしく、罵声や怒声が次々と浴びせられ、いい年にもなって平手打ちをもらうこともざらだったらしい。

description: The children dread Kinzo asking about their current circumstances. WH makes news of his condition the source of stress. His absence relieves scrutiny in Japanese, rather than relieving a health report.
sourceReading: 祖父さまに ... 聞かれる is passive: being asked by Grandfather.

units.text: Even so, hearing about Grandfather's condition caused a significant amount of stress, so while to us grandchildren it was nothing more than a simple meeting, to our parents it was still a real stomachache.
units.note: Both preserve stress from reporting current circumstances to Kinzo, not hearing news of his condition.
units.japanese: それでも、祖父さまに近況を聞かれるのは非常にストレスになることで、俺たち孫にとっては単なる会合に過ぎなくても、親たち息子にとっては今でも胃が痛む会合らしい。

description: Japanese names Kinzo himself, from a remote branch, as the only remaining heir candidate. WH says a branch family including him remained.
sourceReading: 金蔵祖父さましか残ってなかった restricts the survivor set to Kinzo.

units.text: It then became a matter of who in the main family would become the heir, and it seemed as though no one except the branch family, which included Kinzo, was left. Kinzo himself later said that it was such good luck, it was as though fate itself had been turned upside-down.
units.note: Both identify Kinzo himself as the sole remaining heir candidate, not a surviving branch including him.
units.japanese: それで右代宮本家の跡継ぎは誰だってことになったら、分家筋も分家筋の金蔵祖父さましか残ってなかったらしい。

description: The island was reportedly provided for virtually nothing. WH replaces its low price with Tokyo’s poverty, leaving the cheap acquisition unstated.
sourceReading: タダ同然のカネで specifies the transfer price.

units.text: After the war there were prevention measures against food shortages, and, furthermore, having the sponsorship of the GHQ meant that nobody could oppose him. It seems that Tokyo Metropolis had almost no money at the time and offered this land. Later, Tokyo made difficulties by telling Kinzo to return the land, but the pushy GHQ intervened. Anyway, it seems as though under the table bribes worked perfectly. In the end, the city gave up in frustration.
units.note: Both explicitly say island was provided practically free/next to no money.
units.japanese: 当時の東京都はほとんどタダ同然のカネでこの土地を提供したそうだ。

description: The source explains that GHQ was involved despite the forceful transaction. WH says the pushy GHQ intervened after Tokyo demanded the land back, supplying a particular intervention and assigning the pushiness to GHQ.
sourceReading: ＧＨＱが絡んでる denotes involvement; 強引とは言え is concessive, not an adjective identifying GHQ as pushy.

units.text: After the war there were prevention measures against food shortages, and, furthermore, having the sponsorship of the GHQ meant that nobody could oppose him. It seems that Tokyo Metropolis had almost no money at the time and offered this land. Later, Tokyo made difficulties by telling Kinzo to return the land, but the pushy GHQ intervened. Anyway, it seems as though under the table bribes worked perfectly. In the end, the city gave up in frustration.
units.note: MG explicitly retains pushy GHQ intervened after Tokyo demand. UP refers to involvement and inability to act, without asserting a later intervention.
units.japanese: 後に東京都は返せとゴネたらしいが、強引とは言えＧＨＱが絡んでる。

units.text: After the war, there were prevention measures against food shortages, and having the sponsorship of the GHQ meant that nobody could oppose him. From what I've heard, the Tokyo Metropolis of that day offered this land to him practically for free. Later, Tokyo made difficulties by telling Kinzo to return the land, but the pushy GHQ intervened. Anyway, it seems under-the-table bribes did their work well. In the end, the city gave up in frustration.
units.note: MG explicitly retains pushy GHQ intervened after Tokyo demand. UP refers to involvement and inability to act, without asserting a later intervention.
units.japanese:
戦後の食糧難対策ってことで、しかもＧＨＱの肝煎りじゃ誰も逆らえない。当時の東京都はほとんどタダ同然のカネでこの土地を提供したそうだ。後に東京都は返せとゴネたらしいが、強引とは言えＧＨＱが絡んでる。どうせ袖の下もばっちりだったんだろうぜ。
結局、都は泣き寝入りすることになった。

description: Kinzo’s English let him cultivate connections within GHQ. “Take a bite out of the GHQ” replaces that access with an opaque suggestion of attacking or extracting something from it.
sourceReading: 食い込む means penetrating an organization or establishing influence within it in this context.

units.text: Of course, it wasn't all luck. He was skilled with English, and this was cultivated by his western obsession. Using this as a weapon, he was able to take a bite out of the GHQ.
units.note: UP make inroads is explicit; MG sink his teeth into, unlike original take a bite out of, can idiomatically mean become deeply involved. Preceding connection history supports access reading, so do not reuse original WH defect description against changed idiom.
units.japanese: それを武器にＧＨＱに食い込むことができたのだから。
candidates: take a bite out of the GHQ

description: George infers that Gohda was somewhat known in his profession. WH says he probably learned a lot that way, extending George’s work-related dining experience to Gohda.
sourceReading: その道じゃ ... 知られた人 denotes being known in that field.

units.text: "Hahahaha.  Depending on the situation with my job, I also have eaten at many odd places, but compared to all of those, this is an excellent dish.  Gohda-san probably also learned a lot that way."
units.note: Both attribute professional recognition to Gohda rather than extending George dining experience to him. UP could have become frames inferred past possibility within prior-job conversation.
units.japanese: 「はははは。僕も仕事の都合で珍しいところで食事をすることもあるけど、それらと比べても、これはかなりのものだよ。郷田さんは多分、その道じゃ少しは知られた人だったんじゃないかな。」

description: WH retains the chef’s description but omits the explicit instruction that diners must wait until it is finished. Its next “this strict rule” has no explicit antecedent.
sourceReading: それが終わるまでは ... お預け states the waiting rule.

units.text: With such magnificent food distributed in front of everybody, it was time for the chef to extol the virtues of his creation.
units.note: Both expressly state waiting until chef description is finished before eating.
units.japanese: こういう上品なお食事だと、全員の前に配られ、それからシェフによる料理の能書きが語られる。それが終わるまでは基本的にお預け状態だ。

description: Japanese distinguishes separate sweet and sour sauces. WH calls the sauce a blend; the chef’s later instruction at 14097–14098 changes alternating the tastes into enjoying their mixture.
sourceReading: ２つの味 and 交互に distinguish tastes enjoyed in turn.

units.text: Apparently the sauce was a blend of sweet and sour. Despite it being bad manners, I also stuck my little finger in and licked it. Whoa, half of it was sour enough to make you pucker up. If it were yellow, I'd have suspected lemon, but I couldn't guess what kind of sourness would be red.
units.note: MG asks diners to enjoy a mixture despite separate sauces and subsequent return from sour to sweet; UP explicitly says in turn.
units.japanese:
２色のソースは甘味と酸味の２つの味になってるらしい。
俺も行儀は悪いが小指に付けて舐めてみる。

units.text: The sauce is a combination of two reds, strawberry and rose hips. Please enjoy this mixture of the strawberry's sweetness and the rose hip's sourness. Furthermore, the rose petals are merely decorative, so please avoid them while you eat. With that said, please, enjoy."
units.note: MG asks diners to enjoy a mixture despite separate sauces and subsequent return from sour to sweet; UP explicitly says in turn.
units.japanese: 「ソースはストロベリーとローズヒップの２色の赤をご用意しました。ストロベリーの甘味とローズヒップの酸味を交互にお楽しみになって下さい。なお花びらは観賞用となっておりますのでよけてからお召し上がり下さいませ。それではどうぞお楽しみ下さい」

description: At the ongoing lunch, Gohda introduces today’s dessert. WH introduces tonight’s dessert although it is served immediately.
sourceReading: 本日は means today; the scene is explicitly lunch.

units.text: "Well then, allow me to introduce tonight's dessert.  Based on the rose garden that everyone seemed to enjoy so much today, I finished this panna cotta in a rose garden style.  The rose petals scattered across were selected just now from that rose garden. The sauce is a combination of two reds, strawberry and rose hips.  Please enjoy this mixture of the strawberry's sweetness and the rose hip's sourness.  Furthermore, the rose petals are merely decoration, so please avoid them while you eat.  With that said, please, enjoy."
units.note: MG introduces our dessert; UP says tonight’s dessert during ongoing lunch. Both earlier row 186 correctly say today’s dessert.
units.japanese: 「それでは、デザートのご説明をさせていただきます。本日は、ご来賓の皆様が大層お気に入りでございました薔薇の庭園にちなみまして、パンナコッタをローズガーデン風に仕上げてみました。散らしてございます薔薇の花びらは当家の庭園より先ほど採取してきたものでございます。ソースはストロベリーとローズヒップの２色の赤をご用意しました。ストロベリーの甘味とローズヒップの酸味を交互にお楽しみになって下さい。なお花びらは観賞用となっておりますので避けてからお召し上がり下さいませ。それではどうぞお楽しみ下さい。」

units.text: "Well then, allow me to describe tonight's dessert. Based on the rose garden that everyone seemed to enjoy so much today, I finished this panna cotta in a rose garden style. The rose petals scattered across were selected just now from that rose garden."
units.note: MG introduces our dessert; UP says tonight’s dessert during ongoing lunch. Both earlier row 186 correctly say today’s dessert.
units.japanese: 「それでは、デザートのご説明をさせていただきます。本日は、ご来賓の皆様が大層お気に入りでございました薔薇の庭園にちなみまして、パンナコッタをローズガーデン風に仕上げてみました。散らしてございます薔薇の花びらは当家の庭園より先ほど採取してきたものでございます」

description: Narration says whichever way Shannon deflects a question, she ought to do it smoothly. WH says all options would have been tricky, replacing a standard of conduct with an assertion of difficulty.
sourceReading: スマートであるべき imposes a norm of smooth, deft handling.

units.text: There may have been several ways to dodge the question, but all of them would have been tricky. Shannon, who hesitated when hard pressed for a response, was always suffering because of this small weakness. If only Shannon, like Gohda, had a little of the craftiness needed to skillfully shake off a mistake, her days would be a little more comfortable. As far as being able to flawlessly handle her work, this weakness was especially unfortunate.
units.note: UP expressly requires deft delivery; MG requiring quick wits can convey the needed deftness rather than original claim all options inherently tricky. Do not copy old defect analysis onto this changed phrase.
units.japanese: かわし方はいくつかあるかもしれないが、いずれもスマートであるべきだ。

description: Hideyoshi describes the sky as still bright despite the rain forecast. WH says it is still clear, supplying a meteorological condition rather than brightness.
sourceReading: 明るい describes brightness; it does not require a cloudless sky.

units.text: "It's alright if you just go to look at the roses.  But keep a close eye on the weather.  The sky's still clear, but the weather report kept on talkin' about rain."
units.note: Both sky still clear replace Japanese still bright. Cloudy conditions can remain bright; rain forecast caution otherwise retained.
units.japanese: 「薔薇でも見に行ったらえぇ。でも天気には充分注意するんやで。空はまだ明るいが、天気予報は降る降ると繰り返しちょる。」

units.text: "Go ahead and take a look at the roses or somethin'. But keep a close eye on the weather. The sky's still clear, but the weather report kept on talkin' about rain."
units.note: Both sky still clear replace Japanese still bright. Cloudy conditions can remain bright; rain forecast caution otherwise retained.
units.japanese: 「薔薇でも見に行ったらえぇ。でも天気には充分注意するんやで。空はまだ明るいが、天気予報は降る降ると繰り返しちょる」

units.text: "Go look at the roses or something. But keep a close eye on the weather. The sky's still clear, but the weather report kept on talkin' about rain."
units.note: Both sky still clear replace Japanese still bright. Cloudy conditions can remain bright; rain forecast caution otherwise retained.
units.japanese: 「薔薇でも見に行ったらえぇ。でも天気には充分注意するんやで。空はまだ明るいが、天気予報は降る降ると繰り返しちょる」

description: Krauss claims he has always aimed at intellectual discussion. Eva quotes “always, since long ago” back at him and invokes this room decades earlier. WH weakens the claim to “for some time now” and makes her quote his separate remark that her sarcasm has not changed. It changes what the historical rebuke answers.
sourceReading: 昔からいつも is Krauss’s claimed long-standing conduct; Eva repeats those exact words. 的を外す also means missing the mark, not simply poor timing.

units.text: "We have all intended to have an intellectual discussion for some time now, haven't we?  ......It seems that your sarcasm is poorly timed.  Just as it used to be."
units.note: Both preserve always intellectual discussion as Krauss claim and Eva quoted target, linked to decades-earlier scene.
units.japanese:
「知的な会話なら昔からいつも心掛けているじゃないか。……お前の嫌味は、時に的を外している。昔から変わらない。」
「…昔からいつも、ですって？　あらあら。その言葉を綺麗に包装して、何十年か前のこの部屋に届けてあげたいわね。

units.text: "...'Just as it used to be,' is it?  My, my.  I wish I could wrap those words up and send them to this room a few decades ago.  Right, Rosa?"
units.note: Both preserve always intellectual discussion as Krauss claim and Eva quoted target, linked to decades-earlier scene.
units.japanese:
「知的な会話なら昔からいつも心掛けているじゃないか。……お前の嫌味は、時に的を外している。昔から変わらない。」
「…昔からいつも、ですって？　あらあら。その言葉を綺麗に包装して、何十年か前のこの部屋に届けてあげたいわね。

description: Natsuhi attacks the sanity of discussing the living head’s death this way. WH gives her suspicion about Rudolf’s true intentions instead.
sourceReading: 正気を疑う means questioning sanity or sound judgment.

units.text: "The family head is still in good health.  Raising such an inappropriate topic while the sun is still bright...I can't help but doubt your true intentions, Rudolf-san."
units.note: Both preserve Natsuhi questioning Rudolf sanity, rather than suspicions about his true intentions.
units.japanese: 「………当主様は今でも健在でおられます。このような不穏当な話を日も明るい内からなさろうとするなど、留弗夫さんの正気を疑わざるを得ません。」

description: Nanjo starts by correcting the way his three-month remark has taken on a life of its own. WH says he starts because his estimate has not borne out. It changes his stated reason for clarifying the estimate.
sourceReading: 言葉が独り歩き refers to a statement circulating independently of its intended qualifications.

units.text: "Well, first off...  Because my estimate last year that he had only three months to live has not borne out, allow me to start with that revision."
units.note: MG explicitly starts because estimate was not borne out. UP refers to estimate continuing to circulate/make presence felt, without inventing failure as the stated reason.
units.japanese: 「まず初めに…。私が去年申し上げました余命３ヶ月という言葉が独り歩きをしているようですので、その訂正からいたします。」

units.text: "Well, to begin, ...allow me to start with a revision, since my estimate last year that he had only three months left was not borne out."
units.note: MG explicitly starts because estimate was not borne out. UP refers to estimate continuing to circulate/make presence felt, without inventing failure as the stated reason.
units.japanese: 「まず初めに…。私が去年申し上げました余命３ヶ月という言葉が独り歩きをしているようですので、その訂正からいたします」

description: Rosa argues that Father’s condition is already deteriorating and that the day is approaching, so prior discussion is reasonable. WH instead locates deterioration itself in an approaching future day.
sourceReading: 悪くなっていて establishes the current condition; その日 follows the discussion of dying and inheritance.

units.text: "............We are not impatient.  ...However, a decision between the siblings is essential.  It doesn't matter when, but if the day when Father's condition worsens is approaching, discussing the matter beforehand isn't what I would call impatience..."
units.note: MG day Father condition worsens is approaching collapses present deterioration plus approaching death into future deterioration. UP preserves worsening now and the approaching day.
units.japanese: 「……………焦ってるわけじゃない。…でも、兄弟の間での取り決めは必要。それはいつでもいいことだけれども、お父様の具合が悪くなっていて、その日が近付いているというなら、先に話だけしておいても…、それは性急とは言わないと思うし…。」

units.text: ".........We aren't being hasty. ...However, we need to have an agreement between the siblings. It doesn't matter when we do that, but if the day Father's condition worsens is approaching, discussing the matter beforehand hardly seems hasty to me..."
units.note: MG day Father condition worsens is approaching collapses present deterioration plus approaching death into future deterioration. UP preserves worsening now and the approaching day.
units.japanese: 「……………焦ってるわけじゃない。…でも、兄弟の間での取り決めは必要。それはいつでもいいことだけれども、お父様の具合が悪くなっていて、その日が近付いているというなら、先に話だけしておいても…、それは性急とは言わないと思うし…」

description: Natsuhi blames trouble among the companies undertaking the project. WH says there is trouble with the company Krauss contracted with, losing the intercompany dispute in her defense.
sourceReading: 会社間 specifies between companies.

units.text: "......Impertinence!  That is not my husband's fault!  There has just been some trouble with the company that my husband contracted with.  No matter how you look at it, we are victims here!"
units.note: Both trouble with the company omit source dispute between companies undertaking project.
units.japanese: 「……失敬な！　それは主人の手落ちではありません！　主人の仕事を請け負う会社間でトラブルが生じているだけで、うちはあくまでも被害者です！」

units.text: "......Impertinence! That is not my husband's fault! There has just been some trouble with the company that my husband contracted with. No matter how you look at it, we are victims here!"
units.note: Both trouble with the company omit source dispute between companies undertaking project.
units.japanese: 「……失敬な！　それは主人の手落ちではありません！　主人の仕事を請け負う会社間でトラブルが生じているだけで、うちはあくまでも被害者です！」

units.text: "......Impertinence! That is not my husband's fault! There has just been some trouble with the company that my husband contracted with—no matter how you look at it, we are victims here!"
units.note: Both trouble with the company omit source dispute between companies undertaking project.
units.japanese: 「……失敬な！　それは主人の手落ちではありません！　主人の仕事を請け負う会社間でトラブルが生じているだけで、うちはあくまでも被害者です！」

description: Eva says they have already corroborated the reports. WH says she has been collecting evidence, without claiming verification is complete.
sourceReading: 裏も取れてる claims the reports have been checked, not just that material is being gathered.

units.text: "Just spit it out.  ...Did you think that rumors about nonpayment, embezzlement, and projects that disintegrated mid-way wouldn't reach my ears?  I've been collecting evidence."
units.note: MG we even have evidence asserts completed evidential support after heard report; UP I’ve been collecting evidence retains ongoing activity without asserting corroboration achieved.
units.japanese: 「はっきり言ってあげなさいよ。……不払い、横領、トラブルで計画が空中分解しちゃったって話、私たちの耳に届かないとでも思ってるぅ？　裏も取れてるんだから。」

units.text: "Let's not beat around the bush. ......The project disintegrated mid‐way due to nonpayment, embezzlement, and other troubles—did you think the rumors wouldn't reach our ears? I've been collecting evidence."
units.note: MG we even have evidence asserts completed evidential support after heard report; UP I’ve been collecting evidence retains ongoing activity without asserting corroboration achieved.
units.japanese: 「はっきり言ってあげなさいよ。……不払い、横領、トラブルで計画が空中分解しちゃったって話、私たちの耳に届かないとでも思ってるぅ？　裏も取れてるんだから」

description: Rudolf’s roulette analogy says to bet against a losing prospect, and identifies Krauss as one. WH says the iron rule is turning things around in a time of weakness. The rule no longer explains why no investor backs him.
sourceReading: 弱り目と逆に張る means staking against the losing prospect; 張る is betting, and Krauss is identified as that prospect.

units.text: "...And the result, there is none.  There is no backer.  Turning things around during a time of weakness is the iron rule of the money roulette.  Aniki's was a well known time of weakness in this neighborhood.  Surely this era seems set to welcome an economic boom, but when we asked who, with respect to Aniki's failures, would find him worthy of funding, there was no one."
units.note: Both preserve betting against loser/unfortunate prospect and identify Krauss with it; source financial analogy explains absent backers.
units.japanese:
「…結果。いねぇんだよ、そんな後ろ盾は。弱り目と逆に張るのがマネールーレットの鉄則だ。兄貴はこの界隈じゃ、ちょいと知られた弱り目さ。確かに時代は好景気を迎えようとしているが、これまでの兄貴の失敗とを天秤に掛けて、その上で融資に値すると思う連中がいるのか、って言ったら、
誰もいなかったのさ。」

description: Eva tells Natsuhi to withdraw, then indignantly asks whether Natsuhi would order third-ranked Eva to withdraw. WH makes 下がる bowing and turns Eva’s question into “I’m telling you to bow down before” her. Both the action and the target of the quoted order change.
sourceReading: お前が下がりなさい returns the dismissal; この絵羽に下がれと is an incredulous echo of Natsuhi’s demand, marked as a question.

units.text: "How foolish.  Bow down!!  Before Eva of the Ushiromiya family! I'm telling you to bow down before the third ranked in the Ushiromiya family hierarchy, who is allowed to stand at the left shoulder of the head!!  Know your place!!  And then look in a mirror at your shabby figure!!  Where on your clothes is the wing?  Where are you permitted to wear the One-winged Eagle?  Aren't you nothing more than a borrowed womb to house the next successor to the Ushiromiya family!!  Understand your place, you lowly maidservant!!"
units.note: Both replace bowing with withdrawal and restore Eva’s incredulous question about being ordered to withdraw; MG standalone before Eva is awkward but the next sentence states the question explicitly.
units.japanese: 「馬鹿馬鹿しい、お前が下がりなさいッ！！　この右代宮絵羽に！　当主様の左肩を許されている右代宮家序列第３位のこの絵羽に下がれとッ？！　身の程を知りなさいッ！！　そしてお前のそのみすぼらしい姿を鏡に映してみるがいい！！　お前の服のどこに翼が？　どこに片翼の鷲が許されているのか？　貴様など右代宮家の跡継ぎを残すためだけの借り腹じゃないの！！　身の程を弁えるがいい、この端女があッ！！」
candidates: I'm telling you to bow down before

description: Eva sneers that having that woman run things must constantly strain Krauss. WH instead speaks of her having been managed like that, making Natsuhi the recipient of management.
sourceReading: あんなのに切り盛りされてた makes that woman the managing agent and Krauss the affected party.

units.text: "If she's been managed like that, it must worry Nii-san to no end, huh?  *giggle*giggle*...!"
units.note: Both make Natsuhi the person running Krauss household, not the recipient of management.
units.japanese: 「あんなのに切り盛りされてたんじゃ、兄さんも気苦労が絶えないわねぇ？　くすくすくす…！」

description: George says the parents interpreted the epitaph as Kinzo challenging them to a contest of wits. WH says they called it equal to his level of genius. It removes their interpretation of the posted riddle as a challenge.
sourceReading: 知恵比べ denotes matching wits, here with the person who set the riddle.

units.text: "Whether that's what he intended or not, I can't even imagine what his true motive was.  ......All I can say is, this shady epitaph was displayed here so that everyone in the family could see it.  By doing so, he could hint at the existence of the gold while still avoiding telling where the hiding place is.  ......That caused our parents' imagination to run wild and call it equal to Grandfather's level of genius..."
units.note: Both explicitly restore the parents’ interpretation as a battle of wits/challenge.
units.japanese: 「そういうつもりなのかどうか、お祖父さまの胸中は想像もつかないけどね。……ひとつ言えるのは、この胡散臭い碑文を、お祖父さまは一族全員に告示するかのようにここに掲示したこと。そして、黄金の存在はほのめかしながらも、未だにその隠し場所について一切触れないこと。………そこから、親たちが想像を膨らませて、お祖父さまの知恵比べに違いないって言い出した…。」
candidates: equal to Grandfather's level of genius

description: George argues gold is inconvenient for concentrating and storing one’s wealth. WH says it is inconvenient for purchasing assets, changing the purpose at issue in his comparison with securities and portable jewels.
sourceReading: 財産をまとめておく is gathering or keeping wealth together; the following wartime jewels example concerns portability.

units.text: "......However, while that might be possible with 20 billion yen in cash, I don't think it would be very realistic to have that much in gold bars all in one place.  Just as I said, gold is extremely heavy, and it is not very convenient for purchasing assets.  With highly valued stocks and bonds or really expensive precious gems, it wouldn't be unthinkable though.  ...You often hear of people who, in the period of confusion during the war, often traded their wealth for precious gems so that they could carry it around with them.  ......But you don't usually hear stories of people exchanging their wealth for gold."
units.note: Both correctly discuss storing accumulated wealth rather than purchasing assets.
units.japanese: 「……でも、２００億円という現金ならいざ知れず、それと同等の金塊が一所にあるなんて、とても現実的とは思えないね。さっきも言った通り、黄金は非常に重くて、財産をまとめておくにはちょっと便利とは思えないよ。ものすごい額面の有価証券とかものすごく価値のある宝石とか、そういうものなら考えられなくもないけれど。…戦時中の混乱期に、自分の資産を持ち運べるよう、全て宝石などに変えた人たちがいたのは有名な話だからね。……でも、黄金で資産を備蓄したというのはなかなか聞かない。」

description: The source compares carrying a 50-kg person with carrying a 50-kg bale. WH says a person who weighs 50 kg cannot carry a 50-kg bag. The equal-mass comparison between differently shaped loads becomes a body-weight restriction on the carrier.
sourceReading: ５０ｋｇの人間は背負えても treats the person as the carried load, contrasted with the bale.

units.text: "You can also look at it that way....but even one 10 kilogram ingot is pretty heavy to carry around.  Haven't you heard?  A 50 kilogram person can't carry a 50 kilogram bag over their shoulder.  With that many gold bars, the amount of labor and risk for one person would be hard to calculate."
units.note: MG retains the carrier-body-weight substitution; UP restores comparison between equal-weight person and bale.
units.japanese: 「そういう考え方もあるね。…でも、１０ｋｇのインゴット１つでも体感重量は相当のものだよ。聞いたことない？　５０ｋｇの人間は背負えても、５０ｋｇの俵は担げないって。それだけの莫大な重量の金塊を、個人が所有するリスクと手間は計り知れないね。」
candidates: A 50 kilogram person can't carry a 50 kilogram bag

description: Battler contrasts a believable fortune in banknotes with an implausible mountain of gold. WH calls the banknotes annoying and the gold practically pointless, changing doubt about the story’s realism into dislike and lack of utility.
sourceReading: 札束が唸ってる evokes plentiful cash, not annoyance; 現実味がない concerns plausibility.

units.text: "So what you're saying is, while a stack of banknotes worth 20 billion yen would be annoying, 20 billion yen in gold would be such a big mountain that practically it would be kinda pointless."
units.note: MG restores the banknote contrast but still makes the gold practically pointless rather than implausible; UP restores lack of realism. Parent description retained verbatim, with this narrowed surviving scope stated separately.
units.japanese: 「ってことはつまり、２００億円の札束が唸ってるって話ならともかく、２００億円分の黄金が山積みになってるってのは、ちょいと現実味がないわけだな。」
candidates: practically it would be kinda pointless

units.text: "So what you're saying is, while it'd be one thing if you had a stack of banknotes worth 20 billion yen, 20 billion yen in gold would be such a big mountain that practically it'd be kinda pointless."
