description: George says five billion yen could let someone establish any business. WH says any business would prosper, adding confidence in success rather than merely the ability to launch it.
sourceReading: 興せそう denotes being able to start a venture and remains speculative.

units.text: "5 billion yen for each of us......Incredible!  With that kind of money, any business would prosper.  No wait, we could live our whole lives fabulously without working at all."
units.note: Both replace capacity to establish any business with its future prosperity; MG probably softens confidence but does not restore the launch-versus-success distinction.
units.japanese: 「１人頭５０億円か。…すごいね！　それだけあったらどんな事業でも興せそうだよ。いや、そもそも働かずに生涯を優雅に過ごせるだろうね。」

units.text: "5 billion yen for each of us... ...Incredible! With that kind of money, you could probably make any sort of business prosper. In fact, we could live our whole lives fabulously without working at all."
units.note: Both replace capacity to establish any business with its future prosperity; MG probably softens confidence but does not restore the launch-versus-success distinction.
units.japanese: 「１人頭５０億円か。…すごいね！　それだけあったらどんな事業でも興せそうだよ。いや、そもそも働かずに生涯を優雅に過ごせるだろうね」
candidates: make any sort of business prosper

units.text: "5 billion yen for each of us... ...Incredible! With that kind of money, any business would prosper. No, wait, we could live our whole lives fabulously without ever working at all."
units.note: Both replace capacity to establish any business with its future prosperity; MG probably softens confidence but does not restore the launch-versus-success distinction.
units.japanese: 「１人頭５０億円か。…すごいね！　それだけあったらどんな事業でも興せそうだよ。いや、そもそも働かずに生涯を優雅に過ごせるだろうね」

description: Eva reports that Kinzo pointed at the bars and explicitly stated there were ten tons. WH says he used that claim to prove the amount, promoting his declaration into a proof procedure. It also replaces confirmation through multiple sources with confirmation in several ways.
sourceReading: それを指して ... 明言 means pointing at the displayed gold and saying the quantity clearly; 複数の筋 denotes multiple sources.

units.text: "The fact that Father obtained gold bars from an unknown source can be confirmed in several ways.  We heard that, before the president of the Marusoo company died, Father showed him a large amount of gold somewhere.  Father used that claim to prove that that there were 10 tons worth."
units.note: MG now makes Kinzo use the president’s claim as proof of quantity, rather than Kinzo point and declare; this is a changed version of the same declaration-to-proof distortion. MG still changes multiple sources to several ways. UP restores multiple sources and Kinzo’s clear statement, though the pointing gesture is implicit in the shown gold.
units.japanese: 「お父様が出自不明の金塊を持っていたことは複数の筋から確認されているわ。死んだマルソーの会長は生前、お父様に某所で積み上げられた金塊を実際に見せられたという。お父様はそれを指して、１０ｔ分あるとはっきり明言したわ。」

units.text: "The fact that Father obtained gold bars from an unknown source has been confirmed in several ways. We've heard that, before the president of the Marusoo company died, Father showed him a large pile of gold somewhere. Father used that man's claim as proof that there were 10 tons' worth."
units.note: MG now makes Kinzo use the president’s claim as proof of quantity, rather than Kinzo point and declare; this is a changed version of the same declaration-to-proof distortion. MG still changes multiple sources to several ways. UP restores multiple sources and Kinzo’s clear statement, though the pointing gesture is implicit in the shown gold.
units.japanese: 「お父様が出自不明の金塊を持っていたことは複数の筋から確認されているわ。死んだマルソーの会長は生前、お父様に某所で積み上げられた金塊を実際に見せられたという。お父様はそれを指して、１０ｔ分あるとはっきり明言したわ」
candidates: used that man's claim as proof

description: Rudolf proposes a financial investigation of Kinzo; WH adds political status to its scope. The same addition recurs when Krauss describes his own financial difficulty at 16536–16537.
sourceReading: 財政状況 concerns finances. 政界財界 in the preceding dialogue names contacts and does not modify these clauses.

units.text: "......If you insist on it, that's alright.  But Aniki, Father doesn't have long.  Nobody can ensure that he will live to see this day next year.  When Father dies, the inheritance will be passed on.  We will all set up impartial lawyers and accountants to inspect Father's financial and political status."
units.note: Both investigate financial situation only, without the WH political-status addition. Later recurrence in Krauss’s own situation remains to be reviewed.
units.japanese: 「……兄貴がそうだと言い張るんならそれでいいさ。でもよ兄貴。親父は長くない。来年の今日まで生きてるなんて、誰にも保証できねぇんだぜ？　親父が死ねばその時点で遺産相続だ。俺たちは全員の立場から中立な弁護士と会計士を立てて親父の財政状況を調査させるぜ。」

units.text: "......If you insist on it, that's alright.  But Aniki, Father doesn't have long.  Nobody can ensure that he will live to see this day next year.  When Father dies, the inheritance will be passed on.  We will all set up impartial lawyers and accountants to inspect Father's financial and political status."
units.note: Later recurrence also preserves financial situation without introducing political status.
units.japanese: 「……兄貴がそうだと言い張るんならそれでいいさ。でもよ兄貴。親父は長くない。来年の今日まで生きてるなんて、誰にも保証できねぇんだぜ？　親父が死ねばその時点で遺産相続だ。俺たちは全員の立場から中立な弁護士と会計士を立てて親父の財政状況を調査させるぜ。」

description: Krauss wonders what the siblings want in return for their large concession. WH says he worries what collateral they have to make the compromise, shifting his question toward their security rather than their demanded return.
sourceReading: 見返り is what is expected in exchange.

units.text: Krauss, also realizing that this sounded to good to be true, couldn't help but feel doubt... He had to worry about what kind of collateral they had to make this kind of a compromise...
units.note: Both restore wondering what the siblings demand in exchange for their concession, rather than what collateral they possess.
units.japanese: これほどの譲歩に対する見返りが何か、気にならないはずもない…。
candidates: what kind of collateral they had

description: Eva says that if Krauss shows sincerity by paying ten percent, the balance can wait; she asks whether even he can manage that gesture. WH makes Eva show sincerity by asking for ten percent and changes his ability to demonstrate it into his noticing it.
sourceReading: 誠意を見せてくれたら makes Krauss the person asked to demonstrate sincerity; 兄さんにだって示せる retains him as agent.

units.text: "Normally, I'd hope to receive the 7.5 billion right now, all at once.  But out of concern for you, I'll show my sincerity by asking for only ten percent of that for the time being.  It's alright to let the remaining 90 percent carry over until the distribution of the inheritance.  ...Right?  With ten percent to show sincerity, even you would notice it."
units.note: MG still makes Eva/we show sincerity by asking for 10 percent at row 499, but restores Krauss ability to show it at row 502. UP restores both clauses. Parent description reused with surviving scope explicitly narrowed.
units.japanese: 「本当なら今すぐ７５億を一括で払ってもらいたいところよぅ。でも兄さんの立場に配慮して、とりあえず１割を納める誠意を見せてくれたら、残りの９割は遺産分配時に持ち越してくれていいってことなの。…ね？　１割程度の誠意なら、兄さんにだって示せるんじゃない？」
candidates: I'll show my sincerity by asking

units.text: "Normally, we'd hope to receive the 7.5 billion right now, all at once. But out of concern for you, we'll show our sincerity by asking for only ten percent of that for the time being. The remaining 90% can wait until the inheritance is distributed. ...See? Even you'd be capable of managing a mere 10% to show your sincerity."
units.note: MG still makes Eva/we show sincerity by asking for 10 percent at row 499, but restores Krauss ability to show it at row 502. UP restores both clauses. Parent description reused with surviving scope explicitly narrowed.
units.japanese: 「本当なら今すぐ７５億を一括で払ってもらいたいところよぅ。でも兄さんの立場に配慮して、とりあえず１割を納める誠意を見せてくれたら、残りの９割は遺産分配時に持ち越してくれていいってことなの。…ね？　１割程度の誠意なら、兄さんにだって示せるんじゃない？」
candidates: we'll show our sincerity by asking

description: Eva reserves the right to object if their share is adjusted downward by 7.5 billion yen, potentially cancelling the deal’s benefit. WH instead speaks of reducing their portion of 7.5 billion, losing the stated amount of the offset.
sourceReading: ７５億分 modifies the extent of 減る, not the size of 取り分.

units.text: ...It's only natural, right?  We'd be sad if you adjusted our portion of 7.5 billion downwards."
units.note: MG reduces their 7.5-billion share rather than specifying a 7.5-billion downward offset. UP explicitly gives downwards by 7.5 billion.
units.japanese: …当然よねぇ？　７５億分、私たちの取り分が減るように調整されちゃったら悲しいもの。」

units.text: ...It's only natural, right? We'd be so sad if you managed things so that our 7.5 billion share shrank."
units.note: MG reduces their 7.5-billion share rather than specifying a 7.5-billion downward offset. UP explicitly gives downwards by 7.5 billion.
units.japanese: 「…当然よねぇ？　７５億分、私たちの取り分が減るように調整されちゃったら悲しいもの」

description: Rudolf explicitly fears that delay will leave them unable to collect their inheritance. WH retains delay but substitutes the vague “led astray,” omitting the risk of never receiving the money.
sourceReading: 取りっぱぐれる means failing to collect what is due.

units.text: "As a general rule, we wouldn't complain.  As long as you do it neatly, it's fine.  ...As long as you don't do anything significantly obvious, we don't plan to aggravate anything.  We just want the inheritance quickly.  We don't want it to get all drawn out and led astray."
units.note: MG left hanging and UP led astray both omit fear of losing the chance to collect the inheritance; wanting quick distribution alone does not restore that risk.
units.japanese: 「原則的に文句は言わねぇつもりだ。兄貴が綺麗にやってくれたならそれでいい。…よっぽど露骨なことをしなけりゃ、俺たちは事を荒立てるつもりなんかねぇんだぜ。俺たちだって早く遺産は欲しい。いつまでもぐだぐだして取りっぱぐれたくねぇんだ。」

units.text: "We'll avoid complaining, as a general rule. Just make sure you do it neat and tidy. ...As long as you don't try anything that's blatantly obvious, we've got no intention of stirring things up. We want our inheritance quickly too. We don't want it to get all drawn out and left hanging."
units.note: MG left hanging and UP led astray both omit fear of losing the chance to collect the inheritance; wanting quick distribution alone does not restore that risk.
units.japanese: 「原則的に文句は言わねぇつもりだ。兄貴が綺麗にやってくれたならそれでいい。…よっぽど露骨なことをしなけりゃ、俺たちは事を荒立てるつもりなんかねぇんだぜ。俺たちだって早く遺産は欲しい。いつまでもぐだぐだして取りっぱぐれたくねぇんだ」

units.text: "As a general rule, we wouldn't complain. As long as you do it neatly, it's fine. ...As long as you don't do anything significantly obvious, we don't plan to aggravate anything. We want the inheritance quickly as much as you do. We don't want it to get all drawn out and led astray."
units.note: MG left hanging and UP led astray both omit fear of losing the chance to collect the inheritance; wanting quick distribution alone does not restore that risk.
units.japanese: 「原則的に文句は言わねぇつもりだ。兄貴が綺麗にやってくれたならそれでいい。…よっぽど露骨なことをしなけりゃ、俺たちは事を荒立てるつもりなんかねぇんだぜ。俺たちだって早く遺産は欲しい。いつまでもぐだぐだして取りっぱぐれたくねぇんだ」

description: In response to a demand that any gold found be handed over immediately, Eva ostensibly guarantees compliance. WH promises to hold onto it for Krauss, a different action that already evades the handover before narration calls her promise sophistry.
sourceReading: もちろん保証する directly guarantees the immediately preceding seventh condition.

units.text: "Yes, yes.  Of course, we'll hold onto it for you.  *giggle*!"
units.note: MG promises to hold the gold for him rather than hand it over. UP ostensibly guarantees the demanded handover; its separate mistranslation of sophistry is recorded independently.
units.japanese: 「えぇえぇ、もちろん保証するわよぅ？　くすくすくす！」
candidates: we'll hold onto it for you

units.text: "Yes, yes. Of course, we'll hold onto it for you. *giggle*!"
units.note: MG promises to hold the gold for him rather than hand it over. UP ostensibly guarantees the demanded handover; its separate mistranslation of sophistry is recorded independently.
units.japanese: 「えぇえぇ、もちろん保証するわよぅ？　くすくすくす！」
candidates: we'll hold onto it for you

description: Krauss says nasty people bought up Hideyoshi’s shares. WH identifies them as colleagues of his, adding a relationship the Japanese does not establish.
sourceReading: 性質の悪い連中 identifies character, not affiliation with Hideyoshi.

units.text: "However, it is unfortunate that you have neglected your stockholders.  It's also horrible that you were unable to solidify your base when you became stock-listed.  ...Before you realized it, some bad-natured colleagues of yours had bought up a huge share of your company's stock, didn't they?"
units.note: MG identifies hostile share buyers as colleagues; UP fellows does not add that relationship.
units.japanese: 「だが、株主たちに対する還元を怠ったのが悪かった。そして上場した時に足回りを固め切らなかったのもまずかった。……気付いた時には性質の悪い連中に、自社株をだいぶ買い集められていたらしいじゃないですか。」

units.text: "However, it is unfortunate that you have neglected your stockholders. It's even more unfortunate that you were unable to solidify your base when you became stock-listed. ...Before you realized it, some bad-natured colleagues of yours had bought up a huge share of your company's stock, right?"
units.note: MG identifies hostile share buyers as colleagues; UP fellows does not add that relationship.
units.japanese: 「だが、株主たちに対する還元を怠ったのが悪かった。そして上場した時に足回りを固め切らなかったのもまずかった。……気付いた時には性質の悪い連中に、自社株をだいぶ買い集められていたらしいじゃないですか」

description: The shareholders demand exorbitant amounts either for selling shares back or for signing blank proxies at the shareholders’ meeting. WH gives only the share buyback, omitting the alternative transaction for delegated votes.
sourceReading: もしくは ... 白紙委任状への判子 states a second way shareholders demand payment.

units.text: Their efforts had almost collected a majority of the stock in the company. ...At that point, even Hideyoshi noticed and started to buy back the stock, but the stock holders, who realized that the company was undergoing an acquisition maneuver, demanded a ridiculous price for the shares that Hideyoshi was trying to buy back. They continually tortured Hideyoshi, who had no leeway in the negotiation of the price.
units.note: Both omit the separate demand for signing blank proxies at the shareholders meeting. Share-buyback alone does not retain the alternative purchase of voting authority.
units.japanese: …この時点で秀吉も気付き、株の買い戻しを始めたが、会社が買収工作を受けていることを理解している株主たちは、秀吉の買戻し、もしくは総会での白紙委任状への判子に対し皆がそれぞれ法外な金額を要求。
candidates: for the shares that Hideyoshi was trying to buy back

units.text: Thanks to these efforts, this group had almost collected a majority of the company's stock. ...At that point, even Hideyoshi noticed and started to buy back the stock, but the stockholders realized that the company was undergoing an acquisition maneuver... and each demanded a ridiculous price for the shares that Hideyoshi was trying to buy back. They continually tortured Hideyoshi, who had no leeway in the negotiation of the price.
units.note: Both omit the separate demand for signing blank proxies at the shareholders meeting. Share-buyback alone does not retain the alternative purchase of voting authority.
units.japanese: 彼ら勢力は過半数に近い株を抑え始めていた。…この時点で秀吉も気付き、株の買い戻しを始めたが、会社が買収工作を受けていることを理解している株主たちは、秀吉の買戻し、もしくは総会での白紙委任状への判子に対し皆がそれぞれ法外な金額を要求。金額交渉の余地のない秀吉を苛み続けていた。
candidates: for the shares that Hideyoshi was trying to buy back

units.text: Their efforts had almost collected a majority of the stock in the company. ...At that point, even Hideyoshi noticed and started to buy back the stock, but the stockholders, who realized that the company was undergoing an acquisition maneuver, demanded a ridiculous price for the shares that Hideyoshi was trying to buy back. They continually tortured Hideyoshi, who had no leeway in the negotiation of the price.
units.note: Both omit the separate demand for signing blank proxies at the shareholders meeting. Share-buyback alone does not retain the alternative purchase of voting authority.
units.japanese: 彼ら勢力は過半数に近い株を抑え始めていた。…この時点で秀吉も気付き、株の買い戻しを始めたが、会社が買収工作を受けていることを理解している株主たちは、秀吉の買戻し、もしくは総会での白紙委任状への判子に対し皆がそれぞれ法外な金額を要求。金額交渉の余地のない秀吉を苛み続けていた。
candidates: for the shares that Hideyoshi was trying to buy back

description: Rudolf is being driven toward total surrender because he has little prospect of winning. WH says he went for an all-out surrender, converting pressure into his completed chosen response.
sourceReading: 全面的な降伏を迫られていた describes a coerced predicament.

units.text: Rudolf had been building a large amount of wealth with a certain type of niche market. ...However, a niche is a niche. It's definitely not a sunny job. An American corporate giant was trying to accuse Rudolf's company of violating their rights. For various reasons, it was thought that winning the trial was extremely unlikely, and Rudolf went for an all-out surrender.
units.note: Both restore being pressured toward surrender rather than a completed voluntary surrender.
units.japanese: 様々な条件から、裁判での勝ち目は非常に薄いと考えられ、留弗夫は全面的な降伏を迫られていたのである。

description: The source identifies why time favors Krauss: prolonging the deal worsens the others’ cash crisis. WH replaces that specific leverage with his ability to control the deal however he likes.
sourceReading: 引き伸ばすほど ... 有利 is a comparative relation between delay and bargaining advantage.

units.text: In other words, the situation had been reversed. Because only Krauss, who they were threatening, had no urgent need for a large sum of money. Compared to that, the three who were threatening him wanted money quickly, no matter what the cost. So Krauss was able to control this deal however he liked.
units.note: Both restore longer delay favoring Krauss after explaining the others immediate cash needs.
units.japanese: つまり、この取引は引き伸ばすほどに蔵臼に有利なのだ。
candidates: was able to control this deal however he liked

description: Krauss’s triumphant offer is called blatantly insincere in Japanese. WH calls it horribly blunt, describing directness rather than the transparent falseness of his helpful pose.
sourceReading: 白々しい refers to shamelessly obvious pretense in the professed helpfulness.

units.text: Krauss's elated words were horribly blunt. The other siblings could do nothing more than listen, grinding their teeth. .........If they could think of a sponsor that convenient, they wouldn't have kept up this charade.  They had entered this huge battle specifically because they had exhausted all other options.
units.note: MG explicitly says words detached from actual feelings, restoring insincerity; UP horribly blunt retains the wrong judgment of directness.
units.japanese: 勝ち誇った蔵臼の言葉はあまりに白々しい。

units.text:
Krauss's elated words were horribly blunt.
The other siblings could do nothing more than listen, grinding their teeth. .........If they could think of a sponsor that convenient, they wouldn't have kept up this charade. They had entered this huge battle specifically because they had exhausted all other options.
units.note: MG explicitly says words detached from actual feelings, restoring insincerity; UP horribly blunt retains the wrong judgment of directness.
units.japanese:
勝ち誇った蔵臼の言葉はあまりに白々しい。
弟たちは、歯軋りしながらそれを聞き流すしかなかった。………そんな都合のいいスポンサーに心当たりがあったなら、こんな真似はしないのだ。万策が尽きたからこそ、このような大勝負に出ているのだ。

description: Krauss says he will negotiate as hard as he can to obtain accommodation on interest. WH says he will negotiate for the largest interest rate possible. It reverses the professed benefit and makes his nominal assistance explicitly harmful.
sourceReading: 利息を融通してもらえるよう ... 最大限、交渉 places maximum effort on negotiating favorable accommodation, not maximum size on the interest rate.

units.text: "I told you, didn't I.  All I can do is find other sponsors for you.  Of course, I will negotiate for the largest interest rate possible.  Hehheheheh, gahahahahahahahaha!!"
units.note: MG retains highest interest rate. UP replaces it with borrowing the interest as well; that is a different misconstrual of accommodation on interest, not retained highest-rate wording.
units.japanese: 「言ったではないか。私にできるのは他のスポンサーを探すだけだよ。もちろん、利息を融通してもらえるようには最大限、交渉するがね。ふふふふふ、くっくくくくくくく！！」

units.text: "I told you, didn't I? All I can do is find other sponsors for you. Of course, I will negotiate for the highest interest rate possible. Hehheheheh, gahahahahahahahaha!!"
units.note: MG retains highest interest rate. UP replaces it with borrowing the interest as well; that is a different misconstrual of accommodation on interest, not retained highest-rate wording.
units.japanese: 「言ったではないか。私にできるのは他のスポンサーを探すだけだよ。もちろん、利息を融通してもらえるようには最大限、交渉するがね。ふふふふふ、くっくくくくくくく！！」

units.text: "I told you, didn't I? All I can do is find other sponsors for you. Of course, I will do my utmost to negotiate so that you can borrow the interest as well. Hehheheheh, gahahahahahahahaha!!"
units.note: MG retains highest interest rate. UP replaces it with borrowing the interest as well; that is a different misconstrual of accommodation on interest, not retained highest-rate wording.
units.japanese: 「言ったではないか。私にできるのは他のスポンサーを探すだけだよ。もちろん、利息を融通してもらえるようには最大限、交渉するがね。ふふふふふ、くっくくくくくくく！！」

description: Kinzo concedes that Krauss can at least see through something that simple, then calls him only partly incompetent. WH instead asks whether such an act can really be called exposing and labels him an incomplete, incompetent man. The grudging recognition turns into a challenge to the description.
sourceReading: その程度のことは看破できるのか asks whether he is capable of that much; 中途半端に無能 acknowledges the awkward incompleteness of his incompetence.

units.text: "Hmph.  Can you really call something of that level exposing?  That incomplete, incompetent man.  .........What are they doing now?"
units.note: MG asks if obvious facts need exposing rather than grudgingly acknowledging Krauss can see through them, and irresolute does not preserve partly incompetent. UP restores concession and sarcastic failure even to be fully incompetent.
units.japanese: 「ふ。その程度のことは看破できるのか。中途半端に無能な男め。………今はどうしている？」
candidates: Can you really call something of that level exposing?

units.text: "Hmph. Is there even any need to "expose" such obvious facts? That irresolute, incompetent man. .........What are they doing now?"
units.note: MG asks if obvious facts need exposing rather than grudgingly acknowledging Krauss can see through them, and irresolute does not preserve partly incompetent. UP restores concession and sarcastic failure even to be fully incompetent.
units.japanese: 「ふ。その程度のことは看破できるのか。中途半端に無能な男め。………今はどうしている？」
candidates: Is there even any need to "expose" such obvious facts?

description: Genji infers that Kinzo must have a deep purpose behind the epitaph. WH says he has realized that Kinzo’s thoughts are very deep, replacing a tentative inference about purpose with an established judgment of mental depth.
sourceReading: 深いお考えがあってのことと察しします is inferring that there is a considered purpose behind the act.

units.text: "............I don't presume to understand the Master's thoughts.  However, I have realized that those thoughts are very deep."
units.note: MG restores deep reason but I’m sure overstates the inference; UP I sense restores tentative status but describes depth of thoughts rather than considered purpose behind posting the epitaph. Original realized-knowledge wording survives in neither. Parent description reused with surviving components narrowed here.
units.japanese: 「……………私には、お館様のお考えはわかりかねます。ですが、深いお考えがあってのことと察しします。」
candidates: I have realized that those thoughts are very deep

units.text: "......I do not presume to understand the Master's thoughts. However, I'm sure he had a deep reason for doing so."
units.note: MG restores deep reason but I’m sure overstates the inference; UP I sense restores tentative status but describes depth of thoughts rather than considered purpose behind posting the epitaph. Original realized-knowledge wording survives in neither. Parent description reused with surviving components narrowed here.
units.japanese: 「……………私には、お館様のお考えはわかりかねます。深いお考えがあってのこととお察しします」

units.text: "...............I fail to understand the Master's thoughts. I sense that they run very deep."
units.note: MG restores deep reason but I’m sure overstates the inference; UP I sense restores tentative status but describes depth of thoughts rather than considered purpose behind posting the epitaph. Original realized-knowledge wording survives in neither. Parent description reused with surviving components narrowed here.
units.japanese: 「……………私には、お館様のお考えはわかりかねます。深いお考えがあってのこととお察しします」

description: Nanjo jokes that the difficult epitaph should keep him entertained until death comes. WH turns it into free time before someone comes to get us, suggesting an ordinary pickup and adding a plural waiting party.
sourceReading: お迎えが来る is the old man’s euphemism for death in this lifespan context.

units.text: ......Actually, I wrote this epitaph down on my notebook at one point in time.  Night after night, I would try to solve it before going to sleep,   ......but, hahaha, it really is hard.  It looks like there might be some free time to relax and consider it before someone comes to get us.  What do you say, Genji-san?"
units.note: MG retains free time and someone coming to get us; UP rest of my days restores lifelong enjoyment and death endpoint.
units.japanese: ……実は以前、この碑文を手帳に記しましてな。夜な夜な、寝る前に挑んでみたのですが、……はっはっは、実に難しい。お迎えが来るまでの間、ゆっくり楽しむことができそうです。源次さんこそ、いかがですかな？」
candidates: before someone comes to get us

description: The Japanese epitaph explicitly contains 口 within 口にし. WH gives only “tell you of.” The later solution reads written mouth components, together with 其, 里 and 岸, in a place name. English retains village and shore as explicit words but not mouth, making that textual correspondence less available at the initial clue.
sourceReading: The answer-script explanation at 163615–163680 explicitly decomposes the place name and says those components are words appearing in the epitaph. This binds the wordplay to the written components, not merely generic dialogue about a shore.

units.text: If you follow the river downstream, you will find a village. In the village, look for the shore the two will tell you of. There sleeps the key to the Golden Land.
units.note: MG tell and UP speak both leave mouth implicit in initial English wording. Targeted EP7 comparison confirms character decomposition and the retrospective explanatory repairs in each edition. UP explicitly pairs speak with 口 only in the later explanation, not initial epitaph.
units.japanese: その里にて二人が口にし岸を探れ。

units.text:
As you travel down it, you will see a village. 
In that village, look for the shore the two will tell you of. 
There sleeps the key to the Golden Land.
units.note: MG tell and UP speak both leave mouth implicit in initial English wording. Targeted EP7 comparison confirms character decomposition and the retrospective explanatory repairs in each edition. UP explicitly pairs speak with 口 only in the later explanation, not initial epitaph.

川を下れば、やがて里あり。
その里にて二人が口にし岸を探れ。
そこに黄金郷への鍵が眠る。

description: Battler feels Sogakishi is wrong; WH makes him feel it is definitely right. Jessica then says she suspects Sogakishi as the location and proposes an unknown childhood house there; WH makes her doubt that it is Sogakishi. The two positions are reversed, and her suggested house no longer supports her stated position.
sourceReading: 間違いって気がする is doubt about that candidate. Jessica’s 疑ってる identifies the suspected candidate, as confirmed by her example of a childhood home and George’s subsequent refusal to clear Sogakishi.

units.text: "......Hmmmm.  That's a little annoying.  Couldn't a puzzle for the hiding place of a treasure be a little more exact?  Anyway, I get the feeling that Sogakishi is definitely the right place."
units.note: Both restore Battler’s doubt about Sogakishi and Jessica’s continuing suspicion of it, supported by possible unknown childhood house.
units.japanese:
「……うーん。何だかぱっとしねぇなぁ。宝の在り処を隠した謎ってのは、もっとビッタリとはまるモンじゃねぇのかよ。どうも曽我岸ってのがそもそも間違いって気がするぜ。」
「私は曽我岸を疑ってるぜ？　私たちが知らないだけで、例えば祖父さまの子供時代を過ごした家とかがあるかも知れないだろ。１行目に、懐かしき故郷を～って行があるくらいだもんな。…紗音は祖父さまによく酒とか注がされてたろ。昔話とか聞かされたことないのか？」

units.text: "Well, I doubt it's Sogakishi.  It could be talking about some house that Grandfather lived in when he was a kid that we don't know about.  After all, the first line mentioned his beloved hometown.  ...Shannon, you've fed a lot of sake to Grandfather, haven't you?  Hasn't he ever told you about his hometown?"
units.note: Both restore Battler’s doubt about Sogakishi and Jessica’s continuing suspicion of it, supported by possible unknown childhood house.
units.japanese:
「……うーん。何だかぱっとしねぇなぁ。宝の在り処を隠した謎ってのは、もっとビッタリとはまるモンじゃねぇのかよ。どうも曽我岸ってのがそもそも間違いって気がするぜ。」

description: Battler calls the ending of the epitaph the clincher in its increasingly disturbing content. WH says the last part is guaranteed, replacing an evaluative reaction with a statement of certainty.
sourceReading: 極めつけ identifies the culminating example, here the final horrifying proposition subsequently quoted by Shannon.

units.text: "...I see, sacrifices to restore the witch...  That's what it would mean.  As a result, the witch will be revived at the ninth twilight.........That last part is guaranteed."
units.note: MG guaranteed retains assertion of certainty. UP glorious is an ironic evaluation of the horrific climax in the surrounding disturbing-content exchange; it no longer asserts guarantee.
units.japanese: 「…なるほど魔女復活のための生贄か…。そういう解釈にもなるな。その結果、第九の晩に魔女が蘇って……。…最後は極めつけだな。」

units.text: "...I see, sacrifices to restore the witch... Yeah, that's what it'd mean. Near the end, the witch'll be revived on the ninth twilight... ...That last part is guaranteed."
units.note: MG guaranteed retains assertion of certainty. UP glorious is an ironic evaluation of the horrific climax in the surrounding disturbing-content exchange; it no longer asserts guarantee.
units.japanese: 「…なるほど魔女復活のための生贄か…。そういう解釈にもなるな。その結果、第九の晩に魔女が蘇って……。…最後は極めつけだな」

description: Shannon’s legend describes supposedly closed items found open on returning for another round. WH specifies a last round, adding finality to the reported patrol sequence.
sourceReading: もう一度 means again, not one last time.

units.text: "When they did the rounds one last time to check supposedly closed doors, windows and locks, some of those would be open.  Lights that were supposed to be off were turned on, and lights that were supposed to be on went out.  Things left lying around would disappear, and things would appear when no one had any memory of putting them there.  When any of these things happened, the old servants would say that the witch had visited the mansion, invisible, and was playing pranks."
units.note: Both give another round/double-check rather than final patrol.
units.japanese: 「ちゃんと閉めたはずの窓や扉や鍵が、もう一度見回りに来たら開いていたとか。消したはずの灯りが付いていたり、付けたはずの明かりが消えていたり。置いたはずの物がなくなっていたり、置いた覚えのない物が置かれていたり。……そういうことがある度に、古い使用人たちは魔女が姿を消してお屋敷に訪れて、悪戯をしていったのだろうと囁きあったそうです。」

description: Jessica’s example of ordinary apparent witch pranks is failing to find her bag when it is time for school. WH substitutes shoes.
sourceReading: 鞄 is a bag, not shoes.

units.text: "Yeah, she exists.  I remember often being unable to find my shoes before heading to school..."
units.note: Both restore missing bag, not shoes.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、いるよな。私も昔よく、登校の時に限って鞄が見付からなかったりしたもんだぜ…。」

description: Maria seriously considers whether any charm could protect the two cousins, then turns to her notebook. WH says she does so as if there were obviously such a charm, replacing her expressed search for a possible remedy with an assumption of an obvious one.
sourceReading: おまじないはないものかと ... 真剣に悩んで presents a sincere question she is trying to answer.

units.text: Maria, seriously pondering and crossing her arms, began flipping through the pages of her handbook as if there were obviously some charm capable of protecting Jessica and myself from the witch's wrath.
units.note: Both restore serious consideration whether a protective charm exists.
units.japanese: 真里亞は、俺と朱志香に魔女の怒りが及ばないようにするおまじないはないものかと、腕組みをして真剣に悩んでから、手帳のページを捲り始める。

description: Battler says the charm’s material does not matter, its feeling does, and he has not sunk so low as to mock that. WH ends with not planning to ruin everything by making fun of it, changing his personal moral standard into an intention about the consequences of mockery.
sourceReading: 落ちぶれちゃいないつもり is a self-assessment: he does not believe himself so degraded as to ridicule sincere feeling.

units.text: The material quality of the charm wasn't important. The strength of her feelings was. Even I wouldn't plan on ruining everything by making fun of it.
units.note: Both restore Battler’s moral/self-respect standard against mocking sincere feelings rather than merely intention not to ruin things.
units.japanese:
お守りは材質が問題じゃないよな。
気持ちの強さの問題さ。
そいつを小馬鹿にするほど、俺も落ちぶれちゃいないつもりだぜ。

description: George and Shannon react with surprise or conversational acknowledgments to Maria’s answers. WH says they act surprised and agree with everything she says, adding both overt performance and universal assent to her claims.
sourceReading: 相槌を打つ denotes listening responses or acknowledgments; it does not establish endorsement of every proposition. 驚く is not explicitly pretending surprise.

units.text: While eating the cookies Kumasawa-san had baked, Jessica and I asked Maria this and that about black magic. Maria happily chatted away in response to our questions. For each one, George-aniki and Shannon-chan would act surprised and agree with everything she said.
units.note: MG retains act surprised but replaces universal agreement with chime in; only the performance component survives. UP retains both acting surprised and agreement with everything.
units.japanese: その度に譲治の兄貴と紗音ちゃんが驚いたり相槌を打ったりしてくれる。
candidates: act surprised and agree with everything

units.text: While eating the cookies Kumasawa-san had baked, Jessica and I asked Maria this and that about black magic. Maria happily chatted away in response to our questions. Each time, George-aniki and Shannon-chan would act surprised or chime in.
units.note: MG retains act surprised but replaces universal agreement with chime in; only the performance component survives. UP retains both acting surprised and agreement with everything.

description: George tentatively recalls this as the spot before suggesting a wider search. WH has him speculate that it was not here, adding doubt about this location where Japanese offers tentative confirmation.
sourceReading: ここじゃなかったかな is a recollective negative question: wasn’t it here?

units.text: "Maybe it wasn't here...  Let's try spreading out a bit in our search."
units.note: Both retain maybe it wasn’t here instead of tentative recollection that this was the spot. Subsequent wider search proposal does not reverse the polarity of the first sentence.

description: Battler wonders whether they were content with any plausible reason that let them leave the painful scene. WH makes them definitely fine with the reason provided it eased their pain. Their next farewell is unheard and feels guilty and insincere in Japanese; WH makes its being unheard the reason for their guilty consciences. It strengthens the self-accusation while changing its causal connection.
sourceReading: それでよかったのかもしれない retains uncertainty about their own motive. ... 届いていないようだったし ... 後ろめたくて白々しかった coordinates the unheard call with the callers’ unease rather than making the former cause the latter.

units.text: Because we thought that George-aniki's point was probably correct, ...we were fine with using that correct-sounding reason to justify retreating as long as it would ease the pain in our chests.
units.note: Both restore uncertain may/probably account of retreating with a plausible reason. MG separates unheard farewell and guilty/insincere feeling; UP since makes being unheard the cause of guilt, retaining that causal component. Parent description reused with surviving scope narrowed.
units.japanese:
譲治の兄貴の言い分は多分もっともだと思ったし、…そういうもっともらしい理由をつけて、この胸の痛くなる場から退散できるなら、俺たちはそれでよかったのかもしれない。
俺と朱志香は、譲治兄貴に頷き、その場を後にする。
真里亞に、俺たちはゲストハウスに行ってるからなと声を掛けるが、耳には届いていないようだったし、言っている俺たちもどこか後ろめたくて白々しかった…。

units.text: Jessica and I nodded at George-aniki, and we all left. We called towards Maria that we were going to head to the guesthouse, but since it didn't seem to reach her ears, we also had shamelessly guilty consciences...

description: Kinzo specifically offers back the Ushiromiya family headship before casting away his ring. WH calls it the inheritance of the family, leaving the office or authority being surrendered unnamed and making the act sound like a transfer of property or general patrimony.
sourceReading: 家督 here is the family headship or its succession rights; the source separately enumerates wealth and gold elsewhere.

units.text: ...Come, devour as much as you wish...!!  I will overcome that roulette.  Yes, I'll put everything on the line.  First, I'll return the inheritance of the Ushiromiya family.  Accept it!!"
units.note: MG inheritance of family retains unnamed office; UP headship explicitly restores the authority cast away with the ring.
units.japanese: …さぁ、好きなだけ食らうがいいッ…！！　私はそのルーレットに打ち勝つだろう。さぁ、全てを賭すぞ。まずは右代宮家の家督を返そう。受け取るがいいッ！！」

units.text: "...Come, devour to your heart's content...!! I will achieve victory over that roulette. Yes, I'll put everything on the line. First, I'll return the inheritance of the Ushiromiya family. Accept it!!"
units.note: MG inheritance of family retains unnamed office; UP headship explicitly restores the authority cast away with the ring.
units.japanese: 「…さぁ、好きなだけ食らうがいいッ…！！　私はそのルーレットに打ち勝つだろう。さぁ、全てを賭すぞ。まずは右代宮家の家督を返そう。受け取るがいいッ！！」

description: Jessica says assigned self-study is checked rigorously afterward. WH instead supplies a person standing behind her watching everything she does while she studies.
sourceReading: 後で locates the scrutiny afterward; the source does not describe a physically present observer.

units.text: "If the boats don't come, I stay home.  Still, it's not as good as it sounds.  Usually, I'm ordered to study by myself, and it's not that fun with someone standing right behind you watching everything you do."
units.note: MG retains invented continuous over-the-shoulder observer. UP restores rigorous checking, although without explicit afterward; no invented physical watcher remains.
units.japanese: 「船が出なきゃ休みになるぜ。もっとも、そう甘くはねーけどな。大抵、その代わりに自習が指示されて、後でかっちりと見られるからそうそう気楽でもねーさ。」

units.text: "If the boats don't come, I stay home. Still, it's not as good as it sounds. Usually, I'm ordered to study by myself, and it's not that fun with someone standing right behind you watching everything you do."
units.note: MG retains invented continuous over-the-shoulder observer. UP restores rigorous checking, although without explicit afterward; no invented physical watcher remains.
units.japanese: 「船が出なきゃ休みになるぜ。もっとも、そう甘くはねーけどな。大抵、その代わりに自習が指示されて、後でかっちりと見られるからそうそう気楽でもねーさ」

description: Rosa knows her daughter’s nature and feels a chill of dread. WH replaces that reaction with She had always known, adding duration and removing the emotional pivot before she realizes Maria may still be searching.
sourceReading: そしてぞっとする describes her immediate horrified reaction.

units.text: Rosa knew her daughter's nature well. She had always known. Maria was stubbornly honest, ......and if she was ordered to find something that didn't exist, she would look forever and ever. ......Even if rain was pouring down...!!
units.note: Both restore knowledge of daughter nature followed by a chill of dread.
units.japanese:
楼座は我が子の性分をよく知っている。
そしてぞっとする。

description: On George’s answer, Rosa lunges toward him as though about to grapple with him. WH makes her jump as if someone had grabbed her, changing the direction and agency of the physical reaction.
sourceReading: 取っ組みかかるかのように飛びついてくる describes her rushing at the person answering.

units.text: When George-aniki called back, Rosa oba-san jumped as though someone had grabbed her.
units.note: Both restore Rosa moving toward George rather than reacting as though someone grabbed her. MG describes grabbing onto him; the source lunging as if grappling is sufficiently close here that no additional defect is asserted.
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴が返事をすると、楼座叔母さんがまるで取っ組みかかるかのように飛びついてくる。

description: Battler’s shocked You ... were still searching becomes You idiot ... are you still looking, adding an explicit insult to the drenched child.
sourceReading: お前 is a rough familiar second-person address; this line does not call her foolish.

units.text: "You idiot, ......are you still looking?!"
units.note: MG addresses Maria by name, without an insult. UP explicitly adds You idiot; Japanese お前 is the direct address you, not an explicit idiot insult. Shock and concern do not supply that lexical insult.
units.japanese:
「お前、
……まだ探してたのか！！」

description: Rosa decides dinner is a better opportunity to ask who lent Maria the umbrella. WH says she will ask the person who lent it, though that person’s identity is the question she has not resolved.
sourceReading: 貸してくれた人を聞く here is an inquiry into the lender’s identity, as the subsequent dinner questioning confirms.

units.text: Maria, who quickly picked up that her mother didn't believe her, made an angry face once again. So Rosa stopped pursuing the subject. It looked like it would be faster to ask the person who had lent Maria the umbrella during dinner rather than ask Maria herself...
units.note: Both say ask the person who lent it during dinner, rather than ask who lent it. Neither supports crediting Rosa with an identified lender.
units.japanese:
なので楼座はそれ以上を追求するのを止めた。
真里亞に聞くより、夕食の席で貸してくれた人を聞いた方が早そうだ…。

units.text: Maria immediately realized that her mother didn't believe her and started crying out unhappily again. So Rosa stopped pursuing the subject. It'd probably be faster to ask whoever lent Maria the umbrella during dinner, rather than ask Maria herself...
units.note: Both say ask the person who lent it during dinner, rather than ask who lent it. Neither supports crediting Rosa with an identified lender.
units.japanese:
母が自分の言葉を信用してくれなかったことをすぐに感じ取った真里亞は、再び不機嫌そうな声を上げる。なので楼座はそれ以上を追求するのを止めた。
真里亞に聞くより、夕食の席で貸してくれた人を聞いた方が早そうだ…。

description: Krauss recoils thinking Kinzo might emerge, then sighs with relief when he sees Nanjo. WH retains only the alarm and omits the reversal into relief.
sourceReading: しかし ... 南條 ... 安堵 contrasts apprehension about Kinzo with relief at the actual visitor.

units.text: The door to the study opened. Krauss was taken aback, thinking that maybe Kinzo was actually coming out.
units.note: Both explicitly restore Krauss sigh of relief at seeing Nanjo.
units.japanese:
…まさか本当に金蔵が出てきたのかと思い、蔵臼は後退った。
しかしその姿が南條のものだったので、安堵の息を漏らす…。

description: Kanon asks whether to inform the Master. WH has him announce that he will do so, turning a deferential proposal into his own decision.
sourceReading: お知らせしますか is an interrogative offer or consultation.

units.text: "......I will inform the Master."
units.note: Both preserve an interrogative proposal; Genji declines it. No report actually occurs.
units.japanese: 「……お館様にお知らせしますか。」

description: Kanon forces himself to avert his eyes from the garden lights. WH calls the aversion useless, replacing the effort involved with an assertion that the action is futile.
sourceReading: 無理に modifies his effortful action; it does not say the attempt has no effect.

units.text: Kanon looked at the rose garden's lights, dimly visible beyond the window. The dim lights were not enough to illuminate the surrounding area. Looking at those lights felt like making eye contact with the witch, and Kanon uselessly averted his gaze. ...If he didn't, it felt like his eyes would be absorbed by that light......
units.note: Both explicitly describe forcing himself to avert his gaze, followed by subjective fear of eyes being absorbed; neither asserts uselessness.
units.japanese: その光を見ることが、まるで魔女と目を合わせているように感じられて、嘉音は無理に目を逸らすのだった。

description: Gohda tries to enliven dinner through stylish little speeches but falls short. WH supplies jokes left and right and says not one succeeded, changing both his mode of hosting and the description of his failure.
sourceReading: 小洒落たスピーチ describes polished or stylish speeches; ひとつ及ばなかった describes falling short, not a count of jokes with zero successes.

units.text: Gohda-san, the supposed conductor of this musical piece called dinner, did his best to enliven the place, dropping little jokes left and right, but apparently not one of them succeeded.
units.note: MG retains jokes and zero successes. UP retains jokes replacing stylish speeches, but corrects zero successes to falling short; only hosting-mode change survives in UP.
units.japanese: 晩餐という名の演奏の指揮者でもある郷田さんは、場を盛り上げようと、色々と小洒落たスピーチなどで頑張ってくれたが、ひとつ及ばなかったようだ。

units.text: Gohda-san, the supposed conductor of this musical piece called dinner, did his best to enliven the place, dropping little jokes left and right, but apparently not one of them succeeded.
units.note: MG retains jokes and zero successes. UP retains jokes replacing stylish speeches, but corrects zero successes to falling short; only hosting-mode change survives in UP.
units.japanese: 晩餐という名の演奏の指揮者でもある郷田さんは、場を盛り上げようと、色々と小洒落たスピーチなどで頑張ってくれたが、ひとつ及ばなかったようだ。

units.text: Gohda‐san, the supposed conductor of this performance called dinner, did his best to enliven the place, dropping little jokes left and right, but it seemed they didn't quite get there.
units.note: MG retains jokes and zero successes. UP retains jokes replacing stylish speeches, but corrects zero successes to falling short; only hosting-mode change survives in UP.
units.japanese: 晩餐という名の演奏の指揮者でもある郷田さんは、場を盛り上げようと、色々と小洒落たスピーチなどで頑張ってくれたが、ひとつ及ばなかったようだ。

description: The wax seal gives the envelope an air of rank or formality, something Maria should not casually have or play with. WH says the seal makes clear it could not be something she brought as a prank, converting a status impression into an exclusion about her involvement.
sourceReading: 持っていていいものではない concerns the propriety of her holding it; 格を感じさせた reports an impression of its standing. Neither proves how she acquired it or why she brought it.

units.text: When they looked, they noticed that Maria was now holding a beautiful western-style envelope. On the front of the envelope, the Ushiromiya family crest - the One-winged Eagle - was done in gold leaf. Furthermore, the fact that it was sealed with dark-red wax made it clear that this was not something that Maria could have brought as a prank.
units.note: MG retains explicit exclusion of Maria bringing envelope as prank. UP restores class/formality and impropriety of casual handling. Source-authorized inference of Kinzo message at 645–646 is present in Japanese and is not counted as invention.
units.japanese: さらに赤黒い蝋で封までされていて、真里亞がいたずらに持っていていいものではない、格を感じさせた。

units.text: They saw that Maria was now holding a beautiful, Western-style envelope. On the front of the envelope, the Ushiromiya family crest—the One-Winged Eagle—was done in gold leaf. Furthermore, the fact that it was sealed with dark-red wax made it clear that this wasn't something Maria could have brought as a prank.
units.note: MG retains explicit exclusion of Maria bringing envelope as prank. UP restores class/formality and impropriety of casual handling. Source-authorized inference of Kinzo message at 645–646 is present in Japanese and is not counted as invention.
units.japanese: 見れば、いつの間にか真里亞の手には綺麗な洋形封筒が握られていた。その封筒の表面には、右代宮家の家紋である片翼の鷲をイメージしたものが箔押しされていた。さらに赤黒い蝋で封までされていて、真里亞がいたずらに持っていていいものではない、格を感じさせた。

description: Japanese describes the siblings’ fear that the letter contains Kinzo’s intentions and a decisively unfavorable inheritance announcement. WH first asserts that his intentions are in it, then confines their fear to the unfavorable announcement.
sourceReading: The feared content is governed by ... のではないかと心底恐れていた, encompassing the linked clauses.

units.text: One after another, all of the siblings, from Krauss on downwards, rejected Nanjo's statement, saying that the envelope that Maria was holding had not necessarily been sent by Kinzo. They were afraid. Kinzo's intentions were written in there, and they feared from the bottoms of their hearts that it might be some decidedly unfavorable announcement regarding the inheritance.
units.note: MG places both intentions and adverse announcement inside feared content. UP states intentions were written in there before the feared adverse announcement. Earlier source inference at 646 does not erase explicit fear scope here.
units.japanese: その中に、金蔵の意思が書かれていて、遺産に関して何か決定的に不利な発表をするのではないかと心底恐れていた。

description: After Kanon mentions Maria’s letter from Beatrice, Kinzo laughs that that one has already begun. His immediate invitation to Beatrice to enjoy their contest establishes the referent. WH instead says Those fools, did they start already, directing the remark toward a plural group.
sourceReading: あやつ is singular, and the ensuing direct address names Beatrice as the party beginning the contest.

units.text: "...Hahahaha............Those fools, did they start already?
units.note: Both identify a singular female referent before directly addressing Beatrice. UP adds daredevil characterization; no plural children referent remains.
units.japanese: 「…はっはっはっは…。………あやつめ、さっそく始めおったか。

description: Maria is so upset that she ignores even the cousins when they address her. WH describes what would happen if Battler tried to raise his voice, replacing observed behavior toward the group with his conditional expectation about speaking loudly.
sourceReading: 俺たちが声を掛けても無視する有様だった describes her actual state and reaction; 声を掛ける means addressing someone, not raising one’s voice.

units.text: The strange letter that the witch had entrusted Maria with had wiped all memories of dinner from our minds. Maria was repeatedly barraged with questions by Rosa oba-san and the other parents and became increasingly ill-tempered when they refused to believe her. If I tried to raise my voice in this kind of situation, I would just be ignored.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese: 俺たちが声を掛けても無視する有様だった。

units.text: The strange letter that the witch had entrusted to Maria wiped all memories of dinner from our minds. Maria was repeatedly barraged with questions by Aunt Rosa and the other parents... and became increasingly ill-tempered when they refused to believe her. If we kids tried to butt in, they'd probably ignore us.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese: 魔女が真里亞に託した不思議な手紙は、俺たち全員の頭から、どんな晩飯が並んだのかという記憶さえ吹き飛ばしてしまった。真里亞は、楼座叔母さんや他の親族たちにさんざん質問責めにされ、いくら話しても信じてくれないと完全に機嫌を悪くしてしまった。俺たちが声を掛けても無視する有様だった。

description: George would not want to fight like a vulture if only his own interests were at stake, but may need to fight when responsible for other people’s livelihoods. WH says If you are talking about me, no, making the contrast sound like an exception for George personally instead of the distinction between self-interest and responsibility.
sourceReading: 自分だけの話だったら means if it were a matter of oneself alone; the following family and employees clause supplies the explicit contrast.

units.text: "............If you're talking about me, no, I wouldn't want to do that.  However, when your family and your employees, your subordinates and their families are all counting on you, ...there are some times when you must fight."
units.note: Both explicitly restore if only about me/my own benefit as first condition, contrasting dependents.
units.japanese: 「…………………自分だけの話だったら、そんなことはしたくないよ。

description: Battler says even he can easily imagine how much the adults’ interrogation hurt Maria. WH says it was hard for him to imagine, reversing the explicit statement of emotional comprehension.
sourceReading: いくら俺でも想像に難しくない means not difficult to imagine, even for me.

units.text: Maria, who truly looked up to witches, had expected that coming in direct contact with Beatrice and receiving the letter as proof would be an event that would surprise everyone and make them happy. However, the adults had doubted its authenticity, and without swallowing Maria's story, had thoroughly bombarded her with questions. It was hard for me to imagine how much that must have hurt Maria.
units.note: Both say not hard to imagine Maria hurt; correction verified in previous continuous unit paired-ep01-ch08-1-111. No additional rows credited.
units.japanese: …それがどれほど真里亞を傷つけたのか、いくら俺でも想像に難しくない。

description: Kyrie argues that if Beatrice is what she claims to be, her status as Kinzo’s trusted confidant would require an honored reception. WH instead conditions that status on Beatrice really being her name. A genuine name alone cannot establish the status needed for the argument.
sourceReading: 自称する通り refers to her claimed identity and role, not merely whether the proper name is authentic. The immediately following trusted-confidant premise specifies the relevant content.

units.text: "If Beatrice was really her name, this person would definitely be the most honored of guests.  The most honored of confidants, trusted by Grandfather.  ...There's no way that Grandfather wouldn't give that kind of person a warm reception.  She would surely have been ushered into the mansion.  However, we haven't seen anyone."
units.note: Both restore claimed role/identity as condition for honored reception, rather than authenticity of proper name.
units.japanese: 「ベアトリーチェが自称する通りなら、その人物は間違いなく最高の賓客よ。お祖父さまが信頼する最高の腹心。…そんな人物を、お祖父さまが歓待しないわけがない。お屋敷に迎え入れないわけはないのよ。でも私たちは誰も見ていない。」

description: Battler summarizes that all eighteen have been treated as not being the lender. WH says the lender could not have been one of the eighteen, giving the preceding testimony-based conclusion the force of an impossibility.
sourceReading: 違うということになった reports the conclusion reached from the questioning; it does not establish inability or an independently verified exclusion.

units.text: This quickly starting to sound pretty creepy. Someone had lent Maria the umbrella and handed her the letter. This couldn't have been one of the 18. And yet, Beatrice was hidden amongst those 18. What was that person planning, hiding their true form and pretending to be Beatrice...?
units.note: MG explicitly says supposedly none did this. UP says all had been ruled out, reporting the preceding conclusion rather than saying physical inability. Both retain contradiction and nearby fragile-premise caveat; no WH impossibility wording survives.
units.japanese: １８人の全員が違うということになった。

description: Kyrie identifies finding out what sort of person Maria met as the key. WH asks whether Maria encountered someone, shifting the inquiry from identity or description to whether an encounter happened at all.
sourceReading: 何者に出会ったのか asks who or what person she encountered; it is not 誰かに出会ったのか, whether she encountered anyone.

units.text: "Of course, with that reasoning, all of us women would become the primary suspects.  ......Anyway, did Maria-chan encounter someone?  Learning the details of that question would be the best key to solving this riddle.
units.note: Both ask who Maria encountered, restoring identity question rather than whether any encounter occurred.
units.japanese: 「その論法になっちゃうと、私たち女性陣はみんな疑われちゃうことになるんだけどね。……とにかく、真里亞ちゃんが何者に出会ったのか。それの詳細を聞くことが、この謎を解く一番にしてもっとも身近な鍵なのよ。

description: Kyrie says she is uninterested in the inheritance division but excited by the mystery, then Battler marvels that she is tough enough to be excited despite enduring the money debate. WH makes her describe his disinterest and his curiosity, and makes him call the problem exciting and tough before saying adults can be horrible. The exchange loses his wry recognition of her resilience.
sourceReading: 関心ないけど and 知的好奇心が疼くわ characterize the speaker. 実にタフ refers to her ability to stay excited while dragged into exhausting discussion; 大人はすげぇや is his amazed reaction.

units.text: ......I know you don't care about all this back and forth on the distribution of the inheritance, but don't you think this rich western mansion mystery situation is exciting?  Who in the world is this person who gave Maria-chan the letter?  ...It makes your intellectual curiosity ache."
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese:
……遺産分配がどうのこうのって話には関心ないけど、こんな王道洋館ミステリーみたいなシチュエーションにはわくわくしちゃわない？　真里亞ちゃんに手紙を渡した人物は一体誰なのか。……知的好奇心が疼くわ。」
「うんざりするようなカネの話に付き合わされても、わくわくとは、実にタフなことだぜ…。大人はすげぇや。」

units.text: "Even though it's connected to that boring money problem, it's pretty exciting and a really tough problem...  Adults can be pretty horrible."
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.

「うんざりするようなカネの話に付き合わされても、わくわくとは、実にタフなことだぜ…。大人はすげぇや」

「……遺産分配がどうのこうのって話には関心ないけど、こんな王道洋館ミステリーみたいなシチュエーションにはわくわくしちゃわない？　真里亞ちゃんに手紙を渡した人物は一体誰なのか。……知的好奇心が疼くわ」

Who in the world is this person who gave Maria‐chan the letter? ......It makes my intellectual curiosity tingle."
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.

「……遺産分配がどうのこうのって話には関心ないけど、こんな王道洋館ミステリーみたいなシチュエーションにはわくわくしちゃわない？　真里亞ちゃんに手紙を渡した人物は一体誰なのか。……知的好奇心が疼くわ」

units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese:
「……遺産分配がどうのこうのって話には関心ないけど、こんな王道洋館ミステリーみたいなシチュエーションにはわくわくしちゃわない？　真里亞ちゃんに手紙を渡した人物は一体誰なのか。……知的好奇心が疼くわ」
「うんざりするようなカネの話に付き合わされても、わくわくとは、実にタフなことだぜ…。大人はすげぇや」

description: Battler says he had realized what Kyrie was doing, then explains that she had noticed his dejection and was trying to distract him. WH makes the first realization hers as well, omitting his explicit recognition before his explanation.
sourceReading: The narration’s 俺 remains the subject of でも気付いていた. The next sentence introduces Kyrie noticing his mood as the content of his realization.

units.text: I shrugged, surprised. ...But she had noticed it. She had noticed the dejection I had felt because I had overheard our parents' turbulent discussion, and was probably trying to turn my mood around. ...She had at least managed to make me feel good enough to hurl abuse.
units.note: Both restore Battler own realization followed by explanation of Kyrie noticing his dejection.
units.japanese: …でも気付いていた。

description: Eva and Rudolf bring Rosa into their coalition to overwhelm Krauss three to one and press their argument. WH says He was trying to push this crazy theory, continuing the previous Kinzo subject and making him the agent of the coalition’s tactical maneuver.
sourceReading: 絵羽と留弗夫は explicitly identifies Eva and Rudolf as the actors who draw Rosa in and press their argument.

units.text: He was trying to push this crazy theory so that Rosa, who had a weak position among the siblings because of her age, and Eva and Rudolf could join together, and with three against one, could overwhelm Krauss yet again. ......And by doing that, he gave them the power to resettle what had once been a nearly decided conflict.  They had now started repeatedly pressing Krauss to pay them a large amount of money... Using the condition that all of the siblings would guarantee Krauss the succession to the family head, talk about the advance payment which had once been denied was being brought up again.
units.note: MG continues Kinzo he as agent engineering Rosa joining coalition and enabling renewed conflict. UP names Eva and Rudolf as actors dragging Rosa in and pressing Krauss. Source preceding inference that Kinzo aids their position remains distinct.
units.japanese: 絵羽と留弗夫は、兄弟の中では年齢的に劣り立場の弱い楼座を抱き込み、３：１で再び蔵臼を圧倒して、滅茶苦茶な理論を押し通そうとしている。
candidates: trying to push this crazy theory

units.text: He was trying to push this crazy theory so that Rosa, who had a weak position among the siblings because of her age, would join with Eva and Rudolf. Then, with a three-to-one advantage, they'd be able overwhelm Krauss yet again and make their ridiculous theories get accepted by force. ...And by doing that, he gave them the power to resettle what had once been a nearly decided conflict. They had now started repeatedly pressing Krauss to pay them a large amount of money... Using the condition that all of the siblings would guarantee Krauss's position as the Successor, talk about advance payments was being brought up again despite having been rejected once.
units.note: MG continues Kinzo he as agent engineering Rosa joining coalition and enabling renewed conflict. UP names Eva and Rudolf as actors dragging Rosa in and pressing Krauss. Source preceding inference that Kinzo aids their position remains distinct.
units.japanese: 絵羽と留弗夫は、兄弟の中では年齢的に劣り立場の弱い楼座を抱き込み、３：１で再び蔵臼を圧倒して、滅茶苦茶な理論を押し通そうとしている。……そして、一度は大勢の決した戦いを仕切りなおし、多額の現金を支払わそうと何度も畳み掛けてきている…。絶対に家督を引き継げるというセーフティーを兄弟全員が保証することを条件に、一度は拒否した前払い金の話を蒸し返しているのだ。
candidates: trying to push this crazy theory

description: Krauss says this is something he is showing Natsuhi for the first time. WH says it is the first time he has shown it to anyone, adding an exclusion of every prior viewer.
sourceReading: 君に初めて見せる specifies the recipient Natsuhi; it does not quantify over everyone who could previously have seen the object.

units.text: "There's something I want to show you.  ......This is the first time I've shown it to anyone."
units.note: Both specify never shown you before, without excluding other prior viewers.
units.japanese: 「見せたい物がある。……君に初めて見せるものだ。」

description: Natsuhi asks whether she lacks even the standing to help her husband despite being his wife. WH makes her ask whether she is incapable of helping, shifting exclusion from a family role toward personal competence.
sourceReading: 資格 here concerns standing or entitlement, grounded in her immediately preceding contrast between exclusion from the crest and her position as wife.

units.text: Even so, ......are you saying I'm not capable of helping you...?!  Are you.........!!!?"
units.note: MG retains incapable, while UP qualified restores standing in immediate wife/crest contrast. Rows545–548 are prior-unit context, not additional coverage.
units.japanese: なのに、……私には力添えする資格もないのですか…？！　あなた………ッ！！！」

units.text: Even so, ...are you saying I'm not capable of helping you...?! Are you...?!!!"
units.note: MG retains incapable, while UP qualified restores standing in immediate wife/crest contrast. Rows545–548 are prior-unit context, not additional coverage.
units.japanese: 「なのに、……私には力添えする資格もないのですか…？！　あなた………ッ！！！」

description: Natsuhi’s impulse to rebuke Jessica is weak enough that she manages to stop herself from saying it. WH says the words lose strength and do not escape, removing her expressed successful restraint.
sourceReading: それを口に出すのを止まることができた assigns her the ability to stop the rebuke; the weakened impulse makes that possible.

units.text: Just like always, her words were rough and not at all like a girl's. ...Instinctively, words of rebuke rose to Natsuhi's throat. .........However, their strength gave out and they didn't escape her lips.
units.note: MG says words lose strength and do not escape; UP explicitly restores her ability to prevent utterance.
units.japanese: ………だが、その喉を突く力が弱かったお陰でそれを口に出すのを止まることができた。

units.text: Just like always, her words were rough and not at all like a girl's. ...Instinctively, words of rebuke rose to Natsuhi's throat. ......However, their strength gave out and they didn't escape her lips.
units.note: MG says words lose strength and do not escape; UP explicitly restores her ability to prevent utterance.
units.japanese:
いつも通りの、女の子らしくない悪い言葉遣い。…反射的に、叱り付ける言葉が喉を突く。
………だが、その喉を突く力が弱かったお陰でそれを口に出すのを止めることができた。

description: Jessica has not even the slightest remainder of her earlier contempt after seeing her mother’s exhausted face. WH says a tiny bit remains, reversing the zero-remainder statement.
sourceReading: わずかほども残っていなかった is emphatic negation of any remaining amount.

units.text: "...............Really......" Jessica was slightly disconcerted when she first spotted her mother's feebleness. Until just now, she had been filled with contempt for all of the parents, including her mother. ...But now, only a tiny bit of those feelings remained. ......All of it had been wiped out by her mother's completely exhausted face. In its place, the words that George had told her floated back up in her mind. The parents are doing their best in their own way. ...And since they were supporting their family, they couldn't afford to keep everything pleasant, and had a heavy responsibility to fight. ......Couldn't her mother have been standing around in this dimly lit hallway because no one had tried to understand that...?
units.note: Both explicitly say feelings completely gone before confirming exhausted face wiped them out.
units.japanese: …でも、そんな気持ちはもうわずかほども残っていなかった。

description: Battler says the daytime now seems unreal compared with the continuing storm. WH says it sounded like a lie earlier today, relocating the disbelief to earlier in the day and supplying an unstated claim that sounded false.
sourceReading: 今日の日中が嘘のよう compares the current situation with the earlier daytime, using 嘘のよう figuratively for the striking contrast.

units.text: "Oh well, it sounded like a lie earlier today."
units.note: Both explicitly compare current storm with earlier good/dry weather, preserving current disbelief rather than earlier false-sounding claim.
units.japanese: 「やれやれ、今日の日中が嘘のようだぜ。」
candidates: sounded like a lie earlier today

description: The narration describes lifting Maria and placing her onto George’s back. WH explicitly makes George pick her up and pull her over his own back, changing who performs the preparatory lift.
sourceReading: 譲治兄貴の背中に背負わせる is causative: Maria is placed on George’s back to be carried, with George the recipient of assistance rather than the named lifter.

units.text: Maria's body was much lighter than it looked. George-aniki picked her up and pulled her over his back.
units.note: MG narrator lifts Maria onto George back, restoring helper/recipient distinction. UP assigns lift to George himself. Japanese does not explicitly name helper; no independently proved unique helper inferred.
units.japanese: 担ぎ上げ、譲治兄貴の背中に背負わせる。

units.text:
Maria's body was much lighter than it looked.
George‐aniki picked her up and pulled her over his back.
units.note: MG narrator lifts Maria onto George back, restoring helper/recipient distinction. UP assigns lift to George himself. Japanese does not explicitly name helper; no independently proved unique helper inferred.
units.japanese:
真里亞の体は見た目よりずっと軽い。
担ぎ上げ、譲治兄貴の背中に背負わせる。

description: After Jessica tells the joking Battler to stop talking nonsense and enter, first-person narration describes folding the umbrella and entering while she nudges him. WH explicitly says she nudges Shannon, who folds her umbrella and enters.
sourceReading: The omitted subject continues the first-person arrival narration and follows Jessica’s response to Battler’s breast joke; no switch to Shannon is signaled.

units.text: After being nudged by Jessica, Shannon folded up her umbrella and went into the guesthouse.
units.note: MG retains first-person group entering after Jessica urging; UP explicitly assigns nudge and umbrella-folding to Shannon.
units.japanese: 朱志香に小突かれながら傘を畳み、ゲストハウスに入った。

description: Genji tells the servants to call him immediately if anything happens because tonight’s guests are special. WH instead says tonight is special for the Master, replacing the guests’ status with Kinzo’s personal occasion.
sourceReading: 今夜のお客様は explicitly makes tonight’s guests the subject of 特別だ.

units.text: For the Master, tonight is special."
units.note: Both say company tonight is special, restoring guests/company as referent rather than Master occasion. No specific special-guest identity inferred.
units.japanese: 今夜のお客様は、(特別だ/・・・)。」

description: Shannon refers to George eventually founding a company, and he explains what establishing one entails. WH repeatedly replaces founding with making a company prosperous, changing the stated entrepreneurial ambition into improvement of a company.
sourceReading: 会社を興す means establish or found a company, distinct from making one prosper.

units.text: "It's no surprise that someone who will soon make his company prosperous is so well prepared."
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese:
「さすが、やがては会社を興される方はしっかりしていますね。」
「…やっぱり会社を興すというのは大変だね。お金とかそういうのだけじゃないものがとても大事だって、父さんのところで勉強していてわかるよ。会社を興すということは、城を持ち、部下を率いるということ。

units.text: "...Well, making a company prosperous really is a tough job.  Money isn't the only thing that's important.  I learned that well by studying from my father.  Making a company prosperous is like having a castle and leading your subordinates.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
