description: The orphanage sends outstanding residents to its honorary director Kinzo for service; if recognized there, they can leave the orphanage to work for the family. WH has the orphanage offer graduates a life of service under his guidance, removing the specific preliminary placement with him and its progression into employment.
sourceReading: 金蔵の下へ ... 送っていた specifies destination, while 院生 means residents or pupils, not graduates. そこで ties recognition to that placement.

units.text: Under the guidance of the honorary director, Kinzo, the orphanage offered excellent graduates a chance to live a life of service. If they were accepted, they would be able to leave the orphanage and work as servants for the Ushiromiya family. ...This was considered to be the highest honor for a graduate.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese:
孤児院は名誉院長である金蔵の下へ、優秀な院生を奉仕活動に送っていた。
そこで認められれば、孤児院を出て右代宮家で使用人として仕えることができる。

units.text: Under the guidance of Kinzo, their honorary director, the orphanage offered members who excelled a chance for on-the-job serving experience. If their efforts met with Kinzo's approval, they'd be able to leave the orphanage and work as servants for the Ushiromiya family. ...This was considered to be the highest honor for those who lived in the orphanage.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese: そして、福音の家は名誉院長である金蔵の下へ、優秀な院生を奉仕活動に送っていた。そこで認められれば、施設を出て右代宮家で使用人として仕えることができる。…これが、院生の最大の名誉だとされていた。

units.text: Under the guidance of the honorary director, Kinzo, the Gospel House offered excellent students a chance to live a life of service. If they were accepted, they would be able to leave the institute and work as servants for the Ushiromiya family. ...This was considered to be the highest honor for a student.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese: そして、福音の家は名誉院長である金蔵の下へ、優秀な院生を奉仕活動に送っていた。そこで認められれば、施設を出て右代宮家で使用人として仕えることができる。…これが、院生の最大の名誉だとされていた。

description: The source distinguishes residents who are orphans from those disowned by living parents under special circumstances. WH says Or you could say they were all disowned, treating the second group as a restatement applicable to everyone.
sourceReading: さもなければ introduces the alternative category, not a paraphrase of being orphaned.

units.text: All of the graduates from the Fukuin House were orphans. Or you could say that they were all people who, through special circumstances, had been disowned by their parents. ......Because of this, the graduates had been taught to think of each other as their only family. That's why it seemed so natural to Kanon when he called Shannon his sister.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese:
福音の家の院生たちはみんな孤児。
さもなければ特殊な事情により両親に離縁されている者ばかり。

units.text: All of the members of the Fukuin House were orphans. At least, they were all people who had been separated from their parents under special circumstances. ......Because of this, the orphans had been taught to think of each other as their only family. That's why it seemed so natural to both of them when Kanon called Shannon his sister.
units.note: Canonical parent already linked explicitly in receipt findings rather than WH_outcomes. Preserve recorded nuanced dispositions and raw record; no duplicate new parent.
units.japanese:
福音の家の院生たちはみんな孤児。
さもなければ特殊な事情により両親に離縁されている者ばかり。……なので、院生たちは互いが唯一の家族であると教えられていた。だから嘉音が、紗音のことを姉と呼ぶのは、彼らにとってとても自然なことなのだ。

description: Shannon says she gets along with Milady and the other young servants. WH says the other servants’ children, inventing a different group of people in her account of her social life.
sourceReading: 使用人の子たち here refers to young people who are servants, consistent with the surrounding account of orphanage residents entering service.

units.text: ".........Y, ...yes, that's right.  ......I have nowhere to go outside of this mansion.  ......I have been getting along well with Milady and the other servants' children, too.........I am sometimes scolded by Madam, but, ......caring for the rose garden and cleaning the mansion is fun..."
units.note: Both restore other young servants, not servants offspring.
units.japanese: 「………そ、…そうですね。……私はこのお屋敷以外に行く当てもありませんし。……お嬢様とも、他の使用人の子たちとも仲良くやれてますし…。……奥様には時折お叱りを受けますけど、……薔薇の世話やお屋敷のお掃除も楽しいですし…。」

description: George says her life remains inside the shell called Shannon. WH retains only your shell, removing the explicit link between her service name and the restrictive identity he contrasts with Sayo.
sourceReading: 紗音という殻 names the shell; the earlier real-name address and subsequent correction from Shannon to Sayo sustain this identity contrast.

units.text: "So far, you have been living inside your shell.  Aren't you making the mistake of thinking that your life will always continue like this?"
units.note: Both explicitly restore shell called Shannon and surrounding Sayo name contrast.
units.japanese: 「君の人生は、まだ紗音という殻の中でしかないんだ。君は自分の人生が、この生活のままずっと続いていくと勘違いしてるんじゃないかな。」

description: George says he might be able to order her to wear it on her left hand, acknowledges she might obey, but wants this last act to come from Sayo’s will. WH says he probably cannot order it, changing restraint despite possible power into probable inability.
sourceReading: 命令することもできるかもしれない is affirmative possibility; it has no negation.

units.text: "I probably can't order you to wear it on your left hand.  You might be timid and dependent enough to actually obey that kind of an order.  ......But I want this last part to be given by Sayo's own will.  ...Understand?"
units.note: Both restore affirmative possibility of ordering left-hand wear while preserving his desire for Sayo own choice. Earlier cannot-order narration is protected source moral boundary rather than reason to negate explicit later admission.
units.japanese: 「君に、左手に付けて欲しいと命令することもできるかもしれない。君も、命令されればそれに従えるという臆病な甘えがあるかもしれない。……でも、最後のここだけは、君の、……紗代の意思でしてもらいたいんだ。…わかるね？」

description: Being slightly irritated by Gohda brings Shannon down from her earlier dreamy excitement. WH says Because it had come fairly suddenly, changing the emotional cause into the suddenness of an unspecified event.
sourceReading: カチンと来た is getting irritated or offended, not something arriving suddenly. The preceding imposed work explains what irritates her.

units.text: For the time being, as a sign of respect for her elder, Shannon bowed her head, and she left the room to patrol the mansion. Because it had come fairly suddenly, the airy sensation that she had felt a little while ago had lessened a bit.
units.note: Both restore irritation as the cause of calming, rather than suddenness.
units.japanese: ちょっとカチンと来たお陰で、さっきまでのふわふわした感覚が、少し治まることができたのだった。
candidates: Because it had come fairly suddenly

description: Shannon remembers Kanon saying he saw the butterfly and that she did not believe him, treating it as a mistaken sighting, after which he sulked. WH retains only that he reported seeing it, omitting her prior skeptical response and his reaction.
sourceReading: 私は ... 信じてあげなくて explicitly identifies her disbelief; 不貞腐れていた supplies the resulting sulky reaction.

units.text: ...Come to think of it, didn't Kanon-kun once say that he had seen it with his own eyes......? .........Could it possibly... really............? The roar of the thunder gave no answer...
units.note: Both restore Shannon disbelief and Kanon sulking; current speculation remains uncertain.
units.japanese:
……そう言えば、嘉音くんが前に見たことがあるなんて言ってたっけ……？
私は何かの見間違いだろうと信じてあげなくて、不貞腐れていたけど…。

description: Kanon follows a practiced route opening curtains throughout the mansion. WH says he opens one window after another, adding an action on the windows themselves during the morning after the night-time locking routine.
sourceReading: カーテン is curtains. Opening them admits light without opening or unlocking the windows.

units.text: The two of them split up and began opening the curtains throughout the mansion. ...If the curtains remained closed, the inside of the mansion would still be dim, as if it hadn't managed to escape the previous night, and they wouldn't be able to clean. Kanon, in a well rehearsed procedure, went around the mansion opening one window after another without having to retrace his steps once. Even with this horrible weather, by opening the curtains, it began to feel just a little bit like morning.
units.note: MG specifies opening curtains for one window after another; UP explicitly opens windows. Adjacent curtain references limit the retained error exactly as in the WH parent.
units.japanese: 嘉音は慣れた手順で、屋敷内をうまく一筆書きで描けるように回りながら、次々にカーテンを開けていく。

units.text: The two of them split up and began opening the curtains throughout the mansion. ...If the curtains remained closed, the inside of the mansion would be unable to shake off its gloom, as if it hadn't yet managed to escape the previous night. Kanon, following a well versed procedure, went around the mansion opening one window after another without having to retrace his steps once. Even with this horrible weather, by opening the curtains, it began to feel just a little bit like morning.
units.note: MG specifies opening curtains for one window after another; UP explicitly opens windows. Adjacent curtain references limit the retained error exactly as in the WH parent.
units.japanese: 二人は手分けして屋敷内のカーテンを開けることにした。…カーテンに閉ざされたままでは、屋敷の中は未だ昨夜から抜け出せていないかのような薄暗闇を掃えない。嘉音は慣れた手順で、屋敷内をうまく一筆書きで描けるように回りながら、次々にカーテンを開けていく。このようなひどい天気であっても、カーテンを開けることによって、少しは朝の気配を迎え入れることができるのだった。

description: The kitchen is dim and even its ventilation fan is not running. WH says there is no fan for ventilation, much less curtains to open, changing inactive equipment into absent equipment.
sourceReading: 換気扇すら回っていない negates the fan running, not its existence. The darkness and cold convey that breakfast work has not begun.

units.text: He tried to greet Gohda, who he had thought would be preparing the meal inside the kitchen, but Gohda was nowhere to be seen. The kitchen was darkly lit, and there was no fan for ventilation, much less curtains to be opened. Since it was still cold without a hint of a fire, it was obvious that no preparations for breakfast were taking place.
units.note: Both now describe the existing fan as not running, preserving inactive kitchen equipment.
units.japanese: 厨房は薄暗く、カーテンどころか換気扇すら回っていない。
candidates: fan for ventilation, much less curtains

description: Natsuhi puts her hand to her forehead and shakes her head at the breakfast failure. WH says she smacks her head and nods distractedly, changing both gestures.
sourceReading: 額に手を当て is placing a hand on the forehead; 首を振った is shaking her head in this dismayed context.

units.text: Natsuhi was indignant. To her, this was a much bigger problem than the phones not working. And despite that, this piece of information was the part that had been postponed. Why did everything go well most of the time, and then come to something like this when the relatives were visiting... Natsuhi smacked her head with her hand and nodded distractedly.
units.note: Both restore hand to forehead and shaking head; neither invents striking or nodding.
units.japanese: 夏妃は額に手を当て、ふるふると首を振った。

description: The marks resemble someone having put dark red liquid on their fingers and clawed around the knob. WH says liquid is stuck to her fingers, introducing an observation about Natsuhi herself rather than keeping the fingers inside the imagined reconstruction of the marks.
sourceReading: 赤黒い液体を指につけて ... 掻き毟ったような describes what the unpleasant marks look like. The next sentence explicitly imagines someone’s blood-soaked hands and a staged prank.

units.text: Natsuhi exited into the hall and turned around for a second to close the door to her room. The unpleasant "thing" that she saw there silenced her completely. ...There was a dark red liquid stuck to her fingers and some unpleasant marks around the doorknob that looked as though something had been tearing at it. It was as though someone had soaked both of their hands in blood and groped at the door and the knob..., like someone had wanted to stage something like that and left this mark as an awful prank.
units.note: Both keep liquid-coated fingers inside hypothetical reconstruction of marks; neither reports liquid on Natsuhi fingers.
units.japanese: …それは、赤黒い液体を指につけてドアノブの辺りを掻き毟ったような、不快なもの。

description: Natsuhi imagines the missing participants going out in a group to cool their heads. WH says they had all gone off on their own walks, suggesting independent walks rather than the collective excursion in her theory.
sourceReading: ぞろぞろと describes people moving in a group or stream; the next source line imagines Gohda accompanying them to provide assistance.

units.text: When she had heard that Gohda alone was missing, she had thought that he might have slept in or was loafing around somewhere, but once she heard that several of the relatives were also missing, her optimistic way of thinking began to change. Could last night's family conference have continued all night and still be going on? It was also imaginable that they had wanted to cool off their heads after being in that stuffy room, and had all gone off on their own walks through the rain. ...The part about 'cooling off their heads' really sounded like something Krauss would like to say. Probably, Gohda had been called to go with them to aid them with something.
units.note: MG retains walks on their own; UP explicitly restores group walk. Gohda accompaniment and conjectural frame limit the MG error.
units.japanese: それで、部屋の空気も澱んできたので、頭を冷やそう等ということになり、この雨の中、ぞろぞろと散歩に出ている可能性も考えられた。
candidates: gone off on their own walks

units.text: When she'd heard that Gohda alone was missing, she'd assumed he had slept in or was loafing around somewhere. However, now that she'd learned that several of the relatives were also nowhere to be seen, she began to take a slightly more optimistic view. Could last night's family conference have continued all night, up until the present moment? If so, they might have wanted to cool their heads after being shut in a stuffy room, going out for walks on their own through the rain. ...The part about "cooling their heads" really sounded like something Krauss would say. Gohda had probably been summoned to accompany them and aid them in some way.
units.note: MG retains walks on their own; UP explicitly restores group walk. Gohda accompaniment and conjectural frame limit the MG error.
units.japanese: 郷田ひとりだけ姿が見えないと聞いた時は、寝坊したのか、どこかで油を売っているのかと思ったが、親族たちも含めての不在だということになると、もう少し楽観的な考え方に変わって来る。昨夜の親族会議は、下手をすると徹夜となり未だに続いているのではないか。それで、部屋の空気も澱んできたので、頭を冷やそう等ということになり、この雨の中、ぞろぞろと散歩に出ている可能性も考えられた。…頭を冷やそう、等という辺りは、実に蔵臼が好んで言いそうな言葉だった。多分、郷田も何かの世話に呼ばれ同行しているのだろう。

description: Natsuhi leaves quickly without answering, clacking her heels loudly. WH supplies a forceful turn on her heels instead, replacing the audible angry departure with a different gesture.
sourceReading: 踵を強く打ち鳴らしながら describes making her heels sound as she walks, not pivoting on them.

units.text: Natsuhi, without answering, forcefully spun around on her heels and quickly left that place.
units.note: MG still supplies forceful spin; UP restores loud clacking heels during swift departure.
units.japanese: 夏妃は返事をせず、踵を強く打ち鳴らしながら足早にその場を去るのだった。

units.text: Without answering, Natsuhi forcefully spun around on her heels and quickly left that place.
units.note: MG still supplies forceful spin; UP restores loud clacking heels during swift departure.
units.japanese: 夏妃は返事をせず、踵を強く打ち鳴らしながら足早にその場を去るのだった。

description: Maria considers what to do while the older cousins sleep. WH says she thinks about what had happened, converting a practical decision about her next action into reconstruction of past events.
sourceReading: どうしたものか is deliberation over what one should do, not a question of what happened.

units.text: As she rubbed her sleepy eyes and looked around, the loud snoring coming from the three cousins continued. ...For a while, Maria had to think about what had happened. After that, she realized that her mother was not with her and quickly got lonely. Maria left the cousins' room, trying to head to the room that had been arranged for her and her mother. Paying no heed to the three who were sleeping soundly, she made a loud banging sound.
units.note: Both retain what had happened for practical deliberation over what to do.
units.japanese: …真里亞はしばらくの間、どうしたものかと思案しなければならなかった。

units.text: As she rubbed her sleepy eyes and looked around, she was met with the loud snoring of the other three cousins. ...For a while, Maria had to think about what had happened. After that, she realized that her mother wasn't with her, and she quickly got lonely. Maria left the cousins' room, trying to head to the room that had been arranged for her and her mother. Paying no heed to the three who were sleeping soundly, she slammed the door shut.
units.note: Both retain what had happened for practical deliberation over what to do.
units.japanese: 寝惚け眼を擦りながら見渡せば、３人のいとこたちが累々と高いびき。…真里亞はしばらくの間、どうしたものかと思案しなければならなかった。それから、自分が母親と一緒でないことに気付いて急に心細くなる。真里亞は、自分たち親子が泊まることになっていた部屋へ行こうと、いとこ部屋を出て行く。熟睡する３人などお構いなしに、バタンと大きな音を立てて。

units.text: As she rubbed her sleepy eyes and looked around, the loud snoring coming from the three cousins continued. ...For a while, Maria had to think about what had happened. After that, she realized that her mother was not with her, and quickly got lonely. Maria left the cousins' room, trying to head to the room that had been arranged for her and her mother. Paying no heed to the three who were sleeping soundly, she made a loud slamming sound on the way out.
units.note: Both retain what had happened for practical deliberation over what to do.
units.japanese: 寝惚け眼を擦りながら見渡せば、３人のいとこたちが累々と高いびき。…真里亞はしばらくの間、どうしたものかと思案しなければならなかった。それから、自分が母親と一緒でないことに気付いて急に心細くなる。真里亞は、自分たち親子が泊まることになっていた部屋へ行こうと、いとこ部屋を出て行く。熟睡する３人などお構いなしに、バタンと大きな音を立てて。

description: Battler says that while they remain here they have no way to know Rosa’s whereabouts. WH says as long as Rosa is not here they cannot know, shifting the limiting circumstance from their remaining in the cousins’ room to her absence.
sourceReading: ここにいる以上 takes the present group as the subject: being here, away from the mansion and the information available there.

units.text: Maria kept groaning 'uu-uu-' and looking unhappy. It seemed like she wasn't simply lonely because she couldn't find her mother, but actually unhappy because her mother wasn't in the place Maria thought she was and this made her feel like she'd been tricked. She might have been satisfied just to hear where her mother was, but unfortunately, as long as Rosa oba-san wasn't here, we had no way of knowing where she was.
units.note: MG no longer uses the exact erroneous as-long-as-Rosa-is-absent condition, but still omits that their remaining here limits knowledge, replacing it with except that she was not here. Surviving scope is the lost location-based limitation only. UP explicitly restores as long as we were here.
units.japanese: 今どこにいると一言教えてあげられればそれで納得してくれるのかもしれないが、生憎、楼座叔母さんがどこにいるのか、ここにいる以上わかりようもなかった。

units.text: Maria kept groaning "uu-uu-" and looking unhappy. She didn't exactly seem lonely because her mother wasn't around. It was more like she was irritated and thrown off balance because her mother wasn't where she'd expected. If we could just tell her where her mother was, that alone would probably calm her down. But, unfortunately, we had no way of knowing where Aunt Rosa was, except that she wasn't here.
units.note: MG no longer uses the exact erroneous as-long-as-Rosa-is-absent condition, but still omits that their remaining here limits knowledge, replacing it with except that she was not here. Surviving scope is the lost location-based limitation only. UP explicitly restores as long as we were here.
units.japanese:
真里亞は不愉快そうに、うーうー唸り続ける。
母の姿が見えなくて寂しいというよりは、いると思っていた場所にいなかったので、肩透かしが不愉快だったという風に見えた。今どこにいると一言教えてあげられればそれで納得してくれるのかもしれないが、生憎、楼座叔母さんがどこにいるのか、ここにいる以上わかりようもなかった。

description: Kinzo asks whether she is telling him to go downstairs and join the discussion of dividing his estate. WH first commands her to Go back downstairs, then asks about his joining, splitting a single rhetorical objection into a dismissal of her plus a question.
sourceReading: 下に降りて connects to 議論に加われというのか: go down and join, is that what you are telling me? It describes the proposed action for Kinzo.

units.text: ".........Go back downstairs.  Are you asking me to join in on the discussion of how they chew my inheritance to bits after I die?  How foolish.
units.note: MG retains command Go back downstairs followed by rhetorical question; UP connects going downstairs and joining as actions Kinzo is being asked to take.
units.japanese: 「………下に降りて。私の死後、遺産をどのように食い千切るのかを決める議論に加われというのか。馬鹿らしい。

units.text: "......Go back downstairs. Are you asking me to join in as they discuss how to chew up my inheritance after I die? How foolish.
units.note: MG retains command Go back downstairs followed by rhetorical question; UP connects going downstairs and joining as actions Kinzo is being asked to take.
units.japanese: 「………下に降りて。私の死後、遺産をどのように食い千切るのかを決める議論に加われというのか。馬鹿らしい」

description: Natsuhi offers tea and Eva defensively declines. WH says that would be fine, making her accept instead.
sourceReading: 別に結構よ in response to the offer, with her flustered resistance and continuing anger, is a no-thanks refusal.

units.text: "......Th, ...that would be fine."
units.note: MG accepts with That would be fine; UP I will be fine declines in the resistant context.
units.japanese: 「……べ、…別に結構よ。」

units.text: "......Th-That would be fine."
units.note: MG accepts with That would be fine; UP I will be fine declines in the resistant context.
units.japanese: 「……べ、…別に結構よ」

description: Natsuhi thinks that if the missing people have eaten nothing since last night, they should now be hungry. WH asserts they have eaten nothing since last night, then predicts hunger, removing the condition on an unverified part of her explanation.
sourceReading: 昨夜から何も口にしていないなら is conditional. She has no reported knowledge of their meals during the period of absence.

units.text: She didn't know where they were, but they had to be somewhere on this island. They hadn't put anything in their mouths since last night, so their stomachs must be growling about now. They would surely saunter in any time now. ...Natsuhi was already dumbfounded, and she had begun to think that there was no urgent need to find them right then.
units.note: Both assert no food since last night instead of retaining source if; optimistic Natsuhi viewpoint limits authority.
units.japanese: 昨夜から何も口にしていないなら、今頃お腹が鳴り出している頃だ。

units.text: She didn't know where they were, but they had to be somewhere on this island. They hadn't had a thing to eat since the previous night, so their stomachs must be growling about now. They'd probably come plodding back of their own accord before long. ...By now, Natsuhi was thoroughly exasperated and started to feel that there was no reason for them to go out of their way and search.
units.note: Both assert no food since last night instead of retaining source if; optimistic Natsuhi viewpoint limits authority.
units.japanese:
どこにいるか知らないが、どうせこの島のどこかにいる。
昨夜から何も口にしていないなら、今頃お腹が鳴り出している頃だ。向こうからのこのこと帰ってくるに違いない。…もう夏妃は呆れ果て、無理に彼らを探し出す必要性はないと考えるようになっていた。

units.text:
She didn't know where they were, but they had to be somewhere on this island.
They hadn't put anything in their mouths since last night, so their stomachs must be growling about now. They would surely saunter in any time now. ...Natsuhi was already dumbfounded, and she had begun to think that there was no urgent need to find them right then.
units.note: Both assert no food since last night instead of retaining source if; optimistic Natsuhi viewpoint limits authority.
units.japanese:
どこにいるか知らないが、どうせこの島のどこかにいる。
昨夜から何も口にしていないなら、今頃お腹が鳴り出している頃だ。向こうからのこのこと帰ってくるに違いない。…もう夏妃は呆れ果て、無理に彼らを探し出す必要性はないと考えるようになっていた。

description: Eva and Hideyoshi approach after noticing the exchange; narration suggests they have noticed something unusual about Kanon’s manner. WH instead says Maybe Kanon had noticed something that looked strange, replacing their observation of him with his observation of an object.
sourceReading: 嘉音の ... 様子のおかしいところ is the object noticed; the observers continue to be Eva and Hideyoshi from the previous sentence.

units.text: Kanon sounded evasive. He still didn't know where they were, but maybe he had found something with some relation to that. When Eva and Hideyoshi noticed this exchange of words, they came over. Maybe Kanon had noticed something that looked strange.
units.note: Both restore Eva and Hideyoshi noticing Kanon strange behavior.
units.japanese: 嘉音の、どこか様子のおかしいところに気付いているのだろう。
candidates: Maybe Kanon had noticed something that looked strange

description: Kanon says he visited yesterday before the rain began and saw no markings. WH specifies last night before the rain, adding a nighttime placement to the prior clear-shutter observation.
sourceReading: 昨日 is yesterday, with the explicit relative anchor before the rain began. It does not specify night.

units.text: "......Last night, I came here before it started raining, but there was nothing drawn here at that time."
units.note: Both retain Last night rather than yesterday; before rain survives. No independently proven marking time inferred.
units.japanese: 「……昨日、雨が降り出す前にここに来ましたが、その時には何も書かれてませんでした。」

units.text: "......Last night, I came here before it started raining, and there was nothing drawn here at that time."
units.note: Both retain Last night rather than yesterday; before rain survives. No independently proven marking time inferred.
units.japanese: 「……昨日、雨が降り出す前にここに来ましたが、その時には何も書かれてませんでした」

description: The description ends by saying the stylish makeup Rudolf paid unusually close attention to despite being a man is now useless. WH makes it makeup that I thoughtlessly worried about, assigning the concern to Battler and reversing the quality of attention.
sourceReading: 男のくせにやたら気遣ってた describes the man whose ruined face is being contemplated, with unusually great care rather than thoughtlessness. The subsequent cry addresses his father.

units.text: Their faces were smashed, forced into an expression that a normal person couldn't make even after death.  ...I couldn't tell where the eyes or the noses were, but I could find their mouths...because they were gaping wide, the ridges of their teeth exposed!  But their front teeth were missing, and even the cheek that should have covered that was all torn up and exposed!  Even as a man, the stylish makeup that I thoughtlessly worried about was all useless...!!
units.note: MG addresses you and UP says he, both restoring Rudolf unusually great attention rather than Battler thoughtless concern.
units.japanese: 顔面は粉砕され、真っ当な人間なら例え死後でも浮かべられないような表情を作らされている。…目の位置も鼻の位置もわからねぇ、口はわかるぜ、歯茎が剥き出しになってて口をぽっかりと開けているから！　でも、前歯は飛んでるし、そもそもそれを覆う頬っぺただってぐちゃぐちゃで剥き出しで！　男のくせにやたら気遣ってたお洒落化粧も何の役にも立っちゃいない…！！

description: George curses himself because only his worst imaginings always come true. WH says he curses himself for always imagining the worst, shifting the reason from the accuracy of his dread to his tendency to think pessimistically.
sourceReading: 当たってしまう says the worst conjecture proves correct, not merely that he makes it.

units.text: The body that Hideyoshi was looking down on now was hidden in the shadow of a mountain of random objects, in a blind spot to George, who stood by the entrance. ...So George couldn't tell , ...whose body it was...... ...Therefore, .........George cursed himself. He cursed himself for always imagining the worst...!
units.note: Both explicitly restore worst imaginings proving right, not simply his habit of imagining the worst.
units.japanese: いつも……、最悪の想像だけは当たってしまう我が身を呪う…！
candidates: himself for always imagining the worst

description: Hideyoshi interrupts Eva’s suspicion about George and says it does not matter who made Shannon the promise. WH asks Who could possibly be in the wrong here, replacing a refusal to discuss the giver’s identity with an assertion or question about blame.
sourceReading: それが誰かは問題とちゃう says who that person is is not the issue. The next speech says he does not know who gave the ring, maintaining his tactful refusal to name George.

units.text: "Eva!!  Right now that doesn't matter!!  A man made a lifelong promise to Shannon-chan...!  A man promised her happiness for life...  Who could possibly be in the wrong here!?
units.note: Both restore irrelevance of giver identity rather than fault. His deliberate refusal to name giver remains.
units.japanese: 「絵羽ッ！！　今はそんなん関係ないで！！　紗音ちゃんは男に将来を約束されとったんや…！　一生を幸せにしちゃると男に言わせたんや…。それが誰かは問題とちゃうで！

description: Battler says crying hard has calmed him. WH says he will calm down once he has cried his share, leaving the recovery prospective instead of achieved.
sourceReading: 落ち着いた is completed past calm; the crying condition here describes the experience that produced it.

units.text: ".....................I'm sorry.  ...I'll calm down once I've cried my share...  You bastard, Dad, ...I bet you're laughing at me, always talking shit about you, then crying like a baby just 'cause you died.
units.note: Both restore crying already having calmed Battler; recovery remains partial enough to fake smile.
units.japanese: 「……………………すまねぇな。…がっつり泣いたら落ち着いたぜ…。親父の野郎、…普段はクソクソ言ってるくせに、ちょっと死んじまったくらいでピーピー泣くんじゃねーぜって笑ってやがらぁ。

description: Natsuhi watches the children leave before instructing Genji to contact police. WH says she orders him to see that they return, adding a monitoring instruction and losing her preceding observation.
sourceReading: 見届けてから sequences her observation before the quoted police instruction.

units.text: Natsuhi ordered Genji to see that the children returned.
units.note: Both restore Natsuhi observing children departure before police instruction, without adding Genji monitoring order.
units.japanese: 子どもたちが帰っていくのを見届けてから、夏妃は源次に指示する。

description: Eva says Kanon handled the key normally and used it to open the shutter, contaminating possible fingerprints. WH says he usually has it and uses it, inventing recurrent custody and use.
sourceReading: 普通に modifies ordinary handling, and 使用しちゃった is a completed action on this occasion.

units.text: "......I am sure it will be worthwhile to submit it to the police as evidence, but Kanon-kun usually has it, and uses it to open this.  It will probably also have Kanon's fingerprints on it.  Also, that key was handed to Genji just now, and he took it with his bare hands.  ...It doesn't look like it will be very useful as evidence."
units.note: MG restores this occasion for opening but retains usually has it, so unsupported habitual possession survives; habitual use is corrected. UP restores ordinary handling and completed use only.
units.japanese: 「……警察に証拠として提出する価値はあるでしょうけど、嘉音くんが普通に持って、ここを開けるのに使用しちゃったわ。多分、嘉音くんの指紋も付着しちゃってるわよ。そしてその鍵はさっき、源次さんに手渡され、源次さんも素手で受け取ってる。…大した証拠にはなりそうにないわねぇ。」

units.text: "......I'm sure it'll be worth submitting it to the police as evidence, but Kanon-kun usually has it, and he used it to unlock the shed just now. It'll probably have Kanon's fingerprints on it.
units.note: MG restores this occasion for opening but retains usually has it, so unsupported habitual possession survives; habitual use is corrected. UP restores ordinary handling and completed use only.
units.japanese:
「……警察に証拠として提出する価値はあるでしょうけど、嘉音くんが普通に持って、ここを開けるのに使用しちゃったわ。多分、嘉音くんの指紋も付着しちゃってるわよ」
「そしてその鍵はさっき、源次さんに手渡され、源次さんも素手で受け取ってる。…大した証拠にはなりそうにないわねぇ」

units.text: Also, that key was handed to Genji-san just now, and he took it with his bare hands. ...It doesn't look like it'll be very useful as evidence."
units.note: MG restores this occasion for opening but retains usually has it, so unsupported habitual possession survives; habitual use is corrected. UP restores ordinary handling and completed use only.
units.japanese:
「……警察に証拠として提出する価値はあるでしょうけど、嘉音くんが普通に持って、ここを開けるのに使用しちゃったわ。多分、嘉音くんの指紋も付着しちゃってるわよ」
「そしてその鍵はさっき、源次さんに手渡され、源次さんも素手で受け取ってる。…大した証拠にはなりそうにないわねぇ」

description: Hideyoshi sometimes turns his horrified mutterings into questions and directs them at Nanjo. WH says he tried to ask a question and bumped into Nanjo, converting figurative delivery of the questions into a bodily collision.
sourceReading: 問い掛けの形に変えて南條にぶつける means putting those reactions to Nanjo as questions.

units.text: Hideyoshi, fidgeting as he remembered that horrible scene, kept muttering, 'Unbelievable.  That can't be somethin' of this world, it's the work of the devil.' Every once in a while, he tried to ask a question and bumped into Nanjo, but Nanjo, in a calm doctor-like manner, kept repeating that nothing could be understood by only glancing at the scene, and that until the police arrived, he wouldn't know anything.
units.note: Both preserve questions directed at Nanjo, without bodily collision.
units.japanese: それらを時々、問い掛けの形に変えて南條にぶつけていたが、
candidates: tried to ask a question and bumped into Nanjo

description: George asks when his father and companions withdrew from the meeting to rest. WH asks when they finished the meeting and went to sleep, obscuring the distinction between their departure and the end of the gathering.
sourceReading: 打ち合わせを抜けて marks leaving an ongoing meeting; it does not state the meeting ended.

units.text: "Dad, when did all of you finish their meeting and go to sleep......?"
units.note: Both restore father and mother withdrawing rather than meeting ending; remaining participants not assigned same departure.
units.japanese: 「父さんたちが打ち合わせを抜けて休んだのは何時だっけ……？」

description: Jessica recalls her father raising the subject of her grades. WH makes this her talking to her parents about grades, changing both agency and the named parent.
sourceReading: 親父に学校の成績の話をされたり is passive: her father talked to her about her grades.

units.text: "......Really?  Great for you...  I feel like my head's gonna explode.........This is the dining hall, right?  This is where every day I would eat, complain about school, complain about homework, ......talk to my parents about my grades, ......that's what this place is to me......"
units.note: Both restore singular Dad but retain Jessica talking to Dad about grades rather than father raising grades with her. Surviving scope is agency only, not parent identity.
units.japanese:
「……そうかよ、良かったな…。私は頭がどうにかなっちまいそうだぜ…。……ここは食堂だぜ？　私は毎日ここで食事をして、学校のことをぼやいたり、宿題のことをぼやいたり、……親父に学校の成績の話をされたり、
……そういうところなんだぜ……？」

units.text: "......Really? Good for you... I feel like my head's gonna explode... ...This is the dining hall, right? Every day, this is where I'd eat, complain about school, complain about homework, ...talk to my Dad about my grades... ...That's what this place is to me..."
units.note: Both restore singular Dad but retain Jessica talking to Dad about grades rather than father raising grades with her. Surviving scope is agency only, not parent identity.
units.japanese: 「……そうかよ、良かったな…。私は頭がどうにかなっちまいそうだぜ…。……ここは食堂だぜ？　私は毎日ここで食事をして、学校のことをぼやいたり、宿題のことをぼやいたり、……親父に学校の成績の話をされたり、……そういうところなんだぜ……？」

units.text: "......Really? Great for you... I feel like my head's gonna friggin' explode... ......This is the dining hall, you know? This is where every day I would eat, complain about school, complain about homework, ......talk to Dad about my grades, ......that's what this place is to me......"
units.note: Both restore singular Dad but retain Jessica talking to Dad about grades rather than father raising grades with her. Surviving scope is agency only, not parent identity.
units.japanese: 「……そうかよ、良かったな…。私は頭がどうにかなっちまいそうだぜ…。……ここは食堂だぜ？　私は毎日ここで食事をして、学校のことをぼやいたり、宿題のことをぼやいたり、……親父に学校の成績の話をされたり、……そういうところなんだぜ……？」

description: The Japanese singles out the dining hall as one of the comforting places within the mansion. WH describes the mansion interior as the one place where they could feel secure.
sourceReading: この屋敷の中でも心落ち着く場所のひとつ refers to the dining hall as one among comforting places in the mansion.

units.text: Nanjo spoke while looking at everyone's pale faces. ......Even though that horrible scene in the storehouse had felt like something not of this world, at least then we had been able to leave, to cut ourselves off from that place and run away.  Everyone had shared in that feeling. ......However, this dining hall was different. It was in the main wing of the mansion, ...and as Jessica had said, the inside of the mansion was supposed to be the one place where we could feel secure.  It was the same place that all of the relatives had eaten lunch and dinner yesterday. ......The shock of seeing this place smeared with blood reminded us of that horrible spectacle in the storehouse, and forced us to accept that we really hadn't been able to run away from the scene of that tragedy......
units.note: Both restore dining hall as one comforting place within mansion rather than whole mansion as unique refuge.
units.japanese: 母屋である屋敷の中にあり、…そして朱志香の言う通り、この屋敷の中でも心落ち着く場所のひとつだったはずだ。昨日、親類みんなでランチやディナーを楽しんだ場所だ。

description: Maria asks whether someone has died and speaks in a genuinely puzzled or blank manner. WH asks who died and labels her delivery completely calm, replacing uncertainty and lack of comprehension with an identity question and composure.
sourceReading: 誰か死んじゃったの asks whether someone died; きょとん describes her uncomprehending reaction.

units.text: The way she spoke was completely calm. ...Just as though she was talking about someone who had appeared on a television drama, as though it was someone else's problem. ...Jessica probably didn't like that. ......As though trying to say 'Can't you tell just by looking at me, overwhelmed with grief!', she flared up against Maria.
units.note: Both restore Did someone die question. Both still call her delivery completely calm rather than genuinely puzzled or blank; surviving scope is state description only.
units.japanese:
「………うー。…朱志香お姉ちゃん。誰か死んじゃったの？」
本当にきょとんとした言い方。

units.text: ".........Uu-. ...Jessica onee-chan, did someone die?"
units.note: Both restore Did someone die question. Both still call her delivery completely calm rather than genuinely puzzled or blank; surviving scope is state description only.
units.japanese:
「………うー。…朱志香お姉ちゃん。誰か死んじゃったの？」
本当にきょとんとした言い方。…まるでテレビドラマの登場人物の話をしているように他人事だった。…それが朱志香には気に入らなかったのだろう。……これほど悲しみに暮れる自分を見てそれが理解できないのかと言わんばかりに、真里亞に食って掛かる。

units.text: The way she spoke was completely calm. ...Just as though she was talking about someone who had appeared on a television drama, as though it was someone else's problem. ...Jessica probably didn't like that. ...As though trying to say "Can't you tell just by looking at me, overwhelmed with grief?!", she flared up at Maria.
units.note: Both restore Did someone die question. Both still call her delivery completely calm rather than genuinely puzzled or blank; surviving scope is state description only.
units.japanese:
「………うー。…朱志香お姉ちゃん。誰か死んじゃったの？」
本当にきょとんとした言い方。…まるでテレビドラマの登場人物の話をしているように他人事だった。…それが朱志香には気に入らなかったのだろう。……これほど悲しみに暮れる自分を見てそれが理解できないのかと言わんばかりに、真里亞に食って掛かる。

units.text: ".........Uu. ...Jessica onee‐chan. Did someone die?"
units.note: Both restore Did someone die question. Both still call her delivery completely calm rather than genuinely puzzled or blank; surviving scope is state description only.
units.japanese:
「………うー。…朱志香お姉ちゃん。誰か死んじゃったの？」
本当にきょとんとした言い方。…まるでテレビドラマの登場人物の話をしているように他人事だった。…それが朱志香には気に入らなかったのだろう。……これほど悲しみに暮れる自分を見てそれが理解できないのかと言わんばかりに、真里亞に食って掛かる。

units.text: The way she spoke was completely calm. ...Just as though she was talking about characters in a TV drama—as though it didn't affect her at all. ...Jessica probably didn't like that. ......As though trying to say "can't you tell just by looking at me, overwhelmed with grief!", she flared up against Maria.
units.note: Both restore Did someone die question. Both still call her delivery completely calm rather than genuinely puzzled or blank; surviving scope is state description only.
units.japanese:
「………うー。…朱志香お姉ちゃん。誰か死んじゃったの？」
本当にきょとんとした言い方。…まるでテレビドラマの登場人物の話をしているように他人事だった。…それが朱志香には気に入らなかったのだろう。……これほど悲しみに暮れる自分を見てそれが理解できないのかと言わんばかりに、真里亞に食って掛かる。

description: WH changes the unusual appearance of Western vegetables cooked in Japanese style into an unpleasant color caused by cooking.
sourceReading: 違和感のある彩り describes incongruous colors or presentation; 珍しい means unusual, not tasteful.

units.text: Kumasawa-san had taken the tasteful western vegetables, ones that Gohda-san had probably ordered to make the meals feel more elaborate, and cooked them in a Japanese style, making them turn an unpleasant color. As to what Gohda-san had been planning to cook with those ingredients...right then I couldn't even imagine it. If I did think about it, I would be reminded of the way Gohda-san had died, and the inside of my mouth would be filled with a sour taste... For the time being, everyone pretended to eat, but no one was actually going to move their chopsticks.
units.note: Both retain unpleasant color caused by Japanese-style cooking rather than unfamiliar combination of presentation.
units.japanese: 郷田さんが、凝りに凝った料理のために取り寄せただろう珍しい西洋野菜は、熊沢さんによって、和風に料理され、違和感のある彩りとなっていた。

units.text: Kumasawa-san had taken some unusual Western vegetables, ones that Gohda-san had probably ordered for his ultra-elaborate meals, and cooked them in a Japanese style, which made them turn an unpleasant color. As to what Gohda-san had been planning to cook with those ingredients, ...right then I couldn't even imagine it. If I did think about it, I'd be reminded of the way Gohda-san died, and a sour taste would fill the inside of my mouth... Everyone pretended to eat for the time being, but of course, no one made much progress.
units.note: Both retain unpleasant color caused by Japanese-style cooking rather than unfamiliar combination of presentation.
units.japanese: 郷田さんが、凝りに凝った料理のために取り寄せただろう珍しい西洋野菜は、熊沢さんによって、和風に料理され、違和感のある彩りとなっていた。これらの材料によって、郷田さんがどんな料理を作るつもりだったのか…。今となっては想像することもできない。それを想像すれば、郷田さんの死に様が再び蘇り、口の中が酸っぱい何かで満たされる…。みんなは一応、食べるふりだけするのだが、箸が進むはずもなかった。

units.text: Kumasawa‐san had taken the tasteful western vegetables, ones that Gohda‐san had probably special ordered for the purpose of some extravagantly fancy dish, and cooked them in a Japanese style, making them turn an unpleasant color. As to what Gohda‐san had been planning to cook with those ingredients... right then I couldn't even imagine it. If I did think about it, I would be reminded of the way Gohda‐san had died, and the inside of my mouth would be filled with a sour taste... For the time being, everyone pretended to eat, but there was no hope of anyone making any headway into the meal.
units.note: Both retain unpleasant color caused by Japanese-style cooking rather than unfamiliar combination of presentation.
units.japanese: 郷田さんが、凝りに凝った料理のために取り寄せただろう珍しい西洋野菜は、熊沢さんによって、和風に料理され、違和感のある彩りとなっていた。これらの材料によって、郷田さんがどんな料理を作るつもりだったのか…。今となっては想像することもできない。それを想像すれば、郷田さんの死に様が再び蘇り、口の中が酸っぱい何かで満たされる…。みんなは一応、食べるふりだけするのだが、箸が進むはずもなかった。

description: The group is briefed on the current situation. WH instead says everyone began thinking about it, removing the act of making the information known.
sourceReading: 周知が行われた means the situation was communicated to everyone.

units.text: Then everyone began thinking about the current situation. First off, ......Krauss oji-san, my dad, Kyrie-san, Rosa oba-san, Gohda-san and Shannon-chan: six people whose cruelly mutilated corpses had been found in the rose garden storehouse.
units.note: MG pooling knowledge restores collective information exchange; UP explicitly brought up to speed restores briefing.
units.japanese: そして、現状についての周知が行われた。

description: Natsuhi leaves with the three servants following her. WH reverses the action, saying she followed the servants out.
sourceReading: 使用人たちを従え puts Natsuhi at the head of the group.

units.text: Natsuhi oba-san followed the servants, Genji-san, Kumasawa-san, and Kanon-kun, out of the parlor. All that was left was Eva oba-san, Hideyoshi oji-san, Doctor Nanjo, and the four of us children for a total of seven people.
units.note: MG still says Natsuhi followed servants; UP restores her leading them.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんは、使用人たち、源次さんと熊沢さんと嘉音くんを従え、客間を出て行った。

units.text: Aunt Natsuhi followed the servants, Genji-san, Kumasawa-san, and Kanon-kun, out of the parlor. All that was left was Aunt Eva, Uncle Hideyoshi, Doctor Nanjo, and the four of us children, a total of seven people.
units.note: MG still says Natsuhi followed servants; UP restores her leading them.
units.japanese:
夏妃伯母さんは、使用人たち、源次さんと熊沢さんと嘉音くんを従え、客間を出て行った。残ったのは、絵羽伯母さんと秀吉伯父さん。
南條先生と、俺たち子ども４人の合計７人だった。

description: Hideyoshi complains about Sunday morning television programming. WH locates the programming in the middle of the day.
sourceReading: 日曜日の午前中 is Sunday morning.

units.text: "Let's all stick together, and maybe watch some television while we wait.  Unfortunately, I don't think that there'll be any good shows on during the middle of the day on Sunday."
units.note: MG retains middle of day. UP daytime broadens the specific Sunday morning without forcing midday; surviving scope is omitted morning specificity.
units.japanese: 「みんなで仲良く、テレビでも見て待ってよな。しっかし、日曜日の午前中はロクな番組やっとらへんなぁ。」

units.text: "Let's all stick together and maybe watch some television while we wait. Though I doubt we'll find anythin' good in the middle of the day on a Sunday."
units.note: MG retains middle of day. UP daytime broadens the specific Sunday morning without forcing midday; surviving scope is omitted morning specificity.
units.japanese: 「みんなで仲良く、テレビでも見て待ってよな。しっかし、日曜日の午前中はロクな番組やっとらへんなぁ」

units.text: "Let's all stick together, and maybe watch some TV while we wait. Geez, Sunday daytime TV sure doesn't have many good shows on, huh?"
units.note: MG retains middle of day. UP daytime broadens the specific Sunday morning without forcing midday; surviving scope is omitted morning specificity.
units.japanese: 「みんなで仲良く、テレビでも見て待ってよな。しっかし、日曜日の午前中はロクな番組やっとらへんなぁ」

description: Jessica says Shannon had consulted her since several years earlier. WH gives a single talk several years ago, losing the ongoing relationship.
sourceReading: 数年前から and 相談を受けてた describe consultations extending from that earlier time.

units.text: "...............Well, I......several years ago, I had a talk with Shannon.  ...About you, George nii-san."
units.note: MG still supplies single several-years-ago advice approach; UP restores having talks for several years. Later MG 379–380 relationship discussion mitigates but does not restore duration explicitly.
units.japanese: 「…………………私さ。…数年前から、紗音に相談を受けてたぜ。…譲治兄さんのことでさ。」

units.text: ".........Well, ...several years ago, Shannon came to me asking for advice. ...About you, George nii-san."
units.note: MG still supplies single several-years-ago advice approach; UP restores having talks for several years. Later MG 379–380 relationship discussion mitigates but does not restore duration explicitly.
units.japanese: 「…………………私さ。…数年前から、紗音に相談を受けてたぜ。…譲治兄さんのことでさ」

description: Battler laments Shannon receiving an engagement ring and then her life ending. WH has him say I handed her the engagement ring, assigning George’s action to Battler.
sourceReading: 婚約指輪を渡されて is passive: Shannon was given the ring. The speaker comment identifies Battler.

units.text: "......So I handed her the engagement ring, and then, ......it was all over."
units.note: Both restore Shannon receiving ring without assigning gift to Battler.
units.japanese:
「………それが、婚約指輪を渡されて、そこで、
……おしまいかよ。」

description: WH reverses the direction of the emotional substitution.
sourceReading: Sadness gradually gave way to a different emotion.

units.text: I had been acting much calmer than George-aniki and Jessica had been. That wasn't because my sadness was any less intense, or because I had already sprung back to normal. It was just because my sadness was gradually replacing a different emotion.
units.note: Both preserve sadness being replaced by other emotion, identified as anger.
units.japanese: 悲しみが、別の感情に徐々にすり替わっていったからだ。

description: Battler cannot calm his anger until he strikes the culprit. WH says not getting a chance to strike has been eating at him, implying a past missed opportunity.
sourceReading: 一発お見舞いしてやらないことには腹の虫が治まらねぇ expresses a condition for appeasing his current anger.

units.text: "............Rather than sadness, .........it's more like I'm irritated.  What bastard did this and where?  ...It's kinda been eating at me that I didn't get a chance to smack him upside the face."
units.note: MG retains past missed chance to strike; UP restores unable to settle until striking culprit.
units.japanese:
「…………悲しい、ってよりは、
………腹立たしいって気持ちなんすよ。どこのどいつがこんなことをしやがったのか。…横っ面に一発お見舞いしてやらないことには腹の虫が治まらねぇんです。」

units.text: "......Rather than sad, ......I'd say I'm more pissed off. What bastard did this and where? ...It's kinda been eating at me that I didn't get a chance to smack him upside the face."
units.note: MG retains past missed chance to strike; UP restores unable to settle until striking culprit.
units.japanese: 「…………悲しい、ってよりは、………腹立たしいって気持ちなんすよ。どこのどいつがこんなことをしやがったのか。…横っ面に一発お見舞いしてやらないことには腹の虫が治まらねぇんです」

description: WH replaces the ease of understanding a less conspicuous disposal site with there would not have been much to go on.
sourceReading: If the bodies had been thrown into garden bushes, understanding the situation would have been easier.

units.text: Her argument was extremely plain and clear. ......If the bodies had been found thrown somewhere in the bushes of the rose garden, there wouldn't have been much to go on. However, if there was only one key to the storehouse in the servant room, and it was stored with such a large group of keys, a novice would not be able to tell them apart. This meant that the culprit was someone who could normally enter the servant room, and knew where the key was well. ...The family didn't normally go into the servant room. ......Which meant that............
units.note: MG retains little to go on. UP replaces it with no explanation necessary, restoring explanatory focus but overstating source easier to understand; surviving scope is strength of explanatory comparison.
units.japanese: ……遺体が薔薇庭園のどこかの茂みにでも放り込まれていたなら、まだ理解は容易だった。

units.text: Her argument was extremely plain and clear. ...If the bodies had been found thrown somewhere in the bushes of the rose garden, there wouldn't have been much to go on. However, if there was only one key to the storehouse in the servant room, and it was stored with such a large group of keys, a novice would not be able to tell them apart. This meant the culprit was someone who went into the servant room a lot and was familiar with the locations of the keys. ...The family members didn't normally go into the servant room. ...Which meant that.........
units.note: MG retains little to go on. UP replaces it with no explanation necessary, restoring explanatory focus but overstating source easier to understand; surviving scope is strength of explanatory comparison.
units.japanese:
それは非常に単純明快な話だった。……遺体が薔薇庭園のどこかの茂みにでも放り込まれていたなら、まだ理解は容易だった。しかし、たった１つしかない倉庫の鍵は使用人室にあり、しかも大量の鍵と一緒にしまわれており、素人目にはとても判別できない。となると、普段、使用人室に出入りしていて、鍵の所在などについて熟知している人間が犯人ということになる。…使用人室には普通、家人だって入らない。
……ということは…………、

units.text:
Her argument was extremely plain and clear. ......If the bodies had been thrown somewhere in the bushes of the rose garden, no explanation would have been necessary. However, the one key to the storehouse was in the servant room, and stored with a large group of other keys, such that a novice would not be able to tell them apart. This meant that the culprit was someone who was used to going in and out of the servant room, and knew well where the key was. ...The family didn't normally go into the servant room.
......Which meant that............
units.note: MG retains little to go on. UP replaces it with no explanation necessary, restoring explanatory focus but overstating source easier to understand; surviving scope is strength of explanatory comparison.
units.japanese:
それは非常に単純明快な話だった。……遺体が薔薇庭園のどこかの茂みにでも放り込まれていたなら、まだ理解は容易だった。しかし、たった１つしかない倉庫の鍵は使用人室にあり、しかも大量の鍵と一緒にしまわれており、素人目にはとても判別できない。となると、普段、使用人室に出入りしていて、鍵の所在などについて熟知している人間が犯人ということになる。…使用人室には普通、家人だって入らない。
……ということは…………、

description: WH omits attacking the four adults at once and collapses grotesque makeup and graffiti into scribbling makeup on their faces.
sourceReading: 一度に is at once; 悪趣味な化粧と落書き lists makeup and graffiti as separate work.

units.text: "The culprit, ......no, culprits in the plural, would have more than enough weapons in their arsenal if that were the case.  You see it, don't you?  They had to assault the four in the dining hall and kill them, drag a total of six bodies all the way to the storehouse beyond the rose garden, and scribble that disgusting makeup on their faces.  ......There's no way that a single culprit could carry all of this out on their own, right?"
units.note: MG restores separate makeup and shutter graffiti but still omits attacking four at once. UP restores at once but retains collapse into scribbling makeup on faces, losing separate graffiti task.
units.japanese: 「犯人、……うぅん、犯人たちは複数で、そして充分な武装をしていたと考えられるわ。だってそうでしょう？　食堂にいた兄さんたち４人を一度に襲って殺し、合計６人分の遺体を、遥々と薔薇庭園の向こうの倉庫まで運んで、悪趣味な化粧と落書きを施してる。……これだけのことを単独犯で行えるはずもないでしょう？」

units.text: "It's reasonable to think that the culprit...no, culprits...are multiple in number and fairly well armed. They'd have to be, wouldn't they?
units.note: MG restores separate makeup and shutter graffiti but still omits attacking four at once. UP restores at once but retains collapse into scribbling makeup on faces, losing separate graffiti task.
units.japanese:
「犯人、……うぅん、犯人たちは複数で、そして充分な武装をしていたと考えられるわ。だってそうでしょう？」

units.note: MG restores separate makeup and shutter graffiti but still omits attacking four at once. UP restores at once but retains collapse into scribbling makeup on faces, losing separate graffiti task.

units.note: MG restores separate makeup and shutter graffiti but still omits attacking four at once. UP restores at once but retains collapse into scribbling makeup on faces, losing separate graffiti task.

description: Battler endorses Eva’s reasoning as reasonable; WH opens with categorical impossibility.
sourceReading: 道理だ means that is reasonable or that makes sense; the following qualification allows a lone culprit enough time.

units.text: It was impossible.  It might not have been if a single person had enough time, but that would have taken ages. It was probably best to think that a significant number of people had been part of it.
units.note: MG restores It made sense; UP retains It was impossible. Both next qualify feasibility for one person with enough time.
units.japanese: 道理だ。時間さえ掛ければ１人でも不可能ではないだろうが、それではあまりにも手間が掛かる。

units.text: It was impossible. It might not have been if a single person spent enough time on it, but that would have taken ages. It was probably best to think that a significant number of people had been part of it.
units.note: MG restores It made sense; UP retains It was impossible. Both next qualify feasibility for one person with enough time.
units.japanese: 道理だ。時間さえ掛ければ１人でも不可能ではないだろうが、それではあまりにも手間が掛かる。少なくない人数が関わったと考えるのが妥当だろう。

description: Battler says servants hiding bodies in their own keyed storehouse would be especially out of the question. WH only observes other sites existed.
sourceReading: もってのほか rejects that location particularly strongly in the servants-as-culprits counterargument.

units.text: If the servants really had been the culprits, they wouldn't hide the bodies in a place that was tied to themselves. There were other places besides the rose garden storehouse, whose key they themselves controlled. The police would probably immediately pursue whoever had been in control of the key. That would create a danger for exposure. ......If we were to assume that they were the culprits, they had no reason to carry the bodies into the storehouse.
units.note: MG rhetorical why use shed when controlling key and UP certainly not shed both restore particularly unsuitable keyed location.
units.japanese: 自分たちが鍵を管理する薔薇庭園の倉庫などもってのほかだ。

description: WH turns a tentative possibility into at the very least and omits the explicit six-body arrangement in comparing display with killing.
sourceReading: 下手すると marks the possibility that preparing six corpses there mattered more than killing.

units.text: Right, that was where we could 'turn the chessboard over'. So the culprit's goal was to clearly show us the bodies. ......So, at the very least, to the culprit, the appearance of the corpses there meant more than the deaths themselves.
units.note: MG restores six-corpses display but retains at the very least for tentative may-well possibility. UP restores may well and six corpses.
units.japanese:
……つまり犯人にとっては下手すると、(殺すことよりも、あそこに６人の死体を用意する/・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・)
(方が意味があったってことになる/・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・)。

units.text: ...So, at the very least, to the culprit, the appearance of six corpses there meant more than the deaths themselves.
units.note: MG restores six-corpses display but retains at the very least for tentative may-well possibility. UP restores may well and six corpses.
units.japanese: いや、そこでこそ“チェス盤をひっくり返す”ところさ。なら、このこれ見よがしなアピールは犯人の目的そのものってことになる。……つまり犯人にとっては下手すると、殺すことよりも、あそこに６人の死体を用意する方が意味があったってことになる。

description: Eva says Genji will be able to corroborate their return just after midnight. WH says the encounter should be enough to prove their return, changing the stated evidentiary role and adding sufficiency.
sourceReading: 証明してくれる refers back to Genji doing the corroborating for them.

units.text: I think that should be enough to prove that we had returned to the guesthouse a little after midnight.  ......Of course, if my theory was correct, the servants would all be in cahoots, and that wouldn't actually make for an alibi, would it?"
units.note: Both retain encounter should be enough to prove return instead of Genji expected corroboration; preceding uncertainty and accomplice caveat limit sufficiency claim.
units.japanese: だから私たちがゲストハウスに戻ってきた時間は２４時過ぎだと証明してくれると思うわよ。……もっとも、私の仮説通り、使用人たちもグルなのだとしたら、こんなのアリバイにならないけどねぇ？」

units.text: I think that should be enough to prove we returned to the guesthouse a little after midnight. ...Though, if my theory was correct, the servants would all be in cahoots, and that wouldn't actually make for much of an alibi."
units.note: Both retain encounter should be enough to prove return instead of Genji expected corroboration; preceding uncertainty and accomplice caveat limit sufficiency claim.
units.japanese: 「だから私たちがゲストハウスに戻ってきた時間は２４時過ぎだと証明してくれると思うわよ。……もっとも、私の仮説通り、使用人たちもグルなのだとしたら、こんなのアリバイにならないけどねぇ？」

units.text: "I think that should be enough to prove that we returned to the guesthouse a little after midnight. ......Of course, if my theory was correct and the servants were all in cahoots, that wouldn't actually make for an alibi, would it?"
units.note: Both retain encounter should be enough to prove return instead of Genji expected corroboration; preceding uncertainty and accomplice caveat limit sufficiency claim.
units.japanese: 「だから私たちがゲストハウスに戻ってきた時間は２４時過ぎだと証明してくれると思うわよ。……もっとも、私の仮説通り、使用人たちもグルなのだとしたら、こんなのアリバイにならないけどねぇ？」

description: Battler agrees with Eva’s caveat, then jokes that he may be talking to the actual culprit. WH opens by asking whether it is really true.
sourceReading: 確かにそうっすねぇ acknowledges the preceding point as valid.

units.text: "Is that really true?  That'd mean that, right now, I'm playing detective with the real culprit, right?  Ihihi!"
units.note: Both restore agreement with caveat before real-culprit joke.
units.japanese: 「確かにそうっすねぇ？　ってことは俺、今、真犯人と推理ごっこをしてるってことになるんすか？　いっひっひ！」

description: Eva argues that recruiting servants and planning carefully would make her all the more likely to stage accidental deaths. WH says it would make her more capable of doing so.
sourceReading: なおさらそうするでしょうよ is a stronger expectation that she would choose that course under the stated conditions.

units.text: After all, if I just wanted to make them forfeit their rights to the inheritance, the method of their deaths wouldn't have mattered.  On the contrary, you'd expect that I would try to make their deaths look like an accident, wouldn't I?  If I had roped in the servants, and carefully planned everything out, I would be even more capable of doing that."
units.note: Both restore more reason to choose staged accidents when carefully planning with servants, rather than enhanced capability only.
units.japanese: だって、遺産相続権を喪失させるだけなら、どんな死に方だって構わない。むしろ事故死に見せかけた方がスマートでしょう？　使用人たちを抱きこんで、周到に計画していたなら、なおさらそうするでしょうよ。」

description: Hideyoshi cannot reproduce or make out the detailed lettering, although he recognizes the arrangement. WH describes thin characters instead.
sourceReading: 細かい文字 refers to the fine details of the writing in this recollection.

units.text: "Ah, yes, there definitely was somethin' like that drawn there...  Yep, there's no mistakin' the shape.  I don't understand the thin characters, but the arrangement was nearly the same."
units.note: MG retains thin characters rather than detailed lettering; UP exact characters restores inability to reproduce or identify detail.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、確かにそんなのも描いてあったで…！　うん、図形的には間違いなくこれや。細かい文字はわからんが、配列はほぼ同じや。」

units.text: "Ah, yeah, there definitely was somethin' like that drawn there...! Yep, there's no mistakin' the shape. I don't understand the thin characters, but the arrangement was nearly the same."
units.note: MG retains thin characters rather than detailed lettering; UP exact characters restores inability to reproduce or identify detail.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、確かにそんなのも描いてあったで…！　うん、図形的には間違いなくこれや。細かい文字はわからんが、配列はほぼ同じや」

description: WH calls the cross decoration a German swastika in George’s comparison and repeats swastika in Nanjo’s explanation of a religious order’s emblem.
sourceReading: ドイツの十字章 names a German cross decoration; Nanjo links that cross to knights protecting pilgrims. Neither line says 卍 or swastika.

units.text: "...My first impression was that the design resembled a German swastika..."
units.note: Both remove swastika. MG specifies German Cross and Germany absent from maintained Japanese; separate PC-provenance candidate below, not this swastika error.
units.japanese:
「…僕の第一印象では、ドイツの十字章に似たデザインだなって思ったかな…。」
「あー…。確かにこんなデザインや。ということはドイツと何か関係があるんか。」
「ドイツの十字章はもともと、聖地巡礼者を守るための騎士修道士たちの紋章だったそうですな…。」

units.text: "Aah...  It certainly does have that kind of design.  Does that mean it has somethin' to do with Germany?"
units.note: Both remove swastika. MG specifies German Cross and Germany absent from maintained Japanese; separate PC-provenance candidate below, not this swastika error.

units.text: "The swastika was originally a crest from a religious order of knights and was supposed to protect pilgrims traveling to sacred places..."

description: WH attributes familiarity to Maria and places the writing in the corner. The Japanese describes unfamiliar characters written into the spaces within the figure.
sourceReading: 見慣れない is unfamiliar to the observing viewpoint; 図形の隙間 is the gaps in the diagram.

units.text: Jessica tried to smooth things over by praising Maria. Maybe she wanted to make sure that this was still the Maria who everyone knew so well. ...But Maria didn't answer her in any way in particular. With a rustle, Maria began writing characters that seemed familiar to her in the corner of the shape. ...When Hideyoshi oji-san and Doctor Nanjo saw them, their eyes immediately began to open wide...
units.note: Both restore unfamiliar characters and remove false Maria-familiarity attribution; both retain corners for spaces within figure. Surviving scope is placement wording only.
units.japanese: 真里亞は、図形の隙間に見慣れない文字をさらさらと書き込んでいく。

units.text: Jessica tried to smooth things over by praising Maria. Maybe she wanted to confirm that this was still the Maria we all knew so well. ...But Maria didn't answer her in any way in particular. Maria began swiftly writing unfamiliar characters in the corners of the shape. ...When Uncle Hideyoshi and Doctor Nanjo saw them, their eyes immediately began to open wide...
units.note: Both restore unfamiliar characters and remove false Maria-familiarity attribution; both retain corners for spaces within figure. Surviving scope is placement wording only.
units.japanese: 朱志香が取り繕うように褒め言葉を口にする。……みんなのよく知る真里亞であることを確かめたかったのかもしれない。…でも真里亞は特に返事を返してはくれなかった。真里亞は、図形の隙間に見慣れない文字をさらさらと書き込んでいく。…それを見る秀吉伯父さんと南條先生の目がみるみる見開かれていく…。

units.text: Jessica tried to smooth things over by praising Maria. ......Maybe she wanted to make sure that this was still the Maria who everyone knew so well. ...But Maria didn't give her any particular response. Maria started fluently writing unfamiliar characters in the corners of the shape. ...At this sight, the eyes of Uncle Hideyoshi and Doctor Nanjo instantly began to widen...
units.note: Both restore unfamiliar characters and remove false Maria-familiarity attribution; both retain corners for spaces within figure. Surviving scope is placement wording only.
units.japanese: 朱志香が取り繕うように褒め言葉を口にする。……みんなのよく知る真里亞であることを確かめたかったのかもしれない。…でも真里亞は特に返事を返してはくれなかった。真里亞は、図形の隙間に見慣れない文字をさらさらと書き込んでいく。…それを見る秀吉伯父さんと南條先生の目がみるみる見開かれていく…。

description: WH says some people spat something out furiously, dropping what they said: that it was insane.
sourceReading: 狂っていると吐き捨て names their disgusted judgment, alongside hitting their knees.

units.text: It looked like everyone had slowly arrived at the same conclusion. ...Some people were shocked, others spat something out furiously as they punched their knees... ......This was starting to become a seriously disturbing story. ...And since we couldn't accept it, we couldn't understand it.
units.note: Both restore spoken insanity judgment.
units.japanese: …ある者は呆然とし、ある者は狂っていると吐き捨てながら拳を膝に打ち付ける…。

description: WH says they could not understand because they could not accept it. Japanese gives parallel inability to accept and understand, without that causal order.
sourceReading: 納得できねぇし理解もできねぇ coordinates the two failures.

units.text: It looked like everyone had slowly arrived at the same conclusion. ...Some people were shocked, others spat something out furiously as they punched their knees... ......This was starting to become a seriously disturbing story. ...And since we couldn't accept it, we couldn't understand it.
units.note: Both restore parallel inability to accept and understand, without causal ordering.
units.japanese: …しかも納得できねぇし理解もできねぇ。

description: Battler helplessly lets his mind and body be swallowed by the emotions. WH says he trusts to his mind and body as he is swallowed.
sourceReading: 身と心を任せる makes mind and body what he surrenders to the engulfing experience.

units.text: Anger, sadness.  The opposing emotions all swirled up together, and they started to suck me in. Unable to resist, ...I could do nothing but cover my eyes with my hands and trust to my mind and body as I started getting sucked in.........
units.note: MG still trusts to mind and body; UP explicitly entrusts them to swallowing spiral.
units.japanese: 俺は抗うこともできず、…こうして両目を手で覆って飲み込まれていくに身と心を任せるだけだ………。

units.text: Anger, sadness. The opposing emotions all swirled up together, and they started to suck me in. Unable to resist, ...I could do nothing but cover my eyes with my hands and trust to my mind and body as I started getting sucked in......
units.note: MG still trusts to mind and body; UP explicitly entrusts them to swallowing spiral.
units.japanese:
怒り、悲しみ。
相反する感情が渦を巻き、俺を飲み込んでいく。俺は抗うこともできず、…こうして両目を手で覆って飲み込まれていくに身と心を任せるだけだ………。

description: WH substitutes this year’s earnings call for the fiscal year’s income-and-expenditure report.
sourceReading: 今年度の収支報告 is a report of income and expenditure for the fiscal year; no call is named.

units.text: If I were forced to choose, I'd say, rather than demons and monsters, this year's earnings call and angry wives are 100 million times scarier. I'll go further, alright?  If you force me to. What you're scared of is something made to entertain people who have too much time on their hands and too much empty space in their minds. They have so much free time, they don't know what to do with it, so in order to play around with their unusual emotions, they created a culture of demons and monsters and stuff.
units.note: Both retain earnings call for fiscal income-and-expenditure report.
units.japanese: 俺に言わせりゃ、悪魔やら妖怪やらより、今年度の収支報告や、機嫌を悪くした女房の方が一億倍も怖ぇってもんだぜ。

units.text: If I were forced to choose, I'd say, rather than demons and monsters, this year's earnings call and angry wives are 100 million times scarier. I'll go further, okay? From my point of view... Getting scared is a recreational emotion, something for people who've got room to relax both in their hearts and their lifestyles. They had so much free time, they didn't know what to do with it, so in order to entertain their mind with unusual emotions, people started creating a culture with demons and the occult and stuff.
units.note: Both retain earnings call for fiscal income-and-expenditure report.
units.japanese: 俺に言わせりゃ、悪魔やら妖怪やらより、今年度の収支報告や、機嫌を悪くした女房の方が一億倍も怖ぇってもんだぜ。さらに言うぜ？　俺に言わせりゃな。怖がるってのは、心と生活にゆとりのある連中の娯楽的感情なのさ。暇で暇でしょうがないから、連中は変わった感情で心を遊ばせたくて、悪魔だのオカルトだのって文化を作り出したんだよ。

If you ask me... being scared is an emotion for the entertainment of people who have too much time on their hands and too much empty space in their minds. They have so much free time they don't know what to do with it, so in order to play around with unusual emotions, they created a culture of demons and monsters and stuff.
units.note: Both retain earnings call for fiscal income-and-expenditure report.

description: WH renders in my view as if you force me to, making Rudolf’s freely offered lecture sound compelled.
sourceReading: 俺に言わせりゃな introduces his own opinion; it does not state coercion.

units.note: MG adds forced choice at 820 but restores freely offered point of view at 821. UP if you ask me preserves both.

description: Rudolf defines being frightened as an emotion enjoyed by people with room in their minds and lives. WH instead describes what frightens Battler as entertainment for people with empty space in their minds.
sourceReading: 怖がるってのは identifies the experience of fear, while ゆとり denotes spare capacity or ease.

units.text: If I were forced to choose, I'd say, rather than demons and monsters, this year's earnings call and angry wives are 100 million times scarier. I'll go further, alright?  If you force me to. What you're scared of is something made to entertain people who have too much time on their hands and too much empty space in their minds. They have so much free time, they don't know what to do with it, so in order to play around with their unusual emotions, they created a culture of demons and monsters and stuff.
units.note: MG restores getting scared as recreational emotion for those with room in hearts and lives. UP restores being scared as emotion but retains empty space in minds and loses lifestyle latitude.
units.japanese: 怖がるってのは、心と生活にゆとりのある連中の娯楽的感情なのさ。

description: WH says the culprit could not get away until next morning. Japanese says they knew they could not simply escape promptly the following morning either.
sourceReading: 翌朝にすぐ逃げられるわけではない negates availability of prompt next-morning escape.

units.text: With us put on the defensive, we couldn't even guess at the culprit's scheme. ...If you turned it over and looked at it that way, just how far could you see? ......First off, at the time the murders were committed by the culprit, they knew that the island was cut off by the typhoon. Therefore, they should have understood that even if they carried out the murders, they wouldn't be able to get away until the next morning. In short, the culprit had begun without securing a way to escape.
units.note: MG restores cannot get away early next morning; UP retains cannot get away until next morning, implying next morning escape availability.
units.japanese: だから、殺人を実行しても翌朝にすぐ逃げられるわけではないことも理解していたはず。

units.text: With us put on the defensive, we couldn't even guess at the culprit's scheme. ...If you flipped it over and looked at it the other way, just how far could you see? ......First off, at the time the murders were committed by the culprit, they knew that the island was cut off by the typhoon. So, they should have understood that even if they carried out the murders, they wouldn't be able to get away until the next morning. In short, the culprit had begun without securing a way to escape.
units.note: MG restores cannot get away early next morning; UP retains cannot get away until next morning, implying next morning escape availability.
units.japanese: 守勢に立った俺たちには、犯人の目論見はさっぱり見当が付かない。…ひっくり返して見てみたら、一体何が見えるのか。……まず、犯人は殺人を犯す時点で、島が台風に閉ざされているのを知っていた。だから、殺人を実行しても翌朝にすぐ逃げられるわけではないことも理解していたはず。つまり、犯人は退路の確保もなく殺人に踏み切ったわけだ。

description: Battler recalls the letter’s grandiose invitation to enjoy the battle of wits. WH says this person was satisfied with playing one, replacing the quoted challenge with a mental-state claim.
sourceReading: 知恵比べをお楽しみ下さいとかのたまった recalls what the sender proclaimed.

units.text: ......What kind of reaction was the culprit hoping to get out of us by showing this imitation of the occult...? Somehow, that felt like the culprit's weak point... The letter from Beatrice that Maria had read aloud during last night's dinner sprang back into my mind. ......This person was satisfied with playing a battle of wits.
units.note: Both restore the sender invitation to enjoy the contest.
units.japanese: ……知恵比べをお楽しみ下さいとかのたまったやつだ。

description: WH literalizes exposing the adversary’s true nature as pulling off her fake skin and changes Battler’s I into we.
sourceReading: 化けの皮を剥ぐ means expose the disguise or true nature; 俺が makes Battler the agent.

units.text: Isn't that interesting? This is a battle of wits between us and the witch. Will we be sucked up by her occult game first? Or will we pull off her fake skin first? ......There's a whole day until the typhoon passes. Why not enjoy ourselves...?!
units.note: MG retains plural agency and fake-skin calque; UP restores Battler personal agency and idiomatic exposure.
units.japanese: 俺がてめぇの化けの皮を剥いでやるのが早いか。

units.text: Isn't that interesting? This is a battle of wits between us and the witch. Will we be sucked up by her occult game first? Or will we pull off her fake skin first? ...There's a whole day until the typhoon passes. Why not enjoy ourselves...?!
units.note: MG retains plural agency and fake-skin calque; UP restores Battler personal agency and idiomatic exposure.
units.japanese:
面白いじゃねぇか。こいつは俺たちと魔女さまの知恵比べだ。てめぇのオカルトごっこに俺たちが飲み込まれるのが早いか。俺がてめぇの化けの皮を剥いでやるのが早いか。……台風が過ぎるまで、たっぷり一日あるわけだぜ。
楽しませてもらおうじゃねぇか…！

description: Kumasawa recalls Kinzo playing with the gun while striking various cool poses in the woods. WH keeps playing with it but drops the posing.
sourceReading: いろいろとカッコつけて describes trying to look impressive, matching the preceding Western-film enthusiasm.

units.text: "He was quite fond of it right after he managed to acquire it.  It seems the workings that ejected the cartridges were more interesting to him than shooting it, and he played around with it back in the forest all the time.  Hoh-hoh-hoh-ho..."
units.note: Both retain forest play but omit Kinzo striking cool poses.
units.japanese: 「手に入れられたばかりの頃は、大層気に入られておりまして。撃つより、薬莢を出す動作が面白いらしくて、裏の森でいろいろとカッコつけて遊んでおられたもんですよ。ほっほっほっほ…。」

units.text: "He was quite fond of it right after he managed to acquire it. It seems the workings that ejected the cartridges were more interesting to him than shooting it, and he played around with it back in the forest all the time. Hohohohoh..."
units.note: Both retain forest play but omit Kinzo striking cool poses.
units.japanese: 「手に入れられたばかりの頃は、大層気に入られておりまして。撃つより、薬莢を出す動作が面白いらしくて、裏の森でいろいろとカッコつけて遊んでおられたもんですよ。ほっほっほっほ…」

units.text: "He was quite tickled by it when he first got his hands on it. It seems the workings that ejected the cartridges were more interesting to him than shooting it, and he played around with it back in the forest all the time. Hoh‐hoh‐hoh‐ho..."
units.note: Both retain forest play but omit Kinzo striking cool poses.
units.japanese: 「手に入れられたばかりの頃は、大層気に入られておりまして。撃つより、薬莢を出す動作が面白いらしくて、裏の森でいろいろとカッコつけて遊んでおられたもんですよ。ほっほっほっほ…」

description: Eva says the gun is dangerous or alarming. WH says it is the real thing, repeating authenticity instead of stating her concern.
sourceReading: 物騒ねぇ expresses unease at danger.

units.text: "......Still, it's the real thing.  Are you sure you should be dragging this out?"
units.note: MG disturbing and UP dangerous restore Eva unease.
units.japanese: 「……しかし物騒ねぇ。そんなものまで持ち出しちゃうのかしらぁ？」

description: Natsuhi settles heavily onto a sofa and lets out a large sigh. WH says she takes a deep breath.
sourceReading: 大きく溜め息をつく is a deep sigh, an outward expression rather than an inhalation.

units.text: As Natsuhi-san said this, she slumped down into one of the sofas and took a deep breath. She had been trying to find Grandfather as well as check the doors and windows. Since Grandfather was not with her, apparently his whereabouts were still unknown.
units.note: Both retain deep breath in place of the explicit large sigh.
units.japanese: 夏妃さんはそう言うと、どっかりとソファーに腰を下ろし大きく溜め息をつく。

units.text: As Natsuhi-san said this, she slumped down into one of the sofas and took a deep breath. She had been trying to find Grandfather, ...as well as check the doors and windows. Since Grandfather wasn't with her, she probably still didn't know where he was.
units.note: Both retain deep breath in place of the explicit large sigh.
units.japanese: 夏妃さんはそう言うと、どっかりとソファーに腰を下ろし大きく溜め息をつく。屋敷内の戸締りの確認と、…あと祖父さまを探すということになっていたはずだ。そして祖父さまと一緒じゃないところを見ると、その行方は未だわからないというようだった。

units.text: As Natsuhi‐san said this, she slumped down into one of the sofas and took a deep breath. As well as checking the doors and windows, ...she had also been trying to find Grandfather. Since Grandfather was not with her, apparently his whereabouts were still unknown.
units.note: Both retain deep breath in place of the explicit large sigh.
units.japanese: 夏妃さんはそう言うと、どっかりとソファーに腰を下ろし大きく溜め息をつく。屋敷内の戸締りの確認と、…あと祖父さまを探すということになっていたはずだ。そして祖父さまと一緒じゃないところを見ると、その行方は未だわからないというようだった。

units.text: Natsuhi took a deep breath. Though this was a whim of Kinzo's, a man she greatly respected, ...she seemed to resist the idea of hanging it right here in the entrance hall, the face of the mansion. When the white sheet was pulled off, a Western woman wearing a beautiful dress came into view... It was a massive portrait of a woman...
units.note: Same-character repeated lexical family. EP7 Natsuhi sigh directly verified PC160255/160256 and paired row15. Original sofa-setting details are not asserted for this later occurrence; sigh loses exhaled emotional expression in both. A deep breath can accompany discomfort but does not specifically convey the source sigh.
units.japanese: 夏妃は深くため息をつく。敬愛する金蔵の気紛れとはいえ、……屋敷の顔である玄関ホールに、それが飾られることには、強い抵抗があるようだった。白いシーツが取り払われると、そこには、ドレス姿の美しい西洋女性の姿が現れる…。それは、女性の姿を描いた、巨大な肖像画だった……。

units.text: Natsuhi took a deep breath. Though this was a whim of Kinzo's, a man she greatly respected, ......she seemed to resist the idea of hanging it right here in the entrance hall, the face of the mansion. When the white sheet was pulled off, a Western woman wearing a beautiful dress came into view... It was a massive portrait of a woman......
