Original sofa-setting details are not asserted for this later occurrence; sigh loses exhaled emotional expression in both. A deep breath can accompany discomfort but does not specifically convey the source sigh.
units.japanese: 夏妃は深くため息をつく。敬愛する金蔵の気紛れとはいえ、……屋敷の顔である玄関ホールに、それが飾られることには、強い抵抗があるようだった。白いシーツが取り払われると、そこには、ドレス姿の美しい西洋女性の姿が現れる…。それは、女性の姿を描いた、巨大な肖像画だった……。

description: Battler says Kinzo would also be sufficiently suspicious if the letter and killings were extensions of his prank. WH says there was more than enough evidence to doubt him, introducing an evidentiary quantity absent from Japanese.
sourceReading: 充分に疑わしい evaluates how suspicious he would be under the hypothesis; it does not name evidence.

units.text: There was a dangerous atmosphere between the two of them... If you think about who was the most suspicious from the inheritance problem standpoint, Eva oba-san was the obvious answer. ...However, there was no proof that Natsuhi oba-san was innocent. ......No, if you view Beatrice's letter as Grandfather's complicated prank, and think of this case as just an extension of that, there was more than enough evidence to doubt even Grandfather.
units.note: MG reason to suspect expresses hypothetical suspicion; UP retains more than enough evidence. Both retain conditional framing; no actual new observed clue established.
units.japanese: ……いや、そもそもベアトリーチェの手紙が祖父さまの仕組んだ手の込んだ悪戯で、この事件すらもその延長だと言うなら、祖父さまだって充分に疑わしい。

units.text:
There was a dangerous atmosphere between the two of them...
If you thought about who stood to gain the most from the inheritance problem standpoint, Auntie Eva was the obvious answer. ...However, there was no proof that Aunt Natsuhi was innocent. ......No, if you view Beatrice's letter as Grandfather's elaborate prank, and think of this incident as just an extension of that, there was more than enough evidence to doubt even Grandfather.
units.note: MG reason to suspect expresses hypothetical suspicion; UP retains more than enough evidence. Both retain conditional framing; no actual new observed clue established.
units.japanese:
険悪な雰囲気になる二人…。
遺産問題で誰が一番得をするかと考えれば、一番疑わしいのは絵羽伯母さんだ。…しかし、夏妃伯母さんが怪しくないという保証もない。……いや、そもそもベアトリーチェの手紙が祖父さまの仕組んだ手の込んだ悪戯で、この事件すらもその延長だと言うなら、祖父さまだって充分に疑わしい。

description: WH calls the marks traces of blood rather than something resembling blood.
sourceReading: 血の跡のようなもの explicitly preserves resemblance instead of material identification.

units.text: Genji thought back to the time he had seen those traces of blood on the door to Natsuhi's room... With the substance sticking to the door around the doorknob, and the marks of something scratching against the door...it had definitely appeared as though someone had tried to open the door, but couldn't...
units.note: Both preserve bloodlike qualification in Kanon question at 48 but narrate traces of blood at 59, dropping renewed source qualification. Attempted entry remains appearance, not certified event.
units.japanese: 源次は夏妃の部屋の扉の、あの血の跡のようなものを思い出す…。

units.text: Genji thought back to the time he had seen those traces of blood on the door to Natsuhi's room... With the substance sticking to the door around the doorknob, and the marks of something scratching against the door, ...it had definitely appeared as though someone had tried to open the door, but couldn't...
units.note: Both preserve bloodlike qualification in Kanon question at 48 but narrate traces of blood at 59, dropping renewed source qualification. Attempted entry remains appearance, not certified event.
units.japanese: 源次は夏妃の部屋の扉の、あの血の跡のようなものを思い出す…。ドアノブの周りに付着したそれと、掻き毟ったような痕跡は、ドアを開けたかったが開けられなかった、というように確かに見えた…。

units.text: Genji thought back to the time he had seen those traces of blood on the door to Natsuhi's room... With the substance sticking to the door around the doorknob, and the marks of something scratching against the door... it had definitely appeared as though someone had tried to open the door, but couldn't...
units.note: Both preserve bloodlike qualification in Kanon question at 48 but narrate traces of blood at 59, dropping renewed source qualification. Attempted entry remains appearance, not certified event.
units.japanese: 源次は夏妃の部屋の扉の、あの血の跡のようなものを思い出す…。ドアノブの周りに付着したそれと、掻き毟ったような痕跡は、ドアを開けたかったが開けられなかった、というように確かに見えた…。

description: Kanon asks why Madam escaped being sacrificed. WH asks why she was not chosen as a sacrifice, narrowing survival into nonselection.
sourceReading: 生贄を免れた describes escaping the outcome; it does not establish whether she was selected. The following counterfactual separately uses 選ばれてた.

units.text: "...Why, .........was Madam not chosen as a sacrifice...?  If only she had been chosen, ......Shannon wouldn't, ......Shannon wouldn't have had to die..."
units.note: Both narrow escaping sacrifice into not being chosen. Following hypothetical selection does not rule out surviving selection.
units.japanese:
「…どうして、
………奥様は生贄を免れたんだ…。もし奥様が選ばれてたなら、
……紗音は、
……紗音は、死ななくて済んだのにッ…。」

units.text: "...Why... did the Madam avoid being chosen as a sacrifice...? If only she'd been chosen, ...Shannon wouldn't... Shannon wouldn't have had to die..."
units.note: Both narrow escaping sacrifice into not being chosen. Following hypothetical selection does not rule out surviving selection.
units.japanese: 「…どうして、………奥様は生贄を免れたんだ…。もし奥様が選ばれてたなら、……紗音は、……紗音は、死ななくて済んだのにッ…」

units.text: "...Why... ......was Madam not chosen as a sacrifice...? If only she had been chosen, ......Shannon wouldn't, ......Shannon wouldn't have had to die..."
units.note: Both narrow escaping sacrifice into not being chosen. Following hypothetical selection does not rule out surviving selection.
units.japanese: 「…どうして、………奥様は生贄を免れたんだ…。もし奥様が選ばれてたなら、……紗音は、……紗音は、死ななくて済んだのにッ…」

description: WH assigns resignation to Genji’s expression as he intervenes and prepares to explain. Japanese describes a trace of resolve or preparedness.
sourceReading: 覚悟 here indicates bracing himself for the disclosure, reinforced by 話す覚悟を決めた later.

units.text: When I tried to further twist up his collar, Genji-san cut between us and spoke. ...There was a slight sense of resignation on his face. ......It looked like he didn't plan on hiding anything.
units.note: MG made up his mind restores resolve; UP resignation retains opposite attitude. Both preserve disclosure warning.
units.japanese: …その表情にはわずかの覚悟がある。

units.text:
When I tried to further twist up his collar, Genji‐san cut between us and spoke. ...There was a slight sense of resignation on his face.
......It looked like he didn't plan on hiding anything.
units.note: MG made up his mind restores resolve; UP resignation retains opposite attitude. Both preserve disclosure warning.
units.japanese:
さらに嘉音くんの胸倉を捻りあげようとすると、源次さんが割って入りながら言った。…その表情にはわずかの覚悟がある。
……隠す気はないらしかった。

description: Battler acknowledges why Genji prefaced the disclosure with a warning, then says a sane person would indeed take offense. WH says Genji refused to mention it and replaces the sanity qualifier with if you really mean it.
sourceReading: 断る here is giving advance notice or a qualification, matching Genji’s warning at row 29421. 正気じゃあ qualifies the hearer’s sane state, not the speaker’s sincerity.

units.text: "......I see, that's why Genji-san refused to mention it.  ...If you really mean it, of course I'd take it badly.  .............So you're saying that a person named Beatrice actually exists?"
units.note: MG retains refusal and sincerity substitution; UP restores prior warning and sane-person response.
units.japanese: 「……なるほど、源次さんが断るだけはあるぜ。…こいつぁ確かに、正気じゃあ気を悪くする。……………つまり、ベアトリーチェっていう名の人物は実在するんだな？」

units.text: "...I see, that's why Genji-san refused to mention it. ...If you really mean it, of course I'd take it badly. .........So, you're saying that a person named Beatrice actually exists?"
units.note: MG retains refusal and sincerity substitution; UP restores prior warning and sane-person response.
units.japanese: 「……なるほど、源次さんが断るだけはあるぜ。…こいつぁ確かに、正気じゃあ気を悪くする。……………つまり、ベアトリーチェっていう名の人物は実在するんだな？」

description: WH renders Battler’s forced laugh drying up as his sobering up, then applies sobering up to the servants’ eyes. This loses the repeated desiccation image of his fading bravado and their increasingly chilling gaze.
sourceReading: 笑いが乾いていく and 目も乾いていく deliberately repeat drying, followed by Kumasawa’s 乾ききった顔.

units.text: However, there was no trace of a joke in the eyes of the three servants. On the surface, I laughed and tried to look unconcerned, but I was quickly starting to sober up. ...Their eyes were also sobering up fast.
units.note: Both retain sobering up for laugh and eyes. UP restores unprecedented facial expression at 198, but repeated drying metaphor remains lost.
units.japanese:
俺の上辺だけの強がった笑いが、みるみる乾いていく。
…彼らの目も、みるみる乾いていく。

units.text: However, there was no trace of a joke in the eyes of the three servants. On the surface, I laughed and tried to look unconcerned, but I was quickly starting to sober up. ...Their eyes were also sobering up fast.
units.note: Both retain sobering up for laugh and eyes. UP restores unprecedented facial expression at 198, but repeated drying metaphor remains lost.
units.japanese:
だが、使用人たち３人の目に冗談めいたものは欠片ほども見当たらない。俺の上辺だけの強がった笑いが、みるみる乾いていく。
…彼らの目も、みるみる乾いていく。

units.text:
However, there was no trace of a joke in the eyes of the three servants. On the surface, I laughed and tried to look unconcerned, but I was quickly starting to sober up.
...Their eyes were also sobering up fast.
units.note: Both retain sobering up for laugh and eyes. UP restores unprecedented facial expression at 198, but repeated drying metaphor remains lost.
units.japanese:
だが、使用人たち３人の目に冗談めいたものは欠片ほども見当たらない。俺の上辺だけの強がった笑いが、みるみる乾いていく。
…彼らの目も、みるみる乾いていく。

description: The source says Maria laughs as though highly amused, though eerily. WH says her laugh almost sounded insane and was extremely eerie.
sourceReading: さもおかしそう describes finding something funny, not apparent insanity.

units.text: Maria's laugh almost sounded insane, ...and it was extremely eerie. ......It was almost like she was laughing at me because I alone didn't understand.
units.note: Both restore amusement without insanity claim, retaining eerie laugh.
units.japanese: 真里亞はさもおかしそうに、…だけれども不気味に笑う。

description: Battler swallows tensely before looking behind him. WH has him hold his breath tightly.
sourceReading: 硬い唾を飲み込みながら is a nervous swallowing action.

units.text: Holding my breath tightly, I slowly looked over my shoulder. ...Of course, there wasn't anyone there. I've known that the whole time! .........However, everyone in the room except me was focusing on that point as if there was someone there.
units.note: Both replace tense swallowing with breath holding before the shoulder glance.
units.japanese: 俺は硬い唾を飲み込みながら、ゆっくりと背後を、肩越しに見る。

units.text: Holding my breath tightly, I slowly looked over my shoulder. ...Of course, there wasn't anyone there. I've known that the whole time! ......However, everyone in the room except me was focusing on that point as if there was someone there.
units.note: Both replace tense swallowing with breath holding before the shoulder glance.
units.japanese:
俺は硬い唾を飲み込みながら、ゆっくりと背後を、肩越しに見る。…もちろん、そこに誰がいるわけもない。
そんなことはさっきからずっと承知してる！………しかし、この部屋にいる俺以外の全員が、そこにいるらしい人物に焦点を合わせているのだ。

units.text:
Holding my breath tightly, I slowly looked over my shoulder. ...Of course, there wasn't anyone there.
I've known that the whole time! .........However, everyone in the room except me was focusing on that point as if there was someone there.
units.note: Both replace tense swallowing with breath holding before the shoulder glance.
units.japanese:
俺は硬い唾を飲み込みながら、ゆっくりと背後を、肩越しに見る。…もちろん、そこに誰がいるわけもない。
そんなことはさっきからずっと承知してる！………しかし、この部屋にいる俺以外の全員が、そこにいるらしい人物に焦点を合わせているのだ。

description: Maria says there is no telling what curse might have struck him without the charm. WH asks whether he realizes what kind of curse Beatrice would have put on him.
sourceReading: どんな呪いが…わかったものじゃない marks inability to know the imagined curse.

units.text: .........You're lucky, Battler.  Good thing that I gave you that charm yesterday, right?  Don't you realize what kind of curse Beatrice would have put on you by now if you hadn't been carrying it around?  ...You really are lucky, Battler.  Kihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihi...!"
units.note: MG implies hearer can realize which curse; UP restores who knows uncertainty about the counterfactual curse.
units.japanese: ………戦人は幸運だよ。昨日、私にお守りをもらっていて良かったね？　それを身につけてなかったら、今頃、ベアトリーチェのどんな呪いが身に及んでいたかわかったものじゃない。…ホントウに幸運なんだよ戦人は。きひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひ…！」
candidates: kind of curse Beatrice would have put

units.text: "......You're lucky, Battler. Good thing I gave you that charm yesterday, right? Don't you realize what kind of curse Beatrice would have put on you by now if you hadn't been carrying it around? ...You really are lucky, Battler. Kihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihi...!"
units.note: MG implies hearer can realize which curse; UP restores who knows uncertainty about the counterfactual curse.
units.japanese: 「………戦人は幸運だよ。昨日、私にお守りをもらっていて良かったね？　それを身につけていなかったら、今頃、ベアトリーチェのどんな呪いが身に及んでいたかわかったものじゃない。…ホントウに幸運なんだよ戦人は。きひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひ…！」
candidates: kind of curse Beatrice would have put

description: Battler can clearly see Maria is displeased while she does not understand his laughter. WH says she realizes it will not be pleasant for her.
sourceReading: 不快そうなのがよくわかる belongs to the narrator’s perception of her present reaction.

units.text: When Maria saw me suddenly start laughing, she stopped. Even though she didn't understand what I was laughing at, she realized it wouldn't be pleasant for her.
units.note: Both assign prospective unpleasantness recognition to Maria rather than Battler observing her displeasure.
units.japanese: 俺が何を笑っているのかわからず、不快そうなのがよくわかる。

units.text: When Maria saw me suddenly start laughing, she stopped. Even though she didn't understand what I was laughing at, she realized it wouldn't be pleasant for her.
units.note: Both assign prospective unpleasantness recognition to Maria rather than Battler observing her displeasure.
units.japanese:
真里亞は俺が突然笑い出すのを見て、笑うのを止める。
俺が何を笑っているのかわからず、不快そうなのがよくわかる。

units.text:
When Maria saw me suddenly start laughing, she stopped.
Even though she didn't understand what I was laughing at, she realized it wouldn't be pleasant for her.
units.note: Both assign prospective unpleasantness recognition to Maria rather than Battler observing her displeasure.
units.japanese:
真里亞は俺が突然笑い出すのを見て、笑うのを止める。
俺が何を笑っているのかわからず、不快そうなのがよくわかる。

description: Battler says his safety is not thanks to the charm, which he has lost. WH says the charm cannot be the only reason he is alive, allowing it to remain a contributing cause.
sourceReading: お守りのお陰でもねぇ denies credit to the charm; no only qualifier is present.

units.text: ......That means the charm can't be the only reason I'm alive now, and even though I should have been cursed by the witch, I'm perfectly fine.  ......Sorry, but I don't believe in things I don't see with my own eyes.
units.note: MG cannot be the only reason leaves charm as contributing cause; UP cannot be the reason restores categorical rebuttal. Neither establishes exact loss time.
units.japanese: ……だから俺が今この瞬間に無事なのはお守りのお陰でもねぇし、なら魔女さまの呪いがあって当然なのに、今この瞬間もピンピンしてる。……悪いが俺は自分の目で見たものしか信じねぇ。

units.text: "...So the charm can't be the only reason I'm alive now, and even though I should've been cursed by the witch, I'm perfectly fine. ...Sorry, but I don't believe in things I don't see with my own eyes."
units.note: MG cannot be the only reason leaves charm as contributing cause; UP cannot be the reason restores categorical rebuttal. Neither establishes exact loss time.
units.japanese: 「……だから俺が今この瞬間に無事なのはお守りのお陰でもねぇし、なら魔女さまの呪いがあって当然なのに、今この瞬間もピンピンしてる。……悪いが俺は自分の目で見たものしか信じねぇ」

description: WH supplies a preference for a short nap where the source describes wanting a breather or break after eating.
sourceReading: 一服 does not establish sleep; in this context it can mean a rest or smoke break.

units.text: Some people usually head to the bathroom after a meal; others prefer to take a short nap. It seemed that several people had gone out of the parlor, just like I did when I went to the kitchen to drink some water. In the end, Natsuhi's order to keep everyone packed together in the parlor, that no one be left alone and that no one leave the parlor, had to be withdrawn, however reluctantly.
units.note: MG relax restores a break; UP still specifies nap.
units.japanese: 食事が終われば、便所に行きたいヤツもいれば一服したくなるヤツもいる。

units.text: Some people usually head to the bathroom after a meal; others prefer to take a short nap. It seemed that several people had gone out of the parlor, just like I did when I went to the kitchen to drink some water. In the end, Aunt Natsuhi's order to keep everyone packed together in the parlor was reluctantly withdrawn, under the conditions that: no one was to be on their own, and no one was to go far from the parlor.
units.note: MG relax restores a break; UP still specifies nap.
units.japanese: 食事が終われば、便所に行きたいヤツもいれば一服したくなるヤツもいる。俺が厨房へ水を飲みに行ったように、客間から外出した人間は少なくないようだった。結局、夏妃伯母さんの、全員客間に缶詰の号令は、ひとりにならないこと、客間から離れないことが守られるならと、渋々ではあるが撤回されることになった。

description: WH includes no-one-alone and no-one-leaving within the order that was withdrawn. Japanese allows release from compulsory confinement only if no one is alone and people do not go away from the parlor.
sourceReading: ひとりにならないこと、客間から離れないことが守られるなら states conditions retained for relaxing confinement. 離れない must accommodate the explicitly permitted nearby excursions.

units.text: Some people usually head to the bathroom after a meal; others prefer to take a short nap. It seemed that several people had gone out of the parlor, just like I did when I went to the kitchen to drink some water. In the end, Natsuhi's order to keep everyone packed together in the parlor, that no one be left alone and that no one leave the parlor, had to be withdrawn, however reluctantly.
units.note: Both explicitly retain no-one-alone and proximity to parlor as conditions on relaxing confinement.
units.japanese: 結局、夏妃伯母さんの、全員客間に缶詰の号令は、ひとりにならないこと、客間から離れないことが守られるならと、渋々ではあるが撤回されることになった。

description: Battler calls people contrary after they resist compulsory confinement but return when free to leave. WH calls them hypocrites.
sourceReading: 天邪鬼 describes doing the opposite or resisting being told what to do.

units.text: ...I guess it's like 'The North Wind and the Sun'. If you force someone to stay shut in, they'll resist, but if you tell them to do whatever they want, they'll come back, obediently. People sure are hypocrites.
units.note: MG not doing what told restores contrariness; UP hypocrites retains moral accusation.
units.japanese: 人間ってのは天邪鬼なもんだ。

units.text:
...Like that fable. You know, "The North Wind and the Sun".
If you force someone to stay shut in, they'll resist, but if you tell them to do whatever they want, they'll come back, obediently. People sure are hypocrites.
units.note: MG not doing what told restores contrariness; UP hypocrites retains moral accusation.
units.japanese:
…ほらあれだ。北風と太陽ってヤツ。
無理に閉じ込めようとするとみんな抵抗するが、じゃあどうぞお好きにというと大人しく戻ってくる。人間ってのは天邪鬼なもんだ。

description: WH replaces finding lack of individuality intolerable with starting to gain individuality.
sourceReading: 没個性なのが許せなくなる supplies dissatisfaction as the motive for later differentiation.

units.text: Right when humans are born, no one has any individuality, Even so, when they reach their growth period, their sense of self starts to be born, and they start to gain a sense of individuality. They want to be different from other people. ...But that doesn't mean that they will find that they're different from the others in their class, since they are learning the same thing in school and forced into the same lifestyle.
units.note: MG no longer asserts gaining individuality but still omits finding its absence intolerable; wanting difference at 371 supplies motive partially. UP retains gaining individuality in place of intolerance.
units.japanese: ところが成長期を迎え、自我ってやつが生まれ始めると、没個性なのが許せなくなる。

units.text: When humans are born, no one has any individuality. However, when they reach their growth period, their sense of self starts to be born. They want to be different than other people. ...But since everyone else in their class is learning the same things at the same rate and being forced into the same lifestyle, of course they aren't going to find anything that makes them different from everyone else around them.
units.note: MG no longer asserts gaining individuality but still omits finding its absence intolerable; wanting difference at 371 supplies motive partially. UP retains gaining individuality in place of intolerance.
units.japanese:
人間、生まれたばかりの時は誰だって没個性だ。
ところが成長期を迎え、自我ってやつが生まれ始めると、没個性なのが許せなくなる。人と違う何かを持ちたくなる。…しかしだからと言って、学校で等しく同じことを習い、同じ生活を強いられている自分に、クラスの他の連中と違う何かを得られるはずもない。

units.text:
Right when humans are born, no one has any individuality.
However, when they reach their growth period, and their sense of self starts to be born, they start to gain a sense of individuality. They want to be different from other people. ...But of course, they will find that they're no different from the others in their class, since they are learning the same thing in school and forced into the same lifestyle.
units.note: MG no longer asserts gaining individuality but still omits finding its absence intolerable; wanting difference at 371 supplies motive partially. UP retains gaining individuality in place of intolerance.
units.japanese:
人間、生まれたばかりの時は誰だって没個性だ。
ところが成長期を迎え、自我ってやつが生まれ始めると、没個性なのが許せなくなる。人と違う何かを持ちたくなる。…しかしだからと言って、学校で等しく同じことを習い、同じ生活を強いられている自分に、クラスの他の連中と違う何かを得られるはずもない。

description: Japanese describes tough-acting children mocking those around them as childish, then ironically calls them cute children searching for themselves. WH describes people who call this behavior childish and realize it is a child’s self-search.
sourceReading: 周りを子どもっぽいと言って馬鹿にしながらワルぶる連中 identifies the rebellious actors, not outside commentators.

units.text: When they realize that, they start off by breaking the rules, in what's called the rebellious age. Since everyone follows the rules, they want to show off their individuality by breaking them. ...Even people who call this behavior childish and make fun of it, will realize that it's just a cute kid searching for themselves when they look at it this way.
units.note: Both correctly assign childish mockery to tough-acting children, then reframe those children as self-searching.
units.japanese: …周りを子どもっぽいと言って馬鹿にしながらワルぶる連中も、こうして見りゃあ可愛いお子様の自分探しってわけだ。
candidates: people who call this behavior childish

description: WH makes the developmental impulse separation from other children rather than growing out of being a child, merging it with the separately stated desire for individuality.
sourceReading: 子どもから脱却したい means wanting to leave childhood; 他者とは違う then supplies the distinct individuality motive.

units.text: "Therefore, during the period when they try to separate themselves from other children, they also try to take on personalities different from those around them.  If what separates kids and adults is knowledge and experience, then...?"
units.note: MG restores growing out of childhood at 381 but still separates from other children at 395; UP restores both childhood-escape statements.
units.japanese: 「となるとつまり、子どもから脱却したいという衝動を持つ時期に、かつ他者とは違うという個性を持ちたくなる。

units.text: "Therefore, during the period when they try to separate themselves from other children, they also try to take on personality traits different from those around them. And if knowledge and experience is what separates kids and adults..."
units.note: MG restores growing out of childhood at 381 but still separates from other children at 395; UP restores both childhood-escape statements.
units.japanese: 「となるとつまり、子どもから脱却したいという衝動を持つ時期に、かつ他者とは違うという個性を持ちたくなる。子どもからの脱却がつまり、知識や経験なのだとしたら？」

description: WH says Battler was finally able to thank his teacher. Japanese says he only recently became able to feel grateful to the teacher who slapped him.
sourceReading: 感謝できるようになった establishes a change in appreciation, without a communication event.

units.text: ...I actually had been like that. Only recently, I'd finally been able to thank that middle school teacher who had slapped me after school.
units.note: MG thank can imply performed expression; UP explicitly restores becoming able to feel thankful.
units.japanese: そんな俺を放課後にビンタしてくれた中学の先生には、ようやく最近になって感謝できるようになったが。

units.text: ...Okay, that last bit really was true about me. It's only recently that I've been able to thank the middle school teacher who slapped me after school.
units.note: MG thank can imply performed expression; UP explicitly restores becoming able to feel thankful.
units.japanese:
…そりゃー、俺のことだがな。
そんな俺を放課後にビンタしてくれた中学の先生には、ようやく最近になって感謝できるようになったが。

description: WH changes as I said to as you said, children learning to outgrow childhood into we teaching them to awaken, and a convenient delusion prevalent in children’s world into that world growing rapidly.
sourceReading: さっきも言った refers to George’s earlier statement; 子どもたちは…学んで are the learners; 蔓延っている modifies the convenient delusion.

units.text: "As you just said, becoming an adult means gaining knowledge and experience.  We have to teach kids various things so that they can gain knowledge and truly awaken.
units.note: MG restores children learning and prevalent delusion but retains as you said. UP restores as I said and prevalent fantasy but substitutes truly awaken for outgrowing childhood; neither retains original WH we-teaching agency.
units.japanese:
「さっきも言った通り、大人になるというのは、知識や経験を持つことを言う。だから、それを得るために子どもたちは色々なことを学んで子どもを脱却しなければならないんだけど。
…子どもの世界に今も昔も蔓延っている、ある便利な妄想があるんだよ。わかるかい？」

units.text: ...A child's world, both now and in the past, grows rapidly, and there are some delusions which are convenient during that time.  Do you understand?"
units.note: MG restores children learning and prevalent delusion but retains as you said. UP restores as I said and prevalent fantasy but substitutes truly awaken for outgrowing childhood; neither retains original WH we-teaching agency.
units.japanese:
「さっきも言った通り、大人になるというのは、知識や経験を持つことを言う。だから、それを得るために子どもたちは色々なことを学んで子どもを脱却しなければならないんだけど。
…子どもの世界に今も昔も蔓延っている、ある便利な妄想があるんだよ。わかるかい？」

units.text: "As you just said, becoming an adult means gaining knowledge and experience. So, to gain that, it's necessary for children to learn all sorts of things and break free from childhood.
units.note: MG restores children learning and prevalent delusion but retains as you said. UP restores as I said and prevalent fantasy but substitutes truly awaken for outgrowing childhood; neither retains original WH we-teaching agency.
units.japanese:
「さっきも言った通り、大人になるというのは、知識や経験を持つことを言う。だから、それを得るために子どもたちは色々なことを学んで子どもを脱却しなければならないんだけど」
「…子どもの世界に今も昔も蔓延っている、ある便利な妄想があるんだよ。わかるかい？」

units.text: ...However, there are certain "convenient" delusions that you see often in the world of children, both now and in the past. Do you know what I mean?"
units.note: MG restores children learning and prevalent delusion but retains as you said. UP restores as I said and prevalent fantasy but substitutes truly awaken for outgrowing childhood; neither retains original WH we-teaching agency.
units.japanese:
「さっきも言った通り、大人になるというのは、知識や経験を持つことを言う。だから、それを得るために子どもたちは色々なことを学んで子どもを脱却しなければならないんだけど」
「…子どもの世界に今も昔も蔓延っている、ある便利な妄想があるんだよ。わかるかい？」

units.text: "As I said before, becoming an adult means gaining knowledge and experience. So kids must study various things so that they can gain knowledge and truly awaken."
units.note: MG restores children learning and prevalent delusion but retains as you said. UP restores as I said and prevalent fantasy but substitutes truly awaken for outgrowing childhood; neither retains original WH we-teaching agency.
units.japanese:
「さっきも言った通り、大人になるというのは、知識や経験を持つことを言う。だから、それを得るために子どもたちは色々なことを学んで子どもを脱却しなければならないんだけど」
「…子どもの世界に今も昔も蔓延っている、ある便利な妄想があるんだよ。わかるかい？」

units.text: "...There is a specific kind of fantasy useful for this, which is and has always been prolific in the world of children. Do you know what that is?"
units.note: MG restores children learning and prevalent delusion but retains as you said. UP restores as I said and prevalent fantasy but substitutes truly awaken for outgrowing childhood; neither retains original WH we-teaching agency.
units.japanese:
「さっきも言った通り、大人になるというのは、知識や経験を持つことを言う。だから、それを得るために子どもたちは色々なことを学んで子どもを脱却しなければならないんだけど」
「…子どもの世界に今も昔も蔓延っている、ある便利な妄想があるんだよ。わかるかい？」

description: Jessica’s fantasy example is remembering a previous life. WH makes it memories from antiquity, replacing reincarnation-based personal experience with historical antiquity.
sourceReading: 前世 is a prior life, not simply an ancient era.

units.text: "You see it all the time in manga and anime right?  It's kinda like that.  Like memories from antiquity are revived.  Like someone's possessed by the soul of the great something, or whatever."
units.note: Both explicitly restore previous/former life memories, preserving reincarnation example.
units.japanese: 「漫画やアニメに多いだろ？　ほらアレだよ。前世の記憶が蘇って、とか。偉大なる何とかの魂が乗り移って、とか。」

description: George defines parental broad-mindedness as accepting the whole of the child’s identity. WH says whether it is accepted depends on the parent’s broad-mindedness.
sourceReading: 丸ごと受け容れてあげるのが、親の包容力 defines the accepting action as the quality.

units.text: So it's important to go along with them to some degree.  ...Although whether that is accepted is determined by the broad-mindedness of the parent."
units.note: MG retains parent tolerance determining whether to accept. UP restores full acceptance but frames tolerance as prerequisite rather than defining parental broad-mindedness as that acceptance.
units.japanese: だから、ほどほどに付き合ってあげるのが大切なんだよ。…それを丸ごと受け容れてあげるのが、親の包容力というものなんだけどね。」

units.text: So it's important to go along with them to some degree. ...Although the broad-mindedness of the parent determines whether they play along in full or not."
units.note: MG retains parent tolerance determining whether to accept. UP restores full acceptance but frames tolerance as prerequisite rather than defining parental broad-mindedness as that acceptance.
units.japanese: 「だから、ほどほどに付き合ってあげるのが大切なんだよ。…それを丸ごと受け容れてあげるのが、親の包容力というものなんだけどね」

units.text: "So it's important to go along with them to some degree. ...Although to accept it completely requires the tolerance of a parent."
units.note: MG retains parent tolerance determining whether to accept. UP restores full acceptance but frames tolerance as prerequisite rather than defining parental broad-mindedness as that acceptance.
units.japanese: 「だから、ほどほどに付き合ってあげるのが大切なんだよ。…それを丸ごと受け容れてあげるのが、親の包容力というものなんだけどね」

description: WH says it is said an accident will occur if the ritual is omitted. Japanese attributes the warning to the workers and says they claim a major accident is certain.
sourceReading: 職人たちは…必ず大きな事故があると言って identifies both speaker and certainty.

units.text: Of course, even though everyone accepts that curses and the like don't exist in the modern era, ...people are still afraid and still have a little respect for them. You often see it when, in a residential area, someone is building a house, and they call a Shinto priest for a ceremony to honor the god of that plot of land. ...You might think that was just a big waste of time and money, but it is said that if the workers don't do that, a big accident will occur, so they never neglect to do it.
units.note: MG restores big accident but keeps impersonal it is said rather than workers claim. UP attributes prediction to workers; will occur preserves categorical forecast in their speech.
units.japanese: …あんなの時間とカネの無駄遣いだろうと思うかもしれないが、職人たちはこれをやらないと必ず大きな事故があると言って、決して疎かにしないという。

units.text: Of course, even though everyone accepts that curses and the like don't exist in the modern era, ...people are still afraid and still have a little respect for them. You often see it when, in a residential area, someone is building a house, and they call a Shinto priest for a ceremony to honor the god of that plot of land. ...You might think that was just a big waste of time and money, but it is said that if the workers don't do that, a big accident will occur, so they never neglect to do it.
units.note: MG restores big accident but keeps impersonal it is said rather than workers claim. UP attributes prediction to workers; will occur preserves categorical forecast in their speech.
units.japanese: 確かに、祟りなんて存在しないと誰もが認めるこの現代であっても、…人はそれを恐れ、最低限の敬いを残している。家を建てる時に、神主さんを呼んで土地の神さまに敬いを示す儀式は、住宅地でもよく見かけるはずだ。…あんなの時間とカネの無駄遣いだろうと思うかもしれないが、職人たちはこれをやらないと必ず大きな事故があると言って、決して疎かにしないという。

description: WH says unbaptized souls go to hell if they have even the slightest sin. Japanese tentatively recalls that unbaptized souls meet the conditions despite having the least guilt.
sourceReading: 一番罪が軽いとは言え is concessive, not conditional; 確か and はず mark uncertain recollection.

units.text: And this wasn't limited to Japan. It's probably similar to how people baptize babies. Of course, by the Christian doctrine, if unbaptized souls have even the slightest amount of sin, they will still go to hell.
units.note: MG restores if I remember right uncertainty but retains even slightest sin condition. UP restores least-guilt concessive and tentative recollection.
units.japanese: 確か、キリスト教の教義じゃ、洗礼を受けない魂は一番罪が軽いとは言え、地獄送りの要件を満たしていたはずだ。

units.text: And this wasn't limited to Japan. It's probably similar to how foreigners baptize babies. If I remember right, by Christian doctrine, if unbaptized souls have even the slightest amount of sin, they will still go to hell.
units.note: MG restores if I remember right uncertainty but retains even slightest sin condition. UP restores least-guilt concessive and tentative recollection.
units.japanese:
何も日本に限ったものじゃない。
多分、外国人が赤ん坊に洗礼を受けさせるのも似たようなもんだろう。確か、キリスト教の教義じゃ、洗礼を受けない魂は一番罪が軽いとは言え、地獄送りの要件を満たしていたはずだ。

description: Jessica responds that Battler remembers well. WH gives I remember it well, redirecting the acknowledgment to her own memory.
sourceReading: よく覚えてるなぁ addresses Battler after his detailed recall of her joke.

units.text: "I remember it well.  ...Normally, you'd say some little imps took them, but on this island, it's Beatrice.  Man, what a stupid story."
units.note: Both credit Battler good memory, not Jessica own recollection.
units.japanese: 「よく覚えてるなぁ。

description: Battler says the culprit wants to insist that a nineteenth person committed the crime. WH says if that were the case we would have to accept nineteenth-person responsibility.
sourceReading: 訴えたくて仕方がない describes the culprit’s intent to communicate, not a logically compulsory conclusion for the observers.

units.text: ".........In other words, on this island, there's a rule that Beatrice is blamed for anything that couldn't have been done by humans.  Things that humans can't do.  ......How many humans are there?  There's 18.  ............So the culprit, knowing about this rule, wanted to make it appear that this crime was the work of the witch.  If that were the case, we would have to accept that a 19th person was responsible.
units.note: Both assign desire to advertise nineteenth-person responsibility to culprit, rather than necessity for readers to accept actual responsibility. MG proves is stronger connective, limited by Battler explicit no basis or proof at 639.
units.japanese: 「………つまり、この島では、人間にはできないことはベアトリーチェの仕業と置き換えることができるルールがあるってわけだ。人間にはできないこと。……人間は何人だ？　１８人だ。…………つまり犯人は、この島のルールに則って、この事件は魔女の仕業だとアピールしてることになる。つまりそれは、１９人目の仕業ですよと、訴えたくて仕方がないわけだ。
candidates: case, we would have to accept

description: WH says Beatrice refers to interest on all the gold that was created. Japanese says everything generated with the gold as capital is interest.
sourceReading: 黄金を資本に生み出したもの全て includes the family’s subsequent wealth and, in the following interpretation, descendants and household.

units.text: "...Grandfather was granted the gold, and the Ushiromiya house prospered.  In other words, Beatrice is talking about the interest on all of the gold that was created.  ......In other words..."
units.note: Both restore everything produced using gold as capital; UP birthed anticipates bloodline interpretation without reversing financial relation.
units.japanese: 「…お祖父さまは黄金を授かり、右代宮家を再興した。つまり、黄金を資本に生み出したもの全てが利子だってベアトリーチェは言っている。……つまり…、」

description: WH introduces halfway completed for collection that is merely still in progress.
sourceReading: まだ途中 is still underway or unfinished, without a specified fraction.

units.text: "If you read the letter that way, ...these murders are just Beatrice legitimately collecting interest.  ...If that's the case, these crimes will continue.  ...Because the collection of interest is still only halfway completed."
units.note: Both retain halfway completed rather than merely in progress. Source gives no numerical completion fraction; surviving surname holders and killed servants establish broader scope only.
units.japanese: 「あの手紙をそう読み解いたなら、…この殺人はベアトリーチェが行った正当な利子の回収ということになる。…となれば、この事件はまだ続くよ。…利子の回収は、まだ途中なんだからね。」

units.text: "If you interpret the letter that way, ...these murders are just Beatrice legitimately collecting interest. ...If that's the case, these crimes will continue. ...Because the collection of interest is still only halfway completed."
units.note: Both retain halfway completed rather than merely in progress. Source gives no numerical completion fraction; surviving surname holders and killed servants establish broader scope only.
units.japanese: 「あの手紙をそう読み解いたなら、…この殺人はベアトリーチェが行った正当な利子の回収ということになる。…となれば、この事件はまだ続くよ。…利子の回収は、まだ途中なんだからね」

units.text: "If you read the letter that way, ...these murders are just Beatrice legitimately collecting interest. ...If that's the case, these crimes will continue. ...Because the collection of interest is still only halfway completed."
units.note: Both retain halfway completed rather than merely in progress. Source gives no numerical completion fraction; surviving surname holders and killed servants establish broader scope only.
units.japanese: 「あの手紙をそう読み解いたなら、…この殺人はベアトリーチェが行った正当な利子の回収ということになる。…となれば、この事件はまだ続くよ。…利子の回収は、まだ途中なんだからね」

description: Jessica asks why the culprit did not exercise their apparent ability to kill more, potentially everyone in one night. WH says they should have killed more and drops the explicit one-night scope of killing all sleepers.
sourceReading: 殺せたはず concerns capacity; 一晩で bounds the proposed massacre to one night.

units.text: ...But that's weird, George nii-san!  In that case, why only six people?  They should have killed a lot more.  In the worst case, it should have been possible for them to assault everyone while they were sleeping and kill them.  Why didn't they do that?!"
units.note: Both restore possibility/capacity rather than recommendation and explicitly retain killing everyone in a single night.
units.japanese: …でもおかしいよ譲治兄さん！　ならどうして６人だけ？　他に大勢殺せたはず。下手をすれば、寝込みを襲って全員を一晩で殺すことも可能だったはず。どうしてそれをしなかったの？！」

description: WH says understanding depends on how near the points are to the line. Japanese compares the proximity of the two endpoints being connected; distant connections require a greater speculative leap.
sourceReading: 線の両端の点 describes endpoints, and 距離 compares them to each other.

units.text: The closer the points are to the line, the easier it is, intellectually, to understand them. ...And the farther away they are from the line, the more fragmented everything becomes. Therefore, as far the distance between these guesses was concerned, we should call this theory crazy. ...However, if the distance is narrow between the points, you could call the idea limited.
units.note: Both compare distance between endpoints, not points proximity to a line.
units.japanese:
その結ぶ線の両端の点は、距離が近ければ近いほど理知的で理解に容易だ。
…そして離れていれば離れているほどそれを欠いている。

description: WH says his approach was not a mistake. Japanese says it should not be wrong despite seeming far-fetched, retaining a qualification in his self-encouragement.
sourceReading: 間違ってもいないはず expresses expected correctness rather than verified correctness.

units.text: If you can't imagine, you can't reason. ......What I was doing might have been crazy, ...but it also wasn't a mistake. Only the power of imagination could pull out a clue from the darkness. ......And the power of reasoning could tie those clues together.
units.note: MG sure it is not a mistake retains strengthened confidence; UP should not be wrong restores self-encouraging qualification.
units.japanese: ……俺のしていることは、ぶっ飛んでいるかもしれないが、…間違ってもいないはずなんだ。

units.text: If you can't imagine, you can't reason. ...What I'm doing now might be way out there, ...but I'm sure it isn't a mistake either. Only the power of imagination can pull clues out from the darkness. ...And then I can use the power of reasoning to tie those clues together.
units.note: MG sure it is not a mistake retains strengthened confidence; UP should not be wrong restores self-encouraging qualification.
units.japanese:
想像なくして推理もない。
……俺のしていることは、ぶっ飛んでいるかもしれないが、…間違ってもいないはずなんだ。想像の力だけが、闇の中から手掛かりを見つけ出す。
……そしてそれを、推理の力で結びつける。

description: WH says attack with a wall of truth. Japanese makes truth the target of an area-covering volley of speculative ideas.
sourceReading: 面で真実に襲い掛かれ continues firing many arrows of imagination to hit a distant target, rather than asserting those arrows already are truth.

units.text: ......They say that most people who have died in battles were killed by wounds from arrows. ......In a battle you couldn't just shoot off one arrow. You shoot off a whole bunch of arrows at once, and attack the enemy soldiers with a wall of them.  ......So shoot them, over and over! 'Attack with a wall of truth...!'
units.note: Both identify truth as target and arrow wall as means. Prior volley context supplies area-covering metaphor.
units.japanese: “面で真実に襲い掛かれ…！”
candidates: Attack with a wall of truth

description: WH asks whether Kinzo was kidnapped and taken somewhere. Japanese asks whether he was kidnapped and is being held captive somewhere.
sourceReading: 捕らわれている adds continuing captivity, not just relocation.

units.text: If you think about it that way, it explained Grandfather's mysterious disappearance. If the culprit had attacked Grandfather, then judging by the state the six corpses were left in, he should have been displayed somewhere with that horrible makeup added. But despite that, we still hadn't found him. ......Did that mean that Grandfather was kidnapped, and had been taken somewhere?!
units.note: Both restore being held somewhere, corroborated in Eva hypothetical confinement paraphrase; not just transported elsewhere.
units.japanese: ……つまり祖父さまは拉致されて、どこかに捕らわれている？！

description: WH says there is no way in or out except for that key. Eva’s Japanese says the study cannot be entered from outside without the key.
sourceReading: 外から入ることは limits the keyed restriction to external entry.

units.text: "It's simple.  .........Father's study is a closed room, with no way in or out except for that key, right?  I want to verify whether that's true.  There is one entrance to Father's study.  What about the window?  Any other entrances or exits?"
units.note: Both require key for way in or out, whereas source defines external entry only. Following entrance-only testimony does not establish inability to open door from inside without key.
units.japanese: 「シンプルな話よ。………お父様の書斎はその鍵がなければ外から入ることはできない密室よ？　その定義の確認をしたいの。お父様の部屋には入口がひとつある。あとは窓？　他に出入り口は？」
candidates: way in or out except for that key

units.text: "It's simple. ......Father's study is a closed room, with no way in or out except for that key, right? I want to verify whether that's true. There is one entrance to Father's study. What about the window? Any other entrances or exits?"
units.note: Both require key for way in or out, whereas source defines external entry only. Following entrance-only testimony does not establish inability to open door from inside without key.
units.japanese: 「シンプルな話よ。………お父様の書斎はその鍵がなければ外から入ることはできない密室よ？　その定義の確認をしたいの。お父様の部屋には入口がひとつある。あとは窓？　他に出入り口は？」
candidates: way in or out except for that key

units.text: "It's simple. .........Don't forget, Father's study is a locked room, with no way in or out except for that key. I want to double‐check how that's being defined. There is one entrance to Father's study. And also the windows? Any other entrances or exits?"
units.note: Both require key for way in or out, whereas source defines external entry only. Following entrance-only testimony does not establish inability to open door from inside without key.
units.japanese: 「シンプルな話よ。………お父様の書斎はその鍵がなければ外から入ることはできない密室よ？　その定義の確認をしたいの。お父様の部屋には入口がひとつある。あとは窓？　他に出入り口は？」
candidates: way in or out except for that key

description: Eva and Natsuhi describe picking up a folded receipt. WH gives throwing away trash in both turns, introducing disposal of the evidence.
sourceReading: 拾った means picked up; neither turn states what happened to the receipt afterward.

units.text: "Come on.  You threw away some trash, right?  A folded receipt."
units.note: Both restore receipt pickup rather than throwing it away; evidence disposal not introduced.
units.japanese:
「ほらぁ。ゴミを拾ったでしょ？　畳んだレシートを。」
「……確かに、そんなゴミを拾った気がします。それが何か…？」

units.text: "......I do seem to remember throwing away some trash.  What does that have to do with...?"
units.note: Both restore receipt pickup rather than throwing it away; evidence disposal not introduced.
units.japanese:
「ほらぁ。ゴミを拾ったでしょ？　畳んだレシートを。」
「……確かに、そんなゴミを拾った気がします。それが何か…？」

description: Eva identifies a shop she stopped at before reaching the airport. WH locates it in the airport.
sourceReading: 飛行場に着く前に寄った売店 explicitly places the stop before airport arrival.

units.text: "I got that receipt when I bought some candy at a store in the airport." Eva oba-san pulled a small bag of candy out of her handbag.
units.note: MG restores store before arriving at airport; UP retains store in airport.
units.japanese: 「そのレシートは、私が飛行場に着く前に寄った売店で飴玉を買った時にもらったものよ。」

units.text: "I got that receipt when I bought some candy at a store in the airport."
units.note: MG restores store before arriving at airport; UP retains store in airport.
units.japanese: 「そのレシートは、私が飛行場に着く前に寄った売店で飴玉を買った時にもらったものよ」

description: Eva denies both having foreseen something and planning to trap Natsuhi. WH says maybe she had a little foresight while retaining only the trap denial.
sourceReading: 何かを予見してたとか、ましてや…そんなのじゃ断じてない negates both listed explanations.

units.text: "It was really just on a whim, you see?  Maybe I had a little foresight, but I definitely wasn't planning on setting a trap for Natsuhi nee-san or anything.
units.note: Both deny foresight and deliberate trap; no admitted anticipation remains.
units.japanese: 「本当にこれは気まぐれよ？　何かを予見してたとか、ましてや夏妃姉さんを罠に掛けようとか、そんなのじゃ断じてないんだから。

description: Hideyoshi addresses Natsuhi and says she claims to have met and spoken to Father that morning. WH says you said that she met with him, supplying a different female participant and omitting speaking.
sourceReading: 夏妃さんは…会って話をした言うとる keeps Natsuhi as claimant and participant.

units.text: "So at that time, Father was still definitely in his room.  ...However, Natsuhi nee-san.  When you found out that he wasn't there, I hear that all ways in or out of the study were closed, right? ......But even so, you said that she met with him this morning."
units.note: MG restores Natsuhi as addressed person who met Kinzo but omits speaking; UP restores meeting and talking.
units.japanese: …だがな、夏妃姉さん。不在だった書斎は窓も扉も全て締め切られた状態だったそうやないか。……なのに夏妃さんは今朝、お父さんに会って話をした言うとる。」

units.text: "So at that time, Father was still definitely in his room. ...However, Natsuhi nee-san, when you found out he wasn't there, it looks like all ways in or out of the study were closed, right? ...But even so, you said you met with him this morning."
units.note: MG restores Natsuhi as addressed person who met Kinzo but omits speaking; UP restores meeting and talking.
units.japanese: 「ここまでは間違いなくお父さんも部屋にいたやろな。…だがな、夏妃姉さん。不在だった書斎は窓も扉も全て閉め切られた状態だったそうやないか。……なのに夏妃さんは今朝、お父さんに会って話をした言うとる」

description: WH has Nanjo ask why everyone has become gloomy instead of why the exchange has become hostile.
sourceReading: 険悪 refers to deteriorating antagonism among participants.

units.text: "......I, ......I don't understand why everyone has become so gloomy.  Could someone explain it to me...?"
units.note: Both describe gloomy mood instead of hostile exchange; surrounding confrontation does not correct Nanjo wording.
units.japanese: 「……わ、……私には皆さんが何を険悪になっとるのかわかりません。…どなたか、説明してくださいますかな…。」

units.text: "......I-I don't understand why everyone has become so gloomy. Could someone please explain it to me...?"
units.note: Both describe gloomy mood instead of hostile exchange; surrounding confrontation does not correct Nanjo wording.
units.japanese: 「……わ、……私には皆さんが何を険悪になっとるのかわかりません。…どなたか、説明してくださいますかな…」

units.text: "......I, ......I don't understand why everyone has become so gloomy. ...Could someone explain it to me...?"
units.note: Both describe gloomy mood instead of hostile exchange; surrounding confrontation does not correct Nanjo wording.
units.japanese: 「……わ、……私には皆さんが何を険悪になっとるのかわかりません。…どなたか、説明してくださいますかな…」

description: Eva describes fabricating an alibi by falsely reporting the time someone was alive. WH describes confusing time of death, obscuring the testimony-based mechanism.
sourceReading: 生存時刻を偽る specifically concerns a false alive-at-time claim, tied to Natsuhi’s reported morning meeting.

units.text: But Jessica-chan.  You can't say that there was no reason for her to lie and say that Grandfather was in the room, right?  You see it every once in a while in mystery novels, don't you?  That trick of confusing the time of death to create an alibi."
units.note: Both replace false reported survival time at 942 with time-of-death manipulation. Later time-of-death staging remains source content, but does not restore the distinct testimony mechanism in initial explanation.
units.japanese: でもね、朱志香ちゃん？　お父様の在室を偽る価値がまったくないとは限らないのよぅ？　推理小説でもたまに出てくるでしょ？　生存時刻を偽ることによって自分のアリバイを偽証するトリックよぅ。」

units.text: But Jessica-chan, you can't be sure she had no reason to lie and say that Grandfather was in the room. After all, you see it in mystery novels every now and then. That trick where people fake the time of death to create an alibi for themselves."
units.note: Both replace false reported survival time at 942 with time-of-death manipulation. Later time-of-death staging remains source content, but does not restore the distinct testimony mechanism in initial explanation.
units.japanese: 「でもね、朱志香ちゃん？　お父様の在室を偽る価値がまったくないとは限らないのよぅ？　推理小説でもたまに出てくるでしょ？　生存時刻を偽ることによって自分のアリバイを偽証するトリックよぅ」

units.text: "But Jessica‐chan. You can't say that there's no possible reason for her to lie about Father being in the room, right? You see it every once in a while in detective novels, don't you? That trick of confusing the time of death to create an alibi."
units.note: Both replace false reported survival time at 942 with time-of-death manipulation. Later time-of-death staging remains source content, but does not restore the distinct testimony mechanism in initial explanation.
units.japanese: 「でもね、朱志香ちゃん？　お父様の在室を偽る価値がまったくないとは限らないのよぅ？　推理小説でもたまに出てくるでしょ？　生存時刻を偽ることによって自分のアリバイを偽証するトリックよぅ」

description: Eva says examination results are strongly affected by environment and individual differences. WH says it is easy to influence results by messing around with the surroundings, omitting individual variation and adding deliberate intervention.
sourceReading: 左右されやすい names sensitivity to conditions; no agent manipulating conditions is specified.

units.text: "......You think so?  This morning, when Doctor Nanjo looked at the corpses, he was only able to give a vague estimate of the time of death, right?  It would be very easy to influence the results of the autopsy by messing around with the corpses' surroundings.  It's a very relative estimate with an uncertainty of several hours.
units.note: Both restore environmental and individual effects rather than deliberate manipulation.
units.japanese: 「……そうかしらぁ？　今朝、南條先生が亡くなった人たちの死体を見て、死亡時刻を曖昧に見積もられたわよぅ？　検死結果は、環境や個体差に非常に左右されやすい。数時間単位で誤差の出る非常にアバウトなものなのよぅ。

description: Hideyoshi rejects treating the alibi mechanism as only a classic-fiction trick. WH states it is an old trick, losing the negation.
sourceReading: 古典のトリックとちゃう contrasts with Jessica’s claim that it would not work in modern Japan.

units.text: "...However, for an alibi, that's more than enough!  It's an old trick!  It's a trick that works well enough!  ......Natsuhi nee-san.  It's not like we want to suspect you, alright?  We just want you to prove your innocence so we don't have to suspect you."
units.note: MG calls it old trick despite source negation; UP not just for classics restores present applicability contrast.
units.japanese: 「…しかしアリバイの世界は数時間もあれば充分やで！　古典のトリックとちゃう！　充分に通用するトリックなんや！　……夏妃姉さん。わしら、あんたを疑いたいわけやないんやで？　疑いとうないから、潔白を示してほしいだけなんや。」

units.text: "...However, for an alibi, that's more than enough! It's an old trick! It's a trick that works well enough! ...Natsuhi nee-san, it's not like we want to suspect you, okay? We just want you to prove your innocence so we don't have to suspect you."
units.note: MG calls it old trick despite source negation; UP not just for classics restores present applicability contrast.
units.japanese: 「…しかしアリバイの世界は数時間もあれば充分やで！　古典のトリックとちゃう！　充分に通用するトリックなんや！　……夏妃姉さん。わしら、あんたを疑いたいわけやないんやで？　疑いとうないから、潔白を示してほしいだけなんや」

description: The narrator says Natsuhi is induced by Eva’s provocation to raise the rifle. WH says she did so after being told to by Eva, asserting an instruction.
sourceReading: 誘導されるように describes being led or goaded into the action, following Eva’s taunts.

units.text: It wasn't like Natsuhi oba-san had been actually holding that gun at the ready and threatening anyone. But after she was told to by Eva oba-san, she did hold it at the ready! ...Unsurprisingly, once things got to this stage, Jessica and Genji-san tried to stop her.
units.note: MG egged on restores provocation; UP told to asserts instruction as narrator account. Source dialogue taunts shooting, but narrated raising is induced, not direct compliance with a raising command.
units.japanese: でも、絵羽伯母さんに誘導されるように銃を構えさせられてしまう！

units.text:
It wasn't like Aunt Natsuhi had been actually holding that gun at the ready and threatening anyone.
But after she was told to by Auntie Eva, she did hold it at the ready! ...Unsurprisingly, once things got to this stage, Jessica and Genji‐san tried to stop her.
units.note: MG egged on restores provocation; UP told to asserts instruction as narrator account. Source dialogue taunts shooting, but narrated raising is induced, not direct compliance with a raising command.
units.japanese:
別に夏妃伯母さんは銃を構えて威嚇してたわけじゃない。
でも、絵羽伯母さんに誘導されるように銃を構えさせられてしまう！…さすがにこの段階になって、朱志香や源次さんが止めに入った。

description: Natsuhi says she cannot explain it and need not. WH says she cannot explain it so it is unnecessary, inventing a causal justification.
sourceReading: 説明もできませんし、不要です coordinates inability with a separate rejection of obligation.

units.text: "I can't explain that so it's unnecessary!!"
units.note: Both separate inability to explain and refusal of necessity without causal so.
units.japanese: 「そんなこと、説明もできませんし、不要です！！」

description: Battler notes that the competing accounts have now been presented. WH says it is time for him to have his say, replacing his assessment of the available arguments with a turn-taking statement.
sourceReading: 言い分は出揃った describes the accounts being all assembled.

units.text: ............Hmmmm.  ...Looks like it's time for me to have my say.
units.note: MG everyone views on record and UP everyone else said piece both assess available arguments; neither replaces it with Battler own turn announcement.
units.japanese: ……………ふむ。…言い分は出揃ったようだな。

description: Battler says Eva’s bluff of a checkmate will not stand. WH says her argument is not good enough for a clear checkmate, losing the characterization of her certainty as bluff.
sourceReading: ハッタリのチェックメイト identifies the purported decisive conclusion as a bluff.

units.text: "If you only look at it from one angle, then you'd be stuck thinking that it had to be Natsuhi oba-san.  ...It's not like I'm defending her, but that won't be good enough for a clear checkmate.
units.note: Both explicitly restore bluff checkmate rather than merely insufficient certainty.
units.japanese: 「一方からしか見られないから、夏妃伯母さんしかありえないって思い込んじまうのさ。…別に夏妃伯母さんを擁護するわけじゃねぇが、そんなハッタリのチェックメイトじゃ、通用しねぇってことさ。
candidates: good enough for a clear checkmate

description: Battler taunts Eva as the aunt to whom all Kinzo’s inheritance would fall. WH describes all his wealth as already having suddenly fallen into her hands.
sourceReading: 遺産が全部転がり込む identifies her prospective benefit in the inheritance argument, not a completed transfer.

units.text: You've been trying to force Natsuhi oba-san to explain.  I'm sure you can prove your own innocence, right?!  Eva oba-san, who's had all of Grandfather's wealth suddenly plopped down right into her hands!!"
units.note: Both describe wealth already fallen into Eva hands instead of prospective inheritance. Counteraccusation is rhetorical, not actual completed transfer.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんに釈明を強いたんだ。あんたにはもちろん、自身の潔白を釈明できるんだろうなぁ？！　祖父さまの遺産が全部転がり込む絵羽伯母さんよぅ！！」

units.text: "You've been trying to force Aunt Natsuhi to explain. So I'm sure you can prove your own innocence, right?! Especially now that all of Grandfather's wealth has suddenly plopped down right into your hands!!"
units.note: Both describe wealth already fallen into Eva hands instead of prospective inheritance. Counteraccusation is rhetorical, not actual completed transfer.
units.japanese: 「夏妃伯母さんに釈明を強いたんだ。あんたにはもちろん、自身の潔白を釈明できるんだろうなぁ？！　祖父さまの遺産が全部転がり込む絵羽伯母さんよぅ！！」

units.text: "You've been trying to force Aunt Natsuhi to explain. I'm sure you can prove your own innocence, right?! Auntie Eva, who's had all of Grandfather's wealth suddenly dropped right into her hands!!"
units.note: Both describe wealth already fallen into Eva hands instead of prospective inheritance. Counteraccusation is rhetorical, not actual completed transfer.
units.japanese: 「夏妃伯母さんに釈明を強いたんだ。あんたにはもちろん、自身の潔白を釈明できるんだろうなぁ？！　祖父さまの遺産が全部転がり込む絵羽伯母さんよぅ！！」

description: George says everyone equally belongs in the suspect pool. WH says he thinks everyone is equally suspicious, moving from equal inclusion to equal strength of suspicion.
sourceReading: 等しく全員が容疑者 means all are suspects without singling Natsuhi out.

units.text: But, like Battler-kun said, that's not enough to prove that Natsuhi oba-san is this culprit.  ......I think everyone's equally suspicious.  It's not right for only Natsuhi oba-san to be persecuted."
units.note: Both say equally suspicious rather than equal inclusion in suspect pool; no evidence equalizing degree of suspicion given.
units.japanese: でもそれは、戦人くんの言うとおり、夏妃伯母さんが何某かの犯人であることを断定できるものじゃない。……僕たちは等しく全員が容疑者なんだ。夏妃伯母さんだけが責められる道理はない。」

units.text: But, like Battler-kun said, that's not enough to prove that Aunt Natsuhi was responsible for some plot. ...We're all equally suspicious. It's not right for only Aunt Natsuhi to be persecuted."
units.note: Both say equally suspicious rather than equal inclusion in suspect pool; no evidence equalizing degree of suspicion given.
units.japanese: 「でもそれは、戦人くんの言うとおり、夏妃伯母さんが何某かの犯人であることを断定できるものじゃない。……僕たちは等しく全員が容疑者なんだ。夏妃伯母さんだけが責められる道理はない」

units.text: "But, like Battler‐kun said, that's not enough to prove that Aunt Natsuhi is guilty to any degree. ......We're all equally suspicious. It's not right for only Aunt Natsuhi to be persecuted."
units.note: Both say equally suspicious rather than equal inclusion in suspect pool; no evidence equalizing degree of suspicion given.
units.japanese: 「でもそれは、戦人くんの言うとおり、夏妃伯母さんが何某かの犯人であることを断定できるものじゃない。……僕たちは等しく全員が容疑者なんだ。夏妃伯母さんだけが責められる道理はない」

description: Japanese reports an itchy throat for a while followed by gradual improvement. WH forecasts continued itching and says she had it under control.
sourceReading: しばらくは…ようだったが、次第に治まっていった narrates observed symptoms gradually settling.

units.text: Taking the inhaler from Kanon-kun, Jessica used it with a practiced hand. ...It looked like her throat would still itch for a while, but she had it under control...
units.note: MG predicts continued itch and control, while UP restores past itch and gradual settling. Both preserve attack provisionally calmed at 1171.
units.japanese: …しばらくは喉に痒さを感じているようだったが、次第に治まっていった…。

units.text: Taking the inhaler from Kanon-kun, Jessica used it with a practiced hand. ...It looked like her throat would still itch for a while, but she had it under control...
units.note: MG predicts continued itch and control, while UP restores past itch and gradual settling. Both preserve attack provisionally calmed at 1171.
units.japanese: 嘉音くんの手から吸入器を与えられ、朱志香が慣れた手つきでそれを吸う。…しばらくは喉に痒さを感じているようだったが、次第に治まっていった…。

description: Battler considers mutual scrutiny of alibis unnecessary. WH describes finding alibis for each other, changing suspicious probing into cooperative construction or discovery.
sourceReading: 互いのアリバイを探り合う means examining one another’s accounts.

units.text: This disturbance had made the dangerous atmosphere up until now seem slightly unfocused. But that was fine. ......That kind of battle of mutual suspicion was completely unnecessary. When you think about it, even finding alibis for each other and looking for the culprit was probably unnecessary.
units.note: MG finding alibis retains cooperative construction instead of suspicious mutual probing; UP probing restores scrutiny.
units.japanese: 思えば、互いのアリバイを探り合うことも犯人探しも、まったく不要なことかもしれない。

units.text: ......That kind of battle of mutual suspicion was completely unnecessary. When you think about it, even finding alibis for each other and looking for the culprit was probably unnecessary. After all, we're just powerless, ordinary people, and when the police come tomorrow, they'll definitely employ cutting edge techniques and investigate the case thoroughly, solving all of the riddles and arresting the culprit...
units.note: MG finding alibis retains cooperative construction instead of suspicious mutual probing; UP probing restores scrutiny.
units.japanese: 思えば、互いのアリバイを探り合うことも犯人探しも、まったく不要なことかもしれない。

units.text: When you think about it, finding alibis for each other and looking for the culprit is probably meaningless. After all, we're just powerless, ordinary people, and when the police come tomorrow, they'll definitely employ cutting-edge techniques and investigate the case thoroughly, solving all of the riddles and arresting the culprit...
units.note: MG finding alibis retains cooperative construction instead of suspicious mutual probing; UP probing restores scrutiny.
units.japanese: 思えば、互いのアリバイを探り合うことも犯人探しも、まったく不要なことかもしれない。なぜなら、自分たちは無力な市民でしかないが、明日になって警察が来てくれれば、必ずや最先端の技術を駆使して徹底的に捜査し、全ての謎を解いて犯人を逮捕してくれるのだから…。

description: Nanjo acknowledges that people cannot simply relax because told to. WH says it may not be his place to say it.
sourceReading: 言ってできるものではありません acknowledges the limit of verbal advice, not lack of standing.

units.text: "......Probably.  It is only natural...  It may not be my place to say it, but I think we should all relax as much as possible..."
units.note: MG not my place retains speaker authority concern; UP easier said than done restores difficulty of obeying relaxation advice.
units.japanese: 「……でしょうな。無理もないことです…。言ってできるものではありませんが、なるべく皆さん、リラックスしましょう…。」

units.text: "......Probably. It is only natural... It may not be my place to say it, but I think we should all relax as much as possible..."
units.note: MG not my place retains speaker authority concern; UP easier said than done restores difficulty of obeying relaxation advice.
units.japanese: 「……でしょうな。無理もないことです…。言ってできるものではありませんが、なるべく皆さん、リラックスしましょう…」

description: Eva warns Natsuhi not to forget that she too is under surveillance. WH tells her not to forget to keep an eye on herself.
sourceReading: 自分が監視をされている is passive: Natsuhi is watched by others.

units.text: "Thank you, Nee-san.  ...And mind your own business.  I'll be counting on you to keep an eye on everyone, alright?  Because the culprit is definitely here.  ...And Nee-san, make sure you don't forget to keep an eye on yourself, too."
units.note: MG watch yourself reverses surveillance relation; UP being watched restores others watching Natsuhi.
units.japanese: …そして姉さんも自分が監視をされていることを、お忘れなく。」

units.text: "Thank you, Nee-san. ...And mind your own business. I'll be counting on you to keep an eye on everyone, okay? Because the culprit is definitely here. ...And Nee-san, make sure you don't forget to keep an eye on yourself, too."
units.note: MG watch yourself reverses surveillance relation; UP being watched restores others watching Natsuhi.
units.japanese: 「ありがとう、姉さん。…そして余計なお世話よ。姉さんはみんなの監視をよろしくね？　犯人は、この中に必ずいるんだから。…そして姉さんも自分が監視をされていることを、お忘れなく」

description: Eva asks Genji to summon them at dinnertime. WH says the couple will call for him then.
sourceReading: 源次さん、夕食になったら呼んでね addresses Genji with a request to call them.

units.text: "...Yes, that's enough.  .........See you, Natsuhi nee-san.  ......Genji-san, we'll call for you when it's dinnertime.  Until then, we'll lock ourselves in with the chain."
units.note: Both instruct Genji to summon couple at dinner, rather than couple calling for him.
units.japanese: 「…えぇ、充分よぅ。………じゃあね、夏妃姉さん。……源次さん、夕食になったら呼んでね。それまでチェーンを掛けて閉じ篭ってるわ。」

description: Eva turns to her husband asking him also to tell George to come. WH says even you are saying it, as though he has already sided with George.
sourceReading: あなたからも言ってやってよ is a request for her husband’s intervention.

units.text: "George...!  ......Even you're saying it...!"
units.note: Both direct Eva request to husband to persuade George; no prior husband opposition inferred.
units.japanese: 「譲治…！　……あなたからも言ってやってよ…！」

description: WH labels Battler bored after the exhausting mutual accusations. Japanese describes feeling fed up or sick of it.
sourceReading: うんざりした気持ち carries weary exasperation in this context.

units.text: Feeling bored, I started clawing at my head when ......Maria and I made eye contact. Since I had thought she was completely immersed in the TV, I was a little surprised.
units.note: Both retain bored instead of fed up after mutual accusations.
units.japanese: うんざりした気持ちになりながら、頭を掻き毟ると、

units.text: Feeling bored, I started scratching at my head when ...Maria and I made eye contact. I was a little surprised, since I'd thought she was completely immersed in the TV.
units.note: Both retain bored instead of fed up after mutual accusations.
units.japanese: うんざりした気持ちになりながら、頭を掻き毟ると、……真里亞と目が合った。てっきり、テレビに没頭しているのだと思っていたので、少し驚く。

units.text: Feeling bored, I started clawing at my head, when... ...Maria and I made eye contact. Since I had thought she was completely immersed in the TV, I was a little surprised.
units.note: Both retain bored instead of fed up after mutual accusations.
units.japanese: うんざりした気持ちになりながら、頭を掻き毟ると、……真里亞と目が合った。てっきり、テレビに没頭しているのだと思っていたので、少し驚く。

description: Battler says he rejects the nineteenth-person account when others make him believe it, then likewise rejects the eighteen-only account when persuaded of that. WH makes both occasions his wanting to believe.
sourceReading: 信じ込まされる is causative passive, describing being induced to believe.

units.text: Crap...  Nothing's made sense to me for a while now... Just when I want to believe in a 19th person, I deny it, and just when I want to believe that there are only 18 people, I deny that too. Even though I wish that there were more than just the 18 people here, I couldn't accept the existence of that 19th person.
units.note: MG retains own desire to believe as trigger; UP restores being led to believe each competing account, distinct from wishing for outsider at 1299.
units.japanese: １９人目を信じ込まされると、それを否定し、１８人しかいないと信じ込まされると、今度はそれも否定してしまう。

units.text: Crap... Nothing's made sense to me for a while now... Just when I want to believe in a 19th person, I deny it, and just when I want to believe there are only 18 people, I deny that too. Even though I want there to be more than just the 18 people here, I can't accept the existence of that 19th person.
units.note: MG retains own desire to believe as trigger; UP restores being led to believe each competing account, distinct from wishing for outsider at 1299.
units.japanese: くそ…。さっきから自分でもわけがわからなくなるぜ…。１９人目を信じ込まされると、それを否定し、１８人しかいないと信じ込まされると、今度はそれも否定してしまう。１８人以外の何かがいてほしいと思うのに、その１９人目を認められない。

description: Genji says furniture serving the Master should not indulge in suspicious speculation about what he has arranged. WH says distrust would exceed his role, reducing a forbidden interpretive activity to an attitude.
sourceReading: 邪推 means construing suspicious or sinister motives, not simply lacking trust.

units.text: ".........I do not know.  ...Only, I think everything is as the Master hoped, as he has arranged.  ......To distrust that would exceed my role as furniture working for the Master."
units.note: Both replace suspicious speculation about master arrangements with distrust as attitude; role limit remains but activity changes.
units.japanese: 「………わかりません。…ただ、全てはお館様が望まれ、仕組まれたことのように思っています。……それを邪推することは、お館様にお仕えする家具には過ぎたことです。」

units.text: "......I do not know. ...However, I believe everything has proceeded as the Master has hoped and arranged for. ...To distrust that would exceed my role as furniture in service to the Master."
units.note: Both replace suspicious speculation about master arrangements with distrust as attitude; role limit remains but activity changes.
units.japanese: 「………わかりません。…ただ、全てはお館様が望まれ、仕組まれたことのように思っています。……それを邪推することは、お館様にお仕えする家具には過ぎたことです」

units.text: ".........I do not know. ...Only, I think everything is as the Master hoped—as he has arranged. ......To distrust that would exceed my role as furniture working for the Master."
units.note: Both replace suspicious speculation about master arrangements with distrust as attitude; role limit remains but activity changes.
units.japanese: 「………わかりません。…ただ、全てはお館様が望まれ、仕組まれたことのように思っています。……それを邪推することは、お館様にお仕えする家具には過ぎたことです」

description: Nanjo wonders whether even Genji, and indeed Nanjo himself who prides himself on being Kinzo’s only close friend, are merely pieces. WH keeps Genji as subject through the close-friend clause and omits Nanjo’s self-inclusion.
sourceReading: いや、唯一の親友であると自負している自分さえも shifts from Genji to the current viewpoint character Nanjo.

units.text: Nanjo thought about it. ......Isn't everyone just a piece on this chessboard, lined up equally, without any exceptions? ......Wasn't even Genji, who had gained more of Kinzo's trust than anyone, ...no, who was confident of his position as Kinzo's only close friend, ...just another one of the pieces laid out on the chessboard?
units.note: MG continues Genji through only-close-friend clause; UP explicitly restores Nanjo himself as second subject and feared piece.
units.japanese: ……金蔵から最高の信頼を得ている源次であっても、…いや、唯一の親友であると自負している自分さえも、…このチェス盤の上に置かれた駒に過ぎないのではないだろうかと。

units.text: Nanjo thought about it. ......Isn't everyone just a piece on this chessboard, lined up equally, without any exceptions? ......Wasn't even Genji, who had gained more of Kinzo's trust than anyone... no, who was confident of his position as Kinzo's only close friend, ...just another one of the pieces laid out on the chessboard?
units.note: MG continues Genji through only-close-friend clause; UP explicitly restores Nanjo himself as second subject and feared piece.
units.japanese: 南條は思う。……このチェス盤の上には、誰という例外はなく、全員が等しく駒として並べられているのではないだろうか。……金蔵から最高の信頼を得ている源次であっても、…いや、唯一の親友であると自負している自分さえも、…このチェス盤の上に置かれた駒に過ぎないのではないだろうかと。

description: Eva explains Natsuhi’s eagerness to exercise authority as a reaction to having long been sidelined. WH instead describes her as always dependent.
sourceReading: 冷や飯を食う describes neglect or exclusion from favorable treatment; the contrast is between former marginalization and present ascendancy.

units.text: That person, she was always so dependent, and now that Nii-san's dead, she's in such high spirits that she's taking charge.  ...Seriously, how shameless can she be."
units.note: Both restore being left out in cold rather than dependence, explaining eagerness to exercise authority.
units.japanese: あの人、ずっと冷や飯を食ってきたから、兄さんが死んでやっと天下が来たって張り切ってんのよ。…まったく、ずうずうしいったらありゃしない。」

description: The narration describes Eva’s intolerant response to George loving Shannon. WH asserts that George had not been permitted to fall in love with her.
sourceReading: 恋心を寄せているのが許せなかった means she could not tolerate his harboring those feelings, within Eva’s viewpoint.

units.text: George would eventually become successor to the Ushiromiya family. They had raised him strictly with that purpose in mind. George had been worth their while, and had grown into a fabulous young man who wouldn't disappoint no matter where he went. ...That was why he had not been permitted to fall in love with a servant like Shannon.
units.note: MG not permitted imposes prohibition rather than Eva unable to tolerate; UP she could not stand restores her response.
units.japanese: …だから、使用人の紗音如きに恋心を寄せているのが許せなかった。

units.text: George would eventually become the Successor to the Ushiromiya family. They had raised him strictly with that purpose in mind. He had been worth their while and had grown into a fabulous young man, who wouldn't disappoint no matter where he went. ...That was why he had not been permitted to fall in love with a servant like Shannon.
units.note: MG not permitted imposes prohibition rather than Eva unable to tolerate; UP she could not stand restores her response.
units.japanese:
譲治をやがては右代宮家の跡継ぎにする。
その一念で厳しく育ててきた。甲斐あり、譲治はどこに出しても恥ずかしくない素晴らしい青年に成長してくれた。…だから、使用人の紗音如きに恋心を寄せているのが許せなかった。

description: Eva states that her resentment belonged to childhood yet ended up dominating most of her life. WH makes her ask whether it was merely childish, then says it guided her entire life.
sourceReading: それは子どもの頃の感情なのよ is an emphatic assertion about the feeling’s childhood origin; ほとんどを支配した describes its domination of most of her life.

units.text: "........................I, ............have hated Krauss nii-san since long ago.  He was so full of himself, always swaggering around.  So proud that he would one day become the head.  ......So I wanted to get back at him.  ...Was that just a childish emotion...?  But in the end, that emotion guided my entire life.  If that had been all, then it would have been fine!  ......But because of that emotion, I got you and George involved.  I used you."
units.note: MG retains question about childishness and entire life guided. UP restores childhood emotion as statement and domination, but still entire instead of most of life.
units.japanese: ………蔵臼兄さんのことが、昔から嫌いだったわ。偉そうで、威張ってて。自分がやがては当主になるのだと自慢してて。……だから、それに一矢報いてやりたかった。…でも、それは子どもの頃の感情なのよ…？　でも、その感情は、……結局、自分の人生のほとんどを支配した。それだけならまだいい！　……その感情は、あなたや譲治まで巻き込んで、振り回してしまった。」

units.text: ............have hated Krauss nii-san since long ago.  He was so full of himself, always swaggering around.  So proud that he would one day become the head.  ......So I wanted to get back at him.  ...Was that just a childish emotion...?  But in the end, that emotion guided my entire life.  If that had been all, then it would have been fine!  ......But because of that emotion, I got you and George involved.  I used you."

sourceReading: 今、すぐがいい leaves the desired action tied to the newlywed-life exchange; 唇をねだる makes her request for a kiss explicit.

units.text: "No way.  .........Right now, ...I want to go right now."
units.note: MG want to go now still directs wish at immediate trip and nagged lips obscures request for kiss. UP start now links to newlywed continuation and pled for lips restores request.
