description: George wonders whether Genji let him win their past game. WH says he must have done so.
sourceReading: あれは勝たせてくれたのかな marks wondering about the explanation, rather than establishing it.

units.text: "...That's right.  Long ago, he played against me, but he must have let me win."
units.note: Both must have let me win replace George tentative wondering with necessity.
units.japanese: 「…そうなんだ。昔、相手をしてもらったことがあるけど、あれは勝たせてくれたのかな。」

units.text: "...That's right. Long ago, he played against me, but he must've let me win."
units.note: Both must have let me win replace George tentative wondering with necessity.
units.japanese: 「…そうなんだ。昔、相手をしてもらったことがあるけど、あれは勝たせてくれたのかな」

units.text: "...Is that right. I played against him long ago, but he must have let me win."
units.note: Both must have let me win replace George tentative wondering with necessity.
units.japanese: 「…そうなんだ。昔、相手をしてもらったことがあるけど、あれは勝たせてくれたのかな」

description: Maria explains that she is fine because she habitually watches lots of television. WH repeats that she has been watching the whole time.
sourceReading: いつもテレビいっぱい見てる invokes her usual practice as the reason for her tolerance.

units.text: "Uu-.  I've been watching TV the whole time so I'm fine.  Uu-."
units.note: Both always watching establishes habitual television viewing, not merely continuous viewing today.
units.japanese: 「うー。いつもテレビいっぱい見てるから平気。うー。」

description: The narration recalls Natsuhi’s instruction not to be alone without good reason. WH moves unnecessarily onto the act of warning, disparaging the warning instead of restricting Genji’s conduct.
sourceReading: みだりに modifies ひとりにはならない: he was warned against becoming alone indiscriminately or needlessly.

units.text: The distance from the kitchen to the parlor wasn't that large, so Genji had gone and come back by himself, but the guest room was a little farther away. Natsuhi had warned him unnecessarily not to be alone, and just now, Nanjo had also admonished him, saying that it would be better if he held a little more concern for his safety. ...Kanon accompanied Genji, and the two of them went to visit Eva and Hideyoshi in their guest room.
units.note: Both attach avoidance restriction to being alone, not an unnecessary warning. UP without good reason most closely retains source scope; MG whenever possible broadens avoidance but does not retain parent misattachment.
units.japanese: 夏妃にみだりにひとりにはならないようにと注意されたし、ついさっき、南條にも危機感をもっと持った方がいいと諭されたばかり。

description: The usual note tells sleeping guests that the servants came to call them. WH instead says it shows that it is time to come out.
sourceReading: 呼びに来たことを示す records the visit to summon the guest; it does not specify leaving the room as the note’s message.

units.text: But there was no response from inside. Sometimes, when the servants went to call some guests for a meal, the guests would be sleeping so deeply that they wouldn't wake up. ...In times like that, the servants would stick a letter in the door to show that it was time to come out, and leave the guest be. ......But despite that, Genji beat even harder on the door and called out Eva's name.
units.note: MG note shows time to come out; UP shows servants called by, restoring record of visit.
units.japanese: …そういう時は、呼びに来たことを示す手紙を挟んでそっとしておくことになっている。

units.text: But there was no response from inside. Sometimes, when the servants went to call some guests for a meal, the guests would be sleeping so deeply that they wouldn't wake up. ...In times like that, the servants would stick a letter in the door to show that it was time to come out, and leave the guest be. ...But despite that, Genji beat even harder on the door and called out Eva's name.
units.note: MG note shows time to come out; UP shows servants called by, restoring record of visit.
units.japanese: しかし中からは何の返事もない。食事に呼びに行った時、客人が深く眠ってしまっていて起きないことはたまにある。…そういう時は、呼びに来たことを示す手紙を挟んでそっとしておくことになっている。……しかし、源次はそれにもかかわらず、さらに激しく扉を叩いて絵羽の名を呼んだ。

description: Kanon remembers having been warned that this dangerous tool could easily sever fingers. WH describes the kind of thing that brings back memories of a tool that you might have been warned about.
sourceReading: 注意された記憶が蘇る is an actual resurfacing memory in Kanon’s current viewpoint.

units.text: Kanon took down a very large wire cutter that had been hanging on the wall. It was called a cutter, but maybe it would be easier to understand if we said it was shaped like a large pair of pliers. ......The kind of thing that brings back memories of a dangerous tool that you might have been warned could easily cut through one of your fingers...
units.note: Both explicitly restore Kanon remembered actual warning about dangerous cutter, not generic hypothetical memory.
units.japanese: ……指を容易に切断してしまえる危険な工具だと注意された記憶が蘇る…。
candidates: kind of thing that brings back memories
tool that you might have been warned

description: The Japanese identifies the strange nonalphabetic characters between the new figure’s lines as the same as those in the shutter’s circle. WH makes their presence prove that this was the same magic circle.
sourceReading: The grammatical subject is 奇怪な文字, with 同じもの comparing the characters, not asserting identity of the complete geometrical figures.

units.text: However, it would be odd to call this one a 'magic circle'. ...Because, unlike what most people would think of as a magic circle, it wasn't a circle with shapes drawn inside it, but a slightly more geometrical shape. ......But since in the gaps of the figure, there was something written in strange characters that were not from the alphabet, this was doubtlessly the same as the magic circle on the shutter...
units.note: MG same kind as ones on shutter restores comparison of characters. UP restores characters as grammatical subject and removes prove, but compares characters to magic circle itself rather than its characters; surrounding geometric distinction prevents a clean identical-circle claim.
units.japanese: ……しかし、その図形の隙間に書き込まれたアルファベットとは異なる奇怪な文字は、紛れもなく、あのシャッターの魔法陣と同じもの…。

units.text: However, it was dubious whether this one could be called a "magic circle". ...Because, unlike what most people would think of as a magic circle, it wasn't a circle with shapes drawn inside it, but a slightly more geometrical shape. ......However, the strange non‐alphabetical characters written in the gaps of the figure were without doubt the same as the magic circle on the shutter...
units.note: MG same kind as ones on shutter restores comparison of characters. UP restores characters as grammatical subject and removes prove, but compares characters to magic circle itself rather than its characters; surrounding geometric distinction prevents a clean identical-circle claim.
units.japanese: もっとも、今度のものを「魔法陣」と呼んでいいのかは怪しい。…なぜなら、それは魔法陣と聞いて一般人が想像するような、円の内側に図形が描かれたものでなく、もう少し幾何学的な図形が描かれていたからだ。……しかし、その図形の隙間に書き込まれたアルファベットとは異なる奇怪な文字は、紛れもなく、あのシャッターの魔法陣と同じもの…。

description: The source says the eerie marking is not the only reason Kanon is speechless. WH says its eeriness is not the thing responsible, before explaining its sudden appearance.
sourceReading: 不気味さだけではない retains eeriness as one contributing reason and adds the appearance during his absence.

units.text: But the thing that had Kanon struck speechless was not how eerie the magic circle was. ......It was that something like this hadn't been here a short while ago...!!
units.note: Both negate eeriness as cause instead of not only eeriness; sudden appearance remains additional source reason but translations exclude original first reason.
units.japanese: しかし嘉音が絶句しているのは、この魔法陣の不気味さだけではない。

units.text: But the thing that had Kanon struck speechless wasn't how eerie the magic circle was. ...It was that something like this hadn't been here a short while ago...!!
units.note: Both negate eeriness as cause instead of not only eeriness; sudden appearance remains additional source reason but translations exclude original first reason.
units.japanese: しかし嘉音が絶句しているのは、この魔法陣の不気味さだけではない。……こんなものは、さっきはなかったのだ…！！

units.text: But the thing that had Kanon struck speechless was not how eerie the magic circle was. ......Only moments ago, this hadn't been here...!!
units.note: Both negate eeriness as cause instead of not only eeriness; sudden appearance remains additional source reason but translations exclude original first reason.
units.japanese: しかし嘉音が絶句しているのは、この魔法陣の不気味さだけではない。……こんなものは、さっきはなかったのだ…！！

description: The Japanese says the handle’s elaborate design would be unexpected on a mere tool. WH changes the comparison class to an ordinary weapon.
sourceReading: 単なる工具 is a mere or ordinary tool; 凶器 elsewhere identifies the object’s use as a murder weapon, not the comparison class here.

units.text: Even though that forehead was the last place they wanted to look, they couldn't tear their eyes from it... Right there, the weapon was stuck into Eva's forehead, standing almost perfectly upright. And on the handle was a complicated design that you wouldn't expect to see on an ordinary weapon. ......That thing, ...could be summed up with the word 'occult'. ...It was a vulgar object, with a design that might have been of some demon.
units.note: Both compare elaborate handle to ordinary weapon instead of mere tool, losing original comparison class.
units.japanese: その、柄の部分には、単なる工具では考えられないような複雑な意匠がされていた。

units.text: Even though her forehead was the last place they wanted to look, they couldn't tear their eyes from it... Right there, the weapon was stuck into Eva's forehead, standing almost perfectly upright. And on the handle was a complicated design that you wouldn't expect to see on an ordinary weapon. ...That thing...could be summed up with the word "occult". ...It was a vulgar object, with a design that might've been of some demon.
units.note: Both compare elaborate handle to ordinary weapon instead of mere tool, losing original comparison class.
units.japanese:
一番見たくないはずの眉間にどうしても目が行ってしまう…。そこには、凶器が絵羽の眉間から直立するように刺さっている。その、柄の部分には、単なる工具では考えられないような複雑な意匠がされていた。……それは、…一言で言えばオカルト的。
…何かの悪魔をデザインしたかのような悪趣味なものだった。

units.text:
Even though that forehead was the last place they wanted to look, they couldn't tear their eyes from it... Right there, the weapon was stuck into Eva's forehead, standing almost perfectly upright. And on the handle was a design so complicated you could never expect to see it on an ordinary weapon. ......That thing...could be summed up with the word "occult".
...It was a vulgar object, with a design that might have been of some demon.
units.note: Both compare elaborate handle to ordinary weapon instead of mere tool, losing original comparison class.
units.japanese:
一番見たくないはずの眉間にどうしても目が行ってしまう…。そこには、凶器が絵羽の眉間から直立するように刺さっている。その、柄の部分には、単なる工具では考えられないような複雑な意匠がされていた。……それは、…一言で言えばオカルト的。
…何かの悪魔をデザインしたかのような悪趣味なものだった。

description: Nanjo tentatively places the deaths at a point where perhaps an hour has elapsed or perhaps not. WH recommends assuming about one hour has passed, centering the estimate on an elapsed hour.
sourceReading: １時間経ったかどうかというところ leaves open whether the interval has reached one hour; おそらく and だろう retain tentativeness.

units.text: "...I, ......I understand............No signs of postmortem lividity...  Rigor mortis hasn't begun either.  We should probably assume that about one hour has passed since they died...
units.note: MG hour or so centers on elapsed hour; UP barely an hour if that restores possible less-than-hour interval. Nanjo estimate remains tentative and no independent time certification follows.
units.japanese: 「…わ、……わかっとる……。……死斑は出とらんな…。死後硬直も始まっとらん。おそらく、殺されてから１時間経ったかどうかというところだろう…。

units.text: "...I-I understand... ...No signs of postmortem lividity... Rigor mortis hasn't begun either. It would seem that an hour or so has passed since they were killed...
units.note: MG hour or so centers on elapsed hour; UP barely an hour if that restores possible less-than-hour interval. Nanjo estimate remains tentative and no independent time certification follows.
units.japanese: 「…わ、……わかっとる……。……死斑は出とらんな…。死後硬直も始まっとらん。おそらく、殺されてから１時間経ったかどうかというところだろう…」

description: On looking closely at the weapon’s base, the source says there is no blade. WH says he cannot see the blade well, implying an obscured blade rather than its absence.
sourceReading: よく見ると刃がない is a positive observation of absent blade; the next clause explains a conical rather than blade-shaped implement.

units.text: But he couldn't see the blade well at the base of the wound. ...Even more importantly, it wasn't shaped like a flat blade, but was conical. ...He noticed that, rather than a knife, it was more like a short handled spear, something with a shape better suited for thrusting than slicing. Rather than a short spear, some people might call it a thick icepick.
units.note: Both explicitly state no blade and conical thrusting form rather than an obscured blade. Both preserve leaving weapon in place.
units.japanese: しかし、根元の部分をよく見ると刃がない。

description: After identifying George as waiting with the children, the source follows his ominous intuition on seeing Natsuhi’s reaction and his certainty at the gathered crowd. WH assigns both reactions to they and makes the intuition concern Genji as bearer of bad news.
sourceReading: The paragraph topic is George; 子どもたちと一緒に describes his company, not a new plural viewpoint. 虫の報せ is an ominous intuition.

units.text: But the recklessly approaching footsteps were obviously George's even before he came flying into the room. George and the other children had been waiting in the parlor. But when they had seen Genji call Natsuhi out, and had noticed her turn pale and fly out of the room, they had felt that he might have been the bearer of bad news. And when they saw a large group of people gathered around the guest room, they were sure of it...
units.note: MG restores general foreboding rather than Genji bad-news-bearer focus but retains plural they for George own intuition and certainty. UP retains plural and bearer-of-bad-news attribution.
units.japanese:
だが、源次が夏妃を呼び出し、夏妃が真っ青になって客間を飛び出していくのを見て、虫の報せを感じたのだった。
そして、客室に大勢が集まっているのを見て、確信する…。

units.text: But they could tell that those fiercely racing footsteps in the hallway belonged to George, even before he came dashing into the room. George and the other children had been waiting in the parlor. However, when they saw Genji speak to Natsuhi, when they saw her turn pale and fly out of the parlor, they'd felt a sense of foreboding. And when they saw a large group of people gathered around the guest room, they were sure of it...
units.note: MG restores general foreboding rather than Genji bad-news-bearer focus but retains plural they for George own intuition and certainty. UP retains plural and bearer-of-bad-news attribution.
units.japanese: だが、廊下を猛烈に走り近付いてくる足音は、部屋に飛び込んでくる前から譲治のものであることが理解できた。譲治は、子どもたちと一緒に客間で待っていた。だが、源次が夏妃を呼び出し、夏妃が真っ青になって客間を飛び出していくのを見て、虫の報せを感じたのだった。そして、客室に大勢が集まっているのを見て、確信する…。

description: Battler says the witch has put us under pressure and we are entirely on the defensive. WH says she has cornered me and I am always on the defensive, before returning to we.
sourceReading: 俺たちは explicitly includes the group in the chess predicament.

units.text: "Aah...  Damn it, ...I won't cry anymore...  Tears of regret, tears of sadness, I won't shed them again............Aah, it's all useless.  The witch has backed me into a corner.  I'm always on the defensive...!  And that's useless, it's all useless!  I'll turn the chessboard over...!!  That bastard probably thinks we'll be running scared like sheep until tomorrow without trying anything.  ...But guess what, I'll turn it over!!  That bastard can't escape this island until tomorrow either...!  We won't be the ones hiding away, pissing ourselves, that bastard will!  I'll expose you, you'll see.  By tomorrow..., no, I won't wait for tomorrow, tonight. Before tonight's over I'll be gripping you by the collar...!!"
units.note: MG retains me/I and always. UP restores us/we but still always on defensive instead of entirely on defensive at present.
units.japanese: 「あぁ…。くそ、…もう流さねぇぜ…。悔し涙も悲しみの涙も、もう二度と流さねぇぜ…。………あぁ、全然駄目だ。俺たちは魔女さまに詰めを食らってるわけだ。守勢一方ってわけだ…！　そりゃあ駄目だぜ、全然駄目だ！　チェス盤が引っくり返っちまうぜ…！！　野郎は俺たち羊が、明日まで逃げる手段もなく怯えてるだけだろうと思ってるだろうよ。…だがな、引っくり返すぜ！！　明日までこの島から逃げられねぇのは野郎も同じだ…！　小便チビりそうになりながら逃げ隠れするのは俺たちじゃねぇ、野郎の方だ！　暴いてやるぜ、必ずな。明日までに…、いや、明日なんか待たねぇ、今夜だ。今夜中にその胸倉を掴みあげてやらぁ…！！」

units.text: ...Aah, it's all useless. The witch's got me backed into a corner. I'm always on the defensive...! And that's useless, it's all useless! I'll spin the chessboard around...!! That bastard probably thinks we'll be running scared like sheep until tomorrow before we try anything.
units.note: MG retains me/I and always. UP restores us/we but still always on defensive instead of entirely on defensive at present.
units.japanese: 「………あぁ、全然駄目だ。俺たちは魔女さまに詰めを食らってるわけだ。守勢一方ってわけだ…！　そりゃあ駄目だぜ、全然駄目だ！　チェス盤が引っくり返っちまうぜ…！！　野郎は俺たち羊が、明日まで逃げる手段もなく怯えてるだけだろうと思ってるだろうよ」

units.text: ".........Yeah, it's no goddamn good at all. The witch is backing us into a corner. We're always on the defensive...! And that's no good, it's no goddamn good! I'll flip over the chessboard...!! That bastard probably thinks of us like sheep, just cowering in fear until tomorrow with no way of running."
units.note: MG retains me/I and always. UP restores us/we but still always on defensive instead of entirely on defensive at present.
units.japanese: 「………あぁ、全然駄目だ。俺たちは魔女さまに詰めを食らってるわけだ。守勢一方ってわけだ…！　そりゃあ駄目だぜ、全然駄目だ！　チェス盤が引っくり返っちまうぜ…！！　野郎は俺たち羊が、明日まで逃げる手段もなく怯えてるだけだろうと思ってるだろうよ」

description: Battler imagines the culprit expecting the group to remain frightened until tomorrow with no means to escape. WH instead says they will run scared without trying anything, replacing an external constraint with passivity.
sourceReading: 明日まで逃げる手段もなく specifies unavailable means of escape, setting up the next reversal that the culprit is similarly trapped until tomorrow.

units.text: "Aah...  Damn it, ...I won't cry anymore...  Tears of regret, tears of sadness, I won't shed them again............Aah, it's all useless.  The witch has backed me into a corner.  I'm always on the defensive...!  And that's useless, it's all useless!  I'll turn the chessboard over...!!  That bastard probably thinks we'll be running scared like sheep until tomorrow without trying anything.  ...But guess what, I'll turn it over!!  That bastard can't escape this island until tomorrow either...!  We won't be the ones hiding away, pissing ourselves, that bastard will!  I'll expose you, you'll see.  By tomorrow..., no, I won't wait for tomorrow, tonight. Before tonight's over I'll be gripping you by the collar...!!"
units.note: MG before trying anything implies passivity; UP no way of running restores external escape constraint, paired with culprit unable to leave until tomorrow.
units.japanese: 「あぁ…。くそ、…もう流さねぇぜ…。悔し涙も悲しみの涙も、もう二度と流さねぇぜ…。………あぁ、全然駄目だ。俺たちは魔女さまに詰めを食らってるわけだ。守勢一方ってわけだ…！　そりゃあ駄目だぜ、全然駄目だ！　チェス盤が引っくり返っちまうぜ…！！　野郎は俺たち羊が、明日まで逃げる手段もなく怯えてるだけだろうと思ってるだろうよ。…だがな、引っくり返すぜ！！　明日までこの島から逃げられねぇのは野郎も同じだ…！　小便チビりそうになりながら逃げ隠れするのは俺たちじゃねぇ、野郎の方だ！　暴いてやるぜ、必ずな。明日までに…、いや、明日なんか待たねぇ、今夜だ。今夜中にその胸倉を掴みあげてやらぁ…！！」

units.text: ...Aah, it's all useless. The witch's got me backed into a corner. I'm always on the defensive...! And that's useless, it's all useless! I'll spin the chessboard around...!! That bastard probably thinks we'll be running scared like sheep until tomorrow before we try anything.
units.note: MG before trying anything implies passivity; UP no way of running restores external escape constraint, paired with culprit unable to leave until tomorrow.
units.japanese: 「………あぁ、全然駄目だ。俺たちは魔女さまに詰めを食らってるわけだ。守勢一方ってわけだ…！　そりゃあ駄目だぜ、全然駄目だ！　チェス盤が引っくり返っちまうぜ…！！　野郎は俺たち羊が、明日まで逃げる手段もなく怯えてるだけだろうと思ってるだろうよ」

description: After Kanon follows Kumasawa, the Japanese says the remaining people also follow to find the smell’s source, though not running. WH keeps Kanon as subject and invents his searching in other directions.
sourceReading: それ以外の面々も means the rest of the group too; その後を追った gives their movement after the pair.

units.text: After nodding at Genji's order, Kanon followed after her. ...He wasn't running, but as he followed her, he tried to search for the cause of the smell in other directions as well.
units.note: MG keeps Kanon as the searching subject and adds other directions; UP restores the other members following to seek the smell source.
units.japanese: …走るわけではないが、それ以外の面々も臭い元を探すため、その後を追った。

units.text: After nodding at Genji's order, Kanon followed after her. ...He wasn't running, but as he followed her, he tried to search for the cause of the smell in other directions as well.

源次の指示に頷き、嘉音は後を追っていった。
…走るわけではないが、それ以外の面々も臭い元を探すため、その後を追った。

description: The source says George seems already to have climbed out of the abyss of grief. WH says he still has not.
sourceReading: もう ... 這い上がっている is affirmative completed emergence, setting up the replacement by hatred.

units.text: It seemed that George still hadn't climbed out of the abyss of his sorrow. ...All that filled his chest now was the quiet flame of hatred towards the culprit who had stolen the lives of his beloved parents.
units.note: Both restore George having climbed out of sorrow, rather than not yet doing so.
units.japanese: 譲治はもう悲しみの淵からは這い上がっているようだった。

description: The source grounds George’s hatred in the culprit taking his beloved person and his parents. WH collapses the phrase into his beloved parents and omits Shannon from the present motivation.
sourceReading: 自分の愛した人と両親 distinguishes the loved person from both parents.

units.text: It seemed that George still hadn't climbed out of the abyss of his sorrow. ...All that filled his chest now was the quiet flame of hatred towards the culprit who had stolen the lives of his beloved parents.
units.note: MG names the one he loved separately from his parents; UP retains only beloved parents and omits Shannon from this motivation.

description: Battler says the chain’s construction makes outside tampering impossible. WH limits this assertion to opening it from outside.
sourceReading: 外から細工できる covers manipulation or rigging, including the possibility of arranging the secured state; it is not confined to opening.

units.text: "...The chain for this room was set.  ...From what I could tell by looking at it, I'm positive that it couldn't be opened from the outside.  ......In other words, this was a perfect closed room."
units.note: Both restrict outside tampering to opening at row 39; row 46 likewise describes blocking outside entry. The source makes a broader no-tampering assertion. These remain Battler and George reasoning, not independently certified mechanism facts.

description: Battler rejects an attack through the chained doorway because Eva lies on the bed deep inside the room and Hideyoshi is in the bathroom. WH relocates her bed to the center.
sourceReading: 部屋の奥 means the far or inner part of the room, not its center.

units.text: But she was on the bed in the center of the room!  And Hideyoshi oji-san was even in the bathroom.  Looking from the crack in the door, you couldn't even see them, and you couldn't reach them with your hands either.  ......Damn it, it's all useless.  I don't have a clue!!"
units.note: MG restores bed at the back of the room; UP retains center, altering the spatial premise in rejection of an attack through the door gap.
units.japanese: だが絵羽伯母さんは部屋の奥のベッドの上！　しかも秀吉伯父さんはバスルームだった。チェーンの隙間からでは、姿を見ることもできねぇし、手を伸ばすこともできねぇ。…畜生、全然駄目だぜ、さっぱりだ！！」

units.text: "But she was on the bed in the center of the room! And Uncle Hideyoshi was even in the bathroom. Looking from the crack in the door, you couldn't even see them, and you couldn't reach them with your hands either. ......Damn it, this is no goddamn good at all, I don't have a clue!!"
units.note: MG restores bed at the back of the room; UP retains center, altering the spatial premise in rejection of an attack through the door gap.

sourceReading: 開かぬ扉を八方塞の事態に見立て explicitly connects the door image to an intractable situation. There is no finding of another door.

description: The source recalls everyone having gathered at Eva’s room a short while ago. WH specifies a few seconds, adding a much tighter interval to the argument that no one should now be in the boiler room.
sourceReading: さっき is a relative recent-time reference without a numeric seconds limit; intervening departure and discussion do not establish one.

units.text: Kumasawa was so surprised at that sound that her knees gave way yet again and she cowered... ......Because, at that very moment, no one could have been in the boiler room. Just a few seconds ago, everyone had been crowded together around Eva and Hideyoshi's room!  So who caused the sound of a door closing just now?!
units.note: Both retain invented few seconds instead of unspecified recent gathering, tightening the inference about who could be downstairs. Two entrances remain explicit; no independently established culprit exclusion or unsolvability follows.
units.japanese: さっきの絵羽たちの部屋に全員が揃った！　なら、今の扉の音は何者に発せられる音だというのか！

description: The source calls Kanon’s overcoming himself 克己, then repeats that word in the butterflies’ tribute and mockery. WH first calls it self-restraint and later self-sacrifice, breaking the shared description of his defiant self-overcoming.
sourceReading: 克己 is overcoming or mastering oneself; here he suppresses fear and declares independence from furniture status.

units.text: ...Kanon's face was twisted with humiliation. .........It was clear that his self-restraint was being ridiculed somehow. Kanon's brow creased even further, ...and a furious expression that Kanon had never shown anyone appeared on his face. ......The hand grasping the hatchet was shaking.  ...His sweat became drops which slid down...
units.note: MG first restores defiance against his own weaknesses, but later retains self-sacrifice for repeated 克己. UP self-denial and self-sacrifice both displace self-mastery and break recurrence. Fear suppression and independence context support overcoming oneself.

description: The raised arm after losing the hatchet appears to grasp at empty air before dropping to his chest. WH says the hand appears to catch the sky.
sourceReading: 空を掴む in this indoor gesture is grasping at empty space, not literally catching the sky.

units.text: That hand, which looked like it was trying to catch the sky now that the hatchet had been dropped, gradually lowered, ......landing on his chest.  Then, the other hand did the same. ......Right there, a handle with a demon-shaped design was buried into his chest. The same type of weapon that had been stabbed into Eva and Hideyoshi's foreheads...was in Kanon's chest......
units.note: Both retain catching the sky rather than grasping empty air indoors.

units.japanese:
苦悶に歪む嘉音の口の端から、鮮血が零れ落ちる…。
…それは、嘉音の白い肌には過ぎた化粧…。

description: The blood is makeup too much for Kanon’s white skin in the source. WH keeps the makeup image but omits its excess, flattening the macabre incongruity.
sourceReading: 白い肌には過ぎた化粧 makes the blood an excessive adornment relative to his pale skin.

units.text: Kanon was curled up in anguish, fresh blood dribbling from the corner of his mouth... ...It was...makeup over Kanon's white skin...
units.note: MG too extreme and UP too powerful both restore excess of blood-as-makeup against pale skin.
units.japanese: …それは、嘉音の白い肌には過ぎた化粧…。

description: Although prepared to die, Kanon attempts a last resistance even just to accepting the death as given. WH says he can do nothing but accept it, then juxtaposes an unspecified last resistance.
sourceReading: そのままの形で受け容れることにだけでも identifies the minimal target of resistance: acceptance in precisely the imposed form.

units.text: ...Kanon had already been prepared for his own death, ......but although he could do nothing but accept the death he had received, he attempted one last measure of resistance. ...He grasped the handle of the weapon sticking into his chest with both hands, ............and gritting his teeth with an acute, unearthly pain............, ........................he pulled it out.
units.note: MG still says he could do nothing but accept death; UP restores rejection of death in its delivered form, followed by pulling out the weapon.
units.japanese: …嘉音は自身の絶命をすでに覚悟していたが、……与えられた死を、そのままの形で受け容れることにだけでも、最後の抵抗を試みる。

units.text: ...Kanon had already been prepared for his own death, ...but although he could do nothing but accept the death he had received, he attempted one last measure of resistance. ...He grasped the handle of the weapon sticking into his chest with both hands, ......and gritting his teeth with an acute, unearthly pain, ......... ............he pulled it out.
units.note: MG still says he could do nothing but accept death; UP restores rejection of death in its delivered form, followed by pulling out the weapon.
units.japanese: …嘉音は自身の絶命をすでに覚悟していたが、……与えられた死を、そのままの形で受け容れることにだけでも、最後の抵抗を試みる。…そして両手で胸に刺し込まれた凶器の柄を握り、…………この世のものと思えぬ激痛に歯を食いしばりながら……………、…………………………抜く。

description: Kanon’s condition makes investigation of the smell secondary in the source. WH says the stench is no longer important.
sourceReading: 二の次 ranks it below the wounded boy, without dismissing its importance altogether.

units.text: The first one to dash in was Natsuhi, holding the rifle. Battler and Genji dashed in after her. Normally, they probably would've started discussing the origin of that violent stench filling the boiler room. ......But after they saw Kanon, who was lying on the ground as if he were drowning in an ocean of his own blood, the stench wasn't important any more.
units.note: Both say stench no longer important, stronger than source relegating investigation to secondary priority while attending wounded Kanon.
units.japanese: ……だが、血の海に溺れるかのように倒れている嘉音を前に、それは二の次だった。

units.text: The first one to dash in was Natsuhi, holding the rifle. Battler and Genji dashed in after her. Normally, they probably would've started discussing the origin of that violent stench filling the boiler room. ...But after they saw Kanon, who was lying on the ground as if he were drowning in an ocean of his own blood, the stench wasn't important anymore.
units.note: Both say stench no longer important, stronger than source relegating investigation to secondary priority while attending wounded Kanon.
units.japanese: 一番最初に飛び込んできたのは、ライフル銃を構えた夏妃だった。その後に戦人と源次が飛び込んでくる。彼らは本来なら、このボイラー室に充満する猛烈な悪臭の発生源について議論するだろう。……だが、血の海に溺れるかのように倒れている嘉音を前に、それは二の次だった。

units.text: The first one to dash in was Natsuhi, with rifle at the ready. Battler and Genji dashed in after her. Normally, they probably would've started discussing the origin of that violent stench filling the boiler room. ......But after they saw Kanon, who was lying on the ground as if he were drowning in an ocean of his own blood, the stench wasn't important any more.
units.note: Both say stench no longer important, stronger than source relegating investigation to secondary priority while attending wounded Kanon.
units.japanese: 一番最初に飛び込んできたのは、ライフル銃を構えた夏妃だった。その後に戦人と源次が飛び込んでくる。彼らは本来なら、このボイラー室に充満する猛烈な悪臭の発生源について議論するだろう。……だが、血の海に溺れるかのように倒れている嘉音を前に、それは二の次だった。

description: The source has Natsuhi aim her rifle toward the darkness deep in the boiler room. WH places that darkness in the center, altering the direction associated with the subsequently illuminated piping and door.
sourceReading: ボイラー室の奥 is the inner or far part of the room.

units.text: Natsuhi realized that even though Kanon was on the verge of death, he was still conscious, so she sent Genji to get the doctor. ...Natsuhi, holding the rifle aloft, faced the darkness in the center of the boiler room and shouted!
units.note: Both retain center of boiler room instead of darkness deep inside, altering direction of aim and illuminated piping/door.
units.japanese: …夏妃はライフル銃を高々と構えると、ボイラー室の奥の暗がりに向けながら怒鳴る！

units.text: Natsuhi realized that even though Kanon was on the verge of death, he was still conscious, so she sent Genji to get the doctor. ...Natsuhi, holding the rifle aloft, faced the darkness in the center of the boiler room and shouted!
units.note: Both retain center of boiler room instead of darkness deep inside, altering direction of aim and illuminated piping/door.
units.japanese: 夏妃は嘉音が瀕死とはいえ、まだ意識があることに気付き源次に託す。…夏妃はライフル銃を高々と構えると、ボイラー室の奥の暗がりに向けながら怒鳴る！

description: After crying into Natsuhi’s chest, Battler wipes his tears and gives a strained smile, as he has done before, to signal he is done crying. WH says as though he had been like that the whole time, replacing recurrence with a continuous-state comparison.
sourceReading: これまでもそうだったように invokes prior instances of the same recovery gesture, not a claim that this expression persisted throughout the crying.

units.text: Battler, after sobbing into Natsuhi's chest for a while, wiped his tears with a bitter smile, as though he had been like that the whole time, and tried to appear as though he had cried more than enough already...
units.note: MG retains continuous-state as though he had been like that the whole time. UP restores recurrence just as he had done before.
units.japanese: 戦人はしばらくの間、夏妃の胸で号泣した後、これまでもそうだったように、涙を拭きながら苦笑いして、充分に泣き尽くしたことをアピールした…。
candidates: though he had been like that the whole time

units.note: MG retains continuous-state as though he had been like that the whole time. UP restores recurrence just as he had done before.
units.japanese: 戦人はしばらくの間、夏妃の胸で号泣した後、これまでもそうだったように、涙を拭きながら苦笑いして、充分に泣き尽くしたことをアピールした…。
candidates: though he had been like that the whole time

description: The source says the pool Kanon left remains on the floor. WH calls it stains, weakening the stated accumulation of liquid blood.
sourceReading: 血溜まり is pooled blood, not merely staining.

units.text: ...Stains from Kanon-kun's blood remained on the floor. Judging by the large amount of blood lost and the ruthless shape of the weapon that had fallen carelessly to the ground, ......I figured that Doctor Nanjo's treatment would probably end in vain...
units.note: Both retain stains instead of remaining pool. Large blood-loss observation in next row mitigates but does not preserve liquid accumulation.
units.japanese: …床には、嘉音くんが残した血溜まりが残っている。

units.text: ...Stains from Kanon-kun's blood remained on the floor. Judging by the large amount of blood lost and the ruthless shape of the weapon that had fallen carelessly to the ground, ...I figured that Doctor Nanjo's treatment would probably end in vain...
units.note: Both retain stains instead of remaining pool. Large blood-loss observation in next row mitigates but does not preserve liquid accumulation.
units.japanese: …床には、嘉音くんが残した血溜まりが残っている。そのおびただしい出血量と、無造作に転がる凶器の無慈悲な形状から、……多分、南條先生の手当ては徒労に終わるだろうと思った…。

units.text: ...Stains from Kanon‐kun's blood remained on the floor. Judging by the large amount of blood lost and the ruthless shape of the weapon that had fallen unceremoniously to the ground, ......I figured that Doctor Nanjo's treatment would probably end in vain...
units.note: Both retain stains instead of remaining pool. Large blood-loss observation in next row mitigates but does not preserve liquid accumulation.
units.japanese: …床には、嘉音くんが残した血溜まりが残っている。そのおびただしい出血量と、無造作に転がる凶器の無慈悲な形状から、……多分、南條先生の手当ては徒労に終わるだろうと思った…。

description: The source estimates about 25 centimeters overall and about half as the bloody stake portion. WH gives 25 centimeters and half without approximation.
sourceReading: くらい and ほど explicitly qualify both estimates.

units.text: Including the handle, it was 25 centimeters long.  Half of that was the stake shaped part, which was stained with deep red blood. ......The length of the blood-stained part made it clear just how deeply it must have penetrated into Kanon-kun's chest...
units.note: MG retains exact 25 centimeters and half. UP restores about twenty-five but still gives half without source approximation.
units.japanese: 全長は柄の部分も入れて２５ｃｍくらい。その半分ほどが真っ赤に血で染められた杭状の部分。

units.text: Including the handle, it was 25 centimeters long. Half of that was the stake-shaped part, which was stained with deep red blood. ......The length of the blood-stained part made it clear just how deeply it must have penetrated into Kanon-kun's chest...
units.note: MG retains exact 25 centimeters and half. UP restores about twenty-five but still gives half without source approximation.
units.japanese: 全長は柄の部分も入れて２５ｃｍくらい。その半分ほどが真っ赤に血で染められた杭状の部分。……血に染まった部分の長さが、嘉音くんの胸をどれだけ深々と貫いていたかを想像させる…。

units.text: Including the handle, it was about twenty‐five centimeters long. Half of that was the stake‐shaped part, which was stained with deep red blood. ......The length of the blood‐stained part made it clear just how deeply it must have penetrated into Kanon‐kun's chest...
units.note: MG retains exact 25 centimeters and half. UP restores about twenty-five but still gives half without source approximation.
units.japanese: 全長は柄の部分も入れて２５ｃｍくらい。その半分ほどが真っ赤に血で染められた杭状の部分。……血に染まった部分の長さが、嘉音くんの胸をどれだけ深々と貫いていたかを想像させる…。

description: Natsuhi’s report says several of the heads praised as great rulers had polydactyly. WH says the ones praised most for wisdom all had it, dropping the selected subset and adding a superlative.
sourceReading: 名君と讃えられた何人か selects some celebrated heads; みんな refers to those selected people.

units.text: According to Natsuhi oba-san, among the many Ushiromiya family heads, the ones praised most for their wisdom had all possessed polydactyly. ......Because of that, when Grandfather was born, his relatives were all excited at the thought that he might become another wise leader.  And, when the leading relatives all died in the Great Kanto Earthquake, it was apparently argued Grandfather should be the one to restore the family because of the auspicious sign of his birth.
units.note: Both retain superlative wisdom and all such heads rather than several heads praised as great rulers.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんが言うには、右代宮家の歴代当主の中でも名君と讃えられた何人かが、みんな多指症だったらしい。

units.text: According to Aunt Natsuhi, among the many Ushiromiya Family Heads, the ones most praised for their wisdom all had polydactyly. ...Because of that, when Grandfather was born, his relatives were all excited at the thought that he might become another wise leader. And, when the leading relatives all died in the Great Kanto Earthquake, it was apparently argued that Grandfather should be the one to restore the family, because of the auspicious sign of his birth. If Grandfather hadn't disliked his position as the Head so much, this sixth toe probably would've been pretty lucky for him.
units.note: Both retain superlative wisdom and all such heads rather than several heads praised as great rulers.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんが言うには、右代宮家の歴代当主の中でも名君と讃えられた何人かが、みんな多指症だったらしい。……そのため、祖父さまが生まれた時、名君の再来かと親族たちに騒がれたのだそうだ。で、関東大震災で主だった親族たちが全滅し、そこからお家を再興できるのは、吉祥の徴を持って生まれてきた祖父さまだ、ってな論法になったらしい。

units.text: According to Aunt Natsuhi, among the many Ushiromiya family heads, the ones praised most for their wisdom had all possessed polydactyly. ......Because of that, when Grandfather was born, his relatives were all excited at the thought that he might become another wise leader. And, when the leading relatives all died in the Great Kanto Earthquake, it was apparently argued that if anyone could restore the family from that, it would be Grandfather, because of the auspicious sign of his birth.
units.note: Both retain superlative wisdom and all such heads rather than several heads praised as great rulers.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんが言うには、右代宮家の歴代当主の中でも名君と讃えられた何人かが、みんな多指症だったらしい。……そのため、祖父さまが生まれた時、名君の再来かと親族たちに騒がれたのだそうだ。で、関東大震災で主だった親族たちが全滅し、そこからお家を再興できるのは、吉祥の徴を持って生まれてきた祖父さまだ、ってな論法になったらしい。

description: Battler vaguely recalls a country where people with polydactyly are regarded as messengers of a god and revered. WH says they should be treated as gods.
sourceReading: 神さまの使い means a divine messenger or emissary, not the deity itself.

units.text: If Grandfather hadn't disliked his position as the head overly much, this sixth toe must have been pretty lucky for him. ......Come to think of it, I think I've heard about some country where it's believed that people with polydactyly should be treated as gods and revered...
units.note: Both retain treated as gods instead of revered as messengers of a god. MG corresponding sentence is row 431; broad range covers shifted segmentation.
units.japanese: ……そう言えば、どこかの国では多指症の人は神さまの使いだと信じられてて崇められてる、なんて話も聞いたような…。

units.text: ...Come to think of it, I've heard about some country where it's believed people with polydactyly should be treated as gods and revered... This is beside the point, but it's fairly common in mystery novels for a corpse to be burned to hide its identity.
units.note: Both retain treated as gods instead of revered as messengers of a god. MG corresponding sentence is row 431; broad range covers shifted segmentation.
units.japanese: もし祖父さまが当主もまんざらじゃないって思ったんなら、その６本目は幸運の指ってことになるのかもな。……そう言えば、どこかの国では多指症の人は神さまの使いだと信じられてて崇められてる、なんて話も聞いたような…。

units.text: If Grandfather thought being the head was not a bad gig, this sixth toe must have been pretty lucky for him. ......Come to think of it, I think I've heard about some country where it's believed that people with polydactyly should be treated as gods and revered...
units.note: Both retain treated as gods instead of revered as messengers of a god. MG corresponding sentence is row 431; broad range covers shifted segmentation.
units.japanese: もし祖父さまが当主もまんざらじゃないって思ったんなら、その６本目は幸運の指ってことになるのかもな。……そう言えば、どこかの国では多指症の人は神さまの使いだと信じられてて崇められてる、なんて話も聞いたような…。

description: Genji proposes that weak flames may mean prolonged burning and gradual smell accumulation. WH says the body must have begun burning long ago.
sourceReading: ではないかという marks a suggested explanation.

units.text: It isn't clear when Grandfather's corpse started burning in the incinerator. Since, according to Genji, the strength of the flames hadn't been that strong, the body must have started burning a long time ago, so that stench could slowly creep out of the furnace and fill the room bit by bit, eventually pouring out and climbing up the staircase.
units.note: Both retain must have started long ago instead of Genji proposed explanation; explicit uncertainty at 445 mitigates without restoring local modality.
units.japanese: 源次さんが言うには、火勢がそんなに強くなかったので、だいぶ前から焼かれていて、炉から漏れ出した臭いが室内に少しずつ充満し、あふれ出して階段を登ってきたのではないかという。

units.text: It isn't clear when Grandfather's corpse started burning in the incinerator. Since, according to Genji, the strength of the flames hadn't been that strong, the body must have started burning a long time ago, so that stench could slowly creep out of the furnace and fill the room bit by bit, eventually pouring out and climbing up the staircase.
units.note: Both retain must have started long ago instead of Genji proposed explanation; explicit uncertainty at 445 mitigates without restoring local modality.
units.japanese: 祖父さまの遺体はいつ頃から焼却炉で焼かれていたのかははっきりしない。源次さんが言うには、火勢がそんなに強くなかったので、だいぶ前から焼かれていて、炉から漏れ出した臭いが室内に少しずつ充満し、あふれ出して階段を登ってきたのではないかという。

units.text: It wasn't clear when Grandfather's corpse started burning in the incinerator. Since, according to Genji‐san, the flames hadn't been that strong, the body must have started burning a long time ago, and that stench must have slowly crept out of the furnace and filled the room bit by bit, eventually pouring out and climbing up the staircase.
units.note: Both retain must have started long ago instead of Genji proposed explanation; explicit uncertainty at 445 mitigates without restoring local modality.
units.japanese: 祖父さまの遺体はいつ頃から焼却炉で焼かれていたのかははっきりしない。源次さんが言うには、火勢がそんなに強くなかったので、だいぶ前から焼かれていて、炉から漏れ出した臭いが室内に少しずつ充満し、あふれ出して階段を登ってきたのではないかという。

description: The mansion is supposed to be secured; WH says its doors and windows were checked.
sourceReading: 戸締りがされていることになっている states a reported secured state, not merely an inspection.

units.text: However, according to Genji-san, the boiler room is usually locked. ......The possibility that someone outside our group had snuck in and committed the crime was overwhelmingly high, and there was also a good chance that this person was walking around with something like a master key. ...After all, the doors and windows throughout the mansion had been checked. But despite that, the culprit was able to strut around the mansion freely.
units.note: Both retain doors/windows had been checked instead of supposed secured condition, adding an asserted verification event.
units.japanese: …何しろ、今の屋敷内は戸締りがされていることになっている。

units.text: However, according to Genji-san, the boiler room is usually locked. ......The possibility that someone outside our group had snuck in and committed the crime was overwhelmingly high, and there was also a good chance that this person was walking around with something like a master key. ...After all, the doors and windows throughout the mansion had been checked. But despite that, the culprit was able to strut around the mansion freely.
units.note: Both retain doors/windows had been checked instead of supposed secured condition, adding an asserted verification event.
units.japanese: しかし、源次さんが言うには、ボイラー室は普段から施錠されているという。……俺たち以外の誰かが潜んでいて犯行に及んでいる可能性が限りなく高くなり、しかもそいつはマスターキーのようなものを持ち歩いている可能性も高い。…何しろ、今の屋敷内は戸締りがされていることになっている。にもかかわらず、犯人はこうして屋敷内を自由に闊歩しているのだから。

units.text: However, according to Genji‐san, the boiler room is usually locked. ......The probability that someone outside our group was lurking around committing the crimes was now overwhelmingly high, and there was also a good chance that this person was walking around with something like a master key. ...After all, the doors and windows throughout the mansion had been checked. But despite that, the culprit was freely strutting around the mansion.
units.note: Both retain doors/windows had been checked instead of supposed secured condition, adding an asserted verification event.
units.japanese: しかし、源次さんが言うには、ボイラー室は普段から施錠されているという。……俺たち以外の誰かが潜んでいて犯行に及んでいる可能性が限りなく高くなり、しかもそいつはマスターキーのようなものを持ち歩いている可能性も高い。…何しろ、今の屋敷内は戸締りがされていることになっている。にもかかわらず、犯人はこうして屋敷内を自由に闊歩しているのだから。

description: Battler proposes that a person staged their death with a substitute corpse, remains hidden and commits the crimes. WH sequences hiding after committing the crime.
sourceReading: 隠れ潜んでいて犯行に及んでいる makes concealment the state enabling ongoing crimes.

units.text: Had the culprit prepared a fake body beforehand and disguised it to make it look like they'd died...when they'd actually hid somewhere after committing the crime...? ...It sounds ridiculous, but that doesn't mean it's an impossible trick.
units.note: MG keeps hiding after committing the crime, rather than staged-dead culprit remaining hidden and committing crimes. UP restores hiding then continued killings.
units.japanese: 予め身代わりの死体を用意し、自らを死んだと偽装してどこかに隠れ潜んでいて犯行に及んでいるとか…？

units.text: Did the culprit prepare a fake body beforehand and alter it to make it look like they'd died, ...even though they were actually hiding somewhere after committing the crime...? ...It may sound ridiculous, but it wouldn't be an impossible trick to pull off.
units.note: MG keeps hiding after committing the crime, rather than staged-dead culprit remaining hidden and committing crimes. UP restores hiding then continued killings.
units.japanese: 予め身代わりの死体を用意し、自らを死んだと偽装してどこかに隠れ潜んでいて犯行に及んでいるとか…？…そんな馬鹿なと思うが、それでも不可能なトリックじゃない。

description: Battler asks who this witch calling herself Maria is. WH asks who they are, Maria and the one claiming to be a witch.
sourceReading: 真里亞と名乗る modifies 魔女: a single unsettling characterization of Maria.

units.text: ...Just what kind of person is Maria...? .........I only know what Maria was like six years ago, when she was three.  She had been pure and obedient...a good kid. This new Maria six years later and the Maria I knew, ...didn't seem to fit together. ......Just who are they...Maria and the one who claims to be a 'witch'...?
units.note: Both restore single witch calling herself Maria, not separate Maria and another witch.
units.japanese: ……誰なんだ、この、真里亞と名乗る“魔女”は…。

description: The source describes inexplicable incidents as evidence of witch existence to Maria. WH labels the crimes unsolvable.
sourceReading: 不可解 means puzzling or inexplicable, without establishing impossibility of solution.

units.text: To Maria, who obstinately believes in the witch, ......this series of unsolvable crimes is proof that the witch actually exists. Every time something occurs that would be difficult for a human, it becomes a little harder for the rest of us to not believe in Beatrice. It must be an 'intense pleasure' for Maria to see her relatives, who once firmly denied the witch's existence, start acknowledging that witch's existence one by one...
units.note: Both retain unsolvable crimes instead of inexplicable incidents; Maria viewpoint is preserved but characterization becomes categorical unsolvability.
units.japanese: 魔女の存在を頑なに妄信する彼女にとっては、……この一連の不可解な事件は全て、魔女が確かに存在する証。

units.text: To Maria, who obstinately believes in the witch, ......this series of unsolvable crimes is proof that the witch actually exists. Every time something occurs that would be difficult for a human, it becomes a little harder for the rest of us to not believe in Beatrice. It must be an "intense pleasure" for Maria to see her relatives, who once firmly denied the witch's existence, start acknowledging that witch's existence one by one...
units.note: Both retain unsolvable crimes instead of inexplicable incidents; Maria viewpoint is preserved but characterization becomes categorical unsolvability.
units.japanese: 魔女の存在を頑なに妄信する彼女にとっては、……この一連の不可解な事件は全て、魔女が確かに存在する証。人間には困難な何かが起こる度に、俺たちはベアトリーチェという魔女の存在を信じなければならなくなる。それは真里亞にとって、…かつて頑なにその存在を否定し続けた親族たちが、次々に魔女の存在を認めていくという“痛快”なことでもある…。

units.text: To her, with her obstinate belief in witches, ......this series of unsolvable crimes is proof that witches actually exist. Every time something occurs that would be difficult for a human, it becomes a little harder for the rest of us to not believe in that witch called Beatrice. It must be an "intense pleasure" for Maria...to see her relatives, who once firmly denied the witch's existence, start acknowledging her existence one by one...
units.note: Both retain unsolvable crimes instead of inexplicable incidents; Maria viewpoint is preserved but characterization becomes categorical unsolvability.
units.japanese: 魔女の存在を頑なに妄信する彼女にとっては、……この一連の不可解な事件は全て、魔女が確かに存在する証。人間には困難な何かが起こる度に、俺たちはベアトリーチェという魔女の存在を信じなければならなくなる。それは真里亞にとって、…かつて頑なにその存在を否定し続けた親族たちが、次々に魔女の存在を認めていくという“痛快”なことでもある…。

description: Battler tentatively excludes Maria herself as the nineteenth person after invoking her alibi. WH instead denies existence of any nineteenth person.
sourceReading: The continuing subject is Maria: she is merely an enthralled messenger and not the nineteenth person.

units.text: All that's certain is that Maria has been with the rest of us constantly, has always had an alibi, and hasn't done anything that would put her under suspicion. She's simply overjoyed at being made Beatrice's messenger, and there certainly isn't a 19th person... ...............Supposedly.
units.note: Both restore tentative exclusion of Maria herself as nineteenth person, not general denial of a nineteenth person.
units.japanese: ……ベアトリーチェのメッセンジャーにされ、心酔しているだけで、決して１９人目ではない。

description: Battler wonders whether Jessica was present to see Kanon die. WH says she probably cared for him until death, adding an extended caregiving role and strengthening possibility.
sourceReading: 死の瞬間を看取ったのかもしれない concerns possible attendance at the deathbed moment.

units.text: Jessica was crouched in the corridor, crying in anguish. She had probably been taking care of Kanon until the moment of his death. George-aniki tried to approach her with words of comfort, but when Jessica pushed him away, he stopped trying to force her to talk and left her alone.
units.note: Both retain probably taking care until death rather than possible presence at death, adding sustained caregiving and strengthening likelihood.
units.japanese: ……嘉音くんの死の瞬間を、看取ったのかもしれない。

units.text: Jessica was crouched in the corridor, crying softly. ...She had probably been taking care of Kanon-kun until the moment of his death. George-aniki tried to approach her with words of comfort, but when Jessica pushed him away, he stopped trying to force her to talk and left her alone.
units.note: Both retain probably taking care until death rather than possible presence at death, adding sustained caregiving and strengthening likelihood.
units.japanese:
廊下では朱志香がしゃがみ込み、さめざめと泣いていた。
……嘉音くんの死の瞬間を、看取ったのかもしれない。譲治の兄貴が慰めの言葉を掛けているが、朱志香がそれを拒絶したため、それ以上は無理に関わろうとせず、そっとしておいていた。

units.text:
Jessica was crouched in the corridor, crying in anguish.
......She had probably been taking care of Kanon‐kun until the moment of his death. George‐aniki tried to approach her with words of comfort, but when Jessica pushed him away, he stopped trying to interfere and left her alone.
units.note: Both retain probably taking care until death rather than possible presence at death, adding sustained caregiving and strengthening likelihood.
units.japanese:
廊下では朱志香がしゃがみ込み、さめざめと泣いていた。
……嘉音くんの死の瞬間を、看取ったのかもしれない。譲治の兄貴が慰めの言葉を掛けているが、朱志香がそれを拒絶したため、それ以上は無理に関わろうとせず、そっとしておいていた。

description: The source explicitly contrasts Jessica’s usual sensitivity to others with her emotional outburst that leaves Kumasawa ashamed. WH keeps surprise at the outburst but omits the considerate baseline.
sourceReading: 普段、細かい気遣いのできる describes her normal capacity for small acts of consideration.

units.text: Emotion-filled words that I never thought I'd hear coming from Jessica's mouth tumbled out. ...Kumasawa, looking truly sorry, could do nothing but hang her head...
units.note: MG omits usually considerate baseline; UP normally tactful restores it.
units.japanese: 普段、細かい気遣いのできる朱志香の口から出たとは思えない、感情的な言葉が飛び出す。

units.text: Emotion-filled words that I never thought I'd hear coming from Jessica's mouth tumbled out. ...Kumasawa, looking truly sorry, could do nothing but hang her head...
units.note: MG omits usually considerate baseline; UP normally tactful restores it.
units.japanese: 普段、細かい気遣いのできる朱志香の口から出たとは思えない、感情的な言葉が飛び出す。…熊沢さんは申し訳ないと、うな垂れるしかなかった…。

description: As Battler addresses Jessica, George says now is not the time to speak to her. WH says Battler should not have said that, criticizing a completed utterance.
sourceReading: 今は言葉を掛けるべきじゃない is present advice not to approach with words now, grounded in shared overwhelming grief.

units.text: ".........You shouldn't have said that.  ...It's the same for me, ......and probably Battler-kun as well, okay?  We don't know what's going on, and it feels like our hearts are going to split open......"
units.note: MG should not talk now and UP now is not time restore prospective advice rather than criticizing a completed utterance.
units.japanese: 「………今は言葉を掛けるべきじゃない。…僕だって、……そして戦人くんもだろ？

description: George asks whether the culprit is someone we know well. WH asks whether it is someone I know well, narrowing the familiarity set.
sourceReading: 僕ら explicitly refers to the group rather than George alone.

units.text: "What do you mean by that?!  ...Is it possible that the culprit is someone I know well, and that, for some reason, you're covering for them by remaining silent?!  Who gave you that letter?!"
units.note: Both restore someone we know well, not George alone.
units.japanese: 「それはどういう意味だい？！　…ひょっとして、僕らのよく知る人物が犯人で、…君は何かの事情からそれを庇うために黙っているというのかい？！　君は、あの手紙を誰にもらったんだい！」

description: Battler says they can take their time investigating tonight after first selecting a refuge. WH says tonight they can put off the search.
sourceReading: 今夜、ゆっくりできる gives time available for investigation, contrasting the immediate shelter decision.

units.text: "...I agree strongly with Natsuhi oba-san.  ......Tonight, we can put off searching for the culprit.  Instead, it would be better to think of where we can barricade ourselves in."
units.note: Both restore leisurely investigation tonight after finding refuge rather than putting it off tonight.
units.japanese: 「…夏妃伯母さんに極めて同感だぜ。……犯人探しは今夜、ゆっくりできるさ。今はどこで篭城するかを考えた方がいい。」

description: Natsuhi says it should be safe to assume the culprit already obtained a master key in the servant room. WH says it is conceivable.
sourceReading: 考えて間違いないでしょう expresses a qualified but confident conclusion, stronger than possibility alone.

units.text: ".........We know there's a chance that the culprit visited the servant room at some point in time so that they could unlock the shutter to the rose garden shed.  It's conceivable they obtained a master key from there earlier on."
units.note: MG retains merely conceivable acquisition. UP very likely restores strong inference, though source says safe to assume rather than certainty of witnessed acquisition.
units.japanese: 「………そもそも犯人は、薔薇庭園倉庫のシャッターを開けるために、一度使用人室を訪れている可能性があります。そこでマスターキーをすでに入手していると考えて間違いないでしょう。」

units.text: "......In the first place, we know the culprit may have visited the servant room at some point to unlock the garden shed shutter. It's conceivable that they obtained a master key from there earlier on."
units.note: MG retains merely conceivable acquisition. UP very likely restores strong inference, though source says safe to assume rather than certainty of witnessed acquisition.
units.japanese: 「………そもそも犯人は、薔薇庭園倉庫のシャッターを開けるために、一度使用人室を訪れている可能性があります。そこでマスターキーをすでに入手していると考えて間違いないでしょう」

description: The narration acknowledges somewhat lax management resulting from exchanging keys at shift changes. WH adds probably and at times in the past, making the admission tentative and episodic.
sourceReading: 管理が若干ずさんであったことを認めなければならなかった acknowledges the laxity, with 若干 qualifying degree rather than certainty.

units.text: There were many servants serving the Ushiromiya family. Because of that, there were several master keys. Furthermore, every time the shifts changed, the keys were passed between servants, and we had to acknowledge that this had probably gotten a bit sloppy at times in the past.
units.note: MG retains probably and episodic past sloppiness. UP restores direct acknowledgment of somewhat sloppy shift-change management.
units.japanese: また、勤務が交代する度に、それらを使用人の間でやり取りしていたため、その辺りの管理が若干ずさんであったことを認めなければならなかった。

units.text: There were many servants serving the Ushiromiya family. Because of that, there were several master keys. Furthermore, every time one employee started or finished working, the keys were passed between servants, and we had to acknowledge that this had probably gotten a bit sloppy at times in the past.
units.note: MG retains probably and episodic past sloppiness. UP restores direct acknowledgment of somewhat sloppy shift-change management.
units.japanese:
右代宮家は使用人の人数も少なくはない。
そのため、マスターキーは複数本あった。また、勤務が交代する度に、それらを使用人の間でやり取りしていたため、その辺りの管理が若干ずさんであったことを認めなければならなかった。

description: George says the enemy lacks the strength to openly attack the group gathered in one room. WH adds that the room is secure, implying an architectural protection absent from the argument.
sourceReading: 一部屋に固まっている describes clustering together; it does not characterize the room as secure.

units.text: ".........The enemy won't approach us from the front.  I don't know about the first six, but if we look at what happened to my parents and Kanon-kun, ...and even Grandfather, the enemy has only gone after isolated people.  They don't have the power to assault all of us openly in a secure room."
units.note: Both retain secure room, adding architectural security to source argument about group strength. No particular secure room has yet been selected.
units.japanese: 「………敵は正面から来ないよ。最初の６人はともかく、母さんたちや嘉音くん、…そしてお祖父さまの例を見る限り、敵は孤立した人間だけを狙ってる。一部屋に固まっている僕たちのところへ堂々と乗り込んでこられるほどの力はないんだよ。」

units.text: "...The enemy won't approach us from the front. I don't know about the first six, but if we look at what happened to my parents and Kanon-kun, ...and even Grandfather, the enemy has only gone after isolated people. They don't have the power to assault all of us openly in a secure room."
units.note: Both retain secure room, adding architectural security to source argument about group strength. No particular secure room has yet been selected.
units.japanese: 「………敵は正面から来ないよ。最初の６人はともかく、母さんたちや嘉音くん、…そしてお祖父さまの例を見る限り、敵は孤立した人間だけを狙ってる。一部屋に固まっている僕たちのところへ堂々と乗り込んでこられるほどの力はないんだよ」

units.text: ".........The enemy won't approach us from the front. I don't know about the first six, but if we look at what happened to my parents and Kanon‐kun, ...and even Grandfather, the enemy has only gone after isolated people. They don't have the power to assault all of us openly in a secure room."
units.note: Both retain secure room, adding architectural security to source argument about group strength. No particular secure room has yet been selected.
units.japanese: 「………敵は正面から来ないよ。最初の６人はともかく、母さんたちや嘉音くん、…そしてお祖父さまの例を見る限り、敵は孤立した人間だけを狙ってる。一部屋に固まっている僕たちのところへ堂々と乗り込んでこられるほどの力はないんだよ」

description: George conditionally invokes Kinzo getting past the receipt constraint and leaving voluntarily. WH specifies that Natsuhi and Eva walked right past him and thereby removed the receipt.
sourceReading: うまくレシートをやり過ごして does not describe people walking past Kinzo or assign their walking as the removal mechanism.

units.text: "According to your theory, Grandfather skillfully let Natsuhi oba-san and Mother walk right past him, which removed the receipt, and then left the room of his own free will.  ...If you think about it that way, it still might have some worth as a place to barricade ourselves in..."
units.note: Both restore conditional voluntary departure after evading receipt without invented Natsuhi/Eva walking past Kinzo.
units.japanese: 「戦人くんの説の、お祖父さまがうまくレシートをやり過ごして自分の意思で部屋を出た、…と考えるなら、篭城の価値はあるかもしれない…。」

description: Jessica declares she will neither run nor hide and proposes waiting openly. WH says they cannot run away or hide.
sourceReading: 逃げも隠れもしない is a defiant refusal in the proposal, not a statement of incapacity.

units.text: "...Of course, I don't think we'll be able to find them if we just start searching now.  ...In the end, we can't do anything but wait.  Th en it doesn't matter where we wait, does it?!  We can't run away or hide.  Why don't we just take it easy in the parlor, watching TV or something and waiting for Beatrice-sama to appear?!"
units.note: Both restore Jessica refusal to run/hide as volition, not inability.
units.japanese: らどこで待ったって同じだろ？！　逃げも隠れもしない。客間でテレビでも見ながら、のんびり現れるのをまとうじゃねぇかよ、ベアトリーチェさまをよぉ！」

description: Nanjo says they should not take risks until police arrive. WH permits a reading that some risks are acceptable by adding too many.
sourceReading: 危険を冒すべきではありません contains no excess threshold.

units.text: "Well said......  We shouldn't take too many risks before the police get here."
units.note: MG replaces too many with needless risks but still allows risks deemed necessary rather than source categorical avoid risks. UP retains too many.
units.japanese: 「正論ですな……。警察が来るまで、危険を冒すべきではありません。」

units.text: "Well said... We shouldn't take needless risks before the police arrive."
units.note: MG replaces too many with needless risks but still allows risks deemed necessary rather than source categorical avoid risks. UP retains too many.
units.japanese: 「正論ですな……。警察が来るまで、危険を冒すべきではありません」

units.text: "Well said...... We shouldn't take too many risks before the police get here."
units.note: MG replaces too many with needless risks but still allows risks deemed necessary rather than source categorical avoid risks. UP retains too many.
units.japanese: 「正論ですな……。警察が来るまで、危険を冒すべきではありません」

description: Kyrie explains that game theory is deep and requires substantial study to read moves as thoroughly as Battler imagines. WH supplies the opponent as the specific object of study.
sourceReading: 相当の勉強 refers to considerable learning in the ongoing discussion of the complex discipline; no opponent object is specified.

units.text: "But you can't believe in it blindly.  Game theory is a very deep and complicated subject.  Chessboard thinking is just my interpretation that skims the surface of game theory.  ......In order to thoroughly read your opponent's moves like you are imagining, you need to study your opponent.  Additionally, while chessboard theory is convenient and practical, it isn't perfect.  It has many weak points despite its convenience."
units.note: MG still specifies study your opponent instead of substantial study of the deep subject. UP restores do a lot of study.
units.japanese: 「でもね、妄信しちゃ駄目よ。ゲーム理論は非常に奥深く複雑な学問なの。チェス盤思考はその上辺だけを私なりに解釈した考え方に過ぎない。……戦人くんが想像するほどに、相手の手の内を読みきるには、相当の勉強が必要よ。しかも、チェス盤理論は応用の利く便利なものではあっても完璧ではない。便利ではあっても弱点が多い。」

units.text: "But you can't believe in it blindly. Game theory is a very deep and complicated subject. Chessboard thinking is just my interpretation that skims the surface of game theory. ...In order to thoroughly read your opponent's moves like you're imagining, you need to study your opponent.
units.note: MG still specifies study your opponent instead of substantial study of the deep subject. UP restores do a lot of study.

「でもね、妄信しちゃ駄目よ。ゲーム理論は非常に奥深く複雑な学問なの。チェス盤思考はその上辺だけを私なりに解釈した考え方に過ぎない。……戦人くんが想像するほどに、相手の手の内を読みきるには、相当の勉強が必要よ」
「しかも、チェス盤理論は応用の利く便利なものではあっても完璧ではない。便利ではあっても弱点が多い」

units.text: Additionally, while chessboard theory is convenient and practical, it isn't perfect. It has many weak points despite its convenience."
units.note: MG still specifies study your opponent instead of substantial study of the deep subject. UP restores do a lot of study.
