「でもね、妄信しちゃ駄目よ。ゲーム理論は非常に奥深く複雑な学問なの。チェス盤思考はその上辺だけを私なりに解釈した考え方に過ぎない。……戦人くんが想像するほどに、相手の手の内を読みきるには、相当の勉強が必要よ」
「しかも、チェス盤理論は応用の利く便利なものではあっても完璧ではない。便利ではあっても弱点が多い」

description: Battler thinks he has sometimes glimpsed the outline of whoever lies behind the case. WH says he has perceived that person’s plans many times.
sourceReading: 何者かの輪郭 concerns a sketch of the hidden person or agent; it is not explicitly their plans. 何度か is several instances, not a strong many-times claim.

units.text: Many times, I've thought that by using chessboard thinking, I could perceive the plans of the person hiding behind this case. However, I don't know anything about the culprit. ......Am I just playing in a labyrinth of thought?
units.note: MG restores tentative vague information about culprit and avoids plans/many times. UP restores glimpse of person rather than plans but retains many times for source several occasions.
units.japanese: 俺はチェス盤思考で、事件の裏に潜む何者かの輪郭を、何度か捉えたような気でいる。

units.text:
Many times, I'd thought that by using chessboard thinking, I had gotten a glimpse into the person behind these crimes. However, I don't know anything about the culprit.
......Am I just playing in a labyrinth of thought?
units.note: MG restores tentative vague information about culprit and avoids plans/many times. UP restores glimpse of person rather than plans but retains many times for source several occasions.
units.japanese:
俺はチェス盤思考で、事件の裏に潜む何者かの輪郭を、何度か捉えたような気でいる。しかし、俺は犯人のことを何もわかっていない。
……全ては思考の迷路遊びでしかないのか。

description: Someone warns poison may have been added during the kitchen and parlor’s unattended interval. WH instead says it might have been death by poison. This removes the direct food-contamination premise for refusing dinner.
sourceReading: その際に毒を盛られた links poisoning to the just-described temporary absence, with the prepared meal as the danger.

units.text: Everyone was already trapped by paranoia. ...Kumasawa-san had prepared dinner at one point, but after the case involving George-aniki's parents, the kitchen and the parlor had become devoid of people. Someone had said that it might have been death by poison. ...Because of that, we were unable to even touch the food that Kumasawa-san had taken the trouble to make for us.
units.note: Both restore possible food contamination during unattended interval as reason for refusing dinner, separate from first murders poison theory.
units.japanese: その際に毒を盛られたかもしれないと誰かが言い出した。

description: Maria says Beatrice has magic and familiars and might use them to arrange for Kinzo to come out of his own accord. WH invents the causal ability to create a familiar, then makes the departure forced.
sourceReading: 魔法があるし、使い魔だっている lists available resources; 自分から ... 仕向ける preserves induced voluntary departure.

units.text: "............Just as Battler reasoned.  ...Beatrice can't go inside.  But since she has magic, she can create a familiar.  Using them, she might have been able to force Grandfather to leave the study."
units.note: Both restore possession of magic and familiars, without invented familiar creation. MG restores inducing voluntary departure; UP retains force Grandfather to leave, removing of his own accord.
units.japanese: 「…………戦人が推理した通りだよ。…ベアトリーチェは中に入れない。でも、彼女には魔法があるし、使い魔だっている。それらを使って、お祖父さまが自分から書斎を出てくるように仕向けることはできるかも。」

units.text: "............Just as Battler reasoned. ...Beatrice can't go inside. But she has magic, and she also has familiars. Using those, she might have been able to force Grandfather to leave the study."
units.note: Both restore possession of magic and familiars, without invented familiar creation. MG restores inducing voluntary departure; UP retains force Grandfather to leave, removing of his own accord.
units.japanese: 「…………戦人が推理した通りだよ。…ベアトリーチェは中に入れない。でも、彼女には魔法があるし、使い魔だっている。それらを使って、お祖父さまが自分から書斎を出てくるように仕向けることはできるかも」

description: Because he heard rumors beforehand, Battler is not especially surprised by the study. WH says he heard rumors but was still shocked.
sourceReading: ので ... それほど驚きはしなかった is a causal mitigation of surprise, not a concessive persistence of shock.

units.text: Grandfather's study.........I'd heard rumors about it beforehand, but I was still shocked. He had done nothing more than fortify it thoroughly with his occult hobbies. ...If Grandfather's hobby had been chasing after pop idols, these walls might be buried beneath idol posters. Even if I didn't understand it, I did realize that this room was a bundle of all his hobbies.
units.note: Both restore rumor knowledge reducing surprise.
units.japanese: 祖父さまの書斎は、………事前に噂を聞いていたので、それほど驚きはしなかった。

description: Battler is exasperated or overwhelmed by the intolerable smell despite accepting the hobby-filled room. WH calls him dumbfounded, shifting toward astonishment.
sourceReading: 閉口する is finding something intolerable or being at a loss from vexation here, not merely surprise.

units.text: Even so, I couldn't help but remain dumbfounded by the smell of his creepy medicine and the sweet stench that seemed to melt my head...
units.note: Both retain dumbfounded rather than being exasperated/overwhelmed by intolerable odor.
units.japanese: しかしそれでも、怪しげな薬物の臭いと、脳を溶かすような甘い臭いにはさすがに閉口するしかなかった…。

units.text: Even so, I couldn't help but remain dumbfounded by the smell of his creepy medicine and the sweet stench that seemed to melt my head...
units.note: Both retain dumbfounded rather than being exasperated/overwhelmed by intolerable odor.
units.japanese: しかしそれでも、怪しげな薬物の臭いと、脳を溶かすような甘い臭いにはさすがに閉口するしかなかった…。

description: Battler guesses that Maria had hoped another suspicious magic circle would appear. WH says normally you would expect one, turning his inference about her particular interest into a generic expectation.
sourceReading: 大方 ... 期待してたんだろ speculates about Maria’s past expectation in direct address.

units.text: "Normally, you'd expect another weird magic circle to show up."
units.note: Both restore Battler inference that Maria specifically hoped for another circle, rather than generic expectation.
units.japanese: 「大方、また怪しげな魔法陣でも出てくるのを期待してたんだろ。」

description: Battler describes the witch story as already deified among the servants, compatible with Kinzo’s occult interests, and possibly further inflated by things Kinzo told them. WH makes Genji personally close to Kinzo and his hobbies, then personally indoctrinated and increasingly deifying the witch.
sourceReading: The prior topic is the deified Beatrice ghost story among 使用人たち. 親和性 describes compatibility with Kinzo’s occult tastes; the following godification continues the servants’ shared belief, rather than specifying Genji alone.

units.text: ...Still, I had a good guess. ...The ghost story of the witch Beatrice had long been deified among the servants. ......He had probably been very close to Grandfather and his occult hobbies. So there was a good chance that he'd been indoctrinated with even weirder things, and had increasingly come to deify the witch. As Grandfather's most trusted servant, who had sworn loyalty to him, he might be the most influenced by the illusion of the witch that Grandfather had created...
units.note: Both retain Genji personally close to Kinzo/hobbies and personally indoctrinated rather than witch story affinity and possible collective inflation among servants.
units.japanese:
……オカルト趣味の祖父さまとも、さぞや親和性が高いだろう。
だから、祖父さまにさらに妙なことを吹き込まれ、ますますに魔女を神格化していった可能性は高い。

units.text: ...The ghost story of the witch Beatrice had long been deified among the servants. ...He had probably been very close to Grandfather and his occult hobbies. So there was a good chance that he'd been indoctrinated with even weirder things, and had increasingly come to deify the witch. As Grandfather's most trusted servant, who had sworn loyalty to him, he might be the most influenced by the illusion of the witch that Grandfather had created...
units.note: Both retain Genji personally close to Kinzo/hobbies and personally indoctrinated rather than witch story affinity and possible collective inflation among servants.
units.japanese: …ベアトリーチェという魔女は、使用人たちの間ではすでに神格化した怪談だ。……オカルト趣味の祖父さまとも、さぞや親和性が高いだろう。だから、祖父さまにさらに妙なことを吹き込まれ、ますますに魔女を神格化していった可能性は高い。祖父さまに忠誠を誓う最も信頼された使用人だからこそ、祖父さまの生み出した魔女幻想にもっとも感化されているとも言える…。

units.text: ...The ghost story of the witch Beatrice had long been deified among the servants. ......He had probably been very close to Grandfather, too, and his occult hobbies. So there was a good chance that he'd been indoctrinated with even weirder things, and had increasingly come to deify the witch. As Grandfather's most trusted servant, who had sworn loyalty to him, he might be the most influenced by the witch illusion that Grandfather had created...
units.note: Both retain Genji personally close to Kinzo/hobbies and personally indoctrinated rather than witch story affinity and possible collective inflation among servants.
units.japanese: …ベアトリーチェという魔女は、使用人たちの間ではすでに神格化した怪談だ。……オカルト趣味の祖父さまとも、さぞや親和性が高いだろう。だから、祖父さまにさらに妙なことを吹き込まれ、ますますに魔女を神格化していった可能性は高い。祖父さまに忠誠を誓う最も信頼された使用人だからこそ、祖父さまの生み出した魔女幻想にもっとも感化されているとも言える…。

description: Genji says Kinzo loved Beatrice deeply enough to be driven into such madness. WH instead says madness drove him to do what is visible in the room.
sourceReading: このような狂気に駆り立てるほどに qualifies the intensity of the preceding love, with madness as its consequence.

units.text: ......The Master loved Beatrice-sama from the bottom of his heart.  ...It was that madness which drove him to do all that you see here." As Genji-san said this, he spread his arms, as though asking us to look at this room, filled with the signs of Grandfather's madness.
units.note: Both retain madness driving visible research rather than love deep enough to drive him into madness.
units.japanese: ……お館様はベアトリーチェさまを、心の底から愛しておられたのです。…このような狂気に駆り立てるほどに。」

units.text: ...The Master loved Beatrice-sama from the bottom of his heart. ...It was that madness which drove him to do all that you see here."
units.note: Both retain madness driving visible research rather than love deep enough to drive him into madness.
units.japanese: 「……お館様はベアトリーチェさまを、心の底から愛しておられたのです。…このような凶気に駆り立てるほどに」

units.text: "......The Master loved Beatrice‐sama from the bottom of his heart. ...It was that madness which drove him to do all that you see here."
units.note: Both retain madness driving visible research rather than love deep enough to drive him into madness.
units.japanese: 「……お館様はベアトリーチェさまを、心の底から愛しておられたのです。…このような凶気に駆り立てるほどに」

description: The source identifies sorrow at losing the woman and inability to give up on that loss. WH gives sorrow he cannot escape, losing the refusal to relinquish her that motivates resurrection.
sourceReading: それを諦めきれぬ retains failure to accept or abandon the lost beloved, not just enduring sadness.

units.text: All that had been on Grandfather's mind was the loss of a beloved woman, ......and the sorrow that he couldn't escape. ......Earlier, this room had seemed creepy, ...but in an instant, our understanding of it began to change.
units.note: MG inescapable sorrow omits inability to give up lost woman. UP explicitly restores inability to give up on her.
units.japanese: 祖父さまの胸中にあったのは、愛する女性を失い、……それを諦めきれぬ悲しみだけ。

units.text: The only thing on Grandfather's mind had been the loss of a beloved woman... ...and his inescapable sorrow. ...Earlier, this room had seemed creepy, ...but in an instant, it had changed into something we could understand completely.
units.note: MG inescapable sorrow omits inability to give up lost woman. UP explicitly restores inability to give up on her.
units.japanese: 祖父さまの胸中にあったのは、愛する女性を失い、……それを諦めきれぬ悲しみだけ。……ついさっきまで、不気味だと思っていたこの部屋は、…その瞬間に全て理解できるものとなって変わった。

description: The source says Kinzo wants the image of a woman dead for more than thirty years to come alive once again. WH adds one last time, suggesting a final encounter.
sourceReading: もう一度 is once again, with no last or final limitation.

units.text: The creepy books, the magic circles, the medicine, ...all of it. ......All just because he wanted to revive the face of a single woman who had left this world for thirty years, for one last time...
units.note: Both remove one last time; UP once more restores recurrence, MG revive conveys it without finality.
units.japanese: ……すでにこの世を去って３０年以上も経つたったひとりの女性の面影をもう一度蘇らせたいがためだけに…。

description: The source describes Kinzo devoting day after day without sparing a day to his research. WH says he never regretted a minute, inventing an explicit evaluation of his life choices.
sourceReading: 一日も惜しまず conveys unstinting expenditure of time; it does not state absence of regret.

units.text: ......This room was covered with piles upon piles of things having to do with black magic. And Grandfather had spent every day shut in here, immersed in his research and isolated from the outside world, never regretting one minute of it. ......You couldn't help but realize how deep Grandfather's love for Beatrice was...
units.note: MG retains never regretting one minute, invented evaluation. UP day after long day and never taking a day off restore sustained devotion.
units.japanese: そして祖父さまが今日まで一日も惜しまずに閉じ篭り続け、自身の研究に没頭した気の遠くなるような日々。

units.text: ...This room was covered with piles upon piles of things having to do with black magic. And Grandfather spent every day shut in here, immersed in his research and isolated from the outside world, never regretting one minute of it. ...You couldn't help but recognize the depths of Grandfather's love for Beatrice...
units.note: MG retains never regretting one minute, invented evaluation. UP day after long day and never taking a day off restore sustained devotion.
units.japanese:
……この部屋いっぱいに詰め込まれた黒魔術関係の山々。
そして祖父さまが今日まで一日も惜しまずに閉じ篭り続け、自身の研究に没頭した気の遠くなるような日々。……そこから、祖父さまが如何にベアトリーチェを愛したかを感じずにはいられない…。

description: The source says Genji remains silent, presumably because confessing would betray his master even after death. WH says he broke his silence and frames the confession as occurring.
sourceReading: 無言を貫いた is continued silence; それを告白することは describes the hypothetical act that explains his refusal.

units.text: With closed eyes, and an expression as though he was remembering something from the distant past, ......Genji had broken his long silence. ............In making that confession, he probably felt like he was betraying his one and only Master in the most serious way, even though that person was already dead.
units.note: MG retains broken silence/confession occurrence. UP restores maintained silence and hypothetical betrayal.
units.japanese:
源次さんは目蓋を閉じ、遠い日の何かを思い出すような表情を浮かべながらも、
……無言を貫いた。
…………それを告白することは、すでに死んでいても、自分の唯一の主に対する最大の裏切りになってしまうからだろう。

units.text: With closed eyes and the expression of one remembering something from the distant past, ...Genji had broken his long silence. ......In making that confession, he probably felt like he was betraying his one and only Master in the most serious way, even though that person was already dead.
units.note: MG retains broken silence/confession occurrence. UP restores maintained silence and hypothetical betrayal.
units.japanese: 源次さんは目蓋を閉じ、遠い日の何かを思い出すような表情を浮かべながらも、……無言を貫いた。…………それを告白することは、すでに死んでいても、自分の唯一の主に対する最大の裏切りになってしまうからだろう。

description: The source says he tells the resurrection story, believes it, and makes others believe it, carrying it to his grave. WH says he was told, believed and was made to believe.
sourceReading: 語り and 信じさせ are active telling and causative persuasion; only 信じ is his own belief.

units.text: ......Beatrice has revived as a witch, and she is in the mansion even now. ......He had been told that, had believed it, ...had been made to believe it, .........and Genji would take that with him to the grave. This might have been the last service he offered up to his Master.
units.note: Both restore active mantra, belief and making others believe instead of passive indoctrination.
units.japanese:
……そう語り、
信じ、
…信じさせ。
………源次は墓の中までそれを持っていく。

description: Natsuhi states that Kinzo funded the orphanage and opened household servant positions as practical social education. WH introduces it is said, making the factual background itself hearsay before the separately rejected slander.
sourceReading: Her declarative assistance/employment account is distinguished from fools spreading claims of filthy hobbies; it carries no hearsay marker.

units.text: "............It's a worthless story.  It is said that Father heavily supported an orphanage...and that they started having the orphans employed as servants for his house, as part of their social studies.  ...It's nothing more than a story spread by some foolish people, saying that this had something to do with one of Father's filthy hobbies."
units.note: Both directly state funding and employment background before separately rejecting slander, without it is said.
units.japanese: 「……………下らない話です。お父様は孤児院に莫大な援助をし、社会勉強の一環として、当家の使用人雇用枠を開放していました。…それを、お父様に汚らわしい趣味があると吹聴する愚か者がいたというだけの話です。」

description: Maria says continued prayer awaits an almost impossibly unlikely outcome; accumulated intention manifests with magic when that miraculous outcome occurs. WH substitutes wanting an unlimited, impossible effect and omits the rare outcome as the manifestation trigger.
sourceReading: 限りなくありえない出目 is an extraordinarily improbable result of a chance process, not an unlimited effect. 奇跡の出目が現れた時 explicitly conditions manifestation on its appearance.

units.text: ".........Magic works the same way.  ...If you want an unlimited, impossible effect, then you must pray earnestly.  ......Then, the feelings from all those stored up prayers gain magical power and become incarnate.
units.note: MG restores extremely unlikely result sought through prayer but still omits its occurrence as manifestation trigger. UP restores unlikely outcome and explicit when-result-shows trigger; impossible is contextual hyperbole for extreme improbability.
units.japanese: 「………魔術にもそういう考えはあるんだよ。…限りなくありえない出目を期待して、ひたすらに祈祷を続ける。……そうして蓄えられた祈祷の念は、奇跡の出目が現れた時、魔力を持って具現化される。

units.text: "......Magic works the same way. ...You must pray earnestly for an extremely unlikely result. ...Then, the feelings from all those stored up prayers gain magical power and become incarnate.
units.note: MG restores extremely unlikely result sought through prayer but still omits its occurrence as manifestation trigger. UP restores unlikely outcome and explicit when-result-shows trigger; impossible is contextual hyperbole for extreme improbability.
units.japanese: 「………魔術にもそういう考えはあるんだよ。…限りなくありえない出目を期待して、ひたすらに祈祷を続ける。……そうして蓄えられた祈祷の念は、奇跡の出目が現れた時、魔力を持って具現化される」

description: Nanjo says the epitaph indeed traces the subsequent course of events. WH merely says it goes on after that.
sourceReading: その後をなぞっとる connects the content to subsequent developments, setting up the couple and letter matches.

units.text: "However, Natsuhi-san...  Look, ......the epitaph goes on after that..."
units.note: Both restore epitaph fit/tracing subsequent events rather than merely continuing text.
units.japanese: 「だが、夏妃さん…。確かに、……碑文の内容は、その後をなぞっとる…。」

description: Battler searches for a different person whose head had already been pierced if the couple belong to the second twilight. WH says someone else must be gouged in the head.
sourceReading: 抉りこまれていた人物 is retrospective identification, not a new required attack.

units.text: Gouge the head and kill. ......George-aniki's parents were killed with the 'demon's icepicks' gouged into their heads. ...But if that counted for the second twilight, ......someone else must be gouged in the head...
units.note: MG must have been gouged restores past victim search. UP must be gouged retains requirement phrasing rather than already pierced person; immediate Kinzo identification mitigates.
units.japanese:
…だが、それを第二の晩にカウントするなら、
……それ以外に、頭に抉りこまれていた人物…。
candidates: someone else must be gouged in the head

units.text: Gouge the head and kill. ......George‐aniki's parents were killed with the "demon's icepicks" gouged into their heads. ...But if that counted as the second twilight, ......someone else must be gouged in the head...
units.note: MG must have been gouged restores past victim search. UP must be gouged retains requirement phrasing rather than already pierced person; immediate Kinzo identification mitigates.
units.japanese: 頭を抉りて殺せ。……絵羽伯母さんたちは頭に“悪魔のアイスピック”を抉りこまれて殺されていた。…だが、それを第二の晩にカウントするなら、……それ以外に、頭に抉りこまれていた人物…。
candidates: someone else must be gouged in the head

description: Genji contrasts Kinzo’s wisdom with his own mediocre understanding. WH frames the comparison as madness to commoners such as himself.
sourceReading: 凡庸な私 concerns ordinary or limited ability, not the social class category of commoners.

units.text: "............I don't know.  ...The Master is a man who sometimes has the wisdom to see a thousand years into the future.  However, there are times when that appears to be nothing more than madness to commoners such as myself..."
units.note: Both retain commoners rather than Genji mediocre understanding, shifting intellectual limitation to social class.
units.japanese: 「…………わかりません。…お館様は時に千年の未来を見越されるほどの聡明なお方です。しかし、凡庸な私にはそれが狂気としか映らないこともあります…。」

units.text: "......I don't know. ...The Master is a man who sometimes has the wisdom to see a thousand years into the future. However, there are times when that appears to be nothing more than madness to commoners such as myself..."
units.note: Both retain commoners rather than Genji mediocre understanding, shifting intellectual limitation to social class.
units.japanese: 「…………わかりません。…お館様は時に千年の未来を見越されるほどの聡明なお方です。しかし、凡庸な私にはそれが凶気としか映らないこともあります…」

units.text: "............I do not know. ...The Master is a man who sometimes has the wisdom to see a thousand years into the future. However, there are times when that appears to be nothing more than madness to commoners such as myself..."

units.japanese: 「…………わかりません。…お館様は時に千年の未来を見越されるほどの聡明なお方です。しかし、凡庸な私にはそれが凶気としか映らないこともあります…」

description: Battler concludes that the ring had already passed into Beatrice’s hands while Kinzo was alive. WH explicitly assigns the transfer to Kinzo handing it over.
sourceReading: 手に渡っていた establishes receipt or possession without identifying how or by whose deliberate action it arrived.

units.text: At the time that the letter had been read, Grandfather was still alive. ...But at that time, it had already been sealed with wax by the Head's Ring. ...Which meant that Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.
units.note: Both explicitly make Kinzo hand over ring rather than infer ring already in Beatrice possession during his life, adding transfer agency.
units.japanese: …ということは、祖父さまの存命中にすでに指輪はベアトリーチェの手に渡っていたことになる。

units.text: When the letter was read, Grandfather was still alive. ...But at that time, it had already been sealed with wax by the Head's Ring. ...Which meant Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.
units.note: Both explicitly make Kinzo hand over ring rather than infer ring already in Beatrice possession during his life, adding transfer agency.
units.japanese:
あの手紙の時点で、祖父さまはまだ生きていた。
…しかしあの時点ですでに“当主の指輪”による封蝋はされていた。…ということは、祖父さまの存命中にすでに指輪はベアトリーチェの手に渡っていたことになる。

units.text:

...But at that time, it had already been sealed with wax by the Head's Ring. ...Which meant that Grandfather had handed the ring over to Beatrice while he was still alive.

description: Battler initially wonders what is noteworthy about the envelope already visible on the table. WH trails off at something about it, implying suspicion before Natsuhi reveals she holds the earlier envelope.
sourceReading: それが何だというのか means what of it, not something about it.

units.text: Maria was pointing at the top of the table, where the canned food that everyone had been eating just now still lay. A western-style envelope really was sitting there, ......but something about it...
units.note: Both restore initial so what response to familiar envelope before Natsuhi reveals original still held.
units.japanese: そこには、確かにベアトリーチェの洋形封筒が置かれているが、……それが何だというのか。

description: Battler says only the brief opportunity while everyone gathered at the portrait is available for the envelope’s appearance. WH specifies a few seconds and says there was not enough time. The following narration repeats seconds where the source only describes a recent absence and diverted attention.
sourceReading: わずかの隙しかない restricts the opportunity without a seconds measurement or declaring that opportunity insufficient.

units.text: "This isn't funny, there's only the eight of us here!!  There's no way some ninth person snuck in!!  There wasn't enough time during the few seconds that we gathered around the portrait, right?!"
units.note: Both retain few seconds and not enough time at 898 plus repeated seconds at 904/906; source only brief opportunity and recently absent letter. This adds timing precision and changes opportunity claim into insufficient time.
units.japanese: 「冗談じゃねぇ、ここには俺たち８人しかいねぇんだぞ！！　９人目が、こっそり忍び込んでいたなんてこともあるわけがねぇ！！　俺たちがちょいと肖像画の前に集まっていたわずかの隙しかないんだぞッ？！」

description: Battler says only the four suspects could have placed the letter, then separately says an unidentified person among them did. WH makes the first claim only one of the four could have, suggesting exclusive capability.
sourceReading: 彼ら４人だけが scopes only over the four-person set, not a singleton within it.

units.text: Should we really be so quick to make that judgment?! But this time...in this room, in this place, in this moment...in this minimally small bit of time and space, it's obvious. Only one of the four of them could have set the letter there in our blind spot...!! We can't tell who put it there, but it's obvious that one of the four did it...!!
units.note: Both retain only one of four could have placed letter instead of only those four being possible placers followed by unidentified actual placer.
units.japanese: 彼ら４人だけが、俺たちの死角で手紙を置けた…！！

units.text: Should we really be so quick to make that judgment?! But this time...in this room, in this place, in this moment...in this minimally small bit of time and space, it's obvious. Only one of the four of them could have set the letter there in our blind spot...!! We can't tell who put it there, but it's obvious that one of the four did it...!!
units.note: Both retain only one of four could have placed letter instead of only those four being possible placers followed by unidentified actual placer.
units.japanese:
こんな短絡的な決め付けでいいんだろうか？！
だが、今この部屋この場所この瞬間というミニマムな単位の中では明白だ。彼ら４人だけが、俺たちの死角で手紙を置けた…！！
誰が置いたかは識別できないが、彼ら４人の中の誰かが置いたのは明白なんだ…！！

We can't tell who put it there, but it's obvious that one of the four did it...!!

誰が置いたかは識別できないが、彼ら４人の中の誰かが置いたのは明白なんだ…！！

description: Natsuhi calls Genji her father’s foremost subordinate. WH calls him Grandfather’s subordinate, then returns to Father later in the same speech.
sourceReading: お父様 is Natsuhi’s established respectful father-in-law address.

units.text: "............Genji.  You were Grandfather's number one subordinate.  ...Was Beatrice an illusion you showed to Father, with you as the performer?!"
units.note: MG retains Grandfather in Natsuhi speech then Father; UP consistently restores Father.
units.japanese: 「…………源次。あなたはお父様の一番の部下です。…ベアトリーチェとは、あなたがお父様に見せた幻想で、あなたこそがその実行者だったのではないのですか？！」

units.text: "......Genji, you were Grandfather's number one subordinate. ...Was Beatrice an illusion you showed to Father, with you as the performer?!"
units.note: MG retains Grandfather in Natsuhi speech then Father; UP consistently restores Father.
units.japanese: 「…………源次。あなたはお父様の一番の部下です。…ベアトリーチェとは、あなたがお父様に見せた幻想で、あなたこそがその実行者だったのではないのですか？！」

description: The narrator describes Maria as if she were saying she would be fine even if shot. WH guesses she actually thinks so, moving from performed appearance to attributed belief.
sourceReading: と言うかのように frames her demeanor as an apparent message, not access to her belief.

units.text: Not content to doubt just the adults, Natsuhi oba-san pointed the gun relentlessly at Maria too. But Maria acted as though nothing had happened. .........Or maybe she thought she would be fine even if she was shot.
units.note: Both retain guessed actual belief fine if shot rather than appearance as if saying so.
units.japanese: ………あるいは、撃たれても平気だとでも言うかのように。

units.text: Not content to suspect just the adults, Aunt Natsuhi pointed the gun relentlessly at Maria too. But Maria acted as though nothing had happened. ......Or maybe she thought she would be fine even if she was shot.
units.note: Both retain guessed actual belief fine if shot rather than appearance as if saying so.
units.japanese: 大人を疑うだけならともかく、夏妃伯母さんは真里亞にも容赦なく銃口を向けた。しかし真里亞はけろりとしている。………あるいは、撃たれても平気だとでも言うかのように。

description: Natsuhi asks to pose the longstanding question once again. WH makes this the last time, adding ultimatum-like finality.
sourceReading: もう一度 means again or once more, without saying there will be no further asking.

units.text: "Maria-chan.  ...By this point, we can no longer remove someone from suspicion just because they are young.  So for the last time, let me ask the question that everyone's had since last night!
units.note: Both retain last time instead of once again, adding final ultimatum.
units.japanese: 「真里亞ちゃん。…今この場ではもう、幼いから疑いの枠から外すという段階にない。だから誰もが昨夜からずっと持ってきた疑問をもう一度ぶつけさせてもらいます！

units.text: "Maria-chan, ...by this point, we can no longer remove someone from suspicion just because they're young. So for the last time, let me ask the question that everyone's had since last night!
units.note: Both retain last time instead of once again, adding final ultimatum.
units.japanese: 「真里亞ちゃん。…今この場ではもう、幼いから疑いの枠から外すという段階にない。だから誰もが昨夜からずっと持ってきた疑問をもう一度ぶつけさせてもらいます！」

units.text: "Maria‐chan. ...By this point, we can no longer remove someone from suspicion just because they are young. So for the last time, let me ask the question that everyone's brought to you since last night!"
units.note: Both retain last time instead of once again, adding final ultimatum.
units.japanese: 「真里亞ちゃん。…今この場ではもう、幼いから疑いの枠から外すという段階にない。だから誰もが昨夜からずっと持ってきた疑問をもう一度ぶつけさせてもらいます！」

description: Maria asks who they would be satisfied to have as culprit, exposing their contradictory preferences. WH asks whether they are fine calling someone the culprit.
sourceReading: 誰が犯人ならいいの asks which identity would satisfy them, not whether accusing anyone is acceptable.

units.text: "......I don't understand.  ...All of you are fine with calling someone the culprit?  You only believe in Beatrice when you don't want to doubt one of your own.  When you're trying to settle a grudge because someone who's close to you has been killed, only then do you want to believe in a human who you can attack with violence, and deny Beatrice.
units.note: Both restore who they want as culprit, exposing contradictory preferences.
units.japanese: 「……真里亞にはわかんないよ。…戦人たちは、誰が犯人ならいいの？　自分たちの中に犯人がいると信じたくない時だけベアトリーチェを信じて、……親しい人を殺された恨みを晴らしたい時だけ、暴力をぶつけられるニンゲンの犯人を信じたがってベアトリーチェを否定する。

description: Maria says that is why they cannot see Beatrice, linking their preferences to perceptual failure. WH says like I said she cannot be seen, dropping causation and briefly generalizing invisibility.
sourceReading: だから gives the reason derived from the previous speech; お前たち specifies their inability.

units.text: ............Like I said, she can't be seen.  ......Beatrice 'exists'.  You all can't see her!"
units.note: Both restore causal that is why they cannot see her, without generalized inherent invisibility.
units.japanese: …………だから、視えないんだよ。……ベアトリーチェは“い”る。お前たちには視えない！」

description: Battler ranks Kumasawa among the most suspicious suspects unless a device or nineteenth person can be proven. WH uniquely ranks her by far the most likely.
sourceReading: もっとも疑わしい容疑者のひとり explicitly retains membership in a leading set rather than unique superior ranking.

units.text: However, Kumasawa-san really was suspicious just for being the first one to discover that Kanon-kun had been murdered. ...At that time, everyone except Kumasawa-san had an alibi. ......As long as the use of some device...or the existence of some 19th person could not be established, Kumasawa-san was by far the most likely suspect.
units.note: MG retains uniquely by far most likely. UP restores one of most likely; by far intensifies rank but does not retain exclusive-top-suspect claim.
units.japanese: ……何かの仕掛けや、１９人目の存在が立証できない限り、熊沢さんはもっとも疑わしい容疑者のひとりなのだ。

units.text: However, Kumasawa-san really was suspicious just for being the first one to discover that Kanon-kun had been murdered. ...At that time, everyone except Kumasawa-san had an alibi. ...Unless we could prove the existence of some contraption...or the existence of some 19th person, Kumasawa-san was by far the most likely suspect.
units.note: MG retains uniquely by far most likely. UP restores one of most likely; by far intensifies rank but does not retain exclusive-top-suspect claim.
units.japanese: だが、熊沢さんは確かに、嘉音くんの殺人に関してだけは第一発見者という疑わしさがある。…あの時点では、熊沢さん以外の全員にアリバイがある。……何かの仕掛けや、１９人目の存在が立証できない限り、熊沢さんはもっとも疑わしい容疑者のひとりなのだ。

description: Natsuhi promises she will apologize to everyone for tonight’s rudeness when police arrive. WH says all of us will apologize, redistributing her personal responsibility.
sourceReading: 全員に marks recipients of the apology, not its subject.

units.text: "......Yes.  Please understand, at least for tonight.  When the police come, all of us will surely apologize for our rudeness.
units.note: MG retains collective all of us apologize. UP restores Natsuhi I apologize to you all for my rudeness.
units.japanese: 「……えぇ。今夜だけは、わかって下さい。警察が来たら、全員に今夜のこの無礼を必ず謝罪しますから。

units.text: "...Yes. Please understand, at least for tonight. When the police come, all of us will surely apologize for our rudeness.
units.note: MG retains collective all of us apologize. UP restores Natsuhi I apologize to you all for my rudeness.
units.japanese: 「……えぇ。今夜だけは、わかって下さい。警察が来たら、全員に今夜のこの無礼を必ず謝罪しますから」

description: A sense of guilt makes Battler call Maria back. WH calls it knowledge of my crime, making the internal moral feeling an assertion of a crime.
sourceReading: 罪の意識 is consciousness of guilt in the context of expelling a child, not a newly established criminal act.

units.text: Knowledge of my crime made me call Maria back. ...I groped around in my pocket, ......and took out that scorpion keyholder.
units.note: MG knowledge of guilt and UP guilt restore moral feeling rather than asserted knowledge of crime.
units.japanese: 罪の意識が、真里亞を呼び止める。

description: Battler says he could not lose her precious charm, acknowledging its importance to Maria while admitting he lied. WH calls it my precious charm, making his own attachment the expressed reason.
sourceReading: お前の大切なお守り places the importance and possession with Maria.

units.text: "...Back then, I was a little annoyed, and I was just bluffing that I'd lost it.  ......There's no way I'd lose my precious charm."
units.note: MG restores charm given by Maria but precious remains unattributed, not explicitly her precious possession. UP your precious charm restores Maria attachment.
units.japanese: 「…あん時ゃ、何かシャクんなって、なくしたとかホラを吹いただけだ。……お前の大切なお守りを無くすわけねぇだろ。」

units.text: "...Back then, I got ticked off and just bluffed that I'd lost it. ...There's no way I'd lose the precious charm you gave me."
units.note: MG restores charm given by Maria but precious remains unattributed, not explicitly her precious possession. UP your precious charm restores Maria attachment.
units.japanese: 「…あん時ゃ、何かシャクんなって、なくしたとかホラを吹いただけだ。……お前の大切なお守りを無くすわけねぇだろ」

description: Battler wonders whether expelling suspects and waiting until morning will really end everything. WH says everything would probably be over.
sourceReading: 終わるのだろうか is an unresolved question, immediately challenged by the letter’s deadline.

units.text: After chasing out all the suspicious people, all we had to do was stay barricaded here until morning, and everything would probably be over. ......Once the typhoon has passed, when the seagulls cry, everything may be resolved.
units.note: MG retains declarative probably over rather than question whether waiting ends everything. UP explicitly restores question.
units.japanese: 疑わしき人物を全て追い出し、後は朝までここで篭城しているだけで全てが終わるのだろうか。

units.text: After chasing out all the suspicious people, all we had to do was stay barricaded here until morning, and everything would probably be over. ...Once the typhoon has passed, when the seagulls cry, will everything be resolved?
units.note: MG retains declarative probably over rather than question whether waiting ends everything. UP explicitly restores question.
units.japanese: 疑わしき人物を全て追い出し、後は朝までここで篭城しているだけで全てが終わるのだろうか。……台風が過ぎ去り、うみねこのなく頃には、全てが解決しているのだろうか。

description: Battler infers the others expect the circle to reveal an unpleasant message and separately says he agrees. WH asserts that we were sure to find such a message.
sourceReading: 思ったに違いない attributes a probable thought to the others whose lack of interest was just described, not certainty about the message itself.

units.text: No one else showed that much interest in this magic circle. ...Its meaning was unknown, and once we understood it, we were sure to find some message that would cause us unnecessary anguish. ......I also agreed about this. ...However, I couldn't just ignore it, so I killed time pretending to research it...
units.note: Both retain shared we were sure rather than Battler inference of others expectations followed by separate agreement.
units.japanese: …意味不明だし、わかったところで、余計に不快な思いをするメッセージが込められているのだろうと思ったに違いない。

units.text: No one else showed that much interest in this magic circle. ...Its meaning was unknown, and once we understood it, we were sure to find some message that would cause us unnecessary anguish. ...I felt the same way. ...However, I couldn't just ignore it, so I killed time by going through the motions of researching it...
units.note: Both retain shared we were sure rather than Battler inference of others expectations followed by separate agreement.
units.japanese: みんなは、この魔法陣にはそれほどの興味を示さなかった。…意味不明だし、わかったところで、余計に不快な思いをするメッセージが込められているのだろうと思ったに違いない。……それについては俺も同意する。…だが、だからと言って放置もできず、こうして調べ物のふりをしながら時間を潰している…。

units.text: No one else showed that much interest in this magic circle. ...Its meaning was unknown, and once we understood it, we were sure to find some message that would cause us unnecessary anguish. ......I also agreed about this. ...However, I still couldn't let it go, so I killed time pretending to research it...
units.note: Both retain shared we were sure rather than Battler inference of others expectations followed by separate agreement.
units.japanese: みんなは、この魔法陣にはそれほどの興味を示さなかった。…意味不明だし、わかったところで、余計に不快な思いをするメッセージが込められているのだろうと思ったに違いない。……それについては俺も同意する。…だが、だからと言って放置もできず、こうして調べ物のふりをしながら時間を潰している…。

description: George says Natsuhi offers to keep night watch but her body cannot sustain it, so they should rotate. WH says she told us to stay vigilant all night and our bodies cannot handle it.
sourceReading: 不寝番をしてくれる assigns the service to Natsuhi, with her endurance as the concern.

units.text: "Aren't you tired, Battler-kun?  ......You should take a rest while someone else stays awake.  Natsuhi oba-san told us to stay vigilant all night, but there's no way our bodies can handle that.  We should take turns sleeping."
units.note: Both restore Natsuhi offering night watch and her bodily limit, motivating rotation.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんは不寝番をしてくれると言ってるけど、体が持つわけない。ローテーションで休んだ方がいいよ。」
candidates: told us to stay vigilant all night

description: Jessica warns Battler that researching this could get him possessed by something strange. WH warns that he will become obsessed with weird material.
sourceReading: 妙なのに取り憑かれる is possession by something uncanny in this occult exchange; Battler answers by citing his absence of spiritual talent.

units.text: "............Give it a rest.  If you do that, you'll start getting obsessed with all this weird stuff."
units.note: Both restore supernatural possession warning rather than becoming obsessed with material.
units.japanese: 「…………よせよ。そういうのやってると、妙なのに取り憑かれちまうぜ。」

description: George grounds his remarriage hypothesis in Rosa sometimes emotionally taking things out on Maria. WH specifies physical hitting.
sourceReading: 感情的に ... 当たっていた describes venting or lashing out at someone; it does not by itself specify hitting.

units.text: "I think Oba-san thought about remarrying.  ......But I also believe Maria-chan may have become her shackles and made that quite difficult.  ............After all, she sometimes, ...got really emotional and hit Maria-chan."
units.note: MG retains physical hitting for emotional taking-it-out-on Maria. UP restores emotional mistreatment without added specific physical act.
units.japanese: …………だって叔母さんは時折、…ものすごく感情的に真里亞ちゃんに当たっていたから。」

units.text: "I think Aunt Rosa thought about remarrying. ...But I also believe Maria-chan may have become her shackles and made that quite difficult. ......After all, she sometimes... got really emotional and hit Maria-chan."
units.note: MG retains physical hitting for emotional taking-it-out-on Maria. UP restores emotional mistreatment without added specific physical act.
units.japanese: 「叔母さんは再婚だって考えたと思うよ。……でも、真里亞ちゃんの存在が枷になって、非常に難しかったんじゃないかと思うんだ。…………だって叔母さんは時折、…ものすごく感情的に真里亞ちゃんに当たっていたから」

description: Battler wonders whether Maria sought witches as beings who would rescue her from maternal rejection and make her happy. WH asks whether she saved herself while seeking their help.
sourceReading: 自分を助けてくれて ... 存在として places saving agency with the imagined witch; 救いを求めた is seeking rescue, not achieving it.

units.text: ......The sorrow of not being loved by her mother. ...Had Maria saved herself from that, seeking help from witches as beings who could give her happiness? Someday, a witch would come, and using her wonderful magic, would bring Maria happiness. ......Even though she believed that, as she grew older, she had to face reality as her fleeting dreams were sliced to ribbons one by one.
units.note: Both restore witches as rescuing beings and Maria seeking their help, not Maria saving herself. UP explicitly links rescue to maternal sorrow.
units.japanese: …真里亞は、そこから自分を助けてくれて、幸せにしてくれる存在として、魔女に救いを求めたのか。

description: A possible cruel aspect of Natsuhi’s expulsion becomes “a lot of brutal things have happened,” shifting the concession away from her action.
sourceReading: Battler grants that her conduct may have had a cruel side, then explains her maternal duty and willingness to face condemnation.

units.text: "It's true that a lot of brutal things have happened.  ...But as a mother, you thought you should protect your daughter no matter what.  Because of that duty, you chased them out, even though you knew that you would eventually be held responsible for it.
units.note: MG shifts cruelty concession to many brutal events. UP restores degree of cruelty in Natsuhi expulsion.
units.japanese: 「確かに残酷なところはあったかもしれない。…でも、夏妃伯母さんは母として、娘を守りきろうと思った。その責務から、自分がやがては糾弾されることを覚悟で、彼らを追放したんだ。
candidates: lot of brutal things have happened

units.text: "It's true that a lot of brutal things have happened. ...But as a mother, you thought you should protect your daughter no matter what. Because of that duty, you chased them out, even though you knew that you'd eventually be held responsible for it.
units.note: MG shifts cruelty concession to many brutal events. UP restores degree of cruelty in Natsuhi expulsion.
units.japanese: 「確かに残酷なところはあったかもしれない。…でも、夏妃伯母さんは母として、娘を守りきろうと思った。その責務から、自分がやがては糾弾されることを覚悟で、彼らを追放したんだ」
candidates: lot of brutal things have happened

description: 手に掛かっていた is rendered as being “in the culprit’s grasp,” weakening the explicit counterfactual death that grounds George’s gratitude.
sourceReading: George says that, had Natsuhi also lost her composure, they might all have been killed by the culprit by now.

units.text: "......That's right.  ...You've been dealing with these incidents since morning, and you've been pulling all of us along this whole time, without losing your composure.  ......If you were all confused too, the rest of us would probably be in the culprit's grasp by now.  ...So I think that we all have to thank you."
units.note: Both retain culprit grasp rather than counterfactual having been killed by culprit.
units.japanese: ……もし伯母さんまで混乱していたら、僕たちは今頃全員、犯人の手に掛かっていたかもしれない。…だから、僕たちは伯母さんに、感謝しなくちゃいけないと思う。」

units.text: "...That's right. ...You've been dealing with these incidents since morning, and you've been pulling all of us along this whole time, without losing your composure. ...If you were all confused too, the rest of us would probably be in the culprit's grasp by now. ...So I think we all have to thank you."
units.note: Both retain culprit grasp rather than counterfactual having been killed by culprit.
units.japanese: 「……そうだね。…夏妃伯母さんは、朝からずっと続いているこんな事件の中でも、冷静さを失わず、ずっとみんなを牽引してきてくれた」「……もし伯母さんまで混乱していたら、僕たちは今頃全員、犯人の手に掛かっていたかもしれない。…だから、僕たちは伯母さんに、感謝しなくちゃいけないと思う」

units.text: "......Yes. ...You've been dealing with these incidents since morning, and you've been pulling all of us along this whole time, without losing your composure." "......If you had been as confused as the rest of us, every last one of us may have been in the culprit's grasp by now. ...So I think that we all have to thank you."
units.note: Both retain culprit grasp rather than counterfactual having been killed by culprit.
units.japanese: 「……そうだね。…夏妃伯母さんは、朝からずっと続いているこんな事件の中でも、冷静さを失わず、ずっとみんなを牽引してきてくれた」「……もし伯母さんまで混乱していたら、僕たちは今頃全員、犯人の手に掛かっていたかもしれない。…だから、僕たちは伯母さんに、感謝しなくちゃいけないと思う」

description: 綺麗事 is misread as Natsuhi recognizing that she is oversimplifying. This invents self-criticism of her reasoning.
sourceReading: Battler understands her forceful ending as a resolve to protect her daughter even as a demon despite fully understanding the morally attractive sentiments being urged on her.

units.text: That was some pretty strong language at the end there... She realized very well that she was oversimplifying, but even so, she was strongly resolved to protect her daughter even if she had to become a demon. ............But that was because the knowledge of her crime tormented her.
units.note: MG retains self-criticism that own maternal words idealized. UP removes idealized maternal view but still says these were only words, attributing critique of her own statement rather than understanding others platitudes and choosing protection despite them.
units.japanese: 綺麗事は充分に理解している、その上でなお、自分は鬼となってでも娘を守りたいという強い決意。

units.text: That was some pretty strong language at the end there... She realized very well that her words were an idealized view of what a mother should be, but even so, she was strongly resolved to protect her daughter, even if she had to become a demon. ......But that was her guilty conscience tormenting her.
units.note: MG retains self-criticism that own maternal words idealized. UP removes idealized maternal view but still says these were only words, attributing critique of her own statement rather than understanding others platitudes and choosing protection despite them.
units.japanese:
少しだけ強い語尾…。
綺麗事は充分に理解している、その上でなお、自分は鬼となってでも娘を守りたいという強い決意。…………しかしそれは、罪の意識に苛むからゆえのもの。

units.text:
That was some pretty strong language at the end there...
She realized very well that these were only words, but even so, she was strongly resolved to protect her daughter even if she had to become a demon. ............But that was because she was tormented by guilt.
units.note: MG retains self-criticism that own maternal words idealized. UP removes idealized maternal view but still says these were only words, attributing critique of her own statement rather than understanding others platitudes and choosing protection despite them.
units.japanese:
少しだけ強い語尾…。
綺麗事は充分に理解している、その上でなお、自分は鬼となってでも娘を守りたいという強い決意。…………しかしそれは、罪の意識に苛むからゆえのもの。

description: The description that the candlestick looks suited to a dubious ritual disappears.
sourceReading: Battler finds a three-branched candlestick that looks as though it would be used in a suspicious ritual and takes it as a weapon.

units.text: Natsuhi oba-san raised the rifle high and took the lead. I couldn't go unarmed myself. I found a three-pronged candlestick and readied it. Although the pins on it, which were used to fit candles, were short, it was almost like a three-pronged spear.
units.note: MG omits dubious ritual suitability of candelabra. UP explicitly restores it.
units.japanese: 怪しげな儀式に使いそうな三叉の燭台を見つけ、得物とした。

units.text: Aunt Natsuhi raised the rifle high and took the lead. I couldn't go unarmed myself. I found a three-pronged candle stand and readied it. Although the pins on it used to fit candles were short, it was almost like a three-pronged spear.
units.note: MG omits dubious ritual suitability of candelabra. UP explicitly restores it.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんはライフル銃を高々と構え、先頭に立つ。俺も素手というわけには行かない。怪しげな儀式に使いそうな三叉の燭台を見つけ、得物とした。蝋燭を挿すトゲが短いながらもついているそれは、さながら三叉の槍のようだった。

description: The passive 引きずり出されている applied to 俺たち becomes “had thrown them out.” The source’s second stage of the trap is replaced by a repetition of its first stage.
sourceReading: The discord circle seems to have worked: the group has split, and now they themselves have additionally been dragged out into dangerous territory.

units.text: With Natsuhi oba-san in the center, her rifle readied and her finger on the trigger, we moved in a group, our backs together, checking our surroundings in all directions...... It was just as though the magic of that magic circle designed to spread discord had worked.  ...We had split up, and furthermore, had thrown them out into dangerous territory. ......In other words, even now, we were doing just what the culprit wanted us to do.  ...This was a separate world where it wouldn't be odd for anything to suddenly occur...
units.note: Both restore we were divided and dragged into danger as second stage, not merely repeating expulsion of others.
units.japanese: さっきの不和を目論むという魔法陣が、まるでその魔力で成したように。…俺たちは分裂し、しかもその上、危険地帯へ引きずり出されている。

description: The simile adds a graduation ceremony where the source describes being ordered to sing in a school lesson or similar setting.
sourceReading: Maria sings mechanically, like someone singing because a school class requires it, rather than spontaneously from good spirits.

units.text: She wasn't singing naturally, as though she were in a good mood. .........She was singing mechanically, like she was at a graduation ceremony and she'd been ordered to. ...The song she was singing was just a common folk song, one that everyone has probably sung in school at one time or another. ......But why that, in the middle of the night, alone, with all her heart, over and over, why...?!
units.note: MG retains added graduation ceremony; UP restores school music class.
units.japanese: ………それはまるで、学校の授業などで、歌うことを命じられて歌うような、無機質な歌い方。

units.text: She wasn't singing naturally, as though she were in a good mood. ......She was singing mechanically, like she was at a graduation ceremony and she'd been ordered to. ...The song she sang was just a common folk song, one that everyone has probably sung in school at one time or another. ...But why that, in the middle of the night, alone, with all her heart, over and over, why...?!
units.note: MG retains added graduation ceremony; UP restores school music class.
units.japanese: それは、機嫌がよくて自然と口に出てしまうような歌い方ではない。………それはまるで、学校の授業などで、歌うことを命じられて歌うような、無機質な歌い方。…歌っている歌は、誰もが学校で一度は歌ったことがあるに違いない平凡な民謡。……しかし、それを、なぜ、こんな深夜に、ひとりで、一生懸命に、ずっと、どうして…？！

description: 今朝からずっと becomes “In the morning ... the whole time,” contracting the retrospective duration.
sourceReading: They had been in this room throughout the time since that morning; horrors occurring elsewhere had encouraged an unfounded belief that it was safe.

units.text: In the morning, we had been in that room the whole time. ...All of the frightening things had occurred outside that room. So we had been under the impression that only that room was safe. .........That baseless impression was quickly falling apart......
units.note: MG restores almost constantly since morning. UP retains in the morning whole time, shortening retrospective duration.
units.japanese: 今朝からずっとこの部屋の中にいた。

units.text:
In the morning, we had been in that room the whole time.
...All of the frightening things had occurred outside that room.
...So, we had convinced ourselves that even if nowhere else could be trusted, that room alone was safe. .........That baseless impression was quickly falling apart......
units.note: MG restores almost constantly since morning. UP retains in the morning whole time, shortening retrospective duration.
units.japanese:
今朝からずっとこの部屋の中にいた。
…いつも恐ろしいことはこの部屋の外で起こった。
…だから、この部屋だけは安全だと思い込んできた。………その、根拠なき思い込みが、あっさりと崩れ去っていく……。

description: “Like I’d quit now” reverses Battler’s expressed wish to say he does not want to go after all.
sourceReading: With a nervous laugh, Battler says he would like to say “actually, I don’t want to,” then steels himself and imagines striking back with the candlestick.

units.text: "Ihihi...!  Like I'd quit now...!"
units.note: Both restore wish to decline/quit instead of defiant refusal to quit.
units.japanese: 「いっひっひ…！　やっぱ嫌だって言いてぇなぁ…！」

description: 冗談も休み休み言いやがれ is rendered “Calmly joking at a time like this,” treating an idiomatic rebuke as an observation about the manner and timing of a joke.
sourceReading: Battler angrily dismisses the butterfly-entry account as absurd: roughly, give the nonsense a rest.

units.text: "Huuhh?!  Calmly joking at a time like this?!!!  Like hell that happened!  What are you saying?!"
units.note: MG retains Calmly joking at a time like this; UP correctly gives idiomatic imperative Give it a rest with your goddamn jokes.
units.japanese: 「はぁッ？！　冗談も休み休み言いやがれッ！！！　そんなわけねぇだろ？！　お前は何を言ってやがるんだ？！」
candidates: Calmly joking at a time like

units.text: "Huuhh?! Calmly joking at a time like this?!!! Like hell that happened! What are you saying?!"
units.note: MG retains Calmly joking at a time like this; UP correctly gives idiomatic imperative Give it a rest with your goddamn jokes.
units.japanese: 「はぁッ？！　冗談も休み休み言いやがれッ！！！　そんなわけねぇだろ？！　お前は何を言ってやがるんだ？！」
candidates: Calmly joking at a time like

description: 自負する becomes “bearing the title,” giving formal-title language to her own proud claim of representation.
sourceReading: Natsuhi describes herself as someone who takes pride in being the family’s representative, opposing Beatrice’s self-proclaimed succession.

units.text: ......Both I, bearing the title of representative to the Ushiromiya family, and you, the one who claims to succeed the head of the Ushiromiya family, are here right now.  ......At this point, whether you are a witch or not is a trivial problem!
units.note: Both retain bearing the title rather than her self-professed pride in representation; Beatrice’s own claim remains distinguished.
units.japanese: ……右代宮家の代表であると自負する私と、

units.text: "...Both I who bear the title of representative to the Ushiromiya family... and you who claim to succeed the Headship of the Ushiromiya family...are here right now. ...At this point, whether you are a witch or not is a trivial matter!"
units.note: Both retain bearing the title rather than her self-professed pride in representation; Beatrice’s own claim remains distinguished.
units.japanese: 「……右代宮家の代表であると自負する私と、右代宮家の当主を引き継いだと自称する貴女が、今この場にいる。……あなたが本当に魔女なのかどうかは、今となっては些細な問題です！」

units.text: "......Both I, bearing the title of representative to the Ushiromiya family, and you, claiming to have succeeded the head of the Ushiromiya family, are here right now. ......At this point, whether you are a witch or not is a trivial problem!"
units.note: Both retain bearing the title rather than her self-professed pride in representation; Beatrice’s own claim remains distinguished.
units.japanese: 「……右代宮家の代表であると自負する私と、右代宮家の当主を引き継いだと自称する貴女が、今この場にいる。……あなたが本当に魔女なのかどうかは、今となっては些細な問題です！」

description: The assertive 銃声だぜ and 撃ったんだ become “Was that ...?” and “Did ... shoot?”
sourceReading: Battler emphatically says that was a gunshot and that Natsuhi fired it. He then supplies his own confident answer that she shot at the culprit.

units.text: "Was that the sound of a gun just now?!  Did Natsuhi oba-san shoot?!!"
units.note: MG retains questions Was that and Did Aunt Natsuhi shoot; UP restores declarative sound-of-gun and Natsuhi-shot assertions. Target identification remains Battler’s inference in all witnesses.
units.japanese: 「今のは銃声だぜ？！　夏妃伯母さんが撃ったんだッ！！」

units.text: "Was that the sound of a gun just now?! Did Aunt Natsuhi shoot?!!"
units.note: MG retains questions Was that and Did Aunt Natsuhi shoot; UP restores declarative sound-of-gun and Natsuhi-shot assertions. Target identification remains Battler’s inference in all witnesses.
units.japanese: 「今のは銃声だぜ？！　夏妃伯母さんが撃ったんだッ！！」

description: そこは becomes “We were,” relocating the observers to the portrait rather than identifying the place in the darkness toward which Maria ran.
sourceReading: The place they look toward, where Maria runs and clings to the portrait’s subject, is in front of Beatrice’s portrait.

units.text: We were in front of Beatrice's portrait. And, the thing Maria was running up to was, ............the portrait's, ...subject.
units.note: MG explicitly places portrait space in direction of gaze; UP fixes eyes on portrait destination. Neither relocates group there.
units.japanese: そこは、ベアトリーチェの肖像画の前。

description: “isn’t 24:00 is a strange time” contains both contracted and repeated finite “is.”
sourceReading: Battler rhetorically reflects on how strange midnight is, both the culmination of a day and hour zero of the next.

units.text: When you think about it, isn't 24:00 is a strange time? ...It can be called 24:00, and it can also be called 0:00. It's the hour at the culmination of the previous day, ...and at the same time, it is hour zero as the next day begins.
units.note: MG retains isn’t 24:00 is a strange time; UP removes repeated finite is.
units.japanese: 思えば、２４時とは何と奇妙な時間なのか。

units.text: When you think about it, isn't 24:00 is a strange time? ...It can be called 24:00, and it can also be called 0:00. It's the hour at the culmination of the previous day, ...and at the same time, it's hour zero as the next day begins.
units.note: MG retains isn’t 24:00 is a strange time; UP removes repeated finite is.
units.japanese:
思えば、２４時とは何と奇妙な時間なのか。
…２４時とも呼び、０時とも呼ぶ。一日の全てが満ちた時間にして、…同時に新しい一日が始まるゼロの時間でもある。

description: 一喜一憂 is reduced to rejoicing, dropping the alternating delight and concern in the reactions that absorb George’s attention.
sourceReading: George sees only Shannon as she interacts with the fish and reacts with delight or concern to each little thing.

units.text: To use an old-fashioned phrase, these would be rose-colored days.... I'm so entranced that I don't even notice the big tank of the world's largest aquarium. Instead, I see Shannon rejoicing and playing with the fish.
units.note: MG flitting expressions and UP changing emotions restore variation, but neither explicitly preserves paired delight/concern in 一喜一憂; UP happily retains positive framing. Original WH rejoicing wording is not copied into these witness excerpts.
units.japanese: 紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。

units.text: To use an old-fashioned phrase, these really are rose-colored days I'm living in... I'm so entranced that I barely notice that massive tank in the world's largest aquarium anymore. Instead, all I see are the expressions flitting across Shannon's face as she plays with the fish.
units.note: MG flitting expressions and UP changing emotions restore variation, but neither explicitly preserves paired delight/concern in 一喜一憂; UP happily retains positive framing. Original WH rejoicing wording is not copied into these witness excerpts.
units.japanese: 古風な言い方で喩えるなら、これこそまさに薔薇色の日々…。文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。

units.text: To use an old‐fashioned phrase, these would be truly rose‐colored days... I was so entranced that I no longer even noticed the big tank of the world's largest aquarium. Instead, I saw only Shannon happily playing with the fish, all her changing emotions showing on her face.
units.note: MG flitting expressions and UP changing emotions restore variation, but neither explicitly preserves paired delight/concern in 一喜一憂; UP happily retains positive framing. Original WH rejoicing wording is not copied into these witness excerpts.
units.japanese: 古風な言い方で喩えるなら、これこそまさに薔薇色の日々…。文字通りデレデレする僕の眼中に、世界最大の水族館の大水槽はもはや映らない。紗音が魚たちと戯れて一喜一憂する姿を映し続けるのみだ。

description: 自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない becomes “stick to their own view,” turning an inability to possess more than one’s own perspective into language of adhering to it.
sourceReading: However much experience a person gains, they can ultimately possess only their own individual value framework; exchange with someone whose framework differs is therefore interesting.

units.text: No matter how far humans broaden their experiences, they stick to their own view of the world in the end.  Maybe that's why it's so interesting to mingle with people who have a different worldview.
units.note: MG viewing through own-values lens preserves single-perspective limitation; UP explicitly only a single personal worldview. Neither says stubbornly stick to views.
units.japanese: 人間というのは、どんなに見聞を広めようとも、所詮は自分ひとりの価値観しか持てない。だからこそ、異なる価値観を持つ人間と交流することはこんなにも面白いのかもしれない。

description: 全長が１０ｋｍ程度 becomes “10 kilometers in circumference,” changing the dimension and removing its approximation.
sourceReading: Shannon lives as a servant on the small island Rokkenjima, approximately ten kilometers in overall length.

units.text: Shannon, who spent her days as a servant on a small island 10 kilometers in circumference called Rokkenjima, said that with a smile.
units.note: Current JP says 全周, circumference, unlike original-PC parent 全長. Thus circumference is valid here and original dimension error is not inherited; both still omit 程度 approximation around ten kilometers.
units.japanese: 六軒島という、全長が１０ｋｍ程度の小島で使用人として日々を過ごす彼女は、微笑みながらそう言った。

units.text: Shannon, who spent her days as a servant on a small island 10 kilometers in circumference called Rokkenjima, said that with a smile.
units.note: Current JP says 全周, circumference, unlike original-PC parent 全長. Thus circumference is valid here and original dimension error is not inherited; both still omit 程度 approximation around ten kilometers.
units.japanese: 六軒島という、全周が１０ｋｍ程度の小島で使用人として日々を過ごす彼女は、微笑みながらそう言った。

units.text: Shannon, who spent her days as a servant on a small island ten kilometers in circumference called Rokkenjima, said that with a smile.
units.note: Current JP says 全周, circumference, unlike original-PC parent 全長. Thus circumference is valid here and original dimension error is not inherited; both still omit 程度 approximation around ten kilometers.
units.japanese: 六軒島という、全周が１０ｋｍ程度の小島で使用人として日々を過ごす彼女は、微笑みながらそう言った。

description: 白い目で見る becomes staring with “blank eyes,” losing the idiom’s disapproval or contempt.
sourceReading: Their flirtatious exchange is their entire world, so they do not notice however disapprovingly people outside that world look at them.

units.text: To anyone watching us, we might seem like a pretty humorous and embarrassing couple. But it's only after trying to become a couple that you realize. This whole arguing back and forth means the world to us. That's why no matter how much everyone else stared at us with blank eyes, we wouldn't have noticed it.
units.note: MG blank expressions loses disapproval; UP cold looks restores it.
units.japanese: だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。

units.text: To anyone watching us, we might seem like an incredibly charming and embarrassing couple. But it's only after becoming a couple that you realize. To us, this exchange of words is everything, our entire world. That's why no matter how much everyone else stares at us with blank expressions, we never notice.
units.note: MG blank expressions loses disapproval; UP cold looks restores it.
units.japanese:
傍から見ていたなら、僕たちは何と微笑ましく、そして何と恥ずかしい二人なのだろう。しかし二人になってみて初めてわかる。僕たちにとってはこのやり取りが全てで、世界なのだ。
だから世界の外側の人がどんなに白い目で見たって、僕たちは気付かない。

description: 嫌な思いがさせたいわけじゃない is rendered as not wanting her to “think bad of me,” redirecting the reason for moderating his teasing.
sourceReading: George enjoys controlling and monopolizing her emotional reactions, but wants to calibrate the teasing: he does not want to embarrass her and make her feel unpleasant.

units.text: That's why I have to treat her lightly. I don't want her to get embarrassed and think bad of me. That's why I decided to end this topic here and now. I didn't want to be too obstinate.
units.note: Both center Shannon embarrassment/distress rather than her judgment of George.
units.japanese: 彼女を恥ずかしがらせて嫌な思いがさせたいわけじゃない。

description: 秀吉さまの血が濃い becomes “Hideyoshi-sama’s blood is pretty thick on you,” a literal and opaque rendering of inheritance or resemblance.
sourceReading: Shannon thinks George takes strongly after Hideyoshi and warns that he may grow fat if he is not careful.

units.text: "You can't...  If you eat cake after already eating so much, you will get fat.  It looks like Hideyoshi-sama's blood is pretty thick on you, George-sama, so if you don't take care, you will get chubby."
units.note: Both retain literal blood pretty thick in you. English remains awkward inheritance/ressemblance calque; in context subsequent chubbiness gives intended hereditary connection, limiting severity.
units.japanese: 譲治さまは、秀吉さまの血が濃いみたいですから、気をつけないとおデブさんになっちゃいます。」

units.text: "You mustn't... If you eat cake after eating so much, you'll get fat. It looks like Hideyoshi-sama's blood is pretty thick in you, George-sama, so you'll get chubby if you don't take care."
units.note: Both retain literal blood pretty thick in you. English remains awkward inheritance/ressemblance calque; in context subsequent chubbiness gives intended hereditary connection, limiting severity.
units.japanese: 「いけません…。お昼にそんなに食べた上にケーキまで食べたら、太っちゃいますよ。譲治さまは、秀吉さまの血が濃いみたいですから、気をつけないとおデブさんになっちゃいます」

units.text: "You mustn't... If you eat cake after already eating so much, you will get fat. Hideyoshi‐sama's blood seems to run pretty thick in you, George‐sama, so if you don't take care, you will get chubby."
units.note: Both retain literal blood pretty thick in you. English remains awkward inheritance/ressemblance calque; in context subsequent chubbiness gives intended hereditary connection, limiting severity.
units.japanese: 「いけません…。お昼にそんなに食べた上にケーキまで食べたら、太っちゃいますよ。譲治さまは、秀吉さまの血が濃いみたいですから、気をつけないとおデブさんになっちゃいます」

description: 僕のサラダの皿 becomes “my dessert plate,” substituting a different tableware detail.
sourceReading: Shannon cuts her cake to transfer part onto George’s salad plate, which he then draws away to request being fed.

units.text: Shannon cut her own cake and tried to move half to my dessert plate. I had no doubt that she wanted to share the delicious cake's flavor with me. Even so, I boldly and meanly pushed that plate away.
units.note: MG dessert plate retains tableware substitution; UP salad plate restores exact source.
units.japanese: 紗音が自分のケーキを切り分け、それを僕のサラダの皿に移そうとする。

units.text: Shannon cut her own cake and tried to move half to my dessert plate. I had no doubt that she wanted to share the delicious cake's flavor with me. However, I meanly pulled my plate away from her.
units.note: MG dessert plate retains tableware substitution; UP salad plate restores exact source.
units.japanese: 紗音が自分のケーキを切り分け、それを僕のサラダの皿に移そうとする。美味しいケーキの味を、僕と共有したいに違いない。なのに敢えて僕は、意地悪にその皿を引っ込めて遠ざける。

description: 信じてる in George’s narration becomes “we both believed,” supplying Shannon’s belief rather than his belief about what both saw.
sourceReading: Despite the cloudy sky, George believes that a deep-blue sea was reflected in both their eyes.

units.text: After that, we gathered shells, ran from waves and enjoyed each other's company while walking along the beach. In the end, the clouds never parted. However, we both believed that our eyes were still reflecting a deep, blue sea.
units.note: Both we both believed supply Shannon belief where first-person George asserts his belief about their shared perceived sea.
units.japanese: でも、僕たち二人の目には、共に真っ青な海が映っていたと信じてる。

units.text: After that, we gathered shells, ran from waves, and enjoyed each other's company while walking along the beach. In the end, the clouds never parted. However, we both believed that the sea reflected in our eyes was a deep blue.
units.note: Both we both believed supply Shannon belief where first-person George asserts his belief about their shared perceived sea.
units.japanese: その後、僕らは海岸を歩きながら、貝殻を拾ったり、波から逃げたりしてはしゃぎあった。結局、空は曇天のままで晴れなかった。でも、僕たち二人の目には、共に真っ青な海が映っていたと信じてる。

units.text: After that, we gathered shells, ran from the waves, and enjoyed each other's company while walking along the beach. In the end, the clouds never parted. However, we both believed that our eyes were still reflecting a deep, blue sea.
units.note: Both we both believed supply Shannon belief where first-person George asserts his belief about their shared perceived sea.
units.japanese: その後、僕らは海岸を歩きながら、貝殻を拾ったり、波から逃げたりしてはしゃぎあった。結局、空は曇天のままで晴れなかった。でも、僕たち二人の目には、共に真っ青な海が映っていたと信じてる。

description: The wish ご縁があったらな and her admission that she fantasized about it become “When I started this relationship ... it just felt like a delusion.”
sourceReading: Unlike George, Shannon had imagined or fantasized that she might enter a relationship with the considerate, gentlemanly George. She is embarrassed to admit that prior wish.

units.text: "......I only, ......imagined.  No, umm, err!  Rather than imagination, ......it was more like a delusion......  When I started this relationship with you, George-sama, when you're always so considerate and gentlemanly, ...I mean, it just felt like a delusion......."
units.note: Both now preserve prior fantasy of possible relationship, not delusion after starting it.
units.japanese:
「……想像だけは、
……してました。いえそのあの！　想像というよりは、その、
……妄想みたいなもので……。いつも紳士的で思いやりのある、譲治さまとご縁があったらなって、
……その、妄想してただけで……。」

description: The contrast between what she regards as everything and its small share of his total explanation becomes “What she chooses to believe weighs little in my thoughts.”
sourceReading: The thing Shannon believes accounts for the whole encounter carries only a small proportion of George’s own explanation, immediately after his 70 percent effort, 20 percent courage, and 10 percent chance breakdown.

units.text: For a man like me, 70% of an encounter with a girl is an endeavour to try and please her, while 20% of it is raw courage.  And the remaining 10% is luck. What she chooses to believe weighs little in my thoughts. ...Maybe that way of thinking is in itself calculating and typical of men.
units.note: MG smaller factor and UP relative weight restore comparison between chance/miracle and George combined explanation; neither dismisses everything she believes as personally unimportant.
units.japanese: 彼女が全てだと信じるものは、僕の中では全体を占めるウェートが少ない。
candidates: chooses to believe weighs little in my thoughts

description: The passive 強引に抱き寄せられて becomes his forceful embrace “while she dived into my chest,” giving her movement an apparently separate active subject.
sourceReading: Her slender body is forcefully drawn close and consequently comes into his chest like a doll.

units.text: I embraced her shoulder. Then I forcefully embraced her entire body while she dived into my chest like a doll. As I held her head in my arms, we looked at the horizon.
units.note: MG forceful pulling still followed by she dove. UP restores passive her body was pulled but follows with she leapt, leaving active movement phrasing where source makes doll-like movement consequence of forceful embrace.
units.japanese: 華奢な体が、強引に抱き寄せられて、まるで人形のように僕の胸に飛び込んだ。

units.text: I held her shoulder and drew her close. When I forcefully pulled her delicate body towards me, she dove into my chest like a doll. As I held her head in my arms, we both looked at the horizon.
units.note: MG forceful pulling still followed by she dove. UP restores passive her body was pulled but follows with she leapt, leaving active movement phrasing where source makes doll-like movement consequence of forceful embrace.
units.japanese: 彼女の肩を抱き寄せる。華奢な体が、強引に抱き寄せられて、まるで人形のように僕の胸に飛び込んだ。その頭を抱え込みながら、二人して水平線を見る。

units.text: I put my arm around her shoulder and held her close. Her delicate body was pulled irresistibly towards me, and she leapt into my chest like a doll. As I held her head in my arms, we looked at the horizon together.
units.note: MG forceful pulling still followed by she dove. UP restores passive her body was pulled but follows with she leapt, leaving active movement phrasing where source makes doll-like movement consequence of forceful embrace.
units.japanese: 彼女の肩を抱き寄せる。華奢な体が、強引に抱き寄せられて、まるで人形のように僕の胸に飛び込んだ。その頭を抱え込みながら、二人して水平線を見る。

description: 今は気付けない becomes “then, I hadn’t realized,” moving the expressed temporal perspective into retrospective awareness.
sourceReading: At this moment of choosing love and personhood, Shannon cannot recognize that the honey-sweet days also begin new suffering.

units.text: So I try to choose to know love, and become a person. ......Those days were like sweetly melting honey, ......but then, I hadn't realized that they were the beginning of the days filled with a new kind of suffering.......
units.note: Both retrospective did not/had not realize rather than present inability now.
units.japanese: ……それは甘く蕩けるような蜜の日々だけれども、……新しい苦悩の日々の始まりだと、今は気付けない……。

units.text: So I decided to choose the path of knowing love...and tried to become a person. ...Those days were like sweet honey, ...but at the time, I didn't realize that they'd be the start of a new kind of suffering...
units.note: Both retrospective did not/had not realize rather than present inability now.
units.japanese: そして私は愛を知り、人となることを選ぼうとする。……それは甘く蕩けるような蜜の日々だけれども、……新しい苦悩の日々の始まりだと、今は気付けない……。

units.text: And so I learned of love, and decided to choose to become a person. ......Those days were like sweetly melting honey, ......but then, I hadn't realized that they were the beginning of days filled with a new kind of suffering......
units.note: Both retrospective did not/had not realize rather than present inability now.
units.japanese: そして私は愛を知り、人となることを選ぼうとする。……それは甘く蕩けるような蜜の日々だけれども、……新しい苦悩の日々の始まりだと、今は気付けない……。

description: The contrast that age and dirt would devalue an ordinary mirror but instead suggest divinity in this shrine mirror is reduced to a causal statement about its having been offered.
sourceReading: For this particular enshrined mirror, the same worn, cloudy, dirty appearance instead conveys some sacred stature.

units.text: It was an old-looking mirror, dim and dirty. ......If it were an ordinary mirror, that'd probably give you a terribly bad impression of its value. ...However, since the mirror had been offered to this small shrine, it made you feel some kind of divinity.
units.note: Both appearance/that quality explicitly carries old dirty mirror attribute into divinity; placement condition legitimate surrounding framing.
units.japanese: …しかし、この祠に納められている鏡に限っては、むしろそれが何かの神格を感じさせた。

description: The repeated temptation to bite the fruit of knowledge becomes “take a bite of true wisdom,” and having already eaten that fruit becomes tasting “that truth.”
sourceReading: The witch repeats the same temptation as at 40722: bite the fruit of knowledge. Shannon wonders whether she has already eaten it because she has known those maddening feelings.

units.text: The witch whispers. She tempts me to take a bite of true wisdom. Maybe I'm already having a taste of that truth.
units.note: Both fruit of knowledge and that fruit repeat concrete imagery.
units.japanese:
知恵の実をかじりなさいと誘惑する。
あるいは、私はもうその実を口にしてしまっているのかもしれない。
candidates: take a bite of true wisdom

description: A singular trial that is simultaneously small and large becomes “the small and large trials.”
sourceReading: Breaking the mirror is the trial she imposes on herself, surely small yet great.

units.text: Come, have courage. I'll free myself from being mere furniture. And I'll receive new sufferings, and become human. These are surely the small and large trials I must impose on myself.
units.note: MG one small yet large trial; UP plural small and large trials.
units.japanese: これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。

units.text:
Come, have courage. I'll free myself from being mere furniture.
And I'll accept my new sufferings, and become human.
These are surely the small and large trials I must impose on myself.
units.note: MG one small yet large trial; UP plural small and large trials.
units.japanese:
さぁ、勇気を。そして私を家具から解放しよう。
そして新たな苦しみを受け入れることで、人間となろう。
これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。

description: 手を離す気がない becomes “couldn’t spare the time,” replacing lack of intention with inability.
sourceReading: The narrator supposes Kinzo is immersed in research and has no intention of stopping it.

units.text: Genji had supposedly told Kinzo of Eva's family's arrival, but he hadn't come down yet. ...He was probably immersed in his own 'research', and couldn't spare the time. This often happened, so the others waited patiently for their fickle father to come down.
units.note: Both couldn’t spare time retain inability rather than unwillingness to stop research.
units.japanese: …おそらく、自分の「研究」に没頭していて、手を離す気がないのだろう。

units.text: Genji had supposedly told Kinzo of Eva's family's arrival, but he still hadn't come down. ...He was probably immersed in his "research" and couldn't spare the time. This often happened, so the others waited patiently for their fickle father to arrive.
units.note: Both couldn’t spare time retain inability rather than unwillingness to stop research.
units.japanese: 絵羽たちの到着を、源次が金蔵に伝えたはずなのだが、なかなか降りてこない。…おそらく、自分の「研究」に没頭していて、手を離す気がないのだろう。それはよくあることなので、彼らは気まぐれな父が降りてくるまでのんびり待つのだった。

units.text: Genji had supposedly told Kinzo of Eva's family's arrival, but he hadn't come down yet. ...He was probably immersed in his own "research", and couldn't spare the time. This often happened, so the others waited patiently for their fickle father to come down.
units.note: Both couldn’t spare time retain inability rather than unwillingness to stop research.
units.japanese: 絵羽たちの到着を、源次が金蔵に伝えたはずなのだが、なかなか降りてこない。…おそらく、自分の「研究」に没頭していて、手を離す気がないのだろう。それはよくあることなので、彼らは気まぐれな父が降りてくるまでのんびり待つのだった。

description: 国語算数やない becomes “You learn math and language in school, right?” rather than a negation. The contrast with learning an attitude is weakened.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi rhetorically says that what one learns in school is not language and arithmetic, but the stance and attitude needed to learn throughout life.

units.text: "You learn math and language in school, right?  What you really need to learn is the right attitude for learning more.  Once you form that basis, you can finally start a long period of study that'll last your entire life."
units.note: Both restore negation of language/math as main school purpose and contrast with learning attitude.
units.japanese: 「学校で習うのは国語算数やない。モノを学ぶ姿勢と態度を学ぶんや。その基礎ができて、ようやく生涯をかけた勉強が始まるんやで。」
candidates: learn math and language in school, right

description: 男に食わしてもらうため and 貞淑を装う become “dress modestly to entertain men,” replacing economic dependence and a performance of feminine virtue with clothing and entertainment.
sourceReading: Eva says the era when women had to feign chastity or feminine virtue so that men would support them has long ended. She uses this to defend Jessica’s manner of speaking.

units.text: "My, isn't that fascinating, right?  Times change.  The time when we had to dress modestly to entertain men ended a long time ago."
units.note: MG act modest drops dress addition but retains entertain men rather than economic dependence. UP restores feigned purity and literal man allowing us to eat, but calques economic support instead of idiomatic being supported by men.
units.japanese: 「あぁら、これはこれで魅力的よぅ、ねぇ？　時代は変わるのよ。男に食わしてもらうために貞淑を装わなくてはならなかった時代はとっくに終わってるんだから。」

units.text: "Come now, she's quite appealing in her own way, isn't she? Times change. The time when we had to act all modest to entertain men ended long ago."
