units.note: MG act modest drops dress addition but retains entertain men rather than economic dependence. UP restores feigned purity and literal man allowing us to eat, but calques economic support instead of idiomatic being supported by men.
units.japanese: 「あぁら、これはこれで魅力的よぅ、ねぇ？　時代は変わるのよ。男に食わしてもらうために貞淑を装わなくてはならなかった時代はとっくに終わってるんだから」

units.text: "Oh, but this is charming in itself, don't you think? Times change. The times when we had to feign purity in order for a man to allow us to eat ended a long time ago."
units.note: MG act modest drops dress addition but retains entertain men rather than economic dependence. UP restores feigned purity and literal man allowing us to eat, but calques economic support instead of idiomatic being supported by men.
units.japanese: 「あぁら、これはこれで魅力的よぅ、ねぇ？　時代は変わるのよ。男に食わしてもらうために貞淑を装わなくてはならなかった時代はとっくに終わってるんだから」

description: 半ズボン姿 becomes “half-naked,” inventing a state of undress.
sourceReading: Natsuhi remembers George in shorts, running around the beach and returning soaked, as though it were only recently.

units.text: "Thank you, I am alright.  ......But time really has flown.  It feels like just yesterday when you would run around half-naked by the beach and come back soaked."
units.note: Both half-naked retain invented undress where JP says shorts.
units.japanese: ……でも、本当に月日が経つのは早いものね。半ズボン姿で浜辺を駆け巡って、ずぶ濡れになって帰ってきた日が、ついこの間のように思います。」

units.text: "Thank you, I am fine. ...Still, time really has flown. It feels like just yesterday when you would run around half-naked by the beach and come back soaked."
units.note: Both half-naked retain invented undress where JP says shorts.
units.japanese: 「ありがとう、大丈夫です。……でも、本当に月日が経つのは早いものね。半ズボン姿で浜辺を駆け巡って、ずぶ濡れになって帰ってきた日が、ついこの間のように思います」

units.text: "Thank you, I am all right. ......But time really has flown. It feels like just yesterday when you would run around half‐naked by the beach and come back soaked."
units.note: Both half-naked retain invented undress where JP says shorts.
units.japanese: 「ありがとう、大丈夫です。……でも、本当に月日が経つのは早いものね。半ズボン姿で浜辺を駆け巡って、ずぶ濡れになって帰ってきた日が、ついこの間のように思います」

description: 受験を控えたナーバスな年頃 becomes “at the age where she was a novice at studying for tests.” This misreads nervousness as inexperience and generalizes entrance exams.
sourceReading: Jessica too is at a sensitive, nervous age with entrance examinations approaching, explaining the frequent clashes with her education-minded mother.

units.text: Jessica was still at the age where she was a novice at studying for tests. Recently, she had clashed often with her mother, who was enthusiastic about her education.
units.note: MG nerve-racking entrance exams restores nervousness. UP unpredictable age removes novice error but substitutes unpredictability and leaves exams generic.
units.japanese: 朱志香だって、受験を控えたナーバスな年頃だ。
candidates: age where she was a novice at studying for tests

units.text:
Jessica was still at that unpredictable age with exams right around the corner.
Recently, she had clashed often with her mother, who was enthusiastic about her education.
units.note: MG nerve-racking entrance exams restores nervousness. UP unpredictable age removes novice error but substitutes unpredictability and leaves exams generic.
units.japanese:
朱志香だって、受験を控えたナーバスな年頃だ。
最近は教育熱心な母親と激突することが多かった。

description: 身内の恥 is rendered “some shame to herself,” dropping the explicit family referent in Natsuhi’s reason for her emotional outburst.
sourceReading: Though Shannon did nothing wrong, Natsuhi feels that a family embarrassment has been witnessed and impulsively lashes out at her.

units.text: Shannon hadn't actually done anything wrong, but Natsuhi, who felt like some shame to herself had been shown, lashed out at her emotionally. ...This was something that often happened in the Ushiromiya family. But it seemed that Shannon wasn't strong-willed enough to accept it that way.
units.note: Both shame to herself omit family embarrassment as stated cause of Natsuhi outburst.
units.japanese: 紗音に非があったわけではないが、身内の恥を見られたような気持ちになり、つい夏妃は感情的な言葉をぶつけてしまう。

units.text: Shannon hadn't actually done anything wrong, but Natsuhi, who felt like something shameful to herself had been shown, lashed out at her emotionally. ...This was something that often happened in the Ushiromiya family. But it seemed Shannon wasn't strong-willed enough to just accept it and move on.
units.note: Both shame to herself omit family embarrassment as stated cause of Natsuhi outburst.
units.japanese:
紗音に非があったわけではないが、身内の恥を見られたような気持ちになり、つい夏妃は感情的な言葉をぶつけてしまう。…右代宮家ではよくあること。
しかし、そう思って割り切れるほど紗音はたくましくはないようだった。

units.text:
Shannon hadn't actually done anything wrong, but Natsuhi, who felt like some shame to herself had been shown, lashed out at her emotionally. ...This was something that often happened in the Ushiromiya family.
But it seemed that Shannon wasn't strong‐willed enough to accept it that way.
units.note: Both shame to herself omit family embarrassment as stated cause of Natsuhi outburst.
units.japanese:
紗音に非があったわけではないが、身内の恥を見られたような気持ちになり、つい夏妃は感情的な言葉をぶつけてしまう。…右代宮家ではよくあること。
しかし、そう思って割り切れるほど紗音はたくましくはないようだった。

description: “You couldn’t have complemented it as graceful” uses complemented in place of complimented or praised.
sourceReading: Her trembling fingers rattle the tableware; even flattering description could not call the service graceful.

units.text: Her shaking fingers made the utensils clang, and you couldn't have complemented it as graceful. The more pitiful everyone thought that was, the greater the silence grew, the more irritated Natsuhi looked, and the more Shannon cowered... Shannon's thin neck felt like it was being suffocated and choked by the death god of tension.
units.note: Both remove complemented error and clearly express impossibility of honestly calling service graceful.
units.japanese: 震える指は、カチャカチャと食器を鳴らしてしまい、お世辞にも優雅とは言えない。
candidates: couldn't have complemented it as graceful

description: 今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず becomes merely “still hadn’t returned,” while nonchalance is assigned to her time-killing.
sourceReading: After arguing with her mother, Jessica cannot now simply come sheepishly back into the parlor, so she is passing time in the garden.

units.text: Shannon and Jessica could be seen in the rose garden. Jessica, who had gotten into a fight with her mother, still hadn't returned to the parlor, and was nonchalantly killing time like this.
units.note: MG nonchalantly killing time retains displaced adverb and mere nonreturn; UP restores inability to wander back nonchalantly after argument.
units.japanese: 母親と口喧嘩をしてしまった朱志香は、今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず、こうして時間を潰しているのである。

units.text: Shannon and Jessica were in the rose garden. Jessica still hadn't returned to the parlor after getting into a fight with her mother and was nonchalantly killing time here.
units.note: MG nonchalantly killing time retains displaced adverb and mere nonreturn; UP restores inability to wander back nonchalantly after argument.
units.japanese: 紗音と朱志香の姿は薔薇庭園にあった。母親と口喧嘩をしてしまった朱志香は、今更ノコノコと客間には戻れず、こうして時間を潰しているのである。

description: すぐにピンとくる becomes “had struck back,” replacing the immediate intuitive realization that explains Jessica’s teasing question with retaliatory action.
sourceReading: Shannon unusually interrupts Jessica’s criticism with a slightly forceful defense, so Jessica immediately catches on to her attraction to George.

units.text: Shannon had uncharacteristically refuted Jessica's words forcefully, so Jessica had struck back.
units.note: MG caught attention removes retaliatory struck back but stops short of intuitive realization; UP caught on immediately restores recognition explaining teasing question.
units.japanese: 紗音が珍しく、ちょっぴり強い口調で朱志香の言葉を遮ったので、朱志香はすぐにピンとくる。

units.text: For once, Shannon had disagreed with Jessica in a slightly forceful tone, which immediately caught Jessica's attention.
units.note: MG caught attention removes retaliatory struck back but stops short of intuitive realization; UP caught on immediately restores recognition explaining teasing question.
units.japanese: 紗音が珍しく、ちょっぴり強い口調で朱志香の言葉を遮ったので、朱志香はすぐにピンとくる。

description: 浮いた話 becomes “anything bad,” moving from George’s little-discussed love life to a broad claim about his reputation.
sourceReading: Jessica says she rarely hears romantic gossip about George, then recalls his preferred type of girl and finds Shannon a good match.

units.text: "Come to think of it, I almost never hear anything bad about George nii-san.  Huh?  I think I remember hearing him say that family-oriented girls were his type, didn't I?  Nice, that fits you perfectly, Shannon!"
units.note: Both restore romantic-gossip scope rather than broad bad-reputation statement; UP never is stronger than JP rarely, but type-specific inference remains.
units.japanese: 「そういや、譲治兄さんって、あまり浮いた話を聞いたことないし。あれ？　確か以前、家庭的な子がタイプだとか前に聞いたかな？

description: 持たざる者 becomes “those who didn’t keep it,” replacing lack of means with apparent failure to retain something.
sourceReading: This is not borrowing by the have-nots; it is borrowing by people taking the offensive through business expansion.

units.text: This wasn't a loan for those who didn't keep it.  It was a loan for those who were on the offense.
units.note: Both lack-of-means poor/have-nots correctly restore distinction from failure to retain wealth.
units.japanese: 持たざる者の借金とは違う。攻める者の借金なのである。

description: 大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合 becomes a situation in which nervousness forces them to move money, reversing the causal relation.
sourceReading: For the parents, this may be a meeting involving large sums and therefore compelling tension; for Jessica it is a chance to see her cousins.

units.text: To the parents, it might be a situation where they were forced by nervousness to move a lot of money. But to Jessica, who lived on this isolated island called Rokkenjima, it was a precious opportunity to meet up with her cousins.
units.note: MG restores money-related strain but makes meeting strain concern having to move funds, rather than large funds at stake imposing tension. UP explicitly preserves money movement causing stress and JP tentative may.
units.japanese: 親たちにとっては、大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合かもしれない。

units.text: To the parents, these meetings burdened them with the strain of having to move a vast amount of money. But to Jessica, who lived on this isolated island called Rokkenjima, it was a precious opportunity to meet up with her cousins.
units.note: MG restores money-related strain but makes meeting strain concern having to move funds, rather than large funds at stake imposing tension. UP explicitly preserves money movement causing stress and JP tentative may.
units.japanese: 親たちにとっては、大きなお金の動く緊張の強いられる会合かもしれない。でも、六軒島という孤島に住む朱志香にとって、そんな機会は、いとこたちと会うことができる貴重なものでもあった。

description: しっかり返却できるプラン becomes “a plan that could be refused,” dropping the specific assurance of repayment and adding potential rejection.
sourceReading: George says his father arrived with a plan to expand the business using the loan and reliably repay it; the presentation is what remains.

units.text: "It's natural to be prudent when lending money.  Of course, my father will use what he borrows to expand his business, and he came with a plan that could be refused.  Everything else is left up to the presentation.
units.note: Both restore repayment plan, not rejected plan. MG solid probability slightly weakens assurance relative to UP definitely repay but core business/repayment relation restored.
units.japanese: 「お金を貸す時、慎重になるのは当然のことだよ。もちろんうちの父さんも、借り入れた分で事業を拡大し、しっかり返却できるプランを持って訪れてる。あとはプレゼンテーション次第ってところだろうね。

description: 正座をさせる becomes telling Krauss to sit up straight, reducing a compelled kneeling posture to a generic posture correction. The several witnessed occasions are also strengthened to often.
sourceReading: Shannon has on several occasions seen Kinzo slap Krauss or make him sit in seiza, illustrating humiliating treatment of an adult as a child.

units.text: As Shannon hung her head, she thought back on a scene familiar to those who worked in the mansion. Even Krauss, who acted haughtily towards his siblings, was still treated like a child by Kinzo. ...Shannon herself had often seen Kinzo slap Krauss and tell him to sit up straight. ......It was probably very embarrassing to be coerced like that at his age.
units.note: MG sit up straight remains wrong posture; UP restores seiza. Both often retain excessive frequency where JP says witnessed several times.
units.japanese: …紗音も何度か、金蔵が蔵臼に、平手で打ったり、正座をさせているところを見たことがある。

units.text: As Shannon hung her head, she thought back on a scene familiar to those who worked in the mansion. Even Krauss, who acted haughtily towards his siblings, was still treated like a child by Kinzo. ...Shannon herself had often seen Kinzo slap Krauss and tell him to sit up straight. ......It was probably very embarrassing to be coerced like that at his age.
units.note: MG sit up straight remains wrong posture; UP restores seiza. Both often retain excessive frequency where JP says witnessed several times.
units.japanese: 紗音は俯きながら、普段、屋敷に仕えながら見慣れた光景を思い返す。兄弟たちに尊大な態度で振舞う蔵臼ですら、金蔵の前では、未だに子ども扱いなのである。…紗音も何度か、金蔵が蔵臼に、平手で打ったり、正座をさせているところを見たことがある。……いい歳にもなってそれを強いられるのは、相当の屈辱のはずだ。

units.text: As Shannon hung her head, she thought back on those scenes she had grown used to seeing while working in the mansion. Even Krauss, who acted haughtily towards his siblings, was still treated like a child by Kinzo. ...Shannon herself had often seen Kinzo slapping Krauss, or making him sit in seiza‐style. ......It was probably deeply humiliating to have that forced upon him at his age.
units.note: MG sit up straight remains wrong posture; UP restores seiza. Both often retain excessive frequency where JP says witnessed several times.
units.japanese: 紗音は俯きながら、普段、屋敷に仕えながら見慣れた光景を思い返す。兄弟たちに尊大な態度で振舞う蔵臼ですら、金蔵の前では、未だに子ども扱いなのである。…紗音も何度か、金蔵が蔵臼に、平手で打ったり、正座をさせているところを見たことがある。……いい歳にもなってそれを強いられるのは、相当の屈辱のはずだ。

description: 大した言葉ではない becomes “wouldn’t be very long,” replacing the modest significance of the written words with their length.
sourceReading: Written out, her thanks would not look like anything remarkable, yet saying them required a little courage.

units.text: Shannon was finally able to put her thanks into words. If you wrote it out, it wouldn't be very long, ...but Shannon had needed just a little courage to say that out loud.
units.note: MG wouldn’t be very long retains length substitution; UP wouldn’t seem like much restores modest significance of words.
units.japanese: 文字にして書き出せば、それはまるで大した言葉ではないのだけど。…紗音には、それを口にするのに、少しだけの勇気が必要だった。

units.text: Shannon was finally able to put her gratitude into words. If you wrote it out, it wouldn't be very long, ...but Shannon had needed a little spark of courage to say it out loud.
units.note: MG wouldn’t be very long retains length substitution; UP wouldn’t seem like much restores modest significance of words.
units.japanese: 紗音は、ようやく言葉に出して先ほどのお礼を言うことができた。文字にして書き出せば、それはまるで大した言葉ではないのだけど。…紗音には、それを口にするのに、少しだけの勇気が必要だった。

description: The interrupted 身, beginning 身近, becomes “at least one,” and women who already recognize his charm become girls who “will recognize” it.
sourceReading: Shannon starts to say that women aware of his real charm are surely nearby, then retreats to saying there are many. The narrator explains that she likely intended to say someone was close by.

units.text: "Yes, I'm sure you'll run into one.  ......I'm sure there's at least one, ......no, a l, lot of girls that will recognize your real charm." Maybe she wanted to say that there was one really close.
units.note: MG at least one and future will recognize retain both changes. UP not— plus narrator not very far away restores interrupted nearby confession, but will recognize still changes already-aware admirers into future recognition.
units.japanese:
「えぇ、きっと巡り合えると思います。……譲治さまの本当の魅力に気付いている女性は、きっと身、
……いえ、お、大勢いらっしゃると思いますよ。」
本当は、身近にいますよ、と言いたかったのだろう。

units.text: "Yes, I'm sure you'll run into one.  ......I'm sure there's at least one, ......no, a l, lot of girls that will recognize your real charm." Maybe she wanted to say that there was one really close. ...Shannon avoided saying that much, drawing a final line as a servant.
units.note: MG at least one and future will recognize retain both changes. UP not— plus narrator not very far away restores interrupted nearby confession, but will recognize still changes already-aware admirers into future recognition.
units.japanese:
「えぇ、きっと巡り合えると思います。……譲治さまの本当の魅力に気付いている女性は、きっと身、
……いえ、お、大勢いらっしゃると思いますよ。」
本当は、身近にいますよ、と言いたかったのだろう。

units.text: "Yes, I'm sure you'll run into one. ......I'm sure there's at least one... ...no, a l-lot of girls who will recognize your real charm."
units.note: MG at least one and future will recognize retain both changes. UP not— plus narrator not very far away restores interrupted nearby confession, but will recognize still changes already-aware admirers into future recognition.
units.japanese:
「えぇ、きっと巡り合えると思います。……譲治さまの本当の魅力に気付いている女性は、きっと身、……いえ、お、大勢いらっしゃると思いますよ」
本当は、身近にいますよ、と言いたかったのだろう。…それを紗音は、使用人としての最後の一線を守り、はぐらかす。

units.text: She probably wanted to say that there was at least one girl very close to him. ...Shannon avoided saying that much, drawing a final line as a servant.
units.note: MG at least one and future will recognize retain both changes. UP not— plus narrator not very far away restores interrupted nearby confession, but will recognize still changes already-aware admirers into future recognition.
units.japanese:
「えぇ、きっと巡り合えると思います。……譲治さまの本当の魅力に気付いている女性は、きっと身、……いえ、お、大勢いらっしゃると思いますよ」
本当は、身近にいますよ、と言いたかったのだろう。…それを紗音は、使用人としての最後の一線を守り、はぐらかす。

units.text: "Yes, I'm sure you will. ......I'm sure there's a girl not— I mean, a, a, a lot of girls who will recognize your real charm."
units.note: MG at least one and future will recognize retain both changes. UP not— plus narrator not very far away restores interrupted nearby confession, but will recognize still changes already-aware admirers into future recognition.
units.japanese:
「えぇ、きっと巡り合えると思います。……譲治さまの本当の魅力に気付いている女性は、きっと身、……いえ、お、大勢いらっしゃると思いますよ」
本当は、身近にいますよ、と言いたかったのだろう。…それを紗音は、使用人としての最後の一線を守り、はぐらかす。

units.text: She probably wanted to say "there's a girl not very far away". ...She avoided saying that much, drawing a final line as a servant.
units.note: MG at least one and future will recognize retain both changes. UP not— plus narrator not very far away restores interrupted nearby confession, but will recognize still changes already-aware admirers into future recognition.
units.japanese:
「えぇ、きっと巡り合えると思います。……譲治さまの本当の魅力に気付いている女性は、きっと身、……いえ、お、大勢いらっしゃると思いますよ」
本当は、身近にいますよ、と言いたかったのだろう。…それを紗音は、使用人としての最後の一線を守り、はぐらかす。

description: 小意地悪そう becomes “sadistically,” intensifying the teasing observer’s manner beyond the source’s mild mischievousness.
sourceReading: Seeing the two blush, Jessica giggles with a slightly teasing or mischievous air.

units.text: Maybe he had never been praised this much by a girl. George's face turned just as bright red as Shannon's. As she watched the two of them, Jessica giggled sadistically.
units.note: Both sadistically retain excessive intensity for mildly mischievous giggling.
units.japanese: そんな二人を見て、朱志香は小意地悪そうにくすくすと笑うのだった。

units.text: He had probably never been praised this heavily by a girl before. George's face turned just as bright red as Shannon's. As she watched the two of them, Jessica giggled sadistically.
units.note: Both sadistically retain excessive intensity for mildly mischievous giggling.
units.japanese:
女性にここまで褒められたことはなかったのだろう。
紗音のそれに負けないくらい、譲治も真っ赤に赤面する。そんな二人を見て、朱志香は小意地悪そうにくすくすと笑うのだった。

units.text:
Maybe he had never been praised this much by a girl.
George's face turned just as bright red as Shannon's. As she watched the two of them, Jessica giggled sadistically.
units.note: Both sadistically retain excessive intensity for mildly mischievous giggling.
units.japanese:
女性にここまで褒められたことはなかったのだろう。
紗音のそれに負けないくらい、譲治も真っ赤に赤面する。そんな二人を見て、朱志香は小意地悪そうにくすくすと笑うのだった。

description: そっちのお勉強はからっきし becomes “completely abandoning your study of that,” adding an action or choice of neglect where the source assesses his poor capability.
sourceReading: Jessica says that although George is diligent, he is hopeless when it comes to studying romance and escorting a partner.

units.text: "Well, I'm sure you'll eventually find a wonderful partner, George nii-san.  But I don't think you'll be able to escort your partner as you are now, ri-ght?  It looks like you're diligent, but it seems that you've been completely abandoning your study of 'that'."
units.note: MG completely abandoned retains chosen neglect; UP clueless correctly assesses poor capability instead.
units.japanese: 「譲治兄さんも、やがては素敵なパートナーと出会うだろうけどさ。今のままじゃきっと、上手にパートナーをエスコートできないと思うぜー？　勤勉でいらっしゃるようだけど、そっちのお勉強はからっきしみたいだしよ。」

units.text: "Well, I'm sure you'll eventually bump into a wonderful partner, George nii-san, but I doubt you'll be able to properly escort your partner as you are now, right? It looks like you're diligent, but you've completely abandoned your study of "that"."
units.note: MG completely abandoned retains chosen neglect; UP clueless correctly assesses poor capability instead.
units.japanese: 「譲治兄さんも、やがては素敵なパートナーと出会うだろうけどさ。今のままじゃきっと、上手にパートナーをエスコートできないと思うぜー？　勤勉でいらっしゃるようだけど、そっちのお勉強はからっきしみたいだしよ」

description: 少しだけ呆れる becomes “a little shocked,” substituting surprise for exasperation at George’s lack of a girlfriend.
sourceReading: Eva gives a wry smile and is slightly exasperated, immediately after saying his lack of a partner is nothing to brag about.

units.text: Eva smiled bitterly, looking a little shocked.
units.note: Both restore exasperation with bitter smile rather than shock.
units.japanese: 絵羽は苦笑いしながら少しだけ呆れる。

description: 情けない becomes “shameless,” changing embarrassment at perceived inadequacy into a judgment of brazenness or lack of shame.
sourceReading: Given George’s ideal of finding a partner himself, meeting one through his parents feels somewhat pathetic or humiliating to him.

units.text: Surely, as a man, George wanted to find a partner by himself and take her back with him. So it seemed that he thought it would be a bit shameless to meet his partner for the first time in a marriage meeting arranged by his parents.
units.note: Both pathetic restore perceived inadequacy rather than shamelessness.
units.japanese: だから、親に設定された見合いの場で、パートナーと対面するというのは、ちょっぴり情けないものに感じるらしい。

description: 好きな相手なら誰と結婚してもいい becomes the same objection to marrying someone one does not like that George just made.
sourceReading: Eva counters that affection does not justify marrying just anyone; the wedding is brief but married life is long, so a partner should be chosen carefully.

units.text: "That doesn't mean you can argue that it's alright to marry someone you don't even like.  A wedding is instantaneous, but your life as a married couple after that is very, very long.
units.note: Both restore Eva converse objection: liking someone does not authorize marrying anyone, distinct from George objection to marrying disliked person.
units.japanese: 「だからって、好きな相手なら誰と結婚してもいいという論法にはならないわ。結婚は一瞬。でも、その後の夫婦生活はずっとずっと長いの。

description: 立派に成長してくれた becomes “I want to make you grow,” and どこへ出しても恥ずかしくない becomes his never being embarrassed wherever he goes.
sourceReading: Eva praises her only son for having grown so splendidly that she could proudly present him anywhere, then invokes his position as Kinzo’s only male grandchild to demand a suitable partner.

units.text: "I am proud of you, my only son.  I want to make you grow so that you will never be embarrassed no matter where you go.  ...And you are the only grandson to carry Father's blood.  ......We must prudently choose a fitting partner for you."
units.note: MG fine past growth and doing us proud restore both clauses. UP grown into fine man restores growth, but could match up to anyone substitutes competitive comparison for parent being unashamed to present him anywhere.
units.japanese: 「あなたは私の自慢の一人息子よ。どこへ出しても恥ずかしくないくらい、立派に成長してくれたわ。…そして、お父様の血を引く唯一の男孫。……あなたに相応しい相手は慎重に選ばなくてはならない。」

units.text: "You are my pride and joy—my only son. You have grown into a fine man who could match up to anyone. ...And with Battler‐kun leaving the register, you are the only grandson to carry Father's blood. ......We must prudently choose a fitting partner for you."
units.note: MG fine past growth and doing us proud restore both clauses. UP grown into fine man restores growth, but could match up to anyone substitutes competitive comparison for parent being unashamed to present him anywhere.
units.japanese: 「あなたは私の自慢の一人息子よ。どこへ出しても恥ずかしくないくらい、立派に成長してくれたわ。…戦人くんは籍を抜け、あなたが今やお父様の血を引く唯一の男孫。……あなたに相応しい相手は慎重に選ばなくてはならない」

description: 釣り合うと本気でお思い becomes “Did you really think you could snatch George away,” replacing a class-based judgment of matching status with an accusation of taking him.
sourceReading: Eva asks whether an inadequately educated, incompetent, unqualified, uncultured lowly servant really believes she can be a suitable match for George.

units.text: "George is the eldest grandson carrying Father's blood.  He's a person who may bear the burden of the Ushiromiya family someday in the future.  To answer that expectation, he has studied tirelessly, entered a wonderful college, and is getting wonderful grades.  Did you really think you could snatch George away, you uneducated, incompetent, unqualified, uncultured servaaaant?"
units.note: MG snatch George away retains romantic-taking accusation; UP in his league restores class/status matching question.
units.japanese: そんな譲治と、低学歴の無能無資格無教養な使用人風情が釣り合うと本気でお思いぃぃ？」
candidates: really think you could snatch George away

units.text: To answer to that expectation, he has studied tirelessly, entered a wonderful college, and is getting wonderful grades. Did you really think you could snatch George away, you uneducated, incompetent, unqualified, uncultured servaaaant?"
units.note: MG snatch George away retains romantic-taking accusation; UP in his league restores class/status matching question.
units.japanese: 「その期待に応えるために、たくさんの勉強を重ねて素晴らしい大学に入り、素晴らしい成績を残しているわ。そんな譲治と、無能無資格無教養な使用人風情が釣り合うと本気でお思いぃぃ？」
candidates: really think you could snatch George away

units.text: "George is the eldest grandson carrying Father's blood.  He's a person who may bear the burden of the Ushiromiya family someday in the future.  To answer that expectation, he has studied tirelessly, entered a wonderful college, and is getting wonderful grades.  Did you really think you could snatch George away, you uneducated, incompetent, unqualified, uncultured servaaaant?"
units.note: Additional echoed Eva rebuke repeats MG snatch George versus UP in his league; same WH defect, not a new count.
units.japanese: そんな譲治と、低学歴の無能無資格無教養な使用人風情が釣り合うと本気でお思いぃぃ？」
candidates: really think you could snatch George away

units.text: To answer to that expectation, he has studied tirelessly, entered a wonderful college, and is getting wonderful grades. Did you really think you could snatch George away, you uneducated, incompetent, unqualified, uncultured servaaaant?
units.note: Additional echoed Eva rebuke repeats MG snatch George versus UP in his league; same WH defect, not a new count.
units.japanese: 「その期待に応えるために、たくさんの勉強を重ねて素晴らしい大学に入り、素晴らしい成績を残しているわ。そんな譲治と、無能無資格無教養な使用人風情が釣り合うと本気でお思いぃぃ？」
candidates: really think you could snatch George away

description: いい気になっていた becomes “got into a bit of a good mood,” losing self-rebuke for becoming pleased with herself or carried away.
sourceReading: Shannon severely reproaches herself for having let herself become a little carried away, then reminds herself she is furniture.

units.text: ...I am seriously reflecting on how I got into a bit of a good mood. I had forgotten.  I am furniture.
units.note: MG full of myself and UP conceit restore self-rebuke rather than ordinary good mood.
units.japanese: …ちょっとだけいい気になっていたことを、私は猛省する。
candidates: got into a bit of a good mood

description: 手を抜けるべきところ becomes “important steps wherever she could,” changing where Runon takes shortcuts from places suited to them to necessary work.
sourceReading: Runon skillfully eases off where she can appropriately do so, producing work with almost no visible inferiority much faster.

units.text: In contrast, Runon skillfully avoided important steps wherever she could. So she could compete her jobs with a result looked similar to an outsider, but in a much shorter time.  In other words, she was good at cutting corners.
units.note: MG avoiding extra work where possible and UP corners where should be cut preserve suitable shortcuts, not necessary steps.
units.japanese: 対して瑠音は、手を抜けるべきところで上手に抜く。

description: 要領がいい and 要領が悪い become good or bad at “cutting corners,” narrowing practical adeptness to work omission and making the comparison with talking back incoherent.
sourceReading: Runon is efficient and knows how to manage things; by comparison Shannon lacks practical tact when she answers back to an irritated Natsuhi.

units.text: In contrast, Runon skillfully avoided important steps wherever she could. So she could compete her jobs with a result looked similar to an outsider, but in a much shorter time.  In other words, she was good at cutting corners.
units.note: Both shrewd/ not shrewd restore practical/social adeptness across shortcut/backtalk comparison, rather than narrow cutting-corners skill.
units.japanese:
だから傍目にはほとんど遜色のない仕事を、遥かに短時間でこなすように見える。つまり要領がいいということだった。
それに比べれば、不機嫌な夏妃に対して口答えを返してしまった紗音は、本当に要領が悪いというべきだろう…。

units.text: Compared to that, maybe we should say Shannon, who talked back at Natsuhi when Natsuhi was in a bad mood, was bad at cutting corners...
units.note: Both shrewd/ not shrewd restore practical/social adeptness across shortcut/backtalk comparison, rather than narrow cutting-corners skill.
units.japanese:
だから傍目にはほとんど遜色のない仕事を、遥かに短時間でこなすように見える。つまり要領がいいということだった。
それに比べれば、不機嫌な夏妃に対して口答えを返してしまった紗音は、本当に要領が悪いというべきだろう…。

description: The person made to forget the scolding becomes “me” in Shannon’s narration instead of Natsuhi.
sourceReading: Shannon imagines George cheerfully appearing, pretending not to read the atmosphere, and deftly changing the subject so thoroughly that Natsuhi forgets the scolding itself.

units.text: If only George-sama were here. Would he casually step in and save me? I'm sure he would show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he doesn't know what's going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I was ever rebuked by Natsuhi...
units.note: Both make Shannon forget being rebuked, rather than Natsuhi forget having scolded.
units.japanese: わざと空気が読めないかのように陽気に現れ、話題をひらりと逸らし、夏妃に叱責していたことすら忘れさせてしまうに違いない…。

units.text: If only George-sama were here. Would he casually step in and save me? Surely he'd show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he didn't know what was going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I'd ever been rebuked by Natsuhi...
units.note: Both make Shannon forget being rebuked, rather than Natsuhi forget having scolded.
units.japanese:
もしここに譲治さまがいてくれたなら。
さりげなく私を助けてくれただろうか。わざと空気が読めないかのように陽気に現れ、話題をひらりと逸らし、夏妃に叱責していたことすら忘れさせてしまうに違いない…。

units.text:
If only George‐sama had been here,
perhaps he would have casually stepped in and saved me. I'm sure he would show up cheerfully, intentionally acting like he doesn't know what's going on, nimbly change the subject, and make me forget I was ever reprimanded by Natsuhi...
units.note: Both make Shannon forget being rebuked, rather than Natsuhi forget having scolded.
units.japanese:
もしここに譲治さまがいてくれたなら。
さりげなく私を助けてくれただろうか。わざと空気が読めないかのように陽気に現れ、話題をひらりと逸らし、夏妃に叱責していたことすら忘れさせてしまうに違いない…。

description: 素直ではない becomes “dishonest,” suggesting deceit rather than the familiar guarded or contrary manner of his sulky response.
sourceReading: His turning away is typical of Kanon’s difficulty being straightforward or openly receptive; Shannon is nevertheless happy he is angry on her behalf.

units.text: Kanon faced away, acting sulky. It was a dishonest reaction, very like Kanon, ...but I was a little happy. He was getting mad for my sake.
units.note: MG hides true feelings restores guarded/sulky sense; UP dishonest retains deceit implication.
units.japanese: 素直ではない嘉音らしい態度だが、…私には少しだけ嬉しかった。

units.text: Kanon faced away, acting sulky. It was a dishonest reaction, very like Kanon‐kun, ...but I was a little happy. He got angry in my place.
units.note: MG hides true feelings restores guarded/sulky sense; UP dishonest retains deceit implication.
units.japanese: 嘉音は不貞腐れたようにそっぽを向く。素直ではない嘉音らしい態度だが、…私には少しだけ嬉しかった。私の代わりに、怒ってくれたから。

description: 自分を顧みない becomes “didn’t reflect on himself,” misreading disregard for self as a failure of introspection.
sourceReading: Shannon knows that Kanon sometimes fails to consider himself: unless she refuses firmly, he will help her even at the expense of his own work and risk punishment.

units.text: Shannon knew Kanon's character well.  ...Sometimes, he didn't reflect on himself. If I don't refuse forcefully, he will help me even if it means neglecting his own job...
units.note: MG not thinking enough about himself in neglect-work context restores self-disregard; UP reflect on himself retains introspection misreading.
units.japanese:
紗音は嘉音の性分をよく知っていた。…時折、彼は自分を顧みない。
強く断らなくては、彼は自分の仕事を疎かにしてでも私を手伝ってしまうのだ…。

units.text:
Shannon knew Kanon's character well.
...Sometimes, he didn't reflect on himself. If I don't refuse forcefully, he will help me even if it means neglecting his own job...
units.note: MG not thinking enough about himself in neglect-work context restores self-disregard; UP reflect on himself retains introspection misreading.
units.japanese:
紗音は嘉音の性分をよく知っていた。
…時折、彼は自分を顧みない。強く断らなくては、彼は自分の仕事を疎かにしてでも私を手伝ってしまうのだ…。

description: あれも時には愉快なことをする becomes “One can sometimes make something pleasant out of that,” dropping the referent and its action.
sourceReading: After reacting to a heart having been given to furniture, the witch says that “that one” too sometimes does amusing things. The source leaves the agent unnamed here.

units.text: ......I see.  A heart was given to furniture.  One can sometimes make something pleasant out of that...  *cackle*cackle*...!
units.note: MG restores an acting referent but identifies that unnamed one as a man; UP that one restores the referent without naming it. No specific identity is inferred here.
units.japanese: ……なるほど。家具に心を与えたか。あれも時には愉快なことをする…。くっくっくっく…！

units.text: ......I see. So, a heart was given to furniture. It would seem that even that man is capable of some quite amusing things, every now and then... *cackle*cackle*...!
units.note: MG restores an acting referent but identifies that unnamed one as a man; UP that one restores the referent without naming it. No specific identity is inferred here.
units.japanese: ……なるほど。家具に心を与えたか。あれも時には愉快なことをする…。くっくっくっく…！

description: 西暦紀元 becomes “the start of the modern era,” replacing the Christian-era calendar origin in the identification of the unnamed man. The earlier 紀元前 similarly becomes before the modern era.
sourceReading: The witch says that the year of this man’s birth eventually came to be called the beginning of the Christian/common-era reckoning, linking her star-guided man and love teaching to that calendar reference.

units.text: ......How simple and clear, how splendid, exhilarating, pleasant and thrilling.  ...The year that man was finally born was called the start of the modern era.  ......*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG retains before/start of modern era; UP Christian Era and Anno Domini restore the calendar allusion. The historical account remains Beatrice’s claim.
units.japanese: ……何とも単純明快にして豪快爽快愉快痛快。…やがてその男の生まれた年は、西暦紀元と呼ばれるようになったがな。……くっくっくっく！」

units.text: ...How simple and clear, how splendid, exhilarating, pleasant and thrilling. ...The year that man was finally born is called the start of the modern era. ...*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG retains before/start of modern era; UP Christian Era and Anno Domini restore the calendar allusion. The historical account remains Beatrice’s claim.
units.japanese: 「……何とも単純明快にして豪快爽快愉快痛快。…やがてその男の生まれた年は、西暦紀元と呼ばれるようになったがな。……くっくっくっく！」

description: 想い人 becomes “a pair of people with feelings for each other,” adding reciprocity to the offered union.
sourceReading: Beatrice says arranging for Shannon to be united with the person she loves is trivial for her magic.

units.text: "If I use magic, it is no trouble at all to arrange for a pair of people with feelings for each other to be joined."
units.note: MG uses the one you love in both offers. UP corrects row 796 but retains a pair with feelings for each other in row 805, adding established reciprocity.
units.japanese: 「妾の魔法に掛かれば、想い人と結ばれるように取り計らうなど、造作もない。」
candidates: pair of people with feelings for each other

units.text: "With my magic, it is no trouble at all to arrange for a pair of people with feelings for each other to be joined."
units.note: MG uses the one you love in both offers. UP corrects row 796 but retains a pair with feelings for each other in row 805, adding established reciprocity.
units.japanese: 「妾の魔法に掛かれば、想い人と結ばれるように取り計らうなど、造作もない」
candidates: pair of people with feelings for each other

description: 最後の理性で踏み止まる becomes “gave up on her last bit of common sense,” directly reversing the stated action. The near-spoken verification also becomes “Yes, that’s true.”
sourceReading: About to blurt out confirmation that the offer really is true, Shannon checks herself with her last remaining reason and recognizes the witch’s temptation.

units.text: Yes, that's true.  ...Shannon, who almost said that without thinking, gave up on her last bit of common sense.
units.note: Both restore holding back with remaining reason. MG still changes the near-spoken verification into Yes, of course; row 807 explicitly makes it almost spoken despite quotation marks. UP restores the verification and restraint.
units.japanese: それは本当なんですね。…思わずそう口にしてしまいそうな自分を、紗音は最後の理性で踏み止まる。
candidates: gave up on her last bit of common sense

units.text: "Yes, of course." ...Shannon almost said that without thinking, but held back with her last bit of common sense.
units.note: Both restore holding back with remaining reason. MG still changes the near-spoken verification into Yes, of course; row 807 explicitly makes it almost spoken despite quotation marks. UP restores the verification and restraint.
units.japanese: それは本当なんですね。…思わずそう口にしてしまいそうな自分を、紗音は最後の理性で踏み止まる。

description: 自分の苦悩を全て理解してくれる becomes the reason for her worries becoming clear to Shannon.
sourceReading: As she absorbs the witch’s recognition of her humanity, Shannon feels that her suffering is fully understood, drawing her toward the offer.

units.text: ......As she reflected upon those words, ......Shannon felt as though the reason for all her worries was starting to become clear...
units.note: Both restore Shannon feeling that the witch understands her suffering, rather than understanding its cause herself.
units.japanese: ……その言葉は、噛み締めれば噛み締めるほどに。……紗音には、自分の苦悩を全て理解してくれる気がした…。

description: 岩が覗き becomes “which you can see when you gaze at the cliffs,” inventing a viewing condition and losing the protruding offshore rock.
sourceReading: Beatrice asks whether Shannon knows the rock protruding from the sea very near the island, with a small torii and shrine built there.

units.text: "Do you know of the small torii and shrine that have been constructed on the ocean very near this island, which you can see when you gaze at the cliffs...?"
units.note: MG retains the invented view when gazing at cliffs, though the next reef description mitigates it. UP restores construction on the reef.
units.japanese: 「この島のすぐ近くの海に、岩が覗き、そこに小さな鳥居と祠が設けてあるのを知っているか…？」
candidates: see when you gaze at the cliffs

units.text: "Do you know of the small torii and shrine that have been constructed on the ocean very near this island, which you can see when you gaze at the cliffs...?"
units.note: MG retains the invented view when gazing at cliffs, though the next reef description mitigates it. UP restores construction on the reef.
units.japanese: 「この島のすぐ近くの海に、岩が覗き、そこに小さな鳥居と祠が設けてあるのを知っているか…？」
candidates: see when you gaze at the cliffs

description: 不気味な錯覚 becomes a creepy hallucination, giving a sensory-unreality label to her unsettling impression about the bargain.
sourceReading: Shannon is seized by an uncanny mistaken impression: what ought to be breaking the mirror for the witch seems to become something she must do for herself, as though a premise has been substituted.

units.text: "I shall stake my name, Beatrice, on it. The unbreakable days until today will continue into tomorrow and the next day.  And for eternity, in perpetuity." Shannon was trapped by a creepy hallucination.
units.note: Both use illusion instead of hallucination and immediately explain the conceptual premise substitution. No new sensory unreality is asserted.
units.japanese: 紗音は不気味な錯覚に囚われる。

units.text: Shannon was trapped by a creepy hallucination. The mirror was probably something to restrain the witch. ...So breaking the mirror should have been something done for the witch's sake. ......But it felt as though Shannon had to do it for her own sake. It seemed like some premise had been switched...
units.note: Both use illusion instead of hallucination and immediately explain the conceptual premise substitution. No new sensory unreality is asserted.
units.japanese: 紗音は不気味な錯覚に囚われる。

description: 今宵は退散しよう becomes “now, let us disperse,” omitting tonight and including the listeners in a group action.
sourceReading: Beatrice announces that she will withdraw for this night, leaving the reward promise available.

units.text: ".........Well then, now, let us disperse.  Hostile gazes may be pleasant, but they are bad for your figure, right?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*..."
units.note: MG call it a night restores tonight and is an idiomatic departure formula. UP restores tonight but retains plural disperse at 964 and 997.
units.japanese: 「………では、これにて今宵は退散しよう。敵意の眼差しは心地よくあるが、美容にはちと悪いのでな？　くっくくくくく…。」

units.text: ".........Well then, with that, let us disperse for tonight. Hostile gazes may be pleasant, but they are bad for the figure, you see? *cackle*cackle*cackle*..."
units.note: MG call it a night restores tonight and is an idiomatic departure formula. UP restores tonight but retains plural disperse at 964 and 997.
units.japanese: 「………では、これにて今宵は退散しよう。敵意の眼差しは心地よくあるが、美容にはちと悪いのでな？　くっくくくくく…」

description: 人の五感では形容できぬ becomes “couldn’t be noticed with any of the five senses,” replacing a limit of description with a limit of perception.
sourceReading: A pressure impossible to characterize through the human senses gradually fills the room; they immediately recognize its terror even though they cannot understand what it is.

units.text: While she still smiled, the witch's face began to twist itself... And, there was a oppressive feeling that couldn't be noticed with any of the five senses, which gradually filled the room... Even though they couldn't understand it, they immediately realized that it was something terrifying...
units.note: MG retains could not be noticed; UP restores could not be described. Both retain immediate terror and ocean analogy.
units.japanese: そして、人の五感では形容できぬ何かの圧迫感が、徐々に部屋を満たしていく…。
candidates: couldn't be noticed with any of the five senses

units.text: While she still smiled, the witch's face began to twist itself... Then, an oppressive feeling that couldn't be noticed with any of the five senses gradually filled the room... Even though they couldn't understand it, they immediately realized it was something terrifying...
units.note: MG retains could not be noticed; UP restores could not be described. Both retain immediate terror and ocean analogy.
units.japanese: 魔女が笑顔のまま、表情を歪ませ始める…。そして、人の五感では形容できぬ何かの圧迫感が、徐々に部屋を満たしていく…。それが何か理解できなくても、恐ろしいものであることはすぐに理解できた…。
candidates: couldn't be noticed with any of the five senses

description: 体を張って becomes “his body outstretched,” supplying bodily extension in place of personal risk or bodily protection.
sourceReading: Kanon puts himself physically on the line to stand protectively in front of Shannon, sweating under the threat.

units.text: Kanon blocked the way to Shannon, his body outstretched.  ...There was tense sweat on his forehead.
units.note: MG placing his body between them with nearby lethal threat conveys bodily protection and risk without invented extension. UP explicitly states risk of life.
units.japanese: 体を張って紗音の前に立ちはだかる嘉音。…その額に緊迫の汗が浮かぶ。

description: 豆粒大 becomes “the size of a speck,” removing the concrete bean-sized comparison and suggesting a much smaller spot.
sourceReading: A small burn mark approximately the size of a bean appears on the palm and has the shape of a butterfly; Kanon has the same mark.

units.text: On the palm of her hand, a small burn mark had been made, the size of a speck. ...Furthermore, it was shaped like a butterfly...
units.note: MG replaces speck with tiny burn mark, removing the stronger false speck comparison but still omitting bean-sized scale. UP size of a pea restores a concrete seed-sized comparison.
units.japanese: 手の平には豆粒大の大きさの、小さな火傷の痣ができていた。

units.text: There was now a tiny burn mark on the palm of her hand. ...And it was shaped like a butterfly...
units.note: MG replaces speck with tiny burn mark, removing the stronger false speck comparison but still omitting bean-sized scale. UP size of a pea restores a concrete seed-sized comparison.
units.japanese: 手の平には豆粒大の大きさの、小さな火傷の痣ができていた。…しかもそれは、蝶々の形をしていた…。

description: 出会いが水族館をきっかけにした becomes “used the aquarium as an excuse to get together,” inventing purposeful pretext in place of an originating occasion.
sourceReading: They chose Okinawa’s huge aquarium because their relationship began through an aquarium, giving the first overnight aquarium trip commemorative significance.

units.text: Shannon and George had chosen to go to Okinawa because there was a huge aquarium there. And they had used the aquarium as an excuse to get together. Since their relationship had started at an aquarium, having their first overnight trip also be to an aquarium must have held some commemorative value.
units.note: Both remove purposeful aquarium pretext and restore an originating occasion. UP first meeting creates a different continuity issue, recorded separately below.
units.japanese: それは、彼らの出会いが水族館をきっかけにしたものだったからだ。
candidates: used the aquarium as an excuse to get together

description: もはや ... レベルじゃねぇ becomes “already at the level,” replacing the negated threshold with its affirmation.
sourceReading: Jessica says an overnight trip is no longer merely at the level of kissing and hugging: she is pushing the expectation of further sexual progress.

units.text: "Like I said, this overnight trip was so you could overcome that stage, right?!  You're already at the level of things like kissing and hugging, right?!"
units.note: Both restore beyond mere hugs and kisses and retain marriage-vow response and innuendo.
units.japanese: もはやチューとかギューとかのレベルじゃねぇぜー？！」

description: 私なんかより is omitted, reducing the reassurance to a wonderful person appearing soon.
sourceReading: Because Jessica is wonderful, Shannon assures her that someone more wonderful than the person she herself found will surely soon appear for Jessica, using a self-effacing comparison.

units.text: "U, umm...  Milady is a wonderful person, so I'm sure a wonderful person will appear very soon...."
units.note: MG restores a comparison but makes it finding someone quicker than Shannon, rather than a more wonderful prospective partner. UP even more wonderful than I did restores the self-effacing comparative reassurance.
units.japanese: お嬢様は素敵な方ですから、私なんかよりきっと素敵な方がすぐに現れます…。」

units.text: "U-Umm... You're a wonderful person, Milady, so I'm sure you'll find someone wonderful much quicker than me..."
units.note: MG restores a comparison but makes it finding someone quicker than Shannon, rather than a more wonderful prospective partner. UP even more wonderful than I did restores the self-effacing comparative reassurance.
units.japanese: 「あ、あの…。お嬢様は素敵な方ですから、私なんかよりきっと素敵な方がすぐに現れます…」

description: 薔薇が潰れる and アーチが倒れる become being pricked by roses and falling off the arch, changing both anticipated events.
sourceReading: Sitting atop the rose arch would crush the roses and might topple the arch, but since the sitter is a witch the concern is unnecessary.

units.text: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe. Sitting in a place like that would get you pricked by the roses, and it might have been dangerous if you fell off the arch, ...but after all, this was a witch. That would surely be worrying too much.
units.note: MG restores both crushed roses and arch collapse. UP restores crushed roses but retains falling off the arch instead of the arch toppling.
units.japanese: そんなところに腰掛けたら、薔薇が潰れてしまうし、アーチが倒れて危ないかもしれないが、…何しろ相手は魔女なのだ。

units.text: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe. Sitting in a place like that would crush the roses, and it might have been dangerous if you fell off the arch, ...but after all, this was a witch. That was surely an unnecessary concern.
units.note: MG restores both crushed roses and arch collapse. UP restores crushed roses but retains falling off the arch instead of the arch toppling.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、薔薇のアーチの上に腰を掛けながら、上機嫌に煙管をふかしていた。そんなところに腰掛けたら、薔薇が潰れてしまうし、アーチが倒れて危ないかもしれないが、…何しろ相手は魔女なのだ。それは余計な心配に違いなかった。

description: てきめん becomes “instantaneous,” converting the claimed effectiveness of the witch’s magic into an absolute timing assertion.
sourceReading: The witch says her magic is strikingly effective, then insists the relationship was not naturally predetermined but made possible by her power.

units.text: "Naturally, my magic is instantaneous.  Maybe you feel that your meeting was a predetermined fate.  But that isn't correct, don't think this has anything to do with fate."
units.note: MG immediate effects and UP instantaneous both turn efficacy into categorical timing. The following explanation concerns overturning fate, not a measured delay.
units.japanese: 「当然よ、妾の魔法はてきめんである。…そなたにはまるで、二人が出会うのは予め決められた運命であったかのように感じているかも知れぬ。だがそれは間違いよ、ゆめゆめ運命だなどと思うでないぞ。」

units.text: "Naturally. The effects of my magic are immediate. Perhaps you feel your meeting was a predetermined fate. However, that is a mistake. Don't even think fate has anything to do with it."
units.note: MG immediate effects and UP instantaneous both turn efficacy into categorical timing. The following explanation concerns overturning fate, not a measured delay.
units.japanese: 「当然よ、妾の魔法はてきめんである。…そなたにはまるで、二人が出会うのは予め決められた運命であったかのように感じているかも知れぬ。だがそれは間違いよ、ゆめゆめ運命だなどと思うでないぞ」

units.text: "Naturally; my magic is instantaneous. ...You may even be feeling as if your meeting was a predetermined fate. But that isn't correct; don't think for a moment this has anything to do with fate."
units.note: MG immediate effects and UP instantaneous both turn efficacy into categorical timing. The following explanation concerns overturning fate, not a measured delay.
units.japanese: 「当然よ、妾の魔法はてきめんである。…そなたにはまるで、二人が出会うのは予め決められた運命であったかのように感じているかも知れぬ。だがそれは間違いよ、ゆめゆめ運命だなどと思うでないぞ」

description: 現金だ becomes the transformation being “worth money,” losing the teasing appraisal of Shannon’s change when her happy trip is mentioned.
sourceReading: The witch lightly laughs as though calling Shannon’s immediate brightening expedient or quick to respond when the topic suits her.

units.text: Shannon's face suddenly grew bright. The witch laughed lightly, as though that transformation was worth money.
units.note: MG amusement at speed of brightening restores the quick-change teasing. UP worth money retains literal monetary appraisal.
units.japanese: その変わり様を、魔女は現金だとでも言うように軽く笑う。

units.text:
Shannon's face suddenly grew bright.
The witch laughed lightly, as though that transformation was worth money.
units.note: MG amusement at speed of brightening restores the quick-change teasing. UP worth money retains literal monetary appraisal.
units.japanese:
紗音の顔が、ぱーっと明るくなっていく。
その変わり様を、魔女は現金だとでも言うように軽く笑う。

description: 人に請われて ... 道具を与える becomes appearing in response to a person’s summons in order to give a tool, adding an appearance event and a more specific invocation.
sourceReading: According to Beatrice, since long ago she has several times given people objects imbued with magical power at their request.

units.text: According to Beatrice, she had appeared several times in the past in response to a person's summons so that she could give them a tool imbued with some kind of magical power. ...However, when most people used that power to resolve their worries, they quickly came to think of that power as creepy, and, forgetting their feelings of thanks, they threw the tools they had been given away with disgust.
units.note: Both retain appearing in response to summons rather than unspecified requests for magical objects.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェが言うには、大昔から、人に請われて何かの魔力を込めた道具を与えるということは何度かあったらしい。

units.text: According to Beatrice, she had appeared several times in the past in response to a person's summons, to give them some tool imbued with magical power. ...However, when most people used that power to resolve their worries, they quickly grew unsettled by it, forgot their former gratitude, and threw away the tools they had been given with disgust.
units.note: Both retain appearing in response to summons rather than unspecified requests for magical objects.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェが言うには、大昔から、人に請われて何かの魔力を込めた道具を与えるということは何度かあったらしい。…しかし、多くの人は、その力で悩み事を解決すると、今度はその力を不気味がるようになって、感謝の気持ちなど忘れて、授けた道具を忌み嫌い捨ててしまうのだという。

units.text: According to Beatrice, she had appeared several times in the past in response to a person's summons so that she could give them an item imbued with some kind of magical power. ...However, most of them, after they used that power to resolve their worries, would quickly come to think of that power as creepy, and, forgetting their feelings of thanks, they would throw away the items they had been given with disgust.
units.note: Both retain appearing in response to summons rather than unspecified requests for magical objects.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェが言うには、大昔から、人に請われて何かの魔力を込めた道具を与えるということは何度かあったらしい。…しかし、多くの人は、その力で悩み事を解決すると、今度はその力を不気味がるようになって、感謝の気持ちなど忘れて、授けた道具を忌み嫌い捨ててしまうのだという。

description: 魔女を知覚できるか否か becomes “the ability to perceive it,” whose immediate English antecedent is a wavelength.
sourceReading: Each person supposedly has something like a wavelength, and there are large individual differences in whether that person can perceive the witch.

units.text: Shannon didn't know much about Beatrice. First off, she was a ghost-like being who appeared in unexpected places at unexpected times. And it seemed that not everyone could perceive that she was there. It seemed that each person had something called a wavelength, and that the ability to perceive it varied greatly among different people.
units.note: Both restore perceiving witches/the witch rather than perceiving a wavelength. Both still call it something called a wavelength rather than something like a wavelength, strengthening the analogy.
units.japanese: 何でも、人毎に波長のようなものがあり、魔女を知覚できるか否かについては激しい個人差があるのだという。

units.text: The things Shannon actually knew about Beatrice were surprisingly few. First off, she was a ghost-like being who appeared in unexpected places at unexpected times. And it seemed that not everyone could perceive that she was there. Apparently, everyone has something called a wavelength, and the ability to perceive witches varies greatly among different people.
units.note: Both restore perceiving witches/the witch rather than perceiving a wavelength. Both still call it something called a wavelength rather than something like a wavelength, strengthening the analogy.
units.japanese:
紗音がベアトリーチェについて知っていることはそう多くない。まず、彼女は幽霊のような存在で神出鬼没。
そして誰にでも知覚できるわけではないらしい。何でも、人毎に波長のようなものがあり、魔女を知覚できるか否かについては激しい個人差があるのだという。

units.text:
Shannon didn't know much about Beatrice. First off, she was a ghost‐like being who appeared in unexpected places at unexpected times.
And it seemed that not everyone could perceive that she was there. It seemed that each person had something called a wavelength, and that there was a great amount of individual variation in people's ability to perceive the witch.
units.note: Both restore perceiving witches/the witch rather than perceiving a wavelength. Both still call it something called a wavelength rather than something like a wavelength, strengthening the analogy.
units.japanese:
紗音がベアトリーチェについて知っていることはそう多くない。まず、彼女は幽霊のような存在で神出鬼没。
そして誰にでも知覚できるわけではないらしい。何でも、人毎に波長のようなものがあり、魔女を知覚できるか否かについては激しい個人差があるのだという。

description: 寛大に契約に応じてやった becomes “we created a lenient contract,” moving generosity from her acceptance to the agreement’s terms and adding joint creation.
sourceReading: Despite mixed ritual practices, the format and rules were in place, and she graciously agreed to the contract in recognition of his enthusiasm, then gave him gold.

units.text: "A format and rules had been assembled.  Several customs were mixed in, but, well, in deference to his enthusiasm, we created a lenient contract.  ......Then I gave him a mountain of gold."
units.note: Both restore gracious acceptance/responding to the contract without asserting joint creation of lenient terms.
units.japanese: 「一応、書式もルールも揃っていた。いくつかの作法が混在していたが、まぁ、その熱意に免じ寛大に契約に応じてやったのだ。……そして妾は山成す黄金を与えてやった。」

description: どこへ行くこともできない becomes “no matter where I go, I cannot do anything,” exchanging a movement restriction for a general action restriction.
sourceReading: The witch says she has been pinned to the island for decades, cannot reach people with her voice, and cannot go anywhere.

units.text: "......And thanks to that, I'm in this state.  I've been sewn in place on this island for several decades now, without even a friend to drink tea with.  ...No matter who I try to talk to, my voice doesn't reach them, and no matter where I go, I cannot do anything.  Such boring decades."
units.note: MG retains no matter where I go I cannot do anything; UP restores cannot go anywhere. Island confinement remains explicit in both.
units.japanese: 「……お陰でこのザマだ。茶飲み友達もなく、この島にもう何十年も縫い止められている。…誰に話し掛けようとも声は届かず、どこへ行くこともできない。何とも退屈な数十年だったことよ。」
candidates: matter where I go, I cannot do anything

units.text: "...And thanks to that, I'm in this state. I've been sewn in place on this island for several decades now, without even a friend to drink tea with. ...No matter whom I try to talk to, my voice doesn't reach them, and no matter where I go, I cannot do anything. Such boring decades."
units.note: MG retains no matter where I go I cannot do anything; UP restores cannot go anywhere. Island confinement remains explicit in both.
units.japanese: 「……お陰でこのザマだ。茶飲み友達もなく、この島にもう何十年も縫い止められている。…誰に話し掛けようとも声は届かず、どこへ行くこともできない。何とも退屈な数十年だったことよ」
candidates: matter where I go, I cannot do anything

description: 良くないものが溜まり、悪い歪みを引き寄せていた becomes “bad things gathered, drawn towards an evil distortion,” reversing the attraction.
sourceReading: According to the witch, past events in the islands caused undesirable things to accumulate, attracting an adverse distortion; a traveling eastern magician sealed them with a shrine.

units.text: "Aaah, that story.  .........Long ago, it seems various things happened on the islands around this area.  Because of that, bad things gathered, drawn towards an evil distortion.  It seems that a traveling eastern magician or something built a shrine for the repose of souls and sealed them in there."
units.note: Both restore accumulated bad things attracting distortion rather than being attracted by it.
units.japanese: ………この辺りの島で、大昔、色々とあったらしくてな。そのせいで良くないものが溜まり、悪い歪みを引き寄せていたのだ。それを、旅の東洋魔術師か何かが、鎮魂の社を建立して封じ込めたらしい。」
candidates: bad things gathered, drawn towards an evil distortion

description: その笑顔でもう一杯 becomes “ask for that smile again,” omitting the request for another cup.
sourceReading: After praising how coffee tastes when poured with a smile, Krauss asks her for another cup with that smile.

units.text: "Hmph.  Isn't that a good thing?  Coffee is obviously more delicious if it's poured with a smile.  ......Could I ask for that smile again?"
units.note: MG still requests another smile without the cup; UP restores another cup with that smile.
units.japanese: 「ふ。良いことじゃないか。同じ珈琲なら、笑顔で注がれた方がうまいに決まっている。……その笑顔でもう一杯頼めんかね？」

units.text: "Hmph. Wonderful. It goes without saying that coffee is more delicious when poured with a smile. ...Could I ask for that smile once more?"
units.note: MG still requests another smile without the cup; UP restores another cup with that smile.
units.japanese: 「ふ。良いことじゃないか。同じ珈琲なら、笑顔で注がれた方がうまいに決まっている。……その笑顔でもう一杯頼めんかね？」

description: The English reads “After that, was launched,” with no subject for either coordinated verb.
sourceReading: The teaspoon is flicked by unseen fingers and flies into the nearby bushes.

units.text: The witch gripped a teaspoon and flipped it with her fingers, sending it up in the air. ...After that, was launched by the fingers of some invisible person in empty space, and flew straight at a bush close nearby.
units.note: Both supply it as grammatical subject and preserve teaspoon flight into nearby bush, Kanon catch and counterfactual injury.
units.japanese: …するとそれは虚空で見えない何者かの指に強く弾かれ、すぐ近くの茂みの中へ鋭く飛んでいく。

description: 少し厳しい口調 and 非常に厳しく are rendered as speaking seriously and seeming extremely serious, weakening the contrast between gentle Shannon and unusually stern reproach.
sourceReading: She speaks a little sternly; to Kanon, who knows her, it must feel very stern.

units.text: Shannon spoke seriously, which was unusual for her. ...To Kanon, who knew her well, it must have seemed extremely serious. Kanon was excessively surprised at Shannon's style of speech, and remained silent.
units.note: MG restores Shannon sternness at 445–446 but retains Kanon more serious at 461. UP retains serious for both speakers rather than stern/harsh reproach.
units.japanese: 紗音が珍しく、少し厳しい口調で言う。

units.text: There was a touch of sternness in Shannon's voice, which was unusual for her. ...To Kanon, who knew her well, she must've sounded extremely stern. Kanon, looking excessively surprised considering Shannon's tone, fell silent.
units.note: MG restores Shannon sternness at 445–446 but retains Kanon more serious at 461. UP retains serious for both speakers rather than stern/harsh reproach.
units.japanese:
紗音が珍しく、少し厳しい口調で言う。
…それは、彼女をよく知る嘉音にとっては、非常に厳しく感じられるのだろう。紗音の口調に比べれば過剰なくらい嘉音は驚き、閉口する。

units.text:
Shannon spoke seriously, which was unusual for her.
...To Kanon, who knew her well, it must have seemed extremely serious. Kanon showed almost excessive surprise at Shannon's style of speech, and remained silent.
units.note: MG restores Shannon sternness at 445–446 but retains Kanon more serious at 461. UP retains serious for both speakers rather than stern/harsh reproach.
units.japanese:
紗音が珍しく、少し厳しい口調で言う。
…それは、彼女をよく知る嘉音にとっては、非常に厳しく感じられるのだろう。紗音の口調に比べれば過剰なくらい嘉音は驚き、閉口する。

description: 紗音と魔女の交流から焦点をずらしている means the criticism has shifted its focus away from Shannon’s dealings with the witch. English instead places the shift “ever since Shannon had suddenly started meeting with the witch.”
sourceReading: During this conversation, Kanon’s criticism has imperceptibly moved from her association with the witch to her own status and entitlement to love. Shannon quickly notices that change of target.

units.text: It seemed that Kanon's criticism had shifted in focus ever since Shannon had suddenly started meeting with the witch. ...Shannon also noticed that quickly.
units.note: Both restore criticism shifting focus away from witch interaction, not a change dating from contact beginning.
units.japanese: 嘉音の批判は、いつの間にか紗音と魔女の交流から焦点をずらしているようだった。
candidates: ever since Shannon had suddenly started meeting with the witch

description: 自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼 attributes the metaphorical baptism or ordeal to the days spent agonizing over being furniture. “After being baptized as furniture in his days of suffering” instead makes furniture the status conferred by baptism.
sourceReading: The ordeal of days spent suffering over his furniture status has stubbornly closed his heart; the preceding 諦め frames his weak denial as resignation.

units.text: Kanon spat that out, ...but he said it weakly, and turned away. He was probably giving up. ......After being baptized as furniture in his days of suffering, his heart was firmly sealed...
units.note: MG ordeal of suffering and UP baptism of days of suffering both make the days the hardening ordeal, rather than a baptism conferring furniture status.
units.japanese: ……自分が家具であることを苦悩した日々の洗礼が、彼の心を頑なに閉ざしてしまった…。
candidates: After being baptized as furniture in his days of suffering

description: 気分を変えるために gives a purpose: to change his mood or get a change of scene. The English makes a prior change in mood the cause of leaving.
sourceReading: He probably left the study for a change of scene, although his thoughts remain occupied by the same research.

units.text: It was rare for Kinzo to leave his study. ......However, that in itself didn't mean his noble research had been suspended. He may have left the study because of a change in mood, but that didn't mean that the thoughts filling his head were any different from those he had had inside the study.
units.note: MG retains prior mood change as cause of leaving; UP restores leaving for a change of mood.
units.japanese: 気分を変えるために書斎を出たのだろうが、その頭の中をいっぱいに占めているものは、書斎の中のそれと何も変わらない。

units.text: It was rare for Kinzo to leave his study. ...However, the fact that he had didn't mean his noble research had been suspended. He may have left the study because of a change in mood, but that didn't mean the thoughts filling his head were any different from those he had while inside the study.
units.note: MG retains prior mood change as cause of leaving; UP restores leaving for a change of mood.
units.japanese:
金蔵が書斎を出ることは珍しかった。
……しかし、だからといって、彼の高尚な研究が中断されているわけではない。気分を変えるために書斎を出たのだろうが、その頭の中をいっぱいに占めているものは、書斎の中のそれと何も変わらない。

description: 急ぎ金蔵の元へ駆け戻り、自らを楯にしようと思った places rushing back and shielding Kinzo inside Kanon’s intention. English says he “quickly ran back to Kinzo,” making the return happen before his impulse vanishes.
sourceReading: Seeing the witch, he thinks of hurrying back to shield Kinzo; seeing her expression dispels that impulse.

units.text: At once, Kanon, thinking that the witch must be plotting to do Kinzo some harm, quickly ran back to Kinzo, trying to become a shield himself.
units.note: Both narrate a completed return to Kinzo before the protective emotion dissipates; source places rushing back and shielding him inside Kanon’s intention.
units.japanese: 嘉音は咄嗟に、魔女が何か良からぬ陰謀で金蔵に害を為そうとしているに違いないと考え、急ぎ金蔵の元へ駆け戻り、自らを楯にしようと思った。

units.text: At once, thinking that the witch must be plotting to do Kinzo some harm, Kanon dashed back to Kinzo and tried to form a shield with his body.
units.note: Both narrate a completed return to Kinzo before the protective emotion dissipates; source places rushing back and shielding him inside Kanon’s intention.
units.japanese: 嘉音は咄嗟に、魔女が何か良からぬ陰謀で金蔵に害を為そうとしているに違いないと考え、急ぎ金蔵の元へ駆け戻り、自らを楯にしようと思った。

description: “Would he also be able see” omits “to” after “able.”
sourceReading: He wonders whether learning something will let him see something he currently cannot see.

units.text: Kanon took the brooch he had received from Shannon out of his pocket. ......Would he also be able see something that couldn't be seen now, by learning something?
units.note: Both grammatical versions retain learning enabling perception without the missing infinitive marker.
units.japanese: ……自分も、何かを知ることで、今は視えない何かを見ることができるのだろうか。

description: ため息をつこうとしたら means she was about to sigh when the shrill voices startled her. English says she had already taken a deep breath.
sourceReading: Her impending sigh is interrupted by her friends’ squealing.

units.text: After taking a single deep breath, her heart jumped when all her friends suddenly started speaking in shrill voices.
units.note: MG retains completed deep breath; UP restores impending sigh interrupted by friends.
units.japanese: ため息をつこうとしたら、友人たちが黄色い声を一斉に上げたので心臓が飛び上がった。

units.text: After taking a single deep breath, her heart jumped when all her friends suddenly started speaking in shrill voices.
units.note: MG retains completed deep breath; UP restores impending sigh interrupted by friends.
units.japanese: ため息をつこうとしたら、友人たちが黄色い声を一斉に上げたので心臓が飛び上がった。

description: 頭良さそォ reports that he looks smart; “I heard” invents hearsay and changes appearance to reported ability.
sourceReading: Rin’s boyfriend looks really smart.

units.text: "I heard Rin's boyfriend's re-ally smart!  Is it true that guy's a glasses beast?!"
units.note: Both restore looks smart, without invented hearsay.
units.japanese: 「リンの彼氏すっごい頭良さそォ！

description: うちのダンナ、ギャル男だし identifies her current partner as a gyaruo; “my husband’ll be a pretty boy” changes a present claim to future preference and drops the specific fashion type.
sourceReading: Her colloquially named husband/boyfriend is a gyaruo, a particular youth-fashion type.

units.text: "No way, no way, my husband'll be a pretty bo-y!"
units.note: MG retains future husband and pretty boy; UP my man is a gyaru-o restores present partner and type.
units.japanese: 「ダメダメ、うちのダンナ、ギャル男だしー！」

units.text: "No way, no way, my husband'll be a pretty bo-y!"
units.note: MG retains future husband and pretty boy; UP my man is a gyaru-o restores present partner and type.
units.japanese: 「ダメダメ、うちのダンナ、ギャル男だしー！」

description: 全ての女性にとってそうだとは言わないが qualifies the narrator’s generalization. “None of the girls would say it” instead asserts that the girls conceal or refuse to state their motive.
sourceReading: The narrator does not claim this holds for all women, but at least at Jessica’s school the festival amounts to a boyfriend appraisal show.

units.text: ......None of the girls would say it, ...but to them, the cultural festival at Jessica's school was really a boyfriend exhibition.
units.note: Both restore narrator qualification about not all girls.
units.japanese: ……全ての女性にとってそうだとは言わないが、…少なくとも朱志香の学校での文化祭は、彼氏の品評会と同じ意味だった。
candidates: None of the girls would say

description: 何系 asks what type the boyfriend is. “What kind of relationship?” asks about the relationship instead.
sourceReading: Her friends demand a hint about his type, before speculating about suits and glasses.

units.text: "What kind of person is your boyfriend, Jessie?  At least give us a hint.  What kind of relationship?  What kind of relationship?!"
units.note: MG retains relationship question; UP asks boyfriend type.
units.japanese: 何系？

units.text: "So what kind of person is he, Jessie? At least give us a hint. What kind of relationship? What kind of relationship?!"
units.note: MG retains relationship question; UP asks boyfriend type.
units.japanese: 「ジェシの彼氏、どんな人なのォ？　せめてヒントだけでも出してよ。何系？　何系？！」

description: 鬼畜眼鏡 carries a cruel or sadistic glasses-wearing persona. “Glasses beast” preserves neither a normal English description nor a clear cruel-personality meaning.
sourceReading: They ask whether the apparently intelligent glasses wearer really has a sadistic streak.

units.text: "I heard Rin's boyfriend's re-ally smart!  Is it true that guy's a glasses beast?!"
units.note: MG retains opaque glasses beast; UP hard S with glasses restores sadistic personality plus glasses, albeit with slang.
units.japanese: あれで鬼畜眼鏡なの、マジ本当ォ？！」

units.text: "Rin's boyfriend looks re-ally smart! Is it true that guy's a glasses beast?!"
units.note: MG retains opaque glasses beast; UP hard S with glasses restores sadistic personality plus glasses, albeit with slang.
units.japanese: 「リンの彼氏すっごい頭良さそォ！　あれでドＳ眼鏡なの、マジ本当ォ？！」

description: なら万策尽きますね means that in that case all options are exhausted, not “Then try everything else.”
sourceReading: Shannon mockingly says they are out of options and proposes Jessica admit she has no boyfriend, elaborating the humiliating alternative.

units.text: "Then try everything else...  How about meekly confessing to everyone that you don't have a boyfriend?"
units.note: Both restore exhausted options followed by confession, rather than trying all other means.
units.japanese: 「なら万策尽きますね…。大人しく彼氏はいませんと白状なされてはいかがでしょうか。」

description: After Jessica resents Shannon’s triumphant smile but needs her as sole confidante, クッションで窒息死させるのはその後でもいい means she can smother that confidante afterward. English supplies “herself” as the victim.
sourceReading: Jessica can defer her comic revenge on Shannon until after obtaining advice.

units.text: Listening to Shannon's comeback, the likes of which didn't happen even once a year, Jessica hugged her cushion and rolled around on her bed, pretending to faint in agony. She was so frustrated that she couldn't stand Shannon's smile, which looked so triumphant, but right now, she was the only person Jessica could talk with.  She could choke herself to death with her cushion later.
units.note: Both make comic cushion threat target Shannon rather than Jessica herself.
units.japanese: 勝ち誇ったように見えるその笑顔が悔しくてたまらないが、今は唯一の相談相手なのだ。クッションで窒息死させるのはその後でもいい。

description: 話が進まないので言ってしまおう is the narrator deciding to state the obvious crush so the story can proceed. “She had said that because” assigns the disclosure to a female character and makes it a past explanation.
sourceReading: Although spelling it out is tactless given her reaction, let us say it: Jessica has been interested in Kanon ever since he arrived.

units.text: Judging by Jessica's reaction, maybe it had been unrefined to speak of that in detail... She had said that because the discussion wouldn't progress if Jessica kept rolling around on the bed. Jessica had been thinking about Kanon ever since he had shown up.
units.note: Both restore narrator direct disclosure of crush rather than prior explanation by Shannon.
units.japanese:
この朱志香の反応を見る限り、それを詳しく語るのも野暮だろうが…。
いつまでも朱志香が転げ回っているだけでは話が進まないので言ってしまおう。

description: 十数年 is ten-odd years, not a few decades. The estimate in Shannon’s deliberately anachronistic trend joke is lengthened.
sourceReading: She says the misremembered tsundora term will become popular in ten-odd years.

units.text: "For people that aren't honest, like you, Milady, ...what was that word again, I learned it from George-sama.  That's right, weren't they called 'tsundora'?  Sounds like it will become popular after a few decades, doesn't it?"
units.note: MG decade or so is approximate ten-odd years; UP retains a few decades.
units.japanese: そうそう、ツンドラとか言うそうですよ？　あと十数年かすると流行るんだそうですよ？」

units.text: "People who aren't honest about their feelings, such as you, Milady, ...what was that word again, I learned it from George‐sama. That's right, they call them "tsundora". Apparently they will be quite popular a few decades from now, you know?"
units.note: MG decade or so is approximate ten-odd years; UP retains a few decades.
units.japanese: 「お嬢様のような素直じゃない方を、…何でしたっけ、譲治さまに習いました。そうそう、ツンドラとか言うそうですよ？　あと十数年かすると流行るんだそうですよ？」

description: ため息 is a sigh, rendered “took a deep breath.” The closing 深いため息 likewise becomes a deep breath.
sourceReading: Kanon sighs at her flustered silence; the scene ends with his deep sigh contrasting her continued odd cries.

units.text: When he saw that, Kanon took a deep breath. ...Jessica thought he had been shocked, and her face went pale.
units.note: Both restore sigh at 135 and 153, and deep sigh at 168.
units.japanese: その様子を見て嘉音はため息をつく。

description: 呆れられてしまったと思い means she thinks he is exasperated with her; 頭が真っ白 describes her mind going blank. English instead says she thinks he was shocked and her face went pale.
sourceReading: Interpreting his sigh as exasperation at her, Jessica loses her train of thought.

units.text: When he saw that, Kanon took a deep breath. ...Jessica thought he had been shocked, and her face went pale.
units.note: Both restore exasperation/fed up but retain face going pale instead of mind going blank.
units.japanese: …朱志香は呆れられてしまったと思い、頭が真っ白になってしまう。
candidates: shocked, and her face went pale

units.text: When he saw that, Kanon sighed. ...Jessica thought that he was exasperated with her, and her face went pale.
units.note: Both restore exasperation/fed up but retain face going pale instead of mind going blank.
units.japanese:
その様子を見て嘉音はため息をつく。
…朱志香は呆れられてしまったと思い、頭が真っ白になってしまう。

units.text:
Watching her, Kanon sighed.
...Jessica thought he was getting fed up with her, and her face went pale.
units.note: Both restore exasperation/fed up but retain face going pale instead of mind going blank.
units.japanese:
その様子を見て嘉音はため息をつく。
…朱志香は呆れられてしまったと思い、頭が真っ白になってしまう。

description: 僕らは家具だ is “we are furniture,” but the English has “I am furniture.”
sourceReading: In rejecting Shannon’s feelings and possibility of becoming more, Kanon asserts their shared furniture status.

units.text: ...Had Shannon seen something that could not be seen by him? I don't understand Shannon's feelings.  I am furniture.  ...As if I could, become something more than that.
units.note: Both restore we are furniture and inclusive inability to become more.
units.japanese: 紗音の気持ちなんてわからない。僕らは家具だ。…それ以上になんて、なれるものか。

description: 先日 gives an unspecified recent day; English fixes it as yesterday.
sourceReading: Shannon went shopping with him the other day because his usual clothes would not do.

units.text: "...Shannon...said normal clothes wouldn't do, ...so we went and bought this yesterday.  It probably doesn't fit me..."
units.note: MG other day restores unspecified recent date; UP retains yesterday.
units.japanese: 「…紗音が、普段着ではよくないと言って、先日、一緒に買い物を。……似合いませんでしたでしょうか…。」

units.text: "...Shannon...said my normal clothes wouldn't do, ...so we went and bought this yesterday. It probably doesn't fit me..."
units.note: MG other day restores unspecified recent date; UP retains yesterday.
units.japanese: 「…紗音が、普段着ではよくないと言って、先日、一緒に買い物を。……似合いませんでしたでしょうか…」

description: 似合いませんでしたでしょうか asks whether the outfit did not suit him, prompted by Jessica’s flustered compliment. “It probably doesn’t fit me” changes a tentative question about appearance to a negative assessment of fit.
sourceReading: Kanon politely asks whether the clothes did not look right on him.

units.text: "...Shannon...said normal clothes wouldn't do, ...so we went and bought this yesterday.  It probably doesn't fit me..."
units.note: MG asks whether outfit looks strange; UP retains negative fit estimate rather than suitability question.
units.japanese: 「…紗音が、普段着ではよくないと言って、先日、一緒に買い物を。……似合いませんでしたでしょうか…。」

units.text: "...Shannon...said my normal clothes wouldn't do, ...so we went and bought this yesterday. It probably doesn't fit me..."
units.note: MG asks whether outfit looks strange; UP retains negative fit estimate rather than suitability question.
units.japanese: 「…紗音が、普段着ではよくないと言って、先日、一緒に買い物を。……似合いませんでしたでしょうか…」

description: ショタって本当 asks in surprise whether the young-boy claim is true. “She really does like young boys” asserts confirmation and explicitly attributes an enduring preference to Jessica.
sourceReading: The friends excitedly ask whether the shota/young-boy characterization is really true.

units.text: "She really does like young boys!!"
units.note: Both assert enduring young-boy preference as confirmed rather than asking whether the teasing claim is true.
units.japanese: 「ショタって本当ォオオオォ！！」

units.text: "She really is into little kids!!"
units.note: Both assert enduring young-boy preference as confirmed rather than asking whether the teasing claim is true.
units.japanese: 「ショタって本当ォオオオォ！！」

units.text: "She really does like young boys!!!!!"
units.note: Both assert enduring young-boy preference as confirmed rather than asking whether the teasing claim is true.
units.japanese: 「ショタって本当ォオオオォ！！」

description: 勝手が違ってやりにくそう describes discomfort because things work differently from what Kanon knows. English specifies that going by himself would be difficult and uses this as the reason Jessica pushes him out.
sourceReading: Jessica pushes the unsettled, out-of-his-element Kanon into the corridor.
