units.text: She pushed Kanon's back, as it looked like it would be hard for him to go by himself, and chased him out. Even though Kanon was confused by Jessica's attitude and panic, which he had never seen before, he followed her instructions and headed in the direction she had indicated.
units.note: MG removes difficulty going alone but changes unfamiliar arrangements into trouble moving himself, still missing adjustment discomfort. UP restores hard time adjusting and corridor destination.
units.japanese: 何だか勝手が違ってやりにくそうにしている嘉音の背中をぐいぐい押して、廊下に追い出す。

units.text: She pushed Kanon's back, as he seemed to be having trouble moving himself, and chased him out. Even though Kanon was confused by Jessica's attitude and her panicky state, which he'd never seen before, he followed her instructions and headed in the direction she had indicated.
units.note: MG removes difficulty going alone but changes unfamiliar arrangements into trouble moving himself, still missing adjustment discomfort. UP restores hard time adjusting and corridor destination.
units.japanese: 何だか勝手が違ってやりにくそうにしている嘉音の背中をぐいぐい押して、廊下に追い出す。嘉音も、初めて見る朱志香の態度や狼狽ぶりに困惑しながらも指示に従い、指差された方へ向かうのだった。

description: “Groups from the school where singing songs” uses the locative word where in place of the verb were.
sourceReading: A student group is singing, with the audience already enthusiastic.

units.text: When Kanon went down the corridor as Jessica had told him to, he ran into a temporary stage set up where the vending machines should have been. It was probably being rented by the hour by some group or circle. Groups from the school where singing songs, but the place was already getting excited.
units.note: Both grammatical versions preserve singing and excited atmosphere; malformed where is removed.
units.japanese: 学生のグループが歌を歌っているが、それも大いに盛り上がっていた。
candidates: Groups from the school where singing songs

description: 壁にひとり寄りかかる means he leans alone against the wall, not merely approaches it.
sourceReading: Disliking the noise, Kanon stands apart, leaning against a dimly lit wall.

units.text: Disliking that clatter, he approached a dark wall alone. ......So this is what they call high school. It sure is noisy.  ...That's what Kanon thought.
units.note: Both restore leaning against wall alone rather than merely approaching it.
units.japanese: その喧騒を嫌い、薄暗い壁にひとり寄りかかる。

description: ハイカラ describes fashionable or modern, often Western-influenced style, not “highly colored.”
sourceReading: Compared with the classical music he knows, the performance seems very modern and unfamiliar to Kanon.

units.text: ...So to Kanon, the song Jessica sang was, how should you say it, ............very highly colored. An any case, if Natsuhi-sama heard it, she would probably faint.
units.note: MG colorful retains color calque; UP modern restores stylistic sense.
units.japanese: …そんな嘉音にとって、朱志香たちが歌う歌は何と言うかその、…………非常にハイカラなものだった。

units.text: ...So to Kanon, the song Jessica sang was...how should you say it... ...Extremely colorful. In any case, if Natsuhi-sama heard it, she'd probably faint.
units.note: MG colorful retains color calque; UP modern restores stylistic sense.
units.japanese: …そんな嘉音にとって、朱志香たちが歌う歌は何と言うかその、…………非常にハイカラなものだった。少なくとも、夏妃さまが聞かれたら卒倒しそうな雰囲気だった。

description: ノリには付いていけない means he cannot get into or keep up with the mood. “I must not go along with it” makes this a prohibition or duty.
sourceReading: He cannot share the mood, but appreciates how alive and happy Jessica looks.

units.text: ...I must not go along with it, but... ......Anyway, Milady is full of life and looks like she's having a great time.
units.note: MG must not go along retains prohibition; UP could not keep up restores inability to enter mood.
units.japanese: …ノリには付いていけないが。

units.text: ...I must not go along with it, but... ...At any rate, Milady is full of life and looks like she's having a great time.
units.note: MG must not go along retains prohibition; UP could not keep up restores inability to enter mood.
units.japanese: …ノリには付いていけないが。……とにかくお嬢様はすごく楽しそうで生き生きとしていた。

description: 自分というものを殺される is passive: island life suppresses one’s self. English supplies Jessica as an agent forced to kill her own sense of self and narrows the general process Kanon personally knows to her case.
sourceReading: Kanon knows better than anyone how living on Rokkenjima causes one’s individuality to be crushed, recognizing that pressure behind Jessica’s separate school persona.

units.text: ...Don't I know best that during her life on Rokkenjima, she'd had no choice but to kill her sense of self? Then the time she spent, ...not as Milady, the successor to the Ushiromiya family, but as a single girl called Jessica, living life to the fullest, must have been very important to her.
units.note: MG retains Jessica killing her own self; UP life on island kills your sense of self restores causal agent and general experience.
units.japanese: …六軒島での暮らしが、如何に自分というものを殺されるかは他でもない、僕が一番知っているじゃないか。

units.text: ...Don't I know better than anyone...that during her life on Rokkenjima, she's had no choice but to kill her sense of self? So the time she spends...not as Milady, successor to the Ushiromiya family, but as a single girl called Jessica, living life to the fullest, must be very important to her.
units.note: MG retains Jessica killing her own self; UP life on island kills your sense of self restores causal agent and general experience.
units.japanese: …六軒島での暮らしが、如何に自分というものを殺されるかは他でもない、僕が一番知っているじゃないか。なら、…右代宮家の跡継ぎとしてのお嬢様でない、朱志香というひとりの少女として生き生きできる時間がとても大切なものに違いない。

description: 歌に合わせて modifies the fans’ coordinated dancing. English separately says they “sang along,” adding a vocal activity.
sourceReading: Penlight-bearing fans dance in coordinated movements in time with the song.

units.text: But everyone looked like they were having a really good time. The die-hard fans who had even brought pen-lights sang along, dancing crazily with the same movements, almost as though it had been planned ahead.
units.note: Both retain extra audience singing, rather than only coordinated dance to the song.
units.japanese: ペンライトまで持ち込んでいる熱心な観客たちは歌に合わせて、まるで事前に取り決めていたかのようにぴったりと同じ動作で踊り狂っている。

units.text: But everyone looked like they were having a really good time. Some die-hard fans, who had even brought pen-lights, sang along and danced crazily with the same movements, almost as though it had been planned ahead.
units.note: Both retain extra audience singing, rather than only coordinated dance to the song.
units.japanese: でも、みんなすごく楽しそうだった。ペンライトまで持ち込んでいる熱心な観客たちは歌に合わせて、まるで事前に取り決めていたかのようにぴったりと同じ動作で踊り騒いでいる。

units.text: But everyone looked like they were having a really good time. The die‐hard fans, who had even brought pen‐lights, sang along, dancing crazily with the exact same movements, almost as though it had been planned ahead.
units.note: Both retain extra audience singing, rather than only coordinated dance to the song.
units.japanese: でも、みんなすごく楽しそうだった。ペンライトまで持ち込んでいる熱心な観客たちは歌に合わせて、まるで事前に取り決めていたかのようにぴったりと同じ動作で踊り騒いでいる。

description: “An any case” is malformed in place of “In any case” or “At any rate.”
sourceReading: At least the performance would make Natsuhi faint if she heard it.

units.text: ...So to Kanon, the song Jessica sang was, how should you say it, ............very highly colored. An any case, if Natsuhi-sama heard it, she would probably faint.
units.note: Both restore grammatical at any rate/anyway.
units.japanese: 少なくとも、夏妃さまが聞かれたら卒倒しそうな雰囲気だった。

description: あなたによろしくと特に言っておりました conveys a particular request to pass regards to Krauss. “She said to leave it to her” invents an assurance of handling something.
sourceReading: Takamiya specifically asked Natsuhi to give Krauss regards.

units.text: "...Yes, he seemed to be in good health.  That's right, Member Takamiya also came.  She said to leave it to her."
units.note: Both restore passing regards; gender is not inferred as independently established here.
units.japanese: 「…えぇ、お元気なようでした。そうそう、高宮議員もお出でになっておりました。あなたによろしくと特に言っておりましたよ。」

description: 地元の有力者 are locally influential figures, not local volunteers.
sourceReading: School events serve as social occasions for local power holders, including the prominent Ushiromiya family.

units.text: Naturally, the topic of Jessica's cultural festival came up at dinner. School events often became social gatherings for local volunteers. It was the same for the Ushiromiya family, who were celebrities around here. By remembering the names of the important people at the informal gathering, Natsuhi told Krauss the news.
units.note: MG retains volunteers; UP influential people restores power/status.
units.japanese: 学校の行事は地元の有力者たちの社交場となることが多い。

units.text: Naturally, the topic of Jessica's cultural festival came up at dinner. School events often became social gatherings for local volunteers. It was the same for the Ushiromiya family, who were celebrities around here. Natsuhi remembered the name of one VIP after another at that social gathering, telling Krauss the news about them.
units.note: MG retains volunteers; UP influential people restores power/status.
units.japanese:
当然、夕食の席では、朱志香の文化祭の話題が出た。学校の行事は地元の有力者たちの社交場となることが多い。
この辺りの名士である右代宮家にとってもそれは同じだった。夏妃は、親睦会であった要人たちの名を思い出しては、蔵臼に近況を伝えるのだった。

description: “I am always telling you watch your language” omits “to.”
sourceReading: Natsuhi repeatedly tells Jessica to correct that manner of speaking.

units.text: "Jessica.  I am always telling you watch your language."
units.note: Both reprimands are grammatical.
units.japanese: 「朱志香。そういう言葉遣いは改めるよう、いつも言っていますよ。」
candidates: am always telling you watch your language

description: 早い口調はそれを薄れさせます specifies that fast delivery weakens the effect of the passing-quality content. “Your fast style of speech was lacking” drops that relationship.
sourceReading: The content passed muster, but speaking too quickly diminished it; she should learn to pause for a breath.

units.text: "But you spoke the greeting a little quickly.  You passed on content, but your fast style of speech was lacking.  It would be good if you developed a habit of taking a breath every once in a while."
units.note: Both restore fast delivery weakening content impact.
units.japanese: 「ただ、挨拶が少し早口でした。内容は及第点でしたが、早い口調はそれを薄れさせます。一呼吸置く癖をつけるといいでしょう。」
candidates: fast style of speech was lacking

description: 素直に受け取れない describes embarrassment preventing unguarded acceptance. “Couldn’t accept them seriously” suggests failure to credit or seriously receive the praise.
sourceReading: She receives the words she wanted most, but shyness prevents her accepting them straightforwardly.

units.text: Even though she had heard the words she had most wanted to hear, Jessica acted shyly, and couldn't accept them seriously.
units.note: Both restore embarrassed inability to accept praise openly/frankly, not failure to take it seriously.
units.japanese: 一番欲しかった言葉をもらえたくせに、…朱志香は照れてしまい、それを素直に受け取れない。

description: 自分のことを家具だからと言い聞かせてきた means he has been telling himself he is furniture. そう言い聞かせなきゃならない辛いこと describes painful things that made that self-persuasion necessary. English makes him externally instructed and says things were tough because he was instructed that way.
sourceReading: Jessica supposes he endured many painful things that made him need to tell himself he was furniture, and mourns letting that define his whole life.

units.text: "Yeah.  ......Kanon-kun, you've been instructed to say 'because I am furniture'.  ......I'm sure there's been many things that have been tough just because you've been instructed that way.  ...I think that's, ......really unfortunate.  .........But the thought that your entire life will be decided by that, I think that's just sad."
units.note: MG retains external instruction and tough times because of it; UP restores self-persuasion prompted by painful experiences.
units.japanese:
「うん。……嘉音くんは、自分のことを家具だからと言い聞かせてきた。……そう言い聞かせなきゃならない辛いことが、きっとたくさんあったんだと思う。…それについては、
……本当に気の毒だと思う。………でも、それだけで嘉音くんの人生を全て決めちゃうなんて、私はそんなの悲しいと思うんだよ。」

units.text: "Yeah. ...Kanon-kun, you've been instructed to say "because I am furniture". ...I'm sure you've gone through a lot of tough times just because of that.
units.note: MG retains external instruction and tough times because of it; UP restores self-persuasion prompted by painful experiences.
units.japanese:
「うん。……嘉音くんは、自分のことを家具だからと言い聞かせてきた。……そう言い聞かせなきゃならない辛いことが、きっとたくさんあったんだと思う」
「…それについては、……本当に気の毒だと思う。………でも、それだけで嘉音くんの人生を全て決めちゃうなんて、私はそんなの悲しいと思うんだよ」

units.text: ...I think that's... ...really unfortunate. ......But the idea that your entire life'll be decided by that alone...just seems sad to me."
units.note: MG retains external instruction and tough times because of it; UP restores self-persuasion prompted by painful experiences.
units.japanese:
「うん。……嘉音くんは、自分のことを家具だからと言い聞かせてきた。……そう言い聞かせなきゃならない辛いことが、きっとたくさんあったんだと思う」
「…それについては、……本当に気の毒だと思う。………でも、それだけで嘉音くんの人生を全て決めちゃうなんて、私はそんなの悲しいと思うんだよ」

description: いつでも作り出すことができる states a capacity available at any time. “People are always making” asserts an ongoing universal behavior instead.
sourceReading: People can create within themselves another self they can really like, whenever they choose; Jessica explains how doing so lets her live through constrained daily life.

units.text: "You know, people are always making another part of themselves inside themselves that they can really like.  This isn't escaping from reality, okay?  ......When I'm that other part of myself, I can really feel like I'm living a great life.  So no matter how constrained and boring everyday life is, I can definitely live without suffocating."
units.note: Both restore available capacity to create another liked self, not universal ongoing creation.
units.japanese: 「人はさ、自分の中に、自分が本当に好きになれるもう一人の自分をいつでも作り出すことができるんだよ。現実逃避とかとは違うぜ？　……そのもう一人の自分でいる時、私は最高に生きているって実感できる。だから、普段の日常がどんなに窮屈で退屈でも、私はきっと窒息せずに生きていけるってわけ。」

description: 新しい院生 are new residents or pupils of the institution, not new graduates.
sourceReading: Fukuin deliberately gives newcomers new names to give them a new family and life; Kanon is the name in his case.

units.text: In the Fukuin House, because new graduates would be given new families and a new life, they were even given a new name. ......In his case, that was 'Kanon'.
units.note: MG retains new graduates; UP new students restores incoming residents/pupils rather than graduation.
units.japanese: 福音の家は、新しい院生に新しい家族と人生を与えるため、敢えて新しい名前を与える。

units.text: In the Fukuin House, new graduates would be given new families and a new life, so they were also given a new name. ...In his case, that was "Kanon".
units.note: MG retains new graduates; UP new students restores incoming residents/pupils rather than graduation.
units.japanese: 福音の家は、新しい院生に新しい家族と人生を与えるため、敢えて新しい名前を与える。……彼の場合はそれが「嘉音」だ。

description: 元は何という木の幹であったか concerns what tree the material originally came from. English asks whether it was originally a tree trunk at all.
sourceReading: He dismisses the original name as irrelevant to his present identity, comparing it to furniture whose material’s original tree identity no longer matters.

units.text: "No matter what kind of real name I had, ......the only truth now is that here, I am Kanon.  The past has nothing to do with anything.  ......The materials with which furniture is made, whether it was originally the trunk of a tree or not, in the end, it's all the same."
units.note: MG retains whether tree trunk or otherwise, losing original tree identity and comparison. UP restores name of original tree.
units.japanese: 「僕が本当は何という名前であったとしても、……今、ここに嘉音としてあることだけが現実です。過去など何の関係もない。……作られた家具の材料が、元は何という木の幹であったかどうでもいいことと同じです。」

units.text: "No matter what kind of real name I had, ...the only truth now is that here, I am Kanon. The past has nothing to do with anything. ...The materials with which furniture is made, be it a trunk of a tree or otherwise, are meaningless in the end."
units.note: MG retains whether tree trunk or otherwise, losing original tree identity and comparison. UP restores name of original tree.
units.japanese: 「僕が本当は何という名前であったとしても、……今、ここに嘉音としてあることだけが現実です。過去など何の関係もない。……作られた家具の材料が、元は何という木の幹であったかなんてどうでもいいことと同じです」

description: 未来も可能性も、見るべき夢もない denies three things. English says “My future and possibilities, aren’t even a dream I am supposed to see,” retaining future/possibilities as grammatical possessions while changing the denial.
sourceReading: He says he has no future, no possibilities, and no dream he should pursue, then asks her not to speak cruelly of them.

units.text: "......Only a human like Milady can embrace that possibility.  ...I am not like that.  My future and possibilities, aren't even a dream I am supposed to see.
units.note: Both restore explicit denial of all three: future, possibilities and dreams. Permitted/allowed emphasizes the status-based restriction in this character’s speech; no separate unsupported authority identified on this wording alone.
units.japanese: 「……そんな可能性を抱けるのはお嬢様が人間だからです。…僕はそうじゃない。僕には未来も可能性も、見るべき夢もない。
candidates: future and possibilities, aren't even a dream I am supposed to see

description: 紗音をジュリエットになんかしねぇ is George not allowing or making her become a Juliet. English asserts “Shannon isn’t Juliet” instead.
sourceReading: Jessica trusts George will resist opposition and prevent a Juliet-like tragic fate for Shannon, bringing her happiness.

units.text: "Th, ......there's nothing stupid about it!!  And, George nii-san's a wonderful person, and he's bearing both of his parents' expectations.  ...Yeah, when it comes to marriage, I'm sure Eva oba-san will interfere in various ways, and, umm, I think their future prospects look like they'll be full of trouble, alright?!  ...But you know, George nii-san isn't the kind of person who'll surrender to all that!  Shannon isn't Juliet, he'll definitely bring her happiness!!"
units.note: MG retains Shannon is no Juliet rather than George not letting her become Juliet. UP restores George agency.
units.japanese: そりゃ、譲治兄さんは立派な人だし、両親の期待も背負ってる。…確かに、結婚とかになれば絵羽叔母さんが色々と口出しをしてくるだろうし、まぁその、前途は多難だと思うぜ？！　…でもな、譲治兄さんはそんなのに屈する人じゃねぇ！　紗音をジュリエットになんかしねぇぜ、きっと幸せにしてくれる！！」

units.text: And, George nii-san's a wonderful person, and he's bearing both of his parents' expectations.  ...Yeah, when it comes to marriage, I'm sure Eva oba-san will interfere in various ways, and, umm, I think their future prospects look like they'll be full of trouble, alright?!  ...But you know, George nii-san isn't the kind of person who'll surrender to all that!  Shannon isn't Juliet, he'll definitely bring her happiness!!"
units.note: MG retains Shannon is no Juliet rather than George not letting her become Juliet. UP restores George agency.
units.japanese: そりゃ、譲治兄さんは立派な人だし、両親の期待も背負ってる。…確かに、結婚とかになれば絵羽叔母さんが色々と口出しをしてくるだろうし、まぁその、前途は多難だと思うぜ？！　…でもな、譲治兄さんはそんなのに屈する人じゃねぇ！　紗音をジュリエットになんかしねぇぜ、きっと幸せにしてくれる！！」

units.text: "...Th-There's nothing stupid about it!! Sure, George nii-san's a wonderful person, and he's gotta match up to his parents' expectations.
units.note: MG retains Shannon is no Juliet rather than George not letting her become Juliet. UP restores George agency.
units.japanese:
「ば、……馬鹿なってことはないだろ！！　そりゃ、譲治兄さんは立派な人だし、両親の期待も背負ってる」
「…確かに、結婚とかになれば絵羽叔母さんが色々と口出しをしてくるだろうし、まぁその、前途は多難だと思うぜ？！　…でもな、譲治兄さんはそんなのに屈する人じゃねぇ！　紗音をジュリエットになんかしねぇぜ、きっと幸せにしてくれる！！」

units.text: ...I'm sure when it comes to marriage, Aunt Eva'll interfere in various ways, and, umm, I think their future prospects look like they'll be full of trouble, okay?! ...But you know what? George nii-san isn't the kind of guy who'll surrender to that shit! Shannon's no Juliet, and he'll definitely bring her happiness!!"
units.note: MG retains Shannon is no Juliet rather than George not letting her become Juliet. UP restores George agency.
units.japanese:
「ば、……馬鹿なってことはないだろ！！　そりゃ、譲治兄さんは立派な人だし、両親の期待も背負ってる」
「…確かに、結婚とかになれば絵羽叔母さんが色々と口出しをしてくるだろうし、まぁその、前途は多難だと思うぜ？！　…でもな、譲治兄さんはそんなのに屈する人じゃねぇ！　紗音をジュリエットになんかしねぇぜ、きっと幸せにしてくれる！！」

description: English makes her feelings due to his conceit rather than questioning his assumption.
sourceReading: If my belief that you like me is merely my conceit, forgive me.

units.text: "......Milady, if your feelings for me are due to my conceit, then please forgive me."
units.note: Both still make her feelings result from his conceit rather than apologize if his assumption that she likes him is conceited.
units.japanese: 「……お嬢様が僕を好かれているという気持ちが、僕の思いあがりによるものならどうかお許し下さい。」

units.text: "...Milady, if your feelings for me were due to my conceit, then I must ask that you forgive me."
units.note: Both still make her feelings result from his conceit rather than apologize if his assumption that she likes him is conceited.
units.japanese: 「……お嬢様が僕を好かれているという気持ちが、僕の思いあがりによるものならどうかお許し下さい」

units.text: "......Milady, if your feelings for me are due to my conceit, then I beg for your forgiveness."
units.note: Both still make her feelings result from his conceit rather than apologize if his assumption that she likes him is conceited.
units.japanese: 「……お嬢様が僕を好かれているという気持ちが、僕の思いあがりによるものならどうかお許し下さい」

description: 想像がついていて becomes “planned this out until the end,” converting prediction into orchestration.
sourceReading: Kanon accuses her of toying with Shannon while already foreseeing her eventual fate.

units.text: "Don't play dumb!!  You didn't lend Shannon your power because you felt sorry for her.  ...You found a weak point in Shannon's heart as her chest burned with love, and you made her break the mirror that sealed you.  And that's not all, ...you planned this out until the end, and you're toying with her!  Am I wrong?!"
units.note: Both restore foreseeing/guessing the outcome, rather than planning it.
units.japanese:
「惚けるな！！　お前は、紗音を憐れんで力を貸したんじゃない。…恋に胸を焦がす紗音の心の隙をついて自分を封じていた鏡を割らせた。しかもそれだけじゃない、
…その末路まで想像がついていて、弄んでいる！　違うか？！」
candidates: planned this out until the end

description: そなたは…刈り取ったつもり becomes “I had hoped that you would punch a hole in that and harvest it,” reversing viewpoint and changing pruning into hoped-for harvesting.
sourceReading: The witch says Kanon thinks he has taken scissors to Jessica’s faint love and cut it away.

units.text: "Just as you've noticed, there is a faint love in Jessica's heart.  I had hoped that you would punch a hole in that and harvest it."
units.note: Both restore Kanon’s belief that he cut the love out. MG snipped in bud preserves pruning; UP harvested it retains misleading harvest wording despite corrected viewpoint.
units.japanese: 「朱志香の心にはお前が察する通り、淡い恋心があった。そなたはそれに鋏を入れ刈り取ったつもりでいる。」
candidates: hoped that you would punch a hole in that and harvest

units.text: "Just as you suspected, there was a faint love growing in Jessica's heart. You are under the impression that you have snipped it out, harvested it."
units.note: Both restore Kanon’s belief that he cut the love out. MG snipped in bud preserves pruning; UP harvested it retains misleading harvest wording despite corrected viewpoint.
units.japanese: 「朱志香の心にはお前が察する通り、淡い恋心があった。そなたはそれに鋏を入れ刈り取ったつもりでいる」

description: うまく行き過ぎていて becomes “wouldn’t be interesting if they didn’t go too far,” and そこへ行くと becomes “If that happens.”
sourceReading: George and Shannon are currently doing too well to entertain her; by contrast Kanon and Jessica look promising as entertainment.

units.text: "However, regretfully, it wouldn't be interesting if they didn't go too far, right?  If that happens, I think you all would entertain me greatly, *cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: Both restore actual overly smooth progress and contrasting amusement offered by the other pair.
units.japanese: 「しかし、如何せんあの二人はうまく行き過ぎていて面白くなくてな？　そこへ行くと、お前たちは大いに妾を楽しませてくれそうだぞ、くーっくっくっく！」
candidates: wouldn't be interesting if they didn't go too far

description: 対価なく貸すことがあるとでも becomes “Did I not lend them that power without asking for compensation?”
sourceReading: Does he imagine she ever lends power without a price? Watching their inevitable cruel fate is her payment.

units.text: "Did I not lend them that power without asking for compensation?  I'll lend a hand in love.  So that as compensation, I can enjoy watching the cruel fate that the two of them will eventually meet.  Even after one thousand years, no better show exists...!"
units.note: Both restore rhetorical denial of lending without compensation and spectatorship price.
units.japanese: 「妾がその力を対価なく貸すことがあるとでも？　恋に手は貸そう。その対価は、やがて必ず訪れる二人への過酷な運命の鑑賞料としていただくわけよ。これに勝る見世物は千年経っても存在せぬ…！」
candidates: lend them that power without asking for compensation

description: 忘れ去られることほど…悲しいことはない becomes “I won’t be saddened just by you forgetting about me.”
sourceReading: Nothing saddens her more than being forgotten.

units.text: "The bruise on the palm of your hand is already gone, so if you wish, tomorrow morning, you can let my existence disappear like an illusion or a dream.  ......I won't be saddened just by you forgetting about me."
units.note: Both restore nothing sadder than being forgotten.
units.japanese: 「そなたの手の平にもはや痣はなく、そなたが望むならば明日の朝には妾の存在など夢か幻のように消し去ることもできよう。……忘れ去られることほど妾に悲しいことはない。」
candidates: won't be saddened just by you forgetting

description: 欲深な亡者たちが…私を呼び覚ます becomes “I will surely wake the greedy dead.”
sourceReading: The greedy figures will surely awaken her.

units.text: "However, I will definitely be revived.  Make sure that you won't regret that day's coming at any time.  I will surely have my second coming and control everything as this island's true master.  ...That is the time when the door to the Golden Land will be opened again.  ...I will surely wake the greedy dead...!"
units.note: Both restore greedy figures calling or waking the witch rather than witch waking them; MG literal dead is not certified as literal ghosts by this rhetorical usage.
units.japanese: 「だが、妾は必ず蘇る。そしてその日がいつ訪れても後悔することのないよう、自らを戒めよ。私は必ずや再臨し、この島の真の主として全てを支配する。…その時こそ再び黄金郷の扉が開かれる。…欲深な亡者たちが必ずや私を呼び覚ます…！」

description: 満ちぬ潮も月もない becomes “a low tide without the moon”; the time arriving also becomes her visiting at a suitable time.
sourceReading: Just as no tide or moon fails to wax, her magical power too will surely grow full; the fitting time for revival will surely come.

units.text: "I also find it painful when I tend to preserve this form.  But as you ask, I will erase this form for a brief period.  Just like a low tide without the moon, my magical power will surely rise.  ...And I will surely visit, at a time that is appropriate for my revival."
units.note: Both restore inevitable waxing/rising analogy and fitting time arriving, not witch visiting at suitable time.
units.japanese: 「妾もこの姿を保ち続けるのがちと苦しい。しばしそなたの願い通り、姿を消そう。満ちぬ潮も月もないように、我が魔力も必ず満ちる。…そして必ずや訪れよう、妾が蘇るに相応しい時が。」

description: 面白いことをしてくれる appraises what Kinzo does for her amusement. “Do something truly interesting” becomes an imperative for a future act.
sourceReading: Kinzo does such amusing things, she exclaims in her reflection on the three-way deadlock.

units.text: Furniture is created to serve humans. And I cruelly treat humans as playthings during my thousand years of boredom. What a truly pleasant three-way deadlock, that I cannot control furniture! You fool, Kinzo, do something truly interesting! You, furniture, try and see if you can hit me...!
units.note: Both appraise Kinzo’s existing acts rather than commanding a future act.
units.japanese: 金蔵め、実に面白いことをしてくれる！

description: 妾を討てるか challenges furniture to see whether it can vanquish her. “Can hit me” reduces the goal to landing a blow.
sourceReading: Let furniture try to defeat her.

units.text: Furniture is created to serve humans. And I cruelly treat humans as playthings during my thousand years of boredom. What a truly pleasant three-way deadlock, that I cannot control furniture! You fool, Kinzo, do something truly interesting! You, furniture, try and see if you can hit me...!
units.note: MG fell and UP hunt restore vanquishing challenge beyond mere hit.
units.japanese: 家具め、妾を討てるか試みてみるがいい…！

description: 事情を知りつつも says she knows the circumstances yet can do nothing in response to the audible sobbing. English makes the crying voice tell her the situation.
sourceReading: Despite knowing what happened, Kumasawa can only sympathize and leave quietly as she hears Jessica crying.

units.text: "......Oooh, how heart-rending, Jessica-sama.  ...Even though her crying voice that I can hear from her room tells me of the situation, there is nothing I can do.  ...This is all a tragedy due to people who are too young getting too close, when the positions of their birth are too distant.  ...I can do nothing but understand Milady's feelings, hide my footsteps, and quietly walk away..."
units.note: Both still make audible cries convey circumstances instead of preserving existing knowledge despite inability to help.
units.japanese: 「……おぉ、おいたわしや朱志香さま。…寝室から聞こえてくるすすり泣く声に、私は事情を知りつつも、どうしようもないのでございます。…全ては若すぎた二人と近すぎた距離、そして生まれた家柄が遠すぎたゆえの悲劇。…私はただただ、お嬢様のお気持ちを汲み取り、足音を殺して静かに立ち去るのみなのでございます…。」

units.text: "...Oooh, poor Jessica-sama. ...Even though the cries I hear coming from your room tell me of the situation, there is nothing I can do.
units.note: Both still make audible cries convey circumstances instead of preserving existing knowledge despite inability to help.
units.japanese:
「……おぉ、おいたわしや朱志香さま。…寝室から聞こえてくるすすり泣く声に、私は事情を知りつつも、どうしようもないのでございます」
「…全ては若すぎた二人と近すぎた距離、そして生まれた家柄が遠すぎたゆえの悲劇。…私はただただ、お嬢様のお気持ちを汲み取り、足音を殺して静かに立ち去るのみなのでございます…」

units.text: ...This is all a tragedy due to a pair who are too young getting too close, when the positions of their birth are too distant. ...I can do nothing but understand Milady's feelings, hide my footsteps, and quietly walk away..."
units.note: Both still make audible cries convey circumstances instead of preserving existing knowledge despite inability to help.
units.japanese:
「……おぉ、おいたわしや朱志香さま。…寝室から聞こえてくるすすり泣く声に、私は事情を知りつつも、どうしようもないのでございます」
「…全ては若すぎた二人と近すぎた距離、そして生まれた家柄が遠すぎたゆえの悲劇。…私はただただ、お嬢様のお気持ちを汲み取り、足音を殺して静かに立ち去るのみなのでございます…」

units.text: "......Ohhh, how heartrending, Jessica‐sama. ...Even though her crying voice that I can hear from her room tells me of the situation, there is nothing I can do."
units.note: Both still make audible cries convey circumstances instead of preserving existing knowledge despite inability to help.
units.japanese:
「……おぉ、おいたわしや朱志香さま。…寝室から聞こえてくるすすり泣く声に、私は事情を知りつつも、どうしようもないのでございます」
「…全ては若すぎた二人と近すぎた距離、そして生まれた家柄が遠すぎたゆえの悲劇。…私はただただ、お嬢様のお気持ちを汲み取り、足音を殺して静かに立ち去るのみなのでございます…」

units.text: "...This is all a tragedy due to people who are too young getting too close, when the positions of their birth are too distant. ...I can do nothing but understand Milady's feelings, and walk away quietly with silent feet..."
units.note: Both still make audible cries convey circumstances instead of preserving existing knowledge despite inability to help.
units.japanese:
「……おぉ、おいたわしや朱志香さま。…寝室から聞こえてくるすすり泣く声に、私は事情を知りつつも、どうしようもないのでございます」
「…全ては若すぎた二人と近すぎた距離、そして生まれた家柄が遠すぎたゆえの悲劇。…私はただただ、お嬢様のお気持ちを汲み取り、足音を殺して静かに立ち去るのみなのでございます…」

description: 今…作らせてる states the ring is currently being made on his commission. “Now, I will have a ring made” postpones commissioning into an intention.
sourceReading: He is already having a suitable ring made and expects to bring it to the upcoming family conference.

units.text: ...Now, I will have a ring made that's appropriate to give to you.  I think I'll probably bring it to the family conference coming up soon.  I'll give it to you then, so please, I want you to let me hear your answer."
units.note: Both restore ring currently commissioned and conditional announcement if accepted.
units.japanese: …今、君に贈るのに相応しい指輪を作らせてる。多分、今度の親族会議の日には持っていけると思う。その時に贈るから、どうか君の返事を聞かせて欲しいんだ。」
candidates: Now, I will have a ring made

description: 楼座は声を潜めながら modifies Rosa’s manner of warning. English instead supplies lowering Maria’s voice as the content of her warnings.
sourceReading: Rosa repeatedly admonishes her in a lowered voice, but Maria does not listen.

units.text: While it wasn't completely full inside the train, it was really packed, with almost all of the seats occupied by passengers. Among them, Maria was making a fuss, stomping her feet on the seat while Rosa scowled at her. Since earlier, Rosa had warned her many times to lower her voice, but Maria hadn't obeyed her at all.
units.note: MG still substitutes lowering Maria’s voice for Rosa giving warnings quietly; UP explicitly restores Rosa’s low voice.
units.japanese: さっきから楼座は声を潜めながら何度も注意しているのだが、真里亞は一向に聞き入れなかった。

units.text: While it wasn't completely full inside the train, it was really packed, with almost all the seats occupied by passengers. Maria was making a fuss among them, stomping her feet on the seat while Rosa scowled at her. Rosa had warned her many times to lower her voice, but Maria hadn't obeyed her at all.
units.note: MG still substitutes lowering Maria’s voice for Rosa giving warnings quietly; UP explicitly restores Rosa’s low voice.
units.japanese: 満員とは行かないまでも、車内は座席ほとんどが乗客で埋まる程度には大勢いた。そんな中、座席で足をばたばたさせながらわがままを騒ぐ真里亞に、楼座は顔をしかめている。さっきから楼座は声を潜めながら何度も注意しているのだが、真里亞は一向に聞き入れなかった。

description: 幼い真里亞…勘違いしてしまったに違いない assigns the mistaken belief to Maria: persist in a tantrum and mother will yield. English assigns mistaken belief to Rosa and says she thought Maria had listened.
sourceReading: Rosa supposes past indulgence taught Maria that continued tantrums will make mother give in.

units.text: Before, Rosa used to pamper Maria and give in to her at times like this. But, that had probably been a bad thing. When young Maria had complained noisily, her mother had given in, wrongly assuming that Maria had listened to what she had said.
units.note: Both now assign the mistaken tantrum strategy to Maria and preserve Rosa’s reconsideration of indulgence.
units.japanese: 幼い真里亞は駄々をこね続ければ母親は折れて自分の言うことを聞いてくれるものだと勘違いしてしまったに違いない。

description: 心を鬼にして is hardening her heart or forcing herself to be stern despite affection. English says she turned the part wanting to pamper her daughter into a demon.
sourceReading: After a parenting book showed her the mistake, Rosa has been hardening her heart to avoid indulging her beloved daughter.

units.text: Rosa had realized that error with the help of an educational book, and since then, she had turned the part of her heart that wanted to pamper her beloved daughter into a demon... But Rosa managed to get less and less of a mutual understanding with Maria, and started to be discouraged by her own powerlessness little by little...
units.note: Both render hardening her heart rather than a literal demon transformation.
units.japanese: その過ちを教育書で気付かされた楼座は以来、愛娘を甘やかさないよう心を鬼にしているのだが…。

description: 元気なお嬢さん comments on the child’s energy or liveliness; “lovely young lady” offers general praise instead.
sourceReading: The old woman says Maria is an energetic little girl and asks her age, which Rosa hears as humiliating.

units.text: "It's alright, ho ho ho.  She's a lovely young lady.  How old is she?"
units.note: MG spirited restores energetic characterization; UP lovely preserves the generic praise criticized in WH. The subsequent humiliation is preserved in both.
units.japanese: 「いいんですよ、ホッホッホ。元気なお嬢さんですこと。おいくつです？」

units.text: "It's alright, hoh‐hoh‐ho. She's a lovely young lady. How old is she?"
units.note: MG spirited restores energetic characterization; UP lovely preserves the generic praise criticized in WH. The subsequent humiliation is preserved in both.
units.japanese: 「いいんですよ、ホッホッホ。元気なお嬢さんですこと。おいくつです？」

description: 襟首 is the back of the collar; 掴み上げ describes grabbing it up, followed by hair pulled as if tearing it out. English grabs the nape itself, adds dragging, and reduces the hair action to tugging.
sourceReading: Rosa grabs Maria by the back of her collar and pulls her hair as if wrenching it out.

units.text: At the moment she was hit, Maria stopped crying for an instant, but before long, she shouted and cried even more then before. Rosa, whose emotions had exploded, grabbed the nape of Maria's neck and dragged her, tugging at her hair.
units.note: MG retains neck grabbing, dragging and reduced hair tugging; UP restores collar grabbing and pulling as if ripping the hair out.
units.japanese: 感情を弾けさせた楼座は、真里亞の襟首を掴み上げ、その髪の毛を毟るように引っ張った。

units.text: At the moment she was hit, Maria stopped crying for an instant, but before long, she shouted and cried even more than before. Overwhelmed with emotion, Rosa grabbed the nape of Maria's neck and dragged her, tugging at her hair.
units.note: MG retains neck grabbing, dragging and reduced hair tugging; UP restores collar grabbing and pulling as if ripping the hair out.
units.japanese: 打たれたその瞬間は一瞬泣き止むが、真里亞はすぐにそれまでより大きく泣き叫ぶ。感情を弾けさせた楼座は、真里亞の襟首を掴み上げ、その髪の毛を毟るように引っ張った。

description: 頭を打つ becomes “hit Maria’s cheek.”
sourceReading: Rosa repeatedly hits Maria’s head, escalating with the crying.

units.text: Along with those severe words, Rosa hit Maria's cheek over and over again. The more Maria cried and shouted, the more Rosa hit her. And the more Maria was hit, the more intensely she cried and shouted...
units.note: MG still narrows the repeated blows to cheek; UP restores head. Earlier cheek slaps remain distinct actions.
units.japanese: 厳しい言葉と共に、楼座は何度も何度も頭を打つ。

units.text: With those severe words, Rosa hit Maria's cheek over and over again. The more Maria cried and shouted, the more Rosa hit her. And the more Maria was hit, the more intensely she cried and shouted...
units.note: MG still narrows the repeated blows to cheek; UP restores head. Earlier cheek slaps remain distinct actions.
units.japanese:
厳しい言葉と共に、楼座は何度も何度も頭を打つ。
真里亞が泣き叫べば泣き叫ぶほどに打つ。
そして真里亞も打たれれば打たれるほどに激しく泣き叫ぶ…。

description: “Even more then before” uses then instead of comparative than.
sourceReading: Maria immediately cries more loudly than before after the momentary pause.

units.text: At the moment she was hit, Maria stopped crying for an instant, but before long, she shouted and cried even more then before. Rosa, whose emotions had exploded, grabbed the nape of Maria's neck and dragged her, tugging at her hair.
units.note: Both use comparative than correctly.
units.japanese: 打たれたその瞬間は一瞬泣き止むが、真里亞はすぐにそれまでより大きく泣き叫ぶ。

description: “Rosa sweat slightly” uses sweat as an uninflected finite past verb in this narration.
sourceReading: She notices her slight perspiration being chilled painfully by the wind.

units.text: Rosa yelled at the station attendant not to worry anymore, since they would get on the next train. ...And then, finally, or maybe we should say, for the second time, ...she noticed the passengers on the platform staring at her from the distance. ......Rosa sweat slightly and felt the wind torturing her, making her sweat cold.
units.note: MG retains uninflected sweat; UP uses sweated.
units.japanese: ……楼座は自分がうっすらと汗をかき、風がそれを冷たくして苛むのを感じた。

units.text: Rosa yelled at the attendant, saying not to worry anymore, since they'd be getting on the next train. ...And then, finally...or rather, for the second time, ...she noticed the passengers on the platform staring at her from a distance. ...Rosa sweat slightly and felt a breeze make her sweat go cold, tormenting her.
units.note: MG retains uninflected sweat; UP uses sweated.
units.japanese: 楼座は、次の電車に乗るからもう構うなと駅員に怒鳴りつける。…そしてようやく、あるいは再びというべきか、…ホームの乗客たちが遠くからジロジロと見ているのに気付くのだった。……楼座は自分がうっすらと汗をかき、風がそれを冷たくして苛むのを感じた。

description: ぎこちなくも means although awkward; English says “without any restraint.”
sourceReading: Their faces are still red, but their awkward mutual smiles make mother and daughter look warm.

units.text: Both faces were still deep red, ......but the two of them, mother and child, smiled at each other without any restraint, looking warm...
units.note: MG still substitutes unrestrained smiles for awkward smiles; UP restores awkwardness while preserving the warmth of the narrated impression.
units.japanese: まだ互いの顔は真っ赤だったけど、……ぎこちなくも笑いあう二人の親子は温かに見えた…。

units.text: Both faces were still deep red, ...but the two of them, mother and child, smiled warmly at each other without any restraint...
units.note: MG still substitutes unrestrained smiles for awkward smiles; UP restores awkwardness while preserving the warmth of the narrated impression.
units.japanese: まだ互いの顔は真っ赤だったけど、……ぎこちなくも笑いあう二人の親子は温かに見えた…。

description: 全て手配が終わっています states all arrangements are finished. “I’m finishing” makes preparation ongoing. Later 済ませています likewise becomes “I’ll finish.”
sourceReading: Natsuhi says everything is already arranged, inviting Krauss to relax; later she reiterates completed preparations so he can focus on the conference.

units.text: "...I'm finishing all of today's preparations.  For now, shall we relax and wait while drinking tea?"
units.note: Both state preparation completed here. The parent’s later completed-service occurrence will be checked when reached.
units.japanese: 「…今日の準備は全て手配が終わっています。あとはお茶でも飲みながら寛いで待とうではありませんか。」

units.text: "...I'm finishing all of today's preparations.  For now, shall we relax and wait while drinking tea?"
units.note: Later occurrence also restores completed arrangements in both. Retained parent ID is an additional anchor, not a new unique finding.
units.japanese: 「…今日の準備は全て手配が終わっています。あとはお茶でも飲みながら寛いで待とうではありませんか。」

description: 見返り means returns or payoff from investment. “Large collateral” changes this to security for an obligation.
sourceReading: Large investment can bring large returns, but the business seesaw moves widely and slowly and does not give immediate results.

units.text: ...Krauss's project was something like a seesaw where a large amount of money swings. A big investment is linked to large collateral, but with a large-sized seesaw, the swaying is greatly slowed, and it's not something which shows immediate results.
units.note: MG massive payoffs and UP large return restore investment returns rather than collateral.
units.japanese: 大きな投資は大きな見返りに結びつくが、規模の大きなシーソーは揺れが大きくも緩慢で、すぐに結果が出るものではない。

description: 賄いも specifies that the servants’ own meal too will be worth anticipating. English merely says to look forward to the meal tonight.
sourceReading: Gohda promises his fellow servants a good staff meal as well as the guests’ veal dinner.

units.text: "Yes, dinner will be an excellent calf steak...!  A wonderful cut of meat is already anxiously waiting for tonight in the refrigerator.  Please, be sure to look forward to the meal tonight."
units.note: MG still leaves servants’ own meal unspecified. UP explicitly restores that fellow servants too are to anticipate tonight’s food in the kitchen context; its added relay instruction is recorded separately.
units.japanese: 「えぇ、ディナーには仔牛のステーキを…！　素晴らしい肉がすでに保冷庫で今夜を待ちわびておりますよ。賄いも今夜はぜひ期待してください。」
candidates: look forward to the meal tonight

units.text: "Yes, dinner will be calf steak...! A wonderful cut of meat is already anxiously waiting for tonight in the refrigerator. Please, be sure to look forward to dinner."
units.note: MG still leaves servants’ own meal unspecified. UP explicitly restores that fellow servants too are to anticipate tonight’s food in the kitchen context; its added relay instruction is recorded separately.
units.japanese: 「えぇ、ディナーには仔牛のステーキを…！　素晴らしい肉がすでに保冷庫で今夜を待ちわびておりますよ。賄いも今夜はぜひ期待してください」

description: 自慢の料理を披露する is showcasing his prized cooking; “announce the cooking” changes the activity.
sourceReading: Being permitted to present his proud dishes at the family conference is his greatest honor.

units.text: It was rare for Gohda to be in this good of a mood towards his fellow servants. To Gohda, who bragged about being a chef attached to the Ushiromiya family, being qualified to announce the cooking at the family conference was his greatest honor.
units.note: Both restore showcasing or displaying cooking rather than announcing it.
units.japanese: 右代宮家専属シェフを自負する郷田にとって、親族会議で自慢の料理を披露する資格を与えられているのは最高の栄誉なのだ。

description: 長丁場 describes a prolonged undertaking, here extended conference/service duty. “A long journey” suggests travel.
sourceReading: A typhoon may delay the return boat until Monday or Tuesday, making this a long stretch of work; everyone must avoid mistakes.

units.text: "...As long as the typhoon doesn't go too far astray from its course, and depending on the situation, I believe it will affect the boat trip back for everyone in the family.  Maybe the family conference's schedule will be prolonged until around Monday or Tuesday.  ......It will probably be a long journey, but I earnestly ask of you all to not make any blunders."
units.note: MG long task and UP long haul express prolonged duty rather than literal journey.
units.japanese: 「…台風がよほど逸れない限り、場合によっては親族の皆様方のお帰りの船に響くだろう。親族会議の日程が月曜か火曜辺りまで長引くかもしれない。……長丁場になるだろうが、皆くれぐれも粗相のないように頼む。」

description: “She had planned on to hiding” combines incompatible infinitive and gerund constructions.
sourceReading: She presumably thinks she is hiding her excitement somewhat, though Kanon can see it plainly.

units.text: As Shannon blushed just a bit, she turned her gaze away from the clock. ......Was it about time for the airplane carrying the family to arrive at Niijima? ...She had planned on to hiding the fact that her reunion with George after such a long time was making her heart palpitate, but Kanon, who stood at her side, understood her perfectly.
units.note: Retrospective anchor in previous reviewed unit: both remove planned on to hiding grammar; no additional coverage claimed.
units.japanese: …譲治との久しぶりの再会に胸をときめかせているのを、少しは隠しているつもりなのだろうが、脇の嘉音には丸判りだった。

description: カマトト describes affected or pretended innocence, rendered simply “ignorant.”
sourceReading: George reassures himself Shannon would not play so innocent as to mistake which hand is intended, then worries about preserving her free will.

units.text: "Aah, if I don't say properly that it's on the left hand, maybe she'll put on the right hand!  N-, no, Shannon isn't that ignorant, aaah but, if there's no free will, that'd be a little, I mean, uuuuuu, nnnnuuuuuuu, muuuuuuuaaaaaaaaahhhh...!!"
units.note: Both still say ignorant rather than affected innocence; free-will hesitation survives.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、左手とちゃんと言わないと右手にされちゃうかもしれない！　い、いや、紗音もそこまでカマトトじゃないけど、あぁでも、少しは自由意志がないと何だかその、

units.text: "Aah, if I don't say properly that it's on the left hand, maybe she'll put on her right hand! N-No, Shannon isn't that ignorant, aaah, but unless there's some room for her to express her free will, that'd be a little, I mean, uuuuuu, nnnnuuuuuuu, muuuuuuuaaaaaaaaahhhh...!!"
units.note: Both still say ignorant rather than affected innocence; free-will hesitation survives.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、左手とちゃんと言わないと右手にされちゃうかもしれない！　い、いや、紗音もそこまでカマトトじゃないけど、あぁでも、少しは自由意志がないと何だかその、うううううううぅ、んーーーぅううううぅぅうぅ、むぅううううぅああああああぁ…！！　」

units.text: "Aah, if I don't say properly that it's on the left hand, maybe she'll put it on the right hand! N‐no, Shannon isn't that ignorant, aaah, but, if there's no free will, that'd be a little, I mean, uuuuuu, nnnnuuuuuuu, muuuuuuuaaaaaaaaahhhh...!!"
units.note: Both still say ignorant rather than affected innocence; free-will hesitation survives.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、左手とちゃんと言わないと右手にされちゃうかもしれない！　い、いや、紗音もそこまでカマトトじゃないけど、あぁでも、少しは自由意志がないと何だかその、うううううううぅ、んーーーぅううううぅぅうぅ、むぅううううぅああああああぁ…！！　」

description: うんうんうなっている means groaning or humming in thought. “Nodding” supplies a different gesture.
sourceReading: He folds his arms and groans over the proposal phrasing until the knock startles him.

units.text: As he crossed his arms, nodding, someone knocked on the door. George was suddenly brought back to reality.
units.note: MG muttering and UP moaning/groaning restore vocalization instead of nodding.
units.japanese: 腕を組み、うんうんうなっていると個室にノックがある。

description: ほっと胸を撫で下ろす conventionally expresses breathing a sigh of relief; English adds him patting his chest.
sourceReading: Knowing the embarrassing part was not overheard, George is relieved.

units.text: Rudolf washed his hands, laughing cheerfully, and left. ...George knew that the most embarrassing part hasn't been overheard, and he patted his chest, feeling relieved...
units.note: MG relief phrasing removes chest patting; UP retains the literal gesture.
units.japanese: …譲治は恥ずかしい部分を聞かれていなかったと知り、ほっと胸を撫で下ろす…。

units.text: Rudolf washed his hands, laughing cheerfully, and left. ...George knew that the most embarrassing part hadn't been overheard, and he patted his chest in relief...
units.note: MG relief phrasing removes chest patting; UP retains the literal gesture.
units.japanese: 留弗夫はからからと笑いながら手を洗うと、出て行くのだった。…譲治は恥ずかしい部分を聞かれていなかったと知り、ほっと胸を撫で下ろす…。

description: 留弗夫兄さん is Rosa calling Rudolf her older brother. English substitutes Rudolf oji-san, reorienting the kinship label to Maria.
sourceReading: Rosa introduces Battler as her brother Rudolf’s son; Maria then tangles the repeated brother/son terms.

units.text: "Maria.  This is Battler onii-chan.  Rudolf oji-san's son.  ...Understand?"
units.note: MG restores the original PC brother label, resolving the original WH PC inconsistency. PS3-derived Japanese instead has uncle consistently, which UP follows. MG brother wording is therefore yellow PC material rather than a paired defect; disposition here concerns the original parent error, not equivalence to PS3.
units.japanese: 「真里亞。戦人お兄ちゃんよ。留弗夫兄さんの息子さん。…わかる？」

description: “You oftenly see” uses a nonstandard adverb in an ordinary frequency construction.
sourceReading: Battler often sees overseas costume parades on the news, but has never seen them in Japan.

units.text: "That's right, in Japan, Halloween is a minor event.  You oftenly see people marching in costume parades on the news from overseas, but I've never seen it in Japan."
units.note: Both remove nonstandard oftenly.
units.japanese: 「そうだなぁ、日本じゃハロウィンってマイナーなイベントだよな。仮装行列で練り歩くなんて、向こうのニュースではよく見るけど、日本じゃ見たことないぜ。」

description: “What are doing” omits the subject you.
sourceReading: Kumasawa finds Jessica and says Natsuhi was looking for her.

units.text: "Oh, Milady, what are doing in such a place?  Madam was looking for you."
units.note: Both include subject you.
units.japanese: 「おや、お嬢様、こんなところに。奥様が探しておいででしたよ。」

description: 辞めたり勤めたり describes alternating departures and employment. “Busy with retiring and your work” obscures that pattern.
sourceReading: Despite repeatedly quitting and returning, Kumasawa has been coming and going here since as long ago as Genji, so Jessica suspects she knows more about Beatrice.

units.text: "Kumasawa-san, you know, ...you're very busy with retiring and your work and all, but you've been here as long as Genji-san, right?  ......You know more, about Beatrice, don't you?"
units.note: Both restore recurring quitting and employment rather than retirement/work busyness.
units.japanese: 「熊沢さんはさ、…辞めたり勤めたりと急がしいけど、源次さん並みに昔からここに出入りしてるわけでしょ？　……ベアトリーチェのこと、もっと知ってるんじゃないの？」
candidates: busy with retiring and your work

description: むやみに近付かなかった means fishermen did not approach carelessly or indiscriminately. “Unreasonably didn’t approach” instead judges their avoidance irrational.
sourceReading: With many reefs and maritime accidents, fishermen feared the area and avoided approaching rashly.

units.text: "I've also heard that.  It's that story about, since there are lots of sunken rocks and shipwrecks around here, the fishermen got afraid and unreasonably didn't approach here, right?" "......Evil spirits settled down in Akujikishima and continued to eat the souls of people since ancient times.  ...There were lots of people related to this island who were dispossessed of their lives."
units.note: Both remove the assertion that avoidance is irrational. Stayed away whenever/as much as possible still overstates むやみに近付かなかった, not approaching carelessly; record under existing parent rather than a new unique finding.
units.japanese: 「前にも聞いたよ。この辺は暗礁が多くて、海難事故が多かったから、漁民たちが恐れてむやみに近付かなかったって話だろ？」

units.text: "I've heard about that before. Supposedly, there's lots of sunken rocks and shipwrecks around here, so the fishermen got scared and stayed away whenever they could, right?"
units.note: Both remove the assertion that avoidance is irrational. Stayed away whenever/as much as possible still overstates むやみに近付かなかった, not approaching carelessly; record under existing parent rather than a new unique finding.
units.japanese: 「前にも聞いたよ。この辺は暗礁が多くて、海難事故が多かったから、漁民たちが恐れてむやみに近付かなかったって話だろ？」

units.text: "I've heard this before. It's that story about how, 'cause of all the sunken rocks and shipwrecks around here, the fishermen got afraid and stayed away as much as they could, right?"
units.note: Both remove the assertion that avoidance is irrational. Stayed away whenever/as much as possible still overstates むやみに近付かなかった, not approaching carelessly; record under existing parent rather than a new unique finding.
units.japanese: 「前にも聞いたよ。この辺は暗礁が多くて、海難事故が多かったから、漁民たちが恐れてむやみに近付かなかったって話だろ？」

description: 裁判をも辞さない becomes not withdrawing from the trial, implying proceedings already underway.
sourceReading: The other side appears willing to go to court.

units.text: "......Overall, how do you feel about the situation?" "That is, well, ......it seems one thing is not favorable.  It seems the other party doesn't plan to withdraw from the trial at all."
units.note: Both still describe refusing to withdraw from a trial rather than willingness to take the dispute to court.
units.japanese: 「それがその、……ひとつ芳しくないようでして。先方は裁判をも辞さないつもりのようです。」

units.text: "Well, uhhh, ...there does seem to be one unfortunate matter. It appears the other party has no intentions of withdrawing from the trial."
units.note: Both still describe refusing to withdraw from a trial rather than willingness to take the dispute to court.
units.japanese: 「それがその、……ひとつ芳しくないようでして。先方は裁判をも辞さないつもりのようです」

units.text: "Well, I'm afraid......it seems it is not all that favorable. It seems they have no plans of withdrawing from the trial."
units.note: Both still describe refusing to withdraw from a trial rather than willingness to take the dispute to court.
units.japanese: 「それがその、……ひとつ芳しくないようでして。先方は裁判をも辞さないつもりのようです」

description: English says “When we knew it would become like this, we started,” reversing the counterfactual regret.
sourceReading: Had he known this would happen, he would not have started diversification.

units.text: "When we knew it would become like this, we started the diversifying, didn't we...!" "The calculations were that we could escape the capital crisis if we were able to endure for three years.  ...It can't be, to be stabbed here..., really, we're in no position for that...!"
units.note: Both restore counterfactual regret about diversification; UP colloquial if we’d have known does not reverse its meaning.
units.japanese: 「こんなことになるってわかってたら、多角化なんて始めんじゃなかったぜ…。」
candidates: knew it would become like this, we started

description: 数百万＄ becomes several million without a currency, in a Japanese company context.
sourceReading: They urgently need a sponsor capable of providing several million dollars.

units.text: "Stop that.  Do I look like that kind of man?  The contents of my wallet are all exposed to you guys, alright?  The account books over there show all that our company has." "In that case, ......we need to raise money.  We need a sponsor who can draw in several million for us as soon as possible." "......President!  Couldn't something be worked out with one of your associates...?!"
units.note: MG omits the explicitly written dollar currency; UP restores dollars.
units.japanese: 「なら、……金策が必要です。数百万＄単位を引っ張れるスポンサーが、大至急必要です。」

units.text: "In that case, ...we need to raise money. We need a sponsor who can draw in several million for us as soon as possible."
units.note: MG omits the explicitly written dollar currency; UP restores dollars.
units.japanese: 「なら、……金策が必要です。数百万＄単位を引っ張れるスポンサーが、大至急必要です」

description: ゲンコツ一発 loses the punch in favor of at once; お隠れになる, euphemistic death with Father as subject, becomes Rudolf hiding himself.
sourceReading: He would accept a dozen punches from Father if each bought a ten-million loan; otherwise he wishes Father would promptly pass away, then condemns his own dependence and inheritance-seeking.

units.text: ".........If I could borrow ten million at once by prostrating myself before Father, I'd do it a dozen times, but...  If I can't, I better hurry and start to hide myself.  .........I've always depended severily on his financial support, and now I'm going for the inheritance.  ............I'm going to hell.  ...I guess Father won't want to meet me like this......"
units.note: Both restore punches as the price of borrowing and Father’s death as the inheritance alternative.
units.japanese: 「………親父に土下座して、ゲンコツ一発で一千万借りられるなら、１ダースくらいもらっときてぇところなんだがな…。さもなきゃ、とっととお隠れになってくれりゃあいいんだが。………さんざんスネをかじって、今度は遺産目当てか。…………俺は地獄行きだな。…そりゃあ、こんな俺に親父も会いたくはないだろうよ……。」

description: English makes the secretary’s office the call destination and omits the immediate ringing.
sourceReading: The executive instructs the secretary’s office to connect the outside call; Rudolf’s phone immediately rings.

units.text: "......Looks like we can't fool 'em after all.  Ahaha...  Please, transfer it here." "Understood.  Immediately." The executive ordered that the external line be transferred to the secretarial office.
units.note: MG fixes immediate ringing but retains the secretarial office as destination at preceding row 535. UP restores both instruction recipient and immediate ringing. Removed duplicate paired finding from preceding receipt; this is the original WH parent.
units.japanese: 幹部は秘書室に外線をつなぐよう指示する。すぐに留弗夫の前の電話が鳴り響いた。

units.text: The executive ordered that the external line be transferred to the secretarial office. At once, the phone in front of Rudolf rang.
units.note: MG fixes immediate ringing but retains the secretarial office as destination at preceding row 535. UP restores both instruction recipient and immediate ringing. Removed duplicate paired finding from preceding receipt; this is the original WH parent.
units.japanese:
幹部は秘書室に外線をつなぐよう指示する。
すぐに留弗夫の前の電話が鳴り響いた。

description: お前に掛かれば means when subjected to Nanjo’s interpretation; “hits you” misreads the idiom.
sourceReading: Even a researched secret ritual gets called gambling when interpreted by someone unversed in magic, Kinzo complains.

units.text: "Hmph.........I see.  If the secret ritual I devoted my research to hits you who is not proficient at magic as well, would you call it a gamble?  Whatever."
units.note: Both restore Nanjo interpreting/branding the ritual a gamble instead of an event hitting him.
units.japanese: 「ふ…。……なるほど。研究を尽くした秘術の儀式も、魔法に長けぬお前に掛かれば博打呼ばわりか。まぁいい。」

description: この部屋で研究に没頭すれば describes how immersion makes six years pass quickly. English says these years passed “since you began,” assigning a research-start relation.
sourceReading: For someone immersed in research here, six years must seem brief.

units.text: "I guess these six years went by in a blink of an eye to you since you began immersing yourself in your research in this room..."
units.note: Both relate quick passage of six years to immersion in research rather than dating research commencement.
units.japanese: 「金蔵さんにとっての６年など、この部屋で研究に没頭すればあっという間のことでしょうからな…。」

description: 淡白な表情 describes a restrained or emotionally muted expression, not a candid one.
sourceReading: Nanjo looks at the witch’s understated expression, which does not clearly disclose happiness or sadness, then at the leaden sky.

units.text: Nanjo stared at the witch of the portrait, who held a candid facial expression, unable to decide whether she was smiling or sad, and he gazed up at the lead-colored sky......
units.note: MG impassive restores the muted expression; UP candid retains the false characterization.
units.japanese: 南條は、笑っているのか、悲しんでいるのかすらも量れない淡白な表情を浮かべる肖像画の魔女を見やり、鉛色の空を見上げるのだった……。

units.text: After a glance at the witch of the portrait, and her candid expression which he could not place as happy or sad, Nanjo gazed up at the leaden sky......
units.note: MG impassive restores the muted expression; UP candid retains the false characterization.
units.japanese: 南條は、笑っているのか、悲しんでいるのかすらも量れない淡白な表情を浮かべる肖像画の魔女を見やり、鉛色の空を見上げるのだった……。

description: 目は合わせない becomes “couldn’t make his eyes meet hers,” and 相手にもしないという意味ではない becomes “didn’t mean he wasn’t a match for her.” This changes voluntary avoidance and engagement into inability and competitive competence.
sourceReading: He does not meet her eyes, but this does not mean he refuses to engage her: it is his determination not to fall for her schemes and to fight.

units.text: He just couldn't make his eyes meet hers.  But that didn't mean he wasn't a match for her. ...It signified his plain determination to never be taken in by the artifices of this bastard. It was an expression of his powerful determination to fight.
units.note: Both restore voluntary avoidance of eye contact and continued engagement in the contest.
units.japanese:
目は合わせない。でもそれは相手にもしないという意味ではない。
…貴様の術策には決して乗らないという明白な決意。
candidates: couldn't make his eyes meet hers
didn't mean he wasn't a match

description: After asserting he cannot lose while withholding belief, Battler concludes the game is made so his opponent cannot win. English instead concludes “I can’t defeat you.”
sourceReading: His continued refusal to believe prevents his defeat, hence prevents her victory; she replies she can repeat the game until he concedes.

units.text: "............Whatever moves you come at me with, I won't believe you!  ...As long as I stand my ground on that point, I won't lose.  And that's that.  This game was made so that I can't defeat you, right...?"
units.note: Both correctly conclude that Beatrice cannot win under Battler’s refusal strategy; neither reverses this to Battler being unable to defeat her.
units.japanese: 「…………お前がどんな手で来ようが、俺はお前を信じない！　…その一点を俺が貫き通す限り、俺に負けはない。ってことはだ。このゲームはお前に勝てないように出来てるぜ…？」

description: そんなに可哀想なら面倒を見てあげればいい invites Maria to care for the rose if she feels so sorry for it. “Everything would be fine if they looked over this poor thing” changes the personal invitation to a collective action and an assurance of outcome.
sourceReading: George suggests that if she feels so sorry for it, she can look after it, then marks it with a candy wrapper and restores her mood.

units.text: In the midst of all this, there was a single unhealthy rose, and Maria became overwhelmed with dejection at its state. But George used his quick wits, and, saying everything would be fine if they looked over this poor thing, marked it with a candy wrapper, and immediately restored Maria's good mood.
units.note: MG retains collective they and assurance everything would be fine; UP restores individual invitation to Maria to care for the rose.
units.japanese: でも、譲治が機転を利かし、そんなに可哀想なら面倒を見てあげればいいと飴玉の包み紙で目印を付けてあげると、すぐに機嫌を直した。
candidates: everything would be fine if they looked over this poor thing

units.text: In the midst of all this, there was a single unhealthy rose, and Maria became overwhelmed with dejection at its condition. But George used his quick wits, and, saying that everything would be fine if they took care of this poor thing, marked it with a candy wrapper and immediately restored Maria's good mood.
units.note: MG retains collective they and assurance everything would be fine; UP restores individual invitation to Maria to care for the rose.
units.japanese: その中に一輪、枯れ掛けた薔薇があり、真里亞が感傷に囚われ消沈してしまう。でも、譲治が機転を利かし、そんなに可哀想なら面倒を見てあげればいいと飴玉の包み紙で目印を付けてあげると、すぐに機嫌を直した。

description: The English retains the naming of the solar death day as New Year’s Eve/Samhain but drops お祝いした, that they celebrated it.
sourceReading: In Maria’s account, the sun dies at October’s end and revives at winter solstice; people name the death day Samhain/New Year’s Eve and celebrate it.

units.text: "Yes.  So they thought that at the end of October, the sun died, rested its body in the land of the dead, and then revived again at the winter solstice.  Then, they called the day that the sun ended its one year lifespan and died New Year's Eve, or Samhain."
units.note: Both now explicitly include celebration of the solar death day.
units.japanese: 「うん。だから彼らは、１０月の最後に太陽は死に、死の国で体を休めて、冬至の日に再び蘇ると考えたの。それで、太陽が一年の生涯を終えて死ぬその日を大晦日、サヴィンと呼んで、お祝いしたの。」

description: 魔女集会、サバト names the gathering in apposition; English makes Sabbath a day on which the gathering is held.
sourceReading: Witches held a witch gathering, a sabbat, during that season.

units.text: "Uu-!  And you know, the witches, they hold a witch assembly during that time, on the Sabbath.  The witches thank the spirits that give out blessings of prosperity, and reward them."
units.note: Both identify Sabbath/Sabbat as the gathering’s name, not a separate day on which it is held. UP coven terminology is not independently certified here.
units.japanese: 「うー！　そしてね、魔女たちはね、その時期に魔女集会、サバトを開いたの。魔女たちは豊かな恵みをもたらしてくれた精霊たちに感謝し、労ったの。」

description: English extends shared “we” to learning spells and circles and rune secrets, making Beatrice a fellow learner rather than the envisaged teacher.
sourceReading: Maria imagines singing with Beatrice, learning spells, circles and rune secrets from her, and being made a proper witch.

units.text: "And then, we'll eat marshmallow candies together, and she'll bring Maria to the Golden Land with her!  We'll sing magical songs together, learn magic spells together, learn how to draw magic circles together!  And then, we'll learn the secrets of runes, and Maria will become a great witch really, really quickly!"
units.note: MG we learn covers spells, circles and runes. UP still says we learn for spells and circles, but changes rune learning to I; singing together is supported in both.
units.japanese: 「そしてね、一緒にマシュマロお菓子食べて、真里亞も黄金郷に連れてってもらうの！　一緒に魔法のお唄を歌って、魔法の呪文を習って、魔法陣の書き方を習うの！　そしてね、ルーンの秘密を習って、早く早く真里亞を立派な魔女にしてもらうの！」

units.text: "And then, we'll eat marshmallow candies together, and she'll bring me to the Golden Land with her! We'll sing magical songs together, learn magic spells together, learn how to draw magic circles together! And then, we'll learn the secrets of runes, and I'll become a great witch really, really quickly!"
units.note: MG we learn covers spells, circles and runes. UP still says we learn for spells and circles, but changes rune learning to I; singing together is supported in both.
units.japanese: 「そしてね、一緒にマシュマロお菓子食べて、真里亞も黄金郷に連れてってもらうの！　一緒に魔法のお唄を歌って、魔法の呪文を習って、魔法陣の書き方を習うの！　そしてね、ルーンの秘密を習って、早く早く真里亞を立派な魔女にしてもらうの！」

units.text: "And then, we'll eat the marshmallow candies together, and she'll take me to the Golden Land with her! We'll sing magical songs together, learn magic spells together, learn how to draw magic circles together! And then I'm going to learn the secrets of runes, and become a great witch really, really quickly!"
units.note: MG we learn covers spells, circles and runes. UP still says we learn for spells and circles, but changes rune learning to I; singing together is supported in both.
units.japanese: 「そしてね、一緒にマシュマロお菓子食べて、真里亞も黄金郷に連れてってもらうの！　一緒に魔法のお唄を歌って、魔法の呪文を習って、魔法陣の書き方を習うの！　そしてね、ルーンの秘密を習って、早く早く真里亞を立派な魔女にしてもらうの！」

description: English substitutes mother buying something fun for her, and has malformed “supposed to proof.” This loses the shared activity that made any sweet acceptable earlier.
sourceReading: The sweet is proof of the memory of shopping happily with mother, brief though it was.

units.text: To Maria, it was supposed to proof of her memory of that brief span of time when her mother had bought something fun for her... But the fact of the matter was that she saw her mother trampling on it. ...It was as though a brand had been pushed against Maria's eyes, leaving a mark that couldn't be erased...
units.note: MG fixes proof grammar but still substitutes mother buying something fun for the shared enjoyable shopping memory. UP restores shopping together and proof grammar.
units.japanese: 真里亞にとってそれは、束の間とはいえ、母と楽しく買い物をした記憶の証であったはず…。

units.text: To Maria, it was supposed to be proof of a memory...of a brief span of time when her mother had bought something fun for her... But now, that same mother was grinding it into the ground right in front of her. ...It was as though a brand had been pushed into Maria's eyes, leaving a mark that could never be erased...
units.note: MG fixes proof grammar but still substitutes mother buying something fun for the shared enjoyable shopping memory. UP restores shopping together and proof grammar.
units.japanese:
真里亞にとってそれは、束の間とはいえ、母と楽しく買い物をした記憶の証であったはず…。それが他でもない母に踏みにじられる光景。
…それが真里亞の瞳に、消せない焼きごてを押し当てる…。

description: あんたがそんなだから repeats Rosa’s causal blaming formula, “because you are like this.” English substitutes “That’s what you are,” turning the unfinished explanation into a categorical identification.
sourceReading: While denouncing the candy, Rosa repeats that it is because Maria is like this, echoing her earlier blaming of Maria for friendlessness and the endless father trip.

units.text: That's what you are, that's what you are!!  Disgusting disgusting disgusting!!!"
units.note: MG restores because you are like that. UP this is why restores causal form but leaves the repeated blame of Maria’s way of being implicit rather than explicit.
units.japanese: あんたがそんなだからッ、あんたがそんなだからッ！！

units.text: "This is why, you see?! This is why!! Disgusting disgusting disgusting!!!"
units.note: MG restores because you are like that. UP this is why restores causal form but leaves the repeated blame of Maria’s way of being implicit rather than explicit.
units.japanese: 「あんたがそんなんだからッ、あんたがそんなんだからッ！！　気持ち悪い気持ち悪い気持ち悪い！！！」

description: その程度の器にはその程度のが入り込む becomes “Maria can handle that much,” erasing the vessel/entrant account following the bad-witch interpretation.
sourceReading: A vessel of that caliber admits something of that caliber; Maria says she is fine.

units.text: "......It can't be helped.  Maria can handle that much.  Maria is just fine.  Kihihihihihihihihihi......"
units.note: Both restore vessel and entering entity rather than Maria’s personal capacity to withstand abuse.
units.japanese: 「……仕方ないよ。その程度の器にはその程度のが入り込む。…真里亞は全然平気だよ。きひひひひひひひひひ……。」

description: 今日だって会って一緒に遊ぶよ becomes “Why don’t we meet her today and play?” The next turn likewise turns her planned play and study into “Let’s” invitations.
sourceReading: Maria says she is Beatrice’s friend and will meet and play with her today.

units.text: "Kihihihihi...  You know, Maria is friends with Beatrice.  Why don't we meet her today and play?  Kihihihihihihihihi..."
units.note: Both restore Maria’s declared plan to meet/play/study rather than invitations for Kanon to join her.
units.japanese: 「きひひひひ…。真里亞はね、ベアトリーチェとお友達なの。今日だって会って一緒に遊ぶよ？　きひひひひひひひひ…。」
candidates: don't we meet her today and play

description: お迎え, euphemistic death, becomes “I may not even be able to approach,” assigning the fear to Nanjo.
sourceReading: Nanjo jokes that even death’s arrival may fear Kinzo’s force of spirit and be unable to approach.

units.text: ".........For a normal patient, that would probably be the case.  But Kinzo-san has extraordinary willpower.  ...I may not even be able to approach, in fear of that willpower..."
units.note: Both restore Death/reaper as the one too afraid to approach; no claim of Nanjo avoiding Kinzo.
units.japanese: 「………並の患者ならそうでしょうがな。金蔵さんは並外れた気力をお持ちです。…あの気迫に、お迎えも恐れて近寄れないのかもしれませんな…。」

description: その姿をぜひ見てもらいたい becomes “how much you want to see him,” losing who observes whom and the sting of conspicuous filial display.
sourceReading: Krauss sarcastically says he understands Eva wanting Father to witness her newly filial behavior after the prognosis.

units.text: "That's right.  Haven't you quickly become respectful of Father now that his remaining life has been announced, Eva?  ...I see, it isn't as though I can't understand how much you want to see him.  ......Hmph."
units.note: Both still make the phrase Eva wanting to see Father rather than wanting Father to see her conspicuous filial behavior; sarcasm survives but viewing direction does not.
units.japanese: 「その通りだな。絵羽は親父殿が余命を宣告されてから急に親孝行をするようになったじゃないか。…なるほど、その姿をぜひ見てもらいたいという気持ちも、わからなくない。

units.text: "Indeed. Look how quickly you've grown to respect Father, now that you know how much longer he has to live. ...Yes, I believe I do understand why you want to see him so much. ...Hmph."
units.note: Both still make the phrase Eva wanting to see Father rather than wanting Father to see her conspicuous filial behavior; sarcasm survives but viewing direction does not.
units.japanese: 「その通りだな。絵羽は親父殿が余命を宣告されてから急に親孝行をするようになったじゃないか。…なるほど、その姿をぜひ見てもらいたいという気持ちも、わからなくない。……ふ」

units.text: "That's right. Eva, how suddenly you've become respectful to Father since he was told how long he has left. ...Yes, I can just about understand why you might be desperate to see him. ......Hmph."
units.note: Both still make the phrase Eva wanting to see Father rather than wanting Father to see her conspicuous filial behavior; sarcasm survives but viewing direction does not.
units.japanese: 「その通りだな。絵羽は親父殿が余命を宣告されてから急に親孝行をするようになったじゃないか。…なるほど、その姿をぜひ見てもらいたいという気持ちも、わからなくない。……ふ」

description: 忌憚ない becomes “modestly,” suggesting restraint instead of candor.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi urges making precious annual meeting time count with frank, unreserved discussion.

units.text: "Yep!  Just as Rudolf-kun says.  ......We can only gather our faces here once a year.  We must take this precious time seriously and talk together modestly."
units.note: Both restore candid/frank discussion rather than modest restraint.
units.japanese: ……わしらが全員顔を揃えるのは年に一度しかない。貴重な時間を大事にし、忌憚ない話し合いをせんといかん。」

description: 挨拶くらいはさせてほしい becomes wishing he would “come to greet us,” adding Father’s movement toward them.
sourceReading: Rudolf wishes they could at least be allowed to greet Father.

units.text: "...Although if he's that energetic, I wish he'd at least come to greet us.  ...Isn't the point of the family conference to come and see Father's face?  Now I don't know why we came."
units.note: MG still asks Father to come greet them. UP restores allowing them to greet him without requiring his movement.
units.japanese: 「…そこまで元気なら、せめて挨拶くらいはさせてほしいもんなんだがな。…親族会議ってのは親父の顔を見に来たって意味なんだぜ？　これじゃあ、何のために来たのかわからねぇぜ。」

units.text: "...Though, if he's got that much spunk, I wish he'd at least come to greet us. ...Isn't the whole point of this family conference to come and see Dad's face? I'm not even sure why we came now."
units.note: MG still asks Father to come greet them. UP restores allowing them to greet him without requiring his movement.
units.japanese: 「…そこまで元気なら、せめて挨拶くらいはさせてほしいもんなんだがな。…親族会議ってのは親父の顔を見に来たって意味なんだぜ？　これじゃあ、何のために来たのかわからねぇぜ」

description: WH replaces pretending to be on friendly terms with playing a part in a conspiracy.
sourceReading: The narrator suggests Rosa cannot bring herself to feign cordiality now that everyone is here for the sordid inheritance struggle.

units.text: It seemed that Rosa hadn't been able to get along just on the surface. ...They had come here to fight bloodily and dirtily, each trying to steal the inheritance. Maybe by now she didn't want to play a part in a conspiracy.
units.note: MG restores pretending to be chummy; UP retains fellow conspirators instead of superficial friendliness.
units.japanese: 今更馴れ合いのふりなどしたくないのだろう。

units.text: It seemed that Rosa hadn't been able to keep up the charade of amicability. ...They had come here to fight bloodily and dirtily, each trying to steal the inheritance from the others. She probably didn't want to pretend to be fellow conspirators at this stage.
units.note: MG restores pretending to be chummy; UP retains fellow conspirators instead of superficial friendliness.
units.japanese: 楼座は、上辺だけ調子を合わせることができなかったらしい。…遺産の奪い合いという血生臭く、かつ泥臭い議論のためにここに訪れているのだ。今更馴れ合いのふりなどしたくないのだろう。

description: The specific prediction about Maria becomes a generic claim that children who already have rich hearts grow.
sourceReading: Because Maria has such an affectionate mother, Kyrie says she will grow into a child with a rich inner life. Rosa cannot tell how this praise is intended.

units.text: "Yes.  It's because she has such an affectionate mother.  Kids with a rich heart grow."
units.note: Both restore a prediction specifically about Maria growing into a rich-hearted girl, not a generic claim about already rich-hearted children.
units.japanese: 「えぇ。こんなにも愛情たっぷりなお母さんと一緒なんですもの。心の豊かな子に成長しますよ。」

description: WH explicitly names Mama as the victim of the scary witch’s pinching.
sourceReading: Maria says she endured being pinched by the scary witch and waited without crying for Mama to return. Her account separates the abusive witch from the returning mother.

units.text: "...Uu-.  Mama, welcome back.........Maria waited a long time for Mama to come back.  ...Mama was pinched by the scary witch, but Maria held out, waited for Mama to come back without crying..."
units.note: MG pinched me and UP omitted-subject got pinched remove the unsupported assignment of Mama as the victim. Maria’s waiting and bad-witch account remain.
units.japanese: 「…うー。ママ、お帰り…。……真里亞、ママが帰ってくるの、ずっと待ってた。…怖い魔女につねられたけど、我慢してママが帰ってくるの、泣かずに待ってた…。」

description: WH says sunshine would evaporate all their cares and make them feel able to start anew.
sourceReading: The narrator imagines that sunshine might have made the scene suggest all their estrangement had dissolved and a fresh beginning lay ahead. The actual storm makes the scene sad instead.

units.text: If only the brilliant sun had been shining on the two of them, all of their cares would have evaporated, and they would have felt like they could begin anew.
units.note: Both still describe all cares evaporating rather than their mutual emotional tension dissolving. MG might preserves some tentativeness; UP would have felt further strengthens the speculative possibility. Original parent reused.
units.japanese: せめて二人を、燦々とした太陽が照らしていたなら、二人のわだかまりが全て解け、これからのやり直しを感じさせたかもしれない。

units.text: If only the brilliant sun had been shining on the two of them, all of their cares would have evaporated, and it might've felt like they could begin anew.
units.note: Both still describe all cares evaporating rather than their mutual emotional tension dissolving. MG might preserves some tentativeness; UP would have felt further strengthens the speculative possibility. Original parent reused.
units.japanese: せめて二人を、燦々とした太陽が照らしていたなら、二人のわだかまりが全て解け、これからのやり直しを感じさせたかもしれない。

description: 唯一の灯り is translated as “this unique light,” substituting distinctiveness for the absence of any other light.
sourceReading: In Beatrice’s explanation, the lantern is the sole light of the man wandering purgatory, barred from heaven and hell.

units.text: "Hmm, Happy Halloween.  Hoh, for me?  How truly lovely that this unique light, of a man lost in the darkness of purgatory, unable to go to heaven or hell, would be made into a candy like this."
units.note: MG lonely light removes distinctiveness but does not explicitly restore the only-light restriction. UP single and only restores it.
units.japanese: 「うむ、ハッピーハロウィン。ほぅ、これを妾にとな？　天国にも地獄にも行けず、煉獄の闇にて彷徨う男の唯一の灯りも、こうして菓子となれば実に可愛らしいことよ。」

units.text: "Indeed, <Happy Halloween>. Hoh, is this for me? How truly adorable, that a candy would be made out of this, the lonely light of a man lost in the darkness of Purgatory, unable to go to heaven or hell."
units.note: MG lonely light removes distinctiveness but does not explicitly restore the only-light restriction. UP single and only restores it.
units.japanese: 「うむ、ハッピーハロウィン。ほぅ、これを妾にとな？　天国にも地獄にも行けず、煉獄の闇にて彷徨う男の唯一の灯りも、こうして菓子となれば実に可愛らしいことよ」

description: “the witches hand” lacks the singular possessive apostrophe.
sourceReading: The butterflies gather to the one witch’s raised hand.

units.text: The sweet which had been thrown into the air, ......burst into a gold color..., no, that wasn't it.  Those were golden butterflies. It scattered into several golden butterflies, ...and they began to gather at the witches hand, which was held up to the sky. And as she did, .........unbelievably, .........it returned to its beautiful original form, just like the time it had been bought... Only Rosa and the witch had watched that scene.
units.note: Both now use witch’s singular possessive apostrophe correctly.
units.japanese: 何匹もの黄金の蝶に散り、…それは宙に手をかざす魔女の手に集まっていく。

description: 左右しかねない becomes “couldn’t help but influence,” strengthening possible influence into unavoidable influence.
