sourceReading: If Kyrie’s guess is right, this witch probably holds a major key concerning Rudolf’s chief interest and capable of affecting tonight’s family conference.

units.text: ...But if Kyrie's imagination was correct, ......this "witch" probably held a huge key to what her own husband was most interested in, and something that couldn't help but influence tonight's family conference...
units.note: MG retains unavoidable influence. UP removes inevitability but great chance still adds a probability strength not fixed by 左右しかねない, could affect the outcome.
units.japanese: …しかし、もし霧江の想像が当たっているならば、……この「魔女」は恐らく、自分の夫の最大の関心事について、そして今夜の親族会議を左右しかねない、大きな鍵を握っているのだ…。

units.text: ...But if Kyrie's guesses were correct, ...this "witch" probably held a vital key to what her own husband was most interested in, something that couldn't help but influence tonight's family conference...
units.note: MG retains unavoidable influence. UP removes inevitability but great chance still adds a probability strength not fixed by 左右しかねない, could affect the outcome.
units.japanese: …しかし、もし霧江の想像が当たっているならば、……この「魔女」は恐らく、自分の夫の最大の関心事について、そして今夜の親族会議を左右しかねない、大きな鍵を握っているのだ…。

units.text: ...But if Kyrie's imagination was correct, ......this "witch" likely held a huge key to what her own husband was most interested in, and one that stood a great chance of influencing tonight's family conference...
units.note: MG retains unavoidable influence. UP removes inevitability but great chance still adds a probability strength not fixed by 左右しかねない, could affect the outcome.
units.japanese: …しかし、もし霧江の想像が当たっているならば、……この「魔女」は恐らく、自分の夫の最大の関心事について、そして今夜の親族会議を左右しかねない、大きな鍵を握っているのだ…。

description: “Even until he literally became a ghost” supplies becoming a ghost as an endpoint, whereas 亡霊となっても permits the research to continue even after that transformation.
sourceReading: Genji predicts that Kinzo would probably keep researching until reunion with Beatrice, even if he literally became a ghost.

units.text: "......He would probably continue his research until the day he could meet you again, even until he literally became a ghost."
units.note: Both now allow research to continue even after becoming a ghost, until reunion, rather than making becoming a ghost the endpoint.
units.japanese: 「……貴方様と再びお会いする日までは、恐らく、文字通り亡霊となっても研究を続けられるでしょう。」
candidates: until he literally became a ghost

description: 美食 becomes “Gourmets,” changing enjoyment of fine food into people who enjoy it.
sourceReading: Beatrice places fine dining among the pillars of pleasure in human life and calls continued enjoyment of it a secret to avoiding boredom across a millennium.

units.text: "...There's nothing better than being skilled at cooking.  ...Gourmets form the three pillars of pleasure for living in the human world.  Not missing out on this is the secret to not getting bored after a thousand years.  ...*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*."
units.note: Both restore fine food rather than gourmets as people. UP explicitly identifies one of three pillars; MG completes the three pillars remains understandable as completing the triad.
units.japanese: 「…料理の腕が良きことは何にも勝るものよ。…美食は人の世で生きる快楽の三柱を成す。千年を飽きぬにはこれを欠かぬが秘訣よ。…くっくくくくくくく。」

description: “Witches are used like scissors” loses the idiom’s claim that the result depends on skillful use.
sourceReading: The adapted scissors proverb says even a witch can be useful depending on how one uses her, followed by Solomon as a successful example.

units.text: Be that as it may, witches are used like scissors.  ...Sometimes, there are people like King Solomon who succeed in great exploits."
units.note: MG explicitly restores dependence on how witches/scissors are used. UP can be put to use restores utility but not the dependence on manner of use, and adds blunt.
units.japanese: されど、魔女と鋏は使いようだ。…ソロモン王のように、偉業を成し遂げる者も時にはおる。」

units.text: "Be that as it may, witches, like blunt scissors, can be put to use. ...Sometimes, there are people like King Solomon who succeed in great exploits."
units.note: MG explicitly restores dependence on how witches/scissors are used. UP can be put to use restores utility but not the dependence on manner of use, and adds blunt.
units.japanese: 「されど、魔女と鋏は使いようだ。…ソロモン王のように、偉業を成し遂げる者も時にはおる」

description: WH says one does not meet a good fate “such as those described in fairy tales,” attaching the tale comparison to good fates.
sourceReading: In most cases people come to no good, as fairy tales recount; Beatrice contrasts those warnings with the occasional Solomon-like success.

units.text: ".........However, in most cases, one does not meet with a good fate such as those described in fairy tales, right?  *cackle*cackle*...!  .........But Kinzo is crafty.  He has taken in even the interest I am collecting for his own ceremony.  Is he an absurd magician to surpass even me?  ......Or else a fool possessed by madness?  ...Interesting.  Truly interesting...!"
units.note: MG correctly attaches fairy-tale comparison to cruel outcomes. UP still attaches it to good fates, reversing what fairy tales are said to describe.
units.japanese: 「………もっとも、多くの場合は、童話が語るようにロクな目には遭わんがな？　くっくっくっく…！　………しかし金蔵も食えぬ。妾の利子の取立てすらも、自らの儀式に取り込みおった。妾をも超える、とてつもない大魔術師か。……さもなければ狂気に憑り付かれたただの痴れ者か。…面白い。実に面白い…！」
candidates: good fate such as those described in fairy tales

units.text: ".........In most cases, one does not meet with a good fate such as those described in fairy tales, of course? *cackle*cackle*...! .........But Kinzo is crafty. He has incorporated even my collection of interest into his own ritual."
units.note: MG correctly attaches fairy-tale comparison to cruel outcomes. UP still attaches it to good fates, reversing what fairy tales are said to describe.
units.japanese: 「………もっとも、多くの場合は、童話が語るようにロクな目に遭わんがな？　くっくっくっく…！　………しかし金蔵も食えぬ。妾の利子の取立てすらも、自らの儀式に取り込みおった」
candidates: good fate such as those described in fairy tales

description: “Why don’t you ... ask Kinzo” replaces 聞いていよう, an expectation that Kanon has already heard from Kinzo.
sourceReading: As Kinzo’s furniture, Kanon should already have heard about the return of everything to the Golden Land.

units.text: "...Kanon.  Why don't you, as furniture, ask Kinzo about it?  .........The day when everything will be returned to the Golden Land...has come.
units.note: Both restore the expectation that Kanon has already heard from Kinzo rather than directing him to ask in future.
units.japanese: 「…嘉音。家具である貴様なら金蔵から聞いていよう。………全てを、黄金郷へ返す日が、やって来たのだ。

description: “It’s well known that I take this position” changes being somewhat renowned in this field into public knowledge of an attitude.
sourceReading: Beatrice boasts of her reputation for the cruel culinary treatment of human destinies, to the point of attracting visiting spectators.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*!  It's well known that I take this position, right?  ......So much that rare guests come from far away to see my skill at cooking.  ...Heheheheh, even if I say that, it may be something that mere furniture can't understand."
units.note: Both restore being somewhat famous in the field rather than public knowledge of an attitude.
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくく！　妾は、この方面にかけては、ちと知られていてな？　……妾の料理の腕を見に、時には遠方から珍客が見物に来ることすらあるくらいよ。…ふっふふふふ、言っても家具如きには理解できぬか。」
candidates: It's well known that I take this position

description: “Whenever some harm befell them” omits 加える, which assigns the infliction of harm to the witch.
sourceReading: Kanon understands her as a terrifying being who treats human destinies as spectacles and amuses herself by doing harm.

units.text: Kanon wasn't able to understand what the witch was saying. However, he realized well enough that this was a terrifying being who treated the fate of humans as a show, enjoying it whenever some harm befell them.
units.note: MG harm befell still obscures the witch inflicting it; UP doing them harm restores agency.
units.japanese: しかし、人間たちの運命をまるで見世物のように扱い、何かの危害を加えることで面白がっている恐ろしい存在であることは充分に理解できた。

units.text: Kanon couldn't understand what the witch was saying. However, he fully realized that this was a terrifying being who treated the fate of humans as a show, enjoying it whenever some harm befell them.
units.note: MG harm befell still obscures the witch inflicting it; UP doing them harm restores agency.
units.japanese: 嘉音には、魔女が何を言っているのか理解できない。しかし、人間たちの運命をまるで見世物のように扱い、何かの危害を加えることで面白がっている恐ろしい存在であることは充分に理解できた。

description: “A being for which they overflowed with affection” assigns overflowing affection to furniture instead of describing her as overflowing with compassion.
sourceReading: From the furniture’s standpoint, the witch who comes to release them can also be a compassionate being.

units.text: ......However, furniture had no soul or life, much less a fate.  Pitiful "furniture" did nothing but serve until the day they were released from the real world. ...To furniture like that, the witch, who had appeared to release them from everything, was a being for which they overflowed with affection...
units.note: MG received with overflowing affection retains furniture’s affection rather than witch’s compassion; UP overflowing mercy restores the attribute.
units.japanese: …そんな家具たちにとって、全てから解放するために現れた魔女は慈しみ溢れる存在でもある…。

units.text: ...However, furniture has no soul or life, much less a fate. Pitiful "furniture" does nothing but serve until the day they're released from the real world. ...To furniture like that, the witch, who had come to release them from everything, was a being to be received with overflowing affection...
units.note: MG received with overflowing affection retains furniture’s affection rather than witch’s compassion; UP overflowing mercy restores the attribute.
units.japanese: ……しかし、家具には魂も人生も、ましてや運命もない。現世から解放される日まで使役されるだけの哀れな「家具」。…そんな家具たちにとって、全てから解放するために現れた魔女は慈しみ溢れる存在でもある…。

description: “What Jessica was thinking of” makes Jessica the thinker rather than the object of Kanon’s forbidden feelings.
sourceReading: Kanon believes that, as furniture, he is not permitted to think romantically of Jessica, and resents his inconsistency after condemning Shannon’s relationship.

units.text: ......What Jessica was thinking of was not permitted for furniture.  Even though he had tried to realize that, and had found fault with Shannon's relationship, ......how could he still remember Jessica at a time like this. ......He felt a little shameful at his own naivety.  And to forget about Jessica, he turned his thoughts to Shannon.
units.note: Both restore Kanon thinking of Jessica rather than Jessica being the thinker.
units.japanese: ……朱志香を想うことは家具の身には許されぬこと。それを自覚し、紗音の交際を咎めたはずなのに、…このような時に朱志香を思い出すなんて。

description: “She must not” replaces the negative answer to whether release would be something Shannon could gladly accept.
sourceReading: Kanon concludes it would not be welcome: Shannon would retain attachments, causing suffering.

units.text: Could Shannon, ......accept something like that with pleasure? ......She must not. ...Shannon still had remaining regrets. ......That would probably become a great source of pain and torture for Shannon.
units.note: Both restore negative answer to whether Shannon can accept release gladly, not a prohibition directed at her.
units.japanese: ……ならない。

description: WH makes the day “give her emotions that she must not know.” The source has Shannon already possessing forbidden emotions when the long-awaited day arrives.
sourceReading: Her existing love will make the expected liberation intensely painful. Kanon thanks Beatrice for liberation while hating her for making it hard for Shannon to accept.

units.text: "......This day, ......that Shannon should have been waiting impatiently for, will probably force upon her very harsh thoughts, ......and give her emotions that she must not know.  .........I thank you for bringing me, ...us furniture the day of our release as a present."
units.note: MG still makes the day give Shannon forbidden emotions. UP distinguishes her having those emotions from the hard time forced upon her; preceding relationship explains their origin.
units.japanese: 「……紗音は、……待ちわびていたはずの日に、知ってはならない感情を持ち、……とても辛い思いを強いられるだろう。
candidates: give her emotions that she must not know

units.text: "......This day...that Shannon should have been waiting impatiently for...will probably be a harsh burden for her, ...giving her emotions that she must never experience. ......I thank you for granting me...us furniture the day of our release."
units.note: MG still makes the day give Shannon forbidden emotions. UP distinguishes her having those emotions from the hard time forced upon her; preceding relationship explains their origin.
units.japanese: 「……紗音は、……待ちわびていたはずの日に、知ってはならない感情を持ち、……とても辛い思いを強いられるだろう。………僕は、…僕たち家具を解放する日を手土産に訪れてくれたあなたに感謝する」

description: “Being released along with her love meant that she wouldn’t be invited” replaces the contrast between merciful invitation and cruel sacrifice with a causal claim about release with love.
sourceReading: Kanon sees Beatrice intending to torment Shannon and sacrifice her for the ritual, rather than invite her to the Golden Land as a compassionate liberation.

units.text: The witch planned to toy with Shannon, who had known the taste of love..., no, who she had taught the taste of love, as she killed her. Being released along with her love meant that she wouldn't be invited to the Golden Land, but would become a human sacrifice for an evil ceremony, after receiving the limits of torture and pain...!
units.note: Both restore merciful invitation versus cruel sacrifice contrast rather than causal release-with-love claim.
units.japanese: 慈しみのある解放として黄金郷に誘うのではなく、その為の生贄として、責め苦の限りを与え苦しめ抜き、邪悪な儀式の人柱にしようとしている…！
candidates: released along with her love meant that she wouldn't be invited

description: 控えんこともない becomes “I’ll surely hold back,” replacing a hedged concession with assurance.
sourceReading: If Kanon kneels, Beatrice says she might be willing to refrain from choosing Shannon as a sacrifice.

units.text: "What will you do, Kanon...?  If you kneel, I'll surely hold back from choosing Shannon as a sacrifice, okay?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!  I've wanted to make a toy like you surrender just once.  *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*, kuhihihihihihihihi!!"
units.note: MG might and UP may restore hedged willingness to spare Shannon, not a guarantee.
units.japanese: 「どうする、嘉音…？　跪けば、紗音を生贄に選ぶことを控えんこともないぞ？　くっくくくくくくくくくく！　お前のような玩具を、一度屈服させてみたかった。

description: 片膝 becomes “both knees.”
sourceReading: Kanon places one knee on the ground and kneels before the witch, then kisses her shoe.

units.text: ......Kanon, ...............chose to get down on both knees in front of the witch...
units.note: MG still says both knees; UP restores one knee and subsequent shoe contact.
units.japanese: ……嘉音は、……………片膝を付き、魔女の前に跪くことを選ぶ…。

units.text: ...Kanon......chose to get down on both knees in front of the witch...
units.note: MG still says both knees; UP restores one knee and subsequent shoe contact.
units.japanese: ……嘉音は、……………片膝を付き、魔女の前に跪くことを選ぶ…。

description: 態度デカそうにしてて becomes “overreacting that much.”
sourceReading: Jessica teases Battler for having looked so cocky despite being nervous.

units.text: "Tension?  Hehe, you call overreacting that much tension?"
units.note: MG freaking out retains inappropriate reaction reading. UP center of attention removes overreaction but incompletely conveys the arrogant/big-shot demeanor mocked by 態度デカそう.
units.japanese: 「緊張ぉ？　へへ、あんだけ態度デカそうにしてて緊張なんてしてたのかよ。」

units.text: "Tension? Heheh, you call freaking out like that "tension"?"
units.note: MG freaking out retains inappropriate reaction reading. UP center of attention removes overreaction but incompletely conveys the arrogant/big-shot demeanor mocked by 態度デカそう.
units.japanese: 「緊張ぉ？　へへ、あんだけ態度デカそうにしてて緊張なんてしてたのかよ」

units.text: "Tension? Heheh, you go around making yourself the center of attention and now you're saying you were tense?"
units.note: MG freaking out retains inappropriate reaction reading. UP center of attention removes overreaction but incompletely conveys the arrogant/big-shot demeanor mocked by 態度デカそう.
units.japanese: 「緊張ぉ？　へへ、あんだけ態度デカそうにしてて緊張なんてしてたのかよ」

description: “What I’m mean by saying that it’s not my turn now” is grammatically malformed.
sourceReading: Battler clarifies that he means it is not his turn yet, then excuses his confused thinking because he is sleepy.

units.text: ".........That's not what I mean.  What I'm mean by saying that it's not my turn now...  Kuaaaaaaaaaaah......  Sorry, my mind's a mess.  Give me a break......  Munyamunya......"
units.note: Both remove the malformed What I’m mean construction and state the not-my-turn clarification grammatically.
units.japanese: 「………そういう意味じゃねぇ。今は俺の出番じゃねぇって言いたいのさ…。くぁあああぁああぁぁぁ……。悪ぃな、眠くて思考がめちゃくちゃだ。勘弁してくれ……。むにゃむにゃ……。」
candidates: I'm mean by saying that it's not my turn now

description: “Can’t you just do what you want already?” makes the opening sound like an invitation or impatient permission rather than a complaint about what Beatrice is already doing.
sourceReading: Battler objects that she is already doing whatever she pleases and calls the scene absurd.

units.text: ".........Can't you just do what you want already?  ...What is this?  ......It's all screwed up...!!"
units.note: Both now complain about Beatrice already doing as she pleases, rather than inviting her to begin.
units.japanese: 「………もうやりたい放題じゃねぇかよ。…何だこりゃあよ。……滅茶苦茶じゃねぇか…！！」
candidates: Can't you just do what you want already

description: 王道 is rendered “short-cuts.”
sourceReading: Beatrice calls opening a path for the queen on the first move a standard or orthodox approach to chess.

units.text: "...The greatest basis upon which you deny me is simply because I was not laid out as a piece on the game board.  So doing this is nothing more than showing you the queen first, isn't it?  ...Isn't opening the road for the queen in the first move one of the short-cuts in chess?"
units.note: Both restore classic chess opening/play rather than shortcuts.
units.japanese: 「…そなたが妾を否定する最大の根拠は、単に妾が駒としてゲーム盤に並ばなかったからというだけのこと。ならばこうして、クイーンを先に指せばいいだけの話ではないか。…初手にてクイーンに道を開けるはチェスの王道ではないか。」

description: “When she came into the entrance hall” assigns the entrance movement to the visitor instead of Kyrie.
sourceReading: Kyrie reports having briefly greeted the woman when she herself stepped out into the entrance hall, then seeing her ascend with Genji.

units.text: "......Even I only greeted her quickly when she came into the entrance hall.  She looked like she was in her twenties.  I told her my name, but she didn't tell me hers.  ...She was being guided by Genji-san and I saw her go up to the second floor."
units.note: Both still assign entrance-hall movement to the visitor. Japanese describes Kyrie going briefly into the entrance hall and greeting her there; earlier scene establishes the visitor’s separate arrival but does not cure the reported-action subject change.
units.japanese: 「……私も、ちょっと玄関ホールに出た時に挨拶をしただけです。二十歳ちょっとくらいに見えたわ。私は名乗ったんだけど、彼女は名乗らなかった。…源次さんに案内されて、二階へ上って行くのを見たの。」

units.text: "...Even I only greeted her briefly when she came into the entrance hall. She looked like she was a bit over twenty. I told her my name, but she didn't tell me hers. ...She was being guided by Genji-san, and I saw her go up to the second floor."
units.note: Both still assign entrance-hall movement to the visitor. Japanese describes Kyrie going briefly into the entrance hall and greeting her there; earlier scene establishes the visitor’s separate arrival but does not cure the reported-action subject change.
units.japanese: 「……私も、ちょっと玄関ホールに出た時に挨拶をしただけです。二十歳ちょっとくらいに見えたわ。私は名乗ったんだけど、彼女は名乗らなかった。…源次さんに案内されて、二階へ上って行くのを見たの」

units.text: "......Even I only greeted her quickly when she came into the entrance hall. She looked like she was a little over twenty. I told her my name, but she didn't tell me hers. ...She was being guided by Genji‐san, and I saw her go up to the second floor."
units.note: Both still assign entrance-hall movement to the visitor. Japanese describes Kyrie going briefly into the entrance hall and greeting her there; earlier scene establishes the visitor’s separate arrival but does not cure the reported-action subject change.
units.japanese: 「……私も、ちょっと玄関ホールに出た時に挨拶をしただけです。二十歳ちょっとくらいに見えたわ。私は名乗ったんだけど、彼女は名乗らなかった。…源次さんに案内されて、二階へ上って行くのを見たの」

description: その娘がいたなら becomes “If that girl were here,” losing the hypothetical daughter relationship.
sourceReading: Eva speculates that if Beatrice had a daughter, Kinzo would want to leave her everything; she fears a claimed heir and a will.

units.text: "Isn't it obvious!  It's to claim that they are the rightful heir to Father's inheritance!  Father is still captivated by Beatrice.  If that girl were here, you would think he'd want to give up all of his assets!  She might even thrust some strange will before us!"
units.note: Both restore hypothetical daughter of Kinzo and Beatrice rather than simply that girl’s presence.
units.japanese: 「決まってるでしょ！　お父様の遺産の正当な後継者だと言い張るためよ！　お父様は未だにベアトリーチェの虜なのよ。その娘がいたなら、全財産を譲りたいと言い出すはずだわ！　妙な遺言状でも突きつけてくるかもしれない！」

description: “That probably wouldn’t be resolved until the distribution ... is settled” reverses the dependency.
sourceReading: Eva says distribution of the inheritance would probably be impossible until the dispute was settled, making litigation a problem for their urgent cash needs.

units.text: "...For that, if we take it to court, we could probably claim half of a quarter of it..., ......but that probably wouldn't be resolved until the distribution of the inheritance is settled.
units.note: Both restore inability to divide inheritance until the dispute is settled, not the reverse dependency.
units.japanese: 「…そりゃ、裁判沙汰にすれば半分の四分の一は主張できるかもしれないけど…、……多分、決着するまで遺産分割はできなくなるわよ。
candidates: probably wouldn't be resolved until the distribution

description: まとまったカネ becomes “gather money,” dropping the requirement for a substantial sum while introducing collection as the action.
sourceReading: Rudolf says each of them urgently needs a substantial amount of money for their own circumstances; Kyrie repeats that premise.

units.text: "......For all of our various situations, we need to gather money urgently.  ...It's our biggest weak point.  Then, ......what are they after?  Kyrie, ...can you tell?"
units.note: MG still says gather/collect money without substantial sum at these occurrences; UP restores large sum. Both later explicitly retain large sum at 539, an additional anchor without curing the earlier loss.
units.japanese: 「……俺たちは、それぞれの都合で早急にまとまったカネがいる。…俺たち最大のウィークポイントってわけだ。

units.text: "...Each one of us needs to gather money quickly for our own reasons. ...It's our biggest weak point. So, ...what are they after? Kyrie, ...can you guess?"
units.note: MG still says gather/collect money without substantial sum at these occurrences; UP restores large sum. Both later explicitly retain large sum at 539, an additional anchor without curing the earlier loss.
units.japanese: 「……俺たちは、それぞれの都合で早急にまとまったカネがいる。…俺たち最大のウィークポイントってわけだ。なら、……狙いは何だ。霧江、…読めるか？」

description: 対応を打たれる is repeatedly rendered as “interact,” replacing defensive measures with contact.
sourceReading: Kyrie reasons that concealing the arrival may have prevented advance countermeasures; therefore the visitor’s goal may be vulnerable to such measures.

units.text: "However, because it was kept hidden that she could come until today, maybe you could say that she didn't want us to be notified in advance and therefore interact with her.  Which means that, it seems her goal is one that would be disadvantageous to her if we did interact.  ...Understand?"
units.note: Both restore defensive measures/countermeasures at the parent’s repeated occurrences. UP interact at 507 is a separate generic response sentence, not a certification of defensive preparation.
units.japanese: 「でも、今日の今日まで訪れることを伏せていたということは、事前に知らせることで、対応を打たれたくなかったと言えるかもしれない。ということは、彼女の目的は、対応を打たれると不利になるものらしい。…わかる？」

description: 私たちに ... 連れてこさせて becomes “she should have brought,” transferring selection and accompaniment of the lawyer or appraiser from the doubters to the visitor.
sourceReading: If her proof were incontrovertible, she should allow the skeptical siblings to bring a lawyer or appraiser and then confront them with undeniable facts.

units.text: "...That's right.  Since we are in a position to doubt her, she should have brought a lawyer or an expert, and thrust some completely undeniable proof before us.  If she could."
units.note: MG still makes the visitor bring the lawyer/expert. UP restores the doubters choosing and bringing their own lawyers/experts, preserving whose verification would be challenged.
units.japanese: 「…そうね。むしろ、疑う立場にある私たちに、弁護士でも鑑定士でも連れてこさせて、ぐぅの音も出ないくらいに事実を突きつけるべきなのよ。それができるならね。」

units.text: "...That's right. On the contrary, since we're in a position to doubt her, she should've brought a lawyer or an expert and thrust some completely undeniable proof before us. If she could."
units.note: MG still makes the visitor bring the lawyer/expert. UP restores the doubters choosing and bringing their own lawyers/experts, preserving whose verification would be challenged.
units.japanese: 「…そうね。むしろ、疑う立場にある私たちに、弁護士でも鑑定士でも連れてこさせて、ぐぅの音も出ないくらいに事実を突きつけるべきなのよ。それができるならね」

description: “You would probably expect that that some huge surprise” has an extraneous second “that.”
sourceReading: Kyrie predicts a major surprise directly or indirectly connected with the inheritance.

units.text: "......To skip to the conclusion, ...you would probably expect that that some huge surprise would be thrust in front of you, something related either directly or indirectly to the inheritance problem that everyone is so infatuated with.  ...The other party probably plans to have the impact of this alone be enough to overpower us.
units.note: Both remove duplicate that and retain predicted surprise tied to inheritance.
units.japanese: 「……結論から言うと、…皆さんがご執心の、遺産問題に直接、もしくは間接的に絡む相当のサプライズが突きつけられると予想されるわね。…おそらく向こうは、そのインパクトだけでこちらを圧倒できるつもりでいる。
candidates: probably expect that that some huge surprise

description: 公的機関も病院もない becomes “no official connections and no hospital.”
sourceReading: There are no public institutions or hospital on the isolated island where the evidence could be checked.

units.text: There was an odd nuance to those words. Right now, this island was closed off by the typhoon and isolated. They had no official connections and no hospital.
units.note: Both restore public/official institutions rather than connections.
units.japanese: 公的機関も病院もない。

description: WH broadens certificates issued by institutions into “any ... proof with any relation to the outside world.” The continuation also turns externally established truths into truths that “must be proven” outside.
sourceReading: On this island, certificates from any institution can be dismissed as false; even truths already established in the outside world can be called false after contact is lost. Kyrie experiences this as an unsettling illusion of a world governed by falsehood.

units.text: So on this island, no matter what manner of proof with any relation to the outside world was shown, one could claim that it was fiction. It was impossible to prove that something was the truth.
units.note: MG still broadens institution-issued certificates to any outside-related proof, but whose proof lay outside restores prior external establishment instead of a requirement to prove later. UP restores institutional documentation and truths already proven outside.
units.japanese:
だからこの島では、どんな機関が発行した証明書を見せようとも、全て虚偽だと言い張れる。
真実を証明することが不可能なのだ。
外界と途絶し、外界で証明された全ての真実が「虚偽」と呼ばれてしまう…。
candidates: proof with any relation to the outside world

units.text: They were cut off from the outside world, and any truth that must be proven in the outside world would be called 'fiction'... So did that mean, ......that now, on this Rokkenjima, there was nothing that was truthful? ......That everything would be controlled by 'fiction'?
units.note: MG still broadens institution-issued certificates to any outside-related proof, but whose proof lay outside restores prior external establishment instead of a requirement to prove later. UP restores institutional documentation and truths already proven outside.
units.japanese:
だからこの島では、どんな機関が発行した証明書を見せようとも、全て虚偽だと言い張れる。
真実を証明することが不可能なのだ。
外界と途絶し、外界で証明された全ての真実が「虚偽」と呼ばれてしまう…。

units.text: So on this island, no matter what manner of proof related to the outside world was shown, it would always be possible to call it a lie. It would be impossible to prove that something was the truth.
units.note: MG still broadens institution-issued certificates to any outside-related proof, but whose proof lay outside restores prior external establishment instead of a requirement to prove later. UP restores institutional documentation and truths already proven outside.
units.japanese:
だからこの島では、どんな機関が発行した証明書を見せようとも、全て虚偽だと言い張れる。真実を証明することが不可能なのだ。
外界と途絶し、外界で証明された全ての真実が「虚偽」と呼ばれてしまう…。ならばつまり。……今のこの六軒島には、真実など何もないということなのか。……支配しているのは「虚偽」だけということなのか。

units.text: Now that they were isolated from the outside, all truths whose proof lay in the outside world would be called "lies"... So does that mean... ...that right now, on this Rokkenjima, no truth exists at all? ...Does it mean that everything will now be ruled by "lies" alone?
units.note: MG still broadens institution-issued certificates to any outside-related proof, but whose proof lay outside restores prior external establishment instead of a requirement to prove later. UP restores institutional documentation and truths already proven outside.
units.japanese:
だからこの島では、どんな機関が発行した証明書を見せようとも、全て虚偽だと言い張れる。真実を証明することが不可能なのだ。
外界と途絶し、外界で証明された全ての真実が「虚偽」と呼ばれてしまう…。ならばつまり。……今のこの六軒島には、真実など何もないということなのか。……支配しているのは「虚偽」だけということなのか。

description: 自分の知る以外の人間 becomes “humans other than themselves,” dropping the boundary of Rosa’s knowledge.
sourceReading: Rosa assumes there cannot be anyone on the island whom she does not know, since only the family’s estate is there.

units.text: Rosa was astonished. ...Only the Ushiromiya family mansion existed on this island. So there was no way that there were any humans other than themselves on this island. And yet, Maria said that she had been meeting with that suspicious woman every year during the family conference......
units.note: Both retain humans other than themselves, erasing the explicit limit to people Rosa knows.
units.japanese: だから、この島に自分の知る以外の人間がいるわけないのだ。

units.text: Rosa was astonished. ...Only the Ushiromiya family mansion existed on this island. So there couldn't have been any humans other than themselves here. And yet, Maria said she'd been meeting with this suspicious woman every year during the family conference...
units.note: Both retain humans other than themselves, erasing the explicit limit to people Rosa knows.
units.japanese: 楼座は愕然とする。…この島には右代宮家の屋敷があるだけだ。だから、この島に自分の知る以外の人間がいるわけないのだ。なのに真里亞は、何と毎年、親族会議の度にあの怪しげな女と出会っていたという……。

units.text: Rosa was aghast. ...Only the Ushiromiya mansion existed on this island. So there was no way that there were any humans other than themselves on this island. And yet, Maria said that she had been meeting with that suspicious woman every year during the family conference......
units.note: Both retain humans other than themselves, erasing the explicit limit to people Rosa knows.
units.japanese: 楼座は愕然とする。…この島には右代宮家の屋敷があるだけだ。だから、この島に自分の知る以外の人間がいるわけないのだ。なのに真里亞は、何と毎年、親族会議の度にあの怪しげな女と出会っていたという……。

description: “Had come to the family conference every year to play” adds arrival or travel absent from the Japanese conclusion.
sourceReading: Rosa concludes an unknown person exists on Rokkenjima and has played with Maria each year at conference time; she then asks whether the person lives on the island or outside it.

units.text: Rosa had to accept it now. ...There really was a person on this Rokkenjima that she herself hadn't known existed until now, and this person had come to the family conference every year to play with Maria.
units.note: MG still adds come to the family conference every year. UP been playing during the conference restores presence/activity without added travel.
units.japanese: …この六軒島には、自分が今まで存在すら知らなかった人物が確かに存在して、しかも毎年、親族会議の度に真里亞と遊んでいたのだ。
candidates: come to the family conference every year to play

units.text: Rosa had to accept it now. ...There really was a person on this Rokkenjima that she herself hadn't known existed until now, and this person had come to the family conference every year to play with Maria.
units.note: MG still adds come to the family conference every year. UP been playing during the conference restores presence/activity without added travel.
units.japanese: もう楼座は認めざるを得ない。…この六軒島には、自分が今まで存在すら知らなかった人物が確かに存在して、しかも毎年、親族会議の度に真里亞と遊んでいたのだ。
candidates: come to the family conference every year to play

description: “She had been made to hold it by a woman” replaces having the woman who calls herself Beatrice carry the letter.
sourceReading: Having inferred that the letter is from Father, Rosa reasons that his having Beatrice carry it must connect its contents to Beatrice and the inheritance.

units.text: Using common sense, .........one could guess that a huge resolution somehow related to Father's inheritance was probably written inside. Actually, ...since she had been made to hold it by a woman who called herself Beatrice, there was no way that wasn't related. ......Did it mean that this person wants, not just the four, but a total of five people to be included in the inheritance?
units.note: MG replaces being made to hold it with receiving it, but still substitutes woman-to-Rosa custody for Father entrusting the letter to the woman. UP explicitly restores Father giving it to her, the premise of Rosa’s inheritance conjecture.
units.japanese: いや、…それをベアトリーチェと名乗る女性に持たせたのなら、それに関係ないわけがない。
candidates: made to hold it by a woman

units.text: Using common sense, ......one might guess that it contained a huge decision somehow related to Father's inheritance. Actually, ...since she'd received it from a woman who called herself Beatrice, there simply had to be some connection. ...Does it mean this person wants, not just the four, but a total of five people to be included in the inheritance?
units.note: MG replaces being made to hold it with receiving it, but still substitutes woman-to-Rosa custody for Father entrusting the letter to the woman. UP explicitly restores Father giving it to her, the premise of Rosa’s inheritance conjecture.
units.japanese: 常識的に考えれば、………おそらくこの中には、お父様の遺産相続を巡る何かの重大な決定が記されているだろう。いや、…それをベアトリーチェと名乗る女性に持たせたのなら、それに関係ないわけがない。……遺産を４人でなく、彼女を加えた５人で分配しろということなのか。

description: 綺麗事を言っていられる becomes “keep everything pretty,” obscuring the rejection of morally fine but impractical sentiments.
sourceReading: Rosa knows discussing her living father’s inheritance is wrong, but her urgent financial situation leaves no room for pious platitudes. Later she uses the same rationale for breaking her promise.

units.text: ...............I needed a large sum of money, ...and I couldn't wait long. I felt like a sinful daughter for discussing the distribution of Father's inheritance while he was still alive. ......However, this was no time to keep everything pretty.
units.note: MG cheap ideals restores the rejection of impractical moral sentiments at both 696 and 708. UP keep everything pretty / keep things pretty retains the calque in both contexts.
units.japanese: ……しかし、綺麗事を言っていられる段階にない。

units.text: ..................I need a large sum of money, ...and I can't wait long. I do feel like a sinful daughter for discussing the distribution of Father's inheritance while he's still alive. ......However, I'm no longer at a stage where I can afford to keep everything pretty.
units.note: MG cheap ideals restores the rejection of impractical moral sentiments at both 696 and 708. UP keep everything pretty / keep things pretty retains the calque in both contexts.
units.japanese: ………………私には、まとまったお金が必要で、…しかもそれは長くは待てない。お父様の遺産の分配を、まだ存命の内から議論するなんて、自分は罪深い娘だと思う。……しかし、綺麗事を言っていられる段階にない。

description: WH connects excessive boisterousness to “because Rosa had warned her several times.”
sourceReading: Maria was too noisy on the plane, boat, and at lunch, and repeatedly received warnings from Rosa as a result.

units.text: Since they had met Maria in the airport, she had been romping around about Halloween the whole time. ...But maybe she had cut loose a little too much, and acted a little too boisterous on the plane, on the boat, and during lunch, because Rosa had warned her several times.
units.note: Both because clauses attach Rosa’s warnings as the reason for boisterousness, instead of warnings resulting from it.
units.japanese: …ただ、少々ハメを外しすぎたようで、飛行機の中や船の中、昼食の席でも騒がしくし過ぎ、楼座から何度も注意を受けていた。
candidates: because Rosa had warned her several times

units.text: Ever since they'd met Maria at the airport, she'd been romping around, chatting about Halloween the whole time. ...But maybe she'd cut loose a little too much, acting a little too boisterous on the plane, on the boat, and during lunch, ...because Rosa had cautioned her several times.
units.note: Both because clauses attach Rosa’s warnings as the reason for boisterousness, instead of warnings resulting from it.
units.japanese: 今日の真里亞は、飛行場で出会った時から、ずっとハロウィンハロウィンと大はしゃぎしていた。…ただ、少々ハメを外しすぎたようで、飛行機の中や船の中、昼食の席でも騒がしくし過ぎ、楼座から何度も注意を受けていた。

units.text: Ever since they had met Maria in the airport, she had constantly been making a huge fuss about Halloween. ...But it seemed she had cut loose a little too much, and acted a little too boisterous on the plane, on the boat, and during lunch, because Rosa had warned her several times.
units.note: Both because clauses attach Rosa’s warnings as the reason for boisterousness, instead of warnings resulting from it.
units.japanese: 今日の真里亞は、飛行場で出会った時から、ずっとハロウィンハロウィンと大はしゃぎしていた。…ただ、少々ハメを外しすぎたようで、飛行機の中や船の中、昼食の席でも騒がしくし過ぎ、楼座から何度も注意を受けていた。
candidates: because Rosa had warned her several times

description: もう６時 becomes “almost 6:00.”
sourceReading: Looking at the clock shows it is already six. The cousins conclude Maria cannot have been continuously scolded this long.

units.text: When they looked at the clock, they realized that it was almost 6:00. They couldn't really imagine that Maria had been scolded this whole time. Maybe it was time for some anime she watched every week to start. She had probably stayed in the mansion's parlor the whole time.
units.note: Both still say almost six rather than already six.
units.japanese: 時計を見ればもう６時だった。

units.text: When they looked at the clock, they realized it was almost 6:00. Of course, they couldn't imagine she'd been getting scolded all this time. Maybe it was time for some anime she watched every week to start. She probably hadn't left the mansion's parlor.
units.note: Both still say almost six rather than already six.
units.japanese:
時計を見ればもう６時だった。
さすがにずっと叱られているとは思わない。多分、毎週見ているアニメでも始まる時間ではないだろうか。そのまま屋敷の客間に居付いてしまったのだろう。

units.text:
When they looked at the clock, they realized that it was almost six.
They couldn't really imagine that Maria had been being scolded this whole time. Perhaps it had come time for some anime she watched every week to start, or something. She had probably just decided to stay in the mansion's parlor.
units.note: Both still say almost six rather than already six.
units.japanese:
時計を見ればもう６時だった。
さすがにずっと叱られているとは思わない。多分、毎週見ているアニメでも始まる時間ではないだろうか。そのまま屋敷の客間に居付いてしまったのだろう。

description: “I want you to stay with us and be friendly” loses the unchanged mutual friendship dating back to childhood.
sourceReading: Outside working hours George wants them all to remain close friends just as they were back then, without Shannon’s concern about rank.

units.text: "......It's alright to act like that.  Forget when you're working, when you're taking your break, like now, I want you to stay with us and be friendly."
units.note: MG restores old-days reference but stay and be friendly still addresses Shannon rather than explicitly maintaining mutual friendship. UP we could all be friendly together restores the mutual relation.
units.japanese: 仕事中はともかく、こうして休み時間に過ごす時の僕らは、あの頃から変わらない、仲良しで居続けたいね。」
candidates: want you to stay with us and be friendly

units.text: "...Don't worry about "understanding your place" in that sense. When you're on the job is one thing, but when you're taking your break and with us, like now, I'd rather you stay and be friendly, just like the old days."
units.note: MG restores old-days reference but stay and be friendly still addresses Shannon rather than explicitly maintaining mutual friendship. UP we could all be friendly together restores the mutual relation.
units.japanese: 「……いいよ、そんな礼儀云々は。仕事中はともかく、こうして休み時間に過ごす時の僕らは、あの頃から変わらない、仲良しで居続けたいね」

description: 背伸びしてる becomes “starting to grow,” replacing overreaching or acting older with development.
sourceReading: Shannon thinks Kanon is still young but sometimes adopts ideas beyond his age, figuratively standing on tiptoe.

units.text: "...Even though Kanon-kun is still young, I think that he's starting to grow a bit in his way of thinking."
units.note: MG starting to grow treats maturity as development. UP tries a little too hard to be mature restores overreaching.
units.japanese: 「…嘉音くんはまだ幼いのに、考え方が少し背伸びしてるところがあると思うんです。」

units.text: "...Kanon may still be childish in some ways, but I think he's starting to grow a bit in his way of thinking."
units.note: MG starting to grow treats maturity as development. UP tries a little too hard to be mature restores overreaching.
units.japanese: 「…嘉音くんはまだ幼いのに、考え方が少し背伸びしてるところがあると思うんです」

description: 寿退社 becomes “resign and have a party,” omitting marriage as the reason for leaving employment and adding a party.
sourceReading: Jessica teases that Shannon will eventually leave her servant job upon getting married.

units.text: "Heh, I'm jealous.  ......That mean Shannon's gonna resign and have a party soon?"
units.note: MG resign and have a party still omits marriage. UP cutting up a cake suggests a wedding, making the intended occasion recoverable, but leaves marriage implicit and supplies a cake action.
units.japanese: ……ってことは紗音もその内、寿退社ってわけなんだ？」

units.text: "Dang, I'm jealous. ...So, does that mean Shannon's gonna resign and have a party soon?"
units.note: MG resign and have a party still omits marriage. UP cutting up a cake suggests a wedding, making the intended occasion recoverable, but leaves marriage implicit and supplies a cake action.
units.japanese: 「ちぇ、妬けるぜ。……ってことは紗音もその内、寿退社ってわけなんだ？」

units.text: "Tch, I'm jealous. ......Does that mean Shannon's gonna be resigning and cutting up a cake pretty soon?"
units.note: MG resign and have a party still omits marriage. UP cutting up a cake suggests a wedding, making the intended occasion recoverable, but leaves marriage implicit and supplies a cake action.
units.japanese: 「ちぇ、妬けるぜ。……ってことは紗音もその内、寿退社ってわけなんだ？」

description: WH says he has “calmer thoughts like I’m in my old age,” changing the subject of his planning into the manner of his present thinking.
sourceReading: Despite his youth, George is already imagining a peaceful old age with Shannon, grown children, and grandchildren.

units.text: "...For some reason, even at the age I am now, I've started having some calmer thoughts like I'm in my old age.  ......Healthy grown kids, and grandchildren running around.  If only I could spend the rest of my life at a slow pace, surrounded by that, and together with Shannon forever."
units.note: Both restore considering future old age/retirement rather than thinking in the manner of an old person.
units.japanese: 「…僕はこの歳の内からもう、なぜか落ち着いた老後のことを考えてしまうんだよ。……元気に成長した子どもたちと、駆け回る孫たちと。そういうものに囲まれて、いつまでも紗音と二人、ゆっくりと余生を送れたらなって。」
candidates: calmer thoughts like I'm in my old age

description: “No one can worry about who I chose” replaces George’s refusal to let anyone obstruct or constrain his choice of spouse.
sourceReading: George insists no one can stand in the way of whom he chooses as his life partner, and asks whose permission he needs.

units.text: "Ah-hah-hah-ha.  There's no reason for anyone to worry about something like that.  ......No one can worry about who I chose to be my partner.  Shannon makes me happy.  Whose permission do I need?"
units.note: Both restore George excluding other people’s influence or say in his choice of spouse.
units.japanese: ……僕が誰を伴侶に選ぶかは、誰にもはばかられない。紗音は僕が幸せにする。それに誰の許可が？」

description: 紗音は僕が幸せにする becomes “Shannon makes me happy,” reversing who acts for whose happiness and losing the commitment.
sourceReading: George promises that he will make Shannon happy as part of declaring his independent choice of partner.

units.text: "Ah-hah-hah-ha.  There's no reason for anyone to worry about something like that.  ......No one can worry about who I chose to be my partner.  Shannon makes me happy.  Whose permission do I need?"
units.note: Both restore George’s commitment to make Shannon happy, rather than her making him happy.
units.japanese: ……僕が誰を伴侶に選ぶかは、誰にもはばかられない。紗音は僕が幸せにする。それに誰の許可が？」

description: “Boiling over” adds overflowing contents to a pot described as emitting steam.
sourceReading: Gohda argues with Genji while paying no attention to the steaming pot.

units.text: Gohda-san flared up at Genji, paying no heed to the pot that was boiling over.
units.note: MG spitting steam restores steam; UP boiling over still adds overflow.
units.japanese: 郷田さんは、湯気を噴き出す鍋をよそに源次に食って掛かっておりました。

units.text: Gohda‐san was flaring up at Genji, paying no heed to the pot that was boiling over.
units.note: MG spitting steam restores steam; UP boiling over still adds overflow.
units.japanese: 郷田さんは、湯気を噴き出す鍋をよそに源次に食って掛かっておりました。

description: “The task you are confident in” replaces his own work and drops the explicit request to attend to the relatives.
sourceReading: Genji redirects Gohda toward his duties and asks him to take care of serving the family members.

units.text: "......Gohda-san, if you would, please devote your attention entirely towards the task you are confident in, for all of the relatives..."
units.note: Both restore own/assigned duties and attending to relatives, removing confidence as the assignment basis.
units.japanese: 「……郷田さんはご自身の仕事に専念され、親族の皆さんのお相手を、どうかよろしくお願いします…。」

description: “Having approached from a blind spot” replaces Kanon’s stationary listening posture.
sourceReading: Kanon has been leaning against the corridor-side wall at the entrance, out of sight, listening to the argument.

units.text: ...Kanon had heard everything, having approached from a blind spot in the hall along the wall near the entrance to the kitchen. ...He probably knew that if he entered the kitchen, sparks would start to fly his way.
units.note: Both restore stationary leaning while listening out of sight.
units.japanese: …嘉音は死角に当たる、入り口の廊下側壁に寄りかかって話を聞いていたのだ。
candidates: having approached from a blind spot

description: 言わせておきなよ becomes “Let me say it.”
sourceReading: Kanon tells Shannon to let Gohda go on talking, dismissing him as a contemptible man.

units.text: "............Let me say it.  He's a horrible man."
units.note: MG removes asking permission but still frames the clause as Kanon speaking rather than letting Gohda talk. UP Let him rant restores the advice.
units.japanese: 「…………言わせておきなよ。最低の男だ。」

units.text: "......I've got to say it. The man's scum."
units.note: MG removes asking permission but still frames the clause as Kanon speaking rather than letting Gohda talk. UP Let him rant restores the advice.
units.japanese: 「…………言わせておきなよ。最低の男だ」

description: “Known of his failure” substitutes an unspecified male’s past failure for knowing that the seeded love would break down.
sourceReading: Kanon recalls Beatrice saying she sowed the seeds of love knowing they would end in ruin.

units.text: And she had said that. .........She had definitely said that she had known of his failure and had sown the seeds of love.
units.note: Both restore knowing the seeded love would fail, rather than an unspecified male’s past failure. This remains Kanon’s recollection of Beatrice’s claim.
units.japanese: ………破綻することを知っていて恋のタネを蒔いたと確かに言った。

description: “How long we would be able stand” changes uncertainty about how long they must suffer into uncertainty about how long they can bear it, and omits “to” after “able.”
sourceReading: Shannon did not know how much longer they would have to suffer as furniture, and eventually concluded the day of rest would never arrive.

units.text: "..................At one time, in the past, I wished that this day would come.  ......But it never came after so much time.........I didn't know how long we would be able stand being tormented as furniture............So I thought.  ...I thought that day of rest wouldn't come for all eternity."
units.note: Both restore uncertainty about how long suffering must continue, rather than endurance capacity; grammar repaired.
units.japanese: 「………………いつか、…この日が訪れることを、かつては願ってた。……でも、いつまで経っても訪れなくて…。……私たちはいつまで家具として苦しめばいいのか、わからなくて…。………だから私、思ったの。…安息の日なんて、永遠に訪れないんだ、って。」
candidates: long we would be able stand

description: 必ず去らなければならない becomes “must not leave,” reversing obligation into prohibition.
sourceReading: Kanon blames Shannon for developing attachments to a world they are bound to leave.

units.text: "Yeah, it's your fault, Nee-san.  ......If only you hadn't known love.........we would both be happy that this day has finally come!  You built up shameless regrets!  Even though it was a world that you must not leave!!"
units.note: Both restore the obligation to leave the world, rather than a prohibition against leaving.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、姉さんが悪い。……姉さんさえ恋を覚えなかったら…。……僕たちはようやく訪れた今日を喜び合うはずだった！　姉さんが下らない未練を作ってしまったんだ！　必ず去らなければならない世界なのに！！」

description: “Can I still ... let a person cry just because I’m furniture” reverses 泣かせずに済むかな, hoping to avoid making someone cry.
sourceReading: Kanon hopes that becoming human will let him know love and spare someone the tears his furniture status has caused.

units.text: "............And when we've done that, ...maybe I want to, ......be able to know love, like you, Nee-san.  Can I still, .........let a person cry just because I'm furniture......?"
units.note: Both restore the hope of no longer causing tears. MG preserves because I am furniture; UP substitutes calling himself furniture and juxtaposes this with making people cry, weakening the causal status distinction.
units.japanese:
「……………そうしたらさ。…僕も姉さんみたいに、
……恋が知れるかな。もう、家具だからって、
………人を、泣かせずに済むかな……。」
candidates: let a person cry just because I'm furniture

units.text: "...............And then... ...maybe, like you, Nee‐san, ......I'll be able to know love. Maybe I won't have to call myself furniture, .........and make people cry anymore......"
units.note: Both restore the hope of no longer causing tears. MG preserves because I am furniture; UP substitutes calling himself furniture and juxtaposes this with making people cry, weakening the causal status distinction.
units.japanese: 「……………そうしたらさ。…僕も姉さんみたいに、……恋が知れるかな。もう、家具だからって、………人を、泣かせずに済むかな……」

description: “Brighten her mood” assigns the mood being attended to to Jessica rather than Kanon. The source also specifically names her painful smile.
sourceReading: Jessica’s strained smiles as she tries to patch things up and please him, along with her earlier tears, have gradually changed Kanon’s heart.

units.text: The tears Jessica had shown him that day, ......and Jessica's pitiful face as she tried to smooth things over and brighten her mood until today, had slowly wrought some kind of change on Kanon's heart without him knowing it...
units.note: MG stay bright replaces brighten her mood but still directs emotional effort toward Jessica and does not restore her strained smile explicitly. UP restores painful smiles but retains brighten her mood rather than appeasing Kanon.
units.japanese: あの日に見せた朱志香の涙と、……今日までの、取り繕いご機嫌を取るような朱志香の痛々しい笑顔が、知らず知らずの内に、嘉音の心に何かの変化を与えていた…。

units.text: The tears Jessica had shown him that day... and Jessica's pitiful face as she tried to smooth things over and stay bright ever since then... had slowly wrought some kind of change on Kanon's heart without him knowing it...
units.note: MG stay bright replaces brighten her mood but still directs emotional effort toward Jessica and does not restore her strained smile explicitly. UP restores painful smiles but retains brighten her mood rather than appeasing Kanon.
units.japanese: あの日に見せた朱志香の涙と、……今日までの、取り繕いご機嫌を取るような朱志香の痛々しい笑顔が、知らず知らずの内に、嘉音の心に何かの変化を与えていた…。

units.text: The tears Jessica had shown him that day, ......and her painful smiles on all the days since as she tried to smooth things over and brighten her mood... had slowly wrought some kind of change on Kanon's heart without him knowing it...
units.note: MG stay bright replaces brighten her mood but still directs emotional effort toward Jessica and does not restore her strained smile explicitly. UP restores painful smiles but retains brighten her mood rather than appeasing Kanon.
units.japanese: あの日に見せた朱志香の涙と、……今日までの、取り繕いご機嫌を取るような朱志香の痛々しい笑顔が、知らず知らずの内に、嘉音の心に何かの変化を与えていた…。

description: 守りはこれで充分か becomes “That should be good enough for defense”; possible gaps also become “that hole.”
sourceReading: Kinzo wonders whether his defense is adequate and whether bishops or knights might exploit a gap.

units.text: "Be silent.  ......Hmmm.  ......That should be good enough for defense.  Will the bishop and the knight be able to penetrate that hole...?  ............nnnnnnnn..."
units.note: Both retain a declarative judgment of adequate defense in place of Kinzo’s adequacy question, and that opening/hole presents a definite gap rather than whether pieces might find one.

units.note: Both retain a declarative judgment of adequate defense in place of Kinzo’s adequacy question, and that opening/hole presents a definite gap rather than whether pieces might find one.

units.note: Both retain a declarative judgment of adequate defense in place of Kinzo’s adequacy question, and that opening/hole presents a definite gap rather than whether pieces might find one.

description: 仕切り直し becomes “I have a score to settle.”
sourceReading: Nanjo agrees to play again but says they must start afresh, since losing his rook has hurt his current position.

units.text: "......................That is fine, but I have a score to settle.  Losing that rook was a serious blow.
units.note: MG start over and UP rematch restore restarting play rather than settling a score; loss of rook remains the reason.
units.japanese: 「…………………………。…良いですが、仕切り直しですぞ。ルークが落ちてしまったのは痛手ですのでな。

description: “Is everything to Master’s satisfaction?” replaces the question about whether Kinzo’s own preparations are completely ready.
sourceReading: After agreeing to bring dinner, Genji separately asks whether Kinzo’s preparations are all in place. Kinzo answers by describing the room’s layered barriers.

units.text: "......Well then, Master.  I will now carry in your dinner." "It may be my final dinner.  I must savor it.  ......Please, prepare it." "Certainly.  ............Is everything to Master's satisfaction?"
units.note: Both separately ask whether Kinzo’s own preparations are complete/in order, restoring the question answered by his account of barriers rather than asking about satisfaction with dinner.
units.japanese: 「かしこまりました。…………お館様のご準備の方は、万端となりましたか。」

description: “But that was only as a candidate for the sacrifice of the second twilight” substitutes a limiting qualification for Shannon being an especially suitable candidate.
sourceReading: Beatrice confirms the promise, remarks that Shannon had been perfectly suited to the second twilight, and says she conceded under the condition that Shannon reject the engagement.

units.text: "Hmm.  I did.  ......But that was only as a candidate for the sacrifice of the second twilight.  ...Kanon cried and screamed that I should forgive you for that, so I graciously listened to his words.  With the condition that you give up your engagement.  ......*cackle*cackle*, see how gracious I am?"
units.note: Both restore suitability for the second twilight rather than limiting the promise to that twilight; abandonment of engagement remains the condition.
units.japanese: 「うむ。したぞ。……そなたは第二の晩に打ってつけの生贄候補だったのだがな。…嘉音がそれを許せと泣いて叫ぶので寛大に聞き入れてやったのよ。そなたが婚約を破棄すればとの条件付きでな。……くっくくく、妾の何と寛大なことよ。」
candidates: candidate for the sacrifice of the second twilight

description: 唯一の方法 becomes “the way,” losing the explicit exclusivity.
sourceReading: Shannon says she is convinced this is the only way to resist a being who feeds on other people’s distress.

units.text: "I have finally come to understand you.  You like to bully, confuse, and trouble people, and you do it to entertain yourself.  .........So I'm now sure that this is the way to resist you."
units.note: Both explicitly restore only/one single method of resistance; 629 repeats the exclusivity.
units.japanese: ………だから、あなたに抵抗する唯一の方法が、これであると確信した。」

description: “I don’t believe that you inspire it” changes refusal to believe the malice Beatrice tries to suggest into disbelief that Beatrice causes the fate or malice.
sourceReading: Shannon sees fate as a die roll, feels no malicious intent in it, and refuses to believe such intent even if Beatrice tries to plant that interpretation in her.

units.text: "...If that is the fate that you have decided, that is up to you.  ......I won't be afraid of that or go against that.  Because I don't believe that the severe fate that will start occurring from here on is something controlled by your will.  We humans don't know anything about fates that could occur in the future.  Therefore, until the last instant, I'll live to the fullest, relying on my own fate and conviction.  Fate is just a roll of the dice.  You can't feel malice from it.  I don't believe that you inspire it."
units.note: MG refuses belief in claimed malice. UP inject some followed by refusal to believe also concerns the attempted malicious interpretation rather than simply denying causal authorship.
units.japanese: ……私はそれに怯えたり、逆らったりしません。これから起こる苛烈な運命が、あなたの意思によるものだなんて、信じないから。私たち人間は、未来に起こりうる運命など知らない。だからこそ、最後の瞬間まで、自分の信念と運命に従い精一杯生き抜く。運命はただのサイコロの目。そこに悪意なんて感じない。あなたが吹き込もうと、信じない。」

We humans don't know anything about fates that could occur in the future.  Therefore, until the last instant, I'll live to the fullest, relying on my own fate and conviction.  Fate is just a roll of the dice.  You can't feel malice from it.  I don't believe that you inspire it."

description: “If you make soup with both hands” misreads 椀, a bowl, as soup.
sourceReading: Beatrice likens human fates to Fragments that a higher being can scoop up without limit by cupping both hands into a bowl.

units.text: "That's what witches do.  I live off your fates, reigning as a high-order being does over low-order beings.  After all, for all of you, fate is just a Fragment.  If you make soup with both hands, you can scoop out as much as you want."
units.note: Both restore cupped hands scooping fragments rather than making soup.
units.japanese: 「それが魔女というものよ。貴様らの運命を食い物に、高次の存在として低次の存在の上に君臨する。そなたらの運命など所詮はカケラ。両手で椀を作ればいくらでも掬える。」

description: “Whether I invite them to my dinner table” replaces the cattle inevitably furnishing her dinner’s enjoyment.
sourceReading: Whatever the cattle she raises say, the outcome is still that they feed and please her at the table.

units.text: "......Just like how no matter what the beef cows I raise babble, it won't change whether I invite them to my dinner table.  *cackle*cackle*...!"
units.note: Both restore the fixed result of cattle furnishing dinner enjoyment, rather than whether they are invited.
units.japanese: 「……妾に飼われた肉牛どもが何をほざこうとも、妾の食卓を楽しませる結果に変わりはせぬのに同じこと。くっくっくっく…！」
candidates: whether I invite them to my dinner table

description: “Traveled far from across the world” adds global origins for the gathered relatives.
sourceReading: Gohda compares relatives normally living far away and gathering here with liquors brought together from around the world.

units.text: "Master.  Today is the annual family conference.  As a dinner for those who normally live far away, and have traveled far from across the world to gather together, I realized that a sauce made from a blend of fine alcohols from across the world that have never met each other before would be most fitting, so I had it specially prepared."
units.note: Both retain relatives traveling from across the world; source global origins concern the alcohols only.
units.japanese: 「旦那様。本日は年に一度の親族会議でございます。普段は遠方にお住まいの皆様が、遥々お越しになり一堂に集われた夜の晩餐には、世界各地より、普段は出会うことのない各地の銘酒を取り寄せブレンドしたソースが、何よりも相応しいかと存じ、特別にご用意させていただいたのでございます。」
candidates: traveled far from across the world

units.text: As a dinner for those who normally live far away and who have traveled far from across the world to gather together, I realized it would be most fitting to have a sauce made from a blend of fine alcohols from all over the planet that have never met each other before, so I had it specially prepared."

description: “Having Gohda-san handle the truly delicious part” loses the idiom 美味しいところを持ってかれる, being upstaged or having the good part taken away.
sourceReading: Rudolf agrees Gohda anticipated Krauss’s question and neatly took the favorable moment for himself.

units.text: "There's no mistake.  Having Gohda-san handle the truly delicious part."
units.note: MG restores stealing the show but you set him up and a plant at 696 change anticipated question/upstaging into deliberate assistance by Krauss. UP saw it coming and run off with your moment preserve anticipation and loss of the favorable moment.

description: “Might not have know” uses the base verb after “have.”
sourceReading: Gohda had not imagined that Krauss and Natsuhi were unaware of the honored guest.

units.text: Natsuhi's words echoed the question that everyone who didn't know about the visitor, the Golden Witch, was thinking. Gohda was slightly disoriented, as though he hadn't thought Natsuhi would actually question him. ......It had been an honored guest spoken of so severely. He hadn't imagined that Krauss and his wife might not have know.
units.note: Both repair the auxiliary construction: might not know / might not have known.
units.japanese: まさか蔵臼夫婦が知らないとは思わなかった。

description: “Isn’t this really a joke?!” changes the direction of Krauss’s confirmation request.
sourceReading: Krauss asks Gohda to confirm that this really is not a joke, after his own entertainment hypothesis has been challenged.

units.text: "I don't have a clue what you people are talking about!  Gohda, isn't this really a joke?!"
units.note: Both restore asking confirmation that this is not a joke, rather than asking whether it really is a joke.
units.japanese: 「私にはお前たちが何を言っているのかさっぱりだ！　郷田、これは本当に冗談ではないのだな？！」

description: “She had definitely affirmed” makes the transition appear to credit Rosa with the composed sentence, after describing her lost composure.
sourceReading: A calm statement now confirms the visitor’s existence: the following speaker is Kyrie, independently saying she also met the woman.

units.text: Because, with that one composed sentence, she had definitely affirmed that existence.
units.note: Both restore an impersonal calm sentence introducing Kyrie’s corroboration, without crediting Rosa herself. MG nature versus existence is separately adjudicated below.
units.japanese: だから、冷静な一言が、その存在を間違いなく肯定した。

description: “That boat will only make the trip” replaces today’s boat having made only the round trip to transport the family.
sourceReading: Natsuhi claims that today’s boat service consisted only of the family’s transport round trip, and asks whether the woman was aboard.

units.text: "That isn't possible!  In the first place, where did that woman come from?  That boat will only make the trip to the island to escort everyone there and back.  Was she riding on that boat?!"
units.note: MG restores completed arrival rather than future restriction, but drops explicit round trip. UP restores today’s completed escort round trip. Both retain the challenge about another boat.

candidates: boat will only make the trip

units.note: Both call the guest the witch of the portrait and omit that Hideyoshi only says she closely resembles the portrait’s witch. This follows Kyrie’s explicit refusal to certify identity, so the lost qualification remains material.

sourceReading: Battler acknowledges that he cannot expect to be the lone exception to the children’s dismissal.

units.text: "...Guess that means I'm not the only exception."

sourceReading: Kumasawa says the witch may unexpectedly appear to honest, pure-hearted people and play pranks.

units.text: "That's right.  Although Beatrice-sama doesn't usually show herself, I hear that she sometimes unexpectedly does so before honest people with clean hearts.  Hoh-hoh-ho."

description: “Arranged things beforehand” changes agreeing on a common account into unspecified advance arrangements.
sourceReading: People coordinate what they say to encourage Maria’s dream; Battler later describes coordinating their stories and leaving sweets.

units.text: So Maria believed in the legend of the witch. She swallowed the story. ...That was natural for an imaginative girl who believed in witches. So no one said anything to betray her dream. ...On the contrary, they had arranged things beforehand to get her excited about her dreams.
units.note: MG restores working together to say things in the first occurrence, though it broadens this to say and do things and later describes keeping a secret rather than matching accounts. UP uses arranged things and plan it together in both occurrences, retaining nonspecific practical planning.
units.japanese: …むしろ、彼女の夢を盛り上げるように口裏を合わせた。

units.text: That's why Maria believed in the Legend of the Witch. She accepted it entirely. ...That was only natural for an imaginative girl who believed in witches. So people had avoided saying things that would betray her dream. ...On the contrary, they had worked together to say and do things that would help liven up her dreams without her knowing.
units.note: MG restores working together to say things in the first occurrence, though it broadens this to say and do things and later describes keeping a secret rather than matching accounts. units.note: Both consistently spell Maria-chan correctly.

sourceReading: George quietly admits Battler’s suggestion while taking care that Maria not realize what he is admitting.

units.text: "......Who knows."

description: “I heard a lot about it ... from Krauss-san and the others” reverses 聞かれた, being asked.
sourceReading: Nanjo recalls being repeatedly questioned at an earlier family conference about Kinzo’s mistress and possible hidden child.

units.text: "..................At one point, I heard a lot about it at the family conference from Krauss-san and the others.  ......A story that, long before that time, perhaps Kinzo-san had a mistress, and a hidden child with her."
units.note: Both say Nanjo was questioned by Krauss and the others, and preserve their subsequent decision to approach him after Genji did not speak.

description: The name is printed “Beatice.”
sourceReading: Battler asks whether Kinzo had a mistress called Beatrice.

units.text: "And?  ......So, ......did Grandfather have a mistress called Beatice, Doctor Nanjo?"
units.note: Both spell Beatrice correctly in Battler’s question.
units.japanese: 「んで。……結論として南條先生。……祖父さまに、ベアトリーチェという愛人はいたんすか。」

description: “If one loses a mistress and has a child left from them. they pour ...” puts a period between the conditional and its main clause, followed by lowercase “they.”
sourceReading: Nanjo explains the expectation that affection would be redirected to a surviving child, then expressly labels their no-child conclusion an inference.

units.text: "That, I do not know.  ......But Kinzo-san always says that he is researching how to revive Beatrice.  ...Usually, if one loses a mistress and has a child left from them. they pour all of that love on that child.  ......Therefore, we naturally thought that there wasn't a child between Kinzo-san and Beatrice..."
units.note: Both use a grammatical conditional sentence and preserve that the no-child conclusion was an inference rather than proof.
units.japanese: 「それはわかりません。……ただ金蔵さんは、ベアトリーチェを蘇らせるために研究をしていると常々言っておりました。…普通は、愛人を失い忘れ形見がいたならば、そちらにその分の愛情を注ぐものです。……ですから、金蔵さんとベアトリーチェの間に子どもはいなかったろうと私たちは自然に考えました…。」
candidates: loses a mistress and has a child left from them. they pour

description: “Even if that’s misplaced” loses 刺し違えてでも, accepting one’s own death to kill the target.
sourceReading: Jessica reasons that a revenge-seeker prepared to die taking the target down may not fear police, numbers, or the lack of escape.

units.text: "I don't get it.  Revenge is based on emotion, not logic.  Even if that's misplaced, maybe she isn't really afraid of the police or the number of people or that there's no way out."
units.note: MG restores willingness to go down with the opponent; UP explicitly says she may be ready to give her life for revenge. Both reconnect the motive to disregard for police, numbers and escape.
units.japanese: それこそ、刺し違えてでもなんて考えたら、別に警察も人数も退路がなくても、何も怖くはないかも知れねぇぜ。」

description: “Had gotten into ... trouble” and “were about to be sacrificed” strengthen Jessica’s fear of possible future victimization.
sourceReading: Jessica fears that her parents might become embroiled in trouble and fall victim to something terrible.

units.text: It was only natural that Jessica, realizing that, would be frightened that her father and mother had gotten into some kind of trouble, ...and were about to be sacrificed for something terrifying...
units.note: MG restores prospective fear with might get caught up and might become, but narrows becoming victims of something terrible to becoming human sacrifices. UP retains past involvement and imminent sacrifice: had gotten into trouble and were about to be sacrificed.
units.japanese: それを察する朱志香としては、父や母が何かのトラブルに巻き込まれて、…恐ろしいことの犠牲になるのではないかと恐れるのも無理ないことだった…。
candidates: trouble, ...and were about to be sacrificed

units.text: After realizing this, it was only natural for Jessica to be frightened at the thought... that her parents might get caught up in some kind of trouble... and become human sacrifices for something terrifying...
units.note: MG restores prospective fear with might get caught up and might become, but narrows becoming victims of something terrible to becoming human sacrifices. UP retains past involvement and imminent sacrifice: had gotten into trouble and were about to be sacrificed.
units.japanese: それを察する朱志香としては、父や母が何かのトラブルに巻き込まれて、…恐ろしいことの犠牲になるのではないかと恐れるのも無理ないことだった…。

description: “If I think about what I’m suddenly saying” reverses the speaker of the surprising remarks.
sourceReading: Battler reacts to what Maria has suddenly started saying, then answers that of course he does not accept witches.

units.text: "If I think about what I'm suddenly saying, ......that's probably right. Witches couldn't exist.  It's impossible for it to be anything other than a human woman pretending to be one."
units.note: Both make Battler react to Maria’s unexpected challenge rather than reflect on his own speech, then preserve his denial that the visitor is a witch.
units.japanese: 「突然、何を言い出すかと思えば。……そりゃそうだろ。
candidates: think about what I'm suddenly saying

description: WH says the door had been opened; Japanese presents its opening as the announcement whose consequences Shannon now anticipates.
sourceReading: The door to the Golden Land will open. The witch definitely said so.

units.text: Shannon was bitter and sad. ......The door to the Golden Land, had been opened. ......The witch had definitely told her that. That meant, the demise of everything.
units.note: Both use would be opened, retaining the opening as an announced prospect whose consequences Shannon anticipates rather than a completed threshold event.
units.japanese: ……黄金郷の扉が、開かれる。

description: WH makes George want to stick out his chest for the first time since becoming an adult. This misattaches 初めて and treats 一人前 as a past adulthood milestone.
sourceReading: Only once he has become fully established will he proudly bring her home. His training and inability to build his own household explain the delay.

units.text: "Huh?!  Ah, ......err!  It means making a promise to marry.  ...But I think that means it's the same thing as marriage.  ......Honestly, I want to take you as my wife right now, and take you back home.  ......But right now, I am in the middle of training, and I'm still a long way from gaining the ability needed to create my own castle.  That's why I want to stick out my chest for the first time since becoming an adult and take you home with me."
units.note: MG still makes becoming a full adult the prerequisite, losing George’s professional establishment and independence. UP restores becoming an independent man first, followed by proudly taking Shannon home.
units.japanese: 結婚の約束をする、という意味だよ。…でも僕はその意味において結婚と同じものだと考えてる。……本当なら、僕は今すぐにでも君を娶って家へ連れ帰りたい。……でも、僕は今、修行中の身で、まだまだ自らの城を築き上げる力量がない。だからこそ、一人前になって初めて、胸を張って君を連れ帰りたいんだ。」
candidates: chest for the first time since becoming an adult

units.text: It means making a promise to marry.  ...But I think that means it's the same thing as marriage.  ......Honestly, I want to take you as my wife right now, and take you back home.  ......But right now, I am in the middle of training, and I'm still a long way from gaining the ability needed to create my own castle.  That's why I want to stick out my chest for the first time since becoming an adult and take you home with me."
units.note: MG still makes becoming a full adult the prerequisite, losing George’s professional establishment and independence. UP restores becoming an independent man first, followed by proudly taking Shannon home.
