units.text: "Huh?! Ah, ...err! It means making a promise to marry. ...But I think in that sense, it means the same thing as marriage.
units.note: MG still makes becoming a full adult the prerequisite, losing George’s professional establishment and independence. UP restores becoming an independent man first, followed by proudly taking Shannon home.
units.japanese:
「え？！　あ、……えっと！　結婚の約束をする、という意味だよ。…でも僕はその意味において結婚と同じものだと考えてる」
「……本当なら、僕は今すぐにでも君を娶って家へ連れ帰りたい。……でも、僕は今、修行中の身で、まだまだ自らの城を築き上げる力量がない。だからこそ、一人前になって初めて、胸を張って君を連れ帰りたいんだ」

units.text: ......To be honest, I want to take you home as my wife right away. ...But right now, I'm in the middle of training, and I'm still a long way from having the capacity to create my own castle. That's why I want to take you home with me with my head held high, only after I've become a full adult."
units.note: MG still makes becoming a full adult the prerequisite, losing George’s professional establishment and independence. UP restores becoming an independent man first, followed by proudly taking Shannon home.
units.japanese:
「え？！　あ、……えっと！　結婚の約束をする、という意味だよ。…でも僕はその意味において結婚と同じものだと考えてる」
「……本当なら、僕は今すぐにでも君を娶って家へ連れ帰りたい。……でも、僕は今、修行中の身で、まだまだ自らの城を築き上げる力量がない。だからこそ、一人前になって初めて、胸を張って君を連れ帰りたいんだ」

description: 当然だよ is translated as that was sudden, replacing George’s assurance with a reaction to an unexpected remark.
sourceReading: O-of course. An engagement ring is not merely an accessory; it embodies the lovers’ solemn promise.

units.text: "Th, that was sudden.  An engagement ring isn't a simple accessory.  It's an oath between lovers, an honored promise left in the form of a ring."
units.note: Both restore George’s embarrassed but emphatic Of course, followed by his explanation that the ring embodies a solemn promise.
units.japanese: 「と、当然だよ。婚約指輪はただのアクセサリーじゃない。尊い約束を指輪の形で残す、恋人たちの宣誓なんだ。」

description: WH translates 誰にも覆せない as no one can cover that up, substituting concealment for reversal or invalidation.
sourceReading: They declare themselves united, inform everyone afterwards, and no one can overturn that declaration.

units.text: "Yeah.  It's enough to tell God, Father, and Mother about it afterwards.  We'll claim that we are married.  ..........No one can cover that up."
units.note: MG no one will be able to undo it and UP no one can overturn it both restore the declaration’s claimed irrevocability rather than concealment.
units.japanese: 「うん。神さまも、父さんも母さんも全て事後報告で充分さ。僕たちが、二人は結ばれたと一方的に宣言する。………それは誰にも覆せない。」

description: WH says their lives last only a few weeks. Japanese places the brief period of love within their lifetime, and specifies less than a few weeks.
sourceReading: Cicadas fall in love and pass away during a very short period, not even a few weeks, within their lives. The comparison concerns accepting brief love rather than refusing it.

units.text: "......Cicadas, even though their lives last only a few weeks, fall in love and disappear.  .........There are no cicadas that don't fall in love because it will be over in a few weeks."
units.note: MG still says the cicadas’ lives last only a few weeks. UP explicitly places the brief span of love within their whole lives, restoring the source’s scope, though it rounds less than a few weeks to a few weeks.
units.japanese: 「……蝉は、生涯の内、数週間にも満たないわずかな期間で恋をして、消えていくんだって。………数週間で終わる恋だからと、恋をしない蝉はいないんじゃないかな。」
candidates: lives last only a few weeks

units.text: "...Even though their lives last only a few weeks, cicadas fall in love and then vanish. ......But you'll never find a cicada that refused to fall in love simply because it'd end in a few weeks."
units.note: MG still says the cicadas’ lives last only a few weeks. UP explicitly places the brief span of love within their whole lives, restoring the source’s scope, though it rounds less than a few weeks to a few weeks.
units.japanese: 「……蝉は、生涯の内、数週間にも満たないわずかな期間で恋をして、消えていくんだって。………数週間で終わる恋だからと、恋をしない蝉はいないんじゃないかな」
candidates: lives last only a few weeks

description: The counterfactual uses payed Milady any notice instead of paid.
sourceReading: He would not have paid any attention to Milady if the witch had not played her trick.

units.text: "......That witch is detestable...!!  ...Why did she plant these feelings in me...?!  If only, if only she hadn't done that weird prank, I wouldn't have payed Milady any notice...!!!"
units.note: Both use the correct past participle paid in paid Milady any notice.
units.japanese: 「……あの魔女が憎い…！！　僕に、…どうしてこんな気持ちを植えつけて…！　あいつさえ、あいつさえ妙な悪戯をしなければ、僕はお嬢様のことなんか、気にならなかったのに…！！！」

description: The conditions for all of the pieces is the same has plural subject conditions with singular is.
sourceReading: The conditions for every piece are now the same.

units.text: Well now. With this, the conditions for all of the pieces is the same. There are 18 pieces!  13 will be offered as sacrifices! Who will the five that remain alive be? ............And. Will someone destroy this ceremony? Who?!!  How?! Fuhahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahaha!!
units.note: Both use the plural agreement conditions ... are the same and retain the eighteen, thirteen and five counts.
units.japanese: これにて全ての駒の条件は同じよ。
candidates: conditions for all of the pieces is the same

description: わしらも is rendered I, I also, replacing the collective subject with an individual one.
sourceReading: W-we acknowledge it too. Hideyoshi speaks for a group, naturally himself and Eva in this paired exchange.

units.text: ".........I, I also acknowledge it.  ...Can't argue back."
units.note: MG still has Hideyoshi say I-I also acknowledge it, losing his collective assent. UP restores W-we accept it too; Eva then gives her own acknowledgment separately.
units.japanese: 「…………わ、わしらも認める。…ぐぅの音も出ぇへん。」

units.text: "......I-I also acknowledge it. ...Can't argue back."
units.note: MG still has Hideyoshi say I-I also acknowledge it, losing his collective assent. UP restores W-we accept it too; Eva then gives her own acknowledgment separately.
units.japanese: 「…………わ、わしらも認める。…ぐぅの音も出ぇへん」

description: 仇になった is translated has become your mortal enemy rather than has backfired or worked against you.
sourceReading: The convenient Devil’s Proof excuse has now worked to his disadvantage.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*...!  The Devil's Proof was a convenient excuse that you liked using to show that something was impossible to prove, ......but now it's become your mortal enemy, has it not?"
units.note: Both retain become your mortal enemy, personifying the proof rather than saying Battler’s convenient proof strategy has now backfired on him.
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっくっく…！　悪魔の証明は、そなたが好む証明不能への便利な言い訳だったが、……仇になったようだな？」

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*...! The Devil's Proof was a convenient excuse you liked using to handle unprovable matters, ...but now it's become your mortal enemy, has it not?"
units.note: Both retain become your mortal enemy, personifying the proof rather than saying Battler’s convenient proof strategy has now backfired on him.
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっくっく…！　悪魔の証明は、そなたが好む証明不能への便利な言い訳だったが、……仇になったようだな？」

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*...! The Devil's Proof was a convenient excuse that you liked using to show that something was impossible to prove, ......but now it's become your mortal enemy, has it not?"
units.note: Both retain become your mortal enemy, personifying the proof rather than saying Battler’s convenient proof strategy has now backfired on him.
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっくっく…！　悪魔の証明は、そなたが好む証明不能への便利な言い訳だったが、……仇になったようだな？」

description: 人事を尽くして天命を待ちながら is rendered concern themselves with other’s affairs and possess sacred life. The effort/fate relation becomes unrelated propositions; 自惚れたくもなる also becomes want to love themselves.
sourceReading: Having done everything within human power and awaited fate, people still want to flatter themselves that good fortune came from their own ability.

units.text: "...Hmph.  .........Humans are cheap creatures.  ......While they concern themselves with other's affairs and possess sacred life, they want to love themselves, and when they are given good fortune, they say that it was due to their own ability rather than simple good fortune."
units.note: MG removes the original garble and preserves arrogantly crediting one’s own ability, but reduces doing one’s utmost and awaiting Providence to everything being decided by God. UP restores both human effort and awaiting Providence, as well as self-flattery about ability.
units.japanese: 「…ふ。………人間とは安っぽい生き物だな。……人事を尽くして天命を待ちながら、幸運を得られた時には、それが単なる幸運ではなく、己の技量に拠るものだったと自惚れたくもなる。」
candidates: concern themselves with other's affairs and possess sacred life

units.text: "...Hmph. ......Humans are cheap creatures. ...Even though everything is ultimately decided by God, when humans are given good fortune, they arrogantly feel it was due to their own ability."
units.note: MG removes the original garble and preserves arrogantly crediting one’s own ability, but reduces doing one’s utmost and awaiting Providence to everything being decided by God. UP restores both human effort and awaiting Providence, as well as self-flattery about ability.
units.japanese: 「…ふ。………人間とは安っぽい生き物だな。……人事を尽くして天命を待ちながら、幸運を得られた時には、それが単なる幸運ではなく、己の技量に拠るものだったと自惚れたくもなる」

description: 稀な博才 becomes a rare genius, dropping the explicit talent for gambling that the narrator connects to Kinzo’s disposition and the family’s recovery.
sourceReading: His contrary disposition surely gave him exceptional gambling talent and enabled the restoration of the Ushiromiya family in a single generation.

units.text: He became aware of human desire, and forbade it. Things that a human wanted to do, he resisted. ......This eccentricity and rebellious sense had surely given him a rare genius, which must have allowed him to succeed in his exploits as he revived the Ushiromiya family in one generation...
units.note: Both still call it a rare genius without identifying the talent as gambling aptitude.
units.japanese: ……この偏屈かつ捻くれたセンスが、きっと彼に稀な博才を与え、右代宮家を一代にして復興させるという偉業を成し遂げさせたに違いない…。

units.text: He recognized human desires for what they were...and guarded against them. Things that a human would want to do, he resisted. ...This eccentricity and rebellious nature had surely given him a rare genius, making it possible for him to succeed in his exploits as he revived the Ushiromiya family in a single generation...
units.note: Both still call it a rare genius without identifying the talent as gambling aptitude.
units.japanese:
人の欲を自覚し、戒める。
人のしたいことに、抗う。……この偏屈かつ捻くれたセンスが、きっと彼に稀な博才を与え、右代宮家を一代にして復興させるという偉業を成し遂げさせたに違いない…。
candidates: Ushiromiya family in a single generation

units.text:
He became aware of human desire, and forbade it.
Things that a human wanted to do, he resisted. ......This eccentric and rebellious sense had surely given him a rare genius, which must have allowed him to succeed in his exploits as he revived the Ushiromiya family in one generation...
units.note: Both still call it a rare genius without identifying the talent as gambling aptitude.
units.japanese:
人の欲を自覚し、戒める。
人のしたいことに、抗う。……この偏屈かつ捻くれたセンスが、きっと彼に稀な博才を与え、右代宮家を一代にして復興させるという偉業を成し遂げさせたに違いない…。

description: 一度では means she did not understand on the first telling, not for a second. Rosa is the continuing subject of 復唱して, but WH has her having it repeated several times.
sourceReading: Apparently unable to understand on hearing it once, Rosa repeats the report’s words several times before grasping that something strange has happened.

units.text: Genji spoke into Rosa's ear, and told her something in a small voice. For a second, it seemed that Rosa couldn't understand what she had been told, and after having it repeated several times, she realized that apparently, something strange had happened.
units.note: MG retains for a second and has the report repeated to Rosa. UP says she could not understand after hearing it once and that she repeated the words back.
units.japanese: 楼座は、一度では何を言われているか理解できなかったらしく、何度か復唱してからようやく何かおかしなことが起きたらしいことを理解する。

units.text: Genji...whispered something into Rosa's ear. For a second, it seemed Rosa couldn't understand what she'd been told. After having it repeated several times, she realized that apparently, something strange had happened.
units.note: MG retains for a second and has the report repeated to Rosa. UP says she could not understand after hearing it once and that she repeated the words back.
units.japanese: 源次は楼座の耳元に口を寄せ、小声で何かを伝えた。楼座は、一度では何を言われているか理解できなかったらしく、何度か復唱してからようやく何かおかしなことが起きたらしいことを理解する。

description: If one only looked at the exterior ... would have seemed becomes Because they could only see it from the outside, it felt.
sourceReading: Judged from its exterior alone, the chapel would have appeared beautiful and pure, inviting a young couple to marry there.

units.text: Because they could only see it from the outside, it felt like a place of dazzling beauty, where a pair of young lovers might want to hold a ceremony.
units.note: MG removes the false restriction and says Just looking at it from the outside, but still presents the impression as actual rather than the source’s exterior-only hypothetical. UP restores the conditional viewpoint with If all she knew of it was its appearance from the outside, it might have felt.
units.japanese: 外観を見るだけだったなら、若い恋人たちが挙式をしてみたくなるような、美しく清らかなものに感じられただろう。
candidates: Because they could only see it from the outside, it felt

units.text: Just looking at it from the outside, it seemed a place of dazzling beauty, where a pair of young lovers might want to get married.
units.note: MG removes the false restriction and says Just looking at it from the outside, but still presents the impression as actual rather than the source’s exterior-only hypothetical. UP restores the conditional viewpoint with If all she knew of it was its appearance from the outside, it might have felt.
units.japanese: 外観を見るだけだったなら、若い恋人たちが挙式をしてみたくなるような、美しく清らかなものに感じられただろう。
candidates: looking at it from the outside

description: Japanese describes something like a creepy sticky paint suggesting blood. WH identifies the medium as creepy stringy paint, retaining the blood resemblance but removing the uncertainty about what it is.
sourceReading: A huge magic-circle-like design is drawn using an unsettling sticky substance resembling paint and suggesting blood.

units.text: On the door at the entrance to the chapel, was something very large, ...drawn with a creepy, stringy paint that made one think of blood, ...something like a creepy magic circle.
units.note: MG still identifies the substance as paint. UP calls it a paint-like substance and retains both its sticky quality and resemblance to blood.
units.japanese: 礼拝堂の入り口の扉に、……大きく大きく、……血を思わせるネバついた不気味な塗料のようなもので、…不気味な魔法陣のようなものが描かれていたからだ。

units.text: On the door at the entrance to the chapel... was something very large, ...drawn with a creepy, stringy paint that made one think of blood... ...Something like a creepy magic circle.
units.note: MG still identifies the substance as paint. UP calls it a paint-like substance and retains both its sticky quality and resemblance to blood.
units.japanese: 礼拝堂の入り口の扉に、……大きく大きく、……血を思わせるネバついた不気味な塗料のようなもので、…不気味な魔法陣のようなものが描かれていたからだ。

description: After saying she will check Maria, Rosa tells the servants to inform Krauss and the others and receive instructions. WH instead says I’ll tell Krauss and then we’ll follow their instructions.
sourceReading: I will go check on Maria. Also notify Krauss and the others, and get their instructions about what to do next.

units.text: "What are you doing?!!  I'll go check on Maria and come back!  Then, I'll tell Krauss nii-san and the rest.  After that, we'll follow their instructions!"
units.note: Both now have Rosa say that she will check Maria while ordering the servants to inform Krauss and the others and receive or follow their instructions.
units.japanese: 「何やってんのよッ！！　私は真里亞の様子を見てきます！　それから、蔵臼兄さんたちにも知らせて。以後の対応の指示を受けて！」

description: We search ... but uses present search for 探しては見た, an already attempted search.
sourceReading: We looked for a window through which we could enter, but ... If we are to inspect inside, I think we must break a window.

units.text: "We search to see whether there was a window through which we could enter, but...I think that, in order to check inside, we would have to break one of the windows...  What do you think?"
units.note: Both use searched and correctly present the servants’ search for an entry window as already attempted before they report that breaking one would be necessary.
units.japanese: 「入れる窓などがないか、探しては見たのですが…。もし中を確認するのでしたら、窓を破らなければならないかと思います…。いかがいたしましょう。」
candidates: window through which we could enter

description: If asked whether these really were those people becomes if someone told you that.
sourceReading: They were recognizable at a glance, but to affirm that they definitely were those people one would have to approach and check.

units.text: But if someone told you that, you'd still have to go even closer and check. ......Because they seemed almost like dolls.
units.note: MG recasts the caveat as wanting to be sure and needing to check more closely; UP directly restores being asked whether the figures definitely are those people. Neither retains the erroneous response to someone telling them the identity.
units.japanese: だが、それが間違いなくそうかと言われたら、もっと近付いて確認しなくてはならなかった。

description: Even if they deliberately ignored the visitors becomes even if Rosa and the rest assumed they were being ignored.
sourceReading: Even someone determined to ignore them would normally show some reaction; the total absence of reaction prompts the doll impression.

units.text: Rosa and the rest had opened the door, entered all at once with the sound of many footsteps, and called out, asking if anyone was there. ...And yet, there had been no reaction. ...Even if Rosa and the rest assumed that they were being ignored, normally you'd expect there to be some kind of reaction. ......And there hadn't even been that. So at first, it felt like someone had set down some dolls that looked a lot like them...
units.note: MG still makes the condition the observers’ assumption. UP restores the hypothetical that the seated people themselves had chosen to ignore the arrivals.
units.japanese: …仮に無視を決め込んでいたとしても、普通なら少しは何かの反応を示す。

units.text: Rosa and the rest had opened the door, entered all at once with the sound of many footsteps, and called out, asking if anyone was there. ...And yet, there had been no reaction. ...Even if Rosa and the rest assumed they were being ignored, you'd still expect there to be some kind of reaction. ...And there hadn't even been that. So at first, it felt like someone had set down some dolls that greatly resembled those people...
units.note: MG still makes the condition the observers’ assumption. UP restores the hypothetical that the seated people themselves had chosen to ignore the arrivals.
units.japanese: 扉を開き、どやどやと入り込み、誰かいないかと声を掛けた。…にもかかわらず、何の反応も示さない。…仮に無視を決め込んでいたとしても、普通なら少しは何かの反応を示す。……それすらもないのだ。だから第一印象は、彼らによく似た人形が座らせられていると、そう感じたのだ…。
candidates: Rosa and the rest assumed they were being ignored

description: 可愛らしい飲み物の器 describes the attractive drinking vessels. WH changes this to glasses with lovely drinks, shifting the property onto their contents and supplying drinks.
sourceReading: Sweets arranged on plates and cute drinking vessels reinforce the party setting.

units.text: Plates piled up with sweets, glasses with lovely drinks. Several ornaments in the shape of pumpkins... ...They were all decorated in a Halloween style, ...and while it might have been pointless to imagine at a time like this..., she thought that this would surely have made Maria happy if she could see it.
units.note: MG restores the adjective to the vessels with cute pitchers, though it narrows the generic vessels to pitchers and still supplies drinks. UP retains glasses with lovely drinks, leaving the attractive quality on the contents.
units.japanese: お皿に盛り付けられたお菓子や、可愛らしい飲み物の器。

units.text: Plates piled up with sweets, cute pitchers with drinks. All kinds of pumpkin-shaped ornaments... ...They were all decorated in a Halloween style, ...and while this probably wasn't the time to be thinking it, Maria would surely have been delighted to see all this.
units.note: MG restores the adjective to the vessels with cute pitchers, though it narrows the generic vessels to pitchers and still supplies drinks. UP retains glasses with lovely drinks, leaving the attractive quality on the contents.

お皿に盛り付けられたお菓子や、可愛らしい飲み物の器。

description: ラムネ in the list of wrapped sweets becomes sodas, then soda in the spilled sweets and tactile list.
sourceReading: Ramune here are sweets: they are listed with candies, cookies, and chocolates, described as spilling out bloodstained, and contrasted with the sensation of something stepped on.

units.text: When she approached even closer to them, ......she realized that candies were scattered all over the floor. They were all candies, cookies, sodas and chocolates, with very fantasy-styled wrappings... And they were all distributed across the carpet, which was covered with blackberry and cranberry jam...
units.note: MG repeatedly retains soda among solid wrapped and spilled sweets. UP consistently uses fizzy lemon sweets in the initial list, the bloody spill and Rosa’s tactile inventory.
units.japanese: それはとてもファンシーな包み紙に包んだ飴玉や、クッキー、ラムネにチョコレート…。

units.text: When she approached even closer to them, ...she realized that there were snacks scattered all over the floor. Candies, cookies, soda and chocolates, ...all with heavily fantasy-themed packaging... They were all scattered across a carpet covered with blackberry and cranberry jam...
units.note: MG repeatedly retains soda among solid wrapped and spilled sweets. UP consistently uses fizzy lemon sweets in the initial list, the bloody spill and Rosa’s tactile inventory.
units.japanese:
彼らにさらに近付くと、……床にたくさんのお菓子が散らばっているのがわかった。それはとてもファンシーな包み紙に包まれた飴玉や、クッキー、ラムネにチョコレート…。そして、それらはブラックベリーとクランベリーのジャムいっぱいの絨毯の上にばら撒かれていた…。

それだけじゃない。彼らのそのお腹から、……まるで、……まるで！
溢れ出すように！！　お、…お菓子が！飴玉やクッキー、ラムネやチョコレートが、……溢れ出して、血まみれになって、床にばら撒かれているのだ！！
　今、踏みつけたものは何、飴でもクッキーでもラムネでもチョコレートでもない踏み応え！！あぁあああぁ私は恐ろしくて何を踏んづけたのか足の裏を見ることもできないッ！！あああぁあわあああきぃいやぁああああああああぁあああああッ！！！

units.text: And that wasn't all. Out of their stomachs, ...it was almost as though...almost as though... as though they'd poured out...!! A-As though snacks had overflowed from there!! Candies and cookies, soda and chocolates... had poured out, stained with blood, and had scattered across the floor!!
units.note: MG repeatedly retains soda among solid wrapped and spilled sweets. UP consistently uses fizzy lemon sweets in the initial list, the bloody spill and Rosa’s tactile inventory.

description: 苦楽を共にしてきた modifies the siblings/partners with whom Rosa shared life’s joys and hardships. WH relocates it to her present gaze as with a mixture of pleasure and pain.
sourceReading: After the servants leave, she looks again at the fantastical deaths of the siblings and spouses with whom she has shared joys and hardships; despite the horror she finds herself wanting to call the scene beautiful.

units.text: The servants accepted their orders and dashed outside. After watching them leave, ............Rosa once again fixedly cast her eyes upon those fantastical deaths of her siblings and their partners with a mixture of pleasure and pain.  Even though there could be nothing more tragic, ...for some reason, she wanted to describe it as beautiful.........
units.note: Both attach good times and bad or life’s joys and sorrows to Rosa’s shared history with her siblings, then separately describe her present temptation to call the deaths beautiful.
units.japanese: 楼座はそれを見届けてから、……………苦楽を共にしてきた兄弟とその伴侶たちの、……悲惨この上ないのに、…なぜか美しいと形容してしまいたくなる、幻想的な死を、もう一度まじまじと目にするのだった………。

description: 寝惚けて夢でも見たに決まってんぜ explicitly asserts he must have dreamed it. WH substitutes Looks like you were a little more than half-asleep.
sourceReading: Why would toothpaste be in Maria’s bag? You must have dreamed it while half asleep.

units.text: "Why would there be a tube of toothpaste in Maria's handbag?  Looks like you were a little more than half-asleep."
units.note: MG retains the more-than-half-asleep substitution. UP restores Jessica’s assertion that Battler dreamed the whole thing, while its separately recorded vulgar addition is not needed to correct this parent error.
units.japanese: 「何で歯磨きのチューブが真里亞の手提げに入ってるんだよ。寝惚けて夢でも見たに決まってんぜ。」
candidates: Looks like you were a little more than half-asleep

units.text: "Why would there be a tube of toothpaste in Maria's handbag? Looks like you were a little more than half-asleep."
units.note: MG retains the more-than-half-asleep substitution. UP restores Jessica’s assertion that Battler dreamed the whole thing, while its separately recorded vulgar addition is not needed to correct this parent error.
units.japanese: 「何で歯磨きのチューブが真里亞の手提げに入ってるんだよ。寝惚けて夢でも見たに決まってんぜ」

description: 封筒が破かれている becomes someone had opened an envelope, dropping the torn state and supplying an explicit opening agent.
sourceReading: Maria wakes first and makes a fuss that the carefully kept envelope has been torn.

units.text: Battler vaguely remembered Rosa entering the cousins' room. And Maria, who had woken up first, had started rampaging around, saying that someone had opened an envelope that she had been keeping safe. ...And then they had decided that Rosa had come and opened the envelope.
units.note: Both say someone had opened the envelope, omitting Maria’s direct observation that it was torn and supplying an opening agent before the cousins infer Rosa’s involvement.
units.japanese: そして、一番に起きた真里亞が、大事にしまっていた封筒が破かれていると言って、大騒ぎを始めた。

units.text: Battler vaguely remembered Rosa entering the cousins' room. Also, when Maria woke up before the rest of them, she'd started rampaging around, saying that someone had opened the envelope she'd been keeping safe. ...Putting two and two together, they figured that Rosa had probably come and opened the envelope.
units.note: Both say someone had opened the envelope, omitting Maria’s direct observation that it was torn and supplying an opening agent before the cousins infer Rosa’s involvement.
units.japanese: 戦人は楼座がいとこ部屋に入ってきたのをぼんやり覚えていた。そして、一番に起きた真里亞が、大事にしまっていた封筒が破かれていると言って、大騒ぎを始めた。…それで、楼座がやってきて開封したのではないかということになったのだ。

units.text: Battler vaguely remembered Rosa entering the cousins' room. And Maria, who had woken up first, had started rampaging around, saying that someone had opened the envelope that she had been keeping safe. ...And so they had started wondering whether Rosa might have come and opened it.
units.note: Both say someone had opened the envelope, omitting Maria’s direct observation that it was torn and supplying an opening agent before the cousins infer Rosa’s involvement.
units.japanese: 戦人は楼座がいとこ部屋に入ってきたのをぼんやり覚えていた。そして、一番に起きた真里亞が、大事にしまっていた封筒が破かれていると言って、大騒ぎを始めた。…それで、楼座がやってきて開封したのではないかということになったのだ。

description: 眼中にないかのようだった becomes ignored Jessica, converting apparent lack of attention into an unqualified act of ignoring.
sourceReading: The two servants seemed not even to notice Jessica waving; only after the exchange with Nanjo does Kanon finally notice her and bow.

units.text: But the two servants ignored Jessica as she waved her hand. Gohda flew into the servant room, and after Kanon noticed that Nanjo was there, he bowed and approached Nanjo at a quick pace, whispering something into his ear.
units.note: MG says the servants seemed to have bigger things on their minds and later has Kanon finally notice Jessica, retaining apparent inattention. UP directly says they ignored Jessica.
units.japanese: しかし、二人の使用人は手を振る朱志香など眼中にないかのようだった。

units.text: But the two servants ignored Jessica as she waved her hand. Gohda flew into the servant room, and Kanon, noticing that Nanjo was here, bowed and approached him at a quick pace, and whispered something into his ear.
units.note: MG says the servants seemed to have bigger things on their minds and later has Kanon finally notice Jessica, retaining apparent inattention. UP directly says they ignored Jessica.
units.japanese: しかし、二人の使用人は手を振る朱志香など眼中にないかのようだった。郷田は使用人室に飛び込み、嘉音は南條の姿を認めると、一礼してから早足に近付き、耳元で何かを小声で告げた。

description: 趣味が悪い is rendered how bad a hobby can be, treating 趣味 as a pastime rather than taste in this evaluative phrase.
sourceReading: There is a limit even to bad taste. Taking their lives should have been enough, without the grotesque staging.

units.text: "......What the hell is this.........there's a limit to how bad a hobby can be...  Isn't taking someone's life enough... ......What the hell is this!!
units.note: MG explicitly says the staging goes beyond bad taste. UP uses degenerate for the same condemnation, avoiding the erroneous hobby reading while intensifying its moral register.
units.japanese: 「……何だよこりゃあ…。……趣味が悪ぃにも程があるじゃねぇかよ…。命を奪うならそれで充分事足りただろうがよ…。

description: The source describes Maria as stunned by the scene and seemingly having forgotten emotion; Rosa hugs her. WH makes she had forgotten her shock naturally refer to Rosa and replaces emotional blankness with forgotten shock.
sourceReading: Hugging Maria, who was stunned and seemed to have lost all emotion, Rosa wept for the children and their parents.

units.text: While she hugged Maria as though she had forgotten her shock at the horrible scene, Rosa cried for them and their parents. The four groaning and crying voices, their sadness, ...continued to echo in a place which should have known God's love......
units.note: Both explicitly attach the shocked emotional blankness to Maria while Rosa hugs her and cries for the children and their parents.
units.japanese: 惨状に呆然とし、感情を忘れてしまったかのような真里亞を抱きしめながら、楼座は彼らとその両親のためにぼろぼろと涙を零すのだった。

description: よく拝んでおけ ... 父親たちが殺されたことを becomes Worship me, without a doubt, your father and the rest have been killed. The object is incorrectly supplied as me and the inspection command disappears.
sourceReading: Take a good look at the fact that your father and the others really have been killed. The preserved faces allow recognition.

units.text: Worship me, without a doubt, your father and the rest have been killed!!" "R......eally, that's a great service, I'm so happy!!
units.note: Both direct Battler to take a good look at the intact faces and confirm that his father and the others were killed; neither supplies Beatrice as an object of worship.
units.japanese:
(よく拝んでおけ、間違いなく父親たちが殺/・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・)
(されたことを/・・・・・・)！！」
candidates: Worship me, without a doubt, your father and the rest have been killed

description: 身代わりの死体 becomes fake corpses. The source hypothesis concerns other bodies used as substitutes to create an alibi, not necessarily artificial or non-dead objects.
sourceReading: Because the faces were crushed, substitute corpses could have been prepared to construct an alibi; without eliminating that possibility a human-culprit theory can survive.

units.text: "Do you know why?  When you denied my existence in the last game, you thought in a certain way. 'Their faces were crushed, so the identity of the corpses couldn't be checked' 'Therefore, the possibility that fake corpses had been prepared to create an alibi cannot be eliminated' 'As long as that possibility can't be denied a human culprit theory could apply!!" "What did you saaaaaay......!!"
units.note: Both continue to call the hypothetical substitutes fake corpses while preserving the surrounding identity, alibi and human-culprit argument.
units.japanese:
“(だから身代わりの死体を用意してアリバイ/・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・)
(を作った可能性が否定できない/・・・・・・・・・・・・・・)”

units.text: you used this line of thinking..." ""Their faces were crushed, so the identity of the corpses can't be confirmed." "Therefore, we can't eliminate the possibility that fake corpses were prepared to create an alibi." "Unless that possibility's denied, a human culprit theory can still be built!!""
units.note: Both continue to call the hypothetical substitutes fake corpses while preserving the surrounding identity, alibi and human-culprit argument.
units.japanese: 「それは、“顔面が潰され、遺体の身元が確認できない”“だから身代わりの死体を用意してアリバイを作った可能性が否定できない”“その可能性が排除できない限り、人間犯人説は維持できる”！！」

units.text: "That is: "Their faces are crushed, so the identities of the corpses cannot be confirmed"; "therefore, the possibility that fake corpses had been prepared to create an alibi cannot be eliminated"; "as long as that possibility cannot be excluded, the human culprit theory can be maintained"!!"
units.note: Both continue to call the hypothetical substitutes fake corpses while preserving the surrounding identity, alibi and human-culprit argument.
units.japanese: 「それは、“顔面が潰され、遺体の身元が確認できない”“だから身代わりの死体を用意してアリバイを作った可能性が否定できない”“その可能性が排除できない限り、人間犯人説は維持できる”！！」

description: Both instances of 怒り are translated hatred. This shifts an immediate angry response and its possible defensive function toward a more enduring hostile attitude.
sourceReading: Perhaps this was escapist anger to blot out grief rather than pure anger; it nevertheless gives George and Jessica some courage.

units.text: Rather than genuine hatred, maybe it was more of an evasive hatred to blot out his sadness. ......However, it gave a little courage to George and Jessica, who had been crushed by sadness.
units.note: MG uses anger for both Battler’s evasive response and Jessica covering grief. UP retains hatred for Battler’s first response but uses anger for Jessica’s later parallel, correcting one of the parent finding’s two occurrences.
units.japanese: それは、純粋な怒りというよりは、悲しみを塗り潰すための逃避的な怒りだったかもしれない。

units.text: Rather than pure hatred, maybe it was more of an evasive hatred to blot out his sadness. ......However, it gave a little courage to George and Jessica, who were being crushed by sadness.
units.note: MG uses anger for both Battler’s evasive response and Jessica covering grief. UP retains hatred for Battler’s first response but uses anger for Jessica’s later parallel, correcting one of the parent finding’s two occurrences.
units.japanese: それは、純粋な怒りというよりは、悲しみを塗り潰すための逃避的な怒りだったかもしれない。……しかし、悲しみに押し潰されていた譲治や朱志香に、わずかの勇気を与える。

description: 加熱した脳みそ identifies a mind already overheated. WH instead has cooling off my brains before they got too hot, making the gesture preventive.
sourceReading: He again slaps his face with both hands to cool his overheated mind, even if the effort may be futile.

units.text: I smacked my face with both hands again, cooling off my brains before they got too hot. Even though it might have been a wasted effort.
units.note: MG cools his brains before they overloaded and UP cools his brain before it overheated. Both retain a preventive threshold instead of cooling a mind the narration already calls overheated.
units.japanese: 俺はもう一度顔面を両手でぴしゃりと叩き付け、加熱した脳みそを冷やした。
candidates: cooling off my brains before they got too hot

units.text: I smacked my face with both hands again, cooling off my brains before they overloaded. Even though it might've been a wasted effort...
units.note: MG cools his brains before they overloaded and UP cools his brain before it overheated. Both retain a preventive threshold instead of cooling a mind the narration already calls overheated.

units.text: I smacked my face with both hands again, cooling off my brain before it overheated. Even though it might have been a waste of effort.

description: Couldn’t to find anyone inserts to after the modal couldn’t.
sourceReading: Jessica searched behind curtains and under the bed but could not find her.

units.text: Jessica, thinking that she might be hiding somewhere inside the room, peeked behind the curtains and under the bed, but she couldn't to find anyone. However, there definitely were signs that the bed had been used, ......it's an odd way to say it, but the atmosphere in the room grew a little softer.
units.note: Both use couldn’t find anyone without the invalid infinitive marker.
units.japanese: 朱志香は室内のどこかに隠れているかもしれないと、カーテンの陰やベッドの下を覗き込んだが、見つけることはできなかった。

description: 柔らかくなっていた describes an already softened atmosphere noticed as an occupancy trace. Grew a little softer instead narrates a change as the room is being searched.
sourceReading: There were signs of bed use and the room’s air had become a little softer, unlike the hard air of an ordinarily empty place.

units.text: Jessica, thinking that she might be hiding somewhere inside the room, peeked behind the curtains and under the bed, but she couldn't to find anyone. However, there definitely were signs that the bed had been used, ......it's an odd way to say it, but the atmosphere in the room grew a little softer.
units.note: MG describes the atmosphere as already feeling soft and contrasts it with an ordinarily unoccupied room. UP retains had grown a little softer, presenting an observed change instead of the room’s existing softened state.
units.japanese: でも、確かにベッドには使用の痕跡があって、……曖昧な言い方なのだが、部屋の空気が少しだけ柔らかくなっていた。

units.text: Jessica, thinking that she might be hiding somewhere inside the room, peeked behind the curtains and under the bed, but she couldn't find anyone. However, there definitely were signs that the bed had been used, ......and although it's an odd way to say it, the atmosphere in the room had grown a little softer.
units.note: MG describes the atmosphere as already feeling soft and contrasts it with an ordinarily unoccupied room. UP retains had grown a little softer, presenting an observed change instead of the room’s existing softened state.
units.japanese: 朱志香は室内のどこかに隠れているかもしれないと、カーテンの陰やベッドの下を覗き込んだが、見つけることはできなかった。でも、確かにベッドには使用の痕跡があって、……曖昧な言い方なのだが、部屋の空気が少しだけ柔らかくなっていた。

description: そんなに私が怖ぇかよ asks whether Beatrice is that afraid of Jessica. WH says You think you scare me, switching Jessica from the feared person to the supposed frightened person.
sourceReading: Come out! How dare you do that to my parents! Are you that scared of me?

units.text: "Let go!!  Damn it, damn it!  Come out, Beatrice!!  How could you do that to Mom and Dad!!  You think you scare me!!  I'll kill you, I'll kill you!!  I'll beat you to death, so show yourself!!!  I told you to let go of me, damn iiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiit!!"
units.note: MG still asks whether Beatrice thinks she scares Jessica. UP directly asks whether Beatrice is that scared of Jessica.
units.japanese: 出て来やがれベアトリーチェッ！！　よくも父さんと母さんをッ！！　そんなに私が怖ぇかよッ！！

units.text: "Let go!! Damn it, damn it! Come out, Beatrice!! How could you do that to Mom and Dad?!! You think you scare me?!! I'll kill you, I'll kill you!! I'll beat you to death, so show yourself!!! I told you to let go of me, damn iiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiit!!"
units.note: MG still asks whether Beatrice thinks she scares Jessica. UP directly asks whether Beatrice is that scared of Jessica.
units.japanese: 「離せよッ！！　畜生畜生ォ！　出て来やがれベアトリーチェッ！！　よくも父さんと母さんをッ！！　そんなに私が怖ぇかよッ！！　殺してやる殺してやる！！　ブッ殺してやるから姿を現しやがれッ！！！　だから離せって言ってんだろッ、くっそおおおおおぉおぉお！！」

description: 待ち呆ける is translated be that senile ... to wait, treating the waiting expression as a statement about senility.
sourceReading: Do you think I would sit here comfortably, idly waiting for you to burst in?

units.text: 'Do you think I'd be that senile, to wait comfortably in this place for you to barge in here?  You're too wild to be suitable for this intellectual night. What kind of faces did your parents, who raised you to be so stupid, make? Yeah, I saw them, they had a truly stupid look just like you. Now, their bellies are full in the land of sweets!'
units.note: MG retains the invented senility. UP renders the taunt as wasting time waiting comfortably for Jessica to barge in.
units.japanese: “私がぬくぬくとここで、貴方が飛び込んでくるのを待ち呆けるとでも？　知的な夜に、粗暴なる貴方は似合わない。

units.text: 'Did you think I'd be that senile, to just sit around here waiting for you to come barging in? You're way too inelegant for this intellectual night. I can only imagine what the parents who raised you to be such a moron must've looked like. Oh right, I saw them, and they looked just as moronic as you. Now, their bellies are full in the land of sweets!'
units.note: MG retains the invented senility. UP renders the taunt as wasting time waiting comfortably for Jessica to barge in.
units.japanese: “私がぬくぬくとここで、貴方が飛び込んでくるのを待ち呆けるとでも？知的な夜に、粗暴なる貴方は似合わない。こんな間抜けに育てた親はどんな顔？うん、見たよ、本当にそっくりな間抜け面。今はお菓子の国でお腹いっぱい！”

description: どんな顔 asks what the parents who raised such a fool look like. What kind of faces ... make instead asks what expression they made.
sourceReading: What do the parents who raised such a fool look like? Yes, I saw them: equally foolish faces, just like yours.

units.text: 'Do you think I'd be that senile, to wait comfortably in this place for you to barge in here?  You're too wild to be suitable for this intellectual night. What kind of faces did your parents, who raised you to be so stupid, make? Yeah, I saw them, they had a truly stupid look just like you. Now, their bellies are full in the land of sweets!'
units.note: MG asks what the parents must have looked like and follows with their similarly foolish faces. UP replaces make with have, but its after raising you still gives the line a temporal expression reading rather than simply asking what such parents look like.
units.japanese: こんな間抜けに育てた親はどんな顔？

units.text: ―Did you think I'd waste my time waiting comfortably in this place for you to barge in here? You're too wild to be suitable for this intellectual night. What kind of faces must your parents have had after raising you to be such a hapless fool? Yeah, I saw them, they had perfectly stupid faces just like you. Now they are in Candyland with their bellies all full!
units.note: MG asks what the parents must have looked like and follows with their similarly foolish faces. UP replaces make with have, but its after raising you still gives the line a temporal expression reading rather than simply asking what such parents look like.
units.japanese: “私がぬくぬくとここで、貴方が飛び込んでくるのを待ち呆けるとでも？知的な夜に、粗暴なる貴方は似合わない。こんな間抜けに育てた親はどんな顔？うん、見たよ、本当にそっくりな間抜け面。今はお菓子の国でお腹いっぱい！”

description: People lament why nobody hears despite their screaming. WH instead describes a call which cannot be heard by anyone, making an inability assertion.
sourceReading: Kanon hears the voiceless plea of grieving people who lament that nobody hears them however much they cry out.

units.text: Probably, Jessica no longer had the willpower to call for help. ......But Kanon heard it. ...He definitely heard it. ......Kanon definitely heard that voiceless call for help, which is shared by those from across the world who are grieving, and which cannot be heard by anyone even though they scream and scream.
units.note: MG says no one ever seems to hear the endless scream, keeping the failed hearing within the sufferers’ experience rather than asserting impossibility. UP explicitly says the call cannot be heard by anyone.
units.japanese: ……世界中で悲哀に嘆く人々が、なぜこれほどに叫んでいるのに誰も聞こえてくれないのかと嘆くその声なき助けを、確かに嘉音は聞いた。

units.text: Probably, Jessica no longer even had the willpower to call for help. ......But Kanon heard it. ...He definitely heard it. ......Kanon definitely heard that voiceless call for help, which is shared by those from across the world who are grieving, and which, though they scream and scream, cannot be heard by anyone.
units.note: MG says no one ever seems to hear the endless scream, keeping the failed hearing within the sufferers’ experience rather than asserting impossibility. UP explicitly says the call cannot be heard by anyone.
units.japanese: 朱志香はもはや助けを口にする気力もなかっただろう。……でも、嘉音は聞いた。…確かに聞いた。……世界中で悲哀に嘆く人々が、なぜこれほどに叫んでいるのに誰も聞こえてくれないのかと嘆くその声なき助けを、確かに嘉音は聞いた。

description: ベッドに腰掛けさせる becomes having her kneel by the bed, changing both posture and location.
sourceReading: Kanon seats her on the bed, takes the medicine from the basket on the bedside table, and hands it to her.

units.text: After having her kneel by the bed, Kanon took a bronchodilator from a cute basket on a side table by the bed, and handed it to her.
units.note: Both have Kanon seat Jessica on the bed before retrieving and handing her the bronchodilator or inhaler.
units.japanese: ベッドに腰掛けさせると、嘉音はベッド脇のサイドテーブルの上にある可愛い篭の中から気管支拡張剤を取り、手渡した。
candidates: having her kneel by the bed

description: 父さんと母さんは駄目だけど is rendered I’m all messed up over Mom and Dad. The parents are the source clause’s subject, contrasted with Jessica’s eventual recovery.
sourceReading: Dad and Mom aren’t all right, but I’ll be all right after crying a little more. Her answer turns his question toward the people who cannot recover.

units.text: "............I'm, .........alright... .........I'm all messed up over Mom and Dad, .........but, ......after I cry a little longer, .........I'll be alright............"
units.note: Both still make the clause describe Jessica being emotionally messed up over her parents, rather than her contrast between her parents being beyond saving and her own eventual recovery after crying.
units.japanese: ………父さんと母さんは駄目だけど、
candidates: I'm all messed up over Mom and Dad

units.text: "............I'm... ...all right... ......I'm all messed up over Mom and Dad, ......but... after I cry a bit more... ...I'll be all right......"
units.note: Both still make the clause describe Jessica being emotionally messed up over her parents, rather than her contrast between her parents being beyond saving and her own eventual recovery after crying.
units.japanese: 「…………私は、………大丈夫だぜ…。………父さんと母さんは駄目だけど、………私は、……もうちょっと泣きゃ、………大丈夫だぜ…………」
candidates: I'm all messed up over Mom and Dad

units.text: "............I'm... ......alright... .........I'm all messed up over Mom and Dad, .........but, ......after I cry a little longer, .........I'll be alright............"
units.note: Both still make the clause describe Jessica being emotionally messed up over her parents, rather than her contrast between her parents being beyond saving and her own eventual recovery after crying.
units.japanese: 「…………私は、………大丈夫だぜ…。………父さんと母さんは駄目だけど、………私は、……もうちょっと泣きゃ、………大丈夫だぜ…………」
candidates: I'm all messed up over Mom and Dad

description: 言葉をかけたはずだった describes the words he had spoken intending encouragement. WH says He should have said something, then that would actually hurt her, turning an assessment of the completed exchange into an unrealized obligation and hypothetical consequence.
sourceReading: He had meant his words to encourage her, yet felt that they had instead hurt her.

units.text: Kanon bowed once again, and closed the door... .........He should have said something to give her some courage. ............But for some reason, it felt like that would actually hurt her.
units.note: MG says Kanon thought those words would encourage her but now felt they had hurt her. UP likewise says he thought he had spoken to encourage her and then judges the completed exchange harmful.
units.japanese:
………彼女を勇気付けるため、言葉をかけたはずだった。
…………でも、なぜかそれは、かえって傷つけた気がした。

description: The window is described as cooly calling rather than coolly calling.
sourceReading: The window at the end seems invitingly cool.

units.text: As Kanon repeatedly questioned himself, he walked down the corridor. .........He felt like the window at the end was cooly calling to him.
units.note: Both spell coolly with the required double l.
units.japanese: ………突き当たりの窓が、涼しげに自分を誘っている気がした。

description: 当たり前のような顔をしてそこにいた describes being there as though it were perfectly natural; WH makes this making a perfectly ordinary face. The blink is also omitted from the disappearance sentence.
sourceReading: When he blinks and looks down the corridor, the witch who had been standing there as naturally as could be a moment earlier is gone.

units.text: At that time, Kanon definitely heard Jessica's scream. In the instant he looked down the corridor, the witch, who had been making a perfectly ordinary face until a second ago, had disappeared. ...Right now, it was just him, standing alone in the corridor.
units.note: MG restores both Kanon’s blink and Beatrice having stood there nonchalantly or as though naturally present. UP restores the blink but retains making a perfectly ordinary face.
units.japanese:
その時、嘉音は確かに朱志香の悲鳴を聞いた。
瞬きをして廊下の向こうを見た瞬間、直前まで当たり前のような顔をしてそこにいたはずの魔女の姿は掻き消えていた。
…自分は今この瞬間、たったひとりで廊下に立ち尽くしているに過ぎない。
……そして、守りたい人が助けを求めていて、その人は彼方にいる。
自分のすべきことは明白だった。
それは理屈じゃない。
電気的で反射的。
一切の躊躇も雑念もない。
…守りたい人がいて、助けを求めていて。

units.text: At that time, Kanon definitely heard Jessica's scream. The instant he blinked and looked down the corridor, the witch, who had been there making a perfectly ordinary face until a second ago, had disappeared. ...Right now, it was just him, standing alone in the corridor.
units.note: MG restores both Kanon’s blink and Beatrice having stood there nonchalantly or as though naturally present. UP restores the blink but retains making a perfectly ordinary face.
units.japanese: その時、嘉音は確かに朱志香の悲鳴を聞いた。瞬きをして廊下の向こうを見た瞬間、直前まで当たり前のような顔をしてそこにいたはずの魔女の姿は掻き消えていた。…自分は今この瞬間、たったひとりで廊下に立ち尽くしているに過ぎない。

description: だって ... から supplies the reason for the preceding impression that the butterflies were provoking and mocking the attack. WH begins But, making the cessation sound contrasting rather than explanatory.
sourceReading: It seemed they were provoking her attack and mocking her, because when Kanon arrived and she choked they stopped attacking and danced elegantly around the pair.

units.text: But when Kanon ran towards Jessica as she choked, the butterflies stopped attacking her, and this time, they began to elegantly dance a rondo around the two.
units.note: MG still begins But and presents the attack stopping as contrast. UP begins Indeed and preserves the cessation and rondo as evidence for the preceding impression of deliberate mockery.
units.japanese: だって、嘉音が駆けつけ朱志香が咽込んだら、蝶たちは襲うのをやめ、今度は二人の周りを優雅に、ロンドのように舞い始めたから。

units.text: But when Kanon ran towards her, the butterflies stopped attacking and began to dance an elegant rondo around the pair.
units.note: MG still begins But and presents the attack stopping as contrast. UP begins Indeed and preserves the cessation and rondo as evidence for the preceding impression of deliberate mockery.
units.japanese: だって、嘉音が駆けつけ朱志香が咽込んだら、蝶たちは襲うのをやめ、今度は二人の周りを優雅に、ロンドのように舞い始めたから。

description: 知の咀嚼 becomes the bite of wisdom. The source ties Jessica’s opening and closing mouth to a metaphor of mentally chewing on the incomprehensible.
sourceReading: Her flapping mouth was intellectual chewing, trying to digest something beyond comprehension.

units.text: Jessica couldn't comprehend what she was seeing right now, and her mouth kept flapping open and closed... It was the bite of wisdom, which came from trying to understand something incomprehensible.
units.note: MG retains the bite of wisdom. UP explicitly connects taking in and digesting knowledge to the attempt to understand the incomprehensible.
units.japanese: それはまさに、理解不能なものをわかろうとする知の咀嚼。

units.text: Jessica couldn't comprehend what she was seeing right now, and her mouth kept flapping open and closed... It was the bite of wisdom, seen in those trying to understand something incomprehensible.
units.note: MG retains the bite of wisdom. UP explicitly connects taking in and digesting knowledge to the attempt to understand the incomprehensible.
units.japanese: 朱志香は今見ているものが何なのか、理解できず、口をぱくぱくとさせる…。それはまさに、理解不能なものをわかろうとする知の咀嚼。

description: As a symbol that is was not human uses is where it is required.
sourceReading: Two horns symbolize its nonhuman nature.

units.text: ......But its face was different.  It was, strange-looking... ......It was covered with pitch-black hair, ...breathed rotten breath, and its eyes were filled with the same strange subterranean glow as lava. ...And, .........as a symbol that is was not human, ...it had two horns...  It was the figure of a goat-faced attendant who served the witch......
units.note: Both use grammatical constructions identifying the horns as a symbol of nonhuman status.
units.japanese: …そして、………人ならざる者の象徴である、…二本の角…。魔女に仕える山羊面の従者の姿だった……。
candidates: symbol that is was not human

description: 背筋は美しく describes an elegant back/posture, whereas WH says in its composure, shifting the observed physical bearing toward emotional calm.
sourceReading: Though it looked beastlike while climbing up, its elegant posture conveyed dignity worthy of the witch’s attendant.

units.text: The attendant had looked especially like a beast when it had been crawling up, but in its composure, you could see that it had more than enough dignity to be worthy of serving the Golden Witch. ......And you could tell that it was overflowing with the joy of furniture wanting to meet its master's expectations.
units.note: MG restores the observed bearing with the way it carried itself. UP retains in its composure, converting posture into a mental or emotional quality.
units.japanese: 従者は、這い上がる時こそ獣のように見えたが、それの背筋は美しく、黄金の魔女に仕えるに値する気品を充分に備えているように見えた。

description: 青く静か is rendered a cool blue, retaining the color but dropping quietness.
sourceReading: Truly hot flames are blue and quiet, mirroring his calm exterior despite burning wrath.

units.text: "......Hmph.  ......So you act composed even though you're really burning with wrath?  ...I see, they say that truly hot flames burn a cool blue.  Is that how you are now?"
units.note: Both retain cool blue and omit the quiet or still quality of a truly hot flame in Beatrice’s comparison to Kanon’s restrained wrath.
units.japanese: 「……ふ。……憤怒で己を焦がしているくせに冷静を装うか。…なるほど、真に熱き炎は青く静かだという。今のそなたがそうだというのか。」

units.text: "...Hmph. ...So, you'll act composed, even though you're really burning with wrath? ...Yes, they do say that truly hot flames burn a cool blue. Is that how you are now?"
units.note: Both retain cool blue and omit the quiet or still quality of a truly hot flame in Beatrice’s comparison to Kanon’s restrained wrath.
units.japanese: 「……ふ。……憤怒で己を焦がしているくせに冷静を装うか。…なるほど、真に熱き炎は青く静かだという。今のそなたがそうだというのか」

units.text: "......Hmph. ......So you feign composure even though you're really burning with wrath? ...I see, they say that truly hot flames burn a cool blue. Is that how you are now?"
units.note: Both retain cool blue and omit the quiet or still quality of a truly hot flame in Beatrice’s comparison to Kanon’s restrained wrath.
units.japanese: 「……ふ。……憤怒で己を焦がしているくせに冷静を装うか。…なるほど、真に熱き炎は青く静かだという。今のそなたがそうだというのか」

description: 言い訳に呟いても良いぞ gives Kanon mocking permission to mutter that his feel has not returned. WH asks Is it alright to mutter excuses for how your senses don’t return, losing the directed permission and rendering battle rustiness as nonreturning senses.
sourceReading: You may mutter that you have not got your touch back yet as an excuse, if you like.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*.  ......Is it alright to mutter excuses for how your senses don't return?"
units.note: MG restores directed permission with Feel free and renders the lost feel as instincts not yet returned. UP likewise grants permission and uses the idiomatic not being on your game; its final question mark is awkward but does not reinstate the parent error.
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくくくく。……勘が戻らぬことを、言い訳に呟いても良いぞ？」
candidates: alright to mutter excuses for how your senses don't return

description: 断末魔を発する資格も与えられていなかったのか questions whether the attendant was denied even the right to utter its dying cry. WH questions whether it was given the ability to go into death throes.
sourceReading: Perhaps it had not even been granted the right to give a death cry; it collapses into butterflies without the sound of hitting the floor.

units.text: ......Had the goat attendant even been given the ability to go into death throes? ......As its knees buckled and it fell over, it broke into a bunch of gold butterflies with a pop... So there was no sound of it hitting the ground. Even the person who couldn't understand this battle, ...definitely at least realized that Kanon had been magnificent.
units.note: MG retains both ability and bodily death throes. UP restores the right or qualification relation but still substitutes going into death throes for uttering a dying cry.
units.japanese: ……山羊の従者には断末魔を発する資格も与えられていなかったのか。
candidates: given the ability to go into death throes

units.text: ...Perhaps the goat attendant hadn't even been granted the ability to go into death throes. ...As its knees buckled and it fell over, it broke into a bunch of gold butterflies with a pop... So there was no sound of it hitting the ground.
units.note: MG retains both ability and bodily death throes. UP restores the right or qualification relation but still substitutes going into death throes for uttering a dying cry.
units.japanese: ……山羊の従者には断末魔を発する資格も与えられていなかったのか。……それは膝を落として倒れながら、ぶわっと黄金の蝶たちの群れに崩れ散っていく…。だから、床に倒れる音はなかった。
candidates: ability to go into death throes

units.text: ......Had the goat attendant not even been given the right to go into death throes? ......As its knees buckled and it fell over, it crumbled softly into a bunch of gold butterflies... So there was no sound of it hitting the ground.
units.note: MG retains both ability and bodily death throes. UP restores the right or qualification relation but still substitutes going into death throes for uttering a dying cry.
units.japanese: ……山羊の従者には断末魔を発する資格も与えられていなかったのか。……それは膝を落として倒れながら、ぶわっと黄金の蝶たちの群れに崩れ散っていく…。だから、床に倒れる音はなかった。

description: それに免じ refers to sparing him in consideration of the entertaining show. I was going to overlook that instead makes that an offense to forgive, obscuring the basis for her purported mercy.
sourceReading: The show was entertaining enough that she considered letting him off on that account, but his latest insolence changed her mind.

units.text: "Hahahahahahaha...!!  It was quite an interesting show.  I was going to overlook that, and let you get away, but now your rudeness has caused me to change my mind..."
units.note: MG’s Out of respect for that and UP’s In deference to that both connect the entertaining show to Beatrice’s claimed consideration of mercy.
units.japanese: 「はっはっはっはっはっはっは…！！　充分に面白い見世物であったぞ。それに免じ、見逃してやろうかと思ったが、今の無礼で気が変わった…。」
candidates: show.  I was going to overlook

description: Do not allow me even three blinks becomes Don’t keep me waiting, dropping the concrete extreme speed benchmark in the command to execute the second twilight.
sourceReading: Do not give her time for as many as three blinks.

units.text: "I've had enough of this farce.  Quickly, execute the second twilight.  ......Don't keep me waiting, alright?"
units.note: MG retains the unspecified waiting command. UP restores the explicit three-blink limit.
units.japanese: ……妾に瞬きを三つも許すな？」

units.text: "I've had enough of this farce. Quickly, execute the second twilight. ...Don't keep me waiting, got it?"
units.note: MG retains the unspecified waiting command. UP restores the explicit three-blink limit.
units.japanese: 「茶番は飽きた。第二の晩を速やかに遂行せよ。……妾に瞬きを三つも許すな？」

description: 私の姿を追うこともできないのろま becomes a dunce who can’t even chase me. The taunt concerns inability to follow her movement visually and his slowness, rather than intellect or pursuit on foot.
sourceReading: You are putting on airs despite being too slow even to track my form.

units.text: "*giggle*giggle*!  You're acting pretty smart for a dunce who can't even chase me."
units.note: MG restores visual tracking with follow me with his eyes but retains dunce in place of slowness. UP uses slowpoke and follow my moves, preserving both components.
units.japanese: 「くすくす！　私の姿を追うこともできないのろまのくせに、粋がって。」

units.text: "*giggle*giggle*! You're acting pretty smart for a dunce who can't even follow me with his eyes."
units.note: MG restores visual tracking with follow me with his eyes but retains dunce in place of slowness. UP uses slowpoke and follow my moves, preserving both components.
units.japanese: 「くすくす！　私の姿を追うこともできないのろまのくせに、粋がって」

description: 自己犠牲を気取るつもりなんかなかった denies striking a self-sacrificing pose. WH says she had no intention of sacrificing herself, changing a rejection of pretension into a rejection of the action she knowingly takes.
sourceReading: She was not trying to play the self-sacrificing heroine; she thought using her own back was the only way to protect his.

units.text: But she had no way to block it. ...She had no intention of sacrificing herself.  She thought that there was no way other than this to protect Kanon's back. ............So, she could do nothing but block it with her own back.
units.note: MG’s had not planned on it being some act of self-sacrifice and UP’s had no aspirations to martyrdom both deny intended sacrifice rather than denying a self-sacrificing pose. The following necessity remains present in both.
units.japanese: …自己犠牲を気取るつもりなんかなかった。　こうする以外に、嘉音の背中を守れないと思った。

units.text: But she had no way to block it. ...She hadn't planned on it being some act of self-sacrifice. She just couldn't think of any other way to protect Kanon's back. ......So, she could do nothing but block it with her own back.
units.note: MG’s had not planned on it being some act of self-sacrifice and UP’s had no aspirations to martyrdom both deny intended sacrifice rather than denying a self-sacrificing pose. The following necessity remains present in both.
units.japanese:
でも、防ぎようがなかった。
…自己犠牲を気取るつもりなんかなかった。
こうする以外に、嘉音の背中を守れないと思った。…………だから、自らの背中で受けるしかなかった。
candidates: planned on it being some act of self-sacrifice

units.text:
But she had no way to block it.
...She had no aspirations to martyrdom.
She simply thought that there was no way other than this to protect Kanon's back. ............So, she could do nothing but block it with her own back.
units.note: MG’s had not planned on it being some act of self-sacrifice and UP’s had no aspirations to martyrdom both deny intended sacrifice rather than denying a self-sacrificing pose. The following necessity remains present in both.
units.japanese:
でも、防ぎようがなかった。
…自己犠牲を気取るつもりなんかなかった。
こうする以外に、嘉音の背中を守れないと思った。…………だから、自らの背中で受けるしかなかった。

description: 大道具係 becomes stage manager rather than the crew member handling scenery/large props.
sourceReading: A human actor leaves the production; furniture is carried backstage by the scenery or props crew.

units.text: "......If you were a human, I'd say it's time for you to step down, but since you're furniture, maybe I should say it's time for the stage manager to carry you behind the stage!"
units.note: Both retain stage manager, preserving the broad backstage-removal insult but not the scenery or large-props crew role.
units.japanese: 「……人ならば降板とも言おうが、家具のお前の場合は、大道具係が舞台裏に運び出すといったところか！」

units.text: "...If you were a human, I'd say it's time for you to step down, but since you're furniture, maybe I should say it's time for the stage manager to carry you behind the stage!"
units.note: Both retain stage manager, preserving the broad backstage-removal insult but not the scenery or large-props crew role.
units.japanese: 「……人ならば降板とも言おうが、家具のお前の場合は、大道具係が舞台裏に運び出すといったところか！」

description: また私に殺されちゃうの asks whether he is going to be killed by her again. WH adds You wanna be killed by me again, attributing desire instead of predicting a repeated fate.
sourceReading: What? Are you going to get killed by me again?

units.text: "......*giggle*giggle*, wha-t are you talking about?  You wanna be killed by me again?"
units.note: MG retains wanna be killed. UP uses gonna be killed, restoring the predicted repeated fate without assigning Kanon a desire for it.
units.japanese: 「……くすくす、なぁに？　あんた、また私に殺されちゃうの？」
candidates: wanna be killed by me again

units.text: "...*giggle*giggle* Oh, what's this? You wanna be killed by me again?"
units.note: MG retains wanna be killed. UP uses gonna be killed, restoring the predicted repeated fate without assigning Kanon a desire for it.
units.japanese: 「……くすくす、なぁに？　あんた、また私に殺されちゃうの？」
candidates: wanna be killed by me again

description: それから ... ご指示を仰ぐ means Rosa also ordered them to seek Kinzo’s instructions. WH says After that she ordered us to follow your orders, changing both additive linkage and seeking guidance into subsequent compliance.
sourceReading: Gohda and Kanon are calling police under Rosa’s orders; she has also instructed Genji and Shannon to ask Kinzo what to do next.

units.text: "......Under Rosa-sama's orders, Gohda and Kanon are calling the police.  After that, she ordered us to follow your orders, Master.........What shall we do?"
units.note: MG retains both After that and follow your orders. UP restores the additive Also but still says follow your orders rather than seek Kinzo’s instructions.
units.japanese: 「……楼座さまの指示で、郷田と嘉音が警察へ電話しております。それから、お館様に以後のご指示を仰ぐようにとも仰せつかっておりますが…。……いかがいたしますか。」
candidates: After that, she ordered us to follow your orders

units.text: "...Gohda and Kanon followed Rosa-sama's orders and went to call the police. After that, she ordered us to follow your orders, Master... ...What shall we do?"
units.note: MG retains both After that and follow your orders. UP restores the additive Also but still says follow your orders rather than seek Kinzo’s instructions.

units.text: "......Under Rosa‐sama's orders, Gohda and Kanon are calling the police. Also, she has ordered us to follow your orders, my lord... ......What shall we do?"

description: なぜに６×９が４２になるか becomes whether 6x9=42. The source asks for an explanation of the absurd result rather than testing the equation’s validity.
sourceReading: If bored, consider why six times nine gives forty-two; Kinzo calls this the answer to the mystery of humanity and the universe.

units.text: "Didn't I say they should pass the time as they like?!!  They can sing if they want, dance if they want!  They're even free to hang themselves by the neck or jump into a boiling kettle!!  Until 13 people die, they can spend their time as they like.  If that's too boring, then they can wonder about whether 6x9=42, or something!!  That's the answer to the mystery of man and the universe!!"
units.note: MG retains whether the equation is true. UP asks why six times nine is forty-two, restoring the request for an explanation.
units.japanese: 「何をして過ごすも自由だと言っておるッ！！　歌おうが踊ろうが！　首を吊ろうが煮えたぎる大釜に飛び込むも自由ッ！！　１３人が死ぬまで好きに過ごせば良いのだ。そんなに退屈ならばなぜに６×９が４２になるかでも考えていればいいッ！！　それが人と宇宙の神秘の答えだッ！！」

units.text: "Didn't I say they should pass the time as they pleased?!! They can sing if they want, dance if they want! They're even free to hang themselves by the neck or jump into a boiling kettle!! Until 13 people die, they can spend their time as they like. If that's too boring, then they can wonder about whether 6 times 9 is 42, or something!! That's the answer to the mystery of humanity and the universe!!"
units.note: MG retains whether the equation is true. UP asks why six times nine is forty-two, restoring the request for an explanation.

description: Your words are to good for me uses the preposition to in place of the degree adverb too.
sourceReading: Your words are too generous for me / I am unworthy of such praise.

units.text: "Y, ...your words are to good for me...... ...but, umm........."
units.note: Both use the grammatical too good for me.
units.japanese: 「も、…勿体無いお言葉です……。

description: 終戦の ... is cut off after of the end of the war. WH supplies after the war, committing to a temporal relation the unfinished source does not state. It also drops 初めて from the meeting phrase.
sourceReading: His first meeting with Beatrice was long ago; he searches for the Showa year, recalling the end of the war before his sentence breaks off.

units.text: ...Shannon, copy this.  ......My meeting with Beatrice took place a long way back.  What year of the Showa era was it...?  ...I think, after the war......"
units.note: MG restores first meeting and replaces after the war with an interrupted at the end of the war, so. UP avoids after and preserves interruption with an em dash, but still omits first from the meeting phrase and supplies toward the end as the temporal relation.
units.japanese: …紗音、筆記せよ。……私がベアトリーチェに初めて出会ったのは、だいぶ以前に遡る。あれは昭和の何年だったか…。…確か、終戦の……、」

units.text: "...Shannon, copy this. ......My meeting with Beatrice took place a long way back. What year of the Showa era was it...? ...I think it was toward the end of the war—"
units.note: MG restores first meeting and replaces after the war with an interrupted at the end of the war, so. UP avoids after and preserves interruption with an em dash, but still omits first from the meeting phrase and supplies toward the end as the temporal relation.
units.japanese: 「…紗音、筆記せよ。……私がベアトリーチェに初めて出会ったのは、だいぶ以前に遡る。あれは昭和の何年だったか…。…確か、終戦の……、」

description: 私らに ... できることは何もありません becomes nothing more I can accomplish. The source includes the group rather than only the doctor.
sourceReading: There is nothing more we can do by staying here; leave the scene intact for police investigation.

units.text: "Rosa-san.........There is nothing more I can accomplish by remaining here.  ......The phones may not be working, but tomorrow, the boat will come, and we should probably be able to reach the police.  We should leave this place as it is for the police's investigation."
units.note: MG uses impersonal there is nothing more to be gained, which does not isolate Nanjo, and UP explicitly says nothing more we can accomplish.
units.japanese: 「楼座さん…。……私らにこれ以上ここに留まってできることは何もありません。……電話は不通でしょうが、明日になれば船が来てくれて、それで警察へ連絡できるでしょう。警察の捜査のためにも、ここはこのまま残すべきです。」

description: 許してくれよな asks forgiveness for leaving them in a place that is too cold. WH says At least you were allowed to rest in a cool place like this, reversing regret into a purported benefit and adding permission to rest.
sourceReading: Forgive me for leaving you in such an overly cold place; I will certainly avenge you.

units.text: ".........At least you were allowed to rest in a cool place like this.  .........I'll definitely get who did this...  Definitely..."
units.note: Both have Battler ask forgiveness for leaving them in the cold place and preserve his vow to avenge them.
units.japanese: 「………こんな涼しすぎるところに残してくのを、許してくれよな。………絶対に、仇は取るぜ…。絶対にな…。」
candidates: least you were allowed to rest in a cool place like

description: It does seems uses an inflected lexical verb after does.
sourceReading: It does seem that this complicated the inheritance issue.

units.text: "I wouldn't believe that of Kinzo-san.  ...He was a man much more focused on the living now rather than things after death.  .........However, it does seems that this was the root of all the complexity in the inheritance problem."
units.note: Both use the grammatical does seem. MG introduces separate copy defects in the surrounding sentence, recorded as paired findings rather than attributed to this WH parent.
units.japanese: 「金蔵さんに限ってそんなはずは。…死後のことより、生きている今に一生懸命な方でした。………しかし、そのせいで遺産問題をこじれさせるタネとしてしまったようですがな。」

description: 真里亞を英会話教室に通わせてたんすか asks whether Rosa had been sending Maria to English conversation classes. WH asks will you let me take Maria with me to English class, inventing a future plan and Battler as escort or fellow student.
sourceReading: Had Rosa been sending Maria to English conversation classes? Battler then observes that English should be learned from childhood.

units.text: "Ni-ce job, you can shut up now.  Rosa-san, will you let me take Maria with me to English class?  Looks like it's useless to try and learn English unless you start when you're young after all."
units.note: MG asks whether Rosa had Maria take English classes and UP asks whether she had been sending Maria to them. Both remove the invented future plan and Battler participation.
units.japanese: 「よぅしご苦労、もう黙っていいぞ。楼座さん、真里亞を英会話教室に通わせてたんすか？　やっぱ英語は幼い内からやんないと駄目なんだなぁ。」
candidates: let me take Maria with me to English class

description: Japanese states she was a woman who actually existed decades ago, while the mistress relationship is whispered. WH makes it is whispered govern both existence and mistress status.
sourceReading: Whether truly a witch or not, she was a real woman decades earlier, rumored to have been Grandfather’s mistress.

units.text: ".........The forbidden chapel.  ......Whether or not the witch Beatrice really was a witch, it is whispered that she actually existed several decades ago, ......and was Grandfather's mistress."
units.note: MG’s it’s rumored and UP’s she’s whispered both govern the existence claim as well as the mistress relationship, retaining the scope change.

description: この教会を使うことは生涯ない becomes never use it as a church as long as he lived. As a church adds a purpose limitation to the source’s unqualified use claim.
sourceReading: George conjectures that from its construction Kinzo knew he would never use this chapel during his lifetime, while hoping for a miracle enabling marriage there.

units.text: "...By the time he built this chapel, Grandfather probably knew that he would never use it as a church as long as he lived.  ......But, he prayed for the witch to be revived by some miracle.  And he thought that if that miracle occurred, they could be married here..."
units.note: Both retain as a church, narrowing the claim from never using the building to never using it for that purpose.

description: 何が開かずだ challenges the supposed never-opened status. What do you mean, forbidden challenges a prohibition instead, even though the ensuing argument is that a key opens the door without a miracle.
sourceReading: What do you mean it never opens? We are actually entering and leaving, using the key; there is no miracle involved.

units.text: What do you mean, forbidden?  Didn't we just go in ourselves?  That wasn't a miracle or anything.  We brought the key, clunk, and we're in.  That's all that happened, this is ridiculous."
units.note: MG says So much for it being the sealed chapel and UP directly asks What do you mean, never opened? Both restore Battler’s challenge to the claimed closed status.
units.japanese: 何が開かずだ。俺たちだって現にこうして出入りしてる。それは奇跡なんかじゃねぇ。鍵を持ってきて、カチャリとやって入った。ただそれだけの話だぜ、馬鹿馬鹿しい。」

description: 情報が足りないから様子見 becomes There’s no proof so you’ll wait and see. Insufficient information is changed to the absence of proof.
sourceReading: She mocks waiting because not enough information is available, and rejecting reasoning because some information is uncertain.

units.text: "Ha!  That again?  There's no proof so you'll wait and see?  The information is uncertain so it's impossible to reason...?  Ha, this is always the excuse you humans use when you stop thinking.  What is this pretense, you lowly human?!"
units.note: Both explicitly retain not enough information before Beatrice’s wait-and-see taunt, rather than substituting absence of proof.
units.japanese: 「はッ！　またそれか？　情報が足りないから様子見？　不確定情報があるから推理不能ォ…？　はッ、そなたら人間の思考停止の言い訳はいつもそれよ。人間風情が何を気取るか！」
candidates: There's no proof so you'll wait and see

description: 密室の証明にはならない means his failure to find another entrance does not prove it is a closed room. WH instead says it doesn’t prove that it wasn’t a closed room, reversing the proposition whose proof is denied.
sourceReading: His search establishes only that he could not find another entrance, not that none exists and the room is closed.

units.text: ......But that's just because I couldn't find it, it doesn't prove that it wasn't a closed room!!" "If there was a 'hidden door' or something that I wasn't able to find, your premise is completely blown away!!  In other words, whether I was able to find a hidden door or not, you can never deny that there was some method X by which the closed room could be entered!"
units.note: Both now say Battler’s failure to find another entrance does not prove that the chapel was a closed or locked room.
units.japanese:
……だがそれは、(俺が見つけられなかったと/・・・・・・・・・・・・)
(いうだけで/・・・・・)、密室の証明にはならないわけだ！！」
candidates: doesn't prove that it wasn't a closed room

sourceReading: You’ve got nerve saying that! Mystery fans are scary; Christie is grinding her teeth in her grave.

description: 使って開けた becomes made something ... and opened it. The source asserts use of an alternative tool, not its manufacture.
sourceReading: The culprit opened the lock using something other than the legitimate key, perhaps wire or a lock-picking tool.

units.text: "Arg...... Th, then what about this.  The culprit made something other than a legitimate key and opened it!  I don't know what, but maybe a wire!  A tool for picking locks!!"
units.note: MG retains made something other than a legitimate key. UP says used something other than a legitimate key, restoring the asserted action without inventing manufacture.

description: キングを倒す is translated as the king being defeated, and 倒すように跪け as kneel so that your king is defeated. The physical gesture and comparison become a result and causal instruction.
sourceReading: She describes the resigning player tipping the king over, then commands Battler to kneel in a corresponding gesture of submission.

units.text: "Then shout that you resign!!  When someone gives up and shouts that, it is customary for the king to be defeated.  Come on, do you give up?!  Then proclaim your submission, and kneel so that your king is defeated!!  And then you should kiss my shoes!  There's no greater joy than forcing a man like you to lick my shoes, *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*kakakakakakakakakakaka!!"
units.note: MG restores the player physically knocking over their own king, but then says knock your king over by kneeling rather than kneel as though toppling it. UP preserves both the physical custom and the kneeling comparison.
units.japanese: 「ならば叫べ、リザインと！！　投了者はそう叫びキングを倒すのが慣わしよ。さぁ、降参か？！　ならば屈服を宣言せよ、そしてキングを倒すように跪け！！　そして妾の靴にキスをするがいいッ！　お前のような男に靴を舐めさせるのに勝る悦びはないわぁッ、くっくくくくくくっかかかかかかかかかかかッ！！」
candidates: kneel so that your king is defeated

sourceReading: She demands his resignation, taunts that she cannot hear it, and orders him to say it clearly and loudly.

units.text: ......*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!!  Come on, cry out in resignation.  .........Can you hear me?  Say it clearly in a loud voice."

sourceReading: And here I was wondering what you were going to say—how ridiculous.

units.text: "...If you think about what you're saying, it's ridiculous.  This morning, Rosa definitely took an envelope out of Maria's handbag, and thereby obtained the genuine key to the chapel.  ...It wasn't a fake, as you say."

units.note: MG retains If you think about what you’re saying. UP’s I waited all that time for that nonsense restores Beatrice’s reaction to what she had been waiting to hear, though it freely intensifies her dismissal.
units.japanese: 「…何を言い出すかと思えば馬鹿馬鹿しい。楼座は今朝、確かに真里亞の手提げの中から封筒を取り出し、そこから正真正銘の礼拝堂の鍵を手に入れたぞ。…ニセモノなどということはない」

sourceReading: Now the one-move advantage has reversed; now your king must run.

units.text: "Now I've turned it over with just one move.  ...Now it's time for your king to run, Beato."
units.note: MG says I’ve spun it all around with just one move, retaining a one-move action. UP says the one-turn advantage has flipped over, restoring the positional margin.
units.japanese: 「これで一手差は引っ繰り返ったぜ。…今度はお前がキングを逃がす番だな、ベアト。」
