units.text: "I've spun it all around with just one move. ...Now it's your king on the run, Beato."
units.note: MG says I’ve spun it all around with just one move, retaining a one-move action. UP says the one-turn advantage has flipped over, restoring the positional margin.
units.japanese: 「これで一手差は引っ繰り返ったぜ。…今度はお前がキングを逃がす番だな、ベアト」
candidates: I've spun it all around with just one move

description: 俺は期待したぜ becomes I expected that. The source expresses hopes for her perceptiveness, not a prediction of the declaration she just made.
sourceReading: I had hopes for you: surrendering here would have shown you could read the situation, so I’m disappointed.

units.text: ...I expected that.  ......I thought that if you had resigned here, you might be pretty good at reading between the lines.  ......So I'm disappointed. .........You've betrayed my expectations."
units.note: MG says I expected more from you and UP says I had expectations for you. Both restore Battler’s hopes for Beatrice’s perceptiveness rather than a prediction.
units.japanese: …俺は期待したぜ。……ここで降参したなら、少しは読めてるヤツだと思った。……だからガッカリだ。

description: 人間の手でも可能であることを証明するところまで specifies only as far as proving human possibility. WH gives I’ll prove ... possible by human hands without the stopping-point qualification.
sourceReading: His victory condition extends to disproving the witch through a humanly possible explanation; he need not go beyond that to identify the culprit.

units.text: "But I refuse!!  My condition for victory is denying a witch's existence.  I'll prove that this impossible crime with your magic is possible by human hands!!"
units.note: MG retains an unqualified I’ll prove and only explains afterward that Battler will not investigate the culprit. UP explicitly says Once I’ve proven human possibility, I’m done, restoring the stated stopping point before his refusal to identify anyone.
units.japanese: 「(だが拒否する/・・・・・・)ッ！！　俺の勝利条件は魔女の存在を否定することだぜ。貴様の魔法による不可能犯罪を、人間の手でも可能であることを証明するところまで！！」

units.text: "But I refuse!! My condition for victory is denying a witch's existence. I'll prove that this impossible crime done with your magic was actually possible by human hands!!"
units.note: MG retains an unqualified I’ll prove and only explains afterward that Battler will not investigate the culprit. UP explicitly says Once I’ve proven human possibility, I’m done, restoring the stated stopping point before his refusal to identify anyone.
units.japanese: 「だが拒否するッ！！　俺の勝利条件は魔女の存在を否定することだぜ。貴様の魔法による不可能犯罪を、人間の手でも可能であることを証明するところまで！！」

description: 次はどう遊ばせてもらおうか becomes how will you entertain me with this next one. Her deliberation about her next play becomes an addressed demand for another person’s entertainment.
sourceReading: How shall I amuse myself next? There are still plenty of pieces.

units.text: ".........So, how will you entertain me with this next one?  ...There are still many, many pieces left.  ...*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*...!"
units.note: MG retains the addressed demand. UP restores Beatrice deliberating about how to entertain herself next.
units.japanese: 「………さぁて次はどう遊ばせてもらおうか。…まだまだ駒はいくらでもある。…くっくっくっくっくっくっくっく…！」

units.text: "......So, how will you entertain me with this next one? ...There are still many, many pieces left. ...*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*...!"
units.note: MG retains the addressed demand. UP restores Beatrice deliberating about how to entertain herself next.
units.japanese: 「………さぁて次はどう遊ばせてもらおうか。…まだまだ駒はいくらでもある。…くっくっくっくっくっくっくっく…！」

description: 昨日から becomes since last night, narrowing the stated onset of continuous rain.
sourceReading: The rain had continued without stopping since yesterday.

units.text: In the parlor, which had returned to silence, the only sound was that of the TV, which Maria was watching alone. If there was anything audible other than that, it was the sound of the rain which had continued on and on since last night. Every one of those who had viewed that unearthly and horrible scene stayed silent, as though praying that the events of this morning were all a dream.
units.note: MG's previous night and UP's last night both retain the narrowing from yesterday.
units.japanese: それ以外に聞こえるものがあったとしたら、それは昨日から延々と降り続けている雨の音だけだった。

units.text: In the parlor, which had fallen silent again, the only sound was that of the TV that Maria was watching alone. If there was anything audible besides that, it was the sound of the rain, which had continued on and on since the previous night. Every one of those who had witnessed that unearthly and horrible scene stayed silent, as though praying that the events of that morning had all been a dream.
units.note: MG's previous night and UP's last night both retain the narrowing from yesterday.
units.japanese: シンと静まり返った客間の中は、真里亞がひとりで見ているテレビの音だけ聞こえていた。それ以外に聞こえるものがあったとしたら、それは昨日から延々と降り続けている雨の音だけだった。この世のものと思えぬ惨状を見てきた者たちは、この今朝の出来事が全て夢であって欲しいと祈るかのように皆、無言を貫いていた。

units.text: In the parlor, which had returned to silence, the only sound was that of the TV, which Maria was watching alone. If there was anything audible other than that, it was the sound of the rain which had continued on and on since last night. Every one of those people who had viewed that unearthly and horrible scene stayed silent, as though praying that the events of this morning were all a dream.
units.note: MG's previous night and UP's last night both retain the narrowing from yesterday.
units.japanese: シンと静まり返った客間の中は、真里亞がひとりで見ているテレビの音だけ聞こえていた。それ以外に聞こえるものがあったとしたら、それは昨日から延々と降り続けている雨の音だけだった。この世のものと思えぬ惨状を見てきた者たちは、この今朝の出来事が全て夢であって欲しいと祈るかのように皆、無言を貫いていた。

description: 励ましてやりたいとそわそわ becomes went around trying to encourage everyone. The following inability to initiate unnecessary conversation becomes merely being careful what she talked about.
sourceReading: Kumasawa fidgets, wanting to encourage them, but cannot simply intrude with needless talk and appears to be considering how she could help.

units.text: Because Kumasawa alone hadn't seen that, she acted slightly differently. ...She thought that this silence was more difficult to bear, and went around trying to encourage everyone. ...However, it seemed that she was planning to be of some use, even though she had to be careful what she talked to them about...
units.note: Both later versions restore Kumasawa's restless desire to encourage the group without claiming she went around doing so; both also preserve her constraint on speaking.
units.japanese:
…むしろこの沈黙が居辛く、何とかみんなを励ましてやりたいとそわそわしていた。
…しかし、余計なことを話し掛けるわけにもいかず、自分が役に立てることは何かと思案しているようだった…。
candidates: went around trying to encourage everyone

description: それまでは信じている人はほとんどいなかった becomes I believe there are very few people who believe it very much. Before Kinzo’s decline, hardly anyone believed the legend; English makes a present statement about how strongly people believe.
sourceReading: The relatives began believing after Kinzo’s health failed and inheritance became an issue. Before then, almost no one believed.

units.text: "True...  Supposedly, they thought it would be nice if it existed, and only somewhat believed it.  ......All of the relatives started believing in the Legend of the Gold after Kinzo's health worsened and the inheritance problem came up.  I believe there are very few people who believe it very much."
units.note: Both later editions restore the earlier time frame and the near-absence of believers before Kinzo's declining health made inheritance salient.
units.japanese: 「そうですな…。あったらいいなとは思いつつ半信半疑だったはずです。……親族の皆さんが黄金伝説を信じ始めたのは、金蔵さんが健康を崩して遺産問題が浮上してからです。それまでは信じている人はほとんどいなかったと思います。」
candidates: believe there are very few people who believe

description: そうか、それでかな becomes Really, is that so? George’s tentative causal connection to the gold display disappears.
sourceReading: Oh, perhaps that’s why: remember the three ingots on the chapel table, apparently proving the legend real.

units.text: "...Really, is that so?  Do you remember?  On the table in the chapel.  ...There were three gold ingots.  That alone is worth quite a lot.  Couldn't that truly prove that the Legend of the Gold was real?"
units.note: MG's so maybe that's why and UP's I wonder if that's why both restore George's tentative causal connection to the displayed ingots.
units.japanese: 「…そうか、それでかな。覚えてるかい？　礼拝堂のテーブルの上。…黄金のインゴットが３つあったね。あれだけでも相当の価値があるよ。あれはまさに、黄金伝説は実在することを証明してるんじゃないかな。」

description: どうして黄金が積めるんだ becomes why would they pile up that gold. The source’s potential form asks how the culprit can have gold available to pile up; English asks why they would perform the display.
sourceReading: If they want us to find the gold for them, how can they produce a pile of it? It looks as if they have already found it themselves.

units.text: ".........And something else makes even less sense.  ......If they're trying to say that the Legend of the Gold is actually true, why would they pile up that gold?  ......It's almost like the culprit has already found the gold...and is telling us to try and find it too."
units.note: MG asks how they were able to pile up the gold and UP asks how they could prepare it. Both restore the capability and access contradiction rather than asking the purpose of the display.
units.japanese: (どうして黄金が積めるんだ/・・・・・・・・・・・・)。……まるで犯人はもう、自分だけは黄金を見つけていて、お前らも見つけてみろって言ってるみたいに見えるじゃないか。」

description: 何をさせたいか becomes What she wanted to do. The causative target of the letter is removed; the English also makes the ongoing written demand a past intention.
sourceReading: What she wants you to do is written there; can’t you all read?

units.text: "......Kihihi.  It was written down.  What she wanted to do.  Couldn't anyone read it, kihihihihihihihihihi." Maria suddenly laughed in a creepy voice.
units.note: MG restores the group's action with wanted to make us do but retains past tense for the letter's current demand. UP restores both the causative target and present time with wants you to do.
units.japanese: 「……きひひ。書いてあるよ。何をさせたいかは。みんなは文字、読めないのかなぁ、きひひひひひひひひひ。」

units.text: "......Kihihi.  It was written down.  What she wanted to do.  Couldn't anyone read it, kihihihihihihihihihi." Maria suddenly laughed in a creepy voice. ...I'd thought she had been concentrating on the TV, but she was also listening in, apparently. As she remained facing the TV, ...she very simply told us what we were forgetting.
units.note: MG restores the group's action with wanted to make us do but retains past tense for the letter's current demand. UP restores both the causative target and present time with wants you to do.
units.japanese: 「……きひひ。書いてあるよ。何をさせたいかは。みんなは文字、読めないのかなぁ、きひひひひひひひひひ。」

units.text: "...Kihihi. It was written down. What she wanted to make us do. Couldn't anyone read it? Kihihihihihihihihihi."
units.note: MG restores the group's action with wanted to make us do but retains past tense for the letter's current demand. UP restores both the causative target and present time with wants you to do.
units.japanese: 「……きひひ。書いてあるよ。何をさせたいかは。みんなは文字、読めないのかなぁ、きひひひひひひひひひ」

description: それしか聞いてない means Beatrice asks only whether everyone can solve the riddle, not that Maria has not heard anything else. どうせ無理だろうって思ってるに違いない then attributes likely pessimism to Beatrice; WH says I think it’s just impossible.
sourceReading: Beatrice asks only whether they can solve the epitaph; she must think they cannot do it anyway.

units.text: "Beatrice hasn't said once that she wants the gold.  ......I haven't heard that she's said anything except talking about whether we can solve the riddle of the epitaph or not.
units.note: Both later editions make Beatrice the one asking only whether the group can solve the riddle and attribute the pessimistic expectation to her.
units.japanese:
「ベアトリーチェは、黄金が欲しいなんて一言も言ってないよ。……ベアトリーチェは、碑文の謎をみんなが解けるか解けないか、それしか聞いてないんだよ。
…どうせ無理だろうって思ってるに違いないけどね。……きひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひ。」

units.text: ...Although I think it's just impossible.  ......Kihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihi."
units.note: Both later editions make Beatrice the one asking only whether the group can solve the riddle and attribute the pessimistic expectation to her.
units.japanese:
「ベアトリーチェは、黄金が欲しいなんて一言も言ってないよ。……ベアトリーチェは、碑文の謎をみんなが解けるか解けないか、それしか聞いてないんだよ。
…どうせ無理だろうって思ってるに違いないけどね。……きひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひ。」

description: 踵を鳴らしながら becomes her heels squeaking, replacing the audible heel strikes of her brisk approach with a squeak.
sourceReading: She strides rapidly toward Maria with her heels sounding against the floor, then sharply slaps her cheek.

units.text: At that time, everyone jumped at the sound of a door being closed forcefully. When we turned around, Rosa had suddenly returned, bringing Genji and Shannon. ......Then she rapidly approached Maria, her heels squeaking, and hit her on the cheek.
units.note: MG retains squeaking heels. UP's heels clacking restores the sound of firm heel strikes during Rosa's approach.
units.japanese: ……そして、踵を鳴らしながら早足に真里亞に近付くと、びしゃりとその頬を打った。

units.text: At that time, everyone jumped at the sound of a door being slammed shut. When we turned around, we saw that Rosa had suddenly returned, bringing Genji and Shannon. ...Then, she rapidly approached Maria, her heels squeaking, and hit her on the cheek.
units.note: MG retains squeaking heels. UP's heels clacking restores the sound of firm heel strikes during Rosa's approach.
units.japanese: その時、力強く扉を閉める音がして皆ははっとした。振り返ると、いつの間にか楼座が、源次と紗音を連れて帰ってきていた。……そして、踵を鳴らしながら早足に真里亞に近付くと、びしゃりとその頬を打った。

description: 問答無用 becomes Without waiting for a response, turning refusal to entertain discussion into timing before a reply.
sourceReading: She slaps Maria again without allowing any argument or discussion.

units.text: Without waiting for a response, she hit Maria's cheek once more. Everyone could only stand there, shocked.
units.note: Both later editions retain without waiting for a response and therefore preserve the timing substitution for Rosa's refusal to permit argument.
units.japanese: 問答無用でもう一度その頬を打つ。

units.text: Without waiting for a response, she hit Maria's cheek once more. Everyone could only stand there, stunned.
units.note: Both later editions retain without waiting for a response and therefore preserve the timing substitution for Rosa's refusal to permit argument.
units.japanese:
問答無用でもう一度その頬を打つ。
その様子に、一同は呆然とするしかない。

units.text:
Without waiting for a response, she slapped Maria's cheek once more.
Everyone could only stand there, shocked.
units.note: Both later editions retain without waiting for a response and therefore preserve the timing substitution for Rosa's refusal to permit argument.
units.japanese:
問答無用でもう一度その頬を打つ。
その様子に、一同は呆然とするしかない。

description: 何があるかわからない becomes We don’t know what could be there. In context the Japanese warns that anything might happen.
sourceReading: The culprit is nearby; there is no telling what might happen.

units.text: "......This is Father's.  Because of the current situation, I borrowed it specially.  .........Everyone should understand.  The culprit is still nearby.  We don't know what could be there."
units.note: MG's what might happen and UP's what could happen both restore Rosa's warning about unpredictable events rather than unknown contents at a place.
units.japanese: 「……お父様のものです。このような事態ですので、特別に借りてきました。………みんなだってわかってるはず。犯人はまだ、近くにいるのですから。何があるかわからない。」

description: 取り乱していました becomes was slightly distracted. The source reports emotional disarray or loss of composure, not divided attention.
sourceReading: Rosa reports that Kinzo is safe but somewhat upset or discomposed by the sudden events, and will remain in his room.

units.text: "Father was alright, but he was slightly distracted by these sudden events.  ...Fortunately, he said that he won't leave his room, so he's probably safe.  Now, we should do all we can to gather in the same place."
units.note: Both restore emotional agitation rather than distraction. MG separately overstates its degree as considerably shaken; UP's slightly agitated preserves the source's moderation.
units.japanese: 「お父様はご無事でしたが、突然の出来事に多少、取り乱していました。…幸いにも、部屋からは出ないと言っていますので、安全でしょう。あと、私たちは極力、同じ場所に集まるべきです。」

description: 開かぬ扉 becomes unopened doors. Maria names a power to open doors that do not or will not open, not simply doors nobody has opened yet.
sourceReading: She says the first moon circle has the power to open doors that will not open.

units.text: "......It's the first magic circle of the moon.  ...It has the power to open unopened doors."
units.note: MG's unopening restores the category of a door that does not open but is separately nonstandard English. UP's unopenable doors repairs both meaning and expression.
units.japanese: 「……月の１の魔法陣だね。…開かぬ扉を開く力があるよ。」

description: こそこそと逃げて隠れてる becomes sneak away, omitting the expectation that the culprit would hide after fleeing.
sourceReading: He assumed a culprit would sneak away and hide after committing a crime, rather than remain an active immediate danger.

units.text: "I was naive!!  I knew it!!  Since they couldn't escape the island, the culprit was definitely close by! Then why didn't I get cautious sooner!!  ......I was naive!!  I just assumed that the culprit would commit a crime and then sneak away!"
units.note: MG restores both sneak away and hide. UP says only sneak away after committing a crime, retaining the omission of hiding.
units.japanese: 犯人ってヤツは罪を犯したらこそこそと逃げて隠れてるもんだと思い込んでた！」

units.text: "I was naive!! I knew it!! Since they couldn't escape the island, the culprit was definitely close by! Then why wasn't I on my guard straight away!! ......I was naive!! I just assumed that culprits sneak away after they commit a crime!"
units.note: MG restores both sneak away and hide. UP says only sneak away after committing a crime, retaining the omission of hiding.
units.japanese: 「甘かった！！　わかってた！！　島からは逃げられない以上、犯人は必ず近くにいたんだ！　ならどうしてすぐに警戒しなかったんだ！！　……甘えてたッ！！　犯人ってヤツは罪を犯したらこそこそと逃げて隠れてるもんだと思い込んでた！」

description: 押し込まれている becomes pushed away, weakening the idea of a body stuffed into a hiding place. The search result 人間一人がどこかに隠されている becomes a single human hiding, replacing passive concealment with active hiding.
sourceReading: Kanon’s corpse might be stuffed somewhere in the room; the group searches, but no person is concealed anywhere.

units.text: There was a chance that Kanon-kun's corpse had been pushed away somewhere. At Rosa-san's order, everyone searched throughout the room together. ......But there wasn't a single human hiding anywhere.
units.note: Both editions retain pushed away for a possibly stuffed-away corpse and active hiding for the search's failure to find a concealed person.
units.japanese:
嘉音くんの死体がどこかに押し込まれている可能性もあった。
楼座さんの指示に、皆は一斉に室内を探す。
……だが、人間一人がどこかに隠されているということはなかった。

units.text: There was a chance that Kanon-kun's corpse had been pushed away somewhere. At Rosa-san's order, everyone searched throughout the room together. ...But there wasn't a single human hiding anywhere.
units.note: Both editions retain pushed away for a possibly stuffed-away corpse and active hiding for the search's failure to find a concealed person.
units.japanese: 嘉音くんの死体がどこかに押し込まれている可能性もあった。楼座さんの指示に、皆は一斉に室内を探す。……だが、人間一人がどこかに隠されているということはなかった。

units.text: There was also a chance that Kanon‐kun's corpse had been pushed away somewhere. At Rosa‐san's order, everyone searched the room together. ......But there wasn't a single human hiding anywhere.
units.note: Both editions retain pushed away for a possibly stuffed-away corpse and active hiding for the search's failure to find a concealed person.
units.japanese: 嘉音くんの死体がどこかに押し込まれている可能性もあった。楼座さんの指示に、皆は一斉に室内を探す。……だが、人間一人がどこかに隠されているということはなかった。

description: 施錠できる鍵 becomes keys that can unlock this room. The distinction recurs more sharply when 施錠できる at 68588 becomes could have opened this door at 68590.
sourceReading: Rosa asks who could have locked the door after the attack, given that Jessica’s key remained inside and servants held the master keys.

units.text: "This room was locked.  And the only keys that can unlock this room are the master keys that each servant is holding, as well as the key Jessica had.  ......But Jessica-chan's key was closed up in here.  ...Which means it is only possible that one of the master keys locked it."
units.note: Both editions retain unlock for Rosa's first statement about keys capable of locking the room, but both restore the decisive follow-up that only a master key could have locked it.
units.japanese: 「この部屋は施錠されていたわ。そしてこの部屋に施錠できる鍵は使用人のみんなが持っているマスターキーと、朱志香ちゃんが持っているこの鍵しかない。……でも朱志香ちゃんの鍵はここに閉じ込められていた。…ということは、施錠できたのはマスターキーしかありえないの。」
candidates: keys that can unlock this room

units.text: "This room was locked. And the only keys that can unlock it are the master keys, held by each servant, and the key Jessica had.
units.note: Both editions retain unlock for Rosa's first statement about keys capable of locking the room, but both restore the decisive follow-up that only a master key could have locked it.
units.japanese:
「この部屋は施錠されていたわ。そしてこの部屋に施錠できる鍵は使用人のみんなが持っているマスターキーと、朱志香ちゃんが持っているこの鍵しかない」
「……でも朱志香ちゃんの鍵はここに閉じ込められていた。…ということは、施錠できたのはマスターキーしかありえないの」

units.text: ...But Jessica-chan's key was closed up in here. ...Which means it's only possible that one of the master keys locked this room up."
units.note: Both editions retain unlock for Rosa's first statement about keys capable of locking the room, but both restore the decisive follow-up that only a master key could have locked it.
units.japanese:
「この部屋は施錠されていたわ。そしてこの部屋に施錠できる鍵は使用人のみんなが持っているマスターキーと、朱志香ちゃんが持っているこの鍵しかない」
「……でも朱志香ちゃんの鍵はここに閉じ込められていた。…ということは、施錠できたのはマスターキーしかありえないの」

units.text: "This room was locked. And the only keys that can unlock this room are the master keys that each servant is holding, as well as the key Jessica had."
units.note: Both editions retain unlock for Rosa's first statement about keys capable of locking the room, but both restore the decisive follow-up that only a master key could have locked it.
units.japanese:
「この部屋は施錠されていたわ。そしてこの部屋に施錠できる鍵は使用人のみんなが持っているマスターキーと、朱志香ちゃんが持っているこの鍵しかない」
「……でも朱志香ちゃんの鍵はここに閉じ込められていた。…ということは、施錠できたのはマスターキーしかありえないの」
candidates: keys that can unlock this room

units.text: "......But Jessica‐chan's key was closed up in here. ...Which means the only keys that could have locked it are the master keys."
units.note: Both editions retain unlock for Rosa's first statement about keys capable of locking the room, but both restore the decisive follow-up that only a master key could have locked it.
units.japanese:
「この部屋は施錠されていたわ。そしてこの部屋に施錠できる鍵は使用人のみんなが持っているマスターキーと、朱志香ちゃんが持っているこの鍵しかない」
「……でも朱志香ちゃんの鍵はここに閉じ込められていた。…ということは、施錠できたのはマスターキーしかありえないの」

description: あんまりにございます and あんまりですとも become I did no such thing and no such thing. Kumasawa objects that the accusation is excessive or outrageous.
sourceReading: Are you saying I did this? That is too much—far too much!

units.text: "A, are you saying that I visited Milady's room, and did something so horrible?!  I, I, I did no such thing!  Yes, no such thing!!"
units.note: Both editions retain a denial of committing the act rather than Kumasawa's repeated protest that Rosa's accusation is outrageous.
units.japanese: あ、あ、あんまりにございます！　えぇ、あんまりですとも！！」

units.text: "A-are you saying that I visited Milady's room, and did something so horrible?! I, I, I did no such thing! Gracious no, no such thing!!"
units.note: Both editions retain a denial of committing the act rather than Kumasawa's repeated protest that Rosa's accusation is outrageous.
units.japanese: 「わ、私がお嬢様のところを訪れて、こ、こんな惨いことをしたと仰るのですか？！　あ、あ、あんまりにございます！　えぇ、あんまりですとも！！」

units.text: "A‐are you saying that I visited Milady's room, and did something so horrible?! I, I, I did no such thing! Gracious no, no such thing!!"
units.note: Both editions retain a denial of committing the act rather than Kumasawa's repeated protest that Rosa's accusation is outrageous.
units.japanese: 「わ、私がお嬢様のところを訪れて、こ、こんな惨いことをしたと仰るのですか？！　あ、あ、あんまりにございます！　えぇ、あんまりですとも！！」

description: 郷田さんと熊沢さんのどちらかが怪しい becomes who is more suspicious, Gohda-san or Kumasawa-san. A disjunction becomes an explicit comparative ranking.
sourceReading: With the preceding exclusions, the argument would point to either Gohda or Kumasawa as suspicious, though Rosa says she reconsidered upon seeing the body.

units.text: "In that case, I think the argument becomes who is more suspicious, Gohda-san or Kumasawa-san?  ......I even thought that as soon as I entered this room.  .........But still, I thought it was strange.  Look at the state of Jessica-chan's body.  Doesn't everyone think it's strange?"
units.note: Both editions ask who is more suspicious, retaining a ranking where Rosa says the argument would make one or the other suspicious.
units.japanese: 「こうなれば、郷田さんと熊沢さんのどちらかが怪しいという論法になると思うの。……私もこの部屋に入った最初はそう思った。………でもね、おかしいと思ったの。朱志香ちゃんの遺体の様子を見て。みんなはおかしいと思わない？」

units.text: "In that case, the argument becomes who is more suspicious, Gohda-san or Kumasawa-san? ...I thought that myself right after entering this room.
units.note: Both editions ask who is more suspicious, retaining a ranking where Rosa says the argument would make one or the other suspicious.
units.japanese:
「こうなれば、郷田さんと熊沢さんのどちらかが怪しいという論法になると思うの。……私もこの部屋に入った最初はそう思った」
「………でもね、おかしいと思ったの。朱志香ちゃんの遺体の様子を見て。みんなはおかしいと思わない？」

units.text: ......But still, I found it strange. Look at the state of Jessica-chan's body. Doesn't everyone think it's strange?"
units.note: Both editions ask who is more suspicious, retaining a ranking where Rosa says the argument would make one or the other suspicious.
units.japanese:

「………でもね、おかしいと思ったの。朱志香ちゃんの遺体の様子を見て。みんなはおかしいと思わない？」

units.text: "In that case, I think the argument becomes who is more suspicious, Gohda‐san or Kumasawa‐san. ......That's how I thought, too, at least in the first moments after entering this room."
units.note: Both editions ask who is more suspicious, retaining a ranking where Rosa says the argument would make one or the other suspicious.
units.japanese:
「こうなれば、郷田さんと熊沢さんのどちらかが怪しいという論法になると思うの。……私もこの部屋に入った最初はそう思った」
「………でもね、おかしいと思ったの。朱志香ちゃんの遺体の様子を見て。みんなはおかしいと思わない？」

units.text: ".........But then, I thought it was strange. Look at the state of Jessica‐chan's body. Don't you all think it's strange?"
units.note: Both editions ask who is more suspicious, retaining a ranking where Rosa says the argument would make one or the other suspicious.
units.japanese:
「こうなれば、郷田さんと熊沢さんのどちらかが怪しいという論法になると思うの。……私もこの部屋に入った最初はそう思った」
「………でもね、おかしいと思ったの。朱志香ちゃんの遺体の様子を見て。みんなはおかしいと思わない？」

units.text: "In that case, I think the argument becomes who is more suspicious, Gohda-san or Kumasawa-san?  ......I even thought that as soon as I entered this room.  .........But still, I thought it was strange.  Look at the state of Jessica-chan's body.  Doesn't everyone think it's strange?"
units.note: Rosa's later challenge again asks who is more suspicious rather than which one is the culprit. This is recurrence evidence for the existing parent, not a new unique defect.
units.japanese: 「こうなれば、郷田さんと熊沢さんのどちらかが怪しいという論法になると思うの。……私もこの部屋に入った最初はそう思った。………でもね、おかしいと思ったの。朱志香ちゃんの遺体の様子を見て。みんなはおかしいと思わない？」

units.text: "Then is the culprit Gohda-san or Kumasawa-san? Tell me who's more suspicious."
units.note: Rosa's later challenge again asks who is more suspicious rather than which one is the culprit. This is recurrence evidence for the existing parent, not a new unique defect.
units.japanese: 「なら、郷田さんと熊沢さん、どっちが犯人なの？　怪しい方を教えて」

units.text: "Then is the culprit Gohda‐san or is it Kumasawa‐san? Tell me who's more suspicious."
units.note: Rosa's later challenge again asks who is more suspicious rather than which one is the culprit. This is recurrence evidence for the existing parent, not a new unique defect.
units.japanese: 「なら、郷田さんと熊沢さん、どっちが犯人なの？　怪しい方を教えて」

description: Jessica’s frame of mind lead her uses lead where the past-tense form led is required.
sourceReading: Her state of mind led her to shut herself away.

units.text: "......It would be very understandable if Jessica's frame of mind lead her to shut herself up alone in her room.  And those particulars would also fit with Gohda-san's story."
units.note: Both later editions use led, repairing the tense error.
units.japanese: 「……そんな朱志香ちゃんが、ひとりで部屋に閉じ篭ったという心理は、とても理解できるの。そしてこの辺りの経緯は、郷田さんの話とも一致するわ。」

description: 私ども年長組 and 私たち become a senior like me and to me. Kumasawa’s group-based explanation is made singular.
sourceReading: We older servants are too far apart in age from Jessica to understand her well, and she would not have opened her heart to us—right, Gohda?

units.text: "Ho, hohohohohoho!  A senior like me is far too separated by age to understand the feelings of a young person like Milady very well...  And perhaps Milady did not open her heart up to me.  Right, Gohda-san?!"
units.note: MG restores we and us for the older group. UP singularizes the first sentence to a senior like me, then restores plural us in the following sentence.
units.japanese: 私ども年長組は、歳が離れ過ぎていて、お嬢様のような若い方の気持ちはなかなか汲み取れません…。お嬢様も、私たちに心は開かなかったでしょうとも。ねぇ郷田さん？！」

units.text: "Ho, hohohohohoho! A senior like me is far too separated by age to understand the feelings of a young person like Milady very well... And perhaps Milady did not open her heart up to me. Right, Gohda‐san?!"
units.note: MG restores we and us for the older group. UP singularizes the first sentence to a senior like me, then restores plural us in the following sentence.
units.japanese: 「ほ、ほほほほほほ！　私ども年長組は、歳が離れ過ぎていて、お嬢様のような若い方の気持ちはなかなか汲み取れません…。お嬢様も、私たちに心は開かなかったでしょうとも。ねぇ郷田さん？！」

description: コント becomes rondo, substituting a musical form for a staged comic skit.
sourceReading: Their mutual agreement and ingratiating smiles amount to a deeply unpleasant comedy sketch.

units.text: Gohda-san and Kumasawa baa-chan each rubbed their hands together, affirming each other with forced smiles on their faces. It was a really unpleasant rondo.
units.note: MG retains rondo. UP's unpleasant routine restores the sense of a contrived comic performance rather than a musical form.
units.japanese: とても気持ちの悪いコントだった。

units.text: Gohda-san and Kumasawa baa-chan each rubbed their hands together, affirming each other with forced smiles on their faces. It was a truly unpleasant rondo.
units.note: MG retains rondo. UP's unpleasant routine restores the sense of a contrived comic performance rather than a musical form.
units.japanese: 郷田さんと熊沢の婆ちゃんは、互いに揉み手をしながら、愛想笑いを浮かべて互いを肯定しあっている。とても気持ちの悪いコントだった。

description: 自分の危機感がまだ足りないのだろうか becomes it’s probably because I don’t feel the danger we’re in. A question about inadequate awareness becomes a probable explanation asserting no feeling of danger.
sourceReading: He wonders whether his own sense of danger is still insufficient, and whether he ought to see Rosa’s conduct as natural.

units.text: Rosa oba-san glanced at everyone in turn, fingering the gun like it was a toy... .........She seemed so different from the Rosa oba-san who was usually kind. ...No, it's probably because I don't feel the danger we're in. ...Maybe Rosa oba-san's attitude would seem natural if I really felt how much danger we were in...
units.note: Both editions retain probably because and a lack of feeling the danger, replacing Battler's self-question about whether his sense of danger remains insufficient.
units.japanese: …いや、自分の危機感がまだ足りないのだろうか。
candidates: it's probably because I don't feel the danger we're

units.text: Aunt Rosa glanced at everyone in turn, fingering the gun like it was a toy... ......She seemed so different from the kind Aunt Rosa I knew. ...No, it's probably because I'm not fully aware of danger we're in. ...Maybe Aunt Rosa's attitude would seem natural if I could truly sense the peril surrounding us...
units.note: Both editions retain probably because and a lack of feeling the danger, replacing Battler's self-question about whether his sense of danger remains insufficient.
units.japanese:
楼座叔母さんはじろりじろりとみんなの顔を見比べながら、銃を玩具のようにいじっている…。………普段のやさしい楼座叔母さんからは、その姿はあまりにかけ離れている。…いや、自分の危機感がまだ足りないのだろうか。
…楼座叔母さんのそれが、当然であると考えるくらいでなければ、自分には危機感が足りないのだろうか…。

units.text:
Auntie Rosa glanced at everyone in turn, fingering the gun like it was a toy... .........She seemed so different from the normal, kind Auntie Rosa. ...No, it's probably because I still don't feel how much danger we're in.
...Maybe until Auntie Rosa's attitude seemed natural to me, I wasn't fully appreciating the danger...
units.note: Both editions retain probably because and a lack of feeling the danger, replacing Battler's self-question about whether his sense of danger remains insufficient.
units.japanese:
楼座叔母さんはじろりじろりとみんなの顔を見比べながら、銃を玩具のようにいじっている…。………普段のやさしい楼座叔母さんからは、その姿はあまりにかけ離れている。…いや、自分の危機感がまだ足りないのだろうか。
…楼座叔母さんのそれが、当然であると考えるくらいでなければ、自分には危機感が足りないのだろうか…。

description: 醜い押し付け合い becomes ugly battle of humans pressing each other. The reciprocal imposition of blame is reduced to unspecified pressure.
sourceReading: Blame the nineteenth guest and avoid watching humans shove the blame onto one another.

units.text: "What are you worried about?  Make it my fault.  You can just make it the fault of the 19th person, the mystery guest, right?  If you do, you won't have to watch this ugly battle of humans pressing each other, right...?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG restores humans blaming each other. UP retains humans pressing each other and therefore loses the reciprocal transfer of blame.
units.japanese: 「何を悩む。妾のせいにしてしまえぃ。１９人目の謎の来客のせいにすれば良いではないか。そうすれば、人間どもの醜い押し付け合いを見ずに済むぞ…？
candidates: ugly battle of humans pressing each other

units.text: "What's so difficult? Make it my fault. You can just make it the fault of the 19th person, the mystery guest, can you not? If you do, you won't have to watch this ugly battle of humans pressing each other... *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG restores humans blaming each other. UP retains humans pressing each other and therefore loses the reciprocal transfer of blame.
units.japanese: 「何を悩む。妾のせいにしてしまえぃ。１９人目の謎の来客のせいにすれば良いではないか。そうすれば、人間どもの醜い押し付け合いを見ずに済むぞ…？　くっくくくくくく！」
candidates: ugly battle of humans pressing each other

description: ここにいない者へ仮の答えを求める becomes demanded an answer from those not here. The source seeks a tentative answer by turning to an absent person as suspect, not a response supplied by that person.
sourceReading: Their unwillingness to suspect people present makes them turn to someone absent for a provisional solution.

units.text: But no one wanted to suspect. ...They didn't want to suspect anyone here. That weakness in their hearts demanded an answer from those not here...
units.note: Both editions retain demanded an answer from those not present and omit the provisional-scapegoat sense of seeking a tentative answer in an absent person.
units.japanese: その心の弱さが、ここにいない者へ仮の答えを求めてしまう…。

units.text: But no one wanted to suspect. ...They didn't want to suspect anyone here. That weakness in their hearts demanded an answer from those not present...
units.note: Both editions retain demanded an answer from those not present and omit the provisional-scapegoat sense of seeking a tentative answer in an absent person.
units.japanese:
でも誰も疑いたくない。
…ここにいる誰かを疑いたくない。その心の弱さが、ここにいない者へ仮の答えを求めてしまう…。
candidates: demanded an answer from those not present

units.text:
But no one wanted to suspect.
...They didn't want to suspect anyone here. That weakness in their hearts demanded an answer from those not here...
units.note: Both editions retain demanded an answer from those not present and omit the provisional-scapegoat sense of seeking a tentative answer in an absent person.
units.japanese:
でも誰も疑いたくない。
…ここにいる誰かを疑いたくない。その心の弱さが、ここにいない者へ仮の答えを求めてしまう…。

description: 社会を形成して生きる becomes live by molding themselves to fit society. Humans forming social groups becomes individuals fitting an existing society.
sourceReading: Humans live by forming societies; the narrator uses that premise to explain mutual trust and discomfort at forced suspicion.

units.text: Humans are beings who live by molding themselves to fit society. ......In other words, from the time they are born, trusting each other is genetically imprinted on them. ...It is, unpleasant to go against that.
units.note: MG retains molding themselves to fit society. UP's humans are social beings restores the premise that humans live socially without reversing formation into conformity.
units.japanese: 人間ってのは社会を形成して生きる生き物だ。
candidates: live by molding themselves to fit society

units.text: Humans are beings who live by molding themselves to fit society. ...In other words, from the time they're born, trusting each other is genetically imprinted on them. ...It's...unpleasant to go against that.
units.note: MG retains molding themselves to fit society. UP's humans are social beings restores the premise that humans live socially without reversing formation into conformity.
units.japanese:
人間ってのは社会を形成して生きる生き物だ。
……つまりそれは、生まれながらに信じあうことが遺伝子に刷り込まれてるってことだ。…それに、逆らわされる不快感。
candidates: live by molding themselves to fit society

description: a answer should be an answer.
sourceReading: No one answered voluntarily.

units.text: No one gave a answer of their own initiative. ......However, those who met Rosa oba-san's eyes had to nod their heads...
units.note: MG uses an answer. UP retains a answer.
units.japanese: 積極的に返事をした者はいない。

units.text: No one gave a answer of their own initiative. ......However, those who met Auntie Rosa's eyes had to nod their heads...
units.note: MG uses an answer. UP retains a answer.
units.japanese: 積極的に返事をした者はいない。……しかし、楼座叔母さんと目が合った者は、頷かざるを得なかった…。

description: 断定 becomes claimed. The source explicitly contrasts the excuse of a tentative assumption with an actual categorical conclusion.
sourceReading: Under the excuse that it was only an assumption, they definitively concluded that Kanon was the culprit.

units.text: Rosa oba-san made that claim. By using the vague word 'suppose', ...in the end, she encouraged everyone. Everyone nodded weakly, ............and, under the temporary excuse that they were just supposing it, .........they 'claimed' that Kanon was the culprit who had killed Jessica...
units.note: Both later editions use concluded at the emphasized endpoint, restoring the categorical conclusion concealed beneath the group's temporary-assumption excuse.
units.japanese:
一堂は弱々しく頷き、
……………朱志香殺しの犯人は嘉音だと、とりあえず仮定という言い訳の名の下に、
………“断定”した…。

description: 殺され損じゃないか becomes Don’t you care that Kanon’s dead? Jessica says his death and sacrifice have been rendered futile by the false accusation.
sourceReading: This makes Kanon’s death all for nothing; the dead cannot receive honor unless the living acknowledge it.

units.text: "......I can't stand that!!  It's sad!  It's vexing!!  Don't, ......you care that Kanon-kun's dead?!!  The honor of the dead must be accepted by the living!  It doesn't matter who!  Notice it!  Notice it, I beg you!!  Kanon-kun isn't the culprit!!  Aaaaaaaaaaaaaahh, don't go, don't go, everyone!!  Please, don't let it end like this......!  Don't go, ......don't goooooooooooooo!!!"
units.note: MG's Kanon died for nothing and UP's you died for nothing both restore Jessica's protest that the accusation renders his death and sacrifice futile.
units.japanese: 「……こんなの嫌だ！！　悲しい！　悔しい！！　これじゃ、……嘉音くんは殺され損じゃないかッ！！　死者の名誉は、生者が認めなきゃ得られないんだ！　誰でもいい！　気付いて！！　気付いてくれよ、お願いだよ！！　嘉音くんは犯人じゃないッ！！　あぁああぁぁあぁ、行くなよ、行くなよみんなッ！！　頼むから、そのままで終わりにしないで……！　行かないで、……行かないでぇえぇぇぇぇ！！！」

description: 責任を持たねぇとなぁ becomes I don’t take any responsibility. The colloquial contracted obligation means he must take responsibility, not that he refuses it.
sourceReading: I have to take responsibility for what I say and do; despite lacking an argument, I will act.

units.text: "...I don't take any responsibility for my own conduct.  Ihihihihi...!  ............I'm empty-handed with zero weapons to argue with.  ...But you know, I won't hold my finger to my lips anymore!!  Beatrice!!"
units.note: MG's I'd better take responsibility and UP's I've gotta take responsibility both restore Battler's obligation to stand behind his words.
units.japanese: 「…自分の言動には責任を持たねぇとなぁ。いっひっひっひ…！

description: 指をくわえてない becomes won’t hold my finger to my lips. The idiom means he will no longer stand by helplessly; the English suggests a silence gesture.
sourceReading: Even without a prepared argument, I won’t just sit by anymore, Beatrice.

units.text: "...I don't take any responsibility for my own conduct.  Ihihihihi...!  ............I'm empty-handed with zero weapons to argue with.  ...But you know, I won't hold my finger to my lips anymore!!  Beatrice!!"
units.note: MG's not gonna sit around on the sidelines and UP's won't stand here twiddling my thumbs both restore refusal to remain inactive.
units.japanese: …だがな、俺はこれ以上、指をくわえてないぜ！！　ベアトリーチェ！！」
candidates: won't hold my finger to my lips

description: 楽しそうにメシを作る人 becomes someone who can make food that looks so fun. The observed enjoyment belongs to the cook during cooking, not the appearance of the food.
sourceReading: I have never seen someone look so happy while cooking; Gohda enjoys pleasing people, as Kumasawa does.

units.text: "......I've never seen someone who can make food that looks so fun.  ...You're the same.  The same as Kumasawa baa-chan.  ......Gohda-san likes to make people happy."
units.note: MG says Gohda cooks happily and UP says he looks happy making food, both restoring enjoyment displayed by the cook.
units.japanese: 「……こんなに楽しそうにメシを作る人を、俺は見たことがない。…同じなんだよ。熊沢の婆ちゃんと同じだ。……郷田さんは人を喜ばせるのが好きな人なんだ。」
candidates: someone who can make food that looks so fun

description: 危うく見落とすところだった becomes something I dangerously overlooked. The near-miss construction is replaced by an accomplished oversight.
sourceReading: It is simple; I almost missed it, Beato.

units.text: "It's actually simple.  ...It's something I dangerously overlooked.  ......Beato!"
units.note: MG's almost overlooked and UP's came dangerously close to overlooking both restore the near miss rather than saying Battler actually overlooked the clue.
units.japanese: 「実に簡単なことさ。…危うく見落とすところだったぜ。……ベアト！」

description: 証拠なき断定 becomes statements without proof. 断定 identifies categorical judgment, not all statements, including qualified hypotheses.
sourceReading: He will not allow definitive conclusions without evidence; caution is compatible with refusing unsupported declarations of guilt.

units.text: "............But I won't permit statements without proof!!  Being suspicious doesn't make you guilty, it makes you innocent!!  Of course, the world is filled with wolves.  I won't tell you to carelessly believe everyone!"
units.note: MG's conclusions without proof and UP's a conclusion without proof both restore categorical judgment rather than banning unsupported statements generally.
units.japanese: 「……………だが、証拠なき断定だけは許さないッ！！　疑わしきはクロじゃねぇ、シロだ！！　もちろん世の中は狼だらけさ。人を無用心に全て信じろとは言わねぇ！」

description: 掛かったなぁ becomes Has it gotten through? Beatrice refers to Battler having fallen into her trap, not a message reaching his understanding.
sourceReading: You fell for it, didn’t you? You also promised not to suspect the other servants; let’s see you explain your way out.

units.text: "Has it gotten through...?  Furthermore, you said something outrageous about not doubting any of the other servants.  We-ll then, it'll be worth seeing how you gloss this over..."
units.note: MG's I got you and UP's right into my trap both restore Beatrice's claim that Battler took her bait.
units.japanese: 「掛かったなぁ…？　しかもそなたは、他の使用人たちを誰も疑わないなどと大それたことを言ってしまった。さぁて、どう言い繕うのか見物よ…。」

description: 否定されちまうんだろう becomes I’ll probably deny it as best I can. The passive expectation of being decisively rebutted becomes his active intention to deny.
sourceReading: I expect you’ll thoroughly shoot it down anyway, but first let me confirm the closed-room conditions.

units.text: "Shut up.  ...Let's start right away.  I'll probably deny it as best I can, ...but first let's check the definition of this room as a closed room."
units.note: MG retains you'll probably just deny it, assigning Beatrice an expected act of denial rather than Battler expecting his theory to be rebutted. UP's I'll be denied from all angles restores the passive direction.
units.japanese: 「うるせぇぜ。…さっそく始めるぞ。どうせがっつり否定されちまうんだろうが、…先にこの部屋が密室であることの定義を確認させてもらうぜ。」
candidates: I'll probably deny it as best

units.text: "Shut up. ...Let's start right away. You'll probably just deny it anyway, ...but first let's check the definition of this room as a closed room."
units.note: MG retains you'll probably just deny it, assigning Beatrice an expected act of denial rather than Battler expecting his theory to be rebutted. UP's I'll be denied from all angles restores the passive direction.
units.japanese: 「うるせぇぜ。…さっそく始めるぞ。どうせがっつり否定されちまうんだろうが、…先にこの部屋が密室であることの定義を確認させてもらうぜ」

description: 外堀から埋めてく becomes cover up the moat. The idiom describes approaching the core by first closing off peripheral possibilities or conditions.
sourceReading: He must work in from the outside, starting with the question whether the final locking used a master key.

units.text: "......I hate to say it, but I'll have to cover up the moat.  ...Repeat it.  ......'The last time it was locked was due to the master key'."
units.note: MG retains the opaque cover up the moat. UP's tackle this one step at a time restores the function of proceeding through peripheral questions toward the core.
units.japanese: 「……悔しいが、外堀から埋めてくしかないぜ。…復唱要求。……“最後の施錠は、マスターキーによるものである”。」

units.text: "...I hate to say it, but I'll have to cover up the moat first. ...Repeat it. ..."The last time it was locked was due to a master key"."
units.note: MG retains the opaque cover up the moat. UP's tackle this one step at a time restores the function of proceeding through peripheral questions toward the core.
units.japanese: 「……悔しいが、外堀から埋めてくしかないぜ。…復唱要求。……“最後の施錠は、マスターキーによるものである”」

description: 礼拝堂の鍵 becomes lock to the chapel. She recalls Battler exploiting the key issue, particularly its custody and use.
sourceReading: During the chapel-key discussion, he turned her own rule against her, so she now avoids unnecessary risky red declarations.

units.text: "Back when discussing the lock to the chapel, you completely turned the tables on me.  When I have an advantage, there's no need to go out of my way to use red and say things in a risky way.  That's all it is."
units.note: Both editions retain lock to the chapel rather than identifying the chapel key issue that Battler previously exploited.
units.japanese: 「礼拝堂の鍵の時は、そなたにすっかり逆手に取られてしまった。妾が有利な内は、わざわざリスクのある赤を使って発言する必要がない。ただそれだけのことよ。」

units.text: "Back when discussing the lock to the chapel, you completely turned the tables on me. When I have an advantage, there's no need to go out of my way to use red when it might be risky. That's all it is."
units.note: Both editions retain lock to the chapel rather than identifying the chapel key issue that Battler previously exploited.
units.japanese: 「礼拝堂の鍵の時は、そなたにすっかり逆手に取られてしまった。妾が有利な内は、わざわざリスクのある赤を使って発言する必要がない。ただそれだけのことよ」

units.text: "Back when discussing the lock to the chapel, you completely turned the tables on me. When I have an advantage, there's no need to go out of my way to speak using the red, which carries risk. That's all it is."
units.note: Both editions retain lock to the chapel rather than identifying the chapel key issue that Battler previously exploited.
units.japanese: 「礼拝堂の鍵の時は、そなたにすっかり逆手に取られてしまった。妾が有利な内は、わざわざリスクのある赤を使って発言する必要がない。ただそれだけのことよ」

description: 誘導されているよう becomes being provoked. Battler resents the sense that his reasoning is being led in a selected direction.
sourceReading: It feels as though she is steering him; he asks for silence to think.

units.text: "......Damn.  It's annoying being provoked...  Stay quiet a while, I'm thinking...!"
units.note: MG's leading me by the nose and UP's leading me down a path both restore guided reasoning rather than generic provocation.
units.japanese: 「……くそ。誘導されているようでムカつくぜ…。しばらく黙ってろ、考える…！」

description: Red 出入りは出来ぬ becomes does not permit any form of entry. Exit is omitted from a statement which forbids both directions by any method when the door is locked.
sourceReading: When locked, the door permits neither entry nor exit by any method.

units.text: "Of course, this door is the same as the chapel.  When locked, it does not permit any form of entry.
units.note: Both later editions explicitly say entry or exit, restoring the full bidirectional red constraint.
units.japanese: 施錠時には如何なる方法をもってしても出入りは出来ぬ。

description: 仕切り直しだ becomes I have a score to settle. It means a fresh start or reset before organizing the known information.
sourceReading: Start over; think and sort out what is known.

units.text: ............I have a score to settle. ...Anyway, let me think. I'll lay out everything I know.
units.note: MG's step back to square one and UP's let's back up both restore Battler's reasoning reset.
units.japanese: …………仕切り直しだ。

description: しゃあしゃあと becomes so happily. She accuses him of brazenly pretending not to notice the theory’s implications.
sourceReading: How could he so shamelessly advance that theory while pretending not to notice it implicates his cousins?

units.text: And despite that, how could you act like you didn't notice, and say a theory like that so happily...!  *giggle*giggle*giggle*."
units.note: MG's so happily and UP's with such gusto both emphasize enthusiasm rather than Beatrice's accusation that Battler brazenly advanced the theory while feigning ignorance of its implications.
units.japanese: にもかかわらず、それに気付かないフリをして、よくもあれだけの説をしゃあしゃあとのたまえたものよ…！　くすくすくす。」

units.text: And despite that, you acted like you didn't even notice, announcing a theory like that so happily...! *giggle*giggle*giggle*"
units.note: MG's so happily and UP's with such gusto both emphasize enthusiasm rather than Beatrice's accusation that Battler brazenly advanced the theory while feigning ignorance of its implications.
units.japanese: 「にもかかわらず、それに気付かないフリをして、よくもあれだけの説をしゃあしゃあとのたまえたものよ…！　くすくすくす」

units.text: "Quite impressive—in spite of that, you managed to act like you didn't notice, and spoke your theory with such gusto...! *giggle*giggle*giggle*."
units.note: MG's so happily and UP's with such gusto both emphasize enthusiasm rather than Beatrice's accusation that Battler brazenly advanced the theory while feigning ignorance of its implications.
units.japanese: 「にもかかわらず、それに気付かないフリをして、よくもあれだけの説をしゃあしゃあとのたまえたものよ…！　くすくすくす」

description: 王手飛車取り becomes fork the rook. The source explicitly combines the check on the king with taking the rook.
sourceReading: Battler names a simultaneous king-and-rook threat as the image for the two unacceptable alternatives.

units.text: "......So you're trying to say that there are two options, ...accept that a witch opened it with magic, or accept that someone I know is the culprit.  Damn, are you trying to fork the rook!"
units.note: Both editions retain fork the rook and omit the simultaneous check on the king named by the compound shogi tactic.
units.japanese: 「……魔女が魔法で開けたことを認めるか、…俺の知る誰かが犯人であることを認めるかの二択だって言いたいんだな。くそ、王手飛車取りのつもりかよッ！」

units.text: "...So you're trying to say that I've got two options: ...accept that a witch opened it with magic, or accept that someone I know is the culprit. Damn, are you trying to fork the rook?!"
units.note: Both editions retain fork the rook and omit the simultaneous check on the king named by the compound shogi tactic.
units.japanese: 「……魔女が魔法で開けたことを認めるか、…俺の知る誰かが犯人であることを認めるかの二択だって言いたいんだな。くそ、王手飛車取りのつもりかよッ！」

units.text: "......So accept that a witch opened it with magic, ...or accept that someone I know is the culprit—those are my only two options, you're saying. Damn, are you trying to fork the rook?!"
units.note: Both editions retain fork the rook and omit the simultaneous check on the king named by the compound shogi tactic.
units.japanese: 「……魔女が魔法で開けたことを認めるか、…俺の知る誰かが犯人であることを認めるかの二択だって言いたいんだな。くそ、王手飛車取りのつもりかよッ！」

description: 死に損ないのクソババア becomes hag who wouldn’t be a loss if she died. The source derides an old woman as lingering on or half-dead, rather than explicitly judging the loss her death would cause.
sourceReading: That self-important cook and that decrepit old hag are easy scapegoats.

units.text: "......*cackle*.  So, what will you do, Ushiromiya Battleeeeeeer?  Isn't it actually simple...?  Don't you just have to make sacrifices of that overly self-confident cook and that hag who wouldn't be a loss if she died?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle* *cackle*cackle*!!"
units.note: MG retains the judgment that her death would be no loss. UP's hag who should have died years ago freely restores the insult that she has lingered on past death rather than evaluating the loss her death would cause.
units.japanese: 「……くっくっく。さぁてどうする右代宮戦人ァァアァ？　実に簡単な話じゃアないか…？　あの自意識過剰な料理男と、死に損ないのクソババアを、ちょいと生贄に仕立て上げるだけじゃアない。
candidates: hag who wouldn't be a loss if she died

units.text: "...*cackle* So, what will you do, Ushiromiya Battleeeeeeer? Isn't it actually simple...? Don't you just have to make sacrifices of that overly self-confident cook and that hag who wouldn't be a loss if she died? *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!!"
units.note: MG retains the judgment that her death would be no loss. UP's hag who should have died years ago freely restores the insult that she has lingered on past death rather than evaluating the loss her death would cause.
units.japanese: 「……くっくっく。さぁてどうする右代宮戦人ァァアァ？　実に簡単な話じゃアないか…？　あの自意識過剰な料理男と、死に損ないのクソババアを、ちょいと生贄に仕立て上げるだけじゃアない。くーっくくくくくくくくくくくく！！」
candidates: hag who wouldn't be a loss if she died

description: 俺も死にたくないし ... 見つけ出したい becomes I just don’t want to die, so I wanted to find ... . The two motives are coordinated in Japanese, not an explicit causal chain.
sourceReading: He too wants to survive, and wants to find the real killer of his father and the others.

units.text: "...And sorry, Rosa oba-san.  ......It's not like I wanted to resist you.  I just don't want to die, so I wanted to find Dad and the rest's true enemy.  ......Sorry for saying something that wasn't cooperative."
units.note: Both later editions coordinate Battler's desire to live and desire to find the true killer, removing the invented causal relation.
units.japanese: 「…楼座叔母さんもごめんよ。……別に反抗したかったわけじゃない。俺も死にたくないし、親父たちの本当の仇を見つけ出したい。……協調性のないことを言って悪かったぜ。」
candidates: don't want to die, so I wanted to find

description: 一番戦っているようなつもりでいて becomes the one most ready to fight, losing his qualification that he imagines himself fighting hardest. 真実 becomes reality rather than truth.
sourceReading: He probably thinks he is fighting hardest while actually standing farthest from the truth.

units.text: And me...? I denied the witch. ......But I wasn't prepared to lose anything. I was probably the one most ready to fight, ......and the one most separated from reality.
units.note: MG's seemed to be fighting most loses Battler's self-conception and renders truth as reality. UP restores truth and thought himself, but changes fighting hardest into being most ready to fight.
units.japanese: 多分俺は、一番戦っているようなつもりでいて、……一番真実から遠い場所にいる。

units.text: And me...? I denied the witch. ...But I wasn't prepared to lose anything. I was probably the one who seemed to be fighting the most, ...and yet, the one who was most separated from reality.
units.note: MG's seemed to be fighting most loses Battler's self-conception and renders truth as reality. UP restores truth and thought himself, but changes fighting hardest into being most ready to fight.
units.japanese:
俺は…？
魔女は否定する。
……でも、何も失う覚悟がない。多分俺は、一番戦っているようなつもりでいて、……一番真実から遠い場所にいる。

units.text:
And me...?
I denied the witch.
......But I wasn't prepared to lose anything. I was probably the one who thought himself most ready to fight, ......and the one standing furthest from the truth.
units.note: MG's seemed to be fighting most loses Battler's self-conception and renders truth as reality. UP restores truth and thought himself, but changes fighting hardest into being most ready to fight.
units.japanese:
俺は…？
魔女は否定する。
……でも、何も失う覚悟がない。多分俺は、一番戦っているようなつもりでいて、……一番真実から遠い場所にいる。

description: certain that that the culprit contains an unintended duplicated that.
sourceReading: Jessica’s death convinced the group that the culprit remained nearby and would attack when given an opening.

units.text: With Jessica's death, it became certain that that the culprit was hiding somewhere nearby, and that they would come after our lives if they had a chance. According to Genji-san, when tomorrow morning comes, the boat should arrive. The boat had a radio. We could probably contact the police directly with that.
units.note: MG retains certain that that the culprit. UP removes the duplicated word.
units.japanese: 朱志香の死により、犯人は身近に潜んでいて、しかも隙あらば命を狙ってくることが確実となった。

units.text: With Jessica's death, it became certain that that the culprit was hiding somewhere nearby, and that they'd come for our lives if they had a chance. According to Genji-san, when tomorrow morning comes, the boat should arrive. The boat had a radio. We'd probably be able to contact the police directly with that.
units.note: MG retains certain that that the culprit. UP removes the duplicated word.
units.japanese:
朱志香の死により、犯人は身近に潜んでいて、しかも隙あらば命を狙ってくることが確実となった。源次さんの話によれば、明日の朝になれば船が来てくれるはずだという。船には無線もある。
それで直ちに警察へ連絡できるだろう。

description: 明日以降 becomes after tomorrow, excluding tomorrow from the ordinary English time range.
sourceReading: They will prioritize safety and leave investigation to police from tomorrow onward.

units.text: ...That was probably the right thing to do. If a bunch of amateurs like us investigated, there's no way we'd find anything. It would be wisest to focus on protecting ourselves without doing anything unnecessary, and leave it to the police after tomorrow.
units.note: MG's starting tomorrow restores tomorrow and later. UP retains after tomorrow, excluding the day on which police are expected to become reachable.
units.japanese: 余計なことをせず、身の安全を守ることに専念し、明日以降、警察に委ねるのがもっとも賢いことだった。

units.text:
...That was probably the right thing to do.
Even if a bunch of amateurs like us investigated, there's no way we'd find anything. It would be wisest to focus on protecting ourselves without doing anything unnecessary, and leave it to the police after tomorrow.
units.note: MG's starting tomorrow restores tomorrow and later. UP retains after tomorrow, excluding the day on which police are expected to become reachable.
units.japanese:
…恐らく、それは正しいだろう。
自分たち素人が何を捜査したって、何も掴めるわけがない。余計なことをせず、身の安全を守ることに専念し、明日以降、警察に委ねるのがもっとも賢いことだった。

description: 午前中いっぱい becomes all afternoon.
sourceReading: Most spent the whole morning watching television; boredom and fading vigilance followed.

units.text: We had been tense in the beginning, but other than Rosa oba-san, most of the people had spent all afternoon watching TV and were getting bored, so our sense of danger had grown much less intense.
units.note: Both later editions use all morning, restoring the correct part of day.
units.japanese: 最初の内はぴりぴりしていたが、楼座叔母さんを除き、ほとんどの者は午前中いっぱいをテレビを見て過ごしている内にだんだん退屈になり、危機感がだいぶ薄れてしまうのだった。

description: 大人数 becomes a large number of adults. The source’s inferred limit concerns the number of culprits, without an age restriction.
sourceReading: They infer the culprit group is not large and cannot kill the whole assembled group at once.

units.text: From this, we imagined that the culprit wasn't a large number of adults, and they weren't someone who could kill this large group gathered in the parlor all at once.
units.note: MG retains a large number of adults. UP says there weren't a great number of culprits, restoring the inference about culprit count without an age restriction.
units.japanese: ここから想像できるのは、犯人は決して大人数ではなく、客間に集まった大勢を一度に殺せてしまうような存在ではないこと、だった。

units.text: From this, it was possible to imagine that the culprit wasn't a large number of adults, and that they wouldn't be capable of killing this large group gathered in the parlor all at once.
units.note: MG retains a large number of adults. UP says there weren't a great number of culprits, restoring the inference about culprit count without an age restriction.
units.japanese: ここから想像できるのは、犯人は決して大人数ではなく、客間に集まった大勢を一度に殺せてしまうような存在ではないこと、だった。

description: お皿を持ってきて ... 盛り付けをしたいと言い出す becomes said that he ... wanted to bring the plates and pile them up. He brings plates before proposing to arrange the canned food.
sourceReading: Gohda brings plates and proposes at least to present the canned food attractively.

units.text: As a cook, Gohda-san must have felt very let down. As though he wanted to display his skill anyway, Gohda-san said that he at least wanted to bring the plates and pile them up with canned food. At first, Rosa oba-san had been reluctant, examining each one of the plates that were brought, but she hadn't been able to find anything to complain about, and Gohda's 'Chef's Pick Canned Food Combo Lunch' was born.
units.note: Both editions say Gohda wanted to bring or grab plates before arranging the food, retaining the reversed sequence rather than his arriving with plates and proposing presentation.
units.japanese: それでもせめて腕を振るいたかったらしく、郷田さんはお皿を持ってきて、せめて缶詰の盛り付けをしたいと言い出すのだった。
candidates: wanted to bring the plates and pile

units.text: As a cook, Gohda-san must've felt very let down. Apparently eager to display his skill anyway, he said he at least wanted to grab some plates and arrange the canned food on them. At first, Aunt Rosa had been reluctant, examining each one of the plates that were brought, but she hadn't been able to find anything to complain about, and Gohda's "Chef's Pick Canned Food Lunch Combo" was born.
units.note: Both editions say Gohda wanted to bring or grab plates before arranging the food, retaining the reversed sequence rather than his arriving with plates and proposing presentation.
units.japanese: 料理人の郷田さんにとって、それはよほど残念なことだったに違いない。それでもせめて腕を振るいたかったらしく、郷田さんはお皿を持ってきて、せめて缶詰の盛り付けをしたいと言い出すのだった。最初は楼座叔母さんも渋り、持ってこさせた皿をいちいち点検していたが、文句の付け所が特に見付からず、郷田さんによる、“シェフの気まぐれ風缶詰の盛り合わせランチ”はこうして実現したのだった。

units.text: As a cook, Gohda‐san must have felt very let down. As though he wanted to display his skill anyway, he said that he at least wanted to bring the plates and pile them up with canned food. At first, Auntie Rosa had been reluctant, examining each one of the plates that were brought, but she hadn't been able to find anything to complain about, and Gohda‐san's "Chef's Pick Canned Food Combo Lunch" had become a reality.
units.note: Both editions say Gohda wanted to bring or grab plates before arranging the food, retaining the reversed sequence rather than his arriving with plates and proposing presentation.
units.japanese: 料理人の郷田さんにとって、それはよほど残念なことだったに違いない。それでもせめて腕を振るいたかったらしく、郷田さんはお皿を持ってきて、せめて缶詰の盛り付けをしたいと言い出すのだった。最初は楼座叔母さんも渋り、持ってこさせた皿をいちいち点検していたが、文句の付け所が特に見付からず、郷田さんによる、“シェフの気まぐれ風缶詰の盛り合わせランチ”はこうして実現したのだった。
candidates: wanted to bring the plates and pile

description: 男が何人かで行けばいいだろう ... 言ったら becomes talking about how many men should go. The source recalls the proposal that a few men would suffice.
sourceReading: When they proposed sending a few men for Jessica, Rosa invoked the puzzle and insisted everyone go together.

units.text: What had been happening when Rosa oba-san had said the name of this puzzle... That's right. ...When we'd decided to call Jessica, we had been talking about how many men should go, and Rosa oba-san had mentioned 'Wolves and Sheep Puzzle', saying that we should all go together......
units.note: Both editions retain talking about how many men should go rather than Battler's concrete proposal that sending a few men would be enough.
units.japanese: …朱志香を呼びにいこうってことになって、男が何人かで行けばいいだろう何て言ったら、楼座叔母さんが“狼と羊のパズル”と口にして、みんなで一緒に行こうと言い出したのだ……。
candidates: talking about how many men should go

units.text: So, what was happening when Aunt Rosa first mentioned this puzzle...? That's right. ...When we decided to go and get Jessica, we talked about how many men should go, and Aunt Rosa mentioned the "Wolves and Sheep Puzzle", saying we should all go together...
units.note: Both editions retain talking about how many men should go rather than Battler's concrete proposal that sending a few men would be enough.
units.japanese: このパズルの名を、楼座叔母さんはどういう時に口にしたんだっけ…。そうだ。…朱志香を呼びにいこうってことになって、男が何人かで行けばいいだろう何て言ったら、楼座叔母さんが“狼と羊のパズル”と口にして、みんなで一緒に行こうと言い出したのだ……。

units.text: What had been happening when Auntie Rosa had said the name of this puzzle... That's right. ...When we'd decided to go call Jessica, we had been talking about how many men should go, and Auntie Rosa mentioned the "Wolves and Sheep Puzzle", and said that we should all go together......
units.note: Both editions retain talking about how many men should go rather than Battler's concrete proposal that sending a few men would be enough.
units.japanese: このパズルの名を、楼座叔母さんはどういう時に口にしたんだっけ…。そうだ。…朱志香を呼びにいこうってことになって、男が何人かで行けばいいだろう何て言ったら、楼座叔母さんが“狼と羊のパズル”と口にして、みんなで一緒に行こうと言い出したのだ……。
candidates: talking about how many men should go

description: wolves bear their fangs uses bear rather than bare for 牙を剥く.
sourceReading: The wolves expose their fangs when the safe balance breaks.

units.text: That could only mean one thing. ...Rosa oba-san was saying that there was a wolf among us. And when the number of wolves and sheep was balanced, we were safe, but when a situation came up where that wasn't the case, the wolves bear their fangs, ...is that what she thought......?
units.note: Both editions retain bear their fangs instead of bare their fangs.
units.japanese: そして、狼と羊の数が均衡している時は安全だが、それが崩れた環境が現れた時、狼は牙を剥くと、…そう考えている……？

units.text: That could only mean one thing. ...Aunt Rosa was saying that there was a wolf among us. So was she thinking...that we'd be safe if the number of wolves and sheep was in balance, but that the wolves would bear their fangs if the situation changed...?
units.note: Both editions retain bear their fangs instead of bare their fangs.
units.japanese: 意味するところはひとつしかない。…楼座叔母さんは、俺たちの中に「狼」が混じっているというのだ。そして、狼と羊の数が均衡している時は安全だが、それが崩れた環境が現れた時、狼は牙を剥くと、…そう考えている……？

units.text: That could only mean one thing. ...Auntie Rosa was saying that there are "wolves" among us. And when the number of wolves and sheep is balanced, we're safe, but when a situation comes up where that isn't the case, the wolves will bear their fangs—is that what she's thinking......?
units.note: Both editions retain bear their fangs instead of bare their fangs.
units.japanese: 意味するところはひとつしかない。…楼座叔母さんは、俺たちの中に「狼」が混じっているというのだ。そして、狼と羊の数が均衡している時は安全だが、それが崩れた環境が現れた時、狼は牙を剥くと、…そう考えている……？

description: その一味 becomes in league with her after whether the real culprit is Beatrice or not. The source leaves the culprit’s identity open while proposing servant accomplices.
sourceReading: Regardless of whether Beatrice is the real culprit, she thinks the servants can at least be suspected as members of the culprit’s group.

units.text: "Whether the real culprit is Beatrice or not, there is reason for us to suspect that the servants are in league with her.
units.note: MG says the servants are in on it without assigning allegiance to Beatrice. UP retains in league with her and therefore makes Beatrice the principal despite Rosa's explicit identity reservation.
units.japanese: 「真の犯人がベアトリーチェかどうかは別にして。少なくとも使用人たちがその一味であることを疑うことはできると思うの。
candidates: Whether the real culprit is Beatrice

units.text: "Whether the real culprit is Beatrice or not, I think there is reason for us to suspect that the servants are in league with her."
units.note: MG says the servants are in on it without assigning allegiance to Beatrice. UP retains in league with her and therefore makes Beatrice the principal despite Rosa's explicit identity reservation.
units.japanese: 「真の犯人がベアトリーチェかどうかは別にして。少なくとも使用人たちがその一味であることを疑うことはできると思うの」
candidates: Whether the real culprit is Beatrice

description: wanted us to isolate ourselves and attack us one by one coordinates attack under wanted us to, grammatically assigning it to us.
sourceReading: If the culprit intends to isolate the group and attack its members one at a time, a suspicion-producing trick is effective.

units.text: ......That's right. If there was a trick that could lock the door without a master key, this would be a good disguise aimed at casting doubt on the servants. ...If the culprit wanted us to isolate ourselves and attack us one by one, this trick would also be effective at giving rise to paranoia. However, there was no way to lock that door without using a master key...
units.note: MG assigns isolation to the group and attack to the culprit; UP directly says the culprit wanted to isolate and attack them. Both repair the agent relation.
units.japanese: …犯人が俺たちを孤立させて各個に襲おうと考えているなら、このトリックは疑心暗鬼も生み出せる高度なものだ。
candidates: wanted us to isolate ourselves and attack

description: 気を遣う必要がない becomes no one I need to worry about. Rosa describes relief from having to defer to or accommodate someone, in the context of always being treated as less clever than her sister.
sourceReading: Now that she need not watch herself around or accommodate anyone, she feels liberated.

units.text: "The brain speed of a little sister is always the big sister's minus 1.  ...Right now there is no one I need to worry about, so I feel relieved."
units.note: MG adds offending and restores Rosa's relief from accommodating Eva. UP retains no one I need to worry about, leaving the social deference vague.
units.japanese: 「妹の頭の回転速度は、常に姉マイナス１よ。…今は誰にも気を遣う必要がないから、せいせいするわ。」

units.text: "The brain speed of a little sister is always the big sister's minus 1. ...I feel glad that there's no one I need to worry about now."
units.note: MG adds offending and restores Rosa's relief from accommodating Eva. UP retains no one I need to worry about, leaving the social deference vague.
units.japanese: 「妹の頭の回転速度は、常に姉マイナス１よ。…今は誰にも気を遣う必要がないから、せいせいするわ」

description: 疑いそうになった becomes seemed to suspect. The near-onset of suspicion is replaced by an appearance of already suspecting.
sourceReading: Because he nearly began to suspect Kanon, he first demanded the death statement to eliminate that possibility.

units.text: "Because you seemed to suspect Kanon as the culprit, you made me repeat this to destroy that possibility right away.  I understand, I understand.  *cackle*......"
units.note: Both editions say Battler apparently or seemed to suspect Kanon, replacing Beatrice's claim that he came close to doing so.
units.japanese: 「そなたは嘉音が犯人であると疑いそうになった為、真っ先にその可能性を潰すために、これを復唱させたのだ。わかっておるわかっておる。くっくっく……。」

units.text: "You apparently suspected that Kanon was the culprit, so you made me repeat this to destroy that possibility right off the bat. Yes, yes, I understand. *cackle*..."
units.note: Both editions say Battler apparently or seemed to suspect Kanon, replacing Beatrice's claim that he came close to doing so.
units.japanese: 「そなたは嘉音が犯人であると疑いそうになった為、真っ先にその可能性を潰すために、これを復唱させたのだ。わかっておるわかっておる。くっくっく……」

units.text: "Because you seemed to suspect Kanon as the culprit, you made me repeat this to destroy that possibility right away. I understand, I understand. *cackle*......"
units.note: Both editions say Battler apparently or seemed to suspect Kanon, replacing Beatrice's claim that he came close to doing so.
units.japanese: 「そなたは嘉音が犯人であると疑いそうになった為、真っ先にその可能性を潰すために、これを復唱させたのだ。わかっておるわかっておる。くっくっく……」

description: より納得できる推理を聞かせて becomes you’d like to hear some reasoning that is easier to accept? Rosa asks George to provide better reasoning if he rejects hers.
sourceReading: If you can’t accept it, let me hear a more convincing explanation.

units.text: "You can't accept that, so you'd like to hear some reasoning that is easier to accept?  .........There is none.  I've been thinking the whole time.  There's nothing but this!"
units.note: MG tells George to find her a more convincing theory; UP tells him to provide reasoning easier to accept. Both restore Rosa's demand that he supply an alternative.
units.japanese: 「納得できないなら、より納得できる推理を聞かせて？
candidates: you'd like to hear some reasoning that is easier to accept

description: 血は争えない becomes you can’t fight your blood. Battler points to a family resemblance between Rosa’s reasoning and Eva’s.
sourceReading: Family resemblance will out: she argues just like Eva, automatically treating herself as right if others cannot rebut her.

units.text: "...I hate to say this in front of Aniki, but that argument, ......feels just like something Eva oba-san would say.  If we can't argue back, then you automatically assume that you're right.  ......Looks like you can't fight your blood after all, Oba-san."
units.note: Both editions retain the literal can't fight your blood rather than explicitly conveying the family resemblance Battler identifies.
units.japanese: こっちが反論できなきゃ自動的に自分が正しいみたいな。……やっぱり血は争えないな、叔母さん。」

units.text: "...I hate saying this in front of Aniki, but the way you're arguing... feels just like something Aunt Eva might say. It's like you're automatically assuming that you're right, unless we can counter your argument. ...Looks like you can't fight against your own blood after all, Aunt Rosa."
units.note: Both editions retain the literal can't fight your blood rather than explicitly conveying the family resemblance Battler identifies.
units.japanese: 「…兄貴の前で悪いが、その論法。……絵羽伯母さんの雰囲気にそっくりだなぁ。こっちが反論できなきゃ自動的に自分が正しいみたいな。……やっぱり血は争えないな、叔母さん」

units.text: "...I hate to say this in front of Aniki, but that argument... ...feels just like something Auntie Eva would say. If we can't argue back, then you automatically assume that you're right. ......Looks like you can't fight your blood after all, Auntie."
units.note: Both editions retain the literal can't fight your blood rather than explicitly conveying the family resemblance Battler identifies.
units.japanese: 「…兄貴の前で悪いが、その論法。……絵羽伯母さんの雰囲気にそっくりだなぁ。こっちが反論できなきゃ自動的に自分が正しいみたいな。……やっぱり血は争えないな、叔母さん」

description: 二発を撃ち返した becomes fired off a second shot back at her. The source specifies two shots fired in return, not an ordinal second shot.
sourceReading: In her hypothetical cover story, she would claim to have fired back twice and discard two empty casings as support.

units.text: I could just shoot you, *bang*, and think of a fitting excuse later.  Something like, Beatrice appeared outside the window and shot you with a gun.  I would claim that I fired off a second shot back at her, and throw away two shots worth of empty cartridges."
units.note: Both later editions explicitly say Rosa would claim to have fired two shots back, restoring the shot count.
units.japanese: あなたたちをズドンと撃って、後は適当な言い訳をするだけよ。窓の外にベアトリーチェが現れて銃を撃ってきた、とかね。私は二発を撃ち返したと称して、二発分の空薬莢を床に捨てればいい。」
candidates: fired off a second shot back

description: これが正にそうなのかしら becomes I wonder if that’s really true. She wonders whether the present gun-based demonstration is precisely an instance of might is right.
sourceReading: Krauss used to say might is right; perhaps this is exactly what that means in practice.

units.text: "Long ago, there's something Krauss nii-san often said.  Might is right.  .........I wonder if that's really true?"
units.note: MG retains wondering whether the maxim is true. UP asks whether this proves it, still turning Rosa's identification of the present demonstration as an instance into a truth or proof question.
units.japanese: 「蔵臼兄さんが昔、よく言ってたわ。力こそ正義ってね。………これが正にそうなのかしら？」

units.text: "There's something Krauss nii-san used to say all the time, long ago. Might is right. ......Maybe that really is true."
units.note: MG retains wondering whether the maxim is true. UP asks whether this proves it, still turning Rosa's identification of the present demonstration as an instance into a truth or proof question.
units.japanese: 「蔵臼兄さんが昔、よく言ってたわ。力こそ正義ってね。………これが正にそうなのかしら？」

units.text: "There's something Krauss nii‐san often used to say. Might makes right. .........I wonder if this proves that?"
units.note: MG retains wondering whether the maxim is true. UP asks whether this proves it, still turning Rosa's identification of the present demonstration as an instance into a truth or proof question.
units.japanese: 「蔵臼兄さんが昔、よく言ってたわ。力こそ正義ってね。………これが正にそうなのかしら？」

description: かなり冷静を失ってる becomes somewhat lost my composure; 余裕がなく becomes inflexible; 見えるかもしれない becomes must seem. The calibration of Rosa’s self-account changes.
sourceReading: She has lost considerable composure and may seem without her usual ease or emotional room, and a little short-tempered.

units.text: ".........I'm sorry, you two.  I've somewhat lost my composure after all these crimes since morning.  Since you know how I normally am, right now I must seem inflexible and a little short-tempered.
units.note: MG retains somewhat, desperate, and must seem, preserving the altered calibration. UP restores substantial loss of composure, on-edge pressure, and the appearance qualification.
units.japanese: 「………ごめんなさいね、二人とも。私も今朝からの事件続きでかなり冷静を失ってる。普段の私を知る二人から見れば、今の私は余裕がなくて少し短気そうに見えるかもしれない。

units.text: "......I'm sorry, you two. I've somewhat lost my composure after all the crimes since this morning. You know how I normally am, so I must seem desperate and a bit short-tempered right now.
units.note: MG retains somewhat, desperate, and must seem, preserving the altered calibration. UP restores substantial loss of composure, on-edge pressure, and the appearance qualification.
units.japanese: 「………ごめんなさいね、二人とも。私も今朝からの事件続きでかなり冷静さを失ってる。普段の私を知る二人から見れば、今の私は余裕がなくて少し短気そうに見えるかもしれない」

description: 錯覚 becomes hallucinating. He describes mentally slipping into the assumption that the culprit belongs to the familiar eighteen, because he has not personally seen the guest.
sourceReading: He keeps falling into the mistaken impression that the culprit is among the eighteen.

units.text: I hadn't actually seen her face. I'd heard that she was like a double of the witch in that portrait, but because I hadn't seen her directly, no matter how hard I tried, I couldn't really feel like a 19th person was on this island. ...So I had unconsciously been hallucinating that the culprit was one of the 18...
units.note: MG retains hallucinating; UP's illusion describes Battler slipping into a mistaken assumption without implying a sensory hallucination.
units.japanese: …だからつい、１８人の中に犯人がいるような錯覚になっちまう…。

units.text: In fact, I still haven't seen her face. I heard she greatly resembled the witch in that portrait, but since I haven't seen her directly, no matter how hard I try, it doesn't really feel to me like a 19th person is on this island. ...So, I've been subconsciously hallucinating that the culprit's one of the 18...
units.note: MG retains hallucinating; UP's illusion describes Battler slipping into a mistaken assumption without implying a sensory hallucination.
units.japanese: 実のところ、俺は顔を見ていない。魔女の肖像画に瓜二つだったと話は聞いてるが、直接見た訳ではないため、どうしてもこの島に１９人がいるという実感がわかない。…だからつい、１８人の中に犯人がいるような錯覚になっちまう…。

description: 開封した食材 becomes sealed ingredients. The embedded Japanese explicitly says opened ingredients, whereas WH supplies an intact-seal qualification.
sourceReading: Gohda says he made it only with ingredients he opened, so poison will not have been mixed in.

units.text: "It was made only from sealed ingredients, so there won't be any poison mixed in.
units.note: Both editions retain sealed ingredients, reversing the source's statement that Gohda used only ingredients that had already been opened.
units.japanese: 「開封した食材だけで作りましたので、毒が混入しているなんてことはありませんよ。

units.text: "It was made only from sealed ingredients, so there won't be any poison mixed in.
units.note: Both editions retain sealed ingredients, reversing the source's statement that Gohda used only ingredients that had already been opened.
units.japanese: 「開封した食材だけで作りましたので、毒が混入しているなんてことはありませんよ」

units.text: "It was made only from sealed ingredients, so there won't be any poison mixed in."
units.note: Both editions retain sealed ingredients, reversing the source's statement that Gohda used only ingredients that had already been opened.
units.japanese: 「開封した食材だけで作りましたので、毒が混入しているなんてことはありませんよ」

description: その場の雰囲気でそれに納得してしまった becomes The atmosphere in this place accepted that. They were persuaded by the atmosphere at the time; the atmosphere itself did not accept a proposition.
sourceReading: They accepted Rosa’s warning under the mood of that encounter, but hunger would not be satisfied by such a passing emotion.
