units.text: Rosa had fervently told everyone that they didn't notice the danger they were in, and that they must suspect that poison was mixed in with the food. The atmosphere in this place accepted that, but their hunger wouldn't be overcome by that momentary emotion.
units.note: Both later editions restore the people as those led by the mood or atmosphere to agree.
units.japanese: その場の雰囲気でそれに納得してしまったが、空腹というものはそんな一時の感情で納得してくれるものではなかったということだ。

description: ご指示に背いている以上 becomes Seeing that would violate ... . Genji acknowledges that they are already going against Rosa’s instructions; English more naturally locates the violation in the proposed serving to the parlor.
sourceReading: Since they are already disobeying her directions, they should avoid offering it to the family; those who want it may drink.

units.text: "......Seeing that would violate Rosa-sama's instructions, it would be better to give it up.  ......It is alright if only those who want to drink it do so."
units.note: MG keeps would violate and UP changes it to that goes against; in context both attach the breach most naturally to Gohda's proposed serving rather than acknowledging that the unauthorized soup already breaches the order.
units.japanese: 「……楼座さまのご指示に背いている以上、止した方がいいだろう。……飲みたい者だけ飲むといい。」

units.text: "...Seeing that it would violate Rosa-sama's instructions, you had best give up on that idea. ...It's enough that only those who want to eat it do so."
units.note: MG keeps would violate and UP changes it to that goes against; in context both attach the breach most naturally to Gohda's proposed serving rather than acknowledging that the unauthorized soup already breaches the order.
units.japanese: 「……楼座さまのご指示に背いている以上、止した方がいいだろう。……飲みたい者だけ飲むといい」

units.text: "......Seeing as that goes against Rosa‐sama's instructions, you'd better not. ......Those who want to eat it can do so."
units.note: MG keeps would violate and UP changes it to that goes against; in context both attach the breach most naturally to Gohda's proposed serving rather than acknowledging that the unauthorized soup already breaches the order.
units.japanese: 「……楼座さまのご指示に背いている以上、止した方がいいだろう。……飲みたい者だけ飲むといい」

description: stationary box uses the adjective for immobility rather than stationery for 文房具.
sourceReading: Genji takes the knife from a stationery box beside the chess set.

units.text: Genji took a knife with a classical design from a stationary box placed near the chess set. ...It was something to be used instead of a paper knife to open envelopes for statements of delivery and bills. But it was fundamentally a knife. So the blade on it could injure someone...
units.note: MG retains stationary; UP uses the correct stationery.
units.japanese: 源次はチェスの脇に置かれていた文房具箱の中にあったクラシックなデザインのナイフを取る。

units.text: Genji took a knife with a classical design from a stationary box placed near the chess set. ...It was something to be used instead of a paper knife to open envelopes for statements of delivery and bills. But it was still a knife. So the blade on it could injure someone...
units.note: MG retains stationary; UP uses the correct stationery.
units.japanese:
源次はチェスの脇に置かれていた文房具箱の中にあったクラシックなデザインのナイフを取る。…それは、納品書や請求書の封筒を開けるのに、ペーパーナイフ代わりにしていたものだった。しかし本来はナイフ。
だからそれには人を傷付ける刃が付けられている…。

description: 源次 ... 郷田に無言で頷いて合図 becomes Gohda silently signaling his approval. The recipient becomes the actor; English also says both approach where this sentence describes Genji approaching.
sourceReading: Genji approaches the back door himself and silently nods to Gohda, who then cautiously moves to open it.

units.text: Genji hid it in his sleeve with a well-practiced manner. Then they both approached the back door, Gohda silently signaling his approval.
units.note: Both editions make Genji the approaching actor who gives or signals a silent nod to Gohda.
units.japanese: そして自らも勝手口に近付き、郷田に無言で頷いて合図を送った。

description: 傷跡 becomes scar despite the immediately described deep injury pouring blood. In this usage the source describes the mark or wound left by penetration, not necessarily healed tissue.
sourceReading: Nanjo turns him face up and sees a deep gruesome wound in the middle of the chest, apparently made by a spear-like object.

units.text: When Nanjo held him and turned him face up, there was a deep, gruesome scar right in the center of his chest, as though a spear or something had been stuck there. Even now, deep-red blood poured out from there...!
units.note: MG uses wound. UP retains scar while revising the penetration comparison to run through with a spear.
units.japanese: 南條が抱きかかえ仰向けにすると、胸の真ん中に、槍か何かで突き刺されたような、深く惨たらしい傷跡があった。

units.text: When Nanjo held him and turned him face up, there was a deep, gruesome scar right in the center of his chest, as though he had been run through with a spear or something. Even now, deep‐red blood poured out from there...!
units.note: MG uses wound. UP retains scar while revising the penetration comparison to run through with a spear.
units.japanese: 南條が抱きかかえ仰向けにすると、胸の真ん中に、槍か何かで突き刺されたような、深く惨たらしい傷跡があった。そこからは今もどくどくと真っ赤な血が溢れ出している…！

description: 何とか持つかも becomes I might be able to do something. Nanjo’s conditional prognosis concerns the patient holding on, not his own ability to intervene.
sourceReading: If the injury has not reached the lungs, Kanon may somehow hold out; Nanjo then calls for stopping the bleeding.

units.text: "......This is......horrible...  It appears that he has been stabbed with something like a spear.  I, If it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something......  Anyway, stop the bleeding......!"
units.note: Both retain I might be able to do something instead of saying Kanon might hold on if the wound has not reached his lungs.
units.japanese: 「……これは……酷い…。何か槍のようなもので刺されたようです。は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。とにかく、止血を……！」

units.text: "...This is...horrible... He appears to have been stabbed by something like a spear. I-If it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something... At any rate, we must stop the bleeding...!"
units.note: Both retain I might be able to do something instead of saying Kanon might hold on if the wound has not reached his lungs.
units.japanese: 「……これは……酷い…。何か槍のようなもので刺されたようです。は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。とにかく、止血を……！」

units.text: "......This is......horrible... It appears that he has been stabbed with something like a spear. I‐if it hasn't reached the lungs, I might be able to do something...... Anyway, stop the bleeding......!"
units.note: Both retain I might be able to do something instead of saying Kanon might hold on if the wound has not reached his lungs.
units.japanese: 「……これは……酷い…。何か槍のようなもので刺されたようです。は、肺まで届いてなければ何とか持つかも……。とにかく、止血を……！」

description: 眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うよう becomes like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes. The source frames the voice as if he had witnessed her being killed by that person; English substitutes ongoing seeing and generic harm.
sourceReading: The voice sounds as though he had personally watched Jessica being killed at Rosa’s hands.

units.text: Kanon screamed even more hatefully... ...His hate-filled voice made it seem like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.
units.note: MG retains seeing and harmed. UP restores completed witnessing with had seen but still reduces being killed by that person to being harmed.
units.japanese: …まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
candidates: like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes

units.text: Kanon screamed even more hatefully... ...His hate-filled voice made it seem like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.
units.note: MG retains seeing and harmed. UP restores completed witnessing with had seen but still reduces being killed by that person to being harmed.
units.japanese:
なおも恨めしそうに叫ぶ嘉音…。
…まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
candidates: like he was seeing Jessica being harmed right before his eyes

units.text:
Kanon screamed even more hatefully...
...His hate‐filled voice made it seem like he had seen Jessica being harmed right before his eyes.
units.note: MG retains seeing and harmed. UP restores completed witnessing with had seen but still reduces being killed by that person to being harmed.
units.japanese:
なおも恨めしそうに叫ぶ嘉音…。
…まるで、自分の眼前で朱志香がその手にかけられるのを見たとでも言うような呪わしい声だった。
candidates: Jessica being harmed right before his eyes

description: この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう becomes she would probably lose it all in this wind and rain. The passive resulting condition becomes her prospective loss.
sourceReading: The sought material might be found in the rose garden, but all of it would probably already have been lost amid the wind and rain, prompting her to consider the less-clean boiler room.

units.text: Shannon ran.  To where? ......The inside of the mansion had been scrupulously cleaned, so it probably wouldn't be easy to find. She might find it if she searched the rose garden, but she would probably lose it all in this wind and rain...
units.note: Both editions say the sought items have probably already been lost in the wind and rain rather than predicting Shannon will lose them.
units.japanese: 薔薇庭園を探せば見付かるかもしれないが、この風雨の中では全て失われているだろう…。
candidates: probably lose it all in this wind and rain

description: didn’t let his eyes off Kanon is not the intended idiom for maintaining observation.
sourceReading: Nanjo never took his eyes off Kanon.

units.text: Did some medicine take effect at the brink of death, or had Kanon finally stopped even feeling pain? ...For the time being, Kanon had at least gotten over his painful gasping. Nanjo apparently didn't think of this as that great of a trend, and didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.
units.note: Both retain didn't let his eyes off Kanon rather than didn't take his eyes off Kanon.
units.japanese: 南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
candidates: didn't let his eyes off Kanon

units.text: Did some medicine take effect at the brink of death, or was Kanon finally beyond feeling pain? ...For the time being, at least Kanon's painful gasping had subsided. Nanjo apparently didn't view this as a very good sign, ...and he didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.
units.note: Both retain didn't let his eyes off Kanon rather than didn't take his eyes off Kanon.
units.japanese: 何かの薬が土壇場で効いてくれたのだろうか、それともとうとう嘉音は痛みを感じることすら失われてしまったのか。…嘉音はとりあえず苦痛に喘ぐことだけはなくなった。南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
candidates: didn't let his eyes off Kanon

units.text: Had some medicine taken effect at the brink of death, or had Kanon finally stopped even feeling pain? ...For the time being, Kanon had at least gotten over his painful gasping. Nanjo apparently didn't think of this as that great of a trend, and didn't let his eyes off Kanon for a second.
units.note: Both retain didn't let his eyes off Kanon rather than didn't take his eyes off Kanon.
units.japanese: 何かの薬が土壇場で効いてくれたのだろうか、それともとうとう嘉音は痛みを感じることすら失われてしまったのか。…嘉音はとりあえず苦痛に喘ぐことだけはなくなった。南條はそれをあまりよい傾向だと思っていないらしく、一時も目を離さなかった。
candidates: didn't let his eyes off Kanon

description: こちらから仕掛けるべき becomes we should wage war from here. Gohda proposes initiating action, immediately specifying taking the gun under a pretext.
sourceReading: They should act first, at least inventing a reason to take away the gun.

units.text: "But there is still much time before tomorrow comes...!  We can't even imagine what strategy she will use!  Genji-san, we should wage war from here.  If we can at least steal the gun under some pretext, things might work out...!"
units.note: MG says take action first and UP says make the first move; both restore Gohda's proposal to initiate action before specifying the gun.
units.japanese: 源次さん、こちらから仕掛けるべきです。せめて銃さえ理由をこじつけて奪えば、何とかなるかも…！」

description: 朗々と喋る becomes talking brightly. The source highlights strong clear vocal production, not specifically a cheerful manner.
sourceReading: He abruptly speaks in a clear ringing voice despite having seemed asleep.

units.text: Kanon, who they thought had been sleeping quietly, suddenly started talking brightly. Almost like he had been awake the whole time and had suddenly opened his mouth. He looked firm and steady, and Nanjo was slightly relieved, but thinking of the deepness of that wound, he just couldn't wipe away a certain creepy feeling.
units.note: Both retain talking brightly even though the surrounding effect is eerie lucidity rather than cheerfulness.
units.japanese: それまで、静かに眠っていると思っていた嘉音が、急に朗々と喋る。

units.text: Kanon, who they'd thought was sleeping quietly, suddenly started talking brightly. Almost as though he'd been awake this whole time and had suddenly opened his mouth. Kanon looked firm and steady, which relieved Nanjo a bit, but considering the depth of that wound, he couldn't wipe away a certain creepy feeling.
units.note: Both retain talking brightly even though the surrounding effect is eerie lucidity rather than cheerfulness.
units.japanese: それまで、静かに眠っていると思っていた嘉音が、急に朗々と喋る。まるでさっきからずっと起きていて、急に口を開いたかのようだった。その様子がしっかりしていたので、南條は少しだけほっとするが、傷の深さを考えると、どうしてもある不気味さが拭えなかった。

description: 意識を失って当然だ becomes It wouldn’t have been unexpected if ... . The source presents loss of consciousness as the expected outcome, not merely a possible outcome that would not surprise.
sourceReading: Given that much blood loss, unconsciousness should follow; continued clear awareness is anomalous to Nanjo.

units.text: ......He knew because he was a doctor. It wouldn't have been unexpected if Kanon had lost consciousness after losing so much blood. And yet somehow, he had preserved his awareness so clearly. ......Was it youth?  Or was it tenacity? ...Sometimes, the power of human life surpassed common knowledge......
units.note: MG's might easily have lost consciousness remains a possibility rather than the medically expected outcome. UP says Kanon should have been expected to fall unconscious.
units.japanese: 嘉音の出血量なら意識を失って当然だ。

units.text: ...He knew because he was a doctor. After losing so much blood, Kanon might easily have lost consciousness. And yet, somehow, he was still intensely aware of his surroundings. ...Was it youth? Or was it tenacity? ...Sometimes, the power of human life surpassed common knowledge...
units.note: MG's might easily have lost consciousness remains a possibility rather than the medically expected outcome. UP says Kanon should have been expected to fall unconscious.
units.japanese:
……彼は医者だからわかる。嘉音の出血量なら意識を失って当然だ。
なのにこんなにもはっきりとした意識を保てるなんて。……若さ？　それとも執念？
…時に人の生命力は常識を超えることもあるし……。

description: 確実に肺にすら届いているはず becomes had certainly reached as far as his lungs. The source retains はず, marking a strong inference about the injury.
sourceReading: The wound must or should surely have reached even the lungs, given what Nanjo observed.

units.text: When they had stopped the bleeding, Nanjo had groped around a bit inside the bleeding hole with tweezers, to make sure there were no foreign objects inside the affected area, and the great depth of the wound had surprised him. ...The wound had certainly reached as far as his lungs. ......And yet, ...and yet... ......No, on the other hand, the fact that he is alive is fortunate...
units.note: Both state that the wound certainly reached the lungs rather than preserving Nanjo's strong inference that it should have reached them.
units.japanese: …傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。
candidates: certainly reached as far as his lungs

units.text: While stopping the bleeding, Nanjo had groped around a bit inside the bleeding hole with tweezers, making sure there were no foreign objects inside the affected area, and the great depth of the wound had shocked him. ...It had certainly reached as far as his lungs. ...And yet, ...and yet... ...No, but...the fact that he's still alive is wonderful...
units.note: Both state that the wound certainly reached the lungs rather than preserving Nanjo's strong inference that it should have reached them.
units.japanese:
止血の時、患部に何か異物があってはいけないと、血の湧き出す穴をピンセットで少しだけまさぐったが、そのあまりの深さに驚いた。…傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。……なのに、…なのに…。
……いや、でも、生きているのはとにかく幸いなことで…。
candidates: certainly reached as far as his lungs

units.text:
When they had stopped the bleeding, to make sure there were no foreign objects inside the affected area, Nanjo had groped around a bit inside the bleeding hole with tweezers, and the great depth of the wound had surprised him. ...The wound had certainly reached as far as his lungs. ......And yet, ...and yet...
......No, on the other hand, the fact that he is alive is fortunate...
units.note: Both state that the wound certainly reached the lungs rather than preserving Nanjo's strong inference that it should have reached them.
units.japanese:
止血の時、患部に何か異物があってはいけないと、血の湧き出す穴をピンセットで少しだけまさぐったが、そのあまりの深さに驚いた。…傷は確実に肺にすら届いているはずなのだ。……なのに、…なのに…。
……いや、でも、生きているのはとにかく幸いなことで…。
candidates: certainly reached as far as his lungs

description: 糸すら引いていた becomes there was even a thread hanging. The source describes sticky red material stretching into strings, not a separate thread-like object.
sourceReading: The withdrawn fingers are coated in sticky red material which even trails viscous strings.

units.text: That finger was completely sticking into his chest, ......up to its base, ......and then he slowly pulled it out in exactly the same way... The fingers he pulled out, were stained a sticky, solid, deep-red color, and there was even a thread hanging... ...The finger was, up to its base, covered, ......in deep-red...
units.note: Both retain a thread hanging rather than the blood stretching into a sticky strand.
units.japanese: 引き抜かれた指は、粘り気のある真っ赤なもので一色に染められていて、糸すら引いていた…。

units.text: Those fingers were sticking all the way into his chest, ...up to their bases, ...and then he slowly pulled them out in exactly the same way... The fingers he pulled out...were stained a sticky, solid, deep-red color, and there was even a thread hanging... ...The fingers were...covered...up to their bases...in deep-red...
units.note: Both retain a thread hanging rather than the blood stretching into a sticky strand.
units.japanese: その指は完全に、……根元まで胸の中に入り込んで、……それから、差し込まれた時と同じようにゆっくりと引き抜かれ…。引き抜かれた指は、粘り気のある真っ赤なもので一色に染められていて、糸すら引いていた…。…指の、根元まで、ねとりと、……真っ赤に…。

units.text: Having stuck his fingers completely into his chest......up to their base, ......he slowly pulled them out in exactly the same way... The fingers he pulled out were stained a sticky, solid, deep‐red color, and there was even a thread hanging... ...The fingers were, all the way to their base, covered......in deep red...
units.note: Both retain a thread hanging rather than the blood stretching into a sticky strand.
units.japanese: その指は完全に、……根元まで胸の中に入り込んで、……それから、差し込まれた時と同じようにゆっくりと引き抜かれ…。引き抜かれた指は、粘り気のある真っ赤なもので一色に染められていて、糸すら引いていた…。…指の、根元まで、ねとりと、……真っ赤に…。

description: 険しい表情 becomes impregnable expression. The source describes her severe or stern expression, which does not change on seeing the blood.
sourceReading: Her stern expression does not falter when she sees him bloodied.

units.text: At that time, the door was opened vigorously, and Shannon appeared. ...Even after she saw Kanon, stained with fresh blood, her impregnable expression didn't falter.
units.note: Both retain impregnable expression, changing the quality of Shannon's stern look rather than simply saying it did not falter.
units.japanese: …鮮血に染まった嘉音を見ても、その険しい表情は歪まなかった。

units.text: At that moment, the door was slammed open, and Shannon appeared. ...Even after she saw Kanon, stained with fresh blood, her impregnable expression didn't falter.
units.note: Both retain impregnable expression, changing the quality of Shannon's stern look rather than simply saying it did not falter.
units.japanese: その時、威勢よく扉が開き、紗音が現れる。…鮮血に染まった嘉音を見ても、その険しい表情は歪まなかった。

units.text: Just then, the door opened vigorously, and Shannon appeared. ...Even after she saw Kanon stained with fresh blood, her impregnable expression didn't falter.
units.note: Both retain impregnable expression, changing the quality of Shannon's stern look rather than simply saying it did not falter.
units.japanese: その時、威勢よく扉が開き、紗音が現れる。…鮮血に染まった嘉音を見ても、その険しい表情は歪まなかった。

description: 弧を描く３つの美しい紫の軌跡 becomes That arc, which drew three beautiful purple loci. The source counts three trails, each described as arcing; English introduces a singular arc as their producer.
sourceReading: There are three beautiful purple arcing trails, with the following sentence distinguishing the third aimed at Shannon.

units.text: Kanon jumped like a wild goat, ...fleeing from the thing Shannon was holding. Then, from his arm, some kind of afterglow flashed purple and drew a locus. That arc, which drew three beautiful purple loci, traced across the throats of Nanjo and Kumasawa, who had been tending to him. And, in an instant, Nanjo and Kumasawa's throats, ......opened like gaping mouths, ...and from then on, the blood really started spewing out.
units.note: MG retains a singular arc that draws three curves. UP identifies three trails drawn in an arc.
units.japanese: それは弧を描く３つの美しい紫の軌跡で、彼を看護していた南條と熊沢の喉をなぞっていた。
candidates: arc, which drew three beautiful purple loci

units.text: Kanon jumped like a wild goat, ...fleeing from the thing Shannon was holding. Then, from his arm, some kind of afterglow flashed purple and drew a curve through space. That arc, which drew three beautiful purple curves, traced across the throats of Nanjo and Kumasawa, who had been tending to him. And, in an instant, Nanjo's and Kumasawa's throats...opened like gaping mouths, ...and then the blood really started spewing out.
units.note: MG retains a singular arc that draws three curves. UP identifies three trails drawn in an arc.
units.japanese: 嘉音が、カモシカのように跳ねて、…紗音のそれから逃れ飛び上がった。そして、その腕が紫に閃く何かの残光で軌跡を描いた。それは弧を描く３つの美しい紫の軌跡で、彼を看護していた南條と熊沢の喉をなぞっていた。そして、南條と熊沢の喉が、……ぱっくりと口を開き、…血がこれからまさに噴出そうという刹那の時間。
candidates: arc, which drew three beautiful purple

description: 血がこれからまさに噴出そうという刹那 becomes from then on, the blood really started spewing out. The source freezes the instant just before eruption.
sourceReading: Their throats open in the fraction of an instant when blood is just about to gush; the narration continues describing the simultaneous actions before time unfreezes.

units.text: Kanon jumped like a wild goat, ...fleeing from the thing Shannon was holding. Then, from his arm, some kind of afterglow flashed purple and drew a locus. That arc, which drew three beautiful purple loci, traced across the throats of Nanjo and Kumasawa, who had been tending to him. And, in an instant, Nanjo and Kumasawa's throats, ......opened like gaping mouths, ...and from then on, the blood really started spewing out.
units.note: MG still makes the blood start spewing in this frozen instant. UP explicitly locates the image at the instant before it is about to begin.
units.japanese: そして、南條と熊沢の喉が、……ぱっくりと口を開き、…血がこれからまさに噴出そうという刹那の時間。

units.text: Kanon jumped like a wild goat, ...fleeing from the thing Shannon was holding. Then, from his arm, some kind of afterglow flashed purple and drew a curve through space. That arc, which drew three beautiful purple curves, traced across the throats of Nanjo and Kumasawa, who had been tending to him. And, in an instant, Nanjo's and Kumasawa's throats...opened like gaping mouths, ...and then the blood really started spewing out.
units.note: MG still makes the blood start spewing in this frozen instant. UP explicitly locates the image at the instant before it is about to begin.
units.japanese: 嘉音が、カモシカのように跳ねて、…紗音のそれから逃れ飛び上がった。そして、その腕が紫に閃く何かの残光で軌跡を描いた。それは弧を描く３つの美しい紫の軌跡で、彼を看護していた南條と熊沢の喉をなぞっていた。そして、南條と熊沢の喉が、……ぱっくりと口を開き、…血がこれからまさに噴出そうという刹那の時間。

description: 伏せるように床に転げた becomes fallen onto the ground as though hiding. The source describes dropping or rolling low to the floor to evade the attack, not concealment.
sourceReading: Genji pulls Shannon again, and they roll onto the floor, dropping prone.

units.text: But Kanon's target once again disappeared from in front of him. Because Genji had pulled Shannon again, and the two of them had fallen onto the ground as though hiding.
units.note: MG uses a defensive crouch and UP says they keep flat to the floor, both restoring the evasive movement rather than concealment.
units.japanese: 源次が再び紗音を引っ張り、二人で伏せるように床に転げたからだ。
candidates: fallen onto the ground as though hiding

description: 叩きつけて押し付ける becomes pushing him up against the wall. The impact before continued pinning is omitted.
sourceReading: Gohda leaps on him, slams him into the wall and pins him with his weight and strength.

units.text: Gohda wasn't an idiot either. Even if he couldn't fully understand what was going on, he at least realized that if this 'Kanon' wasn't seized, his own life would also be in peril. He sprung at Kanon with his huge body, pushing him up against the wall with his weight and physical strength.
units.note: Both say Gohda pushes Kanon against the wall without the initial slamming impact; UP only removes MG's all.
units.japanese: その巨体で嘉音に飛び掛り、体重と腕力で壁に叩きつけて押し付ける。
candidates: pushing him up against the wall

units.text: Even Gohda was no fool. Even if he couldn't fully understand what was going on, he at least realized that if this "Kanon" wasn't seized, his own life would also be in peril. He sprung at Kanon with his huge body, pushing him up against the wall with all his weight and physical strength.
units.note: Both say Gohda pushes Kanon against the wall without the initial slamming impact; UP only removes MG's all.
units.japanese: 郷田も馬鹿ではない。何が起こっているか理解には及ばなくても、この“嘉音”を取り押さえなければ自分の命も危ういことだけは理解できた。その巨体で嘉音に飛び掛り、体重と腕力で壁に叩きつけて押し付ける。
candidates: pushing him up against the wall

units.text: Gohda wasn't an idiot either. Even if he couldn't fully understand what was going on, he at least realized that if this "Kanon" wasn't seized, his own life would also be in peril. He sprung at Kanon with his huge body, pushing him up against the wall with his weight and physical strength.
units.note: Both say Gohda pushes Kanon against the wall without the initial slamming impact; UP only removes MG's all.
units.japanese: 郷田も馬鹿ではない。何が起こっているか理解には及ばなくても、この“嘉音”を取り押さえなければ自分の命も危ういことだけは理解できた。その巨体で嘉音に飛び掛り、体重と腕力で壁に叩きつけて押し付ける。
candidates: pushing him up against the wall

description: no one payed it much mind uses payed where paid is required.
sourceReading: In the abnormal situation, they regard Genji’s skill as insignificant.

units.text: Under normal circumstances, it should have been surprising to see someone as old as Genji handle a knife so skillfully, but in this abnormal space, no one payed it much mind.
units.note: Both use the correct paid.
units.japanese: 老体の源次がそれだけのナイフの扱いを見せられることは、平時なら驚くべきことだったが、この異常な空間の中では取るに足らないことだとみんな思った。

description: 水に、いや空気中に溶けるかのよう becomes as though water, no, as though the air itself was evaporating. The butterflies are the entities dissolving into a medium; English makes water or air the entity undergoing evaporation.
sourceReading: The butterflies fade into nothing as though dissolving into water—or rather into the air.

units.text: Those butterflies began to softly fade into nothingness, as though water, no, as though the air itself was evaporating, ......and afterwards, all that was left was the three of them sitting on their butts, stained with blood.
units.note: MG makes the butterflies fade into water or air; UP explicitly makes them dissolve into those media. Both restore the butterflies as the disappearing entity.
units.japanese: その蝶たちは、まるで水に、いや空気中に溶けるかのようにすぅっと虚空に消えて行き、……後には、血塗れになって尻餅をつく彼らが残されるだけだった。
candidates: though water, no, as though the air itself was evaporating

description: 亡骸の前にしゃがみ込んで涙を流し becomes sobbed in front of ... remains. The explicit crouching posture is lost.
sourceReading: Shannon crouches in front of Nanjo and Kumasawa’s bodies and cries, while Genji looks down in silence.

units.text: Gohda kept screaming alone, without a clue about what was going on. Shannon sobbed in front of Nanjo's and Kumasawa's remains, ...as Genji watched over her, silent as always...
units.note: Both retain sobbed in front of the remains without Shannon crouching down before them.
units.japanese: 紗音は南條と熊沢の亡骸の前にしゃがみ込んで涙を流し、…源次はそれを見下ろしながら、変わらず無言でいるのだった…。

units.text: Gohda kept screaming alone, without a clue about what was going on. Shannon sobbed in front of Nanjo's and Kumasawa's remains... as Genji watched over her, silent as always...
units.note: Both retain sobbed in front of the remains without Shannon crouching down before them.
units.japanese: 郷田は何が何だかわからないとひとり叫び続ける。紗音は南條と熊沢の亡骸の前にしゃがみ込んで涙を流し、…源次はそれを見下ろしながら、変わらず無言でいるのだった…。

units.text: Gohda kept screaming alone that he had no clue about what was going on. Shannon sobbed in front of Nanjo's and Kumasawa's remains, ...and Genji watched over her, silent as always...
units.note: Both retain sobbed in front of the remains without Shannon crouching down before them.
units.japanese: 郷田は何が何だかわからないとひとり叫び続ける。紗音は南條と熊沢の亡骸の前にしゃがみ込んで涙を流し、…源次はそれを見下ろしながら、変わらず無言でいるのだった…。

description: 昨夜から becomes since yesterday, losing the night-specific starting point.
sourceReading: Rosa describes Beatrice as unaccounted for since last night.

units.text: "What are you saying?!  It's impossible for you to have met anyone other than the witch, Beatrice, whose location has been unknown since yesterday, or Kanon-kun, who has gone missing!  Was it a man or a woman?!  You should be able to tell me at least that much, right?!"
units.note: MG retains since yesterday. UP restores since last night.
units.japanese: 「何を言ってるの？！　あなたが出会ったのは昨夜から所在不明の魔女、ベアトリーチェか、行方不明になっている嘉音くんかのどちらかしかありえない！　男か、女か！　それだけでも答えられるでしょう？！」

units.text: "What are you saying?! You couldn't have met anyone except the witch, Beatrice, whose location has been unknown since yesterday, or Kanon-kun, who's gone missing! Was it a man or a woman?! You should be able to tell me at least that much, right?!"
units.note: MG retains since yesterday. UP restores since last night.
units.japanese: 「何を言ってるの？！　あなたが出会ったのは昨夜から所在不明の魔女、ベアトリーチェか、行方不明になっている嘉音くんかのどちらかしかありえない！　男か、女か！　それだけでも答えられるでしょう？！」

description: 白昼夢と溶け込んで becomes melt away like a daydream. Blending the remembered experience with a waking dream becomes a simile for its disappearance.
sourceReading: Battler thinks Shannon looks liable to let what she just saw merge with a daydream and become impossible to recall.

units.text: And Shannon looked the same way. If she let her guard down, what she had seen just a short while ago would quickly melt away like a daydream, and she wouldn't be able to remember what she saw. ......That's what she looked like.
units.note: Both retain the memory melting away like a daydream rather than blending into one.
units.japanese: ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。

units.text: And Shannon looked the same way. If she let her guard down, what she'd seen just a short while ago would quickly melt away like a daydream, and she wouldn't be able to remember anything. ...That's what she looked like.
units.note: Both retain the memory melting away like a daydream rather than blending into one.
units.japanese: そして、それは紗音も同じに見えた。ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。……そんな風に見えた。

units.text: And Shannon looked the same way. If she let her guard down, what she had seen just a short while ago would quickly melt away like a daydream, and she wouldn't even be able to remember what she saw. ......That's what she looked like.
units.note: Both retain the memory melting away like a daydream rather than blending into one.
units.japanese: そして、それは紗音も同じに見えた。ほんの少し気を許せば、ついさっき見たばかりのことが、すぐに白昼夢と溶け込んでしまって、自分が何を見たのかも思い出せなくなってしまう。……そんな風に見えた。

description: 同じ意味になる becomes her conclusion had been correct from the beginning. Equivalence between a charitable reading of testimony and Rosa’s assertion becomes validation of that assertion.
sourceReading: Interpreted favorably, their testimony amounts to what Rosa initially asserted.

units.text: ...If we interpreted what they were saying favorably, ......it meant that Rosa oba-san's conclusion had been correct from the beginning.
units.note: MG says Rosa's first conclusion was correct; UP retains the original claim that it had been correct from the beginning. Both validate it rather than say the favorable interpretation amounts to the same meaning.
units.japanese: …彼らの言っていることを、好意的に解釈すると、……それは楼座叔母さんが最初に断じているのと同じ意味になる。
candidates: conclusion had been correct from the beginning

units.text: ...If we give their claims the benefit of the doubt, ...it means that Aunt Rosa's first conclusion was correct.
units.note: MG says Rosa's first conclusion was correct; UP retains the original claim that it had been correct from the beginning. Both validate it rather than say the favorable interpretation amounts to the same meaning.
units.japanese: …彼らの言っていることを、好意的に解釈すると、……それは楼座叔母さんが最初に断じているのと同じ意味になる。

units.text: ...If we interpreted what they were saying favorably, ......it meant that Auntie Rosa's conclusion had been correct from the beginning.
units.note: MG says Rosa's first conclusion was correct; UP retains the original claim that it had been correct from the beginning. Both validate it rather than say the favorable interpretation amounts to the same meaning.
units.japanese: …彼らの言っていることを、好意的に解釈すると、……それは楼座叔母さんが最初に断じているのと同じ意味になる。
candidates: conclusion had been correct from the beginning

description: トリックがあるということなのか becomes Kanon-kun had used some trick. The question shifts from whether such a means exists to whether Kanon used it; just as Rosa oba-san thought also supplies an explicit attribution absent here.
sourceReading: Does this mean there really is a trick by which Kanon could escape with the room still locked?

units.text: So just as Rosa oba-san thought, Kanon-kun had used some trick to escape that room while it was locked?!  No, that doesn't matter anymore. The real problem is that Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa-san were killed.
units.note: Both remove the earlier added attribution to Rosa but retain the shift from whether an escape trick exists to whether Kanon used one.
units.japanese: やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！　いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。

units.text: So, does that mean that, after all, Kanon-kun used some trick to escape that room even though it was locked?! No, that doesn't matter anymore. The real problem is that Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa-san were killed.
units.note: Both remove the earlier added attribution to Rosa but retain the shift from whether an escape trick exists to whether Kanon used one.
units.japanese: やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！　いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。南條先生と熊沢さんが殺されたことの方が重要な問題だ。

units.text: So had Kanon‐kun indeed used some trick to escape that room while it was locked?! No, that doesn't matter anymore. The real problem is that Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa‐san were killed.
units.note: Both remove the earlier added attribution to Rosa but retain the shift from whether an escape trick exists to whether Kanon used one.
units.japanese: やはり嘉音くんがあの部屋を施錠したまま抜け出すトリックがあるということなのか？！　いや、今そんなことはどうでもいい。南條先生と熊沢さんが殺されたことの方が重要な問題だ。

description: 吐き気を催し becomes start to vomit, replacing feeling sick with actual vomiting.
sourceReading: Battler expects to keep feeling nauseated whenever scattered red paint recalls the room.

units.text: ......I was acting tough right now, so I didn't mind, ......but for the rest of my life, whenever I see red paint scattered around, I'll probably remember this room and start to vomit. ......My retinas already had this room burned into them. ...In other words, it was too late for me...
units.note: Both say Battler will start to vomit whenever he sees scattered red paint, rather than become nauseated.
units.japanese: ……今の俺は強がっているから気にならないが、……俺は今後の人生において、赤いペンキが散らばっているのを見る度に、この部屋を思い出して吐き気を催し続けるのだろう。

units.text: ...I was acting tough right now, so I didn't mind, ...but for the rest of my life, whenever I see red paint scattered around, I'll probably remember this room and start to vomit. ...My retinas have already had this room burned into them. ...In other words, it's already too late for me...
units.note: Both say Battler will start to vomit whenever he sees scattered red paint, rather than become nauseated.
units.japanese:
……今の俺は強がっているから気にならないが、……俺は今後の人生において、赤いペンキが散らばっているのを見る度に、この部屋を思い出して吐き気を催し続けるのだろう。……もう俺の網膜にこの部屋は焼き付いてしまった。
…つまり俺は手遅れだった…。

units.text:
......I was acting tough right now, so I didn't mind, ......but I would probably remember this room and start to vomit whenever I saw red paint scattered around, for the rest of my life. ......My retinas already had this room burned into them.
...In other words, it was too late for me...
units.note: Both say Battler will start to vomit whenever he sees scattered red paint, rather than become nauseated.
units.japanese:
……今の俺は強がっているから気にならないが、……俺は今後の人生において、赤いペンキが散らばっているのを見る度に、この部屋を思い出して吐き気を催し続けるのだろう。……もう俺の網膜にこの部屋は焼き付いてしまった。
…つまり俺は手遅れだった…。

description: The thing Battler most wants to deny develops cracks in Japanese; English makes Battler himself crack under that thing.
sourceReading: He can feel cracks developing in what he most wants to deny, as the pressure to suspect those close to him grows.

units.text: Even though I was bluffing, that move of the witch's hurt bad... ......I realized I was cracking under the thing I wanted to deny the most. This person's trying to close in on me from two directions.
units.note: MG retains Battler himself cracking. UP says cracks form in the thing he most wants to deny.
units.japanese: ……俺がもっとも否定したいものに、ひびが入るのがわかる。

units.text: Even though I was bluffing, that move of the witch's hurt bad... ......I realized I was cracking under the thing I wanted to deny the most. This person's trying to close in on me from two directions. On the one hand, there's the frontal attack, where she tries to force me to believe there's a witch using closed room tricks that only a witch could do. ......And on the other hand, there's the rear attack, where she tries to lure me into thinking it would be better if there was a witch by strengthening my suspicions of those close to me.
units.note: MG retains Battler himself cracking. UP says cracks form in the thing he most wants to deny.
units.japanese: ……俺がもっとも否定したいものに、ひびが入るのがわかる。

units.text: I may have managed to bluff, but that move of the witch's hurts bad... ...I can tell that I'm cracking under the thing I want to deny the most.
units.note: MG retains Battler himself cracking. UP says cracks form in the thing he most wants to deny.
units.japanese:
虚勢は張るものの、魔女のその指し手はずしりと痛む…。
……俺がもっとも否定したいものに、ひびが入るのがわかる。

description: 紋章入り identifies the envelope by its crest; sealed replaces that identifying mark with a closure condition.
sourceReading: Battler asks whether this is a letter in a crest-bearing envelope like the one at the chapel.

units.text: "What on Earth is that?!  It couldn't be, ......a letter in a sealed envelope, just like in the chapel?!"
units.note: MG identifies only a sealed envelope. UP explicitly includes the crest, restoring the identifying feature despite also calling the envelope sealed.
units.japanese: 「それは一体？！　まさか、……礼拝堂にあったのと同じ、紋章入りの封筒の手紙？！」

units.text: "What on Earth is that?! Could it be...a letter in a sealed envelope, just like in the chapel?!"
units.note: MG identifies only a sealed envelope. UP explicitly includes the crest, restoring the identifying feature despite also calling the envelope sealed.
units.japanese: 「それは一体？！　まさか、……礼拝堂にあったのと同じ、紋章入りの封筒の手紙？！」

description: 赤では言ってはおらぬ is have not said it in red, whereas I won’t say it in red announces future refusal.
sourceReading: Beatrice reminds Battler that she has not asserted this in red.

units.text: "I won't say it in red, alright...?  I won't deny the possibility that after they locked the door and left, someone was hiding in this room, alright...?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG retains future refusal. UP says Beatrice has not said it in red, restoring the status of her preceding statement.
units.japanese: 「妾は赤では言ってはおらぬぞ…？

units.text: "I won't say it in red, okay...? I won't deny the possibility that after they locked the door and left, someone was hiding in this room, okay...? *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG retains future refusal. UP says Beatrice has not said it in red, restoring the status of her preceding statement.
units.japanese: 「妾は赤では言ってはおらぬぞ…？　彼らがこの部屋に施錠をして去った時、この部屋に何者かが隠れていた可能性を否定してはおらぬぞ…？　くっくくくくくくくく！」

description: When they locked the room and left becomes after they locked the door and left.
sourceReading: She has not ruled out someone being hidden inside when the servants locked up and departed.

units.text: "I won't say it in red, alright...?  I won't deny the possibility that after they locked the door and left, someone was hiding in this room, alright...?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG retains after. UP says at the time they locked the door and left.
units.japanese: 彼らがこの部屋に施錠をして去った時、この部屋に何者かが隠れていた可能性を否定してはおらぬぞ…？　くっくくくくくくくく！」
candidates: after they locked the door and left

units.text: "I won't say it in red, okay...? I won't deny the possibility that after they locked the door and left, someone was hiding in this room, okay...? *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG retains after. UP says at the time they locked the door and left.
units.japanese: 「妾は赤では言ってはおらぬぞ…？　彼らがこの部屋に施錠をして去った時、この部屋に何者かが隠れていた可能性を否定してはおらぬぞ…？　くっくくくくくくくく！」
candidates: after they locked the door and left

description: 使用人室の奥 means the back or inner part of the servant room, not its center. Both versions mark the location red.
sourceReading: The room keys are kept in the key box at the back of the servant room.

units.text: "Hmm.  Those are kept in the key box in the center of the servant room.  There are several servant room keys, but all of those are inside the key box."
units.note: Both retain center of the servant room inside the red-marked statement.
units.japanese: それなら使用人室の奥のキーボックスに収められているぞ。
candidates: are kept in the key box

units.text: "Indeed. Those are in the key box in the center of the servant room. There are several servant room keys, but all of those are inside the key box."
units.note: Both retain center of the servant room inside the red-marked statement.
units.japanese: 「うむ。それなら使用人室の奥のキーボックスに収められているぞ。使用人室の鍵は数本あるが、その全てがキーボックスに収められている」

units.text: "Mmhm. Those are in the key box in the center of the servant room. There are several servant room keys, but all of those are inside the key box."
units.note: Both retain center of the servant room inside the red-marked statement.
units.japanese: 「うむ。それなら使用人室の奥のキーボックスに収められているぞ。使用人室の鍵は数本あるが、その全てがキーボックスに収められている」

description: I thought only that the culprit had escaped the closed room becomes I kept thinking that it was something that let the culprit escape. The English supplies an unspecified instrumental subject.
sourceReading: Battler had simply assumed the culprit had got out of the closed room.

units.text: "I kept thinking that it was something that let the culprit escape the closed room.
units.note: MG still says there needed to be some way for escape, preserving an instrumental subject. UP directly says Battler kept thinking the culprit had escaped.
units.japanese: 「俺は、犯人は密室から抜け出したものだとばかり思っていた。
candidates: kept thinking that it was something that let the culprit escape

units.text: "I kept thinking there needed to be some way for the culprit to escape from the closed room.
units.note: MG still says there needed to be some way for escape, preserving an instrumental subject. UP directly says Battler kept thinking the culprit had escaped.
units.japanese: 「俺は、犯人は密室から抜け出したものだとばかり思っていた」

description: Under the bed or in a hidden shelf or anywhere becomes a hidden shelf under the bed. Independent alternatives are combined into one invented arrangement.
sourceReading: Under the bed, in a hidden shelf, anywhere will do: the culprit is waiting for them to leave.

units.text: If there's a hidden shelf under the bed or anything like that, that would be enough. The culprit's hiding somewhere, waiting for us to leave. .........The culprit is also trapped in the closed room even now!! Which means......at this very moment!
units.note: Both retain a hidden shelf under the bed instead of listing under the bed, a hidden shelf, or anywhere else as alternatives.
units.japanese: ベッドの下でも隠し棚でも何でもいい。

units.text: If there's a hidden shelf under the bed or anything like that, that'd be enough. The culprit's hiding somewhere, waiting for us to leave. ......The culprit is also trapped in this closed room even now!!
units.note: Both retain a hidden shelf under the bed instead of listing under the bed, a hidden shelf, or anywhere else as alternatives.
units.japanese:
ベッドの下でも隠し棚でも何でもいい。
どこかに潜み、俺たちが立ち去るのを待っているのだ。………犯人もまた、密室に閉じ込められたままだったのだッ！！

units.text:
If there's a hidden shelf under the bed or anything like that, that would be enough.
The culprit's hiding somewhere, waiting for us to leave. .........The culprit is also trapped in the locked room even now!!
units.note: Both retain a hidden shelf under the bed instead of listing under the bed, a hidden shelf, or anywhere else as alternatives.
units.japanese:
ベッドの下でも隠し棚でも何でもいい。
どこかに潜み、俺たちが立ち去るのを待っているのだ。………犯人もまた、密室に閉じ込められたままだったのだッ！！

description: The subject of 看破したはずだった is Battler: he thought he had seen through how Beatrice deceived him with red-word games. English says you probably saw through me, transferring that recognition to Beatrice and changing successful deception into something she could do.
sourceReading: He thought he had exposed Beatrice’s successful deception through clever use of the red and verbal trickery.

units.text: Beatrice, you bastard, you spoke in riddles by playing around with words and skillfully using the red, and you probably saw through me, realizing that you could skillfully trick me...!!
units.note: MG says Battler was sure he had seen through her method; UP says he thought her red wordplay was smoke and mirrors and was certain she had deceived him. Both restore Battler as the one who believed he recognized the deception.
units.japanese:
ベアトリーチェのヤツめ、赤をうまく使った言葉遊びで煙に撒き、
俺をうまく騙せたに違いないと看破したはずだった…！！

description: 殺された上に遺体が消えたということになっているだけ describes the account that he was killed and his corpse subsequently disappeared. English introduces because he had been killed and makes only thought apply principally to disappearance.
sourceReading: Is it merely the story that he was killed and then his body vanished, while he was never in the servant room at all?

units.text: Yeah, then it's simple. Doctor Nanjo was an accomplice so in other words, he was on the culprits' side...in other words...in other words...so he was never killed in the first place?! We only thought the body disappeared because he had been killed, but he wasn't in the servant room in the first place?!
units.note: MG still frames the thought chiefly as the body disappearing after a killing. UP says they thought both that he had been killed and that the body disappeared, preserving the whole account as provisional.
units.japanese: 殺された上に遺体が消えたということになっているだけで、元から使用人室にはいない？！

units.text: Yeah, then it's simple. Doctor Nanjo was in on it, so in other words, he's on the culprit's side, ...which means...which means... he was never dead in the first place?! We thought his body disappeared after he was killed, but what if he was never in the servant room to begin with?!
units.note: MG still frames the thought chiefly as the body disappearing after a killing. UP says they thought both that he had been killed and that the body disappeared, preserving the whole account as provisional.
units.japanese: あぁ、なら簡単だ。南條先生はグルなんだからつまり、犯人側なんだからつまりつまり、元々殺されてなんかいない？！殺された上に遺体が消えたということになっているだけで、元から使用人室にはいない？！

description: 全てを否定され is passive: everything is denied or refuted against Battler. Will I deny everything changes him into the agent of denial.
sourceReading: Will he have everything refuted and drown in the red sea, or learn the truth and be torn apart by the wolves?

units.text: Which way should I die?! Will I deny everything and drown in a bright-red sea?! Will I know the truth, and have my whole body chewed to bits by the wolves?!
units.note: MG retains Should I deny everything. UP says Battler will have everything denied, restoring him as the target of refutation.
units.japanese: 全てを否定され真っ赤な海に溺れ死ぬのか？！

units.text: Which way should I die?! Should I deny everything and drown in a bright-red sea?! Or should I learn the truth and have my whole body chewed to bits by the wolves?!
units.note: MG retains Should I deny everything. UP says Battler will have everything denied, restoring him as the target of refutation.
units.japanese:
俺はどっちで死ねばいい？！
全てを否定され真っ赤な海に溺れ死ぬのか？！
真実を知り、狼たちに全身を食い千切られるのか？！

description: 誓ってそのようなことは致しません promises that the servants would not do such a thing; nothing of the sort happened denies occurrence instead.
sourceReading: Gohda swears that neither he nor the servants would act in the way Rosa alleges.

units.text: "......Rosa-sama!!  I, Gohda, no, all of the Ushiromiya family servants!  We all swear that nothing of the sort happened!!"
units.note: MG retains nothing of the sort happened. UP says all the servants swear they would do nothing of the sort.
units.japanese: 「……楼座さま！！　この郷田、いえ、右代宮家使用人一同！　誓ってそのようなことは致しません！！」

units.text: "...Rosa-sama!! I, Gohda...no, all of the Ushiromiya family servants! We all swear that nothing of the sort happened!!"
units.note: MG retains nothing of the sort happened. UP says all the servants swear they would do nothing of the sort.
units.japanese: 「……楼座さま！！　この郷田、いえ、右代宮家使用人一同！　誓ってそのようなことは致しません！！」

description: 答えを求める cannot be done without suspecting them; English adds from them and uses demand, making the answer something to extract from the servants.
sourceReading: Battler cannot seek an explanation without suspecting the servants.

units.text: ...But, ......I don't understand anymore!!  I don't understand!! We can't demand an answer from them without suspecting them!!!
units.note: MG uses search for an answer and UP seek an answer, both removing the invented from them object and coercive demand wording.
units.japanese: 彼らを疑わずして、答えを求めることができないんだ！！！

description: 犯人の手に掛けられ explicitly means being killed by the culprit; meet with the culprit omits that causal agency before become corpses.
sourceReading: Their sole chance is to be killed by the culprit and meet Rosa again as corpses.

units.text: ......But, .........that couldn't be done!! They only have one chance to prove their innocence. ......That can only happen when they meet with the culprit, become corpses, and are reunited with Rosa oba-san.
units.note: Both editions retain meet with the culprit and become corpses, omitting the explicit statement that the culprit kills them.
units.japanese: ……彼らが犯人の手に掛けられ、死体となって楼座叔母さんと再会する時だけだ。

units.text: ...But......that couldn't be done!! They only have one chance to prove their innocence. ...That can only happen if they meet with the culprit, become corpses, and are then reunited with Aunt Rosa.
units.note: Both editions retain meet with the culprit and become corpses, omitting the explicit statement that the culprit kills them.
units.japanese: ……だが、………それができないッ！！彼らが無実を証明できる機会はひとつしかない。……彼らが犯人の手に掛けられ、死体となって楼座叔母さんと再会する時だけだ。

units.text: ......But, .........that couldn't be done!! They only have one chance to prove their innocence. ......That can only happen when they meet with the culprit, become corpses, and are reunited with Auntie Rosa.
units.note: Both editions retain meet with the culprit and become corpses, omitting the explicit statement that the culprit kills them.
units.japanese: ……だが、………それができないッ！！彼らが無実を証明できる機会はひとつしかない。……彼らが犯人の手に掛けられ、死体となって楼座叔母さんと再会する時だけだ。

description: まぁ、悪いことじゃないと思うわ means she thinks it is not a bad thing. Sorry, it won’t instead rejects the suggestion that surrendering keys can clear suspicion.
sourceReading: Rosa calls the judgment good: thinking surrender might remove suspicion is elementary, but not a bad step.

units.text: ".....................That's a good judgment.  Those master keys are the greatest basis upon which you have been suspected several times today.  It may seem elementary that letting go of those might clear away that suspicion, but, sorry, it won't."
units.note: MG restores not a bad thing. UP restores the favorable judgment but separately adds start, an unexpressed process framing.
units.japanese: 「………………。……それは良い判断ね。今日、何度もあなたたちが疑われてきた最大の根拠はこのマスターキーのせい。それを手放せば疑いが晴らせるのではないかというのは、初歩的ではあるけれど、まぁ、悪いことじゃないと思うわ。」

description: 一本を掲げて誇示した describes holding up one key conspicuously, not pointing at one inside the handbag.
sourceReading: After throwing the keys into the bag, Rosa raises one of them to flaunt her possession.

units.text: Rosa oba-san snatched Maria's handbag, tossed the master keys in there, and pointed at one of them inside. She was announcing that she had all of the master keys.
units.note: MG says Rosa held one up for everyone to see; UP says she lifted one up for all to see.
units.japanese: 楼座叔母さんは真里亞の手提げを引っ手繰ると、その中にマスターキーをざらざらと放り込み、その内の一本を掲げて誇示した。

description: I’ve been able get omits the infinitive marker to.
sourceReading: Rosa boasts of monopolizing the gun and master keys.

units.text: "I've been able get the gun and all the master keys for myself!  Now, I don't have to suspect anyone.  You all are happy too, right?  Now you don't have to be suspected anymore!  Ahahahahahahahahaha, hah-hah-hah-hah-hah-hah-ha!"
units.note: MG retains been able get; UP supplies been able to get.
units.japanese:
たとえ全員が信用できなくても、私は私自身だけを信用することが出来る！」
「その私が銃とマスターキーを独占できた！
これで私はもう、誰も疑わずに済むの。
あなたたちも嬉しいでしょう？

units.text: "I've been able get the gun and all the master keys for myself! Now, I don't have to suspect anyone. You all are happy too, I take it? Now you don't have to be suspected anymore! Ahahahahahahahahaha, hahahahahahahah!"
units.note: MG retains been able get; UP supplies been able to get.
units.japanese: 「その私が銃とマスターキーを独占できた！　これで私はもう、誰も疑わずに済むの。あなたたちも嬉しいでしょう？　これでもう疑われずに済む！　あっははははははははは、はっはっはっはっはっはっは！」

description: 俺の手を解く describes Maria freeing herself from Battler’s hands or arms before reversing the embrace. Maria let go of my hand implies she had been holding his hand.
sourceReading: Maria loosens Battler’s embrace, then embraces his head in return.

units.text: Maria let go of my hand, ...and then she was the one holding my head.
units.note: Both editions retain Maria let go of my hand before she embraces Battler.
units.japanese: 真里亞は俺の手を解くと、…逆に俺の頭を抱えるように抱いた。
candidates: Maria let go of my hand

units.text: Maria let go of my hand, ...and then she was the one holding my head.
units.note: Both editions retain Maria let go of my hand before she embraces Battler.
units.japanese: 真里亞は俺の手を解くと、…逆に俺の頭を抱えるように抱いた。
candidates: Maria let go of my hand

description: 命を落とすことになろうとも means even if they lose their lives; throwing away this life supplies deliberate disposal.
sourceReading: Even if they die, regaining Rosa’s trust through that would be an honor.

units.text: "......Furniture entrusts its fate to the family.  ......If it comes to throwing away this life, if by that, Rosa-sama's trust could be regained, it would be a great honor."
units.note: MG changes throwing away to giving up but still makes the loss of life an active disposal. UP retains throwing away this life.
units.japanese: 「……家具は、家に運命を委ねます。……命を落とすことになろうとも、それによって楼座さまの信頼を再び勝ち取れるならば、それはとても光栄なことです。」

units.text: "...Furniture entrusts its fate to the family. ...If I could regain your trust by giving up this life of mine, I would consider it a great honor."
units.note: MG changes throwing away to giving up but still makes the loss of life an active disposal. UP retains throwing away this life.
units.japanese: 「……家具は、家に運命を委ねます。……命を落とすことになろうとも、それによって楼座さまの信頼を再び勝ち取れるならば、それはとても光栄なことです」

units.text: "......Furniture entrusts its fate to the family. ......Even if it comes to throwing away this life, if by that your trust could be regained, it would be a great honor."
units.note: MG changes throwing away to giving up but still makes the loss of life an active disposal. UP retains throwing away this life.
units.japanese: 「……家具は、家に運命を委ねます。……命を落とすことになろうとも、それによって楼座さまの信頼を再び勝ち取れるならば、それはとても光栄なことです」

description: 明日の朝食を頼みたい asks Gohda to prepare tomorrow’s breakfast; I can’t wait expresses anticipation instead.
sourceReading: Rosa thanks him and says she would like to entrust tomorrow’s breakfast to him.

units.text: "............Thank you.  I can't wait for your breakfast tomorrow.  ......And the boat will probably come by midday tomorrow.  ...Thanks for everything up until now.  Your cooking was my only pleasure on Rokkenjima."
units.note: MG retains I can't wait for your breakfast. UP restores I would like to ask you for breakfast tomorrow.
units.japanese: 「…………ありがとう。あなたには明日の朝食を頼みたいわ。

units.text: "......Thank you. I can't wait for your breakfast tomorrow. ...And the boat will probably come by midday tomorrow. ...Thanks for everything up until now. Your cooking was my only pleasure on Rokkenjima."
units.note: MG retains I can't wait for your breakfast. UP restores I would like to ask you for breakfast tomorrow.
units.japanese: 「…………ありがとう。あなたには明日の朝食を頼みたいわ。……明日の昼前には船も来るでしょう。…今までありがとう。六軒島で唯一の楽しみがあなたの食事だったわ」

description: Some duplicate keys exists has incorrect subject-verb agreement.
sourceReading: Rosa asserts that duplicate keys must exist.

units.text: "There are five master keys in all?  Who would believe that?  It's obvious that some duplicate keys exists.  ......As if we could trust them just because they pulled keys out of their pockets...!!"
units.note: Both editions use the plural verb exist with duplicate keys.
units.japanese: 「マスターキーは５つで全部？　そんなの誰が信じるの？　どうせ複製の鍵があるに決まってるのよ。……彼らが懐から鍵を出したくらいで信用なんかできるものか…！！」

description: 両手を付いて地に這え commands placing both hands down and crawling on the ground; put your hands together adds a joined-hand posture.
sourceReading: Strip, place both hands on the ground and crawl.

units.text: "Can you do it?  Take off your clothes, be naked, then put your hands together and crawl on the ground.  Clothing is proof of one's humanity.  From now on, you will become furniture, so it's only natural that you will lose that right!!"
units.note: MG says to put the hands on the ground; UP says to put both hands flat and crawl on the ground. Both remove the joined-hand posture.
units.japanese: 「出来るかァ？　服を脱げ、裸になるんだよ、そして両手を付いて地に這え。着衣は霊長にのみ認められた証だ。貴様は今から家具になるんだよ、だからその資格を失う、当然のこと！！」

description: 唸りだす in this troubled deliberation is groaning or a low thoughtful sound, not humming a tune.
sourceReading: George folds his arms and groans again before another long silence.

units.text: George folded his arms and started humming again. ...And the kitchen was once again absorbed by a long silence.
units.note: MG changes humming to mumbling, restoring a troubled low vocalization. UP retains humming.
units.japanese: 譲治は腕を組み、再び唸りだす。

units.text:
George folded his arms and started humming again.
...And the kitchen was once again absorbed by a long silence.
units.note: MG changes humming to mumbling, restoring a troubled low vocalization. UP retains humming.
units.japanese:
譲治は腕を組み、再び唸りだす。
…そして厨房は再び長い沈黙に包まれた。

description: 今の話を本当にしてたら refers to actually telling Rosa this account. If what you said is true instead makes its truth the condition and changes a counterfactual past trouble into present trouble.
sourceReading: If they had actually told Rosa what they have just told George, it would have caused more troublesome complications.

units.text: ......If what you said is true, then we're in even bigger trouble.  ...I see, I understand that Genji-san handled the whole thing composedly."
units.note: Both editions condition the trouble on actually telling Rosa the account, not on whether the account is true.
units.japanese: ……今の話を本当にしてたら、もっと面倒なトラブルになっていただろうね。…なるほど、源次さんがずいぶん冷静な対応をしていたのがわかりました。」

description: 自問している始末 says even eyewitnesses are left asking themselves what it was. Had given up asking asserts cessation instead.
sourceReading: Even those who saw it are themselves still wondering what it was.

units.text: George had not actually seen it, and even when pressed to believe, he just couldn't imagine it. ......It was only natural. Because even the people who had actually seen it had given up asking themselves what it was...
units.note: MG retains had given up asking themselves. UP says the eyewitnesses ended up questioning themselves.
units.japanese: 実際に見た人間たちですら、あれは何だったのかと自問している始末なのだから…。

units.text: George had not actually seen it, and even when pressed to believe, he just couldn't imagine it. ...It was only natural. Because even the people who had actually seen it had given up asking themselves what it was...
units.note: MG retains had given up asking themselves. UP says the eyewitnesses ended up questioning themselves.
units.japanese: 実際に見たわけではない譲治には、信じて欲しいと念を押されても、どうしても想像が及ばない。……無理もないのだ。実際に見た人間たちですら、あれは何だったのかと自問している始末なのだから…。

description: The subject 私たちは continues into 嘉音が帰ってきたと思った; I thought narrows the identification to Genji alone.
sourceReading: There were five of us here, and we thought Kanon had returned through the back door.

units.text: "......I do not have any opinion.  .........All that I would like to say is, ......at that time, there were five people there.  ......And I thought that Kanon had returned through the back door.  Then, we carried him to the servant room, .........something happened, and Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa became people who will never come back."
units.note: Both editions retain I thought, attributing the Kanon identification only to Genji rather than the five witnesses collectively.
units.japanese: ………ひとつだけ申し上げたいのは、……私たちはあの時、ここに５人いた。……そして、嘉音が勝手口から帰ってきたと思った。そして、使用人室に運び、………何かが起こって、南條先生と熊沢が帰らぬ人となってしまった。」
candidates: Kanon had returned through the back door

Then, we carried him to the servant room, .........something happened, and Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa became people who will never come back."
units.note: Both editions retain I thought, attributing the Kanon identification only to Genji rather than the five witnesses collectively.

candidates: Kanon had returned through the back door

units.note: Both editions retain I thought, attributing the Kanon identification only to Genji rather than the five witnesses collectively.

units.text: ...Then, I thought that Kanon had returned through the back door. After that, we carried him to the servant room, ......something happened, and now Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa will never come back to us."
units.note: Both editions retain I thought, attributing the Kanon identification only to Genji rather than the five witnesses collectively.

「………私には、何も意見はありません。………ひとつだけ申し上げたいのは、……私たちはあの時、ここに５人いた」

candidates: Kanon had returned through the back door

「………私には、何も意見はありません。………ひとつだけ申し上げたいのは、……私たちはあの時、ここに５人いた」

units.text: "......And I thought that Kanon had returned through the back door. Then, we carried him to the servant room, .........something happened, and Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa passed on."
units.note: Both editions retain I thought, attributing the Kanon identification only to Genji rather than the five witnesses collectively.
units.japanese:
「………私には、何も意見はありません。………ひとつだけ申し上げたいのは、……私たちはあの時、ここに５人いた」
「……そして、嘉音が勝手口から帰ってきたと思った。そして、使用人室に運び、………何かが起こって、南條先生と熊沢が帰らぬ人となってしまった」
candidates: Kanon had returned through the back door

description: ボンドで貼り付けた means sticking the pieces with glue, not tape.
sourceReading: Even retrieving it and gluing it back together would not restore its efficacy, George jokes.

units.text: "......So when, as they say, the reef was struck by lightning and disappeared, the bottom of the ocean...   Well, I'll bet picking it up and taping it together won't make it effective again.  Hahahahaha."
units.note: Both editions retain taping the mirror together rather than gluing it.
units.japanese: 「……ということは、岩礁が雷で打たれて消えたとか言う時に、海の底か…。まぁ、拾ってボンドで貼り付けたところで、ご利益は戻らないだろうけどね。ははははは。」

units.text: "...So when, as they say, the reef was struck by lightning and disappeared, it must've sank to the bottom of the ocean... Well, I doubt picking it up and taping it together would make it start working again. Hahahahaha."
units.note: Both editions retain taping the mirror together rather than gluing it.
units.japanese: 「……ということは、岩礁が雷で打たれて消えたとか言う時に、海の底か…。まぁ、拾って接着剤で貼り付けたところで、ご利益は戻らないだろうけどね。ははははは」

units.text: "......So when, as they say, the reef was struck by lightning and disappeared, it would have gone to the bottom of the ocean... Well, I'll bet picking it up and taping it together wouldn't have made it effective again anyway. Hahahahaha."
units.note: Both editions retain taping the mirror together rather than gluing it.
units.japanese: 「……ということは、岩礁が雷で打たれて消えたとか言う時に、海の底か…。まぁ、拾って接着剤で貼り付けたところで、ご利益は戻らないだろうけどね。ははははは」

description: Trying find omits to.
sourceReading: George listens for a hint that could ease Shannon’s pain.

units.text: ......Even if he was told a story about witches and evil spirits, it just sounded fake to him. Even so, he listened seriously to Shannon's story, trying find a hint that might relieve at least a little of the pain in her heart.
units.note: MG retains trying find. UP supplies trying to find.
units.japanese: それでも紗音の話を真剣に聞いたのは、彼女の心の痛みを少しでも和らげるヒントが欲しかったからだ。

units.text: ...All this talk about witches and evil spirits just sounded fake to him, even though he was trying to be open-minded. Even so, he listened seriously to Shannon's story, trying find a hint that might relieve at least a little of the pain in her heart.
units.note: MG retains trying find. UP supplies trying to find.
units.japanese: ……魔女や悪霊の話を聞かされても、どうしても眉唾だと思ってしまう。それでも紗音の話を真剣に聞いたのは、彼女の心の痛みを少しでも和らげるヒントが欲しかったからだ。

description: もうないかもしれない becomes are gone now, deleting George’s uncertainty.
sourceReading: The torii and shrine where the mirror was enshrined may no longer be there, but another mirror matters.

units.text: "......The shrine and the torii where it was enshrined are gone now, but the important thing is that there is still another spirit mirror.  .........I've heard that Natsuhi oba-san's family is descended from Shinto priests.  Maybe that isn't just a simple mirror."
units.note: Both editions state that the shrine and torii are gone, omitting George's may no longer exist qualification.
units.japanese: 「……祀っていた鳥居と祠はもうないかもしれないけれど、霊鏡がもう一枚あるのは重要なことだよ。

units.text: "...The shrine and the torii where it was kept are gone now, but the important thing is that there's still another spirit mirror. ......I've heard that Aunt Natsuhi's family is descended from Shinto priests. Maybe that isn't just a simple mirror."
units.note: Both editions state that the shrine and torii are gone, omitting George's may no longer exist qualification.
units.japanese: 「……祀っていた鳥居と祠はもうないかもしれないけれど、霊鏡がもう一枚あるのは重要なことだよ」「………夏妃伯母さんの実家は神職にも通じていると聞いたことがある。それは本当に、単なる鏡ではないかもしれない」

units.note: Both editions state that the shrine and torii are gone, omitting George's may no longer exist qualification.

description: 神職にも通じている says the family has connections with or knowledge extending to the priesthood. Descended from Shinto priests asserts a particular genealogy.
sourceReading: George has heard that Natsuhi’s natal family also has ties to the Shinto priesthood.

units.text: "......The shrine and the torii where it was enshrined are gone now, but the important thing is that there is still another spirit mirror.  .........I've heard that Natsuhi oba-san's family is descended from Shinto priests.  Maybe that isn't just a simple mirror."
units.note: Both editions retain descended from Shinto priests, promoting a broader connection into a specific genealogy.
units.japanese: ………夏妃伯母さんの実家は神職にも通じていると聞いたことがある。それは本当に、単なる鏡ではないかもしれない。」

units.text: "...The shrine and the torii where it was kept are gone now, but the important thing is that there's still another spirit mirror. ......I've heard that Aunt Natsuhi's family is descended from Shinto priests. Maybe that isn't just a simple mirror."
units.note: Both editions retain descended from Shinto priests, promoting a broader connection into a specific genealogy.

units.note: Both editions retain descended from Shinto priests, promoting a broader connection into a specific genealogy.

description: 元よりその覚悟はある means the resolve was already there from the outset, not even more prepared than before.
sourceReading: Because he already intended to confront the family over the engagement, George already has that resolve.

units.text: "When Grandfather gets mad at us, I'll take responsibility.  ......From the beginning, I was planning on fighting with the whole Ushiromiya family today.  So that they would permit my engagement with you.  ...So I'm even more prepared than before."
units.note: MG explicitly says prepared from the start. UP says already prepared after stating that George had planned from the beginning to face the family.
units.japanese: 君との婚約を許してもらうためにね。…だから元よりその覚悟はある。」

description: 誇りある料理人 identifies him as a proud chef; highly praised describes external approval.
sourceReading: As a chef with professional pride, he ordinarily would not want to misuse his cooking tools.

units.text: Gohda was testing several heavy looking cooking tools. ...Normally, a highly praised chef like himself wouldn't want to use them for something other than their intended purpose. But now he was frantic to fulfill the orders of the one he accepted as his master. After some worrying, he took a large, thick-feeling frying pan.
units.note: MG retains highly-praised chef. UP says self-respecting chef, restoring Gohda's own professional pride.
units.japanese: …本来なら、誇りある料理人の彼は用途以外に使いたくなどない。

units.text: Gohda was testing several heavy-looking cooking tools. ...Normally, a highly-praised chef like him wouldn't want to use them for something other than their intended purpose. But now, he was frantic to fulfill the orders of the one he accepted as his master. After some worrying, he took a large, thick-feeling frying pan.
units.note: MG retains highly-praised chef. UP says self-respecting chef, restoring Gohda's own professional pride.
units.japanese:
郷田は、いくつかの重そうな調理道具を吟味している。
…本来なら、誇りある料理人の彼は用途以外に使いたくなどない。しかし今は、彼が主だと認めた者の命令に応えようと必死だった。彼は少し悩んだ末、大きめの重厚感あるフライパンを手にする。

description: 老いぼれ is an insulting or self-deprecating description of an old, worn-out person; senile supplies a more specific implication of mental decline.
sourceReading: Whatever becomes of an old wreck like him depends on the roulette result.

units.text: ...Whatever happens to a senile old man like myself will be decided by the roulette.  I want to sit here and see what the result will be with my own eyes."
units.note: Both editions retain senile old man, adding mental decline to Genji's self-deprecation.
units.japanese: …このような老いぼれがどうなろうと、全てはルーレットの目次第。私は、どのような結果が出るのかを、ここに座って見届けたいと思います。」

units.text: ...The roulette will decide the fate of a senile old man like myself. I will sit here...and see what the result will be with my own eyes."
units.note: Both editions retain senile old man, adding mental decline to Genji's self-deprecation.
units.japanese: 「…このような老いぼれがどうなろうと、全てはルーレットの目次第。私は、どのような結果が出るのかを、ここに座って見届けたいと思います」

units.text: "...Whatever happens to a senile old man like myself will be decided by the roulette. I think I would like to sit here and see what the result will be with my own eyes."
units.note: Both editions retain senile old man, adding mental decline to Genji's self-deprecation.
units.japanese: 「…このような老いぼれがどうなろうと、全てはルーレットの目次第。私は、どのような結果が出るのかを、ここに座って見届けたいと思います」

description: チェス盤の脇へ specifies beside the chessboard. The corner of the room with the chessboard supplies a room-corner location and a different reach.
sourceReading: Genji quietly reaches beside the chessboard, draws something toward himself and conceals it with his palm.

units.text: ......After they flew out of the room, Genji quietly stretched his hand out to the corner of the room with the chessboard. .........He softly pulled something that was there towards himself, and hid it by covering it with his palm.
units.note: Both editions say Genji reaches to the side of the chessboard, removing the invented room corner.
units.japanese: ……彼らが飛び出していった後、源次は、チェス盤の脇へすっと手を伸ばす。
candidates: corner of the room with the chessboard

description: 恐ろしいという感情はわかなかった explicitly says fear did not arise; English describes strange and frightening feelings that he cannot understand.
sourceReading: Strangely, Battler felt no fear despite noticing the three potential remaining victims in the room.

units.text: In which case, could we expect that three more would be gouged in the stomach, knee, and leg and killed? ......Who would that be? ...I looked around the room, noticing that there were three people here, but, how should I say it, my emotions seemed paralyzed. ...I couldn't understand my strange and frightening feelings.
units.note: MG says Battler did not feel frightened; UP says he did not find it terrifying.
units.japanese: …不思議と恐ろしいという感情はわかなかった。

description: 利子 means interest rather than the debt as a whole.
sourceReading: Battler recalls the letter’s abstract promise to give up collecting interest.

units.text: I was sure that the witch had written in her letter that she would give up on collecting the debt, or something abstract like that. ...I optimistically took that to mean that she would give up on killing the whole family, ......but was it really written with that meaning?
units.note: Both editions say collecting interest rather than collecting the debt.
units.japanese: 確か、魔女の手紙には、利子の回収を諦める、みたいな抽象的なことが書かれていた。

description: 誰も死ななくなる states no one will die further; no need for more people to die instead removes necessity without promising cessation.
sourceReading: Maria says the ritual ends and no further person dies when the epitaph is solved.

units.text: "No, that's not true.  ......If you solve the epitaph, Beato's ceremony will be over.  So there won't be any need for more people to die."
units.note: MG says no more people will die. UP retains there won't be any need for more people to die.
units.japanese: 「うぅん、そんなことはない。……この碑文が解けたら、ベアトの儀式はおしまいになる。だからもうそれ以上、誰も死ななくなる。」
candidates: won't be any need for more people to die

units.text: "No, that's not true. ......If you solve the epitaph, Beato's ritual will be over. So there won't be any need for more people to die."
units.note: MG says no more people will die. UP retains there won't be any need for more people to die.
units.japanese: 「うぅん、そんなことはない。……この碑文が解けたら、ベアトの儀式はおしまいになる。だからもうそれ以上、誰も死ななくなる」
candidates: won't be any need for more people to die

description: 魔法というものなの becomes that’s what a witch is.
sourceReading: Risk and weakness are what magic entails, Maria explains.

units.text: "W-ro-ng.  That's what a witch is.  No matter how great the magic, there are definitely risks and weak points.  No, there has to be."
units.note: MG says That's how magic works; UP says That's what magic is.
units.japanese: 「ちーがーうー。それがね、魔法というものなの。どんな大きな魔法にも、絶対にリスクや弱点があるの。うぅん、ないといけないの。」

description: 枯れるのに is concessive, asking why a flower is beautiful despite its eventual withering. English asks why it is beautiful when it withers.
sourceReading: Why are flowers beautiful even though they wither, unlike indistinguishably elaborate artificial flowers?

units.text: "Why is it beautiful when a flower withers?  Why is it that an artificial flower isn't beautiful no matter how elaborate it is, even if you can't tell the difference by looking?
units.note: Both editions restore even though they wither.
units.japanese: 「花は枯れるのにどうして美しいの？　造花は見分けがつかないほど精巧でもどうして美しくないの？

description: 眠ってはいない reports that Rosa is not asleep; couldn’t sleep supplies inability.
sourceReading: She is awake but keeps staring blankly at one empty point.

units.text: I looked vaguely at Rosa oba-san. She was probably tired from being under all this tension the whole time. She couldn't sleep, but she kept staring vaguely at some point off in space.
units.note: MG retains couldn't sleep. UP says she wasn't sleeping.
units.japanese: 眠ってはいないが、宙の何もない一点をぼんやりとずっと見続けていた。

units.text: I looked lazily at Aunt Rosa. She was probably tired from being under all this tension the whole time. She couldn't sleep, but she kept staring vaguely at some point off in space.
units.note: MG retains couldn't sleep. UP says she wasn't sleeping.
units.japanese:
ぼんやりと楼座叔母さんを見る。ずっと緊張を強いられてきたから疲れが出たのだろう。
眠ってはいないが、宙の何もない一点をぼんやりとずっと見続けていた。

description: 心理的に辛い思いをしてきた means she suffered psychologically; her thoughts had become psychologically harsh makes the consequence a quality of her thinking.
sourceReading: Since childhood, conflicting demands for agreement from older siblings caused her psychological distress.

units.text: ...Long ago, I think I heard a bit about it from my dad. Rosa oba-san had originally been a very obedient child. ......But her age was too far separated from the other siblings, and furthermore, because conflicting demands were often made of her by her confrontational siblings, since she was young, her thoughts had become psychologically harsh. Often, when she copied one of her siblings, another sibling would give her a hard time.
units.note: MG says psychologically harsh experiences; UP says psychological hardship. Both restore suffering rather than harsh thoughts.
units.japanese: ……でも、他の兄弟たちと歳が離れ過ぎていて、しかも、対立しがちな兄弟の双方に同意を求められることが多かったため、幼い頃から、心理的に辛い思いをしてきたという。

description: 片方に与した means siding with one party, not copying that sibling.
sourceReading: When Rosa sided with one sibling, the other often made her suffer.

units.text: ...Long ago, I think I heard a bit about it from my dad. Rosa oba-san had originally been a very obedient child. ......But her age was too far separated from the other siblings, and furthermore, because conflicting demands were often made of her by her confrontational siblings, since she was young, her thoughts had become psychologically harsh. Often, when she copied one of her siblings, another sibling would give her a hard time.
units.note: MG retains copied one of her siblings. UP says taken the side of one sibling.
units.japanese: 片方に与したために、もう片方に辛い目にあわせられることも少なくなかったという。

units.text: ...Long ago, I think I heard a bit about it from my dad. Aunt Rosa was originally a very obedient child. ...But her age was too far separated from the other siblings... and they often made conflicting demands of her during their confrontations. Thanks to this, she'd undergone a lot of psychologically harsh experiences in her youth. Often, when she copied one of her siblings, another sibling would give her a hard time.
units.note: MG retains copied one of her siblings. UP says taken the side of one sibling.
units.japanese:
…親父に昔、ちょっとだけ聞いたことがある気がする。
楼座叔母さんは、本来はとても素直な子だった。……でも、他の兄弟たちと歳が離れ過ぎていて、しかも、対立しがちな兄弟の双方に同意を求められることが多かったため、幼い頃から、心理的に辛い思いをしてきたという。片方に与したために、もう片方に辛い目にあわせられることも少なくなかったという。

description: 妾は約束は守る gives a general claim of keeping promises; I will keep my promise narrows it to a singular future commitment. Both are red.
sourceReading: Beatrice keeps promises; she then explains the epitaph outcome and distinguishes deception from breaking promises.

units.text: "I will keep my promise.  If you solve the riddle of the epitaph, you should be able to reach the Golden Land.  When you have, the ceremony will be over.  No more people will die."
units.note: Both editions restore the general I keep my promises in red.
units.japanese: 「妾は約束は守る。碑文の謎を解けば、黄金郷へ至ることができるだろう。さすれば、儀式は終わる。それ以上、誰も死にはせぬ。」

description: 小さな豆粒 becomes a tiny speck, dropping the bean image from the miniature-transformation demand.
sourceReading: Humans exploit loopholes by demanding more wishes or asking the witch to turn into a little bean.

units.text: "...If there's even a small loophole, they'll immediately say something like 'Increase the number of wishes to one hundred', or 'try changing into a tiny speck'."
units.note: MG restores the bean image as turn yourself into a bean, though it omits small. UP retains tiny speck.
units.japanese: 「…少しでも隙があると、連中はすぐに“叶える願いの数を百に増やせ”とか“小さな豆粒に変身してみろ”とか言い出す。」

units.text: "...If there's even a small loophole, they'll immediately say something like "increase the number of wishes to one hundred", or "try transforming into a tiny speck"."
