units.text: Maria fell down. For just an instant, Rosa was ashamed by her thoughts of abandoning her daughter and running away, and at the instant her feet touched ground, she ran back. The goat head that had sprinted over to get the first bite, grabbed hold of the back of Rosa's own child's hair and pulled up...!!
units.note: MG retains both attachment errors. UP correctly limits the abandonment thought to an instant and has Rosa kick against the ground to reverse direction.
units.japanese: 楼座は一瞬だけ、娘を見捨てて駆け去ることを考えたことを恥じ、大地を蹴り戻して瞬時に逆走する。

units.text: Maria fell down. For just an instant, Rosa was ashamed by thoughts of abandoning her daughter and running away, and at the instant her feet touched ground, she ran back. The goat head that had sprinted over to get the first bite... grabbed hold of the back of Rosa's own child's hair and pulled...!!
units.note: MG retains both attachment errors. UP correctly limits the abandonment thought to an instant and has Rosa kick against the ground to reverse direction.
units.japanese: 真里亞が転ぶ。楼座は一瞬だけ、娘を見捨てて駆け去ることを考えたことを恥じ、大地を蹴り戻して瞬時に逆走する。起き上がろうとする我が娘の後ろ髪を、最初のひと齧りにありつこうと疾駆してきた山羊頭が鷲掴みにして引っ張り上げる…！！

description: 腹 is the belly or abdomen. Protruding chest changes the target of the knee strike; the next line retains doubling over from pain in the gut.
sourceReading: Rosa drives her knee into the goat’s protruding belly, causing abdominal pain before forcing the gun into its mouth.

units.text: Rosa rammed into the goat head with her shoulder, spun, bashed the back of her elbow into the goat's jaw, and buried her knee into its protruding chest!! And she thrust the barrel of the gun inside the goat head's mouth as it doubled over from the pain in its gut!
units.note: Both editions retain chest for the source’s belly or abdomen, despite the following gut-pain clause.
units.japanese: 突き出た腹に膝を打ち込むッ！！

units.text: Rosa rammed into the goat head with her shoulder, spun, bashed the back of her elbow into the goat's jaw, and buried her knee into its protruding chest!! And she thrust the barrel of the gun inside the goat head's mouth as it doubled over from the pain in its gut!
units.note: Both editions retain chest for the source’s belly or abdomen, despite the following gut-pain clause.
units.japanese: 楼座が山羊頭に肩からぶつかるッ、回るッ、逆肘が山羊の顎を打ち上げ、突き出た腹に膝を打ち込むッ！！そして内臓の苦痛に身を屈めたその山羊頭の口の中に銃口がねじ込まれるッ！

units.text: Rosa rammed into the goat‐head with her shoulder, spun, bashed the back of her elbow into the goat's jaw, and buried her knee into its protruding chest!! And she thrust the barrel of the gun inside the goat‐head's mouth as it doubled over from the pain in its gut!
units.note: Both editions retain chest for the source’s belly or abdomen, despite the following gut-pain clause.
units.japanese: 楼座が山羊頭に肩からぶつかるッ、回るッ、逆肘が山羊の顎を打ち上げ、突き出た腹に膝を打ち込むッ！！そして内臓の苦痛に身を屈めたその山羊頭の口の中に銃口がねじ込まれるッ！

description: 掌 means palm. She pulled back her fist adds a preparatory action and changes the follow-up strike from a palm to a fist.
sourceReading: Rosa follows with a palm strike to drive the embedded pen deeper.

units.text: That stinger sliced into the left eye of the goat head as it fell over.  Was the goat head's roar a scream? But Rosa's roar was different. She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat head's eye. The pointed tip was gouged into the depths of its head...!
units.note: Both editions retain the added fist withdrawal and replace the source’s palm strike with a fist strike.
units.japanese: 続いて繰り出される掌が目に突き刺さったままの万年筆を打ち抜くのだ。

units.text: Was the goat head's roar a scream? But Rosa's roar was different. She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat head's eye. The pointed tip was gouged into the depths of its head...!
units.note: Both editions retain the added fist withdrawal and replace the source’s palm strike with a fist strike.
units.japanese: 山羊頭の咆哮は悲鳴か。しかし楼座の咆哮は違う。続いて繰り出される掌が目に突き刺さったままの万年筆を打ち抜くのだ。その先端が頭部の深奥を確かにえぐり破壊する…！

units.text: Was the goat‐head's roar a scream? But Rosa's roar was different. She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat‐head's eye. The pointed tip was gouged destructively into the depths of its head...!
units.note: Both editions retain the added fist withdrawal and replace the source’s palm strike with a fist strike.
units.japanese: 山羊頭の咆哮は悲鳴か。しかし楼座の咆哮は違う。続いて繰り出される掌が目に突き刺さったままの万年筆を打ち抜くのだ。その先端が頭部の深奥を確かにえぐり破壊する…！

description: 弾が入った reports that the ammunition is in. Mama, put bullet in reads as an imperative, reversing Maria’s report of having completed the assigned task.
sourceReading: Maria tells Rosa the ammunition is loaded; Rosa praises her and takes the gun Maria throws.

units.text: "Mama, put bullet in!!"
units.note: Both editions make Maria report that the ammunition has been loaded rather than issuing an imperative to Rosa.
units.japanese: 「ママッ、弾が入った！！」

description: 何千万円 denotes some tens of millions of yen, not several million. The magnitude falls by an order of ten in this recollection.
sourceReading: The gold could have yielded tens of millions of yen and allowed Rosa to start her life over.

units.text: Aaaaaaaaaaaaah, what am I doing... I'd had the gold, which would have been worth several million yen. I might have been able to start over with that!!  And yet I fell, lost it, and that's not all, my own life is in danger, even Maria's life is in danger?! ......What has my life been?!!!
units.note: Both editions retain several million yen and reduce the source’s some tens of millions by an order of magnitude.
units.japanese: 黄金を手に入れた、カネにすれば何千万円かになった。

units.text: Aaaaaaaaaaaaah, what am I doing... I had the gold, which would've been worth several million yen. I might've been able to start over with that!! And yet I fell, lost it, and now my own life is in danger, and Maria's too?! ...What has my life been?!!!
units.note: Both editions retain several million yen and reduce the source’s some tens of millions by an order of magnitude.
units.japanese:
あああぁあぁぁ、私は何をやっているんだ…。
黄金を手に入れた、カネにすれば何千万円かになった。それで人生をやり直せたかも！！　なのに転げてなくし、それどころか自分の命も危なくて、真里亞の命まで危なくてッ？！……私の人生って、何だったのッ！！！

units.text:
Aaaaaaaaaaaaah, what am I doing...
I had the gold, it would have been worth several million yen. I might have been able to start over with that!! And yet I fell, lost it, and that's not all, my own life is in danger, even Maria's life is in danger?! ......What has my life been?!!!
units.note: Both editions retain several million yen and reduce the source’s some tens of millions by an order of magnitude.
units.japanese:
あああぁあぁぁ、私は何をやっているんだ…。
黄金を手に入れた、カネにすれば何千万円かになった。それで人生をやり直せたかも！！　なのに転げてなくし、それどころか自分の命も危なくて、真里亞の命まで危なくてッ？！……私の人生って、何だったのッ！！！

description: 世界でたったひとり、ママがいてくれればいい means that all Maria needs is for her one mother to be there for her. It is alright if there is only one Mama in the world shifts the sufficiency condition onto the number of mothers.
sourceReading: There is only one mother, neither a separate good one nor a bad one; Maria only needs that mother to be there and wants to be her mother’s one Maria.

units.text: "Hey, Mama.  ...Did you know?  There is only one Mama in this world.  There's no good Mama or bad Mama.  ...There's just one Mama.  So for Maria, it's alright if there's only one Mama in the world.  And Maria wants to become the only Maria for Mama."
units.note: MG retains not needing any other Mama, shifting the claim toward alternatives. UP correctly says all Maria wants is for her one mother to be present.
units.japanese: 「ねぇ、ママ。…知ってる？　世界にママはひとりしかいないんだよ。いいママも悪いママもいない。…ただ、ママがひとりいるだけなの。だから真里亞は、世界でたったひとり、ママがいてくれればいい。そして、ママにとって、たったひとりの真里亞になりたいの。」

units.text: "Hey, Mama. ...Did you know? You're my only Mama in this world. There's no good Mama or bad Mama. ...There's just one Mama. So I don't need any other Mama in this world. And I wanna be your one and only Maria."
units.note: MG retains not needing any other Mama, shifting the claim toward alternatives. UP correctly says all Maria wants is for her one mother to be present.
units.japanese: 「ねぇ、ママ。…知ってる？　世界にママはひとりしかいないんだよ。いいママも悪いママもいない。…ただ、ママがひとりいるだけなの。だから真里亞は、世界でたったひとり、ママがいてくれればいい。そして、ママにとって、たったひとりの真里亞になりたいの」

description: 機嫌が良くて甘やかしたい describes the mother being in a good mood and wanting to spoil Maria. The Maria who is in a good mood assigns that state to the child.
sourceReading: The Maria her mother wants to spoil when in a good mood and the Maria she finds a nuisance are the same child, just as scary and kind Mama are one mother.

units.text: ".........The Maria who's in a good mood that you want to spoil, and the Maria who's a nuisance and you don't want to be around, aren't different people.  Maria is also just one Maria.  ......So both the scary Mama and the nice Mama are together.  ......To Maria, ...there is just one ......Mama......"
units.note: MG correctly assigns the good mood and desire to spoil Maria to Rosa. UP retains the Maria who is in a good mood.
units.japanese: 「………機嫌が良くて甘やかしたい真里亞と、邪魔だから居て欲しくない真里亞は別人じゃないの。真里亞も、たったひとりの真里亞なの。……だから、怖いママもやさしいママも一緒。

units.text: ".........The Maria who's in a good mood that you want to spoil, and the Maria who's a nuisance and you don't want to be around, aren't different people. I'm also just one Maria. ......So the scary Mama and the nice Mama are just like that. ......To me, ...there is just one... ...Mama......"
units.note: MG correctly assigns the good mood and desire to spoil Maria to Rosa. UP retains the Maria who is in a good mood.
units.japanese: 「………機嫌が良くて甘やかしたい真里亞と、邪魔だから居て欲しくない真里亞は別人じゃないの。真里亞も、たったひとりの真里亞なの。……だから、怖いママもやさしいママも一緒。……真里亞には、…たったひとりの……ママなの……」

description: 遊んであげる here means playing with the child. Had not played it for Maria suggests performing or operating the game for her rather than sharing play.
sourceReading: Rosa bought the puzzle for Maria’s birthday and only played with her that night.

units.text: She had bought that as a birthday present, ......and then hadn't played it for Maria after that night.
units.note: Both editions say Rosa had not played the puzzle with Maria after the first night, restoring shared play.
units.japanese: バースデープレゼントに買ってあげて、……その夜にしか遊んであげなくて。

description: ため息が堪えられない describes being unable to suppress a sigh of admiration. A forced deep breath substitutes a different response.
sourceReading: Even the young narrator cannot help sighing at the vase’s beauty.

units.text: The vase was very beautiful, rich with history and value. Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.
units.note: Both editions retain “forced me to take a deep breath,” substituting breathing for an irrepressible sigh of admiration.
units.japanese: 幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
candidates: forced me to take a deep breath

units.text: The vase was very beautiful, rich with history and value. Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.
units.note: Both editions retain “forced me to take a deep breath,” substituting breathing for an irrepressible sigh of admiration.
units.japanese: それは、とてもとても美しくて、価値と歴史のある素晴らしい壷でした。幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
candidates: forced me to take a deep breath

units.text: The vase was very, very beautiful, rich with history and value. Even as young as I was, it still forced me to take a deep breath when I witnessed its beauty.
units.note: Both editions retain “forced me to take a deep breath,” substituting breathing for an irrepressible sigh of admiration.
units.japanese: それは、とてもとても美しくて、価値と歴史のある素晴らしい壷でした。幼い私が見ても、その美しさにため息が堪えられないほどに。
candidates: forced me to take a deep breath

description: もっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ identifies one of Grandfather’s most treasured collectibles. The English attaches favorite to the collection as a whole instead.
sourceReading: The vase is among Grandfather’s most treasured collection pieces.

units.text: Of course, that was a member of Grandfather's favorite collection. So that I didn't make a mistake and destroy its fragile beauty, I was always strictly ordered to never touch it.
units.note: MG retains “member of Grandfather’s favorite collection.” UP restores one of his favorite collection pieces.
units.japanese: もちろんそれは、お祖父さまにとってもっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ。

units.text: Of course, it was a member of Grandfather's favorite collection. So that I didn't accidentally destroy its fragile beauty, I was always given strict orders never to touch it.
units.note: MG retains “member of Grandfather’s favorite collection.” UP restores one of his favorite collection pieces.
units.japanese: もちろんそれは、お祖父さまにとってもっともお気に入りのコレクションのひとつ。その儚き美しさが、間違って欠けてしまうようなことがないように、私には絶対触れてはならないと日頃から厳命されていました。

description: 軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感 contrasts apparent lightness with silent gravitas. Just glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity drops that contrast and makes the glance confer dignity.
sourceReading: The vase seems translucent yet refined, light yet silently imposing.

units.text: ......But that just made me want to touch it. It was transparent and yet so elegant that just glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity. ...I wanted to see what it felt like to touch a vase like that.
units.note: MG retains the lost transparency/lightness contrast and makes the glance confer dignity. UP restores the visual contrasts and weighty presence.
units.japanese: このような透き通るようで、だけれども気品があって、軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感があり。
candidates: glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity

units.text: ...But that just made me want to touch it. It looked light...and yet so elegant that just glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity. ...I wanted to see what it felt like to touch a vase like that.
units.note: MG retains the lost transparency/lightness contrast and makes the glance confer dignity. UP restores the visual contrasts and weighty presence.
units.japanese: ……でも、だから触れてみたかったのです。このような透き通るようで、だけれども気品があって、軽やかに見えながら物言わぬ重厚感があり。…そんな壷に触れたなら、どんな手触りなのか、試してみたかったのです。
candidates: glancing at it gave it an indescribable sense of dignity

description: 触れてはならぬものだからこそ explains this degree of beauty by its being something one must not touch. Because something this beautiful should not be touched reverses the explanatory relation.
sourceReading: It has such beauty precisely because it is something forbidden to the touch, a beauty dwelling only in extreme fragility.

units.text: However, ...just as Grandfather had said, it was something that shouldn't be touched. Because something this beautiful shouldn't be touched. It was a beauty that could only dwell in something that could break so easily.
units.note: MG retains the reversed relation, saying the vase must not be touched because it is beautiful. UP says its beauty arises precisely because it must not be touched.
units.japanese: これほどの美しさは、触れてはならぬものだからこそ。

units.text: However, ...just as Grandfather had said, it was a thing that shouldn't be touched. Something this beautiful should never be touched. Such beauty can only dwell in something so easily broken.
units.note: MG retains the reversed relation, saying the vase must not be touched because it is beautiful. UP says its beauty arises precisely because it must not be touched.
units.japanese: しかし、…それはお祖父さまが言われた通り、触れてはならないものだったのです。これほどの美しさは、触れてはならぬものだからこそ。触れれば壊れるほどに儚いものにしか宿らぬ美しさ。

description: 黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら describes butterflies glowing fantastically with golden scale dust. Glowing dots shone detaches the dust from them and substitutes dots for powder.
sourceReading: The beautiful butterflies gather, shining fantastically with golden scale dust.

units.text: As mysteriously glowing golden dots shone, the beautiful butterflies began to gather, one at a time. Oh, it's Beatrice. That reliable Golden Witch, Beatrice had arrived.
units.note: MG retains detached glowing dots. UP restores the butterflies glittering with golden powder.
units.japanese: 黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら、その美しき蝶が一匹、二匹と集まります。

units.text: As mysteriously glowing golden dots shone in the air, the butterflies began to gather, one at a time. Oh, it's Beatrice. Beatrice, that reliable Golden Witch, had arrived.
units.note: MG retains detached glowing dots. UP restores the butterflies glittering with golden powder.
units.japanese:
黄金の燐粉で幻想的に輝きながら、その美しき蝶が一匹、二匹と集まります。あぁ、ベアトリーチェです。
頼もしき黄金の魔女、ベアトリーチェが来てくれたのです。

description: Became a group. and there, became the witch’s form separates a lowercase conjunction with a period and leaves the transformation clause without a workable subject.
sourceReading: As butterflies gather into a swarm, her figure appears there.

units.text: The butterflies gathered one after another and became a group. and there, became the witch's form... She was always my ally. Whenever I was in trouble, she would always appear and help me.
units.note: MG replaces the broken clause with a cloud forming and Beatrice appearing. UP makes the gathered butterflies the subject of becoming her form; its punctuation remains awkward, but the original sentence-fragment failure is repaired.
units.japanese: 蝶が次々と集まって群となると、そこには彼女の姿が…。
candidates: became a group. and there, became the witch's form

description: 一度言い聞かせたこと refers to something he has already instructed the child about. Failed to follow something he said even once relocates once onto the disobedience.
sourceReading: Kinzo rages when an instruction he has already given is not followed.

units.text: Grandfather was a very frightening person. And when you failed to follow something he said even once, he would become so mad, with a rage that would make even the fallen angels in hell quiver. Since I knew that so well that it pierced me to the bones, I couldn't do anything but shake like this and cry...
units.note: MG retains “failed ... even once,” attaching once to disobedience. UP restores the condition as failing an instruction already given.
units.japanese: そして、一度言い聞かせたことが守られなかった時は、地獄の堕天使も震え上がるほどに怒り狂うのです。
candidates: failed to follow something he said even once

units.text: Grandfather was a very frightening person. And when you failed to follow something he said even once, he would become so mad, with a rage that would make even the fallen angels in hell quiver. Since I knew that down to my bones, I couldn't do anything but tremble and cry...
units.note: MG retains “failed ... even once,” attaching once to disobedience. UP restores the condition as failing an instruction already given.
units.japanese: お祖父さまはとても恐ろしい方です。そして、一度言い聞かせたことが守られなかった時は、地獄の堕天使も震え上がるほどに怒りくるうのです。私はそれを骨身に染みてよく知っていましたから、こうして震えながら涙を零すしかないのです…。
candidates: failed to follow something he said even once

description: 折檻 denotes punitive chastisement, stronger than being scolded. The earlier English punishment at 83107 shows that the threatened consequence was not consistently limited to verbal reprimand.
sourceReading: Beatrice may provide magic that spares the princess Kinzo’s punishment.

units.text: "I hold no magic to scoop up your fallen tears, princess, but if you want magic that will make it possible for you to avoid being scolded by the Master, I might be able to do something." "R, really...?"
units.note: Both editions reduce 折檻 to being scolded, despite translating the same threatened consequence as punishment at row 41.
units.japanese: 「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません。」

units.text: "I possess no magic that can scoop up your fallen tears, princess, but if you need magic that will prevent the Master from scolding you, I might be able to manage something."
units.note: Both editions reduce 折檻 to being scolded, despite translating the same threatened consequence as punishment at row 41.
units.japanese: 「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません」

units.text: "I hold no magic to scoop up your fallen tears, princess, but if you want magic that will make it possible for you to avoid being scolded by the Master, I might be able to do something."
units.note: Both editions reduce 折檻 to being scolded, despite translating the same threatened consequence as punishment at row 41.
units.japanese: 「零してしまった姫様の涙を掬う魔法は持ち合わせておりませんが、姫様がお館様から折檻を受けなくて済むようにする魔法なら、何とかなるかもしれません」

description: 無限の魔力が備わる says endless magical power is acquired at that level. Considered to be an Endless Witch substitutes a title or classification for the attainment, and supplies the title before the next Japanese reveal.
sourceReading: Upon reaching the level of repeated restoration, a witch possesses endless magic; the honorific name is then introduced.

units.text: "Yes.  When one reaches that level they are considered to be an Endless Witch.  That is the endless level that all witches should reach.  We respect those witches the most and call them this."
units.note: MG prematurely substitutes the Endless Witch title for acquiring endless magical power. UP restores the power attainment and leaves the title reveal to the following lines.
units.japanese: 「えぇ。その境地に達した時、無限の魔力が備わるでしょう。それこそが、魔女の達するべき無限の境地。私たちはその魔女を、最大の敬いをもってこう呼びます。」
candidates: considered to be an Endless Witch

units.text: "Yes. When one reaches that level, they are considered to be an Endless Witch. That is the endless level that all witches ought to reach. We offer the utmost respect to those witches and call them by that title."
units.note: MG prematurely substitutes the Endless Witch title for acquiring endless magical power. UP restores the power attainment and leaves the title reveal to the following lines.
units.japanese: 「えぇ。その境地に達した時、無限の魔力が備わるでしょう。それこそが、魔女の達するべき無限の境地。私たちはその魔女を、最大の敬いをもってこう呼びます」
candidates: considered to be an Endless Witch

description: 有難味を感じる means appreciating the worth of what she has attained. Feel valued changes her gratitude or appreciation into receiving validation.
sourceReading: Beatrice thinks she ought occasionally to appreciate the title earned through long training.

units.text: ...It's a little bit of a waste if I don't feel valued every once in a while.  ......*cackle*cackle*cackle*."
units.note: MG says Beatrice gets a chance to appreciate the title; UP says she feels gratitude for it. Neither retains the original claim that she herself feels valued.
units.japanese: …たまには有難味を感じねば、少々勿体無いというものよ。……くっくくくくく。」

description: 自分の言葉 refers to Beatrice’s own preceding words: the remembered teaching seems to answer them. As though answering herself assigns the reflexive to Teacher.
sourceReading: Beatrice recalls Teacher’s words as if they were a reply to her present question about happiness and the end of training.

units.text: ......I remember her saying something like that as though answering herself.
units.note: MG makes Teacher’s remembered words answer Beatrice directly; UP explicitly makes them an answer to Beatrice’s own words. Both restore the reflexive referent.
units.japanese: ……自分の言葉に答えるかのように、そんなことを言っていたのを思い出す。

description: いくら直しても in this repeated breaking scene means however often Beatrice repairs him. No matter how well replaces repetition with repair quality.
sourceReading: The sisters break him immediately however often Beatrice fixes him.

units.text: "Be silent, you filth!  Since you all devour him like starving dogs, no matter how well Beatrice-sama fixes him, he'll just break right away."
units.note: Both editions retain “no matter how well,” changing repeated repairs into repair quality.
units.japanese: お前たちが飢えた犬みたいにがっつくから、いくらベアトリーチェさまが直しても、すぐ壊しちゃうのよ。」

units.text: "Be silent, filth! If you keep devouring him like starving dogs, of course he'll keep breaking right away, no matter how well Beatrice-sama fixes him up."
units.note: Both editions retain “no matter how well,” changing repeated repairs into repair quality.
units.japanese: 「お黙りなさい、屑どもが！　お前たちが飢えた犬みたいにがっつくから、いくらベアトリーチェさまが直しても、すぐ壊しちゃうのよ」

units.text: "Be silent, you filth! No matter how well Beatrice‐sama fixes him, he just breaks right away, because you all devour him like starving dogs."
units.note: Both editions retain “no matter how well,” changing repeated repairs into repair quality.
units.japanese: 「お黙りなさい、屑どもが！　お前たちが飢えた犬みたいにがっつくから、いくらベアトリーチェさまが直しても、すぐ壊しちゃうのよ」

description: 妾とて元の姿を思い出すのも難しい says even Beatrice finds it difficult to recall the original form. Hard for me to make it remember changes who recalls. The following contrast with making the person himself remember relies on that distinction.
sourceReading: The remains are so ruined that even she struggles to remember his original appearance; having him recall himself is best.

units.text: "...It will be hard for me to make it remember its original form in this state.  It's better to make him remember for himself.  ......Oh, well."
units.note: Both editions restore Beatrice herself recalling the original form, contrasted with making Battler remember it for himself.
units.japanese: 「…このザマでは、妾とて元の姿を思い出すのも難しい。当の本人に思い出させるのが一番か。……やれやれ。」
candidates: hard for me to make it remember

description: 太股 is thighs, not buttocks. The anatomy in Battler’s defiant sexual taunt changes.
sourceReading: He jokes about a harem of large-breasted women with dazzling thighs.

units.text: "Yeah, not bored at all.  Anyway, I get to pick and choose from those big boob Nee-chan's with dazzling asses in my harem.  Thanks to that, I'm not bored at all."
units.note: Both editions retain “dazzling asses,” changing Battler’s reference from thighs to buttocks.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、全然飽きねぇぜ。何しろ、太股の眩しいデカ乳姉ちゃんたちが選り取り見取りのハーレム状態なんだからよ。お陰様でまるで退屈しねぇぜ。」

units.text: "Yeah, no boredom problem here. After all, I get my pick of those massive tit Nee-chan's with the dazzling asses in my harem. Thanks to that, I'm not likely to get bored for a while now."
units.note: Both editions retain “dazzling asses,” changing Battler’s reference from thighs to buttocks.

units.text: "Yeah, I'm not tiring either. I mean, I get to pick and choose from those busty babes with dazzling asses in my harem. Thanks to that, I'm not getting tired at all."
units.note: Both editions retain “dazzling asses,” changing Battler’s reference from thighs to buttocks.

description: Nee-chan’s in pick and choose from those big boob Nee-chan’s is a plural, not a possessive.
sourceReading: Battler refers to the multiple women in his purported harem.

units.text: "Yeah, not bored at all.  Anyway, I get to pick and choose from those big boob Nee-chan's with dazzling asses in my harem.  Thanks to that, I'm not bored at all."
units.note: MG retains the possessive apostrophe in plural “Nee-chan’s.” UP replaces the expression with the grammatical plural “babes.”

description: 今に means before long or eventually; Right now he wants to accept it changes Lucifer’s forecast into a claim of present desire. The following 今だって genuinely refers to the present and its distinct escalation is lost.
sourceReading: They need not force acceptance: before long he will want to admit it in tears; she then claims even now he wants to beg forgiveness.

units.text: "It's alright, we don't have to force him to accept it.  Right now he wants to accept it, crying.  Even now, he really wants to kneel down on the ground pitifully and beg our forgiveness!"
units.note: Both editions restore Lucifer’s forecast that Battler will soon want to admit it and preserve the following escalation to what he allegedly wants even now.
units.japanese: 「いいのよ、無理に認めさせなくても。今に泣きながら認めたくなるわ。
candidates: Right now he wants to accept

description: 咎められ says they were reproached or taken to task. Threatened adds an unstated threat.
sourceReading: Eva rebukes their smoking and drives them out onto the deck.

units.text: Rudolf and Hideyoshi went out onto the deck, and took out some cigarettes. Eva had always hated the smell of cigarettes, but when she was in a bad mood, she got even more oversensitive. When they had decided to spend the time until they reached the island smoking casually, the two of them had been threatened and chased out onto the deck.
units.note: Both editions describe the men being yelled at or scolded and chased onto the deck; neither introduces a threat.
units.japanese: 島に着くまでをのんびり喫煙して過ごそうとした二人はそれを咎められ、甲板に追い出されたのだ。

description: 煙草を転がす in this selling context means dealing or trading in cigarettes, not physically rolling them. The next line says he began consuming his merchandise.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi first traded cigarettes after the war, then began smoking what he sold.

units.text: "Just after the war.  In the beginnin', I was rollin' 'em.  Then I started usin' what I was sellin'.  Wahahahahahahaha."
units.note: Both editions retain “rolling” cigarettes, missing Hideyoshi’s postwar cigarette dealing before he consumed his merchandise.
units.japanese: 「戦後すぐや。最初は煙草を転がしとってなぁ。

units.text: "Just after the war. In the beginnin', I was rollin' 'em. Then I started usin' what I sold. Wahahahahahahaha."
units.note: Both editions retain “rolling” cigarettes, missing Hideyoshi’s postwar cigarette dealing before he consumed his merchandise.
units.japanese: 「戦後すぐや。最初は煙草を転がしとってなぁ。自分の売り物に手を付けてしまったわけや。わははははははは」

units.text: "Just after the war. In the beginnin', I was rollin' 'em. Then I started usin' what I was sellin'. Wahahahahahahaha."
units.note: Both editions retain “rolling” cigarettes, missing Hideyoshi’s postwar cigarette dealing before he consumed his merchandise.
units.japanese: 「戦後すぐや。最初は煙草を転がしとってなぁ。自分の売り物に手を付けてしまったわけや。わははははははは」

description: Had dejectedly ran requires had dejectedly run.
sourceReading: The men have retreated to the deck after Eva scolds them.

units.text: Hideyoshi laughed heartily, but Rudolf chuckled. After they had been scolded by Eva, they had dejectedly ran out onto the deck together.  They had almost certainly been dominated by her.
units.note: MG uses “escaped”; UP uses the grammatical “had dejectedly fled.” Neither retains “had ... ran.”
units.japanese: 絵羽に表で吸えと叱られて、一緒にすごすごと甲板に逃げ出してきたのだ。尻に敷かれているに、ほぼ間違いあるまい。

description: 要領も良くて describes being capable or adept at handling things, not to the point. Hideyoshi’s response そういうのは要領がいいとは言わん rejects precisely that praise, but That won’t accomplish anything replaces the repeated term and the disagreement about Eva’s practical judgment.
sourceReading: Rudolf calls Eva smart and resourceful; Hideyoshi says openly cornering Krauss out of hostility is not resourcefulness.

units.text: "...Aneki has always been smart and to the point.  Her grades were good too.  Compared to that, Aniki was just average.  ...Her just being there beside him should have been enough pressure, but Aneki kept boasting about it and driving Aniki into a corner."
units.note: Both editions repeat “shrewd” in Hideyoshi’s rejection of Rudolf’s praise, restoring the argument about Eva’s practical judgment.
units.japanese: 「…姉貴は昔っから、要領も良くて頭が良かった。成績も良かった。それに比べ、兄貴は凡才だった。…ただ、側にいるだけでも充分にプレッシャーだったろうに、姉貴はわざわざそれを誇示してして兄貴を追い詰めていた。」

description: 大学院 means graduate school. College changes the educational stage of Eva’s rejected ambition; this repeats at 84153 and 84280.
sourceReading: Eva wanted to advance to graduate school and argued it was necessary for her cultivation as the eldest daughter.

units.text: ...Since you can still drink black tea without sugar, it was almost the same as saying that study was unnecessary for a woman. Those infuriating words were ones that my older brother had abused me with when I had been in despair, when I had wanted to go to college but was rejected by Father.
units.note: Both editions retain “college,” lowering Eva’s rejected goal from graduate school; each repeats the error in the following explanation.
units.japanese: この腹立たしい言葉は、私が大学院を希望したが父に拒否され、失意の私に兄が吐いた暴言だ。

units.text: ...Since you can still drink black tea without sugar, he was in effect saying that there was no need for women to study. Those infuriating words were what Nii-san hurled at me in my despair, when I asked to go to college only to be denied by Father.
units.note: Both editions retain “college,” lowering Eva’s rejected goal from graduate school; each repeats the error in the following explanation.
units.japanese: …紅茶は、砂糖がなくとも飲めることを思えば、これはつまり、女に学問は不要だと言っているのとまったく同じだ。この腹立たしい言葉は、私が大学院を希望したが父に拒否され、失意の私に兄が吐いた暴言だ。

units.text: ...Since you can still drink black tea without sugar, it was exactly the same as saying that study was unnecessary for a woman. Those infuriating words were ones that my older brother had abused me with when I had been in despair, wanting to go to college but denied by Father.
units.note: Both editions retain “college,” lowering Eva’s rejected goal from graduate school; each repeats the error in the following explanation.
units.japanese: …紅茶は、砂糖がなくとも飲めることを思えば、これはつまり、女に学問は不要だと言っているのとまったく同じだ。この腹立たしい言葉は、私が大学院を希望したが父に拒否され、失意の私に兄が吐いた暴言だ。

units.text: ...Since you can still drink black tea without sugar, it was almost the same as saying that study was unnecessary for a woman. Those infuriating words were ones that my older brother had abused me with when I had been in despair, when I had wanted to go to college but was rejected by Father.
units.note: Both editions again use “college” for Eva’s proposed graduate-school study.
units.japanese: この腹立たしい言葉は、私が大学院を希望したが父に拒否され、失意の私に兄が吐いた暴言だ。

units.text: "Reckless efforts...?! Is it really that bizarre for me to say I want to go to college?!"
units.note: Both editions again use “college” for Eva’s proposed graduate-school study.
units.japanese: 「暴走した努力ですって…？！　私が大学院に進みたいと言い出すのが、そんなにもおかしいって言うの？！」

units.text: "Reckless attempts, you say...?! Is my saying that I want to go to college really that odd?!"
units.note: Both editions again use “college” for Eva’s proposed graduate-school study.
units.japanese: 「暴走した努力ですって…？！　私が大学院に進みたいと言い出すのが、そんなにもおかしいって言うの？！」

units.text: ...Since you can still drink black tea without sugar, it was almost the same as saying that study was unnecessary for a woman. Those infuriating words were ones that my older brother had abused me with when I had been in despair, when I had wanted to go to college but was rejected by Father.
units.note: Both editions again use “college” for the younger Eva’s proposal to attend graduate school.
units.japanese: この腹立たしい言葉は、私が大学院を希望したが父に拒否され、失意の私に兄が吐いた暴言だ。

units.text: "Let's go to college, study more and more, get excellent grades, and drive Krauss into a corner.
units.note: Both editions again use “college” for the younger Eva’s proposal to attend graduate school.
units.japanese: 「大学院に進んで、もっといっぱい勉強して、優れた成績を出して、蔵臼を追い詰めてやりましょう」

units.text: "Let's go to college, study more and more, get excellent grades, and drive Krauss into a corner."
units.note: Both editions again use “college” for the younger Eva’s proposal to attend graduate school.
units.japanese: 「大学院に進んで、もっといっぱい勉強して、優れた成績を出して、蔵臼を追い詰めてやりましょう」

description: いつ理解したのだろう asks when she came to understand. I probably understood that drops the temporal question and instead qualifies whether she understood at all.
sourceReading: She wonders when she understood her father’s view, perhaps already in girlhood, though acceptance waited until adulthood.

units.text: I probably understood that. ......I had probably understood that since I was a young girl. ...But to truly accept that, I had to wait until I had grown up.
units.note: Both editions first ask when Eva understood and then suggest childhood as a possibility, preserving the temporal question.
units.japanese: それを、私はいつ理解したのだろう。

description: 生徒会 is the student council. Vice-president of his class and class president reduce the scope of the offices compared in Eva’s record of achievement.
sourceReading: Krauss only became student council vice-president, while Eva became president.

units.text: I couldn't stand it.  Even though I always got better grades than my brother, even though while he was stuck as vice-president of his class, I became class president, ...even so, my brother was considered to be the appropriate person to succeed the Ushiromiya family just because he was a man.
units.note: Both editions retain class president and class vice-president instead of student-council offices.
units.japanese: 私は悔しかった。兄よりも常に良い成績を残しているのに、兄は副会長止まりだった生徒会も、私は会長にまでなったのに、…それでも右代宮家の跡継ぎには男であるというだけの理由で、兄が相応しいとされていたからだ。

units.text: I couldn't stand it. Even though I always got better grades than Nii-san, even though I became class president when he never managed more than vice-president, ...even so, Nii-san was considered to be the appropriate successor to the Ushiromiya family just because he was a man.
units.note: Both editions retain class president and class vice-president instead of student-council offices.
units.japanese: 私は悔しかった。兄よりも常に良い成績を残しているのに、兄は副会長止まりだった生徒会も、私は会長にまでなったのに、…それでも右代宮家の跡継ぎには男であるというだけの理由で、兄が相応しいとされていたからだ。

units.text: I couldn't stand it. Even though I always got better grades than my brother, even though I became class president while he was stuck as vice‐president of his class, ...even so, my brother was considered to be the appropriate person to succeed the Ushiromiya family, just because he was a man.
units.note: Both editions retain class president and class vice-president instead of student-council offices.
units.japanese: 私は悔しかった。兄よりも常に良い成績を残しているのに、兄は副会長止まりだった生徒会も、私は会長にまでなったのに、…それでも右代宮家の跡継ぎには男であるというだけの理由で、兄が相応しいとされていたからだ。

description: 女を養う means provide for or support women, not cultivate them.
sourceReading: Krauss asserts that women exist to serve men and men to provide for women.

units.text: "It isn't elegant to accept that, but in order to correct your mistake, I think that a few unpleasant words are necessary.  So let me say it plainly.  Women exist to serve men.  And men exist to cultivate women.  A woman's job is to protect a man's back, to protect their house and raise their children.
units.note: MG restores men providing for women. UP retains “cultivate women,” changing financial support into cultivation.
units.japanese: 「それを認めるのはエレガントではないが、お前の勘違いを正すには、少々毒のある言葉も必要かと思うよ。だから言い切ろう。女は男に仕えるために存在する。そして男は女を養うために存在する。女の仕事は、男の背中を守り、家庭を守って子を育てることだ。
candidates: Women exist to serve men.  And men

units.text: "It isn't elegant to admit that, but in order to correct your mistake, I think that a few unpleasant words are necessary. So let me say it plainly. Women exist to serve men. And men exist to cultivate women. A woman's job is to protect a man's back, to protect their house and raise their children."
units.note: MG restores men providing for women. UP retains “cultivate women,” changing financial support into cultivation.
units.japanese: 「それを認めるのはエレガントではないが、お前の勘違いを正すには、少々毒のある言葉も必要かと思うよ。だから言い切ろう。女は男に仕えるために存在する。そして男は女を養うために存在する。女の仕事は、男の背中を守り、家庭を守って子を育てることだ」
candidates: Women exist to serve men. And men

description: 私は心構えを日々養っている says he cultivates the mindset himself. I have been raised changes an active claim of personal preparation into passive upbringing.
sourceReading: Krauss claims to cultivate his readiness as next head every day.

units.text: "It's about whether or not you know your place.  Every day, I have been raised so that I would be prepared to be the next head.  In the future, that will definitely be essential.  But you are different.  Even though you will marry and lose the Ushiromiya family name, you keep seeing this illusion that you don't need to see.
units.note: Both editions retain passive upbringing—“I have been raised”—instead of Krauss actively cultivating his readiness each day.
units.japanese: 「身の程を弁えているか否かだよ。私は次の当主としての心構えを日々養っている。それは将来、必ず必要になることだ。だがお前は違う。嫁ぎ、右代宮の籍を失うことが決まっているくせに、見る必要のない幻を見ている。

units.text: "It's about knowing one's place. Every day, I have been raised with the readiness of one who will be Head. In the future, that preparation will surely become essential. But you are different. Even though you will marry and lose the Ushiromiya family name, you're being trapped by this unnecessary illusion."
units.note: Both editions retain passive upbringing—“I have been raised”—instead of Krauss actively cultivating his readiness each day.
units.japanese: 「身の程を弁えているか否かだよ。私は次の当主としての心構えを日々養っている。それは将来、必ず必要になることだ。だがお前は違う。嫁ぎ、右代宮の籍を失うことが決まっているくせに、見る必要のない幻を見ている」

units.text: "It's about whether or not you know your place. Every day, I have been raised so that I would be prepared to be the next head. In the future, that will definitely be essential. But you are different. Even though you will marry and lose the Ushiromiya family name, you keep seeing this illusion that you don't need to see."
units.note: Both editions retain passive upbringing—“I have been raised”—instead of Krauss actively cultivating his readiness each day.
units.japanese: 「身の程を弁えているか否かだよ。私は次の当主としての心構えを日々養っている。それは将来、必ず必要になることだ。だがお前は違う。嫁ぎ、右代宮の籍を失うことが決まっているくせに、見る必要のない幻を見ている」

description: お前に期待していることなど何もない means there is nothing he expects from her. What you are expecting is nothing assigns the expectation to Eva and obscures the explicit paternal rejection.
sourceReading: Kinzo says he has no expectations of her and restricts her to cooking, sewing and service to men.

units.text: "Are you still talking about that?!!  How many times do I have to say it before you'll understand?  What you're expecting is nothing at all!  A woman should just learn cooking and sewing, like a woman!!  You aren't prepared at all as a woman!  I can't sense any of the disposition needed to serve a man, the heart to devote yourself to a man!!
units.note: Both editions explicitly make Kinzo the one who expects nothing from Eva.
units.japanese: お前には何度言えばわかるのだ。お前に期待していることなど何もないッ！　女は女らしく、料理や裁縫を学んでおればいい！！　貴様には女の心構えがないのだ！　夫に仕えようとする気心が、男に尽くそうという甲斐甲斐しさがまったく感じられぬ！！

description: 夫の一族に褒め称えられる is being praised by the husband’s family. Brings praise to your husband’s family changes that family from praising agent into beneficiary.
sourceReading: Kinzo commands her to be a good wife whom her husband’s family praises.

units.text: "That's it, right there you're already wrong!!  Your duty is to marry out of the family, and bring me a man who is profitable to me!  And then devote yourself to your husband, give birth to children and increase in number!  Be a good wife who brings praise to your husband's family!!
units.note: Both editions retain a wife who brings praise to her husband’s family instead of one praised by that family.
units.japanese: 「えぇい、その時点でもう間違っておるわッ！！　貴様の役割は、家を出て嫁ぎ、わしにとって有益な男を連れてくることだ！　そして夫に尽くし、子を産み、増やせ！　夫の一族に褒め称えられる良妻であれ！！
candidates: brings praise to your husband's family

units.text: "That's it, that's where you're already wrong!! Your duty is to marry out of the family and bring me a man who is profitable to me! And then, you will devote yourself to your husband, give birth to children and multiply! Be a good wife who brings praise to your husband's family!!"
units.note: Both editions retain a wife who brings praise to her husband’s family instead of one praised by that family.
units.japanese: 「えぇい、その時点でもう間違っておるわッ！！　貴様の役割は、家を出て嫁ぎ、わしにとって有益な男を連れてくることだ！　そして夫に尽くし、子を産み、増やせ！　夫の一族に褒め称えられる良妻であれ！！」
candidates: brings praise to your husband's family

units.text: "That's it, right there you're already wrong!! Your duty is to marry out of the family, and bring me a man who is profitable to me! And then devote yourself to your husband, be fruitful and multiply! Be a good wife who brings praise to your husband's family!!"
units.note: Both editions retain a wife who brings praise to her husband’s family instead of one praised by that family.
units.japanese: 「えぇい、その時点でもう間違っておるわッ！！　貴様の役割は、家を出て嫁ぎ、わしにとって有益な男を連れてくることだ！　そして夫に尽くし、子を産み、増やせ！　夫の一族に褒め称えられる良妻であれ！！」
candidates: brings praise to your husband's family

description: 本心ではない says he does not really mean it. He is not in his right mind adds a claim about mental state instead of denying sincerity.
sourceReading: Krauss tells Eva to leave, says Kinzo does not really mean his words, and promises to calm him.

units.text: "Eva, leave this place.  He's not in his right mind.  I will calm him down."
units.note: Both editions state that Kinzo does not mean the disinheritance threat, without claiming he is out of his mind.
units.japanese: 「絵羽、席を外せ。本心ではないさ。私がなだめておく。」

description: Permissable is a misspelling of permissible.
sourceReading: Kinzo permits women only a supporting role.

units.text: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, and tried to improve myself so that I could help out with that at any time. ......However, in the end, Father never accepted that. To Father, a woman was only meant to support a man, and nothing further than that was permissable.
units.note: MG retains the misspelling “permissable.” UP uses “permissible.”
units.japanese: 父にとって、女は男を支えるものでしかなく、それ以上であることを許さなかったからだ。

units.text: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, trying to improve myself so I could be of use to him at any time. ...However, in the end, Father never acknowledged my efforts. To Father, a woman was only meant to support a man, and nothing further than that was permissable.
units.note: MG retains the misspelling “permissable.” UP uses “permissible.”
units.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。……しかし、それが父に認められることはついになかった。父にとって、女は男を支えるものでしかなく、それ以上であることを許さなかったからだ。

description: 私もまた打たれるかもしれない means she too may be struck, paralleling Krauss. Hit again suggests she was already hit in this encounter, although 84396–84397 explicitly says she was not.
sourceReading: Approaching the angry father may expose her to the same slap Krauss received.

units.text: If I carelessly approached Father now, I would probably be hit again. ...However, I fearlessly tried to approach Father's back. Genji blocked me...
units.note: MG says Eva may be the one hit next, preserving that she has not yet been hit. UP retains “hit again,” falsely implying an earlier blow to her.
units.japanese: 今の父に無用心に近付けば、私もまた打たれるかもしれない。

units.text: If I approached Father carelessly, I would probably be hit again. ...However, I fearlessly tried to approach Father's back. Genji blocked me...
units.note: MG says Eva may be the one hit next, preserving that she has not yet been hit. UP retains “hit again,” falsely implying an earlier blow to her.
units.japanese: 今の父に無用心に近付けば、私もまた打たれるかもしれない。…しかし、私はそれを恐れず、父の背中に近付こうとした。それを源次が制する…。

description: この場は貸しにしておいてやる means he will count this intervention as a favor she owes him. Leave this place to me substitutes reassurance and drops the debt.
sourceReading: His look tells her to leave quickly and that she owes him for this.

units.text: Go quickly and leave this place to me. Krauss gave me a look telling me that...
units.note: Both editions retain “leave this to me” or “I’ll handle this,” omitting Krauss’s signal that Eva will owe him a favor.
units.japanese: 早く行け、この場は貸しにしておいてやる。

units.text: Go quickly and leave this to me. Krauss gave me a look telling me that...
units.note: Both editions retain “leave this to me” or “I’ll handle this,” omitting Krauss’s signal that Eva will owe him a favor.
units.japanese: 早く行け、この場は貸しにしておいてやる。蔵臼はそんな目配せを送ってくるのだった…。

units.text: Go quickly and I'll handle this for you. Krauss gave me a look telling me that...
units.note: Both editions retain “leave this to me” or “I’ll handle this,” omitting Krauss’s signal that Eva will owe him a favor.
units.japanese: 早く行け、この場は貸しにしておいてやる。蔵臼はそんな目配せを送ってくるのだった…。

description: 認められたかった means she wanted Father to recognize her. I was not accepted replaces the motive with its unsuccessful outcome.
sourceReading: She wanted recognition from Father as part of escaping her wretched self.

units.text: "......I wasn't accepted by Father.  I wanted to take advantage of Nii-san's weakness.  I believed that, if I could do that, I could distinguish my wretched self."
units.note: MG retains the failed outcome “Father didn’t accept me.” UP restores Eva’s motive: she wanted Father to accept her.
units.japanese: 「……お父様に認められたかった。兄さんの鼻を明かしてやりたかった。そうすれば、惨めな自分に決別ができると信じていたわ。」

units.text: "...Father didn't accept me. I wanted to teach Nii-san a lesson. I believed that doing this...would let me say goodbye to the wretched creature I once was."
units.note: MG retains the failed outcome “Father didn’t accept me.” UP restores Eva’s motive: she wanted Father to accept her.
units.japanese: 「……お父様に認められたかった。兄さんの鼻を明かしてやりたかった。そうすれば、惨めな自分に決別ができると信じていたわ」

description: 鼻を明かす means show someone up or get the better of them. Take advantage of his weakness invents an exploitative method. The same substitution appears at 84624.
sourceReading: Eva wanted to show her brother up by taking the succession and winning recognition.

units.text: "......I wasn't accepted by Father.  I wanted to take advantage of Nii-san's weakness.  I believed that, if I could do that, I could distinguish my wretched self."
units.note: MG says Eva wanted to teach Krauss a lesson; UP directly restores getting the better of him. Neither retains exploiting a weakness.
units.japanese: 「……お父様に認められたかった。兄さんの鼻を明かしてやりたかった。そうすれば、惨めな自分に決別ができると信じていたわ。」

description: 惨めな自分に決別 means part with or say farewell to her wretched self. Distinguish my wretched self fails to express release from that identity.
sourceReading: She believed recognition and triumph would let her leave her miserable self behind.

units.text: "......I wasn't accepted by Father.  I wanted to take advantage of Nii-san's weakness.  I believed that, if I could do that, I could distinguish my wretched self."
units.note: Both editions restore saying goodbye to or parting ways with Eva’s wretched former self.
units.japanese: 「……お父様に認められたかった。兄さんの鼻を明かしてやりたかった。そうすれば、惨めな自分に決別ができると信じていたわ。」

description: 私の心に入った傷の裂け目 describes the fissure of a wound in her heart. The fate that went into my heart invents fate as the agent and loses the wound noun until the next sewing image.
sourceReading: Those bitter days left a wound in her heart, which the inner girl taught her to stitch up.

units.text: In those days, I had really believed that my life had no purpose other than to be looked down upon by my brother. ...It's painful just remembering those days.  The fate that went into my heart and tore a hole in me... 'She' had taught me how to sew up that wound...
units.note: Both editions restore a wound or tear in Eva’s heart and the following sewing image.
units.japanese: …それは思い出すだけで苦々しい日々。私の心に入った、傷の裂け目…。
candidates: fate that went into my heart

description: その怒りを勉強に費やす means devote that anger to studying. Learn from it makes anger itself the lesson rather than the energy for study.
sourceReading: The inner girl urges her to channel anger into study, the magic that converts anger into power.

units.text: "Then let's use that anger and learn from it.  ......Changing anger into power is my magic.  I've saved you from several predicaments with that power, and allowed you to succeed where you shouldn't have succeeded.  As long as you have my magic, there's nothing you can't do."
units.note: MG restores using anger to fuel learning. UP retains “learn from it,” making anger the lesson.
units.japanese: 「ならば、その怒りを勉強に費やしましょうよ。……怒りを力に換えるのが私の魔法。この力で、何度もあなたの窮地を救い、あなたは成せないはずのことを成し遂げてきた。私の魔法がある限り、あなたに出来ないことなど有りはしないわ。」

units.text: "Then let's use that anger and learn from it. ......Changing anger into power is my magic. I've saved you from several predicaments with that power, and allowed you to achieve things that should have been impossible for you. As long as you have my magic, there's nothing you can't do."
units.note: MG restores using anger to fuel learning. UP retains “learn from it,” making anger the lesson.
units.japanese: 「ならば、その怒りを勉強に費やしましょうよ。……怒りを力に換えるのが私の魔法。この力で、何度もあなたの窮地を救い、あなたは成せないはずのことを成し遂げてきた。私の魔法がある限り、あなたに出来ないことなど有りはしないわ」

description: 彼女は私だからこそわかっている means the younger self understands precisely because she is Eva herself. I understand assigns that insight to the narrator rather than explaining why the inner girl rejects the proposed compromise.
sourceReading: The inner girl knows what Eva really wants because she is another Eva.

units.text: 'She' rejected my timid thoughts. ...I understand.  ......Because 'she' is me, I understand.
units.note: Both editions make adult Eva the one who understands, instead of explaining that the younger self understands because she is Eva.
units.japanese: …わかっているのだ。……“彼女”は私だからこそ、わかっているのだ。

units.text: "She" rejected my timid thoughts. ...I understand. ...Because "she" is me, I understand.
units.note: Both editions make adult Eva the one who understands, instead of explaining that the younger self understands because she is Eva.
units.japanese:
“彼女”は、私のいじけた考えを一蹴する。…わかっているのだ。
……“彼女”は私だからこそ、わかっているのだ。

units.text:
"She" rejected my timid thoughts. ...I know why.
......Because "she" is me, I know why.
units.note: Both editions make adult Eva the one who understands, instead of explaining that the younger self understands because she is Eva.
units.japanese:
“彼女”は、私のいじけた考えを一蹴する。…わかっているのだ。
……“彼女”は私だからこそ、わかっているのだ。

description: 浜の真砂が尽きるより遥かに早く compares the speed of changing feelings with beach sand running out. Many more times than there are grains changes a temporal comparison into a number of changes.
sourceReading: People’s feelings change far sooner than the sand of the shore runs out; Father’s rule can change too.

units.text: .........People's feelings can change many more times than there are grains of sand on a beach.  Even if we don't prove that Krauss is a stupid man, Father will eventually realize it.  ...At that time, the wall that separates man from woman will be demolished by Father, who set it up in the first place.  That day will surely come."
units.note: Both editions change feelings changing before beach sand is exhausted into changing more times than there are grains.
units.japanese: ………人の気持ちなど、浜の真砂が尽きるより遥かに早く変わるわ。蔵臼が愚鈍な男であることは、私たちが立証しなくても、やがてお父様も理解する。…その時、男女の境の下らない垣根は、それを設けたお父様によって取り払われるの。その日は必ず来るわ。」
candidates: many more times than there are grains

units.text: "......Human feelings can change far more often than the number of sand grains on a beach. Krauss is such a stupid man that Father's eventually gonna realize it, even if we don't prove it for him.
units.note: Both editions change feelings changing before beach sand is exhausted into changing more times than there are grains.
units.japanese: 「………人の気持ちなど、浜の真砂が尽きるより遥かに早く変わるわ。蔵臼が愚鈍な男であることは、私たちが立証しなくても、やがてお父様も理解する」

units.text: ".........People's feelings can change many more times than there are grains of sand on a beach. Even if we don't prove that Krauss is a stupid man, Father will eventually realize it."
units.note: Both editions change feelings changing before beach sand is exhausted into changing more times than there are grains.
units.japanese: 「………人の気持ちなど、浜の真砂が尽きるより遥かに早く変わるわ。蔵臼が愚鈍な男であることは、私たちが立証しなくても、やがてお父様も理解する」
candidates: many more times than there are grains

description: あなたと決別する日が来た says the day to break with or part from her has arrived. I am different from you now substitutes difference for deliberate separation.
sourceReading: Growing up has brought the time for Eva to part with her younger self.

units.text: "I'm not throwing anything away.  ......It's just that I've become an adult, and I'm different from you now."
units.note: Both editions restore the deliberate separation from or parting with Eva’s younger self.
units.japanese: 「捨てるんじゃない。……私も大人になって、あなたと決別する日が来たということよ。」

description: 自慢の息子 is a son she is proud of, not one who is confident himself. どこに出しても恥ずかしくない likewise expresses her confidence in presenting him without shame.
sourceReading: Eva calls George her pride, presentable anywhere, then claims her unattained dream may be achieved through him.

units.text: "G, George is a confident son who won't embarrass himself no matter where he goes...!  The dream that wasn't granted me might be granted to George...!  Jessica's grades and behavior aren't good at all.  And she's a woman!  If only Jessica would step down, George would become the heir...!"
units.note: MG restores “a son I’m proud of,” although it then says George will not embarrass himself rather than Eva. UP’s “my pride and joy, who won’t embarrass me” preserves her stance.
units.japanese: 「じょ、譲治はどこに出しても恥ずかしくない自慢の息子よ…！　私には叶えられなかった夢を、譲治なら叶えられるかもしれない…！　朱志香なんて成績も品行も不良じゃない。それに女なのよ！　朱志香さえ辞退してくれれば、譲治が跡継ぎになることだって…！」

units.text: "G, George is a confident son who won't embarrass himself no matter where he goes...!  The dream that wasn't granted me might be granted to George...!  Jessica's grades and behavior aren't good at all.  And she's a woman!  If only Jessica would step down, George would become the heir...!"
units.note: Both call George their wonderful son and say he performs admirably wherever he goes, conveying parental praise without explicitly saying he is the son they are proud of. Neither makes confidence George’s personality trait.
units.japanese: 「じょ、譲治はどこに出しても恥ずかしくない自慢の息子よ…！　私には叶えられなかった夢を、譲治なら叶えられるかもしれない…！　朱志香なんて成績も品行も不良じゃない。それに女なのよ！　朱志香さえ辞退してくれれば、譲治が跡継ぎになることだって…！」

description: 蔑む資格などありはしない says Eva has no right to scorn Jessica. Jessica has not done anything to be scorned for changes a confession of lacking standing into an assertion of Jessica’s innocence.
sourceReading: Eva recognizes she has no right to despise Jessica and is using the same gendered insults that harmed her.

units.text: It was very painful to say it. Am I just forcing my own regrets onto George? Jessica hasn't done anything to be scorned for. Wasn't I just horrible for hitting her with the same words that had caused me so much suffering...?
units.note: Both editions explicitly say Eva has no right to scorn or disparage Jessica.
units.japanese: 朱志香を蔑む資格などありはしないのに。

description: 肩を叩かれ describes a tap or pat on the shoulder. Shook her shoulders specifies a different, more forceful waking action.
sourceReading: Eva reacts sensitively to Kyrie tapping her shoulder and wakes.

units.text: When Kyrie shook her shoulders, Eva jumped and awoke from her doze.
units.note: MG retains Kyrie shaking Eva’s shoulders. UP restores a tap on one shoulder.
units.japanese: 霧江に肩を叩かれ、絵羽は過敏に反応してまどろみから醒める。

units.text: When Kyrie shook her shoulders, Eva jumped and awoke from her doze.
units.note: MG retains Kyrie shaking Eva’s shoulders. UP restores a tap on one shoulder.
units.japanese: 霧江に肩を叩かれ、絵羽は過敏に反応してまどろみから醒める。

description: 眠れるくらい余裕 contrasts being relaxed enough to sleep with Battler’s fear of falling or sinking. Enough spare time instead interprets composure as available time.
sourceReading: Jessica admires being at ease enough to sleep, unlike frightened Battler.

units.text: "Although it's nice that you had enough spare time to be able to sleep, right?  Battler kept saying 'We're gonna fa-ll, we're gonna dro-wn!'.  Can't get bored with this guy around."
units.note: Both editions restore Eva being relaxed enough to sleep, rather than having enough spare time.
units.japanese: 「眠れるくらい余裕があるのは大したもんだぜ？

description: 出て行く means go out. Came in reverses their movement after their exchange with Eva.
sourceReading: Battler and Jessica leave while fooling around; Rudolf then addresses Eva.

units.text: Battler and Jessica came in, messing around. Rudolf also made a face as if asking, 'Are you alright?'.
units.note: MG retains Battler and Jessica coming in, reversing 出て行く. UP correctly has them go back out.
units.japanese: 戦人と朱志香は、はしゃぎながら出て行く。

units.text: Battler and Jessica came in, messing around. Rudolf also made a face as if asking, "Are you okay?"
units.note: MG retains Battler and Jessica coming in, reversing 出て行く. UP correctly has them go back out.
units.japanese:
戦人と朱志香は、はしゃぎながら出て行く。
留弗夫も、大丈夫か？　という表情を見せた。

description: 荷物を持つよ offers to carry the luggage. I have our luggage turns that helpful offer into a possession report.
sourceReading: George offers to carry the luggage and suggests going up to the deck, prompting Eva’s thanks.

units.text: "Mom, I have our luggage.  Let's go up onto the deck."
units.note: Both editions say George already has the luggage instead of offering to carry it.
units.japanese: 「母さん、荷物を持つよ。甲板に上がろう。」

units.text: "Mom, I have our luggage. Let's go up onto the deck."
units.note: Both editions say George already has the luggage instead of offering to carry it.
units.japanese: 「母さん、荷物を持つよ。甲板に上がろう」

units.text: "Mother, I have our luggage. Let's go up onto the deck."
units.note: Both editions say George already has the luggage instead of offering to carry it.
units.japanese: 「母さん、荷物を持つよ。甲板に上がろう」

description: 感謝しとるくらい says George is actually grateful. Should thank you changes Hideyoshi’s reassuring report into a normative statement of what George ought to do.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi reassures Eva that George feels gratitude for her strict upbringing.

units.text: Eva, you haven't done anything wrong.  To the contrary, George should thank you for strictly disciplinin' him, right?"
units.note: Both editions report that George is in fact grateful rather than saying he merely ought to thank Eva.
units.japanese: 絵羽はなーんも悪ぅない。むしろ、譲治は厳しく躾けてくれたと感謝しとるくらいやで？」

description: 立ち眩みを覚えそう means she nearly experiences lightheadedness. Caused her to remember her giddiness misreads 覚える as recollection, replacing a present near-sensation with remembered illness.
sourceReading: The strong sunlight outside almost really makes her feel lightheaded after the anemia excuse.

units.text: It looked like the sunlight outside caused her to remember her giddiness. A small plank was lowered to get off the boat, and Gohda was waiting there, smiling and ready to lend them a hand.
units.note: MG restores Eva herself almost becoming dizzy. UP removes recollection but generalizes the experiencer to “a person” and uses the broader “giddy”; that residual change is recorded separately.
units.japanese: 表の強い日差しに、本当に立ち眩みを覚えそうになる。
candidates: caused her to remember her giddiness

description: 小学校まるまるひとつ分 compares six years with an entire elementary-school course. Back then I was still in elementary school asserts his enrollment instead and loses the duration comparison.
sourceReading: Six years is a whole elementary-school education, so remembering it all is a tall order.

units.text: "...Six years ago, you say?  Anyway, back then I was still in elementary school, right?  It's pretty unfair to force me to remember, don't you think?"
units.note: MG retains an assertion that Battler was still in elementary school. UP restores the comparison between six years and the whole elementary-school span.
units.japanese: 「…６年前のことかぁ。何しろ６年って言ったら、小学校まるまるひとつ分じゃねぇか。覚えてろってのが酷な話だぜー？」
candidates: back then I was still in elementary school

units.text: "...What, you mean six years ago? I mean, I was still in elementary school back then, right? It's pretty unfair to expect me to remember everything, don't you think?"
units.note: MG retains an assertion that Battler was still in elementary school. UP restores the comparison between six years and the whole elementary-school span.
units.japanese: 「…６年前のことかぁ。何しろ６年って言ったら、小学校まるまるひとつ分じゃねぇか。覚えてろってのが酷な話だぜー？」

description: 少し時間を掛けてたみたい reports an apparent earlier delay in recognizing them. You will remember, it just might take a little time changes that observation into a forecast. The following hurt response becomes Should I feel hurt rather than stating that the observed delay was hurtful.
sourceReading: Jessica noticed Battler taking a while to remember them and says that was a little hurtful.

units.text: "No surprise.  You'll remember about us, it just might take a little time.  Should I feel a little hurt?"
units.note: Both editions report Battler’s observed delay in remembering the cousins and Jessica’s resulting hurt, rather than forecasting later recognition.
units.japanese: 「だろうな。私たちのことを思い出すのに、少し時間を掛けてたみたいだもんな。

description: 妙なところで qualifies where Shannon’s memory is good, not merely how surprising its quality is. Surprisingly good drops its odd selectivity.
sourceReading: Jessica remarks that Shannon has a good memory for peculiar things or in odd respects.

units.text: "Come to think of it, that's right.  Shannon's memory is surprisingly good."
units.note: MG says Shannon’s memory is incredible when least expected, preserving unusual selectivity indirectly. UP explicitly says it is surprisingly good for certain things.
units.japanese: 「そういやそうだよな。紗音って妙なところで記憶力がいいんだよな。」

description: 迎えに来る in the white-horse promise means come for or fetch her. Come to greet you reduces the promised action to a greeting.
sourceReading: Battler promises to return riding a white horse to come for Shannon.

units.text: "Let's see.  ......I'm sure that he said something like this when he left.  'I'll be back, <see you again>.  I'll come to greet you riding on a white horse.'"
units.note: Both editions restore Battler promising to come for Shannon on a white horse rather than merely greet her.
units.japanese: きっと白馬に跨って迎えに来るぜ。”」

description: 三度読み直してから口にすべきかどうか考える instructs deciding whether to speak after rereading. Read it three times before you say it out loud removes the decision and presumes eventual speech.
sourceReading: Draft and reread the embarrassing line, then consider whether to say it at all.

units.text: Maria, I'm sure that when you are in middle school, you'll want to say embarrassing things like that...  When that happens, write it on the back of some leaflet, and read it three times before you say it out loud.  If you don't, you'll definitely regret it...
units.note: MG still tells Maria to read three times before speaking, presuming eventual speech. UP restores deciding whether to say it after rereading.
units.japanese: 真里亞もきっと、中学くらいになったら、そういう恥ずかしいことが口にしたくなるからな…。そういう時は、口に出す前にチラシの裏に書いて、三度読み直してから口にすべきかどうか考えるんだぞ。じゃねぇと、きっと後悔するからな…。
candidates: read it three times before you say it out loud

units.text: Maria, I'm sure that when you're in middle school, you'll want to say embarrassing stuff like that... When that happens, make sure you write it down and read it three times before saying it out loud. If you don't, you'll definitely regret it..."
units.note: MG still tells Maria to read three times before speaking, presuming eventual speech. UP restores deciding whether to say it after rereading.
units.japanese: 「真里亞もきっと、中学くらいになったら、そういう恥ずかしいことが口にしたくなるからな…。そういう時は、口に出す前にチラシの裏に書いて、三度読み直してから口にすべきかどうか考えるんだぞ。じゃねぇと、きっと後悔するからな…」

description: You will have tell requires have to tell.
sourceReading: George asks Shannon to tell him privately when Battler is absent.

units.text: But Shannon, you'll have tell me all about it sometime Battler isn't around.  It sounds pretty interesting."
units.note: Both editions retain the ungrammatical “you’ll have tell,” omitting “to.”
units.japanese: でも紗音、後で戦人くんのいないところでこっそり教えてね。

units.text: But Shannon, you'll have tell me all about it sometime Battler isn't around. It sounds pretty interesting."
units.note: Both editions retain the ungrammatical “you’ll have tell,” omitting “to.”
units.japanese: 「でも紗音、後で戦人くんのいないところでこっそり教えてね。何だか面白そうだから」

units.text: "But Shannon, you'll have tell me all about it sometime Battler‐kun isn't around. It sounds pretty interesting."
units.note: Both editions retain the ungrammatical “you’ll have tell,” omitting “to.”
units.japanese: 「でも紗音、後で戦人くんのいないところでこっそり教えてね。何だか面白そうだから」

description: 聞きだそうとする素振り describes George feigning an attempt to draw the embarrassing remarks from Shannon in order to tease Battler. Warming up for when Shannon would tell him changes the staged interrogation into preparation for a future disclosure.
sourceReading: George teases Battler by acting as if he is trying to get Shannon to recount more slips of the tongue.

units.text: For a while, George-aniki laughed at me, as though warming up for when Shannon-chan would tell him about more of my embarrassing misspeaks.
units.note: MG retains George warming up for future disclosure. UP restores his pretending to ask Shannon in order to tease Battler.
units.japanese: しばらくの間、譲治の兄貴は、紗音ちゃんから俺の恥ずかしい失言を聞きだそうとする素振りをして、俺をからかうのだった。

units.text: For a while, George-aniki laughed at me, as though warming up for when Shannon-chan would tell him about more of my embarrassing misspeaks.
units.note: MG retains George warming up for future disclosure. UP restores his pretending to ask Shannon in order to tease Battler.
units.japanese: しばらくの間、譲治の兄貴は、紗音ちゃんから俺の恥ずかしい失言を聞きだそうとする素振りをして、俺をからかうのだった。

description: 人間もできてる means George is mature or well-rounded as a person, not that he is talented.
sourceReading: Battler regards George’s mature character as making him a fitting partner.

units.text: ...Y, yeah but, since when?  Wo-w, a lot can happen in six years......  But still, Aniki really is talented, and Shannon-chan is kind and brave, ......they might be a pretty good match."
units.note: MG calls George an amazing person and UP calls him talented; neither conveys Battler’s judgment that George is mature or well-rounded.
units.japanese: ……い、いやでも、いつの間に？　はー、６年ってすげぇなぁ……。でも、確かに兄貴なら人間もできてるし、紗音ちゃんもやさしくて甲斐甲斐しそうだし、

units.text: ...Y-Yeah, but, since when? Whew, I guess a lot can happen in six years... But yeah, Aniki's an amazing person, and Shannon-chan seems to be kind and brave, ...so they might make a pretty good match."
units.note: MG calls George an amazing person and UP calls him talented; neither conveys Battler’s judgment that George is mature or well-rounded.
units.japanese: 「……い、いやでも、いつの間に？　はー、６年ってすげぇなぁ……。でも、確かに兄貴なら人間もできてるし、紗音ちゃんもやさしくて甲斐甲斐しそうだし、……お似合いかもなぁ」

units.text: "...Y‐yeah, but, since when? Wowww, a lot can happen in six years...... But still, Aniki really is talented, and Shannon‐chan is kind and spirited... ......They might be a pretty good match."
units.note: MG calls George an amazing person and UP calls him talented; neither conveys Battler’s judgment that George is mature or well-rounded.
units.japanese: 「……い、いやでも、いつの間に？　はー、６年ってすげぇなぁ……。でも、確かに兄貴なら人間もできてるし、紗音ちゃんもやさしくて甲斐甲斐しそうだし、……お似合いかもなぁ」

description: 甲斐甲斐しそう means seeming attentive, devoted or diligent in caring for someone, not brave.
sourceReading: Shannon seems kind and devoted, so Battler thinks the couple is well matched.

units.text: ...Y, yeah but, since when?  Wo-w, a lot can happen in six years......  But still, Aniki really is talented, and Shannon-chan is kind and brave, ......they might be a pretty good match."
units.note: MG retains “brave” and UP uses “spirited”; neither conveys Shannon seeming attentive or devoted in caring for someone.

units.text: ...Y-Yeah, but, since when? Whew, I guess a lot can happen in six years... But yeah, Aniki's an amazing person, and Shannon-chan seems to be kind and brave, ...so they might make a pretty good match."
units.note: MG retains “brave” and UP uses “spirited”; neither conveys Shannon seeming attentive or devoted in caring for someone.
