units.text: "...Y‐yeah, but, since when? Wowww, a lot can happen in six years...... But still, Aniki really is talented, and Shannon‐chan is kind and spirited... ......They might be a pretty good match."
units.note: MG retains “brave” and UP uses “spirited”; neither conveys Shannon seeming attentive or devoted in caring for someone.
units.japanese: 「……い、いやでも、いつの間に？　はー、６年ってすげぇなぁ……。でも、確かに兄貴なら人間もできてるし、紗音ちゃんもやさしくて甲斐甲斐しそうだし、……お似合いかもなぁ」

description: 逆ギレされる means being met with angry backlash despite the other person being at fault or initiating things. Betray me like this replaces the conversational anger with disloyalty.
sourceReading: Battler complains that Jessica started the topic and then got angry when he asked her the same question.

units.text: "Even though you're the one who brought up this subject, why do you have to betray me like this?  Women are creatures who always ask questions, and yet, they almost never answer them.  What cruel creatures, seriously."
units.note: Both editions restore Jessica angrily turning on Battler rather than betraying him.
units.japanese: 「話を振ってきたのはそっちのくせに、何で俺が逆ギレされなきゃならねぇんだ。女って生き物は質問ばかりで、そのくせ、自分が質問に答えることは決してないんだよな。ズルイ生き物だぜ、まったく。」

description: 面食らわれた means her one-sided approach took the recipient aback. I got confused puts that reaction in Jessica instead.
sourceReading: The person she confessed to was startled by her unilateral approach and had not seen her as a romantic prospect.

units.text: "No, umm, .........well, umm, it was really one-sided and I got confused, I guess...  It was like they didn't view me that way."
units.note: Both editions assign the startled response to Jessica’s confession recipient rather than to Jessica.
units.japanese: 「いいやその、……。…まぁその、私がすごく一方的だったんで面食らわれたというのかな…。そういう対象だとも思われてなかったという雰囲気。」

description: 神妙な言葉遣いになったかと思うと narrates her suddenly adopting earnest speech and then blushing. As Jessica thought about speaking meekly substitutes contemplation for the observable change.
sourceReading: Jessica’s tone becomes suddenly earnest and she blushes.

units.text: As Jessica thought about suddenly speaking meekly, she blushed faintly. ...I see, even though her confession didn't go well, it looks like she still hasn't given up.
units.note: Both editions narrate Jessica actually adopting an earnest or meek manner of speech and blushing.
units.japanese: 朱志香は、急に神妙な言葉遣いになったかと思うと、ほんのりと頬を染めている。

description: After わかるなぁ, the hypothetical 自分も恋人を作らなくちゃ explains Jessica’s likely response to seeing the couple’s progress. I also wanted to find a girlfriend assigns it to Battler.
sourceReading: Battler understands why witnessing George and Shannon’s romance would make Jessica want a partner herself.

units.text: But still, I understood. After seeing how close George-aniki and Shannon-chan had gotten, I also kinda wanted to find a girlfriend.
units.note: MG still makes Battler want a girlfriend; UP restores his inference that Jessica naturally wants a boyfriend after watching George and Shannon.
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴と紗音ちゃんの仲が進展するのを目の当たりにしてたら、自分も恋人を作らなくちゃって気持ちになってくるだろうよ。

units.text: But still, I get it. After seeing how close George-aniki and Shannon-chan have gotten, I also kinda want to find a girlfriend.
units.note: MG still makes Battler want a girlfriend; UP restores his inference that Jessica naturally wants a boyfriend after watching George and Shannon.
units.japanese: でもまぁ、わかるなぁ。譲治の兄貴と紗音ちゃんの仲が進展するのを目の当たりにしてたら、自分も恋人を作らなくちゃって気持ちになってくるだろうよ。

description: この使用人風情が and 泥棒猫 are imagined insults: lowly servant and romantic thief or homewrecker. As though a servant was the same as a cat who had snuck in substitutes a literal comparison and loses both direct class contempt and romantic theft.
sourceReading: Battler imagines Eva screaming contemptuous servant and love-thief insults at Shannon.

units.text: Eva oba-san would probably become an obstacle to George-aniki and Shannon-chan's love. If Eva oba-san learned that the partner of her only beloved son was Shannon-chan, she would probably scream at her, as though a servant was the same as a cat who had snuck in.
units.note: MG removes the literal cat comparison but still omits Eva’s explicit lowly-servant insult; UP restores both the class insult and homewrecker accusation.
units.japanese: あの絵羽伯母さんに限って、眼に入れても痛くないひとり息子のお相手が紗音ちゃんだと知ったら、この使用人風情がー、泥棒猫ーと絶叫するだろう。
candidates: though a servant was the same as a cat who had snuck

units.text: Aunt Eva would probably become an obstacle to George-aniki and Shannon-chan's love. If Aunt Eva ever learned that Shannon-chan was the partner of her only beloved son, she'd probably scream at her for trying to steal away her precious George.
units.note: MG removes the literal cat comparison but still omits Eva’s explicit lowly-servant insult; UP restores both the class insult and homewrecker accusation.
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴と紗音ちゃんの恋路は、……絵羽伯母さんが障害になるだろうな。あの絵羽伯母さんに限って、眼に入れても痛くないひとり息子のお相手が紗音ちゃんだと知ったら、この使用人風情がー、泥棒猫ーと絶叫するだろう。

description: 厳しそうだ marks Battler’s impression that Natsuhi seems strict on such matters. Was also very strict states that quality as known fact.
sourceReading: Battler guesses Natsuhi too would be strict about her daughter loving a servant.

units.text: And a relationship between Jessica and Kanon-kun would probably be just as full of difficulties. Natsuhi oba-san was also very strict about that kind of thing. ......Anyway, Jessica's husband would probably become the head of the Ushiromiya family in the future.  If that person had once been a servant working for the family, ......well, things would get complicated.
units.note: MG states Natsuhi’s strictness as fact; UP preserves Battler’s impression that she seems likely to be strict.
units.japanese: 夏妃伯母さんも、そういうのにかなり厳しそうだ。

units.text: And a relationship between Jessica and Kanon-kun would probably be just as full of difficulties. Aunt Natsuhi was also very strict about that kind of thing. ...After all, Jessica's husband would probably become the Head of the Ushiromiya family in the future. If that person had once been a servant working for the family...well, things would get complicated.
units.note: MG states Natsuhi’s strictness as fact; UP preserves Battler’s impression that she seems likely to be strict.
units.japanese:
そして朱志香と嘉音くんの恋路も同じく多難だろう。
夏妃伯母さんも、そういうのにかなり厳しそうだ。……何しろ朱志香の旦那は、未来の右代宮家当主になるんだろうからな。それが、自分たちに仕えてた元使用人ってことになったら、……まぁその、複雑に違いない。

description: この六年ですっかり成長し青春を謳歌している modifies the cousins he meets. I had grown and being able to celebrate my youth moves those descriptions to Battler.
sourceReading: Meeting cousins who have grown and are enjoying their youth after six years feels fresh to him.

units.text: ......I had grown a lot these last six years, and being able to celebrate my youth and meet with all of my cousins was truly refreshing. ......It was a little late now, but I realized that I should have gotten back together with everyone a lot sooner, and returned to the Ushiromiya family...
units.note: MG still assigns the growth and enjoyment of youth to Battler; UP correctly applies them to the cousins he meets.
units.japanese: ……この６年ですっかり成長し、青春を謳歌しているいとこたちとの出会いは、本当に新鮮。

units.text: ...I grew a lot these past six years...and being able to celebrate my youth and meet with all of my cousins was truly refreshing. ...It was a bit late now, but I realized that I should've gotten back together with everyone a lot sooner, and returned to the Ushiromiya family...
units.note: MG still assigns the growth and enjoyment of youth to Battler; UP correctly applies them to the cousins he meets.
units.japanese: ……この６年ですっかり成長し、青春を謳歌しているいとこたちとの出会いは、本当に新鮮。……俺は、今更だが、もっと早く鞘に収めて、右代宮の家に帰ってきても良かったかな、なんて思っているのだった…。

description: 今日と明日 explicitly covers both today and tomorrow. I wanted this day to end omits tomorrow from the wish for peaceful completion of the visit.
sourceReading: Battler pleads that both today and tomorrow pass peacefully and happily without strange events.

units.text: Therefore..., I wanted this day to end, without anything weird occurring, in peace and happiness, calmly...
units.note: MG restores the wish for both days to end peacefully as “this pair of days.” UP retains “this day,” omitting tomorrow.
units.japanese: 今日と明日が終わって欲しい…。

units.text: So... I want this day to end, without anything weird occurring, in peace and happiness, calmly...
units.note: MG restores the wish for both days to end peacefully as “this pair of days.” UP retains “this day,” omitting tomorrow.
units.japanese: だから…、何もおかしなことは起こらず、平和に幸せに、穏やかに、今日と明日が終わって欲しい…。

description: 魔界 denotes a demonic or magical realm, whereas spirit world suggests a realm of spirits. This changes one member of the escalating otherworld/demonic-world/fantasy-world sequence.
sourceReading: Beatrice commands the storm to isolate Rokkenjima and cast it into otherworld, demon realm and fantasy realm.

units.text: Come, let us begin this tale of tragedy!  Come to me, winds, rain, typhoon!  Cut this island off from the real world!!  Throw Rokkenjima into another world, into the spirit world, into a world of fantasy!"
units.note: MG retains “spirit world.” UP changes it to “netherworld,” which still denotes an underworld or realm of the dead rather than the demonic or magical realm in the Japanese escalation.
units.japanese: さぁさ、始めようではないか、惨劇の物語を！　訪れよ、雨よ風よ台風よ！　この島を現世より切り離せッ！！　異界へ魔界へ幻想界へ、六軒島を放り込めッ！」

units.text: Come, let us begin this tale of tragedy! Come to me, winds, rain, typhoon! Cut this island off from the real world!! Throw Rokkenjima into another realm, into the spirit world, into a world of fantasy!"
units.note: MG retains “spirit world.” UP changes it to “netherworld,” which still denotes an underworld or realm of the dead rather than the demonic or magical realm in the Japanese escalation.
units.japanese: 「さぁさ、始めようではないか、惨劇の物語を！　訪れよ、雨よ風よ台風よ！　この島を現世より切り離せッ！！　異界へ魔界へ幻想界へ、六軒島を放り込めッ！」

units.text: "Come, let us begin this tale of tragedy! Come to me, rain, winds, typhoon! Cut this island off from the real world!! Throw Rokkenjima into another world, into the netherworld, into a world of fantasy!"
units.note: MG retains “spirit world.” UP changes it to “netherworld,” which still denotes an underworld or realm of the dead rather than the demonic or magical realm in the Japanese escalation.
units.japanese: 「さぁさ、始めようではないか、惨劇の物語を！　訪れよ、雨よ風よ台風よ！　この島を現世より切り離せッ！！　異界へ魔界へ幻想界へ、六軒島を放り込めッ！」

units.text: Come, let us begin this tale of tragedy!  Come to me, winds, rain, typhoon!  Cut this island off from the real world!!  Throw Rokkenjima into another world, into the spirit world, into a world of fantasy!"
units.note: The same 魔界 error recurs: MG uses “spirit world” and UP “netherworld,” neither preserving a demonic or magical realm. This recurrence does not add a unique defect.
units.japanese: さぁさ、始めようではないか、惨劇の物語を！　訪れよ、雨よ風よ台風よ！　この島を現世より切り離せッ！！　異界へ魔界へ幻想界へ、六軒島を放り込めッ！」

units.text: "Indeed. You still resist, but I am a fully-fledged witch. I am in contact with several nonhuman entities in the spirit world."
units.note: The same 魔界 error recurs: MG uses “spirit world” and UP “netherworld,” neither preserving a demonic or magical realm. This recurrence does not add a unique defect.
units.japanese: 「うむ。そなたは抗っておるが、妾はれっきとした魔女だ。魔界に通じ、人ならざる数多の存在と交流を持っておる」

units.text: "Hmm, yes. You still fight it, but I am a fully fledged witch. I am in contact with a good many nonhuman entities in the netherworld."
units.note: The same 魔界 error recurs: MG uses “spirit world” and UP “netherworld,” neither preserving a demonic or magical realm. This recurrence does not add a unique defect.
units.japanese: 「うむ。そなたは抗っておるが、妾はれっきとした魔女だ。魔界に通じ、人ならざる数多の存在と交流を持っておる」

description: 修行にはちょうど良いかとも思う says this search would make a suitable training exercise. Practicing your magic is a very good thing drops the specific assessment of the task.
sourceReading: The missing-rose search seems just right for magical training, but the storm is too harsh for Maria.

units.text: "I think that practicing your magic is a very good thing, but it might be a little too much for you with all of this wind and rain.  ......Allow me to lend you some special power.  Being concerned for their disciples is also one of the duties of a teacher."
units.note: MG retains generic praise of practicing magic. UP restores that this particular search is suitable or ideal practice.
units.japanese: 「魔法の修行にはちょうど良いかとも思うが、この風雨はそなたには少しきつかろう。
candidates: practicing your magic is a very good thing

units.text: "I think practicing your magic is a very good thing, but it might be a little too much for you with all this wind and rain. ...Allow me to lend you some special power. Concern for one's disciples is also one of a teacher's duties."
units.note: MG retains generic praise of practicing magic. UP restores that this particular search is suitable or ideal practice.
units.japanese: 「魔法の修行にはちょうど良いかとも思うが、この風雨はそなたには少しきつかろう。……妾が特別に力を貸してやろう。弟子の身を案ずるのも師匠の役割だからな」
candidates: practicing your magic is a very good thing

description: 風雨に散り describes the flower scattering or perishing in the storm. Uprooted specifies removal of roots absent from the source. The next line instead considers a flower torn off with its branch.
sourceReading: Beatrice says the rose has scattered in the storm and is no longer of this world; the narrator considers branch breakage plausible.

units.text: "It was uprooted by the wind, and is no longer of this world."
units.note: Both editions retain “uprooted,” specifying root removal where the Japanese says the rose scattered or perished in the storm.
units.japanese: 「風雨に散り、すでにこの世のものではない。」

units.text: "It was uprooted by the wind...and is no longer of this world."
units.note: Both editions retain “uprooted,” specifying root removal where the Japanese says the rose scattered or perished in the storm.
units.japanese: 「風雨に散り、すでにこの世のものではない」

description: 薔薇が帰ってこないと嫌だ means she refuses to accept the rose not coming back. Maria’s rose won’t come back, no states a negative prediction rather than her condition or demand.
sourceReading: Maria insists that her rose must return and intends to revive it.

units.text: "......No no no!  Maria's rose!!  Maria's rose won't come back, no!  Maria will bring it back to life with her magic.
units.note: MG retains a negative prediction that the rose will not return. UP restores Maria’s insistence that it has to come back.
units.japanese: 「……やだやだやだ！　真里亞の薔薇なの！！　真里亞の薔薇が帰ってこないと嫌だ！　真里亞の魔法で生き返らせる。

units.text: "...No, no, no! It's my rose!! My rose won't come back, no! I'll bring it back to life with my magic.
units.note: MG retains a negative prediction that the rose will not return. UP restores Maria’s insistence that it has to come back.
units.japanese: 「……やだやだやだ！　真里亞の薔薇なの！！　真里亞の薔薇が帰ってこないと嫌だ！　真里亞の魔法で生き返らせる」

description: The narrator conjectures that opening her eyes would break concentration and lose the magic. She was probably afraid adds Maria’s fear and makes the explanation her mental belief.
sourceReading: The narration revises the lack-of-qualification explanation: perhaps opening her eyes would interrupt concentration and dispel the magic.

units.text: ...Maria, who admired magic and the witch, really wanted to see this fantastical sight. However, as an apprentice, Maria was still not qualified to see it. ...No, she was probably afraid that, if she opened her eyes to look, the power that she had concentrated in her heart would be interrupted, and the magic would be lost.
units.note: Both editions say Maria was probably afraid to open her eyes, turning the narrator’s explanation about broken concentration into her fear.
units.japanese: …いや、見る為に目を開けば、心の力の集中力が途切れ、魔法が失われてしまうからだろう。

description: 金色のモール is golden decorative craft trim or tinsel-like material used as a marker. Lace denotes a different material. The same substitution recurs in Beatrice’s explanation at 86642.
sourceReading: The butterfly becomes gold decorative trim marking the restored rose.

units.text: Beatrice, for the sake of her cute apprentice witch who was moaning even more now in concentration, decided to use one more bit of magic. When she snapped her fingers, a single gold butterfly appeared, fluttered around, and landed on the flower that had just been revived. Then it suddenly burst open and disappeared, becoming golden lace and marking the rose...
units.note: Both editions retain “golden lace” for the golden decorative craft trim used to mark the rose.
units.japanese: それは再び、パチンと弾けて姿を消すと、金色のモールになって目印となってくれた…。

Then it suddenly burst open and disappeared, becoming golden lace and marking the rose...

units.text: Beatrice, for the sake of her cute apprentice witch who was moaning even more now in concentration, decided to cast one more little spell. She snapped her fingers, and a single gold butterfly appeared, fluttered around, and landed on the flower that had just been revived. Then it suddenly burst open and disappeared, becoming golden lace and marking the rose...
units.note: Both editions retain “golden lace” for the golden decorative craft trim used to mark the rose.

description: 大き目 specifies the ring’s relatively large size. Valuable replaces size with worth, which is plausible for gold but not stated here.
sourceReading: Kinzo removes the large golden ring from his finger and throws it into the storm.

units.text: After Kinzo flung the window of his study wide open, he took off the valuable golden ring which had been on his finger, and threw it into the darkness of the raging wind and rain... That ring was struck by lightning, and after twinkling gold for an instant, disappeared.
units.note: MG retains “valuable golden ring,” replacing stated size with inferred worth. UP restores that the ring is reasonably large.
units.japanese: 金蔵は書斎の窓を開け放つと、指にはめていた大き目の黄金の指輪を抜き取り、それを荒れ狂う風雨の闇夜に投げ放つ…。

units.text: Kinzo flung the window of his study open wide, took off the valuable golden ring that had been on his finger, and threw it into the darkness of the raging wind and rain... That ring was struck by lightning, and after twinkling gold for an instant, disappeared.
units.note: MG retains “valuable golden ring,” replacing stated size with inferred worth. UP restores that the ring is reasonably large.
units.japanese: 金蔵は書斎の窓を開け放つと、指にはめていた大き目の黄金の指輪を抜き取り、それを荒れくるう風雨の闇夜に投げ放つ…。その指輪は稲妻に打たれ、金色の瞬きを一瞬だけ見せた後、消え去るのだった。

description: 確かに受け取った acknowledges that she has duly received Kinzo’s proclamation through the returned ring. Of course I will receive it turns acknowledgment into future intention.
sourceReading: Beatrice confirms receipt of Kinzo’s declaration that the game has begun.

units.text: "Hmm.  A proclamation from Kinzo to start the game.  Of course I'll receive it."
units.note: MG retains future acceptance of the ring and proclamation. UP restores Beatrice’s acknowledgment that she has received it.
units.japanese: 「うむ。金蔵によるゲームの開始宣言。確かに受け取ったぞ。」

units.text: "Indeed. This is Kinzo announcing the start of the game. Of course I'll accept it."
units.note: MG retains future acceptance of the ring and proclamation. UP restores Beatrice’s acknowledgment that she has received it.
units.japanese: 「うむ。金蔵によるゲームの開始宣言。確かに受け取ったぞ」

description: WH makes this a costly summoning, replacing the employment arrangement with a magical acquisition cost.
sourceReading: 高給で召し上げて describes taking him into service at a high salary.

units.text: *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!!  Ronove holds a noble rank in hell, the 27th highest ranked great demon.  He's a pretty useful man.  I summoned him at high cost and made him serve me."
units.note: Both editions retain Beatrice summoning Ronove at high cost instead of hiring him on a high salary.

description: The wording “can escape barefooted” turns the idiom of alarm into an ability to escape, weakening Ronove’s teasing praise.
sourceReading: 悪魔も裸足で逃げ出す praises a witch so fearsome that even demons would flee without stopping for shoes.

units.text: "It is an honor to be introduced to you.  While my name is amongst those of the nobles of hell, I now serve as the head furniture of Beatrice-sama, the Great Witch with the standing of a vulgar human, from whom even demons can escape barefooted."
units.note: MG says demons flee before Beatrice, and UP says they flee in fear; both restore the idiom of demons fleeing in alarm rather than an ability to escape barefoot.
units.japanese: 地獄の貴族に名を連ねど、今は卑しいニンゲンの分際で、悪魔も裸足で逃げ出すような大魔女であられるベアトリーチェさまの家具頭として仕える身ですよ。」

description: WH instead invites requests for teacakes, changing Ronove’s confident promise about his baking.
sourceReading: お茶菓子にも乞うご期待 asks Battler to look forward to the sweets too.

units.text: "It is an honor to receive such words of praise.  I'm very confident in my tea brewing abilities, so please look forward to tea time.  Baking cookies is one of my hobbies, so please feel free to request teacakes and such."
units.note: MG still invites Battler to request snacks, changing Ronove’s confident promise about his cookies. UP encourages high expectations for the teacakes and preserves the intended anticipation.
units.japanese: 「お褒めの言葉を賜れまして光栄です。私は、紅茶には自信がございますので、ティータイムを楽しみにしていらして下さいね。クッキーを焼くのが趣味でございますので、お茶菓子にも乞うご期待をお願いいたします。」

units.text: "It is an honor to receive such words of praise. I'm very confident in my tea brewing abilities, so please look forward to tea time. Baking cookies is one of my hobbies, so please feel free to request any snacks you may desire."
units.note: MG still invites Battler to request snacks, changing Ronove’s confident promise about his cookies. UP encourages high expectations for the teacakes and preserves the intended anticipation.
units.japanese: 「お褒めの言葉を賜れまして光栄です。私は、紅茶には自信がございますので、ティータイムを楽しみにしていらして下さいね。クッキーを焼くのが趣味でございますので、お茶菓子にも乞うご期待をお願いいたします」

description: WH says he will leave to retake the post and greet them, placing the resumption ahead rather than presenting it as completed.
sourceReading: Ronove will greet the other furniture to announce that he has resumed his position as head furniture.

units.text: Well then, I will leave for now to retake my post as head of the furniture and to greet the rest of the furniture.  Please forgive my short absence."
units.note: MG says Ronove will leave to retake the post. UP says he will inform the others that he has retaken it, restoring the completed resumption.
units.japanese: それでは、これより他の家具どもに、再び家具頭に着任いたしましたことを挨拶してまいります。しばしの暇をお許しください。」

units.text: "Well then, I will leave for now to retake my post as head furniture and greet my subordinates. Please forgive my short absence."
units.note: MG says Ronove will leave to retake the post. UP says he will inform the others that he has retaken it, restoring the completed resumption.
units.japanese: 「それでは、これより他の家具どもに、再び家具頭に着任いたしましたことを挨拶してまいります。しばしの暇をお許しください」

description: “Common goats” omits their work assignment and substitutes an ordinary or low-status classification.
sourceReading: 雑用の山羊ども identifies goats assigned to miscellaneous menial work, alongside sisters assigned to the ritual.

units.text: "Hmm.  Only the common goats and the seven sisters used for the ceremony have manifested themselves.  You will be able to finish up greeting them with ease."
units.note: Both editions call them “common goats,” omitting that they are assigned menial duties.
units.japanese: 「うむ。顕現しているのは雑用の山羊どもと儀式役の七姉妹だけだ。挨拶も楽に終わろう。」

units.text: "Indeed. Only the common goats and the Seven Sisters used for the ceremony have manifested themselves. You will be able to finish greeting them in no time."
units.note: Both editions call them “common goats,” omitting that they are assigned menial duties.

units.text: "Mmhm. Only the common goats and the Seven Sisters used for the ritual have manifested themselves. You will be able to finish up greeting them with ease."
