description: WH instead says the sisters are still playing around, removing Ronove’s inference about Battler’s prior encounter.
sourceReading: Ronove infers that Battler has already played with the seven sisters, addressing Battler with お遊びになられた.

units.text: "Is that so?  It seems that those seven sisters are still playing around.
units.note: Both editions restore Ronove’s inference that Battler has already played with the Seven Sisters, rather than saying the sisters are still playing around.
units.japanese: 「そうでございますか。七姉妹どもとは、もうお遊びになられたようですね。

description: WH tells Beatrice to consider a more positive approach such as kissing his shoes; the conditional offer and Battler’s role as the person reconsidering disappear.
sourceReading: Battler says he might consider recognizing her more favorably if she cries and kisses his shoes.

units.text: "Heh.  That's because, even if the sun starts rising from the west, I will definitely, definitely definitely, never accept that you're a witch.  You might want to consider a slightly more positive approach, like crying and kissing my shoes."
units.note: MG turns Battler’s conditional willingness to reconsider into advice that Beatrice try a more positive approach. UP restores the conditional offer.
units.japanese: 「へっ。例え、お天道様が西から昇ることがあろうとも、絶対の絶対絶対ッ、お前を魔女だと認定などしねぇからな。泣いて俺の靴にキスしたら、もうちょい前向きに検討してやってもいいぜ。」

units.text: "Heh. That's because, even if the sun starts rising from the west, I will definitely, absolutely never accept that you're a witch. You might wanna try a more positive approach, like crying and kissing my shoes."
units.note: MG turns Battler’s conditional willingness to reconsider into advice that Beatrice try a more positive approach. UP restores the conditional offer.
units.japanese: 「へっ。たとえ、お天道様が西から昇ることがあろうとも、絶対の絶対絶対ッ、お前を魔女だと認定などしねぇからな。泣いて俺の靴にキスしたら、もうちょい前向きに検討してやってもいいぜ」

description: WH asks how many demons among the furniture want to visit, collapsing guests and servants into a single group.
sourceReading: Beatrice lists two groups: furniture serving at her golden mansion and demons visiting it.

units.text: "Hah-hah-hah-ha!  Among the furniture that work at my great golden mansion, how many demons do you think want to come over and play?  They will keep coming.  Many of them will appear.
units.note: MG asks how many demons among the furniture want to visit, collapsing servants and visiting demons. UP separately counts furniture serving there and demons visiting.
units.japanese: 「はっはっはっは！　妾の荘厳なる黄金館に仕える家具どもと、そこへ遊びに来る悪魔たちがどれほどいると思っているのか？　まだまだ訪れるぞ。いくらでも現れるぞ。

units.text: "Hahahaha! Among the furniture that work at my great golden mansion, how many demons do you think want to come over and play? They will keep coming. Many of them will appear."
units.note: MG asks how many demons among the furniture want to visit, collapsing servants and visiting demons. UP separately counts furniture serving there and demons visiting.
units.japanese: 「はっはっはっは！　妾の荘厳なる黄金館に仕える家具どもと、そこへ遊びに来る悪魔たちがどれほどいると思っているのか？　まだまだ訪れるぞ。いくらでも現れるぞ」

description: “Barely stumbled at the very end” replaces maintained resistance with a stumble. “Has slightly restored” also changes ongoing incremental revival into a small completed restoration.
sourceReading: Battler is barely holding firm at the final line despite inward wavering; that wavering gradually revives Beatrice’s power.

units.text: "It is as you say.  You barely stumbled at the very end, but your heart is already wavering, and you are unable to deny that I am a witch.  That wavering in your heart has slightly restored my power as a witch."
units.note: MG restores Battler stopping just short of collapse and Beatrice’s power being slowly restored. UP restores the held final line through a cliff image but retains “has slightly restored,” making incremental recovery a small completed result.
units.japanese: 「そういうことだ。そなたは最後の一線でこそぎりぎり踏みとどまっているが、その心はすでにグラつき、妾が魔女であることを否定できずにいる。その心のグラつきが、妾の魔女としての力を少しずつ蘇らせているのだ。」
candidates: barely stumbled at the very end

units.text: "It is as you say. You have managed to avoid taking that final step off the cliff, but your heart is already wavering, and you are unable to deny that I am a witch. That wavering in your heart has slightly restored my power as a witch."
units.note: MG restores Battler stopping just short of collapse and Beatrice’s power being slowly restored. UP restores the held final line through a cliff image but retains “has slightly restored,” making incremental recovery a small completed result.
units.japanese: 「そういうことだ。そなたは最後の一線でこそぎりぎり踏みとどまっているが、その心はすでにグラつき、妾が魔女であることを否定できずにいる。その心のグラつきが、妾の魔女としての力を少しずつ蘇らせているのだ」

description: “Keep on going” loses the belief that the game position would stay unchanged, which the following chess analogy directly refutes.
sourceReading: Battler thought withholding recognition would maintain the status quo.

units.text: "...D, ......damnit..........I thought that, as long as I didn't accept you, I'd be able to keep on going.  ...But apparently I was mistaken somehow."
units.note: MG restores Battler’s belief that he could keep the position unchanged. UP retains the vaguer “keep on going.”
units.japanese: ……畜生……。…俺は、お前を認めさえしなければ、現状は維持できると思っていた。…だがそれはどうやら誤解だったらしいな。」

units.text: "...D‐ ......dammit....... ...I thought that, as long as I didn't accept you, I'd be able to keep on going. ...But it seems apparently I was mistaken."
units.note: MG restores Battler’s belief that he could keep the position unchanged. UP retains the vaguer “keep on going.”
units.japanese: 「…ち、……畜生……。…俺は、お前を認めさえしなければ、現状は維持できると思っていた。…だがそれはどうやら誤解だったらしいな」

description: WH calls both sets merely pieces, removing the emphasis on substantial losses while Battler protects his king.
sourceReading: 大駒 identifies major pieces, rather than pieces generically; the same term recurs in the prediction at 87245.

units.text: "......And furthermore, you're giving it everything you've got just to help your king escape, and have lost several pieces to me, as well as a large advantage.  It is only natural that further advances will lean in my favor."
units.note: MG retains undifferentiated pieces. UP restores that Battler has lost important pieces while protecting his king.
units.japanese: 「……しかしそなたは、キングを逃すのに精一杯で、いくつもの大駒を失い、莫大なアドバンテージを失っておるわ。後の展開が妾に有利に傾くのは当然のことよ。」

units.text: "...And furthermore, you're giving it everything you've got just to help your king escape, and have lost several pieces to me, as well as a large advantage. It is only natural that further developments will tend to turn in my favor."
units.note: MG retains undifferentiated pieces. UP restores that Battler has lost important pieces while protecting his king.
units.japanese: 「……しかしそなたは、キングを逃すのに精一杯で、いくつもの大駒を失い、莫大なアドバンテージを失っておるわ。後の展開が妾に有利に傾くのは当然のことよ」

description: WH predicts he will be frantic as he tries to avoid checkmate, without predicting his continued escapes before the eventual unavoidable mate.
sourceReading: Beatrice predicts Battler will probably continue desperately escaping checkmate itself while losing major pieces.

units.text: From now on, you will probably be frantic as you try to avoid my checkmate.  ...However, as you do, I will steal your pieces from you one by one.  In the end, you'll have lost everything but your king, and you won't be able to escape no matter how much you try.  Then you will receive a true checkmate."
units.note: MG predicts only frantic attempts to evade checkmate. UP restores that Battler will continue succeeding at those escapes for a time.
units.japanese: 「そなたは恐らくこれからも、死に物狂いで妾のチェックメイトだけからは逃れるだろう。…だが、その間にも妾はそなたの大駒を次々に奪っていく。やがてはキング以外の全てを失い、どのような形でも逃れることの叶わぬ、本当のチェックメイトを受けることになろう。」

units.text: "From now on, you will probably be frantic as you try to avoid my checkmate. ...However, as you do, I will steal your pieces from you one by one. In the end, you'll have lost everything but your king, and you won't be able to escape no matter how much you try. Then you will receive a true checkmate."
units.note: MG predicts only frantic attempts to evade checkmate. UP restores that Battler will continue succeeding at those escapes for a time.
units.japanese: 「そなたは恐らくこれからも、死に物ぐるいで妾のチェックメイトだけからは逃れるだろう。…だが、その間にも妾はそなたの大駒を次々に奪っていく。やがてはキング以外の全てを失い、どのような形でも逃れることの叶わぬ、本当のチェックメイトを受けることになろう」

description: WH directly describes the letter as one Beatrice handed her, removing the report qualification.
sourceReading: The letter is described as one Maria says she received from Beatrice: 渡されたという.

units.text: When Maria finished reading the letter that Beatrice had handed her, everyone was at a loss for words for a while. And then, they all broke the silence at once...
units.note: Both editions directly narrate the letter as one Beatrice handed Maria, removing the source’s report qualification.
units.japanese: 真里亞がベアトリーチェから渡されたという手紙を読み終えると、誰もがしばらくの間、言葉を失った。

units.text: When Maria finished reading the letter that Beatrice had handed her, everyone was at a loss for words for a while. And then, they all broke the silence at once...
units.note: Both editions directly narrate the letter as one Beatrice handed Maria, removing the source’s report qualification.
units.japanese: 真里亞がベアトリーチェから渡されたという手紙を読み終えると、誰もがしばらくの間、言葉を失った。そして、その沈黙は一斉に破られる…。

description: WH says he scares most of them, replacing intensity with the proportion affected.
sourceReading: Krauss greatly frightens the children: 大いに modifies their fear.

units.text: Krauss beat the table and stared at everyone. ...Since that included the children too, he scared most of them...
units.note: MG says Krauss scared most of the children. UP restores that including the children in his glare frightened them greatly.
units.japanese: …それには子どもたちも含まれていたため、大いに彼らを怯えさせた…。

units.text: Krauss beat the table and stared at everyone. ...Since that included the children too, he scared most of them...
units.note: MG says Krauss scared most of the children. UP restores that including the children in his glare frightened them greatly.
units.japanese: 蔵臼はテーブルを叩き、ぎょろりと全員を見渡す。…それには子どもたちも含まれていたため、大いに彼らを怯えさせた…。

description: “I don’t understand” presents Hideyoshi as confused rather than raising uncertainty about Kyrie’s conclusion.
sourceReading: わからんで cautions that they cannot be sure; perhaps this really is Kinzo’s prank.

units.text: "I don't understand.  It might really be one of Father's vulgar pranks...  He might've planned this to shock us a bit, since we've been discussin' the distribution of his inheritance without him..."
units.note: Both editions restore Hideyoshi’s caution that they cannot be sure, rather than presenting him as unable to understand.
units.japanese: 「わからんで。まさにお父さんの、悪趣味な悪戯かも知れへん…。自分抜きで遺産分配の話をまとめようとしているわしらを、ちょいと驚かせたくて仕組んだことかもしれん…。」

description: WH says my magic granted your wish, assigning magic to the speaker alone and recasting the shared result as service to the addressee.
sourceReading: The private interjection says our magic has come true: 私たちの魔法、叶った.

units.text: ......See?  My magic granted your wish......
units.note: MG makes the result Eva’s magic granting another person’s wish. UP restores “Our magic worked,” attributing the result jointly.
units.japanese: ……ほら。私たちの魔法、叶ったわ……。

units.text: ...See? My magic granted your wish...
units.note: MG makes the result Eva’s magic granting another person’s wish. UP restores “Our magic worked,” attributing the result jointly.
units.japanese: ……ほら。私たちの魔法、叶ったわ……。

description: “I understand his shock” attributes an actual shocked response to Kinzo rather than sharing an understandable feeling of exasperation.
sourceReading: Natsuhi says one need not be Kinzo to understand the urge to be exasperated at adults taking such a prank seriously.

units.text: "Seriously!!  How could adults like you take such a worthless prank this seriously...!  Even though I am not Father, I understand his shock!!"
units.note: MG says it understands Kinzo’s contempt and UP his exasperation; both attribute an actual reaction to Kinzo instead of expressing Natsuhi’s own understandable exasperation.
units.japanese: 「まったく！！　そんな下らない悪戯に、大の大人がこれほどまで真に受けるとは…！　お父様でなくても呆れたい気持ち、よくわかります！！」

units.text: "Outrageous!! How can adults like you take such a worthless prank this seriously...?! I don't need to be Father to understand his contempt!!"
units.note: MG says it understands Kinzo’s contempt and UP his exasperation; both attribute an actual reaction to Kinzo instead of expressing Natsuhi’s own understandable exasperation.
units.japanese: 「まったく！！　そんな下らない悪戯を、大の大人がこれほどまで真に受けるとは…！　お父様でなくても呆れたい気持ち、よくわかります！！」

units.text: "Good gracious!! How could adults like you take such a worthless prank this seriously...! Even though I am not Father, I understand well his exasperation!!"
units.note: MG says it understands Kinzo’s contempt and UP his exasperation; both attribute an actual reaction to Kinzo instead of expressing Natsuhi’s own understandable exasperation.
units.japanese: 「まったく！！　そんな下らない悪戯を、大の大人がこれほどまで真に受けるとは…！　お父様でなくても呆れたい気持ち、よくわかります！！」

description: WH instead accuses the others of painting things black and white and states that Kinzo will not stop eating to talk. Both proposals become objections.
sourceReading: Krauss proposes settling the question clearly and having Kinzo put down his chopsticks briefly so they can question him.

units.text: "Ah, aah!  You really are trying to paint things as black and white.  He's probably in the middle of eating in his study now.  He isn't going to put down his chopsticks for a while to talk to us...!"
units.note: Both editions restore Krauss agreeing to settle the matter clearly and interrupt Kinzo’s meal, rather than objecting that the others are painting things black and white.
units.japanese: 「あ、あぁ！　はっきり白黒を付けようじゃないか。今頃は書斎で食事中だろう。一度、箸を休めてもらおうじゃないか…！」

description: WH starts “If you explain it that way” and finishes that this is not something children can do, shifting the conditional subject to Kyrie’s explanation and losing the counterfactual self-description.
sourceReading: Jessica says that if she could compartmentalize the matter so neatly, she would not be a child; the conditional concerns her capacity to separate feelings.

units.text: "If you explain it that way, ......that's not something us kids can do......"
units.note: MG retains a condition about being happy with Kyrie’s explanation. UP’s “If we could be that cut and dried” restores the children’s inability to compartmentalize the adults’ conduct.
units.japanese:
「そう割り切れるなら、
……子どもなんてやってねぇぜ……。」

units.text: "If we could be happy with an explanation like that, ...we wouldn't be kids..."
units.note: MG retains a condition about being happy with Kyrie’s explanation. UP’s “If we could be that cut and dried” restores the children’s inability to compartmentalize the adults’ conduct.
units.japanese: 「そう割り切れるなら、……子どもなんてやってねぇぜ……」

description: WH says it sounds like Grandfather is feeling good about himself, replacing Battler’s approval with Kinzo’s emotion.
sourceReading: Battler feels like saying “Good job, Grandfather” in response to the parents being rebuffed.

units.text: ...Well, it sounds like Grandfather's feeling pretty good about himself. He was probably pretty satisfied with how his strange letter had given his children a good shock, since they had all been so infatuated with the distribution of the inheritance while Grandfather was still alive. I also felt like our despicable parents had gotten what they deserved in all of this confusion.
units.note: MG’s high-five feeling and UP’s pat on the back both restore Battler’s approval of Kinzo rather than assigning self-satisfaction to Kinzo.
units.japanese: …まぁ、こう言っちゃ何だが、祖父さまグッジョブという気分だ。

description: WH places the repeated mentions in talk about the letter, moving the evidence out of the document.
sourceReading: Kinzo’s name appears repeatedly within the witch’s letter.

units.text: Apparently, Grandfather hadn't seemed concerned with the whole thing, but he also hadn't denied anything about the letter either. When talking about the witch's letter, Grandfather's name kept popping up. If Grandfather knew that someone was stealing his name, then considering his character, he would probably be mad with rage.
units.note: MG still places Kinzo’s recurring name in talk about the letter. UP restores that his name appears several times in the letter itself.
units.japanese: 魔女の手紙には、祖父さまの名が何度も出てくる。

units.text: Apparently, Grandfather hadn't seemed concerned with the whole thing, but he also hadn't denied anything about the letter either. When talking about the witch's letter, Grandfather's name kept popping up. If Grandfather knew that someone was stealing his name, then considering his character, he'd probably be mad with rage.
units.note: MG still places Kinzo’s recurring name in talk about the letter. UP restores that his name appears several times in the letter itself.
units.japanese: 祖父さまは構ってくれなかったわけだが、手紙のことを否定することもしなかったらしい。魔女の手紙には、祖父さまの名が何度も出てくる。もし祖父さまが自分の名を騙られたと知ったなら、キャラクター的に考えて怒りくるうところだろう。

description: WH directly narrates that Kinzo knew the contents and ignored them, removing the report marker.
sourceReading: Battler reports that Kinzo apparently ignored the contents even after learning them: 無視していたという.

units.text: But even though Grandfather now knew the contents of that letter, he coldly ignored it. In this case, did that count as a silent yes? Eva oba-san and Dad were trying to interpret the letter in their favor, their greed clearly visible.
units.note: Both editions directly state that Kinzo knew the contents and ignored them, omitting the report qualification.
units.japanese: しかし祖父さまは、手紙の内容を知ってもなお、涼しげに無視していたという。

units.text: But even though Grandfather now knew the contents of that letter, he coldly ignored it. So, did that count as a silent yes? Aunt Eva and Dad were trying to interpret the letter in their favor, their greed clearly visible.
units.note: Both editions directly state that Kinzo knew the contents and ignored them, omitting the report qualification.
units.japanese: しかし祖父さまは、手紙の内容を知ってもなお、涼しげに無視していたという。となると、これはもはや無言のイエスも同然ということなのか。絵羽伯母さんとウチの親父は、この手紙を自分たちに有利に解釈しようと、欲の皮をギチギチに突っ張らせていた。

units.text: But even though Grandfather now knew the contents of that letter, he had coolly ignored it. In this case, did that count as a silent yes? Auntie Eva and Dad had been trying to interpret the letter in their favor, their greed clearly visible.
units.note: Both editions directly state that Kinzo knew the contents and ignored them, omitting the report qualification.
units.japanese: しかし祖父さまは、手紙の内容を知ってもなお、涼しげに無視していたという。となると、これはもはや無言のイエスも同然ということなのか。絵羽伯母さんとウチの親父は、この手紙を自分たちに有利に解釈しようと、欲の皮をギチギチに突っ張らせていた。

description: WH adds that she sobbed when released; the source only describes her exhausted condition then.
sourceReading: On release Maria was limp with exhaustion from crying.

units.text: Maria kept repeating that she had gotten it from Beatrice no matter how many times she was asked. It seemed that the adults felt that she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back and questioned her until she broke out in tears... When Maria was released, she sobbed, all worn out from crying.
units.note: MG says Maria was still sobbing when released. UP describes her as exhausted from crying without adding continued sobbing.
units.japanese: 真里亞は解放された時、泣き疲れてぐったりしていた。

units.text: Maria kept repeating that she'd gotten it from Beatrice no matter how many times she was asked. The adults seemed to think she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back and questioned her until she broke out in tears... When Maria was released, she sobbed, all worn out from crying.
units.note: MG says Maria was still sobbing when released. UP describes her as exhausted from crying without adding continued sobbing.
units.japanese: 真里亞は何度聞かれてもベアトリーチェにもらったと繰り返すだけ。それを大人たちは、誤魔化していると感じたらしく、彼女が泣き出すまで詰問を決して緩めようとはしなかった…。真里亞は解放された時、泣き疲れてぐったりしていた。

description: WH reads the idiom as overtly fighting over the money of the dead. This changes the accusation and introduces a dead owner where the preceding passage emphasizes Kinzo is still alive.
sourceReading: カネの亡者 means people consumed by greed for money; Battler deplores how overtly the adults have become such people.

units.text: George-aniki pleaded on behalf of our parents, saying that he wanted us to understand them. ...I understood his reasoning. No matter how filthy this talk of money was, it wouldn't go away if you just closed your eyes to it. But even so, how could they sink so low as to overtly fight over the money of the dead...
units.note: MG retains overt fighting over a dead person’s money. UP restores the idiom by calling the adults money-grubbing demons.
units.japanese: しかしそれでも、ああもあからさまにカネの亡者に成り下がれるものなのか…。

units.text: George-aniki pleaded on our parents' behalf, saying that he wanted us to understand them. ...I understood his reasoning. No matter how filthy this talk of money was, it wouldn't go away if you just closed your eyes to it. But even so, how could they sink so low as to overtly fight over the money of the dead...?
units.note: MG retains overt fighting over a dead person’s money. UP restores the idiom by calling the adults money-grubbing demons.
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴は、そんな親たちを理解してやってほしいと弁護する。…理屈ではわかる。金の話はどんなに汚くとも、目を閉じれば済む問題ではない。しかしそれでも、ああもあからさまにカネの亡者に成り下がれるものなのか…。

description: WH says Shannon or someone skillfully planned this ahead of time with Maria, losing the specific hypothesis that their accounts were made to agree.
sourceReading: Jessica hypothesizes that someone had Shannon or another person wear the portrait’s dress and coordinate the story with Maria: 口裏を合わせた.

units.text: "Probably..., Shannon or someone put on the dress from that portrait, and skillfully planned this ahead of time with Maria. ...Of course, as soon as Maria saw that dress, that might have been enough to convince her that it was Beatrice."
units.note: MG says someone got Maria to go along with their story, restoring coordinated testimony. UP retains generic advance planning with Maria.
units.japanese: 「恐らく…、あの肖像画のドレスを、紗音辺りにでも着てもらって、うまく真里亞と口裏を合わせたってことじゃねぇのかな。
candidates: skillfully planned this ahead of time with Maria

units.text: "Probably...Shannon or someone put on the dress from that portrait, and skillfully planned this ahead of time with Maria." "...Although of course, as soon as Maria saw that dress, that might have been enough on its own to convince her that it was Beatrice."
units.note: MG says someone got Maria to go along with their story, restoring coordinated testimony. UP retains generic advance planning with Maria.
units.japanese: 「恐らく…、あの肖像画のドレスを、紗音辺りにでも着てもらって、うまく真里亞と口裏を合わせたってことじゃねぇのかな」「…もっとも真里亞の場合、あのドレスを見たら、それだけでベアトリーチェだと信じちまいそうだけどな」
candidates: skillfully planned this ahead of time with Maria

description: WH says failing to consider how troubled Maria was would trouble her even more, changing a present condemnation into a hypothetical causal claim about further distress.
sourceReading: Battler calls the supposed prank utterly inconsiderate or troublesome because it disregards the burden on Maria.

units.text: It was probably true that our occult-loving Grandfather was playing around, since he had chosen that dramatic way of handing the letter over to Maria, who shared the same hobby as he did. ......Failing to consider how much Maria was troubled would trouble her even more, but...
units.note: Both editions condemn Kinzo’s failure to consider the trouble caused to Maria, rather than making it a hypothetical increase in distress.
units.japanese: ……真里亞の迷惑を顧みず、迷惑なことこの上ないが。

description: WH only says someone planning something related to the letter was on the island today. It omits continued current presence.
sourceReading: The deduction is that the person plotting around the letter is still on the island today: まだこの島にいる.

units.text: ...But they could say one thing for certain. Maria had, received this problematic letter, today, on this island. In other words, someone who was planning something related to that letter was on this island today.
units.note: Both editions say the planner was on the island today without preserving that the person is still on the island now.
units.japanese: つまり、あの手紙について策謀を巡らせた人間が、今日、まだこの島にいるということなのだ。

units.text: ...But they could say one thing for certain. Maria had received this problematic letter... received this problematic letter... today, on this island. In other words, someone planning something to do with that letter was on this island today.
units.note: Both editions say the planner was on the island today without preserving that the person is still on the island now.
units.japanese: …しかし、ひとつだけ言えることがある。真里亞が問題の手紙を、今日、この島で受け取ったということだ。つまり、あの手紙について策謀を巡らせた人間が、今日、まだこの島にいるということなのだ。

units.text: ...But they could say one thing for certain. Maria had received this problematic letter... today, on this island. In other words, someone who was planning something related to that letter was on this island today.
units.note: Both editions say the planner was on the island today without preserving that the person is still on the island now.
units.japanese: …しかし、ひとつだけ言えることがある。真里亞が問題の手紙を、今日、この島で受け取ったということだ。つまり、あの手紙について策謀を巡らせた人間が、今日、まだこの島にいるということなのだ。

description: WH says Eva left Krauss dumbfounded by ending the conversation, and Eva asks who is ending it. Inability to conduct a reasonable exchange becomes an act of termination.
sourceReading: Natsuhi says Krauss is merely utterly exasperated with Eva, with whom a conversation cannot be made to work. Eva then asks which of them is impossible to converse with.

units.text: "It is not certain that Father is the one who sent the letter.  You've done nothing but leave my husband dumbfounded by ending this conversation."
units.note: Both editions restore the accusation that the other side cannot conduct a conversation, rather than saying someone ended it.
units.japanese: 「手紙の差出人がお父様と確定したわけではありませんよ。会話の成り立たないあなたに主人が呆れ果てただけです。」

description: WH has everyone deliberately take a deep breath simultaneously to break the tension, adding unanimity, synchronization and purpose.
sourceReading: A sigh that seems to release tension escapes without a clear origin: 誰からともなく and ような.

units.text: After listening to the sound of Gohda's footsteps disappear off into the distance, everyone took a deep breath at the same time to break the tension.
units.note: Both editions make everyone deliberately take a synchronized deep breath to break the tension, replacing an unassigned sigh that escapes after Gohda leaves.
units.japanese: 郷田の足音が遠ざかっていくのを聞き届けると、誰からともなく、緊張を解くようなため息が漏れた。

units.text: After listening to the sound of Gohda's footsteps disappear off into the distance, everyone took a deep breath at the same time to break the tension.
units.note: Both editions make everyone deliberately take a synchronized deep breath to break the tension, replacing an unassigned sigh that escapes after Gohda leaves.
units.japanese: 郷田の足音が遠ざかっていくのを聞き届けると、誰からともなく、緊張を解くようなため息が漏れた。

description: WH substitutes nineteenth person, removing her explicit witch designation in this wry speculation.
sourceReading: Kyrie wonders whether the nineteenth witch is sheltering in the arbor.

units.text: "...It sure is raining hard.  I wonder if this 19th person is taking shelter in the arbor in the rose garden?"
units.note: MG calls Kyrie’s subject a nineteenth person. UP restores her wry phrase “our witch, this nineteenth person.”
units.japanese: 「…本当にすごい雨ね。１９人目の魔女は、今頃、薔薇庭園の東屋で雨宿りでもしているのかしら。」

units.text: "...It sure is raining hard. I wonder if this 19th person is taking shelter in the rose garden arbor about now."
units.note: MG calls Kyrie’s subject a nineteenth person. UP restores her wry phrase “our witch, this nineteenth person.”
units.japanese: 「…本当にすごい雨ね。１９人目の魔女は、今頃、薔薇庭園の東屋で雨宿りでもしているのかしら」

description: “No matter how we try to assign blame” loses the concession permitting trumped-up grounds for firing and replaces it with an effort to establish blame.
sourceReading: Natsuhi says they should have dismissed all One-winged Eagle servants even if they had to invent some unreasonable pretext.

units.text: "...I suspect Genji and the others.  Just as I thought, no matter how we try to assign blame, it would have been better if we had dismissed all of the servants of the One-winged Eagle."
units.note: MG refers to making whatever excuses were needed and UP to finding any excuse, both restoring Natsuhi’s willingness to invent a pretext for dismissal rather than assign blame.
units.japanese: やはり、どんな難癖を付けてでも片翼の鷲の使用人たちは全て解雇した方が良かったんです。」
candidates: matter how we try to assign blame

description: WH says she may really exist on the island, shifting the possibility from past existence to present presence.
sourceReading: Rudolf says the woman in the portrait may really have existed on the island: 存在したかもしれない.

units.text: "Hahahaha.  Of course, nobody believes in some witch riding a broom and flying in the sky.  ......But, the woman in that portrait, ...Beatrice, may really exist on this island."
units.note: Both editions restore the possibility that a woman named Beatrice existed on the island in the past rather than asserting present presence.
units.japanese: ……だが、あの肖像画の女。…ベアトリーチェは本当にこの島に存在したかもしれない。」

description: WH says the rumor was that Kinzo built the mansion because of the mistress, turning the date of the rumor’s circulation into a causal claim about construction.
sourceReading: Rumors of a mistress captivating Kinzo had circulated since the time he first established the mansion on the island.

units.text: It had been whispered from the beginning that Kinzo had built a mansion on this island because of the existence of an entrancing mistress......
units.note: MG says Kinzo built the mansion specifically because of the mistress. UP restores that rumors of the mistress dated from the time he built it.
units.japanese: 金蔵を夢中にさせる愛人の存在は、それこそこの島に屋敷を構えた当初から囁かれていたのだ……。

units.text: From the beginning, it had been whispered that Kinzo had built a mansion on this island specifically because of the existence of an entrancing mistress...
units.note: MG says Kinzo built the mansion specifically because of the mistress. UP restores that rumors of the mistress dated from the time he built it.
units.japanese: 金蔵を夢中にさせる愛人の存在は、それこそこの島に屋敷を構えた当初から囁かれていたのだ……。

description: WH says she scoured the mansion searching for Father when he could not be found. His absence becomes the object of the search rather than the opportunity for it.
sourceReading: Their mother took advantage of Kinzo’s absence to search the mansion thoroughly, suspecting a concealed mistress behind secret access.

units.text: "When Mother was alive, she would often scour the entire mansion searching for Father when he wasn't anywhere to be found.  ......Mother also suspected what Rudolf has just said.  She believed that there was a hidden door or stairway somewhere, and that his blonde-haired mistress was hidden behind it."
units.note: MG says Kinzo’s wife searched the mansion for him when he was missing. UP restores that she searched for the hidden place during Kinzo’s absence.
units.japanese: 「お母様は存命中、よくお父様の不在をついて屋敷内をしらみ潰しに探し回ってたわね。……留弗夫が言ったことを、お母様も疑ってたのよ。どこかに秘密の扉や階段があって、その中に金髪の愛人が隠れていると信じていたわ。」

units.text: "When Mother was alive, she would often scour the entire mansion searching for Father when he wasn't anywhere to be found. ...Mother also suspected what Rudolf just said. She believed there was a hidden door or stairway somewhere, and that his blonde-haired mistress was hidden behind it."
units.note: MG says Kinzo’s wife searched the mansion for him when he was missing. UP restores that she searched for the hidden place during Kinzo’s absence.
units.japanese: 「お母様は存命中、よくお父様の不在をついて屋敷内をしらみ潰しに探し回ってたわね。……留弗夫が言ったことを、お母様も疑ってたのよ。どこかに秘密の扉や階段があって、その中に金髪の愛人が隠れていると信じていたわ」

description: WH instead predicts that a few uncomfortable things might come up.
sourceReading: The possibility of hostile plotting naturally brings a degree of eeriness.

units.text: By preparing for the existence of a 19th person, they were accepting that some unknown person was hidden on this island. And since this person might have been planning something bad for them, it was only natural that a few uncomfortable things might come up...
units.note: MG still moves the unease into the conversation’s ominous direction. UP restores the inherent discomfort accompanying acceptance of a hidden unknown person.
units.japanese: そしてその人物が、何か良からぬことを企んでいるかもしれないともなれば、若干の不気味さを伴うのは当然のことだった…。

units.text: Preparing for the existence of a 19th person... would mean, in effect, acknowledging the presence of some unknown person hidden on this island. And since this person might be planning something shady, it was only natural that the conversation would turn in an ominous direction...
units.note: MG still moves the unease into the conversation’s ominous direction. UP restores the inherent discomfort accompanying acceptance of a hidden unknown person.
units.japanese: １９人目の存在に備えるということはつまり、今この島に、未知の人物が隠れ潜んでいることを認めること。そしてその人物が、何か良からぬことを企んでいるかもしれないともなれば、若干の不気味さを伴うのは当然のことだった…。

description: WH adds for certain, changing temporal permission or distance into epistemic confidence.
sourceReading: Eva says she can say this now, looking back on her mother as pitiable.

units.text: "......Yes, that did happen sometimes.  Mother was always doing things like that in her later years, and that frightening atmosphere still hasn't gone away.  ...I can say it for certain now.  She was a pitiful person."
units.note: Both editions retain “I can say it for certain now,” adding certainty where Eva says only that she can say this now.
units.japanese: …今だから言える。可哀想な人だったわ。」

units.text: "...Yes, that did happen sometimes. Mother was always doing things like that in her later years, and that frightening atmosphere still hasn't gone away. ...I can say it for certain now. She was a person to be pitied."
units.note: Both editions retain “I can say it for certain now,” adding certainty where Eva says only that she can say this now.
units.japanese: 「……あったわね。晩年のお母様はそんなことばかりだったから、未だにその怖い雰囲気が拭えないわ。…今だから言える。可哀想な人だったわ」

units.text: "......Yes, that did happen sometimes. Mother was always doing things like that in her later years, and that frightening atmosphere still hasn't gone away. ...I can say it for certain now. She was a person to be pitied."
units.note: Both editions retain “I can say it for certain now,” adding certainty where Eva says only that she can say this now.
units.japanese: 「……あったわね。晩年のお母様はそんなことばかりだったから、未だにその怖い雰囲気が拭えないわ。…今だから言える。可哀想な人だったわ」

description: WH says Father was not caught foolishly in a hidden room, losing both independent negative search results and treating 愚か as foolishly.
sourceReading: Not only was no hidden room found, Kinzo himself was never found even once.

units.text: "No.  Father wasn't caught foolishly in a hidden room even once.  Every time, after a lot of time had passed, he would suddenly show up somewhere.  Then he'd say that he'd taken a nap in some archive or that the wind had called him down for a walk on the beach.
units.note: MG retains the claim that Kinzo was not caught foolishly in a hidden room. UP restores the two failed search results: neither hidden rooms nor Kinzo were found.
units.japanese: 「いいえ。隠し部屋は愚か、一度たりともお父様が発見されたことはないわ。そしていつも、それからだいぶ時間が経ってからひょっこりと、何処からか姿を現すの。どこかの書庫で昼寝していたとか、風に誘われて浜辺を散歩していたとか何とか言ってね。
candidates: caught foolishly in a hidden room

units.text: "No. Father wasn't caught foolishly in a hidden room even once. Always, after a long time had passed, he would suddenly show up somewhere. Then he'd say that he'd taken a nap in some library room, or that the wind had summoned him to take a walk on the beach."
units.note: MG retains the claim that Kinzo was not caught foolishly in a hidden room. UP restores the two failed search results: neither hidden rooms nor Kinzo were found.
units.japanese: 「いいえ。隠し部屋はおろか、一度たりともお父様が発見されたことはないわ。そしていつも、それからだいぶ時間が経ってからひょっこりと、何処からか姿を現すの。どこかの書庫で昼寝していたとか、風に誘われて浜辺を散歩していたとか何とか言ってね」
candidates: caught foolishly in a hidden room

description: WH says the area outside the mansion is not large, contradicting the large forest and changing the geographical premise.
sourceReading: There are not many significant places outside the mansion to consider, leaving the vast forest as a candidate.

units.text: "Yeah.  Since we couldn't find him no matter how much we looked inside the mansion, we grew increasingly of the opinion that Father might have gone somewhere outside the mansion.  But the area outside the mansion isn't large at all.  ......Which leaves only the forest.
units.note: MG says the area outside the mansion is not large, conflicting with the expansive forest. UP restores that there are few plausible places outside before naming the forest.
units.japanese: 「あぁ。どんなに屋敷中を探しても見付からないんだから、親父は屋敷の外へ行っているのだろうという見解になった。だが、屋敷の外ったって、それほど大した場所はない。……となると残るのは、広大な森だ。

units.text: "Yeah. Since we couldn't find him no matter how much we looked inside the mansion, we got more and more sure that Dad might've been somewhere outside. But the area outside the mansion isn't large at all. ...Which leaves only the forest."
units.note: MG says the area outside the mansion is not large, conflicting with the expansive forest. UP restores that there are few plausible places outside before naming the forest.
units.japanese: 「あぁ。どんなに屋敷中を探しても見付からないんだから、親父は屋敷の外へ行っているのだろうという見解になった。だが、屋敷の外ったって、それほど大した場所はない。……となると残るのは、広大な森だ」

description: WH has Father give her advice after his success and the person then give him actual gold out of gratitude. This reverses the advice and erases the figurative explanation.
sourceReading: Natsuhi proposes that the benefactor gave Kinzo advice helping his business succeed; Kinzo’s gratitude led him to describe that person as giving him gold.

units.text: ".........Possibly, after achieving success in business, Father gave her some kind of valuable advice.  It's natural to think that, out of a sense of gratitude for that, this person gave Father the gold.  If you think about it that way, it's obvious that they would have a close relationship after that.  Rather than a festering relationship with a mistress, it was probably a relationship of gratitude to the person who saved the Ushiromiya family from crisis."
units.note: MG reverses the direction of Natsuhi’s advice and treats the gold literally. UP restores that the woman advised Kinzo and that he figuratively described the benefit as gold.
units.japanese: 「………恐らく、お父様が事業で成功する上で、何か貴重な助言をしてくれたのでしょう。それに恩を感じ、その人物が黄金を与えてくれたというような言い方をしたと考えるのが自然です。そうと考えれば、その後も親交があったのは当然でしょう。それは恐らく、愛人という爛れた関係ではなく、右代宮家の危機を救った恩人としてに違いありません。」

units.text: "......Perhaps Father gave her some kind of valuable advice for succeeding in business. It's natural to think that, out of a sense of gratitude for that, this person gave Father the gold.
units.note: MG reverses the direction of Natsuhi’s advice and treats the gold literally. UP restores that the woman advised Kinzo and that he figuratively described the benefit as gold.
units.japanese:
「………恐らく、お父様が事業で成功する上で、何か貴重な助言をしてくれたのでしょう。それに恩を感じ、その人物が黄金を与えてくれたというような言い方をしたと考えるのが自然です」
「そうと考えれば、その後も親交があったのは当然でしょう。それは恐らく、愛人という爛れた関係ではなく、右代宮家の危機を救った恩人としてに違いありません」

units.text: If you think about it that way, it's obvious that they would have a close relationship after that. Rather than a festering relationship with a mistress, it was probably a relationship of gratitude to the person who saved the Ushiromiya family from its crisis."
units.note: MG reverses the direction of Natsuhi’s advice and treats the gold literally. UP restores that the woman advised Kinzo and that he figuratively described the benefit as gold.
units.japanese:
「………恐らく、お父様が事業で成功する上で、何か貴重な助言をしてくれたのでしょう。それに恩を感じ、その人物が黄金を与えてくれたというような言い方をしたと考えるのが自然です」
「そうと考えれば、その後も親交があったのは当然でしょう。それは恐らく、愛人という爛れた関係ではなく、右代宮家の危機を救った恩人としてに違いありません」

description: WH asks whether Krauss already stumbled on it during that work, turning future speculation into retrospective suspicion.
sourceReading: Rudolf says the hidden mansion might turn up during Krauss’s planned resort development, perhaps with gold there too.

units.text: ...Aniki was planning on expanding this island into a resort, right?  As you were doing that, you didn't manage to stumble on it by chance, did you?  Or maybe unexpectedly find some gold there, too?"
units.note: MG retains a question about whether Krauss already found the mansion and gold. UP restores Rudolf’s speculation that the future resort work might find them.
units.japanese: …兄貴はこの島をリゾート開発する気なんだろ？　その際にひょっこり見付かるかもしれねぇぜ？　案外、そこに黄金もあったりするかもな。」

units.text: ...Aniki, you were planning on expanding this island into a resort, right? As you were doing that, you didn't manage to stumble on it by chance, did you? Maybe you even bumped into some gold there, too."
units.note: MG retains a question about whether Krauss already found the mansion and gold. UP restores Rudolf’s speculation that the future resort work might find them.
units.japanese: 「…兄貴はこの島をリゾート開発する気なんだろ？　その際にひょっこり見付かるかもしれねぇぜ？　案外、そこに黄金もあったりするかもな」

description: WH describes a witch quietly waiting instead.
sourceReading: The mansion stands quietly in the forest.

units.text: "When the mansion was built on this island, Father was at the height of his prosperity.  With his money, he could probably obtain anything, make any of his delusions real.  ...A mansion in the forest where a witch quietly waits... ......It sounds like the kind of situation Father would like."
units.note: Neither edition makes the witch wait quietly. MG instead transfers the mansion’s stillness to its construction and adds that it was built to house the witch; that separate change is recorded under a paired ID. UP restores a quietly standing mansion in which the witch lives.
units.japanese: 「この島に屋敷を建てた頃は、親父殿の特に全盛期だ。カネに物を言わせて、どんな妄想も実現しただろう。…森の中にひっそりたたずむ魔女の屋敷。

description: WH says it was hastily thrown together.
sourceReading: The story is difficult to believe immediately.

units.text: On this island, which the Ushiromiya family had lived on for 30 years now, a hidden mansion that no one knew about had been quietly built, with a witch, who was unknown except for a portrait, living in it... Even this hastily thrown together story, ...might not be completely delusional considering all of Kinzo's strange habits and his vast wealth...
units.note: MG retains “hastily thrown together theory” for a story that is hard to believe. UP restores the difficulty of belief.
units.japanese: にわかには信じられないこの話も、…全て金蔵の奇癖と莫大な財産があれば、決して妄想ではないのかもしれない…。

units.text: On this island, on which the Ushiromiya family had lived for 30 years now, a hidden mansion that no one knew about had been quietly built to house a witch, about whom nothing was known except what could be guessed from a portrait... Even this hastily thrown together theory... might not be completely delusional, considering all of Kinzo's strange habits and his vast wealth...
units.note: MG retains “hastily thrown together theory” for a story that is hard to believe. UP restores the difficulty of belief.
units.japanese: 右代宮家が３０年にもわたって住まってきたこの島に、誰も知らない隠し屋敷がひっそりと建っていて、肖像画でしか知らない魔女が住んでいる…。にわかには信じられないこの話も、…全て金蔵の奇癖と莫大な財産があれば、決して妄想ではないのかもしれない…。

description: WH says an old bag like us, dropping タフな食えない.
sourceReading: Eva imagines a tough, shrewd woman on their level, inferred from the letter.

units.text: ......She might have been a charming young woman at the time, but it is probably appropriate to think that she's now an old bag like us.  I can easily imagine that, given the contents of that letter."
units.note: Both editions retain “old bag like us,” losing Eva’s description of a tough, formidable, or shrewd woman who is hard to deal with.
units.japanese: ……当時は魅惑的な若い女性だったかもしれないけど、今は私たちと同格の、タフな食えない女と考えるのが妥当でしょうね。手紙の内容からもそれは容易に想像できるわ。」

units.text: ...She might've been a charming young woman at the time, but it probably makes sense to assume she's an old bag like us now. I can easily imagine that, given the contents of that letter."
units.note: Both editions retain “old bag like us,” losing Eva’s description of a tough, formidable, or shrewd woman who is hard to deal with.
units.japanese: 「……当時は魅惑的な若い女性だったかもしれないけど、今は私たちと同格の、タフな食えない女と考えるのが妥当でしょうね。手紙の内容からもそれは容易に想像できるわ」

units.text: "......She might have been a charming young woman at the time, but it is probably appropriate to think that she's now an old bag like us. I can easily imagine that, given the contents of that letter."
units.note: Both editions retain “old bag like us,” losing Eva’s description of a tough, formidable, or shrewd woman who is hard to deal with.
units.japanese: 「……当時は魅惑的な若い女性だったかもしれないけど、今は私たちと同格の、タフな食えない女と考えるのが妥当でしょうね。手紙の内容からもそれは容易に想像できるわ」

description: WH describes Krauss as blind to his own shortcomings.
sourceReading: His laugh seems to tell Eva she is ignoring her own shortcomings.

units.text: Krauss laughed, as though blind to his own shortcomings. Of course, Eva was offended, but she didn't strike back.
units.note: MG says Krauss laughs as though the description does not apply to him; UP says he is blind to his own shortcomings. Both make the hypocrisy Krauss’s rather than presenting his laugh as accusing Eva of hypocrisy.
units.japanese: 自分のことを棚に上げて、とでも言うように蔵臼が笑う。

units.text: Krauss laughed as if none of this applied to him. Of course, Eva was offended, but she didn't strike back.
units.note: MG says Krauss laughs as though the description does not apply to him; UP says he is blind to his own shortcomings. Both make the hypocrisy Krauss’s rather than presenting his laugh as accusing Eva of hypocrisy.
units.japanese: 自分のことを棚に上げて、とでも言うように蔵臼が笑う。絵羽はもちろんカチンと来たようだが、買い言葉は返さなかった。

description: WH gives awareness and pride to Father, who regards her as his real wife.
sourceReading: The woman may know she is a mistress while feeling the pride of a legitimate wife.

units.text: Anyway, ...there's a good chance that this love was mutual, unlike with Mother.  Father himself might have been aware that she was his mistress, and yet at the same time, he might have been proud of her as though she were his real wife."
units.note: Both editions correctly give the mistress awareness of being a lover and possible pride as Kinzo’s true wife, rather than assigning that awareness and pride to Kinzo.
units.japanese: 何しろ、…お袋と違い、相思相愛だった可能性が高いからな。本人には、愛人の自覚と同時に、正妻としての誇りもあるかもしれない。」

description: WH says distant days and embellished, losing the gray/color contrast linking oppressive life to the meeting.
sourceReading: Kinzo’s gray days are suddenly colored by meeting the Golden Witch.

units.text: ......Since the time he met that Golden Witch Beatrice in those distant days, Kinzo's Legend of the Gold was quickly embellished into something dramatic. In other words, ...it could mean, that Kinzo really did meet with a woman he loved.
units.note: MG retains “distant days,” losing the gray or unhappy quality that supports the color contrast. UP restores “unhappy days.”
units.japanese: ……金蔵の黄金伝説は、そんな灰色の日々に、黄金の魔女ベアトリーチェに出会うことにより、急にドラマチックなものに彩られていく。

units.text: ...Ever since he met that Golden Witch Beatrice in those distant days, Kinzo's Legend of the Gold was quickly embellished into something dramatic. In other words, ...it could mean... that Kinzo really did find a woman he loved.
units.note: MG retains “distant days,” losing the gray or unhappy quality that supports the color contrast. UP restores “unhappy days.”
units.japanese: ……金蔵の黄金伝説は、そんな灰色の日々に、黄金の魔女ベアトリーチェに出会うことにより、急にドラマチックなものに彩られていく。それはつまり、…金蔵が本当に愛する女性に出会った、ということなのかもしれない。

description: WH says she has nothing to do with this, replacing lack of succession prospects with lack of involvement.
sourceReading: The epitaph condition particularly favors Beatrice, who otherwise has no chance of succeeding.

units.text: "Is that so?  ...If someone can solve the witch's riddle, they will receive the inheritance regardless of rank.  In other words, it is the most advantageous condition that Beatrice could get, since she has nothing to do with this."
units.note: Both editions restore that Beatrice has no chance of succession otherwise, rather than saying she has nothing to do with the matter.
units.japanese: 「そういうことか。…魔女の碑文を解けば、序列に関係なく家督が継げる。つまり、まったく可能性のないベアトリーチェにとってもっとも有利な条件ってわけだ。」

description: WH opens with Don’t say something so shameless, directing the rebuke at what those present say.
sourceReading: Natsuhi exclaims that such shamelessness has limits, condemning the hypothetical mistress’s ambition.

units.text: "D, don't say something so shameless...!  Even if a mistress actually existed, joining in on the battle for the rights to the head's inheritance would be a reckless action far above her place!  What disregard for her own place...!"
units.note: Both editions direct Natsuhi’s condemnation at the hypothetical mistress’s conduct rather than instructing the speakers not to say something shameless.
units.japanese: 「ず、図々しいにもほどがあります…！　仮に愛人が実在したとしても、当主継承権を争おうなど、身の程を弁えぬ暴挙です！　何という身の程知らず…！」

description: WH specifies snatching it before they solve it, adding an unsupported temporal condition that weakens the proposed use of their solving effort.
sourceReading: They consider whether she is urging the siblings to solve the epitaph so she can snatch the gold from the sidelines.

units.text: Could it be that this person was trying to stir the siblings up so that they tried to solve the epitaph, and would then snatch it up before they did solve it...?  That was a very reasonable guess.
units.note: MG adds that the snatching would occur at the last second; UP adds that it would occur before the siblings solve the epitaph. Neither temporal condition appears in Japanese.
units.japanese: ひょっとして、碑文を解くように焚き付けて、脇から掻っ攫おうと考えているのでは…。それは極めて妥当な想像だった。

units.text: Could it be that this person was trying to stir the siblings up so they'd solve the epitaph, and then planned to steal it away at the last second...? It was an extremely logical possibility.
units.note: MG adds that the snatching would occur at the last second; UP adds that it would occur before the siblings solve the epitaph. Neither temporal condition appears in Japanese.
units.japanese: ひょっとして、碑文を解くように焚き付けて、脇から掻っ攫おうと考えているのでは…。それは極めて妥当な想像だった。

units.text: Could it be that this person was trying to stir the siblings up so that they tried to solve the epitaph, and would then snatch it up before they did solve it...? That was a very reasonable guess.
units.note: MG adds that the snatching would occur at the last second; UP adds that it would occur before the siblings solve the epitaph. Neither temporal condition appears in Japanese.
units.japanese: ひょっとして、碑文を解くように焚き付けて、脇から掻っ攫おうと考えているのでは…。それは極めて妥当な想像だった。

description: WH separates the game not being on even footing from some compelling force, obscuring what that force must compel.
sourceReading: The game cannot function without leverage obliging the family to participate on equal terms, including accepting defeat.

units.text: "That's it exactly.  No matter how one-sided a game Beatrice proposes, even if she splendidly shows us the answer, there's no way that we'll obediently hand over the inheritance.  ......So as long as this game isn't on an even footing, unless they have some kind of compelling force, the game won't succeed."
units.note: MG still misconstrues the compelling force as taking the form of a game with equal conditions. UP restores a force that compels the siblings to play under fair conditions.
units.japanese: 「そういうことよ。いくらベアトリーチェが一方的にこんなゲームを提案しても、そして見事その答えを示して見せたとしても。私たちは家督を素直に譲るわけもない。……つまり、私たちがこのゲームに対等な条件で挑まなくてはならないという、強制力がない限り、このゲームは成立しないのよ。」

units.text: "That's it exactly. No matter how Beatrice might one-sidedly propose a game like this, even if she were to spectacularly show us the answer, there's no way we'd obediently hand over the Headship.
units.note: MG still misconstrues the compelling force as taking the form of a game with equal conditions. UP restores a force that compels the siblings to play under fair conditions.
units.japanese:
「そういうことよ。いくらベアトリーチェが一方的にこんなゲームを提案しても、そして見事その答えを示して見せたとしても。私たちは家督を素直に譲るわけもない」
「……つまり、私たちがこのゲームに対等な条件で挑まなくてはならないという、強制力がない限り、このゲームは成立しないのよ」

units.text: ...In other words, unless she has a compelling force in the form of challenging us to a game with equal conditions for us all, this won't truly count as a game."
units.note: MG still misconstrues the compelling force as taking the form of a game with equal conditions. UP restores a force that compels the siblings to play under fair conditions.
units.japanese:
「そういうことよ。いくらベアトリーチェが一方的にこんなゲームを提案しても、そして見事その答えを示して見せたとしても。私たちは家督を素直に譲るわけもない」
「……つまり、私たちがこのゲームに対等な条件で挑まなくてはならないという、強制力がない限り、このゲームは成立しないのよ」

description: WH says it would sound worse, losing the specific ironic implication that her protests suggest financial distress.
sourceReading: The more Natsuhi emotionally denies the relevance of their finances, the more her words sound like the opposite.

units.text: Krauss interrupted Natsuhi as she started to go on and on emotionally. In this situation, the more she went on and on emotionally, the worse it would actually sound.
units.note: Both editions say Natsuhi’s protests sound worse rather than specifying that they produce the opposite impression and make the family sound financially distressed.
units.japanese: 今の状況では、彼女が感情的にまくし立てればまくし立てるほど、それは逆に聞こえた。

units.text: Krauss interrupted Natsuhi as she started to go on and on emotionally. In this situation, the more she went on like that, the worse it would actually sound.
units.note: Both editions say Natsuhi’s protests sound worse rather than specifying that they produce the opposite impression and make the family sound financially distressed.
units.japanese: 感情的にまくし立てる夏妃を、蔵臼が制する。今の状況では、彼女が感情的にまくし立てればまくし立てるほど、それは逆に聞こえた。

units.text: Krauss interrupted Natsuhi as she started to go on emotionally. In this situation, the more she went on and on emotionally, the worse it would actually sound for them.
units.note: Both editions say Natsuhi’s protests sound worse rather than specifying that they produce the opposite impression and make the family sound financially distressed.
units.japanese: 感情的にまくし立てる夏妃を、蔵臼が制する。今の状況では、彼女が感情的にまくし立てればまくし立てるほど、それは逆に聞こえた。

description: WH says they have been collecting evidence and his position is not one to be proud of, losing completed corroboration and the demand to stop posturing.
sourceReading: Rudolf says they have corroborated the facts and this is no time for Krauss to put on appearances.

units.text: "Aniki, we've been collecting evidence.  Your position right now is not one to be proud of.
units.note: Both editions retain “collecting evidence” for already corroborated information. UP restores that this is not the time to put up a front, while MG changes it to a position not worth pride.
units.japanese: 「兄貴。裏は取れてんだぜ。今は見栄を張ってる場合じゃない。

units.text: "Aniki, we've been collecting evidence. Your position right now isn't one to be proud of.
units.note: Both editions retain “collecting evidence” for already corroborated information. UP restores that this is not the time to put up a front, while MG changes it to a position not worth pride.
units.japanese: 「兄貴。裏は取れてんだぜ。今は見栄を張ってる場合じゃない」

units.text: "Aniki, we've been collecting evidence. Now is not the time to be putting up a front."
units.note: Both editions retain “collecting evidence” for already corroborated information. UP restores that this is not the time to put up a front, while MG changes it to a position not worth pride.
units.japanese: 「兄貴。裏は取れてんだぜ。今は見栄を張ってる場合じゃない」

description: WH says because they had a little money stored up, replacing payment offered with wealth possessed.
sourceReading: Eva resists giving up headship merely because someone piles money before them as an offer.

units.text: "............Th, ...this isn't funny.  ...The thought that we'd give up the inheritance to some woman of doubtful origin..., ......just because they had a little money stored up......"
units.note: MG retains money merely stored up by the outsider. UP restores money being tossed or offered to Eva as the condition that tempts her.
units.japanese: 「…………じょ、…冗談じゃないわよ。…多少お金を積まれたくらいで…、……どこの馬の骨とも知れない女に家督を譲るなんて……。」
candidates: because they had a little money stored

units.text: "......Th-This isn't funny. ...To think we'd give up the Headship to some woman of doubtful origin... ...just because she had a little money stored up..."
units.note: MG retains money merely stored up by the outsider. UP restores money being tossed or offered to Eva as the condition that tempts her.
units.japanese: 「…………じょ、…冗談じゃないわよ。…多少お金を積まれたくらいで…、……どこの馬の骨とも知れない女に家督を譲るなんて……」

description: WH has That would means rather than would mean.
sourceReading: That would mean receiving ten times their original estimate.

units.text: "...Yeah.  That would means she's treating us with ten times our original goal.  That alone would be more than enough for us.  ......It's not like I have any attachment to the Ushiromiya name.  I'd be happy to sell it off..."
units.note: Both editions use the grammatical “would mean,” correcting original WH’s “would means.”
units.japanese: 「…あぁ。俺たちは当初の見積もりの１０倍も弾まれちまうことになる。そんだけあれば俺たちは充分だぜ。……どうせ、右代宮なんて名前に未練はねぇんだ。喜んで売っ払ってやらぁ…。」

description: WH says a moat has been dug around Krauss, reversing the removal of defensive barriers into their construction.
sourceReading: All defensive moats except Krauss’s central stronghold are filled in: the other siblings are bought off, leaving him alone to negotiate.

units.text: A moat had been dug all around Krauss. In that case, the negotiations would be one-on-one between her and Krauss.
units.note: MG says a moat was dug around Krauss, reversing the Japanese siege metaphor. UP restores that all outer obstacles or defenses around the central stronghold Krauss would be removed.
units.japanese: 本丸の蔵臼以外の堀は全て埋まるわけだ。

units.text: A moat had been dug all around Krauss. In that case, the negotiations would be one-on-one between her and Krauss.
units.note: MG says a moat was dug around Krauss, reversing the Japanese siege metaphor. UP restores that all outer obstacles or defenses around the central stronghold Krauss would be removed.
units.japanese: 本丸の蔵臼以外の堀は全て埋まるわけだ。そうなれば、交渉は彼女と蔵臼の一対一になる。

description: WH adds political weakness and states his private willingness as fact rather than retaining だろう.
sourceReading: Krauss’s finances are bad; despite bluffing, he probably thinks he could negotiate depending on the amount.

units.text: He tried to look strong, but Krauss's financial and political situation was extremely weak. ...He did bluff in front of his siblings, but on the inside, he was thinking that it might be alright to enter negotiations depending on the sum of money involved.
units.note: Both editions add political weakness to Krauss’s financial distress. MG also states his private willingness as fact; UP restores the narrator’s probabilistic judgment with “probably.”
units.japanese:
強気を装ってはいるが、蔵臼の財政状況も非常に悪い。
…兄弟たちの前では、虚勢を張っているが、内心は、金額次第では交渉に応じても良いと思っているだろう。

units.text: He tried to look strong, but Krauss's financial and political situation was extremely weak. ...He might bluff in front of his siblings, but on the inside, he was considering entering negotiations, depending on the sum of money involved.

description: WH says the questioner called the four relatives together, introducing an organizer’s action absent from 揃い.
sourceReading: Four blood relatives of the question-setter are gathered; if they pool their wits they might solve it by chance.

units.text: After all, we have here four of Father's children by blood, right?  The questioner called together four blood relatives who, if they tried frantically to work together and avoid having those assets stolen from them, might come across the answer of the riddle by chance."
units.note: MG says the questioner called the four blood relatives together, inventing an organizing action. UP restores four relatives being assembled or present together.
units.japanese: 何しろ、ここにはお父さんの血を引く子どもが４人もいるのよ？　出題者の血縁者が４人も揃い、財産を奪われまいと死に物狂いで知恵を出し合ったなら、偶然にも謎が解けてしまうこともあるかもしれない。」

units.text: "After all, we have here four of Father's children by blood, right? The questioner called together four blood relatives who, if they tried frantically to work together and avoid having those assets stolen from them, might come across the answer of the riddle by chance."
units.note: MG says the questioner called the four blood relatives together, inventing an organizing action. UP restores four relatives being assembled or present together.

description: WH says it might have had that effect, downgrading the conceded result to a possibility.
sourceReading: Kyrie acknowledges that the letter did have the effect of dividing the sibling alliance.

units.text: ......Of course, it might have had the effect of splitting apart the siblings' alliance, but if that was her only goal, why would she take this risk, however slight it might be......?  I think that's reckless.
units.note: Both editions say the letter might have split the siblings, downgrading Kyrie’s concession that it did have that effect.
units.japanese: ……確かに、兄弟の連帯を分断するという効果はあったけれど、それを狙うためだけに、わずかとは言えこのようなリスクを……？　私は無用心だと思う。

units.text: ...Of course, it might have had the effect of splitting apart the siblings' alliance, but if that was her only goal, why would she take this risk, however slight it might be...? That seems reckless to me."

description: WH makes a plate on the tray filled with both tea and cookies.
sourceReading: The silver tray carries steaming tea and a plate of cookies.

units.text: Beato's butler, who called himself Ronove, appeared out of nowhere. A plate set on a silver tray that he held was filled with delicious-looking, steaming black tea and cookies.
units.note: Both editions place a plate filled with steaming tea and cookies on the tray, physically putting the tea inside the cookie plate rather than placing a cup and a cookie plate on the tray.
units.japanese: 手に持つ銀のトレーには、美味しそうに湯気を立てる紅茶とクッキーを盛り付けた皿が置かれていた。

units.text: Beato's butler, who called himself Ronove, appeared out of nowhere in particular. Placed upon the silver tray that he held was a plate filled with delicious‐looking, steaming black tea and cookies.
units.note: Both editions place a plate filled with steaming tea and cookies on the tray, physically putting the tea inside the cookie plate rather than placing a cup and a cookie plate on the tray.

description: WH says when I feel like it, assuming eventual willingness.
sourceReading: Battler says he will eat if he feels like it, leaving acceptance conditional.

units.text: "I'll eat some when I feel like it.  Set it down over there and get out of here."
units.note: Both editions say Battler will eat the cookies when he feels like it, presupposing eventual willingness instead of leaving it conditional.

sourceReading: Even after Battler recognizes his weakness, it remains; the eighteen-person attack can still target it.

units.text: ......Battler-sama, you may already understand, but there are still plenty of weak points.  Maybe the '18 people attack' will be an effective move.  As an attempt to judge how strong your defense is, it may be interesting to challenge that point again."

units.text: ...As long as I understand my weak points, and as long as she wants to attack those weak points, ......it's as if I've induced her to attack there...

description: WH says That isn’t a move appropriate for you to use, reversing the assertion and redirecting the move to his opponents.
sourceReading: Battler says there is no move more appropriate for witches and demons than Devil’s Proof.

units.text: "Witches and demons and the like...  That isn't a move appropriate for you to use.  ......It's one of those

units.japanese: 「魔女だの悪魔だの。お前らにこれほど相応しい一手はないぜ。……それがこいつっ、

description: WH says Because it is impossible to prove, changing the conclusion about needing evidence into an impossibility claim.
sourceReading: Battler concludes that proof is unnecessary for his proposed move.

units.text: And some moves exist which can only be used in a game against a witch.  There are cheap moves! And that's what this 'Devil's Proof' is. Because it's impossible to prove!
units.note: MG says proof is impossible where Battler concludes evidence is unnecessary. UP restores the conclusion that evidence is unnecessary.
units.japanese: ゆえに、証拠は不要！

units.text: And some moves exist that can only be used in a game against a witch. There are cheap moves! And that's what this "Devil's Proof" is. Because it's impossible to prove!

だから、魔女とのゲームでしか使えない手がある。
卑劣な一手がある！それがこの“悪魔の証明”。
ゆえに、証拠は不要！

description: WH says he has become quite devious, adding an emphasis on cunning or deceit.
sourceReading: Ronove says three games naturally teach Battler how to handle things more effectively: 要領がよくなる.

units.text: "......I see.  You have learned from your defeat last time.  That is good.  It is no surprise that by the third game you have become quite devious.
units.note: Both editions say Battler has become devious after three games, replacing Ronove’s observation that he has become more efficient or has learned the ropes.
units.japanese: 「……なるほど。前回の失敗を学ばれているのですね。良いことですよ。さすがに三度もゲームを重ねると要領がよくなるものです。

description: WH says it will not be enough, turning acceptance of adequate opposition into a claim that the opposition is insufficient.
sourceReading: Battler accepts the challenge: witch or demon, either is a worthy opponent, 相手に不足はない.

units.text: "......Come on.  I don't care if you're a witch or a demon, it won't be enough!"
units.note: MG says Battler has no shortage of opponents, still failing to say that a witch or demon is a worthy or sufficient opponent. UP restores that he will take either one on.
units.japanese: 「……来いよ。魔女だろうと悪魔だろうと、相手に不足はねぇ！」

units.text: "...Let's have it. I've got no shortage of opponents, be they witches or demons!"
units.note: MG says Battler has no shortage of opponents, still failing to say that a witch or demon is a worthy or sufficient opponent. UP restores that he will take either one on.
units.japanese: 「……来いよ。魔女だろうと悪魔だろうと、相手に不足はねぇ！」

description: WH has The room was filled dazzling golden butterflies, omitting with.
sourceReading: The room is filled with dazzling golden butterflies.

units.text: Just then, ...aah, that enraging laugh I'd heard so many times started echoing. The room was filled dazzling golden butterflies, and in the center of that whirlwind, the Golden Witch appeared.
units.note: Both editions restore “filled with dazzling golden butterflies,” supplying the missing preposition.
units.japanese: 部屋が眩い黄金の蝶たちで満たされ、その金色の旋風の中に、あの黄金の魔女が姿を現す。
candidates: room was filled dazzling golden butterflies

description: WH says she was certain the day would come, replacing surprise with confident prior expectation.
sourceReading: Beatrice marvels that the day should come when she would show this move to Battler: よもや...来ようとは.

units.text: ......'Hempel's Raven', was it?  That move is so familiar I could almost laugh.  I was certain the day would come when it would be introduced to Battler.  It's a classic move to use against the 'Devil's Proof'.
units.note: MG says the day has come when Beatrice gets to show Hempel’s Raven to Battler, losing her surprise. UP restores “to think the day would come.”
units.japanese: ……“ヘンペルのカラス”か。何とも笑える懐かしい一手よ。よもや戦人に披露する日が来ようとはな。それは“悪魔の証明”に並ぶ古典的一手だ。

units.text: ..."Hempel's Raven", was it? Such a familiar old move I could almost laugh. To think the day has come when I get to show it off to Battler. It's a classic move to use against a "Devil's Proof"."

sourceReading: Hempel’s Raven is a classic move alongside, or on a par with, Devil’s Proof.

description: WH says he speaks most respectably of her from his heart, shifting the claim from inward respect to how he speaks.
sourceReading: Ronove claims to respect Milady sincerely from his heart.

units.text: "Nonsense.  Why would I speak such gossip about Milady, of whom I speak most respectably from my heart?"
units.note: MG restores Ronove’s sincere inward respect. UP retains a claim about having only words of heartfelt respect, shifting respect toward speech.
units.japanese: 「滅相もない。心より尊敬申し上げているお嬢様に、この私めがどうしてそのような陰口を申せましょうか。」

units.text: "By no means. I have only words of the highest heartfelt respect for Milady; why would I speak such gossip?"
units.note: MG restores Ronove’s sincere inward respect. UP retains a claim about having only words of heartfelt respect, shifting respect toward speech.
units.japanese: 「滅相もない。心より尊敬申し上げているお嬢様に、この私めがどうしてそのような陰口を申せましょうか」

description: WH jumps directly from no cookie in this box to the other box being the winner, erasing the staged intermediate proposition.
sourceReading: The explicit intermediate step is this box has no cookie, therefore this box is not the winner. The following sentence uses the two-box premise to infer the other box wins.

units.text: However, if the box that you open is empty, then the reverse, Hempel's raven, is satisfied.  It means that 'this box does not have a cookie in it, therefore, the other box is the winner'.
units.note: Both editions preserve the staged inference: the opened box is shown not to be the winner, then the fixed two-box premise establishes that the other box wins.
units.japanese: しかし、開けた箱が空っぽだったなら、この時は逆に“ヘンペルのカラス”を満たす。“この箱にクッキーが入っていない＝この箱はアタリではない”となるのだから。

description: WH says Let’s try and keep things simple, replacing a jab at Battler’s comprehension with an inclusive proposal.
sourceReading: Beatrice says it should not be such a difficult matter to understand.

units.text: "Only that I've countered your move.  Let's try and keep things simple.  Ronove, explain.  It seems you've made things easy enough for Battler to understand with your cookie in a box analogy."
units.note: MG proposes keeping things simple, replacing Beatrice’s taunt that the point should not be difficult. UP restores the taunt.
units.japanese: 「そなたの指し手を逆手に取っただけだがな。そう難しい話ではあるまいに。

description: WH says he took a risk that he might be forced to accept one of the eighteen, omitting when the move is refuted and weakening the necessary consequence under that condition.
sourceReading: Battler’s nineteenth-person strategy entails that when it is refuted he must admit an explanation using only the eighteen.

units.text: "That's right.  As soon as you played that move to explain everything with a 19th person, you had already taken on a risk that you might be forced to accept that the culprit was one of the 18."
units.note: MG omits the condition that the nineteenth-person move must first be thwarted before Battler is forced back onto the eighteen. UP restores the condition.
units.japanese: 「その通りよ。そなたの１９人目で全てを説明する一手は、それが破られた時、１８人でしか説明できないことを認めざるを得ないリスクを背負っている。」

units.text: "That's right. As soon as you played that move and attempted to explain everything with a 19th person, you'd already taken on a risk that you might be forced to accept that the culprit was one of the 18."
units.note: MG omits the condition that the nineteenth-person move must first be thwarted before Battler is forced back onto the eighteen. UP restores the condition.

description: WH says the police would not come, weakening explicit inability into predicted nonarrival.
sourceReading: The typhoon prevents the police from coming to the island.

units.text: However, in reality, that was infinitely impossible. The police wouldn't come here in this typhoon. We couldn't have a scientific investigation, we didn't have any experts on this sort of thing, and we couldn't do anything. In short, we couldn't show anything decisively! It was impossible for me to find any proof other than simply gulping down whatever alibis each of the 18 gave.
units.note: Both editions say the police would not come, weakening the explicit inability to reach the island during the typhoon.
units.japanese: ここには台風で警察が来られない。

units.text: However, in reality, that'll be almost absolutely impossible. The police wouldn't come here in this typhoon. We don't have access to scientific investigations or experts or anything. In short, we can't prove anything decisively! It'll be impossible for me to find any proof other than simply gulping down whatever alibis each of the 18 give.
units.note: Both editions say the police would not come, weakening the explicit inability to reach the island during the typhoon.
units.japanese:
しかし、それは現実には限りなく不可能なのだ。ここには台風で警察が来られない。
科学捜査も鑑識も何もない。
つまり、何も確定的に示せない！俺には１８人が口々に主張するアリバイを鵜呑みにする以上の検証が不可能なのだ。

units.text:
However, in reality, that's as close as you can get to impossible. The police wouldn't come here in this typhoon.
There would be no scientific investigations, no autopsies, no nothing.
In short, I can't show anything decisively! It's impossible for me to find any proof other than simply gulping down whatever alibis each of the 18 give.
units.note: Both editions say the police would not come, weakening the explicit inability to reach the island during the typhoon.
units.japanese:
しかし、それは現実には限りなく不可能なのだ。ここには台風で警察が来られない。
科学捜査も鑑識も何もない。
つまり、何も確定的に示せない！俺には１８人が口々に主張するアリバイを鵜呑みにする以上の検証が不可能なのだ。

description: WH says they can be proven true or false, adding falsification to the claimed use.
sourceReading: Ronove says various reckless arguments can be substantiated.

units.text: "By using 'Hempel's Raven', various reckless arguments become possible to prove true or false.
units.note: MG says reckless arguments can be proven true or false, adding disproof. UP restores only that they can be proven.
units.japanese: 「“ヘンペルのカラス”を使えば、様々な暴論が実証可能なのです。

units.text: "By using "Hempel's Raven", various reckless arguments become possible to prove true or false.
units.note: MG says reckless arguments can be proven true or false, adding disproof. UP restores only that they can be proven.
units.japanese: 「“ヘンペルのカラス”を使えば、様々な暴論が実証可能なのです」

description: WH already says bring ill fortune down upon them in the premise, collapsing the distinction between the purported demonstration and its abusive execution.
sourceReading: The explanatory premise says demonstrate that people without the protection are unhappy; the next sentence then describes causing their misfortune to demonstrate it.

units.text: "So in order to prove that servants of gods are blessed with divine protection, they only have to bring ill fortune down upon those people who don't receive that divine protection.
units.note: MG turns proving others’ misfortune into actively bringing misfortune upon them one sentence early. UP preserves the distinction until the following execution step.
units.japanese: 「つまり、神の僕がその加護によって幸福であることを実証する為には、その加護を受けぬ人々が不幸であることを実証すればいいわけです。

units.text: "So in order to prove that servants of gods are blessed with divine protection, they only have to bring ill fortune down upon those people who don't receive such protection."
units.note: MG turns proving others’ misfortune into actively bringing misfortune upon them one sentence early. UP preserves the distinction until the following execution step.
units.japanese: 「つまり、神の僕がその加護によって幸福であることを実証する為には、その加護を受けぬ人々が不幸であることを実証すればいいわけです」

description: WH says people who do not believe in them, dropping the stated object their god and leaving the referent ambiguous.
sourceReading: Those people do not believe in the actors’ own god: 自らの神を信じない.

units.text: .........So by bringing misfortune down upon those people who don't believe in them, they prove their blessedness."
units.note: MG says people who do not believe in “them,” leaving the referent ambiguous. UP restores people who do not believe in their god.
units.japanese: ………そして彼らは、自らの神を信じない人々を不幸に突き落とすことで、自らの幸福を実証する。」

units.text: "......So, by bringing misfortune down upon those who don't believe in them, they prove their blessedness."
units.note: MG says people who do not believe in “them,” leaving the referent ambiguous. UP restores people who do not believe in their god.
units.japanese: 「………そして彼らは、自らの神を信じない人々を不幸に突き落とすことで、自らの幸福を実証する」

description: WH says they are trying to speak in riddles, replacing the imperative self-warning with a description of their action.
sourceReading: Battler tells himself not to be hoodwinked by strange trivia.

units.text: Not yet.........don't give up this useless struggle yet. Who cares about 'Whoever's Raven'? They're just trying to speak in riddles by bringing up some weird bits of trivia...
units.note: MG restores Battler warning himself not to be confused by trivia. UP retains a statement that the opponents are trying to speak in riddles.
units.japanese: おかしな豆知識で煙に撒かれるな…。

units.text:
Not yet... ......Don't give up this struggle yet. Who cares about "Whoever's Raven"?
They're just trying to speak in riddles by bringing up some weird bits of trivia...
units.note: MG restores Battler warning himself not to be confused by trivia. UP retains a statement that the opponents are trying to speak in riddles.
units.japanese:
まだだ…。……悪足掻きを止めるな。何が“何たらのカラス”だ。
おかしな豆知識で煙に巻かれるな…。

description: WH asks if he plans to keep thinking on this level, suggesting intellectual quality rather than time spent on a minor challenge.
sourceReading: Beatrice taunts Battler for considering a long think over this small opening exchange.

units.text: "......We are still in the opening part of the game.  Do you plan to keep thinking on this level?"
units.note: MG asks whether Battler will keep thinking “on this level,” suggesting intellectual quality. UP restores Beatrice’s taunt about spending so long on an opening-stage problem.
units.japanese: 「……まだまだ序盤だぞ。この程度で長考するつもりか？」

units.text: "...We're still in the opening part of the game. Do you plan to keep thinking on this level?"
units.note: MG asks whether Battler will keep thinking “on this level,” suggesting intellectual quality. UP restores Beatrice’s taunt about spending so long on an opening-stage problem.
units.japanese: 「……まだまだ序盤だぞ。この程度で長考するつもりか？」

description: WH says Endless control means that I am able to kill endlessly, changing infinity from the object of control and destruction into their duration.
sourceReading: To command infinity means she can also destroy infinity, explicitly anticipating the defeat of infinite regress.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!!  How foolish...  Who do you think I am?  I am the Endless Witch!  The thought that you could challenge me endlessly is just absurd.  Endless control means that I am able to kill endlessly."
units.note: MG turns controlling and killing infinity into endless control and endless killing. UP restores infinity as the object controlled and killed.
units.japanese: 無限を操ることはつまり、無限を殺すこともできるということ。」
candidates: Endless control means that I am able to kill endlessly

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!! How foolish... Who do you think I am? I am the Endless Witch! The thought that you could challenge me endlessly is just absurd. Endless control means that I am able to kill endlessly."
units.note: MG turns controlling and killing infinity into endless control and endless killing. UP restores infinity as the object controlled and killed.
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくくくくくくくくく！！　愚かしいぞ…。妾を誰と心得る？　妾こそは無限の魔女！　その妾に無限にて挑むとは片腹痛いわ。無限を操ることはつまり、無限を殺すこともできるということ」
candidates: Endless control means that I am able to kill endlessly

description: WH asks where to strike for the kill, omitting the object 拠り所, his argumentative foothold.
sourceReading: Beatrice asks which support or basis she should cut down to plunge Battler into despair.

units.text: *cackle*cackle*!  See-, Battle-r.  What truth shall I tell in red this time?  Where shall I strike for the kill and force you into hopelessness?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*!  Come, show me your usual frightened face......"
units.note: Both editions ask where Beatrice should strike for the kill, omitting the argumentative foothold or support she threatens to cut down.
units.japanese: くっくっくっく！　ほぅら、戦人ぁ。今度はどんな真実を赤で語ってみせようか？　どんな拠り所を叩き斬って、そなたを絶望に突き落としてやろうか？　くっくっくっくっく！　そら、いつもの怯えた顔を見せてみるがいい……。」

units.text: *cackle*cackle*! See, Battleeer? What truth shall I tell in red this time? Where shall I strike for the kill and force you into hopelessness? *cackle*cackle*cackle*! Come, show me your usual frightened face..."
