units.note: Both editions ask where Beatrice should strike for the kill, omitting the argumentative foothold or support she threatens to cut down.
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっく！　ほぅら、戦人ぁ。今度はどんな真実を赤で語ってみせようか？　どんな拠り所を叩き斬って、そなたを絶望に突き落としてやろうか？　くっくっくっくっく！　そら、いつもの怯えた顔を見せてみるがいい……」

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*! Come now, Battlerrr. What truth shall I tell in red this time? Where shall I strike for the kill and force you into hopelessness? *cackle*cackle*cackle*! Come, show me your usual frightened face......"
units.note: Both editions ask where Beatrice should strike for the kill, omitting the argumentative foothold or support she threatens to cut down.
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっく！　ほぅら、戦人ぁ。今度はどんな真実を赤で語ってみせようか？　どんな拠り所を叩き斬って、そなたを絶望に突き落としてやろうか？　くっくっくっくっく！　そら、いつもの怯えた顔を見せてみるがいい……」

description: WH says red had not always been a weapon only Beato could use, shifting usefulness into who can wield it.
sourceReading: Red does not necessarily always work as Beatrice’s weapon; careless use can harm her.

units.text: That's right, the red hadn't always been a weapon that only Beato could use.  It was the other way around.  If she used it the wrong way, it was dangerous enough that she could bring about her own death. If she used it carelessly and said something which ended up denying herself, that would be exactly the same thing as self-destructing.
units.note: Both editions restore that red does not always work in Beatrice’s favor, rather than discussing who is able to wield it.
units.japanese: そうさ。赤は常にベアトの武器になるとは限らない。それどころか、誤って使えば、自らをも死に至らしかねないほどに危険なのだ。

description: WH describes stabbing at each other in a simultaneous clash, losing the explicit mutual-defeat consequence of 刺し違えても相打ち.
sourceReading: Battler says she might choose mutual destruction by taking him down with her.

units.text: But before that, it would mean your defeat! Saying in red that the culprit is a human is equivalent to your proclamation of resignation!!  If you want us to stab at each other in a simultaneous clash, I think that's a pretty interesting move.  However, this battle will end in my victory!!"
units.note: Both editions say Beatrice is prepared to die while striking Battler, but do not clearly preserve the explicit mutual-defeat result of taking each other down together.
units.japanese: 人間が犯人だとお前が赤で語ることは、お前の投了宣言にも等しい！！　お前が、俺と刺し違えても相打ちにしたいってんなら、それも面白い一手だろうぜ。だが、この勝負は俺の勝ちで終わるッ！！」
candidates: each other in a simultaneous clash

units.text: "But before that, it would mean your defeat! Saying in red that the culprit is a human is equivalent to your proclamation of resignation!! If you want to strike me a blow so badly you're prepared to die at the same time, I think that's a pretty interesting move. However, this battle will end in my victory!!"
units.note: Both editions say Beatrice is prepared to die while striking Battler, but do not clearly preserve the explicit mutual-defeat result of taking each other down together.
units.japanese: 「だが、それはそれ以前にお前の敗北も意味するッ！　人間が犯人だとお前が赤で語ることは、お前の投了宣言にも等しい！！　お前が、俺と刺し違えても相打ちにしたいってんなら、それも面白い一手だろうぜ。だが、この勝負は俺の勝ちで終わるッ！！」

units.text: "But before that, it would mean your defeat! Saying in red that the culprit is a human is equivalent to your proclamation of resignation!! If you want to strike me a blow so badly you're prepared to die at the same time, I think that's a pretty interesting move. However, this battle will end in my victory!!"
units.note: Both editions say Beatrice is prepared to die while striking Battler, but do not clearly preserve the explicit mutual-defeat result of taking each other down together.
units.japanese: 「だが、それはそれ以前にお前の敗北も意味するッ！　人間が犯人だとお前が赤で語ることは、お前の投了宣言にも等しい！！　お前が、俺と刺し違えても相打ちにしたいってんなら、それも面白い一手だろうぜ。だが、この勝負は俺の勝ちで終わるッ！！」

description: WH says a little part of his heart splits, replacing the supports he relies on with an emotional wound.
sourceReading: Red repeatedly cuts apart Battler’s scant supports or footholds.

units.text: Beatrice's red was her true trump card. When that person spoke in red, it was surely the truth, and no amount of proof or counterarguments could change that. Until now she had used that to severely wound me, and each time a little part of my heart would split in half.
units.note: Both editions restore Battler’s small emotional supports or foundations being split, rather than a piece of his heart itself splitting.
units.japanese: それらは俺を何度も叩き斬り、わずかな心の拠り所をいつも真っ二つにしてきた。

description: WH says this time it is your plan, changing the game-turn reference.
sourceReading: Battler tells Beatrice that it is now her turn to move.

units.text: "So, this time it's your plan.  ......That's right.  To use your 'Hempel's Raven', first, you'll have to confirm in red how many humans there are other than the 18.  And after that, if you proclaim in red that none of the people in this group are the culprit, ......that's right, that might be a fatal wound to me."
units.note: MG says it is time to hear Beatrice’s plan, changing the explicit game-turn reference. UP restores “your move.”
units.japanese: 「さぁ、今度はお前の手番だぜ。……そうさ。お前の“ヘンペルのカラス”を使うには、まず、１８人以外に何人の人間がいるのかを、赤で確定させる必要がある。その上で、それらの人間についてさらに赤で犯人でないことを宣言したならば、……なるほど、こいつは俺にとって致命傷になるだろうぜ。」

units.text: "Okay, now it's time to hear your plan. ...That's right. To use your "Hempel's Raven", first, you'll have to confirm in red how many humans there are other than the 18.
units.note: MG says it is time to hear Beatrice’s plan, changing the explicit game-turn reference. UP restores “your move.”
units.japanese: 「さぁ、今度はお前の手番だぜ。……そうさ。お前の“ヘンペルのカラス”を使うには、まず、１８人以外に何人の人間がいるのかを、赤で確定させる必要がある」

description: WH tells him to consider the weakness and make them move forward, replacing distance management and forcing the first draw with different tactical acts.
sourceReading: Battler measures fighting distance carefully, retreats gradually and makes his opponent draw first.

units.text: Consider that weakness with care, ...and retreat step by step.  Make them move forward. The more she recklessly flourished that red, the more chances I would get to strike back.
units.note: MG replaces careful distance management and making Beatrice draw first with gauging distance and making her move forward. UP restores the sword-drawing tactic.
units.japanese: 間合いを慎重に計りながら、…じりじりと後退するんだ。向こうに先に抜かせるんだ。

units.text: Gauge the distance between us with care, ...retreating step by step. Make them move forward. The more she recklessly flourished that red, the more chances I would get to strike back.
units.note: MG replaces careful distance management and making Beatrice draw first with gauging distance and making her move forward. UP restores the sword-drawing tactic.
units.japanese: 間合いを慎重に計りながら、…じりじりと後退するんだ。向こうに先に抜かせるんだ。ヤツが闇雲に赤を振り回せば振り回すほど、俺に反撃のチャンスは増える。

description: WH says to corner her so she will not be able to refute him with red, reversing the intended tactical result.
sourceReading: Battler tells himself to corner her so she has no choice but to counter in red.

units.text: Don't be afraid of the red. Keep her cornered, so that she won't be able to refute me with the red......! No matter how oppressively she speaks in red, ......that's right, that red itself is the same as fresh blood leaking from her wound.
units.note: Both editions restore Battler cornering Beatrice so she is forced to answer in red, rather than preventing a red reply.
units.japanese: むしろ、赤で反論せざるを得ないよう、追い詰めろ……！

description: WH asks her to tell him the total without specifying red in this sentence.
sourceReading: Battler demands that she state the island’s total population in red.

units.text: "So.  ...What's wrong?  ......First of all, why don't you tell me how many people are on this island total?  If you don't, your raven can't cut me up......!"
units.note: MG asks for the island’s total population without specifying that it must be stated in red. UP restores the red requirement.
units.japanese: 「さぁ。…どうしたよ。……まずはこの島に合計で何人いるのか、赤で語ってもらおうじゃねぇか。さもないと、お前のカラスは俺に斬り込めないぜ……！」

units.text: "So, ...what's wrong? ...First of all, why don't you tell me how many people are on this island total? If you don't, your raven can't cut me up...!"
units.note: MG asks for the island’s total population without specifying that it must be stated in red. UP restores the red requirement.
units.japanese: 「さぁ。…どうしたよ。……まずはこの島に合計で何人いるのか、赤で語ってもらおうじゃねぇか。さもないと、お前のカラスは俺に斬り込めないぜ……！」

description: WH says she probably planned to smile back, making the performed smile itself merely intended.
sourceReading: Beatrice smiles back, presumably intending to project composure, but cannot hide her sweat.

units.text: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her next move. Beato probably planned to smile back and appear relaxed, ......but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now she had completely lost that relaxedness which had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.
units.note: MG says Beatrice probably thought she had managed to smile back, making the smile itself uncertain. UP restores the actual smile followed by her probable intention.
units.japanese: ベアトは笑いを返し、余裕をアピールしたつもりだったろうが、……額に浮かぶ汗を隠せない。

units.text: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her into making her next move. Beato probably thought she'd managed to smile back and appear confident, ...but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now, she had completely lost the confident feeling that had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.
units.note: MG says Beatrice probably thought she had managed to smile back, making the smile itself uncertain. UP restores the actual smile followed by her probable intention.
units.japanese: 味方のはずのロノウェが、主に悪戯っぽく次の手を急かす。ベアトは笑いを返し、余裕をアピールしたつもりだったろうが、……額に浮かぶ汗を隠せない。格下の相手を鼻であしらってやろうという余裕は、今や完全に失われていた。

description: WH calls the opponent worthless, replacing comparative ability or rank with total lack of worth.
sourceReading: She had felt relaxed enough to dismiss an opponent beneath her level.

units.text: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her next move. Beato probably planned to smile back and appear relaxed, ......but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now she had completely lost that relaxedness which had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.
units.note: Both editions call Battler a worthless opponent instead of a lower-ranked or inferior one.
units.japanese: 格下の相手を鼻であしらってやろうという余裕は、今や完全に失われていた。

units.text: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her into making her next move. Beato probably thought she'd managed to smile back and appear confident, ...but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now, she had completely lost the confident feeling that had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.
units.note: Both editions call Battler a worthless opponent instead of a lower-ranked or inferior one.
units.japanese: 味方のはずのロノウェが、主に悪戯っぽく次の手を急かす。ベアトは笑いを返し、余裕をアピールしたつもりだったろうが、……額に浮かぶ汗を隠せない。格下の相手を鼻であしらってやろうという余裕は、今や完全に失われていた。

units.text: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her next move. Beato smiled back, probably intending to demonstrate that she was still relaxed, ......but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now she had completely lost that relaxedness which had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.
units.note: Both editions call Battler a worthless opponent instead of a lower-ranked or inferior one.
units.japanese: 味方のはずのロノウェが、主に悪戯っぽく次の手を急かす。ベアトは笑いを返し、余裕をアピールしたつもりだったろうが、……額に浮かぶ汗を隠せない。格下の相手を鼻であしらってやろうという余裕は、今や完全に失われていた。

description: WH says the worse red for me, using the comparative in place of the superlative.
sourceReading: Battler avoids the worst red for him.

units.text: Whew...! I had avoided what would have been the worse red for me.
units.note: Both editions use the superlative “worst red,” correcting original WH’s comparative “worse.”
units.japanese: 俺にとって、最悪の赤は回避された。

description: WH first calls X an enormous hint, making a hypothetical argumentative resource sound like supplied evidence.
sourceReading: X is a very substantial major piece to concede at the opening, able to answer the specified all-alibi scenarios.

units.text: ......If that X is allowed in my first move, that's a really enormous hint, right?  Anyway, from now on, all of the tricks that were impossible for the 18 people, can be explained with human X outside of the 18 people.  ......This is a huge piece that can break open all of the rooms that you called closed because everyone had an alibi...!"
units.note: MG removes original WH’s “enormous hint” but newly casts X as a piece Beatrice loses; that new wording is recorded separately. UP restores X as a huge piece she allows Battler to have.
units.japanese: ……このＸは、初手で許すには相当デカい大駒だぜ？　何しろ、以後、１８人の誰にも不可能だった、という根拠のトリックは、全て１８人以外の人間Ｘで説明可能になる。……全員アリバイ系の密室を、全て打ち破れる大駒だ…！」

description: WH says save her from this, shifting the immediate object of rescue from the piece to Beatrice.
sourceReading: Drawing red could rescue the threatened major piece just described.

units.text: It looked like Beato also noticed her current plight. She couldn't just let such an important piece go, especially this close to the beginning of the game... If she pulled out her red treasured sword, it wouldn't be that difficult to save her from this. ......But Beato was completely aware that I was expecting it. She was afraid that a careless red truth might end up strangling her own neck...!
units.note: MG retains saving Beatrice from the predicament instead of saving the important piece. UP restores the piece as the object rescued.
units.japanese: 赤き宝刀を抜けば、それを救うことは難しくないだろう。

units.text: It looked like Beato also noticed her current plight. She couldn't just let such an important piece go, especially this close to the beginning of the game... If she pulled out her red treasured sword, it wouldn't be that difficult to save herself from this. ...But Beato was completely aware that I was expecting it. She was afraid that a careless red truth might end up strangling her own neck...!
units.note: MG retains saving Beatrice from the predicament instead of saving the important piece. UP restores the piece as the object rescued.
units.japanese: ベアトも、現在の窮状をよく理解しているようだった。これほどの大駒を、これほどの序盤に見捨てられるわけもない…。赤き宝刀を抜けば、それを救うことは難しくないだろう。……しかしベアトは、むしろ俺がそれを待ち受けていることも、充分に察している。迂闊な赤き真実が、自らの首を絞めることになるかもしれないと怯えている…！

description: WH says valleys between truths, substituting truth statements or truths for reality.
sourceReading: Witches can exist only in the gaps of reality.

units.text: They could only exist in the valleys between truths. ...They were a fragile existence, curled up in these cracks, frantically trying to protect themselves from the brutal winds of truth, and they could only barely exist like a mirage by surviving on falsehoods and illusions.
units.note: MG retains “valleys between truths” for gaps in reality. UP restores cracks in reality.
units.japanese: それが存在できるのは、現実の狭間だけ。

units.text: They can only exist in the valleys between truths. ...They have a fragile existence, curled up in these cracks, frantically trying to protect themselves from the brutal winds of truth, and they can only barely exist like a mirage by surviving on falsehoods and illusions.
units.note: MG retains “valleys between truths” for gaps in reality. UP restores cracks in reality.
units.japanese: それが存在できるのは、現実の狭間だけ。…その隙間にて、真実の暴風から必死に身を守って縮こまり、虚偽と幻想で食い繋いでいる時だけ、蜃気楼のように細々と存在できる脆弱な存在なのだ。

description: WH says witches cannot help but deny themselves, making the possible adverse result inevitable.
sourceReading: Red is reality itself and could negate the witch using it.

units.text: That was the truth by which witches couldn't help but deny themselves, using the red words which only they could use. ......The more they brandish their red words......the more they begin to lose bit by bit that crack in truth inside which they can endure.
units.note: Both editions restore potential self-denial: red might or risks denying witches, rather than making self-denial inevitable.
units.japanese: つまり、魔女だけが使える赤は、自らを否定しかねない現実そのもの。

description: WH says she has really been pierced to the bone, replacing deep understanding with an injury image; the following sentence also replaces resolve with preparation.
sourceReading: Beatrice knows better than anyone, to her very bones, that using red requires considerable resolve.

units.text: Don't be afraid.  Stay strong...! I know that she is the one who has really been pierced to the bone. Because her red treasured sword couldn't easily be used without a lot of preparation...!
units.note: MG retains both being pierced to the bone for deep understanding and preparation for resolve. UP restores knowing it deep down and considerable resolve.
units.japanese: ヤツが一番骨身に染みてわかってるんだ。
candidates: really been pierced to the bone

units.text: Don't be afraid. Stay strong...! I know that she's the one who's really been pierced to the bone. After all, her red treasured sword can't be used without a lot of preparation...!
units.note: MG retains both being pierced to the bone for deep understanding and preparation for resolve. UP restores knowing it deep down and considerable resolve.
units.japanese:
怯えるな。強気でいろ…！
ヤツが一番骨身に染みてわかってるんだ。赤き宝刀は、相当の覚悟がなければ容易には使えないのだということを…！
candidates: really been pierced to the bone

description: WH describes red words she does not have to use, substituting lack of necessity for intentional withholding.
sourceReading: Deliberately choosing not to use red can itself be a red-like tactic, producing fear through the sheathed sword.

units.text: "......Red words that I don't have to use are a kind of red words in themselves.  You called it my red treasured sword.  A pleasant example.  I will use it too.  ......A treasured sword is at its best when it is sheathed.  In fact, there are times it can instill even more fear because it is sheathed."
units.note: Both editions restore deliberate nonuse of red, rather than red she does not need to use.
units.japanese: 「……敢えて使わぬ赤もまた、赤らしい使い方よ。そなたは赤き宝刀と呼んだな。愉快な例えよ。妾も使おう。……宝刀は抜かぬ内が花よ。むしろ抜かぬことによって醸せる畏怖というものもある。」

description: WH says being a poor loser would last for the whole early part, reversing the ending marker into continuing behavior.
sourceReading: Her sour-grapes retort apparently puts a period to the opening battle.

units.text: Her being a poor loser looked like it would last for the whole early part of the game. Even so, I couldn't relax my guard at all. ...I was unable to relax my feeling of tension until I was greeted by the sound of Ronove's applause...
units.note: Both editions restore the bitter remark as the end of the opening battle rather than behavior expected to last throughout it.
units.japanese: その負け惜しみが、事実上、序盤戦のピリオドとなったらしい。
candidates: last for the whole early part

description: WH calls it encouragement, weakening the corrective function of the setback.
sourceReading: Because Beatrice quickly grows arrogant, Ronove calls the occasional stimulus of losing a point good medicine.

units.text: "How could you think that?  I am innocently celebrating your ability that has enabled you to take one shot at Milady, even though it is only the first round.  ...In any event, Milady is a person who is quick to become arrogant.  I believe that a little encouragement such as that makes for a good medicine every once in a while."
units.note: MG retains “encouragement” for the corrective stimulus Ronove says may be good medicine. UP restores “stimulation.”
units.japanese: …何しろお嬢様はすぐ増長するお方。たまにはこのような刺激も良い薬かと思いますよ。」

units.text: "How could you think that? I am innocently celebrating your ability, which has enabled you to take one shot at Milady, even though it is only the first round. ...In any event, Milady is a person who is quick to become arrogant. I believe that a little encouragement such as this can be good medicine every once in a while."
units.note: MG retains “encouragement” for the corrective stimulus Ronove says may be good medicine. UP restores “stimulation.”
units.japanese: 「まさか。序盤とは言え、お嬢様より一本を奪った手腕を純粋に祝福いたしております。…何しろお嬢様はすぐ増長するお方。たまにはこのような刺激も良い薬かと思いますよ」

description: WH says it is a piece that you would hate to miss, assigning the evaluation to her addressee.
sourceReading: Beatrice regards this as a major piece too valuable to let slip, motivating her next move.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*...  It really is a big piece that you'd hate to miss.
units.note: MG restores Beatrice as the evaluator with “I’d hate,” though “lose it” replaces overlooking the piece. UP retains the inherited second-person “you’d hate to miss.”
units.japanese: 「くっくっく…。やはり、見逃すには惜しい大駒よ。

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*... It really is a big piece that you'd hate to miss."
units.note: MG restores Beatrice as the evaluator with “I’d hate,” though “lose it” replaces overlooking the piece. UP retains the inherited second-person “you’d hate to miss.”
units.japanese: 「くっくっく…。やはり、見逃すには惜しい大駒よ」

description: WH says she could not deny it, strengthening observed non-denial into inability to dispute it.
sourceReading: Rosa does not deny the apparent connection between her distraction and their topic.

units.text: At those words, everyone stared at Rosa together. As if in response, Rosa's shoulders quivered. Apparently Kyrie's guess hadn't been wrong. ...Rosa couldn't deny that either...
units.note: MG retains inability to deny the point. UP restores the observed fact that Rosa does not deny it.
units.japanese: …楼座もまた、それを否定しない…。

units.text: At those words, everyone stared at Rosa together. As if in response, Rosa's shoulders quivered. Apparently, Kyrie's guess hadn't been wrong. ...Rosa couldn't deny it either...
units.note: MG retains inability to deny the point. UP restores the observed fact that Rosa does not deny it.
units.japanese:
その言葉に、みんなが一斉に楼座に注目する。それに応えるように、楼座もびくりと肩を震わせた。霧江の指摘は間違っていないようだった。
…楼座もまた、それを否定しない…。

description: WH says We said we would talk, replacing a gentle request with an assertion of a prior agreement.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi asks Rosa to tell them, following reassurance that worrying alone is unnecessarily distant.

units.text: "All of us've just sworn to remain united, haven't we?  Don't be reserved, worryin' by yourself.  We said we'd talk."
units.note: MG retains “We said we’d talk,” inventing a prior agreement. UP restores the request to talk it over.
units.japanese: 「わしら全員で団結しようって誓い合ったばかりやないか。ひとりで悩むなんて、水臭い話やで。話したってぇな。」

units.text: "We all just swore to remain united, didn't we? Don't hold back, worryin' by yourself. We said we'd talk."
units.note: MG retains “We said we’d talk,” inventing a prior agreement. UP restores the request to talk it over.
units.japanese: 「わしら全員で団結しようって誓い合ったばかりやないか。ひとりで悩むなんて、水臭い話やで。話したってぇな」

description: WH calls her Grandfather’s mistress, misassigning Rosa’s generational relationship to Kinzo.
sourceReading: Rosa identifies Beatrice as her father’s mistress.

units.text: "No, umm............Th, this mistress of Grandfather's, this Beatrice, ......I was wondering if she is still, .........alive..."
units.note: Both editions restore Rosa’s “Father” rather than misassigning Kinzo as her grandfather.
units.japanese:
「いえ、その……。……ベ、ベアトリーチェっていう、お父様の愛人って、……本当にその、
………生きてるのかしらって思って…。」

description: WH says she kept talking, unable to stop, losing the characterization of what she says as disconnected.
sourceReading: Rosa blurts disconnected or incoherent things while clutching her head.

units.text: It was so sudden that everyone was lost for words. Rosa kept on talking, unable to stop, holding her head as her hair flew all about...
units.note: Both editions retain “kept on talking, unable to stop,” replacing the characterization of Rosa’s words as incoherent or disconnected.
units.japanese: 楼座は取りとめもないことを口走りながら、髪を振り乱しながら頭を抱えていた…。
candidates: kept on talking, unable to stop

units.text: It was so sudden that everyone was lost for words. Rosa kept on talking, unable to stop, holding her head as her hair flew all about...
units.note: Both editions retain “kept on talking, unable to stop,” replacing the characterization of Rosa’s words as incoherent or disconnected.
units.japanese: 突然のことに、誰もが言葉を失う。楼座は取りとめもないことを口走りながら、髪を振り乱しながら頭を抱えていた…。
candidates: kept on talking, unable to stop

description: WH says he exaggerates his age, introducing a performance of age rather than age-appropriate manner.
sourceReading: Kinzo sits down with ceremonious or ponderous gestures appropriate to his age.

units.text: I sat in the garden chair, and beckoned Kinzo to do the same. Kinzo sat down heavily, exaggerating his age.
units.note: Both editions retain Kinzo “exaggerating his age,” replacing his age-appropriate, ceremonious manner with a performance of age.
units.japanese: 金蔵は年齢相応のもったいぶった仕草で深々と腰を下ろした。

units.text: I sat in a garden chair and beckoned Kinzo to do the same. Kinzo sat down heavily, exaggerating his age.
units.note: Both editions retain Kinzo “exaggerating his age,” replacing his age-appropriate, ceremonious manner with a performance of age.
units.japanese:
妾はガーデンチェアに腰掛け、金蔵にも座るように勧める。
金蔵は年齢相応のもったいぶった仕草で深々と腰を下ろした。

units.text:
I sat in the garden chair, and beckoned Kinzo to do the same.
Kinzo sat down heavily, exaggerating his age.
units.note: Both editions retain Kinzo “exaggerating his age,” replacing his age-appropriate, ceremonious manner with a performance of age.
units.japanese:
妾はガーデンチェアに腰掛け、金蔵にも座るように勧める。
金蔵は年齢相応のもったいぶった仕草で深々と腰を下ろした。

description: WH says In my younger days, I sometimes wanted to, adding a personal recollection.
sourceReading: Kinzo says that in youth one sometimes wants to play in an exitless maze of thought, classifying her concern that way.

units.text: "What's this?  ......Don't you even understand yourself what it is you want to know?  That is baffling.  In my younger days, I sometimes wanted to play in the maze of thought that has no exit.  Maybe that is what your worries are..."
units.note: MG restores the general observation “In one’s youth.” UP retains Kinzo’s invented personal recollection “In my younger days.”
units.japanese: 「何だ。……何が知りたいのか、自分でもわからぬというのか。それは不可解な。若き日には、出口無き思考の迷路にて遊びたくなることもある。そなたの悩みもそれであろう…。」

units.text: "What's this? ......Don't you even understand yourself what it is you want to know? That is baffling. In my younger days, I sometimes found myself wanting to play in the maze of thought that has no exit. Maybe that is what your worries are..."
units.note: MG restores the general observation “In one’s youth.” UP retains Kinzo’s invented personal recollection “In my younger days.”
units.japanese: 「何だ。……何が知りたいのか、自分でもわからぬというのか。それは不可解な。若き日には、出口無き思考の迷路にて遊びたくなることもある。そなたの悩みもそれであろう…」

description: WH asks how long she will be able to continue her days here, shifting an imposed or unexplained stay toward ability or permission to keep staying.
sourceReading: She asks how long she is supposed to go on spending her days here: いつまで...過ごせば良いのか.

units.text: ......Who am I, what am I?  ...How long have I been here, ...and how long will I be able to continue my days here?"
units.note: MG restores the imposed duration with “how long will I have to.” UP removes original WH’s ability wording but still asks how long she “will” continue, omitting how long she is supposed to remain.
units.japanese: ……妾は誰で、何で。…いつからここにいて、…そしていつまでここで日々を過ごせば良いのか。」

units.text: "......Who am I, what am I? ...How long have I been here, ...and how long will I continue my days here?"
units.note: MG restores the imposed duration with “how long will I have to.” UP removes original WH’s ability wording but still asks how long she “will” continue, omitting how long she is supposed to remain.
units.japanese: 「……妾は誰で、何で。…いつからここにいて、…そしていつまでここで日々を過ごせば良いのか」

description: WH says I did think of it that way, apparently endorsing Battler’s bird-in-a-cage description rather than explaining unquestioned normality.
sourceReading: She thought this was simply how things were, since it had been her life from earliest awareness and she never questioned it.

units.text: "......I did think of it that way.  Anyway, as soon as I became aware, I was living like that.  I didn't even think to question it."
units.note: MG changes the wording to “That’s what I thought at the time” but still appears to endorse Battler’s cage metaphor. UP restores that Beatrice regarded the life as simply how things were.
units.japanese: 「……そういうモノだと思っていた。何しろ、気付いた時からそういう生活だったからな。疑問にも思わなかった。」

units.text: "...That's what I thought at the time. After all, as soon as I became aware, I was living like that. I didn't even think to question it."
units.note: MG changes the wording to “That’s what I thought at the time” but still appears to endorse Battler’s cage metaphor. UP restores that Beatrice regarded the life as simply how things were.
units.japanese: 「……そういうモノだと思っていた。何しろ、気付いた時からそういう生活だったからな。疑問にも思わなかった」
candidates: That's what I thought at the time

description: WH retains only the intended disappearance.
sourceReading: She says she gave gold and was then supposed to disappear until the contract ended.

units.text: "Hmm.  That is correct.  ...Then I was supposed to hide myself until the contract was over.  But, .........well, it's tough being a popular woman.  .........By some turn of events, Kinzo fell in love with me."
units.note: Both editions omit Beatrice explicitly saying that she gave Kinzo the gold from her own stated sequence before the intended disappearance.
units.japanese: 「うむ。それは正しい。…そして妾は黄金を授け、契約の終わる時まで姿を消すはずだった。

units.text: "Indeed. That is correct. ...Then, I was supposed to vanish until the contract was complete. But......well, popular women have it rough. ......By some turn of events, Kinzo fell in love with me."
units.note: Both editions omit Beatrice explicitly saying that she gave Kinzo the gold from her own stated sequence before the intended disappearance.
units.japanese: 「うむ。それは正しい。…そして妾は黄金を授け、契約の終わる時まで姿を消すはずだった。しかし、………まぁ、モテる女の辛いとこよな。………金蔵は、こともあろうか、妾に恋をした」

units.text: "Yes. That is correct. ...Then I was supposed to hide myself until the contract was over. But, .........well, it's tough being a popular woman. .........By some turn of events, Kinzo fell in love with me."
units.note: Both editions omit Beatrice explicitly saying that she gave Kinzo the gold from her own stated sequence before the intended disappearance.
units.japanese: 「うむ。それは正しい。…そして妾は黄金を授け、契約の終わる時まで姿を消すはずだった。しかし、………まぁ、モテる女の辛いとこよな。………金蔵は、こともあろうか、妾に恋をした」

description: WH says annoying at best, changing maximal irritation into an awkward best-case qualification.
sourceReading: Kinzo’s love is an utterly troublesome matter for her: 迷惑この上ない.

units.text: ".........Hmph.  Well, to me it was annoying at best.
units.note: Both editions restore maximal irritation rather than original WH’s contradictory “annoying at best.”
units.japanese: 「………ふ。まぁ、妾にとっては迷惑この上ない話よ。

description: WH writes It’s name instead of Its name.
sourceReading: The mansion’s name is Kuwadorian.

units.text: "......Indeed.  Just as you imagine, this is deep in the forest of Rokkenjima.  A hidden mansion not to be found from the outside world.  It's name is Kuwadorian (Nine Birds' Retreat)."
units.note: Both editions use possessive “Its name,” correcting original WH’s “It’s name.”
units.japanese: 「……いかにも。そなたの想像通り、ここは六軒島の森深く。外界からは見つけることも叶わぬ隠し屋敷。その名も九羽鳥庵（くわどりあん）。」

description: WH says if I do not ask, the story will not continue, replacing his willingness to hear her account with questioning.
sourceReading: Battler says the story cannot proceed unless he listens.

units.text: "..................... ......I'll decide whether I believe or not.  ...After all, if I don't ask, the story won't continue.  Tell me.  ...The story from your past."
units.note: MG retains “if I don’t ask,” replacing Battler’s willingness to hear the account with questioning. UP restores “if I don’t hear it.”
units.japanese: ……信じるかどうかは俺が判断するぜ。…聞かなきゃ話も進まねぇしな。話せよ。…お前の昔話を。」

units.text: "............ ...I'll decide whether I believe or not. ...After all, if I don't ask, the story won't continue. Tell me. ...Let's hear this story from your past."
units.note: MG retains “if I don’t ask,” replacing Battler’s willingness to hear the account with questioning. UP restores “if I don’t hear it.”
units.japanese: 「………………………。……信じるかどうかは俺が判断するぜ。…聞かなきゃ話も進まねぇしな。話せよ。…お前の昔話を」

units.text: "..................... ......I'll decide whether I believe or not.  ...After all, if I don't ask, the story won't continue.  Tell me.  ...The story from your past."
units.note: MG again uses “the more I ask” for the more Battler hears. UP restores hearing. This recurrence remains under the existing canonical parent.
units.japanese: ……信じるかどうかは俺が判断するぜ。…聞かなきゃ話も進まねぇしな。話せよ。…お前の昔話を。」

units.text: "Heh, in the beginning, I showed a little interest, thinking that there might be some huge hint hidden here, but the more I ask, the weirder this story starts to get. I get the feeling that even though this is supposed to be a game about denying witches, I'm suddenly being forced to just swallow this story about witches."
units.note: MG again uses “the more I ask” for the more Battler hears. UP restores hearing. This recurrence remains under the existing canonical parent.
units.japanese: 「へ。最初は何か重大なヒントが隠されているだろうと、多少の興味を示したが。聞けば聞くほどおかしな話になっていく。魔女を否定するゲームのはずなのに、いつの間にか魔女話を鵜呑みにさせられていく気がするぜ」

description: WH says the vessel can be restricted in many ways through magic, reversing the relation between embodied limitations and magic acting on the body.
sourceReading: The physical body is a vessel with many constraints when it comes to magic.

units.text: "After trying to resist in various ways, I eventually reached the conclusion that, to escape from Kinzo's barrier, I would have to throw away this body of flesh.  ......The physical body is a vessel which can be restricted in many ways through magic."
units.note: Both editions restore the body as a vessel carrying many restrictions in relation to magic, rather than a vessel restricted through magic.
units.japanese: 「様々な抵抗を試みた結果、金蔵の結界から逃れるには、肉の体を捨てるほかないという結論に至った。……肉体というものは、魔法を語る上でとても制約の多い器なのだ。」
candidates: restricted in many ways through magic

description: WH substitutes shows that she is willing to die, weakening an actual death in the hypothetical comparison to demonstrated willingness.
sourceReading: Normally, if the woman of an unrequited love dies, even a longstanding passion would cool.

units.text: ...No, he was a frightening person.  Normally, when the woman of someone's unrequited love shows that she is willing to die, it should be enough to bring that person to their senses, even if their love was 100 years old.  ......I guess he was a petty excuse of a magician after all.  ......*cackle*."
units.note: MG retains showing willingness to die instead of the hypothetical woman actually dying. UP restores taking her own life.
units.japanese: …いやいや、恐ろしいヤツ。普通は、片思いの女が死んで見せれば、百年の恋も醒めるであろうに。……だからこそあれも魔術師の端くれなのか。……くっくっく。」
candidates: shows that she is willing to die

units.text: "...Oh, he was a fearsome person. Normally, when the object of one's unrequited love shows that she is willing to die, it should be enough to bring that person to their senses, even if their love has lasted a hundred years. ...Perhaps that's why even he managed to become a sorceror of sorts. ...*cackle*."
units.note: MG retains showing willingness to die instead of the hypothetical woman actually dying. UP restores taking her own life.
units.japanese: 「…いやいや、恐ろしいヤツ。普通は、片思いの女が死んで見せれば、百年の恋も醒めるであろうに。……だからこそあれも魔術師の端くれなのか。……くっくっく」
candidates: shows that she is willing to die

description: WH says he seized her body, replacing the captured entity and breaking the transition to the soul’s cage.
sourceReading: Kinzo catches her soul and brings it back, then needs a special cage to hold it.

units.text: ".........Then Kinzo seized my body and brought me back.  However, a cage to hold a seized soul cannot be made from iron or lead.  ......Only one thing remained."
units.note: Both editions restore Kinzo seizing Beatrice’s soul rather than her body.
units.japanese: 「…………そして金蔵は、妾の魂を捕まえ、連れ戻したのだ。だが、魂を捕らえておく檻は、鉄でも鉛でも作れない。……ただひとつを除いて。」

description: WH makes Battler say she was not clever enough to finish the job, adding an intelligence-based insult to his dismissive summary.
sourceReading: Battler says she could not fully die, or failed to die properly.

units.text: ".....................So in summary, is it something like this?  Grandfather persistently courted you, you started to hate it, and you committed suicide, but you weren't clever enough to finish the job?  ...Damn, you really took a roundabout way to say something like that."
units.note: Both editions retain Battler saying Beatrice was not clever enough to complete suicide, adding an intelligence-based insult.
units.japanese: 「…………………。…要約するとこういうことか。祖父さまがしつこく求愛するんで嫌になり自殺したが、うまく死に切れなかったってことだろう？　…回りくどい言い方しやがってからに。」
candidates: clever enough to finish the job

units.text: "......... ...So to sum up, it's like this? Grandfather obstinately courted you, you started to hate it, and you committed suicide, but you weren't clever enough to finish the job? ...Damn, you really took a roundabout way to say something like that."
units.note: Both editions retain Battler saying Beatrice was not clever enough to complete suicide, adding an intelligence-based insult.
units.japanese: 「…………………。…要約するとこういうことか。祖父さまがしつこく求愛するんで嫌になり自殺したが、うまく死に切れなかったってことだろう？　…回りくどい言い方しやがってからに」
candidates: clever enough to finish the job

units.text: "..................... ...So in summary, is it something like this? Grandfather persistently courted you, you started to hate it, and you committed suicide, but you weren't clever enough to finish the job? ...Damn, you really took a roundabout way to say something like that."
units.note: Both editions retain Battler saying Beatrice was not clever enough to complete suicide, adding an intelligence-based insult.
units.japanese: 「…………………。…要約するとこういうことか。祖父さまがしつこく求愛するんで嫌になり自殺したが、うまく死に切れなかったってことだろう？　…回りくどい言い方しやがってからに」
candidates: clever enough to finish the job

description: WH substitutes earplugs for the earwax Battler dismissively says he will pick.
sourceReading: He will pick his earwax while she rambles.

units.text: "Sorry, but I don't feel like listening to this any more.  Just keep rambling on to yourself as much as you want.  I'll just pick my earplugs or something."
units.note: Both editions restore earwax rather than original WH’s earplugs.
units.japanese: 「悪いがこれ以上、耳を貸す気はねぇな。勝手に好きなだけほざいてろよ。耳クソでもほじってるからよー。」

description: WH moves the degree modifier from Battler’s slightly mocking gesture to Beatrice’s sensitive reaction.
sourceReading: Beatrice reacts sensitively to his slightly mocking gesture.

units.text: After I made fun of her, Beato reacted a little sensitively. It looked like, even though making fun of people was her specialty, she was horrible at being made fun of by other people.
units.note: Both editions move the slight degree from Battler’s mocking gesture to Beatrice reacting “a little sensitively.”
units.japanese: 俺のちょいと馬鹿にした仕草に、ベアトは敏感に反応する。

units.text: After I made fun of her, Beato reacted a little sensitively. It looked like, even though making fun of people was her specialty, she was horrible at being made fun of by others.
units.note: Both editions move the slight degree from Battler’s mocking gesture to Beatrice reacting “a little sensitively.”
units.japanese: 俺のちょいと馬鹿にした仕草に、ベアトは敏感に反応する。人を馬鹿にするのは大の得意だが、人から馬鹿にされるのはまったく駄目だと見える。

description: WH changes Beatrice’s reason for refusing to continue into a refusal to speak ridiculously.
sourceReading: She too finds it ridiculous and has no desire to talk.

units.text: "Ronove.  That is enough of this story.  This person said that it was too ridiculous to listen to.  I also have no intention of speaking ridiculously."
units.note: MG makes Battler too ridiculous to talk to, while UP makes Beatrice feel ridiculous. Both still alter her reason: she finds the matter too ridiculous to feel like continuing.
units.japanese: 「ロノウェ。もうその話は良い。こやつは馬鹿馬鹿しくて聞けんと言うでな。妾も馬鹿馬鹿しくて話す気にもならぬ。」

units.text: "Ronove, enough of that. This person just said it was too ridiculous to be worth listening to. Well, he's too ridiculous to be worth talking to."
units.note: MG makes Battler too ridiculous to talk to, while UP makes Beatrice feel ridiculous. Both still alter her reason: she finds the matter too ridiculous to feel like continuing.
units.japanese: 「ロノウェ。もうその話はよい。こやつは馬鹿馬鹿しくて聞けんと言うでな。妾も馬鹿馬鹿しくて話す気にもならぬ」

units.text: "Ronove. That is enough of that story. He says that it is too ridiculous to listen to. I now also feel ridiculous and have no intention of speaking."
units.note: MG makes Battler too ridiculous to talk to, while UP makes Beatrice feel ridiculous. Both still alter her reason: she finds the matter too ridiculous to feel like continuing.
units.japanese: 「ロノウェ。もうその話はよい。こやつは馬鹿馬鹿しくて聞けんと言うでな。妾も馬鹿馬鹿しくて話す気にもならぬ」

description: WH calls Milady completely like a human, replacing human status with resemblance.
sourceReading: She is Milady as a human, with no witch powers.

units.text: "Yes.  That is correct.  It grew to be completely identical.  However, it did not possess her power as a witch.  ......Milady was completely like a human."
units.note: Both editions restore Milady’s human status rather than saying she was merely like a human.
units.japanese: 「はい。その通りでございます。まさに瓜二つに成長なされました。しかし魔女としての力は持ち合わせておりません。……あくまでも人間としてのお嬢様なのです。」

description: WH says Kinzo betrayed her instead of losing his temper at the rejection and confining her.
sourceReading: He irrationally turns angry at her rejection and locks her up.

units.text: Grandfather met Beatrice. He then fell in love with her and courted her, but she didn't nod her head in agreement. And then he betrayed her and shut her up inside this hidden mansion. Beatrice tried to escape, but no matter what she did, she couldn't succeed, ......so she finally chose her own death.
units.note: Both editions restore Kinzo becoming angry at rejection instead of betraying Beatrice.
units.japanese: それで逆ギレして隠し屋敷に閉じ込めてしまったわけだ。

description: WH removes the proposed parent-child relation at its first introduction, saying there was a girl resembling Beatrice.
sourceReading: Battler proposes that Beatrice had a daughter, or rather a baby, who was her living image.

units.text: ......And then, .........no. ...Maybe there was a girl that looked just like Beatrice, ...no, a baby. And Grandfather raised this child with care.
units.note: Both editions omit the proposed parent-child relationship at its first introduction, saying only that a girl or baby resembled Beatrice.
units.japanese: …ベアトリーチェには、生き写しの娘、…いや、赤ん坊がいたとか。

units.text: ...And then, ......no. ...Maybe there was a girl who looked just like Beatrice...no, a baby. Grandfather raised this child with care.
units.note: Both editions omit the proposed parent-child relationship at its first introduction, saying only that a girl or baby resembled Beatrice.
units.japanese: ……それで、………うーん。…ベアトリーチェには、生き写しの娘、…いや、赤ん坊がいたとか。それで祖父さまはその子を大事に育てたわけだ。

units.text: ......And then, .........hmm. ...Maybe there was a girl that looked just like Beatrice, ...no, a baby. And Grandfather raised this child with care.
units.note: Both editions omit the proposed parent-child relationship at its first introduction, saying only that a girl or baby resembled Beatrice.
units.japanese: ……それで、………うーん。…ベアトリーチェには、生き写しの娘、…いや、赤ん坊がいたとか。それで祖父さまはその子を大事に育てたわけだ。

description: WH has Ronove claim he is apparently lacking as a demon, instead of explaining that he too is a demon, however modest his rank.
sourceReading: He is, after all, a demon of sorts, which explains his ability to speak red.

units.text: "Apparently I am lacking as a demon.  ...Please keep this a secret from Milady, alright?"
units.note: MG changes the inherited defect into an appearance-based caveat, “I may not look it.” UP restores Ronove’s modest-rank claim that he is still a demon.
units.japanese: 「これでも悪魔の端くれでございますので。…お嬢様には内緒にしてくださいね？」

units.text: "I may not look it, but I am a demon. ...Please keep this a secret from Milady, yes?"
units.note: MG changes the inherited defect into an appearance-based caveat, “I may not look it.” UP restores Ronove’s modest-rank claim that he is still a demon.
units.japanese: 「これでも悪魔の端くれでございますので。…お嬢様には内緒にしてくださいね？」

description: WH omits in red from the hypothetical witch-existence statement that would leave Battler helpless.
sourceReading: Being told in red that a witch exists would leave him helpless from the outset.

units.text: "......So, to say it quickly, you mean that point blank questions are prohibited?  Well, that's true, I guess.  If I were told 'a witch exists', I'd have to give up from the start."
units.note: MG again omits “in red” from the hypothetical witch-existence statement. UP restores it.
units.japanese: まー、そりゃそうだよな。赤で、“魔女は実在する”って言われちまったら、俺はハナからお手上げだぜ。」

units.text: "...So, to say it quickly, you're saying point-blank questions are prohibited? Well, that's true, I guess. If I were told "a witch exists", I'd have to give up from the start."
units.note: MG again omits “in red” from the hypothetical witch-existence statement. UP restores it.
units.japanese: 「……早い話が、身も蓋もない質問は禁止だと、そう言いたいわけだな？　まー、そりゃそうだよな。赤で、“魔女は実在する”って言われちまったら、俺はハナからお手上げだぜ」

description: WH makes Kinzo believe a soul was placed into a new body, omits raising the child, and weakens the reincarnation belief with maybe.
sourceReading: Battler interprets the soul-transfer story as meaning Kinzo raised the child believing her to be Beatrice’s reincarnation.

units.text: ......And then, ......her soul was put in a homunculus and...... No, no, if I accept that, it's the same as accepting the witch. I can interpret that part like this. She probably had, ......a posthumous daughter. Grandfather must have believed that her soul was put into a new physical body..., and maybe that the child was the reincarnation of Beatrice...
units.note: MG retains belief attributed directly to Kinzo, omits raising the child, and weakens the reincarnation inference. UP restores the full reconstruction.
units.japanese: 魂を新しい肉体に込めた…、みたいな話は多分、その子をベアトリーチェの生まれ変わりだと信じて育てた、という意味に違いない…。

units.text: ......And then, ...her soul was put in a homunculus and... No, no, if I accept that, it's the same as accepting the witch. I can interpret that part like this. She probably...had a posthumous daughter. Grandfather must've believed that her soul had been placed in a new physical body... and might have thought that the child was the reincarnation of Beatrice...
units.note: MG retains belief attributed directly to Kinzo, omits raising the child, and weakens the reincarnation inference. UP restores the full reconstruction.
units.japanese:
……それで、……ホムンクルスに魂を……。駄目だ駄目だ、こいつを受け容れちまったら、魔女を認めたも同然だぜ。そこはこう解釈するんだ。
死んだ彼女には多分、……忘れ形見の娘がいたんだろう。魂を新しい肉体に込めた…、みたいな話は多分、その子をベアトリーチェの生まれ変わりだと信じて育てた、という意味に違いない…。

description: WH labels the daughter posthumous, adding an apparent birth-after-death chronology.
sourceReading: The dead woman probably left behind a daughter as a keepsake of her.

units.text: ......And then, ......her soul was put in a homunculus and...... No, no, if I accept that, it's the same as accepting the witch. I can interpret that part like this. She probably had, ......a posthumous daughter. Grandfather must have believed that her soul was put into a new physical body..., and maybe that the child was the reincarnation of Beatrice...
units.note: MG retains “posthumous daughter,” adding birth after death. UP restores a daughter left behind at death.
units.japanese: 死んだ彼女には多分、……忘れ形見の娘がいたんだろう。

units.text: ......And then, ...her soul was put in a homunculus and... No, no, if I accept that, it's the same as accepting the witch. I can interpret that part like this. She probably...had a posthumous daughter. Grandfather must've believed that her soul had been placed in a new physical body... and might have thought that the child was the reincarnation of Beatrice...
units.note: MG retains “posthumous daughter,” adding birth after death. UP restores a daughter left behind at death.
units.japanese:
……それで、……ホムンクルスに魂を……。駄目だ駄目だ、こいつを受け容れちまったら、魔女を認めたも同然だぜ。そこはこう解釈するんだ。
死んだ彼女には多分、……忘れ形見の娘がいたんだろう。魂を新しい肉体に込めた…、みたいな話は多分、その子をベアトリーチェの生まれ変わりだと信じて育てた、という意味に違いない…。

description: WH says Battler must be glad the scapegoat is Milady, assigning the delight to him.
sourceReading: Ronove finds it most amusing that the sacrificial scapegoat is Milady.

units.text: ......A sacrificial sheep that you can shift the blame of any crime onto.  And you must be so glad that it is Milady.  Pu ku ku ku."
units.note: MG restores Ronove’s own amusement that Milady is the scapegoat. UP retains assigning delight to Battler.
units.japanese: ……如何なる罪をも擦り付けることのできる生贄の羊。それがお嬢様とは実に愉快。ぷっくっくっく。」

units.text: "......A sacrificial sheep that you can shift the blame of any crime onto. And you must be so glad that it is Milady. Pu ku ku ku."
units.note: MG restores Ronove’s own amusement that Milady is the scapegoat. UP retains assigning delight to Battler.
units.japanese: 「……如何なる罪をも擦り付けることのできる生贄の羊。それがお嬢様とは実に愉快。ぷっくっくっく」

description: WH says the urgent business seems more important than chatting with Battler, replacing Ronove’s recognition that he has chatted too much.
sourceReading: It seems he has indulged in a little too much conversation with Battler.

units.text: "My, my, what kind of urgent business could it be?  ......It does seem to be slightly more important than chatting with Battler-sama. Well then, Battler-sama, if you will excuse me.  Please continue to enjoy your game with Milady."
units.note: Both editions restore Ronove’s recognition that he chatted too long rather than saying the urgent business is more important than chatting.
units.japanese: 「はて。至急のどのような御用やら。……少々、戦人さまとのお喋りが過ぎたようですね。

description: WH says the blade is sticking into the back of Battler’s hand between his fingers, losing the hairbreadth clearance and implying penetration.
sourceReading: The razor-like blades have been driven in within a hair’s breadth of his hand and the spaces between his fingers.

units.text: The tips of those sharp nails were like blades with a red manicure. ......The spaces between the bases of my fingers hurt sharply. ......That razor-like blade was sticking sharply into the back of my hand between my fingers...
units.note: MG preserves the hairbreadth clearance between Lucifer’s blades and Battler’s hand. UP twice implies penetration or sticking into the hand/gaps, retaining the canonical spatial defect.
units.japanese: ……そのカミソリのような刃が、俺の手の甲と、指と指の間に紙一重で打ち込まれているのだ…。

units.text: The tips of those sharp nails were like blades with a red manicure. ......The spaces between the bases of my fingers prickled. ......Those razor‐like blades were sticking sharply into the back of my hand, and into the spaces between my fingers...
units.note: MG preserves the hairbreadth clearance between Lucifer’s blades and Battler’s hand. UP twice implies penetration or sticking into the hand/gaps, retaining the canonical spatial defect.
units.japanese: その鋭い爪の先端は、赤いマニキュアで彩られた刀身のよう。……指と指の付け根の間が、チリリと痛む。……そのカミソリのような刃が、俺の手の甲と、指と指の間に紙一重で打ち込まれているのだ…。

description: WH says the blades did not even cause his hand to shake, replacing his inability to move it for fear of the blades.
sourceReading: With those three blades there, he cannot so much as let his carelessly extended right hand tremble; only cold sweat escapes.

units.text: By now, those three blades didn't even cause that right hand which I had carelessly outstretched to shake, and only resulted in a single line of cold sweat dripping down.
units.note: Both editions restore Battler being unable or not permitted to move his hand for fear of the blades.
units.japanese: その三本の刃に、迂闊な俺の右手は震わせることもできず、今頃になって、冷たい汗を一筋零すしかない。

description: WH has Battler promise to keep saying the same line whenever Lucifer knocks him down, reversing his proposed retaliation and replacing someday with no matter when.
sourceReading: Someday he will push her down and say the same line to her.

units.text: "......You bitch.  No matter when you knock me down, I'll keep saying the same line."
units.note: Both editions restore Battler promising someday to push Lucifer down and repeat her line, rather than continually repeating it whenever she knocks him down.
units.japanese: 「………クソッタレ。いつか押し倒して同じセリフを言ってやるぜ。」

description: Krauss nii-san becomes Krauss-san while the brother and sister forms remain for Rudolf and Eva.
sourceReading: She names all three siblings with their familial older-sibling addresses.

units.text: Mother scolded me horribly, saying that my name was a disgrace to the Ushiromiya family. ......Of course, I was doing the best I could. But I had none of Krauss-san's dignity, I couldn't get excellent grades like Eva nee-san, and I had no leadership like Rudolf nii-san. ...I never stood out, didn't particularly excel at anything, and it was almost like I was asking myself why I had been born into the Ushiromiya family.
units.note: Both editions preserve Krauss nii-san consistently with Eva nee-san and Rudolf nii-san.
units.japanese: でも、蔵臼兄さんのような貫禄は全然なかったし、絵羽姉さんのような立派な成績はとても取れなかったし、留弗夫兄さんのようなリーダーシップがあったわけでもない。

description: WH makes running away from home and passive suicide alternatives, with or maybe.
sourceReading: In a sense her flight was both running away from home and a passive form of suicide.

units.text: Even though I say run away, there was no way I could have left Rokkenjima and gone somewhere else. But, anyway, I wanted to run away from the mansion and the way I was at the time. ......In a way, it was like running away from home, or maybe a half-hearted suicide...
units.note: Both editions retain the false alternative “or maybe” between running away and passive suicide. UP additionally changes passive suicide into half-hearted suicide, recorded separately above.
units.japanese: ……ある意味それは、家出でもあり、消極的な自殺でもあった…。

units.text: Though I say "run away", there was no way I could've left Rokkenjima and gone somewhere else. But, anyway, I wanted to run away from the mansion and my own self at that time. ...In a way, it was like a kid running away from home, or maybe a passive sort of suicide...
units.note: Both editions retain the false alternative “or maybe” between running away and passive suicide. UP additionally changes passive suicide into half-hearted suicide, recorded separately above.
units.japanese: 逃げ出すと言っても、六軒島を出てどこかへ行けるはずもない。でも、とにかくお屋敷と今の自分から逃げ出したかった。……ある意味それは、家出でもあり、消極的な自殺でもあった…。

units.text: Even though I say run away, there was no way I could have left Rokkenjima and gone somewhere else. But, anyway, I wanted to run away from the mansion and the way I was at the time. ......In a way, it was like running away from home, or maybe a half‐hearted suicide...
units.note: Both editions retain the false alternative “or maybe” between running away and passive suicide. UP additionally changes passive suicide into half-hearted suicide, recorded separately above.
units.japanese: 逃げ出すと言っても、六軒島を出てどこかへ行けるはずもない。でも、とにかくお屋敷と今の自分から逃げ出したかった。……ある意味それは、家出でもあり、消極的な自殺でもあった…。

description: WH links escaping the family, getting lost and worrying them as a combined sequence ending in revenge.
sourceReading: She thought going deep into the forest would let her escape the family, or that getting lost and worrying them would let her retaliate.

units.text: "......I wanted to disappear.  Or maybe it was that child-like form of resistance where I tried to make my parents worry by disappearing............I thought childishly that if I went into the center of the forest, escaped from the Ushiromiya house, and maybe became lost, then I would make them worry and be able to get back at them."
units.note: MG links escaping the family, becoming lost, worrying the parents, and revenge into one combined sequence. UP restores the alternatives.
units.japanese: 「……いなくなりたかったの。…あるいは、いなくなることによって親を心配させたいという、子どもなりの反抗だったのかも…。………私は、森のはるか奥に行けば、右代宮の家から逃れられる、あるいは迷子になって心配させることで仕返しができると、子どもながらに思ったの。」

units.text: ......I childishly thought that if I went into the center of the forest, escaped from the Ushiromiya house, and maybe became lost, then I'd make them worry and teach them a lesson."
units.note: MG links escaping the family, becoming lost, worrying the parents, and revenge into one combined sequence. UP restores the alternatives.
units.japanese: 「………私は、森のはるか奥に行けば、右代宮の家から逃れられる、あるいは迷子になって心配させることで仕返しができると、子どもながらに思ったの」

description: WH describes the mansion surroundings as prepared to be developed, adding a future development stage.
sourceReading: Only the ground around the mansion has been levelled or cleared; the rest is undeveloped.

units.text: "On Rokkenjima, only the land around the mansion has been prepared to be developed.  ...The rest is completely uncultivated, and it would probably take a considerable effort to survey the entire island."
units.note: Both editions say the land around the mansion was made ready for development rather than simply leveled or cleared.
units.japanese: 「六軒島は、この屋敷の周りが整地されているだけに過ぎねぇ。…他は完全に未開で、全島測量は、相当の手間が掛かるだろうな。」

units.text: "On Rokkenjima, only the land around the mansion is ready to be developed on. ...The rest is completely uncultivated, and it'd probably take a lot of work to survey the entire island."
units.note: Both editions say the land around the mansion was made ready for development rather than simply leveled or cleared.
units.japanese: 「六軒島は、この屋敷の周りが整地されているだけに過ぎねぇ。…他は完全に未開で、全島測量は、相当の手間が掛かるだろうな」

units.text: "The only part of Rokkenjima that got made ready for development is the area around the mansion. ...The rest is completely uncultivated, and it would probably take considerable effort to survey the entire island."
units.note: Both editions say the land around the mansion was made ready for development rather than simply leveled or cleared.
units.japanese: 「六軒島は、この屋敷の周りが整地されているだけに過ぎねぇ。…他は完全に未開で、全島測量は、相当の手間が掛かるだろうな」

description: WH substitutes running for her continued walking.
sourceReading: She kept walking blindly and randomly, on and on.

units.text: Blindly, randomly, I kept running, on and on. Suddenly, it felt like I had come across something like an animal trail. I was very tired, and had no idea how far I had walked, so at that time, I naturally took the easiest path to walk on.
units.note: Both editions replace Rosa’s continued walking with running.
units.japanese: 闇雲に、でたらめに、どこまでも歩き続けたわ。

units.text: Blindly, randomly, I kept running, on and on. Suddenly, I came across something I thought was an animal trail. I was very tired and had no idea how far I'd walked, so at that time, I naturally took the easiest path.
units.note: Both editions replace Rosa’s continued walking with running.
units.japanese: 闇雲に、でたらめに、どこまでも歩き続けたわ。突然、獣道のようなものに出た気がしたの。どれだけ歩いたかわからず、とても疲れていたから、その頃には自然と歩きやすい方へ向かうようになっていたわ。

units.text: Blindly, randomly, I kept running, on and on. Suddenly, it felt like I had come across something like an animal trail. I had no idea how far I'd walked, and I was very tired, so by then, I was just naturally taking the easiest path to walk on.
units.note: Both editions replace Rosa’s continued walking with running.
units.japanese: 闇雲に、でたらめに、どこまでも歩き続けたわ。突然、獣道のようなものに出た気がしたの。どれだけ歩いたかわからず、とても疲れていたから、その頃には自然と歩きやすい方へ向かうようになっていたわ。

description: WH says Rosa spun around for an instant before thinking she had returned.
sourceReading: For a moment she thought she might have made a circuit and returned to the original mansion.

units.text: As I did, .........suddenly, right before my eyes, a very, very tall fence appeared. It was a fence wonderfully adorned in a gothic style. For an instant, I spun around, thinking that I might have returned to the original mansion. Of course, there were fences around the mansion to stop us from entering the forest. But this fence was decorated differently, ......and moreover, it was very tall. It probably reached a full two stories up.
units.note: MG restores that Rosa thought she had gotten turned around. UP retains her physically spinning around.
units.japanese: 私は一瞬、ぐるりと回って、元のお屋敷に戻ってきてしまったのではないかと思ったわ。

units.text: As I did, .........suddenly, right before my eyes, a very, very tall fence appeared. It was a fence wonderfully adorned in a gothic style. For an instant, I spun around, thinking that I might have returned to the original mansion. Of course, there were fences around the mansion to stop us from entering the forest. But this fence was decorated differently, ......and most of all, it was very tall.
units.note: MG restores that Rosa thought she had gotten turned around. UP retains her physically spinning around.
units.japanese: すると、………突然、目の前に、とてもとても高い柵が現れたの。それはゴシック調の素敵な装飾のされた柵。私は一瞬、ぐるりと回って、元のお屋敷に戻ってきてしまったのではないかと思ったわ。確かに、私たちが森へ入らないように、お屋敷でも柵はあった。でも、それとは装飾が違う柵だったし、……何より、とても高かったの。

description: WH makes both alternatives explanations of an impression and attributes difficult walking to her child’s legs.
sourceReading: The fence may really have enclosed a vast area, or she may merely have had that impression because she was a child and the forest was difficult to walk through.

units.text: But it wasn't that easy. The fence had a length to match its height, and no matter how far I went, I didn't reach a corner. It probably gave me the impression that it encircled a very massive area, ...or maybe it was because my child's legs made it difficult to walk in the forest.
units.note: Both editions restore the first alternative as an actually vast enclosed area, but still attribute the walking difficulty directly to Rosa’s child legs rather than the forest and her child pace jointly creating that impression.
units.japanese: 相当広大な範囲を囲んでいたのかもしれないし、…あるいは子どもの足だし、森は歩きにくかったからそういう印象を持ったのかもしれないわ。

units.text: But it wasn't that easy. The fence had an incredible length to match its incredible height, and no matter how far I went, I didn't reach a corner. It might have encircled a massive area, ...or maybe I just had that impression because my child's legs made it difficult to walk in the forest.
units.note: Both editions restore the first alternative as an actually vast enclosed area, but still attribute the walking difficulty directly to Rosa’s child legs rather than the forest and her child pace jointly creating that impression.
units.japanese: でも、そう簡単には行かなかった。その柵は高さに負けないくらい、とてもとても長くて、いつまで経っても角を迎えなかった。相当広大な範囲を囲んでいたのかもしれないし、…あるいは子どもの足だし、森は歩きにくかったからそういう印象を持ったのかもしれないわ。

units.text: But it wasn't that easy. The fence had a length to match its height, and no matter how far I went, I didn't reach a corner. It might have been enclosing a very massive area, ...or maybe it just felt that way because my child's legs made it difficult to walk in the forest.
units.note: Both editions restore the first alternative as an actually vast enclosed area, but still attribute the walking difficulty directly to Rosa’s child legs rather than the forest and her child pace jointly creating that impression.
units.japanese: でも、そう簡単には行かなかった。その柵は高さに負けないくらい、とてもとても長くて、いつまで経っても角を迎えなかった。相当広大な範囲を囲んでいたのかもしれないし、…あるいは子どもの足だし、森は歩きにくかったからそういう印象を持ったのかもしれないわ。

description: WH uses she had addressed to him without using honorifics, leaving addressed without its required direct object.
sourceReading: She addressed her formidable father without an honorific.

units.text: I was only a little surprised. ...After all, Father was a great man feared by everyone. And she had addressed to him without using honorifics. So she quickly became frightening. ...After all, if she could refer to my fearsome father that way, she must have been a witch with incredible power.
units.note: Both editions repair WH’s ungrammatical “addressed to him,” using grammatical descriptions of referring to Kinzo without honorifics.
units.japanese: そのお父様を、呼びつけにしたのだから。
candidates: addressed to him without using honorifics

description: WH omits tea from drinking together and adds usually to arranged visits.
sourceReading: Every few days Kinzo visited, on some arranged days and some unexpected ones, to drink tea or walk together.

units.text: "Yes.  Once every few days, usually on an arranged day but sometimes suddenly, Father would appear casually, and they would drink together, or take a walk together or something.  She said that, by coincidence, she was by herself on the day I visited."
units.note: MG retains both “usually on an arranged day” and nonspecific “drink together.” UP restores unweighted arranged/unexpected visits and tea.
units.japanese: 「えぇ。何日かに一度、約束されている日もあれば、突然の日もあったそうだけど、ふらりとお父様が訪れては、一緒にお茶を飲んだり、散歩したりしたんですって。私が訪れたその日は、たまたま彼女ひとりだったと言っていたわ。」

units.text: "Yes. Once every few days, usually on an arranged day but sometimes suddenly, Father would casually appear and they'd drink together, or else take a walk together or something. She said she just happened to be alone on the day I visited."
units.note: MG retains both “usually on an arranged day” and nonspecific “drink together.” UP restores unweighted arranged/unexpected visits and tea.
units.japanese: 「えぇ。何日かに一度、約束されている日もあれば、突然の日もあったそうだけど、ふらりとお父様が訪れては、一緒にお茶を飲んだり、散歩したりしたんですって。私が訪れたその日は、たまたま彼女ひとりだったと言っていたわ」

description: WH says we can be sure instead of presenting Natsuhi’s personal conviction that there was no indecent relationship.
sourceReading: Natsuhi is convinced their contact had no improper sexual meaning.

units.text: "......We can be sure that it was not an indecent relationship."
units.note: MG retains collective “We can be sure.” UP restores Natsuhi’s explicitly personal conviction.
units.japanese: 「……如何わしい意味での交流はなかったと確信しています。」

units.text: "...We can be sure this was no indecent relationship."
units.note: MG retains collective “We can be sure.” UP restores Natsuhi’s explicitly personal conviction.
units.japanese: 「……如何わしい意味での交流はなかったと確信しています」

description: WH makes Rosa judge whether she could solve the trouble by talking to Beatrice.
sourceReading: Rosa senses that Beatrice feels telling Rosa her troubles would solve nothing, and is saddened by that atmosphere.

units.text: "There was definitely something she was worried about.  ......I remember that when I noticed that it didn't seem like something I could resolve just by talking to her, I was also really sad.
units.note: Both editions continue to make Rosa assess whether she could solve the problem by talking to Beatrice, rather than sensing Beatrice’s belief that disclosure to Rosa would solve nothing.
units.japanese: 「彼女はきっと何か悩みがあった。……それを私に話したところで何の解決にもならない、というような雰囲気が読み取れて、私もとても悲しかったのを覚えてる。

units.text: "She was definitely worried about something. ...I remember feeling really sad myself, when I realized it wasn't something I could do anything about by talking to her."
units.note: Both editions continue to make Rosa assess whether she could solve the problem by talking to Beatrice, rather than sensing Beatrice’s belief that disclosure to Rosa would solve nothing.
units.japanese: 「彼女はきっと何か悩みがあった。……それを私に話したところで何の解決にもならない、というような雰囲気が読み取れて、私もとても悲しかったのを覚えてる」

units.text: "There was definitely something on her mind. ......I remember getting the impression that it wasn't something that I could resolve just by talking to her, and feeling very sad about it as well."
units.note: Both editions continue to make Rosa assess whether she could solve the problem by talking to Beatrice, rather than sensing Beatrice’s belief that disclosure to Rosa would solve nothing.
units.japanese: 「彼女はきっと何か悩みがあった。……それを私に話したところで何の解決にもならない、というような雰囲気が読み取れて、私もとても悲しかったのを覚えてる」

description: WH replaces the incongruity of a forest witch fearing wolves with a hedge that she might have been a witch.
sourceReading: For someone of the stature of the forest witch, she oddly seems frightened of wolves.

units.text: This person who might have been a witch, was for some reason scared of and didn't like wolves. I remember it looked pretty comical.
units.note: Both editions restore the incongruity of the forest witch herself fearing wolves without changing it into uncertainty over whether she was a witch.
units.japanese: 森の魔女ともあろうものが、どういうわけか狼は怖くて苦手みたいだった。

description: WH substitutes gate for fence in Rosa’s invitation.
sourceReading: She invites Beatrice to go beyond the fence.

units.text: "Do you want to try, ......going outside the gate?"
units.note: Both editions correctly invite Beatrice beyond the fence and then distinguish the closed gate from Rosa’s gap through the fence.
units.japanese: 「柵の外へ、

description: WH moves the extraordinary degree from the required courage to the first step, calling the step unspeakable.
sourceReading: The first step into an unknown outside world must have required courage beyond imagining.

units.text: She was starting to realize that she couldn't stay there forever. She was starting to realize that she had to go outside sometime. But, since she didn't know about the outside world, she must have needed the courage to take that unspeakable first step outside...
units.note: MG retains “unspeakable first step,” moving the extraordinary degree away from the courage. UP restores an unimaginable amount of courage.
units.japanese: でも、外の世界のことを知らない彼女にとって、外へ踏み出す第一歩は想像を絶する勇気が必要だったに違いない…。

units.text: She was starting to realize that she couldn't stay there forever. She was starting to realize that she had to go outside someday. But, since she didn't know about the outside world, she must have needed courage to take that unspeakable first step outside...
units.note: MG retains “unspeakable first step,” moving the extraordinary degree away from the courage. UP restores an unimaginable amount of courage.
units.japanese: 彼女は、いつまでもここにいてはいけないと気付き始めていた。いつかは外へ出なくてはならないと気付き始めていた。でも、外の世界のことを知らない彼女にとって、外へ踏み出す第一歩は想像を絶する勇気が必要だったに違いない…。

description: WH says she had surely been born with the resolution to leave, reversing the first-time decision into an innate determination.
sourceReading: She voices a decision to go outside that she has probably made for the first time in her life.

units.text: And she had therefore resolved herself. She put that resolution to go outside into words, that resolution which she had surely been born with.
units.note: Both editions correctly present this as probably Beatrice’s first such decision in her life, rather than a resolution possessed from birth.
units.japanese: 外へ出たいと、きっと生まれて初めてに違いない決意を、口にしたのだ。

description: WH calls the soft smile farsightedness instead of a composed or detached understanding reached after resolving to depart.
sourceReading: Rosa wonders whether her smile reflects the serenity of having made up her mind to leave the cage.

units.text: I was just a little surprised when she finally showed me a very soft smile. Could that have been, ...a farsightedness caused by her determination to venture out from her cage? That soft smile which I wouldn't have imagined could have come out of that dark face...
units.note: MG retains “farsightedness.” UP renders 達観 as inner peace arising from her readiness to leave, preserving the composed emotional state.
units.japanese: それはひょっとすると、…篭より旅立つ覚悟ができたからこその、達観なのか。

units.text: I was just a little surprised when she finally gave me a gentle smile. Could that have been... a farsightedness brought about by her decision to venture out from her cage? It was a smile so gentle, I couldn't imagine that it had come from that once dark face...
units.note: MG retains “farsightedness.” UP renders 達観 as inner peace arising from her readiness to leave, preserving the composed emotional state.
units.japanese: 彼女が、ようやく、とてもやわらかい笑顔を見せてくれたので、ちょっぴりだけ驚いてしまった。それはひょっとすると、…篭より旅立つ覚悟ができたからこその、達観なのか。それまでの暗い顔からは想像もつかないくらい、やわらかい笑顔だった…。

description: WH describes Rosa as growing impatient when she realizes the danger of darkness.
sourceReading: She becomes anxious or flustered at the prospect of being caught in the forest after dark.

units.text: There were no lights in the forest, and I hadn't brought a flashlight. I realized that it would be terrible if it got dark while we were still like this, and grew impatient.
units.note: Both editions describe Rosa as growing impatient, retaining WH’s emotional shift from anxious or flustered urgency.
units.japanese: このまま暗くなったら大変なことになるだろうと気付き、焦ったわ。

units.text: There were no lights in the forest, and I hadn't brought a flashlight. I realized it would be terrible if it got dark while we were still like this...and grew impatient.
units.note: Both editions describe Rosa as growing impatient, retaining WH’s emotional shift from anxious or flustered urgency.
units.japanese:
森の中には灯りはないし、懐中電灯だって持っていない。
このまま暗くなったら大変なことになるだろうと気付き、焦ったわ。

units.text:
There were no lights in the forest, and I hadn't brought a flashlight.
I realized that it would be terrible if it got dark while we were still like this, and grew impatient.
units.note: Both editions describe Rosa as growing impatient, retaining WH’s emotional shift from anxious or flustered urgency.
units.japanese:
森の中には灯りはないし、懐中電灯だって持っていない。
このまま暗くなったら大変なことになるだろうと気付き、焦ったわ。

description: WH denies a reason to complain, rather than expressing that she cannot afford to complain while responsible for Beatrice.
sourceReading: She cannot sit there whining; she must guide the trusting woman out.

units.text: I already had no clue which trail I had come by, and was completely lost... At this rate, without even knowing where to walk, night would definitely fall. But there was no reason to complain. Because that woman following behind me was so innocent and having so much fun.  ...Therefore, I definitely had to guide the way through this forest, for her smile as well.
units.note: MG uses “no time to cry” and UP “didn’t have the luxury to complain”; both preserve inability to indulge distress while responsible for Beatrice.
units.japanese: でも、泣き言なんて言っていられない。

description: WH says Rosa thought there was no other way, replacing her consideration of whether there was another plan because the proposed descent looked dangerous.
sourceReading: She proposes descending but, because it looks dangerous, wonders whether another plan is possible.

units.text: So I planned to somehow go down the rocky cliff. ...It looked pretty dangerous, but I thought there was no other way. However, Beatrice agreed with my plan without any doubts. ......Even though she was probably older than me, ...she meekly obeyed me, almost as though she were some kind of chick who believed I was a mother bird.
units.note: MG retains the conclusion that there was no other way. UP restores Rosa’s open question about whether another route exists.
units.japanese: …一応、危なそうだったし、他に案はないかと思って。
candidates: thought there was no other way

units.text: So, I suggested that we go down that rocky cliff somehow. ...It looked pretty dangerous, but I figured there was no other way. However, Beatrice agreed to my plan without any doubts. ...Even though she was probably older than me, ...she meekly obeyed, almost as though she were some kind of chick who thought I was her mother.
units.note: MG retains the conclusion that there was no other way. UP restores Rosa’s open question about whether another route exists.
units.japanese:
だから、何とかして岩壁を降りようと提案したの。
…一応、危なそうだったし、他に案はないかと思って。でも、ベアトリーチェは私の提案に何の疑いもなく頷いた。……歳は向こうの方が上だろうに、…まるで私を親鳥だと信じるアヒルか何かの雛のように、本当に素直に従ったわ。

description: WH asks whether Rosa just said aquariums have fish, instead of noticing that none of the examples discussed has turned out to be a fish.
sourceReading: Despite being an aquarium, no fish has appeared in their discussion so far.

units.text: "What's this?  Didn't you just say that there were fish in aquariums?"
units.note: MG restores the joke that none of the creatures discussed has been a fish. UP retains a challenge to Rosa’s supposed prior statement about fish in aquariums.
units.japanese: 「何だ。水族館なのに、さっきから魚が出てこんぞ？」

units.text: "What's this? Didn't you say that there were fish in aquariums?"
units.note: MG restores the joke that none of the creatures discussed has been a fish. UP retains a challenge to Rosa’s supposed prior statement about fish in aquariums.
units.japanese: 「何だ。水族館なのに、さっきから魚が出てこんぞ？」

description: WH introduces as she tried to ask me and presents the sound as simply funny, replacing the conditional listening perspective.
sourceReading: She suddenly lets out a short startled sound that might sound comical depending on how one hears it; Rosa then thinks it may have been a scream.

units.text: As she tried to ask me, she spoke in a funny, ...rushed and short voice, ...no, it was probably a scream. That voice rose suddenly. ......Her body separated from the cliff, and gently fell down.
units.note: Both editions restore the conditional listening perspective on whether Beatrice’s abrupt cry might sound funny and remove the invented attempt to ask a question.
units.japanese: 彼女が聞きようによっては滑稽な、

description: WH has Battler propose that Beatrice was pretending to be dead, adding voluntary deception to the possible survival state.
sourceReading: He proposes she was alive in a state of apparent death or something similar and that Rosa mistakenly judged her dead.

units.text: Don't mess with me, that can't be...!  Rosa oba-san was a kid, so she was rushed.  It's not like there was a doctor.  She probably made a mistake, thinking you were dead, and you probably, umm, ......were alive and pretending to be dead or something.  Isn't that right?!"
units.note: MG retains voluntary pretending or playing dead. UP consistently restores a state of apparent death without deliberate performance.
units.japanese: ふざけるな、そんなわけはない…！　楼座叔母さんは子どもだったし焦ってた。医者がいたわけでもない。多分、死んだと誤解しただけで、お前は多分その、……仮死状態か何かで生きていたんだ。そうだろッ？！」

units.text: "Don't mess with me, that's impossible...! Aunt Rosa was a kid, and she was panicked. And it's not like a doctor was there. She probably just mistakenly thought you were dead, and you were probably...umm...alive and pretending to be dead or something. Isn't that right?!"
units.note: MG retains voluntary pretending or playing dead. UP consistently restores a state of apparent death without deliberate performance.
units.japanese: 「ふざけるな、そんなわけはない…！　楼座叔母さんは子どもだったし焦ってた。医者がいたわけでもない。多分、死んだと誤解しただけで、お前は多分その、……仮死状態か何かで生きていたんだ。そうだろッ？！」

description: WH calls Beatrice’s ensuing account witch girl tricks instead of witch-girl talk.
sourceReading: Battler dismissively permits her to indulge in witch talk, which he will listen to as a tea-cake substitute.

units.text: "............I don't have a clue anymore.  ......Keep having fun with your witch girl tricks.  I'll listen instead of eating tea cakes!  What the, it's empty.  Hey, could I get some more black tea?"
units.note: MG retains “witch girl tricks.” UP restores “witch-girl talk,” matching Battler’s invitation to continue speaking.
units.japanese: 「……………もう、さっぱりだぜ。……好きなだけ魔女っ子トークに興じろよ。

units.text: "......I don't have a clue anymore. ...Keep having fun with your witch girl tricks. I'll listen to that in place of a snack! What the...it's empty. Hey, could I get some more black tea?"
units.note: MG retains “witch girl tricks.” UP restores “witch-girl talk,” matching Battler’s invitation to continue speaking.
units.japanese: 「……………もう、さっぱりだぜ。……好きなだけ魔女っ子トークに興じろよ。茶菓の代わりに聞いてやらぁ！　何だ、空っぽか。おい、紅茶のお代わりを頼むぜ」

description: WH says he has more than enough tea cakes rather than expecting the metaphorical tea cakes to be substantial.
sourceReading: He expects the story serving as tea cakes to be substantial, so half a cup will do.

units.text: "Well, I've got more than enough tea cakes.  Half will be fine."
units.note: MG retains an already abundant supply of snacks. UP removes snacks but still says he already has “more than enough to go with it,” rather than predicting the coming story will be substantial.
units.japanese: 「どうせ茶菓がボリューム満点だろうからよ。半分でいいぜ。」

units.text: "Well, I've got more than enough snacks. Half will be fine."
units.note: MG retains an already abundant supply of snacks. UP removes snacks but still says he already has “more than enough to go with it,” rather than predicting the coming story will be substantial.
units.japanese: 「どうせ茶菓がボリューム満点だろうからよ。半分でいいぜ」

units.text: "Well, I've got more than enough to go with it. Half will be fine."
