units.note: MG retains an already abundant supply of snacks. UP removes snacks but still says he already has “more than enough to go with it,” rather than predicting the coming story will be substantial.
units.japanese: 「どうせ茶菓がボリューム満点だろうからよ。半分でいいぜ」

description: WH uses brought myself together for the recovery of self after the body’s death.
sourceReading: Through being able to die accidentally, she has finally regained herself, including her witch memories and identity.

units.text: While I had been imprisoned in a cage of flesh, I had completely lost my memory as a witch. However, thanks to Rosa, if you could say that... Thanks to my accidental death, I had now finally brought myself together......
units.note: MG restores that Beatrice regained herself. UP retains “brought myself together,” suggesting composure rather than recovered identity.
units.japanese: 事故で死ねたお陰で、妾は今、ようやく自らを取り戻したのだ……。

units.text: While I had been imprisoned in a cage of flesh, I had completely lost my memory as a witch. However, thanks to Rosa, if you could say that... Thanks to my accidental but fortunate death, I had now finally brought myself together......
units.note: MG restores that Beatrice regained herself. UP retains “brought myself together,” suggesting composure rather than recovered identity.
units.japanese: 肉の檻に囚われている間、妾の魔女としての記憶は完全に失われていた。しかし、楼座のお陰で、とでも言うべきか。事故で死ねたお陰で、妾は今、ようやく自らを取り戻したのだ……。

description: WH makes Kinzo repay what he borrowed instead of Beatrice planning to repay him for his treatment of her.
sourceReading: She considers how to pay Kinzo back for everything he has done to her.

units.text: And to escape even a little from the light of the sun, I rode the wind and lightly passed over the cliff. It would probably be somewhat cool in the forest. Anyway, I'll take some time to recuperate, and regain my original power. ......As I think of how Kinzo will repay all that he has borrowed.
units.note: Both editions restore Beatrice’s retaliatory agency: MG makes Kinzo pay, while UP has her pay Kinzo back for what he did.
units.japanese: ……これまでの借りを、金蔵にどう返してやるかを思案しながら。

description: WH describes Kinzo as not dismayed instead of not merely sitting by while she escaped.
sourceReading: Kinzo did not sit idly by, though a capture method could not be prepared immediately.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*.  When I turned into butterflies and slipped into the forest, it was already no longer possible for Kinzo to find me.  ......However, Kinzo was not dismayed.  Still, he was unable to immediately prepare a way to catch me.
units.note: MG retains “not dismayed.” UP restores that Kinzo did not stand by doing nothing.
units.japanese: ……だが、金蔵も指をくわえているわけではなかった。しかし、妾を捕らえる方法はすぐに用意は出来ぬ。

units.text: "*cackle*cackle* When I turned into butterflies and slipped into the forest, it was already no longer possible for Kinzo to find me. ...However, Kinzo was not dismayed. Still, he was not immediately able to prepare a way to catch me."
units.note: MG retains “not dismayed.” UP restores that Kinzo did not stand by doing nothing.
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっく。蝶に姿を変え、森に紛れた妾を探し出すことなど、もはや金蔵には不可能なこと。……だが、金蔵も指をくわえているわけではなかった。しかし、妾を捕らえる方法はすぐに用意は出来ぬ」

description: WH changes intended soup-drinking into inability to drink it.
sourceReading: Giving chopsticks rather than a spoon for soup she wants or is about to drink illustrates being given an unfamiliar tool.

units.text: If it was Western magic, I would have some knowledge.  For any barrier, there would have been some measures I could have taken.  But Eastern magic is outside my area of expertise.  It was as if I had been given chopsticks instead of a spoon for some soup that I couldn't drink."
units.note: MG restores soup Beatrice wants to drink. UP restores intention but introduces a separate drink-to-eat change recorded as a paired defect.
units.japanese: 妾も、西洋魔術であれば心得がある。どのような結界であっても、何かの手が打てたであろう。しかし東洋魔術は専門外よ。妾が飲まんとするスープに対し、スプーンではなく箸を与えられたようなものだ。」

description: WH says even if she had one thousand days to regain power, instead of saying recovery would already have taken that long without the added impediment.
sourceReading: A recovery already expected to require a thousand days now had to take much longer under Eastern magic.

units.text: In a space strongly controlled by Eastern magic, Western magic loses much of its power.  Even if she had one thousand days to regain her power, she would have to wait many, many more."
units.note: MG retains the hypothetical allowance as “Even if she were given one thousand days.” UP restores a thousand-day normal estimate made longer by the barrier.
units.japanese: 「東洋魔術が強く支配する空間では、西洋魔術はひどく力を失います。ただでさえ千日は掛けたであろう力を取り戻す時間を、さらにさらに長く掛けねばならなかったのです。」

units.text: "In a space dominated by Eastern magic, Western magic loses much of its power. Even if she were given one thousand days to regain her strength, she would have to wait many, many more."
units.note: MG retains the hypothetical allowance as “Even if she were given one thousand days.” UP restores a thousand-day normal estimate made longer by the barrier.
units.japanese: 「東洋魔術が強く支配する空間では、西洋魔術はひどく力を失います。ただでさえ千日は掛けたであろう力を取り戻す時間を、さらにさらに長く掛けねばならなかったのです」

description: WH writes fourth through eight twilights, using a cardinal where the endpoint requires eighth.
sourceReading: Five sacrifices span the fourth through eighth twilights.

units.text: "That was the witch's epitaph.  It is a song of sacrifices.  ......Six people at the first twilight.  Two people at the second twilight.  And then five more people on the fourth through eight twilights.  A forbidden ceremony, involving the offering of a total of 13 people as sacrifices...  Those sacrifices were to be chosen randomly, and the one who held the ceremony, Kinzo himself, was not an exception."
units.note: MG retains “fourth through eight twilights.” UP restores the ordinal endpoint “eighth.”
units.japanese:
……第一の晩に６人。
第二の晩に２人。
そして第四の晩から第八の晩にかけて５人。
合計１３人の生贄を捧げる、禁じられた儀式…。
その生贄はランダムに決められ、儀式を執り行う金蔵自身も例外にはなりません」

units.text: "That is the witch's epitaph. A song of sacrifices. ...Six people on the first twilight. Two people on the second. And then five more people on the fourth through eight twilights. A forbidden ceremony, involving the offering of a total of 13 people as sacrifices... Those sacrifices were to be chosen randomly, and the one who held the ceremony, Kinzo himself, was no exception."
units.note: MG retains “fourth through eight twilights.” UP restores the ordinal endpoint “eighth.”
units.japanese: 「それが、魔女の碑文。生贄の唄でございます。……第一の晩に６人。第二の晩に２人。そして第四の晩から第八の晩にかけて５人。合計１３人の生贄を捧げる、禁じられた儀式…。その生贄はランダムに決められ、儀式を執り行う金蔵自身も例外にはなりません」

description: WH says the exceptional decades might settle the debt, replacing her possible indebtedness to Kinzo for relief from boredom.
sourceReading: Taking that relief into account, she may owe Kinzo something.

units.text: ......I had been horribly stabbed in the back by Kinzo, but it was an exceptional time, even amid the thousand years that have passed until now.  After all, boredom is my natural enemy.  To Kinzo, who offered me a chance to run away from that for several decades, yes, if you include that, it might settle the debt.
units.note: Both editions preserve Beatrice’s possible indebtedness to Kinzo for relieving her boredom rather than saying the experience settled a debt.
units.japanese: ……金蔵にはさんざん煮え湯を飲まされたが、今となってはこの千年でも稀な時間だった。何しろ、魔女の天敵は退屈よ。それから逃れることのできる数十年間を提供した金蔵には、なるほど、それも含めて借りがあるやも知れぬ。

description: WH says Battler is doubting one of the eighteen and perhaps castling, instead of naming suspicion as the last escape available to him.
sourceReading: Reluctantly suspecting one of the eighteen will be his final escape, his castling move.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*!  Perhaps you are castling.  Though reluctantly, you are doubting one of the 18 people as your last way out.
units.note: MG prematurely says Battler is already doubting one of the eighteen and perhaps castling. UP restores this as the last escape route available to him.
units.japanese: 「くっくっく！　そなたにとって、渋々とではあっても、１８人の誰かを疑うことが最後の逃げ道、キャスリングとなるであろうな。

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*! Perhaps you are castling. Though reluctantly, you are doubting one of the 18 people as your last way out.
units.note: MG prematurely says Battler is already doubting one of the eighteen and perhaps castling. UP restores this as the last escape route available to him.
units.japanese: 「くっくっく！　そなたにとって、渋々とではあっても、１８人の誰かを疑うことが最後の逃げ道、キャスリングとなるであろうな」

description: WH omits making Battler acknowledge Beatrice from the description of overcoming his eighteen pieces to reach checkmate.
sourceReading: Overcoming those eighteen possible culprits and making him acknowledge her is difficult.

units.text: ..........However, it will be difficult for me from here on.  If you throw away appearances, you could prepare a culprit freely amid 18 people!  Making you reach checkmate by evading those 18 pieces, .........will be truly difficult."
units.note: MG omits forcing Battler to acknowledge Beatrice from the checkmate condition. UP restores that explicit victory requirement.
units.japanese: ………しかし、妾はここからが難しいのだ。そなたは形振りさえ捨てれば、１８人もの人間を自在に犯人に仕立てあげられる！　その１８人の駒を潜り抜け、妾を認めさせチェックメイトに至るのは、

units.text: ......However, it will be difficult for me from here on out. If you choose to stop caring about propriety, you could prepare a culprit freely amid 18 people! Making you reach checkmate by evading those 18 pieces... ...will be truly difficult."
units.note: MG omits forcing Battler to acknowledge Beatrice from the checkmate condition. UP restores that explicit victory requirement.
units.japanese: 「………しかし、妾はここからが難しいのだ。そなたは形振りさえ捨てれば、１８人もの人間を自在に犯人に仕立てあげられる！　その１８人の駒を潜り抜け、妾を認めさせチェックメイトに至るのは、………実に難しいことよ」

description: WH replaces Beatrice’s offer to shoulder the blame with Were you trying to hide that from me?
sourceReading: If he does not want to suspect his beloved eighteen, she will take that blame upon herself; why reject her?

units.text: "It looks like you have finally reached the end of your battle with this third game, doesn't it?  There's nowhere to run anymore, right?  *cackle*cackle*!  You don't want to doubt any of those beloved people in the 18, do you?  Were you trying to hide that from me?  And yet, why do you refuse me?
units.note: MG retains a question about Battler hiding something from Beatrice. UP restores her offer to take the burden of accusing the eighteen from him.
units.japanese: 「三度に及んだそなたとのゲームも、いよいよ終盤戦のようではないか。もう逃げ場はないぞ？　くっくっく！　お前の大好きな１８人を疑いたくないだろぉ？　妾がそれを被ってやるぞ？　なのになぜ妾を拒むのか？

units.text: "It looks like we're finally approaching the end, in the third round of this game of ours. You've nowhere to run anymore, right? *cackle*cackle*! You don't want to suspect any of those beloved people in the 18, do you? Were you trying to hide that from me? Then why do you refuse me?"
units.note: MG retains a question about Battler hiding something from Beatrice. UP restores her offer to take the burden of accusing the eighteen from him.
units.japanese: 「三度に及んだそなたとのゲームも、いよいよ終盤戦のようではないか。もう逃げ場はないぞ？　くっくっく！　お前の大好きな１８人を疑いたくないだろぉ？　妾がそれを被ってやるぞ？　なのになぜ妾を拒むのか？」

description: WH says she knows his unskillful method of attack, reversing the direction of the tactical weakness.
sourceReading: She knows exactly what kind of attack he has trouble facing.

units.text: That should suit you, let's do that.  I now thoroughly know of your unskillful method of attack!  *cackle*cackle*cackle* hihihihihihihihihihi!!"
units.note: Both editions restore Beatrice’s knowledge of attack methods Battler cannot handle, rather than calling his own attacks unskillful.
units.japanese: そなたにはそれが似合うだろう、そうしよう。すでにそなたの苦手とする攻め方も知り抜いておるわ！　くっくくくくくっひひひひひひひひひひ！！」

description: WH says time began to count back again, suggesting reverse counting rather than restarting.
sourceReading: Having returned from twenty-four to zero, time starts counting anew.

units.text: On the antique clock with the intricate design that had been sitting on his desk, the two overlapping hands tilted to the right, and began to slide. The measure of time that counted to 24 had returned to 0, and had begun to count back again...
units.note: MG retains “count back again,” suggesting reverse counting. UP restores renewed counting, despite its separate redundant construction.
units.japanese: ２４を数えた時の刻みが０に戻り、再びそれを数え直していた…。

units.text: On the antique clock with the intricate design that had been sitting on his desk, the two overlapping hands tilted to the right and began to slide. The measure of time that counted up to 24...had returned to 0...and had begun to count back again...
units.note: MG retains “count back again,” suggesting reverse counting. UP restores renewed counting, despite its separate redundant construction.
units.japanese: 机の上に置かれた、凝った意匠の施されたアンティークの時計は、重なっていた２本の針を右に傾かせ、ずらし始めている。２４を数えた時の刻みが０に戻り、再びそれを数え直していた…。

description: WH says the higher existence became an oracle through the cards, rather than giving an oracle through them.
sourceReading: Disrespecting the result also disrespects the higher being that grants a revelation through tarot.

units.text: The most forbidden action in tarot reading was to try predicting the same thing twice. That was a desecration to the result of the fortune telling, and also desecrated the existence higher than humans which became an oracle through the tarot cards.
units.note: MG restores higher beings that give revelations. UP preserves the giver relation as a higher existence delivering signs, though its wording remains stiff.
units.japanese: それは占いの結果に対する冒涜であり、タロットを通じて神託を与えてくれる、人より上位の存在への冒涜ともなるのである。

description: WH uses the nonstandard past tense seeked.
sourceReading: He seeks an arithmetic miracle in a roulette of luck.

units.text: What the best result was depended on the definition, but if he demanded the best result in a strict sense, it was the same as a simple roulette of luck, where he seeked an arithmetic miracle. ......However, to Kinzo, who made miracles of numbers the basis of his magical power, this could become very much like a magic ritual.
units.note: MG retains the nonstandard past tense “seeked.” UP uses “sought.”
units.japanese: 最高の結果がどの程度のものかの定義にもよるが、厳密な意味での最高の結果を求めたなら、それは単なる算数的奇跡を求める運のルーレットと同じになる。

units.text: The mark he set for this "most favorable result" would vary, but when he demanded the most favorable result in a strictly literal sense, it was the same as a simple roulette of luck, where he seeked an arithmetic miracle. ...However, Kinzo used miracles of numbers as the basis of his magical power, so this functioned perfectly well as a magical ritual.
units.note: MG retains the nonstandard past tense “seeked.” UP uses “sought.”
units.japanese: 最高の結果がどの程度のものかの定義にもよるが、厳密な意味での最高の結果を求めたなら、それは単なる算数的奇跡を求める運のルーレットと同じになる。……しかし、数字の奇跡こそを魔力の根源とする金蔵にとって、それは充分、魔法の儀式となり得た。

description: WH says the procedure could become very much like a magic ritual rather than qualify as a magic ritual for Kinzo.
sourceReading: For Kinzo, whose magic is grounded in numerical miracles, it can fully constitute a magical ritual.

units.text: What the best result was depended on the definition, but if he demanded the best result in a strict sense, it was the same as a simple roulette of luck, where he seeked an arithmetic miracle. ......However, to Kinzo, who made miracles of numbers the basis of his magical power, this could become very much like a magic ritual.
units.note: MG says the procedure functioned as a magical ritual. UP retains that it merely became “like” one.
units.japanese: ……しかし、数字の奇跡こそを魔力の根源とする金蔵にとって、それは充分、魔法の儀式となり得た。
candidates: become very much like a magic ritual

units.text: It would depend on how he defined the result most favorable to him, but if he demanded the best result in a strict sense, it would be the same as a simple roulette of luck, where he sought an arithmetic miracle. ......However, to Kinzo, who made miracles of numbers the basis of his magical power, this could become very much like a magic ritual.
units.note: MG says the procedure functioned as a magical ritual. UP retains that it merely became “like” one.
units.japanese: 最高の結果がどの程度のものかの定義にもよるが、厳密な意味での最高の結果を求めたなら、それは単なる算数的奇跡を求める運のルーレットと同じになる。……しかし、数字の奇跡こそを魔力の根源とする金蔵にとって、それは充分、魔法の儀式となり得た。
candidates: become very much like a magic ritual

description: WH drops the rarity qualifier and says the bad cards should not appear.
sourceReading: Bad cards not expected to appear so readily recur and thwart his desired miracle.

units.text: Kinzo stopped his hands for a second. ...It seemed the result he expected wasn't showing up. On the contrary, many bad cards that shouldn't appear appeared repeatedly, and continued to interfere with the miracle Kinzo wished for.
units.note: Both editions preserve that the bad cards should not appear so often rather than saying they should never appear.
units.japanese: それどころか、そうそう出るはずのない悪いカードが繰り返し現れ、金蔵の求める奇跡を妨害し続けていた。

description: WH attaches different from normal to the oracle and duplicates that, losing the unusual flow as the circumstance from which he derives it.
sourceReading: From the unusual course of the readings, Kinzo seems to have received some revelation.

units.text: It seemed that Kinzo had received some oracle that that was different from normal. But judging by the unlucky cards scattered over the desk, it was difficult to imagine that the oracle had been a good sign...
units.note: MG still makes the revelation itself different from normal, while removing the doubled word. UP restores the abnormal course of readings as the basis for the sign.
units.japanese: 普段とは違う流れに、金蔵は何かの神託を得たらしい。

units.text: Kinzo seemed to have received some revelation that was different from normal. But, judging by the unlucky cards scattered across his desk, it was difficult to imagine that the omen had been a good one...
units.note: MG still makes the revelation itself different from normal, while removing the doubled word. UP restores the abnormal course of readings as the basis for the sign.
units.japanese: 普段とは違う流れに、金蔵は何かの神託を得たらしい。しかし、不吉なカードたちが机の上に散らばる様を見る限り、その神託が良き報せであるとは考え難かった…。

description: WH uses As she did. she heard, splitting a subordinate introductory clause from its main clause with a period.
sourceReading: At that point she hears approaching footsteps.

units.text: As she did. she heard the sound of footsteps splashing through puddles. Shannon immediately chased away the emotions welling up inside her.
units.note: Both editions repair the broken “As she did. she heard” construction.
units.japanese: そこへ、ばたばたと水溜りを踏み散らしながら駆けてくる足音を聞く。

description: WH says I have to go back soon in place of Shannon’s apology for not having returned promptly.
sourceReading: She apologizes for not coming back immediately, fearing reprimand for spending too long with George.

units.text: "......Genji-sama?  Kanon-kun too...!  I, I'm sorry, I have to go back soon, umm..."
units.note: MG retains a future need to return soon. UP restores Shannon’s apology for not returning promptly.
units.japanese: 「……源次さま？　嘉音くんも…！　す、すみません、すぐに戻らなくてその…、」

units.text: "...Genji-sama? And Kanon-kun too...! I-I'm sorry, I have to go back soon, umm..."
units.note: MG retains a future need to return soon. UP restores Shannon’s apology for not returning promptly.
units.japanese: 「……源次さま？　嘉音くんも…！　す、すみません、すぐに戻らなくてその…、」

description: WH invents a conditional convenience in carrying out the ceremony alone.
sourceReading: Kanon sarcastically calls Kinzo’s premonition convenient or self-serving, given that he initiated the ritual himself.

units.text: "He said he had a premonition of misfortune.  ......It would be convenient if he could carry out the ceremony by himself."
units.note: Both editions preserve Kanon’s sarcastic criticism that Kinzo initiated the ritual and now reports an ominous premonition.
units.japanese: 「不吉な予感がするってさ。……自分で儀式を起こしておいて、都合のいい話さ。」

description: WH reduces Kanon’s ability to suppress his presence to hiding footsteps.
sourceReading: Kanon is particularly constituted to conceal his presence, appearing and disappearing unnoticed.

units.text: Kanon was especially good at hiding his footsteps. ...Like he was a cat. He was able to suddenly be there without anyone noticing, and leave in the same way. For example, even though he stepped in the puddles, the sound he made was far smaller than that of the rain hitting the puddles...
units.note: MG retains the narrowing of Kanon’s concealed presence to footsteps. UP restores hiding his presence.
units.japanese: 嘉音は特に、気配を殺せるように出来ている。

units.text: Kanon was especially good at hiding his footsteps. ...Just like a cat. He was able to suddenly be there without anyone noticing and leave in the same way. For example, even though he stepped in puddles, the sound he made was far smaller than that of the rain hitting them...
units.note: MG retains the narrowing of Kanon’s concealed presence to footsteps. UP restores hiding his presence.
units.japanese: 嘉音は特に、気配を殺せるように出来ている。…例えるならば猫。誰にも気取られることなく、いつの間にかそこにいて、いつの間にか立ち去ることができる。だからたとえ、水溜りを踏むことになろうとも、その音は水溜りを叩く雨音よりも遥かに小さい…。

description: WH says servants appear when they needed to, dropping the household as the people needing them and rendering unobtrusiveness as unconcernedly.
sourceReading: Like unnoticed furniture, servants should appear unobtrusively when the household needs them; this is their greatest virtue.

units.text: Genji also had that ability. ...Well, originally, those servants called furniture were supposed to be like that. Just like how desks and closets went unnoticed by members of the family, the servants also treated being able to appear unconcernedly when they needed to as a great virtue.
units.note: MG uses passive “whenever they were needed,” restoring the household’s need. UP retains “when they needed to,” attaching necessity to the servants.
units.japanese: 家人が机や戸棚に対して何の気配も感じないように、使用人もそうであり、彼らが必要とする時にさりげなく現れるのが最大の美徳なのだ。

units.text: Genji also had that ability. ...Well, in the first place, that was how the servants were supposed to be, even going by the name of furniture. Just like how desks and closets go unnoticed by members of the family, the servants also treated being able to show up unobtrusively when they needed to as their greatest virtue.
units.note: MG uses passive “whenever they were needed,” restoring the household’s need. UP retains “when they needed to,” attaching necessity to the servants.
units.japanese: 源次もまた、そういう力を持ち合わせていた。…いや、本来、家具とまで呼ばれる使用人はそうあるべきなのだ。家人が机や戸棚に対して何の気配も感じないように、使用人もそうであり、彼らが必要とする時にさりげなく現れるのが最大の美徳なのだ。

description: WH writes that is really was a strong lock, colliding present and past verb forms.
sourceReading: The heavy turn seemingly indicates securely locked status.

units.text: Genji pulled a gold key out of his pocket. It was the only key to the study that existed, other than the one Kinzo held. He stuck it in the key hole, and turned it heavily. ......At first glance, it looked like that meant that is really was a strong lock.
units.note: Both editions repair WH’s “is was” collision in the lock sentence.
units.japanese: ……一見、それは確かに厳重な施錠を示した。

description: WH adds or a fraud to Kanon’s explanation of how furniture changes according to its master.
sourceReading: Depending on their master, furniture can become kind, cruel, or behave in any manner.

units.text: The color of tension didn't disappear from Kanon's expression in the slightest. ......If furniture served a different master, they could be kind or brutal or a fraud. ...If he called himself furniture serving the hated Beatrice, then surely he was a despicable being as well...
units.note: Both editions restore that furniture can become kind, cruel, or anything else depending on its master, without inventing fraud.
units.japanese: ……家具は仕える主が違えば、やさしくも残酷にも如何様にでもなる。

description: WH writes for a some time.
sourceReading: After laughing for a while in the raging fire, he collapses.

units.text: After laughing and howling in the roaring flames for a some time, Kinzo flopped to the ground, as though he was a puppet whose strings had been cut. Those incredible blazing flames disappeared as though he had been completely burned up, and afterwards, all that was left was a festering and burnt corpse that would make you want to avert your eyes...
units.note: MG retains “for a some time”; UP repairs it to “for some time.”
units.japanese: しばらくの間、猛火の中で吼えるように笑い続けた後、まるで糸の切れた操り人形のように、金蔵はばたりと倒れる。

units.text: After laughing and howling in the roaring flames for a some time, Kinzo flopped to the ground, as though he was a puppet whose strings had been cut. Those incredible blazing flames disappeared as though he'd been completely burned up, and afterwards, nothing remained but a festering and burnt corpse that one could hardly bear to look at...
units.note: MG retains “for a some time”; UP repairs it to “for some time.”
units.japanese: しばらくの間、猛火の中で吼えるように笑い続けた後、まるで糸の切れた操り人形のように、金蔵はばたりと倒れる。あれほど燃え盛っていた炎は、まるでもう全てを焼き尽くしたかのように消え、後には焼け爛れ、目を背けたくなるような遺体が残されただけだった…。

description: WH describes the immediately burned corpse as festering, adding a suppurating or decaying condition.
sourceReading: The fire leaves a horribly scorched corpse, burned and ravaged.

units.text: After laughing and howling in the roaring flames for a some time, Kinzo flopped to the ground, as though he was a puppet whose strings had been cut. Those incredible blazing flames disappeared as though he had been completely burned up, and afterwards, all that was left was a festering and burnt corpse that would make you want to avert your eyes...
units.note: Both editions retain “festering” for the immediately burned remains.
units.japanese: あれほど燃え盛っていた炎は、まるでもう全てを焼き尽くしたかのように消え、後には焼け爛れ、目を背けたくなるような遺体が残されただけだった…。

units.text: After laughing and howling in the roaring flames for a some time, Kinzo flopped to the ground, as though he was a puppet whose strings had been cut. Those incredible blazing flames disappeared as though he'd been completely burned up, and afterwards, nothing remained but a festering and burnt corpse that one could hardly bear to look at...
units.note: Both editions retain “festering” for the immediately burned remains.
units.japanese: しばらくの間、猛火の中で吼えるように笑い続けた後、まるで糸の切れた操り人形のように、金蔵はばたりと倒れる。あれほど燃え盛っていた炎は、まるでもう全てを焼き尽くしたかのように消え、後には焼け爛れ、目を背けたくなるような遺体が残されただけだった…。

units.text: After laughing and howling in the roaring flames for some time, Kinzo flopped to the ground, as though he was a puppet whose strings had been cut. Those incredible blazing flames disappeared as though they had burned up everything there was to burn, and afterwards, all that was left was a festering and burnt body that would make you want to avert your eyes...
units.note: Both editions retain “festering” for the immediately burned remains.
units.japanese: しばらくの間、猛火の中で吼えるように笑い続けた後、まるで糸の切れた操り人形のように、金蔵はばたりと倒れる。あれほど燃え盛っていた炎は、まるでもう全てを焼き尽くしたかのように消え、後には焼け爛れ、目を背けたくなるような遺体が残されただけだった…。

description: WH makes Beatrice say Kanon does not hate her much instead of saying she does not dislike him much.
sourceReading: She cannot get along with Kanon despite not disliking him particularly.

units.text: "It seems I just can't get along with Kanon.  It's not as though you hate me that much, right...?"
units.note: Both editions restore Beatrice as the subject of the limited dislike; UP converts the litotes into positive liking but does not retain WH’s reversed subject.
units.japanese: 「妾はつくづく、嘉音とは仲良くなれぬようだ。そう嫌いでもないというのにな…？」

description: WH says his reaction differed from what he anticipated and therefore made them laugh.
sourceReading: Contrary to his intention, his hostile gesture makes Beatrice and Ronove laugh.

units.text: Beatrice grinned. Kanon violently averted his gaze, obviously unhappy. ...His reaction was so different from what he had anticipated that it made the witch and her butler laugh.
units.note: Both editions still say Kanon’s reaction differed from what he intended and thereby caused the laughter.
units.japanese: …その仕草は、彼の思惑とは異なり、魔女とその執事を笑わせた。

units.text: Beatrice grinned. Kanon violently averted his gaze, obviously unhappy. ...His reaction was so different from what he wanted to do that it made the witch and her butler laugh.
units.note: Both editions still say Kanon’s reaction differed from what he intended and thereby caused the laughter.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェはニコリと、あるいはニヤリと微笑む。嘉音は乱暴に視線を逸らし、あからさまな不快感を示した。…その仕草は、彼の思惑とは異なり、魔女とその執事を笑わせた。

units.text: Beatrice smiled broadly, or perhaps wickedly. Kanon violently averted his gaze, obviously disturbed. ...His reaction was so different from what he had obviously intended that it made the witch and her butler laugh.
units.note: Both editions still say Kanon’s reaction differed from what he intended and thereby caused the laughter.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェはニコリと、あるいはニヤリと微笑む。嘉音は乱暴に視線を逸らし、あからさまな不快感を示した。…その仕草は、彼の思惑とは異なり、魔女とその執事を笑わせた。

description: WH uses had ... came instead of had ... come.
sourceReading: They have innocently come into the place where sacrifices await.

units.text: Kanon was taken aback by that creepy laughter... Beatrice's reason for being here was not just to take Kinzo's life. The first twilight required six sacrifices. Kinzo alone wasn't nearly enough. ...And they had just nonchalantly came to this place...
units.note: MG uses “walked” and UP uses “come,” so neither retains WH’s “had ... came” error.
units.japanese: …そしてそこへ、自分たちがのこのこと訪れている…。

description: WH singularizes the perceptive servants who immediately understand the sacrifice count into He.
sourceReading: They quickly infer the implication, and five brings to mind the number of servants.

units.text: He instinctively figured it out immediately... Six sacrifices were required for the first twilight. After Kinzo, how many more would you need to add up to six? ......In this mansion, the number 5 instantly made them think of the number of servants here...
units.note: Both editions use a plural subject for the perceptive servants rather than WH’s singular “He.”
units.japanese: 勘のいい彼らはすぐに察した…。

description: WH renders Ronove’s pride as I think honorably of you.
sourceReading: As a fellow piece of furniture, Ronove is proud of Genji.

units.text: "......As I expected of you, Genji.  As furniture like you, I think honorably of you."
units.note: MG restores Ronove’s pride; UP retains “I think honorably of you.”
units.japanese: 「……源次はさすがですね。同じ家具として、あなたを誇りに思いますよ。」

units.text: "......As I expected of you, Genji. As fellow furniture, I think honorably of you."
units.note: MG restores Ronove’s pride; UP retains “I think honorably of you.”
units.japanese: 「……源次はさすがですね。同じ家具として、あなたを誇りに思いますよ」

description: WH asks Is that still, a regret? after the ring, instead of asking whether she remains free of lingering attachment despite it.
sourceReading: Even after receiving George’s ring, does she still have no attachment that makes her reluctant to die?

units.text: ".........I heard that George-sama gave you a ring.  Is that still, a regret?"
units.note: MG asks whether Shannon still maintains that she has no regrets and UP directly asks whether she has none; their respective answers fit those questions and neither retains WH’s claim that the ring itself is a regret.
units.japanese: 「………譲治さまに指輪を贈られたそうだな。それでもなお、未練はないか。」

description: WH intensifies the ritual not being something to dispute or alter now into Kanon couldn’t care less about it.
sourceReading: For Kanon, the evil ritual itself is not something he can now do much about; surviving and obtaining his wish matter more.

units.text: By this point, Kanon couldn't care less about this evil ceremony the witch and the rest were trying to carry out. ......On the contrary, it was much more important that he remain alive so that he could be invited to the Golden Land, ...and have his wish granted by Beatrice there...
units.note: Both editions retain complete-indifference language: MG says Kanon “couldn’t care less,” while UP says he did not care “in the slightest.”
units.japanese: 嘉音にとって、魔女たちが執り行おうとしている邪悪な儀式は、それ自体が今更どうこうというものではない。

units.text: By this point, Kanon couldn't care less about this evil ceremony the witch and the rest were trying to carry out. ...On the contrary, it was much more important that he remain alive so that he could be invited to the Golden Land... and have his wish granted by Beatrice there...
units.note: Both editions retain complete-indifference language: MG says Kanon “couldn’t care less,” while UP says he did not care “in the slightest.”
units.japanese: 嘉音にとって、魔女たちが執り行おうとしている邪悪な儀式は、それ自体が今更どうこうというものではない。……むしろ、生き残って黄金郷へ招かれ、…そこでベアトリーチェによって願いを叶えてもらえることの方が重要な意味を持っていた…。

units.text: The evil ritual the witch and the rest were trying to carry out was, at this point, not something that Kanon cared about in the slightest. ......On the contrary, it was much more important for him to survive, be invited to the Golden Land, ...and have his wish granted by Beatrice there...
units.note: Both editions retain complete-indifference language: MG says Kanon “couldn’t care less,” while UP says he did not care “in the slightest.”
units.japanese: 嘉音にとって、魔女たちが執り行おうとしている邪悪な儀式は、それ自体が今更どうこうというものではない。……むしろ、生き残って黄金郷へ招かれ、…そこでベアトリーチェによって願いを叶えてもらえることの方が重要な意味を持っていた…。

description: WH inserts not into awful at not thinking, reversing Beatrice’s taunt.
sourceReading: She claims Battler is really poor at thinking and urges him to stop reasoning.

units.text: I know, you really are awful at not thinking about things, right??  Stop, stoooop, *cackle*cackle*!  Look look, obviously fantasy, obviously fantasy, kihhihihyahyahhyahhyahhyahhyahhyaaaaaahhh!!"
units.note: Neither edition retains WH’s inserted negation. MG introduces a separate preference-versus-ability defect recorded above; UP restores the claim that Battler is bad at thinking.
units.japanese: 知ってんだよ、モノを考えンの本当は苦手なんだろォ？？　止めちまえ止めちまえェエ、くっくっくっく！　ほらほらどうせファンタジーどうせファンタジー、くっひひひゃひゃっひゃっひゃっひゃっひゃっひゃあぁああぁ！！」

description: WH adds I’m still, assigning the wonderful state to Lucifer and making the offer depend on her current mood.
sourceReading: If he apologizes, she will let him alone die gently in a supremely wonderful state.

units.text: You're a cute kid, so apologize...  If you do, I'll let you die gently, gently, while I'm still in a wonderful mood......"
units.note: Both editions remove WH’s assignment of the wonderful state to Lucifer’s own mood. MG’s impersonal “while it still feels great” is less explicit than UP but no longer says “while I’m still in a wonderful mood.”
units.japanese: 可愛い子なんだから、謝っちゃいなさいよ…。　そうしたら、あなただけは、最高にステキな気分の中で、やさしくやさしく逝かせてアゲル……。」
candidates: I'm still in a wonderful mood

description: WH calls Kanon stronger where Beatrice says he shows better aptitude or technique than against Satan.
sourceReading: His performance or skill looks better than in the Satan encounter.

units.text: "......Isn't he stronger than he was against Satan?"
units.note: Both editions retain “stronger” instead of evaluating Kanon’s improved aptitude or technique.
units.japanese: 「……あやつ、サタンの時よりも筋がいいではないか。」

units.text: "...Isn't he stronger than he was against Satan?"
units.note: Both editions retain “stronger” instead of evaluating Kanon’s improved aptitude or technique.
units.japanese: 「……あやつ、サタンの時よりも筋がいいではないか」

description: WH substitutes furniture for humans in Ronove’s generalization about beings that sometimes become witches and treat demons as butlers.
sourceReading: Humans are frightening: sometimes they even become witches and make demons their butlers.

units.text: "That is why furniture is so frightening.  Sometimes they even become witches, and treat demons as butlers."
units.note: Both editions correctly restore humans as the beings Ronove calls frightening.
units.japanese: 「だから人間は恐ろしいのです。たまに魔女にまでなり、悪魔を執事扱いにしたりいたしますよ。」
candidates: become witches, and treat demons as butlers
frightening.  Sometimes they even become witches

description: WH describes Lucifer as completely deranged instead of performing ample disruption before attacking.
sourceReading: She thoroughly confounds her opponent with her movement, then attacks his heart.

units.text: After Lucifer was completely deranged, with a speed approaching the limits that a human eye could follow, she flew at Kanon's heart...
units.note: MG has Lucifer fly about wildly and UP says she “went wild”; neither clearly preserves that she deliberately disorients Kanon before attacking.
units.japanese: 人の目では捉えることの出来ない領域にまで踏み込んだ速度で、ルシファーは存分に撹乱した後に、嘉音のその心臓に喰らい付く…。

units.text: After flying about wildly for some time, with a speed approaching the limits of what a human eye could follow, Lucifer flew at Kanon's heart...
units.note: MG has Lucifer fly about wildly and UP says she “went wild”; neither clearly preserves that she deliberately disorients Kanon before attacking.
units.japanese: 人の目では捉えることの出来ない領域にまで踏み込んだ速度で、ルシファーは存分に撹乱した後に、嘉音のその心臓に喰らい付く…。

units.text: With a speed exceeding even the limits that the human eye could follow, Lucifer went wild, and flew at Kanon's heart...
units.note: MG has Lucifer fly about wildly and UP says she “went wild”; neither clearly preserves that she deliberately disorients Kanon before attacking.
units.japanese: 人の目では捉えることの出来ない領域にまで踏み込んだ速度で、ルシファーは存分に撹乱した後に、嘉音のその心臓に喰らい付く…。

description: WH makes her speed approach what human eyes can follow rather than enter a range they cannot perceive.
sourceReading: She moves at a speed beyond what human eyes can track.

units.text: After Lucifer was completely deranged, with a speed approaching the limits that a human eye could follow, she flew at Kanon's heart...
units.note: MG retains speed merely approaching what human eyes can follow; UP restores speed exceeding the limit of human sight.
units.japanese: 人の目では捉えることの出来ない領域にまで踏み込んだ速度で、ルシファーは存分に撹乱した後に、嘉音のその心臓に喰らい付く…。

units.text: After flying about wildly for some time, with a speed approaching the limits of what a human eye could follow, Lucifer flew at Kanon's heart...
units.note: MG retains speed merely approaching what human eyes can follow; UP restores speed exceeding the limit of human sight.
units.japanese: 人の目では捉えることの出来ない領域にまで踏み込んだ速度で、ルシファーは存分に撹乱した後に、嘉音のその心臓に喰らい付く…。

description: WH specifies breaking bones as the stake is removed rather than gouging bone.
sourceReading: The stake’s extraction makes the sound of gouging bone and further spilling blood.

units.text: When she heard the sound of breaking bones and even more blood dripping down, Shannon looked away without thinking. There was an air hole in the back of the pierced hand so big that you could clearly see through to the other side...
units.note: Both editions retain breaking bones instead of the sound of the stake gouging bone as it is removed.
units.japanese: 骨を抉る音と、さらに血が零れる音が聞こえた。紗音は思わず目を背ける。

units.text: When she heard the sound of breaking bones and even more blood dripping down, Shannon looked away reflexively. There was an air hole in the back of the pierced hand so big, you could clearly see through to the other side...
units.note: Both editions retain breaking bones instead of the sound of the stake gouging bone as it is removed.
units.japanese:
骨を抉る音と、さらに血が零れる音が聞こえた。
紗音は思わず目を背ける。抜いた手の甲には、はっきりと向こうを覗くことが出来るほどの無惨な風穴が残されていた…。

units.text:
The sound of breaking bones and even more blood dripping down could be heard.
Shannon instinctively averted her eyes. There was an air hole in the back of the pierced hand so big that you could clearly see through to the other side...
units.note: Both editions retain breaking bones instead of the sound of the stake gouging bone as it is removed.
units.japanese:
骨を抉る音と、さらに血が零れる音が聞こえた。
紗音は思わず目を背ける。抜いた手の甲には、はっきりと向こうを覗くことが出来るほどの無惨な風穴が残されていた…。

description: WH says Ronove’s true intention seemed obvious to Kanon instead of saying his congratulation felt insincere.
sourceReading: To Kanon, who paid for victory with a grave wound, the applause seems transparently hollow.

units.text: Ronove was clapping his hands. ...To Kanon, who had a wound on his left hand that couldn't be closed after achieving a painful victory, Ronove's true intention seemed pretty obvious.
units.note: MG renders the applause as mockery and UP as shallow; neither retains WH’s unrelated claim that Ronove’s true intention seemed obvious.
units.japanese: …左手に、塞ぐこともできぬほどの傷を負って、辛い勝利を収めた嘉音にとっては、白々しくしか感じられない。

description: WH says the magic had been effecting Lucifer, using effecting where affecting is required.
sourceReading: The magic applied to her is undone.

units.text: Beatrice waved her pipe again. When she did, the magic that had been effecting Lucifer was released. ......So as a horribly natural result, this time she properly 'fell' back onto the floor.
units.note: MG retains “effecting Lucifer”; UP corrects the verb to “affecting.”
units.japanese: すると彼女に掛けられた魔法は解かれた。

units.text: Beatrice waved her pipe again. When she did, the magic that had been effecting Lucifer was released. ...So, as a horribly natural result, this time she "fell" properly, back onto the floor.
units.note: MG retains “effecting Lucifer”; UP corrects the verb to “affecting.”
units.japanese: もう一度ベアトリーチェは煙管を回す。すると彼女に掛けられた魔法は解かれた。……だからひどく当然の結果として、彼女は床に、再び極めて正当に“墜落”した。

description: WH describes the competent sisters as having to clean up fighting scenes, suggesting aftermath cleanup rather than doing the violent work.
sourceReading: The competent younger sisters will handle all the rough or violent work.

units.text: "...That's why I'm always saying Lucifer-nee shouldn't do anything.  It's alright if she just brags all the time.  Because those of us who are superior always have to clean up the fighting scenes."
units.note: MG restores that the capable sisters handle all rough work; UP retains “clean up the fighting scenes.”
units.japanese: 荒事は全て、優秀な私たちで片付けるのだから。」

units.text: "...That's why I'm always saying Lucifer‐nee shouldn't do anything. It's alright if she just brags all the time. Because we superior ones always have to clean up the fighting scenes."
units.note: MG restores that the capable sisters handle all rough work; UP retains “clean up the fighting scenes.”
units.japanese: 「…だからルシファー姉は何もしなくていいといつも言っている。お姉様は威張ってだけいればいい。荒事は全て、優秀な私たちで片付けるのだから」

description: WH says now they are gathered they are the Seven Stakes, losing the explicit only-as-seven emphasis.
sourceReading: Only when all seven are together are they the Seven Sisters of Purgatory; they should cooperate and carry out her work.

units.text: Now that you are all gathered here, you are the Seven Stakes of Purgatory, right?  Be nice and execute the task I give you.  Swiftly, right?"
units.note: MG says the group are the Seven Stakes only together, while UP says being a seven-person unit makes them the Seven Sisters; both restore the only-as-seven condition.
units.japanese: そなたらは７人揃ってこその煉獄の七姉妹であろうが。仲良くして妾の仕事を遂行せよ。迅速にな？」

description: WH changes each sister reproaching Lucifer as ineffectual into unanimously closing in on an objectively worthless sister.
sourceReading: The sisters each call their elder sister ineffectual, reproaching and insulting her.

units.text: The seven sisters of Purgatory unanimously closed in on their worthless sister.  Abusing her. ...Even Kanon, who had been fighting for his life until a second ago, couldn't bear to look straight at it...
units.note: MG retains the sisters unanimously closing in on a worthless Lucifer; UP restores their spoken taunts and verbal abuse.
units.japanese: 煉獄の七姉妹たちは、口々に不甲斐ないと姉を詰る。罵る。

units.text: The Seven Sisters of Purgatory unanimously closed in on their worthless sister. Abusing her. ...Even Kanon, who had been fighting for his life until a second ago, couldn't bear to look at it...
units.note: MG retains the sisters unanimously closing in on a worthless Lucifer; UP restores their spoken taunts and verbal abuse.
units.japanese: 煉獄の七姉妹たちは、口々に不甲斐ないと姉を詰る。罵る。…それは、ついさっきまで命をやり取りしていた嘉音にとってすら、正視に耐えない…。

description: WH says Lucifer hears her sisters’ curses instead of throwing curses at them before yielding to the request.
sourceReading: After repeatedly grinding her teeth and cursing her younger sisters, Lucifer trembles and complies.

units.text: After grinding her teeth over and over, after hearing her sisters' curses, ............as she trembled all over, ......Lucifer answered her sisters' request...
units.note: MG retains Lucifer hearing her sisters’ curses; UP restores Lucifer as the one hurling curses at them.
units.japanese:
ルシファーは何度も歯軋りを繰り返し、妹たちに呪いの言葉を投げ掛けた後、……………わなわなと震えながら、
……妹たちの要望に応じる…。

units.text: After grinding her teeth over and over after hearing her sisters' curses, ......Lucifer trembled all over... and answered her sisters' request...
units.note: MG retains Lucifer hearing her sisters’ curses; UP restores Lucifer as the one hurling curses at them.
units.japanese: ルシファーは何度も歯軋りを繰り返し、妹たちに呪いの言葉を投げ掛けた後、……………わなわなと震えながら、……妹たちの要望に応じる…。

description: WH describes carving a red character, losing the accumulating sequence of straight-line wounds.
sourceReading: Red marks like the single horizontal stroke 一 are progressively cut into his body one after another.

units.text: The seven sisters jumped around the room faster than the eye could see, deciding how they would kill Kanon. They tortured Kanon with their cruel giggles, sometimes making a close pass at him. ...They kept scraping his arms, shoulders, and cheeks, carving a red character into his body...
units.note: MG still treats the accumulating red straight-line wounds as letters; UP restores red lines.
units.japanese: …腕、肩、頬などが、チリチリとかすられ、削られ、彼の体は次第に赤い一文字の模様が次々刻まれていく…。

units.text: The Seven Sisters jumped around the room faster than the eye could see, examining how they could best kill Kanon. They tortured Kanon with their cruel giggles, sometimes making a close pass at him. ...They kept scraping his arms, shoulders, and cheeks, gradually carving red letters into his body...
units.note: MG still treats the accumulating red straight-line wounds as letters; UP restores red lines.
units.japanese: 七姉妹たちは目にも留まらぬ速度で室内を跳ね回り、嘉音をどう殺そうかと吟味する。残酷なくすくす笑いと、ちょっかいを出すように時折かする彼女らが嘉音を苛む。…腕、肩、頬などが、チリチリとかすられ、削られ、彼の体は次第に赤い一文字の模様が次々刻まれていく…。

description: WH substitutes You’re mean for the accusation that Shannon’s intervention is unfair.
sourceReading: Leviathan complains it is unfair and that Shannon has no part in the contest.

units.text: "Whaaaat!!  You're me-an!  This has nothing to do with yo-u!"
units.note: MG retains “You’re mean” for the accusation of unfair intervention; UP restores “That’s cheating.”
units.japanese: 「何ぃー！！　ずーるいー！　あんたは関係ないでしょぉー！」

units.text: "Whaaaat?!! You're me-an! This has nothing to do with yo-u!"
units.note: MG retains “You’re mean” for the accusation of unfair intervention; UP restores “That’s cheating.”
units.japanese: 「何ぃー！！　ずーるいー！　あんたは関係ないでしょぉー！」

description: WH turns Belphegor’s formal deferential expression of gratitude into Wow, I’m so happy.
sourceReading: She formally acknowledges the favor or honor of Beatrice’s permission.

units.text: "Wow, I'm so happy.  Come on, I'll make you regret coming out uninvited!"
units.note: Both editions replace WH’s casual “Wow, I’m so happy” with an expression of gratitude; MG is explicitly formal.
units.japanese: 「ありがたき幸せ。

description: WH reverses the denial that death is always the same into Isn’t death the same?
sourceReading: Deaths are not all alike, she warns, contrasting peaceful and harsh deaths.

units.text: ......Isn't death the same?  An intense death would torture you even more than dying, right?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: Both editions restore that deaths are not all the same.
units.japanese: ……死は同じではないぞ？　苛烈な死は、死して尚、苛むぞ？

description: WH substitutes even more than dying for torment persisting even after death.
sourceReading: A brutal death will torment the victim even after she has died.

units.text: ......Isn't death the same?  An intense death would torture you even more than dying, right?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG still compares the anguish with merely dying rather than saying torment persists after death; UP restores torment even after death.
units.japanese: ……死は同じではないぞ？　苛烈な死は、死して尚、苛むぞ？

units.text: ...Not all deaths are the same. A cruel death will cause you far more anguish than merely dying. *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: MG still compares the anguish with merely dying rather than saying torment persists after death; UP restores torment even after death.
units.japanese: 「……死は同じではないぞ？　苛烈な死は、死して尚、苛むぞ？　くっくくくくくくく！」

description: WH renders このところ as this part of you instead of recently and changes the general remark about love’s uncertain attainment into her particular past love.
sourceReading: Beatrice finds Shannon uninteresting lately and says the period around whether love will be fulfilled is its most interesting stage.

units.text: "........................Hmmmm.  In any case, this part of you isn't amusing.  Whether or not you would achieve love was the most interesting part.
units.note: Both editions restore a temporal reading and the general proposition about love rather than WH’s “this part of you” and Shannon-specific past love. MG’s overly narrow present-moment wording is recorded separately above.
units.japanese: 「……………………。……ふぅむ。どうにもそなたはこのところ面白みに欠けるな？　恋というヤツは、達するかどうかの辺りが一番面白い。

description: WH says That only happened for the first instant after describing blood oozing, then asserts a rose shape.
sourceReading: For just the first instant, the emerging blood also looks like a crimson rose pattern.

units.text: When Genji removed his hand, .........bright-red fresh blood oozed out of there. That only happened for the first instant, and it was shaped like a crimson rose...
units.note: MG retains “It only happened” and then asserts a rose shape; UP restores that the stain merely appeared rose-shaped for the first instant.
units.japanese: それは最初の一瞬だけ、真紅の薔薇模様にも見えた…。

units.text: When Genji removed his hand, ......bright-red, fresh blood oozed out of there. It only happened for the first instant, and it was shaped like a crimson rose...
units.note: MG retains “It only happened” and then asserts a rose shape; UP restores that the stain merely appeared rose-shaped for the first instant.
units.japanese: 源次がその手を離すと、………そこには真っ赤な鮮血が湧き出していた。それは最初の一瞬だけ、真紅の薔薇模様にも見えた…。

description: WH calls the eye-covering hand left instead of right and substitutes face for eyes.
sourceReading: Genji withdraws the right hand covering Shannon’s eyes, revealing her peaceful expression.

units.text: And when he removed his left hand covering her face, .........There was a peaceful expression on Shannon's face, as though she was sleeping. ......And she fell softly, ...silently, .........and slept.
units.note: MG restores the right hand but still says it covered Shannon’s face; UP restores both the right hand and her eyes.
units.japanese: そして紗音の目を覆っていた右手を離すと、

units.text: And when he removed his right hand covering her face, ......there was a peaceful expression there, as though she was sleeping. ......And she fell softly, ...silently, ......and slept.
units.note: MG restores the right hand but still says it covered Shannon’s face; UP restores both the right hand and her eyes.
units.japanese: そして紗音の目を覆っていた右手を離すと、………紗音は眠るような安らかな表情を浮かべていて。……そして、ふわりと、…音もなく倒れて、………眠った。

description: WH describes Ronove’s expression as mysterious rather than solemn or grave beneath his smile.
sourceReading: Only Ronove shows something sober or solemn within his smile.

units.text: Beatrice and the seven sisters were shocked by this scene. ...Only Ronove had a mysterious expression along with his smile.
units.note: Both editions retain “mysterious” for Ronove’s solemn or grave expression beneath his smile.
units.japanese: …ロノウェだけが笑みの中に神妙なものを浮かべていた。

units.text: This scene left Beatrice and the Seven Sisters stunned. ...Only Ronove wore a mysterious smile.
units.note: Both editions retain “mysterious” for Ronove’s solemn or grave expression beneath his smile.
units.japanese:
ベアトリーチェと七姉妹たちはその光景に呆然とする。
…ロノウェだけが笑みの中に神妙なものを浮かべていた。

units.text:
Beatrice and the Seven Sisters were shocked by this scene.
...Only Ronove had a mysterious expression along with his smile.
units.note: Both editions retain “mysterious” for Ronove’s solemn or grave expression beneath his smile.
units.japanese:
ベアトリーチェと七姉妹たちはその光景に呆然とする。
…ロノウェだけが笑みの中に神妙なものを浮かべていた。

description: The interrupted English objection preserves surprise but omits 勝手な真似, Beatrice’s explicit complaint that Ronove is acting on his own authority.
sourceReading: Hey, acting on your own like that...! Beatrice objects to Ronove granting Genji a peaceful death before she can torture him.

units.text: "Wha?!  Wait, what are you...!"
units.note: MG restores Beatrice’s objection that Ronove is acting beyond his authority (“not your place”); UP retains the generic interrupted “what are you.”
units.japanese: 「ちょっ？！　おいッ勝手な真似を…！」

units.text: "Wha?! Wait, what are you...!"
units.note: MG restores Beatrice’s objection that Ronove is acting beyond his authority (“not your place”); UP retains the generic interrupted “what are you.”
units.japanese: 「ちょっ？！　おいッ勝手な真似を…！」

description: WH says there had never been anything on Rokkenjima outside the Ushiromiya family. It adds never and substitutes anything for the household occupancy premise.
sourceReading: The Ushiromiya household is the only presence on the island, which makes checking locks seem of limited practical value.

units.text: Gohda was doing the nighttime rounds. There had never been anything on Rokkenjima outside the Ushiromiya family. So checking that the doors and windows were all closed had no real purpose. However, since Natsuhi had scolded that this was careless, the nighttime rounds had become part of the servants' daily routine.
units.note: MG restores the household-occupancy premise but still adds the absolute “always”; UP retains “never” and substitutes anything for household presence.
units.japanese: そもそも、六軒島には右代宮家以外は存在しない。
candidates: never been anything on Rokkenjima outside the Ushiromiya family

units.text: Gohda was doing the nighttime rounds. Rokkenjima had always been empty, except for the Ushiromiya Family household. So, checking that the doors and windows were all closed had no real purpose. However, ever since the time Natsuhi had condemned such an attitude as being careless, the nighttime rounds had become part of the servants' daily routine.
units.note: MG restores the household-occupancy premise but still adds the absolute “always”; UP retains “never” and substitutes anything for household presence.
units.japanese:
郷田は、夜の見回りをしていた。そもそも、六軒島には右代宮家以外は存在しない。
だから戸締りやその確認には、それほど意味があるわけではない。しかし、夏妃がそれを無用心だと咎めて以来、夜回りは使用人たちの日課に組み込まれた。

units.text:
Gohda was doing the nighttime rounds. There had never been anything on Rokkenjima outside the Ushiromiya family.
So checking that the doors and windows were all closed had no real purpose. However, ever since Natsuhi had scolded them saying that this was careless, the nighttime rounds had become part of the servants' daily routine.
units.note: MG restores the household-occupancy premise but still adds the absolute “always”; UP retains “never” and substitutes anything for household presence.
units.japanese:
郷田は、夜の見回りをしていた。そもそも、六軒島には右代宮家以外は存在しない。
だから戸締りやその確認には、それほど意味があるわけではない。しかし、夏妃がそれを無用心だと咎めて以来、夜回りは使用人たちの日課に組み込まれた。
