description: WH supplies people who thought they were alone in the mansion as the circumstance of the ghost stories.
sourceReading: Stories arose about eerie sounds or figures inside the mansion where no one was supposed to be.

units.text: ......The reason that Natsuhi had ordered this was the occasional disturbances of the witch. Everyone who came and left this island knew about the legend of Beatrice, the witch of the forest. This had become established as this island's characteristic ghost story. Because of that, it was only natural that some people would say that, when they thought they were alone in the mansion..., they would hear a strange sound or see the shadow of a person.
units.note: Both editions supply people believing themselves alone as the circumstance of the reported sounds and shadows.
units.japanese: だから時折、誰もいないはずの屋敷内に、不気味な音や人影が…、というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
candidates: thought they were alone in the mansion

units.text: ...In the first place, Natsuhi had ordered this because of the occasional witch disturbances. Everyone who came and left this island knew about the legend of Beatrice, the witch of the forest. It had become established as this island's characteristic ghost story. Because of that, it was only natural that some people would claim that, when they thought they were alone in the mansion, ...they would hear a strange sound or see the shadow of a person.
units.note: Both editions supply people believing themselves alone as the circumstance of the reported sounds and shadows.
units.japanese: ……そもそも、夏妃が夜回りを命じたのは、時折起こった、魔女騒動のせいだった。この島に出入りする者なら誰もが知る、森の魔女ベアトリーチェの伝説。それはこの島独自の怪談として根付いていた。だから時折、誰もいないはずの屋敷内に、不気味な音や人影が…、というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
candidates: thought they were alone in the mansion

units.text: ......The reason that Natsuhi had ordered this was the occasional disturbances of the witch. Everyone who visited this island knew about the legend of Beatrice, the witch of the forest. This had become established as this island's characteristic ghost story. Because of that, it was only natural that some people would occasionally say that, when they thought they were alone in the mansion, ...they had heard strange sounds, or seen the shadow of a person.
units.note: Both editions supply people believing themselves alone as the circumstance of the reported sounds and shadows.
units.japanese: ……そもそも、夏妃が夜回りを命じたのは、時折起こった、魔女騒動のせいだった。この島に出入りする者なら誰もが知る、森の魔女ベアトリーチェの伝説。それはこの島独自の怪談として根付いていた。だから時折、誰もいないはずの屋敷内に、不気味な音や人影が…、というような話は、自然と起こったものだった。
candidates: thought they were alone in the mansion

description: WH replaces Gohda’s vague suggestion of a small angle-related issue with the judgment that it was not a big problem.
sourceReading: He wonders why the lid rattled but vaguely supposes some minor issue with its angle or the like, choosing not to dwell on it.

units.text: By now, Gohda had realized that he had been a coward. ......So while he still had some doubts about what had caused the lid to make that sound, ...he thought it wasn't a big problem, and decided not to worry about it too much.
units.note: MG still replaces the vague angle or positioning explanation with “it wasn’t a big problem”; UP restores a quirk of positioning.
units.japanese: ……ならばなぜ、蓋が鳴っていたのかという疑問ももちろん湧いたが、…ちょっとした角度とかの問題、などと抽象的に考え、深くは悩まないことにした。

units.text: By now, Gohda realized that he had been a coward. ...So, while he still had some doubts as to what had caused the lid to make that sound, ...he figured it wasn't a big problem, and decided not to worry about it too much.
units.note: MG still replaces the vague angle or positioning explanation with “it wasn’t a big problem”; UP restores a quirk of positioning.
units.japanese: 郷田は今頃になって、自分が小心者であったことを自覚する。……ならばなぜ、蓋が鳴っていたのかという疑問ももちろん湧いたが、…ちょっとした角度とかの問題、などと抽象的に考え、深くは悩まないことにした。

description: The sister interprets the unmoving Kumasawa as having resigned herself to her fate; WH instead has the sister announce I’m ready.
sourceReading: She has given up / accepted her fate, so I’ll take her.

units.text: I'm ready, all mine all mine all mi-ne!  You blockheads can just sit there and watch! I told you, nooooooo, this one's miiiiiiiiiiiiine!!
units.note: Both editions keep Kumasawa as the person presumed resigned instead of making the sister announce “I’m ready.” UP’s separate surrender wording is recorded above.
units.japanese: 観念したんだよ、いただきいただき、いっただきぃ！　ノロマなあんたたちはぼんやり見てればいいのよ！

description: WH renders 折檻される as being scolded, removing physical punishment from the sisters’ anticipated consequence.
sourceReading: If they take longer, Beatrice will punish them physically.

units.text: Come on, if we take any longer we'll be scolded by Beatrice-sama!  Let's take care of it all at once!
units.note: Both editions retain “scolded,” removing the physical punishment in 折檻.
units.japanese: さぁ、これ以上時間を掛けたらベアトリーチェさまに折檻されるよ！　一気に片付けてやる！

units.text: Come on, if we take any longer, we'll be scolded by Beatrice-sama! Let's take care of it all at once!
units.note: Both editions retain “scolded,” removing the physical punishment in 折檻.
units.japanese: さぁ、これ以上時間を掛けたらベアトリーチェさまに折檻されるよ！　一気に片付けてやる！

units.text: Come on, if we take any longer we'll be scolded by Beatrice‐sama! Let's take care of it all at once!
units.note: Both editions retain “scolded,” removing the physical punishment in 折檻.
units.japanese: さぁ、これ以上時間を掛けたらベアトリーチェさまに折檻されるよ！　一気に片付けてやる！

description: WH says the sisters would be apprenticed to Kumasawa, where Lucifer objects to doing menial service by fetching the person she requests.
sourceReading: Do you think we would do such an errand / act as your lackeys?

units.text: "D, do you think we'd be apprenticed to you like that?!"
units.note: MG restores the refusal to run an errand; UP retains the claim that the sisters would be apprenticed to Kumasawa.
units.japanese: 「そ、そのような丁稚奉公、私たちがすると思うッ？！」

units.text: "D‐do you think we'd be apprenticed to you like that?!"
units.note: MG restores the refusal to run an errand; UP retains the claim that the sisters would be apprenticed to Kumasawa.
units.japanese: 「そ、そのような丁稚奉公、私たちがすると思うッ？！」

description: The English assigns burst and disappeared to she, after making the golden light passive wrapping.
sourceReading: The gathered butterflies become golden radiance, envelop her, and burst/disappear, revealing another form where Kumasawa had stood.

units.text: Gold butterflies appeared in ones and twos from the garden of roses and began to gather around Kumasawa... Then, after she was wrapped in a golden sparkle, she burst and disappeared, and Kumasawa's form was no longer there. ...Instead, there was another Golden Witch, .........the one who had, in the past, explained to Beatrice the path of an Endless Witch, the only person Beatrice had called Teacher in her entire life.
units.note: MG assigns bursting and disappearing to Kumasawa; UP restores the golden butterflies as the things that envelop, burst, and vanish.
units.japanese: そして黄金の輝きとなって彼女を包んだ後、弾けて消えると、そこには熊沢の姿はなかった。

units.text: Gold butterflies appeared in ones and twos from the garden of roses and began to gather around Kumasawa... Then, after she was wrapped in a golden sparkle, she burst and disappeared, and Kumasawa's form was no longer there. ...Instead, there was another Golden Witch, ......the one who once taught the path of an Endless Witch to Beatrice, and the only person Beatrice ever called Teacher.
units.note: MG assigns bursting and disappearing to Kumasawa; UP restores the golden butterflies as the things that envelop, burst, and vanish.
units.japanese: 薔薇の園から一匹二匹と現れた黄金の蝶たちが、次第に熊沢の周りに集まり始める…。そして黄金の輝きとなって彼女を包んだ後、弾けて消えると、そこには熊沢の姿はなかった。…代わりにそこにあったのは、………ベアトリーチェにかつて、無限の魔女の道を説き、生涯でただひとり、師匠と呼んだ、もう一人の黄金の魔女の姿だった。

description: The teacher explains that furniture merely serves its master and that the master bears all the guilt. WH adds her to crimes, narrowing the statement to crimes attributed to the master herself.
sourceReading: All the guilt belongs to the master, including what the furniture does in her service.

units.text: "Ronove.  Have the furniture children step back.  Furniture only serves its master.  The master is responsible for all of her crimes."
units.note: Both editions retain “her crimes,” narrowing the teacher’s general statement that the master bears all guilt.
units.japanese: 「ロノウェ。家具の子たちを下げなさい。家具は主に仕えるだけです。全ての罪は主が背負います。」

units.text: "Ronove, have that young furniture step back. Furniture only serves its master. The master is responsible for all of her crimes."
units.note: Both editions retain “her crimes,” narrowing the teacher’s general statement that the master bears all guilt.
units.japanese: 「ロノウェ。家具の子たちを下げなさい。家具は主に仕えるだけです。全ての罪は主が背負います」

units.text: "Ronove. Have the furniture children step back. Furniture merely serves its master. The master is responsible for all of her crimes."
units.note: Both editions retain “her crimes,” narrowing the teacher’s general statement that the master bears all guilt.
units.japanese: 「ロノウェ。家具の子たちを下げなさい。家具は主に仕えるだけです。全ての罪は主が背負います」

description: WH replaces the conditional 粗相があるようならば with It seems there has been a mistake, so and turns the resulting threat into a request.
sourceReading: If there is any lapse in your hospitality/performance, I will have you return my name and the title of Endless Witch.

units.text: "Let's see.  This reunion was longer in coming than the visit of a comet.  Shall I accept your hospitality?  .........It seems there has been a mistake, ......so will you give back my name and the title of Endless Witch?"
units.note: Both editions restore a conditional threat: if Beatrice commits a blunder, the teacher will take back her name and title.
units.japanese: ………粗相があるようならば、我が名と無限の魔女の称号。……返してもらいますよ？」
candidates: name and the title of Endless Witch
seems there has been a mistake

description: WH attaches long ago to what you were, specifying a past version of the teacher, rather than the time when the pupil claims she surpassed her.
sourceReading: See how far I surpassed you long ago.

units.text: ......As you say, Teacher.  See how splendid your disciple has become, and see how far she has surpassed what you were long ago...!"
units.note: MG attaches long ago to the time Beatrice surpassed her teacher; UP retains “what you were long ago.”
units.japanese: ……仰せのままに、お師匠様。あなたの弟子が、どれほど立派になったか。そして、とっくの昔にどれほどあなたを凌駕したか、とくとご覧に入れましょう…！」

units.text: "......As you say, Master. See how splendid your disciple has become, and see how far she has surpassed what you were long ago...!"
units.note: MG attaches long ago to the time Beatrice surpassed her teacher; UP retains “what you were long ago.”
units.japanese: 「……仰せのままに、お師匠様。あなたの弟子が、どれほど立派になったか。そして、とっくの昔にどれほどあなたを凌駕したか、とくとご覧に入れましょう…！」

description: WH attaches ridiculously to the teacher’s unwillingness to open her eyes, rather than explaining that this level of attack is too trivial to merit doing so.
sourceReading: At this level it is so trifling that you do not even feel inclined to open your eyes.

units.text: "...*cackle*cackle*.  I'd expect nothing less from you, Teacher.  It looks like you ridiculously don't feel like opening your eyes even at this level...!
units.note: Both editions correctly make the attack’s trivial level the reason the teacher cannot be bothered to open her eyes.
units.japanese: 「…くっくっくっく。さすがお師匠様。この程度じゃ、馬鹿馬鹿しくて瞼を開く気にもならないらしい…！

description: WH explicitly addresses you as the person who would have to want to wreck the island.
sourceReading: Unless I attack with the resolve to destroy the whole island, it seems I cannot get you to open your eyes / overcome this defense.

units.text: If you don't want to wreck the whole island, it looks like that'll be impossible, riiiiiight?  Come, arise, Shoulder War Towers!!"
units.note: MG still makes the teacher the person who must be prepared to wreck the island; UP restores Beatrice as the speaker referring to her own required effort.
units.japanese: 島ごとぶっ壊す気でなきゃ、無理らしいぜぇええぇ？　さぁさお出でなさい、双肩の戦塔！！」

units.text: But I doubt you'll be able to win unless you're prepared to wreck this whole island, seeeeeeee? Come, arise, Shoulder War Towers!!"
units.note: MG still makes the teacher the person who must be prepared to wreck the island; UP restores Beatrice as the speaker referring to her own required effort.
units.japanese: 「島ごとぶっ壊す気でなきゃ、無理らしいぜぇええぇ？　さぁさお出でなさい、双肩の戦塔！！」

description: WH adds behind to the towers’ placement and changes the comparison from a butterfly between great trees to one through a large tree.
sourceReading: The tiny witch flanked by two immense towers resembles a butterfly dancing between great trees.

units.text: As Beatrice elegantly floated in the gap between the massive two-headed towers, she looked down on her teacher, sneering with an absolute superiority. With the two massive towers lined up behind her shoulders, the witch looked very small, like a butterfly dancing through a large tree.
units.note: Both editions restore the butterfly between large trees but retain the unsupported placement “behind her shoulders.”
units.japanese: 巨大なる塔を双肩に並べる魔女はあまりに小さく見え、まるで大樹の間を舞う蝶のように見えた。

units.text: As Beatrice elegantly floated in the gap between the massive two-headed towers, she looked down on her teacher, sneering with a sense of absolute superiority. With the two massive towers lined up behind her shoulders, the witch looked very small, like a butterfly dancing between huge trees.
units.note: Both editions restore the butterfly between large trees but retain the unsupported placement “behind her shoulders.”
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェはその巨大な双頭の塔の狭間に優雅に浮かびながら、師匠を見下ろし、絶対の優位に嘲笑う。巨大なる塔を双肩に並べる魔女はあまりに小さく見え、まるで大樹の間を舞う蝶のように見えた。

units.text: As Beatrice elegantly floated in the gap between the massive two‐headed towers, she looked down on her master, sneering with an absolute superiority. With the two massive towers lined up behind her shoulders, the witch looked very small, like a butterfly dancing between large trees.
units.note: Both editions restore the butterfly between large trees but retain the unsupported placement “behind her shoulders.”
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェはその巨大な双頭の塔の狭間に優雅に浮かびながら、師匠を見下ろし、絶対の優位に嘲笑う。巨大なる塔を双肩に並べる魔女はあまりに小さく見え、まるで大樹の間を舞う蝶のように見えた。

description: 軽く千を超える becomes a little over a thousand.
sourceReading: The shots easily exceed a thousand.

units.text: The ballista shots that numbered a little over a thousand were all fired at once, drawing a beautiful geometric curtain of death. The boorish sound as the bowstrings were played was probably even deeper than the sound of a death god swinging its sickle.
units.note: MG says over a thousand and UP says easily over a thousand, both restoring 軽く千を超える.
units.japanese: 一斉に放たれる軽く千を超えるバリスタ弾が、美しい幾何学模様で死のカーテンを描く。

description: 何億もの is expressed as several billion rather than hundreds of millions.
sourceReading: The exploding towers consist of hundreds of millions of golden butterflies.

units.text: The Shoulder War Towers exploded in gold. They became several billion gold butterflies. Those butterflies took the shape of seven massive armored soldiers. Each stretched a full 50 merute into the sky, and they lined up in front of Beatrice, protecting their master and holding massive shields which towered like windmills.
units.note: Both editions retain “several billion” for 何億もの, which means hundreds of millions.
units.japanese: それは何億もの黄金の蝶たち。

units.text: The Shoulder War Towers exploded in gold. They became several billion gold butterflies. Those butterflies took the shape of seven massive armored soldiers. Each stretched a full 50 merute into the sky, and they lined up in front of Beatrice, protecting their master and holding massive shields that towered like windmills.
units.note: Both editions retain “several billion” for 何億もの, which means hundreds of millions.
units.japanese:
双肩の戦塔は黄金色の大爆発を起こす。
それは何億もの黄金の蝶たち。その蝶たちが７人の巨人装甲兵を模る。それぞれが５０メルテもの見上げるばかりの身長を持ち、そびえ立つ風車のような大きさの巨大楯をかざしてベアトリーチェの前に並んで主を守る。

units.text:
The Shoulder War Towers exploded in gold.
They became several billion gold butterflies. Those butterflies took the shape of seven massive armored soldiers. Each stretched a full 50 merute into the sky, and they lined up in front of Beatrice, protecting their master and holding massive shields which towered like windmills.
units.note: Both editions retain “several billion” for 何億もの, which means hundreds of millions.
units.japanese:
双肩の戦塔は黄金色の大爆発を起こす。
それは何億もの黄金の蝶たち。その蝶たちが７人の巨人装甲兵を模る。それぞれが５０メルテもの見上げるばかりの身長を持ち、そびえ立つ風車のような大きさの巨大楯をかざしてベアトリーチェの前に並んで主を守る。

description: WH summons disciples of Hephaestus, omitting the god himself from ヘパイストスと弟子たち.
sourceReading: Come forth, Hephaestus and your disciples; grant me a fitting shield.

units.text: "Of course I haven't forgotten, Teacher!  Come arise, disciples of Hephaestus.  Bestow upon me a worthy shield!!"
units.note: MG summons only the disciples of Hephaestus; UP restores Hephaestus himself and his disciples.
units.japanese: さぁさお出でなさい、ヘパイストスと弟子たち。我に相応しき楯を与え給えぇえ！！」

units.text: "Of course I haven't forgotten, Teacher! Come arise, disciples of Hephaestus. Bestow upon me a worthy shield!!"
units.note: MG summons only the disciples of Hephaestus; UP restores Hephaestus himself and his disciples.
units.japanese: 「もちろん忘れませんとも、お師匠様ァ！　さぁさお出でなさい、ヘパイストスと弟子たち。我に相応しき楯を与え給えぇえ！！」

description: English makes the goddess the giver and chief god the recipient.
sourceReading: The supreme defensive wall was given by the chief god to the goddess.

units.text: That was the absolute defensive wall given to the chief god by the goddess. The Aegis Shield.
units.note: Both editions restore the chief god as giver and the goddess as recipient of the absolute defensive wall.
units.japanese: それこそは主神が女神に与えた絶対の防御壁。

description: WH says She avoided the holy spear where Ronove explicitly corrects the apparent block by saying the divine spear avoided it.
sourceReading: The divine spear itself avoided the shield, because the gods forbid an absolute spear and absolute shield from fighting.

units.text: "No, that is not correct.  She avoided the holy spear.  It is the law of the gods that an absolute spear and an absolute shield must not fight each other.  Although in the end, it means the same thing as defending against it."
units.note: MG restores the spear as grammatical subject but gives it the wrong object, recorded separately above; UP correctly says the spear avoids the impact.
units.japanese: 「いいえ違います。神なる槍がよけたのです。絶対の槍と絶対の楯は争ってはいけないのが神々の掟。

units.text: "No, that is not correct. The divine spear avoided her. It is the law of the gods that an absolute spear and an absolute shield must never fight one another. Although, in the end, it means the same thing as defending against it."
units.note: MG restores the spear as grammatical subject but gives it the wrong object, recorded separately above; UP correctly says the spear avoids the impact.
units.japanese: 「いいえ違います。神なる槍がよけたのです。絶対の槍と絶対の楯は争ってはいけないのが神々の掟。それはつまり、防いだのと同じことですがね」

description: WH turns the teacher’s limiting rebuke into a causal account of general skill improvement.
sourceReading: You have improved only at this sort of violent business.

units.text: "..................Your skills have improved from engaging in these fights all the time."
units.note: MG retains a general improvement from frequent fighting; UP restores that rough fighting is the only area of improvement.
units.japanese: 「………………このような荒事ばかり腕をあげましたね。」

units.text: ".........Your skills have improved from engaging in these fights so often."
units.note: MG retains a general improvement from frequent fighting; UP restores that rough fighting is the only area of improvement.
units.japanese: 「………………このような荒事ばかり腕をあげましたね」

description: WH has the spears scatter into a golden splash before falling, whereas the source says they descend while scattering golden spray.
sourceReading: The spears fall in front of the giants, trailing/scattering gold spray, and the giants then smash them with kicks.

units.text: At once, each of the giants lifted one of their legs high, and firmly stomped on the tips of the handles. As the earth shook with a thunderous sound, the seven lightning spears spun beautifully and flew up above the Giant Soldiers' heads. ...They scattered into a golden splash and began to fall before the giants. Each of the giants squared off, and with the force of their whole body, they kicked and smashed them.
units.note: MG says the spears first scatter into a splash and then fall; UP restores that they fall while spraying gold.
units.japanese: …それが黄金の飛沫を撒き散らしながら彼らの前に落ちてくる。

units.text: ...They scattered into a golden splash and began to fall before the giants. Each of the giants squared off, and with the force of their whole body, they kicked and smashed them. The broken pieces numbered exactly 30, and became lightning spears of exactly the same size as the original, which made 210 for all 7 of them, and all of those burst at once, and each of those split into 30 thorns, so that there were 6300. They became a barrage of thunderclouds drawing a beautiful geometric pattern, and then each of those changed into three bolts of lightning, so that 18,900 thunderbolts shot at Beatrice the Predecessor.
units.note: MG says the spears first scatter into a splash and then fall; UP restores that they fall while spraying gold.
units.japanese: …それが黄金の飛沫を撒き散らしながら彼らの前に落ちてくる。

units.text: At once, each of the giants lifted one of their legs high...and firmly stomped on the tips of the handles. As the earth shook with a thunderous sound, the seven lightning spears spun beautifully and flew up above the Giant Soldiers' heads. ...They scattered into a golden splash and began to fall before the giants.
units.note: MG says the spears first scatter into a splash and then fall; UP restores that they fall while spraying gold.
units.japanese: 巨人たちは一斉に片足を大きく振り上げると、その柄の先端を強く踏みつける。轟音と地響きが鳴り響き、７つの稲妻槍が美しく回転しながら巨人兵たちの頭上に飛び上がった。…それが黄金の飛沫を撒き散らしながら彼らの前に落ちてくる。

description: WH replaces the direction where the sun should set with the direction where it supposedly had sunk, and omits the sunrise characterization of the impossible light.
sourceReading: From the direction where the sun should set, Beatrice senses the impossible light of a sunrise.

units.text: At that time, from the direction that the sun had supposedly sunk, she felt the impossible rays of sunlight. A brilliant ray of light shone on her profile. It was the figure of the teacher, holding aloft the Spear of the Gods that had supposedly been repelled a short while ago. ...She bore a sparkle like the sun on her back, and made it shine on the incarnation of darkness.
units.note: MG retains a sun that supposedly had set and omits sunrise; UP restores the direction where it should set but still calls the light generic sunlight rather than impossible sunrise light.
units.japanese: その時、日が沈むはずの方角より、ありえない日の出の光を感じた。

units.text: At that time, from the direction that the sun had supposedly set, she felt the impossible rays of sunlight. A brilliant ray of light shone on her profile. It was the figure of her teacher, holding aloft the Spear of the Gods that had supposedly been repelled a short while ago. ...She bore a sparkle like the sun on her back and made it shine on the incarnation of darkness.
units.note: MG retains a sun that supposedly had set and omits sunrise; UP restores the direction where it should set but still calls the light generic sunlight rather than impossible sunrise light.
units.japanese:
その時、日が沈むはずの方角より、ありえない日の出の光を感じた。眩しき一条の光が彼女の横顔を照らす。それはさっき弾かれたはずの神の槍を掲げる師匠の姿。
…太陽の如き輝きを背負い、暗黒の化身を一条に照らす。

units.text:
At that moment, from the direction the sun was supposed to set, she felt an impossible ray of sunlight. A brilliant ray of light shone on her profile. It was the figure of the master, holding aloft the spear of the gods that had supposedly been repelled a short while ago.
...She bore a brilliant radiance like the sun on her back, and made it shine on the incarnation of darkness.
units.note: MG retains a sun that supposedly had set and omits sunrise; UP restores the direction where it should set but still calls the light generic sunlight rather than impossible sunrise light.
units.japanese:
その時、日が沈むはずの方角より、ありえない日の出の光を感じた。眩しき一条の光が彼女の横顔を照らす。それはさっき弾かれたはずの神の槍を掲げる師匠の姿。
…太陽の如き輝きを背負い、暗黒の化身を一条に照らす。

description: WH begins As Beatrice watched rather than describing Beatrice as seen from the teacher’s new position; it also drops her having driven herself into the trap.
sourceReading: Seen from there, Beatrice is a cornered mouse who has trapped herself in a longitudinal dead end formed by the giants’ line.

units.text: ...As Beatrice watched, she was trapped like a mouse in a cage, cornered in a dead-end formed by the Giant Soldier Battle Line. By now, the Predecessor Beatrice had seized a position directly alongside the Giant Soldier Battle Line.
units.note: Both editions make Beatrice the watcher and say she was trapped, losing the teacher’s viewpoint and Beatrice having driven herself into the trap.
units.japanese: …そこより見たベアトリーチェは、巨人兵の戦列で出来た縦の袋小路に自らを追い込んだ袋の鼠。

units.text: ...As Beatrice watched, she was trapped like a mouse in a cage, cornered in a dead end formed by the Giant Soldier Battle Line. By now, the Predecessor Beatrice had seized a position directly alongside that Line.
units.note: Both editions make Beatrice the watcher and say she was trapped, losing the teacher’s viewpoint and Beatrice having driven herself into the trap.
units.japanese: …そこより見たベアトリーチェは、巨人兵の戦列で出来た縦の袋小路に自らを追い込んだ袋の鼠。今、先代ベアトリーチェは巨人兵の戦列を真横から捕らえていた。

units.text: ...Beatrice, watching from there, was trapped like a mouse in a cage, cornered in a dead‐end formed by the Giant Soldier Battle Line. By now, the Predecessor Beatrice had seized a position directly alongside the Giant Soldier Battle Line.
units.note: Both editions make Beatrice the watcher and say she was trapped, losing the teacher’s viewpoint and Beatrice having driven herself into the trap.
units.japanese: …そこより見たベアトリーチェは、巨人兵の戦列で出来た縦の袋小路に自らを追い込んだ袋の鼠。今、先代ベアトリーチェは巨人兵の戦列を真横から捕らえていた。

description: The clause did not reach she who uses nominative she where the verb requires object her.
sourceReading: The hammer did not reach her, who had escaped behind the tower.

units.text: Before the whirlwind of this massive chunk of metal, Beatrice was nothing more than a mere speck. The instant the whirlwind started to suck Beatrice in, Beatrice's form turned into a massive War Tower. The Iron Hammer smashed the War Tower, scattered tremendous amounts of rubble, but it did not reach she who had escaped behind it.
units.note: Both editions retain “did not reach she” instead of object-case “her.”
units.japanese: 鉄槌は戦塔を砕き、凄まじい瓦礫を撒き散らすが、その後へと逃れていた彼女には届かなかった。

units.text: Before the whirlwind of that massive chunk of metal, Beatrice was nothing more than a mere speck. The instant the whirlwind started to suck Beatrice in, she appeared to change into a massive War Tower. The Iron Hammer smashed the War Tower, scattering tremendous amounts of rubble, but it did not reach she who had escaped behind it.
units.note: Both editions retain “did not reach she” instead of object-case “her.”
units.japanese: 巨大な鉄塊の旋風の前に、ベアトリーチェなど一粒の豆に過ぎない。その旋風がベアトリーチェを飲み込もうとした瞬間、ベアトリーチェの姿が巨大な戦塔に変わる。鉄槌は戦塔を砕き、凄まじい瓦礫を撒き散らすが、その後へと逃れていた彼女には届かなかった。

description: WH says there was nothing in the rose garden instead of the garden appearing as though nothing had happened.
sourceReading: On becoming aware of the surroundings, the rose garden is back to its undisturbed appearance.

units.text: If you looked around, there was nothing in the rose garden. ...The butler and the rest were watching the two witches confronting each other.
units.note: MG says the garden was empty and UP says it was the empty garden again; neither restores the garden appearing as though nothing had happened.
units.japanese: 気付けばそこは、何事もない薔薇庭園。

units.text: If you looked around, the rose garden was empty. ...The butler and the rest were watching the two witches confronting each other.
units.note: MG says the garden was empty and UP says it was the empty garden again; neither restores the garden appearing as though nothing had happened.
units.japanese:
気付けばそこは、何事もない薔薇庭園。
…二人の魔女が対峙し、その執事たちが見届けている。

units.text:
Suddenly, that place was the empty rose garden once more.
...The butler and the rest were watching the two witches confronting each other.
units.note: MG says the garden was empty and UP says it was the empty garden again; neither restores the garden appearing as though nothing had happened.
units.japanese:
気付けばそこは、何事もない薔薇庭園。
…二人の魔女が対峙し、その執事たちが見届けている。

description: WH replaces bubbles/foam of blood at Beatrice’s mouth with a strand dangling from it.
sourceReading: Blood bubbles appear at her mouth, making her brave bitter smile look more pitiful.

units.text: Beatrice wore a bitter smile of false courage, but a strand of blood dangled from her mouth, making her look even more pitiful.
units.note: Both editions retain a strand of blood instead of blood bubbles or foam at Beatrice’s mouth.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは痩せ我慢のように苦笑いを浮かべるが、口元からは血の泡が浮き、その憐れさを引き立たせた。

units.text: Beatrice wore a bitter smile of false courage, but a strand of blood dangled from her mouth, making her look even more pitiful.
units.note: Both editions retain a strand of blood instead of blood bubbles or foam at Beatrice’s mouth.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは痩せ我慢のように苦笑いを浮かべるが、口元からは血の泡が浮き、その憐れさを引き立たせた。

description: WH replaces 元の姿に戻してあげましょう, the teacher’s announced restoration of Beatrice, with You should return to your original form.
sourceReading: I shall take back my name and restore you to your original form; relinquish excessive power and live the life fitting you.

units.text: "I will take my name back from you.  You should return to your original form.  Perhaps you should relinquish this power which is beyond you, and live a life suitable for yourself.
units.note: Both editions restore the teacher as the agent who will return Beatrice to her original form.
units.japanese: 「あなたから我が名を奪います。元の姿に戻してあげましょう。過ぎたる力を手放し、己に相応しい生を全うするが良いでしょう。

description: WH says Instantly her form began to grow faint rather than describing gradual fading.
sourceReading: Her form gradually grows faint.

units.text: The Predecessor Beatrice was shocked. ...Instantly, her form began to grow faint...
units.note: MG restores gradual fading; UP retains the instantaneous-onset wording verbatim.
units.japanese: …次第にその姿が薄くなっていく…。
candidates: Instantly, her form began to grow faint

description: WH explicitly conditions revival on the teacher wanting to play again, rather than Beatrice wanting another game with her toy.
sourceReading: Whenever I feel like playing again, I can revive you, then make you remember being a corpse when I have had enough.

units.text: ".........It was fun, Teacher.  If you want to play again, I'll revive you any time.  Because once we've had some fun, I'll make you remember that you were a corpse again.
units.note: Both retain the teacher as the person whose wish to play triggers revival, rather than Beatrice reviving her toy whenever Beatrice wants another game.
units.japanese: お師匠様。また遊びたくなったら、いつでも蘇らせてやるよ。それで適当に遊んだら、死体だったことをまた思い出させてやるからさぁ。

units.text: "......It was fun, Teacher. If you want to play again, I'll revive you any time. And once we've had some fun, I'll make you remember that you're a corpse again."
units.note: Both retain the teacher as the person whose wish to play triggers revival, rather than Beatrice reviving her toy whenever Beatrice wants another game.
units.japanese: 「………楽しかったぞ、お師匠様。また遊びたくなったら、いつでも蘇らせてやるよ。それで適当に遊んだら、死体だったことをまた思い出させてやるからさぁ」

units.text: ".........It was fun, Master. If you want to play again, I'll revive you any time. And once we've had some fun, I'll make you remember that you were a corpse again."
units.note: Both retain the teacher as the person whose wish to play triggers revival, rather than Beatrice reviving her toy whenever Beatrice wants another game.
units.japanese: 「………楽しかったぞ、お師匠様。また遊びたくなったら、いつでも蘇らせてやるよ。それで適当に遊んだら、死体だったことをまた思い出させてやるからさぁ」

description: WH renders 胸が張れる as this is heartrending, changing proud satisfaction after a narrow victory into emotional distress.
sourceReading: But now I can hold my head high / be proud, having finally surpassed my teacher completely.

units.text: "You fool, it was a difficult victory!!  ............If I hadn't tricked her with the four towers, I would have been the one to die!  ......As I would expect from Teacher.  .........But this is heartrending.
units.note: Both restore Beatrice’s pride after the narrow victory and explicitly connect it to surpassing her teacher.
units.japanese: …………四つ子塔で騙せてなかったら死んでおったのは妾の方よッ！　……さすがはお師匠様。………だがこれで胸が張れるというもの。

description: WH renders 出来ねぇのは千兆も承知 as an imperative Accept that there is a quadrillion things you cannot do. The exaggerated number modifies Beatrice’s knowing in Japanese, not a count of Battler’s limitations.
sourceReading: I know a quadrillion times over / perfectly well that you cannot do it: produce the counterattack just demanded.

units.text: Come come, look look look, my turn is over, seeeeeeeeee?!  Show me your response, counterattack!!  You can't, can yoooooouuu?  Accept that there's a quadrillion things you can't do!!  You're useless against this, riiiiiiiiiight?  You actually like this kind of fantasy, don't yooooouuu??
units.note: MG retains the imperative and turns the number into a count of incapacities; UP restores Beatrice’s exaggerated certainty that Battler cannot answer.
units.japanese: さぁさぁ、ほらほらほら、妾の手番は終わったぜえええぇえ？！　受け手を指せよ、反撃しろよ！！　出来ねぇだろォオオォ？　出来ねぇのは千兆も承知よォ！！　お前、こういうのダメだもんなぁあぁあぁ？　こういうファンタジー、本当は大好きなんだもんなああぁ？？

units.text: "Come on, come on, look, look, look, my turn's over, seeeeeeeeee?! Show me your response, launch your counterattack!! You can't, can yoooooouuu? Accept that there's a quadrillion things you can't do!! You're useless against this, riiiiiiiiiight? You actually like this kind of fantasy, don't yooooouuu??"
units.note: MG retains the imperative and turns the number into a count of incapacities; UP restores Beatrice’s exaggerated certainty that Battler cannot answer.
units.japanese: 「さぁさぁ、ほらほらほら、妾の手番は終わったぜえええぇえ？！　受け手を指せよ、反撃しろよ！！　出来ねぇだろォオオォ？　出来ねぇのは千兆も承知よォ！！　お前、こういうのダメだもんなぁあぁあぁ？　こういうファンタジー、本当は大好きなんだもんなああぁ？？」

description: WH substitutes an opened window for drawn curtains.
sourceReading: They can tell morning only by drawing the curtains and seeing the slightly brighter overcast sky.

units.text: There was no way to notice the coming of morning without opening a window and looking at the cloudy sky, which had become a tiny bit lighter. It wasn't a refreshing morning.  All that could be heard was the sound of the rain, which had kept falling since last night, and the howl of the wind...
units.note: Both editions retain an opened window in place of opening the curtains.
units.japanese: 朝の訪れを知るには、カーテンを開けてわずかに明るくなった曇天を見上げるほかなかった。

units.text: There would've been no way to tell that morning had come without opening a window and looking up at the cloudy sky, which had become a tiny bit lighter. It wasn't a refreshing morning. All that could be heard was the sound of the rain, which hadn't stopped falling since last night, and the howl of the wind...
units.note: Both editions retain an opened window in place of opening the curtains.
units.japanese: 朝の訪れを知るには、カーテンを開けてわずかに明るくなった曇天を見上げるほかなかった。清々しい朝ではない。昨夜からずっと降り続く雨と、唸る風の音が聞こえるだけだった…。

units.text: There was no way to notice the coming of morning without opening a window and looking at the cloudy sky, which had become a tiny bit lighter. It wasn't a refreshing morning. All that could be heard was the sound of the rain, which had kept falling since last night, and the howl of the wind...
units.note: Both editions retain an opened window in place of opening the curtains.
units.japanese: 朝の訪れを知るには、カーテンを開けてわずかに明るくなった曇天を見上げるほかなかった。清々しい朝ではない。昨夜からずっと降り続く雨と、唸る風の音が聞こえるだけだった…。

description: WH takes どんと来い as the rain or spears coming down with a bang.
sourceReading: Rain or spears, bring it on: that is the attitude they are taking.

units.text: "Wahhaha.  Whether it's rain or spears, it's comin' down with a bang.
units.note: MG retains the mistaken “coming down with a bang”; UP restores Hideyoshi’s “bring it on” response.
units.japanese: 「わっはっは。雨が降ろうと、槍が降ろうと、どんと来いっちゅうとこやな。

units.text: "Wahhaha. Whether it's rain or spears, it's comin' down with a bang.
units.note: MG retains the mistaken “coming down with a bang”; UP restores Hideyoshi’s “bring it on” response.
units.japanese: 「わっはっは。雨が降ろうと、槍が降ろうと、どんと来いっちゅうとこやな」

description: WH expands the adults’ claimed anticipation from most likely opposing moves to every trick they could use.
sourceReading: They should have anticipated most of the moves the other side will probably make.

units.text: "That is correct.  ......However, I believe we have thought of every trick they could use against us."
units.note: MG expands most anticipated moves to every trick; UP restores “almost every.”
units.japanese: 「そういうことだ。……だが、向こうが打って来るだろうほとんどの手は想定できたはずだ。」

units.text: "True. ...However, I believe we have anticipated every trick they might use against us."
units.note: MG expands most anticipated moves to every trick; UP restores “almost every.”
units.japanese: 「そういうことだ。……だが、向こうが打って来るだろうほとんどの手は想定できたはずだ」

description: WH changes traces of a person getting out of the bedding into traces of bedding being taken out.
sourceReading: The nap room is empty; there are signs someone left the futon, but it is not warm.

units.text: "The nap room is also empty.  There were signs that a futon had been taken out, but it wasn't warm."
units.note: Both now say the bedding showed signs of use rather than being taken out, but neither preserves the more specific traces of someone having climbed out of it; UP also pluralizes the futon.
units.japanese: 「仮眠室も空っぽよ。布団を抜け出した跡はあるけど、温かくはなかったわ。」

units.text: "The nap room is also empty. There were signs that a futon had been slept in, but it wasn't warm."
units.note: Both now say the bedding showed signs of use rather than being taken out, but neither preserves the more specific traces of someone having climbed out of it; UP also pluralizes the futon.
units.japanese: 「仮眠室も空っぽよ。布団を抜け出した跡はあるけど、温かくはなかったわ」

units.text: "The nap room was also empty. There were signs that the futons had been used, but they weren't warm."
units.note: Both now say the bedding showed signs of use rather than being taken out, but neither preserves the more specific traces of someone having climbed out of it; UP also pluralizes the futon.
units.japanese: 「仮眠室も空っぽよ。布団を抜け出した跡はあるけど、温かくはなかったわ」

description: WH explicitly says he left the scribbles and hid himself, and calls the conjecture your reasoning rather than Krauss and the others’ conjecture.
sourceReading: Perhaps Krauss and the others were right: this is a game arranged on Father’s orders, with the servants leaving the marks and hiding to make the family do something.

units.text: "Hey, ...isn't your reasonin' right on this?  ......This is probably a game planned on Father's orders.  Surely, he left those creepy scribbles and hid himself somewhere, trying to make us do somethin'."
units.note: MG retains both “everyone’s reasoning” and Kinzo as the one who left the marks and hid. UP restores Krauss and the others as owners of the conjecture but still makes Kinzo, rather than the servants acting on his orders, the hidden agent.
units.japanese: 「こらぁ、…蔵臼兄さんたちの想像が当たったんとちゃうか。……多分、お父さんの指示で仕組んだゲームなんや。あの不気味な落書きを残して、どこかに姿を隠して、わしらに何かをさせたいに違いないんや。」

units.text: "Hey, ...isn't everyone's reasonin' right on this? ...This is probably a game Father set up. He must've left those creepy scribbles and hid himself somewhere, tryin' to make us do somethin'."
units.note: MG retains both “everyone’s reasoning” and Kinzo as the one who left the marks and hid. UP restores Krauss and the others as owners of the conjecture but still makes Kinzo, rather than the servants acting on his orders, the hidden agent.
units.japanese: 「こらぁ、…蔵臼兄さんたちの想像が当たったんとちゃうか。……多分、お父さんの指示で仕組んだゲームなんや。あの不気味な落書きを残して、どこかに姿を隠して、わしらに何かをさせたいに違いないんや」

units.text: "Y'know what, I think Krauss nii‐san and the others might've hit on it, don't you? ......This is probably a game planned on Father's orders. I'd bet my bottom dollar, he left those creepy scribbles and hid himself somewhere, tryin' to make us do somethin'."
units.note: MG retains both “everyone’s reasoning” and Kinzo as the one who left the marks and hid. UP restores Krauss and the others as owners of the conjecture but still makes Kinzo, rather than the servants acting on his orders, the hidden agent.
units.japanese: 「こらぁ、…蔵臼兄さんたちの想像が当たったんとちゃうか。……多分、お父さんの指示で仕組んだゲームなんや。あの不気味な落書きを残して、どこかに姿を隠して、わしらに何かをさせたいに違いないんや」

description: WH replaces the distinct 遺産 and 家督 succession with wealth and inheritance, both property-centered expressions.
sourceReading: Is this a test of who deserves to inherit the estate and headship of the family?

units.text: "......Are you saying that he's trying to see who is fit to succeed his wealth and inheritance?  ...Isn't that a bit..."
units.note: Both distinguish inherited wealth from succession to the family headship.
units.japanese: 「……遺産や家督を誰が引き継ぐに相応しいか、確かめようって言うことですか？　…いくら何でも、それは…。」

description: The narration’s alternative formulation that unpleasant conjectures come true is translated as the situation giving Rudolf a bad feeling.
sourceReading: Hard as it is to believe—or should one say that the unpleasant things one imagines tend to come true—Rudolf’s prediction proved correct.

units.text: On the other side, in the mansion... In a way that was hard to believe, ...or maybe we should say in a way that gave him a bad feeling... Rudolf's prediction was right on. ...Because the same magic circle scribble that had been drawn on the doors to the boiler room and the parlor had been found in multiple places throughout the mansion.
units.note: MG retains the bad-feeling attribution. UP restores the general formulation that something unpleasant proves right but still substitutes “bad feelings” for adverse conjectures or expectations.
units.japanese: 信じ難いことに、…あるいは嫌な想像は当たると言うべきなのか…。

units.text: At the same time, in the mansion... In a way that was hard to believe, ...or maybe we should say in a way that gave him a bad feeling... Rudolf's prediction was spot on. ...The same magic circle graffiti that had been drawn on the doors to the boiler room and the parlor...had been found in multiple places throughout the mansion.
units.note: MG retains the bad-feeling attribution. UP restores the general formulation that something unpleasant proves right but still substitutes “bad feelings” for adverse conjectures or expectations.
units.japanese: 一方、屋敷では…。信じ難いことに、…あるいは嫌な想像は当たると言うべきなのか…。留弗夫の予感は的中していた。…客間の扉とボイラー室の扉に書かれていたのと同じ魔法陣の落書きが、屋敷内から他にも複数、見付かったからだ。

units.text: Meanwhile, in the mansion... Unbelievably, ...or maybe we should say that bad feelings have a tendency to be right... Rudolf's prediction was right on. ...Because the same magic circle graffiti that had been drawn on the doors to the boiler room and the parlor had been found in multiple other places throughout the mansion.
units.note: MG retains the bad-feeling attribution. UP restores the general formulation that something unpleasant proves right but still substitutes “bad feelings” for adverse conjectures or expectations.
units.japanese: 一方、屋敷では…。信じ難いことに、…あるいは嫌な想像は当たると言うべきなのか…。留弗夫の予感は的中していた。…客間の扉とボイラー室の扉に書かれていたのと同じ魔法陣の落書きが、屋敷内から他にも複数、見付かったからだ。

description: WH makes Eva say Father and the servants are hiding where she says they have disappeared from view.
sourceReading: Father and the servants have vanished, and the mansion is full of strange magic circles.

units.text: "This isn't funny.  Father and the servants are hiding, and there are strange magic circles all over the mansion.  ......What in the world is happening...?!"
units.note: Both say Kinzo and the servants are hiding, rather than that they have disappeared from sight.
units.japanese: 「冗談じゃないわ。お父様も使用人も姿を消し、屋敷中のあちこちにおかしな魔法陣だらけ。……一体、何が起こってるっていうのよ…！」
candidates: Father and the servants are hiding

units.text: "This isn't funny. Father and the servants are hiding, and there are strange magic circles all over the mansion. ...What in the world is happening...?!"
units.note: Both say Kinzo and the servants are hiding, rather than that they have disappeared from sight.
units.japanese: 「冗談じゃないわ。お父様も使用人も姿を消し、屋敷中のあちこちにおかしな魔法陣だらけ。……一体、何が起こってるっていうのよ…！」
candidates: Father and the servants are hiding

units.text: "This isn't funny. Father and the servants are hiding, and there are strange magic circles all over the mansion. ......What in the world is happening...?!"
units.note: Both say Kinzo and the servants are hiding, rather than that they have disappeared from sight.
units.japanese: 「冗談じゃないわ。お父様も使用人も姿を消し、屋敷中のあちこちにおかしな魔法陣だらけ。……一体、何が起こってるっていうのよ…！」
candidates: Father and the servants are hiding

description: WH attributes clearing the curtain to wind, rather than the narrated action of sweeping it aside.
sourceReading: After wind and rain set the curtain dancing, they sweep it to the side to look inside.

units.text: When he suddenly opened the window, the wind and rain made the curtain dance around violently. The curtain was blown to the side. ...They could see the parlor they knew well. They were a little relieved. ......Because they had thought that maybe, there would be another bizarre magic circle inside the room, or possibly the traces of some creepy ceremony.
units.note: MG retains wind as the agent that clears the curtain; UP restores a person sweeping it aside.
units.japanese: カーテンを横へ薙ぐ。

units.text: When he suddenly opened the window, the wind and rain made the curtain dance around violently. That curtain was blown to the side. ...They could see into the parlor they knew well. They were a little relieved. ...They'd thought there might be another bizarre magic circle inside the room, or possibly the traces of some creepy ceremony.
units.note: MG retains wind as the agent that clears the curtain; UP restores a person sweeping it aside.
units.japanese: 窓をがらりと開けると、風雨でカーテンが乱暴に舞い踊った。カーテンを横へ薙ぐ。…そこには彼らのよく知る客間があった。少しだけほっとする。……ひょっとしたら、室内も怪しげな魔法陣や、もしくは不気味な儀式の痕跡でいっぱいではないかと思ったからだ。

description: WH places Battler crouching under the table where the source describes him holding his head and lying/slumping face down at the table.
sourceReading: Battler holds his head, bent face down over the table, visibly shutting out sight and sound.

units.text: Battler was crouching under the table, holding his head...  His pitiful figure made it plainly clear that he didn't want to see anything, didn't want to hear anything...
units.note: MG retains Battler crouching under the table. UP restores him slumped at the table with his head pressed down.
units.japanese: 戦人は頭を抱えてテーブルに伏していた…。何も見たくない、何も聞きたくないという意思が露骨に伝わる痛々しい姿だった…。

units.text: Battler was crouching under the table, holding his head... His pitiful figure made it plainly clear that he didn't want to see anything, didn't want to hear anything...
units.note: MG retains Battler crouching under the table. UP restores him slumped at the table with his head pressed down.
units.japanese: 戦人は頭を抱えてテーブルに伏していた…。何も見たくない、何も聞きたくないという意思が露骨に伝わる痛々しい姿だった…。

description: WH treats 延長 as lengthening novels, rather than placing the locked-room puzzle within the familiar detective-fiction framework. It also adds That one again.
sourceReading: A locked room with its key trapped inside is an extension of the sort of detective fiction one commonly reads; that is something he can understand.

units.text: "......A closed room with the key shut up inside.  That one again.  I know that that's often used to prolong detective novels. ......But, ......still...  That big flashy thing.......  Damn it........."
units.note: Both restore the locked-room device as an extension of familiar detective-fiction conventions rather than something used to prolong novels.
units.japanese: 「……密室に鍵が閉じ込められて、とかってヤツなら、よくある推理小説の延長だろってことはわかるさ。

description: WH translates 酸化反応 only as a chemical reaction, omitting oxidation.
sourceReading: Things burn because of an oxidation reaction; Battler says Lavoisier refuted phlogiston theory.

units.text: "......No, things burn because of a chemical reaction.  Lavoisier abolished the phlogiston theory."
units.note: MG retains generic “chemical reaction,” omitting oxidation; UP restores an oxidation reaction.
units.japanese: 「……いいや、物が燃えるのは酸化反応だ。フロギストン説はラヴォアジェが否定したはずだぜ。」

units.text: "...No, things burn because of a chemical reaction. Lavoisier abolished the phlogiston theory."
units.note: MG retains generic “chemical reaction,” omitting oxidation; UP restores an oxidation reaction.
units.japanese: 「……いいや、物が燃えるのは酸化反応だ。フロギストン説はラヴォアジェが否定したはずだぜ」

description: WH frames divine love as replacing gravity rather than interpreting even gravity itself as an expression of divine love.
sourceReading: Even gravity is God’s love? This is a remnant of the era when religion explained everything.

units.text: "The love of god instead of gravity?  ...Well, that's probably the remnants from the period when religion rather than science was used to explain everything."
units.note: MG restores gravity itself as divine love. UP restores gravity as the object but says it was explained by divine love, retaining a weaker explanatory relation rather than identity.
units.japanese: 「重力すらも神の愛なのか？　…まぁ、科学より宗教が万物を説明した時代の名残だろうぜ。」

units.text: "Even gravity was explained by God's love? ...Well, that's probably a leftover from a period when religion rather than science was used to explain everything."
units.note: MG restores gravity itself as divine love. UP restores gravity as the object but says it was explained by divine love, retaining a weaker explanatory relation rather than identity.
units.japanese: 「重力すらも神の愛なのか？　…まぁ、科学より宗教が万物を説明した時代の名残だろうぜ」

description: WH defines Devil’s Proof sophistry as claiming that proving a negative is impossible, rather than exploiting that impossibility.
sourceReading: The teacher says Devil’s Proof is sophistry exploiting the impossibility of proving a negative fact; this local example differs because one television can be dismantled.

units.text: "A 'Devil's Proof' is a form of underhanded sophistry formed by claiming that it is impossible to prove a negative fact.  However, it is different from what I am talking about with Braun tubes.  That could be resolved just by taking apart a single television."
units.note: Both define Devil’s Proof as sophistry exploiting the impossibility of proving a negative, and distinguish the directly testable television claim.
units.japanese: 「“悪魔の証明”は消極的事実の証明が不可能であることを逆手に取った詭弁です。しかし、今のブラウン管の話は違う。テレビをたった１台分解すれば済むだけの話ですよ。」

description: WH says Beatrice might shake her staff and pluck the apple with magic, then claim she dropped it. Japanese places the staff, magical plucking and fall together within an as-if claim.
sourceReading: She may claim as though she waved her staff, magically plucked the apple and dropped it to the ground; this remains only her account of the observed result.

units.text: "That's right.  That child will probably even try to explain an apple falling from a tree with magic.  That child might shake her staff and pluck the apple with magic, and claim that she dropped it to the earth.
units.note: MG places the staff, magical plucking, and fall inside a hypothetical claim. UP retains the sequence as actual magical acts followed only by a claim about dropping the apple.
units.japanese: 「そうです。あの子は木からリンゴが落ちることすらも、魔法で説明しようとするでしょう。あの子は一見、杖を振るって魔法にてリンゴをもぎ取り、大地に落としたかのように“主張”するかもしれない。
candidates: shake her staff and pluck the apple with magic

units.text: "That's right. That child will probably even try to explain an apple falling from a tree with magic. That child might shake her staff and pluck the apple with magic, and claim that she dropped it to the earth."
units.note: MG places the staff, magical plucking, and fall inside a hypothetical claim. UP retains the sequence as actual magical acts followed only by a claim about dropping the apple.
units.japanese: 「そうです。あの子は木からリンゴが落ちることすらも、魔法で説明しようとするでしょう。あの子は一見、杖を振るって魔法にてリンゴをもぎ取り、大地に落としたかのように“主張”するかもしれない」
candidates: shake her staff and pluck the apple with magic

description: WH writes cooly in Battler’s commitment to fight calmly.
sourceReading: I will coolly / calmly pursue my own fight to the end.

units.text: "Yeah, watch it.  ............I won't listen to her babbling anymore.  I'll cooly fight to the end.  I definitely won't get provoked by her anymore."
units.note: Both correct the misspelling “cooly” to “coolly.”
units.japanese: 「あぁ、見てろよ。…………もうあいつの寝言には耳を貸さねぇ。とことん冷静に俺の戦いを貫いてやる。もうあいつの挑発には絶対に乗らねぇ。」

description: WH changes until we know the contents of the tube into because we do not know, and renders the garden’s emptiness as nothing to prove that rather than evidence for Battler’s account of the magical battle as a claim.
sourceReading: The magical account stands only until the contents are known; the current absence of anything in the garden supports his counterclaim that nothing happened.

units.text: "In this very moment, there is nothing at all in the rose garden.  Towers may have sprouted with magic until a short while ago.  However, that's just because we don't know what's inside the Braun tube.  ......It is your interpretation that it was a magical battle, and that's nothing more than a claim.  Right here, right now, there is nothing at all to prove that.
units.note: Both restore the temporal limit “until we learn what is inside the tube” and identify the empty garden as evidence for Battler’s claim that the magical battle did not occur.
units.japanese: 「今この瞬間。薔薇庭園には何もない。…さっきまでは魔法で塔が生えていたかもしれねぇさ。だが、それはブラウン管の中を知るまでだ。……魔法バトルはお前の解釈、主張に過ぎない。今この場に何もないのがその証拠だ。

description: WH calls the stage only the second twilight where Beatrice explicitly says she cannot rampage from the first twilight onward.
sourceReading: She cannot make such a huge mess already at the first twilight, and likes the garden, so she claims to have fought inside a protective barrier.

units.text: ".................. ......Hahaha, hah-hah-hah-hah-ha!  You know, obviously I can't make a huge mess when it's only the second twilight, and I do like that rose garden, you see?  To prevent any damage, I fought inside a barrier.  So it's only natural that it wouldn't have any influence on reality."
units.note: Both restore Beatrice’s statement that she cannot rampage from the first twilight onward, rather than calling the present stage the second twilight.
units.japanese: ……ははは、はっはっはっはっは！　あのなぁ、さすがに第一の晩から大暴れは出来ぬし、妾もこの薔薇庭園は気に入っているのでな？　被害を及ぼさないため、結界の中で戦っておったのだ。だから現実には何の影響も与えていないのは当然のことよ。」

description: WH retains four guns but omits そっくり, their looking alike.
sourceReading: There were four matching-looking guns, remnants of Kinzo’s western-film enthusiasm.

units.text: The adults were grasping members of Grandfather's collection, short-barrel Winchester rifles. ...Apparently a remnant from a western-obsessed time, there were four guns altogether. Those had been split up between the four siblings: Krauss oji-san, Eva oba-san, my dad, and Rosa oba-san. Paper boxes filled with bullets lay on the table, and the siblings were silently loading them.
units.note: MG retains four rifles without saying they are identical; UP restores four identical guns.
units.japanese: …西部劇被れだった時代の名残らしく、そっくりな銃が４丁もあった。

units.text: The adults were holding items from what was apparently Grandfather's collection, short-barrel Winchester rifles. ...Apparently relics from a time he'd been obsessed with Westerns, there were four guns altogether. Those had been split up among the four siblings: Uncle Krauss, Aunt Eva, my dad, and Aunt Rosa. Paper boxes filled with bullets lay on the table, and the siblings were silently loading them.
units.note: MG retains four rifles without saying they are identical; UP restores four identical guns.
units.japanese: 大人たちは祖父さまのコレクションとかいう、ショートバレルのライフル銃をいじっていた。…西部劇被れだった時代の名残らしく、そっくりな銃が４丁もあった。それを蔵臼伯父さん、絵羽伯母さん、ウチの親父、楼座叔母さんの４兄弟で分ける。机の上には弾丸の詰まった紙箱が置かれ、４兄弟たちは黙々と弾丸を装填していた。

description: WH replaces the need for a telephone engineer before the police with needing one more than police right now.
sourceReading: The problem is that they need a telephone repair technician before they can obtain police help.

units.text: "The problem is that we need a telephone engineer more than the police right now."
units.note: MG says a telephone engineer is needed more than police right now; UP restores that one is needed before police can be contacted.
units.japanese: 「問題は、警察より先に電話技師が必要だという点だがね。」

units.text: "The problem...is that we need a telephone engineer more than the police right now."
units.note: MG says a telephone engineer is needed more than police right now; UP restores that one is needed before police can be contacted.
units.japanese: 「問題は、警察より先に電話技師が必要だという点だがね」

description: WH omits 火にくべられ, the report of placing Kinzo into the fire, while retaining location and burned condition.
sourceReading: Grandfather was fed into the fire in the boiler room and burned all over.

units.text: First, early that morning. In various places throughout the mansion, a total of six corpses, of Grandfather and all the servants, had been found one after another. First, Grandfather had been in the boiler room, completely burnt. The servants had died, shut up in the various rooms throughout the mansion which had had magic circles drawn on them.
units.note: MG retains only Kinzo’s burned condition; UP restores that he was fed to the flames.
units.japanese: まず、祖父さまはボイラー室で火にくべられ丸焼けに。

units.text: First, early that morning. In various places throughout the mansion, a total of six corpses, including Grandfather and all the servants, had been found one after another. First, Grandfather had been in the boiler room, completely burnt. The servants had died, each shut up in the rooms throughout the mansion that had magic circles drawn on them.
units.note: MG retains only Kinzo’s burned condition; UP restores that he was fed to the flames.
units.japanese: まず早朝。祖父さまと使用人全員の合計６人の死体が、屋敷中の各所から相次いで見付かった。まず、祖父さまはボイラー室で火にくべられ丸焼けに。使用人たちは屋敷内のそれぞれの場所で、魔法陣の描かれた部屋に閉じ込められて死んでいた。

description: WH retains the mansion being too large but drops the adults’ assessment that it is not safe.
sourceReading: They judge the mansion too large to be safe, retrieve guns and move to the guesthouse.

units.text: They say that Natsuhi oba-san has been strict on locking the doors and windows for the night. And yet, some suspicious person had entered the mansion. ...The adults had decided that the inside of the mansion was too large, so they had pulled out the guns and moved to the guesthouse, where we had been. .........Which brings us to the present.
units.note: Both restore the adults’ assessment that the mansion is too large to be safe.
units.japanese: …大人たちは、屋敷内は広すぎて安全ではないと判断し、銃を引っ張り出して、俺たちのいるゲストハウスへ移動してきたのだ。

description: WH renders 見事 as miraculously, implying extraordinary luck or a miracle rather than commendable success.
sourceReading: If someone successfully / brilliantly solves the epitaph, the writer promises gold, headship and power.

units.text: If a person appears who can miraculously solve the riddle of the epitaph, I will give them all the gold of the Golden Land, the Ushiromiya family inheritance, and all of my power.
units.note: MG retains “miraculously”; UP restores commendable skill in solving the epitaph.
units.japanese: 見事、碑文の謎を解けた人間が現れたなら、黄金郷の全ての黄金を与え、右代宮家の家督と、我が力の全てを与えるでしょう。

units.text: If a person appears who can miraculously solve it, I will give them all the gold of the Golden Land, the Ushiromiya Family Headship, and all of my power.
units.note: MG retains “miraculously”; UP restores commendable skill in solving the epitaph.
units.japanese: 見事、碑文の謎を解けた人間が現れたなら、黄金郷の全ての黄金を与え、右代宮家の家督と、我が力の全てを与えるでしょう。

description: WH states the epitaph is written on the witch’s portrait.
sourceReading: The strange epitaph is written/displayed at the portrait’s location in the mansion hall.

units.text: ...This riddle of the epitaph was, that thing. That strange epitaph written on the portrait of the witch that was displayed in the hall of the mansion. Grandfather was the one who ordered that it be written, and the person who solved it would, supposedly, be given the inheritance or the hidden gold or something like that.
units.note: MG places the writing by the portrait and UP explicitly says in the same place; neither says it is written on the portrait.
units.japanese: 屋敷の大広間に掲げられた魔女の肖像画のところに書いてある怪しげな碑文。

description: WH renders 前回も前々回も as this time and the time before that, and マスターキー as keys.
sourceReading: In the last game and the game before that, mansion-familiar servants carrying master keys always ranked highest among suspects.

units.text: "......That makes sense.  ...Both this time and the time before that.  The servants who know everything about the mansion and who walk around with keys are all the most suspicious people.
units.note: MG restores the previous two games but still generalizes master keys to keys; UP restores both details.
units.japanese: 「……筋だな。…前回も前々回も。屋敷に精通し、マスターキーを持ち歩く使用人たち全員は、常に最高順位で疑わしい人物だった。

units.text: "...That makes sense. ...That was true both last time and the time before that. The servants, who know everything about the mansion and who walk around with keys, always fall into the most suspicious category of people."
units.note: MG restores the previous two games but still generalizes master keys to keys; UP restores both details.
units.japanese: 「……筋だな。…前回も前々回も。屋敷に精通し、マスターキーを持ち歩く使用人たち全員は、常に最高順位で疑わしい人物だった」

description: WH adds only to the escape route and makes Battler finally running toward it instead of a future route Beatrice predicts he will use.
sourceReading: She probably first blocked the line of retreat that you would eventually resort to.

units.text: "Therefore, ......that child went straight for them.  She probably blocked the only way of escape that you are finally running towards."
units.note: Both remove the added “only/finally” framing and preserve Beatrice blocking a future escape route Battler would resort to.
units.japanese: 「故に。……あの子はそこを真っ先に切りに来た。あなたがやがて逃げ込むであろう退路を、真っ先に塞ぎに来たのでしょう。」

description: WH says stealing the pieces for the 18 and descending, omitting the explicit all and having finished removing them before descending.
sourceReading: After taking all eighteen pieces away completely, she would descend as the supposedly nonexistent nineteenth person and demand witch recognition.

units.text: "......That child will probably come at you by stealing the pieces for the 18, and descending as a 19th person who shouldn't exist, thereby making you accept that she is a witch.  ......That is because now that her intimidation strategy of trying to force you to surrender by showing you magic has failed, she can only make a frontal attack."
units.note: MG restores all eighteen pieces but still makes their taking overlap with the nineteenth-person appearance rather than being completed first; UP retains the original WH wording.
units.japanese: 「……あの子は、その１８人の駒を全て奪いきった上で、存在しないはずの１９人目として降臨し、あなたに自らが魔女であることを認めさせる手で来るでしょう。……魔法を見せ付けることで強引に屈服させる、恫喝的手法がもはや通じない以上、あの子に指せるのは正攻法だけなのですから。」
candidates: stealing the pieces for the 18, and descending

units.text: "...That child will probably come at you by stealing the pieces for all the 18, ...while also making an appearance as a 19th person who shouldn't exist, for then you would be forced to accept that your opponent is a witch.
units.note: MG restores all eighteen pieces but still makes their taking overlap with the nineteenth-person appearance rather than being completed first; UP retains the original WH wording.
units.japanese:
「……あの子は、その１８人の駒を全て奪いきった上で、存在しないはずの１９人目として降臨し、あなたに自らが魔女であることを認めさせる手で来るでしょう」
「……魔法を見せ付けることで強引に屈服させる、恫喝的手法がもはや通じない以上、あの子に指せるのは正攻法だけなのですから」

units.text: ...After all, now that the intimidation approach has failed, trying to force you to surrender by showing you magic, the only remaining option is a frontal attack."
units.note: MG restores all eighteen pieces but still makes their taking overlap with the nineteenth-person appearance rather than being completed first; UP retains the original WH wording.
units.japanese:
「……あの子は、その１８人の駒を全て奪いきった上で、存在しないはずの１９人目として降臨し、あなたに自らが魔女であることを認めさせる手で来るでしょう」
「……魔法を見せ付けることで強引に屈服させる、恫喝的手法がもはや通じない以上、あの子に指せるのは正攻法だけなのですから」

units.text: "......That child will probably come at you by stealing the pieces for the 18, and descending as a 19th person who shouldn't exist, thereby making you accept that she is a witch."
units.note: MG restores all eighteen pieces but still makes their taking overlap with the nineteenth-person appearance rather than being completed first; UP retains the original WH wording.
units.japanese:
「……あの子は、その１８人の駒を全て奪いきった上で、存在しないはずの１９人目として降臨し、あなたに自らが魔女であることを認めさせる手で来るでしょう」
「……魔法を見せ付けることで強引に屈服させる、恫喝的手法がもはや通じない以上、あの子に指せるのは正攻法だけなのですから」
candidates: stealing the pieces for the 18, and descending

units.text: "......That is because now that her intimidation strategy of trying to force you to submit by showing you magic has failed, she can only make a frontal attack."
units.note: MG restores all eighteen pieces but still makes their taking overlap with the nineteenth-person appearance rather than being completed first; UP retains the original WH wording.
units.japanese:
「……あの子は、その１８人の駒を全て奪いきった上で、存在しないはずの１９人目として降臨し、あなたに自らが魔女であることを認めさせる手で来るでしょう」
「……魔法を見せ付けることで強引に屈服させる、恫喝的手法がもはや通じない以上、あの子に指せるのは正攻法だけなのですから」

description: WH has Battler ask whether a telephone-linked device would not count as remote control, reversing the positive force of the Japanese rhetorical negative question.
sourceReading: Wouldn’t a device linked to the extension telephone count as remote control too?

units.text: "There's also an extension telephone in the parlor.  A device linked with that wouldn't count as remote control, right?!"
units.note: Both retain the negative “wouldn’t count as remote control, right?” where Battler positively challenges that it would count.
units.japanese: 「客間には内線電話もあるぜ。それと連動した仕掛けは遠隔操作にはならねぇのか？！」
candidates: wouldn't count as remote control, right

units.text: "There's also an extension telephone in the parlor. A device connected to that wouldn't count as remote control, right?!"
units.note: Both retain the negative “wouldn’t count as remote control, right?” where Battler positively challenges that it would count.
units.japanese: 「客間には内線電話もあるぜ。それと連動した仕掛けは遠隔操作にはならねぇのか？！」
candidates: wouldn't count as remote control, right

units.text: "There's also an extension telephone in the parlor. A device linked with that wouldn't count as remote control, right?!"
units.note: Both retain the negative “wouldn’t count as remote control, right?” where Battler positively challenges that it would count.
units.japanese: 「客間には内線電話もあるぜ。それと連動した仕掛けは遠隔操作にはならねぇのか？！」
candidates: wouldn't count as remote control, right

description: WH asks what Battler thinks of my move, instead of asking what his move will be.
sourceReading: What is your move, Battler? If nothing occurs to you, she offers her magical reconstruction.

units.text: *cackle*, so, Battleer?  What do you think of my move?  If you can't think of anything in particular, I can show you how I made the goats carry the corpses, and seal all of the rooms with magiiic?"
units.note: MG retains Beatrice asking what Battler thinks of her move; UP restores her demand for Battler’s next move.
units.japanese: くっくっく、それで戦人ぁ？　お前の指し手はどうなんだよぅ？　特に思いつかないんなら、妾が山羊たちに遺体を運ばせて、魔法にて全ての扉を封じるところを特別に見せてやってもいいんだぜぇえぇ？」

units.text: *cackle* So, Battleer? What do you think of my move? If you can't think of anything in particular, I wouldn't mind showing you how I made the goats carry the corpses... and seal all of the rooms with magic, okaaaaay?"
units.note: MG retains Beatrice asking what Battler thinks of her move; UP restores her demand for Battler’s next move.
units.japanese: 「くっくっく、それで戦人ぁ？　お前の指し手はどうなんだよぅ？　特に思いつかないんなら、妾が山羊たちに遺体を運ばせて、魔法にて全ての扉を封じるところを特別に見せてやってもいいんだぜぇえぇ？」

description: WH makes Beatrice act out her toad oil and kitchen knife, instead of picturing such demonstrations soon starting beside her magical display.
sourceReading: Carry on your magic demonstration; before long the toad-oil and multipurpose-knife demonstrations will be starting next door too.

units.text: So, in other words!  There's no need for me to listen to your bullshit!!  Act out how you lock the door with your seven-colored magic by waving your magic staff or something as much as you like.  And while you're doing that, you can act out your toad oil and all-purpose kitchen knife!
units.note: MG no longer makes Beatrice personally perform the toad-oil and knife demonstrations, but reduces the predicted neighboring sales demonstrations to a loose comparison. UP restores the full image.
units.japanese: それはつまり！　お前の戯言に耳を貸す必要は何もないってことさッ！！　好きに魔法の杖でも振るって七色の魔法で扉を閉めるところでも実演してろってんだ。隣でその内、ガマの油と万能包丁の実演も始まるぜ！

units.text: "In other words, there's no need for me to pay attention to your bullshit!! Go ahead and show me how you can lock the door with your multi-colored magic simply by waving your magic staff. Just like those guys with their toad oil and all-purpose kitchen knives!"
units.note: MG no longer makes Beatrice personally perform the toad-oil and knife demonstrations, but reduces the predicted neighboring sales demonstrations to a loose comparison. UP restores the full image.
units.japanese: 「それはつまり！　お前の戯言に耳を貸す必要は何もないってことさッ！！　好きに魔法の杖でも振るって七色の魔法で扉を閉めるところでも実演してろってんだ。隣でその内、ガマの油と万能包丁の実演も始まるぜ！」

description: WH translates 少しは構え as told him to prepare himself.
sourceReading: I am their opponent—pay at least some attention to me.

units.text: "Wh, what are those people doing?  ......Looks like they're having a good time leaving me out of the discussion.  I am their opponent, right...?  Even though I told him to prepare himself..."
units.note: Both restore Beatrice complaining that Battler should pay her some attention rather than claiming she told him to prepare himself.
units.japanese: 「な、何だよォ、あいつら。……妾を除け者にして楽しそうだなぁ。妾は対戦者であるぞ…？　少しは構えと言うのに…。」

description: WH renders ひとつ引き出した as one removed, and 王道 as shortcut, losing the distinction between extracting a red confirmation and eliminating a standard explanation.
sourceReading: I have drawn out one confirmation; the classic playing-dead route is now ruled out.

units.text: "Why are you so out of it?  ...Alright.  So the first one has been removed.  That shortcut that they're pretending to be dead has been denied from the beginning."
units.note: Both restore Battler drawing a red confirmation from Beatrice and then eliminating the standard feigned-death explanation.
units.japanese: …よし。まずはひとつ引き出したぞ。死んだフリって王道はまず否定されたな。」

description: WH drops the fatal nature of the wound and recasts securing eventual death as determining that a wound was received and death followed.
sourceReading: If a fatal wound ensures the victim will die after some time, the fleeing victim can lock himself in before dying, inadvertently making the room closed.

units.text: "...Hmph.  A classic closed room murder.  In the case where it is determined that the victim received the wound, and then died sometime after that.  It is possible that a closed room could be constructed unexpectedly if the victim holed up inside the room to escape the murderer, and then died after locking it."
units.note: Both restore the fatal wound, doomed later death, victim flight, self-locking, and unintended locked-room sequence.
units.japanese: 「…ふ。密室殺人の古典ですか。致命傷を与え、しばらく後に死ぬことを確実とした場合。犠牲者が殺人者から逃れるために部屋に篭り、施錠後に死亡したなら、予期せずして密室が構成されることはありえます。」

description: WH renders 立派な遠隔殺人 as an excellent remote murder, making an evaluative statement where Battler argues that a trap qualifies as remote murder.
