description: With plural victims, their head and chest has defective number agreement and blurs the distributive reading that the two bodies would bear the fourth- and fifth-twilight wounds to the head and chest respectively.
sourceReading: Battler expects Nanjo and Kumasawa to be found as the fourth- and fifth-twilight victims, with the corresponding head and chest wounds.

units.text: Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa baa-chan's corpses hadn't been found. ...However, if we reasonably assumed that they were the sacrifices of the fourth and fifth twilights, ......they would surely be found in a pitiful state, with their head and chest gouged.
units.note: Both editions retain plural victims with their singular head and chest.
units.japanese: …しかし、順当に第四の晩と第五の晩の犠牲者だと考えるならば、……頭と胸をえぐった、気の毒な姿で発見されるに違いない。

units.text: Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa baa-chan's corpses still haven't been found. ...However, if this follows the pattern and they're the sacrifices for the fourth and fifth twilights, ...they'll surely be found in a pitiful state, with their head and chest gouged.
units.note: Both editions retain plural victims with their singular head and chest.
units.japanese: 南條先生と熊沢の婆ちゃんの遺体は、見付かっていない。…しかし、順当に第四の晩と第五の晩の犠牲者だと考えるならば、……頭と胸を抉った、気の毒な姿で発見されるに違いない。

units.text: The bodies of Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa baa‐chan hadn't been found. ...However, if we reasonably assumed that they were the sacrifices of the fourth and fifth twilights, ......they would surely be found in a pitiful state, with their head and chest gouged.
units.note: Both editions retain plural victims with their singular head and chest.
units.japanese: 南條先生と熊沢の婆ちゃんの遺体は、見付かっていない。…しかし、順当に第四の晩と第五の晩の犠牲者だと考えるならば、……頭と胸を抉った、気の毒な姿で発見されるに違いない。

description: 親父によく言われた is past and means Battler was often told this by his father. Dad often tells me shifts the remembered advice into the present habitual tense after Rudolf's death.
sourceReading: Battler recalls Rudolf repeatedly warning him that contracts are frightening and that careless signers deserve to be exploited.

units.text: "......Dad often tells me something.  He says that there's nothing as scary as contracts.  ......He said it's only natural that people who agree without reading them thoroughly will be chewed to the bone.  ...He made a killing through vice."
units.note: MG says There's this thing Dad always says; UP retains Dad often tells me. Both keep present habitual speech.
units.japanese: 「……親父によく言われたぜ。契約書ほど怖ぇもんはねぇって。……よく読まずにハンコを押すヤツは、骨の髄までしゃぶられて当然だって言ってたぜ。…悪徳で荒稼ぎしてやがったんだな。」

units.text: "...There's this thing Dad always says. He says there's nothing as scary as contracts. ...According to him, it's only natural that people who sign without reading them thoroughly will get chewed to the bone. ...He's made a killing through vice."

description: ガラスの破片で鋭い歯を持つ depicts the broken window as having sharp teeth made of glass shards. Surrounded with shards preserves the hazard but removes the predatory image during the escape.
sourceReading: The broken window's glass teeth make it unsafe to pass through without a prepared foothold, which the group has no time to arrange.

units.text: However, they needed a good footing to get out of the window, which was surrounded with shards of broken glass. When they had entered, there had been enough time to prepare for that, but now there was none.
units.note: MG says surrounded by shards and UP surrounded with shards; both preserve the hazard but omit the glass-teeth image.
units.japanese:
しかし、ガラスの破片で鋭い歯を持つ窓を抜けるには充分な足場が必要だった。
入る時にはそれを用意する時間もあったが、今はない。

description: 煮えたぎった describes lava boiling or seething within the goats' red eyes. Boiled eyes of lava makes boiled modify the completed state of the eyes and produces an unnatural image.
sourceReading: The new servants have goat heads and bright-red eyes like seething lava.

units.text: They weren't servants working for Ushiromiya Kinzo or Ushiromiya Krauss. ...They were new servants, who worked for the new master of the mansion, the Golden Witch Beatrice, who had goat's heads and bright-red, boiled eyes of lava!!
units.note: Both editions retain bright-red, boiled eyes of lava.
units.japanese: …新しき屋敷の主、黄金の魔女ベアトリーチェに仕える、山羊の頭を持ち、真っ赤に煮えたぎった溶岩の眼を持つ、新しき使用人たちッ！！

units.text: And not servants working for Ushiromiya Kinzo or Ushiromiya Krauss. ...These new servants, who worked for the new master of the mansion, the Golden Witch Beatrice, had goat heads and bright-red, boiled eyes of lava!!
units.note: Both editions retain bright-red, boiled eyes of lava.
units.japanese: 右代宮金蔵や右代宮蔵臼に仕える使用人ではない。…新しき屋敷の主、黄金の魔女ベアトリーチェに仕える、山羊の頭を持ち、真っ赤に煮えたぎった溶岩の眼を持つ、新しき使用人たちッ！！

units.text: They weren't servants working for Ushiromiya Kinzo or Ushiromiya Krauss. ...They were new servants, who worked for the new master of the mansion, the Golden Witch Beatrice, and who had goats' heads and bright‐red, boiled eyes of lava!!

description: 整然と率いながら describes Beatrice leading six new servants in orderly formation. Trimly directed is unnatural English and does not clearly present the approaching procession's order.
sourceReading: Laughing loudly, Beatrice leads six goat-headed servants in orderly formation down the corridor through the darkness.

units.text: As the new master laughed loudly and trimly directed six of the new servants, he saw them pierce the darkness as they came. ...Of course, she was clad in the gold butterflies that were her symbol.
units.note: Both editions retain trimly directed six of the new servants.
units.japanese: 新しき主が高笑いしながら、新しき使用人たちを６人も整然と率いながら、廊下の彼方から暗闇を切り裂きながらやって来るのが見えた。
candidates: trimly directed six of the new servants

units.text: As the new master laughed loudly and trimly directed six of the new servants, he saw them approach, piercing the darkness as they came. ...Of course, she was clad in the gold butterflies that were her symbol.
units.note: Both editions retain trimly directed six of the new servants.
units.japanese: 新しき主が高笑いしながら、新しき使用人たちを６人も整然と率いながら、廊下の彼方から暗闇を切り裂きながらやって来るのが見えた。…もちろん、彼女の象徴である黄金の蝶たちをまといながら。

description: 嘉音の面影 describes Kanon's likeness or recognizable image in the transformed goat attendant. Kanon's face narrows the resemblance to one body part.
sourceReading: The transformed attendant unmistakably bears Kanon's likeness, although the narration and Shannon continue to identify it as an impostor.

units.text: When the witch snapped her fingers, ......one of the six goat attendants, ......glittered gold and changed into Kanon. It was definitely a sight to make one doubt their eyes. ...It was definitely Kanon's face. ......However, in those eyes, there was none of that sincere glint of Kanon's. ...They were only the vague eyes of furniture that only obeyed the orders of the witch.
units.note: Both editions retain It was definitely Kanon's face, narrowing the transformed attendant's recognizable likeness to his face.
units.japanese: …間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。

units.text: When the witch snapped her fingers, ...one of the six goat attendants...glittered gold and changed into Kanon. It was definitely a sight to make one doubt their eyes. ...It was definitely Kanon's face. ...However, in those eyes, the glint of Kanon's integrity was nowhere to be seen. ...They were the hazy eyes of furniture that only obeyed the orders of the witch.
units.note: Both editions retain It was definitely Kanon's face, narrowing the transformed attendant's recognizable likeness to his face.
units.japanese:
魔女が指を弾くと、……６人いた山羊の従者の１人の姿が、……金色の輝きと共に嘉音に変わる。それは間違いなく目を疑う光景。
…間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。……しかし、その瞳には、嘉音が浮かべていた誠実な輝きはまるでない。…魔女の命令に従うだけの家具の、濁った目があるだけだ。

units.text:
When the witch snapped her fingers, ......one of the six goat attendants......glittered gold and changed into Kanon. It was definitely a sight to make one doubt their eyes.
...It was definitely Kanon's face. ......However, in those eyes, there was none of that sincere glint of Kanon's. ...They were only the clouded eyes of furniture that did nothing but obey the orders of the witch.
units.note: Both editions retain It was definitely Kanon's face, narrowing the transformed attendant's recognizable likeness to his face.
units.japanese:
魔女が指を弾くと、……６人いた山羊の従者の１人の姿が、……金色の輝きと共に嘉音に変わる。それは間違いなく目を疑う光景。
…間違いなくそれは嘉音の面影。……しかし、その瞳には、嘉音が浮かべていた誠実な輝きはまるでない。…魔女の命令に従うだけの家具の、濁った目があるだけだ。

description: 螺旋状に刻まれた溝 is a groove carved in a spiral into the small stake. Ditch denotes a much larger channel in the ground and misdescribes the object's surface detail.
sourceReading: The stake's spiral-carved groove makes it resemble a small drill.

units.text: Maybe it seemed like a miniature version of those lances western knights used on horseback. The ditch that had been inscribed in a spiral shape made it also look like a drill. ......However, the grip had an occult-like design of a demon or something, so instead of a weapon used in war, it felt like something that would be used in a ceremony to offer up a sacrifice.
units.note: MG uses plural spiral-shaped ditches for the stake's carved grooves. UP correctly calls them grooves.
units.japanese: 螺旋状に刻まれた溝は、あるいは小さなドリルのようにも見えた。

units.text: Maybe it was like a miniature version of those lances western knights used on horseback. The spiral-shaped ditches in it made it also look like a small drill. ...However, the grip had an occult design modeled off a demon or something, so instead of a weapon used in war, it felt like something that would be used in a ceremony to offer up living sacrifices.
units.note: MG uses plural spiral-shaped ditches for the stake's carved grooves. UP correctly calls them grooves.
units.japanese: 例えるなら、西洋騎士が使う騎乗槍をミニチュアにしたような感じなのか。螺旋状に刻まれた溝は、あるいは小さなドリルのようにも見えた。……しかし、握りの部分には、オカルト染みた、悪魔か何かの意匠が施されていて、戦争に使う武器というよりは、生贄を捧げるのに使う儀式用という感じだった。

description: 泥棒が荒らした後 compares the room to the aftermath of a burglar ransacking it. A robber had just broken in states unauthorized entry but omits the destructive search that defines the comparison.
sourceReading: Natsuhi's room looks as though a burglar has ransacked it, with drawers opened or pulled out and their contents scattered across the floor.

units.text: The inside of the room looked as though a robber had just broken in. Drawers were flung open, pulled out, with their contents thrown about, devastated so that it looked nothing like the room of the methodical Natsuhi oba-san.
units.note: Both editions retain the comparison to a robber merely breaking in; the following drawer and floor details separately restore the ransacking.
units.japanese: 部屋の中は、まるで泥棒が荒らした後のような感じだった。

units.text: The inside of the room looked as though a robber had just broken in. Drawers had been flung open, pulled out, and had their contents thrown about all over the place, leaving the room so cluttered you'd never believe it belonged to the methodical Aunt Natsuhi.
units.note: Both editions retain the comparison to a robber merely breaking in; the following drawer and floor details separately restore the ransacking.
units.japanese: 部屋の中は、まるで泥棒が荒らした後のような感じだった。引き出しなどが開け放され、引き抜かれてその中身を床にぶちまけたりしていて、几帳面な夏妃伯母さんの部屋とは思えない荒らされようだった。

units.text: The inside of the room looked as though a robber had just broken in. Drawers were flung open, pulled out, with their contents thrown all over the floor, the room devastated so that it looked nothing like the room of the methodical Aunt Natsuhi.
units.note: Both editions retain the comparison to a robber merely breaking in; the following drawer and floor details separately restore the ransacking.
units.japanese: 部屋の中は、まるで泥棒が荒らした後のような感じだった。引き出しなどが開け放され、引き抜かれてその中身を床にぶちまけたりしていて、几帳面な夏妃伯母さんの部屋とは思えない荒らされようだった。

description: それを尻目に means Battler enters the parlor on his own while disregarding Rosa's continuing inspection or watching it sidelong. Entered the parlor behind her turns the idiom into a spatial relation.
sourceReading: After watching Rosa inspect the room from the corridor for a while, Battler decides he has waited long enough and enters on his own, disregarding her continued checking.

units.text: If I said anything unnecessary, it would turn into another fight. For a while, I gazed at her from the corridor, figured I had waited just about long enough, and entered the parlor behind her.
units.note: Both editions retain entered the parlor behind her, converting Battler's disregard for Rosa's ongoing inspection into a spatial relation.
units.japanese: 俺はしばらくの間、その様子を廊下で眺め、もうそろそろいいかなと思い、それを尻目に勝手に客間に入る。

units.text: If I said anything careless, it would turn into another fight. For a while, I gazed at her from the corridor, figured I'd waited just about long enough, and entered the parlor behind her.
units.note: Both editions retain entered the parlor behind her, converting Battler's disregard for Rosa's ongoing inspection into a spatial relation.
units.japanese:
余計なことを言えばまた喧嘩になる。
俺はしばらくの間、その様子を廊下で眺め、もうそろそろいいかなと思い、それを尻目に勝手に客間に入る。

units.text:

For a while, I gazed at her from the corridor, figured I had waited just about long enough, and entered the parlor behind her.

俺はしばらくの間、その様子を廊下で眺め、もうそろそろいいかなと思い、それを尻目に勝手に客間に入る。

description: 肉親 means one's blood relatives or close kin. Parents narrows Rosa's statement to a single family relationship immediately before she questions Battler's claimed identity and relation to the victims.
sourceReading: Rosa says she does not want to believe someone could sell the lives of their own blood relatives even for an enormous amount of money.

units.text: "That's right.  Even if you could have received a large amount of money, I don't want to believe that a demon who would sell their own parents exists."
units.note: Both editions retain parents for the broader blood-relative term.
units.japanese: 「そうね。たとえ莫大なお金がもらえるとしたとしても、そんなことで肉親の命を切り売りできるような悪魔がいるなんて信じたくないわ。」

units.text: "True. Even if you were offered a large sum of money, I don't want to believe in the existence of the sort of demon who could sell out their own parents."
units.note: Both editions retain parents for the broader blood-relative term.
units.japanese: 「そうね。たとえ莫大なお金がもらえるとしたとしても、そんなことで肉親の命を切り売りできるような悪魔がいるなんて信じたくないわ」

description: 戦人くんにとって…親でなかった asks what follows if Rudolf and the others were not parents to Battler. In your eyes makes their parenthood depend on Battler's subjective view, weakening the factual hypothetical that leads into Rosa's impostor accusation.
sourceReading: Rosa proposes that the family-murder objection fails if Rudolf and the others are not actually parental relations for the person presenting himself as Battler.

units.text: "But, ...maybe he exists.  No, that's a bad way to say it.  ......What if, in your eyes, Battler-kun, Rudolf nii-san and Kyrie-san weren't your parents?"
units.note: MG asks what if Battler did not view Rudolf and Kyrie as parents; UP retains in your eyes. Both make the hypothetical subjective rather than factual kinship.
units.japanese: 「でもね、…いるかもしれない。うぅん、言い方が悪いわね。……例えば、戦人くんにとって、留弗夫兄さんたちが親でなかったとしたら？」

units.text: "Then again, ...maybe such a demon does exist. No, that's a bad way to say it. ...What if you didn't view Rudolf nii-san and Kyrie-san as your parents?"

sourceReading: Kinzo begs to meet Beatrice once more and says that simply being allowed to apologize would be enough.

sourceReading: Kinzo begs that, even at the moment of death, he at least be allowed to offer Beatrice one word of apology.

Beatriiiiiiiiice......  Whaaaa, hic, aaaaaaaah, whaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!"

units.text: ......At least... ...let me... apologize... just once, Beatriiiiiiiiice... Aaaaagghh, hic, aaaaaaaah, aaaaaaaagggghghhh!"

units.text: Kinzo waited, with the opposite seat empty. ......Surely, very soon, his opponent would appear there, ......and he would be able to restart this game again...
units.note: Both editions say the opponent would appear there, omitting that Kinzo imagines the opponent returning.

sourceReading: Beatrice orders the furniture to undo each costly button carefully and threatens to sew on one of its eyeballs if it tears a button off by mistake.

Those buttons are each worth more than one of your eyeballs.  ...If you make a mistake and break them, I'll sow your eyeballs in instead... *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!!"

sourceReading: Beatrice judges that the captive is still not fit to serve as her furniture, then says she will shape him into furniture suited only to her.

units.text: ".........Hmph.  So, you are still far from being appropriate for my furniture.

sourceReading: The goat nobles' mouths show many ugly teeth and carelessly dribble saliva or remnants of meat and wine.

units.text: The goat nobles were surrounding the crouching furniture... It seemed that their blazing, blood-red eyes couldn't hide their ecstasy at this new young food that they had been given. And from the ugly teeth that stuck out of countless mouths, saliva, ...or maybe the traces of meat and wine that they had just eaten, dribbled down...

description: 巨漢の山羊頭 is one giant goat-headed pursuer. Giant goat heads and they pluralize that attacker, and the plural continues through the four gunshots and charge.
sourceReading: A single huge goat-headed pursuer runs from beyond the rose bushes; Rosa lands four shots in its chest, but it continues charging.

units.text: Maria, who had been released, hugged Rosa. But the pursuers were still coming!  They could see the giant goat heads, who had given up pretending to be human, running towards them from across the rose bushes.
units.note: MG pluralizes the single giant pursuer throughout its charge and the four hits. UP consistently uses one goat-headed attacker.

description: 弾を入れて in context tells Maria to load the several spare rounds she has just picked up. Put the bullet in makes the ammunition singular and uses an awkward definite article.
sourceReading: Rosa orders Maria to load ammunition into the gun quickly while Rosa charges the next pursuer.

units.text: "Put the bullet in!!  Quickly!!"
units.note: MG retains the singular definite bullet. UP tells Maria to put the bullets in, matching the several rounds she has gathered.
units.japanese: 「弾を入れてッ！！　早くッ！！」

units.text: "Put the bullet in!! Quickly!!"

description: 頭部をつんのめらせた describes the goat-headed figure with its head pitched or knocked forward. As it fell over makes the whole figure fall before the later line where it finally crashes to the ground.
sourceReading: Rosa drives the pen into the left eye while the pursuer’s head pitches forward; only after the follow-up strike does the giant fall to earth.

units.text: Rosa pulled a fountain pen from her pocket. But she held it crooked. She placed it in her palm, in the gap between her middle finger and her ring finger so that it stuck out when she made a fist, almost like it was a stinger growing out of her fist. That stinger sliced into the left eye of the goat head as it fell over.  Was the goat head's roar a scream?
units.note: MG makes the whole goat fall while the pen first enters its eye. UP limits the motion to its head toppling forward before the later bodily crash.
units.japanese: その毒針が、頭部をつんのめらせた山羊頭の左目に突き刺さる。山羊頭の咆哮は悲鳴か。

units.text: That stinger sliced into the left eye of the goat head as it fell over.  Was the goat head's roar a scream? But Rosa's roar was different. She pulled back her fist and slammed it into the fountain pen that was still sticking into the goat head's eye. The pointed tip was gouged into the depths of its head...!
units.note: MG makes the whole goat fall while the pen first enters its eye. UP limits the motion to its head toppling forward before the later bodily crash.
units.japanese: その毒針が、頭部をつんのめらせた山羊頭の左目に突き刺さる。山羊頭の咆哮は悲鳴か。

description: わざわざ曲がりくねらせて距離感を出している says the grove path was deliberately made winding to create a sense of distance. Turned and twisted many times, and only seemed long drops that design or purpose.
sourceReading: Rosa knows the path was intentionally made to wind so it would feel longer, allowing her to cut straight through the grove.

units.text: But Rosa knew.  This path through the grove turned and twisted many times, and only seemed long.  She tore straight through it! She had always played here since she was a kid. So she knew!
units.note: MG says the winding path only seemed long without preserving deliberate design. UP says it twists to make it seem long.

units.text: But Rosa knew. This path through the grove turned and twisted many times, and only seemed to be long. She tore straight through it! She had played here often since her childhood years. So she knew!
units.note: MG says the winding path only seemed long without preserving deliberate design. UP says it twists to make it seem long.
units.japanese:
しかし楼座は知っている。この木立の道は、わざわざ曲がりくねらせて距離感を出しているだけなのだ。まっすぐ突き抜ける！子どもの頃からずっと遊んでた。
だから知っている！

description: 閃いて describes the golden butterflies flashing or sparkling as they announce the prey. Waving substitutes a physical gesture or oscillation for their emitted light.
sourceReading: The golden butterflies surround Rosa and Maria, flashing and clamoring as though calling attention to the prey.

units.text: The lightly dancing gold pursuers arrived. The gold butterflies surrounded Rosa and Maria, waving and clamoring as though saying 'the prize is here, the prize is here'. Rosa couldn't even try to get up. The violent pain from her broken ankle was so great that she couldn't ignore it, even in her last moments.
units.note: MG retains waving butterflies. UP restores sparkling as their visual signal.
units.japanese: 黄金の蝶たちが楼座たちを取り巻き、獲物はここにいるぞここにいるぞと閃いて騒ぎ立てる。

description: 家 here means the family or household Rosa was born into, as the immediately following complaint names her older brother and sister. Incomprehensible house instead points to a building.
sourceReading: Rosa rages that she was born into an incomprehensible family and had an irritating older brother and sister from birth.

units.text: I was born in an incomprehensible house! With an irritating older brother and sister since the day I was born!! What did I do?! No matter what I did or didn't do, I was always in trouble and bullied and made fun of!! What has my life been?!?!
units.note: MG changes house to family, matching Rosa’s complaint about her siblings. UP retains the inherited house wording.
units.japanese:
わけのわかんない家に生まれて！
生まれた時からムカつく兄と姉がいて！！

units.text:
I was born in an incomprehensible house!
With an irritating older brother and sister since the day I was born!! What did I do?! No matter what I did or didn't do, I was always in trouble and bullied and made fun of!! What has my life been?!?!
units.note: MG changes house to family, matching Rosa’s complaint about her siblings. UP retains the inherited house wording.
units.japanese:
わけのわかんない家に生まれて！
生まれた時からムカつく兄と姉がいて！！私が何をしたの？！何をしてもしなくてもいっつも怒られて虐められて馬鹿にされてッ！！　私の人生は何だったの？！？！

description: 数千万円 means tens of millions of yen. Several ten million is not an idiomatic or grammatical English numeral expression for that value.
sourceReading: Rosa estimates that each individual gold ingot is worth tens of millions of yen and cannot fathom the total value of the roomful.

units.text: As the witch blew on her pipe, seven colors of smoke wrapped around the surroundings. When she did, the inside of the parlor, ...had suddenly become filled with stacks of gold ingots. It looked like a shining gold-colored wall. ...If each ingot was worth several ten million yen, how much would all of this be worth? It seemed sinful to even think of that number.
units.note: MG retains the malformed several ten million yen. UP correctly says tens of millions of yen.
units.japanese: …インゴットひとつで数千万円の価値があるのだとしたら、ここにある全てで一体いくらくらいになるというのでしょう。

units.text: As the witch blew on her pipe, multi-colored smoke enshrouded their surroundings. As she did this, the inside of the parlor...was suddenly filled with stacks of gold ingots. It looked like a shining gold-colored wall. ...If each ingot was worth several ten million yen, how much would all of this be worth? It seemed sinful to even think of such a number.
units.note: MG retains the malformed several ten million yen. UP correctly says tens of millions of yen.
units.japanese: 魔女が煙管を吹かすと、七色の煙が辺りを包みました。すると、客間の中は、…いつの間にか積み上げた黄金のインゴットでいっぱいになっていました。それは眩い黄金色の壁のようにも見えます。…インゴットひとつで数千万円の価値があるのだとしたら、ここにある全てで一体いくらくらいになるというのでしょう。その数字を知ることすら罪深く感じられるのでした。

description: 蔵臼兄さんと絵羽姉さんが揃っていないと means when Krauss and Eva were not both together or present as a pair. When Krauss and Eva weren’t around narrows this to both being absent.
sourceReading: Although Rudolf was normally bullied too, whenever Krauss and Eva were not together he bullied Rosa as though making up both of their shares.

units.text: ...And when Krauss nii-san wasn't around, he was violent like Krauss nii-san, and when Eva nee-san wasn't around he played dirty like Eva nee-san. And even though he was also bullied most of the time, when Krauss nii-san and Eva nee-san weren't around, he gave me two people's worth of bullying. ......So I really hated Rudolf nii-san.
units.note: Both editions say when Krauss and Eva weren’t around, narrowing the source condition from the pair not being together to neither being present.
units.japanese: そして、普段は自分も虐められているくせに、蔵臼兄さんと絵羽姉さんが揃っていないと、二人分をまとめるかのように私を同じく虐めました。

units.text: ...And when Krauss nii-san wasn't around, he would be violent like Krauss nii-san, and when Eva nee-san wasn't around, he would play dirty like Eva nee-san. And even though he was also bullied most of the time, when Krauss nii-san and Eva nee-san weren't around, he gave me two people's worth of bullying. ...So I really hated Rudolf nii-san.
units.note: Both editions say when Krauss and Eva weren’t around, narrowing the source condition from the pair not being together to neither being present.

description: それをいつまでも引き摺る means continuing to dwell on, carry, or remain affected by those painful childhood memories. Dragged out forever suggests prolonging a process or story and does not idiomatically express their lingering hold.
sourceReading: Rosa reflects that adults are not supposed to remain burdened by childhood injustices forever, but should bury and gradually forget them.

units.text: ......Oh, but this is my memory from when I was a kid. A large amount of unreasonable things happened when I was a kid. And that couldn't be dragged out forever. With time, those memories were buried away, and forgetting those bit by bit was supposed to be part of growing up and becoming an adult. So becoming an adult is the same thing as separating yourself from all of those memories.
units.note: MG replaces dragging memories out with holding onto grudges, which restores lingering but narrows the burden to resentment. UP retains drag them out forever in an active construction.
units.japanese: そして、それをいつまでも引き摺っていてはいけない。

units.text:
......Oh, but these are my memories from when I was a kid. Quite a lot of unfair things happen when you're a kid.
And you can't drag them out forever. In time, you bury them away in the far reaches of memory, and forget them bit by bit; that is supposed to be what it means to grow up, and become an adult. So becoming an adult is the same thing as separating yourself from all of those memories.
units.note: MG replaces dragging memories out with holding onto grudges, which restores lingering but narrows the burden to resentment. UP retains drag them out forever in an active construction.
units.japanese:
……あぁ、でもこれは子どもの頃の記憶のはず。子どもの頃には少なからずの理不尽なこともあるものです。
そして、それをいつまでも引き摺っていてはいけない。時と共に記憶の彼方に葬り、それを少しずつ忘れていくのが成長であり、大人になることだったはず。だから大人になるということは、それら全ての記憶と決別することだったのです。

description: 褒美であると言われても means even if Rosa were told that the altered world was a reward. While you could call it a gift instead assigns the labeling to Rosa and changes the hypothetical explanatory act.
sourceReading: Without memories of suffering, Rosa would not understand or accept the altered sibling-free world as a reward even if someone described it to her as one.

units.text: "But that way, your 'memories of being hurt by your older siblings' wouldn't remain, and in that sense, while you could call it a gift, you wouldn't be able to accept it."
units.note: MG retains Rosa herself potentially calling the world a gift. UP correctly says she could not acknowledge it as a reward, preserving the externally proposed label.
units.japanese: 「しかしそれでは、そなたは“兄と姉に苦しめられた記憶”が残らず、ゆえにそれを以って褒美であると言われても納得はできまい。」

units.text: "But that way, your "memories of being hurt by your older siblings" wouldn't remain, and in that sense, while you might call it a gift, you wouldn't be able to accept it."

description: 日々の飽食 refers to an everyday state of plenty or freedom from hunger. Daily gluttony adds culpable overindulgence and changes the young people from beneficiaries of abundance into excessive eaters.
sourceReading: Beatrice compares erased hunger to young people failing to feel gratitude for the food abundance they experience every day.

units.text: "If starvation is healed, that person is satisfied.  Even if you erase starvation itself, no one will thank you.  Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony.  ......Understand?"
units.note: Both editions retain daily gluttony and add culpable overindulgence to the analogy about unappreciated abundance.
units.japanese: 「飢えは癒してこそ満たされる。飢えそのものをなかったことにしても、誰も感謝しない。日々の飽食に感謝する若者がいないようにな。……わかるか？」

units.text: "A person is only satisfied when their starvation is healed. But if you make it so they never starved in the first place, none of them will thank you. Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony. ...Understand?"
units.note: Both editions retain daily gluttony and add culpable overindulgence to the analogy about unappreciated abundance.
units.japanese: 「飢えは癒してこそ満たされる。飢えそのものをなかったことにしても、誰も感謝しない。日々の飽食に感謝する若者がいないようにな。……わかるか？」

units.text: "It is the relieving of hunger that brings satisfaction. If you erase hunger itself, no one will thank you. Just like how there are no young people who give thanks for their daily gluttony. ......Understand?"
units.note: Both editions retain daily gluttony and add culpable overindulgence to the analogy about unappreciated abundance.

description: とろける describes the tongue meat becoming meltingly tender in the mouth. Enchanting substitutes emotional charm and loses the food-texture image in both the question and narration.
sourceReading: Beatrice taunts Rosa that Eva’s tongue must be soft and melt in her mouth; the narration repeats that sweet, soft, melting quality.

units.text: "How does your double-tongued sister taste?  It must be quite soft and enchanting, right?  *cackle*cackle*!"
units.note: Both editions retain enchanting for tongue meat that literally melts in the mouth.
units.japanese:
「姉の二枚舌のお味はどうか？　さぞや柔らかくとろけるであろう？　くっくっくっく！」
それはさぞや口の中で甘く柔らかくとろけるでしょう。

units.text: Maybe it was quite sweet, soft and enchanting in her mouth. After all, Eva's lies were always sweet, and young Rosa had always listened to them. ...So you could say that the taste of the stimulating pepper seasoning that was added expressed the details of those lies well.

description: 呆けるように開いた口 describes Rosa’s mouth hanging open blankly or dazedly while her body remains unresponsive. Hanging open with shock supplies a specific startled emotion.
sourceReading: Rosa tries to close her lips, but the red liquid is poured into her dazedly open mouth and fills it with ghastly sweetness.

units.text: Once again, the goat head servants tilted a deep red glass against her mouth. ...Rosa tried resisting by closing her lips, but the deep red liquid was relentlessly poured into her mouth, which was hanging open with shock, and the inside of her mouth was filled with a ghastly sweetness...
units.note: Both editions retain shock as the cause of Rosa’s open mouth and lose the source’s dazed or blank state.
units.japanese: …楼座は唇を閉じようと抵抗を試みますが、呆けるように開いた口に、その真っ赤な液体は容赦なく注ぎ込まれ、口の中を不気味な甘みで満たしていくのです…。

description: 不安 denotes anxiety, apprehension, or unease about the banquet that will follow. Feel uncomfortable weakens the explicit anticipatory fear to a broad state of discomfort.
sourceReading: Because the ghastly blood wine is only the aperitif, Rosa cannot avoid feeling anxious about the banquet still to come.

units.text: ......Now that she knew that this ghastly substance wasn't a simple aperitif, Rosa couldn't help but feel uncomfortable about what would happen if this banquet continued.

description: 肝臓のフォワグラ explicitly identifies the liver course as foie gras. Liver pate broadens it to a generic preparation and loses the force-feeding association within the torture menu.
sourceReading: Beatrice lists soup made from boiled brains and foie gras made from a liver among the dishes prepared from Rosa’s victims.

units.text: "Does it please you...?  There's still much more food.  Sea bass pie wrapped in the skin of Rudolf's face. Soup with boiled brains, liver pate.  And look forward to dessert, *cackle*cackle*!!  It's not just your siblings, see?  I have lavishly arranged all of those who you have trusted and yet betrayed you.  Why don't we continue this banquet for all eternity, until your heart is satisfied.

description: 全身があわ立つほどに嬉しい describes claimed joy intense enough to make Rosa’s whole body prickle or break into goosebumps. Skin is crawling conventionally signals disgust, fear, or revulsion, the opposite affect Beatrice is attributing to her.
sourceReading: Beatrice taunts Rosa that beneath her reluctant exterior she is so delighted that her whole body rises in goosebumps.

units.text: ......You're happy, right, Ushiromiya Rosaaaa?  Don't pretend that you hate it, I know that you're really happy, alright?  If you want to laugh, then you can laugh, if you won't feel better until you've heard a raw performance of your annoying older sibling's screams, then I'll let you hear them as often as you want.  It's alright that you are so unwilling.  That's your personality, right?  You're actually so happy that your skin is crawling all over.
units.note: Both editions retain skin crawling, whose conventional disgust or fear connotation conflicts with the hidden joy Beatrice alleges.

なのに、表向きは苦しんでるフリをしてるだけなんだよなァ？」

description: お部屋を台無しにした says Maria ruined or wrecked the room during her lonely outburst. Made a mess of the room weakens the scale to ordinary disorder.
sourceReading: Maria recalls becoming lonely and acting out when Rosa stayed away with a man, ruining the room.

units.text: ".........After all, Maria always does horrible things to Mama.  Even when Mama brings a man over, Maria can't stay quiet.  When Mama stayed over with a man, Maria got lonely and unruly and made a mess of the room.  When Maria went to search by herself, she got lost, the police picked her up and Mama was shamed.  Mama, who cried after Maria didn't come home for several days, who had to be consoled by the neighbors, was shamed."
units.note: Both editions retain making a mess of the room and soften Maria’s account of ruining it.
units.japanese: 「………だって、真里亞はいつもママにひどいことばかり。ママが男の人を連れてくる時も静かにできなかった。ママが男の人とお泊まりしてくる時、寂しくて暴れてお部屋を台無しにした。勝手に探しに行って迷子になって警察のお世話になってママに恥をかかせた。何日も帰ってこなくても、泣いちゃって、近所の人に慰めてもらってママに恥をかかせた。」
candidates: made a mess of the room

units.text: "No problem, I'll teach you that I, Ushiromiya Battler, am a man who'll stand back up even after crawling in the mud!!
units.note: Both editions retain crawling through mud in both occurrences and lose Battler’s repeated image of drinking it before rising.

sourceReading: Beatrice accuses Bernkastel of entering another’s territory as a spectator while secretly betting heavily on Beatrice losing.

units.text: "Were you planning on hiding it?  You're an outrageous person to come into someone else's territory from such a great distance and work against me.  You came to watch from the sidelines, and probably to push strongly for my defeat.  I've guessed right, haven't I...?"
units.note: MG retains pushing strongly for Beatrice’s defeat. UP restores a large stake placed in her defeat and preserves the wagering frame.

sourceReading: Bernkastel compares the listener to her former self, trapped in a maze of cruel fate and toyed with at a witch’s whim.

units.text: ......Beato saw through me, so I'll confess. You are now just like I was in the past, when I was imprisoned inside Lambda's world. Shut inside a labyrinth of cruel fate, tormented by a witch, in a manner of speaking. ...I am a witch who was born from there. ......So maybe I'm like an older sister to you.  So I decided that I'd lend you my power.
units.note: MG retains in a manner of speaking and loses torment at the witch’s whim. UP correctly says tormented at the whims of a witch.

units.japanese: 「…いたいた。ベルンはいじけてどっか行っちゃったかしら？　くすくす、本当にざまぁないったらありゃしない。」

units.text: "...Ah, there you are. I wonder where Bern shrank off to? *giggle* Could she be any more lame?"
units.note: Both editions retain “shrank off,” losing the specific idea that Bernkastel went away to sulk.
units.japanese: 「…いたいた。ベルンはいじけてどっか行っちゃったかしら？　くすくす、本当にざまぁないったらありゃしない」

units.text: "...Ah, there you are. Did Bern shrink off somewhere? *giggle*, could she be any more lame?"
units.note: Both editions retain “shrank off,” losing the specific idea that Bernkastel went away to sulk.
units.japanese: 「…いたいた。ベルンはいじけてどっか行っちゃったかしら？　くすくす、本当にざまぁないったらありゃしない」

description: ざまぁない expresses malicious satisfaction that Bernkastel has received an embarrassing or deserved comeuppance. Could she be any more lame only insults her condition and loses Lambdadelta’s “serves her right” schadenfreude.
sourceReading: Lambdadelta giggles over Bernkastel’s presumed sulking and says that humiliating state serves her right.

units.text: "...Ah, there you are.  I wonder where Bern shrank off to?  *giggle*, could she be any more lame?"
units.note: Both editions retain “lame,” losing Lambdadelta’s malicious “serves her right” stance; the same wording recurs at rows 179–181 without creating another unique defect.
units.japanese: 「…いたいた。ベルンはいじけてどっか行っちゃったかしら？　くすくす、本当にざまぁないったらありゃしない。」

units.text: "...Ah, there you are. I wonder where Bern shrank off to? *giggle* Could she be any more lame?"
units.note: Both editions retain “lame,” losing Lambdadelta’s malicious “serves her right” stance; the same wording recurs at rows 179–181 without creating another unique defect.
units.japanese: 「…いたいた。ベルンはいじけてどっか行っちゃったかしら？　くすくす、本当にざまぁないったらありゃしない」

units.note: Both editions retain “lame,” losing Lambdadelta’s malicious “serves her right” stance; the same wording recurs at rows 179–181 without creating another unique defect.
units.japanese: 「…いたいた。ベルンはいじけてどっか行っちゃったかしら？　くすくす、本当にざまぁないったらありゃしない」

description: むかむかする here means remembering the claimed unfair loss makes Lambdadelta irritated or angry. Makes me queasy selects the word’s nausea sense and changes resentment into physical sickness.
sourceReading: Lambdadelta insists the prior game did not count as a loss and becomes angry merely remembering Bernkastel’s use of the concession.

units.text: ......W, well, last time, I felt just a little pity and said that she could advance her pieces from anywhere she wants, and then that idiot Bern, without taking notice of my compassion, started with a-ll of her pawns on my side of the board!! What's up with that, that wasn't a loss or anything!!  Aaah, just remembering that makes me queasy.
units.note: Both editions retain “queasy,” changing Lambdadelta’s anger at the remembered loss into nausea.
units.japanese: 何よあれ、あんなの負けでも何でもないんだからぁ！！　あぁ、思い出しただけでもむかむかするわ。

units.text: ...W-Well, last time, right when I felt just a little pity and said she could start with her pieces anywhere she wanted, that idiot Bern, without taking notice of my compassion, started with all of her pawns on my side of the board!! What's up with that? That wasn't a loss or anything!! Aaah, just remembering it makes me queasy.
units.note: Both editions retain “queasy,” changing Lambdadelta’s anger at the remembered loss into nausea.
units.japanese: ……ま、まぁ、前回は私がついつい哀れになって好きな場所から駒を進めていいわよって言ったら、ベルンのヤツ、お情けの空気も読めずに手持ちのポーンをぜーんぶ入城させた状態から始めて！！何よあれ、あんなの負けでも何でもないんだからぁ！！　あぁ、思い出しただけでもむかむかするわ。

units.text: ......W‐well, last time, I felt just a little pity and said that she could start her pieces anywhere she wants, and then that idiot Bern totally didn't pick up on my compassion and started with aaall of her pawns promoted on the eighth rank!! What's up with that, that wasn't a loss or anything!! Aaah, just remembering that makes me queasy.
units.note: Both editions retain “queasy,” changing Lambdadelta’s anger at the remembered loss into nausea.
units.japanese: ……ま、まぁ、前回は私がついつい哀れになって好きな場所から駒を進めていいわよって言ったら、ベルンのヤツ、お情けの空気も読めずに手持ちのポーンをぜーんぶ入城させた状態から始めて！！何よあれ、あんなの負けでも何でもないんだからぁ！！　あぁ、思い出しただけでもむかむかするわ。

description: 悪い遊びが過ぎる says Beatrice’s malicious playing around goes too far. She has too much bad fun is unnatural English and turns excessive conduct into possession of a quantity of fun.
sourceReading: Lambdadelta says Beatrice confuses means and ends and lets her cruel play go too far, thereby creating and exposing weaknesses.

units.text: She is sometimes mistaken in her strategy and goals. And she has too much bad fun. As a result, she even makes and exposes her own weak points. It's impossible for one of the strongest witches like me to understand why she acts so relaxed. Why she lowers her own chances of winning.
units.note: Both editions retain the unnatural “too much bad fun,” blurring the claim that Beatrice lets malicious play go too far.
units.japanese:
手段と目的を時に履き違える。
そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。
その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。

units.text: She sometimes mistakes her means for her ends. And she has too much dark fun. Sometimes, that even ends up creating and exposing her own weak points. For a super-powerful witch like me, it's hard to understand why she's able to act so tough. Why she lowers her own chances of winning.
units.note: Both editions retain the unnatural “too much bad fun,” blurring the claim that Beatrice lets malicious play go too far.
units.japanese: 手段と目的を時に履き違える。そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。

units.text: She sometimes mistakes the means for the end. And she has too much bad fun. As a result, she makes and even exposes her own weak points. It's impossible for a strongest‐ever witch like me to understand why she acts so relaxed. Lowering her own chances of winning.
units.note: Both editions retain the unnatural “too much bad fun,” blurring the claim that Beatrice lets malicious play go too far.
units.japanese: 手段と目的を時に履き違える。そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。

description: あなたに魔女を認めさせる describes making the addressee acknowledge the witch or witchhood at issue in Beatrice’s game. Making you accept witches plural broadens the condition into accepting witches as a general class.
sourceReading: Bernkastel says one of Beatrice’s victory conditions is unquestionably to make the listener acknowledge the witch rather than submit to that recognition.

units.text: What's the most important element in defense during a witch's battle? Rather than trying to win, try not to lose. ...If you lose when you accept her, then you definitely must not accept her. ......Making you accept witches. There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.
units.note: Both editions retain plural “witches,” broadening the stated condition beyond the witch at issue.
units.japanese:
……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。
これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。

units.text: What's the most important element in defense during a witch's battle? Rather than trying to win, try not to lose. ...If accepting her means your defeat, then you definitely mustn't accept her. ...Making you accept witches. There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.
units.note: Both editions retain plural “witches,” broadening the stated condition beyond the witch at issue.
units.japanese: 魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ？勝とうとするより、負けないようにしなさい。…認めたら負けなら、断じて認めては駄目。……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。

units.text: Defense is crucial during a witch's battle, you know? Rather than trying to win, try not to lose. ...If you lose when you accept her, then you definitely must not accept her. ......Making you accept witches. There is no longer any doubt that this is one of Beatrice's victory conditions.
units.note: Both editions retain plural “witches,” broadening the stated condition beyond the witch at issue.
units.japanese: 魔女の戦いは守りが肝心よ？勝とうとするより、負けないようにしなさい。…認めたら負けなら、断じて認めては駄目。……あなたに魔女を認めさせること。これがベアトリーチェの勝利条件のひとつであることはもはや、疑いようもないのだから。

description: しくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出す describes the child first weeping quietly and eventually breaking into loud, unrestrained wailing. Breaking into tears and sobbing flattens that progression and loses the final intensity.
sourceReading: Terrified of Grandfather’s punishment, the child’s crying escalates from quiet weeping until she is bawling loudly.

units.text: I would probably be scolded by Grandfather. Probably very harshly. Frightened, I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing...
units.note: Both editions use the shared “breaking into tears and sobbing,” flattening the explicit escalation from quiet weeping to loud wailing.
units.japanese: それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。

units.text: Grandfather will probably scold me. Probably very harshly. I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing, frightened...
units.note: Both editions use the shared “breaking into tears and sobbing,” flattening the explicit escalation from quiet weeping to loud wailing.
units.japanese:
私はお祖父さまに叱られるでしょう。
とても厳しく叱られるでしょう。それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。

units.text:
I would probably be scolded by Grandfather.
Probably very harshly. Frightened, I ended up breaking into tears and sobbing...
units.note: Both editions use the shared “breaking into tears and sobbing,” flattening the explicit escalation from quiet weeping to loud wailing.
units.japanese:
私はお祖父さまに叱られるでしょう。
とても厳しく叱られるでしょう。それに怯え、私はしくしくと、仕舞いにはわんわんと泣き出すのでした…。

description: The surrounding narration is Beatrice’s first-person interior monologue, marked explicitly by 妾 before and after this sentence. She shook her head lightly abruptly changes the unexpressed Japanese subject into an external third-person narrator.
sourceReading: While reflecting on the Endless Witch title in her own voice, Beatrice lightly shakes her head and continues her monologue.

units.text: She shook her head lightly. If it is called the highest level, that means that there is nothing higher. An eternal dead end, the beginning of eternal boredom.
units.note: MG retains an external “She” inside Beatrice’s first-person monologue. UP restores “I shook my head.”
units.japanese: 緩やかに頭を振る。

units.text: She shook her head lightly. If it's the highest possible level, that means there's nothing higher. An eternal dead end, the beginning of eternal boredom.
units.note: MG retains an external “She” inside Beatrice’s first-person monologue. UP restores “I shook my head.”
units.japanese:
緩やかに頭を振る。最高の到達点とは曰く、それ以上がないということ。
永遠の行き止まり、永遠の退屈の始まりだ。

description: 卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほど says boredom is so dangerous that even Great Witches bearing the title Lady fear it. This is frighteningly true instead makes the preceding proposition itself frightening and loses those witches as the experiencers of fear.
sourceReading: Beatrice calls boredom the worst poison to witches, feared even by the highest titled Great Witches.

units.text: Boredom is the worst poison that kills all witches. ......To the Great Witches who are given the title 'Lady', this is frighteningly true. It is the eternal poison that tortures them because of the eternal bliss that they have reached...
units.note: MG explicitly says even titled Great Witches fear boredom. UP retains the original-WH shift by saying the proposition is “frighteningly true.”
units.japanese: ……卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほどの。

units.text:
Boredom is the worst poison that kills all witches. ......To the Great Witches who hold the title "Lady", this is frighteningly true.
It is the eternal poison that tortures them because of the eternal bliss that they have reached...
units.note: MG explicitly says even titled Great Witches fear boredom. UP retains the original-WH shift by saying the proposition is “frighteningly true.”
units.japanese:
退屈は全ての魔女を殺す最悪の毒。……卿の称号を持つ大魔女とて恐れるほどの。
永遠の至福に辿り着いた故に苛む、永遠の毒…。

description: 静かにせぬか、やかましい is an angry demand that the sisters be quiet because they are noisy. Couldn’t you be silent, shut up combines a question and command with broken punctuation and contradictory conversational force.
sourceReading: Beatrice bellows at the noisy Stakes to be quiet, frightening all seven into hiding.

units.text: "Couldn't you be silent, shut up!!"
units.note: MG replaces the broken construction with a natural complaint about the infernal racket. UP changes “Couldn’t” to “Can you not” but still splices “be silent, shut up” into one malformed command.
units.japanese: 「静かにせぬか、やかましいッ！！」

units.text: "Can you not be silent, shut up!!"
units.note: MG replaces the broken construction with a natural complaint about the infernal racket. UP changes “Couldn’t” to “Can you not” but still splices “be silent, shut up” into one malformed command.
units.japanese: 「静かにせぬか、やかましいッ！！」

description: 告げる here means Beatrice speaks or proclaims before chanting. And I told is incomplete English because tell requires an object or recipient in this use.
sourceReading: Beatrice raises her golden pipe, speaks, chants, and makes the ruined body remember its form.

units.text: I waved my golden pipe. And I told.  I chanted.  I made it remember.
units.note: MG uses the grammatical “Then I spoke.” UP retains the intransitive “And I told.”
units.japanese: そして告げる。詠う。思い出させる。

units.text: I waved my golden pipe. And I told. I chanted. I made it remember.
units.note: MG uses the grammatical “Then I spoke.” UP retains the intransitive “And I told.”
units.japanese: 妾は黄金の煙管を振り上げる。そして告げる。詠う。思い出させる。

description: 誰が誰と connects the scattered pieces as who belonged with whom, continuing their grotesque personification as they remember themselves. Which part should go with which part flattens them into ordinary parts, while where should join with where is also missing a grammatical subject.
sourceReading: The pitiful meat pieces remember who was connected to whom and how their locations fit together as Beatrice mockingly coaches them.

units.text: By the power of the magic, the pitiful pieces of meat began to remember what their form had been. Which part should go with which part, and where should join with where?
units.note: MG retains generic parts and the subjectless “where should join.” UP restores “who was connected to who” and a deliberate fragment parallel to the Japanese sequence.
units.japanese: 誰が誰と繋がっていたのか。どことどこがどう組みあがっていたのか。
candidates: part should go with which part

units.text: By the power of magic, the pitiful pieces of meat began to remember what their form had been. Which part should go with which part, and where should join with where?
units.note: MG retains generic parts and the subjectless “where should join.” UP restores “who was connected to who” and a deliberate fragment parallel to the Japanese sequence.
units.japanese: 哀れな肉片が、魔法の力によって、自分たちがどのような姿をしていたのか、思い出し始める。誰が誰と繋がっていたのか。どことどこがどう組みあがっていたのか。
candidates: part should go with which part

description: 駄目だな and 全然駄目だぜ repeat Battler’s characteristic evaluation that the alleged hell is no good or fails to measure up. That’s just useless and it’s all useless instead judge utility and lose the recurring verbal motif.
sourceReading: Battler defiantly dismisses Beatrice’s torture as nowhere near good enough to count as hell, repeating his familiar “no good” phrasing.

units.text: "Heh, ...hehehehe.  You call this hell?  That's just useless.  Aah, it's all useless."
units.note: MG retains “useless” twice. UP restores Battler’s recurring “no good” formulation, including its emphatic second use.
units.japanese: 「へ、…へへへへ。この程度で地獄かよ、駄目だな。あぁ、全然駄目だぜ。」

units.text: "Heh, ...hehehehe. You call this hell? That's just useless. Aah, it's all useless."
units.note: MG retains “useless” twice. UP restores Battler’s recurring “no good” formulation, including its emphatic second use.
units.japanese: 「へ、…へへへへ。この程度で地獄かよ、駄目だな。あぁ、全然駄目だぜ」

description: 虚勢など張らずに素直になれば tells Battler to stop bluffing or putting on a brave front and be honest with himself. Stayed obedient changes candor about his suffering into compliance or submission to the torturers.
sourceReading: A Stake says Battler would suffer less if he stopped acting tough and admitted his true feelings.

units.text: "If you didn't bluff and stayed obedient, this would be much easier."
units.note: MG retains “stayed obedient,” turning honesty into compliance. UP restores the contrast between acting tough and being honest with himself.
units.japanese: 「虚勢など張らずに素直になれば、もっと楽になれるのに。」

units.text: "If you just stayed obedient instead of acting tough, this would go much easier."
units.note: MG retains “stayed obedient,” turning honesty into compliance. UP restores the contrast between acting tough and being honest with himself.
units.japanese: 「虚勢など張らずに素直になれば、もっと楽になれるのに」

description: どこを貫いちゃおう uses 貫く for piercing or stabbing through Battler and leads into the Stakes choosing body parts. Where should I strike weakens the specified penetrative violence to a generic blow.
sourceReading: Leviathan eagerly asks which part of Battler she should pierce next after his answer is rejected.

units.text: "Wrong, wrong?!  Right, this time me, my turn!  Whe-re should I strike!"
units.note: Both editions retain “strike,” weakening Leviathan’s stated intent to pierce or stab through Battler.
units.japanese: 「ハズレたね、ハズレたねぇ？！　さぁ今度は私よ、私の番なのよ！　どぉこを貫いちゃおっかなぁ！」

units.text: "He was wrong, right, right? Okay, this time it's me, my turn! Wheeere should I strike?!"
units.note: Both editions retain “strike,” weakening Leviathan’s stated intent to pierce or stab through Battler.
units.japanese: 「ハズレたね、ハズレたねぇ？！　さぁ今度は私よ、私の番なのよ！　どぉこを貫いちゃおっかなぁ！」

units.text: "He got it wrong? He got it wrong?! Right, this time me, my turn! Wherrre should I strike!"
units.note: Both editions retain “strike,” weakening Leviathan’s stated intent to pierce or stab through Battler.
units.japanese: 「ハズレたね、ハズレたねぇ？！　さぁ今度は私よ、私の番なのよ！　どぉこを貫いちゃおっかなぁ！」

description: 人間とトリック coordinates humans and tricks as the two things Battler has failed to use to explain the events. Human tricks collapses them into a single compound category and removes the explicit human-agent component.
sourceReading: Satan taunts Battler for being unable to explain anything through human perpetrators and nonmagical tricks.

units.text: "Even though you can't explain anything with human tricks?  Are you a moron?!  Know your place!"
units.note: Both editions retain the compound “human tricks,” collapsing the explicit coordinate standard of humans and tricks.
units.japanese: 「人間とトリックで何も説明できないくせに？　馬ッ鹿じゃないの？！

units.text: "Even though you can't explain anything with human tricks? Are you stupid?! Know your place!"
units.note: Both editions retain the compound “human tricks,” collapsing the explicit coordinate standard of humans and tricks.
units.japanese: 「人間とトリックで何も説明できないくせに？　馬ッ鹿じゃないの？！　この身の程知らずが！」

units.text: "Even though you can't explain anything with human tricks? Are you a moron?! Know your place!"
units.note: Both editions retain the compound “human tricks,” collapsing the explicit coordinate standard of humans and tricks.
units.japanese: 「人間とトリックで何も説明できないくせに？　馬ッ鹿じゃないの？！　この身の程知らずが！」

description: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする states that endless resurrection also makes endless death freely controllable. Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will is a sentence fragment and loses the causal relation from resurrection to repeated death.
sourceReading: Because Beatrice can resurrect Battler endlessly, she can also subject him to death endlessly at will.

units.text: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will. Before the Endless Witch Beatrice, all death and life has no meaning. Even death can't become the key to escape from my cage.
units.note: MG retains the fragment and lost causal relation. UP restores endless rebirths as what grants control over endless deaths.
units.japanese: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。
candidates: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death

units.text: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will. Before the Endless Witch Beatrice, all death and life has no meaning. Even death can't become the key to escape from my cage.
units.note: MG retains the fragment and lost causal relation. UP restores endless rebirths as what grants control over endless deaths.
units.japanese: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。無限の魔女ベアトリーチェの前には、全ての生き死には意味をなさない。死すらも、妾の檻から逃れる鍵にはなり得ないのだ。
candidates: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death

description: All death and life has no meaning gives the coordinated subject death and life a singular verb. Standard English requires have, and the reversed fixed pairing further roughens Beatrice’s declarative narration.
sourceReading: Before Beatrice as the Endless Witch, every life and death is meaningless because neither state permits escape.

units.text: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will. Before the Endless Witch Beatrice, all death and life has no meaning. Even death can't become the key to escape from my cage.
units.note: Both editions retain “all death and life has,” using a singular verb with the coordinated subject.
units.japanese: 無限の魔女ベアトリーチェの前には、全ての生き死には意味をなさない。
candidates: death and life has no meaning

units.text: Giving eternal rebirth and eternal death at will. Before the Endless Witch Beatrice, all death and life has no meaning. Even death can't become the key to escape from my cage.
units.note: Both editions retain “all death and life has,” using a singular verb with the coordinated subject.
units.japanese: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。無限の魔女ベアトリーチェの前には、全ての生き死には意味をなさない。死すらも、妾の檻から逃れる鍵にはなり得ないのだ。
candidates: death and life has no meaning

units.text: Endless rebirths give me free reign over endless deaths, too. Before the Endless Witch Beatrice, all death and life has no meaning. Even death can't serve as the key to escape from my cage.
units.note: Both editions retain “all death and life has,” using a singular verb with the coordinated subject.
units.japanese: 無限の蘇生は、無限の死をも自在にする。無限の魔女ベアトリーチェの前には、全ての生き死には意味をなさない。死すらも、妾の檻から逃れる鍵にはなり得ないのだ。
candidates: death and life has no meaning

description: それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そう says Eva plans to press or attack the suspected private appropriation as leverage to draw money from Krauss. Schemed to take that money away from Krauss omits the leverage mechanism and ambiguously makes the target Kinzo’s already-embezzled wealth.
sourceReading: Eva recruits Rudolf and Rosa so they can confront Krauss with his suspected misuse of the family fortune and force him to pay them.

units.text: Eva had called Rudolf and Rosa into an alliance, and they had schemed to take that money away from Krauss.
units.note: MG retains the generic scheme to take money away. UP restores exploiting the suspected embezzlement as leverage to draw money from Krauss.
units.japanese: 絵羽は、留弗夫と楼座に連帯を呼び掛け、それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そうと企んでいる…。
candidates: schemed to take that money away from Krauss

units.text: Eva had asked Rudolf and Rosa to form an alliance, and they were now scheming to take that money away from Krauss.
units.note: MG retains the generic scheme to take money away. UP restores exploiting the suspected embezzlement as leverage to draw money from Krauss.
units.japanese: 絵羽は、留弗夫と楼座に連帯を呼び掛け、それを突く事で蔵臼からカネを引き出そうと企んでいる…。
candidates: take that money away from Krauss

description: 父には到底及ばなくても concedes that Eva is nowhere near or cannot possibly equal Kinzo. Even if I couldn’t quite reach Father’s level softens that acknowledged gulf into a narrow shortfall.
sourceReading: Eva says that although she could not remotely match her father, she deepened her financial and economic knowledge so she could assist him.

units.text: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, and tried to improve myself so that I could help out with that at any time. ......However, in the end, Father never accepted that. To Father, a woman was only meant to support a man, and nothing further than that was permissable.
units.note: MG retains “couldn’t quite reach,” softening Eva’s admitted distance from Kinzo. UP says she was far from reaching his level.
units.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。

units.text: Even if I couldn't quite reach Father's level, I deepened my knowledge in economics and finance, trying to improve myself so I could be of use to him at any time. ...However, in the end, Father never acknowledged my efforts. To Father, a woman was only meant to support a man, and nothing further than that was permissable.
units.note: MG retains “couldn’t quite reach,” softening Eva’s admitted distance from Kinzo. UP says she was far from reaching his level.
units.japanese: 父には到底及ばなくても、金融や経済に学識を深め、いつでもその手伝いができるよう自分を研磨してきたはずだった。……しかし、それが父に認められることはついになかった。父にとって、女は男を支えるものでしかなく、それ以上であることを許さなかったからだ。

description: 百億 is ten billion, not a billion. The English reduces Eva’s hyperbolic count of grievances by a factor of ten at the peak of her inability to voice them.
sourceReading: Eva says ten billion complaints, grudges, resentments, and unforgettable humiliations race through her mind at once.

units.text: What's so unsatisfying, you say...? A billion things are.  Grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget kept floating through the back of my mind. And all of them built up at the same time, coming out of my throat as a shameful moan.
units.note: Both editions retain one billion instead of ten billion, reducing Eva’s emotional hyperbole.
units.japanese: 百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。

units.text: What's my complaint, you say...? I've got a billion of them. Grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget kept floating through the back of my mind. They all built up at the same time, coming out of my throat as a shameful moan.
units.note: Both editions retain one billion instead of ten billion, reducing Eva’s emotional hyperbole.
units.japanese: 何が不満か、だって…？百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。そしてそれらが一度にせり上がって来るものだから、喉の奥から出てくるのは情けない呻き声だけだった。

units.text: What's so unsatisfying, he says...? A billion grudges, hard feelings, humiliations that I'll never forget crossed through the back of my mind. And all of them built up at the same time, coming out of my throat as nothing more than a shameful moan.
units.note: Both editions retain one billion instead of ten billion, reducing Eva’s emotional hyperbole.
units.japanese: 何が不満か、だって…？百億の不満、恨み辛み、忘れえぬ屈辱がいくらでも脳裏を過ぎる。そしてそれらが一度にせり上がって来るものだから、喉の奥から出てくるのは情けない呻き声だけだった。

description: 茶の作法 asks whether Eva possesses the etiquette or formal accomplishments of tea service, not whether she can simply make tea. The English lowers Kinzo’s class-coded demand for feminine refinement into a basic practical skill.
sourceReading: Kinzo demands to know what Eva can do to please a man, asking whether she knows formal tea etiquette or has cooking talent.

units.text: Can't you do anything to please a man?  Do you think you can make tea?  Do you have any talent in cooking?  You have nothing!!  All you have done is to try and act like Krauss, right?!!  Krauss will succeed the Ushiromiya family!  If you are unsatisfied with that, then you are disobeying me!!
units.note: Both editions retain the basic ability to make tea instead of formal tea etiquette or accomplishment.
units.japanese: お前に、男を喜ばせる何ができるというのか？　茶の作法があるというのか。料理の才能があるというのか。何もないッ！！　お前がやっているのはみんな蔵臼の真似事ばかりではないかッ！！　右代宮家は蔵臼が継ぐ！　お前がそれに不満を唱えるというのなら、それはこの私に逆らうということだ！！

units.text: "Just what is it that you can do to please a man? Do you think you can make tea? Do you have any talent in cooking? You have nothing!!
units.note: Both editions retain the basic ability to make tea instead of formal tea etiquette or accomplishment.
units.japanese: 「お前に、男を喜ばせる何ができるというのか？　茶の作法があるというのか。料理の才能があるというのか。何もないッ！！」

units.text: "What can you do that is capable of pleasing a man? Do you think you can make tea? Do you have any talent in cooking? You have nothing!!"
units.note: Both editions retain the basic ability to make tea instead of formal tea etiquette or accomplishment.
units.japanese: 「お前に、男を喜ばせる何ができるというのか？　茶の作法があるというのか。料理の才能があるというのか。何もないッ！！」

description: 何でもなさそうな顔をしてる says Krauss wears a face as though nothing is wrong or acts unaffected. Acts like we’re nothing instead makes Eva and her younger self the object of his dismissal, changing concealed distress into contempt for them.
sourceReading: Young Eva says Krauss outwardly looks untroubled but must already feel severely cornered inside.

units.text: That guy makes a face as though we're nothing, but I'm sure he feels pretty well cornered in his heart.  If only he would just learn his place and die.  If he did, we could become the head.  Rudolf would just refuse.  That kid can't go against us."
units.note: Both editions retain “acts like we’re nothing,” changing Krauss’s outwardly unaffected face into dismissal of the Evas.
units.japanese: あいつ、何でもなさそうな顔をしてるけど、きっと心は相当追い詰められてるわ。早く身の程を思い知って死んじゃえばいいのに。そうすれば、私たちが当主になれる。留弗夫は辞退してくれるわ。あの子は私には逆らえないもの。」

units.text: That guy acts like we're nothing, but I'm sure he feels pretty well cornered in the inside. If only he'd just learn his place and die. If he did, we could become the Head. Rudolf won't take the job. That kid can't go against us."
units.note: Both editions retain “acts like we’re nothing,” changing Krauss’s outwardly unaffected face into dismissal of the Evas.
units.japanese: 「あいつ、何でもなさそうな顔をしてるけど、きっと心は相当追い詰められてるわ。早く身の程を思い知って死んじゃえばいいのに。そうすれば、私たちが当主になれる。留弗夫は辞退してくれるわ。あの子は私には逆らえないもの」

units.text: "That guy makes a face as though we're nothing, but I'm sure he feels pretty well cornered in his heart. If only he would just learn his place and die. If he did, we could become the head. Rudolf will be nice enough to decline. That kid can't go against us."
units.note: Both editions retain “acts like we’re nothing,” changing Krauss’s outwardly unaffected face into dismissal of the Evas.
units.japanese: 「あいつ、何でもなさそうな顔をしてるけど、きっと心は相当追い詰められてるわ。早く身の程を思い知って死んじゃえばいいのに。そうすれば、私たちが当主になれる。留弗夫は辞退してくれるわ。あの子は私には逆らえないもの」

description: いじけた考え describes Eva’s sulky, self-pitying, or defeatist idea of abandoning her ambition and proving herself through a husband instead. Timid thoughts reduces that resentful retreat to lack of courage.
sourceReading: Young Eva summarily rejects adult Eva’s embittered fallback plan to become a lady and find a man superior to Krauss.

units.text: 'She' rejected my timid thoughts. ...I understand.  ......Because 'she' is me, I understand.
units.note: Both editions retain “timid thoughts,” reducing the sulky, self-pitying or defeatist quality of Eva’s fallback.
units.japanese: “彼女”は、私のいじけた考えを一蹴する。

units.text: "She" rejected my timid thoughts. ...I understand. ...Because "she" is me, I understand.
units.note: Both editions retain “timid thoughts,” reducing the sulky, self-pitying or defeatist quality of Eva’s fallback.
units.japanese:
“彼女”は、私のいじけた考えを一蹴する。…わかっているのだ。
……“彼女”は私だからこそ、わかっているのだ。

units.text:
"She" rejected my timid thoughts. ...I know why.
......Because "she" is me, I know why.
units.note: Both editions retain “timid thoughts,” reducing the sulky, self-pitying or defeatist quality of Eva’s fallback.
units.japanese:
“彼女”は、私のいじけた考えを一蹴する。…わかっているのだ。
……“彼女”は私だからこそ、わかっているのだ。

description: 泣き寝入りする is an idiom for giving up and suffering an injustice or defeat without obtaining redress. Cry yourself to sleep literalizes its components and invents sleep as the response to Eva’s failed plan.
sourceReading: Young Eva mocks the money-extraction plan as boring and tells adult Eva she might as well abandon it and accept defeat without redress.

units.text: "...What a boring plan.  Why don't you just give up and cry yourself to sleep...?" "....................."
units.note: Both editions literalize 泣き寝入り as crying to sleep; UP further adds “forever.”
units.japanese: 「…つまんない計画。そんなのさっさとやめて、泣き寝入りでもしちゃえば…？」

units.text: "...What a boring plan. Why don't you just give up on that and cry yourself to sleep...?"
units.note: Both editions literalize 泣き寝入り as crying to sleep; UP further adds “forever.”
units.japanese: 「…つまんない計画。そんなのさっさとやめて、泣き寝入りでもしちゃえば…？」

units.text: "...What a boring plan. Why don't you just give that up and cry yourself to sleep forever...?"
units.note: Both editions literalize 泣き寝入り as crying to sleep; UP further adds “forever.”
units.japanese: 「…つまんない計画。そんなのさっさとやめて、泣き寝入りでもしちゃえば…？」

description: 肩を貸す says Hideyoshi will lend Eva his shoulder so she can physically lean on him because she may be anemic. Lend her a hand generalizes the support and loses the bodily action used to send George ahead.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi tells George that Eva may be anemic and that he will give her his shoulder for support.

units.text: "George.  Take the luggage and go on ahead.  Your mother's probably anemic, so I'll lend her a hand."
units.note: Both editions retain lending Eva a hand, losing Hideyoshi’s offer of his shoulder for physical support.
units.japanese: 「譲治。荷物を持って先に行ってなさい。母さんは貧血だろ、わしが肩を貸すわ。」

units.text: "George, take our luggage and go on ahead. Your mother's probably feeling anemic, so I'll lend her a hand."
units.note: Both editions retain lending Eva a hand, losing Hideyoshi’s offer of his shoulder for physical support.
units.japanese: 「譲治。荷物を持って先に行ってなさい。母さんは貧血だろ、わしが肩を貸すわ」

units.text: "George. Take the luggage and go on ahead. Your mother's probably anemic, so I'll lend her a hand."
units.note: Both editions retain lending Eva a hand, losing Hideyoshi’s offer of his shoulder for physical support.
units.japanese: 「譲治。荷物を持って先に行ってなさい。母さんは貧血だろ、わしが肩を貸すわ」

description: 神妙な顔 describes Eva’s grave, solemn, or unusually serious expression after the dream. Meek face instead suggests submissiveness or timidity, assigning a different emotional posture.
sourceReading: Once they are alone, Hideyoshi asks why Eva looks so solemn, prompting her confession about George.

units.text: "...What's wrong?  Why the meek face?"
units.note: Both editions retain “meek face,” replacing Eva’s grave or solemn expression.
units.japanese: 「…どないしたんや。神妙な顔して。」

units.text: "...What's wrong? Why the meek face?"
units.note: Both editions retain “meek face,” replacing Eva’s grave or solemn expression.
units.japanese: 「…どないしたんや。神妙な顔して」

units.text: "...What's wrong? Why the meek face?"
units.note: Both editions retain “meek face,” replacing Eva’s grave or solemn expression.
units.japanese: 「…どないしたんや。神妙な顔して」

description: イカレて means Hideyoshi claims his tie pin has gone wrong or broken. Got a bit crooked turns the invented malfunction into a minor alignment problem.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi hides Eva’s face and gives Kumasawa a deliberately vague excuse that his tie pin has broken.

units.text: "Yeah, sorry.  My necktie pin just got a little crooked!  We're alright, and we'll be out in a second.  Wait outside for us!"
units.note: Both editions retain a crooked tie pin instead of Hideyoshi’s claim that it has broken or malfunctioned.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、すまんなぁ。ちょいとわしのネクタイピンがイカレてもうてな！　もう大丈夫や、すぐ行くで。外で待っててや！」

units.text: "Yeah, sorry. My necktie pin just got a bit crooked! We're fine, and we'll be out in a sec. Wait outside for us!"
units.note: Both editions retain a crooked tie pin instead of Hideyoshi’s claim that it has broken or malfunctioned.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、すまんなぁ。ちょいとわしのネクタイピンがイカレてもうてな！　もう大丈夫や、すぐ行くで。外で待っててや！」

units.text: "Yeah, sorry. My necktie pin just got a little crooked! We're alright, and we'll be out in a second. Wait outside for us!"
units.note: Both editions retain a crooked tie pin instead of Hideyoshi’s claim that it has broken or malfunctioned.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、すまんなぁ。ちょいとわしのネクタイピンがイカレてもうてな！　もう大丈夫や、すぐ行くで。外で待っててや！」

description: 婦人病 is Hideyoshi’s euphemistic claim that Eva has a gynecological or women’s complaint. A woman’s disease is unnatural English and sounds like an unspecified literal disease rather than his embarrassing gendered cover story.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi jokingly tells Gohda that Eva’s brief weakness is a women’s health issue and not to worry, embarrassing Eva.

units.text: "It's a woman's disease.  Don't worry about it.  Wahhahahahahaha."
units.note: MG retains the unnatural “woman’s disease.” UP uses the natural euphemism “her hormones,” which is somewhat more specific than the broad Japanese complaint but fits Hideyoshi’s cover story.
units.japanese: 「婦人病っちゅうやっちゃ。気にせんといてや。わっはははははは。」

units.text: "It's a woman's disease. Don't worry about it. Wahhahahahahaha."
units.note: MG retains the unnatural “woman’s disease.” UP uses the natural euphemism “her hormones,” which is somewhat more specific than the broad Japanese complaint but fits Hideyoshi’s cover story.
units.japanese: 「婦人病っちゅうやっちゃ。気にせんといてや。わっはははははは」

description: 脇腹 is Hideyoshi’s side or flank. Gut relocates Eva’s elbow jab to the front of his abdomen.
sourceReading: Embarrassed by Hideyoshi’s public excuse, Eva gives him a small elbow jab in the side after telling him not to say such things.

units.text: Eva elbowed Hideyoshi in the gut. By that time, her normal expression had returned, which allowed Hideyoshi to relax a little.
units.note: Both editions retain Eva elbowing Hideyoshi in the gut instead of his side or flank.
units.japanese: 絵羽が肘で秀吉の脇腹を小突く。

units.text: Eva elbowed Hideyoshi in the gut. By that time, her normal expression had returned, which allowed Hideyoshi to relax a little.
units.note: Both editions retain Eva elbowing Hideyoshi in the gut instead of his side or flank.
units.japanese: 絵羽が肘で秀吉の脇腹を小突く。その時にはもう、いつもの表情に戻っていたので、秀吉は少し安心するのだった。

description: 汚れた大人 expresses Eva’s sense that adulthood has tainted, sullied, or corrupted her, distancing her from her younger voice. Shameless adult instead says she lacks shame, assigning a different moral defect.
sourceReading: Eva realizes that her younger self’s voice feels distant because she has become a sullied adult.

units.text: After becoming a shameless adult, ...the voice of her young self was distant.
units.note: Both editions retain “shameless adult,” changing Eva’s sense of being tainted or corrupted into lack of shame.
units.japanese: 汚れた大人になってしまったから、

units.text: After becoming a shameless adult, ...the voice of her young self was distant.
units.note: Both editions retain “shameless adult,” changing Eva’s sense of being tainted or corrupted into lack of shame.
units.japanese: 汚れた大人になってしまったから、…少女時代の声が、遠いのだ。

description: ケツが痒くなってきた gives Battler a deliberately crude, bodily image—his ass is starting to itch—from realizing Shannon suppressed romantic lines from his childhood crush. I can’t take it replaces that specific comic embarrassment with generic distress.
sourceReading: Battler groans that his ass is starting to itch as he realizes the omitted embarrassing remarks probably concerned his old attraction to Shannon.

units.text: .........Which means that, the collection of my embarrassing lines that Shannon-chan had just held back on, ......probably had something to do with that...  Aaaaaaaaaaarrghh, I can't take it...
units.note: Both editions replace Battler’s itching-ass metaphor with the generic “I can’t take it.”
units.japanese: ………ってことは、さっき紗音ちゃんが自重してくれた、俺の６年前の恥ずかしいセリフ集は、……それ関係って可能性が高いな…。うぉおおおおぉおぉおぉ、ケツが痒くなってきたぜ…。

units.text: ......Which means that...the collection of embarrassing lines Shannon-chan had just held back on... probably had something to do with that... Aaaaaaaaaaarrghh, I can't take it...
units.note: Both editions replace Battler’s itching-ass metaphor with the generic “I can’t take it.”
