units.text: .........Which means that...my collection of embarrassing lines that Shannon‐chan just held back on... ...probably has something to do with that... Aaaaaaaaaaarrghh, I can't take it...
units.note: Both editions replace Battler’s itching-ass metaphor with the generic “I can’t take it.”
units.japanese: ………ってことは、さっき紗音ちゃんが自重してくれた、俺の６年前の恥ずかしいセリフ集は、……それ関係って可能性が高いな…。うぉおおおおぉおぉおぉ、ケツが痒くなってきたぜ…。

description: ズルイ calls women unfair, sneaky, or underhanded for asking questions while refusing to answer them. Cruel assigns callous harmfulness rather than the conversational double standard Battler is complaining about.
sourceReading: After Jessica angrily evades the same romantic question she asked him, Battler jokes that women are unfair creatures who ask but never answer.

units.text: "Even though you're the one who brought up this subject, why do you have to betray me like this?  Women are creatures who always ask questions, and yet, they almost never answer them.  What cruel creatures, seriously."
units.note: Both editions retain “cruel” for Battler’s accusation that women are unfair or sly about asking and answering questions.
units.japanese: 「話を振ってきたのはそっちのくせに、何で俺が逆ギレされなきゃならねぇんだ。女って生き物は質問ばかりで、そのくせ、自分が質問に答えることは決してないんだよな。ズルイ生き物だぜ、まったく。」

units.text: "If you're the one who brought up this subject, why are you yelling at me now? Women are creatures who always ask questions, and yet almost never answer them. What cruel creatures, seriously."
units.note: Both editions retain “cruel” for Battler’s accusation that women are unfair or sly about asking and answering questions.
units.japanese: 「話を振ってきたのはそっちのくせに、何で俺が逆ギレされなきゃならねぇんだ。女って生き物は質問ばかりで、そのくせ、自分が質問に答えることは決してないんだよな。ズルイ生き物だぜ、まったく」

units.text: "You're the one who brought up this subject, why do you have to go and get mad at me? Women are creatures who always ask questions, and yet, they almost never answer them. What cruel creatures, seriously."
units.note: Both editions retain “cruel” for Battler’s accusation that women are unfair or sly about asking and answering questions.
units.japanese: 「話を振ってきたのはそっちのくせに、何で俺が逆ギレされなきゃならねぇんだ。女って生き物は質問ばかりで、そのくせ、自分が質問に答えることは決してないんだよな。ズルイ生き物だぜ、まったく」

description: 青春時代 means youth or adolescence as a life period. Six years of puberty substitutes the biological maturation process and makes the entire six-year span one of puberty.
sourceReading: Battler reflects that six years during one’s youth carry great weight and pass quickly.

units.text: Six years.  ...Six years of puberty are pretty important, and they had gone by pretty fast.
units.note: Both editions retain “six years of puberty” instead of six years during youth or adolescence.
units.japanese: ６年か。…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。

units.text: Six years. ...Six years of puberty are pretty important, and they went by pretty fast.
units.note: Both editions retain “six years of puberty” instead of six years during youth or adolescence.
units.japanese: ６年か。…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。

units.text: Six years. ...Those six years of puberty are pretty important, and they go by so fast.
units.note: Both editions retain “six years of puberty” instead of six years during youth or adolescence.
units.japanese: ６年か。…青春時代の６年ってのは重く、そして早いもんだ。

description: 恥ずかしいことのついでだ presents the proposed vow as something to do while they are already saying embarrassing things. Now the next embarrassing thing instead announces a separate item in a sequence.
sourceReading: Jessica uses their existing embarrassment as an opening to propose that the cousins swear to believe in their lasting friendship and happiness.

units.text: "Alright.  Now the next embarrassing thing.  Let's all swear to believe together, alright?  That we'll all always be friendly, that we'll always be happy."
units.note: MG restores Jessica using the existing embarrassing talk as an opening for the vow. UP retains the announcement of “the next embarrassing thing.”
units.japanese: 「よし。なら恥ずかしいことのついでだ。私たちはみんなで信じ合うと誓おうぜ？　みんないつまでも仲良しで、いつまでも幸せでいようって。」

units.text: "Alright. Now the next embarrassing thing. Let's all swear to believe together, alright? That we'll all always be friendly, that we'll always be happy."
units.note: MG restores Jessica using the existing embarrassing talk as an opening for the vow. UP retains the announcement of “the next embarrassing thing.”
units.japanese: 「よし。なら恥ずかしいことのついでだ。私たちはみんなで信じ合うと誓おうぜ？　みんないつまでも仲良しで、いつまでも幸せでいようって」

description: 青春し describes the cousins actively living or enjoying their youth as they renew their friendship. As youthful as we were reduces that activity to possessing the quality of youth.
sourceReading: Battler insists that the cousins are fully enjoying their youth and renewing their old friendship despite the adults' schemes and the approaching storm.

units.text: Who cares about what our parents expect? Who cares about the inheritance and the honor of our old family? As youthful as we were, we were renewing our old friendship. And we all believed together that we could all be happy.
units.note: MG retains “As youthful as we were,” and UP revises it to “We’re so young”; both reduce actively enjoying youth to simply being young.
units.japanese: 俺たちはこんなにも青春し、旧交を温めあっているんだ。

units.text: Who cares about what our parents are planning? Who cares about the inheritance and the honor of our old family? As youthful as we were, we were renewing our old friendship. And we all believed together that we could find happiness.
units.note: MG retains “As youthful as we were,” and UP revises it to “We’re so young”; both reduce actively enjoying youth to simply being young.
units.japanese:
親たちの思惑なんか知ったことか。
遺産も旧家とやらの面子も知ったことじゃない。俺たちはこんなにも青春し、旧交を温めあっているんだ。
そして、みんながみんな、幸せになれると信じ合ってる。

units.text:
Who gives a crap about what our parents are plotting?
Who gives a crap about the inheritance and the honor of our old family? We're so young, and renewing our old friendship.
And every one of us believes together that we can all be happy.
units.note: MG retains “As youthful as we were,” and UP revises it to “We’re so young”; both reduce actively enjoying youth to simply being young.
units.japanese:
親たちの思惑なんか知ったことか。
遺産も旧家とやらの面子も知ったことじゃない。俺たちはこんなにも青春し、旧交を温めあっているんだ。
そして、みんながみんな、幸せになれると信じ合ってる。

description: ちょんと describes Beatrice giving the golden flower a light little poke. In just the right way replaces the poke's delicate manner with procedural correctness.
sourceReading: Beatrice lightly taps the golden flower, and its glow scatters like a bursting golden soap bubble.

units.text: Then, the fully grown rose bloomed, creating one golden flower. And when Beatrice poked it with her finger in just the right way, the gold-colored sparkle scattered, just as if a golden soap bubble had popped, and what remained was a single beautiful rose.
units.note: Both editions retain “poked it ... in just the right way,” replacing Beatrice’s light little poke with procedural correctness.
units.japanese: それにベアトリーチェが、ちょんと指で突っつくと、まるで黄金のシャボン玉が割れるかのように金色の輝きは飛び散り、後には美しい一輪の薔薇が残るのだった。

units.text: Then, the fully-grown rose bloomed, creating one golden flower. And when Beatrice poked it with her finger in just the right way, the gold-colored sparkle scattered, just as if a golden soap bubble had popped, and what remained was a single beautiful rose.
units.note: Both editions retain “poked it ... in just the right way,” replacing Beatrice’s light little poke with procedural correctness.
units.japanese: そして延びた薔薇は、大きな黄金の花を一輪、開花させる。それにベアトリーチェが、ちょんと指で突っつくと、まるで黄金のシャボン玉が割れるかのように金色の輝きは飛び散り、後には美しい一輪の薔薇が残るのだった。

units.text: Then, the fully grown rose bloomed, creating one golden flower. And when Beatrice poked it with her finger in just the right way, the gold‐colored sparkles scattered, just as if a golden soap bubble had popped, and what remained was a single beautiful rose.
units.note: Both editions retain “poked it ... in just the right way,” replacing Beatrice’s light little poke with procedural correctness.
units.japanese: そして延びた薔薇は、大きな黄金の花を一輪、開花させる。それにベアトリーチェが、ちょんと指で突っつくと、まるで黄金のシャボン玉が割れるかのように金色の輝きは飛び散り、後には美しい一輪の薔薇が残るのだった。

description: もうひとつ offers one more service, with no claim that it will be the final one. One last service adds finality absent from Beatrice's offer.
sourceReading: Beatrice offers Maria one more favor by marking the revived rose so it can be distinguished from the others.

units.text: ......However, if we just leave it mixed in with these other roses, you won't be able to tell it apart.  Shall I perform one last service?"
units.note: Both editions retain “one last service,” adding finality to Beatrice’s offer of one more service.
units.japanese: ……だが、このままでは他の薔薇たちに混じってしまい、区別がつかなくなってしまうというものよ。もうひとつサービスしておくか。」

units.text: ...However, if we just leave it mixed in with these other roses, you won't be able to tell it apart. Shall I perform one last service?"
units.note: Both editions retain “one last service,” adding finality to Beatrice’s offer of one more service.
units.japanese: 「……だが、このままでは他の薔薇たちに混じってしまい、区別がつかなくなってしまうというものよ。もうひとつサービスしておくか」

units.text: "......However, if we just leave it mixed in with these other roses, you won't be able to tell it apart. Shall I perform one last service?"
units.note: Both editions retain “one last service,” adding finality to Beatrice’s offer of one more service.

description: なおも唸り続けて says Maria is still continuing to groan while concentrating. Moaning even more now introduces an increase in intensity rather than persistence.
sourceReading: Maria keeps her eyes shut and continues groaning in concentration while Beatrice adds a marker to the rose.

units.text: Beatrice, for the sake of her cute apprentice witch who was moaning even more now in concentration, decided to use one more bit of magic. When she snapped her fingers, a single gold butterfly appeared, fluttered around, and landed on the flower that had just been revived. Then it suddenly burst open and disappeared, becoming golden lace and marking the rose...
units.note: Both editions retain “moaning even more now,” changing Maria’s continued groaning into increased intensity.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、なおも唸り続けて集中を続けている可愛い見習い魔女のために、もうひとつだけ魔法を掛けることにする。

units.text: Beatrice, for the sake of her cute apprentice who was moaning even more now in concentration, decided to use one more bit of magic. When she snapped her fingers, a single gold butterfly appeared, fluttered around, and landed on the flower that had just been revived. Then it suddenly burst open and disappeared, becoming golden lace and marking the rose...
units.note: Both editions retain “moaning even more now,” changing Maria’s continued groaning into increased intensity.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、なおも唸り続けて集中を続けている可愛い見習い魔女のために、もうひとつだけ魔法を掛けることにする。パチンと指を鳴らすと、黄金の蝶が一匹現れ、ひらひらと舞い、蘇ったばかりの花に止まる。それは再び、パチンと弾けて姿を消すと、金色のモールになって目印となってくれた…。

units.text: Beatrice, for the sake of her cute apprentice witch who was moaning even more now in concentration, decided to cast one more little spell. She snapped her fingers, and a single gold butterfly appeared, fluttered around, and landed on the flower that had just been revived. Then it suddenly burst open and disappeared, becoming golden lace and marking the rose...
units.note: Both editions retain “moaning even more now,” changing Maria’s continued groaning into increased intensity.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、なおも唸り続けて集中を続けている可愛い見習い魔女のために、もうひとつだけ魔法を掛けることにする。パチンと指を鳴らすと、黄金の蝶が一匹現れ、ひらひらと舞い、蘇ったばかりの花に止まる。それは再び、パチンと弾けて姿を消すと、金色のモールになって目印となってくれた…。

description: アンティを支払う uses the standard gambling action of paying or putting up the ante. Make the ante is nonstandard here and obscures Kinzo's declaration that he is staking the ring.
sourceReading: Kinzo announces that he will pay the ante for the game and returns the golden ring Beatrice once gave him.

units.text: So, let us make the ante.  All that you have given should be returned to you in the end.  Come, take it!!"
units.note: MG retains the nonstandard “make the ante.” UP restores “pay the ante.”
units.japanese: さぁ、アンティを支払おうではないか。そなたに授けられ、最後にはそなたに全て返すべきものだ。

units.text: So then, let us make the ante. All that you have given should be returned to you in the end. Come, take it!!"
units.note: MG retains the nonstandard “make the ante.” UP restores “pay the ante.”
units.japanese: 「さぁ、アンティを支払おうではないか。そなたに授けられ、最後にはそなたに全て返すべきものだ。さぁ、受け取れい！！」

description: 太もも姉ちゃんたち jokingly identifies the Seven Sisters as the thigh-showing girls or ladies. Ass nee-sans substitutes a different body part and produces an unclear hybrid phrase.
sourceReading: Battler complains that seven thigh-baring women appeared after the swarming goat heads, followed now by a butler.

units.text: "Isn't that obvious, another incomprehensible guy's just appeared!!  Back when I was grumbling that goat-headed people would start doing the Bon dance, goat-heads started showing up in swarms, and since then, not only have those seven ass nee-sans appeared, but now even a butler has shown up!!  It doesn't make sense, cut it out!!"
units.note: MG retains “ass nee-sans.” UP revises this to “sexy-ass babes,” which preserves coarse sexualization but still omits Battler’s thigh-based visual nickname.
units.japanese: 山羊頭が盆踊りを始めるのかとぼやいたら、山羊頭がうようよ現れて、太もも姉ちゃんたちが７人も出てきてその上、今度は執事まで出てきやがった！！　わけわかんねぇよ、もういい加減にしやがれよッ！！」

units.text: "Yeah, no shit, another incomprehensible guy just showed up!! First I grumble about goat-headed people doing the Bon dance, and then goat-heads start showing up in swarms, and since then, not only have those seven ass nee-sans appeared, but now there's even a butler!! It doesn't make sense, cut it out!!"
units.note: MG retains “ass nee-sans.” UP revises this to “sexy-ass babes,” which preserves coarse sexualization but still omits Battler’s thigh-based visual nickname.

units.text: "I'll bet. No sane people would hang out with you. First some goat monsters, then those ass nee-chans, and this time a demon butler's showed up. ...I hate to think about it, but the way things are going, I wouldn't be surprised if even more weird people appeared..."
units.note: MG again uses “ass nee-chans” and UP “sexy-assed babes,” both omitting Battler’s thigh-based nickname. This recurrence is not counted again.
units.japanese: 「だろうな。お前の関係にはロクな連中がいねぇぜ。山羊のバケモノに太もも姉ちゃんに、そして今度は悪魔の執事と来たわけだ。……まさかとは思うが、この調子でまだおかしな連中が増えるってんじゃねぇだろうな…」

units.text: "I'm sure. None of your contacts are halfway near decent. First some goat monsters, then those sexy‐assed babes, and this time a demon butler's showed up. ......I don't want to say it, but there better not be more and more of these weird guys to come..."
units.note: MG again uses “ass nee-chans” and UP “sexy-assed babes,” both omitting Battler’s thigh-based nickname. This recurrence is not counted again.

description: こっそり摘み食い continues Ronove's flirtation by joking that he will not sneak a taste or nibble of Beatrice's guest. Stealthily snatch your guest away preserves romantic rivalry but removes the eating metaphor and its sexual innuendo.
sourceReading: When Beatrice jokingly expresses jealousy, Ronove assures her that he will not secretly sample Battler for himself.

units.text: "My, my.  I apologize for making you jealous, Milady.  I will not stealthily snatch your guest away from you.
units.note: Both editions retain “snatch your guest away,” preserving jealousy but losing Ronove’s eating metaphor and sexual double entendre.
units.japanese: 「これはこれは。お嬢様に嫉妬させてしまい、申し訳ございませんでした。お嬢様のお客人をこっそり摘み食いなどいたしませんよ。

units.text: "My, my. I apologize for making you jealous, Milady. I shall not sneakily snatch your guest away from you."
units.note: Both editions retain “snatch your guest away,” preserving jealousy but losing Ronove’s eating metaphor and sexual double entendre.
units.japanese: 「これはこれは。お嬢様に嫉妬させてしまい、申し訳ございませんでした。お嬢様のお客人をこっそり摘み食いなどいたしませんよ」

units.text: "My, my. I apologize most humbly for making you jealous, Milady. I will not stealthily snatch your guest away from you."
units.note: Both editions retain “snatch your guest away,” preserving jealousy but losing Ronove’s eating metaphor and sexual double entendre.
units.japanese: 「これはこれは。お嬢様に嫉妬させてしまい、申し訳ございませんでした。お嬢様のお客人をこっそり摘み食いなどいたしませんよ」

description: Battler begins with a dismissive へっ and declares that even if the sun rose in the west he would never acknowledge Beatrice as a witch. That's because invents a causal connector with no proposition for the following even-if clause to explain.
sourceReading: Battler directly rebuts Beatrice's claim that conversation proves acknowledgment by vowing never to recognize her as a witch under any circumstances.

units.text: "Heh.  That's because, even if the sun starts rising from the west, I will definitely, definitely definitely, never accept that you're a witch.  You might want to consider a slightly more positive approach, like crying and kissing my shoes."
units.note: Both editions retain the unsupported “That’s because” before Battler’s even-if denial.
units.japanese: 「へっ。例え、お天道様が西から昇ることがあろうとも、絶対の絶対絶対ッ、お前を魔女だと認定などしねぇからな。泣いて俺の靴にキスしたら、もうちょい前向きに検討してやってもいいぜ。」

units.text: "Heh. That's because, even if the sun starts rising from the west, I will definitely, absolutely never accept that you're a witch. You might wanna try a more positive approach, like crying and kissing my shoes."
units.note: Both editions retain the unsupported “That’s because” before Battler’s even-if denial.
units.japanese: 「へっ。たとえ、お天道様が西から昇ることがあろうとも、絶対の絶対絶対ッ、お前を魔女だと認定などしねぇからな。泣いて俺の靴にキスしたら、もうちょい前向きに検討してやってもいいぜ」

units.text: "Heh. That's because, even if the sun starts rising from the west, I will definitely, definitely‐definitely, never accept that you're a witch. Maybe if you start crying and kissing my shoes, I might be willing to have a more constructive discussion."
units.note: Both editions retain the unsupported “That’s because” before Battler’s even-if denial.
units.japanese: 「へっ。たとえ、お天道様が西から昇ることがあろうとも、絶対の絶対絶対ッ、お前を魔女だと認定などしねぇからな。泣いて俺の靴にキスしたら、もうちょい前向きに検討してやってもいいぜ」

description: あれほどの屈辱を受けてまで says Battler submitted even at the cost of enduring that much humiliation. Submitted so much that you received all of that humiliation reverses the relation and makes the humiliation a consequence or measure of submission.
sourceReading: Beatrice taunts Battler for having yielded in the previous game despite the extreme humiliation involved.

units.text: "That's right.  Bit by bit, you are surrendering to me...!  Didn't you submit to me in the last game so much that you received all of that humiliation?
units.note: Both editions retain the reversal that makes humiliation result from Battler’s submission instead of something he endured despite submitting.
units.japanese: 「そうだ。そなたは少しずつ少しずつ妾に屈している…！　前回のゲームでは、あれほどの屈辱を受けてまで妾に屈服したではないか。

units.text: "That's right. Bit by bit, you are surrendering to me...! Isn't all that humiliation you suffered in the last game a result of you submitting to me so deeply?
units.note: Both editions retain the reversal that makes humiliation result from Battler’s submission instead of something he endured despite submitting.
units.japanese: 「そうだ。そなたは少しずつ少しずつ妾に屈している…！　前回のゲームでは、あれほどの屈辱を受けてまで妾に屈服したではないか」

units.text: "That's right. Bit by bit, you are surrendering to me...! You submitted to me so much in the last game that you received all of that humiliation, did you not?"
units.note: Both editions retain the reversal that makes humiliation result from Battler’s submission instead of something he endured despite submitting.
units.japanese: 「そうだ。そなたは少しずつ少しずつ妾に屈している…！　前回のゲームでは、あれほどの屈辱を受けてまで妾に屈服したではないか」

description: Beatrice says Battler's back was truly pleasant for resting or throwing her feet upon. Had to sacrifice your back invents Battler's deliberate sacrifice and replaces Beatrice's appraisal of him as a footrest.
sourceReading: Beatrice humiliates Battler by fondly recalling how comfortable his back was beneath her feet.

units.text: Wasn't it great when you had to sacrifice your back for my feet?  *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!!"
units.note: MG retains Battler sacrificing his back for Beatrice’s feet. UP restores Beatrice’s appraisal that his back made a pleasant footrest.
units.japanese: そなたの背中は、妾の足を投げ出すには本当に良いものだったぞ？　くーっくっくっくっくっく！！」

units.text: Wasn't it great when you had to sacrifice your back for the sake of my feet? *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!!"
units.note: MG retains Battler sacrificing his back for Beatrice’s feet. UP restores Beatrice’s appraisal that his back made a pleasant footrest.
units.japanese: 「そなたの背中は、妾の足を投げ出すには本当に良いものだったぞ？　くーっくっくっくっくっく！！」

sourceReading: Eva's hostile inner voice follows its direct abuse of Rosa with the absurd command that she bite her navel and die.

description: のんびり待ってる says Kyrie will wait leisurely or take it easy while waiting for dessert. Wait patiently changes relaxed detachment into tolerance or forbearance and weakens the contrast with the others rushing upstairs.
sourceReading: Kyrie calmly thanks Rudolf and says she will relax and wait for Gohda to bring dessert while the others verify the letter.

units.text: "......Thank you.  I will wait patiently for Gohda-san to bring the dessert."
units.note: Both editions retain “wait patiently,” losing Kyrie’s leisurely, detached wait for dessert while the others rush upstairs.
units.japanese: 「……ありがと。郷田さんがデザートを持ってくるのを、のんびり待ってるわ。」

units.text: "...Thank you. I'll wait patiently for Gohda-san to bring in dessert."

description: 誤魔化している says the adults apparently felt Maria was evading, fudging, or covering something up. Trying to trick them assigns her a more active intention to deceive the adults.
sourceReading: The adults interpret Maria's repeated answer as evasive and continue pressing her until she cries.

units.text: Maria kept repeating that she had gotten it from Beatrice no matter how many times she was asked. It seemed that the adults felt that she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back and questioned her until she broke out in tears... When Maria was released, she sobbed, all worn out from crying.
units.note: Both editions retain the adults’ belief that Maria was trying to trick them, strengthening evasion into active deception.
units.japanese: それを大人たちは、誤魔化していると感じたらしく、彼女が泣き出すまで詰問を決して緩めようとはしなかった…。

It seemed that the adults felt that she was trying to trick them, so they didn't hold back, and questioned her until she broke out in tears... By the time Maria was released, she had cried herself to the point of exhaustion.

sourceReading: Hideyoshi notices the suddenly hostile atmosphere among the siblings and asks what they are discussing.

units.text: "What's this, what's this?  Why's everyone gotten so gloomy...?  What are you talkin' about?

description: 未開の森 means undeveloped, unexplored, or uncharted forest. Uncivilized forest applies a social condition to terrain and gives an awkward, misleading description of Rokkenjima's untouched woods.
sourceReading: Kyrie summarizes the rumor that Kinzo may have built a secret mansion for his mistress somewhere in the island's undeveloped forest.

units.text: ......So people have wondered whether he might have built a secret mansion somewhere in the uncivilized forest for his mistress to live in?  That's a rather large-scale story."
units.note: Both editions retain “uncivilized forest” for Rokkenjima’s undeveloped or uncharted forest.
units.japanese: ……そして未開の森のどこかに、愛人を住まわせるための隠し屋敷を作ったかもしれないと、そう思われてたのね？　ずいぶん、スケールの大きな話ね。」

units.text: ...So people have suspected that he built a secret mansion somewhere in the uncivilized forest for his mistress to live in? That would be quite a large-scale scheme."
units.note: Both editions retain “uncivilized forest” for Rokkenjima’s undeveloped or uncharted forest.

units.text: "......So people have wondered whether he might have built a secret mansion somewhere in the uncivilized forest for his mistress to live in? That's a rather large‐scale story."
units.note: Both editions retain “uncivilized forest” for Rokkenjima’s undeveloped or uncharted forest.

description: 摩り替わり says the witch legend was replaced or swapped out for the mistress theory. Refined into instead presents the mistress theory as a more precise development of the witch theory.
sourceReading: The witch legend was supplanted by the mistress theory, which eventually led to rumors that Kinzo secretly visited his mistress.

units.text: ......However, after the witch theory began to be refined into the theory about his mistress, it was eventually whispered that he was secretly going back and forth to this mistress."
units.note: Both editions retain “refined into,” presenting the mistress theory as a refinement of the witch theory instead of a theory that replaced it.
units.japanese: ……しかし、魔女伝説が愛人説に摩り替わり、やがてそれは、こっそり愛人のもとへ通っているのではないかと囁かれるようになった。」

units.text: "...However, when the witch theory was slowly refined into the theory about his mistress, people eventually whispered that he was secretly going back and forth to see her."
units.note: Both editions retain “refined into,” presenting the mistress theory as a refinement of the witch theory instead of a theory that replaced it.
units.japanese: 「……しかし、魔女伝説が愛人説に掏り替わり、やがてそれは、こっそり愛人のもとへ通っているのではないかと囁かれるようになった」

units.text: "......However, after the witch theory began to be refined into the theory about his mistress, it was eventually whispered that he was secretly going back and forth to see her."
units.note: Both editions retain “refined into,” presenting the mistress theory as a refinement of the witch theory instead of a theory that replaced it.
units.japanese: 「……しかし、魔女伝説が愛人説に掏り替わり、やがてそれは、こっそり愛人のもとへ通っているのではないかと囁かれるようになった」

description: うそぶいていた describes the servants airily, brazenly, or affectedly claiming that Kinzo turned into butterflies. Exaggerated instead says they overstated an underlying account.
sourceReading: Some servants would make the fanciful claim that Kinzo had transformed into butterflies and danced through the rose garden.

units.text: ...But it was always some place where the servants had already looked.  ......We never knew where Father had gone.  Since that time, Grandfather started to become famous for his adoration of the occult, so some of the servants exaggerated, saying that he might have turned into butterflies and danced around the rose garden."
units.note: Both editions call the servants’ fanciful claim an exaggeration rather than conveying their airy or affected manner of making it.
units.japanese: …でも、それらの場所は何れも使用人たちが必ず探している場所。……お父様がどこに行っていたのかは、いつもわからなかった。当時からお父様はオカルトに傾倒していることが有名だったから、一部の使用人たちは、蝶にでも化けて、薔薇庭園を舞っていたのだろうなんてうそぶいていたっけ。」

units.text: Even at that time, Grandfather was famous for his occult inclinations, so some of the servants exaggerated, saying that he might have turned into butterflies and danced around the rose garden."
units.note: Both editions call the servants’ fanciful claim an exaggeration rather than conveying their airy or affected manner of making it.
units.japanese: 「当時からお父様はオカルトに傾倒していることが有名だったから、一部の使用人たちは、蝶にでも化けて、薔薇庭園を舞っていたのだろうなんてうそぶいていたっけ」

units.text: "By that time, Father was already famous for his adoration of the occult, so some of the servants exaggerated, saying that he might have turned into butterflies and danced around the rose garden."
units.note: Both editions call the servants’ fanciful claim an exaggeration rather than conveying their airy or affected manner of making it.
units.japanese: 「当時からお父様はオカルトに傾倒していることが有名だったから、一部の使用人たちは、蝶にでも化けて、薔薇庭園を舞っていたのだろうなんてうそぶいていたっけ」

description: 長いこと口にすることをはばかられてきた says everyone had long refrained from voicing the suspicion. They hesitated for a long time without speaking recasts that history as one extended silence.
sourceReading: Each sibling had considered the suspicion excessive and had avoided saying it aloud for a long time, despite all sharing it.

units.text: ......Was there a hidden mansion on this island, and had Kinzo's mistress been living there in hiding for a long, long time......? Everyone thought that they were being too suspicious, and they hesitated for a long time without speaking, but.........everyone shared a common opinion.
units.note: MG turns years of reluctance to voice the shared theory into a long hesitation without speaking. UP restores the longstanding history.
units.japanese: 誰もが勘繰り過ぎだと思い、長いこと口にすることをはばかられてきたが…。……全員が持つ共通の見解であったのだ。
candidates: hesitated for a long time without speaking

units.text: ...Was there a hidden mansion on this island, and had Kinzo's mistress been living there in hiding for a long, long time...? Everyone thought they were being too suspicious, and they hesitated for a long time without speaking, ...but everyone shared a common opinion.
units.note: MG turns years of reluctance to voice the shared theory into a long hesitation without speaking. UP restores the longstanding history.
units.japanese: ……この島には誰も知らない隠し屋敷があり、そこにずっとずっと、金蔵の愛人が隠れ住まっている……？誰もが勘繰り過ぎだと思い、長いこと口にすることをはばかられてきたが…。……全員が持つ共通の見解であったのだ。
candidates: hesitated for a long time without speaking

description: 計上しようとしてた says Krauss tried to put or budget a full-island survey into the resort-development plan, and 出来なくなった says the earlier trouble prevented it from being carried out. WH instead says he had been planning the investigation and was not very successful, allowing a failed or partial search to have occurred.
sourceReading: Eva knows Krauss tried to include a full survey of the island under the resort-development budget or plan, but the earlier financial trouble left him unable to carry it out.

units.text: "Don't play dumb.  ...We know that, although you say that you are opening a resort, you have really been planning to investigate the entire island, right?  Judging by all that trouble and confusion we were talking about earlier, you haven't been very successful, have you?"
units.note: MG retains both the loss of the budgeting action and the implication of an unsuccessful investigation. UP restores that the survey could not be carried out, but still omits the budgeting action and adds that resort development was “just a cover.”
units.japanese:
「惚けないでよ。…兄さんがリゾート開発と称して、島の全域調査を計上しようとしてたのを知ってるのよぅ？
例のトラブルのごたごたで出来なくなっちゃったそうだけどね？」

units.text: "Don't play dumb. ...We know that, although you say you're opening a resort, you have really been planning to investigate the entire island, right? Judging by all that trouble and confusion we were talking about earlier, you haven't been very successful, have you?"
units.note: MG retains both the loss of the budgeting action and the implication of an unsuccessful investigation. UP restores that the survey could not be carried out, but still omits the budgeting action and adds that resort development was “just a cover.”

units.text: "Don't play dumb. ...Although you say that you're opening a resort, we know that it's just a cover for a full‐scale investigation of the entire island, okay? Although, it sounds as if, due to all that trouble and confusion we were talking about earlier, you haven't been able to carry it out, of course?"
units.note: MG retains both the loss of the budgeting action and the implication of an unsuccessful investigation. UP restores that the survey could not be carried out, but still omits the budgeting action and adds that resort development was “just a cover.”
units.japanese: 「惚けないでよ。…兄さんがリゾート開発と称して、島の全域調査を計上しようとしてたのを知ってるのよぅ？　例のトラブルのごたごたで出来なくなっちゃったそうだけどね？」

description: 具体的な証拠 means concrete or specific evidence. Physical proof narrows the possible basis for Krauss's conviction to material evidence.
sourceReading: The siblings do not know whether Krauss's conviction is mere assumption or rests on concrete evidence.

units.text: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him over-thinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof. ......Still, if Krauss, with all his guile, was sure, that was enough proof for the other siblings to be sure, too...
units.note: Both editions narrow unspecified concrete evidence to physical proof.
units.japanese: その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。

units.text: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him overthinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof. ...Still, if Krauss, with all his guile, was sure, that was enough proof for the other siblings to be sure too...
units.note: Both editions narrow unspecified concrete evidence to physical proof.
units.japanese: その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。……しかし、悪知恵の働く蔵臼がそれを確信している以上、それに足る根拠があるに違いないと兄弟たちもまた確信していた…。

units.text: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him over‐thinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof. ......However, if Krauss, with all his guile, was convinced, then the other siblings were similarly convinced that there must be a sufficient basis for it...
units.note: Both editions narrow unspecified concrete evidence to physical proof.
units.japanese: その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。……しかし、悪知恵の働く蔵臼がそれを確信している以上、それに足る根拠があるに違いないと兄弟たちもまた確信していた…。

description: The siblings infer that a guileful Krauss must have grounds sufficient for his conviction. WH instead makes Krauss's conviction itself enough proof for the siblings, collapsing their inference about undisclosed grounds into circular evidence.
sourceReading: Because the shrewd Krauss is convinced, his siblings become convinced that he must possess a sufficient basis for that belief.

units.text: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him over-thinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof. ......Still, if Krauss, with all his guile, was sure, that was enough proof for the other siblings to be sure, too...
units.note: MG makes Krauss’s conviction itself enough proof for the siblings. UP restores their inference that he must possess sufficient grounds.
units.japanese: ……しかし、悪知恵の働く蔵臼がそれを確信している以上、それに足る根拠があるに違いないと兄弟たちもまた確信していた…。

units.text: They couldn't tell whether that conviction was just him overthinking things, or whether it was based on some physical proof. ...Still, if Krauss, with all his guile, was sure, that was enough proof for the other siblings to be sure too...
units.note: MG makes Krauss’s conviction itself enough proof for the siblings. UP restores their inference that he must possess sufficient grounds.
units.japanese: その確信は、単なる思い込みなのか、それとも具体的な証拠があってのことなのかはわからない。……しかし、悪知恵の働く蔵臼がそれを確信している以上、それに足る根拠があるに違いないと兄弟たちもまた確信していた…。

description: 霧江の言い分は揺るぐものではない says Kyrie's argument or position remains unshaken. WH instead says the importance of what she said does not waver, changing validity or force into importance.
sourceReading: Even granting Kinzo's extraordinary capabilities, Kyrie's practical objection to secretly supporting a person for thirty years remains intact.

units.text: However, that didn't cause the importance of what Kyrie had said to waver. This was different from stealthily raising a kitten in a cardboard box and keeping it a secret from your parents. Taking care of a person in secret over a period of 30 years would be an incalculably massive task...
units.note: Both editions say the importance of Kyrie’s point remains unshaken rather than saying her practical argument itself remains unshaken.
units.japanese: しかし、それでも霧江の言い分は揺るぐものではない。

units.text: However, that didn't cause the importance of what Kyrie had said to waver. This was different from stealthily raising a kitten in a cardboard box and keeping it a secret from your parents. Taking care of a person in secret over a period of 30 years would be an incalculably massive task...
units.note: Both editions say the importance of Kyrie’s point remains unshaken rather than saying her practical argument itself remains unshaken.
units.japanese: しかし、それでも霧江の言い分は揺るぐものではない。こっそりと、親に内緒で段ボール箱に猫を飼うのとはわけが違う。人間ひとりを３０年にもわたって秘密に世話するなんて、その手間は計り知れないくらいに膨大だろう…。

units.text: However, that didn't shake the importance of what Kyrie had said. This was different from stealthily raising a kitten in a cardboard box and keeping it a secret from your parents. Taking care of a person in secret over a period of thirty years would be an incalculably massive task...
units.note: Both editions say the importance of Kyrie’s point remains unshaken rather than saying her practical argument itself remains unshaken.
units.japanese: しかし、それでも霧江の言い分は揺るぐものではない。こっそりと、親に内緒で段ボール箱に猫を飼うのとはわけが違う。人間ひとりを３０年にもわたって秘密に世話するなんて、その手間は計り知れないくらいに膨大だろう…。

description: 参加したい says the hypothetical mistress would want to participate in the inheritance dispute with pride. WH says she should join, weakening her asserted desire into an expectation about participation.
sourceReading: If the siblings' theory is correct, the mistress herself should want to enter Kinzo's inheritance dispute proudly.

units.text: "Quit it, Aniki.  ......So if everything we imagine is true, then she should throw out her chest with pride and join in on Father's inheritance problem.
units.note: MG says the mistress should be joining the dispute, still weakening her desire to participate proudly. UP restores that she should want to participate with pride.
units.japanese: 「よせよ兄貴。……そして俺たちの想像が本当なら、親父の遺産問題に彼女は胸を張って参加したいはずなんだ。

units.text: "Quit it, Aniki. ...So if everything we're thinking's true, then she should be joining in on Dad's inheritance problem with her head held high.
units.note: MG says the mistress should be joining the dispute, still weakening her desire to participate proudly. UP restores that she should want to participate with pride.
units.japanese: 「よせよ兄貴。……そして俺たちの想像が本当なら、親父の遺産問題に彼女は胸を張って参加したいはずなんだ」

description: 食い込む気、満々 says she would be fully intent on muscling into the headship struggle. WH says she might feel confident doing so, replacing intention with confidence.
sourceReading: On this theory, the mistress would fully intend to claim not only property rights but a place in the struggle over succession.

units.text: "...In which case, she might feel confident encroaching in on not just the rights to his assets, but the battle over the inheritance as well."
units.note: MG retains confidence in staking a claim where Japanese gives the mistress full intention to muscle into the succession struggle. UP restores full intention.
units.japanese: 「…となると、財産権どころか、家督争いにも食い込む気、満々ってことになるで。」

units.text: "...Which means she might feel confident staking her claim, not just for the rights to his assets, but regarding the battle over the Headship too."
units.note: MG retains confidence in staking a claim where Japanese gives the mistress full intention to muscle into the succession struggle. UP restores full intention.
units.japanese: 「…となると、財産権どころか、家督争いにも食い込む気、満々ってことになるで」

description: ビタ一文譲るものか says the hypothetical mistress would not yield a single penny to the unloved wife's children. WH omits the absolute amount and says only that she would hate giving it up.
sourceReading: The narration reasons that she would naturally refuse to give even one penny to the children of Kinzo's loveless marriage.

units.text: The revival of the Ushiromiya family had been made possible by the gold Beatrice had bestowed. ...That was quite a distinguishing service she had provided. She had built that wealth together with Kinzo, so it was natural that she would have thought of herself as the one who should inherit it...  It would also be natural for her to despise the thought of giving that up to the children of the wife Kinzo had never loved.
units.note: MG omits “a single cent” and says she would hate giving the wealth up. UP restores her imagined refusal to give the children even one cent.
units.japanese: 自分と金蔵の二人で築いた財産なのだから、それを引き継ぐのは自分だと考えるのは自然な流れ…。愛のない妻から生まれた子どもたちに、ビタ一文譲るものかと考えるのも、これもまた自然な流れだろう。

units.text: The revival of the Ushiromiya family was made possible by the gold Beatrice had bestowed. ...That was quite a distinguishing service she had provided. She had built that wealth together with Kinzo, so it was natural that she would think of herself as the one who should inherit it... It would also be natural for her to despise the thought of giving it up to the children of the wife Kinzo never loved.
units.note: MG omits “a single cent” and says she would hate giving the wealth up. UP restores her imagined refusal to give the children even one cent.
units.japanese: 右代宮家の復興は、ベアトリーチェが黄金を授けたことによって成し遂げられた。…つまり、彼女の手柄ということになる。自分と金蔵の二人で築いた財産なのだから、それを引き継ぐのは自分だと考えるのは自然な流れ…。愛のない妻から生まれた子どもたちに、ビタ一文譲るものかと考えるのも、これもまた自然な流れだろう。

description: 愛はなくとも血を受け継ぐ私たち contrasts the loved mistress with us, who inherit Kinzo's blood even without his love. WH calls them the relatives he does not love, omitting blood descent and broadening the group beyond his children.
sourceReading: Eva frames the contest as Kinzo's beloved mistress against his unloved but blood-related children.

units.text: And also, Father has given that reckless action his silent approval.  ......Will the person who succeeds the Ushiromiya family be his mistress Beatrice, or one of us, the relatives he doesn't love?  Maybe he wants to make us struggle over that to see who is worthy."
units.note: MG calls the siblings unloved relatives, omitting the contrast that they inherit Kinzo’s blood despite lacking his love. UP restores the blood relationship.
units.japanese: それに、お父様はこの暴挙を黙認されている。……右代宮家を継ぐのは愛人ベアトリーチェか、愛はなくとも血を受け継ぐ私たちか。それを争わせて確かめたいというのでしょうね。」

units.text: Father has even given it his silent approval. ...Will the person who succeeds the Ushiromiya family be his mistress Beatrice, or one of us, the relatives he doesn't love? Maybe he wants to make us struggle over that to see who's worthy."
units.note: MG calls the siblings unloved relatives, omitting the contrast that they inherit Kinzo’s blood despite lacking his love. UP restores the blood relationship.
units.japanese: 「それに、お父様はこの暴挙を黙認されている。……右代宮家を継ぐのは愛人ベアトリーチェか、愛はなくとも血を受け継ぐ私たちか。それを争わせて確かめたいというのでしょうね」

description: 充分な勝算 means that the party proposing the condition must see a good chance of winning. A significant advantage instead asserts a favorable feature of the condition without directly stating expected odds of victory.
sourceReading: Kyrie infers that because the other party proposed this condition, that party must believe it has sufficiently good prospects of winning under it.

units.text: "......However, since it was the other party that brought up this condition, I wonder if that means that the other party has a significant advantage."
units.note: Both editions call the condition a significant advantage instead of reporting the proposer’s assessed chance of winning. MG also changes proposing the condition into bringing a rule to light; that separate change is recorded under a paired ID.
units.japanese: 「……でも、その条件を向こうが出してきたということは、向こうは充分な勝算があるということじゃないのかしら。」

units.text: "...However, since she's the one who brought this rule to light in the first place, maybe that means it gives her a significant advantage."
units.note: Both editions call the condition a significant advantage instead of reporting the proposer’s assessed chance of winning. MG also changes proposing the condition into bringing a rule to light; that separate change is recorded under a paired ID.
units.japanese: 「……でも、その条件を向こうが出してきたということは、向こうは充分な勝算があるということじゃないのかしら」

description: あの手紙の文面通りなら conditions the claim on the letter's wording being as stated: Beatrice is Kinzo's consulting alchemist. WH instead says if Beatrice meant that letter literally, assigning interpretive intent to Beatrice and changing the condition.
sourceReading: If the letter's account is taken as written, Beatrice is Kinzo's consulting alchemist and therefore the manager of the gold.

units.text: "Th, that's right.  ...In the first place, if Beatrice meant that letter literally, then she's Father's alchemist.  In other words, she's the manager of his gold.  It wouldn't be strange at all if she knew where it was hidden, would it?!
units.note: Both editions condition the claim on Beatrice meaning the letter literally rather than on the letter’s account being taken as written.
units.japanese: 「そ、それもそうや。…第一、ベアトリーチェはあの手紙の文面通りなら、お父さんの顧問錬金術師。つまり、黄金の管理者や。その隠し場所を知っていても何の不思議もないやないか！

units.text: "Th-That's right. ...In the first place, if Beatrice meant that letter literally, then she's Father's alchemist. In other words, she's the manager of his gold. It wouldn't be strange at all if she knew where it was hidden, would it?!"
units.note: Both editions condition the claim on Beatrice meaning the letter literally rather than on the letter’s account being taken as written.
units.japanese: 「そ、それもそうや。…第一、ベアトリーチェはあの手紙の文面通りなら、お父さんの顧問錬金術師。つまり、黄金の管理者や。その隠し場所を知っていても何の不思議もないやないか！」

units.text: "Tha‐that's a point, too. ...In the first place, if Beatrice meant that letter literally, then she's Father's alchemist. In other words, she's the manager of his gold. It wouldn't be strange at all if she knew where it was hidden, would it?!"
units.note: Both editions condition the claim on Beatrice meaning the letter literally rather than on the letter’s account being taken as written.
units.japanese: 「そ、それもそうや。…第一、ベアトリーチェはあの手紙の文面通りなら、お父さんの顧問錬金術師。つまり、黄金の管理者や。その隠し場所を知っていても何の不思議もないやないか！」

description: 本当に黄金を持っているか questions whether she really possesses the gold now. WH asks whether she had any gold in the first place, shifting the doubt to past possession.
sourceReading: Krauss questions whether she truly has the gold, since a real possessor could simply keep quiet and appropriate it.

units.text: "...If you think about it like that, don't you start to doubt whether she really had any gold in the first place?  Why would she tell us about it?  All she'd have to do would be stay silent and embezzle it."
units.note: MG asks whether Beatrice ever had gold, shifting the doubt to past possession. UP restores doubt about whether she currently has it.
units.japanese: 「…そこまで考えると、そもそも彼女が本当に黄金を持っているかどうかは怪しいと思わんかね？　なぜ我々にその存在を教える。黙って着服すれば良いものを。」

units.text: "...If you think about it like that, don't you start to doubt whether she really had any gold in the first place? Why would she tell us about it? All she has to do is keep quiet and embezzle it."
units.note: MG asks whether Beatrice ever had gold, shifting the doubt to past possession. UP restores doubt about whether she currently has it.
units.japanese: 「…そこまで考えると、そもそも彼女が本当に黄金を持っているかどうかは怪しいと思わんかね？　なぜ我々にその存在を教える。黙って着服すれば良いものを」

description: 可能性は低くないかもしれない cautiously says the possibility may not be low. A pretty good chance strengthens Kyrie's nested hedge into a positive probability judgment.
sourceReading: After reversing the perspective, Kyrie cautiously suggests that the chance the sender actually possesses the gold may not be low.

units.text: "............No, if you turn the chessboard over, there might be a pretty good chance that they actually do have the gold."
units.note: Both editions strengthen Kyrie’s cautious possibility “may not be low” into a pretty good chance.
units.japanese: 「…………いえ。チェス盤を引っ繰り返して考えれば、黄金を実際に持っている可能性は低くないかもしれない。」

units.text: "......No, if you spin the chessboard around, there might be a pretty good chance that they actually do have the gold."
units.note: Both editions strengthen Kyrie’s cautious possibility “may not be low” into a pretty good chance.
units.japanese: 「…………いえ。チェス盤を引っ繰り返して考えれば、黄金を実際に持っている可能性は低くないかもしれない」

units.text: "............No, if you flip over the chessboard, there might be a pretty good chance that they actually do have the gold."
units.note: Both editions strengthen Kyrie’s cautious possibility “may not be low” into a pretty good chance.
units.japanese: 「…………いえ。チェス盤を引っ繰り返して考えれば、黄金を実際に持っている可能性は低くないかもしれない」

description: 後者の方が期待できる says they honestly expect more value from Beatrice's payment than from the remaining inheritance. More enticing shifts the comparison from expected financial return to subjective attraction.
sourceReading: They privately expect Beatrice's compensation for recognizing her as head to exceed their shares of the depleted family estate.

units.text: They knew that much of the Ushiromiya family assets had been eaten up by Krauss. The dregs that remained of that inheritance, ...versus the 'compensation for being accepted as the head' that Beatrice would pay. It was a shame, but honestly, the former was less enticing than the latter.
units.note: Both editions say Beatrice’s payment is more enticing rather than that the adults expect a greater financial return from it than from the depleted estate.
units.japanese: 残念だが、前者より後者の方が期待できるというのが本音だった。

units.text: They knew that Krauss had eaten up much of the Ushiromiya family's assets. So, it was dregs that remained of that inheritance, ...versus "the cost of being accepted as the Head" that Beatrice would pay. It was a shame, but honestly, the former was less enticing than the latter.
units.note: Both editions say Beatrice’s payment is more enticing rather than that the adults expect a greater financial return from it than from the depleted estate.
units.japanese: 右代宮家の財産は、かなりが蔵臼に食い潰されていることがわかっている。その残り滓の遺産分配と、ベアトリーチェが支払う“家督を認める対価”。残念だが、前者より後者の方が期待できるというのが本音だった。

description: 不甲斐ない condemns Krauss's younger siblings as pathetic, unreliable, or lacking in resolve. Cowardly narrows Natsuhi's contempt to fearfulness.
sourceReading: Natsuhi calls the younger siblings feckless for being willing to sell the Ushiromiya family's glory for money.

units.text: "Dear...!  The amount of money isn't the problem, right?!  Your cowardly younger siblings are trying to sell the glory of the Ushiromiya family for money, right?!  Why aren't you displaying your dignity as the oldest son?!"
units.note: Both editions call the younger siblings cowardly rather than feckless, pathetic, or unreliable.
units.japanese: 「あなた…！　金額の問題じゃないでしょう？！　不甲斐ない弟たちは、お金で右代宮家の栄光を売り払うつもりなのですよ？！　ここで長男の威厳を示さずして何とするのですッ！」

units.text: "Dear...! The amount of money isn't the problem, right?! Your cowardly younger siblings are trying to sell the glory of the Ushiromiya family for money, don't you see?! Why aren't you displaying your dignity as the oldest son?!"
units.note: Both editions call the younger siblings cowardly rather than feckless, pathetic, or unreliable.

description: ここで長男の威厳を示さずして何とする demands that Krauss show the dignity of the eldest son now. Why aren't you displaying your dignity instead treats his present failure as the question.
sourceReading: Natsuhi exhorts Krauss that this is precisely the moment to demonstrate his authority and dignity as the eldest son.

units.note: Both editions ask why Krauss is not displaying dignity instead of exhorting him that this is the moment to display it.

description: １０ｔ全てを提供してくれるかは皮算用 says expecting her to provide all ten tons is premature wishful calculation. Saying ten tons is an optimistic figure instead casts doubt on the quantity or valuation itself.
sourceReading: Kyrie concedes that it is premature to assume Beatrice would offer them the entire ten tons, while maintaining that the proposal could still be attractive.

units.text: "Even if 10 tons might be a bit of an optimistic figure, .........I see, it would still be a fascinating prospect for us.  ...We were trying to form an alliance among the siblings to kick this outsider called Beatrice out.
units.note: MG calls ten tons an optimistic figure, shifting the uncertainty to the amount. UP restores that expecting Beatrice to provide the full ten tons is premature.
units.japanese: 「１０ｔ全てを提供してくれるかは、さすがに皮算用だとしても。………なるほど、私たちにとって魅力的な話になるわね。…私たちは、ベアトリーチェなどという余所者を弾き出すために兄弟同盟を組もうとしていた。

units.text: "Even if 10 tons is a slightly optimistic figure, ......yes, it'd still be a fascinating prospect for us. ...We were trying to form an alliance among the siblings to kick this outsider called Beatrice out."
units.note: MG calls ten tons an optimistic figure, shifting the uncertainty to the amount. UP restores that expecting Beatrice to provide the full ten tons is premature.
units.japanese: 「１０ｔ全てを提供してくれるかは、さすがに皮算用だとしても。………なるほど、私たちにとって魅力的な話になるわね。…私たちは、ベアトリーチェなどという余所者を弾き出すために兄弟同盟を組もうとしていた」

description: WH's the all of the gold is grammatically malformed for 黄金を全て, which means all the gold.
sourceReading: Kyrie asks why Beatrice would create a new game promising to hand over the headship and all the gold to whoever solves the epitaph.

units.text: However, Kyrie still thought there might be a catch. If this was a declaration of victory, Beatrice would only have to display the gold openly, and state that she would buy the inheritance. And yet, she had gone to all of this trouble, telling the siblings to try and solve the epitaph.  And why had she set up this 'new game', where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the inheritance to the person who solved the epitaph?
units.note: Both editions retain the malformed phrase “the all of the gold.”
units.japanese: なのに、わざわざこの期に及んで、碑文を解いてみろ、解けたら家督と黄金を全て引き渡そうと、“新たなゲーム”を仕掛けてくる意味が、どこにあるというのか。

units.text: However, Kyrie still thought there might be a catch. If this was a declaration of victory, Beatrice would only have had to display the gold openly and state her intent to buy the inheritance. And yet, she had gone to all of this trouble, telling the siblings to try and solve the epitaph. Why did she set up this "new game", where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the inheritance to the epitaph solver?
units.note: Both editions retain the malformed phrase “the all of the gold.”
units.japanese: しかし、霧江はまだ少し引っ掛かると考えていた。もし勝利宣言ならば、勝者らしく、黄金を堂々と示し、家督を買い取ると宣言すればいいだけの話だ。なのに、わざわざこの期に及んで、碑文を解いてみろ、解けたら家督と黄金を全て引き渡そうと、“新たなゲーム”を仕掛けてくる意味が、どこにあるというのか。

units.text: However, Kyrie still felt something was slightly out of place. If this was a declaration of victory, Beatrice would only have to display the gold openly, and state that she would buy the family headship. And yet, even at this late stage, she was explicitly telling the siblings to try to solve the epitaph. Why had she set up this "new game", where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the right to succeed the head to the person who solved the epitaph?
units.note: Both editions retain the malformed phrase “the all of the gold.”
units.japanese: しかし、霧江はまだ少し引っ掛かると考えていた。もし勝利宣言ならば、勝者らしく、黄金を堂々と示し、家督を買い取ると宣言すればいいだけの話だ。なのに、わざわざこの期に及んで、碑文を解いてみろ、解けたら家督と黄金を全て引き渡そうと、“新たなゲーム”を仕掛けてくる意味が、どこにあるというのか。

description: 何万分の一 gives a concrete order of magnitude: a chance on the order of one in tens of thousands. Extremely small omits Kyrie's numerical framing.
sourceReading: Kyrie concedes that even if Beatrice expects failure, there remains perhaps a one-in-tens-of-thousands chance that the siblings solve the epitaph.

units.text: "The witch sent us a letter of challenge, forcing us to try and solve the epitaph.  She might be taking us lightly, thinking we could never solve it.  ......However, there should be at least an extremely small chance that we will solve it.
units.note: Both editions replace Kyrie’s one-in-tens-of-thousands scale with an unspecified extremely small chance.
units.japanese: 「魔女は、碑文を解いてみろと私たちに挑戦状を送ったわ。どうせ解けないだろうと、タカを括ってるでしょうけどね。……でも、何万分の一かの確率で、私たちが解いてしまう可能性もあるはず。

units.text: "The witch sent us a letter of challenge, forcing us to try and solve the epitaph. She might be taking us lightly, thinking we could never solve it. ...However, at the very least, there ought to be an extremely small chance that we do solve it."
units.note: Both editions replace Kyrie’s one-in-tens-of-thousands scale with an unspecified extremely small chance.
units.japanese: 「魔女は、碑文を解いてみろと私たちに挑戦状を送ったわ。どうせ解けないだろうと、タカを括ってるでしょうけどね。……でも、何万分の一かの確率で、私たちが解いてしまう可能性もあるはず」

units.text: "The witch sent us a letter of challenge, telling us to try to solve the epitaph. She might be taking us lightly, thinking we could never solve it. ......However, there should be at least an extremely small chance that we will solve it."
units.note: Both editions replace Kyrie’s one-in-tens-of-thousands scale with an unspecified extremely small chance.
units.japanese: 「魔女は、碑文を解いてみろと私たちに挑戦状を送ったわ。どうせ解けないだろうと、タカを括ってるでしょうけどね。……でも、何万分の一かの確率で、私たちが解いてしまう可能性もあるはず」

description: 彼女以外の人間が暴けたなら means if someone other than Beatrice managed to uncover the hiding place. If it was exposed to someone makes that person a passive recipient and removes the solving or discovery action central to Kyrie's risk analysis.
sourceReading: Beatrice's negotiating advantage would collapse if another person successfully uncovered the gold's hiding place.

units.text: The reason the witch had a superior position on the negotiations compared to the siblings was that only she knew the location of the hidden gold. But if that hiding place was exposed to someone other than her, the witch's superior position would crumble.
units.note: Both editions make someone other than Beatrice a passive recipient of the exposed hiding place instead of an agent who uncovers it.
units.japanese: だがもし、その隠し場所を彼女以外の人間が暴けたなら、魔女の優位は崩れる。

units.text: The reason the witch had a superior position in negotiations compared to the siblings...was that only she knew the location of the hidden gold. But if that hiding place was exposed to someone other than her, the witch's advantage would crumble.
units.note: Both editions make someone other than Beatrice a passive recipient of the exposed hiding place instead of an agent who uncovers it.
units.japanese: 魔女が４兄弟に対し交渉で優位に立てるのは、彼女が唯一、黄金の隠し場所を知っているからだ。だがもし、その隠し場所を彼女以外の人間が暴けたなら、魔女の優位は崩れる。

description: もしも解いたなら is a direct condition: if I solve it. If only I solved it is unidiomatic here and introduces a wistful or counterfactual nuance before Eva's determined challenge.
sourceReading: Eva asks whether solving the epitaph would make her head, then resolves to solve it and accept the witch's challenge.

units.text: If only I solved it, I would be made the head, right...? ...I'll solve it...  I'll accept the witch's challenge. As if those other idiot siblings could solve it.
units.note: Both editions retain the unidiomatic and wistful “If only I solved it” before Eva’s determined declaration that she will solve it.
units.japanese: もしも解いたなら、私を当主にしてくれるのね…？

units.text: If only I solved it, I would be made the Head, right...? ...I'll solve it... I'll accept the witch's challenge.
units.note: Both editions retain the unidiomatic and wistful “If only I solved it” before Eva’s determined declaration that she will solve it.
units.japanese: もしも解いたなら、私を当主にしてくれるのね…？…解いてやる…。魔女の挑戦を受けてやるわ。

units.text: If only I solved it, I would be made the head, right...? ...I'll solve it... I'll accept the witch's challenge.
units.note: Both editions retain the unidiomatic and wistful “If only I solved it” before Eva’s determined declaration that she will solve it.
units.japanese: もしも解いたなら、私を当主にしてくれるのね…？…解いてやる…。魔女の挑戦を受けてやるわ。

description: 左様でございますか means Is that so or Very well. Will that be acceptable instead asks Battler to approve the arrangement he has just ordered.
sourceReading: Ronove acknowledges Battler's instruction, says he will comply, and sarcastically predicts regret after the cookies cool.

units.text: "Will that be acceptable?  Then I shall do so.  You may eat them when they get cold and stale, and then regret as much as you like that you did not eat them when they were freshly baked."
units.note: Both editions ask whether the arrangement will be acceptable instead of acknowledging Battler’s instruction.
units.japanese: 「左様でございますか。それではそのようにいたしますよ。冷めてからお召し上がりになって、焼きたてを召し上がらなかったことを存分に後悔なされると良いでしょう。」

units.text: "Will that be acceptable? Then I shall do so. You may eat them when they get cold and stale, and then regret to the fullest that you did not eat them while they were fresh."
units.note: Both editions ask whether the arrangement will be acceptable instead of acknowledging Battler’s instruction.
units.japanese: 「左様でございますか。それではそのようにいたしますよ。冷めてからお召し上がりになって、焼きたてを召し上がらなかったことを存分に後悔なされると良いでしょう」

description: 冷めてから says to eat them after they have cooled. Cold and stale adds deterioration not stated in Japanese and not entailed by merely letting fresh cookies cool.
sourceReading: Ronove tells Battler to eat the cookies after they cool and regret not eating them freshly baked.

units.note: Both editions add that the cookies will become stale when Japanese says only that they will cool.

description: ご高説 sarcastically invites Battler's lofty exposition or learned theory. Opinion removes Ronove's mock deference and the inflated status he jokingly grants Battler's idea.
sourceReading: Ronove politely and sarcastically asks to hear Battler's supposedly lofty explanation after mocking his shallow wit.

units.text: "......In any case, it appears that you are now more confident regarding the matter of a 19th person's existence, right?  Would you be gracious enough to allow me to hear your opinion?"
units.note: Both editions reduce Ronove’s sarcastic invitation to a lofty exposition to a polite request for Battler’s opinion.
units.japanese: 「……大方、１９人目の存在に自信を深めたからでございましょう？　よろしければ、ぜひご高説をお聞かせ願えますか？」

units.text: "...In any case, it appears you are now more confident in the existence of a 19th person, yes? Would you be gracious enough to allow me to hear your opinion?"
units.note: Both editions reduce Ronove’s sarcastic invitation to a lofty exposition to a polite request for Battler’s opinion.
units.japanese: 「……大方、１９人目の存在に自信を深めたからでございましょう？　よろしければ、ぜひご高説をお聞かせ願えますか？」

units.text: "......I imagine it is because you have gained increased confidence in the existence of a 19th person? Would you be gracious enough to allow me to hear your opinion?"
units.note: Both editions reduce Ronove’s sarcastic invitation to a lofty exposition to a polite request for Battler’s opinion.
units.japanese: 「……大方、１９人目の存在に自信を深めたからでございましょう？　よろしければ、ぜひご高説をお聞かせ願えますか？」

description: 存分に says Battler can suspect the nineteenth person as fully or freely as he likes. WH omits that extent and says only that he can suspect the person and pursue a human-culprit theory.
sourceReading: Without suspecting the eighteen people he respects, Battler can direct suspicion at the nineteenth person to his heart's content and pursue a human culprit.

units.text: In any event, unlike how unprepared you were in the games up until now, let us call the fact that you now have a compass bearing on how to fight, ...a dramatic leap forward.  With this, you can suspect a 19th person and can pursue your theory that the culprit is a human, without having to doubt any of the 18 you love and respect."
units.note: MG omits the extent of suspecting the nineteenth person freely or fully. UP substitutes “easily,” which still does not convey doing so to one’s heart’s content.
units.japanese: 何れにせよ、これまでのゲームでの無策と違い、戦い方に指針を持たれるのは、劇的飛躍と申せましょう。これで戦人さまは、敬愛する１８人を疑わずに、存分に１９人目を疑い、人間犯人説を追求できるわけでございます。」

units.text: "In any event, in contrast to how unprepared you were in the previous games, the fact that you now have a compass bearing on how to fight... ...is a dramatic leap forward, let us say. With this, you can suspect a 19th person and pursue your theory that the culprit is a human, without having to doubt any of the 18 you love and respect."
units.note: MG omits the extent of suspecting the nineteenth person freely or fully. UP substitutes “easily,” which still does not convey doing so to one’s heart’s content.
units.japanese: 「何れにせよ、これまでのゲームでの無策と違い、戦い方に指針を持たれるのは、劇的飛躍と申せましょう。これで戦人さまは、敬愛する１８人を疑わずに、存分に１９人目を疑い、人間犯人説を追求できるわけでございます」

units.text: "In any event, unlike how unprepared you were in the games up until now, let us call the fact that you now have a compass bearing on how to fight...a dramatic leap forward. With this, you need not doubt any of the 18 you love and respect, and can easily suspect a 19th person, and pursue your theory that the culprit is a human."
units.note: MG omits the extent of suspecting the nineteenth person freely or fully. UP substitutes “easily,” which still does not convey doing so to one’s heart’s content.
units.japanese: 「何れにせよ、これまでのゲームでの無策と違い、戦い方に指針を持たれるのは、劇的飛躍と申せましょう。これで戦人さまは、敬愛する１８人を疑わずに、存分に１９人目を疑い、人間犯人説を追求できるわけでございます」

description: 迷う必要なんかないトリック describes tricks or incidents over which Battler need not remain uncertain if a nineteenth person exists. Tricks I could have mentioned without hesitation shifts the ease from resolving the incidents to speaking about them.
sourceReading: Several incidents, including Kanon's boiler-room death, would no longer leave Battler at a loss if he allowed a nineteenth person.

units.text: "That's it exactly.  Like in the first game, when Kanon-kun was killed in the boiler room, ...there were plenty of tricks I could have mentioned without hesitation, as long as a 19th person existed."
units.note: MG retains tricks Battler could mention without hesitation. UP instead calls them tricks he can use, separately changing explanatory incidents into tactical resources.
units.japanese: 「そういうことさ。最初のゲームの、嘉音くんが殺されたボイラー室とか、…他にも他にも、１９人目が存在していたなら、迷う必要なんかないトリックはいくつもある。」
candidates: tricks I could have mentioned without hesitation

units.text: "That's it exactly. Like in the first game, when Kanon-kun was killed in the boiler room, ...and a bunch of other places, ...there were plenty of tricks I could've mentioned without hesitation,
units.note: MG retains tricks Battler could mention without hesitation. UP instead calls them tricks he can use, separately changing explanatory incidents into tactical resources.
units.japanese: 「そういうことさ。最初のゲームの、嘉音くんが殺されたボイラー室とか、…他にも他にも、１９人目が存在していたなら、迷う必要なんかないトリックはいくつもある」

units.text: "That's it exactly. Like in the first game, when Kanon‐kun was killed in the boiler room, ...and a bunch of other places, there are countless tricks I can use without hesitation if a 19th person existed."
units.note: MG retains tricks Battler could mention without hesitation. UP instead calls them tricks he can use, separately changing explanatory incidents into tactical resources.
units.japanese: 「そういうことさ。最初のゲームの、嘉音くんが殺されたボイラー室とか、…他にも他にも、１９人目が存在していたなら、迷う必要なんかないトリックはいくつもある」

description: 何かを示されると broadly says when humans are shown or presented with something, they answer by demanding evidence. When you try to make some claim narrows the trigger to a verbal assertion and adds an explicit claimant.
sourceReading: Battler says humans characteristically respond to anything presented to them by demanding evidence.

units.text: When you try to make some claim to humans like us, we always counterattack by telling you to show some proof. Because that's a human move. But I'm fighting with a witch. I'm taking part in a battle with someone who isn't human!
units.note: MG retains a claim being made as the trigger for demanding proof. UP changes the broader presentation into humans being accused, a separate narrowing recorded under a paired ID.
units.japanese:
俺たち人間は、何かを示されると、必ず証拠を示せと反論する。
それが人間の指し手だからだ。

units.text: When you try to make some claim to humans like us, we always counterattack by telling you to show some proof. Because that's a human move. But I'm fighting with a witch. I'm taking part in a battle with someone who isn't human!
units.note: MG retains a claim being made as the trigger for demanding proof. UP changes the broader presentation into humans being accused, a separate narrowing recorded under a paired ID.
units.japanese:
俺たち人間は、何かを示されると、必ず証拠を示せと反論する。それが人間の指し手だからだ。だが、俺は魔女と戦っている。
人ならざる者との戦いに臨んでいる！

units.text:
When we humans are accused of something, we always counterattack by saying to show some evidence. Because that's a human move. But I'm fighting with a witch.
I'm taking part in a battle with someone who isn't human!
units.note: MG retains a claim being made as the trigger for demanding proof. UP changes the broader presentation into humans being accused, a separate narrowing recorded under a paired ID.
units.japanese:
俺たち人間は、何かを示されると、必ず証拠を示せと反論する。それが人間の指し手だからだ。だが、俺は魔女と戦っている。
人ならざる者との戦いに臨んでいる！

description: 前回の失敗 means Battler's previous mistake or failure, specifically allowing his resolve not to suspect the eighteen to waver. Previous defeat reframes the lesson as avoiding another loss in the game.
sourceReading: Battler declares that he will never again repeat the earlier failure of letting Beatrice exploit his wavering resolve and turn him against the eighteen.

units.text: "......Anyway, with this move, I won't have to doubt any of the 18 who are close to me again.  I won't repeat a defeat like last time again...!!"
units.note: Both editions call Battler’s previous mistake or failure a defeat, shifting his vow from avoiding the specific lapse of suspecting the eighteen to avoiding another overall loss.
units.japanese: 「……とにかく、この一手で俺は二度と親しい１８人のみんなを疑わなくて済む。俺は二度とッ、前回の失敗は繰り返さないッ…！！」

units.text: "...Anyway, with this move, I won't have to doubt any of the 18 who are close to me again. I won't suffer a defeat like last time again...!!"
units.note: Both editions call Battler’s previous mistake or failure a defeat, shifting his vow from avoiding the specific lapse of suspecting the eighteen to avoiding another overall loss.
units.japanese: 「……とにかく、この一手で俺は二度と親しい１８人のみんなを疑わなくて済む。俺は二度とッ、前回の失敗は繰り返さないッ…！！」

units.text: "......Anyway, with this move, I'll never again have to doubt any of the 18 who are close to me. I will never again repeat the defeat I suffered last time...!!"
units.note: Both editions call Battler’s previous mistake or failure a defeat, shifting his vow from avoiding the specific lapse of suspecting the eighteen to avoiding another overall loss.
units.japanese: 「……とにかく、この一手で俺は二度と親しい１８人のみんなを疑わなくて済む。俺は二度とッ、前回の失敗は繰り返さないッ…！！」

description: 鑑識 means forensic examination or identification work. Autopsies narrows the unavailable investigative capability to postmortem examination of bodies.
sourceReading: Because the typhoon prevents police access, Battler lacks scientific investigation and forensic examination of any kind.

units.text: However, in reality, that was infinitely impossible. The police wouldn't come here in this typhoon. We couldn't have a scientific investigation, we didn't have any experts on this sort of thing, and we couldn't do anything. In short, we couldn't show anything decisively! It was impossible for me to find any proof other than simply gulping down whatever alibis each of the 18 gave.
units.note: MG replaces autopsies with the broader but vague “experts,” removing the specific narrowing while failing to name forensic examination. UP retains autopsies.
units.japanese: 科学捜査も鑑識も何もない。

units.text:
However, in reality, that's as close as you can get to impossible. The police wouldn't come here in this typhoon.
There would be no scientific investigations, no autopsies, no nothing.
In short, I can't show anything decisively! It's impossible for me to find any proof other than simply gulping down whatever alibis each of the 18 give.
units.note: MG replaces autopsies with the broader but vague “experts,” removing the specific narrowing while failing to name forensic examination. UP retains autopsies.
units.japanese:
しかし、それは現実には限りなく不可能なのだ。ここには台風で警察が来られない。
科学捜査も鑑識も何もない。
つまり、何も確定的に示せない！俺には１８人が口々に主張するアリバイを鵜呑みにする以上の検証が不可能なのだ。

description: 鎖で縛って監禁する says all eighteen would have to be bound in chains and confined or imprisoned. Bound in chains and watch over them replaces confinement with supervision.
sourceReading: Battler says fully proving all eighteen boxes empty would require restraining and confining all eighteen people.

units.text: ...However, in reality, something like that was impossible! In other words, I would have to expend an incredible effort just to check the contents of one box. And there were 18 of them!  In other words, unless I bound all 18 of them in chains and watched over them, it would be impossible to prove that all of them had empty boxes.
units.note: Both editions replace binding and confining all eighteen with binding and watching them.
units.japanese: しかもそれを１８箱分も！　つまり、１８人全員を鎖で縛って監禁するくらいじゃなきゃ、全員の完全な空箱証明は不可能だ。

units.text: ...However, in practical terms, that'll be impossible! In other words, I'd have to expend an incredible effort just to check the contents of one box. And there are 18 of them! In other words, unless I bound all 18 of them in chains and watch over them, it'll be impossible to prove that all of them have empty boxes.
units.note: Both editions replace binding and confining all eighteen with binding and watching them.
units.japanese:
…しかし、そんなことは現実的に不可能だ！
つまり、俺にはたった１箱でも、その中身を確認するには膨大な手間を必要とするわけだ。しかもそれを１８箱分も！　つまり、１８人全員を鎖で縛って監禁するくらいじゃなきゃ、全員の完全な空箱証明は不可能だ。

units.text:
...However, in reality, something like that is impossible!
In other words, I have to expend an incredible effort just to check the contents of one box. And there are 18 of them! In other words, unless I bind all 18 of them in chains and watch over them, it's impossible to prove that all of them have empty boxes.
units.note: Both editions replace binding and confining all eighteen with binding and watching them.
units.japanese:
…しかし、そんなことは現実的に不可能だ！
つまり、俺にはたった１箱でも、その中身を確認するには膨大な手間を必要とするわけだ。しかもそれを１８箱分も！　つまり、１８人全員を鎖で縛って監禁するくらいじゃなきゃ、全員の完全な空箱証明は不可能だ。

description: 幸福である means being happy or fortunate. Blessed introduces specifically divine favor into the proposition before the following lines explain happiness as the claimed result of divine protection.
sourceReading: The proposition equates being happy with serving a god, then its purported contrapositive says a person who is not a servant must not be happy.

units.text: "It is a very, very convenient move.  Not only demons, but gods also use it.  When they propose 'blessed, therefore god's servant', the contrapositive is 'if a human is not a servant of god, then he must not be blessed'."
units.note: Both editions use blessed status for the proposition’s happiness, introducing divine favor before it is offered as the cause.
units.japanese: 「これはとてもとても便利な一手ですよ。悪魔どころか、神々も好む一手です。“幸福である＝神の僕”を命題とする時、対偶は“神の僕でない人間＝幸福であってはいけない”となります。」

units.text: "It is a very, very convenient move. Not only demons, but gods also use it. When they propose that "the blessed = the servants of a god", the contrapositive is "a human is not a servant of a god = he must not be blessed"."
units.note: Both editions use blessed status for the proposition’s happiness, introducing divine favor before it is offered as the cause.
units.japanese: 「これはとてもとても便利な一手ですよ。悪魔どころか、神々も好む一手です。“幸福である＝神の僕”を命題とする時、対偶は“神の僕でない人間＝幸福であってはいけない”となります」

units.text: "It is a very, very convenient move. Not only demons, but gods also use it. When you propose "blessed = God's servant", the contrapositive is "if a human is not a servant of God, then he must not be blessed"."
units.note: Both editions use blessed status for the proposition’s happiness, introducing divine favor before it is offered as the cause.
units.japanese: 「これはとてもとても便利な一手ですよ。悪魔どころか、神々も好む一手です。“幸福である＝神の僕”を命題とする時、対偶は“神の僕でない人間＝幸福であってはいけない”となります」

description: 箱が２つしかない states the premise that there are exactly two boxes. No more than two permits there to be only one, even though inferring that the other box wins requires two boxes.
sourceReading: Given exactly two boxes, proving the opened box is empty establishes that the other box is the winner.

units.text: That is because, as long as we accept the premise that there are no more than two boxes, the contrapositive shows that the other box is automatically the winner."
units.note: Both editions loosen the required premise of exactly two boxes to no more than two boxes.
units.japanese: そしてそれは、箱が２つしかないことを前提としている限り、それはもう片方の箱が自動的にアタリであることを対偶的に示している。」

units.text: "And as long as we accept the premise that there are no more than two boxes, the contrapositive shows that the other box is automatically the winner."
units.note: Both editions loosen the required premise of exactly two boxes to no more than two boxes.
units.japanese: 「そしてそれは、箱が２つしかないことを前提としている限り、もう片方の箱が自動的にアタリであることを対偶的に示している」

units.text: "And that means, as long as we accept the premise that there are no more than two boxes, the contrapositive shows that the other box is automatically the winner."
units.note: Both editions loosen the required premise of exactly two boxes to no more than two boxes.
units.japanese: 「そしてそれは、箱が２つしかないことを前提としている限り、もう片方の箱が自動的にアタリであることを対偶的に示している」

description: １８人しかいない says there are exactly or only eighteen people on the island. No more than eighteen supplies only an upper bound and permits fewer than eighteen.
sourceReading: Battler asks whether it is delusional to deny the witch while believing all eighteen people innocent on an island containing only those eighteen.

units.text: Was it really, ...impossible...?! To continue denying the witch on an island with no more than 18 people, and still believe in the innocence of those 18 people, .........or was that just a delusion?!  Was I just trying to escape reality?!
units.note: Both editions say the island has no more than eighteen people, loosening Battler’s exact known-population premise into an upper bound.
units.japanese: １８人しかいないこの島で、魔女を否定しつつ、にもかかわらず、１８人の無実を信じるなんて、………そんなのは妄想なのか？！　現実逃避でしかないのか？！

units.text: Is this...gonna be impossible after all...?! To continue denying the witch on an island with no more than 18 people... and still believe in the innocence of those 18 people... ...Is that just a delusion?! Am I just trying to escape reality?!
units.note: Both editions say the island has no more than eighteen people, loosening Battler’s exact known-population premise into an upper bound.
units.japanese: やはり、…無理なのか…？！１８人しかいないこの島で、魔女を否定しつつ、にもかかわらず、１８人の無実を信じるなんて、………そんなのは妄想なのか？！　現実逃避でしかないのか？！

units.text: Was it really...impossible...?! To continue denying the witch on an island with no more than 18 people, and yet still believe in the innocence of those 18 people... .........Was that just a delusion?! Was I just trying to escape reality?!
units.note: Both editions say the island has no more than eighteen people, loosening Battler’s exact known-population premise into an upper bound.
units.japanese: やはり、…無理なのか…？！１８人しかいないこの島で、魔女を否定しつつ、にもかかわらず、１８人の無実を信じるなんて、………そんなのは妄想なのか？！　現実逃避でしかないのか？！

description: アリバイの証明が終えられない says Beatrice could never finish proving the successive outsiders' alibis. Kept searching for their alibis replaces the impossible proof burden with an indefinite search for alibis.
sourceReading: Each proved alibi would make Battler posit another outsider, preventing Beatrice from ever completing the chain of alibi proofs.

units.text: "Hmm, I see.  .........Even if I somehow prove an alibi for the 19th person, as soon as I do, you will think up a 20th person, and claim that they are the culprit.  By repeating this endlessly, you would make it so I kept searching for their alibis for all eternity.  ......I see, I see, *cackle*cackle*!  Just like a demon king summoning a plague of locusts.  I wouldn't expect anything less from Kinzo's grandchild.  It looks like you have been gifted with a talent in summoning."
units.note: Both editions replace Beatrice’s endless burden of proving successive alibis with endlessly searching for alibis.
units.japanese: 「ふむ、なるほど。………妾が１９人目のアリバイを何らかの方法で証明したとしても。その瞬間にそなたは２０人目を生み出し、犯人だと主張する。これを無限に繰り返すことによって、妾は永遠に彼らのアリバイの証明が終えられないというわけか。……なるほどなるほど、くっくっくっく！　さながら蝗の大群を呼び出す魔王よな。さすがは金蔵の孫よ。召喚術の才能には恵まれていると見える。」

units.text: "Hmm, I see. ......Even if I somehow prove an alibi for the 19th person, as soon as I do, you will think up a 20th person and claim that they are the culprit. By repeating this endlessly, you would make it so I kept searching for their alibis for all eternity.
units.note: Both editions replace Beatrice’s endless burden of proving successive alibis with endlessly searching for alibis.

units.note: Both editions replace Beatrice’s endless burden of proving successive alibis with endlessly searching for alibis.
