description: 斬れば repeatedly depicts Beatrice cutting down each numbered outsider. When your person folds changes her active destruction into the piece conceding or collapsing on its own and introduces a card-game image.
sourceReading: Beatrice imagines cutting down each successive outsider only for Battler to summon another without end.

units.text: "......When your 19th person folds, you will call a 20th, and when your 20th person folds, you will call a 21st, and when your 21 person folds and your 22nd person folds, you will call 23rd person, a 34th person, a 64358223579673204th person, will you trifle with me for all eternity?!
units.note: Both editions make Battler’s successive outsider pieces fold instead of Beatrice cutting them down.
units.japanese: 「……妾が１９人目を斬れば、そなたは２０人目を呼び、２０人目を斬れば２１人目を呼び、２１人目を斬れば２２人目を斬れば、２３人目を呼び３４人目を呼び６４３５８２２３５７９６７３２０４人目を呼びッ、妾を永遠に翻弄できるとでも？！

units.text: "...When your 19th person folds, you will summon a 20th, and when your 20th person folds, you will summon a 21st, and when your 21 person folds and your 22nd person folds, you will summon a 23rd person, a 34th person, a 64358223579673204th person! Did you think you'd have me at your mercy for all eternity?!"
units.note: Both editions make Battler’s successive outsider pieces fold instead of Beatrice cutting them down.

units.note: Both editions make Battler’s successive outsider pieces fold instead of Beatrice cutting them down.

description: Japanese pictures the sole path Battler finds between two cliffs, with the abyss below if he falls, followed by a single tightrope. My only way across the chasm of Hell compresses the cliffs, abyss, and discovered path into a different generic chasm image.
sourceReading: Red truth is Battler's only path between cliffs over an abyss, a single tightrope that immediately develops into walking on a blade.

units.text: It was my only way across the chasm of hell.  Just a single tightrope. Her merciless blood-red blade was the only way I could survive. ...This wasn't just walking on a tightrope, it was like literally walking on the edge of a blade...
units.note: Both editions compress the path between cliffs over an abyss into a way across a chasm of Hell before retaining the tightrope and blade images.
units.japanese: 落ちれば奈落という、崖と崖の間に見出す唯一の活路。たった一本の綱渡り。
candidates: way across the chasm of hell

description: 弱点を抱え says Battler was burdened with the weakness of having to deny both the witch and the eighteen. Held on to a weak point makes the vulnerability sound like something he voluntarily maintained.
sourceReading: Battler carried an inherent double-denial weakness without understanding it, allowing Beatrice to exploit it in the previous game.

units.text: Of course I was afraid. Because of her contrapositive, my victory condition, the denial of the witch, meant that the culprit was a human. But I didn't want to search for the culprit amid the 18. ...Therefore, I held on to a weak point, since I had to claim that it couldn't be a witch or one of the 18 at the same time.  Since I had been unable to understand that last time, that was where she had hit me, leaving me tattered and defeated.
units.note: MG says Battler stuck to a weak position and UP says he held onto a weak point. Both make his structural burden sound voluntarily maintained.
units.japanese: …だからこそ、魔女も１８人も同時に否定しなければならないという弱点を抱え、にもかかわらずそれを理解できず、そこを突かれて前回はボロボロに負けた。
candidates: held on to a weak point

units.text: Of course I'm afraid. Because my victory condition is the denial of witches, then, to use her contrapositive logic, the culprit must be human. But I didn't want to search for a culprit amid the 18. ...That's what made me stick to a weak position, since I had to claim both that it couldn't be a witch and that it couldn't be one of the 18. Last time, I was unable to understand that, so that's where she hit me, leaving me tattered and defeated.
units.note: MG says Battler stuck to a weak position and UP says he held onto a weak point. Both make his structural burden sound voluntarily maintained.
units.japanese: もちろん、俺は恐れている。俺の勝利条件である魔女否定は、ヤツの言う対偶では、＝犯人は人間、となる。でも俺は、１８人の中に犯人を求めたくない。…だからこそ、魔女も１８人も同時に否定しなければならないという弱点を抱え、にもかかわらずそれを理解できず、そこを突かれて前回はボロボロに負けた。

units.text: Of course I'm afraid. In terms of her contrapositive, my victory condition—the denial of the witch—meant that the culprit was a human. But I didn't want to search for the culprit amid the 18. ...Therefore, I held on to a weak point, since I had to deny the witch and the 18 at the same time. Since I had been unable to understand that last time, that was where she had hit me, leaving me tattered and defeated.

sourceReading: Ronove teasingly urges Beatrice to make her next move before the tea goes cold.

units.text: "It appears to be a stalemate.  That black tea I worked so hard to make is getting cold, Milady."

candidates: black tea I worked so hard to make

description: あまりに有利な幸先 calls Beatrice's refusal an extremely favorable start or omen for Battler. A big sign of my advantage turns the favorable opening itself into evidence that he already possesses an advantage.
sourceReading: Battler treats Beatrice's refusal to state the worst red as an extraordinarily favorable beginning for his position.

units.text: But Beato had not proclaimed my ultimate and greatest weakness in red. She had rejected repeating it, even though there was no reason why she shouldn't have struck, even though it was a weakness she should have been drooling at. She hadn't sliced me up with red by using that move, which should have been as good as forking a rook and the king...! ......This was a big sign of my advantage.
units.note: Both editions turn Beatrice’s refusal into a sign of Battler’s advantage rather than an extremely favorable start.
units.japanese: ……これは、俺にとってあまりに有利な幸先だ。

units.text: But Beato hadn't proclaimed my ultimate and greatest weakness in red. description: 今日まで says that no one has answered Beatrice's question to this day, including the present. Until today can imply that the situation changed today and someone has now answered it.
sourceReading: Beatrice says that no one has ever answered who she is through the present moment; everyone still averts their gaze and evades her.

units.text: "......Who am I?  Until today, no one has answered me this question.  ......For some reason, everyone averts their gaze and evades me."
units.note: MG retains “Until today,” which can imply that an answer arrives today. UP restores “To this day.”
units.japanese: 「……妾は何者なのか。この問いに、今日まで応えてくれた者はおらぬ。……なぜか皆、目を逸らし、はぐらかす。」

description: この疑問を…抱かせないため says Kinzo's behavior seems intended to prevent Beatrice from continuing to harbor this doubt. Force me to stop my further questioning changes the internal uncertainty into overtly asking questions.
sourceReading: Beatrice reads Kinzo's dismissive laugh as another attempt to keep her from dwelling further on the unresolved question of her identity.

units.text: Kinzo laughed as though it was a trivial matter. ...However, I couldn't help but feel that this behavior was another attempt to force me to stop my further questioning.
units.note: Both editions retain stopping further questioning for Kinzo’s apparent attempt to prevent Beatrice from continuing to harbor the doubt.

sourceReading: Battler sarcastically marvels that occult-obsessed Kinzo supposedly possessed enough power to pin the Great Witch Beatrice to the island.

units.text: "Isn't that awesome.  Everyone knew Grandfather was obsessed with the occult, but......that he would have the power to root down the Great Witch Beatrice...
units.note: Both editions retain the malformed “root down” for Kinzo supposedly pinning Beatrice to the island.

description: その戒め is Kinzo's restraint or binding upon Beatrice. Escape his guard changes the object into a guard, watch, or defensive stance rather than the condition restraining her.
sourceReading: Beatrice says she tried every way she could to escape Kinzo's binding, but his barrier was too strong to break.

units.text: ......However, I never nodded my head.  I tried to do something to escape his guard, but that barrier was firm, and I couldn't break it."
units.note: MG retains escaping Kinzo’s guard for escaping his restraint. UP restores restrictions.

description: いつの間にか says Battler feels that, before he knew it, he was being made to swallow the witch story. Suddenly changes his belated recognition of a gradual transition into abrupt onset.
sourceReading: As he listens, Battler realizes that the purported witch-denial game has imperceptibly shifted into asking him to accept a witch narrative wholesale.

units.text: "Heh, in the beginning, I showed a little interest, thinking that there might be some huge hint hidden, but the more I ask, the weirder this story starts to get.  I get the feeling that even though this is supposed to be a game about denying witches, I'm suddenly being made to just swallow this story about witches."
units.note: Both editions retain “suddenly” for Battler realizing before he knew it that he was being led into accepting the witch story.
units.japanese: 「へ。最初は何か重大なヒントが隠されているだろうと、多少の興味を示したが。聞けば聞くほどおかしな話になっていく。魔女を否定するゲームのはずなのに、いつの間にか魔女話を鵜呑みにさせられていく気がするぜ。」

description: とてもわかりやすい modifies Beatrice's emotion: her loneliness is extremely easy to read despite her brazen expression. In that really easy to understand expression instead calls the expression itself readable and conflicts with its continued brazenness.
sourceReading: Battler glimpses the plainly legible emotion of loneliness beneath Beatrice's still-brazen outward expression when he rejects her story.

units.text: When I started showing a cold attitude, Beato acted unusually discouraged. Of course, her expression was still shameless..., but I had the feeling that I was able to catch a glimpse of loneliness because I hadn't found the story of her past interesting, in that really easy to understand expression of hers.
units.note: Both editions retain an easy-to-understand expression instead of the plainly readable emotion beneath Beatrice’s brazen expression.

description: ちょっぴりフォローしてやる means Battler gives Beatrice a small conciliatory follow-up or softens his treatment of her. Cover for her suggests taking over a duty, compensating for a mistake, or concealing something on her behalf.
sourceReading: Feeling a little sorry for Beatrice, Battler maintains his careless posture but offers a slight conciliatory gesture by inviting her to continue.

units.text: ......For some reason, that slight reaction made her seem pitiful, so even though I kept my careless attitude, I decided to cover for her slightly. Damn it, even though she's an irritating witch, I'm still weak against her because her chromosomes are XX...
units.note: MG retains “cover for her” for Battler’s slight conciliatory follow-up. UP’s “humor her” restores his decision to indulge and continue listening.
units.japanese: ……そのわずかの仕草が、どういうわけか気の毒に感じ、俺は投げ遣りな態度を崩さないまま、だけれどもちょっぴりフォローしてやる。

description: Ronove's honorific narration treats the reincarnated Beatrice as お嬢様, a human girl. It grew and it did not possess call her an inanimate thing across two clauses.
sourceReading: Ronove respectfully says that Milady grew into the former Beatrice's exact likeness but possessed no witch powers and remained human.

units.text: "Yes.  That is correct.  It grew to be completely identical.  However, it did not possess her power as a witch.  ......Milady was completely like a human."
units.note: MG retains “it” for the reincarnated human girl across the growth and witch-power clauses. UP restores “she.”

description: 隠し屋敷が実在する asks what assurance exists that the hidden mansion presently exists. Actually existed shifts the issue into whether it existed in the past.
sourceReading: Battler doubts that Kuwadorian is a real place at all and considers that Beatrice may have invented it on the spot.

units.text: ...No no no. This might be some bullshit Beato cooked up to confuse me. As if I could accept any of this...!  In the first place, Kuwadorian was it?  There's no proof whatsoever that a hidden mansion actually existed. Couldn't this be something she had just fabricated on the spot?

description: 指し手がなくなる describes a stalemate position in which the player has no legal move. All moves would disappear makes moves themselves vanish rather than become unavailable to the player.
sourceReading: Ronove contrasts perpetual repetition with stalemate: one repeats moves indefinitely, while the other leaves a player with no legal move and therefore deadlocks progress.

units.text: "Like that chess term, which means a perpetual repetition of moves, saying such a thing would make any further progress in this game impossible.  This would be the opposite of an endless repetition of moves, because all moves would disappear, and it would bring about a kind of deadlock.  In chess this would lead to a draw, just as if there were a perpetual repetition of moves.  ...However, there is no draw in you and Milady's game.  Therefore, I am unable to answer a question that would bring about a stalemate."
units.note: Both editions retain the image of all moves disappearing rather than a player having no legal move.
units.japanese: 「チェスの用語で、千日手のパーペチュアルと同様に、それ以上のゲーム進行が不可能になる宣言です。これは、千日手とは正反対で、指し手がなくなる、ある種の手詰まりの状態を指します。パーペチュアルに同じで、チェスではこれを引き分けにしております。…ただし、お嬢様と戦人さまのゲームでは引き分けがございません。ですので、ステイルメイトになる質問には、赤でお答えすることができないのです。」

units.text: "It's a chess term referring to a state in which, similar to a "perpetual check", any further progress in a game becomes impossible. This would be the opposite of an endless repetition of moves, because all moves would disappear, and it would bring about a kind of deadlock.
units.note: Both editions retain the image of all moves disappearing rather than a player having no legal move.

sourceReading: Because the game permits no draw, Ronove says he cannot provide a red answer that would halt the game in stalemate.

units.text: "Like that chess term, which means a perpetual repetition of moves, saying such a thing would make any further progress in this game impossible.  This would be the opposite of an endless repetition of moves, because all moves would disappear, and it would bring about a kind of deadlock.  In chess this would lead to a draw, just as if there were a perpetual repetition of moves.  ...However, there is no draw in you and Milady's game.  Therefore, I am unable to answer a question that would bring about a stalemate."
units.note: MG omits that Ronove specifically cannot answer the stalemate-producing question in red. UP restores the qualifier.
units.japanese: 「チェスの用語で、千日手のパーペチュアルと同様に、それ以上のゲーム進行が不可能になる宣言です。これは、千日手とは正反対で、指し手がなくなる、ある種の手詰まりの状態を指します。パーペチュアルに同じで、チェスではこれを引き分けにしております。…ただし、お嬢様と戦人さまのゲームでは引き分けがございません。ですので、ステイルメイトになる質問には、赤でお答えすることができないのです。」

units.text: In chess, this would lead to a draw, just as a perpetual check would. ...However, there can be no draws in the game between you and Milady. Therefore, I am unable to answer a question that would bring about a stalemate."
units.note: MG omits that Ronove specifically cannot answer the stalemate-producing question in red. UP restores the qualifier.
units.japanese: 「パーペチュアルに同じで、チェスではこれを引き分けにしております。…ただし、お嬢様と戦人さまのゲームでは引き分けがございません。ですので、ステイルメイトになる質問には、赤でお答えすることができないのです」

description: 確認するのを忘れてた says Battler realizes that he forgot to check something important. I was forgetting presents forgetting as an ongoing process rather than a completed omission he has just noticed.
sourceReading: Battler abandons the blocked population question and realizes he had forgotten to establish when the memory scene occurs.

units.text: ......I'll give up on that and search for a different question.  ...That's right.  I was forgetting to check something important.  .........This is a story about Beato's memories, right?  When did it happen?  It couldn't be happening right now, right?"

description: 右代宮家に名を連ねる者が情けない says Rosa's mother scolded her as pathetic or shameful for someone bearing the Ushiromiya name. My name was a disgrace says Rosa's own name itself disgraced the family.
sourceReading: Rosa's mother condemns her complaints as unworthy of a member of the Ushiromiya family, intensifying the pressure Rosa feels to meet its standards.

units.text: Even though my tutor had promised to keep it a secret, ...apparently, they told Mother all about how I had complained. Mother scolded me horribly, saying that my name was a disgrace to the Ushiromiya family. ......Of course, I was doing the best I could.
units.note: MG retains Rosa’s own name as a disgrace to the family. UP restores that Rosa herself was condemned as a disgraceful family member.

お母様は、右代宮家に名を連ねる者が情けないと、私をひどく叱ったわ。

units.text: Mother scolded me horribly, saying that my name was a disgrace to the Ushiromiya family. ......Of course, I was doing the best I could. But I had none of Krauss-san's dignity, I couldn't get excellent grades like Eva nee-san, and I had no leadership like Rudolf nii-san. ...I never stood out, didn't particularly excel at anything, and it was almost like I was asking myself why I had been born into the Ushiromiya family.

家庭教師が、内緒よと約束したはずなのに、…私が漏らした泣き言を、全てお母様に話してしまったらしい。お母様は、右代宮家に名を連ねる者が情けないと、私をひどく叱ったわ。

units.note: Both editions retain air becoming “thicker and thicker” instead of increasingly stagnant or stale around the warm fireplace.
units.japanese: それは例えるなら、冬の日の暖かな暖炉が、少しずつ空気を澱ませて頭痛を感じさせるようなもの…？

units.text: For example, maybe it was like how a hot fireplace on a winter day makes the air get thicker and thicker, giving you a headache... Even though you know you shouldn't keep things the way they are, you still need courage to open the window and be tormented by the cold wind...
units.note: Both editions retain air becoming “thicker and thicker” instead of increasingly stagnant or stale around the warm fireplace.
units.japanese: それは例えるなら、冬の日の暖かな暖炉が、少しずつ空気を澱ませて頭痛を感じさせるようなもの…？このままここに居続けてはいけないと知りつつも、窓を開け寒風に身を苛むには、なお勇気が必要なのだ…。

units.text: To liken it to something, perhaps it was similar to how a hot fireplace on a winter day makes the air get thicker and thicker, giving you a headache...? Even though you know that you shouldn't keep things the way they are, you still need the courage to open the window and be tormented by the cold wind...
units.note: Both editions retain air becoming “thicker and thicker” instead of increasingly stagnant or stale around the warm fireplace.
units.japanese: それは例えるなら、冬の日の暖かな暖炉が、少しずつ空気を澱ませて頭痛を感じさせるようなもの…？このままここに居続けてはいけないと知りつつも、窓を開け寒風に身を苛むには、なお勇気が必要なのだ…。

description: WH says Rosa was nervous about how to do it in secret. The source says the question arose of how she could do it without Father knowing, describing an unresolved practical doubt rather than explicitly naming anxiety.
sourceReading: Although Rosa wonders how she could possibly take Beatrice to those places without Father finding out, Beatrice’s delighted smile makes her nod along anyway.

units.text: ...I was nervous about how I would do it and keep it a secret from Father, ...but her face looked so happy, so I went along with her and nodded. But it seemed that the meaning behind my vague expression was not communicated to her. It seemed that she believed that I would really take her to all of those places.
units.note: Both editions retain explicit nervousness in place of Rosa’s practical question about secretly fulfilling the promise.
units.japanese: …お父様に内緒でどうやって、という疑問は沸いたけど、…彼女があまりに嬉しそうに笑うものだから、私は調子を合わせて頷いてしまう。

units.text: ...I was nervous about how I could keep it a secret from Father, ...but her face looked so happy, so I went along with her and nodded. But she seemed not to notice the meaning behind my vague smile. She seemed to believe that I'd really take her to all those places.
units.note: Both editions retain explicit nervousness in place of Rosa’s practical question about secretly fulfilling the promise.
units.japanese: …お父様に内緒でどうやって、という疑問は沸いたけど、…彼女があまりに嬉しそうに笑うものだから、私は調子を合わせて頷いてしまう。でも、彼女には私のそんな曖昧な笑顔の意味は伝わらないようだった。ここを出れば、私が本当にそれらへ連れてってくれると、信じたようだった。

units.text: ...I was nervous about how I would do it and keep it a secret from Father, ...but her face looked so happy, so I went along with her and nodded. But it seemed that the meaning behind my vague expression was not communicated to her. It seemed that she believed that I would really take her to all of those places if we left.
units.note: Both editions retain explicit nervousness in place of Rosa’s practical question about secretly fulfilling the promise.
units.japanese: …お父様に内緒でどうやって、という疑問は沸いたけど、…彼女があまりに嬉しそうに笑うものだから、私は調子を合わせて頷いてしまう。でも、彼女には私のそんな曖昧な笑顔の意味は伝わらないようだった。ここを出れば、私が本当にそれらへ連れてってくれると、信じたようだった。

description: WH translates 真っ逆さまに落ち as “fallen upside down.” The source says Beatrice fell headlong or straight down, describing the manner and direction of the fall rather than a static inverted posture.
sourceReading: Beatrice fell headlong from that height and struck her head hard on the pointed tip of the rocks below.

units.text: Beatrice had fallen upside down from a cliff of that height, ......and her head had smashed against the pointed tip of those sharp rocks. .........You would probably die, ......from that height, ......on those rocks......
units.note: Both editions retain “upside-down” in place of the source’s headlong or straight-down fall.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、岩壁のあの高さから真っ逆さまに落ち、……あの尖った岩の先端で頭部を強打した。

units.text: Beatrice had fallen upside down from a cliff of that height, ...and her head had smashed against the pointed tip of those sharp rocks. ............You would die, wouldn't you, after landing on those rocks... from that height...
units.note: Both editions retain “upside-down” in place of the source’s headlong or straight-down fall.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、岩壁のあの高さから真っ逆さまに落ち、……あの尖った岩の先端で頭部を強打した。…………死ぬだろ、……あの高さで、……こんな岩じゃ……。

units.text: Beatrice had fallen upside‐down from a cliff of that height, ......and her head had smashed against the pointed tip of those sharp rocks. ............You would die, wouldn't you, ......from that height, ......on those rocks......
units.note: Both editions retain “upside-down” in place of the source’s headlong or straight-down fall.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、岩壁のあの高さから真っ逆さまに落ち、……あの尖った岩の先端で頭部を強打した。…………死ぬだろ、……あの高さで、……こんな岩じゃ……。

description: WH changes 楼座叔母さんが立ち去った後, sometime after Rosa left, into “as soon as” she left, adding immediate timing to Battler’s speculative revival scenario.
sourceReading: Battler argues that Beatrice may really have remained alive and miraculously resumed breathing after Rosa departed.

units.text: Rosa oba-san probably just mistakenly thought that she was dead. But she was really alive, and as soon as Rosa oba-san left, would miraculously breathe again. ......And then she had somehow lived until today, and opened the curtain on the scene of her revenge. Otherwise, the facts wouldn't fit together!!
units.note: Both editions retain “as soon as” Rosa left, adding immediacy to Battler’s hypothetical revival.
units.japanese: だが本当は生きてて、楼座叔母さんが立ち去った後に奇跡的に息を吹き返したんだ。

units.text: Aunt Rosa probably just mistakenly thought she was dead. But she was actually alive, and as soon as Aunt Rosa left, would miraculously breathe again. ...Then, she somehow lived on until today...and opened the curtain on her revenge drama. Otherwise, the facts don't fit together!!
units.note: Both editions retain “as soon as” Rosa left, adding immediacy to Battler’s hypothetical revival.
units.japanese: 楼座叔母さんは死んだと思い込んでるだろう。だが本当は生きてて、楼座叔母さんが立ち去った後に奇跡的に息を吹き返したんだ。……そしてどうにかして今日まで生き延び、復讐劇の幕を開けるんだ。そうじゃなきゃつじつまが合わねぇ！！

units.text: Auntie Rosa probably just mistakenly thought that she was dead. But she was really alive, and as soon as Auntie Rosa left, she miraculously started breathing again. ......And then she somehow lived until today, and would open the curtain on the scene of her revenge. Otherwise, the facts don't fit together!!
units.note: Both editions retain “as soon as” Rosa left, adding immediacy to Battler’s hypothetical revival.
units.japanese: 楼座叔母さんは死んだと思い込んでるだろう。だが本当は生きてて、楼座叔母さんが立ち去った後に奇跡的に息を吹き返したんだ。……そしてどうにかして今日まで生き延び、復讐劇の幕を開けるんだ。そうじゃなきゃつじつまが合わねぇ！！

description: WH renders すぅっと落ちていった as “gently fell down.” The adverb depicts her body slipping or gliding smoothly away from the cliff, not a gentle fall; the latter softens a fatal ten-meter descent onto rocks.
sourceReading: After the abrupt cry, Beatrice’s body separates from the cliff and slips smoothly downward.

units.text: As she tried to ask me, she spoke in a funny, ...rushed and short voice, ...no, it was probably a scream. That voice rose suddenly. ......Her body separated from the cliff, and gently fell down.
units.note: MG changes the motion to a silent fall, avoiding the gentle characterization. UP retains “gently fell down.”
units.japanese: ……彼女の体が岩壁から離れて、すぅっと落ちていった。

units.text: She made...some might have described it as a funny, ...rushed and short voice, ...no, probably it was a scream, I think. She suddenly made a sound like that. ......Her body separated from the cliff, and gently fell down.
units.note: MG changes the motion to a silent fall, avoiding the gentle characterization. UP retains “gently fell down.”
units.japanese: 彼女が聞きようによっては滑稽な、…慌てた短い声、…いえ、多分それは悲鳴だったのかも。そんな声を唐突にあげた。……彼女の体が岩壁から離れて、すぅっと落ちていった。

description: WH omits すごい from Rosa’s description of blood pouring out, removing the explicitly tremendous or shocking quantity before it rapidly spreads like a red carpet.
sourceReading: Rosa recalls Beatrice lying with her eyes open while an enormous or shocking amount of blood poured out and rapidly spread into a red carpet.

units.text: "Yes, she died!!  It was a rocky beach, many sharp and dangerous rocks lay exposed!!  Her eyes were still open, the blood kept pouring out...suddenly a red carpet was spreading out...!
units.note: MG restores an incredible amount of blood. UP retains the omission of the source’s explicit quantity.
units.japanese: 「えぇ、死んだわッ！！　岩浜だったもの、尖った危険な岩がたくさんむき出しになっていた！！　目を見開いたまま、すごい血が溢れ出して…たちまち真っ赤な絨毯を広げていった…！

units.text: "Yes, she died!! It was a rocky beach, many sharp and dangerous rocks lay exposed!! Her eyes were still open, the blood kept pouring out... Suddenly a red carpet was spreading out...!"
units.note: MG restores an incredible amount of blood. UP retains the omission of the source’s explicit quantity.
units.japanese: 「えぇ、死んだわッ！！　岩浜だったもの、尖った危険な岩がたくさんむき出しになっていた！！　目を見開いたまま、すごい血が溢れ出して…たちまち真っ赤な絨毯を広げていった…！」

description: WH renders 妾の与り知れぬところで as “without me.” Beatrice complains that her body turned into a lump of meat outside her knowledge, not merely without her presence.
sourceReading: Meta-Beatrice mockingly complains that her body arbitrarily became a lump of meat somewhere beyond her knowledge.

units.text: "......How long do you plan on remaining dead?  Open your eyes already.  Seriously, just turning into a lump of meat without me."
units.note: MG changes “without me” to “while I’m gone,” still framing absence rather than knowledge. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese: 「……いつまで死んでいるつもりか。いい加減に目を覚ませ。まったく、妾の与り知れぬところで勝手に肉塊に姿を変えおって。」

units.text: "...How long do you plan on remaining dead? Open your eyes already. Darn you, turning into a lump of meat all by yourself while I'm gone."
units.note: MG changes “without me” to “while I’m gone,” still framing absence rather than knowledge. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese: 「……いつまで死んでいるつもりか。いい加減に目を覚ませ。まったく、妾の与り知れぬところで勝手に肉塊に姿を変えおって」

units.text: "......How long do you plan on remaining dead? Open your eyes already. Honestly, just turning into a lump of meat without me."
units.note: MG changes “without me” to “while I’m gone,” still framing absence rather than knowledge. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese: 「……いつまで死んでいるつもりか。いい加減に目を覚ませ。まったく、妾の与り知れぬところで勝手に肉塊に姿を変えおって」

description: WH renders 太もも姉ちゃん as “ass nee-chan.” Battler’s crude nickname explicitly refers to the woman’s thighs, not her buttocks.
sourceReading: Battler crudely says he was flirting with Beatrice’s “thighs lady” or “thighs nee-chan.”

units.text: "I was just flirting with your friend the ass nee-chan.  ......More importantly, what is all this?"
units.note: Both editions retain the substitution of buttocks for Battler’s explicit thigh-focused nickname.
units.japanese: 「お前ぇのとこの太もも姉ちゃんとイチャついてただけだぜ。

units.text: "I was just flirting with your ass nee-chan friends. ...More importantly, what the heck's going on here?"
units.note: Both editions retain the substitution of buttocks for Battler’s explicit thigh-focused nickname.
units.japanese: 「お前ぇのとこの太もも姉ちゃんとイチャついてただけだぜ。……それより、こりゃどういうことだ」

units.text: "I was just flirting with your friend the sexy‐assed chick. ......More importantly, what is all this?"
units.note: Both editions retain the substitution of buttocks for Battler’s explicit thigh-focused nickname.
units.japanese: 「お前ぇのとこの太もも姉ちゃんとイチャついてただけだぜ。……それより、こりゃどういうことだ」

description: WH changes Beatrice’s speculation that Rosa may have become frightened and wanted to flee the scene into Rosa having escaped from a scene that itself became frightening. It promotes a possible desire into completed action and shifts the fear away from Rosa.
sourceReading: Unable to see Rosa, Beatrice wonders whether she went to fetch a doctor or instead became frightened and wanted to flee the scene.

units.text: I already couldn't see Rosa. Had she gone to call a doctor, or had she escaped from a scene which had become frightening? ...That no longer matters. That soulless shell is no longer worth anything.
units.note: MG restores that Rosa herself was terrified but still makes her run away rather than possibly want to flee. UP retains WH’s wording and both changes.
units.japanese: 医者を呼びに行ったのか、恐ろしくなってこの場を逃げたくなったのか。

units.text: I couldn't see Rosa anymore. Did she go to call a doctor, or was she so terrified that she ran away? ...It no longer matters. That soulless shell no longer has any value.
units.note: MG restores that Rosa herself was terrified but still makes her run away rather than possibly want to flee. UP retains WH’s wording and both changes.
units.japanese:
楼座の姿はもう見えない。医者を呼びに行ったのか、恐ろしくなってこの場を逃げたくなったのか。…今更どうでもいいことだ。
魂の抜け殻に、今更何の価値もないのだ。

units.text:
Rosa was already nowhere to be seen. Had she gone to call a doctor, or had she escaped from a scene which had become frightening? ...That no longer matters.
That soulless shell is no longer worth anything.
units.note: MG restores that Rosa herself was terrified but still makes her run away rather than possibly want to flee. UP retains WH’s wording and both changes.
units.japanese:
楼座の姿はもう見えない。医者を呼びに行ったのか、恐ろしくなってこの場を逃げたくなったのか。…今更どうでもいいことだ。
魂の抜け殻に、今更何の価値もないのだ。

description: WH says Beatrice “destroyed” her human form. 姿を崩す says she let the form collapse or dissolved it before changing into butterflies, not that she destroyed it.
sourceReading: Because maintaining a human shape is painful in her weakened state, Beatrice dissolves that form and changes into several golden butterflies.

units.text: I destroyed my human form. Then I changed it to several gold butterflies. ......Hmm, with my magic power as frail as it is now, this form is easier.
units.note: Both editions retain “destroyed my human form” instead of dissolving or letting the form collapse.
units.japanese: 私は人の姿を崩す。

units.text: I destroyed my human form. Then, I changed it into several gold butterflies. ...Yes, with my magical power as frail as it is now, this form is easier to maintain.
units.note: Both editions retain “destroyed my human form” instead of dissolving or letting the form collapse.
units.japanese:
私は人の姿を崩す。
そして数匹の黄金の蝶に姿を変えた。……うむ、今の私の弱々しい魔力では、この程度の姿の方が楽でいい。

units.text:
I destroyed my human form.
Then I changed it to several gold butterflies. ......Yes, with my magic power as frail as it is now, this form is easier.
units.note: Both editions retain “destroyed my human form” instead of dissolving or letting the form collapse.
units.japanese:
私は人の姿を崩す。
そして数匹の黄金の蝶に姿を変えた。……うむ、今の私の弱々しい魔力では、この程度の姿の方が楽でいい。

description: WH translates ひらりと宙を舞いながら as “dancing alone through the air.” ひらり describes light or graceful fluttering motion; it does not say Beatrice is alone.
sourceReading: Fluttering lightly through the air, Beatrice looks down at the shore one final time.

units.text: Dancing alone through the air, I looked down at the shore one more time. On the rocky shore, lay the figure of what had once been me, ......and that I would eventually regain.
units.note: Both editions retain “dancing alone,” adding solitude and dropping the light fluttering motion.
units.japanese: ひらりと宙を舞いながら、もう一度だけ海岸を見下ろす。

units.text: Dancing alone through the air, I looked down at the shore one more time. On the rocky shore...lay the figure of what had once been me, ...the figure I would eventually regain.
units.note: Both editions retain “dancing alone,” adding solitude and dropping the light fluttering motion.
units.japanese: ひらりと宙を舞いながら、もう一度だけ海岸を見下ろす。岩浜に、かつての妾が、……そして、やがて妾が取り戻そうとしている姿が、横たわっている。

units.text: Dancing alone through the air, I looked down at the shore one more time. On the rocky shore lay the figure I had once possessed, ......and that I would eventually regain.
units.note: Both editions retain “dancing alone,” adding solitude and dropping the light fluttering motion.
units.japanese: ひらりと宙を舞いながら、もう一度だけ海岸を見下ろす。岩浜に、かつての妾が、……そして、やがて妾が取り戻そうとしている姿が、横たわっている。

description: WH’s “You may regret” turns 悔やむがいい from a taunting command—Kinzo should regret not being present—into permission or possibility.
sourceReading: Beatrice triumphantly tells the absent Kinzo to regret not being there, because he can no longer capture her.

units.text: *cackle*cackle*.  Oh, Kinzo. You may regret that you are not here now. No longer will you be able to capture me. ...*cackle*cackle*!
units.note: MG restores the taunting imperative “Regret.” UP retains the permissive “You may regret.”
units.japanese: 今この場にいないことを悔やむがいい。

units.text:
*cackle*cackle*. Oh, Kinzo.
You may regret that you are not here now.
No longer will you be able to capture me.
...*cackle*cackle*!
units.note: MG restores the taunting imperative “Regret.” UP retains the permissive “You may regret.”
units.japanese:
くっくっく、金蔵よ。
今この場にいないことを悔やむがいい。
もう妾を捕らえることはできぬぞ。
…くっくっくっく！

description: WH renders あらゆる秘術 as “every magic.” The source says Kinzo exhausted every secret or esoteric art for finding and capturing Beatrice, not every instance or system of magic.
sourceReading: During those twenty years, Kinzo failed in every secret art he attempted to locate and capture Beatrice.

units.text: ......That period of 20 years was fortunate for me.  Kinzo tried to use every magic to find and capture me, and failed in them all.  A human cannot bring about miracles very many times.  Even simply holding me captive for that long had been a miracle far above his place.  It would be unthinkable for me to be captured like that multiple times."
units.note: MG improves unidiomatic “every magic” to “all sorts of magic” but still generalizes secret arts to magic. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese: ……妾にとって幸運だったのは、その間の２０年間。金蔵は妾を探し出し捕らえるあらゆる秘術にことごとく失敗した点だったか。人間に起こせる奇跡の数などたかが知れている。妾をあれだけ長く捕らえていただけでも、充分に身に過ぎた奇跡だ。そう何度も捕らえられては堪らぬわ。」

units.text: "...That period of 20 years was fortunate for me. Kinzo tried to use all sorts of magic to find and capture me, but each failed.
units.note: MG improves unidiomatic “every magic” to “all sorts of magic” but still generalizes secret arts to magic. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese:
「……妾にとって幸運だったのは、その間の２０年間。金蔵は妾を探し出し捕らえるあらゆる秘術にことごとく失敗した点だったか」
「人間に起こせる奇跡の数などたかが知れている。妾をあれだけ長く捕らえていただけでも、充分に身に過ぎた奇跡だ。そう何度も捕らえられては堪らぬわ」

units.text: There's a limit to how many miracles a single human can bring about. Even simply holding me captive for that long had been a miracle far above his place. It would be unthinkable for me to be captured like that multiple times."
units.note: MG improves unidiomatic “every magic” to “all sorts of magic” but still generalizes secret arts to magic. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese:
「……妾にとって幸運だったのは、その間の２０年間。金蔵は妾を探し出し捕らえるあらゆる秘術にことごとく失敗した点だったか」
「人間に起こせる奇跡の数などたかが知れている。妾をあれだけ長く捕らえていただけでも、充分に身に過ぎた奇跡だ。そう何度も捕らえられては堪らぬわ」

units.text: "......What was fortunate for me was that during those twenty years, Kinzo tried to use every magic to find and capture me, and failed in them all."
units.note: MG improves unidiomatic “every magic” to “all sorts of magic” but still generalizes secret arts to magic. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese:
「……妾にとって幸運だったのは、その間の２０年間。金蔵は妾を探し出し捕らえるあらゆる秘術にことごとく失敗した点だったか」

units.note: MG improves unidiomatic “every magic” to “all sorts of magic” but still generalizes secret arts to magic. UP retains WH’s wording.
units.japanese:
「……妾にとって幸運だったのは、その間の２０年間。金蔵は妾を探し出し捕らえるあらゆる秘術にことごとく失敗した点だったか」
「人間に起こせる奇跡の数などたかが知れている。妾をあれだけ長く捕らえていただけでも、充分に身に過ぎた奇跡だ。そう何度も捕らえられては堪らぬわ」

description: WH renders 残りわずかな寿命の最後の一瞬 as “the last bit of his remaining life,” weakening the specific final instant of Kinzo’s dwindling lifespan into an extended final portion.
sourceReading: Kinzo stakes his life on the roughly one-in-three chance and hopes to reunite with Beatrice at the very last instant of his little remaining lifespan.

units.text: ......In other words, the odds that Kinzo will be able to meet me again are probably around one third.  He bet his own life on those odds, wishing for a reunion with me for the last bit of his remaining life."
units.note: Both editions retain “the last bit” of Kinzo’s remaining life instead of the final instant.
units.japanese: ……つまり、金蔵が妾に再び会える確率は大体、三分の一と言ったところか。その確率に自らの命を賭し、残りわずかな寿命の最後の一瞬に、妾との再会を望んだのだ。」

description: WH passively says the thirteen sacrifices “were chosen randomly.” With 妾 as the continuing subject, Beatrice says she capriciously chooses them, preserving her claimed agency and whim.
sourceReading: After accepting Kinzo’s game, Beatrice says she first chooses thirteen people capriciously as sacrifices and enjoys watching the resulting human conflict.

units.text: .........Then the 13 people were chosen randomly as sacrifices.  And by just doing that, you were all so confused, and when you showed me various aspects of the fabric of human relationships as you stood against me, it gave me great pleasure.  I really like this game of Kinzo's!  *cackle*cackle*."
units.note: MG retains passive random selection. UP restores Beatrice as the speaker who arbitrarily chooses the thirteen sacrifices.
units.japanese: ………そして１３人の生贄を気まぐれに決めるのだ。そしてその過程で、お前たちが右往左往し、妾に立ち向かおうと様々な人間模様を見せてくれることは、妾にとって非常に愉快なことだ。妾はこの金蔵のゲームを、実に気に入っている！　くっくっくっく。」

units.text: ......Then, 13 people are chosen at random to be sacrifices. While that happens, you all run about, showing me all kinds of human interactions as you try to oppose me, and entertaining me greatly. Yes, I truly have taken a liking to this game of Kinzo's! *cackle*cackle*."
units.note: MG retains passive random selection. UP restores Beatrice as the speaker who arbitrarily chooses the thirteen sacrifices.
units.japanese: 「………そして１３人の生贄を気まぐれに決めるのだ。そしてその過程で、お前たちが右往左往し、妾に立ち向かおうと様々な人間模様を見せてくれることは、妾にとって非常に愉快なことだ。妾はこの金蔵のゲームを、実に気に入っている！　くっくっくっく」

description: WH renders 妾こそが１９人目であろうな as the categorical “I am the 19th person.” The source is tauntingly inferential or concessive: she supposes that would make her the nineteenth person.
sourceReading: Responding to Battler’s demand, Beatrice agrees that she herself would presumably be the nineteenth person, immediately before denying that nineteen or more humans exist on Rokkenjima.

units.text: "That is true, I am the 19th person.  *cackle*cackle*!  But it's useless, right?  It's all useless!!"
units.note: MG categorically says “I am the 19th person.” UP intensifies this to “I most surely am,” removing rather than preserving the source hedge.
units.japanese: 「そうであるな、妾こそが１９人目であろうな。

units.text: "That is true, I am the 19th person. *cackle*cackle*! But it's useless, right? It's all useless!!"
units.note: MG categorically says “I am the 19th person.” UP intensifies this to “I most surely am,” removing rather than preserving the source hedge.
units.japanese: 「そうであるな、妾こそが１９人目であろうな。くっくっくっく！　だが駄目だぜ？　全然駄目だぁ！！」

units.text: "That is true, I most surely am the 19th person. *cackle*cackle*cackle*! But it's no good, I'm afraid...? It's no goddamn good at all!!"
units.note: MG categorically says “I am the 19th person.” UP intensifies this to “I most surely am,” removing rather than preserving the source hedge.
units.japanese: 「そうであるな、妾こそが１９人目であろうな。くっくっくっく！　だが駄目だぜ？　全然駄目だぁ！！」

description: WH says Battler can “prepare a culprit” among the eighteen. 犯人に仕立てあげる means he can frame, construct, or cast any of the eighteen as the culprit once he abandons appearances.
sourceReading: If Battler stops caring about appearances, he can freely frame any of the eighteen people as the culprit, making Beatrice’s route through all eighteen possibilities difficult.

units.text: ..........However, it will be difficult for me from here on.  If you throw away appearances, you could prepare a culprit freely amid 18 people!  Making you reach checkmate by evading those 18 pieces, .........will be truly difficult."
units.note: Both editions retain “prepare a culprit” rather than frame or cast one of the eighteen as the culprit.
units.japanese: ………しかし、妾はここからが難しいのだ。そなたは形振りさえ捨てれば、１８人もの人間を自在に犯人に仕立てあげられる！　その１８人の駒を潜り抜け、妾を認めさせチェックメイトに至るのは、

units.text: ......However, it will be difficult for me from here on out. If you choose to stop caring about propriety, you could prepare a culprit freely amid 18 people! Making you reach checkmate by evading those 18 pieces... ...will be truly difficult."
units.note: Both editions retain “prepare a culprit” rather than frame or cast one of the eighteen as the culprit.
units.japanese: 「………しかし、妾はここからが難しいのだ。そなたは形振りさえ捨てれば、１８人もの人間を自在に犯人に仕立てあげられる！　その１８人の駒を潜り抜け、妾を認めさせチェックメイトに至るのは、………実に難しいことよ」

units.text: ".........However, for me, the hard part is just beginning. You need only throw away appearances, and you can prepare a culprit freely amid the 18 people! Finding a route through those 18 pieces, in order to checkmate you and force you to accept me, .........will be truly difficult."
units.note: Both editions retain “prepare a culprit” rather than frame or cast one of the eighteen as the culprit.
units.japanese: 「………しかし、妾はここからが難しいのだ。そなたは形振りさえ捨てれば、１８人もの人間を自在に犯人に仕立てあげられる！　その１８人の駒を潜り抜け、妾を認めさせチェックメイトに至るのは、………実に難しいことよ」

description: WH says Shannon’s face “had been cooled off by” the frigid air. The source has Shannon actively cooling her flushed face in the cold air, an ongoing action rather than a completed passive result.
sourceReading: Outside the entrance, Shannon uses the cold air to cool her flushed face after George’s proposal.

units.text: In front of the entrance hall, Shannon's previously burning face had been cooled off by the frigid air. ...She had thought, ......that George's proposal would surely come sometime. It wasn't that her heart was not prepared. And she had nodded as if in answer.
units.note: MG retains a completed passive result, adding “once burning.” UP restores Shannon actively cooling her flushed face.
units.japanese: 紗音は玄関前で、冷えた空気に火照った顔を冷ましていた。
candidates: face had been cooled off by the frigid air

units.text: In front of the entrance hall, Shannon's once burning face had been cooled off by the frigid air. ...She had thought... that George's proposal would surely come sooner or later. It wasn't as though she hadn't prepared herself mentally. And she had answered by nodding.
units.note: MG retains a completed passive result, adding “once burning.” UP restores Shannon actively cooling her flushed face.
units.japanese:
紗音は玄関前で、冷えた空気に火照った顔を冷ましていた。…譲治からの求婚は、……きっといつかあるだろうと思っていた。心の準備はなかったわけではない。
そして、応える形で頷いてしまった。
candidates: face had been cooled off by the frigid air

description: WH renders 浮かれた気持ち as “emotions welling up inside her.” The source specifically says Shannon drives away her buoyant, elated mood when she hears the approaching footsteps.
sourceReading: Hearing someone run toward her through the puddles, Shannon immediately suppresses the elation left by the proposal.

units.text: As she did. she heard the sound of footsteps splashing through puddles. Shannon immediately chased away the emotions welling up inside her.
units.note: Both editions retain generic “emotions welling up” rather than Shannon’s specifically elated mood.
units.japanese: 紗音はすぐに浮かれた気持ちを追い出した。

units.text: As she did, she heard the sound of footsteps splashing through puddles. Shannon immediately chased away the emotions welling up inside her.
units.note: Both editions retain generic “emotions welling up” rather than Shannon’s specifically elated mood.
units.japanese: そこへ、ばたばたと水溜りを踏み散らしながら駆けてくる足音を聞く。紗音はすぐに浮かれた気持ちを追い出した。

units.text: As she did, she heard the sound of footsteps coming towards her, splashing through puddles. Shannon immediately chased away the emotions welling up inside her.
units.note: Both editions retain generic “emotions welling up” rather than Shannon’s specifically elated mood.
units.japanese: そこへ、ばたばたと水溜りを踏み散らしながら駆けてくる足音を聞く。紗音はすぐに浮かれた気持ちを追い出した。

description: WH says Kanon stepped in the puddles. 水溜りを踏むことになろうとも is hypothetical: even if he were to step in a puddle, his sound would be quieter than the rain.
sourceReading: Kanon suppresses his presence so completely that even if he stepped in a puddle, the sound would be far quieter than rain striking it.

units.text: Kanon was especially good at hiding his footsteps. ...Like he was a cat. He was able to suddenly be there without anyone noticing, and leave in the same way. For example, even though he stepped in the puddles, the sound he made was far smaller than that of the rain hitting the puddles...
units.note: MG retains an actual puddle step. UP restores the hypothetical “even if” illustration.
units.japanese: だから例え、水溜りを踏むことになろうとも、その音は水溜りを叩く雨音よりも遥かに小さい…。

units.text: Kanon was especially good at hiding his footsteps. ...Just like a cat. He was able to suddenly be there without anyone noticing and leave in the same way. For example, even though he stepped in puddles, the sound he made was far smaller than that of the rain hitting them...
units.note: MG retains an actual puddle step. UP restores the hypothetical “even if” illustration.
units.japanese: 嘉音は特に、気配を殺せるように出来ている。…例えるならば猫。誰にも気取られることなく、いつの間にかそこにいて、いつの間にか立ち去ることができる。だからたとえ、水溜りを踏むことになろうとも、その音は水溜りを叩く雨音よりも遥かに小さい…。

description: WH writes “a desecration to the result.” Standard English requires desecration of the result.
sourceReading: Repeating a tarot reading desecrates both the divination’s result and the higher being that grants revelation through the cards.

units.text: The most forbidden action in tarot reading was to try predicting the same thing twice. That was a desecration to the result of the fortune telling, and also desecrated the existence higher than humans which became an oracle through the tarot cards.
units.note: MG avoids the preposition error by replacing desecration with ridicule, creating a separate word-choice defect. UP retains “desecration to.”
units.japanese: それは占いの結果に対する冒涜であり、タロットを通じて神託を与えてくれる、人より上位の存在への冒涜ともなるのである。

units.text: The most forbidden action in tarot reading is to try predicting the same thing twice. It is a desecration to the result of the fortune telling, and also desecrates the existence higher than humans which delivers signs through the tarot cards.
units.note: MG avoids the preposition error by replacing desecration with ridicule, creating a separate word-choice defect. UP retains “desecration to.”
units.japanese: タロット占いでもっとも禁じられている行為は、同じことを二度占うことである。それは占いの結果に対する冒涜であり、タロットを通じて神託を与えてくれる、人より上位の存在への冒涜ともなるのである。

description: WH renders Genji’s formal 扉を失礼させていただきます as “Excuse us about the door.” He is respectfully announcing and apologizing that he will open or enter through the door without Kinzo’s permission.
sourceReading: After receiving no answer, Genji formally asks his master’s pardon for opening the study door himself.

units.text: "Master.  Excuse us about the door."
units.note: Both editions retain the unidiomatic “Excuse us about the door.”
units.japanese: 「お館様。扉を失礼させていただきます。」

units.text: "Master, excuse us about the door."
units.note: Both editions retain the unidiomatic “Excuse us about the door.”
units.japanese: 「お館様。扉を失礼させていただきます」

units.text: "My lord. Excuse us about the door."
units.note: Both editions retain the unidiomatic “Excuse us about the door.”
units.japanese: 「お館様。扉を失礼させていただきます」

description: WH says Genji “turned it heavily.” 重い手応えで describes the heavy resistance or feel he receives while turning the key, not the manner or force with which he turns it.
sourceReading: Genji inserts the key and turns it against a heavy, lock-like resistance.

units.text: Genji pulled a gold key out of his pocket. It was the only key to the study that existed, other than the one Kinzo held. He stuck it in the key hole, and turned it heavily. ......At first glance, it looked like that meant that is really was a strong lock.
units.note: Both editions retain “turned it heavily” instead of describing heavy resistance from the key or lock.
units.japanese: 鍵穴にそれを刺し、重い手応えで捻る。

units.text: Genji pulled a gold key out of his pocket. It was the only key to the study that existed, other than the one Kinzo held. He stuck it in the key hole and turned it heavily. ...At first glance, that seemed to prove that it was a sturdy lock.
units.note: Both editions retain “turned it heavily” instead of describing heavy resistance from the key or lock.
units.japanese:
源次は懐より、黄金の鍵を取り出す。
金蔵が持つ以外に、唯一存在する書斎の鍵だ。鍵穴にそれを刺し、重い手応えで捻る。
……一見、それは確かに厳重な施錠を示した。

units.text:
Genji pulled a gold key out of his pocket.
It was the only key to the study that existed, other than the one Kinzo held. He stuck it in the keyhole, and turned it heavily.
......At a glance, that would have indicated that it really was a strong lock.
units.note: Both editions retain “turned it heavily” instead of describing heavy resistance from the key or lock.

源次は懐より、黄金の鍵を取り出す。

……一見、それは確かに厳重な施錠を示した。

description: WH says the key’s heavy response indicates “a strong lock.” 厳重な施錠 describes the door appearing securely locked, a state, rather than the lock mechanism being sturdy or strong.
sourceReading: To ordinary physical observation, the heavy turn appears to show that the study door was securely locked, even though the magical barrier was already broken.

units.text: Genji pulled a gold key out of his pocket. It was the only key to the study that existed, other than the one Kinzo held. He stuck it in the key hole, and turned it heavily. ......At first glance, it looked like that meant that is really was a strong lock.
units.note: Both editions still describe a sturdy or strong lock rather than the observed securely locked state.

description: WH calls Kanon’s gaze “disrespectful.” 畏怖を感じないその眼 means his eyes show no awe or fear; Lucifer resents his fearlessness, not a breach of respect or manners.
sourceReading: Lucifer hates the eyes with which Kanon faces her without awe or fear.

units.text: Hehhheheheheheheheheh, that disrespectful gaze of yours... ...is really ticking me oooffff!!"
units.note: Both editions retain “disrespectful gaze” for Kanon’s eyes showing no fear or awe.
units.japanese: ふっふふふふふふふふふッ、気に入らないわぁ、畏怖を感じないその眼っ、

units.text: Hehhheheheheheheheheh, that disrespectful gaze of yours... ...is really ticking me offff!!"
units.note: Both editions retain “disrespectful gaze” for Kanon’s eyes showing no fear or awe.
units.japanese: 「ふっふふふふふふふふふッ、気に入らないわぁ、畏怖を感じないその眼っ、本当に気に入らないわぁああッ！！」

units.text: "Hehhheh{0eh{0eh{0eh{0eh{0eheheh, I don't like it, that disrespectful gaze of yours... I really don't like iiiiit!!"
units.note: Both editions retain “disrespectful gaze” for Kanon’s eyes showing no fear or awe.
units.japanese: 「ふっふふふふふふふふふッ、気に入らないわぁ、畏怖を感じないその眼っ、本当に気に入らないわぁああッ！！」

description: WH calls the gaping puncture through Kanon’s hand “an air hole.” 風穴 here is a large through-hole or wound, not a ventilation opening.
sourceReading: After Kanon pulls out the stake, a gruesome hole remains through the back of his hand, large enough to see through.

units.text: When she heard the sound of breaking bones and even more blood dripping down, Shannon looked away without thinking. There was an air hole in the back of the pierced hand so big that you could clearly see through to the other side...
units.note: Both editions retain the literal and inappropriate “air hole” description of the through-wound.
units.japanese: 抜いた手の甲には、はっきりと向こうを覗くことが出来るほどの無惨な風穴が残されていた…。

units.text: When she heard the sound of breaking bones and even more blood dripping down, Shannon looked away reflexively. There was an air hole in the back of the pierced hand so big, you could clearly see through to the other side...
units.note: Both editions retain the literal and inappropriate “air hole” description of the through-wound.
units.japanese:
骨を抉る音と、さらに血が零れる音が聞こえた。
紗音は思わず目を背ける。抜いた手の甲には、はっきりと向こうを覗くことが出来るほどの無惨な風穴が残されていた…。

units.text:
The sound of breaking bones and even more blood dripping down could be heard.
Shannon instinctively averted her eyes. There was an air hole in the back of the pierced hand so big that you could clearly see through to the other side...
units.note: Both editions retain the literal and inappropriate “air hole” description of the through-wound.
units.japanese:
骨を抉る音と、さらに血が零れる音が聞こえた。
紗音は思わず目を背ける。抜いた手の甲には、はっきりと向こうを覗くことが出来るほどの無惨な風穴が残されていた…。

description: WH writes that Lucifer’s shame “effects all the sisters.” The verb meaning influences or has an impact on is affects; effects means brings about or causes.
sourceReading: Satan says Lucifer’s disgrace lowers or damages the standing of all seven sisters.

units.text: "That's enough!  Come on, this shame effects all the sisters!  We won't let them return alive!"
units.note: MG retains “shame effects us all”; UP uses a correct construction describing shame brought upon the sisters.
units.japanese: 「もう充分よ！　さぁ、この屈辱は姉妹全員の屈辱！　生かして帰しはしないわよッ！」

units.text: "That's enough! Come on, this shame effects us all! We won't let them leave here alive!"
units.note: MG retains “shame effects us all”; UP uses a correct construction describing shame brought upon the sisters.
units.japanese: 「もう充分よ！　さぁ、この屈辱は姉妹全員の屈辱！　生かして帰しはしないわよッ！」

description: WH writes “an hatchet.” In standard modern English, hatchet begins with a pronounced consonant and takes the article a.
sourceReading: The sisters cut into Shannon’s barrier as if using a hatchet, then a saw, and finally a chainsaw.

units.text: The sound like beetles jumping around grew even more fierce and filled the room. The red barrier started to get cut up and eroded away as though with an hatchet, a saw, no, a chainsaw by now...
units.note: MG retains “an hatchet”; UP correctly uses “a hatchet.”
units.japanese: 赤い結界を斧で鋸で、いや、今やチェーンソーのように切り刻み、侵食していく…。

units.text: A sound like beetles jumping about grew even fiercer and filled the room. The red barrier began to be cut up and eroded away as though with an hatchet, a saw...no, a chainsaw by now...
units.note: MG retains “an hatchet”; UP correctly uses “a hatchet.”
units.japanese: 甲虫が跳ね回って飛び回るような音が、さらに激しくなって部屋を満たす。赤い結界を斧で鋸で、いや、今やチェーンソーのように切り刻み、侵食していく…。

description: WH begins Beatrice’s balloon-of-life explanation with “Even though,” leaving it as a sentence fragment and changing her causal claim into a concession without a main clause.
sourceReading: Beatrice complains that Genji is boring because the fun of a balloon of life lies in pricking it with a needle and making it burst vigorously.

units.text: "......What a boring person.  ...Even though it's fun to poke the balloon of life with a needle so that it forcefully explodes."
units.note: MG retains the fragmentary “Even though” construction; UP restores a complete causal explanation of the balloon metaphor.
units.japanese: 「……つまらぬヤツ。…生命の風船は、針にて突き、威勢よく割るから面白いのだろうが。」

units.text: "...What a boring person. ...Even though it's so fun to poke the balloon of life with a needle so that it forcefully explodes."
units.note: MG retains the fragmentary “Even though” construction; UP restores a complete causal explanation of the balloon metaphor.
units.japanese: 「……つまらぬヤツ。…生命の風船は、針にて突き、威勢よく割るから面白いのだろうが」

description: WH renders 気に留めるほどにもございません as “not enough to pay attention to.” Ronove politely says the matter is not even worth Beatrice’s concern or notice.
sourceReading: Ronove reminds Beatrice that a Great Witch should regard this incident as beneath her notice and should not lose composure over Shannon’s provocation.

units.text: "Are you not a powerful Great Witch, Milady?  Something such as this is not enough to pay attention to.  ......Having the blood rush to your head because of provocation from someone like Shannon, isn't like you."
units.note: MG idiomatically says the event is hardly worthy of Beatrice’s concern; UP retains “not enough to pay attention to.”
units.japanese: 「お嬢様は偉大なる大魔女ではございませんか。この程度、気に留めるほどにもございませんよ。

units.text: "Are you not a powerful Great Witch, Milady? Something such as this is not enough to pay attention to. ......It is not like you to allow the blood to rush to your head because of provocation from someone like Shannon."
units.note: MG idiomatically says the event is hardly worthy of Beatrice’s concern; UP retains “not enough to pay attention to.”
units.japanese: 「お嬢様は偉大なる大魔女ではございませんか。この程度、気に留めるほどにもございませんよ。……紗音ごときの挑発で頭に血を上らせるなど、らしくもない」

description: WH says the lid of one pot falls off. 一部の鍋は蓋を落として says some of the pots lose their lids before more pots follow, not that only one pot does.
sourceReading: The kitchen-wide rattling intensifies until lids fall from some pots; then other pots lose their lids one after another and arms emerge.

units.text: All of the pots and utensils in the kitchen started clanking at once. It grew even stronger, so that finally, the lid to one of the pots fell off...! And, ......from inside that pot, .........a slender white arm reached out.
units.note: Both editions say one pot lid initially falls, rather than lids falling from some pots.
units.japanese: それはさらに一層強くなり、とうとう一部の鍋は蓋を落としてしまうほどにまでなる…！

units.text: All of the pots and dishes in the kitchen started clanking at once. It grew even stronger, so that finally, the lid to one of the pots fell off...! And...from inside that pot, ......a slender white arm reached out.
units.note: Both editions say one pot lid initially falls, rather than lids falling from some pots.
units.japanese: 厨房中の鍋が、食器が、一斉にカタカタと音を鳴らし始める。それはさらに一層強くなり、とうとう一部の鍋は蓋を落としてしまうほどにまでなる…！そして、……蓋を落とした鍋の中からは、………ぬぅぅっと、白く細い腕が、伸びだす。

units.text: All of the pots and utensils in the kitchen started clanking at once. And it grew stronger still, until finally, it became so strong that the lid to one of the pots fell off...! And, ......from inside that pot, .........a slender white arm slowly streeeetched out.
units.note: Both editions say one pot lid initially falls, rather than lids falling from some pots.
units.japanese: 厨房中の鍋が、食器が、一斉にカタカタと音を鳴らし始める。それはさらに一層強くなり、とうとう一部の鍋は蓋を落としてしまうほどにまでなる…！そして、……蓋を落とした鍋の中からは、………ぬぅぅっと、白く細い腕が、伸びだす。

description: WH says Gohda “had not slighted that.” The source idiom says that despite his wry smile, he respects the local practice in accordance with “when in Rome”; the English object and phrasing are unnatural.
sourceReading: Gohda privately regarded the witch talk as childish, but outwardly respected and followed the island’s custom.

units.text: He had smiled bitterly, but he had thought when in Rome, do as the Romans do, and had not slighted that. Gohda went along with it on the outside, but in his heart he had thought it was a childish trick.  ......At first.
units.note: MG idiomatically says Gohda took the custom seriously; UP retains “had not slighted that.”
units.japanese:
苦笑はするが、それを蔑ろにしないのが、郷に入りては郷に従えというもの。
郷田も上辺は合わせたが、内心は子供だましだと思っていたものだ。……最初は。

units.text: He smiled bitterly, but he thought when in Rome, do as the Romans do, and had not slighted that. Gohda went along with it on the outside, but in his heart he thought it was a childish trick. ......At first.
units.note: MG idiomatically says Gohda took the custom seriously; UP retains “had not slighted that.”
units.japanese: 苦笑はするが、それを蔑ろにしないのが、郷に入りては郷に従えというもの。郷田も上辺は合わせたが、内心は子供だましだと思っていたものだ。……最初は。

description: WH calls Beatrice and her teacher’s meeting a “long awaited reunion.” 久し振りの再会 means a reunion after a long absence; it does not say either party desired it, and the teacher has just said she hoped never to be awakened or reunited.
sourceReading: Beatrice mockingly asks what tea she should prepare for their reunion after so long apart; the teacher accepts the hospitality while treating her awakening as regrettable.

units.text: "Well then.  ......Teacher.  What tea shall I prepare for our long awaited reunion?"
units.note: Both editions call the reunion “long-awaited,” despite the teacher’s stated wish never to awaken or meet again.
units.japanese: 「さぁって。……お師匠様。久し振りの再会にはどんなお茶のご用意が良いかなぁ？」

units.text: "Well then, ...Teacher, what tea shall I prepare for our long-awaited reunion?"
units.note: Both editions call the reunion “long-awaited,” despite the teacher’s stated wish never to awaken or meet again.
units.japanese: 「さぁって。……お師匠様。久し振りの再会にはどんなお茶のご用意が良いかなぁ？」

units.text: "Well then. ......Master. What tea shall I prepare for our long awaited reunion?"
units.note: Both editions call the reunion “long-awaited,” despite the teacher’s stated wish never to awaken or meet again.
units.japanese: 「さぁって。……お師匠様。久し振りの再会にはどんなお茶のご用意が良いかなぁ？」

description: WH calls Beatrice’s welcome “hospitality with a very quick temper,” unnaturally assigning a temperament to hospitality. The teacher dryly calls it a characteristically impatient or short-tempered reception.
sourceReading: After Battler’s panicked outburst, the teacher teases Beatrice that this is a very impatient form of hospitality, just like her.

units.text: "Hoh-hoh-ho...  Just like you, hospitality with a very quick temper."
units.note: Both editions retain “hospitality with a very quick temper.”
units.japanese: 「ほっほっほ…。あなたらしい、とても短気な持て成しですね。」
candidates: hospitality with a very quick temper

units.text: "Hohohoh... That's just like you, hospitality with a very quick temper."
units.note: Both editions retain “hospitality with a very quick temper.”
units.japanese: 「ほっほっほ…。あなたらしい、とても短気なもてなしですね」
candidates: hospitality with a very quick temper

units.note: Both editions retain “hospitality with a very quick temper.”

description: WH replaces Beatrice’s comparison to “a single bean” before the enormous iron hammer with the generic “a mere speck,” losing the concrete comic scale image.
sourceReading: Before the whirlwind of the gigantic mass of iron, Beatrice is no more than a single bean.

units.text: Before the whirlwind of this massive chunk of metal, Beatrice was nothing more than a mere speck. The instant the whirlwind started to suck Beatrice in, Beatrice's form turned into a massive War Tower. The Iron Hammer smashed the War Tower, scattered tremendous amounts of rubble, but it did not reach she who had escaped behind it.
units.note: Both editions replace the single-bean comparison with a generic speck.
units.japanese: 巨大な鉄塊の旋風の前に、ベアトリーチェなど一粒の豆に過ぎない。

units.text: Before the whirlwind of that massive chunk of metal, Beatrice was nothing more than a mere speck. The instant the whirlwind started to suck Beatrice in, she appeared to change into a massive War Tower. The Iron Hammer smashed the War Tower, scattering tremendous amounts of rubble, but it did not reach she who had escaped behind it.
units.note: Both editions replace the single-bean comparison with a generic speck.
units.japanese: 巨大な鉄塊の旋風の前に、ベアトリーチェなど一粒の豆に過ぎない。その旋風がベアトリーチェを飲み込もうとした瞬間、ベアトリーチェの姿が巨大な戦塔に変わる。鉄槌は戦塔を砕き、凄まじい瓦礫を撒き散らすが、その後へと逃れていた彼女には届かなかった。

description: WH calls Beatrice’s final trump card “a War Tower for dodging.” 変わり身の戦塔 is a substitution or decoy tower that takes her place and saves her from danger once; the mechanism is replacement, not enhanced evasion.
sourceReading: Beatrice converts or substitutes a one-use War Tower for herself, letting the hammer strike the tower while she escapes behind it.

units.text: However, this War Tower truly was the witch's last trump card. It was a War Tower for dodging that could only save her from danger once. But this tower was impregnable.  No weapon could break through it.
units.note: Both editions retain “War Tower for dodging” instead of the one-use substitution or decoy mechanism.
units.japanese:
しかし、この戦塔は実は魔女の最後の切り札だった。
危機をたった一度だけ救ってくれる変わり身の戦塔だったのだ。

units.text: However, this War Tower was actually the witch's last trump card. It was a War Tower for dodging that could only save her from danger once. But this tower was impregnable. No weapon could break through it.

description: WH states “I had already been defeated in the last game” as fact, although the Japanese keeps both the prior defeat and the present surrender ceremony within Battler’s かもしれない conjecture.
sourceReading: Battler wonders whether he may already have lost the previous game and whether the current game may therefore be only the signing ceremony for his surrender.

units.text: Maybe I had mistakenly assumed that I was playing a game on an even footing with Beato. I had already been defeated in the last game, ...and this may just be the signing ceremony of my surrender.
units.note: MG keeps prior defeat hypothetical with “Maybe”; UP retains WH’s factual “I had already been defeated” while hedging only the surrender ceremony.
units.japanese: すでに前回敗北して、…これはその、降伏の調印式なだけなのかもしれない。
candidates: already been defeated in the last game

description: WH says Lavoisier “abolished” the phlogiston theory and that the caloric theory “was abolished by Joule.” The Japanese 否定した means that their work refuted or disproved those theories, not that they formally abolished them.
sourceReading: Battler says Lavoisier refuted the phlogiston theory and Joule refuted the caloric theory by establishing heat as energy rather than substance.

units.text: "......No, things burn because of a chemical reaction.  Lavoisier abolished the phlogiston theory."
units.note: Both retain “abolished” for the refutation of the phlogiston and caloric theories.
units.japanese: 「……いいや、物が燃えるのは酸化反応だ。フロギストン説はラヴォアジェが否定したはずだぜ。」

units.text: "...No, things burn because of a chemical reaction. Lavoisier abolished the phlogiston theory."

units.japanese: 「……いいや、物が燃えるのは酸化反応だ。フロギストン説はラヴォアジェが否定したはずだぜ」

description: WH changes Battler’s “we have no idea how a television’s cathode-ray tube produces an image” into “I don’t have a clue,” narrowing a claim about ordinary users’ shared ignorance to his personal knowledge.
sourceReading: Battler generalizes that people use televisions without understanding the cathode-ray tube’s mechanism, just as earlier people performed rain rites without understanding updrafts.

units.text: "............That's pretty interesting.  ...Well, logically, that's true.  ...For example, I don't have a clue why the Braun tubes in a TV show a picture.  However, I think it's completely normal to see things shown on a TV.  Even if I don't understand the principles behind Braun tubes, I at least know that 'if I push the switch I can watch TV'.  ...It's exactly the same as having a rain ceremony without understanding updrafts.  ......In other words, if I don't know the principles, even TV is the same as magic, no, could you say it is magic?"
units.note: Both narrow Battler’s collective “we do not understand” to personal “I do not understand.”
units.japanese: 「……………面白ぇ話だな。…まぁ、理屈から言やぁそうだ。…例えば俺たちはテレビのブラウン管にどうして画像が映るのか、理屈はさっぱりわかってない。でも、テレビに物が映るのは当り前だと思ってる。ブラウン管の原理を知らなくても、“スイッチを押せばテレビが見られる”ことだけは知っている。…上昇気流を理解せずに雨乞いをするのとまったく同じだ。……つまり、原理を知らないならば、テレビだって“魔法”も同然、いや、魔法そのものだろうってわけか。」

description: WH says the epitaph solver would receive “the inheritance or the hidden gold,” replacing 家督—the Ushiromiya family headship and succession—with generic inherited property.
sourceReading: Battler recalls the epitaph as promising the family headship and the hidden gold to whoever solves it.

units.text: ...This riddle of the epitaph was, that thing. That strange epitaph written on the portrait of the witch that was displayed in the hall of the mansion. Grandfather was the one who ordered that it be written, and the person who solved it would, supposedly, be given the inheritance or the hidden gold or something like that.
units.note: MG retains generic inheritance in Battler’s recap; UP restores the family headship.
units.japanese: 祖父さまが書かせたもので、それを解いた者に家督を譲るとか、隠された黄金を譲るとか騒がせた例のアレだ。

units.text: ...This riddle of the epitaph was...that thing. That strange epitaph written by the portrait of the witch on display in the hall of the mansion. Grandfather was the one who had it written, and the person who solved it would, supposedly, be given the inheritance or the hidden gold or something like that.
units.note: MG retains generic inheritance in Battler’s recap; UP restores the family headship.
units.japanese: …碑文の謎ってのは、例のアレだ。屋敷の大広間に掲げられた魔女の肖像画のところに書いてある怪しげな碑文。祖父さまが書かせたもので、それを解いた者に家督を譲るとか、隠された黄金を譲るとか騒がせた例のアレだ。

description: WH calls the epitaph an “unintelligible riddle.” 難解 means difficult or hard to solve; the riddle is comprehensible enough to pose a valid challenge, not meaningless or impossible to understand.
sourceReading: The culprit again demands that the family solve the exceptionally difficult epitaph and threatens to kill everyone if they fail.

units.text: After it had been displayed there several years ago, even though the relatives had said it was stupid, they had secretly challenged that riddle in the shadows. However, up until today, no one had solved it. We had once again been told to solve that unintelligible riddle, and this time, we had been threatened that if we didn't solve it, we would all be killed. ......If this wasn't a game, what would you call it...
units.note: Both retain “unintelligible” for a riddle characterized as difficult.
units.japanese: その難解な謎を、解いてみろと再び突きつけ、しかも解けなければ皆殺しだと脅迫している。

units.text: Ever since it was first put on display there several years ago, the relatives had secretly tried to solve that riddle, despite saying on the surface that the whole idea was silly. However, up until today, no one had solved it. We were once again being urged to solve that unintelligible riddle, and this time, we were faced with the threat that we'd all be killed if we didn't solve it. ...If that wasn't a "game", what else could it be...?
units.note: Both retain “unintelligible” for a riddle characterized as difficult.
units.japanese: 何年か前に掲げられて以来、親族たちは口では馬鹿にしながらも、影ではこっそりその謎に挑戦していたという。しかし、誰も解けずに今日に至っている。その難解な謎を、解いてみろと再び突きつけ、しかも解けなければ皆殺しだと脅迫している。……これを“ゲーム”と言わずして何というのか…。

units.text: Ever since it was first displayed there several years ago, all the relatives, despite making fun of it in the open, had been secretly been challenging that riddle in private. However, up until today, no one had solved it. We had once again been told to solve that unintelligible riddle, and this time, we had been threatened that if we didn't solve it, we would all be killed. ......If this wasn't a "game", what would you call it...
units.note: Both retain “unintelligible” for a riddle characterized as difficult.
units.japanese: 何年か前に掲げられて以来、親族たちは口では馬鹿にしながらも、影ではこっそりその謎に挑戦していたという。しかし、誰も解けずに今日に至っている。その難解な謎を、解いてみろと再び突きつけ、しかも解けなければ皆殺しだと脅迫している。……これを“ゲーム”と言わずして何というのか…。

description: WH says the adults “set up camp in the lobby.” The source says they regarded or configured the lobby as a fortress after checking every lock, emphasizing its defensive function.
sourceReading: After securing the guesthouse, the adults treat the lobby as their fortress while handling the guns and waiting through the long day.

units.text: After the adults had carefully checked that the doors and windows in the guesthouse were locked, they had set up camp in the lobby. And as they fingered their guns to distract themselves from the tension, their expressions showed that they were already fatigued from this long day, which had still barely begun...
units.note: Both replace the explicit lobby-as-fortress image with setting up camp.
units.japanese: 大人たちは、ゲストハウス内の戸締りを厳重に確認した後、このロビーを砦に見立てる。
candidates: set up camp in the lobby

units.text: After the adults carefully checked that the doors and windows in the guesthouse were locked, they set up camp in the lobby. As they loaded their guns to distract themselves from the tension, their expressions showed that they were already fatigued from this long day, which had still barely begun...
units.note: Both replace the explicit lobby-as-fortress image with setting up camp.
units.japanese: 大人たちは、ゲストハウス内の戸締りを厳重に確認した後、このロビーを砦に見立てる。そして銃を弄って緊張を紛らわしながら、まだまだ始まったばかりの長い一日に、早くも疲労の表情を見せるのだった…。
candidates: set up camp in the lobby

description: WH says “suicide is a naive word.” Battler calls 自殺 a 甘い言い方—too soft, lenient, or insufficiently restrictive a formulation to corner Beatrice—not an innocent or unsophisticated term.
sourceReading: Battler says merely asking about suicide is too weakly worded to force the needed concession, so he demands the stronger proposition that all six deaths were homicides.

units.text: "Right!!  But suicide is a naive word that won't corner her!!  Beato, this is the end!!
units.note: Both retain “naive word” for Battler’s judgment that “suicide” is too soft and loophole-prone a formulation.
units.japanese: 「あぁ！！　だが、自殺なんて甘い言い方じゃ追い詰められねぇぜ！！　ベアト、こいつで詰めだ！！

units.text: "Right!! But suicide's a naive word that won't corner her!! Beato, this'll stop you!!
units.note: Both retain “naive word” for Battler’s judgment that “suicide” is too soft and loophole-prone a formulation.
units.japanese: 「あぁ！！　だが、自殺なんて甘い言い方じゃ追い詰められねぇぜ！！　ベアト、こいつで詰めだ！！」

units.text: "Right!! But suicide is a naive word that won't corner her!! Beato, this is the end!!"
units.note: Both retain “naive word” for Battler’s judgment that “suicide” is too soft and loophole-prone a formulation.
units.japanese: 「あぁ！！　だが、自殺なんて甘い言い方じゃ追い詰められねぇぜ！！　ベアト、こいつで詰めだ！！」

description: WH renders 達観 as “a far-sighted view.” Here it describes Beatrice’s detached, resigned composure—as though accepting that Battler may laugh—not foresight or long-range judgment.
sourceReading: Beatrice speaks with a detached resignation that seems to say Battler may laugh if he wishes.

units.text: Beato told me that frankly. It seemed as though she had taken a far-sighted view, as though saying 'if you want to laugh, then laugh'. ......It was a bit of a kill-joy, and I lost my desire to deliver the final blow.
units.note: Both retain “far-sighted view” for Beatrice’s detached resignation.
units.japanese: 笑いたくば笑えというような達観も感じられた。

units.text: Beato told me that frankly. It seemed she'd taken a far-sighted view, as though saying "If you want to laugh, then laugh". ...It was a bit of a killjoy, and I lost my desire to deliver the final blow.
units.note: Both retain “far-sighted view” for Beatrice’s detached resignation.
units.japanese:
ベアトは淡白にそう告げる。
笑いたくば笑えというような達観も感じられた。……何となく興醒めして、追い討ちをする気も薄れた。

units.text:
Beato told me that frankly.
It seemed as though she had taken a far‐sighted view, as though saying "if you want to laugh, then laugh". ......It was a bit of a buzzkill, and I lost my desire to attack her further.
units.note: Both retain “far-sighted view” for Beatrice’s detached resignation.
units.japanese:
ベアトは淡白にそう告げる。
笑いたくば笑えというような達観も感じられた。……何となく興醒めして、追い討ちをする気も薄れた。

description: WH says Battler “accepted it.” 飲み込んでおく means he swallows his objection and lets Beatrice’s cowardly behavior pass in the dignity of victory, not that he accepts or endorses the behavior itself.
sourceReading: Battler thinks her behavior cowardly but decides, as the victor, to swallow the complaint and let it go.

units.text: Even though she ridiculed me horribly when I showed signs of defeat, she was so pathetic when it was her turn. I think she's a pretty unfair person, but I decided to act with dignity as a winner and accepted it.
units.note: MG changes the action to letting it slide; UP retains “accepted it.”
units.japanese: 何だか卑怯なヤツだなとは思うが、そこは勝者の貫禄で飲み込んでおくことにする。

units.text: Even though she ridiculed me horribly when I showed signs of defeat, she was so pathetic when it was her turn. I thought of her as a pretty unfair person, but I decided to act with dignity as a winner and accepted it.
units.note: MG changes the action to letting it slide; UP retains “accepted it.”
units.japanese: 俺が敗色濃厚な時はさんざん嘲りまくってくれたくせに、自分が逆になるとこのザマと来た。何だか卑怯なヤツだなとは思うが、そこは勝者の貫禄で飲み込んでおくことにする。

description: WH renders 現地へ足を運ぶ as Father “dragged himself to the actual location.” The idiom simply means making a trip or going there; it does not imply reluctance, exhaustion, or bodily difficulty.
sourceReading: Even if Kinzo personally went back to the area now, he probably could not identify where he had lived.

units.text: "That was only as a vacation.  ......But the townscape had changed completely from Father's time.  After all, it was caught up in the war, wasn't it?  It was impossible to even figure out where Father actually lived.  ...Probably, even if Father dragged himself to the actual location, by now, even he wouldn't be able to determine where it was that he lived."
units.note: MG restores a neutral trip to the location; UP retains the unsupported “dragged himself” wording.
units.japanese:
「あくまでも旅行としてよ。
……でも、町並みは当時と完全に変わってる。
何しろ戦争を挟んでるのよ？
お父様がどこに住んでいたのかさえ、正確な場所の把握は不可能よ。
…多分、お父様が自ら現地へ足を運んでも、
今となっては、どこに住んでいたか特定できないでしょうね」
「あちらさんもずいぶん目覚しく復興したって話だからな…」
candidates: Father dragged himself to the actual location

units.text: "That was only as a vacation. ......But the townscape had changed completely from Father's time. After all, there was a war in between. It was impossible to even figure out where Father actually lived. ...Probably, even if Father dragged himself to the actual location, by now, even he wouldn't be able to determine where it was that he lived."

description: WH says there is “a single blank line” after the first two epitaph lines. 一度改行してる means the text makes a line break there, not that an empty line separates the sections.
sourceReading: Kyrie observes that the text breaks to a new line after those two lines and uses that formatting boundary to infer a completed unit.

units.text: ".........My beloved hometown, the sweetfish river running through it.  You who seek the Golden Land, follow its path downstream and seek the key.  ...After these two lines, there is a single blank line.  ...Something is being presented with just these two lines.  What if the next three lines continue based upon that something?"
units.note: Both retain “a single blank line” for the line break Kyrie uses to segment the epitaph.
units.japanese: 「………懐かしき、故郷を貫く鮎の川。黄金郷を目指す者よ、これを下りて鍵を探せ。…ここまでの２行で、一度改行してるのよね。…この２行だけで、何かの提示が成立するのよ。その何かに基づいて次の３行が続くんじゃないかしら。」

description: WH says Kyrie will “have to give up” but will try solving it anyway. お手上げ describes being stumped or at a loss; she explicitly proceeds with a provisional attempt rather than abandoning it.
sourceReading: Kyrie admits she is currently stumped because the key is unknown, but says she will make an attempt anyway.

units.text: "...........................This is...very difficult.  ...By starting with 'He who lays hand upon the key', it probably means that you won't be able to continue without understanding the key.  ...I'll have to give up, but I'll take a shot at trying to solve it anyway."
units.note: Both retain Kyrie saying she will give up before immediately saying she will attempt the reconstruction anyway.
units.japanese: 「………………………。………これは、とても難しいわね。…“鍵を手にせし者は”から始まるということは多分、鍵を理解していないと話が進まない。…お手上げではあるけれど、一応、挑戦してみるわね。」

units.text: "......... ......This is...very difficult. ...It starts with "the one who obtains the key", so you probably won't be able to continue without knowing what that key means. ...I'll have to give up on that, but I'll take a shot at trying to solve it anyway."
