description: The source calls the Western vegetables unusual or rare. UP calls them tasteful, replacing unfamiliarity or rarity with aesthetic approval. MG preserves unusual.

units.text: Kumasawa‐san had taken the tasteful western vegetables, ones that Gohda‐san had probably special ordered for the purpose of some extravagantly fancy dish, and cooked them in a Japanese style, making them turn an unpleasant color. As to what Gohda‐san had been planning to cook with those ingredients... right then I couldn't even imagine it. If I did think about it, I would be reminded of the way Gohda‐san had died, and the inside of my mouth would be filled with a sour taste... For the time being, everyone pretended to eat, but there was no hope of anyone making any headway into the meal.
units.japanese: 郷田さんが、凝りに凝った料理のために取り寄せただろう珍しい西洋野菜は、熊沢さんによって、和風に料理され、違和感のある彩りとなっていた。これらの材料によって、郷田さんがどんな料理を作るつもりだったのか…。今となっては想像することもできない。それを想像すれば、郷田さんの死に様が再び蘇り、口の中が酸っぱい何かで満たされる…。みんなは一応、食べるふりだけするのだが、箸が進むはずもなかった。

description: Battler reflects that he can currently perceive nothing beyond malice toward all of them. UP says none of us could grasp anything except malice, attributing his limit of interpretation to the entire group. MG preserves the first-person perception.

units.text:
In other words, the culprit wanted to display these murders. To who? ......To us. It was a message.
The culprit was trying to shove something in our faces. ...I didn't know what that could be. At the current time, none of us could grasp anything from this vulgar mass murder except malice.
units.japanese:
つまり、犯人はこの殺人を誇示しているわけだ。誰に？……俺たちにだ。こいつはメッセージだ。
犯人たちは俺たちに、何かを突きつけている。…それが何か、わからない。現時点では、この趣味の悪い大量殺人は、俺たち全員への悪意以上のものは感じ取れない。
candidates: none of us could grasp anything

description: Both editions turn everyone settling into sofas of their individual choosing into their favorite sofas. 思い思い describes separate individual choices, without establishing habitual favorite seats.

units.text: I finally noticed that the inside of the parlor had gone quiet again. Everyone had sunk into their favorite sofas, some deep in thought, some irritated, some acting depressed. Maria was once again enjoying the TV as if she'd never left it. It looked like she found the commercials more fun than the boring program, and she happily yelled "uu-uu-" and giggled.
units.japanese: 気付けば、客間の中は静まり返っていた。みんな、思い思いのソファーに腰を沈め、何かを考え込んだり、イラついたり、落ち込んだりしている。真里亞はさっきからずっとそうであったかのように、再びテレビの前に戻り観賞を続けている。…退屈な番組よりＣＭの方が楽しいらしく、うーうーきゃっきゃと喜んでいた。

units.text: I finally noticed that the inside of the parlor had gone quiet again. Everyone had sunk into their favorite sofas, some deep in thought, some irritated, some depressed. Maria was once again enjoying the television as if she had never left it. ...It looked like she found the commercials more fun than the boring program, and she happily yelled "uu‐uu" and giggled.
units.japanese: 気付けば、客間の中は静まり返っていた。みんな、思い思いのソファーに腰を沈め、何かを考え込んだり、イラついたり、落ち込んだりしている。真里亞はさっきからずっとそうであったかのように、再びテレビの前に戻り観賞を続けている。…退屈な番組よりＣＭの方が楽しいらしく、うーうーきゃっきゃと喜んでいた。

description: Both editions amplify the single tapping sound コツリ from the hallway into a loud, sharp noise. The source gives a small hard tap before the surprised turn and discovery of Battler.

units.text: Just then, a loud, sharp noise came in from the hall. Both of them turned around, surprised.
units.japanese:
その時、廊下からコツリと音がした。
二人は驚き、振り返る。

units.text:
Just then, a loud, sharp noise resounded from the hall.
Both of them turned around, surprised.
units.japanese:
その時、廊下からコツリと音がした。
二人は驚き、振り返る。

description: MG drops other than that theory from Battler condition, saying if there were no way to make Kinzo disappear. Japanese says if there were no disappearance method other than Eva theory, then Natsuhi guilt could be asserted. UP preserves other than yours.

units.text: "It's true that your theory's an interesting one. And if you could say for sure that there was no way to make Grandfather disappear, then you probably would be able to prove that the last person to see him, Aunt Natsuhi, was guilty." "However, since there still is a possibility she's innocent and these accusations are false, we can't be sure about that!!"
units.japanese: 「絵羽伯母さんの説は確かに面白い。そして、その説以外に祖父さまが失踪できる方法がないって言い切れるなら、最終目撃者である夏妃伯母さんがクロであると確かに言い切れるだろう」「だが、夏妃伯母さんが無実で、濡れ衣である可能性が残っている以上、そうだと断言することはできねぇ！！」

description: MG assigns the portrait vigil and longing to a male he. Kumasawa is explaining that Beatrice, who no longer has a body, reportedly stands before her portrait yearning for her former appearance. UP restores she and her old form.

units.text: "I have heard that the portrait shows what Beatrice-sama looked like back when she had a human form... ...It seems he yearned for that figure so much, he would often stand in front of that portrait... ...Hohohoh..."
units.japanese: 「ベアトリーチェさまが人の姿をされていた頃の絵が、あの肖像画のものなのだとか…。……そのお姿を懐かしみ、よく肖像画の前にたたずまれているそうな…。…ほっほっほ…」

description: Both editions change Maria letting out one small sigh before lowering her head into taking a single short breath. The source explicitly describes a sigh, losing its expressive action in the translations.

units.text: Maria, after taking a single, short breath, hung her head, ...and then raised her face again.
units.japanese: 真里亞は、一度だけ小さな溜め息を漏らしてから俯き、……そして顔を上げる。

units.text: Maria, after taking a single, short breath, hung her head, ......and then raised her face again.
units.japanese: 真里亞は、一度だけ小さな溜め息を漏らしてから俯き、……そして顔を上げる。

description: MG turns Jessica letting out a large breath in admiration into taking a deep breath. UP puffed out air restores the outward action.

units.text: Jessica took a deep breath in admiration... It looked like Aniki had guessed right.
units.japanese:
朱志香は感服したかのように大きく息を漏らす…。
どうも、兄貴の見立ての通りらしい。

description: UP turns workers falling ill one after another with mysterious high fevers into all workers being suddenly taken out by a fever. This adds total coverage and simultaneous onset while losing the high temperature. MG preserves successive illness but also omits high.

units.text: You also hear about how, if an Inari shrine is carelessly removed during a town re-planning, there'd be a curse by Kitsune-sama. I think I might've read somewhere that when the occupying forces were trying to expand an airport, they tried to remove an Inari-san that was in the way, and the workers kept getting struck down by mysterious fevers.
units.japanese: 稲荷神社を区画整理なんかで不用意にどかすと、おキツネさまの祟りがあるってのも聞く話だ。占領軍が飛行場を拡張しようとして、邪魔なお稲荷さんをどかそうとしたら、作業員が次々と謎の高熱で倒れたなんて話をどこかで読んだことがある気がする。

units.text: You also hear about how, if an Inari shrine is carelessly removed during a town replanning, there would be a curse by Kitsune‐sama. I think I might have read somewhere that when the occupying forces were trying to expand an airport, and had to remove an Inari‐san that was in the way, all of the workers were suddenly taken out by some mysterious fever.
units.japanese: 稲荷神社を区画整理なんかで不用意にどかすと、おキツネさまの祟りがあるってのも聞く話だ。占領軍が飛行場を拡張しようとして、邪魔なお稲荷さんをどかそうとしたら、作業員が次々と謎の高熱で倒れたなんて話をどこかで読んだことがある気がする。

description: MG assigns watching television to Eva as she sits beside Hideyoshi. Japanese describes Hideyoshi lying on the bed watching television; UP restores that subject.

units.text: Eva, sulking cutely and looking at the television, sat alongside Hideyoshi, who was lying on the bed.
units.japanese: 絵羽は可愛らしく膨れながら、テレビを見ながらベッドに横たわっている秀吉の脇に座る。

description: Battler conditionally accepts research resurrecting the beloved woman and Kinzo living out his lifespan believing her soul revived. UP instead says the research brought life back to Grandfather, shifting the resurrection target to Kinzo. MG preserves research aimed at the woman, though its wording compresses the conditional.

units.text: "...In that case, I'll believe. ...If spending half of his life on research is what brought life back to Grandfather, and if believing that the soul of the woman he loved had been resurrected is what enabled him to live to a ripe old age, ...I'll believe too."
units.japanese: 「…なら、俺は信じたぜ。…祖父さまが半生を掛けて研究したことで蘇り、愛した女の魂が蘇ったと信じて寿命を全うできるって言うんなら、…俺も信じたぜ」

description: UP uses inverted direct-question word order inside an indirect question: “can you tell me why were you facing”. George is asking why Maria faced the wall; the embedded clause requires “why you were facing”. MG retains a grammatical direct question.

units.text: "...Maria‐chan, ......can you tell me why were you facing the wall and singing that song...?"
units.japanese: 「…真里亞ちゃんは、……どうして壁を向いてお歌を歌っていたのかな…？」
candidates: tell me why were you facing

description: Maria says guns have no effect on Beatrice specifically. MG makes this a general claim that guns are useless against witches; UP preserves Beatrice as the target. The MG line broadens the asserted immunity beyond the source’s named individual.

units.text: "......Kihihihihihi. Give it up, Battler. ...Guns are useless against witches. Survival and all that stuff doesn't matter...because it's over. The journey has already ended. ......See, look at the clock."
units.japanese: 「…………きひひひひひ。よしなよ戦人。…ベアトリーチェに銃なんて意味ないよ。それに、生き残るも何も、もうおしまいなんだよ。もう、旅は終わったんだよ。……ほら、時計を見てごらん」

description: Bern specifies plums costing 200 yen per pack as the tea ingredient. MG’s “The kind that goes for 200 yen a pack” attaches the price to the tea rather than explicitly to the plums. UP restores “Those dried plums that go for 200 yen a pack”.

units.text: "...Dried plum black tea. ...The kind that goes for 200 yen a pack."
units.japanese: 「……梅干紅茶。……梅干は１パック２００円のヤツよ」
candidates: kind that goes for 200 yen a pack

description: Beatrice says Bern single-handedly repelled/defeated Lambdadelta. MG says Lambdadelta was dethroned, adding loss of a throne or governing position absent the source. UP preserves fended off, although its lone-piece wording stylizes the single-handed feat.

units.text: "That a powerless Lady Witch like you possesses a power that none can approach is what is truly terrifying. After all, that Great Witch, Lady Lambdadelta, was dethroned by you alone."
units.japanese: 「その無力な魔女殿が、何人たりとも寄せ付けぬ力をお持ちなのだから恐れ入る。かの大魔女、ラムダデルタ卿を単騎にて退けられたのだから」

description: George says underage drinking may adversely affect development. / Rhetorical question asserts alcohol can stunt growth; narrower than adverse development but retains possibility. / Known to stunt growth strengthens possibility into an established effect; local character speech nuance only, no medical judgment or mystery consequence.
sourceReading: George says underage drinking may adversely affect development.

units.text: "Th‐that's no good, Battler‐kun, you're still a minor! Drinking alcohol is known to stunt the growth of minors and... ...um, never mind."
units.japanese: 「だ、駄目だよ、戦人くんはまだ未成年じゃないか！　未成年の飲酒は発育に悪影響を及ぼす可能性が…、って、う〜ん」

description: As long as she is with Rudolf, Kyrie will not let him do that alone. / Since we have been together, I have not let him recasts a continuing condition and declared intention as a retrospective claim about the whole relationship. / As long as / will not preserves the condition and intention.
sourceReading: As long as she is with Rudolf, Kyrie will not let him do that alone.

units.text: "Oh, you don't need to worry about that at all. Since we've been together, I haven't let him do that on his own."
units.japanese: 「あら、そんな心配は全然不要よ？　私と一緒にいる以上、そんなことひとりでさせやしないもの」

description: Only Kyrie can hold Rudolf’s reins / keep him under control. / Reigning in substitutes ruling for the idiom reining in. / Same spelling error retained; context keeps the intended control meaning understandable.
sourceReading: Only Kyrie can hold Rudolf’s reins / keep him under control.

units.text: "No kidding. You're the only one capable of reigning in that old bastard. As his son, I'm more than happy to let you take over."
units.japanese: 「いやいやまったく。あのクソ親父の手綱は霧江さんにしか無理っすよ。実の息子の俺も、喜んで譲っちゃいますわ」

units.text: "Oh, no kidding. You're the only one capable of reigning in that old bastard. As his son, I'm more than happy to let you take over."
units.japanese: 「いやいやまったく。あのクソ親父の手綱は霧江さんにしか無理っすよ。実の息子の俺も、喜んで譲っちゃいますわ」

description: Eva says she made a mistake during a martial-arts demonstration and her partner foamed at the mouth. / Practice match / opponent replaces demonstration / partner; out cold also removes the specific foaming symptom. / Same changes preserved.
sourceReading: Eva says she made a mistake during a martial-arts demonstration and her partner foamed at the mouth.

units.text: "Rudooolf? Did you know that a single direct blow to the side of the head like that would knock you unconscious? Not so long ago, I accidently connected in a practice match and my opponent was out cold."
units.japanese: 「留ぅ弗〜夫ぅ〜？　側頭部直撃だと一発で昏倒するわよぅ？　この間、演武でミスって相方、泡吹いちゃったんだからねぇ？」

units.text: "Rudo~lf? Did you know that a single direct blow to the side of the head like that would knock you unconscious? Not so long ago, I accidentally connected in a practice match, and my opponent was out cold."
units.japanese: 「留ぅ弗〜夫ぅ〜？　側頭部直撃だと一発で昏倒するわよぅ？　この間、演武でミスって相方、泡吹いちゃったんだからねぇ？」

description: George is now an adult and no longer requires active child-rearing, leaving room for another child. / About to go off on his own introduces imminent independent departure instead of existing freedom from child-care. / Same unsupported impending departure.
sourceReading: George is now an adult and no longer requires active child-rearing, leaving room for another child.

units.text: "Oh, then why not consider making a little brother for George-kun? He's already a fine adult who's about to go off on his own, so it might be a good time to have another child."
units.japanese: 「あら、譲治くんに弟を作ってあげるという話はないんですか？　もう譲治くんも立派な大人になって手も離れたでしょうから、次の子がいてもいいでしょうに」

units.text: "Oh, then why not consider making a little brother for George‐kun? He's already a fine adult who's about to go off on his own, so it might be a good time to have another child."
units.japanese: 「あら、譲治くんに弟を作ってあげるという話はないんですか？　もう譲治くんも立派な大人になって手も離れたでしょうから、次の子がいてもいいでしょうに」

description: Maria cites a witch friend of her own saying miracles require belief. MG makes the friend one of Beatrice’s witch friends (“her witch friends”), shifting the relationship and ownership of Maria’s cited testimony. UP correctly says “my witch friends”.

units.text: "Like I kept saying, Beatrice exists. It all went bad because no one ever believed. Uu-! Even one of her witch friends says that miracles won't occur if you don't believe. Uu-!"
units.japanese: 「だから真里亞は、ベアトリーチェがいるーってずっと言ってる。みんなずっと信じなかったから駄目だった。うー！　信じないと奇跡は起きないって、友達の魔女も言ってる！　うー！」

description: Battler says the culprit could secure a door gap limited by the chain. Both translations instead say it was possible to look in through that crack, replacing availability of a working aperture with a visual-access proposition.

units.text: "...Well, ...we did have to leave that trick alone during the story. Anyway, there's at least a good chance the culprit had a key. And it was possible to look in through the crack of the door that the chain allowed.
units.japanese: 「…まぁ、……確かにそのトリックは劇中でも保留になったままだったな。とにかく、犯人は鍵だけは持ってる可能性が高いからな。チェーンに許される程度の、扉の隙間は確保できたわけだ」

units.text: "...Well, ......you're right, we did have to leave that trick alone during the story. Anyways, there's a good chance that the culprit had the key at least. And it was possible to look in through the crack of the door that the chain allowed."
units.japanese: 「…まぁ、……確かにそのトリックは劇中でも保留になったままだったな。とにかく、犯人は鍵だけは持ってる可能性が高いからな。チェーンに許される程度の、扉の隙間は確保できたわけだ」

description: Battler alternatively proposes bringing something out through the gap. MG instead suggests sticking something through it, losing the outward extraction direction and collapsing the distinct alternative into insertion. UP preserves brought something out.

units.text: ...I know this is a stretch, but it's possible some device was used through that crack. ...Like maybe they stuck something through it...?"
units.japanese: 「……非常に苦しい話だが、その隙間から何かの仕掛けを施した可能性はありえるな。…いや、あるいは、その隙間から、何かを出したとか…？」

description: Battler asserts that the present crime could be managed by a human somehow, despite lacking an explanation. MG broadens this to there being nothing humans cannot do if they try hard enough. UP keeps the assertion about managing this case.

units.text: "...Hmmmm, well, even though a door chain is incredibly simple, it's a big factor in setting up a closed room... ...Still, there's probably some closed room trick they could've used. If you bought some closed room mystery novels from the bookstore, you could probably find some trick that'd fit perfectly. ...Anyway, I can't think of one now, ...but I claim that there's nothing humans can't do if they try hard enough."
units.japanese: 「……んんん、確かにチェーンってのは、偉いシンプルだが、密室を構成するでかい要素だな…。………だが、密室トリックなんておよそやり尽くされてるんだ。そこいらの書店で密室ミステリーを数冊買ってくりゃ、どうせビンゴなトリックが見付かるだろうぜ」「……とにかく、俺には思いつかねぇが、どうにかやりくりすりゃあ、人間にできないことはないだろうって断言できる」

description: Battler says witches are the desperate explanation raised only after human possibilities have all been ruled out. MG substitutes a first-person commitment, “I’ll only accept that it’s a witch in desperation”, making him promise conditional acceptance rather than state the order in which explanations should be considered. UP preserves the methodological formulation.

units.text: "That's not it... It's just, uh, I can't easily accept that a 19th person existed...and even if one did, I think we should construct our argument from the point of view that the culprit was a human. I'll only accept that it's a witch in desperation, at the very end, after everything else has been disproved."
units.japanese: 「そういうわけじゃねぇ…。ただその、安易に１９人目を肯定はできねぇし、仮にいたとしてもそれは人間だって見地から話を構築すべきであって、それら全部を否定しきった最後の最後で苦し紛れに出てくるのが魔女だろって話をしたいんだ」
candidates: I'll only accept that it's a witch in desperation

description: Beatrice concludes that Battler’s attitude makes sense given his resistance to magic. MG instead says “I accept that attitude of yours”, shifting explanatory understanding into personal acceptance or approval. UP preserves “That attitude of yours makes a great deal of sense”.

units.text: ...You're a natural enemy of us witches. ...No matter how much we turn your world upside down, you never believe in us. Therefore, the magic won't succeed. ...I accept that attitude of yours. *cackle*cackle*...!"
units.japanese: 「……我ら魔女の天敵よ。…どう逆さに振るって見せようとも、決して我らを信じない。だから魔法が及ばない。…お前のその態度にも納得が行こうというものよ。くっくっくっく…！」

description: The incantation commands bringing/wielding the seven stakes qualified as absolving deadly sins. MG splits the qualification into a separate imperative, “Forgive the deadly sins and hold the Seven Stakes”, changing what the summoned children are commanded to do and detaching the stakes’ stated function. UP preserves the relative clause attached to the stakes.

units.text: "Come, arise, children. I am the guide of Purgatory. Forgive the deadly sins and hold the Seven Stakes."
units.japanese: 「さぁさ、お出でなさいな子どもたち。我こそは煉獄の案内人。大罪を赦せし七つの杭を持て」
candidates: Forgive the deadly sins and hold the Seven Stakes

description: Hideyoshi calls George still 半人前 in the discussion of professional learning: not yet fully competent/experienced. Both translate this as not a full man yet, shifting the immediate assessment toward adult manhood rather than skill or experience. The next study exhortation mitigates but does not restore the idiomatic meaning.

units.text: "George isn't quite a full man yet! He'd better always keep that in mind and embrace his studies."
units.japanese: 「譲治もまだまだ半人前や！　それを常に忘れんで、勉強に励むんやで」

units.text: "You're not a full man yet, George! Always keep that in mind, and embrace your studies."
units.japanese: 「譲治もまだまだ半人前や！　それを常に忘れんで、勉強に励むんやで」

description: George identifies a company president who has been helping/looking after him. UP says “I’m currently in the service of a company president”, specifying an employment/service relationship beyond お世話になっている. MG preserves looked after me, consistent with earlier introductions to experienced mentors.

units.text: "I'm currently in the service of a company president who knows a lot about black tea. After enough time listening to his expositions, I picked up a little of it."
units.japanese: 「お世話になっている社長さんに紅茶の詳しい人がいまして。講釈を聞いている内に少しだけわかるようになりました」
candidates: I'm currently in the service of a company president

description: Eva pats Shannon’s shoulder as if reinforcing her warning. MG calls the gesture urging her on, replacing emphasis on the private admonition with encouragement. UP restores as though to underscore her message.

units.text: When their secret conversation ended, Eva patted Shannon's shoulders, as though she was urging her on.
units.japanese: そして内緒話を終え、まるで念を押すように紗音の肩を、ポンと叩く。

description: Kanon says Shannon should simply have nodded in silence rather than added a reply. Both English versions replace nodding with hanging her head in silence, changing compliant acknowledgment into a posture of shame or submission.

units.text: "......You're still as clumsy as always, Nee-san. Milady has been in a bad mood since this morning. That just now happened because you talked too much, when you should've just hung your head in silence."
units.japanese: 「………姉さんは相変わらず不器用だね。奥様は今朝から虫の居所が悪い。黙って頷いてればいいものを、余計なことを言うから」

units.text: ".........You're still as clumsy as always, Nee‐san. Madam has been in a bad mood since this morning. You spoke out of turn when you should have hung your head in silence."
units.japanese: 「………姉さんは相変わらず不器用だね。奥様は今朝から虫の居所が悪い。黙って頷いてればいいものを、余計なことを言うから」

description: UP makes Shannon support the portrait on her back. The source places the wall and hanging portrait behind her as she backs away while looking at the witch; it does not describe carrying or supporting the picture. MG preserves the portrait behind/touching her back.

units.text: The witch giggled at how Shannon's reaction didn't betray her expectations. Shannon realized that she had met with a being that mustn't be met with, and she took a step backwards. ......That's where the wall and the portrait were, so even as she gazed at the witch, she supported the witch's portrait on her back.
units.japanese: 魔女は紗音の見せた反応が予想を裏切らなかったことを、くすくすと笑う。紗音は、出会ってはいけない存在に出会ってしまったことに気付き、よろりと後ずさる。……そこには壁と肖像画があるわけで、彼女は、魔女を見据えながら、魔女の肖像画を背負うのだった。

description: MG turns permission to be proud into an obligation to be praised. Beatrice licenses Shannon’s own pride in being human; she does not call for external praise. UP preserves You should be proud.

units.text: ...You kind-hearted child. You ought to be praised. Now that you have gained this knowledge, you are no longer furniture. You are now "human". I recognize that with all the authority of my name."
units.japanese: 「……心優しき娘よ。そなたは誇っていい。それを知った今、そなたはもはや家具にあらず。そなたは今こそ『人間』なのだ。我が名にかけて、それを認めようぞ」

description: UP changes an ordinary or mediocre person struggling to understand into an inferior being. This intensifies the ontological hierarchy immediately after Beatrice recognizes Shannon as human. MG common person preserves the ordinary-person reference.

units.text: "Hmph. Is it hard for an inferior being to understand? ...Oh, well. *cackle*cackle*... Forgive me. It has been a long time since I have spoken with a human. I shall apologize for my talkativeness."
units.japanese: 「ふ。凡庸の身には理解も辛き話か。…まぁ良いわ。くっくっくっく…。許すがいい。久しぶりに人間と話すのでな。饒舌が過ぎたことを謝ろう」

description: Both replace Shannon’s defensive guardedness with a hostile attitude. The source follows her fear of the sinister witch and says she is braced or on guard; it does not assert antagonistic intent. UP also explicitly calls her attitude hostility in the narrator’s next sentence.

units.text: "...I may not differ much from the image of a detestable witch that you hold in your mind. However, I do bestow my favor upon those who respect me. Aren't humans the same? Well, I doubt any human would bestow a favor upon one with such a hostile attitude."
units.japanese: 「……妾は確かにそなたらが忌み嫌う魔女像から離れはせぬ。だが、妾は敬う者には好意を返す。それは人間も同じであろう？　そのように身構えられて好意を返せる人間も、またおらぬと思うがな？」

units.text: "......I may be no different from the image of a detestable witch that you humans hold in your minds. However, I respond with goodwill to those who respect me. Aren't humans the same? Although, I doubt any human would respond with goodwill to a hostile attitude like that..."
units.japanese:
「……妾は確かにそなたらが忌み嫌う魔女像から離れはせぬ。だが、妾は敬う者には好意を返す。それは人間も同じであろう？　そのように身構えられて好意を返せる人間も、またおらぬと思うがな？」
紗音は、自分の態度が客人に失礼なものであったことにようやく気付く。そして、…彼女が先ほど口にしてくれた言葉をようやく噛み締める。

units.text: Shannon finally realized that her hostility was rude to this guest. And...she finally digested the words that had been spoken to her a short while ago.
units.japanese:
「……妾は確かにそなたらが忌み嫌う魔女像から離れはせぬ。だが、妾は敬う者には好意を返す。それは人間も同じであろう？　そのように身構えられて好意を返せる人間も、またおらぬと思うがな？」
紗音は、自分の態度が客人に失礼なものであったことにようやく気付く。そして、…彼女が先ほど口にしてくれた言葉をようやく噛み締める。

description: MG asks why a witch would seek human help instead of acting herself, omitting Shannon’s explicit surprise that a being of a witch’s stature cannot do it herself. UP preserves the inability. The subsequent opposing-magic explanation mitigates but does not restore the initial articulated inference.

units.text: It was quite a suspicious request. Shannon didn't know the details, but anything stored inside a shrine would have to be something sacred. ...And she wants me to break it? Why would a witch ask a human for help, instead of doing it herself...?
units.japanese:
それはあまりに胡散臭い願いだった。謂れは知らないが、鳥居と祠があって、そこに納められた物があったなら、それは神聖なものに違いない。……それを割って欲しい？
魔女ともあろう者が、自らそれをできず、人間に頼むというのか…？

description: MG changes Beatrice’s claim to have done no more than offer an opportunity as a reward into a future promise to grant a chance, and omits as a reward. UP retains the already-offered opportunity and reward framing. The source retrospectively defends the bargain before restating freedom of choice.

units.text: "I will do nothing but grant you a chance to bring your feelings to fruition. ...It's up to you to decide whether you'll break it or not. If you break it, I shall grant your wish."
units.japanese: 「妾はあくまでも褒美としてそなたに想いを成就する機会を与えたに過ぎぬ。……割ろうが割るまいが、そなたの自由だ。割れば、妾はそなたの願いを叶える」

description: Both add sending Kanon off to Beatrice’s pardon. 許してつかわす is an elevated formula granting forgiveness, not forgiveness followed by dispatching him. Beatrice herself announces departure in the next sentence.

units.text: "......Very well. If you ask, I will forgive you just this once. ...Kanon, is it? In deference to her, I shall forgive you tonight and send you off. You ought to thank me. Well then, let us call it a night."
units.japanese: 「………良かろう。そなたが求めるなら特別に許そう。…嘉音とやら。彼女に免じて今宵は許してつかわす。感謝するがよいぞ。さて、今宵はこれで退散する」

units.text: ".........Very well. At your request, I will grant him special pardon. ...Kanon, is it? In deference to her, I shall forgive you tonight and send you off. Be thankful. Well then, we will disperse for tonight."
units.japanese: 「………良かろう。そなたが求めるなら特別に許そう。…嘉音とやら。彼女に免じて今宵は許してつかわす。感謝するがよいぞ。さて、今宵はこれで退散する」

description: MG has Beatrice tell the pleading Shannon I will forgive you just this once. The source grants pardon at Shannon’s request, with Kanon identified as recipient immediately afterward. UP correctly says at your request I will grant him special pardon.

units.text: "......Very well. If you ask, I will forgive you just this once. ...Kanon, is it? In deference to her, I shall forgive you tonight and send you off. You ought to thank me. Well then, let us call it a night."
units.japanese: 「………良かろう。そなたが求めるなら特別に許そう。…嘉音とやら。彼女に免じて今宵は許してつかわす。感謝するがよいぞ。さて、今宵はこれで退散する」

description: UP calls the aquarium the occasion of their first meeting, despite the established long acquaintance before their aquarium date. In this context 出会い and 縁 refer to the beginning of their romance. MG correctly says it gave them the opportunity to start going out.

units.text: Shannon and George had chosen to go to Okinawa because there was a huge aquarium there. That was because their first meeting had revolved around an aquarium. Since they had started at an aquarium, having their first overnight trip also be to an aquarium must have held some commemorative value.
units.japanese: 紗音と譲治が旅行先を沖縄に選んだのは、巨大な水族館があったからだった。それは、彼らの出会いが水族館をきっかけにしたものだったからだ。水族館で始まった縁だから、初めてのお泊り旅行の行き先も水族館というちょっと記念的な意味もあったに違いない。

description: MG describes Jessica pretending to faint in agony. The source describes her writhing in frustration on the bed while complaining about their romance, without specifying feigned loss of consciousness. UP preserves writhing.

units.text: For a while, Jessica chewed her present, complaining about romance and pretending to faint in agony on her bed.
units.japanese: 朱志香はしばらくの間、もぐもぐとお土産を頬張りながら、ベッドの上で、人の恋路をあーだこーだとグチグチ言いながら悶絶しているのだった。

description: MG makes Shannon run to the side table and search around on it. The source has her rush to Jessica and look at the nearby table, where the medicine is located. UP preserves the destination and look.

units.text: Shannon hurriedly ran over to a nearby side table and started searching around on top of it. A cute basket was placed there, and inside of it was Jessica's bronchodilator. Shannon picked it up and handed it over to Jessica.
units.japanese: 紗音は慌てて駆け寄り、近くのサイドテーブルの上を見る。そこには可愛らしい篭が置かれ、その中に朱志香用の気管支拡張剤があった。それを取り、朱志香に渡す。

description: MG changes Jessica’s teasing into cheering Shannon on when explaining how her true feelings surfaced. Japanese distinguishes her sincere wish to congratulate her friend from the teasing through which envy and insecurity emerge. UP made fun of preserves the contrast.

units.text: Before she realized it, Jessica was shedding huge tears. Jessica didn't really feel like crying, and of course, she felt like supporting Shannon's progress in love as a friend. ...However, as she had cheered Shannon on, her true feelings had suddenly gotten mixed in, and she couldn't help but shed tears...
units.japanese: いつの間にか、朱志香は大粒の涙を浮かべていた。朱志香は別に泣く気などなかったし、もちろん紗音の恋路が順調に進んでいることを友人として祝福する気持ちもあった。…でも、囃し立てている内に、いつの間にか本音が混じり始めて、つい涙が零れてしまったのだ…。

description: MG interprets Jessica’s turning away as not wanting to trouble Shannon. The source presents the gesture as if she did not want attention, followed by Shannon recognizing a desire not to be pressed further. UP preserves attention-seeking denial.

units.text: Jessica faced away, acting as though she didn't really want to trouble Shannon, waving her hand as though chasing Shannon away.
units.japanese: 朱志香は、構って欲しいわけじゃないというような仕草で背中を向けると、追い払うような感じで手をひらひらと振る。

description: Both have Beatrice happily blow on her pipe. 煙管をふかす here means smoking or puffing at the pipe; blowing on the object changes the action and leaves the smoking image unexpressed.

units.text: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe. Sitting in a place like that would crush the roses, and it might have been dangerous if the arch fell over, ...but this was a witch, after all. Showing concern for her safety was probably a waste of time.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、薔薇のアーチの上に腰を掛けながら、上機嫌に煙管をふかしていた。そんなところに腰掛けたら、薔薇が潰れてしまうし、アーチが倒れて危ないかもしれないが、…何しろ相手は魔女なのだ。それは余計な心配に違いなかった。

units.text: As Beatrice sat on the rose arch, she happily blew on her pipe. Sitting in a place like that would crush the roses, and it might have been dangerous if you fell off the arch, ...but after all, this was a witch. That was surely an unnecessary concern.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、薔薇のアーチの上に腰を掛けながら、上機嫌に煙管をふかしていた。そんなところに腰掛けたら、薔薇が潰れてしまうし、アーチが倒れて危ないかもしれないが、…何しろ相手は魔女なのだ。それは余計な心配に違いなかった。

description: MG says Shannon remembered the witch’s words, rather than the witch’s words making her remember the supposed impossibility of her relationship. UP preserves the words as the trigger. The following thought restores the content but the immediate reminder mechanism is changed.

units.text: Shannon had just gotten wrapped up in those sweet days...and had started believing the illusion that all fate revolved around her. ...But she remembered the witch's words.
units.japanese: 紗音は、ついつい甘い日々に浮かれ、全ての運命が自分を中心に回っていると錯覚してしまいそうになっていた。…でも、魔女の言葉で思い出す。

description: The source says fear outweighed gratitude after reliance on the power. MG substitutes fear rather than gratitude, suppressing coexistence and relative degree; UP substitutes fear more often than gratitude, changing intensity into frequency.

units.text: Beatrice was definitely a witch, with a strange and terrifying power. Most people probably wouldn't want to stick around her if they could help it. Surely, even those who had relied on that strange power sometimes felt fear rather than gratitude as a result. ...It must have deeply hurt the witch to have that happen over and over.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは間違いなく魔女であり、不思議な、恐ろしい力を持っている。できることなら付き合いなどしたくないと誰もが思うだろう。時に、その不思議な力に頼りながらも、その結果は感謝より畏怖の気持ちの方が大きかったに違いない。………そんな繰り返しがきっと、魔女を深く傷つけていったに違いない。

units.text: Beatrice was definitely a witch, with a strange and terrifying power. Most likely, no one would go along with her if they could help it. And even though on occasion they had relied on her strange power, it had undoubtedly resulted in fear more often than gratitude. .........It must have deeply hurt the witch when that repeated over and over.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは間違いなく魔女であり、不思議な、恐ろしい力を持っている。できることなら付き合いなどしたくないと誰もが思うだろう。時に、その不思議な力に頼りながらも、その結果は感謝より畏怖の気持ちの方が大きかったに違いない。………そんな繰り返しがきっと、魔女を深く傷つけていったに違いない。

description: UP makes Kinzo the person with the greatest lack of magical talent, adding no one with a more pitiful lack. Japanese says he too lacks talent to a pitiable degree, without ranking him against everyone. MG preserves also and pitiable lack.

units.text: "............Kinzo is the same. There is no one with a more pitiful lack of magical talent. ...It's the blood. He has so little talent, he is worthy of sympathy."
units.japanese: 「…………金蔵も同じよ。あれにも気の毒なくらいに魔法の才能がない。…血だな。同情に値するほど才能がない」

description: MG changes Kinzo having fulfilled all dreams obtainable in the human world into being able to fulfill dreams satisfied by obtainable objects. This replaces completed attainment with capacity and narrows worldly aspirations to objects. UP retains completed satisfaction of worldly dreams.

units.text: "Once Kinzo gained his vast fortune, he could realize every dream that can be satisfied by objects obtainable in the human world. ......And in the end, he searched for the truth of this world."
units.japanese: 「そして、莫大な財産を得た金蔵は、人の世で手に入れることのできる全ての夢を叶えきった。………そして、最後に世界の真理を求めたのだ」

description: MG changes Beatrice’s reassurance that Shannon need not remember the single element into there being no need to worry. The source’s specific deflection of recollection is lost; UP preserves no need to remember.

units.text: The single element. ......She seemed to remember the witch using that word before. When Beatrice saw Shannon trying to remember what that was, she laughed bitterly, waving her hand and saying there was no need to worry.
units.japanese: 一なる元素。………以前に彼女の口から聞かされた言葉のような気がする。それが何だったか思い出そうとする紗音の表情を見て、ベアトリーチェは苦笑いしながら、思い出さなくて良い良いと手を振る。

description: MG removes Beatrice directing Shannon’s assistance: she had her help regain power becomes Shannon helped, and I had you destroy the dining arrangement becomes you destroyed it. UP preserves the causative direction in both places. This changes the source’s repeated attribution of orchestration.

units.text: During that time, her words had reached Shannon, who never forgot to show sincere respect for the witch. And Shannon had helped the witch regain her power, if only a little bit. ...As a result, it was now possible for the witch to drink tea with Shannon like this...
units.japanese:
そんな中、魔女に強い敬いを忘れない紗音に言葉が届いたのだ。そして、自分の力をわずかでも取り戻す手伝いをさせたのだ。…その結果、こうして紗音とお茶を飲めるようになった…。
「だからそなたに日本風の客席を打ち壊し、場を一度白紙に戻させたのだ。そのお陰で、ようやく妾の注文した料理が届き力が戻った、というところか。もっとも、ようやく食前酒が届いたというところよ」

units.text: "So, you destroyed that Japanese-style guest seating and returned the area to a blank slate for a time. Thanks to that, the meal I had ordered was finally delivered, and my power came back, you could say. However, so far, only the aperitif has arrived.
units.japanese:
そんな中、魔女に強い敬いを忘れない紗音に言葉が届いたのだ。そして、自分の力をわずかでも取り戻す手伝いをさせたのだ。…その結果、こうして紗音とお茶を飲めるようになった…。
「だからそなたに日本風の客席を打ち壊し、場を一度白紙に戻させたのだ。そのお陰で、ようやく妾の注文した料理が届き力が戻った、というところか。もっとも、ようやく食前酒が届いたというところよ」

description: UP replaces kaiseki cuisine already laid out in the Japanese-style dining area with Japanese tableware. The source describes a competing meal, not simply different utensils or dishes as objects. MG Japanese-style dishes can retain food in context.

units.text: "......If I were to use food as an example, maybe it would go something like this. Let's say that I have ordered some Western cuisine, which is being made in the kitchen. However, when it comes time for it to be served, the seating is in the Japanese style, and Japanese tableware has been laid out." "So the kitchen is unable to take out the plate which would be out of place, and no matter how long I wait, my Western food won't arrive—something like that."
units.japanese: 「……料理に例えるならこうか。妾の注文した西洋料理が厨房でまさに料理されているとする。ところが、いざ配膳しようとしたら、客席は日本風で懐石料理が並べられている場だった」「だから厨房は場違いな皿を出せず、妾のところへはいつまで経っても西洋料理が届かない…、と言った感じよの」

description: Both make Beatrice describe a foolish discussion with a human. 他愛ない話 is light or inconsequential conversation here, fitting newly possible casual friendship; foolish adds disparagement to the content.

units.text: "...Although I may not look it, I was known for doing extremely brutal things in the past. ...I've gotten soft. Now I can even have a foolish discussion while drinking tea with a human."
units.japanese: 「……こう見えても、昔は残酷極まりないことで知られた妾だったが。…丸くなったものよ。人間とこうして他愛ない話で茶を交わせるようになるのだから」

units.text: "......Although I may not look it, I was known for doing extremely brutal things in the past. ...I've gotten soft. Now I can even have a foolish discussion while drinking tea with a human."
units.japanese: 「……こう見えても、昔は残酷極まりないことで知られた妾だったが。…丸くなったものよ。人間とこうして他愛ない話で茶を交わせるようになるのだから」

description: MG makes Kanon deny that they possess what it takes to love or be loved. 資格 here denies eligibility or entitlement from their asserted furniture status, not their psychological capacity for love. UP unqualified preserves the status-based claim.

units.text: "No, you aren't. We have never possessed what it takes to love or be loved."
units.japanese: 「いや、人間じゃない。僕らには愛する資格も、愛される資格も初めからない」
candidates: takes to love or be loved

description: MG says Kanon does not understand what Shannon means before she asks the sea-color question. Japanese specifically says he cannot tell what she is pointing at; the question’s deeper meaning becomes the separate uncertainty at row 519. UP preserves the visual-reference uncertainty.

units.text: Shannon quietly pointed at the sea, towards the horizon. Kanon didn't understand what she meant, and couldn't do anything except look between the horizon and Shannon's expression, which seemed to be posing a riddle.
units.japanese: 紗音は海を、水平線の彼方をすっと指差す。嘉音には具体的に何を指差しているのかわからなくて、水平線と謎掛けをするような紗音の表情を交互に見比べるしかない。

description: MG describes a world where the single element existed, rather than a world filled with it. The source’s fulfilled or filled condition connects love to the perceived blue sea; mere existence weakens that relation. UP world full of that element preserves it.

units.text: ...The single element of the world. She spoke once more of the world where it existed, where the sea was deep blue.
units.japanese: …世界の一なる元素。それが満たされた、海が真っ青な世界を、もう一度だけ言う。

description: Both say Beatrice tried to rest her hand on Kinzo’s shoulder. The source’s concessive formulation says he notices nothing even with her hand placed on his shoulder, without specifying an unsuccessful attempt. Introducing tried weakens the contrast between contact and nonperception.

units.text: Right behind Kinzo, as he repeated the witch's name over and over, desiring to be reunited with her more than anything else, was the witch herself. And yet, Kinzo didn't notice anything. ...When Beatrice tried to rest her hand on his shoulder, he didn't notice.
units.japanese:
魔女の名を何度も繰り返し、再会を何よりも欲する金蔵のすぐ後に当の魔女がいる。なのに、金蔵は何も気付けない。
……ベアトリーチェが、その肩に手を載せようと、何も気付かない。
candidates: Beatrice tried to rest her hand

units.text:
Right behind Kinzo, as he repeated the witch's name over and over, desiring to be reunited with her more than anything else, was the witch herself. And yet, Kinzo couldn't notice a thing.
......Even when Beatrice tried to rest her hand on his shoulder, he didn't notice a thing.
units.japanese:
魔女の名を何度も繰り返し、再会を何よりも欲する金蔵のすぐ後に当の魔女がいる。なのに、金蔵は何も気付けない。
……ベアトリーチェが、その肩に手を載せようと、何も気付かない。
candidates: Beatrice tried to rest her hand

description: MG changes almost no young men on Rokkenjima into young men rarely visiting it. The source grounds Jessica’s interest in scarcity of young men present on the island, without identifying rarity of visitor traffic as the reason. UP preserves island presence.

units.text: It was extremely rare for young men to visit Rokkenjima. So maybe it was natural for Jessica, a girl in puberty, to develop an interest in Kanon. But if anyone said that, it would destroy the romantic ideals of a maiden's pure heart and love at first sight.
units.japanese:
六軒島に若い男はほとんどいない。
だから、朱志香が嘉音に興味を持ったのは思春期の少女として当然のことだったかもしれない。でもそれを言ってしまったら乙女の純情や一目惚れというロマンを蔑ろにしてしまう。

description: UP makes Jessica feel shameless rather than find her feigned ignorance unconvincing or transparent. The next thought explicitly admits she knows who is arriving; MG transparent attempt to play dumb preserves this self-conscious performance.

units.text:
Even I felt kind of shameless. Did I just say "sorry, who"?!
Like I don't know who's shown up...!
Aaaaaaaaah, crap, crap, crap, my mind is blank...
units.japanese:
自分でも何だか白々しい。ごめん、誰…、だって？！
だ、誰が訪ねてくるかなんてわかってるくせに…！
あぁああぁああ、駄目だ駄目だ頭が真っ白だぜ…。

description: MG renders 榎本 as Emoto, dropping the no syllable from the surname. UP Enomoto preserves the source name.

units.text: "It appeared so. That person is also very energetic. Oh, and I believe President Emoto also made an appearance."
units.japanese: 「そのようでした。あの方も精力的な方です。そうそう、あと榎本会長もお出ででしたっけ」

description: MG entitled brat and UP spoiled little kid add moral judgments of entitlement or indulgence to Jessica’s realization that she is merely childish. The source self-reproach concerns immature desire for parental recognition; it does not specify being spoiled or entitled.

units.text: Jessica laughed at what she was sulking over. ...She laughed at what kind of words she could possibly have been expecting. ...That was dumb of me. In the end, I was just acting like an entitled brat. I'm a little exasperated with myself, and it makes me want to laugh.
units.japanese:
朱志香は、自分が何を不貞腐れてるのだろうと笑う。…さっき、どんな言葉を掛けられれば自分は満足したのかを想像して、笑う。……馬鹿馬鹿しかった。結局、自分がお子様なだけだった。
何だか呆れて、笑いたくなる。

units.text:
Jessica laughed at what she was sulking over. ...Laughed at what kind of words she would have had to receive to be satisfied. ......Ridiculous. In the end, I'm just a spoiled little kid.
I can't believe myself—it's almost funny.
units.japanese:
朱志香は、自分が何を不貞腐れてるのだろうと笑う。…さっき、どんな言葉を掛けられれば自分は満足したのかを想像して、笑う。……馬鹿馬鹿しかった。結局、自分がお子様なだけだった。
何だか呆れて、笑いたくなる。

description: MG changes the expression Kanon habitually sees on Jessica into the expression Jessica wears when looking at Kanon. This invents a specifically Kanon-directed facial manner instead of the familiar island persona that he now recognizes as concealing her mood. UP retains Kanon as observer.

units.text: Jessica's expression became the one she always wore when looking at Kanon. The listless Jessica from a second ago was gone.
units.japanese:
朱志香の表情は、嘉音がいつも見るそれになっていた。
ついさっきまでの物憂げな朱志香ではない。

description: MG saw Jessica trod away uses the past form after saw instead of the bare infinitive tread; UP trodded uses a nonstandard past form instead of trod. Both disrupt the departure sentence, though the action is recoverable.

units.text: Kanon saw Jessica trod away with her back to him, looking disheartened. But then, she suddenly broke into a reckless dash and disappeared in the direction of the mansion...
units.japanese: 背を向けた朱志香は、元気なくとぼとぼと歩み去るかに見えた。だが突然、がむしゃらに駆け出し、屋敷の方へ消えていった…。

units.text: Jessica turned her back to him, and slowly trodded away, looking disheartened. But suddenly, she started dashing pell‐mell, and disappeared in the direction of the mansion...
units.japanese: 背を向けた朱志香は、元気なくとぼとぼと歩み去るかに見えた。だが突然、がむしゃらに駆け出し、屋敷の方へ消えていった…。

description: MG makes the broken brooch evaporate like water. The source compares its disappearance to dissolving into water before it changes into golden butterflies. UP preserves the dissolving image.

units.text: Kanon ground his foot even more into the stomped brooch. He felt it break under his foot. Then, it evaporated like water... and changed into butterflies that sparkled gold, fluttering out from beneath Kanon's foot...
units.japanese:
嘉音は踏みつけたままのブローチをさらに踏みにじる。
…パキリと割れた感触が足の裏に伝わった。するとそれはさらりと水に溶けるように消え去り、黄金に輝く蝶たちに変わって嘉音の足の裏からひらひらと舞い散っていった…。

description: 座席で locates Maria in her seat while she kicks her feet. MG makes her stomp her feet on the seat, adding contact with the seat surface. UP keeps the seated kicking motion.

units.text: While it wasn't completely full inside the train, it was really packed, with almost all the seats occupied by passengers. Maria was making a fuss among them, stomping her feet on the seat while Rosa scowled at her. Rosa had warned her many times to lower her voice, but Maria hadn't obeyed her at all.
units.japanese: 満員とは行かないまでも、車内は座席ほとんどが乗客で埋まる程度には大勢いた。そんな中、座席で足をばたばたさせながらわがままを騒ぐ真里亞に、楼座は顔をしかめている。さっきから楼座は声を潜めながら何度も注意しているのだが、真里亞は一向に聞き入れなかった。

description: 隣の座席 places the old woman in the adjacent seat. UP places her across from Maria, then calls her next to them at row 59; MG nearby is less precise initially but preserves adjacency at row 59.

units.text: As Maria kicked her feet, a stout old woman sitting in the seat across from Maria picked a candy out of her handbag and gave it to her.
units.japanese: 足をばたばたとさせる真里亞の隣の座席に座っていた恰幅のいい老婦人が、ハンドバッグの中からのど飴を取り出し、差し出した。

description: ほくほくしながら describes Maria walking with delighted satisfaction. MG adds audible chuckling to herself; UP preserves pleased feeling without inventing a vocal action.

units.text: They exited through the turnstiles of the station in this unknown town. Maria walked across the pedestrian crossing together with her mother, chuckling to herself, as though she was walking in an amusement park.
units.japanese:
二人は見知らぬ町の駅で改札を出る。
真里亞は、母と渡る横断歩道を、まるで遊園地で歩くようにほくほくしながら歩む。

description: 確信があったからだ explains Krauss’s actual confidence as the reason for increasing investment. MG converts this to a hypothetical rule about what you would only do if confident, weakening attribution of the belief to Krauss. UP retains his confidence as his actual motivation.

units.text: At times, it's possible to make further investments, so that the seesaw inclines faster towards the side you want. ...Of course, you'd only do that if you were confident you'd be able to recover all your investments in the not-so-distant future.
units.japanese: 時に、そのシーソーが早く良い方へ傾くよう、さらに投資をすることもある。……もちろん、遠くない将来に、かさんだ投資が全て取り返せるという確信があったからだ。

description: 賄いも今夜はぜひ期待してください asks the interlocutor to look forward to the servants’ meal too. UP adds an instruction to let the other servants know and an explicit promise not to disappoint them; neither speech act is stated in this line.

units.text: "Yes, dinner will be an excellent calf steak...! A wonderful cut of meat is already in the refrigerator anxiously waiting for tonight. Please, let the other servants know to look forward to tonight—I will not disappoint them either."
units.japanese: 「えぇ、ディナーには仔牛のステーキを…！　素晴らしい肉がすでに保冷庫で今夜を待ちわびておりますよ。賄いも今夜はぜひ期待してください」

description: 嘉音には丸判りだった asserts that Shannon’s excitement is completely obvious to Kanon. MG changes the assertion to Kanon seemed to see through her, introducing uncertainty about his awareness. UP preserves his definite understanding.

units.text: As Shannon blushed just a bit, she turned her gaze away from the clock. ...Was it about time for the airplane carrying the family to arrive at Niijima? ...She'd tried to hide the fact that her upcoming, long-awaited reunion with George was making her heart race, but Kanon, who stood beside her, seemed to see right through her.
units.japanese:
紗音は頬をわずかにだけ赤らめると、時計から目を逸らす。……もう親族たちの飛行機は新島に着いたころだろうか。
…譲治との久しぶりの再会に胸をときめかせているのを、少しは隠しているつもりなのだろうが、脇の嘉音には丸判りだった。

description: 牽引力のある男性 describes an assertive man who takes the lead. UP a man with traction calques the metaphor into mechanical grip without clearly conveying the interpersonal quality. MG more assertive preserves that quality.

units.text: "That's not it... Shannon likes a man with traction. It, it must have a more powerful feel to it...!"
units.japanese: 「違うな…。紗音は牽引力のある男性が好きなんだ。も、もっと馬力がある感じじゃないと駄目だ…！」

description: MG maybe she’ll put on her right hand omits the object of put, leaving the intended placement of the ring grammatically incomplete. UP put it on the right hand restores the object.

units.text: "Aah, if I don't say properly that it's on the left hand, maybe she'll put on her right hand! N-No, Shannon isn't that ignorant, aaah, but unless there's some room for her to express her free will, that'd be a little, I mean, uuuuuu, nnnnuuuuuuu, muuuuuuuaaaaaaaaahhhh...!!"
units.japanese: 「あぁ、左手とちゃんと言わないと右手にされちゃうかもしれない！　い、いや、紗音もそこまでカマトトじゃないけど、あぁでも、少しは自由意志がないと何だかその、うううううううぅ、んーーーぅううううぅぅうぅ、むぅううううぅああああああぁ…！！　」
candidates: maybe she'll put on her right hand

description: 子どもには子どものコミュニケーションがある admires children’s own way of communicating. MG substitutes admiration of how good children are at getting along, changing the observation from a distinct mode of communication to proficiency at harmony. UP preserves the source observation.

units.text: The adults were amazed at how good children can be at getting along with each other. Maria had been throwing a tantrum because she wanted a Halloween festival, so Battler, who knew about trick-or-treating, must have felt like an ally.
units.japanese: 大人たちは、子どもには子どものコミュニケーションがあるのだなぁと感服する。ハロウィンのお祭りがしたいと駄々をこねていた真里亞にとって、トリックオアトリートを理解してくれた戦人はきっと仲間のように感じられたに違いない。

description: MG one of her descendants suddenly appears and tell us mismatches singular appears with plural tell. UP show up and tell follows the modal will and is grammatical.

units.text: "I mean Beatrice-sama. ...Nobody knows her background. Could she be Grandfather's mistress from long ago? ...What if one of her descendants suddenly appears and tell us to return the gold we were given, or something?"
units.japanese: 「ベアトリーチェさまだよ。……素性は誰も知らない。あるいは大昔の祖父さまの愛人なのか。……その子孫がひょっこりと現れて、授けた黄金を返せなんて言い出すかもしれないぜ？」

description: 先生は高給取りだから、与太話もできねぇや jokes that Rudolf cannot afford idle chatter because the lawyer is highly paid. MG no idle chitchat turns this into a directive against chatting, losing the speaker’s inability/cost joke. UP retains I can’t even chat idly.

units.text: "Thank you very much, sir. Please contact me if anything new happens. We're paying you the big bucks, so no idle chitchat. Hahahaha. <Thank you, thank you, goodbye.>"
units.japanese: 「ありがとう先生。また進展があったら連絡してください。先生は高給取りだから、与太話もできねぇや。はっはっはっは。サンキューサンキュー、グッバーイ」

description: MG spells turbulence as turbulance. UP uses turbulence.

units.text: The airplane suddenly shook, probably due to turbulance. Rudolf was jostled awake. He'd woken early that morning and ended up drifting off to sleep while resting in his seat.
units.japanese:
ガクンと飛行機が大きく揺れる。気流のせいだろう。その衝撃で留弗夫は目を覚ます。
朝が早かったせいもあり、座席に座って一息ついたらあっさり眠ってしまったのだ。

description: The reflection follows Nanjo looking out the window and ends with Nanjo looking at the portrait. その心当たりがひとりいた gives him one candidate for the guest who might draw Kinzo out. MG explicitly assigns the person in mind to Kinzo instead of the observing Nanjo. UP he retains the contextual Nanjo perspective without inserting Kinzo’s name.

units.text: As he is now, I doubt Kinzo would pay any heed to any sort of guest. ...Could any guest possibly make Kinzo come out "when the time comes", as he said? Kinzo had a single person in mind, but that was a guest who certainly wouldn't appear...
units.japanese: 今の金蔵は、どんな来客が訪れようとも関心を持たないだろう。…そんな金蔵に、出るべき時に出ると言わしめる来客などいるのだろうか。その心当たりがひとりいたが、それは絶対に現れるわけもない来客…。

description: MG he’s became uses became where the present perfect requires become. UP has become is grammatical.

units.text: "That's right, Battler-kun from Rudolf-san's family. I hear he'll be coming after an absence of six years. I'm sure he's became a splendid boy."
units.japanese: 「ほら、留弗夫さんのところの戦人くんです。６年ぶりにお出でになるそうじゃありませんか。きっと立派になっていますよ」

description: UP a unusual way uses a before the vowel sound in unusual. MG for once avoids this grammar error.

units.text: Kinzo reacted in a unusual way to Nanjo's words and turned around.
units.japanese: 南條の言葉に、珍しく金蔵が反応し振り返る。

description: 大切な機会 calls Halloween an important opportunity for witches to interact with otherworldly visitors. MG the most important chance adds a superlative ranking not stated here. UP precious opportunity preserves importance without ranking.

units.text: "So Halloween is a time when those two worlds intermingle? In other words, it's the most important chance for witches to intermingle with guests from that world. Is that what you're trying to say?"
units.japanese: 「つまり、ハロウィンはこの世とあの世の交流のある時期ってわけなんだな？　それでつまり、魔女たちにとってはそういう世界の客人たちと交流できる大切な機会だったと。そう言いたいわけか」

description: 感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね allows gratitude for the harvest as a fitting interpretation of giving candy. UP the reason ... must be because ... they should be thanked strengthens this into a necessary causal explanation. MG you might say preserves the tentative allowance.

units.text: "Halloween costumes are an imitation of the visitors from the other side. ......So, then, the reason we give candy to them must be because of a feeling that they should be thanked for the yearly harvest."
units.japanese: 「ハロウィンの仮装は、向こうから来る客人たちの模倣。……つまり、彼らにお菓子を施すのは、一年の収穫への感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね」

description: MG changes inventing protective rituals into performing them.
sourceReading: 生み出していった narrates the practices being developed; original WH created enchantments and UP invented protective rituals preserve creation.

units.text: At the time, people believed that souls returning to the physical world would go into people's houses or possess people and do bad things. So, in order to avoid harm, they performed rituals. One of those was to imitate creepy monsters and scare the souls back, which was apparently a way to avoid being possessed.
units.japanese: 現世に戻ってくる霊魂たちが、人々の家に入ってきたり、あるいは取り憑いて悪さをすると当時の人々は信じていた。そこで彼らは、これらの害を受けないようなおまじないを生み出していった。そのひとつが、不気味な怪物の姿を模して、霊魂たちを逆に怖がらせ、取り憑かれないようにしようというものだったらしい。

description: スケールのでかい話 comments on the large scale of Maria’s account or ambition. MG detailed and impressive replaces scope with elaborateness and favorable appraisal; UP large-scale dream retains the magnitude.

units.text: "Oh...? That sounds pretty detailed and impressive. ...By the way, who was Beatrice again? ...Hmm, I know I've heard that name somewhere before..."
units.japanese: 「へー…。そいつぁ何だかスケールのでかい話だな。……ところでベアトリーチェって誰だっけ？　……何だっけ、えっとえっと、聞いた名前だな…」

description: UP marshmallows that look they have fluorescent paint omits like between look and they. MG look like they have is grammatical.

units.text: "Because you made that ruckus in the train, I had to go to all the trouble of getting off and buying you those disgusting monster marshmallows that look they have fluorescent paint on them... We were even late because I bought them for you. How much more will you have to embarrass me before you're satisfied......?!"
units.japanese: 「電車であんなに騒ぐから、わざわざ電車降りてまでその蛍光塗料みたいな気持ち悪いオバケマシュマロを買ってやったのよ…。遅刻してまであんたに買ってやったのよ。あんたどこまで私の顔を潰せば気が済むのよ……！」
candidates: marshmallows that look they have fluorescent paint

description: 全員顔を揃える means everyone meeting or gathering together. UP gather our faces mechanically translates the idiom into an unnatural physical object for gather; MG meet in person conveys the meeting.

units.text: "Yep! Just as Rudolf‐kun says. ......We can only gather our faces here once a year. We've gotta value this precious time we've got, and talk together frankly."
units.japanese: 「そうや！　留弗夫くんの言う通りや。……わしらが全員顔を揃えるのは年に一度しかない。貴重な時間を大事にし、忌憚ない話し合いをせんといかん」

description: 鼻の下を伸ばした describes Hideyoshi and Rudolf’s leering or besotted expression as they watch Shannon leave. MG substitutes a general trait, had a soft spot for women, while UP turned heads supplies a neutral movement. Both weaken the immediate lustful reaction.

units.text: Shannon bowed politely and left the room. As Hideyoshi and Rudolf, who had a soft spot for women, watched her go, ...the atmosphere in the room began to revert back to what it had been right before Shannon's visit.
units.japanese: 紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。

units.text: Shannon bowed politely and left the room. After Hideyoshi and Rudolf watched her go with turned heads, ...the atmosphere in the room began to revert back to what it had been right before Shannon had visited.
units.japanese: 紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。

description: 人影に飛びつく describes Maria leaping onto or clinging to the arriving figure. Both translations reduce this to dashing over to the figure, preserving approach but losing the physical contact. The following explanation likewise replaces jumping onto a stranger with dashing over.

units.text: Maria dashed over to the shadow. ...Normally, Rosa would scold her daughter if she dashed over to someone whom she hadn't seen before and didn't know. ...But Rosa forgot to do that, was unable to do anything but stand there, stunned.
units.japanese: 真里亞がその人影に飛びつく。……普段の楼座なら、見ず知らずの人に娘が飛びつくようなことがあれば叱る。…しかし楼座は、それを忘れて、ただただ呆然とするしかできなかった。

units.text: Maria dashed over to the figure. ......Normally, Rosa would scold her daughter if she dashed over to a complete stranger. ...But Rosa forgot about that, unable to do anything but stand there, shocked.
units.japanese: 真里亞がその人影に飛びつく。……普段の楼座なら、見ず知らずの人に娘が飛びつくようなことがあれば叱る。…しかし楼座は、それを忘れて、ただただ呆然とするしかできなかった。

description: MG there could no more fitting sacrifice omits be after could. UP there is no one more fitting is grammatical.

units.text: ...Don't you think there could no more fitting sacrifice for the second twilight than Shannon as she is now...? *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle!!"
units.japanese: 「……今の紗音なら、これほど相応しい第二の晩の生贄もないとは思わぬか…？　くっくくくくくくくくくく！！」

description: The joking proverb says the person lying down after eating becomes a mackerel. MG it’ll become a mackerel supplies an unrelated it as transformation subject; UP you’ll become restores the person addressed.

units.text: "My, my. They say that if you lie down right after eating, it'll become a mackerel. Hohohoh...!"
units.japanese: 「おやおや。食事の後にすぐ横になると鯖になると申しますよ。ほっほっほ…！」

description: 名乗ってすらいない says the woman has not even introduced herself to Kyrie. MG she’s refused to introduce herself adds an explicit refusal rather than the stated absence of introduction. UP hasn’t even named herself preserves the observation.

units.text: "That would be for the best. ...Already, she's refused to introduce herself to Kyrie-san. ...We can't let our conference be disturbed by the statements of some unknown woman."
units.japanese: 「それが最善ね。……現に霧江さんに対して名乗ってすらいない。…正体不明の女の発言で私たちの会議がかき回されちゃ堪らないわ」

description: 留弗夫と絵羽の夫婦 includes Rudolf’s and Eva’s couples in the inheritance-protecting coalition. Both translations narrow the narrated participants to Rudolf and Eva alone, omitting their spouses from this collective action.

units.text: Rudolf and Eva always formed a united front as siblings at times like this, sickened by the idea that their own inheritance might be snatched away by an outsider.
units.japanese: 留弗夫と絵羽の夫婦は、自分たちの遺産を余所者に掻っ攫われて堪るかと、こんな時ばかり兄弟で結束するのだった。

units.text: It was only at a time like this that Rudolf and Eva united as siblings, sickened by the idea that their own inheritance might be snatched away by an outsider.
units.japanese: 留弗夫と絵羽の夫婦は、自分たちの遺産を余所者に掻っ攫われて堪るかと、こんな時ばかり兄弟で結束するのだった。

description: UP renders Rosa’s 談合 with Eva and Rudolf as consulting, weakening her admission of collusion to extract money from Krauss.
sourceReading: Rosa admits she has even colluded with her siblings to extract money, reinforcing her awareness of improper conduct. Later 相談 at 709 is ordinary consultation about the letter.

units.text: ...And I'm even consulting with Rudolf nii‐san and Eva nee‐san in order to get some money out of Krauss nii‐san. With myself in this situation, .........I can't help but sense something ominous in the appearance of the witch...
units.japanese: …そして、蔵臼兄さんからお金を引き出すため、絵羽姉さんや留弗夫兄さんと談合してすらいる。そんな私にとって、………魔女の出現は、不吉なものを予見させずにはいられないのだ…。

description: UP take back all the hard times we had misstates Kanon’s wish to make up for past suffering as reclaiming the hard times themselves.
sourceReading: これまでの辛かった分を取り戻したい means recovering what past suffering cost them, living to compensate for it together. MG make up for all the suffering conveys that desire.

units.text: "I don't like it. ......Together with you, I want to take back all the hard times we had. I won't become a sacrifice. You and I will remain alive. And we'll reach the Golden Land together."
units.japanese: 「僕は嫌だ。……これまでの辛かった分を、姉さんと取り戻したい。生贄なんてごめんだ。僕と姉さんは生き残る。そして二人で黄金郷へ辿り着く」
candidates: take back all the hard times

description: MG since the early evening shifts Nanjo’s chess visit from starting before evening to starting in the evening.
sourceReading: 夕方前からずっと establishes play beginning before evening and continuing; UP preserves before evening.

units.text: Nanjo could be seen in the study. Because Kinzo had forcefully pestered him into finishing their long-lasting chess game, they had been playing against each other since the early evening.
units.japanese: 南條の姿は、書斎の中にあった。長く続けられてきた二人のチェスの決着を、金蔵が強くせがんだため、夕方前からずっと相手をさせられていたのだ。

description: Both quick-tempered replaces the slight urgency in Beatrice’s call after Shannon turns away.
sourceReading: 性急 describes her call becoming a little more hasty or urgent, evidence that Shannon’s departure affected her.

units.text: Shannon gave a reserved bow and faced away. ...With that gesture, maybe she really did take a shot back at the witch, just as Beatrice had said. ...Because, when the witch called out again, she sounded a little more quick-tempered than she had before.
units.japanese:
紗音は他人行儀に頭を下げ、背を向ける。
…その仕草は、魔女の言う通り、確かに一矢報いたのかもしれない。…それまでに比べると、魔女の呼びかけはほんの少しだけ性急だったからだ。

units.text:
Shannon gave a reserved bow as she would to a stranger, and faced away.
...With that gesture, maybe she really had taken a shot back at the witch, just as Beatrice had mentioned. ...Because when the witch called out again, she sounded a little more quick‐tempered than she had before.
units.japanese:
紗音は他人行儀に頭を下げ、背を向ける。
…その仕草は、魔女の言う通り、確かに一矢報いたのかもしれない。…それまでに比べると、魔女の呼びかけはほんの少しだけ性急だったからだ。

description: MG still had not answered turns Shannon’s decision to give no further replies into an absence of an earlier answer.
sourceReading: もう返事をしなかった means she no longer answered, after dismissing further business; UP gave no more answers preserves that cutoff.

units.text: A flat-out interruption. Shannon still hadn't answered her. And the sound of the door closing came instead of an answer.
units.japanese:
ぴしゃりと遮る。
もう紗音は返事をしなかった。そして扉が閉じられるその音が、返事の代わりとなるのだった。

description: Both loud argument adds audible escalation to the siblings’ verbal sparring over the sauce.
sourceReading: 鍔迫り合い metaphorically describes close sparring; the source says dinner basically proceeds amicably without specifying raised voices.

units.text: It looked like the siblings quickly got into a loud argument about the sauce, ...but for the most part, dinner proceeded peacefully.
units.japanese: たかだかソースの話で、さっそく兄弟たちは鍔迫り合いをしているようだったが、…基本的に晩餐は和やかに進んだ。

units.text: It looked like the siblings quickly got into a loud argument about something as trivial as the sauce, ...but for the most part, dinner proceeded peacefully.
units.japanese: たかだかソースの話で、さっそく兄弟たちは鍔迫り合いをしているようだったが、…基本的に晩餐は和やかに進んだ。

description: MG This was most fabulous part omits the article before the superlative noun phrase.
sourceReading: English requires the most fabulous part here. UP supplies the article.

units.text: This was most fabulous part of the family conference... Dinner.
units.japanese:
親族会議でもっとも華やかな時間。
それが晩餐だった。

description: MG became able serve omits to in able to serve.
sourceReading: The infinitive complement requires to; UP could unveil is grammatical.

units.text: Because of that, she and Krauss eventually hired Gohda, who had confidence in his cooking abilities. ...Thanks to that, they became able serve wonderful dinners they could be confident in, but by that time, Kinzo had closed himself up in his study and never appeared for dinner. Maybe you could call that ironic...
units.japanese: その為、蔵臼夫妻はやがて、料理の腕に自信のある郷田を雇うことになる。……その結果、自信の持てる素晴らしい晩餐を披露できるようになったにもかかわらず、その頃には金蔵は書斎に引き篭もるようになっていて晩餐に姿を現さなくなったのだから、皮肉と言えたかもしれない…。

description: MG confirm the nature of what she was describing beyond doubt substitutes certainty about the visitor’s nature for corroborating her existence.
sourceReading: その存在を肯定した confirms existence through Kyrie’s testimony. Kyrie then explicitly withholds a conclusion that the woman is Beatrice and labels her portrait identification subjective.

units.text: Because of that, it only took a single, calmly-spoken sentence to confirm the nature of what she was describing beyond doubt.
units.japanese: だから、冷静な一言が、その存在を間違いなく肯定した。
candidates: confirm the nature of what she was describing beyond doubt

description: MG’s ‘Of course they’d wouldn’t want’ combines two auxiliary constructions and is ungrammatical.
sourceReading: The adults realize they naturally would not want their children present for the sordid inheritance discussion.

units.text: ...Of course they'd wouldn't want their children to remain. So they all immediately agreed with Rosa's plan.
units.japanese:
…この場に自分の子どもを居続けさせたいわけもない。
だから、全員が楼座の提案にすぐ同意した。

description: UP’s ‘slightly emotionally’ is an unidiomatic rendering of Rosa becoming somewhat emotional as she shouts at the children.
sourceReading: Rosa is a little overcome by emotion when she orders the children back to the guesthouse.

units.text: Rosa yelled at the children, slightly emotionally. The children didn't understand why they were suddenly being yelled at now, but Eva and the rest came to the same realization as Rosa after a delay. They were talking so grandly about the filthy topic of the inheritance in front of the children.
units.japanese: 楼座が少しだけ感情的に子どもたちに怒鳴りつける。子どもたちは、どうしてここで突然自分たちにお鉢が回ってくるのか理解できなかったが、遅れて絵羽たちは理解した。自分たちは、子どもたちの前で遺産相続の泥臭い話を、これほど盛大にしているのだ。

description: Both omit that the family and servants actively spread Kinzo’s witch image while affirming it, reducing the legend’s construction to acting as though they believed or publicly accepting it.
sourceReading: 家人や使用人たちが肯定し吹聴していった says the household and servants affirmed and circulated Kinzo’s imagined witch figure to please him, through which it became an island fairy tale or ghost story.

units.text: "Beatrice" referred to that character in the fairy tale about the Rokkenjima witch. To keep Kinzo in a good mood, the family and servants acted as though they believed in the witch of his delusions. That's how Rokkenjima's fairy tale...or maybe ghost story...had come into being...
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、六軒島の魔女というおとぎ話の中の存在を指し示す名前だ。金蔵がずっと妄想してきた魔女像は、家人や使用人たちが金蔵のご機嫌取りをするために、肯定し吹聴していったため、六軒島のおとぎ話、あるいは怪談として確立していった…。

units.text: Beatrice was a name which referred to the being in that fairy tale about the Rokkenjima witch. Because the family and the servants publicly accepted the image of the witch of Kinzo's delusions to keep him in a good mood, it became established as Rokkenjima's fairy tale, or maybe ghost story...
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェは、六軒島の魔女というおとぎ話の中の存在を指し示す名前だ。金蔵がずっと妄想してきた魔女像は、家人や使用人たちが金蔵のご機嫌取りをするために、肯定し吹聴していったため、六軒島のおとぎ話、あるいは怪談として確立していった…。

description: MG’s ‘was finally starting taking shape’ combines incompatible aspect constructions.
sourceReading: Battler finally arrives at a provisional understanding of the island witch’s identity or nature.

units.text: The true nature of the Rokkenjima witch was finally starting taking shape in Battler's mind. ...However, their current situation overrode this understanding, and in fact, it completely overturned its very premise...
units.japanese: 戦人は、六軒島の魔女の正体について、ようやく一定の理解を得るのだった。………だが、現在の状況は、その理解のさらに上に立ち、しかもその前提を全てひっくり返すものだ…。

description: MG’s ‘If not’ makes the desired sound of blood conditional on the preceding alternatives being false, where ならば advances the thought: if a sound must fill his ears, he wants it to be his blood.
sourceReading: Kinzo considers rain, a waterfall and radio static, then wishes that the ever-present sound instead be his own circulating blood proving he remains alive.

units.text: If not, I want it to be the sound of blood flowing through my body. ...I want it to be the sound of the blood circulating throughout me, telling me that I am still alive...
units.japanese: ならば血潮の音であってほしい。……まだこの体に血が巡り、私が生き永らえていることを教えてくれる音であってほしい…。

description: UP’s ‘the ears’ removes the opening monologue’s first-person possessor and produces nonidiomatic English; the following line explicitly identifies the body and life as Kinzo’s own.
sourceReading: Kinzo’s inward monologue asks what sound always fills his ears and wishes it were the blood in his body assuring him that he remains alive.

units.text:
......What was the sound that always filled the ears?
The sound of the rain, the sound of a waterfall, or was it radio static?
units.japanese:
……いつも耳を満たすのは何の音か。
雨の音か、滝の音か、それとも無線の砂嵐なのか。

description: MG changes Kinzo’s ‘I will not say that’ into ‘I mustn’t be bothered by such trivialities,’ replacing a refusal to voice his frustration with a judgment about its importance and his emotional response.
sourceReading: Kinzo admits that not knowing whether luck or his own efforts spared him is frustrating, then says he will refrain from saying more about it.

units.text: "......Morning has come, which means... ......hmmm. ...It would appear I've avoided becoming one of the first sacrifices. ...Was I merely lucky when the roulette was spun, ...or is this the fruit of my efforts? How irritating that I cannot tell the difference, but I mustn't be bothered by such trivialities."
units.japanese: 「………朝を迎えた、ということは…。……………ふむ。……どうやら、最初の生贄は逃れたということらしい。……ルーレットの目が幸運だったのか、…我が努力の賜物なのか、区別の付かぬところが何とももどかしいが、それは言うまい」
candidates: mustn't be bothered by such trivialities

description: MG says this year’s conference might have ‘done the same’ as last year’s pre-dawn session, dropping the escalation to continuing until early morning.
sourceReading: Last year’s meeting continued into the hours before dawn; Shannon considers that this year’s might finally have continued all the way into early morning and therefore knocks.

units.text: ...Last year, the family conference had continued into the early hours of the morning. It wouldn't have been odd if this year's conference had done the same. Considering the possibility that they were still having a discussion inside, she knocked. But there was no response, so she opened the door and said good morning.
units.japanese: …昨年は、親族会議は未明にまで及んだ。今年の親族会議は、とうとう早朝にまで及んでも不思議はない。まだ中で会議が続いている可能性を考え、ノックしたのだった。だが反応はなかったので、おはようございますと口にしながら扉を開ける。

description: MG leaves Genji’s whispered line without a closing quotation mark before narration resumes.
sourceReading: Genji begins to tell Rosa what was found at the chapel; the narration then withholds the whispered content.

units.text: "Yes... ......Actually, at the chapel......

description: MG omits Rosa’s repeated ‘I can’t do something like that’ after identifying the chapel as precious to her father, reducing the fearful insistence behind her refusal to authorize a broken window.
sourceReading: Rosa says she cannot possibly grant that permission, identifies the chapel as precious to her father, and emphatically repeats that she cannot do such a thing.

units.text: "...There's no way I can give you approval to do something like that. This is Father's precious chapel. ........."
units.japanese: 「…そんな許可、私に出せるわけがないわ。お父様の大切な礼拝堂なのよ、そんなことできないわよ。…………………」

description: UP says Rosa ‘climbed up to the altar,’ introducing an ascent absent from 祭壇に歩み寄りながら, which only says she approached or walked toward it.
sourceReading: Rosa continues calling to her siblings as she walks toward the altar, receives no reaction, and internally accepts that the figures are the missing adults themselves.

units.text:
As she climbed up to the altar, she called out again, but still, the others gave no reaction. ......Yes, ...by now, Rosa had accepted it. ......They were not dolls—
she had accepted that they were those very people......!
units.japanese:
祭壇に歩み寄りながら、なおも声を掛けるが、それでも彼らが反応を返すことはなかった。……あぁ、…もう楼座は自分で認めている。……彼らが人形ではなく、
彼らそのものであることを認めている……！

description: MG changes Rosa’s stomach into the group’s chests when she imagines the sweets swelling unpleasantly inside her after seeing the opened abdomens.
sourceReading: Rosa feels as though her own stomach is swelling nauseatingly from within and imagines candy about to overflow from it, which triggers another bout of vomiting.

units.text: Their own chests felt like they were expanding unpleasantly from the inside!! Rumbling, churning, ...and it was surely because candy was about to overflow from their stomachs!!
units.japanese: 自分のお腹が気持ち悪く内側から膨れていくような気がする！！　ごろごろころころ…、きっとそれはお腹の中にお菓子が溢れ出そうとしていてッ！！

description: MG’s ‘a bit too late for medical care’ markedly weakens とっくの昔に手遅れ, Rosa’s recognition that treatment has been hopelessly too late for a long time.
sourceReading: Rosa reflexively asks for Nanjo, then recognizes that any treatment has long since become far too late for the six victims.

units.text: Why even bring Doctor Nanjo here? It's a bit too late for medical care...!
units.japanese:
南條に来てもらってなんだというのか。
手当てなどとっくの昔に手遅れだというのに……！
candidates: bit too late for medical care

description: UP adds the vulgar oath ‘I’d bet my ass’ to Jessica’s assertion that Battler must have dreamed Rosa’s visit.
sourceReading: Jessica dismisses Battler’s half-awake recollection by asserting in rough casual speech that he must have been dreaming.

units.text: "Why would there be a tube of toothpaste in Maria's handbag? I'd bet my ass you dreamed the whole thing."
units.japanese: 「何で歯磨きのチューブが真里亞の手提げに入ってるんだよ。寝惚けて夢でも見たに決まってんぜ」

description: UP’s ‘well-built stomach’ misreads 恰幅の良いお腹, which describes Nanjo’s portly or generously rounded belly rather than an athletic build.
sourceReading: Sobbing Maria buries her face in Nanjo’s ample, portly belly while he remains bewildered by the morning’s commotion.

units.text: Maria buried her face in Nanjo's well‐built stomach, sobbing and crying. ...Nanjo could do nothing but be bewildered at what was going on so early in the morning.
units.japanese: 真里亞が泣きじゃくりながら南條の恰幅の良いお腹に顔を埋めながら泣く。…南條は、早朝から一体何が起こっているのかと困惑する他なかった。

description: MG drops the negation from Battler’s Alice comparison, changing ‘did Alice never regret her needless curiosity?’ into a neutral question about whether she regretted it.
sourceReading: Retrospective Battler wonders whether Alice, after chasing the watch-bearing rabbit, never regretted the unnecessary curiosity that led her onward.

units.text: Aaah, ...and then we realized. Kanon-kun had called Doctor Nanjo, but he hadn't called us. ...So we shouldn't have gone with them. I wonder if Alice regretted her excess curiosity when she chased after that rabbit holding a clock...
units.japanese: あぁ……、そして俺たちは理解する。嘉音くんは南條先生を呼びはしたが、俺たちは呼ばなかった。…だから付いていってはいけなかったんだ。時計を持ったウサギを追いかけたアリスは、余計な好奇心を後悔したことはなかったのだろうか……。

description: MG changes Maria’s announcement that the witch’s banquet is now beginning into ‘Come, let us begin,’ making her an apparent joint initiator of the banquet.
sourceReading: Maria gleefully announces that the sacrifice ritual has begun and that the witch’s banquet is now starting on Halloween as the witches gather to celebrate.

units.text: Come, let us begin the witch's banquet. Tonight is Halloween, so now the witches will gather to celebrate. Ki-hihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihihi!!"
units.japanese: 「さぁさ始まるよ、魔女の宴が。今宵はハロウィン、魔女たちが今こそ祝い集う。きーっひっひっひっひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひひ！！」

description: UP combines ‘she’ with the reflexive ‘themselves’ in ‘Is she some unknown person trying to involve themselves,’ producing a mismatched antecedent.
sourceReading: Battler asks whether Beatrice is an unknown person attempting to involve herself in the inheritance dispute, or the legendary witch Maria describes.

units.text:
Who is this person called Beatrice?
Is she some unknown person trying to involve themselves with the inheritance problem, like our parents were freaking out about at dinner last night? ......Or is the culprit the witch from the Legend of the Gold, like Maria says?!
units.japanese:
ベアトリーチェというのは何者なんだ。
昨日の晩餐で親父たちが騒いでいたように、遺産相続問題に絡もうとする未知の人物なのか。……それとも真里亞がのたまうように、黄金伝説の魔女さまが犯人だってのかよ？！
candidates: unknown person trying to involve themselves

description: Both replace Maria’s characteristic third-person self-reference in ‘take Maria with you’ with first-person ‘me.’
sourceReading: Maria addresses Beatrice, asks her to open the Golden Land’s door quickly, and asks her to take Maria along, referring to herself by name.

units.text: "...Quickly, open the door to the Golden Land. And take me with you. ...Kihihihihihihihihihihihihihi!"
units.japanese: 「……早く黄金郷への扉を開いて。そして真里亞を連れてって。…きひひひひひひひひひひひひひ！」

units.text: "......Hurry up and open the door to the Golden Land. And take me away. ...Kihihi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hihihi!"
units.japanese: 「……早く黄金郷への扉を開いて。そして真里亞を連れてって。…きひひひひひひひひひひひひひ！」

description: UP changes Jessica’s individual claim that she will know by looking Beatrice in the eye into the collective ‘we’ll know.’
sourceReading: Jessica insists that she personally can expose Beatrice by confronting her and looking into her eyes.

units.text: "So what?!! If we grab her by the collar, she'll definitely confess!! If we can look her in the eye, we'll know!! I'll see through her!! A witch?! Beatrice?!! I'll expose her for who she is!!"
units.japanese: 「だから何だってんだッ！！　本人の胸倉、捻り上げてやれば白状するに決まってるぜ！！　目を見ればわかるんだよッ！！　私が見破ってやる！！　何が魔女だベアトリーチェだッ！！　バケの皮を剥いでやるッ！！」

description: UP’s ‘an important honored guest to the Master’ uses the wrong preposition for the relationship and produces nonidiomatic English.
sourceReading: Gohda reminds Jessica that Beatrice is Kinzo’s important honored guest.

units.text: "We still don't know who the culprit is! And Beatrice‐sama is an important honored guest to the Master...!"
units.japanese: 「誰が犯人かはまだわかりませんぞ！　それにベアトリーチェさまは、お館様の大切な賓客です…！」
candidates: important honored guest to the Master

description: MG uses the nonstandard phrase ‘forcing their way in here in search for her’; the fixed expression requires ‘in search of her.’
sourceReading: Kanon knows that forcing their way into the room in search of Beatrice will not make her comply; she will watch and mock their failure.

units.text: ...However, Kanon alone had met her. He understood what kind of being that witch was, ...what kind of personality she had. So, he knew that forcing their way in here in search for her...definitely wouldn't work out.
units.japanese: …しかし、嘉音だけは会っている。そしてあの魔女がどういう存在で、……どんな性分なのかを理解している。だから、自分たちが彼女の姿を求めてここへ押しかけたなら、絶対、思い通りになどさせるわけがないのだ。
candidates: forcing their way in here in search

description: MG pluralizes the single lamp bulb into ‘the lightbulbs all shattered,’ inventing multiple bulbs in the room damage.
sourceReading: Jessica swings the bedside lamp into walls and furniture; its bulb immediately bursts and scatters fragments around the room.

units.text: As soon as she read the message, Jessica went into a wild rage, crumpled the paper up, and threw it. Then, she grabbed a light stand by the bedside and violently swung it around, mercilessly hitting the walls and furniture with it. ...The lightbulbs all shattered at once, and the fragments were scattered across the room.
