units.japanese: メッセージを読んだ途端、朱志香は激しく怒り、便箋をぐしゃぐしゃに丸めて叩きつける。そして、ベッドサイドにあったインテリアスタンドを掴むと、それを乱暴に振り回して、それを壁や家具にひたすら叩き付けた。…たちまち電球が破裂しその破片を辺りにばら撒いた。

description: UP drops that Jessica is burning herself up with the flames of anger, reducing Gohda’s impression of self-consuming rage to simply burning with anger.
sourceReading: Gohda sees Jessica as having lost herself to rage and scorching herself in its flames, while Kanon recognizes the grief concealed beneath it.

units.text: Gohda grabbed the table lamp Jessica had been swinging around and took it from her. ...Because if she kept swinging it around, she might hit something and get injured. ...To Gohda's eyes, Jessica probably looked mad with rage, burning with the flames of anger.
units.japanese: 郷田は、朱志香の振り回すインテリアスタンドを取り上げる。…これ以上、振り回せば、どこかにぶつけて怪我をするかもしれないからだ。…郷田の目には、朱志香が怒りに我を忘れ、憤怒の炎で己を焦がしているに違いないと映ったのだろう。

description: MG changes Jessica’s description of an asthma attack exhausting itself into a threshold where the asthma merely ‘got serious enough.’
sourceReading: Jessica often said that after coughing through or exhausting an asthma attack, the suffering felt as though she might vomit up her entire stomach.

units.text: Jessica often said that when her asthma got serious enough, it hurt so bad that it felt like she'd vomit up her whole stomach. Her face was pale, and her gaze wavered. And yet, the coughing continued... ...Even so, ...her sadness was probably even stronger...
units.japanese:
朱志香はよく、喘息をし尽くすと胃袋丸ごとを吐き出しそうになるような苦しみになると口にしていた。顔色は蒼白で、目の焦点も定まっていなかった。
なのに咳だけはまだ繰り返している…。……それでも多分、…それよりも悲しみの方が勝っているのだ…。

description: UP’s ‘forgot to walk around with her medicine’ is a nonidiomatic rendering of forgetting to carry the medicine with her.
sourceReading: Jessica sometimes forgets to carry her medication, so Kanon normally anticipates this and secretly carries a spare inhaler from the servants’ first-aid kit.

units.text: ......Jessica sometimes forgot to walk around with her medicine. When it seemed that this was the case, Kanon would take notice and secretly carry around the inhaler from the first‐aid kit in the servant room, but he hadn't done so today. ......He scolded himself, as though wondering how, after failing to bring it with him on a day like this, he could call himself furniture.
units.japanese: ……朱志香は時折、薬を持ち歩くのを忘れる。そんな気配のある時には、気を利かせて、使用人室の救急箱にある予備をこっそり持ち歩くのだが、今日はその準備がなかった。……こんな日に持ち歩かなくて、どうして自分は家具などと言えるのかと自分を責めた。
candidates: forgot to walk around with her medicine

description: UP places a comma after the closing quotation mark in ‘He had said “Are you alright”, to her?’, producing invalid dialogue punctuation and splitting the verb from its complement.
sourceReading: Kanon condemns himself for asking Jessica whether she was alright when her pain made the inadequacy of that question obvious.

units.text:
Kanon regretted misspeaking. ......He had said "Are you alright", to her?
...Was he really unable to notice the pain in her heart? ............This was why he was, ultimately, mere furniture.
This was why he couldn't become human...
units.japanese:
嘉音は失言を悔いる。……今の彼女に、「大丈夫か」？
…何て自分は心の痛みを読めないのか。…………だから、所詮は家具。
だから人間になれない…。

description: UP’s ‘some kind of hope flew to Jessica’s eyes’ uses the wrong motion collocation for an emotion briefly appearing in someone’s gaze.
sourceReading: A trace of hope briefly appears in Jessica’s eyes when Kanon promises not to abandon her, then vanishes as fleetingly as first snow on a river.

units.text: For just an instant, it looked like some kind of hope flew to Jessica's eyes. ...But it was very faint, ...and disappeared like the first snow does on the surface of a river.
units.japanese: 朱志香は一瞬だけ、確かに瞳に何かの希望を浮かべた。…でもそれはとても儚く、初雪が川面に消えるように、すっ…と消える。
candidates: kind of hope flew to Jessica's eyes

description: MG’s ‘Let me teach you them’ uses an invalid ordering for two pronoun objects; it requires ‘teach them to you.’
sourceReading: Beatrice offers to teach Kanon the three ways to hurt a woman before enumerating them.

units.text: "There are three ways to hurt a woman. ...Let me teach you them. One is to hurt them with a blade. Another is to hurt them in their heart.
units.japanese: 「女の傷付け方は３つある。…特別に妾が教えてやろう。１つは刃物で傷つける。１つは心で傷つける」
candidates: three ways to hurt a woman

description: MG’s ‘the pleasure ... never tires me’ says the pleasure does not make Beatrice tired rather than that she never tires of that pleasure.
sourceReading: Beatrice says she never grows bored of the pleasure of laughing at the tragic fate of a young couple.

units.text: *cackle*cackle*! Still, though you may not be worth my time on your own, if the two of you are gathered, that's all I need. ...The pleasure that comes from laughing at the fates of young couples never tires me."
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっく！　しかしそなたもひとりではそれに値しなくても、二人揃えば充分に足りる。……若々しき男女の悲運を笑う喜びは何度繰り返しても飽きぬのでな」

description: MG’s passive ‘thirteen people will be sacrificed on my whims’ weakens Beatrice’s explicit agency in selecting and making thirteen people sacrifices according to her whims.
sourceReading: Beatrice declares that, following the ritual, she capriciously chooses thirteen people as sacrifices and remains free to kill more for amusement.

units.text: "Following the rules of the ceremony, 13 people will be sacrificed on my whims. However, there's no rule that says I can't kill more."
units.japanese: 「儀式に従い、妾は気まぐれに１３人を生贄とする。だが、それ以上を殺してはならないとの決まりはない」
candidates: people will be sacrificed on my whims

description: MG’s ‘everything fits to the plot’ uses a nonstandard preposition and makes the scripted progression sound like a compatibility test; 筋書き通り means everything is going according to plan or script.
sourceReading: Beatrice laughs that everything has proceeded according to her script and compares Kanon’s helpless position to a carp awaiting the knife.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle* Ahahahaha!! Now everything fits to the plot. Now, you're carp on the chopping board.
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくははははは！！　これで全ては筋書き通りよ。今やそなたは俎上の鯉よの」

description: UP changes ‘it is inevitable that the witch will appear’ into ‘it is essential,’ turning a claimed necessary consequence into a requirement or desirable necessity.
sourceReading: Beatrice theatrically claims that when princess and knight assemble, the witch’s appearance follows inevitably.

units.text: "It's essential that the witch appears when the princess and the knight are together. ......Come now, won't you show me how much power Kinzo's furniture holds?"
units.japanese: 「姫に騎士が揃わば、魔女が現れるのは必然よ。……どれ、金蔵の家具がどの程度の力を持つか、見せてもらおうではないか」

description: UP’s ‘one handmade’ leaves handmade functioning as an unsupported nominal adjective. The Japanese contrasts the mass-produced attendant with a handmade creation; English requires a noun such as piece, creation, or one.
sourceReading: Beatrice concedes that the disposable attendant could not defeat a handmade creation and that Kanon is not entirely beneath contempt.

units.text: "......Hmph. So it couldn't win against one handmade. ...It seems that you aren't so pathetic."
units.japanese: 「……ふ。ハンドメイドには勝てぬか。…そこまで見下げたものではないらしい」

description: MG’s ‘what we should tell Rosa-sama?’ uses declarative word order in a direct question. It requires ‘what should we tell Rosa-sama?’ or the original WH construction ‘is there anything I should tell Rosa-sama?’
sourceReading: Shannon hesitantly asks what she should report to Rosa.

units.text: "...Umm, ...what we should tell Rosa-sama?"
units.japanese: 「…その……。…楼座さまには何とお伝えいたしましょうか」

description: MG’s ‘Even though Father even never approached it himself’ combines even though with an extra even before never, producing an ungrammatical concessive clause.
sourceReading: Although Kinzo himself never approached the chapel, he had the servants clean it several times a year and keep it ready for use.

units.text: "Even though Father even never approached it himself, for some reason, he made the servants give it a major cleaning several times a year. It felt like he kept it clean all the time so that it could be used at any moment."
units.japanese: 「お父様自身、まったく近付かなかったのに、なぜか年に何度か使用人たちに大掃除をさせていたわ。……常に清潔にしていて、まるで、いつ使用する時が来てもいいように、という感じだった」
candidates: though Father even never approached it himself

description: MG misspells occurring as ‘occuring’ in Nanjo’s contrast between Kinzo’s focus on life and events after death.
sourceReading: Nanjo says Kinzo concentrated on the present life rather than what came after death.

units.text: "I wouldn't believe that of Kinzo-san. ...He was a man much more focused on the living now than matters occuring after death. ......Though, this does seem to be root cause of the current inheritance problem."
units.japanese: 「金蔵さんに限ってそんなはずは。…死後のことより、生きている今に一生懸命な方でした。………しかし、そのせいで遺産問題をこじれさせるタネとしてしまったようですがな」

description: MG’s ‘this does seem to be root cause’ omits the article required before the singular count noun: ‘the root cause’ or ‘a root cause.’
sourceReading: Nanjo adds that Kinzo’s attitude seems to have planted the seed that complicated the inheritance dispute.

units.text: "I wouldn't believe that of Kinzo-san. ...He was a man much more focused on the living now than matters occuring after death. ......Though, this does seem to be root cause of the current inheritance problem."
units.japanese: 「金蔵さんに限ってそんなはずは。…死後のことより、生きている今に一生懸命な方でした。………しかし、そのせいで遺産問題をこじれさせるタネとしてしまったようですがな」

description: UP changes ‘there is no way to reason it out’ into ‘guessing is useless.’ 推理 refers to reasoning or deduction, and しようがない says it cannot be done; the edit recasts an information-limit claim as a judgment about the value of guessing.
sourceReading: Battler argues that insufficient information makes deduction impossible because any explanation or trick could be proposed.

units.text: "It's just like the locked rooms last time. ...Not enough information!! It's impossible to reason like this! Any excuse could be made, any trick could work!! Guessing is useless!"
units.japanese: 「前回の密室と同じだ。…情報不足ッ！！　こんなのじゃ推理不能だ！　何の言い訳でもできるぜ、どんな手品だって通じる！！　推理なんてしようがねぇ！」

description: MG’s ‘in the any of closed room murders’ combines incompatible constructions and lacks the possessive or attributive structure needed for ‘in any of the closed-room murders.’
sourceReading: Beatrice boasts that humanity has never produced a single truly complete closed room in a century of locked-room murders.

units.text: "In other words, there hasn't been a completed closed room in the any of closed room murders that humans have built over the last century!!"
units.japanese: 「つまり、人間どもが積み重ねた百年の密室殺人など、ただの一度も完成されたことはないのだッ！！」

description: MG renders 根拠否定, rejection of the grounds or basis for a claim, as ‘rejecting the source.’ This narrows the epistemic objection from denying supporting grounds generally to disputing a source’s authority or provenance.
sourceReading: Beatrice mocks the human tactic of first demanding information and then denying its grounds, and says red truth will remove that escape route.

units.text: "Of course not. I'll give you the thing people like you always demand. The reason you always stop thinking and then moan about it...is "a lack of information"! And if you are then given information, you start doubting whether the information is true or not by "rejecting the source"!"
units.japanese:
「まさかまさか。そなたらが求めて止まなかったものを与えようというのだ。貴様ら無能どもがいつも嘆いてみせる思考停止の理由、“情報不足”！　そして、それに対し情報を与えると今度はその情報の真偽を疑う“根拠否定”！」
「妾がどのような魔法の一手を仕掛けようとも、そなたには常に“情報不足”や“根拠否定”を繰り返すことで延々と逃げ続けることができる」

units.text: "No matter what magical move I use, you can always keep running away by chanting "lack of information" and by "rejecting the source"."
units.japanese:
「まさかまさか。そなたらが求めて止まなかったものを与えようというのだ。貴様ら無能どもがいつも嘆いてみせる思考停止の理由、“情報不足”！　そして、それに対し情報を与えると今度はその情報の真偽を疑う“根拠否定”！」
「妾がどのような魔法の一手を仕掛けようとも、そなたには常に“情報不足”や“根拠否定”を繰り返すことで延々と逃げ続けることができる」

description: UP’s ‘That disposition is good’ uses disposition for 心意気, producing an unnatural endorsement of temperament where Beatrice praises Battler’s resolve or spirit.
sourceReading: Beatrice approves of Battler’s determination to settle their contest decisively before proposing a new rule.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*! That disposition is good! .........So I had a thought. I think I'll add a new rule to this game between you and me."
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっく！　その心意気や良し！　………そこで妾は考えた。妾とそなたのゲームに新しいルールを追加しようと思う」

description: MG’s ‘I’d be happy to I give you’ leaves an extra finite pronoun-verb sequence after the infinitive marker, making the sentence ungrammatical.
sourceReading: Beatrice says she will give Battler the information and grounds he wants so the game does not become unbearably dull.

units.text: "...Even though I would still win in the end that way, it would be extremely boring. ...Because of that, I'd be happy to I give you the "information" and "sources" you so desire."
units.japanese: 「…これでは最終的に妾が勝つことが変わらぬとしても、あまりに退屈を極める。……その為、妾はそなたが望む“情報”と“根拠”を与えてやろうと思う」
candidates: I'd be happy to I give

description: UP changes Battler’s concessive premise ‘given that you are a witch’ into the counterfactual-sounding ‘if you were a witch.’ He is temporarily granting Beatrice’s premise to explain why requiring displayed proof would spoil the game, not withdrawing the concession here.
sourceReading: Battler grants for purposes of the rule explanation that, since she is a witch who can do anything by magic, demanding demonstrations from her would create an unfair game.

units.text: "W‐......well, that is true. ...If you were a witch, there'd be no need for you to show proof. ......Because you could do anything with magic... That's nasty... What an unfair game...!"
units.japanese: 「た、……確かにもっともだ。…お前が魔女である以上、証拠を示す必要がない。……何でも魔法で出来ちまうんだからな、ひでぇ話だぜ…。何て不利なゲームだ…！」

description: MG adds ‘the hands of your new master’ to Beatrice’s promise of the pleasure of surrendering oneself. The source contains submission or entrusting oneself but does not explicitly assign Battler a new master or mention hands or fate.
sourceReading: Beatrice taunts that surrender is only a moment’s shame and afterward only the pleasure of giving or yielding oneself remains.

units.text: "...What happened? You fell silent all of a sudden. Fear not. Surrender is but a momentary shame. After that, all that remains is the joy of entrusting your fate entirely to the hands of your new master...
units.japanese: 「……どうしたぁ？　急に黙り込んだな。安心しろ。屈服は一時の恥よ。後に待つは身を委ねる悦びだけよ…」

description: MG replaces 寝惚けるな, ‘don’t talk in your sleep’ or ‘wake up,’ with ‘Enough babbling,’ dropping Battler’s retort that Beatrice is dreaming or inattentive rather than merely talking too much.
sourceReading: After Beatrice says she cannot hear his resignation, Battler tells her not to dream or sleep-talk: she is only refusing to listen.

units.text: "......Enough babbling. You're just refusing to listen. ...So I'll say it once more. ...I won't resign. ...Continue. Resume the game."
units.japanese: 「…………寝惚けるな。お前が聞こうとしていないだけだぜ。…ならもう一度言う。……投了はない。……続行だ。ゲームを再開するぞ」

description: UP changes ‘the thinking method humans produced over a hundred years’ into a technique ‘humans gave birth to a century ago.’ The source describes a century of accumulated development, while UP places the method’s origin at one point a century in the past.
sourceReading: Beatrice invites Battler to try the mode of reasoning humanity developed over the course of a century.

units.text: "Here it is. ......The thinking technique that humans gave birth to a century ago. Give it a try, *cackle*cackle*!!"
units.japanese: 「来たな。……人間どもの生み出した百年の思考術か。試してみるが良いぞ、くっくっくっく！！」
candidates: humans gave birth to a century ago

description: MG’s ‘known there was key inside’ omits the article required before singular count noun key.
sourceReading: Maria might have learned by touch that a key was inside the unopened envelope, but could not verify that it was the chapel key.

units.text: "Yesterday, Maria received an envelope from you. She didn't open it, but she might've felt it and known there was key inside. ...But it's not like she'd have been able to confirm absolutely that it was the key to the chapel."
units.japanese: 「真里亞は昨日、お前から封筒をもらってる。真里亞は開封しなかったが、手触りで鍵が入っていたことを知ったかもしれない。……だが、間違いなく礼拝堂の鍵だと確認できたわけじゃない」

description: UP's ‘gaze that wasn't quite pleasant’ turns Rosa's look into an unpleasant one. The source says it differed somewhat from a fond or heartwarming gaze, leaving her feeling withheld rather than defining it as negative.
sourceReading: Rosa watches Maria with a gaze that is not quite one of fond warmth.

units.text: Perhaps Rosa had some opinions about this attitude, which was clearly different from normal people. ......She stared at Maria's back with a gaze that wasn't quite pleasant.
units.japanese: そんな、明らかに普通の人と違うセンスに、楼座は何か思うところがあるのだろうか。……微笑ましいのとは少し違う眼差しで、彼女はじっとその背中を見ているのだった。

description: UP's ‘had grown a complex’ uses an unidiomatic verb with complex; Rosa had developed or acquired an inferiority complex.
sourceReading: Repeated comparison with her older siblings caused Rosa to develop a complex about her supposed incompetence.

units.text:
Rosa had been the youngest sibling, with a large difference in age between her and the others.
So she was always treated as a child. Every time she learned something new, it was something obvious to her brothers and sister, and she had grown a complex, thinking that she must be incompetent. So she had formed a passive attitude, asking her brothers and sister for advice every time something happened...
units.japanese:
楼座は、他の兄弟から大きく歳の差のある末っ子だった。
だからいつも子ども扱いだった。自分が新しく覚えたことは、いつも兄や姉たちにとって当り前のことで、自分が無能に違いないとコンプレックスを抱いてきた。そのため、何かある度に兄や姉たちに指示を乞う受身な体質になってしまっていた…。

description: MG misspells ‘unmanageable’ as ‘unmanagable.’
sourceReading: Rosa assumes Kinzo has begun shouting incoherently again and the situation has become unmanageable.

units.text: Genji and Shannon, whom she had sent to see Kinzo, hadn't returned yet. ...She had a good guess at what was going on. He was probably yelling something nonsensical again and becoming unmanagable. ...His precious chapel had been defiled with blood. That was easy to imagine.
units.japanese:
金蔵のところへ行かせた源次と紗音がまだ戻らないのだ。…大方想像はつく。また何か支離滅裂なことを怒鳴りだし、収拾が付かなくなっているのだろう。…大事な礼拝堂が血で汚されたのだ。
それは想像に容易だった。

description: MG omits the indefinite article in ‘just single sheet of gold leaf.’
sourceReading: An uninformed observer would see only a single butterfly-shaped sheet of gold leaf stuck to Rosa's back.

units.text: Rosa didn't notice it. If someone not in-the-know saw it, they'd probably assume it was just single sheet of gold leaf in the shape of a butterfly that had been stuck there. Without noticing a thing, Rosa continued heading towards Kinzo's study...
units.japanese: 楼座は気付かない。そして知らぬ者が見たとしても、蝶の形をした金箔が一枚、張り付いてるくらいにしか見えないだろう。楼座は気付かず、そのまま金蔵の書斎へ向かっていく……。

description: UP uses plural agreement in ‘the number of keys that could open this door are limited.’ The head noun number requires ‘is limited.’
sourceReading: The number of keys capable of opening the door is limited, and their holders are known.

units.text: ......It's just as she says. ...If I started arguing that someone holding a master key was the culprit, this locked room could be easily broken. ......However, since the number of keys that could open this door are limited, and furthermore it's clearly known who holds them, saying that would mean that I was suspecting someone I knew well...
units.japanese: ……言われる通りだ。…マスターキーを持つ誰かが犯人だという論法で展開すれば、この密室は簡単に破れる。……しかし、この扉を開けられる鍵の本数が限定されていて、しかもそれを持つ人間がはっきりしている以上、それを口にすることは即ち、俺のよく知る誰かを疑うということだ…。
candidates: number of keys that could open this door are limited

description: MG prints ‘a first aid kid’ where the intended item is a first aid kit.
sourceReading: Battler recalls ordinary luggage contents: changes of clothes, regularly carried medicine, and Kyrie's cosmetics.

units.text: "Same here. At the most, there were some changes of clothes, a first aid kid, Kyrie-san's makeup. Stuff like that, I think. Aunt Rosa's luggage also looked pretty light."
units.japanese: 「うちも同じだぜ。せいぜい着替えと常備薬、霧江さんの化粧道具。そんなもんだったと思う。楼座叔母さんの荷物も軽そうに見えたぜ」

description: MG's ‘does make some sense’ weakens 一番筋が通る, which identifies the preceding theft theory as the explanation that makes the most sense among the alternatives currently proposed.
sourceReading: Battler concedes that having the family solve the epitaph and then stealing the gold is the explanation that presently makes the most sense, before listing contradictions.

units.text: "......Yeah, that does make some sense. ...But there are a couple parts that don't fit. To start, our parents, who should've been the most likely to solve the epitaph, were killed first. That seems to create a contradiction right off the bat to me."
units.japanese: 「…………確かにそれが一番筋が通る。…しかし腑に落ちない点もいくつかあるぜ。まず、碑文を一番解けそうな人物である親たちが真っ先に殺されてる。これはいきなり矛盾があるように思う」

description: Both MG's ‘I don't care’ and UP's ‘Don't caaare’ replace Maria's 知ぃらない, ‘I don't know.’ Her stated lack of knowledge about solving the epitaph becomes indifference to whether she can solve it.
sourceReading: Asked whether she can solve the epitaph, Maria says she does not know; she expects admission to the Golden Land and will not interfere with Beatrice.

units.text: "...I don't care. After all, she'll take me to the Golden Land. So I won't get in Beatrice's way. Kihihihihihihihihihihi, ouch."
units.japanese: 「…知ぃらない。だって、真里亞は黄金郷へ連れてってもらうんだもん。ベアトリーチェの邪魔なんかしないよ。きひひひひひひひひひひ、あ痛」

units.text: "...Don't caaare. She's going to take me to the Golden Land, so. Won't get in Beatrice's way. Kihihi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hi{0hihihi, ouch."
units.japanese: 「…知ぃらない。だって、真里亞は黄金郷へ連れてってもらうんだもん。ベアトリーチェの邪魔なんかしないよ。きひひひひひひひひひひ、あ痛」

description: MG's ‘considerably shaken’ intensifies 多少取り乱していました, which says Kinzo was somewhat discomposed by the sudden events.
sourceReading: Rosa reports that Kinzo was safe but somewhat discomposed by the sudden events and intended to remain in his room.

units.text: "Father was fine, but he was considerably shaken by these sudden events. ...Fortunately, he said he won't leave his room, so he should be safe. For now, we should all try to stay together as much as possible."
units.japanese: 「お父様はご無事でしたが、突然の出来事に多少、取り乱していました。…幸いにも、部屋からは出ないと言っていますので、安全でしょう。あと、私たちは極力、同じ場所に集まるべきです」

description: UP uses the nonstandard superlative ‘the most safe’ instead of ‘the safest.’
sourceReading: Rosa says that if the entire group remains together and stable, preserving that arrangement is safest.

units.text: "............No. Let's all go together. ...It's a "Wolves and Sheep Puzzle". If we're all gathered together here in equilibrium, that situation is the most safe."
units.japanese: 「…………いいえ。みんなで一緒に行きましょう。…“狼と羊のパズル”なのよ。私たちがここに揃い安定しているなら、この状態が一番安全」

description: MG's ‘unopening doors’ uses a nonstandard adjective for doors that cannot or will not open. It repairs original WH's ‘unopened’ category error but leaves an unnatural English construction.
sourceReading: Maria says the first magic circle of the moon has the power to open doors that do not or cannot open.

units.text: "...It's the first magic circle of the moon. ...It has the power to open unopening doors."
units.japanese: 「……月の１の魔法陣だね。…開かぬ扉を開く力があるよ」
candidates: first magic circle of the moon

description: MG misspells ‘corpses’ as ‘coprses.’
sourceReading: Battler recalls that six corpses lay beyond the chapel door marked with a magic circle.

units.text: Genji nodded, and Gohda quickly unlocked the door with the master key. ...In the back of my mind, horrible images floated up and disappeared, one after another. ...A magic circle had been drawn on the door to the chapel. Behind that lay six coprses.
units.japanese:
源次が頷くと、郷田はすぐにマスターキーで鍵を開ける。…俺の脳裏に、嫌な想像が次々に浮かんでは消える。
……礼拝堂の扉に魔法陣が書かれていた。
そしてその向こうには６人の死体があった。

description: MG weakens 背中を刺されてる, ‘was stabbed in the back,’ to ‘was struck in the back.’ The visible wound and embedded blade make the attack specifically a stabbing, not an unspecified blow.
sourceReading: Rosa observes that Jessica was stabbed in the back and uses her exposed back to argue that she admitted someone she trusted.

units.text: "Jessica-chan was struck in the back. ......Come on, they say it all the time, right? That in crimes where the victim is struck in the back, there's a high likelihood that the culprit was someone whose face was known to the victim. She definitely wouldn't invite a person she didn't trust into her room...and defenselessly expose her back."
units.japanese: 「朱志香ちゃんは背中を刺されてるの。………ほら、よく一般的に言うでしょう？　背中を刺された事件は顔見知りが犯人の可能性が高いって。部屋に気を許せないような人を招き入れて、背中を無防備に晒したりなんか、絶対にしない」

description: MG omits the closing quotation mark after Rosa's categorical italicized accusation that Kanon killed Jessica.
sourceReading: Rosa concludes her speech by declaring that Kanon killed Jessica; the next line begins another speaker's response.

units.text: "But take care. Most likely...no, there's no doubt about it. ...... Kanon-kun killed Jessica-chan.
units.japanese: 「でも、用心して。多分恐らく、いや確実ね。………嘉音くんが、朱志香ちゃんを殺した」

description: MG misspells ‘consensus’ as ‘concensus.’
sourceReading: The atmosphere of the group does not condemn Nanjo's proposal to keep Kanon under suspicion as a precaution.

units.text: The general concensus certainly didn't seem to find fault with Nanjo for what he said. True, no one actually thought Kanon was the culprit. ...But unless they suspected him, they'd have to suspect one of the servants here. ...We didn't want to do that. We didn't want to suspect. We didn't want to be suspected.
units.japanese:
場の雰囲気は、決して南條を責めなかった。
嘉音が犯人だなんて、本当のところ、誰も思っていない。…しかし、彼を疑わなければ、今この場にいる使用人の誰かを疑わなければならなくなる。……それが嫌だった。
疑うのが、嫌だった。
疑われるのが、嫌だった。

description: UP's ‘I've just met Gohda-san yesterday’ incorrectly combines present perfect with the finished past-time adverb yesterday.
sourceReading: Battler met Gohda only yesterday and therefore does not yet know him well, but has understood one thing about him.

units.text: "And I've just met Gohda‐san yesterday. ......Honestly, I still don't really understand him. ......But there is one thing I understand."
units.japanese: 「そして郷田さんとは、俺は昨日会ったばかりだ。……正直、この人のことはまだよく理解していない。……だがわかったことがある」

description: UP's ‘Humans were originally supposed to be creatures that trust each other’ shifts Battler's present generalization about human nature into a past-oriented state. 本来 here means fundamentally or by nature, not formerly.
sourceReading: Battler says humans should by nature trust one another, but learn suspicion to survive in a harsh world.

units.text: "Humans were originally supposed to be creatures that trust each other. ...But in order to live in a tough world, we learn to be wary. ...So we'll doubt anything. We are sad creatures. ...I won't deny that's our nature."
units.japanese: 「人間ってのは本来、信じ合う生き物のはずだ。…なのに世知辛い世の中を生きるために、疑り深さを覚えちまう。…だから何でも疑っちまう。俺たちは悲しい生き物だな。…そのサガを、俺は否定しねぇ」
candidates: Humans were originally supposed to be creatures that trust each other

description: UP changes Battler's current stance ‘unless there is clear proof, I don't want to cast suspicion’ into ‘as long as that didn't happen, I didn't want to cast any suspicions.’ The present evidentiary rule becomes a retrospective preference.
sourceReading: Battler recognizes his contradiction: he must seek a human explanation, but presently refuses to suspect a person unless clear evidence compels him.

units.text: I don't want to suspect someone. ......Of course, if there was some clear proof, I would have to believe that person was the culprit, ...but as long as that didn't happen, I didn't want to cast any suspicions.
units.japanese: 俺は誰かを疑いたくない。……もちろん、明白な証拠があるならば犯人であることを信じざるを得ないが、…それがない限り、疑いをかけたくない。
candidates: long as that didn't happen, I didn't want to cast any suspicions

description: MG uses the nonstandard plural idiom ‘be on our guards.’ Standard English is ‘be on our guard.’
sourceReading: George says caution is sensible but excessive suspicion is not.

units.text: "Aunt Rosa, ...I heard about the puzzle from Battler-kun. ...I don't think it's wrong to be on our guards, but I also think there's such a thing as being too suspicious."
units.japanese: 「楼座叔母さん。…パズルの話は戦人くんに聞いたよ。…用心深いのは悪いことじゃないと思うけど、さすがに疑り深すぎるのもどうかと思うよ」

description: UP weakens George's ‘there's something I want to be angry about’ to ‘there's something I don't like,’ reducing his explicitly angry objection to Rosa placing Shannon in danger.
sourceReading: George says he has something to be angry about: under Rosa's own theory, sending Shannon to the kitchen placed her in danger.

units.text: ".........Th‐there's something I don't like! In that case, Shannon, who you sent to the kitchen, is in a dangerous situation, isn't she?!! We should also go to the kitchen right now! No matter who might or might not be a wolf! If we can form a balance by gathering together, I think we should maintain that!!"
units.japanese: 「………ぼ、僕は怒りたいことがある！　じゃあ、厨房へ行かされてる紗音は危険な状態じゃないか！！　今すぐ僕たちも厨房へ行くべきだ！　誰が狼だろうと狼でなかろうと！　僕たち全員が揃っていれば均衡するなら、それを保ち続けるべきだと思う！！」

description: UP's ‘let by this once-in-a-lifetime chance’ is not an English expression for allowing an opportunity to pass.
sourceReading: Rosa asks whether, if she were the culprit, she would let the rare opportunity created by the servants' departure pass unused.

units.text: "Think about it. What if I were the culprit? Do you think I would let by this once‐in‐a‐lifetime chance I got when the servants left?"
units.japanese: 「考えてもみて。私が犯人だったらどう？　使用人たちが出て行ったこの千載一遇の機会を逃すと思う？」

description: UP's ‘with a well-practiced manner’ uses manner as though it named a hand movement; the source describes Genji concealing the knife with practiced handling.
sourceReading: Genji deftly conceals the knife inside his sleeve with a practiced movement of the hands.

units.text:
Genji hid it in his sleeve with a well‐practiced manner.
Then he too approached the back door, and signaled to Gohda with a silent nod.
units.japanese:
源次はそれを、慣れた手つきで袖の内側に隠し持つ。
そして自らも勝手口に近付き、郷田に無言で頷いて合図を送った。

description: MG changes Genji's disbelief that Rosa would ‘do such a thing’ into disbelief that she would ‘say something like that,’ redirecting his hesitation from the accused violence to Kanon's reported threat.
sourceReading: Genji cannot readily believe that Rosa would commit the acts Kanon attributes to her.

units.text: "...I find it hard to believe. ...To think that Rosa-sama would say something like that..."
units.japanese: 「……にわかには信じられん。……楼座さまがそのようなことを……」

description: MG renders Kanon's ほら (‘look’) as ‘Hey’ while he directs the others to inspect his exposed wound.
sourceReading: Kanon says the wound is fine and prompts the others to look at it before asking whether they agree.

units.text: "I said it's fine. ...Hey. See...? This is...nothing, right...?"
units.japanese: 「大丈夫ですって。……ほら。ねぇ…？　大した傷じゃ、ないでしょう…？」

description: MG adds necessity twice and changes Shannon's ‘I want to check’ into ‘there's something I need to ask you,’ framing her prepared identity test as a verbal question.
sourceReading: Shannon says she went to the boiler room because she was looking for something, then says she wants to verify whether the person before her is really Kanon.

units.text: "That's right. I went to the boiler room. There was something I had to find. ...More importantly, there's something I need to ask you. Are you...really Kanon-kun?"
units.japanese: 「うん。ボイラー室に行ってきたの。捜し物があって。………それより、確かめたいの。あなたは本当に、…嘉音くん？」
candidates: there's something I need to ask

description: MG changes Genji's inability to explain ‘what we saw’ into inability to explain ‘what happened in front of us,’ replacing his carefully limited observation claim with an event claim.
sourceReading: Genji says even the witnesses themselves cannot properly explain what they saw.

units.text: "......Even we cannot adequately explain what happened in front of us."
units.japanese: 「………………私たちにも、見たものをうまく説明できません」

description: UP renders Gohda's ‘at first I thought that was so’ as ‘at first, I thought I knew,’ changing his initial identification of the visitor into a broader claim of knowledge.
sourceReading: Gohda says that at first he thought the person was Kanon and still believes that, despite being unable to reconcile it with what followed.

units.text: "...I don't know! Certainly, ...in the beginning, I thought I knew. No, I still think it was! But.........what in the world was that!! ...I don't know... ...I don't know!!"
units.japanese: 「…わからないんですッ！　確かに、…最初はそうだと思っていました。いや、今でもそうだと思ってるんです！でも、………あれは一体ッ！！　…わからない…、…わからない！！」

description: MG turns Battler's interest in inspecting the bodies into something he had already been wanting to do, inventing a stronger prior intention.
sourceReading: Battler says Rosa's proposal to inspect the bodies is also of interest to him.

units.text: That was something I'd been wanting to do too. The witnesses had been unable to figure anything out, but they'd been shaken. ...If those of us who hadn't been at the scene calmly looked at the corpses, we might find something.
units.japanese: それは俺も関心のあることだった。混乱した彼らには何が何だかわからなくても、…その現場に居合わせなかった俺たちは冷静に遺体を見て、何かを気がつけるかもしれない。

description: MG omits Battler's explicit ‘just like I was’ comparison when he is surprised that Rosa, like him, is concerned about the bodies.
sourceReading: Battler is surprised that Rosa shares his concern with the bodies because he believes her priorities should differ from his investigative aim.

units.text: ......But it was a little surprising to learn that Aunt Rosa was also concerned about the bodies. Even at this point, I still wanted to use any clues I could find to expose the culprit and the truth myself.
units.japanese: ………しかし、楼座叔母さんもまた、俺と同様に遺体が気になるのは少しだけ意外だった。俺はこの期に及んでも、何かの手掛かりがあれば、犯人や真相をこの手で暴いてやりたいと思っている。

description: UP's ‘He had finished off Doctor Nanjo and ran off’ mismatches the coordinated verbs, shifting from past perfect to simple past inside one completed hypothetical sequence.
sourceReading: In Battler's reconstruction, the first culprit kills Nanjo and then escapes somewhere.

units.text:
The first person was Kanon‐kun, or maybe an impostor that looked like him.
He had finished off Doctor Nanjo and ran off somewhere. The second person was......probably the 19th person, Beatrice, whose location was unknown.
units.japanese:
一人目は、嘉音くん、もしくは彼に酷似した何者かの仕業。
彼は南條先生を葬り、どこかへ逃げ去った。二人目は、……多分、所在不明の１９人目、ベアトリーチェだ。
candidates: finished off Doctor Nanjo and ran off

description: MG changes Beatrice luring Battler toward thinking it would be preferable to believe in a witch into luring him into ‘wanting a witch to exist,’ replacing a forced epistemic preference with personal desire.
sourceReading: Battler thinks Beatrice is making suspicion of his companions so painful that accepting a witch would seem preferable by comparison.

units.text: This person's trying to close in on me from two directions. On the one hand, there's the frontal attack, where she tries to force me to believe there's a witch using closed room tricks that only a witch could do. ...And on the other hand, there's the rear attack, where she tries to lure me into wanting a witch to exist... by strengthening my suspicions of those close to me.
units.japanese: こいつは、二つの方向から俺を締め上げている。一つは、魔女にしかできない密室トリックで、俺に魔女を無理やり信じさせようとする力技のような正攻法。……そしてもう一つは、身内の疑いを濃厚にすることで、俺に魔女を信じた方がマシだと誘導しようとする搦め手だ。

description: MG uses the ungrammatical perfect construction ‘my means have became my goal’; the past participle must be ‘become.’
sourceReading: Beatrice says relying exclusively on the indirect attack would be the foolish result of allowing a means to become the goal.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle* I will not abandon my frontal attack. ...A rear attack only has meaning because it advances at the same time as the front. If I were to degenerate into only using the rear attack, it would merely result in a foolish plan where my means have became my goal."
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっく。正攻法は欠かぬ。…搦め手は正攻法と同時に進めてこそ意味がある。搦め手のみに堕するは、手段が目的となった時に起こる愚策に過ぎぬぞ」

description: UP reverses Battler's requested red repetition by inserting ‘no’: he asks Beatrice to repeat that someone was hiding in the servant room, not that no one was hiding there.
sourceReading: Battler challenges Beatrice to repeat his positive hidden-culprit premise—‘someone was hiding in the servant room’—in red; she refuses because she says the premise is about to collapse.

units.text: "...Ihihi, really? Well then, won't you repeat "no one was hiding in the servant room" in that red you're so proud of?"
units.japanese: 「…いっひっひ、そうですかい。じゃあ、お得意の赤で“何者かが使用人室に隠れていた”を復唱してもらおうじゃないか」

description: UP changes the letter's request for indulgence or forgiveness over borrowing the bodies into ‘please accept my apologies,’ substituting an apology for a request that the recipients tolerate the act.
sourceReading: The letter says the borrowed bodies will be returned later and formally asks the family to pardon or indulge this use.

units.text: "......P.S. I borrowed the two bodies for the ritual. I will return them later, so please accept my apologies. ...Furthermore, since these keys belong to all of you, I shall return them."
units.japanese: 「……追伸。二人の遺体を儀式にお借りします。後ほどご返却いたしますので、ご容赦をお願い致します。…あと、この鍵は皆様の物ですのでご返却いたします」

description: MG ends the letter's key-return sentence with two periods before the closing quotation mark.
sourceReading: The postscript ends after stating that the keys are being returned to their owners.

units.text: "...P.S. I borrowed those two corpses for my ceremony. They will be returned to you in due time, so I crave your indulgence. ...Also, these keys belong to you, so I return them to you now.."
units.japanese: 「……追伸。二人の遺体を儀式にお借りします。後ほどご返却いたしますので、ご容赦をお願い致します。…あと、この鍵は皆様の物ですのでご返却いたします」

description: MG repeatedly changes Battler's established ‘turn/flip the chessboard over’ formulation into ‘spin the chessboard around,’ replacing inversion of viewpoint with rotation.
sourceReading: Beatrice taunts Battler about flipping over the chessboard, and Battler repeats the phrase as he adopts the culprit's viewpoint.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*! What happened to that spinning the chessboard around thing that you're so proud of...? Please, announce your boastful strange theory."
units.japanese:
「くっくっくっく！　お得意のチェス盤を引っ繰り返すとやらはどうした…？　自慢の珍説をぜひ披露してみよ」
「……………チェス盤を、引っ繰り返す。…………俺が犯人ならどうする。死体をどこかへ運び出す。……手紙を残す。………内側から鍵を閉める。……ここから何かの方法で部屋を脱出すればいいんだ」

units.text: "...Spin...the chessboard around. ......What would I do if I were the culprit? I carry the corpses off somewhere. ...I leave a letter. ......I lock the door from the inside. ...Then I just have to escape this room by some means.
units.japanese:
「くっくっくっく！　お得意のチェス盤を引っ繰り返すとやらはどうした…？　自慢の珍説をぜひ披露してみよ」
「……………チェス盤を、引っ繰り返す。…………俺が犯人ならどうする。死体をどこかへ運び出す。……手紙を残す。………内側から鍵を閉める。……ここから何かの方法で部屋を脱出すればいいんだ」

description: MG omits the opening quotation mark when Battler resumes speaking with ‘Damn it, is that even possible?!’ after his culprit-viewpoint reconstruction.
sourceReading: A new quoted Battler utterance begins as he challenges whether escape is possible under the red constraints.

units.text: ......Damn it, is that even possible?! I was told in red that you can't get outside except through the door or the window...!
units.japanese: 「………くそッ、そんな方法はあるのか？！　扉と窓以外からは外に出られないと赤で言われちまってる…！」
candidates: Damn it, is that even possible

description: MG turns the fragment ‘And what I understood just now’ into the directive ‘Now move from there to what I've just learned,’ inventing an addressee and an instruction in Battler's internal reasoning.
sourceReading: Battler transitions from his previous theories to what he has now realized about Beatrice's definition of a hidden door.

units.text: Now move from there to what I've just learned. That term, "hidden door", refers to things that make it possible to enter or leave a room. ...In other words, that category doesn't cover things that don't actually lead in or out of the room, even if these things could never be recognized by people who didn't know about them beforehand.
units.japanese: そして今わかったこと。魔女の言っている「隠し扉」は、外部に出入りできるものを指す。……つまり、外部に出入りできず、しかも知らない人には気付けないものは「隠し扉」の定義に入らないことになっている。
candidates: Now move from there to what I've just learned

description: MG changes the third person in Jessica's room who ‘was hiding’ there into someone ‘from Jessica's room’ who ‘is hiding here,’ prematurely shifting the earlier-room example into the present servant room.
sourceReading: Battler first applies the hidden-compartment interpretation retrospectively to the hypothetical third person in Jessica's room, then says the same method may solve the present servant-room mystery.

units.text: So, if we had something like a "hidden shelf" or a "secret closet", for example, that wouldn't count as a "hidden door"! That means the third person from Jessica's room is hiding here, waiting for us to leave!
units.japanese: つまり、例えば「隠し棚」や「秘密のクローゼット」みたいなものは「隠し扉」に定義されてないわけだ！つまり、朱志香の部屋の３人目の人物はここに隠れて俺たちをやり過ごしたんだ！

description: MG omits opening quotation marks from two new Battler utterances: his repetition request at row 365 and his ‘Whoops’ correction at row 389.
sourceReading: Each passage begins a separately quoted Battler utterance before closing normally later in the same speech.

units.text: Repeat it! "There is no one in this room other than us"! By us, I mean me, George-aniki, Maria, Aunt Rosa, Genji-san, Gohda-san, and Shannon-chan, got it?! What do you think?!! You can't say it, right?!"
units.japanese:
「復唱要求！　“この部屋には俺たち以外の誰もいない”！　俺たちってのは、俺、譲治の兄貴、真里亞、楼座叔母さん、源次さん、郷田さん、紗音ちゃんのことだぜ？！　どうだッ！！　言えねぇだろう？！」
「おっと、死体の朱志香ももちろん含む。よって、朱志香の部屋の件、そしてこの使用人室の件の両方について、そなたが認識していた以外の人間は存在しない。誰も隠れていない」

units.text: Whoops, the corpse of Jessica is also included. Therefore, both in the case of Jessica's room and the case of this servant room, no humans exist that you were not aware of. No one is hiding."
units.japanese:
「復唱要求！　“この部屋には俺たち以外の誰もいない”！　俺たちってのは、俺、譲治の兄貴、真里亞、楼座叔母さん、源次さん、郷田さん、紗音ちゃんのことだぜ？！　どうだッ！！　言えねぇだろう？！」
「おっと、死体の朱志香ももちろん含む。よって、朱志香の部屋の件、そしてこの使用人室の件の両方について、そなたが認識していた以外の人間は存在しない。誰も隠れていない」

description: MG reduces Battler's targeted ‘Damn that Beatrice’ to the generic expletive ‘Dammit,’ omitting the person toward whom his anger is directed.
sourceReading: Battler angrily singles out Beatrice before recounting how he thought he had seen through her red-word deception.

units.text: Dammit, , I was so sure that I'd finally seen through her, that I'd seen how she distracted me with her clever red wordplay and fooled me.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェのヤツめ、赤をうまく使った言葉遊びで煙に巻き、俺をうまく騙せたに違いないと看破したはずだった…！！

description: UP changes Battler's hostile ‘that bastard Beatrice’ into the specifically gendered slur ‘Beatrice, you bitch,’ sharpening and narrowing the insult beyond ヤツめ.
sourceReading: Battler curses Beatrice with an angry, broadly contemptuous reference before describing her deception.

units.text: Dammit, , I was so sure that I'd finally seen through her, that I'd seen how she distracted me with her clever red wordplay and fooled me.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェのヤツめ、赤をうまく使った言葉遊びで煙に巻き、俺をうまく騙せたに違いないと看破したはずだった…！！

units.text: Beatrice, you bitch, I thought you were all smoke and mirrors, playing word games that made clever use of red, I was certain you'd just cleverly deceived me...!!
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェのヤツめ、赤をうまく使った言葉遊びで煙に巻き、俺をうまく騙せたに違いないと看破したはずだった…！！

description: MG repeatedly damages quotation boundaries: it joins Rosa's separate lines at 517–518 and 524–525, begins Gohda's reply with an apostrophe at 520, and inserts an opening quotation mark into narration at 599.
sourceReading: The source separates Rosa's successive utterances, marks Gohda's reply with a normal opening quotation mark, and presents the abduction theory at row 599 as narration.

units.text: "You kept saying those two were dead, but they aren't here. ...And now we have this letter from Beatrice, where she's been kind enough to confess that she carried the corpses off." "...It's as simple as that.
units.japanese:
「あなたたちが死んだ死んだという二人はここにいない。…そしてベアトリーチェからの手紙があり、親切にも死体は持ち去ったと告白してくれている。……そういうことよ」
「もう茶番は飽き飽きしたわ！！」
「ちゃ、……茶番って、……どういう意味ですか…！」
「私は朱志香ちゃんの部屋で言ったわ。……信用できるのは自分自身と、死体となって見付かった者以外いないってね」
「そして死体が見付からない以上、あの二人が殺されたことを認めるわけにはいかない」
彼らが南條先生たちを拉致して他所で殺し、密室は彼らのマスターキーで施錠した。これ以外の方法で密室を打ち破らない限り、……彼らの無実は証明できないのだ…。

units.text: I've had enough of this farce!!"
units.japanese:
「あなたたちが死んだ死んだという二人はここにいない。…そしてベアトリーチェからの手紙があり、親切にも死体は持ち去ったと告白してくれている。……そういうことよ」

units.text: 'W- What do you mean... by farce...?!"

「あなたたちが死んだ死んだという二人はここにいない。…そしてベアトリーチェからの手紙があり、親切にも死体は持ち去ったと告白してくれている。……そういうことよ」

units.text: "I said it in Jessica-chan's room. ...You can't trust anyone but yourself and those whose corpses have been found.
units.japanese:
「あなたたちが死んだ死んだという二人はここにいない。…そしてベアトリーチェからの手紙があり、親切にも死体は持ち去ったと告白してくれている。……そういうことよ」

彼らが南條先生たちを拉致して他所で殺し、密室は彼らのマスターキーで施錠した。これ以外の方法で密室を打ち破らない限り、……彼らの無実は証明できないのだ…。

units.text: And since we can't find the corpses of those two people, we must not accept that they've been killed."
units.japanese:
「あなたたちが死んだ死んだという二人はここにいない。…そしてベアトリーチェからの手紙があり、親切にも死体は持ち去ったと告白してくれている。……そういうことよ」

units.text: "They kidnapped Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa-san, killed them in another place, and locked the closed room with their own master keys." Unless the closed room could be broken by a method other than that one, ...it would be impossible to prove their innocence...

「あなたたちが死んだ死んだという二人はここにいない。…そしてベアトリーチェからの手紙があり、親切にも死体は持ち去ったと告白してくれている。……そういうことよ」
「もう茶番は飽き飽きしたわ！！」
「ちゃ、……茶番って、……どういう意味ですか…！」
「私は朱志香ちゃんの部屋で言ったわ。……信用できるのは自分自身と、死体となって見付かった者以外いないってね」
「そして死体が見付からない以上、あの二人が殺されたことを認めるわけにはいかない」
彼らが南條先生たちを拉致して他所で殺し、密室は彼らのマスターキーで施錠した。これ以外の方法で密室を打ち破らない限り、……彼らの無実は証明できないのだ…。

description: MG changes Rosa's claim that Nanjo and Kumasawa made it appear they were killed into ‘We're supposed to believe that they've been killed,’ shifting from the suspects' staged act to the group's expected belief.
sourceReading: Rosa asserts that Nanjo and Kumasawa are alive, have staged their deaths, and are hiding in the mansion to attack the group.

units.text: "Doctor Nanjo and Kumasawa-san aren't dead, they're alive! We're supposed to believe that they've been killed, but they're definitely hiding somewhere in this mansion. So that they can attack us!!"
units.japanese: 「南條先生と熊沢さんは死んでないわ、生きているッ！　殺されたということにして、この屋敷のどこかに隠れているのよ。私たちを襲うためにね！！」
candidates: We're supposed to believe that they've been killed

description: MG turns Rosa's inability to believe the claim that the two were killed into ‘we mustn't believe you,’ changing the object from the death report to the witnesses and changing epistemic inability into a prohibition.
sourceReading: Because there are no bodies, Rosa says she cannot accept the servants' particular assertion that Nanjo and Kumasawa were killed, and suggests the servants may have coordinated a lie.

units.text: "You all say that those two were killed. But since there are no corpses, we mustn't believe you. There's a chance that you worked out a story beforehand, that you're lying!!"
units.japanese: 「あなたたちは、南條先生たちは殺されたという。でも死体がない以上、それを信じるわけにはいかないわ。あなたたちが口裏を合わせてそういう嘘をついている可能性があるもの！！」

description: MG converts Rosa's condition that finding the bodies would establish innocence into the direct command ‘Find Doctor Nanjo's and Kumasawa-san's bodies!!’
sourceReading: Rosa says there is a way to believe the servants' innocence: the bodies of Nanjo and Kumasawa must be found.

units.text: "There's a good way to prove your innocence, isn't there? Find Doctor Nanjo's and Kumasawa-san's bodies!!"
units.japanese: 「あなたたちの無実を信じる方法はちゃんとあるわよぅ？　南條先生と熊沢さんの遺体が見付かることよ！！」
candidates: Find Doctor Nanjo's and Kumasawa-san's bodies

description: UP's ‘as blood by the name of tears flowed out’ is an unidiomatic construction for tears serving metaphorically as blood from Shannon's wounded heart.
sourceReading: Battler sees Shannon's tears as the metaphorical blood flowing from a heart deeply stabbed by Rosa's words.

units.text: It wasn't just George‐aniki; ...even I could recognize that Shannon‐chan had been stabbed deep into her heart, as blood by the name of tears flowed out...
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴じゃなくたって、…俺にだって、紗音ちゃんが心を深々と突き刺されて、涙という血を流しているのがわかる…。
candidates: blood by the name of tears flowed

description: MG uses ‘we've been searching an answer,’ omitting the required preposition ‘for.’
sourceReading: Battler says that seeking an answer is what keeps making everything stranger and concludes that he no longer wants one.

units.text: Yeah, bit by bit, I'm starting to understand... ...It's because we've been searching an answer, ...that's why everything keeps going wrong...
units.japanese: あぁあぁ、だんだんわかって来たよ…。……答えなんか求めるから、…どんどんおかしくなっていっちまうんだ…。

description: UP turns Rosa's judgment that surrendering the keys is ‘not a bad thing’ into ‘not a bad start,’ adding the idea that it is only the beginning of a process.
sourceReading: Rosa says that giving up the master keys to clear suspicion is elementary but not a bad thing.

units.text: ".................. ......That's good judgment. Those master keys are the greatest basis upon which you have been suspected several times today. Relinquishing them in order to clear away that suspicion may only be a first step, but, well, I think it isn't a bad start."
units.japanese: 「………………。……それは良い判断ね。今日、何度もあなたたちが疑われてきた最大の根拠はこのマスターキー。それを手放せば疑いが晴らせるのではないかというのは、初歩的ではあるけれど、まぁ、悪いことじゃないと思うわ」

description: MG says only that Rosa has all the master keys, omitting Battler's explicit claim that the only master keys now are those Rosa holds.
sourceReading: Battler declares that the master keys in Rosa's possession are now the only master keys.

units.text: "...A-Are you satisfied now, Aunt Rosa? ...Now you have all the master keys. ...Doesn't that satisfy you?!!"
units.japanese: 「こ、………これで満足かい、楼座叔母さん。……これでマスターキーは楼座叔母さんが持つものだけだ。……これで、満足なんだろッ！！」

description: MG renders Maria's approving それでいいんだよ as ‘That's enough,’ which can sound like a demand to stop rather than reassurance that Battler's acceptance is right.
sourceReading: Maria approvingly tells Battler that accepting the witch is the right way and then embraces him.

units.text: "...That's enough, Battler. ......Beatrice "existed". ...You had so much trouble believing, so you couldn't see her. ......Witches "exist". They "exist". And will "come" soon."
units.japanese: 「……それでいいんだよ、戦人。…………ベアトリーチェは、“い”たの。……戦人が、なかなかそれを信じられなかったから、見えなかったの。…………魔女は“い”るの。“い”る。もうすぐ“来”る」

description: UP's ‘so couldn't see her’ omits the grammatical subject ‘you.’
sourceReading: Maria says Battler could not see Beatrice because he did not believe.

units.text: "......That's the way, Battler. ............Beatrice "existed". ......You just couldn't believe that easily, so couldn't see her. ............The witch "exists". "Exists". Will soon "come"."
units.japanese: 「……それでいいんだよ、戦人。…………ベアトリーチェは、“い”たの。……戦人が、なかなかそれを信じられなかったから、見えなかったの。…………魔女は“い”るの。“い”る。もうすぐ“来”る」

description: MG changes Battler's ‘I'm not afraid’ into reassurance that Maria need not be afraid, and reduces his wish to hold hands and remain together always to ‘Stay with me, hands joined.’
sourceReading: Battler tells Maria that he is not afraid and asks to hold hands and stay together with her always.

units.text: ......There's no need to be afraid, okay? Stay with me, hands joined, ...okay...? Let's think about the riddle of the epitaph together. Let's think about Beato's puzzle. ......Beato has been saying it from the beginning. She hasn't said anything other than "let's play and solve this puzzle"."
units.japanese: 「…………怖くないよ？　真里亞と一緒に、おててを繋いで、…ずっと一緒にいよ…？　一緒に碑文の謎を考えよ。ベアトの問題を考えよ。………ベアトは最初から言ってるよ。この問題を解いて遊ぼうとしか言ってないよ」

description: UP removes Gohda's characteristic third-person self-reference この郷田 from his promise to prepare the finest food, replacing it with a generic ‘I promise.’
sourceReading: Gohda formally names himself while promising that he personally will prepare his finest cooking whenever called upon.

units.text: ".........I will also be waiting in the kitchen. ......If you need anything, please command me at any time. .........If you wish for some warm food, I promise to have the very best prepared for you."
units.japanese: 「………私も、厨房に控えております。……何かございましたら、いつでもご用命下さい。………温かい食事をお望みでしたら、いつでもこの郷田、最高のお料理を用意させていただきます」

description: UP says ‘There are no more master keys anymore,’ redundantly combining no more with anymore.
sourceReading: Shannon says that no other master keys remain and that George will be safe with Rosa in the parlor.

units.text: "...It's alright, George‐sama... Please, return to the parlor. There are no more master keys anymore. So if you are with Rosa‐sama in the parlor, you won't be threatened by anyone."
units.japanese: 「…いいんです、譲治さま…。どうか客間にお戻りになって下さい。もうマスターキーは他にありません。だから楼座さまとご一緒に客間にいれば、誰にも脅かされません」
candidates: are no more master keys anymore

description: MG fails to close Battler's first utterance at row 788 or open his new inheritance-and-gold utterance at row 789, erasing the source's deliberate dialogue break.
sourceReading: Battler first says he does not suspect anyone; after a dialogue break, he dismisses inheritance and gold as reasons for murder.

units.text: "...It's...not like I suspect Shannon-chan and the other servants ...or anyone at all... I don't want to suspect anyone...
units.japanese:
「……俺は、……決して紗音ちゃんや他の使用人を、…いや、誰かを疑ってるわけじゃないんだ……。誰も疑いたくないんだ…」
「遺産？　黄金？　…そんなの下らねぇじゃねぇかよ…。…そんなので殺し合いなんて、…あるわけねぇじゃねぇかよ……」

units.text: The inheritance? The gold? ...That's all nothing... ...There's no way people are killing each other over things like that..."
units.japanese:
「……俺は、……決して紗音ちゃんや他の使用人を、…いや、誰かを疑ってるわけじゃないんだ……。誰も疑いたくないんだ…」
「遺産？　黄金？　…そんなの下らねぇじゃねぇかよ…。…そんなので殺し合いなんて、…あるわけねぇじゃねぇかよ……」

description: UP twice inserts ‘sure’ into Beatrice's promise to appear and speak in red, producing ‘Then I'll appear, sure, I'll say it in red, sure!’ without a corresponding hedge or verbal tic in the source.
sourceReading: Beatrice says that if Battler obeys, she will appear, state the key limit in red, and tell Rosa.

units.text: "Then kneel, make your tongue crawl on my shoes. Can you do it? You can do it, riiiiiiiight?? Then I'll appear, sure, I'll say it in red, sure! I'll tell Rosa that there are only five master keys!!"
units.japanese: 「そして跪けよ、妾の靴に舌を這わせろ。出来るか？　出来るンだよなアァアア？？　そうしたら現れてやるよ赤で言ってやる！　マスターキーは５本しかないって、楼座に言ってやるよ！！」
candidates: I'll appear, sure, I'll say it in red, sure

description: MG changes Beatrice's taunt that Battler's slight wavering is already sufficient into praise that he has ‘done well’ and a ‘tingly feeling,’ replacing psychological instability with a bodily sensation.
sourceReading: Beatrice says that Battler need not actually discard his pride: it is enough that he wavered for a moment under her demand.

units.text: "Oh, but of course, you'll never abandon that lordly pride of yours. But you've done well, you've done more than enough, and you're starting to get that tingly feeling, aren't you?
units.japanese: 「あぁでもわかってる、誇り高きお前がプライドを捨てられるわけがない。それでもいいんだよ充分なんだよ、ちょっとグラァって来ただろォ？」

description: UP changes the narration's retrospective judgment that George had thought he had reassured Shannon into the first-person claim ‘I remembered cheering her up,’ inventing an act of recollection and shifting the narrative person.
sourceReading: George had believed that dismissing the object as an old dusty mirror had reassured Shannon after he forgave her.

units.text:
......Just breaking a mirror in some musty shrine wouldn't change the fate of our meeting. And that would never cause any curse.
I remembered cheering her up, saying it was only a musty mirror covered in dust.
units.japanese:
……古ぼけた祠にある鏡を割ったくらいで、僕たちの出会いの運命は変わらない。そして、それによって何の祟りもあるものか。
ただの埃に塗れた古ぼけた鏡だったさと元気付けたはずだった。

description: UP converts Gohda's interrupted disbelief—‘But, surely it couldn't really...’—into the affirmative ‘it's astonishing, she really—,’ making him begin to assert Beatrice's existence before Shannon cuts in.
sourceReading: After admitting that he had only performed outward belief, Gohda begins an incredulous question about whether Beatrice could truly exist; Shannon interrupts with a categorical answer.

units.text: "In the beginning, I thought it was ridiculous, but since it appeared indiscreet to comment on that, ...outwardly, I conducted myself as if I also believed it. ......But, it's astonishing, she really—"
units.japanese: 「最初は馬鹿馬鹿しいと思っていましたが、それを批判すると何だか不謹慎そうな空気があったもので、…私も表向きは信じているように振舞ってきました。……しかし、まさか本当に、」

description: UP renders 由緒正しい as ‘historically rich,’ an unnatural phrase for a spirit mirror of venerable or distinguished provenance.
sourceReading: Gohda uncertainly recalls that Natsuhi's spirit mirror has distinguished provenance and strong protective power.

units.text: "Yes. I believe she received it as one of the mementos of her grandfather or something, and that it held a very strong magic repelling power, a "historically rich"(?) spirit mirror or something..."
units.japanese: 「はい。お祖父さまの形見分けか何かでもらったものだそうで、とても強い魔除けの力を持つ、由緒正しい？　霊鏡だとか何とか…」

description: MG misspells ‘explanation’ as ‘explaination’ when George says they can explain disturbing Natsuhi's body to the police.
sourceReading: George admits that touching the body before police arrive is wrong but says they will give a proper explanation.

units.text: "...In that case, Aunt Natsuhi should've had a key on her person. ...Aunt Natsuhi's corpse should still be in the chapel. We probably shouldn't be disturbing it before the police come, but we can give a full explaination later."
units.japanese: 「……ならばその鍵は夏妃伯母さんが持ち歩いているはず。…礼拝堂にはまだ夏妃伯母さんの遺体があるはずだ。警察が来る前に勝手にいじってしまうのは悪いことだけれど、それについてはちゃんと説明しよう」

description: MG drops the honorific from George's request to ‘Genji’ at row 168 despite his otherwise consistent address as Genji-san in this exchange.
sourceReading: George respectfully asks Genji-san to prepare umbrellas while assigning tasks to the servants.

units.text: "Shannon, get a flashlight! Gohda-san, find something that looks like it can break the glass! Sorry Genji, but can you be on umbrella duty?"
units.japanese: 「紗音は懐中電灯を！　郷田さんはガラスを割れそうな道具を！　源次さんはすみません、傘の用意をお願いします」

description: MG adds ‘sir’ to the three servants' simultaneous reply and represents the shared quotation with six quote marks, although the source simply has all three answer ‘Yes!’
sourceReading: Shannon, Gohda, and Genji answer George's assignments together with an energetic yes.

units.text: """Yes sir!"""

description: MG calls Gohda's frying pan ‘thick-feeling,’ an unnatural rendering of 重厚感ある, which describes a solid, weighty, imposing pan.
sourceReading: After considering several heavy cooking tools, Gohda chooses a large, substantial frying pan.

units.text: Gohda was testing several heavy-looking cooking tools. ...Normally, a highly-praised chef like him wouldn't want to use them for something other than their intended purpose. But now, he was frantic to fulfill the orders of the one he accepted as his master. After some worrying, he took a large, thick-feeling frying pan.
units.japanese:
郷田は、いくつかの重そうな調理道具を吟味している。
…本来なら、誇りある料理人の彼は用途以外に使いたくなどない。しかし今は、彼が主だと認めた者の命令に応えようと必死だった。彼は少し悩んだ末、大きめの重厚感あるフライパンを手にする。

description: UP broadens Battler's inability to feel that solving the riddle would save himself into whether it would save ‘us,’ changing the immediate object of his doubt from personal survival to the whole group.
sourceReading: Battler cannot feel assured that solving the riddle will really save him and suspects that doing so may merely serve the culprit.

units.text: I didn't really feel that solving this riddle would actually save us. .........I thought that even if we did solve it, that would be doing just what the culprit wanted us to, and it would all be a wasted effort...
units.japanese: この謎を解くことで、本当に自分が助かるのか、実感できない。………仮に解けたとしても、それは犯人の思う壺で、結局は全て無駄な努力なのではないかと思ってしまう…。

description: MG replaces Battler's quiz-show image of sounding a buzzer and raising his hand with raising his hand and crying ‘I got it,’ losing the audible answer-buzzer mechanism.
sourceReading: Battler jokingly imagines buzzing in, raising his hand, submitting the answer to the witch, and having it checked.

units.text: "...What do we do if we solve the riddle? Should we raise a hand and cry "I got it!", tell the witch our answer, and see what she says?"
units.japanese: 「……謎が解けたらどうするんだ。ピンポーンって鳴らして挙手して、解答を魔女に伝えて答えあわせをするのか」

description: UP strengthens Battler's qualified claim that magical risk is ‘somewhat’ incompatible with his chessboard theory and that a best move seeks an advantageous development into outright conflict and a move that ‘promises’ one.
sourceReading: Battler says risk-taking does not sit entirely comfortably with his preferred theory, under which one searches for the lowest-risk move while expecting a favorable development.

units.text: So, ...if you don't bear a risk, nothing can be gained. That is doubtlessly the way of the world, ......but it was in conflict with the chessboard theory style of thinking that I liked.
units.japanese:
リスクを負わなければ、何も得られない、…か。それは間違いなく世の中の真理だが、……俺が好むチェス盤理論の考えとは少し相容れなかった。
チェスにおける指し手とは、常にリスクのもっとも少なく、有利な展開を期待する最善手の模索だ。ギャンブルのような運否天賦で手は指さない。……そう、知的ゲームに博打性の入り込む余地はありえないのだ。

units.text: A move in chess is always a search for the best play, that minimizes the risk, and promises an advantageous turn of events. You don't trust your plays to chance, like in gambling. ......That's right, there's no room for gambling in an intellectual game.
units.japanese:
リスクを負わなければ、何も得られない、…か。それは間違いなく世の中の真理だが、……俺が好むチェス盤理論の考えとは少し相容れなかった。
チェスにおける指し手とは、常にリスクのもっとも少なく、有利な展開を期待する最善手の模索だ。ギャンブルのような運否天賦で手は指さない。……そう、知的ゲームに博打性の入り込む余地はありえないのだ。

description: MG changes Battler's suspicion that the epitaph is a smokescreen meant to mislead him into the claim that Beatrice is misleading him by ‘speaking in riddles,’ shifting the tactic from deliberate distraction to obscure language.
sourceReading: Battler suspects that drawing attention to the epitaph is a smokescreen intended to make the survivors misunderstand something.

units.text: I thought she was probably making us focus on the epitaph to fool us in some way, speaking in riddles. ...But according to Maria, that alone was impossible. She said this was a genuine risk that the witch had taken, and therefore proof that this was a formal ceremony for magic.
units.japanese: 俺は多分、この碑文に注目させることで何かを誤解させて煙に巻かせようとしているんだろうと思っている。……しかし真里亞は、そんなことだけは絶対にありえないという。これは魔女が示した純粋なリスクであり、ゆえに正式な魔法の儀式である証拠だという。

description: MG recasts Battler's ‘clever advance notice,’ suggestive locked-room staging, and excessive theatrical presentation as a ‘kindhearted’ notice, ‘self-aware’ locked rooms, and ‘over-acting.’
sourceReading: Battler argues that a simple massacre required none of the culprit's clever notices, suggestive locked-room staging, or other excessive theatrics.

units.text: If she just wanted to massacre us all, she could've done it quietly, without this whole crazy setup. There was no need for that kindhearted advance notice, all this self-aware closed room stuff, or any of the rest. ...It's all over-acting. I've got no clue what it means.
units.japanese:
俺たちを皆殺しにしたいだけなら、大仕掛けなど打たずに、こっそり密かにやればいい。気の利いた予告状も、思わせぶりな密室演出も何も必要ない。…全てが過剰演出。
まったく意味がわからない。

description: MG says Battler looked ‘lazily’ at Rosa where ぼんやり means vaguely or absent-mindedly, adding indolence to his exhausted contemplation.
sourceReading: Lost in thought, Battler looks vaguely toward the exhausted Rosa as he applies chessboard reasoning to her distrust.

units.text: I looked lazily at Aunt Rosa. She was probably tired from being under all this tension the whole time. She couldn't sleep, but she kept staring vaguely at some point off in space.
units.japanese:
ぼんやりと楼座叔母さんを見る。ずっと緊張を強いられてきたから疲れが出たのだろう。
眠ってはいないが、宙の何もない一点をぼんやりとずっと見続けていた。

description: UP has Battler call Beatrice's conduct ‘all this shit,’ adding explicit profanity where 滅茶苦茶 refers to the outrageous chaos or reckless acts she has committed.
sourceReading: Battler protests that after everything outrageous Beatrice has done, she still expects him to trust her observance of rules.

units.text: "..................... ......Even after pulling all this shit, you're still telling me to trust in at least the rules?"
units.japanese: 「…………………。……これだけ滅茶苦茶やってきて、それでもルールだけは信じろってのかよ」

description: MG drops Beatrice's comparison that humans are ‘far more’ selfish and wicked than she is, reducing it to the non-comparative ‘humans are the truly selfish monsters.’
sourceReading: From Beatrice's perspective, humans are much more selfish and wicked than a witch, particularly in their unreliable contracts.

units.text: "From my perspective, humans are the truly selfish monsters. ...There's nothing as dubious as a human's promise. Even I sometimes make contracts with humans, but you wouldn't imagine how strict an agreement must be made just to grant a single foolish wish."
units.japanese: 「妾から見れば、人間の方がよっぽど利己的で外道な存在よ。……人間の約束ほど、疑わしいものはない。妾も時に人間と契約するが、下らない願いひとつ叶えるのにどれほど厳重に取り決めをするか想像もつくまい」
candidates: humans are the truly selfish monsters

description: MG renders Beatrice's 察しろ—an instruction to infer how Rudolf learned his view of fraud—as ‘Imagine it,’ obscuring the implied deduction that he had personally suffered fraud.
sourceReading: Beatrice tells Battler to infer that people are not born knowing fraud: Rudolf learned it because he had suffered it somewhere.

units.text: "......Imagine it. When people are born, they know nothing of fraud. ...They get it from somewhere. And so they learn it."
units.japanese: 「…………察しろ。人は生まれながらに詐欺を知りはせぬ。…どこかで被った。だから覚えた」

description: MG turns sins that people cannot help foisting onto one another into ‘crimes ... where people must press up against each other,’ losing the transfer of harm across people.
sourceReading: Beatrice reflects on the sin of a human world in which people cannot stop imposing their injuries and wrongdoing on one another.

units.text: "Yes, the crimes of the human world, where people must press up against each other. ...Let me see, I've heard that from a witch somewhere. Oh well. ...I'm not as heartless as you think, you see? *cackle*cackle*cackle*!"
units.japanese: 「押し付けあわずにはいられぬ人の世の罪、か。……はて、どこの魔女に聞いたやら。まぁいい。……そなたが思っているほど、妾も無慈悲ではないぞ？　くっくくくっくっく！」
candidates: people must press up against each other

description: MG omits Battler's しかもまた, which stresses that Beatrice has killed a large group yet again, and leaves only ‘You killed so many people.’
sourceReading: Battler condemns Beatrice for killing another large group of people, again, by cruel methods.

units.text: "Liar!! You killed so many people!! And you did it in such horrible ways too! How could you not be heartless?!!
units.japanese: 「嘘をつけ！！　これだけの大勢を、しかもまたッ！！　こんな残酷な方法で殺しておいて、何が無慈悲ではないだ！！」

description: MG weakens とても正視できるようなものではなかった, which says the deteriorated bodies could not be looked at directly, into something one merely ‘wouldn't want’ to look at.
sourceReading: After half a day of decomposition and insects gathering, the bodies are impossible to face directly.

units.text: ...Now that half a day had passed, the bodies of Natsuhi and the rest had changed completely. Small bugs sniffing out the smell of death had started to gather. ...It really wasn't something you'd want to look at directly...
units.japanese:
……夏妃たちの遺体は半日を経て、変わり果てていた。
死臭を嗅ぎ付けた小さな羽虫たちが群がり始めている。
…とても正視できるようなものではなかった…。

description: MG says the blizzard of gold leaf ‘seeped up’ from around the table, weakening ぶわっと湧き上がった, which describes it suddenly billowing or surging upward.
sourceReading: When Shannon raises the key, a blizzard of gold leaf suddenly billows up around the table and resolves into countless butterflies.

units.text: After all, Shannon hadn't noticed. George and Gohda, watching from afar, noticed it first. After all, when Shannon had held the key up high, ...a blizzard of gold leaf had seeped up from around the table.
units.japanese:
なぜなら、紗音は気付かなかった。
遠くから見ていた譲治と郷田が先に気がつけた。紗音が鍵を高々と掲げた時、……テーブルの周りから、ぶわっと金箔の吹雪が湧き上がったからだ。
candidates: seeped up from around the table

description: UP replaces Gohda's defiant ‘Don't underestimate me!’ with ‘You want a piece of me?!’, changing his response to the attacking swarm into a challenge inviting confrontation.
sourceReading: While holding off the butterflies for George, Gohda shouts that they must not underestimate him.

units.text: "George‐sama, quickly!! Damn it, you want a piece of me?! Uooooooooooooooohhh!!"
units.japanese: 「譲治さま、お早く！！　くそッ、なめるな、うおおおおおおお！！」

description: MG has Beatrice promise a warm reception ‘before’ a wonderful dinner, while the source says she must entertain them with the wonderful dinner itself.
sourceReading: Claiming to be the mansion's host, Beatrice says she must entertain the three with a wonderful dinner.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*, hahahahahahahahahahahaha!! It's almost time for dinner, is it not? ...I am the host of this mansion now. So I must give you a warm reception before your wonderful dinner. ...And look, we even have "three people", fit to order. ...My, my, how truly, truly convenient!!"
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくく、はっははははははははははは！！　そろそろ晩餐の時間ではないか。……すでに妾はこの屋敷のホストである。そなたらを素晴らしきディナーで歓待しなくてはならぬというもの。……おあつらえ向きに“三人”ではないか。……これはこれは実に実に好都合ッ！！」

description: MG's ‘three people, fit to order’ is an unnatural rendering of おあつらえ向きに三人, which means that the group conveniently or perfectly consists of three people.
sourceReading: Beatrice gleefully observes that there are exactly three convenient prospective dinner victims.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*, hahahahahahahahahahahaha!! It's almost time for dinner, is it not? ...I am the host of this mansion now. So I must give you a warm reception before your wonderful dinner. ...And look, we even have "three people", fit to order. ...My, my, how truly, truly convenient!!"
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくく、はっははははははははははは！！　そろそろ晩餐の時間ではないか。……すでに妾はこの屋敷のホストである。そなたらを素晴らしきディナーで歓待しなくてはならぬというもの。……おあつらえ向きに“三人”ではないか。……これはこれは実に実に好都合ッ！！」

description: UP leaves Shannon's sentence grammatically incomplete as ‘I never knew where it actually...!’ where she says she had only heard the story and did not know the mirror's actual location.
sourceReading: Shannon says she had only heard about the treasure box and had not heard where it was actually kept.

units.text: "It's just something I heard...! I never knew where it actually...!"
units.japanese: 「話に聞いただけです…！　実際にどこにあるかまでは…！」

description: UP adds a ‘corner’ beside the bed at rows 585 and 587 even though ベッドの脇 means simply beside or next to the bed.
sourceReading: Shannon guesses that the mirror is at the dresser or beside the bed; only an incense burner, book, and glasses are beside the bed.

units.text: ".........I, I think it's probably in her dresser, or in the corner by the bed!"
units.japanese:
「………た、多分、お化粧台か、ベッドの脇にあるんじゃないかと思います！」
紗音が女性のセンスでそう断言する。でも、ベッドの脇には香炉と読みかけの小説と眼鏡が置いてあるだけだった。しかし、化粧台は立派で引き出しも多く、彼女が宝物をここにしまっていたとしても納得できるというものだった。

units.text: Shannon claimed that because of her woman's sense. But in the corner by the bed, there was only an incense burner, a half‐read novel, and a pair of glasses. But the dresser was elegant and had many drawers, and it would be understandable if she had kept some of her valuables there.
units.japanese:
「………た、多分、お化粧台か、ベッドの脇にあるんじゃないかと思います！」
紗音が女性のセンスでそう断言する。でも、ベッドの脇には香炉と読みかけの小説と眼鏡が置いてあるだけだった。しかし、化粧台は立派で引き出しも多く、彼女が宝物をここにしまっていたとしても納得できるというものだった。

description: MG collapses the narration's explicit distinction between 人影, a human silhouette, and shadows cast by nonhuman beings into the shorter statement that these were not shadows of ‘people’ because the beings were not Human.
sourceReading: The narrator rejects calling the approaching shapes human silhouettes because 人影 specifically denotes the shadow or figure of a human, and these beings are not human.

units.text: No, it wasn't shadows of "people". ...Because they weren't Human at all!!
units.japanese:
いや、それは人影という言葉は相応しくない。
なぜなら、人影はニンゲンの影のことだ。……ニンゲンじゃない存在の影は、人影とは表現できない！！

description: MG changes the door physically refusing to stay closed into the lock refusing to stay engaged: ‘It won't lock’ and ‘Even if I lock it, it unlocks.’
sourceReading: After Gohda closes and locks the door, it springs back open; each time he closes it, it opens again before the procession reaches it.

units.text: "U-Uwaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!! I-It won't lock!! Even if I lock it, it unlocks! What's going on, dammitdammitdammitdammit!!"
units.japanese: 「う、うわあああぁああああぁあ！！　し、閉まらない！！　閉めても開いてしまう！　どうなってんだこりゃ、くそくそくそくそ！！」

description: UP replaces the source's shrill scream ‘like tearing silk’ with a scream ‘that would make glass shatter,’ changing a comparison of sound quality into an invented physical effect.
sourceReading: Direct supernatural contact turns Gohda's brave roar into a pathetic, genuinely terrified shriek as sharp as tearing silk.

units.text:
But he was still lucky.
He wasn't touching them directly.
Because they were on the other side of the door. So it was natural that if he did touch them directly, ...Gohda's cry would turn from something brave into a shameful, ...and yet very real scream that would make glass shatter.
units.japanese:
しかし、それでもまだ幸いだった。
直接触れているわけではない。
扉越しなのだから。だから、直接触れたなら、…郷田のその叫びは勇ましいものから、絹を裂くような情けない、…だけれどもそれこそ本当の、悲鳴に変わるのは当然のことだった。
candidates: scream that would make glass shatter

description: MG changes the plural ‘new masters of this room’ welcomed by the opening door into the singular ‘new master,’ assigning the welcome solely to Beatrice rather than the entering supernatural group.
sourceReading: Once Gohda falls, the door opens by itself and appears to recognize and welcome the room's new masters: the goat attendants and Beatrice enter in succession.

units.text: As it did, the door opened softly, even though no one was pushing it, ...welcoming in the new master of this room. It looked almost as though the door itself had accepted her.
units.japanese: すると扉は、誰が押しているわけでもないのに、すぅっと開き、……この部屋の新しき主たちを迎え入れた。まるで扉自身がそれを認めたかのように見えた。

description: MG inserts ‘sample’ into Beatrice's recognition of Shannon as another piece of Kinzo's excellent furniture, making Shannon an example or specimen rather than simply another servant in that class.
sourceReading: Beatrice remembers that Shannon, too, was one of Kinzo's excellent pieces of furniture, adding that she has matured much more than Kanon.

units.text: "......I'd forgotten. You're another sample of Kinzo's outstanding furniture. And you've matured much more than Kanon..."
units.japanese: 「………忘れていた。そなたもまた、金蔵の優れた家具だったな。それも、嘉音よりだいぶ熟成した、……」

description: UP leaves the false Kanon's intended attack without a finite verb: ‘Shannon, who still hadn't prepared her heart, apart with a single stroke.’
sourceReading: The false Kanon intends to cut or tear apart the emotionally unprepared Shannon with one stroke.

units.text:
......From the impostor Kanon's arm, ...a strangely shining trail extended.
.........It planned to tear Shannon apart with that. ......Shannon, who still hadn't prepared her heart, apart with a single stroke...
units.japanese:
……偽者の嘉音の腕から、…不気味に光る軌跡が伸びる。
………それで紗音を切り裂くつもりなのだ。……まだ心の整理がつかない紗音を、一刀で…。
candidates: Shannon, who still hadn't prepared her heart, apart with a single stroke

description: MG changes the missing preparation needed to draw out the spirit mirror's power into missing tools.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Shannon lacks both the necessary preparation and time, and refuses to grant either.

units.text: "I see, so that spirit mirror is lending you strength... But you don't have the tools or the time to draw out its true power."
units.japanese: 「なるほど、霊鏡がそなたに力を貸しているというのか…。しかしその霊鏡の本当の力を引き出すには、準備も時間も足りないな」

description: MG replaces Beatrice's claim that love is lust and cannot be discussed only through pretty shoujo-manga platitudes with the categorical claim that love is ‘totally meaningless unless you're sleeping together.’
sourceReading: Beatrice crudely equates love with sexual desire and rejects speaking of it only in clean, idealized shoujo-manga terms.

units.text: "...Ha! Don't speak in cheap ideals, like some poet!! Love is lust, totally meaningless unless you're sleeping together. Men are mere flies and maggots that get drawn to your female scent and crowd around you. Do you still not understand that at your aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaage?"
units.japanese: 「……は！　綺麗事を詩人のように語るなッ！！　愛は情欲なんだョ少女マンガみたく綺麗事ばっかりで語れネェんだよ。男どもはお前のニオイに引かれて群がる蛆蝿どもなんだよォ。そんなことも、その歳でまだ理解できねェのかよォオオオォ？」
candidates: totally meaningless unless you're sleeping together

description: MG turns Beatrice's threat to reveal ‘the filthy reality of his love’ into the specific assertion that George has only ever desired Shannon's flesh.
sourceReading: After threatening to turn Shannon into a maggot and test George's love, Beatrice promises to show her the filthy reality of that love without yet stating the test's outcome as fact.

units.text: I'll show you that this guy's only had his eyes on your fleeeeeeeeeeeeeeesh, die you piece of craaaaaaaaaaaaap, don't you tell me about looooooooooooooooooove!!"
units.japanese: 「そいつの愛のど汚ネェ現実ってやつを教えてやるよォオオオォオオ、死ねよガラクタがあぁああてめぇが愛を語るんじゃねえええぇェエエエェェエェエエエエエ！！」

description: UP renders Beatrice's taunting question as the ungrammatical ‘What is this you call that resiiiisssting?!’
sourceReading: Beatrice mocks the barrier by asking whether Shannon thinks that counts as resistance.

units.text: "What is this you call that resiiiisssting?!"
units.japanese: 「何だよそれは抵抗してるつもりかよォオォオォ？！」

description: MG breaks the repeated 削る shaving image and its cheese comparison by saying the barrier is being ‘erased’ and Parmigiano-Reggiano is harder to ‘cut through.’
sourceReading: Beatrice says the barrier is being shaved or scraped away, compares the effort with shaving hard Parmigiano-Reggiano, and the narration repeats that the storm shaves the cylindrical wall down.

units.text: see see see see see it's being eraaaaaaased crackcrunchsmacksnap how thin how shameful, Parmigiano-Reggiano would be harder to cut through than your frail resistaaaaaaaaaaaance hiiyahhaaahahaah!!"
units.japanese: 「ほらほらほらほらほら削られてるぜェエェカリカリコリコリガリガリゴリゴリ何て薄くて情けないんだよ、お前のその薄っぺらな抵抗に比べたらパルミジャーノ・レッジアーノの方がまァだ削るのに苦労がいるぜェエエエェエエエエエェヒィヤッハーァッハッハアッ！！」

description: UP's ‘a witch of one thousand’ leaves the source's thousand-year-witch description grammatically incomplete.
sourceReading: Beatrice contrasts furniture not yet a hundred years old with herself as a thousand-year witch.

units.text: "Whaat...? Hohh. ......I wonder, what did this furniture, who hasn't lived even a hundred years, just say to a witch of one thousand......?"
units.japanese: 「何ぃ…？　ほぉぅ。……千年の魔女に、百年も至らぬ家具が、今なんと言ったか……？」

description: MG weakens the stated consequence of Genji's restricted access into probability: ‘That probably made his rounds go a lot faster than usual.’
sourceReading: Because Genji can inspect little beyond corridors and windows, he is able to complete the route much faster than usual.

units.text: He had returned his master key to Rosa, so the places he could reach were extremely limited. All he could do was walk around the hallways, checking to make sure all the windows were closed. That probably made his rounds go a lot faster than usual.
units.japanese:
楼座にマスターキーを返した為、彼が見回れる場所はかなり限定されていた。せいぜい廊下を回り、窓の戸締りを確認するくらいだ。
だから、普段よりもだいぶ早く順路を回れるのだった。
candidates: probably made his rounds go a lot faster than usual

description: MG turns Rosa's statement that she will check the room's locks before leaving into the inclusive instruction ‘let's check,’ briefly assigning the task to the group.
sourceReading: Rosa stops Battler and says she will check the room's locks before they leave; the narration then says she personally checks every window.

units.text: "Battler-kun, wait! Just in case, let's check the doors and windows of this room. Wait a second."
units.japanese: 「戦人くん、待って！　念の為、部屋の戸締りを確認していくわ。ちょっと待ってね」

description: UP describes a singular gaping wound ‘on their necks,’ then directs the group's gaze ‘in’ Nanjo's knee and Kumasawa's ankle rather than to those body parts.
sourceReading: Each corpse has a gaping neck wound; the observers then look down, first to Nanjo's knee and then to Kumasawa's ankle, where the ritual objects are located.

units.text: That gaping wound on their necks definitely made me want to avert my eyes, but after seeing the Halloween party in the chapel, even though I thought it was horrible, it was no longer enough to make me feel sick.
