units.japanese:
そのばっくりと開いた首の傷は確かに目を背けたくなるものだったが、礼拝堂のハロウィンパーティを見た俺には、惨いとは思っても、もはや吐き気を催すほどのものではなかった。
それより、俺たちの目線は足元に向けられた。
南條先生の膝に。熊沢さんの足首に。……それぞれ、悪魔的な装飾のされたナイフか杭のようなものが刺し込まれているのだ。…朱志香の背中を貫いていたものと同じものに違いなかった。

units.text:
Instead, our gazes were directed to their legs.
In Doctor Nanjo's knee. In Kumasawa‐san's ankle. ......Driven into each of them was something like a knife or a stake with a demonic decoration. ...They would surely be the same as the one that had pierced Jessica's back.
units.japanese:
そのばっくりと開いた首の傷は確かに目を背けたくなるものだったが、礼拝堂のハロウィンパーティを見た俺には、惨いとは思っても、もはや吐き気を催すほどのものではなかった。
それより、俺たちの目線は足元に向けられた。
南條先生の膝に。熊沢さんの足首に。……それぞれ、悪魔的な装飾のされたナイフか杭のようなものが刺し込まれているのだ。…朱志香の背中を貫いていたものと同じものに違いなかった。

description: UP says the embedded object is ‘the same as Jessica-chan,’ grammatically equating the object with Jessica rather than saying the situation is the same as in Jessica's case.
sourceReading: Rosa observes that this is the same as what happened with Jessica and wonders whether it is an occult ritual.

units.text: "......What is this? ...It's the same as Jessica‐chan. Is this supposed to be some kind of occult ritual, I wonder?"
units.japanese: 「……これは何なの？　…朱志香ちゃんの時と同じね。何かオカルトの儀式のつもり、なのかしら？」

description: MG changes the group's shared expectations into Battler's alone when the opened bedroom reveals exactly what ‘my expectations’ anticipated.
sourceReading: The scene inside does not betray what the group collectively imagined from the door's condition.

units.text: Aunt Rosa told me to be on my guard, and I opened the door without really guarding myself in any way. And then, ......there was a scene laid out before us that didn't betray my expectations at all.
units.japanese: 楼座叔母さんが、用心してねというのを聞きながら、俺は特に何の用心もなく扉を開く。そして、………そこには、俺たちの想像を、まったく裏切らない光景が広がっていた。

description: UP places Shannon ‘face down over the front of the dresser’ rather than face down on the floor in front of it.
sourceReading: Shannon's body lies face down in a pool of blood in front of the dressing table.

units.text:
Shannon‐chan's body was face down over the front of the dresser, lying in a sea of blood. In its horribly broken mirror, sprayed with blood, had she seen her final worldly expression? ...Because she was face down, I couldn't see her face, but I could imagine even without seeing it. Nearby, in the sea of blood she lay in, a demon's stake had fallen... ......Only the fourth twilight was left.
Gouge the head and kill...
units.japanese:
紗音ちゃんの遺体は、化粧台の前にうつ伏せに、血の海に倒れていた。血の飛沫が飛び散り、醜く割れた鏡で、彼女はこの世で最後の自分の顔を見たのだろうか。…うつ伏せのため、彼女の顔は見えなかったが、見ずとも想像はついた。うつ伏せの血の海に、傍らに転がる悪魔の杭…。……残るのは第四の晩。
頭をえぐりて殺せ…。
candidates: face down over the front of the dresser

description: UP changes Shannon seeing her last face in this world into seeing her ‘final worldly expression.’
sourceReading: The narrator wonders whether Shannon saw her own face for the last time in the shattered, blood-spattered mirror.

units.text:
Shannon‐chan's body was face down over the front of the dresser, lying in a sea of blood. In its horribly broken mirror, sprayed with blood, had she seen her final worldly expression? ...Because she was face down, I couldn't see her face, but I could imagine even without seeing it. Nearby, in the sea of blood she lay in, a demon's stake had fallen... ......Only the fourth twilight was left.
Gouge the head and kill...
units.japanese:
紗音ちゃんの遺体は、化粧台の前にうつ伏せに、血の海に倒れていた。血の飛沫が飛び散り、醜く割れた鏡で、彼女はこの世で最後の自分の顔を見たのだろうか。…うつ伏せのため、彼女の顔は見えなかったが、見ずとも想像はついた。うつ伏せの血の海に、傍らに転がる悪魔の杭…。……残るのは第四の晩。
頭をえぐりて殺せ…。

description: UP generalizes Maria's warning from ‘the witch’ as a singular presence to witches as a plural class.
sourceReading: Maria says the witch is fickle and terrifying and may sometimes kill humans partly for amusement, but assures Battler he is safe with her.

units.text: "......It'll be alright, Battler. ......If you're with me, it'll be alright. .........Witches are very fickle, and they're terrifying beings who maybe kill humans for fun sometimes."
units.japanese: 「……大丈夫だよ、戦人。……真里亞と居れば、大丈夫。………魔女はとても気まぐれで、時に面白半分に人間を殺すかもしれない恐ろしい存在だけれども」

description: UP says Rosa finished ‘investigating their deaths’ where the source says she finished examining the three corpses.
sourceReading: After Rosa finishes her inspection of the three bodies, she expels the others, recovers both keys, and reseals the room.

units.text: After Auntie Rosa finished investigating their deaths, she proclaimed that she would seal this room again, chased the rest of us out, stole back the master key she had lent me, and locked the door again.
units.japanese: 楼座叔母さんは３人の検死が終わると、この部屋を再び封印すると宣言し、一方的に俺たちを追い出し、俺に預けたマスターキーを奪い返して、再び施錠した。

description: MG calls the key recovered from George merely ‘the key’ and omits that it is Natsuhi's room's original key, distinct from Rosa's master key.
sourceReading: Rosa recovers the master key from Battler and also the room's original key that George had possessed, then locks the room.

units.text: Apparently, George-aniki had been holding the key to Aunt Natsuhi's room. She also collected that.
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴が夏妃伯母さんの部屋の、本来の鍵を持っていたらしい。それも回収していた。

description: UP turns Rosa's possession of all master keys into the more specific physical claim that she had every master key ‘in her hand.’
sourceReading: Rosa has all master keys at hand or in her possession, while the room's original key was locked inside, producing the fourth closed-room inference.

units.text:
............Wait a second.
She had all of the master keys in her hand. And if the original key had been shut up inside that room, ......wasn't this another locked room? So this is a fourth locked room......?
units.japanese:
…………おいおい。
マスターキーは全て手元にある。そして本来の鍵が部屋に閉じ込められていたなら、……また密室じゃないか。第四の密室ってわけかよ……。

description: UP changes Beatrice having shown not even a trace of her presence into Battler personally not having sensed her.
sourceReading: Battler counts Grandfather and Beatrice, the nineteenth guest who has not shown even a sign of herself, among those not confirmed dead.

units.text: Now that we had been released from our suspicion of those three, ......we once again returned to the parlor. I don't have a clue what's going on anymore. ......If only the dead are safe, and everyone alive is a wolf, ......then all that's left is me, Auntie Rosa, Maria, and Genji‐san. ......Only those, Grandfather, and that 19th person—the guest who I hadn't even sensed— Beatrice.
units.japanese: 俺たちは、あの３人に対する疑いから解放され、……再び客間へ戻る。もう、何が何だかわからない。……死んでいる者だけが正しくて、生きている者が全て狼だと言うなら、……あとに残るは、俺に楼座叔母さんに真里亞、それに源次さん。……そして、祖父さまと、気配すら見せない１９人目の来客、ベアトリーチェだけ。

description: UP expands Genji's ‘one sincerity’ that wins trust into ‘a single unending faithfulness,’ importing duration from his following wish to remain faithful until the end.
sourceReading: Genji contrasts a hundred excuses with one act or quality of sincerity, then separately says he wants to remain sincere to the end even without their trust.

units.text: "...I believe that trust will be won not with a hundred excuses, but with a single unending faithfulness. ......Even if I am not able to gain your trust, I wish to be faithful until the end."
units.japanese: 「…私は、信頼を勝ち得るのは常に、百の言い訳ではなく、一つの誠実であると信じています。……たとえ信頼をいただけなくても、私は最後まで誠実でありたいと思います」

description: MG changes Rosa asking Genji to let her reconcile with him tomorrow into ‘please let us make up again,’ distributing the initiative and responsibility across both parties.
sourceReading: Rosa acknowledges her harsh treatment and asks Genji to allow her to make amends or reconcile with him the next day.

units.text: "......After your long years of service, I find it truly painful to treat you so poorly. ...But please understand about tonight. ...And, when tomorrow comes, please let us make up again."
units.japanese: 「………長年、右代宮家に仕えてくれたあなたにこんな仕打ちをするのは本当に心苦しいんだけれど。…今夜はわかってください。……そして、明日になったら、もう一度仲直りさせてください」
candidates: please let us make up again

description: UP narrows Rosa's statement that the room's security is intact to ‘the locks on the windows,’ then has Battler say the room was merely ‘closed’ instead of secured.
sourceReading: Rosa says there is no problem with the room's securing and calls it safe. Battler recalls that they verified its security, locked the room, returned to find it still secure, and cannot explain the letter's entry.

units.text: "......It's alright. There was no problem with the locks on the windows. This room is safe."
units.japanese:
「……大丈夫。戸締りに問題はないわ。この部屋は安全よ」
「いッ、いやその！　ここに置いてあったんだ。どうしてだよ？！　この部屋はちゃんと戸締りをしていたのに！！　どうしてだよ？！　どうして！！」

units.text: "W‐wait, err! It was just placed here. Why?! Even though we properly checked to make sure this room was closed!! Why?! Why!!"
units.japanese:
「……大丈夫。戸締りに問題はないわ。この部屋は安全よ」
「いッ、いやその！　ここに置いてあったんだ。どうしてだよ？！　この部屋はちゃんと戸締りをしていたのに！！　どうしてだよ？！　どうして！！」

description: UP twice changes the state ‘it had been left/was lying here’ into ‘it was just placed here,’ adding a recent placement event to Battler's account of the letter.
sourceReading: Battler tells Maria and Rosa that when he came back the envelope was lying there; he does not witness or date the act of placement.

units.text: "Ah, ......right. When I came here just now, ...i‐it was just placed here."
units.japanese:
「あ、……あぁ。今ここに来たら、…お、置いてあった」
「いッ、いやその！　ここに置いてあったんだ。どうしてだよ？！　この部屋はちゃんと戸締りをしていたのに！！　どうしてだよ？！　どうして！！」

units.text: "W‐wait, err! It was just placed here. Why?! Even though we properly checked to make sure this room was closed!! Why?! Why!!"
units.japanese:
「あ、……あぁ。今ここに来たら、…お、置いてあった」
「いッ、いやその！　ここに置いてあったんだ。どうしてだよ？！　この部屋はちゃんと戸締りをしていたのに！！　どうしてだよ？！　どうして！！」

description: MG reduces Rosa's explicit question ‘are you really Battler-kun, Rudolf nii-san's son?’ to ‘are you really that Battler-kun?’, omitting the parentage relation at the center of her impostor argument.
sourceReading: Rosa concedes that Ushiromiya Battler may be Rudolf's child, then asks whether the person present is really that Battler, Rudolf's son, before citing the six-year absence.

units.text: "...But are you really that Battler-kun?!"
units.japanese: 「……でも、あなた本当に留弗夫兄さんの息子の戦人くんなのぅ？！」

description: UP says Aunt Natsuhi's room is where George and the others ‘died,’ while the source and MG state only that they were found or lay dead there.
sourceReading: Battler argues that Natsuhi's room, in which George and the others were found dead, was locked; the statement locates the bodies without independently proving the place of death.

units.text: "The door to Aunt Natsuhi's room, where George‐aniki and the others died, was locked! George‐aniki was holding the key to that room, right?! And by now, the only one holding a master key is you! Weren't you the only one who could have locked that room?!?!"
units.japanese: 「譲治の兄貴たちが死んでいた、夏妃伯母さんの部屋には鍵が掛かってた！　部屋の鍵は譲治の兄貴が持っていたんだろ？！　そしてマスターキーを持ってるのは今や楼座叔母さんだけだぜッ？！　あの部屋に施錠できたのはあんただけじゃねぇかよッ？！？！」

description: MG omits Battler's explicit extension from himself, Maria, and Genji to ‘all the others’ when he rejects every human as the culprit.
sourceReading: Battler insists that Rosa cannot be the culprit, nor can he, Maria, Genji, or any of the others; he attributes everything to the witch.

units.text: "So there's no way you're the culprit, and there's no way Maria, Genji-san or I am either!! Why has it come to this?!!
units.japanese: 「だから、楼座叔母さんが犯人のわけがないし、俺や真里亞だって、そして源次さんだって他のみんなだって、犯人のわけがないんだああぁッ！！　どうしてこんなことにッ！！」

description: MG renders Kinzo's willingness to give up his life for Beatrice's smile as ‘I will not regret this life,’ changing the value of losing his life into retrospective regret about having lived it.
sourceReading: Kinzo says he does not care if he dies and would not begrudge or spare his life if he could see Beatrice's smile once more.

units.text: "......Beatrice, very soon, ...I will have a chance to be reunited with your smile. ......I care not if I die! If I can just see your smile one more time, I will not regret this life!
units.japanese: 「………ベアトリーチェ。もうじき、……お前の微笑みに再会できる。…………死んでもいい！　お前の微笑みがもう一度見られるならこの命は惜しくないッ！」

description: MG turns Battler's dark recognition that his ‘escort’ has finally come into the neutral realization that someone has come to greet him.
sourceReading: After waiting without resistance for the murderer or witch to kill him, Battler hears a knock and realizes that whoever has come to fetch him at death has finally arrived.

units.text: Then, ...someone knocked. Battler realized that someone had finally come to greet him...
units.japanese: その時、……ノックが鳴った。戦人はようやく自分のお迎えが来たことを悟る…。

description: UP changes the definite Golden Witch alternative into ‘a witch’ when Battler imagines who might come to kill him.
sourceReading: Battler contrasts the unseen murderer with the Golden Witch and hopes that, if it is the witch, she will take his life with spectacular magic.

units.text: He hadn't bothered to lock it. He did think that maybe the shapeless murderer, or the Golden Witch, might come to kill him now that he was isolated, but he no longer thought about resisting that.
units.japanese: 別に鍵は掛けていない。姿なき殺人犯、もしくは黄金の魔女が、一人ぼっちになった自分を殺しに来るかもしれないと思ったが、それに抗おうとはもう思わなかった。

description: MG removes Genji's probability marker and states categorically that Battler ‘will learn the truth.’
sourceReading: Genji says Battler will probably or presumably come to know the truth, then leaves acceptance, belief, or denial to him.

units.text: "Why? What? ...There is no need for questions like that. ...You will learn the truth, and that is all. I will leave it completely up to you, Battler-sama, whether to accept it, believe it, or deny it."
units.japanese: 「なぜ？　も。なに？　も。…何も必要ありません。…戦人さまはただ、真実を知ることになるでしょう。それをお認めになるか、お信じになるか、あるいは否定されるかも、全て戦人さまにお任せいたします」

description: UP changes Genji's silence reinforcing Battler's resignation into silence that makes him consider that resignation more deeply.
sourceReading: Battler feels Genji's silence further confirms or drives home his resigned expectation that he may not receive another chance to study.

units.text: Genji‐san's silence forced me to consider that resignation of mine more deeply...
units.japanese: 源次さんのその沈黙は、俺のある種の諦観を、さらに念押すものに感じられるのだった…。

description: MG turns the reception seating in front of the study desk into the malformed singular description ‘on a sofa like a reception chair,’ obscuring the room layout before Battler sees Kinzo's back.
sourceReading: In front of the study desk is a sofa reception area or guest seating, where Battler sees Kinzo from behind and someone opposite him.

units.text: It was almost like golden leaf confetti. The interior of Grandfather's study was filled with a golden glow... And, ...on a sofa like a reception chair in front of the study desk, ......I could see Grandfather's back.
units.japanese:
それはまるで、金箔の紙吹雪。
祖父さまの書斎の中は黄金の輝きで満たされていた…。そして、……書斎机の前にソファーの応接席があり、………祖父さまの背中が見えた。

description: UP changes Battler's challenge to make him understand or accept Beatrice's claim into a demand that she make him ‘admit’ it.
sourceReading: Battler challenges Beatrice to convince him that she truly is a witch capable of strange and magnificent great magic; if he submits, he will grant the promised kiss or anything else.

units.text: "...D‐............Damn you, talking so tough!! Yeah, alright. Try to make me admit it. ...Try to make me admit that you're a witch and that you can use weird, awesome, and great magic!!"
units.japanese: 「…で、…………でけぇ口を叩きやがって！！　あぁいいぜ。俺を納得させて見ろよ。…お前が間違いなく魔女さまで、不思議でステキな大魔法を使えるってことを納得させてみろよ！！」

description: UP initially makes Rosa reach toward multiple gold ingots and describes them collectively as heavy, where the source tracks one ingot before clarifying that it is one among the group.
sourceReading: Rosa reaches for a gold ingot; it is extremely heavy, she wraps that one in a blanket, and says even this single ingot should be worth over ten million.

units.text: Rosa finally arrived at the chapel. She pointed her gun around her, screaming the witch's name, but there was no way there would be an answer. After grimacing slightly, she noisily approached the table where her siblings' corpses were still exposed, and stretched out her arm towards the gold ingots.
units.japanese:
楼座はとうとう礼拝堂までやって来る。そして銃を辺りに向けながら魔女の名を叫ぶが、答えが返るはずもなかった。表情を少しだけ歪めた後、兄弟たちが未だに遺骸を晒すテーブルに踵を鳴らしながら近付き、黄金のインゴットに手を伸ばす。
それはあまりに重かったが、楼座は気にしない。
ブランケットにそのひとつを包み、担ぎ上げる。

units.text:
They were very heavy, but Rosa paid that no regard.
She wrapped one of them up in a blanket, and slung it over her shoulder.
units.japanese:
楼座はとうとう礼拝堂までやって来る。そして銃を辺りに向けながら魔女の名を叫ぶが、答えが返るはずもなかった。表情を少しだけ歪めた後、兄弟たちが未だに遺骸を晒すテーブルに踵を鳴らしながら近付き、黄金のインゴットに手を伸ばす。
それはあまりに重かったが、楼座は気にしない。
ブランケットにそのひとつを包み、担ぎ上げる。

description: MG changes Kinzo's realization ‘That's right; that was what I should have done’ into the approving exclamation ‘Isn't that splendid!’
sourceReading: Kinzo realizes the correct chess response, declares that he will sacrifice the rook, and resolves to lose everything necessary to reach Beatrice's king.

units.text: "......That's right. Isn't that splendid! I care not, I abandon that rook! You, woman, are a king that cannot be reached without the resolve to lose everything one has. I'll corner you, Beatriiiiice. Hihahahahahahahahahaha!"
units.japanese: 「…………そうだ。それで良かったのだ！　構わぬ、ルークを捨てるぞ！　持てるモノ全てを失う覚悟がなければ、至ることもできぬキングがお前という女なのだ。追い詰めるぞ、ベアトリーチェぇえぇ。ひっはははははははははは！」

description: MG's ‘What an truly elegant night’ uses an before an adverb and produces an ungrammatical exclamation.
sourceReading: Kinzo declares the night deeply pleasant and truly elegant as the chess game reaches its conclusion.

units.text: "...How pleasant! What an truly elegant night. Hehahahahahahaha...!!"
units.japanese: 「……心地よし！　実に優雅な夜だ。くっはっはっはっはっはっはっは…！！」

description: UP says Beatrice's feet were ‘sitting’ on the footrest, assigning a seated posture to her feet rather than saying they rested on it.
sourceReading: Beatrice lounges elegantly with her legs extended from the sofa and her feet resting on a footstool that is actually a human on all fours.

units.text: The witch was relaxing elegantly, her feet thrown out from the sofa and sitting on top of a footrest. ...However, the footrest wasn't a part of the sofa, ......it was a Humanhuman. Which was down on all fours......
units.japanese: 魔女はソファーから投げ出した足を足置き椅子に載せ、優雅に寛いでいた。…しかし、その足置き椅子はソファーの一部ではなく、……ニンゲンだった。四つん這いになった…。

description: MG weakens the narrator's rejection of real goat heads from ‘there is no way it is the latter’ to ‘it probably couldn't be the latter.’
sourceReading: The figures may be wearing goat masks or truly have goat heads. Although the latter should be impossible, the bizarre world makes the narrator seriously unsure which is true.

units.text: But they all had one thing in common, and that thing was exceedingly bizarre. ...Because all of them...had goat heads. Was it a goat mask masquerade, ......or did they really have goat heads? ...It probably couldn't be the latter, but in this bizarre world, I really didn't know which was true...
units.japanese: しかし、彼らは皆、ある一点で共通していて、そしてその点がこの上なく異様だった。……なぜなら、彼らは全て、…山羊の頭だったからだ。それが山羊の仮面による仮面舞踏会なのか、………本当に山羊の頭なのかはわからない。…後者のわけがないのだが、この異様な世界では、どちらかわからないと本気で考えてしまう…。

description: MG makes Beatrice’s close acquaintances “deeply intimate” without stating that their intimacy was with her, then has them embrace without an object; the source says those close to Beatrice embraced her.
sourceReading: The guests greet the revived Beatrice in turn, and those who had been close to her embrace her in joy at their reunion.

units.text: The goat nobles offered unanimous words of celebration in some long-forgotten language. And those who were deeply intimate embraced, filled with joy at their reunion. As the witch offered greetings of reunion, ...the witch's furniture followed behind her the whole time.
units.japanese: 山羊の貴族たちは、太古の失われた言語で口々に祝いの言葉を掛ける。そして親交の深かった者たちは、抱擁を交し合って再会を喜び合った。そうした魔女の再会の挨拶に、…魔女の家具はずっと付き従う。

description: MG calls the chained human furniture him and he before the Japanese narration first uses a male pronoun, prematurely specifying the captive’s gender in this local reveal sequence.
sourceReading: The narration initially refers only to the human furniture and its restraints, withholding a gendered pronoun until 彼 appears later in the scene at row 209.

units.text: ......There was a chain around its neck. The other end was gripped in the witch's hand, like it was a trained dog. It wasn't there to restrain him. ...Those chains were a restraining device whose only purpose was to wound the furniture's dignity... He wasn't permitted to wear anything else on his body.
units.japanese:
………首には鎖が。
そして魔女の手に飼い犬のように握られている。拘束のためのものではない。
…尊厳を傷つけるためだけの、拘束具…。それ以外には何も身に着けることが許されていなかった。

description: MG says Beatrice’s household members scattered into gold butterflies, presenting a transformation or dispersal; the source says they borrowed the form of golden butterflies.
sourceReading: As the boundary is cut open, the Golden Witch’s household celebrates her resurrection while taking the form of golden butterflies.

units.text: Surrounded by the goats' delighted voices, the mansion of the human world and the mansion of those not human overlapped, ...and the members of the household who praised the resurrection of the Golden Witch scattered into gold butterflies... and poured out of the depths of hell...
units.japanese: 山羊たちの歓喜の声の中、人の世の屋敷と、人ならざる者の屋敷が重なり、……黄金の魔女の復活を称える眷族たちが黄金の蝶の姿を借りて、……地獄の底より溢れ出す…。

description: UP uses the plural verb were with the singular subject “what the witches demanded,” producing a subject–verb agreement error.
sourceReading: The narration says the second realization was that what the witches demanded was not an autograph.

units.text: The goat nobles were suddenly crushing in around Kinzo. ...Almost like they were kids demanding the autograph of some famous movie star. There were two differences. First, they were witches, not kids. And second, what the witches demanded were not autographs.
units.japanese: 山羊の貴族たちは、いつの間にか金蔵を揉みくちゃにしていた。…まるで、人気のムービースターからサインをねだる子どもたちのように。違う点は二つ。一つは、彼らが子どもでなく魔女であったこと。そしてもう一つは、魔女たちが強請ったのはサインではなかったこと。

description: UP says Maria “tripped over” without supplying an object, leaving the phrasal verb grammatically incomplete where the source simply says she fell.
sourceReading: Maria falls while trying to keep up with Rosa.

units.text: Maria tripped over. Rosa, ashamed that for just an instant she had entertained thoughts of abandoning her daughter and running away, kicked back against the ground and instantly reversed direction. As Rosa's own child tried to stand, the goat‐head that had sprinted over to get the first bite grabbed a fistful of her hair and pulled her up from the back...!!
units.japanese: 真里亞が転ぶ。楼座は一瞬だけ、娘を見捨てて駆け去ることを考えたことを恥じ、大地を蹴り戻して瞬時に逆走する。起き上がろうとする我が娘の後ろ髪を、最初のひと齧りにありつこうと疾駆してきた山羊頭が鷲掴みにして引っ張り上げる…！！

description: UP combines “had always played” with “since she was a kid,” producing an awkward and normally incompatible perfect construction for Rosa’s long childhood familiarity with the grove.
sourceReading: Rosa had played in this area continuously or repeatedly since childhood, so she knows the grove and its shortcut.

units.text:
But Rosa knew. This path through the grove was only turning and twisting many times to make it seem long. She tore straight through it! She had always played here since she was a kid.
So she knew!
units.japanese:
しかし楼座は知っている。この木立の道は、わざわざ曲がりくねらせて距離感を出しているだけなのだ。まっすぐ突き抜ける！子どもの頃からずっと遊んでた。
だから知っている！

description: UP joins two independent clauses with only a comma in “I had the gold, it would have been worth several million yen,” creating a comma splice.
sourceReading: Rosa laments that she had obtained gold worth tens of millions of yen and might have been able to restart her life with it.

units.text:
Aaaaaaaaaaaaah, what am I doing...
I had the gold, it would have been worth several million yen. I might have been able to start over with that!! And yet I fell, lost it, and that's not all, my own life is in danger, even Maria's life is in danger?! ......What has my life been?!!!
units.japanese:
あああぁあぁぁ、私は何をやっているんだ…。
黄金を手に入れた、カネにすれば何千万円かになった。それで人生をやり直せたかも！！　なのに転げてなくし、それどころか自分の命も危なくて、真里亞の命まで危なくてッ？！……私の人生って、何だったのッ！！！
candidates: gold, it would have been worth several million yen

description: MG replaces Rosa’s explicit older brother and older sister with the generic plural “older siblings,” dropping the source’s gender and one-of-each family detail.
sourceReading: Rosa rages that she was born into this incomprehensible family with an irritating older brother and an irritating older sister.

units.text: I was born into an incomprehensible family! With irritating older siblings since the day I was born!! What did I do?! No matter what I did or didn't do, I was always in trouble and bullied and made fun of!! What has my life been?!?!
units.japanese:
わけのわかんない家に生まれて！
生まれた時からムカつく兄と姉がいて！！私が何をしたの？！何をしてもしなくてもいっつも怒られて虐められて馬鹿にされてッ！！　私の人生は何だったの？！？！

description: MG reduces Rosa’s near-certainty that the tea must have been prepared for her to the weaker “probably.”
sourceReading: Rosa sees tea laid out and concludes that it was presumably, indeed surely, prepared for her.

units.text: She could see a room that looked like a parlor. ...And there was some tea that had been prepared. It had probably been made for her. Around the room, some glitter that looked like gold leaf drifted about, making the scene look quite fantastical. ...When she eventually realized that they were gold butterflies, it further strengthened that impression.
units.japanese:
そこは、客間のような部屋に見えました。……そしてそこにはお茶の用意がありました。
恐らく、自分の為に用意されているに違いありません。部屋の中に金箔のようなキラキラが舞っていて、とても幻想的でした。…それはやがて黄金の蝶であるとわかり、さらにそれを際立たせるのでした。

description: UP ends Rosa’s internal question “What is she...talking about” with a period, changing the explicitly interrogative thought into a statement fragment.
sourceReading: Still mentally fogged, Rosa wonders what Beatrice is talking about and repeats that she does not know.

units.text: ............What is she...talking about. ...I don't know, ...I don't know.
units.japanese: …………何の話を、しているのだろう。…わからない、…わからない。

description: UP’s “a mountain of gold, like I gave to Kinzo” omits the comparative object and produces a malformed clause where the source refers to the mountain of gold Beatrice gave him.
sourceReading: Beatrice says giving Rosa a mountain of gold, as she gave one to Kinzo, would be effortless.

units.text: "I am commonly called the Golden Witch. Bestowing a mountain of gold, like I gave to Kinzo, is no problem for me. ......After all, every pleasure of the human world can be expressed in terms of cash. Put another way, gold is human pleasure itself."
units.japanese: 「妾の通り名は黄金の魔女。金蔵に与えたように、山成す黄金を与えることは造作もない。……何しろ、人の世の快楽は全てカネで換算できる。即ち、黄金こそが人の世の快楽そのものなのだ」
candidates: mountain of gold, like I gave to Kinzo

description: MG generalizes the pipe’s explicitly seven-colored smoke to merely multicolored smoke.
sourceReading: When Beatrice blows on her pipe, smoke of seven colors surrounds the room before the gold ingots appear.

units.text: As the witch blew on her pipe, multi-colored smoke enshrouded their surroundings. As she did this, the inside of the parlor...was suddenly filled with stacks of gold ingots. It looked like a shining gold-colored wall. ...If each ingot was worth several ten million yen, how much would all of this be worth? It seemed sinful to even think of such a number.
units.japanese: 魔女が煙管を吹かすと、七色の煙が辺りを包みました。すると、客間の中は、…いつの間にか積み上げた黄金のインゴットでいっぱいになっていました。それは眩い黄金色の壁のようにも見えます。…インゴットひとつで数千万円の価値があるのだとしたら、ここにある全てで一体いくらくらいになるというのでしょう。その数字を知ることすら罪深く感じられるのでした。

description: MG changes the things no amount of gold can satisfy into things gold cannot “settle,” replacing emotional fulfillment with resolution or payment.
sourceReading: Beatrice knows that some human needs remain unfulfilled no matter how high gold is piled, leaving voids money cannot fill.

units.text: "...However, the human world is difficult. I know there are some things that cannot be settled, no matter how high into the sky you pile up gold. I know there are cracks that cannot be filled.
units.japanese: 「……しかし、人の世は難しい。どれほど空高く積み上げた黄金であろうとも、満たされぬものがあることを知っている。埋められぬ隙間があることを知っている」

description: MG invents gratitude by telling Rosa there is “No need to thank me out loud”; the source only says she need not voice the wish or void Beatrice claims to read from her face.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Rosa need not put her desire into words because the void in her heart is visible on her face.

units.text: "...No need to thank me out loud. I can tell right away. It's written on your face and in the corners of your heart, *cackle*cackle*!"
units.japanese: 「……口にせずとも良い。そなたの心の隙間など、顔に書いてあるからすぐにわかるぞ、くっくっく！」
candidates: need to thank me out loud

description: UP says a wound may have to be opened “once,” omitting 今一度 and losing that it must be opened once again after having closed over the embedded fragment.
sourceReading: A wound that closed around a fragment may need to be reopened in order to heal completely.

units.text: "......This is... ...deep, deep. ......Sometimes, wounds close up while a fragment of something is still inside. ...Even when those wounds appear to have healed, they will continue to throb for all eternity. Sometimes you have to open the wound once to completely heal it."
units.japanese: 「……これは、……深い、深い。……時に、破片を飲み込んだまま傷口が閉じてしまうこともある。…そういう傷は見た目には癒えていても、永遠に疼きを感じ続けるものだ。完全に治すために、今一度、傷口を開くこともあろう」

description: MG breaks the parallel modal construction in “I might rewind time, and giving you a world,” using a gerund where the coordinated verb must be “give.”
sourceReading: Beatrice says she could rewind time and give Rosa a world in which she had no elder siblings.

units.text: "...How can I heal you? It's possible, but not easy. ...I might rewind time, and giving you a world where you have no older siblings."
units.japanese: 「……どうやって癒すのか。可能ではあるが簡単ではない。…時間を巻き戻し、そなたに兄と姉がいなかった世界を与えることもできよう」
candidates: rewind time, and giving you a world

description: MG invents exactly two goat-headed servants when the Japanese gives no number.
sourceReading: After Beatrice claps, goat-headed servants are present around Rosa and begin preparing and serving the meal; their number is unspecified.

units.text: As the witch clapped twice, there were suddenly two goat head servants there, and they began to prepare the meal. From the beautiful dishes adorning the table, they efficiently took some food and began to pile it up on Rosa's plate.
units.japanese: 魔女が手をパンパンと叩くと、いつの間にか周りには山羊頭の使用人たちがいて、食事の準備を始めていました。彼らはテーブルを飾る美しき料理皿から、要領よく料理を取り、楼座の皿を盛り上げていきました。

description: UP omits the explicit “living blood” that Rosa is forced to drink, recasting the sentence around her brother repeatedly dying to color the wine.
sourceReading: The wine is sweet because it contains the fresh blood of the brother Rosa hated, with its red color gathered through dozens of repeated deaths.

units.text: It was definitely a fragrant sweetness. Her brother, who she had thought of so hatefully, and who had made her soak her pillow so many times, had died dozens of times over to tinge this wine crimson, so it must have tasted sweet. But Rosa tried to spit it out. Because of that, the deep red wine that spilled out of Rosa's mouth made her look as if she was covered in blood.
units.japanese: それは間違いなく芳香のある甘み。あれほど憎く思い枕を何度も濡らした兄の生き血を、何十も繰り返した死で集めた紅みで染めたワインが、甘くないわけがありません。でも、楼座は吐き出そうとしました。そのせいで、楼座は口から溢れた真っ赤なワインでまるで血塗れのように見えました。

description: MG says the wine spilling from Rosa’s mouth “looked just like a bloodstain,” assigning the resemblance to the liquid; the source says Rosa herself looked covered in blood.
sourceReading: As Rosa spits out the red wine, the liquid overflowing from her mouth makes her look as though she is covered in blood.

units.text: It definitely was a fragrant sweetness. The living blood of her brother, who had given her such hateful thoughts and made her soak her pillow so many times, had been collected from his death, repeated dozens of times. How could the crimson-stained wine not be sweet? But Rosa tried to spit it out. Because of that, the deep red wine that spilled out of Rosa's mouth looked just like a bloodstain.
units.japanese: それは間違いなく芳香のある甘み。あれほど憎く思い枕を何度も濡らした兄の生き血を、何十も繰り返した死で集めた紅みで染めたワインが、甘くないわけがありません。でも、楼座は吐き出そうとしました。そのせいで、楼座は口から溢れた真っ赤なワインでまるで血塗れのように見えました。
candidates: Rosa's mouth looked just like a bloodstain

description: MG switches Maria from directly addressing Rosa to third person in “Maybe she’ll eat me and think I’m delicious,” weakening the child’s immediate plea to her mother.
sourceReading: Maria asks Rosa directly whether, by eating Maria and finding her delicious, Mama might finally feel glad that Maria existed.

units.text: "And then, maybe Mama will be happy I exist for the first time. Maybe she'll eat me and think I'm delicious.
units.japanese: 「そしたら、ママに初めて真里亞がいてよかったって思ってもらえるかな。真里亞を食べて、美味しかったって思ってもらえるかな」
candidates: Maybe she'll eat me and think I'm delicious

description: UP changes Rosa’s plea “forgive me” to “let me go,” replacing remorse and a request for pardon with a request for physical release.
sourceReading: Rosa begs for the ordeal to stop and asks to be forgiven before pleading that no more food be put in her mouth.

units.text: "Please stop, please let me go!! No, stop it already, don't put it...in my mouth... uuuuulg, gweeeeeeeeeeeeehh!!"
units.japanese: 「もうやめて、もう許して！！　嫌、もうやめて、口に、入れないで…、ううぅぐッ、げぇえええぇッ！！」

description: UP leaves the phrasal verb incomplete in “methods by which you tried to talk yourself out,” omitting what Battler tried to talk his way out of.
sourceReading: Beatrice says her red statements crushed most of Battler’s evasive excuses in the many closed-room problems and asks what sophistry he will try next.

units.text: "And while we're waiting, I have much I want to hear from you! There were many locked rooms in this game. Using red, I've smashed to bits most of the methods by which you tried to talk yourself out. What other evasive quibbles will you show me now?!!"
units.japanese: 「その間に貴様にはたっぷりと聞かせてもらおうではないか。此度のゲームでは密室も多いぞ。そなたの逃げ口上のほとんどを妾が赤で叩き潰した。その上でさらにどのような屁理屈で言い逃れてみせるのかッ！！」
candidates: methods by which you tried to talk yourself

description: UP adds “goddamn” to Battler’s closing catchphrase although the Japanese intensifies it through repetition and shouting without profanity.
sourceReading: Battler shouts his repeated catchphrase: “It’s no good—It’s completely no good!”

units.text: "Aaah, it's no good, it's no goddamn good at aaaaaa{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-aaaaaaallllll!!!"
units.japanese: 「ああ駄目だぜ、全然駄目だッうをおああああああああああああああぁああぁあああああぁあッ！！！」

description: UP renders Beatrice’s criticism 手厳しい as “How remorseless,” assigning lack of mercy rather than saying Bernkastel’s evaluation is severe or harsh.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Bernkastel remains a harsh grader and calls her dismissive response severe.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*. My, my, a harsh critic as always. ......And I was so certain that even Lady Bernkastel, who has no love for boredom, would surely be satisfied by this compelling development... How remorseless."
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっく、これはこれは、相変わらずお点が辛い。……退屈を愛さないベルンカステル卿に相応しい迫力ある展開だったと自負していただけにこれは手厳しい」

description: UP uses the malformed progressive “It is pleasing me too” for Bernkastel’s simple statement that she too finds the prospect enjoyable.
sourceReading: Bernkastel says she too is pleased and came specifically to watch the confident Beatrice lose badly.

units.text: "......Yes. It is pleasing me too. After all, I came all this way just because I wanted to see you brimming with that confidence, only to fall apart and lose."
units.japanese: 「……えぇ。私も愉快よ。そこまで自信満々のあなたがボロボロに負けるところが見たくて、遥々やって来たんだもの」

description: MG changes Beatrice’s invitation to enjoy the valuable relationship or connection created by this occasion into enjoying their “precious time together.”
sourceReading: Beatrice welcomes Lambdadelta and proposes that they enjoy the valuable bond or encounter this occasion has created.

units.text: "That would be well. "Going easy" has never been written in my dictionary. *cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*! Lady Lambdadelta, let us enjoy our precious time together."
units.japanese: 「それが良かろう。元より、妾の辞書に手加減の文字はないのでな。くっくっくくくくくくくく！　ラムダデルタ卿、この度の貴重な縁を楽しもうではないか」

description: UP renders 見させてもらった as “I took a glimpse,” removing the permission or benefit expressed by being allowed to see part of Beatrice’s game.
sourceReading: Bernkastel says she was allowed a glimpse of Beatrice’s game and then offers advice from what she saw.

units.text: Certainly, that child's game is quite unfair. I took a glimpse of the game board, and the tricks are so mean and cunning, and the scenic tricks are filthy to a degree that probably far surpasses that of Lambdadelta's game board.
units.japanese: 確かにあの子のゲームはあまりに卑劣。ゲーム盤を少しだけ見させてもらったけど、あまりに卑劣かつ狡猾な仕掛けで、その舞台仕掛けの嫌らしさは多分、ラムダデルタのゲーム盤のそれを遥かに上回るわ。

description: MG adds the profanity “fucked up so bad” where Lambdadelta only says that seeing Bernkastel’s piece in such a sorry state feels wonderful.
sourceReading: Lambdadelta delights in the pathetic condition of Bernkastel’s piece.

units.text: Because of that, I won't be able to rest until I see Bern's speechless face. And since you, Bern's piece, fucked up so bad, I'm feeling just great! Plus, she may not look it, but that girl really hates to lose, so I'll bet she's off somewhere grinding her teeth and crying her eyes out right now. How totally lame, *giggle*, hoohohohohohohohoh!
units.japanese: そんなわけで、この私は、ベルンがぎゃふんとする顔を見ないと腹の虫が収まらないわけ。そんなわけなんで、ベルンの駒のあんたがそんなザマなんで、私は最高にいい気分なわけ！しかもあの子はあれでいて本当に負けず嫌いだから、きっと今頃悔しくって歯軋りをして涙をぽろぽろ流してるわよ、本当にざまぁないわよ、くすくす、ほーっほっほっほっほっほ！

description: MG translates 余裕ぶった as Beatrice acting “so tough,” changing a display of composure or ease into toughness.
sourceReading: Lambdadelta cannot understand why Beatrice puts on such an air of composure while lowering her own chances of victory.

units.text: She sometimes mistakes her means for her ends. And she has too much dark fun. Sometimes, that even ends up creating and exposing her own weak points. For a super-powerful witch like me, it's hard to understand why she's able to act so tough. Why she lowers her own chances of winning.
units.japanese: 手段と目的を時に履き違える。そして悪い遊びが過ぎる。その結果、自ら弱点を作り晒してさえいる。私のような最強の魔女から見れば、何でこんな余裕ぶったことをするのか理解できない。自ら勝率を下げてるなんてね。

description: UP renders 素直で正直 as “obedient and honest,” replacing straightforward or direct predictability with submissiveness.
sourceReading: Lambdadelta characterizes herself as straightforward and honest in contrast with Beatrice’s indirect play.

units.text: .........But, well. That's why the type of witch like Bern who reads her opponent and dodges their moves has a really bad matchup with her. 'Cause reading her doesn't work. ...It's probably really easy for Bern to read and handle an obedient and honest type like me. That makes me so mad!
units.japanese: ………でも、ま。そのせいで、ベルンみたいな、相手を読んでかわすタイプの魔女には非常に相性が悪いってわけよ。読みが効かないから。…ベルンにとっては、私みたいな素直で正直なタイプは、読みやすくてやりやすいんでしょうね。ムカつくことに！

description: MG contains the typographical error “Bascially” for “Basically.”
sourceReading: The sentence opens with a normal summarizing transition.

units.text: Well, maybe that doesn't matter. Even though my paper loses to Bern's scissors, if I was a sheet of super-paper, which is way more awesome than normal paper, I could beat even scissors, right?! Bascially, I, Lady Lambdadelta, am {ruby:a moron:super-paper! Hohohohoh!
units.japanese: まー、どうでもいいことかしら。確かに私のパーはベルンのチョキに負けるけど、パーよりはるかに凄い超パーだったら、チョキにだって勝てるでしょ？！つまりこのラムダデルタ卿は、超パーってわけ！ほっほっほっほ！

description: UP renders 趣味の悪い as “nasty hobbies,” literalizing 趣味 and changing Beatrice’s bad taste into a claim about her activities.
sourceReading: Lambdadelta calls Beatrice’s taste bad while speculating about why she prolongs the game.

units.text: It looks like the color's come back to your face a little. That Beato, she's having fun torturing some piece called Rosa. At a glance, you'd think she has really nasty hobbies, right?
units.japanese: 少しは血色が戻ってきたみたいね。ベアトのヤツ、楼座とかいう駒を虐めて遊んでるわ。一見すると本当に趣味の悪いヤツだと思うでしょ？

description: MG coordinates past “was ... worried” with present “choose” in the same account of selecting lunch, breaking the intended past-tense narration. UP correctly uses chose.

units.text: But with Shannon beside me, this buffet felt different. I couldn't shamefully pile on only the things I liked. I was...how should I put it...worried about my appearance and choose a menu suited for a snob: toast, salad and coffee. If I'd been by myself, I would've made a pile of oily stuff like yakisoba, mashed potatoes, gratin, and so on.
units.japanese:
でも、紗音と一緒のバイキングは違う。
好きなものだけみっともなく山盛りにできない。何て言うのかその、…見栄えを気にしてしまい、トーストにサラダにコーヒーなんて、キザったらしいメニューにしてしまう。僕ひとりだったなら、焼きそばやマッシュポテトにグラタン等の油っぽいのを山盛りにしてるところだ。

description: George says they had only exchanged greetings at infrequent family gatherings. MG reduces this to only meeting at those gatherings, dropping the limited interaction that grounds his surprise at their present intimacy. UP explicitly restores only ever exchange greetings.

units.text: "I'm also surprised. I didn't just meet you yesterday or today, Shannon-chan. We've known each other for years now. However, we can only meet during those family meetings that only happen a few times a year.
units.japanese: 「僕もびっくりしてるよ。紗音ちゃんと出会ったのは、昨日今日のことじゃない。何年も前から面識もある。でも、年に何度もない親族の会合の席で挨拶をするだけ」

description: Shannon wonders whether men cannot be persuaded to believe such things. MG makes it categorical: no matter how often you tell men, they will never believe it. UP preserves conjectural perhaps.

units.text: ...No matter how often you tell men something like this, they'll never believe it. Kanon-kun didn't believe me at all either."
units.japanese: 「…男の方に、いくら言ってもこういうのは信じてもらえないんでしょうか。嘉音くんも全然信じてくれませんし」
candidates: matter how often you tell men

description: Narrator has only just learned how to operate the motorboat. UP instead says she had just been told about the boat, changing newly acquired operational instruction into merely learning of its existence. MG preserves just learned how to use.

units.text:
Taking a motorboat that I had just been told about, I made my way to this islet. No, I couldn't possibly call it an islet.
It'd really be more appropriate to call it a reef.
units.japanese:
私は、教えてもらったばかりのモーターボートで、この小島にやって来た。いや、小島とは到底呼べない。
岩礁と呼んだ方が正しいだろう。

description: Source describes this self-imposed ordeal as small yet large. UP makes these plural small and large trials, replacing one paradoxically assessed act with distinct categories of ordeals. MG preserves a small yet large trial.

units.text:
Come, have courage. I'll free myself from being mere furniture.
And I'll accept my new sufferings, and become human.
These are surely the small and large trials I must impose on myself.
units.japanese:
さぁ、勇気を。そして私を家具から解放しよう。
そして新たな苦しみを受け入れることで、人間となろう。
これは自分に課す、きっと小さくて大きな試練。

description: Source contrasts many days of inner conflict with a recollection far too brief to match them. MG says merely finishing reflections in the blink of an eye, preserving brevity but losing the disproportionate relation. UP restores far too brief to do them justice.

units.text: I raise the mirror high... ...I think back on the days of conflict that came before... ...And, finishing my reflections in the blink of an eye, ... I throw it down.
units.japanese: それを振り上げ、………私は、今日までの葛藤の日々を思い返し、……それに見合わぬほどわずかな時間で回想を終えて、……叩き付けた。
candidates: reflections in the blink of an eye

description: MG turns the continuing marital characterization that Hideyoshi is almost certainly under Eva’s thumb into the narrower observation that there was little doubt who got her way “in that exchange.”
sourceReading: Rudolf sees Hideyoshi retreat to the deck after Eva’s scolding and concludes that Hideyoshi is almost certainly henpecked or under her thumb.

units.text: Hideyoshi laughed heartily, but Rudolf snickered. After being scolded by Eva, they'd escaped to the deck together with their tails between their legs. There was little doubt who had gotten her way in that exchange.
units.japanese: 秀吉は豪快そうに笑って見せるが、留弗夫はくすりと笑う。絵羽に表で吸えと叱られて、一緒にすごすごと甲板に逃げ出してきたのだ。尻に敷かれているに、ほぼ間違いあるまい。

description: MG replaces Eva’s disgust at Krauss switching his first-person pronoun from rough 俺 to formal 私 with remarks about “noble sentiments” and “flowery prose,” erasing the linguistic evidence that he has begun performing the role of family head.
sourceReading: Eva mocks Krauss for suddenly calling himself watashi when he used ore until recently, reading the pronoun change as pretension to the headship.

units.text: "That's just disgusting. What's this about "noble sentiments"? I'd call that flowery prose, coming from you. Are you pretending to be the Head already?"
units.japanese: 「気持ち悪い。何が“私”よ。この間まで“俺”だったくせに。もう当主気取りなの？」

description: MG misspells “undoubtedly” as “undoubtably.”
sourceReading: Krauss concedes that Eva is unquestionably the eldest daughter of the glorious Ushiromiya family.

units.text: "Yes, it is bizarre. You undoubtably are the oldest daughter of the glorious Ushiromiya family. One day, you will support that family crest by being wed to the partner most valuable for Father.
units.japanese: 「あぁ、おかしいね。お前は確かに栄光ある右代宮家の長女だよ。やがてはその家紋を背負って、父にとってもっとも価値ある相手と婚約することになるだろう」
candidates: daughter of the glorious Ushiromiya family

description: MG makes Krauss say he must correct Eva before she “leave[s] this family,” while 社会に出る means before she enters society or adult public life; marriage out of the family is a separate later claim.
sourceReading: Krauss claims that as Eva’s brother he must correct her supposed misunderstanding before she goes out into society.

units.text: "Most women realize this without being told. They realize it on their own. ...But even after all these years, you still haven't realized that about yourself. So I've decided to clear away that misunderstanding for you before you leave this family. You ought to thank me."
units.japanese: 「それは本来、言葉で気付かされることではない。自ずと気付くことだ。…しかしお前は、いくつになってもそれを自覚しなかったな。だから社会に出る前に、兄である私がその誤解を解くのだよ。感謝して欲しいものだね」

description: MG renders 長男が聞いて呆れる as Kinzo being “embarrassed to hear this from my eldest son,” instead of saying Krauss is a disgrace or mockery of the title eldest son.
sourceReading: Kinzo scorns Krauss as a disgraceful excuse for an eldest son and immediately slaps him.

units.text: "Krauss, are you fighting with your siblings again? Why don't you have the dignity to act as a leader for your brother and sisters? How shameful! I'm embarrassed to hear this from my eldest son!"
units.japanese: 「蔵臼。また兄弟喧嘩か。お前にはなぜに弟や妹たちを率いる貫禄が宿らぬのか。情けない！　長男が聞いて呆れるぞ！」
candidates: embarrassed to hear this from my eldest son

description: MG omits “of” in “As a member the Ushiromiya family,” producing an ungrammatical noun phrase during Eva’s interrupted plea.
sourceReading: Eva begins to say that as a member of the Ushiromiya family she will not bring shame to Kinzo’s name.

units.text: "A-As a member the Ushiromiya family, I won't bring shame to your na-"
units.japanese: 「わ、私は右代宮家の人間として、お父様の名に恥ずかしくない、」

description: MG changes Krauss’s claim that he has just admonished Eva on precisely this issue into the habitual “that’s just what I’m always telling Eva,” weakening his immediate lie or intervention to protect her from Kinzo.
sourceReading: Krauss tells Kinzo that he has just finished warning Eva about the same problem and claims she promised to change, buying her time to leave.

units.text: "Father, that's just what I'm always telling Eva. Eva has promised that she will have a change of heart and act like a lady. Couldn't you postpone that decision for just a little longer?"
units.japanese: 「お父さん、それは私からよく絵羽に言い聞かせたところです。絵羽もこれからは心を入れ替えて、レディとして振舞うと約束してくれました。どうかもう少しの猶予をいただけませんか」
candidates: that's just what I'm always telling Eva

description: MG misspells “threatening” as “threating” in Eva’s self-questioning account of using her grades against Krauss.
sourceReading: Eva wonders whether she earned grades that threatened or intimidated Krauss merely to discharge childhood resentment.

units.text: ...But doesn't that mean my love of learning comes entirely from a stupid complex I've got against Nii-san? Father wanted me to become a lady with whom he could go out in public and not be embarrassed. ...Did I betray his hopes, earning good grades and threating Nii-san just to satisfy a childhood resentment...?
units.japanese: …だとしたら、私の向学心の根底は、兄へのつまらぬコンプレックスだけではないか。父は私に、社交界へ連れて行っても恥ずかしくないレディを期待した。…それを私が裏切って、兄を脅かす成績を当て付け、幼少の頃の恨み辛みを晴らしていただけ…？

description: MG uses the ungrammatical construction “letting you to succeed” where English requires either “letting you succeed” or “allowing you to succeed.”
sourceReading: Young Eva says her magic has repeatedly saved adult Eva from crises and enabled achievements that should have been impossible.

units.text: "Then let's use that anger to fuel our learning. ...Changing anger into power is my magic. I've saved you from a bunch of tight spots with that power, letting you to succeed when you shouldn't have. As long as you have my magic, there's nothing you can't do."
units.japanese: 「ならば、その怒りを勉強に費やしましょうよ。……怒りを力に換えるのが私の魔法。この力で、何度もあなたの窮地を救い、あなたは成せないはずのことを成し遂げてきた。私の魔法がある限り、あなたに出来ないことなど有りはしないわ」

description: UP adds the profanity “fucking” to young Eva’s wish that Kinzo and Krauss would hurry up and die; the Japanese is hostile but contains no corresponding obscenity.
sourceReading: Young Eva calls Kinzo and Krauss the worst male chauvinists and wishes they would hurry up and die.

units.text: "...Father and Krauss are the worst kind of male supremacists. I wish they'd just fucking die already."
units.japanese: 「…お父様も蔵臼も、最低の男尊主義者だわ。早く死んじゃえばいいのに」

description: UP renders 滅多なことでは口にできない as words Eva could not say “carelessly,” suggesting insufficient caution rather than words she could hardly or rarely bring herself to utter.
sourceReading: The younger self voices harsh curses on Eva’s behalf that adult Eva could not readily bring herself to say.

units.text: ......She would curse in my place. Words that I couldn't say carelessly, ...she would say for me. ...Even though I understood that she was just another part of myself inside of me, ...I felt like she was the only ally I had who would sympathize with me.
units.japanese: ……彼女は、私の代わりに悪態を付く。私には滅多なことでは口にできない言葉を、…彼女が私に代わって口にしてくれる。…内なるもうひとりの自分であるとわかっていても、…私にとっては、唯一同情してくれる味方なのだ。

description: MG says sympathy might do “a lot” to calm Eva’s heart, while 幾分か limits the relief to some degree or somewhat.
sourceReading: Eva recognizes that sympathy may ease her heart somewhat but cannot improve the actual situation.

units.text: However, while sympathy might do a lot to calm my heart, it won't do anything to improve my current situation. ...In the end, she can only console me for however long it takes me to be dejected by reality...before I finally accept it.
units.japanese: だが、同情は心を幾分か楽にしてくれるかもしれないが、現状を何も改善してはくれない。……結局、現実に落胆し、それを受け容れるのに必要な時間分だけ、心を慰めてくれるだけなのだ。
candidates: sympathy might do a lot to calm

description: UP changes Eva’s goal of becoming a lady who can enter high society proudly into becoming someone Father can take out and boast about, transferring agency and pride from Eva to Kinzo.
sourceReading: Eva considers whether she should become the sort of lady Kinzo expects—one able to appear in high society with her own head held high.

units.text: Shouldn't I aim to become the kind of lady that Father hoped for, someone he can take out into society and boast about? Father might take a better view of me if I were reborn. ......Maybe my brother could find his own lifestyle, and I could find mine.
units.japanese: お父様の期待するような、社交界に胸を張って出られる淑女を目指すべきなのではないだろうか。お父様も、生まれ変わった私を見直してくれるかもしれない。……兄は兄、私は私で、それぞれの生き方を見つけられるかもしれない。

description: MG says Eva might find her own way “just as Nii-san has found his,” asserting that Krauss has already found a way of life; the source only imagines that brother and sister might each find their respective paths.
sourceReading: Eva imagines that Krauss can be Krauss and she can be herself, with each perhaps finding a distinct way to live.

units.text: Maybe I should aim to become the kind of lady Father wants, someone who can proudly participate in high society. And if I'm reborn, maybe Father will change his opinion of me. ...Maybe I can find my own lifestyle, just as Nii-san has found his.
units.japanese: お父様の期待するような、社交界に胸を張って出られる淑女を目指すべきなのではないだろうか。お父様も、生まれ変わった私を見直してくれるかもしれない。……兄は兄、私は私で、それぞれの生き方を見つけられるかもしれない。

description: MG calls Jessica “a delinquent” in both grades and behavior, while 不良 here says those qualities are poor or bad; it does not label Jessica herself a delinquent.
sourceReading: Eva disparages Jessica’s grades and conduct as poor, then invokes Jessica’s sex while arguing for George as heir.

units.text: "G-George is a son I'm proud of, one who won't embarrass himself no matter where he goes...! The dream I wasn't granted might come true for George...! Jessica's a delinquent in both her grades and her behavior. And she's a woman! If only Jessica would step down, George would become the heir...!"
units.japanese: 「じょ、譲治はどこに出しても恥ずかしくない自慢の息子よ…！　私には叶えられなかった夢を、譲治なら叶えられるかもしれない…！　朱志香なんて成績も品行も不良じゃない。それに女なのよ！　朱志香さえ辞退してくれれば、譲治が跡継ぎになることだって…！」

description: MG misspells “embarrassing” as “embarassing” when Eva apologizes for being seen asleep.
sourceReading: Eva says she showed everyone an embarrassing side of herself and apologizes.

units.text: "...Maybe. I let you all see something embarassing. I'm sorry."
units.japanese: 「……まぁね。恥ずかしいところを見せちゃったわ。ごめんなさい」

description: UP renders 苦手 as things everyone “doesn’t like,” changing Battler’s defensive claim that everyone has one or two weaknesses or things they cannot handle into personal dislikes.
sourceReading: Embarrassed by his fear during the trip, Battler protests that everyone has one or two things they are bad at or unable to handle.

units.text: "Sh‐shut up! Everyone has one or two things they don't like...!"
units.japanese: 「う、うるせーな。人間誰しも苦手のひとつやふたつくらいあるもんだぜ…！」
candidates: Everyone has one or two things

description: MG says Eva’s “hopes got in the way a bit,” while 思惑が多少混じる concedes that her own designs or ulterior aims were mixed into George’s upbringing; obstruction is substituted for mixed motive.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi reassures Eva that even if her personal designs entered into how she raised George, the result turned out well.

units.text: "That isn't true. George is our wonderful son, and he'll always perform admirably wherever he goes. Eva, even if you let your own hopes get in the way a bit, everythin' turned out okay in the end, hasn't it?!
units.japanese: 「そんなことあらへん。譲治はどこに出しても恥ずかしゅうない、わしらの自慢の息子や。仮に、絵羽の思惑が多少混じっとったとしても、結果オーライっちゅうもんやないか！」

description: MG misspells “something” as “someting” in Eva’s reflection that troubling Hideyoshi is not what a good wife does.
sourceReading: Eva forces herself to stand because continuing to burden Hideyoshi with her bad mood is not conduct befitting a good wife.

units.text: Even Eva had to stand up without grumbling now. ...She had to stop forcing her bad mood onto her husband and causing him any more trouble. ...Because that wasn't someting a "good wife" would do.
units.japanese: 絵羽も、さすがに愚図らず立ち上がる。…これ以上、自分の不機嫌に夫を振り回し、迷惑を掛けることはできない。……それは“良妻”のすることではないのだから。

description: UP generalizes Eva’s near-lightheadedness into bright sunlight being enough to make “a person” go giddy, losing Eva as the experiencer and weakening the physical near-sensation into an ambiguous term that can mean excitement or silliness.
sourceReading: When Eva steps into the strong sunlight, she genuinely feels as if she may become lightheaded.

units.text: The bright sunlight outside was almost enough to really make a person go giddy. A small plank was lowered to get off the boat, and Gohda was waiting there, smiling and ready to lend them a hand.
units.japanese: 表の強い日差しに、本当に立ち眩みを覚えそうになる。船着場との間に掛けられた下船用の橋板の前で、郷田が手を貸そうと、にこやかに微笑みながら待っていた。

description: MG says Hideyoshi held tightly to Eva’s “shoulders” plural, while the source has him draw her firmly close by one shoulder in a wordless side embrace.
sourceReading: After hearing Eva’s despair, Hideyoshi draws her close by the shoulder, conveying through the firmness of the embrace that she need say no more.

units.text: Hideyoshi heard her talking to herself. When Hideyoshi held on tightly to Eva's shoulders, his firmness alone told her that there was no need to say any more...
units.japanese: その独り言は秀吉に聞かれていた。秀吉は絵羽の肩をぐっと抱き寄せると、その力強さだけで、それ以上を語る必要はないと伝えるのだった…。

description: MG changes Battler’s claim that expecting him to remember six-year-old events is unreasonable into “I’m the one who has it bad, being forced to remember,” reframing impossibility as personal mistreatment or hardship.
sourceReading: Battler protests that after six years it is unreasonable to expect him to remember everyone clearly.

units.text: "Come on, this was six years ago, right? I'm the one who has it bad, being forced to remember...!"
units.japanese: 「いや、さすがに６年前だぜ？　覚えてろって方が無理があるぜ…！」
candidates: I'm the one who has it bad, being forced to remember

description: MG misspells “embarrassing” as “embarassing” during Battler’s prolonged scream.
sourceReading: Battler screams for Shannon to stop because the remembered white-horse promise is intensely embarrassing.

units.text: "Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaahhh, stop iiiiiiiiit, so embarassiiiiiiiiiiing!!"
units.japanese: 「ぎゃああああああああぁああぁあぁ、らめええぇえぇ、恥ずかすぃいいいいぃいいぃぃぃ！！」

description: UP uses the ungrammatical transitive construction “a memory I want to disappear”; in standard English Battler wants the memory to disappear or wants to erase it.
sourceReading: Battler melodramatically calls the episode a bittersweet, embarrassing memory from adolescence that he wants erased.

units.text: "Still, everyone has to pass through that painful period... That's right, that's how you know your place, learn shame, and become an adult. Yes, this is a memory I want to disappear, the bittersweet kind of thing that everyone does in adolescence as they transition to becoming adults... Aaaaarrggh..."
units.japanese: 「いや、誰しもがそういう痛々しい時代を潜り抜けていくのだ…。そうさ、そうして身の程を知り恥を覚えて大人になるんだ。そうさ、これは大人への過渡期なら誰もが犯す青春の甘酸っぱくて恥ずかしい、消し去りたい記憶なんだ…。うおーぐおー…」

description: MG says George looked as though he was “flirting with Shannon,” while the narration only says he teamed up with her in joking around; the romantic relationship is inferred afterward from his unusual familiarity.
sourceReading: George jokingly teams up with Shannon, and Battler notices that his unusually frank familiarity with a servant may indicate they are dating.

units.text: George looked like he was flirting with Shannon, ...but he seemed somewhat open and frank about it. He was always that way with his cousins, but he usually took on a reserved, gentlemanly attitude when he came in contact with the servants. ...When I thought about it, I got the feeling he was being a bit overly friendly, which seemed strange.
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴は、紗音ちゃんとつるむ様にしてふざけているわけだが、……何というか、とても気さくでフランクな感じだった。彼は、いとこ相手にならフランクだが、使用人たちには節度ある紳士的態度で接していたはずだ。…それを思うと、何だかちょっぴり馴れ馴れしいようにも感じ、わずかな違和感を覚えた。

description: UP renders 何人か as “a lot of girls,” overstating the several or some girls Battler says he has spoken with.
sourceReading: Battler says he has talked with several girls during the six years away.

units.text: "Hmm, I wonder. There's a lot of girls that I play with. But I don't have that "special one" yet. ......I'm probably just a kid. I think it's more fun to be noisy with a large group of people than being alone with one person."
units.japanese: 「さぁてどうだろうな。一緒に遊ぶ女の子は何人かいるぜ。だけどオンリーワンって関係はまだねぇな。……俺がお子様なんだろうよ。誰かと二人っきりでいるより、みんな大勢でわいわいやってる方が楽しいように思えるんだ」

description: MG renders 勘繰り過ぎ as “getting paranoid,” adding an extreme or clinical coloring to Battler’s admission that he may simply be overthinking or too suspicious.
sourceReading: Battler checks himself and says he may be reading too much into Jessica’s behavior.

units.text: "N-No, that's not... Wahahahaha, now you're getting paranoid...!!"
units.japanese: 「い、いやそんなことは…。わはははは、勘繰り過ぎだって…！！」

description: MG reduces 使用人との恋が二人か, the explicit observation that two cousins are in love with servants, to the singular and elliptical “but love with a servant...”; the following Romeo-and-Juliet comparison recovers two pairs but not the omitted count and parallel relationship statement.
sourceReading: Battler observes that two cousins are in love with servants and compares the two relationships to Romeo and Juliet.

units.text: I didn't think of the Ushiromiya family as a noble family, ...but love with a servant... I wouldn't have dreamed that two pairs of Romeo and Juliet would be right next to me...
units.japanese: 右代宮家を高貴な一族だなんて思っちゃいないが、…使用人との恋が二人か。ロミオとジュリエットが身近に二組もいるなんて夢にも思わなかったぜ…。

description: MG renders もっと早く鞘に収めて as “gotten back together with everyone,” losing Battler’s thought that he should have settled or buried the quarrel earlier and turning conflict resolution into a general reunion.
sourceReading: Battler thinks he might have settled the family quarrel and returned to the Ushiromiya family sooner.

units.text: ...I grew a lot these past six years...and being able to celebrate my youth and meet with all of my cousins was truly refreshing. ...It was a bit late now, but I realized that I should've gotten back together with everyone a lot sooner, and returned to the Ushiromiya family...
units.japanese: ……この６年ですっかり成長し、青春を謳歌しているいとこたちとの出会いは、本当に新鮮。……俺は、今更だが、もっと早く鞘に収めて、右代宮の家に帰ってきても良かったかな、なんて思っているのだった…。

description: UP renders 普段の親戚同士 as “our normal families,” changing Battler’s joke about relatives ordinarily not getting along into a claim about the cousins’ regular or immediate families.
sourceReading: Battler jokes that Jessica’s emphasis makes it sound as though relatives normally have bad relationships.

units.text: "Hey, hey, if you put the emphasis there, doesn't that make it sound like our normal families don't get along well?"
units.japanese: 「おいおい、そこを強調するとまるで、普段の親戚同士の仲が悪いように聞こえちまうぜ？」

description: MG’s “hard to stay together, much less remain friends” reverses the scalar relation in 一緒にいることどころか、仲良くいることさえ: Shannon says that without wishing for it, people have difficulty even remaining friendly, let alone staying together.
sourceReading: Shannon says people must actively wish for their bond because even remaining friendly, much less remaining together forever, is difficult.

units.text: "But I think it's very important. People are creatures who find it very hard to stay together, much less remain friends, unless they truly desire it."
units.japanese: 「でも、とても大切なことだと思いますよ。人は願わねば、いつまでも一緒にいることどころか、仲良くいることさえ難しい生き物なのですから」
candidates: hard to stay together, much less remain friends

description: UP turns どんなに楽しく懐かしく振舞おうと, however happily and nostalgically the cousins behave, into “No matter how long it had been, or how much fun we were having,” inventing elapsed duration and dropping their consciously nostalgic behavior.
sourceReading: However happily and nostalgically the cousins act together, dark clouds are approaching Rokkenjima.

units.text: No matter how long it had been, or how much fun we were having, it didn't stop the dark clouds from approaching Rokkenjima. ......I wonder if the typhoon will pass and show us the refreshing sky before we leave this island.
units.japanese: 俺たちいとこがどんなに楽しく懐かしく振舞おうと、六軒島には暗雲が近付いている。……俺たちがこの島を去る頃には、台風は通り過ぎ、清々しい空を見せてくれるだろうか。
candidates: matter how long it had been, or how much fun we were having

description: MG says Maria could not fail to “notice” the worsening wind and cold rain, while 気にならないわけもない says she could not be unbothered or unconcerned by it. Awareness replaces physical or emotional disturbance.
sourceReading: Maria is necessarily bothered by the worsening wind and cold rain, but fear of losing the rose drives her to continue searching.

units.text: The wind grew increasingly strong, and the rain turned into cold, large drops. There was no way even Maria would fail to notice this.
units.japanese:
風はますますに強くなり、雨は冷たく大粒になっていく。
真里亞とて、それが気にならないわけもない。

description: MG combines present ability with the past-oriented phrase “as I pleased” in “I can ... kill and revive as I pleased.” The Japanese presents Beatrice’s current unrestricted power, requiring “as I please.”
sourceReading: Beatrice proclaims that she can now freely break, repair, kill, or revive every soul.

units.text: By now, I can break and repair any soul if I try, not just that of a rose, and kill and revive as I pleased.
units.japanese: 今や、妾の手にかかれば薔薇に限らず、全ての魂は壊すも直すも、殺すも蘇らせるも思いのまま。
candidates: kill and revive as I pleased

description: MG says the storm barrier seals Rokkenjima off from the “natural world,” while 現世 means the present, real, or living world. Natural world suggests nature as opposed to human civilization and misstates the boundary being invoked.
sourceReading: The storm barrier closes Rokkenjima off from the present or real world, preparing Beatrice’s descent within the tale’s fantasy framing.

units.text: Come, the barrier of the storm has now sealed Rokkenjima off from the natural world. Now is the time for the Golden Witch, Beatrice, to descend as an Endless Witch.
units.japanese: さぁ、嵐の結界は六軒島を現世より閉ざした。今こそ、無限の魔女にして黄金の魔女、ベアトリーチェの降臨する時。
candidates: Rokkenjima off from the natural world

description: UP renders そなたも言うようになったな, Beatrice’s amused observation that Battler has started saying cheeky things like that, as “You have started to grow some guts,” promoting the verbal development into a broader gain in courage.
sourceReading: Beatrice laughs that Battler has learned to make cutting remarks like his joke about the Seven Sisters fitting their master.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*! You have started to grow some guts!"
units.japanese: 「くっくっくっくっく！　そなたも言うようになったな！」

description: MG says “No sane people would hang out with you” for お前の関係にはロクな連中がいねぇ, which condemns Beatrice’s associates as no good or not decent. Sanity replaces moral or qualitative worth.
sourceReading: Battler insults Beatrice by saying there is not a decent person among her associates.

units.text: "I'll bet. No sane people would hang out with you. First some goat monsters, then those ass nee-chans, and this time a demon butler's showed up. ...I hate to think about it, but the way things are going, I wouldn't be surprised if even more weird people appeared..."
units.japanese: 「だろうな。お前の関係にはロクな連中がいねぇぜ。山羊のバケモノに太もも姉ちゃんに、そして今度は悪魔の執事と来たわけだ。……まさかとは思うが、この調子でまだおかしな連中が増えるってんじゃねぇだろうな…」

description: MG turns Battler’s apprehensive “surely you aren’t saying even more weird people will keep appearing” into “I wouldn’t be surprised if even more weird people appeared,” replacing resistance and dread with resigned expectation.
sourceReading: Battler anxiously asks Beatrice to deny that still more strange figures will appear at this rate.

units.text: "I'll bet. No sane people would hang out with you. First some goat monsters, then those ass nee-chans, and this time a demon butler's showed up. ...I hate to think about it, but the way things are going, I wouldn't be surprised if even more weird people appeared..."
units.japanese: 「だろうな。お前の関係にはロクな連中がいねぇぜ。山羊のバケモノに太もも姉ちゃんに、そして今度は悪魔の執事と来たわけだ。……まさかとは思うが、この調子でまだおかしな連中が増えるってんじゃねぇだろうな…」
candidates: wouldn't be surprised if even more weird people appeared

description: MG says the first solver receives “the inheritance along with all of his wealth,” collapsing 家督, succession to the family headship, into inheritance and making the following wealth redundant. UP preserves “the headship along with all of his wealth.”
sourceReading: Eva reads the letter as saying that the first person to solve the epitaph receives both the Ushiromiya headship and all of Kinzo’s property.

units.text: "...That's right. If you interpret the contents literally, ...then this is a test from Father. The epitaph of the witch has been displayed in the hall for quite some time now, so that any one of us could solve it. There was plenty of notice. That means he was saying that the first person to solve it would be handed the inheritance along with all of his wealth, right...?"
units.japanese: 「……そうね。文面通りに解釈するなら、…これはお父様からのテストね。魔女の碑文は、私たち誰にでも解けるように、ずっと広間に掲示されていた。告示期間は充分。最初に解けた人間に、家督と全ての財産を渡すと、そう言っているわけよね…？」
candidates: saying that the first person to solve
inheritance along with all of his wealth

description: MG translates 忘れてあげて as “forget it for now,” omitting the benefactive あげて: Kyrie asks the children to forget it for their parents’ sake, before explaining that the adults are fighting for their futures.
sourceReading: Kyrie acknowledges the children’s pain but asks them, for their parents’ sake, to set the scene aside and not greet the adults coldly when they return hurt.

units.text: "I know it's hard. But forget it for now.
units.japanese: 「辛いのはわかるわ。でも、今は忘れてあげて」

description: UP renders 憮然とした as “astonished.” Battler and Jessica are sullen, displeased, or indignant after the adults’ behavior; surprise is not the stated emotion.
sourceReading: Battler and Jessica, visibly displeased by the adults’ conduct, are glad to move to the guesthouse.

units.text: Jessica and I, both astonished, were happy to move over to the guesthouse. We didn't want to be under the same roof as those filthy adults, their heads so filled with thoughts about money.
units.japanese: 憮然とした俺と朱志香は、喜んでゲストハウスへ移動することにした。カネのことで頭がいっぱいの、汚い大人たちと同じ屋根の屋敷にいたくなかったのだ。

description: MG turns もやもやしたものが晴れない, an unresolved haze, unease, or doubt that will not clear, into “we couldn’t clear away a gloomy feeling.” Gloom substitutes sadness or darkness for unresolved uncertainty about the sender.
sourceReading: Despite agreeing not to question Maria further, the cousins cannot dispel their unresolved doubt about who gave her the letter.

units.text: ...Even though we said that, we couldn't clear away a gloomy feeling.
units.japanese: ……そうは言ったものの。俺たちだって、もやもやしたものが晴れない。
candidates: couldn't clear away a gloomy feeling

description: MG duplicates “received this problematic letter” across rows 94–95, displacing the intended isolated emphasis on “today” before “on this island.” The proposition remains recoverable at row 96, but the staged evidentiary rhythm is broken.
sourceReading: The narration isolates three facts for emphasis: Maria received the letter, today, on this island; therefore its planner is still present today.

units.text: ...But they could say one thing for certain. Maria had received this problematic letter... received this problematic letter... today, on this island. In other words, someone planning something to do with that letter was on this island today.
units.japanese: …しかし、ひとつだけ言えることがある。真里亞が問題の手紙を、今日、この島で受け取ったということだ。つまり、あの手紙について策謀を巡らせた人間が、今日、まだこの島にいるということなのだ。

description: UP says Krauss’s realization means they will not have to waste “so much” time, while これ以上 means no more or no further time. It weakens Eva’s claim that the wasted discussion can now stop entirely.
sourceReading: Eva sarcastically says that now Krauss has noticed the impasse, they need waste no further time.

units.text: "That's right. Now that you realized it, we won't have to waste so much."
units.japanese: 「そうね。兄さんが気付いてくれるだけで、これ以上を浪費しなくて済むわ」

description: MG renders 一服 as a generic “short break,” but Eva is asking Rudolf whether he wants a smoke, as his reply about declining because of her mood confirms. The concrete smoking action disappears.
sourceReading: Eva asks Rudolf whether he is ready for a smoke; he declines because she appears to be in a bad mood.

units.text: "That sounds good. It would probably be wiser if we cooled our heads. Don't you want to take a short break too, dear?"
units.japanese: 「そうね。頭を冷やした方が賢明そう。あなたも、そろそろ一服したくなってきたんじゃない？」

description: MG renders 自己を厳しく律する as “keeping strictly to the rules.” Natsuhi praises Kinzo’s strict self-discipline and restraint, not adherence to external rules.
sourceReading: Natsuhi calls Kinzo an exemplary man who disciplines himself strictly and rejects the idea that he brought a mistress to the island.

units.text: "Father was always exemplary at keeping strictly to the rules! It is completely inconceivable that he would bring something so filthy onto this island...!"
units.japanese: 「お父様は自己を厳しく律する模範的な方です！　そのような汚らわしい存在を島に連れ込むなど、到底考えられません…！」

description: MG says Kinzo built “all the buildings” on Rokkenjima for 六軒島の設備、全て, which encompasses all of the island’s facilities or infrastructure. Buildings narrows the scope of what he created.
sourceReading: Rudolf says Kinzo created all of Rokkenjima’s facilities himself, supporting rumors of mechanisms, rooms, and buildings known only to him.

units.text: "...I'm sorry, Natsuhi-san. I know how much you respect Dad, but that rumor's been around for a long time. All the buildings on Rokkenjima were built by Dad on his own."
units.japanese: 「……親父を尊敬してる夏妃さんにゃ悪いが、だいぶ昔からそういう噂はあったんだよな。親父は自分ひとりでこの六軒島の設備、全てを作り上げた」

description: MG prints “extraordinar[l]y” as “extraordinarly” while describing Kinzo’s extreme care not to be seen.
sourceReading: Krauss says Kinzo was cautious about being watched to an abnormal or extraordinary degree.

units.text: "...Of course, it was a failure. Every time Father went out, he was oddly intent on avoiding places where he might be seen...and was extremely careful to prevent anyone from spotting him. And, he was extraordinarly earnest in his attempts to do so.
units.japanese: 「…もちろん失敗したよ。親父は表へ出る時、異様に人目を嫌い、誰かに見られてないか警戒していた。それこそ異常なくらいにね」

description: MG says the hidden mansion “had been quietly built to house a witch.” Japanese says a hidden mansion stands quietly and a witch lives there; it neither characterizes the construction as quiet nor states that housing her was its construction purpose.
sourceReading: The family imagines an unknown mansion standing quietly on the island, with the portrait’s witch living inside it.

units.text: On this island, on which the Ushiromiya family had lived for 30 years now, a hidden mansion that no one knew about had been quietly built to house a witch, about whom nothing was known except what could be guessed from a portrait... Even this hastily thrown together theory... might not be completely delusional, considering all of Kinzo's strange habits and his vast wealth...
units.japanese: 右代宮家が３０年にもわたって住まってきたこの島に、誰も知らない隠し屋敷がひっそりと建っていて、肖像画でしか知らない魔女が住んでいる…。にわかには信じられないこの話も、…全て金蔵の奇癖と莫大な財産があれば、決して妄想ではないのかもしれない…。
candidates: quietly built to house a witch

description: MG renders それもお父さんなりのね as facilities “in a way that would satisfy Father.” Kyrie means facilities arranged in Father’s own characteristic way, not facilities intended to satisfy him.
sourceReading: Kyrie imagines whatever facilities Kinzo himself would devise to keep his beloved woman healthy and comfortable.

units.text: "Think of the facilities needed to let his beloved woman live healthily. ...And in a way that would satisfy Father. For example, even if it was on a small scale, it would have to be an intricate and pleasant residence."
units.japanese: 「愛する女性が健やかに過ごせるような設備よ。……それもお父さんなりのね。それはたとえ、規模が小さかったとしても、趣向を凝らした快適な邸宅に違いない」

description: MG says the other party “brought this rule to light.” Japanese says the other party proposed or put forward the condition, which is the basis for Kyrie’s inference that it expects to win. Revealing an existing rule does not establish authorship or choice of the terms.
sourceReading: Because the other party itself put forward the condition, Kyrie infers that it must believe it has good prospects under those terms.

units.text: "...However, since she's the one who brought this rule to light in the first place, maybe that means it gives her a significant advantage."
units.japanese: 「……でも、その条件を向こうが出してきたということは、向こうは充分な勝算があるということじゃないのかしら」

description: MG says solving the epitaph would cause the gold to be “stolen from her.” Japanese only says the gold would be taken, without establishing that Beatrice currently possesses or owns it; her possession is the disputed premise Kyrie addresses immediately afterward.
sourceReading: The narration questions why the sender would invite the siblings to solve the epitaph if doing so could result in the gold being taken, then considers a plan to exploit their solution.

units.text: That certainly was the case. If the epitaph showed the way to the hidden gold, why would she challenge them to try and solve it? If they actually did solve it, wouldn't the gold all be stolen from her...?
units.japanese: 確かにその通りだった。碑文が黄金の隠し場所を示しているなら、なぜそれを解いてみろなどと挑発を？　仮に解かれたら、黄金を奪われてしまうではないか…。

description: MG’s “it was dregs that remained of that inheritance” is grammatically malformed and obscures the comparison between shares of the estate’s remaining scraps and Beatrice’s proposed compensation.
sourceReading: The adults compare division of the depleted estate’s remnants with compensation Beatrice might pay for recognition as head.

units.text: They knew that Krauss had eaten up much of the Ushiromiya family's assets. So, it was dregs that remained of that inheritance, ...versus "the cost of being accepted as the Head" that Beatrice would pay. It was a shame, but honestly, the former was less enticing than the latter.
units.japanese: 右代宮家の財産は、かなりが蔵臼に食い潰されていることがわかっている。その残り滓の遺産分配と、ベアトリーチェが支払う“家督を認める対価”。残念だが、前者より後者の方が期待できるというのが本音だった。
candidates: dregs that remained of that inheritance

description: MG says the three younger siblings “never had anything to do with the inheritance.” Japanese says they have no connection to the right of succeeding the family head; they plainly remain prospective heirs to Kinzo’s property.
sourceReading: Unlike Krauss, the three younger siblings have no initial claim to succeed as family head and may therefore accept money to recognize Beatrice’s succession.

units.text: If the three younger siblings, who never had anything to do with the inheritance, were paid enough money to satisfy them, they would happily accept Beatrice as the next Head.
units.japanese: そもそも当主継承権と関係のない蔵臼以外の兄弟は、納得できるカネが支払われれば、喜んでベアトリーチェの当主継承を認めるだろう。
candidates: never had anything to do with the inheritance

description: MG says Krauss’s “situation” would probably be investigated when the estate was distributed. Japanese says he would be held responsible or called to account for embezzling Kinzo’s personal assets.
sourceReading: Estate distribution would expose Krauss’s appropriation of Kinzo’s assets and lead the siblings to pursue his responsibility for it.

units.text: In order to bury his losses, Krauss had taken advantage of the fact that Kinzo had shut himself up in his room...and had embezzled Kinzo's personal assets. Therefore, when Kinzo died and the inheritance was distributed, Krauss's situation would probably be investigated.
units.japanese: 蔵臼は損失を埋めるため、金蔵が引き篭もっているのをいい事に、金蔵の個人資産を着服していた。だから、金蔵が逝去して遺産分配になれば、その責任を追及されることになるだろう。
candidates: Krauss's situation would probably be investigated

description: MG says Kinzo “once ordered” the epitaph to be displayed. Japanese states that Kinzo put the epitaph on display; it does not insert an intermediary order or mark the act as a one-time past occurrence.
sourceReading: Kinzo displayed the epitaph, no one solved it through the present day, and Beatrice therefore “solved” Kinzo’s game.

units.text: ...Kinzo once ordered that the epitaph be put on display. And until today, no one had solved it. So Beatrice "solved" it. In other words, this is less of a game and more like Beatrice's declaration of victory...
units.japanese:
…金蔵は碑文を掲示した。
そして今日まで誰も解けなかった。だからベアトリーチェが“解いた”。ならばつまり、これはゲームというより、ベアトリーチェの勝利宣言のようなものなのか…。

description: MG says Kyrie thought “there might be a catch.” 引っ掛かる says something still bothered her or did not quite sit right; “a catch” prematurely specifies the unease as a hidden drawback or trap.
sourceReading: Kyrie still feels a slight unresolved inconsistency in the victory-declaration theory and continues analyzing it.

units.text: However, Kyrie still thought there might be a catch. If this was a declaration of victory, Beatrice would only have had to display the gold openly and state her intent to buy the inheritance. And yet, she had gone to all of this trouble, telling the siblings to try and solve the epitaph.
