Why did she set up this "new game", where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the inheritance to the epitaph solver?
units.japanese: しかし、霧江はまだ少し引っ掛かると考えていた。もし勝利宣言ならば、勝者らしく、黄金を堂々と示し、家督を買い取ると宣言すればいいだけの話だ。なのに、わざわざこの期に及んで、碑文を解いてみろ、解けたら家督と黄金を全て引き渡そうと、“新たなゲーム”を仕掛けてくる意味が、どこにあるというのか。
candidates: thought there might be a catch

description: MG says Beatrice could state her intent to “buy the inheritance.” Japanese says she could announce that she would buy the family headship, the office at issue in the proposed exchange.
sourceReading: If this were simply a victory declaration, Beatrice could display the gold and openly offer to buy the family headship.

units.text: However, Kyrie still thought there might be a catch. If this was a declaration of victory, Beatrice would only have had to display the gold openly and state her intent to buy the inheritance. And yet, she had gone to all of this trouble, telling the siblings to try and solve the epitaph. Why did she set up this "new game", where she agreed to hand over the all of the gold and the inheritance to the epitaph solver?
units.japanese: しかし、霧江はまだ少し引っ掛かると考えていた。もし勝利宣言ならば、勝者らしく、黄金を堂々と示し、家督を買い取ると宣言すればいいだけの話だ。なのに、わざわざこの期に及んで、碑文を解いてみろ、解けたら家督と黄金を全て引き渡そうと、“新たなゲーム”を仕掛けてくる意味が、どこにあるというのか。
candidates: state her intent to buy the inheritance

description: MG says the challenge letter was “forcing” the siblings to solve the epitaph. Japanese says it challenged or told them to try; the letter cannot compel participation, and the preceding reasoning depends on their freedom to reject the game.
sourceReading: The witch challenged the siblings to solve the epitaph while arrogantly assuming they could not, despite a tiny residual chance that they might.

units.text: "The witch sent us a letter of challenge, forcing us to try and solve the epitaph. She might be taking us lightly, thinking we could never solve it. ...However, at the very least, there ought to be an extremely small chance that we do solve it."
units.japanese: 「魔女は、碑文を解いてみろと私たちに挑戦状を送ったわ。どうせ解けないだろうと、タカを括ってるでしょうけどね。……でも、何万分の一かの確率で、私たちが解いてしまう可能性もあるはず」

description: UP says the witch has “a superior position on the negotiations.” The required idiom is a superior position in the negotiations, which MG supplies.
sourceReading: Knowing the gold’s location gives the witch a superior position in negotiations with the four siblings.

units.text: The reason the witch had a superior position on the negotiations compared to the siblings was that only she knew the location of the hidden gold. But if that hiding place was exposed to someone other than her, the witch's superior position would crumble.
units.japanese: 魔女が４兄弟に対し交渉で優位に立てるのは、彼女が唯一、黄金の隠し場所を知っているからだ。だがもし、その隠し場所を彼女以外の人間が暴けたなら、魔女の優位は崩れる。

description: UP renders 間抜けな兄弟たち as “braindead siblings.” The source insult means foolish or idiotic siblings; “braindead” is a harsher, modern slang insult that changes Eva’s register.
sourceReading: Eva contemptuously dismisses her other siblings as fools incapable of solving the epitaph and resolves to prove her own fitness.

units.text: As if my other braindead siblings could solve it. I'll solve it by myself, and then I'll prove that I am the one who is fit to succeed the Ushiromiya family......
units.japanese: 他の間抜けな兄弟たちに解けるものか。私ひとりが解いて、私こそが右代宮家を引き継ぐに相応しいということを証明してやるわ……。

description: MG calls Battler’s discovery “a big scoop.” 大きい情報 means important or significant information; “scoop” adds a journalistic sense of exclusive news.
sourceReading: Battler calls the possibility of more than eighteen people a major piece of information for breaking the magic-crime equation.

units.text: ...So there can be more than 18 people! Which means I can defeat the line of reasoning that says any crime impossible for all 18 people must involve magic. ...That's a big scoop."
units.japanese: 「……つまり人間は１８人以上いる！　ということは、１８人全員に不可能だから魔法犯罪である、という図式は崩せるわけだ。……これは大きい情報だぜ」

description: MG changes Ronove’s report that he heard Battler say he had found good information and rejoice into “you seemed to have found some useful information that quite pleased you.” This removes the explicit speech basis and turns it into Ronove’s observation.
sourceReading: Ronove says he heard Battler announce that he had found good information and sound pleased about it.

units.text: "...Setting that aside, how has the game been proceeding? Just now, you seemed to have found some useful information that quite pleased you. Well now, I wonder what your shallow wit has conjured up."
units.japanese: 「……それはさておき。ゲームの方はいかがでございますか？　先ほど、良い情報を見つけたようなことを言われ、お喜びになられていたようですが。はてさて、どのような浅知恵が思いついたやら」
candidates: seemed to have found some useful information that quite pleased

description: UP adds “goddamn” to Battler’s repeated 全然ダメだ. The source emphatically says it is no good at all but contains no profanity here.
sourceReading: Battler emphatically rejects sacrificing any of the eighteen people he cares about.

units.text: "However, I will steadfastly refuse to do that!! Yeah, that's no good, that's no goddamn good at all! Every one of those 18 people is either a parent, a relative or a cousin to me! And those reliable servants, who are sometimes serious and sometimes funny. I won't let myself use any one of them as a sacrifice!!"
units.japanese: 「しかし、それは断固拒否するッ！！　あぁダメだぜ、全然ダメだ！　１８人はみんな俺にとって親たちや親戚たちやいとこたち！　そして真面目だったり面白かったりする頼もしい使用人の人たちだ。俺はその人たちの誰を生贄にすることも許せないッ！！」

description: UP says there are countless “tricks I can use” if a nineteenth person exists. Japanese refers to numerous tricks or incidents over which Battler would no longer need to hesitate; it does not present them as tools he deploys.
sourceReading: Battler says many prior incidents, including Kanon’s boiler-room death, become straightforward to explain if a nineteenth person is allowed.

units.text: "That's it exactly. Like in the first game, when Kanon‐kun was killed in the boiler room, ...and a bunch of other places, there are countless tricks I can use without hesitation if a 19th person existed."
units.japanese: 「そういうことさ。最初のゲームの、嘉音くんが殺されたボイラー室とか、…他にも他にも、１９人目が存在していたなら、迷う必要なんかないトリックはいくつもある」
candidates: are countless tricks I can use

description: MG says a nineteenth person “must’ve” visited Maria and delivered the letter. Japanese says the event can be explained by positing that a nineteenth person did so; it presents an available human explanation, not a necessary conclusion.
sourceReading: Even if all eighteen have alibis, Battler can easily explain the delivery by hypothesizing that a nineteenth person visited Maria.

units.text: Using this argument, it's easy to explain, for example, the problematic case that has already occurred in this game, "who gave Maria the letter?" Even if all 18 people have alibis, I could easily explain everything by saying that a 19th person must've visited her and given her the letter.
units.japanese: この論法なら例えば、今回のゲームでもすでに問題提起されている、“真里亞に手紙を渡したのは誰か？”という問いも簡単に説明できる。１８人全員にアリバイがあろうとも、ゆえに１９人目の人物が訪れて手紙を渡したと、実に簡単に説明できるのだ。

description: MG says Ronove would “ambush” Battler’s nineteenth-person piece. 迎え撃つ means meet, counter, or attack an advancing opponent; “ambush” adds concealment and surprise.
sourceReading: Ronove says the proper response is to meet or counter the nineteenth-person piece by demanding proof of its existence.

units.text: "...I believe it would be appropriate to ambush the piece representing this 19th person that you mentioned. Battler-sama, you have never met this 19th person, yes? Would you please show some proof that this 19th person exists?"
units.japanese: 「……戦人さまが指された、１９人目の駒を迎え撃つのが妥当でございましょう。戦人さまは１９人目にお会いしておりませんね？　１９人目が存在する証拠をお願いできますかな？」

description: UP asks Battler openly whether he has ever met the nineteenth person. Japanese presupposes that he has not and asks for confirmation: “You haven’t met this nineteenth person, have you?”
sourceReading: Ronove states his understanding that Battler has not met the proposed person, then demands evidence that the person exists.

units.text: "......I believe it would be appropriate to attack this 19th piece that you have played. Battler‐sama, have you ever met this 19th person? May I ask you for some proof that this 19th person exists?"
units.japanese: 「……戦人さまが指された、１９人目の駒を迎え撃つのが妥当でございましょう。戦人さまは１９人目にお会いしておりませんね？　１９人目が存在する証拠をお願いできますかな？」

description: UP says humans demand evidence when they “are accused of something.” Japanese broadly says they do so when something is shown or presented to them; accusation is only one narrower situation.
sourceReading: Battler generalizes that humans answer anything presented to them by demanding evidence.

units.text:
When we humans are accused of something, we always counterattack by saying to show some evidence. Because that's a human move. But I'm fighting with a witch.
I'm taking part in a battle with someone who isn't human!
units.japanese:
俺たち人間は、何かを示されると、必ず証拠を示せと反論する。それが人間の指し手だからだ。だが、俺は魔女と戦っている。
人ならざる者との戦いに臨んでいる！

description: MG calls Beatrice a “problematic and mysterious mistress.” 問題の means the mistress in question, not a mistress who is herself problematic.
sourceReading: Battler calls her the enigmatic mistress under discussion and argues that her deliberate hiding explains why she cannot be found.

units.text: In other words, because this problematic and mysterious mistress is craftily hiding herself, it'd be perfectly natural if you never found her no matter how hard you looked. So, you can't say that your inability to find this 19th person proves that she doesn't exist. Therefore, it's impossible to deny the 19th person's existence. Beato used the "Devil's Proof" to make denying her own existence impossible, but this time it's become my weapon.
units.japanese:
つまり、問題の謎の愛人は狡猾に隠れているわけだから、どんなに探しても見付からないのは当然。だから、１９人目が見付からないこと＝１９人目はいない、とはならないわけだ。ゆえに、１９人目の否定は不可能。
ベアトが自らの存在を否定不能とした“悪魔の証明”が、今度はそのまま俺の武器になったわけだ。

description: UP says “it is impossible to disprove a 19th person.” Japanese says it is impossible to deny or disprove the nineteenth person’s existence; omitting “existence” leaves an ungrammatical object for disprove.
sourceReading: Because failure to find the nineteenth person does not establish nonexistence, Battler concludes that the person’s existence cannot be disproved.

units.text:
In other words, the enigmatic mistress in question is craftily hiding herself, so it's perfectly natural that you can never find her no matter how hard you look. So you can't say that "The 19th person can't be found = The 19th person doesn't exist". Therefore, it is impossible to disprove a 19th person.
Beato used the "Devil's Proof" to make denying her existence impossible, but this time it's become my weapon.
units.japanese:
つまり、問題の謎の愛人は狡猾に隠れているわけだから、どんなに探しても見付からないのは当然。だから、１９人目が見付からないこと＝１９人目はいない、とはならないわけだ。ゆえに、１９人目の否定は不可能。
ベアトが自らの存在を否定不能とした“悪魔の証明”が、今度はそのまま俺の武器になったわけだ。

description: UP says doubts arise “at whether” a large hidden group could move through the mansion unnoticed. Standard English requires doubts about whether, which MG supplies.
sourceReading: Battler acknowledges the natural doubt about whether a large group could hide inside the mansion without being noticed.

units.text: Of course, doubts will naturally arise at whether a large group of people like that could sneak around the mansion without being noticed, but those are all settled by the "Devil's Proof". Because not seeing or not noticing a hundred people inside the mansion does not disprove that they were there.
units.japanese: それだけの大勢の人間が、あの屋敷内に気配もなく潜んでいたのかという疑問は当然、出るだろうが、これも“悪魔の証明”で決着できる。気配がなかった姿を見なかった＝屋敷内に１００人いたことの否定、にはならないからだ。

description: UP says Ronove has “no excuse” for moving without Beatrice present. 申し訳ない expresses apology or feeling sorry; it does not concede that his conduct is indefensible.
sourceReading: Ronove apologizes for advancing the game in his mistress’s absence, then admits that he has become interested.

units.text: "Although I have no excuse for making moves by myself when Milady is absent, .........I find that I too have become slightly interested. ...I wonder if you would permit me to make yet another move on Milady's behalf?"
units.japanese: 「お嬢様のおられないところで、勝手に手を進めてしまうのは申し訳ないのですが。………私も少し、面白くなってきてしまったところです。…お嬢様に代わり、さらに一手進めさせていただきましょうか」

description: MG calls Hempel’s Raven a “familiar old move.” 懐かしい describes it as nostalgic, while familiar merely says it is known; the personal reminiscence in Beatrice’s reaction is weakened.
sourceReading: Beatrice greets Hempel’s Raven as an amusing, nostalgic old move and is surprised to have occasion to show it to Battler.

units.text: ..."Hempel's Raven", was it? Such a familiar old move I could almost laugh. To think the day has come when I get to show it off to Battler. It's a classic move to use against a "Devil's Proof"."
units.japanese: 「……“ヘンペルのカラス”か。何とも笑える懐かしい一手よ。よもや戦人に披露する日が来ようとはな。それは“悪魔の証明”に並ぶ古典的一手だ」

description: MG changes Battler’s complaint that Beatrice laughs vulgarly or without class into “laughing like a freak.” The source criticizes manners; MG instead depicts abnormality.
sourceReading: Battler insults Beatrice for her persistently vulgar, undignified laugh and reports Ronove’s similar criticism.

units.text: "So you've finally shown up, you guffawing witch. I see you're laughing like a freak just as usual. ...This guy was talking behind your back just now, telling me how undignified you look when you do that. Right?"
units.japanese: 「出やがったな、ゲラゲラ魔女め。相変わらず下品に笑いやがって。……こいつもお前のこと、笑い方に品がねぇって陰口言ってたぜ。なぁ？」

description: UP pluralizes Battler’s example to catching “the ravens” and checking whether they are black. Japanese has him naively propose catching a single raven, an answer that motivates Beatrice’s subsequent lesson; the translation silently makes his method more comprehensive.
sourceReading: Battler says one could catch a raven and confirm that it is black; Beatrice then develops the conditional and contrapositive argument.

units.text: "Huh? What are you talking about?? Prove that ravens are black... ...Wouldn't you just have to catch the ravens and check to see if they're black?"
units.japanese: 「は？　何の話だ？？　カラスが黒いことを証明って…。…カラスを捕まえてきて、色が黒いことを確認すりゃいいだけの話だろ」

description: MG renders “if it is a raven, it is black” as the equation “a raven = black.” That collapses a conditional property relation into identity or equivalence and makes the following contrapositive explanation less precise.
sourceReading: Beatrice formalizes “if something is a raven, then it is black,” then states its contrapositive: if a bird is not black, it is not a raven.

units.text: "That's right. You must simply prove that "a raven = black". Do you see that, if you instead prove that "birds that aren't black = not ravens", you would reach the same argument?
units.japanese: 「その通り。“カラス＝黒い”、を証明すれば良い。ということは、“黒くない鳥＝カラスではない”、を証明しても、同じ論法になるのがわかるかな？」

description: MG has Beatrice say “All I’ve done is say it the other way around.” Japanese says Battler has merely stated the same proposition the other way around; MG reverses the subject of the argumentative act.
sourceReading: After Beatrice explains the empty nineteenth box consequence, she tells Battler that he himself merely stated that proposition in the reverse form.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*! If I go first and prove that the inside of the 19th person box is empty, you will automatically have to accept that the cookie is in the 18 person box. All I've done is say it the other way around, yes?"
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくく！　妾が１９人目の箱の中身が空っぽであることを先に証明すれば、そなたは自動的に、１８人の箱の中にクッキーがあることを認めなければならないということになる。そなたは、それを逆の言い方で口にしたに過ぎんのだぞ？」
candidates: I've done is say it the other way around

description: MG says “This isn’t a cookie we’re talking about.” クッキーという言い方がいけない says the problem lies in using a cookie as the framing or analogy, not that the object under discussion literally is not a cookie.
sourceReading: Battler realizes that the benign cookie framing obscures the asymmetry, so he rebuilds the analogy with one bomb among nineteen boxes.

units.text: ...Wait, if I really think about it, this counter is really disadvantageous for me. This isn't a cookie we're talking about. If I imagine that the "loser" treasure chest actually has a bomb in it, it gets even clearer.
units.japanese:
…いや、よくよく考えれば、これは俺にばかりやたらと不利な返し技だ。クッキーという言い方がいけない。
宝箱の中に爆弾というハズレが１つだけ入っていると考え直してみると、さらによくわかる。

description: MG says Battler personally has to “prove” the eighteen people’s innocence. Japanese says he must completely confirm their innocence for himself; the burden described is exhaustive personal verification, not necessarily formal proof.
sourceReading: Unable to verify more than their asserted alibis, Battler would need to personally and completely confirm each person’s innocence through continuous observation.

units.text: That means I personally have to prove their innocence, and I have to do it perfectly. Like by staying with them the whole time, never letting them out of my sight for a second. By doing that, I could probably be sure of that person's innocence, sure that the bomb isn't in their box.
units.japanese: ならば、俺個人が彼らの無実を完全に確認しきらなければならない。例えば、ずっと一緒にいて一秒も漏らさず監視してるとか。そういうことをすれば、その人物に関してだけは無実を、箱の中に爆弾がないと確認できたことになるだろう。

description: UP says “the necessary cost to bring humans misfortune is much cheaper.” A cost is lower or smaller, not cheaper; the comparative predicate is grammatically malformed.
sourceReading: Making people unhappy costs far less than giving them happiness.

units.text: "It takes an enormous cost to give humans happiness. ...However, the necessary cost to bring humans misfortune is much cheaper."
units.japanese: 「人に幸福を与えるには莫大なコストが掛かる。…しかし、人を不幸にするのに必要なコストははるかに安上がりだ」
candidates: necessary cost to bring humans misfortune is much cheaper

description: UP says the gods can provide divine protection “at the lowest cost.” 低コスト means at low cost; it does not claim this method is the absolute minimum among all possibilities.
sourceReading: The speakers joke that Hempel’s Raven lets gods give believers the joy of protection at low cost by making nonbelievers miserable.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*. So by using "Hempel's Raven", gods can actually give believers the joy of divine protection at the lowest cost."
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくくくく。つまり、“ヘンペルのカラス”を使えば、神々は実に低コストで信者に加護の喜びを与えられるわけよ」
candidates: divine protection at the lowest cost

description: UP reduces Battler’s self-command 悪足掻きを止めるな to “Don’t give up this struggle.” 悪足掻き explicitly characterizes it as desperate, futile, or ugly last-ditch resistance.
sourceReading: Battler orders himself not to stop his desperate last-ditch resistance even after Beatrice’s counter shakes him.

units.text:
Not yet... ......Don't give up this struggle yet. Who cares about "Whoever's Raven"?
They're just trying to speak in riddles by bringing up some weird bits of trivia...
units.japanese:
まだだ…。……悪足掻きを止めるな。何が“何たらのカラス”だ。
おかしな豆知識で煙に巻かれるな…。

description: MG tells Battler to believe in “the spear you’ve drawn.” 繰り出した describes a spear thrust or extended into attack; “drawn” imports the action used for a sword or bow and blurs the continuing attack image.
sourceReading: Battler tells himself to trust the spear he has already thrust forward and drive it in with still greater force.

units.text: I used the "Devil's Proof". Don't feel uncertain about something you've used once. Believe in the spear you've drawn. And then, forcefully...gouge it in...!
units.japanese:
こっちは“悪魔の証明”で仕掛けた。
一度仕掛けた手に不安を持つな。
繰り出した槍を信じろ。さらに力強く、……抉り出せ……！
candidates: Believe in the spear you've drawn

description: MG says “They countered my twisted logic,” although ヤツ refers to Beatrice in the singular and the following action is her response.
sourceReading: Battler recognizes that Beatrice answered his sophistry with even more outrageous sophistry.

units.text: They countered my twisted logic with something even more twisted. So the only thing that could counter that...would be even crazier twisted logic...!
units.japanese:
俺の屁理屈に、ヤツも飛び切りの屁理屈で返してきた。
ならばそれに反撃できるのも、さらにぶっ飛んだ屁理屈だけなんだ…！

description: UP renders 無限の魔女 as “the Endless Witch, the Infinite Witch.” The source supplies one title; adding a second synonymous title duplicates it and disrupts established terminology.
sourceReading: Beatrice identifies herself by her established title, the Endless Witch, and claims control over infinity.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!! How foolish... Who do you think I am? I am the Endless Witch, the Infinite Witch! For you to challenge me at infinity is absurd. Having control over infinity means also that I am able to kill infinity."
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくくくくくくくくく！！　愚かしいぞ…。妾を誰と心得る？　妾こそは無限の魔女！　その妾に無限にて挑むとは片腹痛いわ。無限を操ることはつまり、無限を殺すこともできるということ」

description: MG says Battler challenges Beatrice “endlessly.” 無限にて挑む says he challenges her with infinity—the infinite regress is his weapon—not merely that the challenge continues for a long time.
sourceReading: Beatrice mocks Battler for trying to challenge the witch who controls infinity by wielding an infinite regress against her.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*!! How foolish... Who do you think I am? I am the Endless Witch! The thought that you could challenge me endlessly is just absurd. Endless control means that I am able to kill endlessly."
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくくくくくくくくく！！　愚かしいぞ…。妾を誰と心得る？　妾こそは無限の魔女！　その妾に無限にて挑むとは片腹痛いわ。無限を操ることはつまり、無限を殺すこともできるということ」

description: MG says that when Beatrice speaks in red, it “will contain” no illusions. Japanese states a standing rule in the present: red contains no illusion whenever she speaks it.
sourceReading: Beatrice states the general authority of red truth, then explains how a red population ceiling would stop Battler from creating another outsider.

units.text: "When I speak in red, it will contain absolutely no illusions. If I say once in red that there are no more than 100 people on this island, you will no longer be permitted to create a 101st person.
units.japanese: 「妾が赤で語る時、そこには一切の幻想がない。妾がこの島には１００人しかいないと一言赤で語れば、そなたにはもはや１０１人目を生み出すことは叶わぬのだ」

description: MG writes that Battler can “gleam” information from careless red use. The required verb is “glean”; gleam is a visible shine and is the wrong word.
sourceReading: Carelessly used red can give Battler information with which to investigate the truth, as in the prior chapel battle.

units.text: However, if she uses it carelessly, then I can also gleam a little information about the truth. ...In the last game, I used that to my advantage, especially during the chapel's closed room trick, and almost completely got her boxed in at one point.
units.japanese: だが、迂闊に使えばそれは俺に真相を探る情報とされてしまうこともある。…俺は前回、特に礼拝堂の密室トリックの時、それを逆手に取り、一度はぎりぎりまで追い詰めたはずだ。

description: MG pluralizes 一縷の望み into “my only rays of hope.” The source uses a single thread or ray of hope, which supports the following single-tightrope image; “only rays” is internally awkward and breaks the singular progression.
sourceReading: Beatrice’s red has repeatedly cut Battler’s single thread of hope, yet red is also the single tightrope and blade-edge path he can trust.

units.text: Of course her red's always wiping out my only rays of hope. But...don't be afraid of that. On this island overcome with falsehoods and illusions, the only thing I can trust is... the information she speaks in red.
units.japanese: 確かにヤツの赤は、いつも俺の一縷の望みをぶった斬ってきた。しかし、……それを恐れるな。この、虚偽と幻想で侵食された島で、たったひとつ信じることができるのが、ヤツが語る赤の情報だけなのだ。

description: UP says Ronove “roguishly rushed her next move.” The missing verb phrase “into making” leaves rushed with an inanimate direct object and makes the sentence ungrammatical.
sourceReading: Ronove mischievously urges his mistress to make her next move despite ostensibly being her ally.

units.text: Ronove, who was supposed to be her ally, roguishly rushed her next move. Beato smiled back, probably intending to demonstrate that she was still relaxed, ......but she couldn't hide the sweat building up on her forehead. By now she had completely lost that relaxedness which had allowed her to turn her nose up at her worthless opponent.
units.japanese: 味方のはずのロノウェが、主に悪戯っぽく次の手を急かす。ベアトは笑いを返し、余裕をアピールしたつもりだったろうが、……額に浮かぶ汗を隠せない。格下の相手を鼻であしらってやろうという余裕は、今や完全に失われていた。

description: MG says Beatrice would lose a massive piece by declining the repetition request. The source says X is a major piece that she would be allowing Battler to have on his first move; the piece becomes his argumentative resource rather than one of her pieces being captured.
sourceReading: If Beatrice will not deny at least nineteen people in red, she allows Battler the powerful X piece: arbitrarily many outsiders who can explain crimes impossible for the eighteen.

units.text: "...That X is a pretty massive piece to lose on your first move, right? After all, from now on, all of the tricks that were impossible for the 18... can be explained with a human X who isn't in that group. ...This huge piece can break open all the rooms you said were closed because everyone had an alibi...!"
units.japanese: 「……このＸは、初手で許すには相当デカい大駒だぜ？　何しろ、以後、１８人の誰にも不可能だった、という根拠のトリックは、全て１８人以外の人間Ｘで説明可能になる。……全員アリバイ系の密室を、全て打ち破れる大駒だ…！」

description: UP renders カチンと来る as “enrages even me.” The expression means that Ronove sometimes irritates or ticks off even Beatrice; “enrages” substantially heightens the stated emotion.
sourceReading: Beatrice agrees that Ronove has a sharp tongue and says that even she sometimes gets irritated with him.

units.text: "Isn't that so? Sometimes he enrages even me."
units.japanese: 「であろぅ？　たまに妾でもカチンと来るぞ」

description: UP says Beatrice “is sending letters to us.” The source refers to her sending this letter, singular, as the reason she must be alive; the plural invents repeated correspondence.
sourceReading: Eva points to the single letter presently under discussion as apparent evidence that Beatrice is alive.

units.text: "Huh? Obviously she's alive. She's sending letters to us, what more do you want?"
units.japanese: 「はぁ？　そりゃ生きてるに決まってるでしょう。こうして手紙を送ってくるぐらいだもの」

description: MG says the exchange “proves” Beatrice once had a charming adolescent phase. The source says only that this is a story about her having such a phase; “prove” adds an evidentiary conclusion to Battler’s teasing dismissal.
sourceReading: Battler lightly dismisses Beatrice’s identity crisis as the ordinary, almost endearing philosophical anxiety people experience in adolescence.

units.text: "Well, in puberty, everyone's captured by those philosophical worries at least once, wondering what meaning there is in their life. Doesn't this just prove you had a charming period like that at one point?"
units.japanese: 「ま、誰でも思春期になると、自分の生きる意味とは何ぞやみたいな、哲学的な悩みに一度は囚われるものさ。お前にもそんな微笑ましい時期があっただけという話だろ？」

description: UP says Beatrice could not take one step “outside those of my own accord.” The plural demonstrative has no grammatical spatial object and leaves the boundary she cannot cross malformed.
sourceReading: Beatrice could move freely through the mansion and garden but could not take even one step beyond them by her own will.

units.text: "......I could walk freely throughout the mansion and the garden, but my desire to take just one step outside those of my own accord was never granted."
units.japanese: 「……妾はな、屋敷と庭は自由に歩けたが、その外へは、自らの意思ではたった一歩、出ることさえ叶わなかったのだ」
candidates: step outside those of my own accord

description: UP says Beatrice sees a beach below the cliff. She says 海, the sea, and immediately asks whether an aquarium is there; the rocky shore is introduced later by Rosa.
sourceReading: Beatrice observes that the sea lies below them and asks whether an aquarium is there.

units.text: "Mmhm. I will be careful. I see there's a beach if we go down there. Is there an aquarium there?"
units.japanese: 「うむ。気をつけるぞ。下へ降りたら、海があるな。そこに水族館があるのか」

description: MG changes Battler’s singular “thighs lady” into plural “ass nee-chan friends.” In addition to retaining WH’s wrong body part, it invents multiple women.
sourceReading: Battler says he was flirting with Beatrice’s one thigh-focused woman or “thighs nee-chan.”

units.text: "I was just flirting with your ass nee-chan friends. ...More importantly, what the heck's going on here?"
units.japanese: 「お前ぇのとこの太もも姉ちゃんとイチャついてただけだぜ。……それより、こりゃどういうことだ」

description: UP’s “How does that look like being alive to you?” is ungrammatical; English requires either “How does that look alive?” or “How does that look like it is alive?”
sourceReading: Beatrice challenges Battler to explain how the visibly dead body could possibly look alive, then states in red that she is definitely dead.

units.text: "How does that look like being alive to you? She's definitely dead!"
units.japanese: 「それのどこが生きているように見えるというのか。間違いなく死んでいる！」

description: MG says the butterflies “flew up the side of the cliff.” 岩壁を越える says they floated over or crossed the cliff, returning toward the forest; it does not describe flight alongside the cliff face.
sourceReading: To avoid the sunlight, Beatrice’s butterflies ride the wind lightly over the cliff toward the cooler forest.

units.text: To escape even a little from the light of the sun, I rode the wind and gently flew up the side of the cliff. It will probably be a bit cooler in the forest. Anyway, I'll take some time to recuperate and regain my former power. ...As I ponder how to make Kinzo pay up all he owes me.
units.japanese: そして日の光を少しでも逃れるため、私は風に乗ってふわりと岩壁を越える。森の中なら多少は涼しいだろう。とにかく、ゆっくり時間を掛けて養生し、元の力を取り戻そう。……これまでの借りを、金蔵にどう返してやるかを思案しながら。
candidates: flew up the side of the cliff

description: MG changes Beatrice’s open “Do you know?” into “Didn’t you know?”, presupposing Battler should already know about the offshore shrine.
sourceReading: Beatrice asks whether Battler knows of the small Eastern-magic shrine on a reef beyond the harbor.

units.text: "Indeed. A magical one. ......Didn't you know? On the sea in front of the harbor is a reef...upon which sits a small shrine of Eastern magic."
units.japanese: 「うむ。それを魔法的に行なったのだ。………そなたは知っておるか？　船着場の先の洋上に岩礁が浮かび、そこに小さな東洋魔術の祠があることを」

description: UP changes soup Beatrice intends to drink into soup she is “trying to eat.” 飲む explicitly uses drinking as the action in the spoon-versus-chopsticks analogy.
sourceReading: Eastern magic is compared to receiving chopsticks instead of a spoon for soup one intends to drink.

units.text: "If it was Western magic, I would have some knowledge. For any barrier, there would have been some measures I could have taken. But Eastern magic is outside my area of expertise. It was as if I had been given chopsticks instead of a spoon for some soup I was trying to eat."
units.japanese: 「妾も、西洋魔術であれば心得がある。どのような結界であっても、何かの手が打てたであろう。しかし東洋魔術は専門外よ。妾が飲まんとするスープに対し、スプーンではなく箸を与えられたようなものだ」

description: UP omits the subject from “while it didn’t mean the same thing as death, did require a corresponding level of resolve.” The main clause needs “it” before “did require.”
sourceReading: For Beatrice, abandoning her body was not quite death but required resolve comparable to accepting death.

units.text: "Well, if you want to think of it that way. However, I am not a spirit. Even though I am a witch, in the beginning, I was born with a human's body of flesh. So for me, throwing away that physical body, while it didn't mean the same thing as death, did require a corresponding level of resolve."
units.japanese: 「まぁ、そんなものと考えれば良い。しかし、妾は精霊ではない。魔女ではあっても、元々は肉の体で生れ落ちた人間だ。その妾にとって肉体を捨てるということは、死を意味するほどではないにしても、それに準ずる覚悟が必要だった」
candidates: didn't mean the same thing as death, did require a corresponding level of resolve

description: MG says Beatrice was “so desperate to escape that” she became only a soul. The source says she became a soul and tried to escape; the added emotional degree and result construction recast the sequence as desperation causing the transformation.
sourceReading: Beatrice says that after becoming a soul and attempting to escape, Kinzo still had no intention of letting her get away.

units.text: "No. I mean my body, relaxing in the garden chair over there. ......Even though I was so desperate to escape that I became naught but a soul, Kinzo still had no intention of letting me go."
units.japanese: 「違う。そこのガーデンチェアにてくつろぐ妾の体のことだ。………金蔵は、魂となって抜け出そうとした妾を、それでもなお逃すつもりはなかったのだ」
candidates: Kinzo still had no intention of letting

description: UP turns Battler’s rough rhetorical disbelief into “That’s goddamn impossible and you know it!” The source contains neither the added profanity nor an assertion that Beatrice herself knows the claim is impossible.
sourceReading: Battler exclaims that such a thing cannot possibly exist and demands agreement through a rough rhetorical question.

units.text: "Huh?! Ridiculous...! That's goddamn impossible and you know it!"
units.japanese: 「はぁ？！　馬鹿馬鹿しい…！　そんなのあるわけねぇだろ？！」
candidates: That's goddamn impossible and you know

description: UP misspells “thirteen” as “thirteeen” in the first statement that Kinzo devised a ritual offering thirteen sacrifices.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Kinzo devised a ritual to revive her by offering thirteen sacrifices.

units.text: "Mmhm. While Kinzo searched for a hidden art to capture me again, he ended up at that. ...............Then, he finally worked out the ritual involving the offering of thirteeen sacrifices to revive me again."
units.japanese: 「うむ。金蔵は妾を再び捕らえる秘術を探る内に、そこに行き着いたのだ。……………そして、１３人の生贄を捧げることで妾を再び蘇らせる儀式を、ついに編み出したのだ」

description: UP calls 生贄の唄 a “poem of sacrifices.” 唄 identifies it as a song or chant; the epitaph may be a poem as a whole, but Ronove specifically names its sacrificial song.
sourceReading: Ronove calls the witch’s epitaph a song or chant of sacrifices and enumerates the thirteen victims.

units.text: "That is the witch's epitaph. It is a poem of sacrifices. ......Six people on the first twilight. Two people on the second twilight. And then five more people on the fourth through eighth twilights. A forbidden ritual, involving the offering of a total of thirteen people as sacrifices... Those sacrifices are chosen randomly, and the one holding the ritual, Kinzo himself, is not an exception."
units.japanese: 「それが、魔女の碑文。生贄の唄でございます。……第一の晩に６人。第二の晩に２人。そして第四の晩から第八の晩にかけて５人。合計１３人の生贄を捧げる、禁じられた儀式…。その生贄はランダムに決められ、儀式を執り行う金蔵自身も例外にはなりません」

description: UP uses the nonstandard spelling “nightmareish” instead of “nightmarish” in Beatrice’s description of Kinzo’s treatment.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Kinzo put her through bitter betrayal or severe suffering, though she now regards those decades as exceptionally rare in her thousand years.

units.text: "......Kinzo put me through a nightmareish ordeal, but thinking back on it now, it was an extraordinary period, even amid the past thousand years. After all, the natural enemy of a witch is boredom. To Kinzo, who offered me a chance to run away from that for several decades, yes, considering that among other things, I might have a slight debt to him."
units.japanese: 「……金蔵にはさんざん煮え湯を飲まされたが、今となってはこの千年でも稀な時間だった。何しろ、魔女の天敵は退屈よ。それから逃れることのできる数十年間を提供した金蔵には、なるほど、それも含めて借りがあるやも知れぬ」

description: UP inserts “goddamn” into Beatrice’s signature 全然駄目だ, which means that Battler’s argument is completely no good. The source line contains emphatic rejection but no profanity.
sourceReading: Beatrice mockingly declares Battler’s apparent nineteenth-person conclusion completely useless or no good before giving red truth.

units.text: "That is true, I most surely am the 19th person. *cackle*cackle*cackle*! But it's no good, I'm afraid...? It's no goddamn good at all!!"
units.japanese: 「そうであるな、妾こそが１９人目であろうな。くっくっくっく！　だが駄目だぜ？　全然駄目だぁ！！」

description: MG makes Ronove say “I’m baking” the new cookies. 焼かせている is causative: he is currently having new cookies baked, without saying that he personally performs the baking.
sourceReading: Ronove says that new cookies are being baked under his direction and proposes Beatrice’s past as the snack substitute until they are ready.

units.text: "I'm baking some new cookies right now. Until they're ready, I thought you might find the story of Milady's past to be a perfect substitute for a snack. Pu ku ku...!"
units.japanese: 「新しいクッキーを今、焼かせているところでございます。それまで、お茶菓子代わりにお嬢様の昔話がちょうどいいかと思いまして。ぷっくっく…！」

description: MG has Beatrice tell Ronove to “serve our food and then go.” The source tells him to withdraw promptly once he finishes serving; it does not introduce food or a collective meal.
sourceReading: Beatrice leaves and orders Ronove to withdraw as soon as he finishes his current service, without wasting time chatting with Battler.

units.text: "...D-Didn't I say that's enough talking about me?! Such unpleasant people, the lot of you. I'm leaving! Ronove, serve our food and then go. No pointless chitchat with Battler."
units.japanese: 「も、…もう妾の話はよいというのに！　揃って不愉快なヤツらだ。妾は席を外すぞ！　ロノウェ、給仕を済ませたらとっとと下がるのだぞ。戦人と無駄話などするでないぞ」
candidates: serve our food and then go

description: MG renders Battler’s thoughtful うーん as “no.” The source marks hesitation while he works out the next step of his reinterpretation; “no” instead makes him reject a proposition before introducing Beatrice’s possible daughter.
sourceReading: Battler hesitates while extending his mundane reconstruction from Beatrice’s death to the possibility that she left an identical daughter or infant.

units.text: ...And then, ......no. ...Maybe there was a girl who looked just like Beatrice...no, a baby. Grandfather raised this child with care.
units.japanese: ……それで、………うーん。…ベアトリーチェには、生き写しの娘、…いや、赤ん坊がいたとか。それで祖父さまはその子を大事に育てたわけだ。

description: MG has Battler tell Ronove “You said she was born from a homunculus.” The source explicitly refers to “that woman,” Beatrice, as the speaker; Ronove is being asked to confirm somebody else’s claim.
sourceReading: Battler says Beatrice claimed to have been born from a homunculus and asks Ronove whether such an unscientific magical existence is real.

units.text: "Th‐thanks a lot. I'll ask for some more red. You said she was born from a homunculus, but does that kind of unscientific, magical thing actually exist?!"
units.japanese: 「た、助かるぜ。さらに赤で頼む。あいつ、ホムンクルスから生まれたなんて言いやがったが、そんな非科学的な魔法的存在、実在するのか？！」
candidates: said she was born from a homunculus

description: MG says Battler cannot “play your next hand.” The chess term 一手 is the next move; a hand is a set of cards or an entire deal, not one chess action.
sourceReading: Ronove explains that if Battler cannot make his next move, Beatrice never receives another turn and the game remains frozen.

units.text: "Since you would not be able to play your next hand, it would never become Milady's turn, and the game would stop there for all eternity. As a result, Milady would be unable to force you to submit. ...That would be a deadlock situation.
units.japanese: 「戦人さまが次の一手を打てない以上、お嬢様に手番が回ってくることはなく、ゲームはそこで永遠に止まってしまう。その結果、お嬢様があなたを屈服させることもできない。……これが手詰まりの状態です」

description: MG calls game-ending 身も蓋もない questions “point-blank questions.” Point-blank means direct or blunt; the source describes questions that leave no room for the game or discussion to continue.
sourceReading: Battler summarizes that questions whose answers would settle the premise outright and halt play are prohibited from receiving red answers.

units.text: "...So, to say it quickly, you're saying point-blank questions are prohibited? Well, that's true, I guess. If I were told "a witch exists", I'd have to give up from the start."
units.japanese: 「……早い話が、身も蓋もない質問は禁止だと、そう言いたいわけだな？　まー、そりゃそうだよな。赤で、“魔女は実在する”って言われちまったら、俺はハナからお手上げだぜ」

description: MG renders Battler’s irritated tongue click ちぇ as “Heh,” changing annoyance into a chuckle or amused reaction.
sourceReading: Battler clicks his tongue in disappointment when Ronove refuses to answer the population request.

units.text: "Heh. Just when I thought you might actually be useful.
units.japanese: 「ちぇ。一瞬でも、使えるヤツと思ったのによ」

description: MG calls 1967 “The world of 19 years previous.” Without “ago” or another comparison point, previous cannot idiomatically express the dated scene’s relation to 1986.
sourceReading: Ronove states in red that this is the world of 1967, nineteen years ago relative to the game’s present.

units.text: "Correct. This is the world of 1967. The world of 19 years previous."
units.japanese: 「はい。ここは１９６７年の世界。１９年前の世界でございます」

description: MG says “at least 19 years ago” Beatrice existed on the island. The source says she had existed there as the nineteenth person for at least the preceding nineteen years, expressing duration rather than one point in time.
sourceReading: Battler infers that Beatrice had been present on Rokkenjima as a nineteenth person for at least nineteen years leading up to the 1986 game.

units.text: ...That means, at least 19 years ago, Beato existed on this island as the 19th person, ...umm...
units.japanese: …だとしたらつまり、少なくとも１９年前からベアトは１９人目としてこの島に存在してて、……えぇと……。

description: UP makes Battler say “The only thing that I can definitely say in red.” Battler cannot use red; he is summarizing what can be established with red through Ronove.
sourceReading: Battler reduces the speculation to the sole fact that can definitely be stated in red: a human Beatrice existed at the hidden mansion in 1967.

units.text: "......I'm starting to get confused. ...In any event, none of this leaves the realm of guesswork. The only thing that I can definitely say in red, is that in 1967, in a hidden mansion on Rokkenjima, Beatrice existed as a human. That's all."
units.japanese: 「……混乱してきたぜ。…いずれにせよ、憶測の域を出ない。確実に赤で言えることは、１９６７年の六軒島の隠し屋敷に、人間としてのベアトリーチェが存在した。それだけだ」
candidates: thing that I can definitely say in red

description: MG says Ronove “touched the watch stem.” 弄ろうとする says he moves to manipulate the crown, and the butterflies appear at that moment; MG turns the attempted or incipient action into a completed touch.
sourceReading: Ronove takes out a pocket watch and is about to manipulate or wind its crown to advance time when golden butterflies gather behind him.

units.text: Ronove pulled a stylish pocket watch from his pocket and touched the watch stem.
units.japanese: ロノウェはポケットより、洒落た懐中時計を取り出し、その竜頭を弄ろうとする。

description: MG writes “It’s seems my chat,” combining “it is” with a finite verb. The sentence requires “It seems.”
sourceReading: Ronove realizes that he has spent slightly too long chatting with Battler and excuses himself to answer Beatrice’s urgent summons.

units.text: "My, my, what kind of urgent business could it be? ...It's seems my chat with Battler-sama has run a tad long." "Well then, Battler-sama, if you will excuse me. Please continue to enjoy your game with Milady."
units.japanese: 「はて。至急のどのような御用やら。……少々、戦人さまとのお喋りが過ぎたようですね。それでは戦人さま、私めはこれで失礼させていただきます。どうか引き続き、お嬢様とのゲームをお楽しみ下さい」

description: MG translates 面汚しな愚妹ども only as “disgraceful younger sisters,” omitting 愚, Lucifer’s additional insult that they are foolish or stupid.
sourceReading: Lucifer proudly distinguishes herself from her disgraceful, foolish younger sisters and demands respect appropriate to her rank.

units.text: "......I'm not like my disgraceful younger sisters. If you don't show proper respect, you will regret it."
units.japanese: 「………他の面汚しな愚妹どもとは訳が違うの。それに見合った敬意を示さないと、後悔することになるわよ」

description: MG says Rosa questioned “more and more” why she had been born. The source says she lost her understanding of why she had been born, without a progressive increase.
sourceReading: Under repeated family pressure and a sense that she excelled at nothing, Rosa ceased to understand why she had been born.

units.text: I began to question more and more why I'd even been born at all. ...This is what happened on the day I experienced my mind going blank for the first time...
units.japanese:
何の為に生まれてきたのかわからなくなって。
…初めて頭の中が真っ白になるのを経験した、あの日のこと……。

description: UP renders 消極的な自殺 as “half-hearted suicide.” The phrase means passive suicide: disappearing and exposing oneself to harm without directly performing a decisive suicidal act. “Half-hearted” instead suggests weak commitment or insufficient resolve.
sourceReading: Rosa retrospectively describes running away as both leaving home and a passive form of suicide, while also considering it a child’s attempt to worry her parents.

units.text: Even though I say run away, there was no way I could have left Rokkenjima and gone somewhere else. But, anyway, I wanted to run away from the mansion and the way I was at the time. ......In a way, it was like running away from home, or maybe a half‐hearted suicide...
units.japanese: 逃げ出すと言っても、六軒島を出てどこかへ行けるはずもない。でも、とにかくお屋敷と今の自分から逃げ出したかった。……ある意味それは、家出でもあり、消極的な自殺でもあった…。

description: UP adds that reaching farther from the Ushiromiya family “made me feel good.” The source says only that this was Rosa’s feeling or mindset: crossing a harsher forest would mean escaping farther from the family.
sourceReading: Rosa felt that the more forbidding the forest she crossed, the farther she would have escaped from the Ushiromiya family.

units.text: "...Of course. So, I kept going wherever I could, and kept going deeper and deeper in. ......It was a horrible forest without any paths, but that was comforting to me then. ...If I could make it through such a dangerous forest, then it would be that much greater of an escape from the Ushiromiya family, ...which made me feel good."
units.japanese: 「…もちろんよ。だから、通れる方へ通れる方へ、とにかく奥へ奥へ進んだわ。……道なんかないひどい森だったけど、あの時の私にはそれが心地よかったの。…それほどの険しい森を抜けたなら、その分、右代宮家から逃れられるって、…そんな気持ちだったの」

description: MG changes the 業者 who built the mansion into “the businessman.” The source refers to the contractor, construction company, or builders who performed the work, not one generic businessman.
sourceReading: Eva suggests asking the contractor or builders responsible for constructing the main mansion what they know from that time.

units.text: "But just knowing that it actually exists is helpful. It would take some money, but if we enlisted an aerial photography company to investigate, or asked the businessman who constructed this mansion about what happened at the time, we could probably find some way to search for it."
units.japanese: 「でも、確かに存在するとわかっただけでも収穫よ。お金は掛かるだろうけど、例えば航空写真の会社に調査を頼むとか、このお屋敷を建設した業者に当時のことを聞くとか、調べる方法はあるかもしれないわね」

description: MG says Rosa “had little confidence in those days.” 自信を失いかけていた describes her beginning to lose confidence in her daily life; MG replaces an ongoing deterioration with a static low level and drops what her confidence concerned.
sourceReading: Rosa says that as she was beginning to lose confidence in how her life was going, she believed Beatrice’s help was her sole possible salvation.

units.text: At the time, ...I believed in the legend of the witch of the forest, Beatrice. I had been told that she was frightening, but some of the servants told me that she'd sometimes help you if you respected her. ...Since I had little confidence in those days, I believed the only way I could be saved was by receiving her help.
units.japanese: 私ね、……当時は森の魔女、ベアトリーチェの伝説を信じてたの。恐ろしい存在だと聞かされてはいたけれど、使用人の人は、敬いを持っていれば助けてくれることもあるって教えてくれて。……日々に自信を失いかけていた私には、彼女に助けてもらうことだけが、唯一の救いだと信じてたの。

description: UP renders 言葉が通じる as “she could be talked with.” The passive construction is unidiomatic and shifts mutual successful communication into Beatrice being an available target of speech.
sourceReading: Rosa is relieved because she realizes that she and Beatrice can understand or communicate with each other.

units.text:
Those were the first words she said to me.
...That calmed me down a little bit.
Because I realized that she could be talked with. Because I hadn't been turned into a frog just by meeting her eyes, like the terrifying witch in that fairy tale.
units.japanese:
それが彼女が私に掛けた最初の言葉。
…ちょっぴり安心したわ。
言葉が通じることがわかったから。おとぎ話の恐ろしい魔女のように、目が合っただけでカエルにされてしまわなかったから。

description: UP changes Beatrice’s question about whether Rosa is one of Kinzo’s family into a declarative conclusion.
sourceReading: After hearing the Ushiromiya name, Beatrice asks whether Rosa is a member of Kinzo’s family; Rosa then confirms that she is his daughter.

units.text: "......Ushiromiya. .....................Hoh. ...So you are one of Kinzo's family."
units.japanese: 「……右代宮。…………………ほぅ。…金蔵の一族の人間なのか」

description: UP says “she quickly became frightening,” making Beatrice change into something frightening. The source says Rosa suddenly became frightened of her.
sourceReading: Rosa suddenly becomes afraid because Beatrice addresses her fearsome father without an honorific, which Rosa takes as evidence of immense witch power.

units.text:
I was just a little surprised.
...After all, Father was a great man feared by everyone. And she had referred to him without using honorifics.
So she quickly became frightening. ...After all, if she could refer to my fearsome father that way, she must be a witch with incredible power.
units.japanese:
ちょっぴりだけ驚いたわ。
…だって、お父様は誰にも恐れられる偉大な方。そのお父様を、呼びつけにしたのだから。
だから急に恐ろしくなってしまったの。…だって、あの恐ろしいお父様を呼びつけにできるほど、彼女はすごい力を持った魔女に違いないのだから。

description: MG uses “some breed of stray dogs” for 野犬の類. 類 means stray or wild dogs or something of that sort; “breed” incorrectly suggests a biological breed classification.
sourceReading: Natsuhi proposes that there might have been stray or wild dogs, or similar animals, and that the fence may have protected against them.

units.text: "...Wolves aside, could there have been some breed of stray dogs there at the time? Perhaps the fence was there to protect against those."
units.japanese: 「…狼はともかく、野犬の類でもいたのではありませんか？　その為の柵だったかも知れません」

description: UP’s “No surprise she felt it hard” is unidiomatic and weakens 苦労もあった, which says Beatrice must have suffered hardships or had a difficult time under confinement.
sourceReading: Rudolf infers that despite her beautiful mansion, garden, and clothes, Beatrice must have felt constrained and endured considerable hardship.

units.text: "Even though she had beautiful clothes, a beautiful mansion, and a garden, she must have felt very constrained. No surprise she felt it hard. .........And then?"
units.japanese: 「綺麗なドレスに綺麗な屋敷や庭があっても、さぞや窮屈な思いをしてたんだろうぜ。そりゃ苦労もあったろうさ。………それで？」

description: MG replaces Rosa’s “I don’t know how it will turn out, but...” with a premature “I’ll take her out,” then repeats the decision on the following line. This removes her explicit uncertainty and duplicates the resolution.
sourceReading: Rosa does not know what the consequences will be, but resolves to take Beatrice out of the mansion.

units.text: ......I'll take her out. ...but I'll take her away from here. Of course, I won't be able to talk to Father, and not Mother either. ......Should I talk to Onii-sama or Onee-sama? No, what about that reliable Genji-san... or, that's right, what about Kumasawa-san, to whom I can always talk when I'm in trouble.
units.japanese:
どうなるかはわからないけれど……、……彼女を連れ出そう。お父様はもちろん、お母様にも相談できないだろう。………お兄様かお姉様に相談を？
うぅん、頼りになる源次さんか、…そうだ、困った時はいつも相談に乗ってくれる熊沢さんはどうだろう。

description: MG misspells “responsibility” as “responsiblity” in Rosa’s resolve to take responsibility for the situation.
sourceReading: Having brought Beatrice outside, Rosa says she must somehow take responsibility and resolve the situation.

units.text: She was too innocent, and apparently, she couldn't understand at all how frightening it would be to face the night inside the forest. But I was the one who brought her outside. ...I had to take responsiblity somehow and resolve this situation.
units.japanese:
彼女は無邪気すぎて、森の中で夜を迎えてしまうことがどれほど恐ろしいか、まったく理解できていないようだった。でも、外へ連れ出したのは私。
…何とか責任を持って、この事態を解決しなくちゃ。

description: MG omits “to” from “managed reach the ocean,” producing an ungrammatical narration line at the successful end of the forest crossing.
sourceReading: After considerable difficulty, Rosa and Beatrice fortunately manage to reach the sea.

units.text: Then, after going through various troubles, I fortunately managed reach the ocean... At that time, I still didn't even have a clue where I was on the island, but for the time being, I was just a little reassured, realizing that if I just went around this way, I would surely be able to return to the mansion.
units.japanese: そして、色々と苦労したけれど、幸いにも海に出ることができた…。今、島のどこにいるのかは、相変わらず見当もつかなかったけれど、とにかく、こちら回りに進めば、必ずお屋敷へ帰れるとわかって、ちょっとだけ安心したわ。

description: UP says Rosa “planned” to descend the rocky cliff. 提案した says she proposed the descent to Beatrice, which is why Beatrice can then agree to her proposal.
sourceReading: Rosa proposes that they somehow descend the rocky cliff, while also wondering whether another plan might be possible because it looks dangerous.

units.text:
So I planned to somehow go down the rocky cliff.
...It did look pretty dangerous, and I wondered if there was some other way. However, Beatrice agreed with my plan without any doubts. ......Even though she was probably older than me, ...she obeyed me truly obediently, almost as though she were some kind of chick who believed I was a mother bird.
units.japanese:
だから、何とかして岩壁を降りようと提案したの。
…一応、危なそうだったし、他に案はないかと思って。でも、ベアトリーチェは私の提案に何の疑いもなく頷いた。……歳は向こうの方が上だろうに、…まるで私を親鳥だと信じるアヒルか何かの雛のように、本当に素直に従ったわ。

description: UP says time “had begun to start counting again.” Begun and start redundantly express the same inception; “had begun counting again” is the grammatical form.
sourceReading: After the clock passes from twenty-four to zero, it begins counting anew.

units.text: On the antique clock with an intricate design that was sitting on his desk, the two overlapping hands had begun to tilt to the right, and separate from one another. The passage of time that had counted to 24 had returned to 0, and begun to start counting again...
units.japanese: 机の上に置かれた、凝った意匠の施されたアンティークの時計は、重なっていた２本の針を右に傾かせ、ずらし始めている。２４を数えた時の刻みが０に戻り、再びそれを数え直していた…。

description: MG says repeating the reading “ridicules” its result. 冒涜 is desecration or profanation: Kinzo describes sacrilege against both the result and the higher being, not mockery.
sourceReading: Ordinary tarot doctrine treats a repeated reading as desecrating both the first result and the higher being that grants revelation.

units.text: The most forbidden action in tarot reading is trying to predict the same thing twice. To do so ridicules the results of fortune telling... and also desecrates those beings higher than humans that give revelations through the tarot cards.
units.japanese: タロット占いでもっとも禁じられている行為は、同じことを二度占うことである。それは占いの結果に対する冒涜であり、タロットを通じて神託を与えてくれる、人より上位の存在への冒涜ともなるのである。

description: UP inserts a comma between the full subject clause and its verb in “they who could understand things that people couldn’t perceive, were able...”. The comma improperly splits subject from predicate.
sourceReading: The servants can perceive an otherwise invisible dramatic change in the doorknob’s magical barrier.

units.text:
Of course, there was no change to the doorknob that the eye could see.
However, they who could understand things that people couldn't perceive, were able to recognize the dramatic change...
units.japanese:
もちろん、見た目にはそのドアノブに何の変化もない。
しかし、人には知覚できぬものを理解できる彼らには、その劇的変化が理解できた…。
candidates: understand things that people couldn't perceive, were able

description: UP says the door “had long been wide open” to magical beings. すでに開きっぱなしと同じ means the broken barrier made it equivalent to being left open already; it supplies no long duration.
sourceReading: Once the barrier is broken, the physically locked door is effectively already open to anyone with magical power.

units.text: However, the fact that the barrier had been destroyed... meant that this door had long been wide open for anyone with magical power...
units.japanese: しかし、結界が破られているということは、魔力ある者にとって、この扉はすでに開きっぱなしと同じ意味だ…。
candidates: door had long been wide open

description: UP says Kinzo was sitting “in a reception sofa.” A person sits on a sofa; “in” incorrectly treats it like an enclosing seat or location.
sourceReading: Kinzo sits on a reception sofa with his back toward the entering servants.

units.text: They immediately discovered Kinzo's figure. ......He was sitting in a reception sofa so that his back faced them.
units.japanese: 金蔵の姿はすぐに見つけられた。……応接ソファーに背を向けるようにして座っていた。

description: UP says Kanon “observed” that Beatrice and Kinzo were playing chess. ようやく知った marks his realization or discovery after recognizing the tableau, not merely an act of watching.
sourceReading: Kanon finally realizes that Beatrice and Kinzo have been playing chess across from one another.

units.text: Then, Kanon finally observed. Beatrice and Kinzo were enjoying a chess game, sitting in facing reception sofas. But Kinzo hadn't even quivered. He was holding his head with both hands, his eyes closed tight, ...as he contemplated his next move.
units.japanese: そして嘉音はようやく知った。ベアトリーチェと金蔵は応接ソファーに向かい合い、チェスを興じていたのだ。しかし、金蔵は微動だにしない。両手で自らの頭を抱え、固く目を瞑り…、次の手を黙考しているのだ。

description: MG turns Kanon’s direct accusation “even though you toy with and kill people” into “We know you’re just a murderer who kills for fun.” It invents a collective “we know,” recasts an action as an identity label, and adds “just.”
sourceReading: Kanon calls Beatrice a liar and accuses her of toying with people as she kills them.

units.text: "...L-Liar. We know you're just a murderer who kills for fun..."
units.japanese: 「…う、嘘を吐け。弄んで殺しているくせに……」
candidates: know you're just a murderer who kills for fun

description: UP renders “Several decades that were not boring...!” as a sentence fragment without a finite verb, unlike the complete source declaration.
sourceReading: Beatrice tells Kinzo that their contest gave her several decades free from boredom.

units.text: "It is to me too. ......Concluding my contest with you may bring a flood of emotions, but it has already surpassed love and hate. ...It was fun. Several decades that were not boring...!"
units.japanese: 「妾もだ。……そなたとの勝負に決着がつくことは、万感の思いあれど、もはや恩讐を越える。…楽しかったぞ。退屈しない数十年であった…！」
candidates: Several decades that were not boring

description: UP calls George “the person of [Shannon’s] thoughts.” 想い人 is her beloved or the person she loves, and the literal calque is not idiomatic English.
sourceReading: Shannon probably wanted to spend a little more warm time with George, the man she loved.

units.text: Shannon had not yet reached as high of a philosophical state of mind as Genji. There probably really were regrets left in her heart. ...She probably wanted to spend a little more warm time with the person of her thoughts, George.
units.japanese: 紗音は、源次に比べるとまだ達観の境地には達していなかった。本当はまだ心の中に未練があっただろう。…想い人の譲治と、もう少し温かな時間を過ごしたかっただろう。
candidates: probably wanted to spend a little more warm time

description: MG twice renders 達観 as “far-sighted,” first for Shannon’s detached acceptance and then for Genji and Shannon’s shared state. 達観 here is philosophical detachment or resignation, not foresight about the future.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Shannon has recently become markedly detached; the narration then contrasts Genji and Shannon’s attained detachment with Kanon’s anguish.

units.text: "She's been taking such a far-sighted view of things lately. I must've tormented her too much last time. Speaking of which, didn't I do the same to Battler?
units.japanese:
「最近、こやつめはだいぶ達観しよった。…どうも前回、苛め過ぎたようだ。それを言ったら戦人もか？」
達観の境地に達した二人に比べ、…嘉音の表情には苦々しい苦悶が浮かぶ。唐突に現れた魔女に、終焉を告げられて、何の未練もなく受け容れるには、嘉音はまだまだ若かった…。

units.text: Compared to the two who had taken a far-sighted approach, ...there was a painful anguish on Kanon's face. Kanon was still far too young to accept his demise after being told of it by a suddenly appearing witch...
units.japanese:
「最近、こやつめはだいぶ達観しよった。…どうも前回、苛め過ぎたようだ。それを言ったら戦人もか？」
達観の境地に達した二人に比べ、…嘉音の表情には苦々しい苦悶が浮かぶ。唐突に現れた魔女に、終焉を告げられて、何の未練もなく受け容れるには、嘉音はまだまだ若かった…。

description: UP says Beatrice orders Kanon to defeat “my furniture of the Seven Stakes of Purgatory.” The construction incorrectly makes the Seven Stakes sound like a group possessing or classifying some other furniture; they themselves are Beatrice’s furniture.
sourceReading: Beatrice commands Kanon to defeat her furniture, the Seven Stakes of Purgatory.

units.text: "Show me that you can defeat my furniture of the Seven Stakes of Purgatory. If you manage to come out the admirable victor, .........hm, let us see..."
units.japanese: 「我が家具、煉獄の七杭を打ち破って見せよ。見事打ち破って見せたなら、………そうだな」
candidates: defeat my furniture of the Seven Stakes of Purgatory

units.text: "I did promise you, didn't I? If you could defeat my furniture, of the Seven Stakes of Purgatory, riiiiiiight? Come, arise, Seven Stakes of Purgatory. The six younger sisters of the worthless elder sister!"
units.note: UP repeats the malformed “my furniture, of the Seven Stakes of Purgatory” construction while restating Beatrice’s promise.
units.japanese: 「妾は確かにそなたと約束したぞ？　妾の家具、煉獄の七杭を打ち破ったなら、となぁああぁ？　さぁさお出でなさい、煉獄の七杭。不甲斐なき長女の６人の妹たち！」
candidates: defeat my furniture, of the Seven Stakes of Purgatory

description: MG turns Beatrice’s claim that the conspicuous magical combat has ruined Battler’s position into “it’d be a waste to miss it.” The source attacks the viability of his denial and reasoning; it does not tell him that missing the spectacle would be wasteful.
sourceReading: With all the whooshing and clashing displayed directly before Battler, Beatrice taunts that his attempt to deny magic or sustain his reasoning is ruined, then urges him to stop thinking.

units.text: "If you've got all this happening right in front of you, it'd be a waste to miss it, don't you thiiiiiink? Look, look, look, just stop thinking, magic exists! This is fantasy! Don't close your eyes, look closely, look, look, look, look!!"
units.japanese: 「こうして目の前でブォンブォンカキンカキンやられちゃあ、台無しだよなぁああぁ？　ほらほらほらほら、もう思考なんて止めちまえよォ、魔法はあるんだって！　これはファンタジーなんだッて！　目を閉じるなよ、しっかり見ろよ、ほらほらほらほらほらァ！！」
candidates: it'd be a waste to miss

description: MG makes Beatrice say Battler “doesn’t really like to think things through.” 苦手 means he is bad at thinking, so the taunt attacks his intellectual ability rather than his preference or willingness.
sourceReading: Beatrice claims she knows Battler is actually bad at thinking and uses that alleged weakness to urge him to stop reasoning and accept fantasy.

units.text: I know your secret, you actually don't really like to think things through, right?? Then just stop, stoooop, *cackle*cackle*! Look, look, it's gotta be fantasy, gotta be fantasy, kihhihihyahyahhyahhyahhyahhyahhyaaaaaahhh!!"
units.japanese: 「知ってんだよ、モノを考えンの本当は苦手なんだろォ？？　止めちまえ止めちまえェエ、くっくっくっく！　ほらほらどうせファンタジーどうせファンタジー、くっひひひゃひゃっひゃっひゃっひゃっひゃっひゃあぁああぁ！！」

description: UP promises “I’ll spare you” from Lucifer’s flaying and whipping if Kanon apologizes. 特別に許してあげてもいい presents this as something she may be willing to pardon or exempt him from as a special concession, not an unconditional promise.
sourceReading: Lucifer says that, if Kanon crawls and apologizes, she might specially let him off the threatened flaying and whipping.

units.text: ".........This guy's gotten obstinate. ...Get down on the ground right now and apologize for being so conceited that you thought you could "at least beat me". If you do, I'll spare you, alright...?"
units.japanese:
「………こいつ、意地になっちゃってぇ。…私になら勝てるなんて思いあがりをしたことを、今すぐ床に這いつくばって謝ってごらんなさい…？　そうしたら、特別に許してあげてもいいわよぅ…？」
「生きながら生皮を剥がして、絶命するまで全身を鞭打ってのた打ち回らすのを、特別に許してあげてもいいわよぅ。ふっふふふふふふふふふふ！」

units.text: "I'll spare you from having your skin ripped off while you're still alive, and being lashed all over your body as you squirm until you die. Hehheh{0eh{0eh{0eh{0eh{0eh{0eh{0eheheh!"
units.japanese:
「………こいつ、意地になっちゃってぇ。…私になら勝てるなんて思いあがりをしたことを、今すぐ床に這いつくばって謝ってごらんなさい…？　そうしたら、特別に許してあげてもいいわよぅ…？」
「生きながら生皮を剥がして、絶命するまで全身を鞭打ってのた打ち回らすのを、特別に許してあげてもいいわよぅ。ふっふふふふふふふふふふ！」

description: MG describes a glowing red “curve” extending straight from Kanon’s arm. 軌跡 is the weapon’s trail or trajectory; calling it a curve directly conflicts with the stated straight extension.
sourceReading: A red trail flashes straight out from Kanon’s arm and stops exactly beneath Lucifer’s chin at her throat.

units.text: The glowing red curve extended straight out from Kanon's arm, ...pointing at Lucifer's throat, just beneath the tip of her chin...
units.japanese: 嘉音の腕より閃く赤き軌跡が真っ直ぐに伸び、……ルシファーの喉元を指し、顎の先端をぴったりと捉えていた…。

description: MG writes that Lucifer fell down “wretching.” The required word for making vomiting motions is “retching”; “wretching” is a nonstandard misspelling derived from “wretch.”
sourceReading: After Kanon releases her, Lucifer lies face-down, making motions as though vomiting and groaning from the pain in her throat.

units.text: But even so, Kanon released the witch's furniture. ...Was it his naive humanism, his pity for another furniture, or a final bit of respect to the witch? In any case, when she was released, Lucifer fell face-down on the ground, wretching and moaning over the pain in her throat...
units.japanese: しかしそれでも、嘉音は魔女の家具を解放した。……彼の甘いヒューマニズムか、家具同士の憐れみか、それとも魔女への最後の敬意かはわからない。何れにせよ、解放されたルシファーは床に突っ伏し、嘔吐するような仕草をしながら、喉の苦しみに呻いていた…。

description: UP says Kanon’s struggle “has gone some way to proving” Kinzo’s research correct. 正しさがひとつ、実証されました says one point or item of its correctness has now been demonstrated; it does not reduce the result to merely partial progress toward proof.
sourceReading: Ronove says Kanon’s struggle has demonstrated one proposition establishing the correctness of Kinzo’s research.

units.text: "Spectacular, Kanon. ......Your great efforts have gone some way to proving Kinzo's research correct."
units.japanese: 「お見事ですよ、嘉音。……あなたの奮闘により、金蔵の研究の正しさがひとつ、実証されました」
candidates: gone some way to proving Kinzo's research correct

description: UP calls witches and demons “unjust.” 非道 describes them as ruthless, cruel, or inhumane; the contrast is between their general brutality and their exceptional nobility concerning contracts, not between ordinary unfairness and contracts.
sourceReading: Beatrice says witches and demons are ruthless, yet surpass humans in their nobility where contracts are concerned.

units.text: "Mhm. Of course I have not forgotten. Witches and demons are admittedly unjust. However, we are much more noble than humans when it comes to our contracts."
units.japanese: 「うむ。もちろん忘れてはおらぬぞ。魔女も悪魔も非道ではある。だがしかし契約に限っては人間など及ばぬほどに高潔だ」

description: MG says witches and demons are nobler than humans “when it comes to keeping promises.” 契約 specifically concerns contracts, a recurrent magical institution with formal terms; replacing it with generic promises broadens the rule and drops the terminology.
sourceReading: Witches and demons may be ruthless, but in matters of contract they are more noble than humans; Beatrice therefore will not repudiate the bargain she made with Kanon.

units.text: "Indeed. Of course I haven't forgotten. Witches and demons may be inhumane. However, we are much more noble than humans when it comes to keeping promises."
units.japanese: 「うむ。もちろん忘れてはおらぬぞ。魔女も悪魔も非道ではある。だがしかし契約に限っては人間など及ばぬほどに高潔だ」
candidates: humans when it comes to keeping promises

description: MG says Shannon is “not quite amusing at the present moment.” このところ means recently or lately, describing a continuing recent change in her; “the present moment” narrows that development to the immediate instant.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Shannon has lately lacked entertainment value, then generalizes that love is most interesting while its fulfillment remains uncertain.

units.text: "......... ...Hmmmm. At any rate, you're not quite amusing at the present moment. Romance is most interesting when you're wondering whether it will succeed or not."
units.japanese: 「……………………。……ふぅむ。どうにもそなたはこのところ面白みに欠けるな？　恋というヤツは、達するかどうかの辺りが一番面白い」
candidates: quite amusing at the present moment

description: UP makes Shannon say she could not “match up to [Genji’s] greatness.” 高み is the elevated state or level of detachment Genji attained; “greatness” converts that comparison of achieved composure into a broad judgment of his personal stature.
sourceReading: Shannon apologizes that she ultimately could not attain Genji’s elevated level of detachment and accept death without intervening.

units.text: "......My apologies. In the end, I wasn't able to match up to your greatness, Genji‐sama."
units.japanese: 「……申し訳ございません。やはり私には、源次さまの高みには至れませんでした」

description: UP writes “This is why you’re furniture you don’t even smell like a human” without a conjunction or punctuation between two independent clauses.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Shannon’s detachment is precisely why she is furniture: she does not even smell human.

units.text: "......Nnnngggggaaaaaaaaahhhh, you're pissing me off. That philosophic view is really irritating!! This is why you're furniture you don't even smell like a humaaaaaan!!"
units.japanese: 「……んんんんぁあああぁあああぁあぁ、イライラするぜェ。その達観が本当にイラつくぜぇえぇ？！　だから家具なんだよ、お前からは人間の臭いがしねぇえんだよぉおおお！！」
candidates: you're furniture you don't even smell like

description: UP inserts “goddamn” twice into Beatrice’s rapid sequence of incomprehension and shock. The Japanese is emphatic and vulgar in delivery but contains no corresponding profanity in those positions.
sourceReading: Beatrice erupts that she cannot understand Shannon at all, piling up expressions of disappointment, shock, and stupefaction before declaring her wholly hopeless.

units.text: "It's not a regreeeeeet, this is called LIVING!! You received a ring, so it's alright if you die, what?! Aaaaah, I can't understand it, not a clue not a hope, goddamn astonished, goddamn shocked, no goddamn good at aa{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-a{-aalll!!"
units.japanese: 「未練じゃねぇえええぇえ、それが生きるってもんだッ！！　指輪もらったから死んでもいいとかッ！　あああぁ理解できねぇ、さっぱりがっかり愕然呆然ッ、全然駄目だぜええええぇえ！！」

description: MG misspells “emanating” as “eminating” when the crimson stain spreads from beneath Genji’s hand.
sourceReading: A crimson stain gently spreads from the place where Genji presses his left hand near Shannon’s collarbone.

units.text: After that, Genji softly pressed his left hand near her collarbone... ...As he did, eminating from that area... a crimson stain gently spread out.
units.japanese: それから源次は、左手を、彼女の鎖骨の辺りにやさしく押し当てる…。……すると、その左手を押し当てたところから、……真紅の染みがやさしく広がる。

description: UP has Gohda address the portrait as “Great witch of the portrait.” The Japanese 魔女さま is the respectful “Witch-sama” or “Lady Witch”; it does not add the rank or power claim “Great Witch.”
sourceReading: Gohda half-jokingly and respectfully appeals to the witch of the portrait to go easy on him because he will work diligently.

units.text: "So there's a curse if you make fun of the witch of the portrait, huh. ......Seems like there were servants who got hurt really bad and quit, too. ...I'd hate to be injured. I'm already this old. Doubt I'll ever be blessed with a workplace this hospitable again... Aaah. Great witch of the portrait. I'm really gonna work hard here, so please go easy on me."
units.japanese: 「肖像画の魔女を馬鹿にすると、祟りがあるか。……大怪我をして辞めた使用人もいるらしいし。…怪我は勘弁だなぁ。俺もこの歳だ。二度とこんな厚遇の職場にゃ恵まれねぇだろうよ…。あー。肖像画の魔女さま。真面目に働きますんで、ひとつ穏便に頼みます」

description: UP says Kumasawa has “given herself up,” which ordinarily means surrendered herself to an opponent. 観念した here means the sisters assume she has resigned herself to her fate; it does not describe a voluntary surrender into their custody.
sourceReading: Seeing Kumasawa standing motionless in the rain, one sister assumes she has resigned herself to the inevitable and claims the kill.

units.text:
She's given herself up, all mine all mine all miiine!
You slowpokes can just sit there and watch! I told you, nooooooo, this one's miiiiiiiiiiiiine!!
units.japanese:
観念したんだよ、いただきいただき、いっただきぃ！
ノロマなあんたたちはぼんやり見てればいいのよ！だから駄目ぇえええぇ、今度は私がもらうのぉおおおおぉおお！！

description: UP answers “I never even dreamed...” with “Yes, me too.” A negative statement requires “neither did I” or an equivalent negative response, especially in the teacher’s formal voice.
sourceReading: Beatrice says she never dreamed they would meet again; the teacher agrees that she likewise never dreamed her sleep would be disturbed.

units.text: "Yes, me too. ...Certainly, I never even dreamed that my sleep would be disturbed."
units.japanese: 「えぇ、私もですよ。…よもやまた、眠りを妨げられるとは夢にも思いませんでした」

description: UP says “For those who do not listen the first time, I say it a second” and “I do not speak it a third.” Both clauses omit the required noun “time,” producing unidiomatic English in the teacher’s warning.
sourceReading: The teacher warns that she will repeat herself once for anyone who fails to listen, but will not issue a third warning.

units.text: "I have already surrendered that name to this child. ......Come now, step back. Furniture girls. ......For those who do not listen the first time, I say it a second. However, I do not speak it a third..."
units.japanese: 「その名はもう、その子に譲りました。……さぁ、下がりなさい。家具の娘たち。……私は一度聞かぬとしても、二度言います。しかし、三度目は口にしませんよ…？」
candidates: listen the first time, I say it a second

description: UP makes Battler call transformed Kumasawa “an attractive lady.” 姉ちゃん marks her as a young woman or young lady in contrast with “Granny Kumasawa”; it does not state Battler’s judgment that she is attractive.
sourceReading: Battler demands to know why Granny Kumasawa has transformed into a young woman and who she is.

units.text: "Y‐...you... Who are you? Why did Kumasawa baa‐chan turn into an attractive lady like this?! I mean, who are you?! I don't get it?! What kind of special effects are these?! My head feels like it's gonna explode!!"
units.japanese: 「あ、…あんた…、何者なんだ。熊沢のばあちゃんが、どうしてこんな姉ちゃんに化けるんだ？！　つーか、あんた誰だよッ？！　訳がわからねぇ？！　これは何の特撮なんだ？！　俺は頭がどうにかなっちまいそうだッ！！」

description: UP says Beatrice sneers “with an absolute superiority.” Superiority is uncountable in this construction; idiomatic English requires “with absolute superiority” or, as MG has it, “with a sense of absolute superiority.”
sourceReading: Beatrice floats between the enormous towers, looks down on her teacher, and sneers from a position of absolute superiority.

units.text: As Beatrice elegantly floated in the gap between the massive two‐headed towers, she looked down on her master, sneering with an absolute superiority. With the two massive towers lined up behind her shoulders, the witch looked very small, like a butterfly dancing between large trees.
units.japanese: ベアトリーチェはその巨大な双頭の塔の狭間に優雅に浮かびながら、師匠を見下ろし、絶対の優位に嘲笑う。巨大なる塔を双肩に並べる魔女はあまりに小さく見え、まるで大樹の間を舞う蝶のように見えた。

description: UP writes “the whole giants’ regiment,” an unidiomatic possessive construction. The source describes the entire regiment of giants or giant regiment forming the defensive wall.
sourceReading: When the whole regiment of giants once joined their shields, they protected King Wilhelm’s castle even from wind and rain.

units.text: Once in the past, when the massive shields these giants held had been readied by the whole giants' regiment, they had protected King Wilhelm's castle not only from arrows, but from the wind and the rain, and when they had faced upwards and held their shields to the heavens, not a single raindrop had gotten through.
units.japanese: 巨人たちが構える巨大楯は、かつて巨人連隊全員が連なって構えた時、ヴィルヘルム王の居城を矢だけでなく、風雨からすら守り、天に向けてかざした時には雨粒の一滴すらも許さなかったという。

description: MG says “The divine spear avoided her.” The source says the spear itself avoided the absolute shield or their forbidden clash; making the teacher the object leaves the spear avoiding its own wielder rather than the impact.
sourceReading: The teacher corrects the apparent block: under divine law, the absolute spear itself avoids colliding with the absolute shield, which is functionally equivalent to being blocked.

units.text: "No, that is not correct. The divine spear avoided her. It is the law of the gods that an absolute spear and an absolute shield must never fight one another. Although, in the end, it means the same thing as defending against it."
units.japanese: 「いいえ違います。神なる槍がよけたのです。絶対の槍と絶対の楯は争ってはいけないのが神々の掟。それはつまり、防いだのと同じことですがね」

description: MG says the near-20,000-bolt attack met “no resistance.” 手応えがない means Beatrice feels no impact, contact, or confirming response from the supposed hit; it does not mean the teacher offered no resistance.
sourceReading: Although the barrage should have reduced the teacher to dust, Beatrice feels no impact or confirmation and immediately realizes she has been tricked.

units.text: That bundle of almost 20,000 thunderbolts must have reduced the teacher's body to dust. But there had been no resistance. Beatrice knew immediately that she had been fooled.
units.japanese: ２万にも届きかねない稲妻の束は確かに師匠の体を塵に変えたはずだった。しかし手応えがない。ベアトリーチェは一杯食わされたとすぐに直感する。

description: UP writes that the spear “In mid-air... sprung up into the air once more,” redundantly placing an object already in mid-air into the air again. The source says it bounces once through space, leaps upward, and transforms.
sourceReading: After being launched, the divine spear bounces once through space, springs upward, and changes into the heavenly iron hammer.

units.text: In mid‐air, it sprung up into the air once more, and changed its form once again.
units.japanese: それは空間で一度跳ねて飛び上がると、再びその姿を変えた。
candidates: sprung up into the air once

description: UP says Beatrice will “lose the fact that you are my disciple.” The source says she will cease to be the teacher’s disciple; the re-edit leaves an ungrammatical, abstract “lose the fact” construction.
sourceReading: Beatrice will lose her status or place as the teacher’s disciple, while remaining the lady whom the teacher serves.

units.text: ".........It's alright, Milady. You will lose the fact that you are my disciple, but that will not change the fact that you are the lady I serve."
units.japanese: 「………大丈夫ですよ、お嬢様。あなたは私の弟子であることを失いますが、私の仕えるお嬢様であることに変わりはありません」
candidates: lose the fact that you are my disciple

description: UP turns two disappearances into acts of erasure: the teacher “began to completely erase her form,” then the spear “erased itself.” The source says her form completely vanishes and the spear also disappears, without assigning either entity an act of erasing itself.
sourceReading: As the teacher fully remembers that she was already dead, her form vanishes completely; the spear piercing Beatrice disappears with her.

units.text: Then the Predecessor slowly remembered that she had already been killed, ......and began to completely erase her form.
units.japanese:
そして彼女は自らがすでに殺されていたことを徐々に思い出し、……姿を完全に消していく。
するとベアトリーチェを貫いていた槍も姿を消した。ベアトリーチェはようやく大地に降り立つ。
…傷跡など、わずかほども残っていなかった。
candidates: began to completely erase her form

units.text:
When she did, the spear which had pierced Beatrice also erased itself. Beatrice finally fell and landed on her feet.
...There wasn't even a trace of a scar.
units.japanese:
そして彼女は自らがすでに殺されていたことを徐々に思い出し、……姿を完全に消していく。
するとベアトリーチェを貫いていた槍も姿を消した。ベアトリーチェはようやく大地に降り立つ。
…傷跡など、わずかほども残っていなかった。

description: UP renders 魔女はいるも何も as the direct question “Do witches exist, I ask?!” Battler is doing the opposite: saying the spectacle has gone far beyond the mere question of whether witches exist.
sourceReading: Forget merely asking whether witches exist: after that tremendous fantasy, Battler no longer knows what he can deny.

units.text: "Do witches exist, I ask?! After all those kabooms and kabangs, after being shown all that tremendous fantasy, what can I deny now?!! I don't get it anymore! It was like that last time too, but how can I deny that awesome, wonderful magical battle?!"
units.japanese: 「魔女はいるも何も！　あんなどっかんどっかん、凄まじいファンタジーを見せ付けられて、今の俺は何を否定すりゃいいんだよ！！　もうわかんねぇッ！　前回もそうだが、このイカス素敵なマジカルバトルをどう否定すりゃいいんだよッ？！」

description: UP translates Battler’s ふざけるな as “Fuck you!!” The source is an angry command to stop fooling or messing with him; the re-edit turns his objection to Ronove’s invitation into a direct obscenity aimed at Ronove.
sourceReading: Battler angrily tells Ronove to stop messing with him and demands to know how he is supposed to rebut the spectacle.

units.text: "Fuck you!! How the hell can I make a counterargument?!"
units.japanese: 「ふざけるなッ！！　何をどう反論すりゃいいってんだッ？！」

description: UP writes “Some teenage brat has a whole bunch of some strange special abilities,” combining incompatible quantity constructions and singularizing the source’s teenage kids.
sourceReading: Teenage kids have lots of strange special abilities and stage explosive battles with the fate of the world at stake.

units.text: "I know all about it, this kind of stuff's been going around everywhere lately hasn't it?! In manga and light novels, in anime and movies!
