Some teenage brat has a whole bunch of some strange special abilities, and there's all these kabooms and badooms with the fate of the world at risk!"
units.japanese: 「知ってんダヨ、今時こんなの巷にいくらでも溢れてるじゃねぇかァ？！　漫画に小説、アニメに映画ッ！　１０代くらいのガキンチョたちがおかしな特殊能力いっぱい持ってて、世界の命運かけてドッカンバッカンやるやつぅ！」
candidates: teenage brat has a whole bunch of some strange special abilities

description: MG changes Krauss’s “at my age” into “at our age,” extending his personal complaint about the strain of an all-nighter to the group.
sourceReading: Krauss accepts the suggestion to rest and says that staying up all night is hard on him at his age.

units.text: "...A good plan. Staying up all night is trying at our age."
units.japanese: 「…良い提案だ。この歳に徹夜は堪えるよ」

description: MG turns Rudolf’s collective “Let’s go wash our faces; we must look awful” into “I’ll go wash my face... I probably look horrible,” changing the proposed group movement into a solitary one.
sourceReading: Rudolf proposes that the group go wash their faces and remarks that they must look terrible after the all-nighter.

units.text: "I'll go wash my face or something. I probably look horrible."
units.japanese: 「顔でも洗ってこようぜ。きっとひでぇツラさ」

description: MG says Natsuhi’s group noticed something strange “near the parlor.” 客間の異変 is an abnormality of or involving the parlor itself: the marked and locked door subsequently examined.
sourceReading: On the way to find someone in the servants’ room, Natsuhi’s group notices that something is wrong with the parlor itself.

units.text: At the same time, when Natsuhi's group was on its way to search for someone in the servant room, they noticed something strange near the parlor.
units.japanese: 一方、夏妃たちは使用人室へ誰かを探しに行く途中、客間の異変に気付く。
candidates: noticed something strange near the parlor

description: UP says Krauss doubts Kinzo will be “good-natured enough” to listen. 素直に describes compliant, straightforward willingness to hear him out, not general kindness or temperament.
sourceReading: Krauss will ask Kinzo what is happening, though he doubts his father will straightforwardly or obediently hear him out.

units.text: "......We might have become involved in a bizarre game of Father's. ...I will go to him and ask about the situation. ......Though I doubt he'll be good‐natured enough to listen to me."
units.japanese: 「……親父殿の、おかしなゲームに巻き込まれているのかもしれんな。…私は親父殿のところへ行って、事情を聞いてみよう。……まぁ、素直に話を聞いてくれるとは思えんがね」

description: MG reads 良さそう as desire—“it certainly would be nice” if a crested envelope appeared. Kyrie is assessing what ought plausibly to accompany a game announcement, not expressing that such an envelope would please her.
sourceReading: If this is a game, it would be reasonable or unsurprising for another crested envelope like Maria’s to appear.

units.text: "...In that case, I wonder if they'll give us an announcement of the game or some explanation of it. ...It certainly would be nice if an envelope with the crest, like the one handed to Maria-chan, were to appear."
units.japanese: 「…なら、ゲームの開始宣言、もしくはゲームの説明などがあったりはしないのかしら。……真里亞ちゃんに渡したような、紋章入りの封筒が出てきても良さそうだけど」

description: MG misspells “reflexively” as “reflecively” when Beatrice recoils from Battler’s rage.
sourceReading: Beatrice involuntarily recoils at Battler’s sudden fury.

units.text: Beatrice winced reflecively at Battler's sudden rage.
units.japanese: 戦人の突然の激昂に、ベアトリーチェは思わずたじろぐ。

description: UP changes Battler’s repeated “I don’t know, I don’t know, I don’t understand” into “I don’t care, I don’t care, I don’t get it.” The source foregrounds epistemic collapse, not indifference.
sourceReading: Battler screams that he does not know or understand, rejects witches, magic, and the impossible spectacle, and demands to be left alone.

units.text: "Aaaah, I don't care I don't care I don't get it!! I won't accept witches or magic, I won't accept something that fucked up!! Uuooooooooooohhh, I said DON'T TALK TO MEEEE{-E{-E{-E{-E{-E{-E{-E{-E{-E{-E{-E{-EEEEE!!!"
units.japanese: 「あぁ知らねぇ知らねぇわからねぇええ！！　魔女も魔法も認めねぇ、あんな滅茶苦茶も認めねぇ！！　うおおおおおおおおおお、俺に話し掛けるなっつってんだぁああああああああああぁああぁッ！！！」
candidates: don't care I don't care I don't get

description: MG calls the predecessor “a defeated chess piece” outside the board. 取られた駒 is a captured or taken piece: her removal from play, not merely having lost a contest, grounds the explanation that she can no longer act.
sourceReading: Having died, the predecessor is like a captured chess piece resting outside the board and therefore unable to intervene as an active piece.

units.text: "No, I did die. ...Now, I am nothing more than a defeated chess piece loitering outside the chessboard."
units.japanese: 「いいえ、死にましたよ。…今の私は、取られた駒がチェス盤の外でくつろいでいるだけに過ぎません」

description: UP changes Battler’s conclusion “then it is magic itself, I suppose” into the question “could you say it is magic?” The source has him accepting the analogy’s logical consequence, not asking the predecessor to supply it.
sourceReading: Battler reasons that, if he does not know the mechanism, television is equivalent to magic—indeed, magic itself.

units.text: "...It's exactly the same as having a rain ceremony without understanding thermals. ......In other words, if I don't know the principles, even TV is the same as "magic", no, could you say it is magic?"
units.japanese: 「…上昇気流を理解せずに雨乞いをするのとまったく同じだ。……つまり、原理を知らないならば、テレビだって“魔法”も同然、いや、魔法そのものだろうってわけか」

description: MG says “That book lied” for 偽書, which identifies the source as a forged, spurious, or fake book. It changes the status of the document into the anthropomorphic act of lying.
sourceReading: The predecessor jokingly declares Battler’s technical source a spurious book, then offers gremlins as the true explanation.

units.text: "That book lied. Actually, there are small people called gremlins shut up inside the Braun tubes, and they do their work with magic."
units.japanese: 「それは偽書です。真実は、ブラウン管の中に、グレムリンという妖精が閉じ込められていて、魔法で仕事をしてくれているからなのですよ」

description: MG says the island “has been moved” from the world of science, introducing an unnamed mover. The source is intransitive: the island has shifted or moved to the midpoint between science and magic.
sourceReading: Rokkenjima has moved from the world of science to an impartial position midway between the worlds of science and magic.

units.text: ...To a resident of the world of science such as yourself, at a glance, it may feel as though this island had been sucked into a world of magic. That might not be wrong, but it is not accurate. Strictly speaking, it has been moved from the world of science to the gap between that world and the world of magic. So, at a glance, it appears to you as though the world is tilted towards the magical side. ...But, in reality, this island is now in a perfectly impartial position with relation to those two opposing worlds.
units.japanese: …科学の世界の住人であるあなたには、一見、この島は魔法の世界に飲み込まれてしまったように感じるでしょう。それは正しくもありますが正確ではない。厳密には、科学の世界から、科学と魔法の世界の中間に移ったのです。だから、あなたには一見、世界が魔法側に傾いたように見える。……しかし実は、２つの相反する世界にとって限りなく公平な位置に、今のこの島はあるのです。
candidates: moved from the world of science

description: MG asks whether everything has been “totally not in my favor,” an unidiomatic negated construction for Battler’s complaint that developments have been overwhelmingly disadvantageous to him.
sourceReading: Battler objects that every development has been overwhelmingly unfavorable to him, despite the claimed impartiality.

units.text: "...I don't really get it... The gap between reality and magic? A perfectly impartial world? How's that? Hasn't pretty much everything that's happened been totally not in my favor...?!"
units.japanese: 「……よくわからねぇ…。現実と魔法の中間？　限りなく公平な世界？　どこがだよ。俺に圧倒的に不利な展開ばっかりじゃねぇかよ…！」

description: MG changes merely lending an ear to Beatrice’s claim into already finding it convincing. The source says listening may make a claim sound or look true; conviction is the possible result, not the condition.
sourceReading: If Battler listens to Beatrice’s claim, it may consequently sound and appear as though it were true—exactly what he was made to see.

units.text: "At this moment, both your claim and that child's claim exist in the court at the same time. ...If you find your opponent's claim convincing, it might sound like truth to you. It might look like truth to you. That is exactly what you saw."
units.japanese: 「この瞬間、法廷には、あなたの主張とあの子の主張が同時に存在する。……もしも、あの子の主張に耳を傾けたならば、それはあたかも真実に聞こえてしまうかもしれない。見えてしまうかもしれない。あなたはまさにそれを見せつけられた」

description: MG says “that set of truths shrinks with observation.” The source’s それ refers to the uncertain wavefunction, which collapses through observation as possible truths are selected down to one; it is not a set of truths literally shrinking.
sourceReading: Observation collapses the uncertain wavefunction, eliminating innumerable possible truths until one truth remains, like a judicial verdict.

units.text: "That set of truths shrinks with observation, and countless truths are weeded out to become one truth. It is like when, in court, the judge hands down his judgement. The two truths from the prosecutor's and the defense's claims... are reduced in number by the judgement and become one."
units.japanese: 「それは観測されることによって収縮し、無数の真実が淘汰されてたったひとつの真実になる。法廷で例えるならば、これは裁判長による判決行為にも似ているでしょう。検察側、弁護側がそれぞれに主張する２つの真実は、判決によって収縮し、１つとなるのです」
candidates: set of truths shrinks with observation

description: UP writes “victory and loss is not determined,” using a singular verb with the compound subject “victory and loss.”
sourceReading: In the chess analogy, victory and defeat are decided by the players themselves rather than by a judge.

units.text: "That itself is the "game" which that child has challenged you to. Perhaps, instead of a court, I should use chess as an example. Victory and loss is not determined by a judge. You who are fighting will decide it yourselves."
units.japanese: 「それこそが、あの子があなたに挑んだ“ゲーム”なのです。裁判ではなく、チェスと例えるべきでしょう。勝敗は裁判官が決めるのではない。戦っているあなたたち自身が決めるのです」
candidates: Victory and loss is not determined

description: MG removes the closing and reopening quotation marks between Virgilia saying she has no name and then proposing a temporary one, merging two separately punctuated utterances into one.
sourceReading: Virgilia first answers that she has no name; after that utterance closes, she separately proposes taking a provisional name.

units.text: "...Beatrice used to be my name, but now that I have surrendered it, I do not have a name.
units.japanese:
「…ベアトリーチェはかつて私の名でしたが、譲ってしまった今、私は名前を持ちません」
「………ならば仮の名でも名乗りましょう。……ワルギリアス。…いえ、ワルギリアではいかがです？」

units.text: ......So, I shall take a temporary name. ...Virgilius. ...No, how about Virgilia?"
units.japanese:
「…ベアトリーチェはかつて私の名でしたが、譲ってしまった今、私は名前を持ちません」
「………ならば仮の名でも名乗りましょう。……ワルギリアス。…いえ、ワルギリアではいかがです？」

description: MG says Virgilia looks forward to seeing how far Battler can “fight with” her disciple. The source and context mean how far he can fight against Beatrice; “with” permits the opposite relation of fighting alongside her.
sourceReading: Virgilia looks forward to seeing how far Battler can carry his fight against her disciple Beatrice.

units.text: ...Come, if your heart is prepared, return to your opponent, ...return to the chessboard where that child is seated. ...I look forward to seeing how far you can fight with my disciple."
units.japanese: 「…さぁ、心の準備がいいなら、あの子の元へ、……あの子の座するチェス盤の正面へお戻りなさい。……私の弟子とどこまで戦えるか、楽しみにしていますよ」

description: MG weakens Battler’s observational declaration “this is what is inside the cathode-ray tube” to “it’s just like the inside of a Braun tube.” The source identifies the present empty garden as the decisive inspection, not merely an analogy resembling one.
sourceReading: The absent towers and spears in the present garden are, for Battler’s argument, the observed contents of the tube that collapse the competing account.

units.text: "In this rose garden, where do you see those spears, and towers you made lying around? ......They aren't here, are they? ...In other words, it's just like the inside of a Braun tube."
units.japanese: 「この薔薇庭園のどこに。お前らがにょきにょき生やした塔が、槍が。どこに転がってんだ。…………ねぇじゃないか。……つまり、こいつがブラウン管の中身ってわけさ」
candidates: it's just like the inside of a Braun tube

description: MG says Beatrice “had the fight occur inside a barrier,” making her cause or arrange the fight. The source says she herself fought within a barrier to prevent damage.
sourceReading: Beatrice says that she fought inside a barrier so the battle would cause no damage or effect in reality.

units.text: "......... ...Hahaha, hahahahaha! Come now, of course I can't make a huge mess when it's only the first twilight, and I am rather fond of that rose garden, you see? To prevent any damage, I had the fight occur inside a barrier. So it's only natural that it wouldn't have any influence on reality."
units.japanese: 「………………。……ははは、はっはっはっはっは！　あのなぁ、さすがに第一の晩から大暴れは出来ぬし、妾もこの薔薇庭園は気に入っているのでな？　被害を及ぼさないため、結界の中で戦っておったのだ。だから現実には何の影響も与えていないのは当然のことよ」

description: MG turns the adults’ 思惑—their motives, designs, or agendas—into what they “expected.” The opening sets aside parental intentions before contrasting the children’s hoped-for reunion, not merely forecasts.
sourceReading: Whatever the parents’ private agendas, the children expected only two enjoyable days of deepening ties among the cousins.

units.text: ...Forget what the adults expected. At least for us kids, these were supposed to be a fun couple of days where the cousins deepened their friendship.
units.japanese:
……親たちの思惑はともかく。
少なくとも俺たち子どもにとっては、いとこたちと親睦を深め合うだけの、楽しい二日間のはずだった。

description: UP says the adults were “grasping members of Grandfather’s collection,” treating the rifles as members rather than items.
sourceReading: The adults handle short-barreled rifles from Kinzo’s collection and divide the four matching guns among the four siblings.

units.text: The adults were grasping members of Grandfather's collection... of short‐barrel rifles. ...Apparently a remnant from the period when he was obsessed by westerns, there were four identical guns altogether. Those had been split up between the four siblings: Uncle Krauss, Auntie Eva, my dad, and Auntie Rosa. Paper boxes filled with bullets lay on the table, and the siblings were silently loading their guns.
units.japanese: 大人たちは祖父さまのコレクションとかいう、ショートバレルのライフル銃をいじっていた。…西部劇被れだった時代の名残らしく、そっくりな銃が４丁もあった。それを蔵臼伯父さん、絵羽伯母さん、ウチの親父、楼座叔母さんの４兄弟で分ける。机の上には弾丸の詰まった紙箱が置かれ、４兄弟たちは黙々と弾丸を装填していた。
candidates: adults were grasping members of Grandfather's collection

description: UP begins the isolation conclusion with the malformed phrase “Both us, and the culprit,” omitting the required “of” after “both.”
sourceReading: Both the family and the culprit are trapped on the island until the typhoon passes.

units.text: "......Both us, and the culprit... have been imprisoned on this island, then, until the typhoon passes."
units.japanese: 「……私たちも。そして犯人も。…つまりは台風が通り過ぎるまで、この島に閉じ込められたってわけね」

description: MG reduces Kyrie’s conclusion that “we and the culprit” are trapped on the island to “this island will be closed off,” omitting the explicitly symmetrical confinement of suspects and victims.
sourceReading: Until the typhoon passes, the family and the culprit alike are trapped together on Rokkenjima.

units.text: "...It's the same for us... and the culprit. ...Until the typhoon passes, this island will be closed off."
units.japanese: 「……私たちも。そして犯人も。…つまりは台風が通り過ぎるまで、この島に閉じ込められたってわけね」

description: MG writes “locking the doors and windows at the night.” English requires “at night” or “during the night.”
sourceReading: Natsuhi had ordered strict nighttime locking of the mansion.

units.text: They say Aunt Natsuhi's been strict about locking the doors and windows at the night. And yet, some suspicious person had entered and left the mansion. ...The adults had decided that the inside of the mansion was too large to be safe, so they had pulled out the guns and moved to the guesthouse, where we had been. ......Which brings us to the present.
units.japanese:
夏妃伯母さんは夜間の戸締りを厳重にさせていたという。
にもかかわらず、屋敷の中を不審者が出入りした。…大人たちは、屋敷内は広すぎて安全ではないと判断し、銃を引っ張り出して、俺たちのいるゲストハウスへ移動してきたのだ。………そして現在に至る。
candidates: locking the doors and windows at the night

description: UP twice reduces 出入り—the unknown culprit entering and leaving the mansion—to entry alone. The source stresses that the person could move in and out despite nighttime security.
sourceReading: Despite strict locks, an unknown person entered and exited the mansion, making it a permeable danger zone rather than a secure home.

units.text:
Aunt Natsuhi said that they were strict on locking the doors and windows at night.
And yet, some suspicious person had entered the mansion. ...The adults had decided that the inside of the mansion was too large to be safe, so they had pulled out the guns and moved to the guesthouse, where we had been. .........Which brings us to the present.
units.japanese:
夏妃伯母さんは夜間の戸締りを厳重にさせていたという。
にもかかわらず、屋敷の中を不審者が出入りした。…大人たちは、屋敷内は広すぎて安全ではないと判断し、銃を引っ張り出して、俺たちのいるゲストハウスへ移動してきたのだ。………そして現在に至る。
譲治の兄貴たちは、紗音ちゃんの遺体を一目みたいと懇願するが、大人たちは警察が来るまで駄目だと突っぱねる。それは現場保全のために全ての部屋を封印したというだけの意味ではない。…何しろ、６人も殺した犯人が徘徊した屋敷なのだ。今の右代宮家にとって、本宅であるはずの屋敷は、未知の殺人犯が出入りしている危険地帯も同然なのだ…。

units.text: George‐aniki and us others begged to see Shannon‐chan's body, but the adults refused point blank, saying that we must not until the police arrive. That wasn't just because they had sealed all the rooms to preserve the scene. ...After all, the culprit who had killed six people had wandered about that mansion. To the Ushiromiya family right now, the mansion which should have been their home... was like a danger zone that an unknown murderer had entered...
units.japanese:
夏妃伯母さんは夜間の戸締りを厳重にさせていたという。
にもかかわらず、屋敷の中を不審者が出入りした。…大人たちは、屋敷内は広すぎて安全ではないと判断し、銃を引っ張り出して、俺たちのいるゲストハウスへ移動してきたのだ。………そして現在に至る。
譲治の兄貴たちは、紗音ちゃんの遺体を一目みたいと懇願するが、大人たちは警察が来るまで駄目だと突っぱねる。それは現場保全のために全ての部屋を封印したというだけの意味ではない。…何しろ、６人も殺した犯人が徘徊した屋敷なのだ。今の右代宮家にとって、本宅であるはずの屋敷は、未知の殺人犯が出入りしている危険地帯も同然なのだ…。

description: MG says only George begged to see Shannon’s body. 譲治の兄貴たち is George and the others; UP preserves the group request.
sourceReading: George and the other children plead to see the bodies, but the adults refuse until police arrive.

units.text: George-aniki had begged to see Shannon-chan's corpse, but the adults had refused, saying that he mustn't do so until the police arrived. That wasn't just because they wanted to seal all the rooms to preserve the scene. ...After all, the culprit who had killed six people was wandering about the mansion. To the Ushiromiya family right now, the mansion that should've been their home... was now a danger zone that an unknown murderer could enter and leave at will...
units.japanese: 譲治の兄貴たちは、紗音ちゃんの遺体を一目みたいと懇願するが、大人たちは警察が来るまで駄目だと突っぱねる。それは現場保全のために全ての部屋を封印したというだけの意味ではない。…何しろ、６人も殺した犯人が徘徊した屋敷なのだ。今の右代宮家にとって、本宅であるはずの屋敷は、未知の殺人犯が出入りしている危険地帯も同然なのだ…。

description: MG changes the letter’s game condition from whether the family can solve the epitaph to merely trying to solve it. The announced contest tests successful solution, not participation or effort.
sourceReading: Beatrice states that the game is whether anyone can solve the epitaph, not whether anyone can catch her; failure to solve it brings more sacrifices.

units.text: So that there will be no misunderstandings... The game I seek is for everyone to try and solve the riddle of the epitaph, not for you to try and catch me.
units.japanese:
誤解なきように。
私が求めるゲームは、皆さんが碑文の謎を解けるかどうかであって、私を捕まえられるかどうかではありません。

description: UP writes “more wise” where the standard comparative is “wiser.”
sourceReading: The letter says it is wiser to spend time solving the epitaph than searching for Beatrice.

units.text:
If you do not solve the riddle of the epitaph, the pitiful sacrifices will further increase in number.
It would be more wise to spend your time solving the epitaph than searching for me.
units.japanese:
碑文の謎を解かなければ、哀れな生贄はさらに増えるでしょう。
時間は、私の姿を探すより、碑文の謎解きに割いた方が賢明です。
candidates: time solving the epitaph than searching

description: UP writes “had been secretly been challenging,” duplicating the auxiliary “been.”
sourceReading: Although they mocked it publicly, the relatives secretly tried to solve the riddle and none had succeeded.

units.text: Ever since it was first displayed there several years ago, all the relatives, despite making fun of it in the open, had been secretly been challenging that riddle in private. However, up until today, no one had solved it. We had once again been told to solve that unintelligible riddle, and this time, we had been threatened that if we didn't solve it, we would all be killed. ......If this wasn't a "game", what would you call it...
units.japanese: 何年か前に掲げられて以来、親族たちは口では馬鹿にしながらも、影ではこっそりその謎に挑戦していたという。しかし、誰も解けずに今日に至っている。その難解な謎を、解いてみろと再び突きつけ、しかも解けなければ皆殺しだと脅迫している。……これを“ゲーム”と言わずして何というのか…。

description: MG says the adults “loaded their guns” to distract themselves from tension. The source says they handled, fiddled with, or fingered the guns; loading had already been described separately.
sourceReading: The adults handle their guns as a nervous distraction while fatigue already shows early in the long day.

units.text: After the adults carefully checked that the doors and windows in the guesthouse were locked, they set up camp in the lobby. As they loaded their guns to distract themselves from the tension, their expressions showed that they were already fatigued from this long day, which had still barely begun...
units.japanese: 大人たちは、ゲストハウス内の戸締りを厳重に確認した後、このロビーを砦に見立てる。そして銃を弄って緊張を紛らわしながら、まだまだ始まったばかりの長い一日に、早くも疲労の表情を見せるのだった…。
candidates: loaded their guns to distract themselves

description: UP says Madam “would turn out to be our enemy,” making her status an eventual discovery. The source says Beatrice’s side has made Madam their foe, emphasizing the present alignment and agency in opposing her.
sourceReading: Ronove remarks that having Madam as their enemy will be troublesome because she can read many of their moves.

units.text: "......Imagine that Madam would turn out to be our enemy. How unfortunate, Milady. ...Our moves will be read thoroughly."
units.japanese: 「……マダムを敵に回すことになるとは。厄介ですね、お嬢様。…手の内をだいぶ読まれますよ」
candidates: Madam would turn out to be our enemy

description: MG omits the closing quotation after Virgilia’s “Yes” and the reopening mark before her reconstruction, merging two separately punctuated utterances.
sourceReading: Virgilia first acknowledges Battler, then begins a distinct formal statement about Shannon’s body and master key.

units.text: "Yes.
units.japanese:
「はい」
「………紗音の遺体はマスターキー１本を所持。発見した親族がこれを回収」

units.text: ......Shannon's corpse was in possession of one master key. The relatives who discovered her collected this."
units.japanese:
「はい」
「………紗音の遺体はマスターキー１本を所持。発見した親族がこれを回収」

description: MG first calls the five master keys collectively “the master key,” then says the one individual key can unlock “certain rooms.” The source defines one unique individual key for one specific room in addition to the five master keys.
sourceReading: Each specific room can be opened by any of the five master keys or by exactly one unique individual key assigned to that room.

units.text: "...The key to a second floor guest room... The only key other than the master key that can open the door to that second floor guest room. Is that definition correct?"
units.japanese:
「……２階客室の鍵…。それは、２階客室の扉を、マスターキー以外に唯一開けることができる鍵だ、という定義でいいのか？」
「つまり、ある特定の部屋を開けるには、マスターキー５本に加え、その１本しかないというわけです」

units.text: "In other words, apart from the five master keys, there will be only one key that can unlock certain rooms."
units.japanese:
「……２階客室の鍵…。それは、２階客室の扉を、マスターキー以外に唯一開けることができる鍵だ、という定義でいいのか？」
「つまり、ある特定の部屋を開けるには、マスターキー５本に加え、その１本しかないというわけです」

description: UP repeatedly labels the third-floor 控え室 a “servants’ quarters.” The noun is a waiting or anteroom; “quarters” instead identifies residential accommodation.
sourceReading: The envelope contains the key to the third-floor waiting room, where Gohda’s body is found inside the next locked room.

units.text: "And like Shannon, there was a Western envelope discovered alongside her. Inside was the key to the third‐floor servants' quarters. The relatives moved to the third‐floor servants' quarters."
units.japanese:
「そして紗音同様に遺体の傍らに洋形封筒を発見。中には３階控え室の鍵が。親族は３階控え室へ移動」
「そして３階控え室の扉にも魔法陣で、さらに施錠されていて？」

units.text: "And there was a magic circle on the door to the third‐floor servants' quarters, and that door was locked?"
units.japanese:
「そして紗音同様に遺体の傍らに洋形封筒を発見。中には３階控え室の鍵が。親族は３階控え室へ移動」
「そして３階控え室の扉にも魔法陣で、さらに施錠されていて？」

description: MG says Beatrice sticks her tongue “at” Ronove. The source only says she sticks out her tongue without shame after his rebuke; it does not direct the gesture at him.
sourceReading: After Ronove admonishes her, Beatrice unapologetically sticks out her tongue.

units.text: When Ronove rebuked her, Beato stuck her tongue at him without showing any signs of shame.
units.japanese: ロノウェがたしなめると、ベアトは悪びれた様子もなくペロリと舌を出す。

description: MG changes Beatrice’s habitual “I end up in a good mood whenever I play with Battler” into the completed event “Playing with Battler just put me into such a good mood.”
sourceReading: Beatrice explains that playing with Battler habitually or inevitably puts her in a good mood.

units.text: "Uhihihi, sorry, sorry. Playing with Battler just put me into such a good mood.
units.japanese: 「うっひっひっひ、悪ぃ悪ぃ。ついつい戦人と遊んでると上機嫌になってしまうのでなァ」
candidates: Playing with Battler just put me into such a good mood

description: MG turns Battler’s “I’ll search for a weakness” into the command “Search for a weakness!!” Coming immediately after his order for Virgilia to reconstruct the scene, this transfers the analytical action to her.
sourceReading: Battler orders Virgilia to reconstruct the scene, then declares that he himself will look for a flaw, beginning with the possibility that someone played dead.

units.text: "Virgilia, let's reconstruct the crime scene! Search for a weakness!! Were they all definitely dead? If one of them is just playing dead, this isn't a closed room at all!"
units.japanese: 「ワルギリア、事件現場を再構築！　粗を探すぜ！！　全員は間違いなく死亡してるのか？　誰かが死んだふりしてんならこんなの密室でも何でもねぇ！」

description: MG tells Battler to “kneel to the fact” that Beatrice controls locks. The source tells him to kneel and watch her freely control the locks with magic; the object of worshipful observation is her demonstration, not an abstract fact.
sourceReading: Beatrice taunts Battler to kneel obediently and watch her use wonderful magic to control the locks at will.

units.text: "...What will you do, what will you dooo? As if a human could manage anything by now. Obediently kneel to the fact that I can control locks at will with my wonderful magic, okaaaaaay?"
units.japanese: 「……どうするどうするゥ？　人間にはもはやどうしようもないであろうがぁ。大人しく妾がステキな魔法で鍵を自由自在にするところを跪いて拝見しろよぉおぉ？」

description: MG writes “So they somehow killed from outside the rooms,” leaving the transitive verb “killed” without its required object. The source says the culprit killed the victims somehow from outside.
sourceReading: If the culprit was not inside, the culprit was outside and somehow killed the six victims from there.

units.text: "...Up until this point, I've just been checking for the classic tricks. Now's when our showdown over the closed rooms really starts, okay...? If the culprit isn't on the inside, they're on the outside. So they somehow killed from outside the rooms."
units.japanese: 「…ここまでは古典の確認だ。お前との密室対決はここからだぜ…？　犯人は内側にいないなら、外にいる。そして外からどうにかして彼らを殺したんだ」
candidates: somehow killed from outside the rooms

description: MG defines a trap by absence of “the one who planned it out.” 仕掛け人 is the person who sets or operates the device; planning and physical setup are distinct roles, and the trap definition concerns direct participation by the setter.
sourceReading: A trap is any device capable of carrying out murder without direct involvement by the person who set it.

units.text: "Pu ku ku... So, it refers to all arrangements that could carry out a murder without the direct participation of the one who planned it out. Perhaps we might sum it up that way."
units.japanese: 「ぷっくっく…。仕掛け人が直接関与することなしに殺人を遂行できる全ての仕掛け、という定義でよろしいかと思いますよ」

description: MG changes Battler’s past counterfactual—if Beatrice had displayed magic at that moment, he would have surrendered—into a present possibility: if she “decided” to show magic, he “might” surrender.
sourceReading: Battler retrospectively recognizes that, had Beatrice shown magic at his moment of weakness, he probably would have submitted; that was her established tactic.

units.text: "...And if you decided to show off some bizarre magic at this moment, I might even have surrendered. ......It's that favorite strategy of yours.
units.japanese: 「……このタイミングで、お前におかしな魔法を実演されたら、そりゃあ屈服もしてただろうさ。………これがお前の得意戦術だ」

description: MG says it “has been announced” that Kinzo has little time left. 余命を宣告される means receiving a terminal prognosis or being told one’s remaining lifespan, not a public announcement.
sourceReading: Kinzo has been given a prognosis that he has little time left, supplying a possible motive to use his death as a message.

units.text: "...Well, one cannot be certain that there was no motive. ...For example, it has been announced that Kinzo only had a short time left to live. Perhaps he did not regret losing his short remaining life and used his own death to send a message. ...It might be possible to attach such a motive.
units.japanese: 「……まぁ、動機がないとは言い切れませんね。…例えば、金蔵は余命があとわずかと宣告されています。残りわずかの生を惜しまず、自らの死をメッセージとした、…という動機付けも不可能ではないかもしれません」

description: MG renders Battler’s “this is checkmate” as “this’ll stop you,” weakening the explicit game-state claim made by the stronger homicide repetition request.
sourceReading: Battler declares the all-homicide repetition request checkmate because it would eliminate the culprit-suicide construction.

units.text: "Right!! But suicide's a naive word that won't corner her!! Beato, this'll stop you!!
units.japanese: 「あぁ！！　だが、自殺なんて甘い言い方じゃ追い詰められねぇぜ！！　ベアト、こいつで詰めだ！！」

description: UP says the culprit “carried out a suicide” after constructing the locked room. 自殺を図った means attempted or undertook suicide; completion is precisely what the following exchange has not yet established.
sourceReading: Battler hypothesizes that one of the six was the culprit and attempted or undertook suicide after constructing the locked room.

units.text: "Checkmate!! One of the six was the culprit, and they carried out a suicide after constructing the locked room! We're done!!"
units.japanese: 「チェックメイト！！　６人の中に犯人がいて、密室構築後に自殺を図った！　以上だッ！！」
candidates: carried out a suicide after constructing the locked room

description: UP renders Battler’s irritated tongue click `ちッ` as “Heh,” turning annoyance at Beatrice’s successful red reply into a small laugh.
sourceReading: Battler clicks his tongue in frustration, admits she could state the red denial after all, and notices her panic.

units.text: "Heh, ......what the hell, so you can say it... ...But isn't that weird? Why are you so panicked...?"
units.japanese: 「ちッ、……何だよ、言えるじゃねぇかよ…。…だがおかしいな。何であんなに狼狽してるんだ…？」

description: MG turns Virgilia’s judgment that Ronove’s strategy-time request presents no problem into advice that Battler should accept the request.
sourceReading: Virgilia judges the request legitimate and says she believes there is no problem with granting it.

units.text: "...It's a fair request. Perhaps you should accept it."
units.japanese: 「……正当な要求です。問題ないかと」

description: MG replaces Beatrice nearly misjudging when to withdraw with the generic claim that withdrawal would have been the correct move.
sourceReading: Beatrice became fixated on escaping check, was ready to sacrifice major pieces, and nearly mistimed her strategic withdrawal before Ronove intervened.

units.text: "Ronove certainly is thinking clearly. ...He probably gave your opponent some time to cool down. ...That child grew too stubborn trying to remove your check... and was about to easily let several large pieces go. ...After all, the first twilight is only a skirmish. ...The correct move at that time would have been to withdraw."
units.japanese: 「ロノウェは冷静ですね。…おそらくあの子に頭を冷やす時間を与えたのでしょう。……あの子はあなたのチェックを外すことに意地になり、いくつかの大駒を易々と見捨てようとしていた。…第一の晩など、所詮は前哨戦。……あの子は引き際を誤り掛けた」

units.text: "Ronove is composed. ...He probably gave that child some time to cool her head. ......That child was stubbornly trying to remove your check, and was going to easily let several large pieces go. ...After all, the first twilight is only a skirmish. ......That child mistook her timing."
units.japanese: 「ロノウェは冷静ですね。…おそらくあの子に頭を冷やす時間を与えたのでしょう。……あの子はあなたのチェックを外すことに意地になり、いくつかの大駒を易々と見捨てようとしていた。…第一の晩など、所詮は前哨戦。……あの子は引き際を誤り掛けた」

description: UP says Battler should “measure this as” his victory. 判断して良い means he may regard or count it as his win; “measure” is an unnatural calque that obscures the judgment.
sourceReading: Virgilia tells Battler it is reasonable to count the exchange as his victory despite Beatrice limiting her losses.

units.text: "However, you should measure this as your victory. They seem to have just barely prevented a large loss, but without a doubt, you dealt considerable damage. ......I am sure you were able to understand well the depths of that wound by watching the way she panicked."
units.japanese: 「でも、これはあなたの勝ちだと判断して良いでしょう。向こうはぎりぎりで大きな損失を踏み止まったようですが、それでもかなりのダメージを与えたに違いありません。……その傷の深さは、あの子の狼狽ぶりから充分理解できたはずですよ」

description: MG says Beatrice’s sorry state after the tables turn is “the best she’s got.” このザマ criticizes the pathetic state she is in, not the quality of her attempted retaliation or performance.
sourceReading: After mercilessly mocking Battler when he seemed likely to lose, Beatrice is now reduced to this pathetic state when their positions reverse.

units.text: Even though she ridiculed me horribly when I showed signs of defeat, this is the best she's got when the tables are turned. I did feel that was pretty cowardly of her, but I decided to act with dignity as the victor and let it slide.
units.japanese: 俺が敗色濃厚な時はさんざん嘲りまくってくれたくせに、自分が逆になるとこのザマと来た。何だか卑怯なヤツだなとは思うが、そこは勝者の貫禄で飲み込んでおくことにする。

description: MG says the true enemy of a siege is keeping fear of the unseen culprit alive. The source says the challenge is sustaining the siege itself for a long time, despite that fear.
sourceReading: The greater enemy of holding out may be whether the group can sustain the siege over time, rather than its fear of the unseen culprit.

units.text: When being beseiged, your true enemy isn't so much the fear of an unseen culprit... as it is keeping such fears alive for long periods of time.
units.japanese: 篭城の真の敵は、姿の見えぬ犯人への恐怖より、それを延々と持続させることができるかどうかの方かもしれない。

description: UP literally renders 人垣 as “a fence of people.” The established expression means that the onlookers naturally formed a crowd around the copied epitaph.
sourceReading: Everyone immediately peers at the epitaph sheet, naturally forming a crowd around it.

units.text:
Natsuhi immediately brought a B4 blank sheet of paper from the servant room. Kyrie borrowed Eva's notebook, wrote out the epitaph on the paper, and laid it out on the table. Straight away, everyone peered down at it.
...A fence of people naturally formed.
units.japanese:
すぐに夏妃は、使用人室からＢ４ほどの無地の紙を持ってきた。霧江は絵羽の手帳を借りると、そこに碑文を書き出し、テーブルの上に置いた。それを一同はさっそく覗き込む。
…自然と人垣が出来た。

description: UP ends Kyrie’s conclusion with the ungrammatical fragment “say specifically what river.” The source says the first two lines should identify this particular “river” clearly, rather than leave its identity vague.
sourceReading: Those two lines alone must permit a clear identification of the specific “river,” instead of leaving the reader uncertain which river is meant.

units.text: "......I don't know. In any case, after just these two lines, it's not something vague like you don't know which river it is... you're able to narrow it down and say specifically what "{loghint:kawa:river"."
units.japanese: 「……わからないわ。とにかくその２行だけで、どの川かわからないとか、そんなあやふやじゃなくて。はっきりとこの“川”という特定ができるのよ」

description: UP renders お手上げ as “we’re screwed.” Rudolf says they are stumped or at a loss unless they identify the sweetfish river; the added vulgarity overstates both register and predicament.
sourceReading: They are at an impasse unless they can identify what the “sweetfish river” really is, especially since it need not be a literal river.

units.text: "So we're screwed unless we know what the "sweetfish river" really is... And there's no guarantee it even means a literal river."
units.japanese: 「“鮎の川”の正体がわからねぇとお手上げか…。しかも文字通り、河川を指した保証もねぇと来た」

description: UP says Battler has reached a level where he can “go along with” Beatrice. 釣り合う means matching or being a worthy equal to her, which is the basis of her claimed satisfaction.
sourceReading: Beatrice claims she is pleased that the previously inadequate Battler has finally reached a level commensurate with her own.

units.text: "......Noooope? I'm not dissatisfied about that. I'm actually more satisfied now that that worthless Battler has finally reached the level where he can go along with me."
units.japanese: 「……べーつにぃ。そんなの不満ではないぞ。不甲斐ない戦人がようやく妾に釣りあうレベルになったのでむしろ満足してるくらいだぞー」
candidates: level where he can go along

description: UP says Ronove “hid himself” after Beatrice ordered him away. 姿を消す here describes him vanishing from the scene, not remaining present but concealed.
sourceReading: At Beatrice’s command, Ronove bows and vanishes, leaving Beatrice and Virgilia behind.

units.text: Ronove bowed his head, still laughing, and hid himself. After that, all that remained was the figure of Beatrice, who was grumpy and irritated, and Virgilia, who was coolly enjoying her tea.
units.japanese: ロノウェは、笑いを混じらせたまま頭を下げ、姿を消す。あとにはカリカリとイラついているベアトリーチェと、涼しげに紅茶を嗜むワルギリアの姿が残った。

description: UP says Battler has “all the right ideas in his head.” すっかり知恵を付けた means he has now acquired substantial tactical wisdom or savvy; it does not certify that all his ideas are correct.
sourceReading: Beatrice complains that Battler has become much savvier, making it difficult to decide how to attack him next.

units.text: ".........But now that Battler has all the right ideas in his head, how should I plot against him...?"
units.japanese: 「………しかし、すっかり知恵を付けた戦人にどう仕掛ければ良いというのか…」
candidates: Battler has all the right ideas in his head

description: UP says Beatrice “harshly boasted” that she surpassed her master. 散々 marks repeated, extensive, or brazen boasting; it does not describe the boast’s manner as harsh.
sourceReading: Virgilia recalls that Beatrice repeatedly and emphatically boasted of surpassing her master.

units.text: "I believe you harshly boasted that you had surpassed your master, correct?"
units.japanese: 「師匠を超えたと散々豪語していた気がしますが？」

description: UP adds “sleep forever” when Eva’s inner voice tells her to get under a futon and sleep if she is so tired. The source contains no permanent or death-adjacent qualifier.
sourceReading: Eva’s inner voice taunts her to give up, resign, and simply go to sleep under a futon if she is that tired.

units.text: ".........Are you going to give up and resign already? If you're that tired, why not just go into a futon and sleep forever...?"
units.japanese: 「………もう投げ出して降参？　そんなに眠いなら、お布団かぶって眠っちゃえば…？」

description: MG says Eva has the book-door “ready to be opened.” The source says she is already opening it yet still cannot reach the other side, which is the frustration driving the breakthrough.
sourceReading: Eva imagines herself with both hands on the door and already opening it, yet still unable to cross to the Golden Land beyond.

units.text: Am I touching the door with both hands, with the book...no, the door right there in front of me, ready to be opened, ...and yet still unable to reach the other side?
units.japanese: 私は、その扉にこうして両手を掛け、ページ、…いや、扉を開いているというのに、その向こうへ未だ至れないと言うのか。

description: UP turns Eva’s startled “Wh-what is this place?!” into the unfinished line “I-isn’t this inside the—?!” introducing an unsupported location guess and leaving the sentence grammatically incomplete.
sourceReading: Eva opens the metal door and asks in shock what this place is; her following first impression is that it might connect to a mansion room.

description: UP says Eva will “succeed all of the gold and the Ushiromiya family inheritance,” then repeats that she has succeeded the family inheritance. The source distinguishes inheriting the gold from succeeding to the family headship; “succeed” cannot directly take the gold as its object in this sense.
sourceReading: Eva confirms that she may inherit all the gold and succeed to the Ushiromiya family headship; the ring proves that she has now succeeded to that headship.

units.text: "...You were the one who sent that letter? So I'll succeed all of the gold and the Ushiromiya family inheritance, right...? You wrote that in your letter. And I overcame that challenge...!"
units.japanese:
「…あの手紙の差出人はあなた？　なら私は全ての黄金と右代宮家の家督を引き継げるのよね…？　あなたはそう、あの手紙に記したわ。そして私はその挑戦に打ち勝った…！」
「今よりそれはそなたのもの。それを指にはめ、兄弟たちの前で高々と掲げるが良い。そなたが今や右代宮家の家督を継いだことに、誰も疑いを挟めぬであろうぞ」
candidates: succeed all of the gold and the Ushiromiya family inheritance

units.text: "From now on, it is yours. You may put it on your finger and display it high before your siblings. None should doubt that you have now succeeded the Ushiromiya family inheritance."
units.japanese:
「…あの手紙の差出人はあなた？　なら私は全ての黄金と右代宮家の家督を引き継げるのよね…？　あなたはそう、あの手紙に記したわ。そして私はその挑戦に打ち勝った…！」
「今よりそれはそなたのもの。それを指にはめ、兄弟たちの前で高々と掲げるが良い。そなたが今や右代宮家の家督を継いだことに、誰も疑いを挟めぬであろうぞ」

description: UP changes Bernkastel’s present judgment that Eva’s succession “is not worthy” of her recommendation into the counterfactual “wouldn’t have been worthy,” implying a past disqualification rather than her current refusal to endorse it.
sourceReading: Bernkastel presently judges the succession a coincidence rather than a miracle and says it is not worthy of her recommendation.

units.text: "......From my point of view, your succession, well, it's more of a coincidence than a miracle. You wouldn't have been worthy of my recommendation."
units.japanese: 「……私から見ればあなたの継承は、まぁ、奇跡というよりは偶然ね。私が推薦するには値しない」

description: UP calques 差し支えない as saying that viewing the young witch as Eva’s internal separate being “may not be a hindrance.” Virgilia says that provisional interpretation is acceptable or presents no problem.
sourceReading: For the time being, it is acceptable to understand the young witch as a visualization of a separate entity within Ushiromiya Eva, though Battler should not accept that interpretation uncritically.

units.text: "For now, grasping it as a visualization of a different being inside Ushiromiya Eva may not be a hindrance, I believe."
units.japanese: 「右代宮絵羽の内面的別存在の視覚化、と今は捉えていただき、差し支えないかと思いますよ」

description: UP says the gathered audience applauds “as though he had ended some kind of ceremony,” making Battler the agent who ended it. The narration only observes that some ceremony seems to have concluded at that point.
sourceReading: When Battler joins the louder clapping, the assembly responds with great applause as though a ceremony has just ended, making his and Beato’s applause seem like the final recognition required.

units.text: And when he did, as though he had ended some kind of ceremony, everyone present put their hands together in loud applause, and highly praised the newly born Beatrice. It was just as though Battler's and Beato's applause had been the final thing needed for her succession......
units.japanese: すると何かの儀式を終えたのか、そこで一堂は大きな拍手で新生ベアトリーチェを大きく讃えた。それはまるで戦人たちの拍手が、彼女の承認に必要な最後のものであったかのようだった……。
candidates: though he had ended some kind of ceremony

description: MG says thinking about raising money makes Eva’s “headache hurt even worse.” A headache is the pain itself; the source simply says her headache has grown more severe.
sourceReading: Eva covertly invokes the March funding deadline and says thinking about it has made her headache worse.

units.text: "......You're right. Just thinking about raising money by March makes my headache hurt even worse."
units.japanese: 「…………そうね。３月までの金策を考えたら頭痛が酷くなって来ちゃったわ」

description: UP says Maria merely “tends to get irritable” at times like this. 癇癪を起こす means throwing a tantrum, which predicts the loud behavioral episode immediately heard upstairs.
sourceReading: Rosa worries because Maria is prone to throwing tantrums under this kind of stress; the adults immediately hear her stomping and crying upstairs.

units.text: "I wonder if the kids up there have also built up stress. ......I'm worried about Maria. She tends to get irritable in times like this."
units.japanese: 「上の子たちも、だいぶストレスが溜まってるんじゃないかしら。……真里亞が心配だわ。こういう時は癇癪を起こしやすいの」

description: UP changes Maria’s emphatic present identification—“That is Beatrice’s and my rose”—to “That was,” making the shared status sound ended while Maria is insisting it still governs her duty to care for it.
sourceReading: Maria insists that the rose is hers and Beatrice’s, so she must care for it or Beatrice will be angry.

units.text: "Uu‐uu‐uu‐uu!! That was Beatrice's and my rooose!! So if I don't take care of it, Beatrice will get mad at meee!! It might be broken again! Uu‐uu‐uu! Uu‐uu‐uu‐uu!!"
units.japanese: 「うーうーうーうー！！　あれはベアトリーチェと真里亞の薔薇なのー！！　だから大切にしないとベアトリーチェに怒られちゃうのー！！　また折れちゃってるかもしれない！　うーうーうー！　うーうーうーうー！！」

description: UP says “Then you’ve been a witch once too.” The present perfect is incompatible with the completed childhood state and “once” is misplaced; Hideyoshi simply says that Eva was a witch too.
sourceReading: Hideyoshi accepts Eva’s childhood account and says, “Then you were a witch too.”

units.text: "Oh? That so? Then you've been a witch once too."
units.japanese: 「ほぅ。ほんまかいな。じゃあお前も魔女やったんやな」
candidates: you've been a witch once too

description: UP says the noise may be “taking a toll on her headache.” A disturbance can take a toll on Eva or aggravate her headache, but it cannot idiomatically take a toll on the headache itself.
sourceReading: The noise may be aggravating Eva’s headache, causing her to moan and pull the covers over herself.

units.text:
...That was probably very annoying to listen to.
Or maybe it was taking a toll on her headache.
Eva moaned as though in pain, and buried herself in the covers.
units.japanese:
…それがよほど耳障りなのだろう。
あるいは頭痛に堪えるのかもしれない。
絵羽は苦しそうに呻き、布団を被った。
candidates: taking a toll on her headache

description: UP uses “Hideyoshi suggested to call Doctor Nanjo.” Suggest takes a gerund or a that-clause here: “suggested calling” or “suggested that they call.”
sourceReading: Hideyoshi repeatedly proposes calling Nanjo, but Eva firmly refuses.

units.text: ...Even though he understood that, Hideyoshi suspected that this sudden fever was the sign of some serious illness. Several times, Hideyoshi decided to call for Doctor Nanjo, but Eva resisted firmly, ...pleading with him and saying that it was even more important that he didn't take his hand away...
units.japanese: ……そう理屈ではわかっていても、この絵羽の急な発熱は、何か良くない病気の発症ではないかと疑ってしまう。秀吉は何度か南條を呼ぼうと提案したが、絵羽はそれを頑なに拒み、…それより、自分の手を離さないでほしいと懇願する…。

units.text: ......Even though he understood that, Hideyoshi suspected that Eva's sudden fever was the sign of some serious illness. Several times, Hideyoshi suggested to call Doctor Nanjo, but Eva resisted firmly, ...pleading with him and saying that it was even more important that he didn't take his hand away...
units.japanese: ……そう理屈ではわかっていても、この絵羽の急な発熱は、何か良くない病気の発症ではないかと疑ってしまう。秀吉は何度か南條を呼ぼうと提案したが、絵羽はそれを頑なに拒み、…それより、自分の手を離さないでほしいと懇願する…。
candidates: Hideyoshi suggested to call Doctor Nanjo

description: UP writes “a ocean of jelly,” where the vowel sound requires “an ocean.”
sourceReading: The witch offers to drown Rosa in an ocean of jelly.

units.text:
I can let you drown in a ocean of jelly!
I can swallow you up in a mountain of cake!
I can even make you grow butterfly wings and let you fly around the garden! I'll do them one after another, let's start with the ocean of jelly, okay...?!
units.japanese:
あなたをゼリーの海で溺れさせてあげることも！
ケーキの山で飲み込んであげることも！
蝶の羽を生やしてお庭を散歩させてあげることさえね？！順番に叶えてあげるわ、まずはゼリーの海からね…？！

description: UP writes “I’ve done things a little flashy,” using the adjective flashy where an adverb or a manner phrase is required.
sourceReading: Beato acknowledges that she has done various things flamboyantly up to now.

units.text: "...Up until this point, umm, I've done things a little flashy, but, ......umm, ......well, the dignity of the Golden Witch is also important, so, what I'm trying to say is—"
units.japanese: 「…これまではだな、その、妾も色々派手にやってきたわけだが。……その、……まぁ、黄金の魔女としての威厳も大事であり、まぁ、そのだな…、」
candidates: I've done things a little flashy

description: UP repeatedly uses “decorum” for the instruction to exercise restraint: at the concluding 自重気味 and 自重しろ clauses it shifts curbing excess into polite or dignified conduct. The source already distinguishes dignity from the additional demand for self-restraint.
sourceReading: Beato asks the successor to avoid excessive torment, proceed more simply, act with dignity and restrain herself; the successor repeats the restraint instruction resentfully.

units.text: "Well, ...that's all I want to say. So, take care as you continue, alright? Go with dignity, and, ...umm, decorum, befitting the Golden Witch, alright? ......You should do your best. I will be watching over you."
units.japanese:
「ま、…妾が言いたいのはそれだけだ。それでは引き続きしっかりな？　黄金の魔女らしく、貫禄を持って、…その、自重気味にな？　……頑張るが良いぞ。そなたを見守っておる」
「…………………自重しろ……、………か」

「ま、…妾が言いたいのはそれだけだ。それでは引き続きしっかりな？　黄金の魔女らしく、貫禄を持って、…その、自重気味にな？　……頑張るが良いぞ。そなたを見守っておる」
「…………………自重しろ……、………か」

description: UP renders 練りに練った犯行 as a crime “they’ve been planning for ages,” adding a long preparation period where the source specifies thorough, elaborate planning.
sourceReading: Rudolf considers a concealed person familiar with the mansion executing a carefully worked-out crime.

units.text: "......In that case, it's more natural to think there's someone hiding on this island who knows the mansion inside out, carrying out a crime they've been planning for ages. In other words, from the time that the typhoon came to this island and sealed it off from the outside world, there were more than 18 people on this island."
units.japanese: 「……となりゃこの島に、屋敷に精通した何者かが潜んでいて、練りに練った犯行を実行したと考える方が自然だろうよ。つまり、この島には台風が来て外界と途絶された時点で、１８人以上の人間がいたんだ」
candidates: crime they've been planning for ages

description: MG writes “an fool,” where the consonant sound requires “a fool.”
sourceReading: The speaker urges the other to stop doing foolish things and playing witch.

units.text: "Stop acting like an fool...! Haven't you played at being a witch enough? We found the gold. And we've even been promised the position of the Successor. We'll probably need to tightrope walk just a bit, but by now, that's a dream that will definitely come true. ...Beyond that, what more could you wish for...?!"
units.japanese: 「馬鹿なことは止めて…！　魔女ごっこはもう充分でしょう？　私たちは黄金を見つけたわ。そして次期当主の座だって約束されてるわ。ほんの少しの綱渡りは必要だろうけど、もうそれは絶対に叶う夢。……なのにこれ以上、あなたは何を望むというの…？！」

description: MG writes “forcing me support it,” omitting the required to in “forcing me to support it.”
sourceReading: The speaker claims to compensate for immature magical power with Eva’s vitality.

units.text: "My inexperience with magical power is forcing me support it with your vitality. Until I finish the ceremony and become a full witch, you might have to bear the burden. I'll take that as payment for making two of your dreams come true."
units.japanese: 「私の魔力が未熟な分を、あなたの生気で補ってるの。私が儀式を終えて完全な魔女になるまで、あなたに負担を掛けるかもね。それくらいは、２つの夢を叶えてあげた対価ってことにしてもらうわよ」

description: UP writes “every of one them” instead of “every one of them.”
sourceReading: Everyone is exhausted and would collapse if they relaxed their vigilance.

units.text: Hideyoshi and Eva retreated from the lobby. ...Of course, Eva wasn't the only one who wasn't feeling well. They hadn't gotten a wink of sleep since the previous night, and had been pressed by tension since the morning. ...They were mustering their energy to protect their families, but if they relaxed even a little, surely every of one them would be down and out...
units.japanese: 秀吉と絵羽はロビーを退出する。…もっとも、体調が悪いのは絵羽だけではない。昨夜から一睡もしておらず、朝からずっと緊張を強いられている。…家族を守るために気力を振り絞っているが、わずかでも気を緩めれば、きっと誰もがダウンしてしまうに違いなかった…。

description: MG reverses the king metaphor from not carelessly moving about the center to not moving the king away from the center.
sourceReading: The king does not carelessly wander about the center; this is described as royal and witchly dignity.

units.text: "And you don't unnecessarily move your king away from the center. That's part of a monarch's... ...and a witch's dignity!"
units.japanese: 「キングは濫りに中央を動かないものよ。それが王者の、…魔女の貫禄よ！」

description: MG omits the clause identifying the woman’s stolen partner and leaves the malformed continuation “and who’s burned with envy.”
sourceReading: Kyrie demands whether Leviathan understands the madness of a woman whose man was stolen and who has remained envious for eighteen years.

units.text: ".........How could you understand the madness of a woman... and who's burned with envy for 18 years...?!!"
units.japanese: 「………てめぇに男を取られて、１８年間嫉妬し続ける女の凶気がわかるかよ…ッ！！」

description: UP twice substitutes “talk you/someone up” for flirting or chatting someone up, changing the meaning to praising or promoting a person.
sourceReading: Rudolf promises to woo Belphegor in heaven; Kyrie then asks whether he was wooing someone just now.

units.text: "......You were a good woman. Go to heaven before me and do your makeup. I'll definitely come and talk you up."
units.japanese:
「……お前はいい女だったぜ。先に天国で化粧して待ってろ。きっと口説きに行くからな」
「……大丈夫？　今、誰か口説いてなかった？」

units.text: "......Are you alright? Were you talking someone up just now?"
units.japanese:
「……お前はいい女だったぜ。先に天国で化粧して待ってろ。きっと口説きに行くからな」
「……大丈夫？　今、誰か口説いてなかった？」

description: MG changes the actual prior brutal killings into a hypothetical statement about how the witch would normally kill them.
sourceReading: Ronove considers saying that the witch actually killed them far more brutally than the returned bodies reveal.

units.text: Even though Ronove knew it would be superfluous, he contemplated telling Battler the truth. ...Normally, the witch would have killed them in a much, much more horrible way. ...The corpses had been left in this manner only because Beato had suggested to the witch that she show restraint.
units.japanese: ロノウェは蛇足と知りつつ、戦人に伝えるべきかと思った。…本当は魔女は、彼らをもっともっと惨たらしく殺したのだ。……ベアトがそれを控えるようにと魔女に進言したから、この程度の死体で済む。

description: MG writes “the one’s she’d made before,” using the possessive or contraction one’s in place of the plural ones.
sourceReading: Beato’s entrance is somewhat quieter than her earlier appearances.

units.text: After a few heartbeats, gold butterflies gathered together in midair and created Beato's form. ...It was a much more docile appearance than the one's she'd made before.
units.japanese: 数心拍を置いてから、虚空に黄金の蝶が群れ集まり、ベアトの姿を形作る。…それまでの彼女の登場に比べると、幾分、大人しげなものだった。

description: UP weakens Battler’s command not to torment someone into “don’t tease them,” in the explicit context of repeated killing and abuse.
sourceReading: If killing, do it without prolonged suffering; do not toy with lives, and if not killing, do not torment the victim.

units.text: ".........If you're going to kill them, get it over with! Don't toy with them!! If you aren't going to kill them, then don't tease them!! You're taking advantage of the fact that you can do as you will with people's lives, and you've forgotten the sanctity of life. So I can't accept you...!"
units.japanese: 「………殺すなら一思いに殺せ！　弄ぶな！！　殺さないならいたぶるな！！　お前は人の命を自在に操れるのをいいことに、命の尊厳を忘れてしまった。だから俺は認められないんだ…！」

description: MG writes “This was supposed to a fight,” omitting be from supposed to be.
sourceReading: This is supposed to be a contest between a witch and a human, so an unqualified witch cannot be his opponent.

units.text: "...This was supposed to a fight between a witch and a human. If you aren't a witch, then you aren't qualified to be my opponent. ......Understand?"
units.japanese: 「……これは魔女と人間の戦いのはず。ならば魔女でないお前に、俺の相手としての資格はない。………わかるな？」
candidates: between a witch and a human

description: MG writes “I wouldn’t care I met with the wrath of God,” omitting if from the conditional clause.
sourceReading: George would not care even if divine wrath burned him, provided he could revive Shannon.

units.text: "...I wouldn't care I met with the wrath of God and had my body burned. ......Even if it was just for a short amount of time, ...if I could revive Shannon again, .........I would sacrifice the rest of my life to the same research as Grandfather.
units.japanese: 「……神の怒りに触れて、この身を焼かれようとも構わない。………わずかな時間でもいいから、……紗音を再び蘇らせてくれるなら。………………僕は残りの人生全てを、お祖父さまと同じ研究に捧げるよ」
candidates: wouldn't care I met with the wrath of God

description: UP changes Beato’s declaration that she will cast the spell into “I may cast the spell,” making her committed next action sound uncertain or permissive.
sourceReading: Beato says she will cast the spell, whereupon a gap will open in the door to the underworld; she cannot retrieve the soul herself.

units.text: "...I'm telling you that I don't require something like that. ............I may cast the spell. Then, a gap would open in the door to Hades."
units.japanese: 「…そんなもの要らぬというのに。…………妾は魔法を唱える。さすれば冥府の扉に隙間が出来よう」

description: MG misspells definitely as “definitiely” in Krauss’s promise to wake Eva.
sourceReading: Krauss promises that they will certainly wake her if needed.

units.text: "Take it easy. At least close your eyes. If something happens that you need to be awake for, we will definitiely wake you."
units.japanese: 「無理はするな。せめて目を閉じていたまえ。もし、起こさねばならぬ時は必ず起こしてやるから」

description: MG contains the malformed clause “as though it this was” in the holding-cell comparison.
sourceReading: The guesthouse seems to have been only a waiting room for sacrifices to be killed in turn.

units.text: In this way, the four of us decided to leave the guesthouse. ...Even though it should have been safe to barricade ourselves here, ...we lost eight people after doing so. It was almost as though it this was a holding cell from which the sacrifices could be killed one after another.
units.japanese: こうして俺たち４人はゲストハウスを出ることになった。……ここに篭城すれば安全と言って俺たちは篭り、……そして８人を失った。それはまるで、生贄を順番に殺すための控え室でしかなかったかのようだ。

description: MG replaces the continuing difficulty of the road to becoming a true witch with greater length.
sourceReading: The road remains steep/difficult; UP preserves an uphill struggle.

units.text: "......Ha, ...*cackle*... ...I see. ...Yes, the road to becoming a true witch will be much, much longer than this..."
units.japanese: 「…………く、…くっくっく…。…そうか。……本当の魔女への道は、まだまだ険しいなぁ…」
candidates: road to becoming a true witch

description: UP replaces the dismissal of minor opponents with an explicit everyone-except-Eva command, inserting the name Eva before the later direct accusation.
sourceReading: Battler orders the small fry to stand back, then orders the fake witch to sit.

units.text: "If your name's not Eva, get the hell out of here!! And you get in your seat, you goddamn fake witch!! I'll tear that mask of yours off!!!"
units.japanese: 「雑魚は下がっていろッ！！　席に着け、この似非魔女めッ！！　てめえのバケの皮は俺が剥ぐッ！！！」

description: UP adds unsupported eternal duration to the witch’s concession and humiliation taunts.
sourceReading: The witch invites him to concede the contest without an explicit permanent-duration qualification.

units.text: "*cackle*cackle*cackle*cackle*, ahha{0ha{0ha{0ha{0ha{0ha{0ha{0hahaha!! Just do it, resign!! Why don't you just accept it forever? Why don't you just lose forever?!"
units.note: JP1655 explicitly makes solitude eternal, but does not extend that duration to dying, crying or apologizing. PC WH132098 and132217 likewise omit those additions.
units.japanese: 「くっくくくくくくくく、あっはははははははははは！！　しちゃいなさいよぅ、リザイン！！　認めちゃえば？　負けちゃえばぁ？！」

description: UP attaches murdered by that person to Doctor Nanjo’s death rather than to Nanjo, creating a dangling participle.
sourceReading: Nanjo was unquestionably killed by another, openly from the front by that person.

units.text:
I.........no longer knew......what was what anymore. There were absolutely no weak points in her red. She had said in red that all 15 people had died.
She had said in red that no people existed other than the 18. In other words, no more than three people—me, Jessica, and Auntie Eva—existed. And even though none of those three people were the culprit, Doctor Nanjo was killed. And without a doubt, Doctor Nanjo's death was a homicide, murdered by "that person" openly from the front...! And she claims "that person"......is a witch.........?!!
units.japanese:
俺には、………もう、何が何だか、……わからない。ヤツの赤には、一切の隙がない。１５人全員の死亡を赤で語った。
１８人以外に存在しないと赤で語った。つまり、俺と朱志香と絵羽伯母さんの３人しか、存在しない。そしてその３人全員が犯人ではないのに、南條先生が殺された。そして南條先生は間違いなく他殺で、真正面から堂々と“そいつ”に殺害された…！そして“そいつ”が、魔女だと、……言うのか………！！

description: MG uses covered rather than covering after time I spent, producing an ungrammatical verb construction.
sourceReading: Thinking this through would defeat the purpose of having covered his ears.

units.text: So, in other words, ......... ...No, ...I must not think of that. ......If I do, ...then the time I spent covered my ears would be made pointless.
units.japanese: それはつまり、…………………。……いや、……それを考えてはいけない。………それを考えたら、…俺は耳を塞いだことにならないのだ。

description: MG writes “a candy jars,” combining a singular indefinite article with a plural noun.
sourceReading: Objects such as confectionery tins and bottles fall from the shelf.

units.text: She searched around with her hands, trying to find some way to escape. But even though she should have known this room well, just being unable to see made it like a closed room of darkness. She ran into a shelf or something, and things like a candy jars and bottles fell down, hitting her on the head.
units.japanese: 何とか逃れようと、手探りで辺りを探る。しかし、よく知るはずの部屋は、目が見えなくなっただけで、暗黒の密室も同然だ。棚か何かにぶつかってしまい、その上に積んであった菓子缶や瓶のようなものが降ってきて、彼女の頭にぶつかる。

description: MG duplicates as in “I exist only as as a soul now.”
sourceReading: Kanon describes himself as an existence consisting only of a soul.

units.text: "......I exist only as as a soul now. So I cannot touch you, Milady. I cannot do anything except talk to you like this. ...With my current weak existence, I can do nothing more than that, ...but I should be able to be of some aid to you, Milady."
units.japanese: 「………僕は魂だけの存在です。だから、お嬢様に触れることはできません。こうして言葉を掛けることしかできない。……それだけしかできないか弱い存在ですが、…それでもお嬢様の力になれるはずです」
candidates: exist only as as a soul now

description: MG omits Beato’s name before the narration corrects it to Beatrice, leaving no correcting an absent expression.
sourceReading: Beato’s form—no, Beatrice’s form—still stands barring the way.

units.text: The cruel witch was surprised and stepped back. It was thinner than a lace curtain... ...no, Beatrice's form was still standing there. Even after being laid bare so tragically like this, ...she refused to let evil through that door.
units.japanese: 残酷なる魔女は驚き、後退る。レースのカーテンよりも薄い姿だけれど…。……ベアトの姿が、…いや、ベアトリーチェの姿が、まだそこに立ちはだかっていた。このような無惨な姿を晒してなおも、……邪悪にこの扉を譲ろうとしないのだ。

description: UP asserts that the lightning was a direct hit, whereas Japanese places the direct hit and reduction to ash under expectation.
sourceReading: The strike should have hit the woman directly and reduced her to ash, yet not even a hair was singed.

units.text: Beato raised her gold pipe high, and the massive chandelier hanging in the hall crackled with electricity, and from that fell an almighty purple thunderbolt...! It was a direct hit on the woman right below it, and should have turned her to ash. However, ......not a single hair was singed.
units.japanese: ベアトが黄金の煙管を振り上げると、ホールの天上の巨大なシャンデリアがバリバリと帯電して、そこから凄まじい紫の落雷が落ちる…！それは、真下の女に直撃し、消し炭にしてしまうはずだった。しかし、……髪の毛一本、焦がせていない。

description: MG substitutes an icicle for needle ice and separates truth from the explicitly identified spring in the closing metaphor.
sourceReading: She is only needle ice afraid of the spring that is truth.

units.text: "I'll show you that before the truth, you're like an icicle scared of the coming spring! Prepare yourself, Golden Witch! Beatrice!!!"
units.japanese: 「あんたなんて、真実という春に怯える霜柱でしかないことを教えてやるッ！　覚悟なさい、黄金の魔女ッ！　ベアトリーチェ！！！」

description: UP writes why I am rather than why am I in a direct question.
sourceReading: Lambda asks why she alone is not told.

units.text: "Why, why, why I am the only one you won't tell, you meanie!! Okay, in exchange, I'll teach you a special secret that only I know! So tell me!"
units.japanese: 「何よ何よ、何で私にだけ教えてくれないのよ、意地悪ぅー！！　じゃあ、私だけが気付いた、取って置きの秘密を特別に教えてあげるわ！　だから教えなさいよ！」

description: MG misspells Ange’s Japanese name as 縝寿 instead of 縁寿 in the inline name introduction.
sourceReading: The guard announces Ange, 縁寿.

units.text: "...Ange (縝寿)-san has arrived in the lobby below. Should we let her pass?"
units.japanese: 「……縁寿さんが下のロビーに到着しました。お通ししてよろしいですか」

description: MG repeats the absence of a surviving child and omits the accompanying complaint that her fortune will also be stolen.
sourceReading: She leaves no child and even her fortune is taken, which she cannot forgive.

units.text: "......I built this future for George's sake. ...To think that it would be snatched away by you. ...To think that it would be stolen away by Rudolf's daughter... ......I can't bear it. ......To think that not only will I not leave a child, ...without even leaving behind a child... ......That, ...I cannot forgive......!"
units.japanese: 「………譲治のために築いた未来だった。……それを、あんたに掠め取られるなんて。…留弗夫の娘に奪われるなんて…。………私は悔しい。……子も残せず、…財産すらも奪われるなんて、………それが私には、……許せない…………！」

description: MG omits to after great in great let you have that kind of life.
sourceReading: Eva wants to invite Ange into that life.

units.text: Oh, every day really is wonderful, you see? I decided it'd be great let you have that kind of life, when you're so young and have so much ahead of you. Doesn't that sound absolutely wonderful?"
units.japanese: 「あぁ、本当に素敵な毎日よ？　そんな日々に、若くて先の長いあなたを、ぜひ招待してあげようと思いついたの。本当に素敵でしょう？」
candidates: great let you have that kind of life

description: MG writes as though if were absolute truth instead of as though it were.
sourceReading: The rumor is whispered as if true.

units.text: During that time, the talk shows were always mentioning Ushiromiya Eva, always spreading rumors about her countless financial misdeeds. ...Those who knew who her "daughter" was naturally began to keep their distance. ...Even now, she was called a witch at school, and anytime something bad happened, even if there was no proof, it would be whispered—whispered as though if were absolute truth—that she had imposed her will on the school staff.
units.japanese: 右代宮絵羽はその頃、ワイドショーを常に賑わせ、数々の経済的悪行で常に取り沙汰されていた。……その“娘”であると知る周囲は、自然と彼女を敬遠していく。…彼女は今や、学園においても魔女と呼ばれ、何か良からぬことがある度に、彼女の意を汲んだ学校側が何か工作をしたのだと、証拠もなく真実のように囁かれている。

description: MG combines that and the same in Every time I had that the same dream.
sourceReading: Each occurrence of the same dream repeats her effort.

units.text: ...Every time I had that the same dream, I uselessly tried to stretch out my hand even more forcefully, over and over and over. Even if only Battler nii-san had lived... ......Then, perhaps, we'd at least be able to support each other in my cold and lonely reality. But his hand never reaches me.
units.japanese: ……私は同じ夢を見る度に、さらに力強く手を伸ばそうと、夢の中で無駄な努力を繰り返すのだ。せめて戦人兄さんだけでも、生きていてくれたなら。………私はこの冷たく寂しい現実を、せめて二人で支えあいながら生きていけるのではないか。でも、その手はいつも、届かない。
candidates: Every time I had that the same dream

description: MG changes a rumor that the school acted in accordance with Ange’s wishes into a claim that she imposed her will on the staff.
sourceReading: The school is said to have arranged something by anticipating or following her wishes.

units.text: During that time, the talk shows were always mentioning Ushiromiya Eva, always spreading rumors about her countless financial misdeeds. ...Those who knew who her "daughter" was naturally began to keep their distance. ...Even now, she was called a witch at school, and anytime something bad happened, even if there was no proof, it would be whispered—whispered as though if were absolute truth—that she had imposed her will on the school staff.
units.japanese: 右代宮絵羽はその頃、ワイドショーを常に賑わせ、数々の経済的悪行で常に取り沙汰されていた。……その“娘”であると知る周囲は、自然と彼女を敬遠していく。…彼女は今や、学園においても魔女と呼ばれ、何か良からぬことがある度に、彼女の意を汲んだ学校側が何か工作をしたのだと、証拠もなく真実のように囁かれている。

description: MG changes the nearest cage into the cage that wraps the tightest around Ange.
sourceReading: The surrounding guards are the cage closest to her.

units.text: At that time, I heard a *clunk*. ...It was the sound of the door that opened to the staircase to the roof. It was Aunt Eva's guards. ...They're only "guards" in name. Aren't they the cage that wraps the tightest around me, shutting me in?
units.japanese:
その時、バタンという音が聞こえた。
…屋上へ通じる階段室の扉の開く音だ。絵羽伯母さんのところの護衛どもだった。…護衛とは名ばかり。
私を閉じ込める、もっとも身近な檻じゃないか。
candidates: cage that wraps the tightest around

description: UP uses the past perfect “the vase had been broken” at the exact moment the child broke it, making the vase sound already broken before her act rather than stating the resulting fact that “the vase was broken.”
sourceReading: The narrator says that from the moment she broke the vase, the fact or fate “the vase was broken” had been established.

units.text: I understood the meaning of what Beatrice had said. ...At the time that I broke the vase, "the vase had been broken". Beatrice had shown me that the vase had been restored, but that had been a temporary thing. It didn't mean the fate that "the vase had been broken" had changed.
units.japanese: 私はベアトリーチェが言った意味を理解します。…私が壷を割ってしまった時点で、“壷は割れた”のです。ベアトリーチェは、壷を蘇らせて見せたが、それは仮のもの。“壷は割れた”という運命までも変えたわけではない。

description: MG makes Beatrice offer discipleship until the child gets tired “of me,” while お飽きになるまで leaves the object general and the original WH wording correctly makes it until she gets tired of the arrangement.
sourceReading: Beatrice conditionally accepts the child as her disciple until the child grows bored or tired of it.

units.text: "...I understand. Then, until you get tired of me, I will make you my disciple. ...Will you call me Teacher?"
units.japanese: 「……わかりました。では、姫様がお飽きになるまで、私の弟子にして差し上げましょう。…私のことを、お師匠様と呼べますか？」

description: UP leaves Beatrice’s reflection at row 156 as the sentence fragment “A name that I had yearned for ... now just another one of my titles,” omitting the finite verb connecting the former aspiration to its present status.
sourceReading: The title once represented Beatrice’s highest aspiration, but is now merely one of her titles.

units.text: Endless Witch, was it? A name that I had yearned for in the past as the highest achievement...now just another one of my titles. No, you can even call it a name.
units.japanese: 無限の魔女、か。かつては憧れた、最高の到達点の称号は今や、妾にとってほんの肩書きのひとつでしかない。いや、代名詞とすら言っていいか。
candidates: now just another one of my titles

description: UP renders 代名詞 as merely “a name,” losing Beatrice’s claim that Endless Witch has become virtually synonymous with her or functions as her defining epithet.
sourceReading: Beatrice says Endless Witch is more than one title among many and could almost be called her synonym or defining byword.

units.text: Endless Witch, was it? A name that I had yearned for in the past as the highest achievement...now just another one of my titles. No, you can even call it a name.
units.japanese: 無限の魔女、か。かつては憧れた、最高の到達点の称号は今や、妾にとってほんの肩書きのひとつでしかない。いや、代名詞とすら言っていいか。

description: MG changes Leviathan’s direct taunt that Battler “got it wrong” into the third-person “He was wrong,” then turns the repetition into “right, right?” as if seeking confirmation.
sourceReading: Leviathan excitedly tells Battler twice that he got the answer wrong before claiming her turn.

units.text: "He was wrong, right, right? Okay, this time it's me, my turn! Wheeere should I strike?!"
units.japanese: 「ハズレたね、ハズレたねぇ？！　さぁ今度は私よ、私の番なのよ！　どぉこを貫いちゃおっかなぁ！」

description: MG renders Leviathan’s childish-defiant いいもん as “okay?!,” turning “Fine, I’ll take his shoulder!” into a request for or challenge about permission.
sourceReading: After being left behind, Leviathan consoles herself defiantly that it is fine because she will take Battler’s shoulder.

units.text: "Waaah!! Me too, me too! I'll take his shoulder, okay?!"
units.japanese: 「わぁん！！　私も私もぉー！　私は肩をもらっちゃうからいいもん！」

description: MG replaces Beatrice’s promise to toy with Battler “over and over again” with doing so “to my heart’s content,” losing the explicit repetition that ties the threat to endless resurrection.
sourceReading: Beatrice orders Battler to recover his form again and says she will toy with him any number of times.

units.text: "Come, Battler. Remember your original form again. I'll toy with you to my heart's content, understand?
units.japanese: 「さぁ、戦人。再び元の姿を思い出すがいい。何度でも弄んでやるぞ？」

description: MG makes the next murder drama something that passively “will unfold,” removing Beatrice’s volitional role in staging it.
sourceReading: Beatrice asks what kind of murder drama she should stage or unfold on the next game board.

units.text: Let's see, what kind of murder play will unfold on the next game board? Come, bring it in. Let the next game begin, Ushiromiya Battleeer!!"
units.japanese: 「さぁて、次なるゲーム盤ではどのような殺人劇を繰り広げよう？　さぁ、新しきゲーム盤を持て。次なるゲームを始めようではないか、右代宮戦人ぁ！！」
candidates: unfold on the next game board

description: UP renders 殺人劇 as a “murder spree,” losing Beatrice’s theatrical framing of the next game as a staged murder drama or spectacle.
sourceReading: Beatrice describes the next board’s killings as a murder drama she will stage.

units.text: "Now then, what kind of murder spree shall I unleash on the next game board? Come, bring the new game board. Why don't we begin the next game, Ushiromiya Battler!!"
units.japanese: 「さぁて、次なるゲーム盤ではどのような殺人劇を繰り広げよう？　さぁ、新しきゲーム盤を持て。次なるゲームを始めようではないか、右代宮戦人ぁ！！」

description: MG reduces “bring the new game board” to “bring it in,” omitting the explicit object and its newness at the transition into Episode 3.
sourceReading: Beatrice orders that a new game board be brought so the next game with Battler can begin.

units.text: Let's see, what kind of murder play will unfold on the next game board? Come, bring it in. Let the next game begin, Ushiromiya Battleeer!!"
units.japanese: 「さぁて、次なるゲーム盤ではどのような殺人劇を繰り広げよう？　さぁ、新しきゲーム盤を持て。次なるゲームを始めようではないか、右代宮戦人ぁ！！」

description: MG reverses Beato’s recognition that Ronove understands into her own assertion that she knows.
sourceReading: So you understand.

units.text: "I-I know that much...! I also...umm...thought that if he was too disheartened to join us at the table, even though the fourth game is finally starting, that would be such a pain, so I came to you, thinking that it'd be better to prepare a counter-measure for that case beforehand...!"
units.japanese: 「わ、わかっておるではないか…！」「妾はそのだな、いよいよ第４のゲームが始まるというのに、もしもあやつが意気消沈していて卓に着かないというようなことがあったら、また面倒だなァと思い、そうならば先に対策を準備した方が良いかと思い、お前に先にそれを問うたわけだ…！」

description: Both re-edits substitute misanthropy for distrust of people.
sourceReading: Such treatment would ordinarily make a person distrust others.

units.text: "Pukukukuku. It is only natural. ...After all, you {nobreak:tho rough ly destroyed him, Milady. That would turn most anyone into a misanthrope."
units.japanese:
「ぷっくくくく。無理もありますまい。…何しろお嬢様が、徹・底・的ッにおやりになられましたからな。普通なら人間不信になりましょうな」
「ほぉ、ニンゲン不信なら好都合！　ニンゲンなど見限って魔女を信じると良いぞ、わっはっはっは……。……………あ、…あぁ、コホン。済まぬ、ふざけが過ぎた」

units.text: "Hoh, distrust of Humans? How convenient! Let him give up on Humans and trust witches, wahahaha... ......O-Oh, *cough*. Sorry, I shouldn't fool around too much."
units.japanese:
「ぷっくくくく。無理もありますまい。…何しろお嬢様が、徹・底・的ッにおやりになられましたからな。普通なら人間不信になりましょうな」
「ほぉ、ニンゲン不信なら好都合！　ニンゲンなど見限って魔女を信じると良いぞ、わっはっはっは……。……………あ、…あぁ、コホン。済まぬ、ふざけが過ぎた」

units.text: "Pukkukukuku. It is only natural. ...After all, you {nobreak:com‐ pre‐ hensively destroyed him, Milady. That would turn most anyone into a misanthrope."
units.japanese:
「ぷっくくくく。無理もありますまい。…何しろお嬢様が、徹・底・的ッにおやりになられましたからな。普通なら人間不信になりましょうな」
「ほぉ、ニンゲン不信なら好都合！　ニンゲンなど見限って魔女を信じると良いぞ、わっはっはっは……。……………あ、…あぁ、コホン。済まぬ、ふざけが過ぎた」

units.text: "Hoh, distrust of Humanhumans? How convenient! Let him give up on Humanhumans and trust witches, wahahaha... ...............O‐...oh, *cough*. Sorry, I took it too far."
units.japanese:
「ぷっくくくく。無理もありますまい。…何しろお嬢様が、徹・底・的ッにおやりになられましたからな。普通なら人間不信になりましょうな」
「ほぉ、ニンゲン不信なら好都合！　ニンゲンなど見限って魔女を信じると良いぞ、わっはっはっは……。……………あ、…あぁ、コホン。済まぬ、ふざけが過ぎた」

description: UP changes facial lotion into eau de toilette in the tears taunt.
sourceReading: Beato wishes she had collected his tears for facial lotion.

units.text: "*cackle*. Then who was that person crying their eyes out in frustration last time? I should've collected your copious tears in a bottle and used it as eau de toilette."
units.japanese: 「くっくっく。前回、あれだけ悔し涙を流しておったのはどこの誰だと言うのか。あの涙をたっぷりと小瓶にでも集め、化粧水にすれば良かったわ」

description: UP turns presumed distribution of the questionnaire into a categorical assertion.
sourceReading: 配布されてるはず expresses expected distribution rather than direct knowledge.

units.text: "You must have been. The dormitory leader distributed a copy to everyone. If you lost it, all you have to do is honestly say so."
units.japanese: 「そんなはずありませんよ。寮長から全員にちゃんと配布されてるはずです。なくしてしまったならそうと素直に仰ればいいのに」

description: UP changes the uncertainly recalled Anti-Rosa brand name to Auntie Rosa.
sourceReading: Ange tentatively recalls アンチローザ, Anti-Rosa, with a slogan rejecting yesterday’s self.

units.text:
Auntie Rosa ran a clothing design company. It did actually seem to have a brand name, too, for what that's worth.
......I think it was just called <Auntie Rosa>, in English...? The slogan was supposedly "I can't forgive the way I was before today". ...Unfortunately, I've never met anyone who knew of that brand name. Maybe it wasn't that famous.
units.japanese:
楼座叔母さんは洋服のデザイン会社をやっている。一応、ブランド名もあるらしい。
……何だっけ、アンチローザだったっけ…？“昨日までの自分が、許せない”、がキャッチコピーらしい。…残念ながら、そのブランド名を知っている人間には会った事がない。あまり有名ではないのだろう。

description: UP omits to in Listen what he said.
sourceReading: Maria excitedly invokes Sakutaro; UP chooses an ungrammatical listen construction.

units.text: "Uu! Playing with Sakutaro! Listen what he said, *giggle*giggle*!"
units.japanese: 「うー！　さくたろと遊んでるの！　さくたろったらね、きゃっきゃっきゃ！」

description: MG changes being bad at room cleaning into disliking it.
sourceReading: 片付けは苦手 describes difficulty or lack of aptitude.

units.text: Maria started fishing around her messy room. Rosa often told her to clean it up, but Maria apparently didn't like doing it. However, Maria herself knew more or less where everything was. So much so that if it were to be cleaned up, she would have trouble finding where anything was.
units.japanese: 真里亞はごちゃごちゃの部屋の中を漁り始める。楼座によく片付けるようにと言われるのだが、どうにもお部屋の片付けは苦手だ。でも、真里亞自身には何がどこにあるのか大よそわかっている。むしろ、勝手に片付けられてしまうと、所在がわからなくなってしまうので困るくらいだ。

description: UP expands Maria’s promised magical achievement into a joint achievement with Ange.
sourceReading: Maria says she will become a wonderful witch, then show Ange her achievement.

units.text: "I know we'll become wonderful witches, flying in the sky on our brooms, and drawing rainbows with our wands, making candy fall from the sky. I know I can do it. And when I do, I'll show you too. It'll be like a scene from a wonderful dream."
units.japanese: 「きっと素敵な魔女になって、箒でお空を駆けて、ケーンで虹を描いて飴玉を空から降らせるの。真里亞はきっと出来るよ。そしたら縁寿にも見せてあげるね。きっとそれは素敵な夢の中のような光景だから」

description: UP adds the insanity epithet nutcase to classmates’ gossip about Ange.
sourceReading: あれぇ refers contemptuously to Ange without an explicit insanity epithet.

units.text: "Messed up... I think the nutcase is seeing ghosts or something."
units.japanese: 「ヤバくない？　心霊とか見えちゃってンじゃないの、あれぇ」

description: MG attaches after Eva’s death to her building the business rather than the subsequent entrustment.
sourceReading: The senior figures were entrusted with Eva’s business group after her death.

units.text: This old gentleman was one of those leaders who had been entrusted with the business group Eva had built up after she passed away. The one he called Chairman was the former Chairman, Ushiromiya Eva. His company once had friendly ties with Hideyoshi's business, and he'd had a close relationship with both Hideyoshi and Eva.
units.japanese: 老紳士は、絵羽亡き後、彼女が築き上げた企業グループを任された重鎮の一人だった。彼が会長と呼ぶのは、前会長、右代宮絵羽のことだ。彼の会社はかつて、秀吉の会社と友好的な関係にあり、秀吉や絵羽とも親密な交流があった。

description: UP adds a lifetime murder plan to the hypothesis of one-time commission.
